issues.title: [Benchmark] bench run stop_engine: taskkill result unchecked and wait timeout discarded, a failed engine kill is silent
issues.author: GoldenLeafBird
issues.body:
`strata_cli/bench_standard.py` at v0.2.1 (commit 90767252), `stop_engine`
(around lines 697-720):

```python
if os.name == "nt":
    subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(proc.pid), "/T", "/F"], capture_output=True, timeout=60)
...
try:
    proc.wait(30)
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    pass
```

The taskkill return code and output are never checked and the wait timeout is
discarded, so a denied or failed kill produces no message. On my run
(2026-10-20, run id 20261020T105417Z-5b4dbf77) the engine start came up in a
state that denied the kill (Access is denied, likely an elevated or stuck
tree), and the runner reported a normal finish while two python processes kept
port 8080 until a manual elevated taskkill. Five freshly started engines on
the same machine died to the first taskkill, so the unchecked result is the
defect; my denied kill was the trigger.

Related, same artifact: the run folder's `engine.log` is 0 bytes by design on
this path, because the serve layer writes to the run config's own log file and
the runner's capture records nothing. Consider pointing the artifact at the
config log path, or noting in the protocol that engine.log can be empty on
Windows.

Reproduction status: one occurrence in one run. Environment: Windows 10 build
19044, source checkout at v0.2.1, RX 7900 XTX, engine 0.1.45.

issues.title: [Other] setup.py WIN_HIP_ASSET still names strata-windows-x64-hip.zip, which no 0.2.x release ships
issues.author: GoldenLeafBird
issues.body:
`setup.py` at v0.2.1 (commit 90767252) fetches the Windows HIP engine through
`WIN_HIP_ASSET = "strata-windows-x64-hip.zip"` (line 3473) from
`releases/latest/download/`. That asset name no longer exists:

- `releases/download/v0.2.1/strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` returns 404.
- `releases/latest/download/strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` redirects to the v0.2.1
  asset and returns 404.
- The zip shipped through v0.1.45 (the 0.1.45 one has SHA-256 starting
  `75a2ff9c`). The 0.2.0-beta and v0.2.1 releases ship per-GPU names instead:
  `Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip.exe`, `Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip-rdna3.exe`,
  `strata-engine-0.1.46-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3.tar.gz`,
  `strata-engine-0.1.46-windows-x86_64-hip-rx9070.tar.gz`.

Effect: on a fresh Windows AMD source checkout at v0.2.1, the engine step of
setup fails with "no ready-made AMD engine for this Strata version" and points
at self-building (`tools\hip\build_windows.bat` plus `START-HERE.bat
--prebuilt`). Machines that installed a 0.1.45 engine earlier are unaffected
until they need a fetch again, because `update_installed_engine` only fetches
when the installed engine is older than 0.1.45. `docs/AMD_HIP.md` (around line
136) still tells users to take the zip "from the release".

Reproduction status: the 404s are live checks. The setup hard-fail text is
code reading, not an executed run (my installed engine passes the minimum, so
the fetch path did not trigger on my machine).

Environment: Windows 10 build 19044, source checkout at tag v0.2.1, AMD Radeon
RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, engine 0.1.45 prebuilt installed.

Suggested fix: teach `WIN_HIP_ASSET` the per-GPU package names (the GPU is
known at setup time), or ship a flat zip again alongside the per-GPU packages.

issues.title: [Engine] Windows HIP (gfx1100): batched PLE block silently misreads prompts in ~1 of 8 engine starts; STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0 fixes it
issues.author: giacomobord-prog
issues.body:
**Setup**
- Windows 11, RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) + RX 7900 XT, i9-13900K, 64 GB DDR5; AMD Adrenalin 26.9.2 (driver 32.0.32015.2008)
- Engine 0.1.45.3 built locally with `tools\hip\build_windows.bat` (`STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1100`, `STRATA_NO_VISION=1`), ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 (TheRock wheels)
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, one card (XTX, `"gpu": 0`), 64K context, `--kv int8`, MTP `--spec 4`, `--prefill auto`, no hipBLASLt tuning table

**Symptom**
In some engine starts every prompt longer than ~64 tokens is misread for the whole session: no error, no NaN, the model answers fluently but about something else ("your message is just `##`", answers in Chinese, an invented question). Prompts of 64 tokens or fewer are always read correctly. Restarting the engine usually clears it. The log of a bad start is identical to a good one (same slots, free VRAM, chunk size); the only visible difference is that a 176-token prompt is read ~15% faster in bad sessions (1.39-1.44 s vs 1.62-1.70 s).

**Reproduction**
A script that starts the server, sends two prompts (102 and 176 tokens, answer must contain a given word/number) and stops it, repeated:

| Configuration | Bad starts |
|---|---|
| default | 3 / 24 |
| `STRATA_PF_STEP_SYNC=1` | 2 / 16 |
| `STRATA_WMMA_GEMM=1` | 1 / 24 |
| `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0` | **0 / 24** |

So the batched PLE block at layer 1 (`prefill.cpp`, `if (l == 1 && ple_on && ple_batch)`: the BF16 key/value GEMMs + `native_ple_postops_batch`) is involved. It does not look like a race between prefill steps (step sync does not help) nor hipBLAS alone (WMMA GEMMs still failed once). The bad state seems to be decided once per engine start and then stays for the session. Possibly related: #224 (illegal memory access in the same block) and #541 (HIP stall avoided by `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0`), both closed - here it fails silently instead.

**Workaround**
`"env": {"STRATA_PLE_BATCH": "0"}` in the run config. Cost on this machine: prompt 810 -> 710 tok/s at 3.5K tokens, 865 -> 814 tok/s at 10.7K; decode unchanged (52-70 tok/s).

Logs of failing starts and the test script are available if useful.

issues.title: [Engine] Recommended IQ3_XXS on 32 GB RAM + 16 GB VRAM generates at 0.5–7 t/s
issues.author: POMXARK
issues.body:
### Problem
The size Strata recommends for 48 GB RAM + VRAM (IQ3_XXS, 47.0 GB) fills system RAM on a 32 GB RAM + 16 GB VRAM PC. Generation runs at 5–7 t/s and drops to 0.5 t/s as the context grows, against the published 62 t/s. The GPU stays almost idle. A simple question in the built-in Strata chat did not finish in 20 minutes.

### Environment
- Strata version / commit: <version>
- OS: Windows 11 23H2 (build 22631)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5080 16 GB, driver 617.14, CUDA 13.4, PCIe Gen3 x16
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5700X (8C/16T)
- RAM: 32 GB DDR4 (XMP: <on/off>)
- Storage: W:\Strata\Strata-data on <NVMe / SATA SSD>
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS (GSQ-RCO)
- Settings: context 64K, resource mode "Leave 20% for my work", image reading on
- Client: the built-in Strata GUI chat with its agent tools (workspace "Strata")

### Reproduce
1. On the PC above, pick the model recommended for 48 GB (IQ3_XXS) and keep the defaults listed above.
2. The Strata UI shows "43.9 GB RAM + VRAM" and "About 10 GB will be read from SSD, so answers may be slower".
3. In a new Strata chat, attach a screenshot and ask: "how do I add the Strata model to OpenCode" (asked in Russian).

### Expected
An answer within a few minutes, with generation close to the published 62 t/s for IQ3_XXS. Otherwise, a recommended size that leaves enough free RAM for a normal desktop session.

### Actual
- The model thinks for 2m 41s, then calls tools: the glob `**/opencode*` times out ("Glob timed out (huge home dir)"), and two pwsh commands run.
- After that the status stays at "Preparing answer..." for 19m 10s with only 869 tokens generated, and no answer is ever given.
- Request log from the Strata dashboard for the same session:

~~~text
time      prompt   reused   output   gen t/s   duration
14:21:38      53        0        1       7.6     16.9 s
14:25:12   7,068        0      897       5.1    5m 55s
14:31:40   8,010    7,964      142       5.8     34.4 s
14:39:49   8,317    8,152      144       5.9     45.1 s
14:40:43  19,139    8,462        2       0.5    3m 42s
~~~
- Prompt processing: 35–50 t/s, while the published figure is 1,750 t/s.

### Evidence
- System RAM: 25.9 / 32 GB after the first requests, 31.0 / 32 GB at 19K context.
- VRAM: 14.1–14.2 / 16 GB; experts in VRAM: 3,405 (5.6 GB).
- GPU load during generation: 6–8 %, power draw 47–58 W out of 360 W.
- PCIe traffic to the GPU: 18–48 MB/s; disk read: 4–6 MB/s.
- The "VRAM hit rate" column is empty ("—") for every request.
- Log: strata-<model>.log attached (sanitized). Screenshots of the chat and the dashboard attached.

Same PC with plain llama.cpp and a model that fits fully in VRAM, used as a coding agent in OpenCode:
~~~bat
llama-server.exe -hf unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-IQ3_XXS ^
  -ngl 99 -c 65536 -fa on -np 1 --jinja --cache-ram 0 ^
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 ^
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2
~~~
Result: 30–70 t/s generation and stable tool calls; a question like this one is answered in a couple of minutes. So the hardware can run a coding model quickly; the slowdown comes from the recommended Strata size not fitting in free memory.

Suggestions:
- Subtract the memory already in use (Windows, browser and IDE take 6–10 GB) when recommending a size, or warn when less than about 8 GB would stay free.
- Show the expert cache hit rate in the UI, so users can tell whether VRAM, RAM or SSD is the bottleneck.

### Reproduction status
Reproduced by me on the hardware above, in one session with several requests. Not yet retested with "Full performance" mode, XMP on, or with other applications closed.


### Test results (update)

Short prompt without tools, new chat in the Strata GUI, same IQ3_XXS model:

> Write a C++17 function that parses a CSV line with quoted fields. No explanation.

~~~text
request                               output   duration   average
CSV function (C++17)                     454    3m 4s     ~2.5 t/s
"how to add the model to OpenCode"     1,183   19m 31s    ~1.0 t/s
~~~

- Settings: context 64K, "Read pictures" on.
- The Strata UI warns: "About 10 GB will be read from the SSD, so answers can be a little slower."
- The dashboard shows Speed as "Unavailable" for these requests, so I could only compute the averages (output / duration). The first figure may include model load time.
- After the requests the model was unloaded ("No model loaded"; RAM 7.0 / 32 GB, VRAM 1.2 / 16 GB).

Storage note: all model files are on an external SSD connected over USB Type-C. llama.cpp loads Qwen3.8-27B from the same drive and still generates at 30–70 t/s, because that model fits fully in VRAM and the drive is read only at load time. With Strata the recommended size relies on reading about 10 GB from this drive during generation, and the UI gives no warning that external or USB storage is unsuitable for that.

issues.title: [Other] Docker 0.2.x: no way to run the engine without the `strata launch` wrapper (re-downloads existing GGUFs, forces an API key)
issues.author: nullata
issues.body:
### Area

[Other] (setup and installation: the Docker image's entrypoint)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Docker

### What happened

I run Strata as a backend for an orchestrator. The orchestrator manages model files, ports, auth, GPU assignment, restarts and the UI. All it needs from Strata is: **here are the weights, serve them on a port.**

The 0.1.x image did that. After rebuilding from `main` (0.2.x), a container started with the GGUF shards already mounted where 0.1.x read them (`/data/models/<tag>/<original name>`) **ignored them and started downloading the model again**. The download is ~70-110 GB. There was no "files not found" error. It just downloaded.

`docs/DOCKER.md` now says *"The old volume layout (`/data/config`, `/data/models`) is not read"*. That was documented after the fact under "From the older image", with no deprecation period. If you pass no `MODEL`, the image picks a model on its own and downloads that too.

**Expected:** an inference server never fetches tens of gigabytes because a path moved. It fails loudly instead.

The re-download is the part I saw. The rest of this report comes from reading the 0.2.x source to work out why. Those items are **unconfirmed static analysis**, marked as such, with file references. They all have the same cause: the 0.2.x image makes `strata launch` (a desktop/TUI flow with presets, tuning, access modes, key generation, a status loop and its own downloader) the only door into the engine, and none of it can be turned off.

#### 1. Mandatory API key, enforced by the wrapper and not the server (unconfirmed static analysis)

`serve/server.py` handles no-key operation correctly: Host-header allow-listing via `allowed_hosts` / `STRATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, origin checks against DNS rebinding, and `/health` outside the auth gate. That's a well-designed keyless mode for a private network.

`strata_cli/cli.py` `_launch_plan()` overrides it:

```python
if host not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1") and not has_key:
    raise ProfileError("non-loopback serving requires an API key in the run config or STRATA_API_KEY")
```

`docker/entrypoint.sh` hard-codes `--access lan`. So inside a container, where loopback-only is useless, a key is always required. If you don't give one, it makes one up and stores it in the volume (`/data/state/api-key`). Going by the code, any client that doesn't send that key gets `401`.

A container on an internal Docker network behind a proxy that does its own auth doesn't need a second key, and that isn't Strata's decision to make. The server already has the right primitive (`STRATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`). The launcher overrules the server's own security model.

#### 2. The 0.1.x env vars were dropped without a replacement (from `docs/DOCKER.md` and `entrypoint.sh`)

`HOST`, `LOW_RAM`, `REINSTALL`, `LAYER_SPLIT`, `RESIDENT_BUDGET_GIB`, `KV_STREAMING` and `CONFIG` are now *"ignored with a warning"*.

- `REINSTALL=1` was the only explicit way to rebuild a model's config after changing context, vision, KV or low-RAM. What replaced it is presets: state saved in the volume that decides which settings win. The entrypoint even deletes your run configs when `GPU`/`GPUS` changes, because `launch --gpu` otherwise doesn't apply to a model that's already set up.
- `LOW_RAM` matters because setup reads the **host's** `/proc/meminfo` and not the cgroup limit. That's still true (the entrypoint now only *warns* about a memory limit), and the override is gone from the image's interface. `setup.py --low-ram` itself still exists.

Warning about an env var and then ignoring it is not a migration path. Either honour them for a release or refuse to start.

#### 3. The container polices its own lifecycle (unconfirmed static analysis)

`docker/entrypoint.sh` runs a loop that calls `strata launch --status` every 10 s and exits after three misses. Liveness belongs to the orchestrator (Docker healthchecks, k8s probes, or whatever started the container), not a shell loop inside it. I haven't seen it fire. But nothing in the loop distinguishes "server gone" from "status probe slow", and with one request at a time and long prefills, that difference matters.

#### 4. Presets, tuning, model "recommendation", access modes, key files

`PRESET`, `TUNE`/`RETUNE`, "Strata picks the model it recommends for this card", `--access local|lan|cloudflare|tailscale`, `--save-preset`, `/data/state/api-key`. These are desktop-app features. In a container they're state the operator didn't ask for, can't see without `docker exec`, and that can change behaviour from one start to the next.

#### 5. Internals moved with no stable surface

`setup.py` moved from `/opt/strata` to `/opt/strata/terminal`, and its tables gained families that don't fit their previous shape (`"ready": True` with no `hf`/`file`; single-file `gyro` without `{i}`). That's fair game for internals. But there is no **supported** machine-readable alternative for an integrator (a catalogue command, a structured setup-progress file), so integrators scrape, and break.

#### Is Strata an engine or an appliance?

Strata currently presents itself as three things at once:

1. **An inference engine** (`serve/server.py` and the engine component): fast, careful, with a sane security model.
2. **An installer** (`setup.py`): reasonable as a one-shot tool.
3. **A consumer appliance** (`strata launch`, presets, tuning, access modes, generated keys, self-supervision).

The 0.2.x Docker image makes (3) the only door into (1). That's the wrong way round for a **container image**, whose users are by definition operators who already run something on top of it.

What makes this worse: **everything an operator needs is still in the image.** `setup.py --setup --yes --no-start --gguf-dir ... --low-ram ...` still accepts every option the wrapper drops. `serve/server.py --engine strata --config ... --host 0.0.0.0` runs keyless with `STRATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (it warns, it doesn't refuse). And `entrypoint.sh` passes through any command that isn't `run`. The engine was never the problem. The wrapper is the problem, because it's the only supported way in.

#### What would fix it

In order of preference:

1. **A supported server-only mode**, e.g. `docker run strata serve` or `MODE=engine`. It runs setup with `--gguf-dir` if needed, then `serve/server.py` on that run config. It never downloads model files, never generates keys, and respects `STRATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. `strata launch` stays the default for people who want the appliance.
2. **Make the launcher honour the server's own options**: keyless with `STRATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, a `NO_DOWNLOAD=1` that turns a missing file into a hard error, and a way to turn off the status loop.
3. **A documented, versioned integration surface**: a JSON catalogue command, a structured setup-progress file, and a promise that the env-var contract only changes at a major version, with a deprecation window.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. With a 0.1.x image, set up a model whose shards sit in the mounted folder: `-v /path/to/IQ2_XS:/data/models/IQ2_XS -e FAMILY=qwen -e MODEL=IQ2_XS`. No download happens.
2. Rebuild the image from `main` (0.2.x) and start it with the same mounts and env.
3. The container starts downloading the model.

Workaround in use: override the entrypoint, run `/opt/strata/terminal/setup.py` in Control mode with `--gguf-dir`, then start `serve/server.py` directly. This depends on internal paths that may move again in the next release.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally: the re-download. Items 1 and 3: unconfirmed static analysis, as marked.

### Strata version

`9ae93f7` (0.2.x, built from `main`; 0.1.45 worked)

### Graphics card, memory and system

irrelevant

### Model, size and settings

irrelevant

### Logs

irrelevant

issues.title: Picking a single GPU in the app (Ryzen iGPU + discrete Radeon) is broken twice over
issues.author: squidwardboom

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Strata | 0.1.45.3, **Windows app install** (`Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-hip-rdna3.exe`) |
| Engine | `strata-engine` 0.1.45.3, `windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3` |
| CPU / iGPU | Ryzen 7 7800X3D → `AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics`, **gfx1036** |
| GPU | **AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX**, gfx1100, 24 GB |
| Install | default `LOCALAPPDATA` layout; model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S |

The two cards matter: HIP numbers the **iGPU 0** and the **7900 XTX 1**, while the display-adapter order used elsewhere numbers them the other way round.

```
> strata-device.exe --list-devices
device 0: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics
  arch gfx1036, 43.7 GiB, wave32
  cannot run: GPU 0 (AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics, gfx1036) is not an architecture this Strata engine was compiled for
  (gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1151); ... or choose another GPU with HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES
device 1: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
  arch gfx1100, 24.0 GiB, wave32
```

```
> Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | select Name
AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX      <- display-adapter order: 0
AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics     <- display-adapter order: 1
```

---

## Bug 1 — a single-card pick is sent as `gpus` and rejected by the schema

### Steps

1. Settings → pick the GPU → select **Radeon RX 7900 XTX** (the only card the list offers; the iGPU is correctly filtered out).
2. Load the model.

### Actual

```
Gpus='0' is not valid (several GPUs sharing the model: '0,2' or 'all' (experimental))
```

### Expected

The card is accepted and the model loads.

### Cause

`strata_install` carries two mutually exclusive GPU parameters:

```python
# control/tools/strata_mcp.py:1470
GPUS_PATTERN = r"all|\d{1,2}(,\d{1,2}){1,7}"

# control/tools/strata_mcp.py:1532-1535
"gpu":  {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 63,
         "description": "one GPU, as nvidia-smi numbers them (default: the one with the most VRAM)"},
"gpus": {"type": "string", "pattern": GPUS_PATTERN, "maxLength": 40,
         "description": "several GPUs sharing the model: '0,2' or 'all' (experimental)"},
```

```python
# control/tools/strata_mcp.py:1807-1808
if gpu is not None and gpus is not None:
    raise ToolError("give gpu (one card) or gpus (several), not both")
```

The one-card case is meant to go through `gpu` (integer). The app's Settings puts the selection into `gpus` instead, as a string — so a single card arrives as `"0"`, which `GPUS_PATTERN` cannot match (it needs ≥ 2 comma-separated cards, or `all`). The schema rejects it before it ever reaches `install_plan()`.

### Suggested fix

When exactly one card is selected, emit `gpu: <n>` (integer). Reserve `gpus` for 2+ cards. Optionally make the pattern accept a single number and treat it as the one-card case, so a client that never distinguishes the two still works.

---

## Bug 2 — with the app install, that number is the display-adapter index, not the HIP ordinal, so the engine starts on the iGPU and dies

Fixing bug 1 alone (sending `gpu=0`) does **not** help on this machine: the UI's `0` means "the first usable card in display-adapter order", but the engine receives it as `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, which is the iGPU.

### Actual

```
server_exited (exit code 1): EngineDied: the engine exited before it was ready (see strata-iq3_s.log)
```

```
strata: GPU 0 (AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics, gfx1036) is not an architecture this Strata engine was
        compiled for (gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1151); compile it for this card
        (./setup.sh --backend hip, or -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1036, docs/AMD_HIP.md)
        or choose another GPU with HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES
```

### Cause

`serve/server.py` already has the correction for this (#325), and says what should feed it:

```python
# control/serve/server.py:2964-2977
def hip_visible(cfg: dict) -> list[int]:
    """AMD: the devices the engine should see, as the HIP runtime numbers them (HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES).

    On Linux setup's KFD order is HIP's order, so the config's "gpu" is it.  On Windows setup finds the cards in the
    display-adapter order, and an integrated Radeon that HIP also enumerates takes ordinal 0 and pushes the discrete
    card to 1 (#325): setup records the ordinal `strata-device --list-devices` gave the card as "hip_ordinal", which
    wins for a one-card config.  Without it (a config from before), the config's "gpu"."""
    ordinal = cfg.get("hip_ordinal")
    if ordinal is not None and str(ordinal).strip() != "" and len(gpu_list(cfg)) <= 1:
        ...
    return ordered_gpus(cfg)
```

Two things stop that from working on the app install:

**(a) The card list is built in display-adapter order, because the HIP probe is never found.**

```python
# control/setup.py:3503-3513
def hip_devices(probe=None, text=None) -> list[dict] | None:
    if text is None:
        probe = probe or ROOT / "engine" / ("strata-device.exe" if WIN else "strata-device")
        ...
        if not probe.exists() or not hip_engine:
            return None
```

`ROOT` is `Path(__file__).resolve().parent` = `<install>\control`, and the app install keeps the engine in the **component** layout, not at `<install>\control\engine`:

```
<LOCALAPPDATA>\Programs\Strata\control\            <- ROOT
<LOCALAPPDATA>\Programs\Strata\engine-bundle\0.1.45.3-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3\strata-device.exe
<LOCALAPPDATA>\Strata\components\engine\0.1.45.3-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3\strata-device.exe   <- the one that runs
```

So `hip_devices()` returns `None`, and `amd_gpus_win()` falls back to `amd_gpus_windows()`:

```python
# control/setup.py:3319-3333
def amd_gpus_win() -> list[dict]:
    """Windows: the AMD GPUs as the HIP runtime numbers them once the HIP engine is installed (hip_devices), else in
    the display-adapter order (amd_gpus_windows)."""
    hip = hip_devices()
    if not hip:
        return amd_gpus_windows()
```

Observed on this machine:

```
amd_gpus_win():
  index=0  AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX       arch=gfx1100   usable=True
  index=1  AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics      arch=unknown   usable=False
```

The 7900 XTX is therefore offered as **GPU 0**, and that 0 is what lands in the config as `"gpu": 0` — which the engine reads as HIP ordinal 0, the iGPU.

Note the Terminal / `git clone` install does not hit this: there `ROOT\engine\strata-device.exe` exists, `hip_devices()` succeeds, and the same card is correctly numbered 1. The two install layouts number the same card differently, and only the app layout gets it wrong.

**(b) Nothing ever writes `hip_ordinal`.** The docstring above says setup records it, but a tree-wide grep for `hip_ordinal` finds only readers and tests — no producer:

```
control/serve/replicas.py:98        c.pop("hip_ordinal", None)
control/serve/server.py:2969,2971   docstring + cfg.get("hip_ordinal")
control/serve/test_server.py:1786-1794
control/serve/test_replicas.py:37,46
```

So no Windows AMD install reaches `hip_visible()` with an ordinal, and the fallback `ordered_gpus(cfg)` always feeds the display-adapter index to `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.

### Suggested fix

1. Make `hip_devices()` resolve the probe through `strata_control.engine_component` (`engine_dir()` / the current engine component folder) instead of the hardcoded `ROOT / "engine"`, so the app's component layout numbers cards the way HIP does. Then `gpu: 1` for this machine is correct without any ordinal at all.
2. Independently, have setup/Control actually record `hip_ordinal` (from `strata-device --list-devices`) when it writes a one-card Windows AMD config, as `hip_visible()` already expects.
3. As cheap insurance, `hip_visible()` could skip devices whose arch the engine cannot run (`--list-devices` already prints `cannot run:` for them) instead of trusting the ordinal blindly.

---

## Workaround that works today

Add the ordinal by hand to the run config (`<LOCALAPPDATA>\Strata\install\strata-<model>.json`):

```json
"backend": "hip",
"gpu": 0,
"hip_ordinal": 1,
```

With that the model loads and answers normally:

```
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.45.3)
strata generate: expert cache 5749 slots, 10.92 GiB of VRAM
```

## Related

#325 (iGPU takes HIP ordinal 0), #524, #942

issues.title: Work resource profile sets --pool-workers from logical threads, not physical cores (more workers than cores on any SMT machine)
issues.author: squidwardboom

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

issues.body:
## What happens

On any SMT/hyper-threaded machine, choosing the **"Work"** resource profile (the wording in the UI is *"We reserve GPU memory and limit CPU expert workers to leave headroom for other apps"*) produces a `--pool-workers` value that is **larger than the number of physical cores**.

On this PC:

| | value |
|---|---|
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, **8 physical cores / 16 logical** threads |
| profile chosen in the UI | `work` |
| `--pool-workers` the app writes | **12** |
| physical cores available | 8 |
| setup's own recommendation for this CPU | `--pool-workers 7` |

So the profile whose stated purpose is to *limit* CPU workers ends up adding workers — more than either the "Full speed" profile or no setting at all would produce.

The visible symptom is a **permanently pegged CPU** (100 % on all threads) while the model is loaded and generating, even while idle between requests.

## Where it comes from

Three small steps. Each one looks reasonable on its own.

**1. The Python hardware report counts logical processors.**

`control/tools/strata_mcp.py`, `Hardware._hardware()` (line 837 before the change):

```python
hw["cpu"] = {"name": name, "cores": os.cpu_count(), "avx2": avx2, "avx512": avx512}
```

`os.cpu_count()` is documented as the number of **logical** CPUs — 16 here. (`_mac_hardware()` at line 927 has the same shape.)

**2. The host treats that number as physical cores.**

`host/server/native-resources.mjs:11-16`, in `resourceSettings()`:

```js
const cores=Number(hardware?.cpu?.cores)||0;
if(profile==='work'&&cores>1){
 const at=args.indexOf('--pool-workers'),previous=at>=0?Number(args[at+1]):0;
 const workers=Math.max(1,Math.floor(cores*.8));remove('--pool-workers');
 args.push('--pool-workers',String(previous>0?Math.min(previous,workers):workers));
}
```

`Math.floor(16*0.8)` = **12**.

That this field is meant to be *physical* cores is confirmed elsewhere in the same codebase — `host/server/engine.mjs:288` reads "CPU threads exceed physical cores (`hw.cpu.cores`)", and `host/server/catalog.mjs:63` says "cores: physical cores detected on this machine". Note also the fallback at `host/server/native-control.mjs:103-107`, `const cores=os.cpus().length`, which is logical as well, so the fallback path has the same result.

**3. The value is never checked against what the CPU can actually use.**

Nothing between these two functions compares the result with the physical core count. Strata already *knows* this is harmful, in two places that this path does not consult:

* `control/strata_control/tune_knobs.py:158` lists `--pool-workers` as a known-bad setting:
  `{"flag": "--pool-workers", "test": "above_engine_default", "reason": "more helper threads than the engine chose made it 36% slower"}`
* `control/setup.py`'s `pool_workers_note()` warns, for exactly this configuration:
  `the config asks for 12 CPU expert workers, more than its physical cores: extra workers can make Strata slower. Recommended: --pool-workers 7`

So the installer will warn a user who typed `--pool-workers 12` by hand, and the app will hand that same value to every user who picks the "Work" profile.

## Measured effect (same model, same prompt, one variable changed)

Model IQ3_S on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX. Same request each run (`max_tokens 256`, `temperature 0`), one warm-up run then one measured run. Only `--pool-workers` differs.

| | `--pool-workers 12` (app's `work` profile) | `--pool-workers 7` (this CPU's value) |
|---|---|---|
| generation | 27.85 tok/s | **38.12 tok/s** (+36.9 %) |
| `strata` CPU busy50 | 188.3 % | 95.8 % (−49 %) |
| `strata` CPU peak | 1162.3 % | 789.2 % (−32 %) |
| whole PC peak | 98.2 % | 83.1 % |

The **+36.9 %** matches the note in `tune_knobs.py:158` almost exactly: the app's "Work" profile reproduces, by default and on every SMT machine, the one setting upstream measured as 36 % slower.

## Suggested fix

Report physical cores. `strata_control.tune_machine.cpu()` already returns them (`{'model': 'AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor', 'logical': 16, 'physical': 8, 'hybrid': False}`), so the change is local:

```python
# control/tools/strata_mcp.py — replacing both os.cpu_count() calls in the cpu dict
try:
    import strata_control.tune_machine as tm
    n = tm.cpu().get("physical")
    if isinstance(n, int) and n > 0:
        return n
except Exception:
    pass
return os.cpu_count() or 1
```

With physical cores reported, `Math.floor(8*0.8)` = 6 workers, and the `Math.min(previous, workers)` already in `native-resources.mjs` keeps any hand-set value safer than that.

Two further hardening suggestions, separate from the fix above:

1. Have `resourceSettings()` clamp workers to the physical core count even when the OS cannot report one, so a bad hardware probe degrades to "no `--pool-workers`" instead of "one per thread".
2. Surface `pool_workers_note()`'s warning in the UI when the profile itself produces a setting that the note would complain about. Right now the app never sees it.

## Environment

* Strata **0.2.0-beta**, installed with the Windows app (`Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-hip-rdna3.exe`), not from git.
* Windows 11, engine `0.1.45.3-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3`.
* Ryzen 7 7800X3D (8c/16t) + Radeon RX 7900 XTX, 63 GB RAM.
* The resulting run configuration after picking "Work":
  `--pool-workers 12 --vram-reserve-mib 4915 --resident-budget-gib 40`

## Aside worth knowing

Editing `install/strata-iq3_s.json` while the app is running does **not** stick. The host keeps the model configuration in memory and writes it back from there (`native-control.mjs:268`, and `resourceSettings()` runs again on every start), so any manual `--pool-workers` edit is regenerated from the profile on the next start. That is why the local workaround had to be the source change above, plus restarting the host: no amount of editing the JSON survives.

Hi,

I'm experiencing an issue when loading the gyro-gyro-s model in Strata. The engine starts, but it reports that no ROCm-capable device is detected when attempting to place the native embedding in VRAM.

This is a fresh Strata installation performed using the Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip-rdna3.exe installer. My GPU has the latest available graphics driver and BIOS. The issue occurs during model loading.

System specifications

GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT
CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X
System RAM: 64 GB
GPU driver: Latest available version
GPU BIOS: Latest available version
Operating system: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit
Strata installer: Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip-rdna3.exe
Strata engine version reported in logs: 0.1.46-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3
Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Gyro-S-TQ1_0.gguf
Pack: gyro-gyro-s


Steps to reproduce

Download and install Strata using Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip-rdna3.exe.
Launch Strata and select the gyro-gyro-s pack.
Start loading the model.
The engine reports that no ROCm-capable device is detected.

Expected behavior

Strata should detect the AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT and successfully load the model, including placing the native embedding in VRAM.

Actual behavior

The engine reports that no ROCm-capable device is detected and cannot place the 497 MiB native embedding in VRAM.

Logs

```
[strata] 2026-10-20 12:57:38 engine started: C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Local\Strata\components\engine\0.1.46-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3\strata.exe --serve --pack C:\Users\<USERNAME>\Documents\Strata\packs\gyro-gyro-s --native C:\Users\<USERNAME>\Documents\Strata\models\gyro-Gyro-S\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Gyro-S-TQ1_0.gguf --ple-gguf C:\Users\<USERNAME>\Documents\Strata\models\gyro-Gyro-S\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Gyro-S-TQ1_0.gguf --expert-profile C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Local\Programs\Strata\control\data\expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp C:\Users\<USERNAME>\Documents\Strata\mtp\rt --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --pool-workers 12 --vram-reserve-mib 3276
```

Additional observations

issues.title: [Other] ctest ggml_tq_overlay: cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake fails under CMake 3.x (IN_LIST without CMP0057 in -P mode)
issues.author: Norhiro
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

Expected: ctest `ggml_tq_overlay` passes with any CMake the project accepts (`cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)`). Actual: it fails with CMake 3.31.
When the build is configured with CMake 3.31, ctest runs the overlay check with that same `cmake -P` and it stops at the first `IN_LIST`:

```
CMake Error at .../cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake:16 (if):
  if given arguments:
    "_n" "MATCHES" "^mmq-config-" "OR" "_n" "IN_LIST" "_patched"
  Unknown arguments specified
```

(CMake also warns that policy CMP0057 is not set.) A `-P` script has no `cmake_minimum_required`, so CMake 3.x applies the OLD behaviour of CMP0057 and `IN_LIST` is not an operator. The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` asks for `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)`, so 3.24–3.31 can configure the tree and then fail this test. CMake 4.x always has CMP0057 NEW. The same script with CMake 4.4.3 (the version in `requirements-build.txt`) prints `-- ggml_tq_overlay_test: ok`.

**Suggested change:** add `cmake_policy(SET CMP0057 NEW)` (or `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)`) at the top of `cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake`. `cmake/strata_ggml_tq_overlay.cmake`, which it includes, has no `IN_LIST`, and at configure time it runs under the project's own policies. Not tested with 3.31 beyond the error above.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```
cmake-3.31 -DLLAMA=<llama.cpp at 3cf03257> -DOUT=/tmp/ovl -P cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake   # error
cmake-4.4  -DLLAMA=<llama.cpp at 3cf03257> -DOUT=/tmp/ovl -P cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake   # ok
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (source, commit `3d1fb480`). `main` on 2026-10-20 has the same line 16.

### Graphics card, memory and system

Fedora 44, CMake 3.31.10 (pip) and 4.4.3 (pip), llama.cpp `3cf03257` (the pinned commit, unmodified).

issues.title: [Engine] isa_guard_check fails on Linux builds: tq_rows_avx512 (tq_avx512.cpp) is not in WIDE_PUBLIC / WIDE_OBJECTS
issues.author: Norhiro
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

Expected: `isa_guard_check` passes when every wide-ISA function is reached only behind a CPU check. Actual: it fails on one such function.
On a CUDA build of 0.2.0-beta with `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`, ctest `isa_guard_check` fails:

```
check_isa_guard: .../libstrata_kernels_cpu.a: 481 functions, 70 hold wide-ISA instructions, 1 not allowed
  VIOLATION strata::kernels::cpu::tq_detail::tq_rows_avx512(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long, int, strata::kernels::cpu::tq_detail::TqAct const* const*, int, float* (606 wide instructions, first vmovq): wide-ISA code in an unlisted public function
```

#3358 shows the same violation on a HIP build ("outside the wide-ISA translation units (object tq_avx512.cpp.o)"), mentioned there as a side note.

As far as I can see this is a gap in the list, not an unguarded call. `tq_rows_avx512` is reached only through `tq_rows(tq_isa(), ...)` (tq_cpu.cpp:174). `tq_isa()` picks `TqIsa::avx512` only when `tq_isa_ok(TqIsa::avx512)` → `cpu_avx512_ok()`, and `tq_rows` aborts on an ISA the CPU lacks (tq_cpu.cpp:185). This host has no AVX2. No illegal instruction was seen in the engine or in any other test. All the AVX1/AVX2 parity tests pass: `router_dot_parity_avx`, `iq_avx1_parity`, `iq_avx2_parity`, `q8k_quant_parity_avx`.

**Suggested change (tested here)** in `tools/check_isa_guard.py`:

- add `"tq_rows_avx512"` to `WIDE_PUBLIC`
- add `"tq_avx512.cpp"` to `WIDE_OBJECTS` (so it is also in `INIT_FREE_OBJECTS`)
- add `"tq_avx2.cpp"` to the extra `INIT_FREE_OBJECTS`. It is compiled above the AVX baseline like `nvfp4_avx2.cpp`, so a static initialiser there would run on every CPU (#2324).

With these three changes the check reports `0 not allowed` on the same library. `tq_avx2.cpp` currently has no static initialiser, so adding it changes nothing today; it guards against a future one.

**Related, also seen here (already listed in #3358):** `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` and `native_hadamard_test` print `this ggml has no trellis types (build with STRATA_GGML_DIR = the agention ... fork)` and exit as **failed**. With the default upstream llama.cpp they would read better as **skipped** (`SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77`).

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```
cmake -S . -B build-tests -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86
cmake --build build-tests && cd build-tests && ctest -R isa_guard_check --output-on-failure
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (source, commit `3d1fb480`). `main` on 2026-10-20 has no `tq_rows_avx512` / `tq_avx512.cpp` in `tools/check_isa_guard.py`.

### Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 3060 12 GB (driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.3 from the pip wheels, g++ 14.4.1), 2 × Xeon E5-2630 v2 (AVX, no AVX2/FMA), 252 GB DDR3, Fedora 44, binutils objdump.

issues.title: [Engine] serve/lifeline.py: the portable watcher does not end the child when the child's ps state changes (test_lifeline fails 5/5 on Linux)
issues.author: Norhiro
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

Expected: with `STRATA_LIFELINE=watcher`, killing the server ends its child. Actual: the child keeps running.
`serve.test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed` fails on every run on this machine (5 of 5 runs alone, and in the full Python suite):

```
AssertionError: False is not true : the child outlived a killed server (watcher)
```

The other five tests in the module pass, including `test_a_child_ends_when_its_server_is_killed` (the Linux `pdeathsig` path). So this concerns the portable watcher, which Linux uses only when `STRATA_LIFELINE=watcher` is set. As far as I can tell from the code, macOS uses it by default.

From reading `serve/lifeline.py`: the start token is `"s:" + ps -o lstart=,stat= -p PID`, so it includes the process **state**. `_start_token()` runs right after the child starts, while the child is still running (`R`). When the watcher's pipe closes, `start_of()` sees the child sleeping (`S`). The tokens differ, the watcher assumes the PID was reused, and it does not signal the child. The state change is easy to show:

```
>>> c = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(5)"])
>>> ps -o lstart=,stat= -p c.pid        -> '火 10月 20 16:11:52 2026 R'
>>> (1 s later)                          -> '火 10月 20 16:11:52 2026 S'
```

**Suggested change (tested here)**

Use only the start time for the token and keep the state just to detect a zombie. In both `_WATCHER.start_of()` and `_start_token()`:

```python
    if not out or out.endswith("Z"):
        return None                       # "" in _start_token
    return "s:" + out.rsplit(None, 1)[0]  # lstart only: the state (R/S/D, +, l ...) changes during a process's life
```

With this change in a copy of the tree, `serve.test_lifeline` passed 6/6 tests on 5 of 5 runs. `lstart` is in the locale's format (Japanese here). It is still compared with itself, so the locale should not matter.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```
python -m unittest serve.test_lifeline
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (source, commit `3d1fb480`). `main` on 2026-10-20 still has `ps -o lstart=,stat=` at lines 103 and 138.

### Graphics card, memory and system

Not GPU related. 2 × Xeon E5-2630 v2 (Ivy Bridge-EP, AVX without AVX2/FMA), 252 GB DDR3, Fedora 44 (kernel 7.2.5), Python 3.14.7, procps-ng 4.0.6.

issues.title: [Other] macOS: ./setup.sh on a fresh checkout no longer installs cmake and ninja, the Metal build fails
issues.author: Flo5k5
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

On a fresh source checkout on a Mac, `./setup.sh` stops at step 4 ("the Strata engine (Metal)"): CMake cannot run `ninja`. Step 3 still prints `numpy, jinja2, ..., cmake, ninja installed`, but neither is in `.venv`.

The cause looks like a242537 ("setup: split build helpers (cmake, ninja) out of the runtime requirements"). It moved `cmake` and `ninja` to `requirements-build.txt` and made `setup.py`'s `cmake_build()` install the missing ones before a compile, but `metal/setup_mac.py` (which `setup.py` hands a macOS run to) was not changed:

- step 3 still installs `requirements.txt` only, while its comment and message say cmake and ninja come with it (`metal/setup_mac.py`, lines 419-421 on 9ae93f7);
- `build_engine()` and `build_vision()` call `tool("cmake")` / `tool("ninja")`, which fall back to the bare name when neither `.venv` nor `PATH` has the tool.

`docs/MAC.md` (step 3) and the module docstring still say "CMake and Ninja come from pip". An older `.venv` keeps the helpers it already had, so this only shows on a new install.

`.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-build.txt`, then `./setup.sh` again, works around it.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

On a Mac without `ninja` on `PATH` (here `cmake` came from Homebrew):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata && cd Strata   # 9ae93f7
./setup.sh --update --yes
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

`main` at 9ae93f7 (first seen on 3d1fb48, 0.2.0-beta)

### Graphics card, memory and system

Apple M5 Pro, 64 GB unified memory, macOS 27.0.1

### Model, size and settings

Not relevant: the failure is before the model download (Q2_0 was the recommended choice).

### Logs

`build-metal/build.log`:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:14 (project):
  Running

   'ninja' '--version'

  failed with:

   no such file or directory


CMake Error: CMAKE_C_COMPILER not set, after EnableLanguage
CMake Error: CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER not set, after EnableLanguage
CMake Error: CMAKE_OBJCXX_COMPILER not set, after EnableLanguage
-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```

A fix that installs the helpers before a compile, as `cmake_build()` does, follows in a pull request.

issues.title: [GUI] Let user pin the desktop app's port so localhost API clients survive updates
issues.author: couleurs256
issues.body:
## Description
First: thank you for the "stable window origin" work (fixed preferred port 47831) — it already solved most of my issues. This is a small follow-up on the edge case that remains.

**Problem.** 
I run the Windows desktop app as the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a local agent; the host port IS the API base URL (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1`). When 47831 is still held by the previous instance during an update, `pick_stable_port()` silently falls back to a random port. Two things break at once: every client config (base URL + key) must be redone by hand, and the window origin changes, so the app's own chat list/settings start empty — which the code comments in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` already note.

**What I'd like** (goal, not implementation):
1. a supported way to pin the host port — a setting, or an env var honored on Windows (`STRATA_WINDOW_PORT` seems to be internal to the Linux window process, and `STRATA_PORT` is overwritten by the launcher);
2. failing that, don't fall back silently: warn and name the process holding 47831, so an API user knows why their URL changed;
3. document port 47831 and the fallback rule (the docs only mention 8080, the Terminal path).

**What I do today:** after each update I find the listening port in Strata's serving section. Observed on my Windows 11 machine updating v0.2.0-beta -> v0.2.1: the app stored most sessions on 47831 and one launch on a random port — the update where the old instance still held 47831. Not a deterministic reproduction, just what a normal update did.

**Trigger detail:** this happened through the in-app updater (GUI -> update). Since the updater relaunches the app while the previous host may still be draining its engines (and holding 47831), the fresh instance picks a random fallback port on that restart. Closing the app first isn't an option in that flow — the updater drives the quit/relaunch itself.


Thanks in advance, the app is awesome!

0.2.0-beta

## Description
After installing and configuring the new Windows GUI, Strata 0.2.0 cannot start Coder IQ_1 as it throws an OOM. The same model starts perfectly if launched from the old START-HERE.bat profile.

issues.title: [Benchmark] Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151) suite on 0.1.45: --mmap-experts + STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 decode +12-15%
issues.author: mistral13
issues.body:
# [Benchmark] Strix Halo (gfx1151) suite on 0.1.45: --mmap-experts + STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 decode +12-15%, UD-IQ4_XS prefill fixed, shared-GPU-memory placement idea

Measured on 2026-10-19 / 2026-10-20 by `mistral13`.

Follow-up to [#3032](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3032) (my first suite report, engine 0.44.1). Same Strix Halo machine, same test suite
(re-run with the engine's own timings), now on **Strata 0.1.45** with the bug fix from
[#3098](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3098) used locally. Coder IQ1_M was replaced by
**qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q6_k_xl**, and the setup takes the port-handling findings from
[#3029](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3029) into account (the suite pins one port for config, server and
bench call and kills any stale engine before every step, so no run can accidentally measure a leftover server).

Speed only — no correctness or recall check was run. Main new results:

- **`--mmap-experts` combined with `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0` is the fastest decode on this APU for both Flash-Next
  quants**: unsloth-ud-iq4_xs chat decode 34.3 → 38.5 tok/s (+12.2 %), and with `--pool-workers 6` 39.6 tok/s
  (+15.5 %); iq3_xxs 34.7 → 39.4 tok/s (+13.5 %), best agent decode 44.7 tok/s. Note `docs/STRIX_HALO.md` lists
  `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` as the gfx1151 default (it paid +1.8 % / +6.7 % on 0.1.40) — on 0.1.45 **turning it off**
  measured clearly faster, so the per-PC calibration or the doc may want a look.
- **The big prefill gap of the first suite is gone**: unsloth-ud-iq4_xs prompt was 322–355 tok/s on 0.44.1 (much
  worse than iq3_xxs and coder-iq1_m then) and now measures 643–665 tok/s — as fast as the other models. Prompt
  speed is still strongly model-dependent: qwen3.6-35B falls from 596 tok/s (4K) to 373 tok/s (32K) while both
  Flash-Next quants stay flat at 620–665.
- qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q6_k_xl gives the **best chat decode (50.5 tok/s, TTFT 0.25 s)** of the whole suite, but its
  **agent conversation-cache hit is 0 %** (30k tokens re-read per session, per-turn TTFT grows to ~27 s) while both
  Flash-Next packs hit ~68.7 % — looks specific to this arch/model path, details below.
- Placement idea measured out (bottom of this report): on this unified-memory APU the mmap variants keep **almost
  nothing in "shared GPU memory" (0.9 GiB) while process RAM is nearly full (41.5 GiB)** — see
  [shared-memory placement idea](#possible-improvement-shared-gpu-memory-instead-of-normal-ram).

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics (Strix Halo APU, `gfx1151`), 64 GiB BIOS carve-out seen as VRAM
  (+ 32 GB shared with system RAM; 108 GB usable by the GPU). No discrete PCIe link — CPU and iGPU share one pool.
- CPU: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395 w/ Radeon 8060S (16 cores / 32 threads, AVX-512)
- Installed RAM: 128 GB unified memory (64 GB seen by the OS + 64 GB VRAM carve-out)
- Storage: not yet verified; OS/SSD details not measured
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200); GPU driver: 32.0.31036.15
- Strata: project 0.1.45 (git checkout `477ac13c`), engine **0.1.45 prebuilt** Windows HIP binary
  (`engine/BUILD.json`: prebuilt, windows-x64, archs incl. gfx1151, ROCm 10.2.0, hipBLASLt 100500), with the
  [#3098](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3098) bug fix used locally (not a source build of the engine)
- Background workloads and power limits: as in #3032, other programs were open during the suite; background load
  was not controlled and no power limit was set.

## Model and configuration

- Models (GGUF filenames from this install, quantization in brackets):
  - `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs` [IQ3_XXS + PLE file] — `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf`
    (+ `-00002` as `--ple-gguf`)
  - `qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs` [UD-IQ4_XS] — `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf` … `-00003`
  - `qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q6_k_xl` [UD-Q6_K_XL, arch `qwen35moe`] — `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf` (native path,
    no pack/expert-profile; the file fits resident, no GPU expert cache)
- Context: 262144 tokens; KV type: int8; KV streaming on (setup default); expert cache: auto; vision: off.
- MTP: `rt` draft layer (`--spec 4`) for the Flash-Next packs; qwen3.6 native default `--mtp 2` (one variant `--mtp 4`).
  Thinking off, temperature 0 (suite standard). Calibration re-measured per model for this build
  (`START-HERE.bat --calibrate`); iq3_xxs settled at `--pcie-frac 1.00 --spec-min-p 0.70` (43.5 tok/s at calibration).
- Environment: `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt`; variants additionally set
  `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0`, `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1`.

Representative launch commands (full per-variant command in each variant's `config-used.json` and `README.md`):

```text
# iq3_xxs variant "--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0"
strata.exe --pack iq3_xxs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf \
  --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf \
  --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto \
  --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --pcie-frac 1.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --mmap-experts
  env: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt, STRATA_SH_STREAM=0

# unsloth-ud-iq4_xs default (START-HERE config; other variants add --pool-workers / --mmap-experts / --expert-cache)
strata.exe --pack unsloth-ud-iq4_xs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto \
  --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --resident-budget-gib 36 --spec-min-p 0.5

# qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q6_k_xl default (native path)
strata.exe --native Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf --max-context 262144 --prefill auto --mtp 2
```

## Method

Same self-written updated suite as #3032 (`suite/strata_suite.py` + `suite.toml` in the Strata folder): per model it runs
`START-HERE.bat` setup and `--calibrate`, edits the generated config per variant, then `BENCH.bat --long`
(`tools/strata_bench.py --long`): short chat, fresh 4K/16K/32K prompts (unique tag, no cache help, 24 new tokens),
5-turn agent session with the conversation cache. 3 runs per test, medians with ranges; engine timings for
prompt/decode, client-measured TTFT. 90 s cooldown between runs; stale engines killed first; all bench calls pass
`--config` and the same port (finding from [#3029](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3029)), so every variant
measures its own freshly started server. Suite window: 2026-10-19 22:09 → 2026-10-20 01:12.

Memory is now sampled every 5 s during each run (`memory_samples.csv` next to each variant's data):
`RAM strata` = strata.exe private working set, `RAM system` = total in-use system RAM, `VRAM` = dedicated GPU
memory, `shared GPU` = shared GPU memory (system RAM mapped for the GPU); the peaks include model load.

## Results

Ranked by chat decode. `pp` = prompt tok/s. Full ranking views `ranking.md` / `ranking.csv`, per-run folders
(the generated `README.md` + `results.json` + `engine-log-excerpt.txt`) and `comparisons/` keep the ranges.

| # | run | chat tok/s | agent tok/s | 4K pp | 16K pp | 32K pp | 32K TTFT s | RAM strata GiB | RAM system GiB | VRAM GiB | shared GPU GiB | expert cache GiB |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | qwen36-ud-q6_k_xl:default | 50.5 | 38.0 | 578.8 | 482.9 | 373.5 | 85.8 | 30.6 | 46.7 | 49.4 | 0.8 | - |
| 2 | qwen36-ud-q6_k_xl:--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 --mtp 4 | 50.5 | 38.1 | 595.8 | 479.3 | 379.2 | 84.6 | 30.6 | 46.4 | 49.4 | 0.8 | - |
| 3 | qwen36-ud-q6_k_xl:--mtp 4 | 50.5 | 37.9 | 591.8 | 471.5 | 375.1 | 85.5 | 30.6 | 46.4 | 49.4 | 0.8 | - |
| 4 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--pool-workers 6 --mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 | 39.6 | 37.7 | 657.4 | 663.2 | 644.4 | 49.8 | 8.3 | 29.8 | 63.7 | 12.0 | 55.4 |
| 5 | iq3_xxs:--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 | 39.4 | 44.7 | 620.3 | 636.0 | 620.3 | 51.7 | 41.5 | 57.5 | 50.5 | 0.9 | 40.0 |
| 6 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 | 38.6 | 43.3 | 621.4 | 636.5 | 620.1 | 51.8 | 41.4 | 57.3 | 50.5 | 0.9 | 40.0 |
| 7 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0 | 38.5 | 38.1 | 657.5 | 664.1 | 645.2 | 49.8 | 8.3 | 29.6 | 63.7 | 12.0 | 55.4 |
| 8 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 | 36.2 | 40.4 | 565.9 | 605.2 | 590.1 | 54.4 | 41.4 | 57.3 | 26.6 | 40.8 | 16.0 |
| 9 | iq3_xxs:--mmap-experts | 34.7 | 40.0 | 612.6 | 637.1 | 618.6 | 51.9 | 41.6 | 57.5 | 50.7 | 0.9 | 40.0 |
| 10 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--expert-cache 20000 | 34.5 | 32.7 | 656.3 | 664.7 | 645.3 | 49.8 | 8.3 | 29.9 | 63.7 | 12.2 | 55.4 |
| 11 | iq3_xxs:low-ram mmap | 34.3 | 38.7 | 604.4 | 616.3 | 621.4 | 51.6 | 41.6 | 58.4 | 50.7 | 0.9 | 40.0 |
| 12 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:default | 34.3 | 33.8 | 656.8 | 662.9 | 643.4 | 49.9 | 8.3 | 30.0 | 63.8 | 12.3 | 55.4 |
| 13 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--pool-workers 6 | 34.1 | 33.8 | 655.8 | 663.8 | 641.9 | 50.0 | 8.3 | 29.8 | 63.8 | 12.4 | 55.4 |

One configuration did not complete: the first calibration attempt for qwen36-ud-q6_k_xl reported
"calibration: no result" (stored, no values); the three qwen3.6 variants themselves ran OK, without calibration
values applied.

### What was better than what (vs. each model's default / equivalent)

| Change | chat decode | agent decode | prompt tok/s | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unsloth: + `--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0` | **+12.2 %** | **+12.7 %** | ±0 % | chat TTFT −5 % |
| unsloth: + `--pool-workers 6 --mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0` | **+15.5 %** | +11.5 % | ±0 % | best unsloth chat |
| iq3_xxs: `--mmap-experts` with `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0` vs 1 | **+13.5 %** (39.4 vs 34.7) | +11.8 % | ±0 % | best iq3 chat + agent |
| unsloth: `--expert-cache 20000` | +0.6 % | −3.3 % | ±0 % | no effect (cache already fills VRAM) |
| qwen3.6: `--mtp 4` / `+--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0` | ±0 % | ±0 % | +2…+3 % at 4K | within noise |
| unsloth UD-IQ4_XS prompt speed, 0.44.1 → 0.1.45 | — | — | **~330 → ~655** | cross-suite, not a controlled A/B |

- `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` / `--pool-workers 6` without the mmap changes is no longer a win on 0.1.45
  (iq3_xxs pool-workers variant is 2.8 tok/s *below* `--mmap-experts STRATA_SH_STREAM=0`).
- Docs impact: `STRIX_HALO.md` marks `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` as the gfx1151 default because it paid on 0.1.40;
  on this 0.1.45 build the opposite measured (both models). A calibration fork "SH_STREAM off vs on" (as
  `tools/calibrate.py` already does for other engines) would decide per PC.

### Prompt speed is strongly model-dependent

- unsloth-ud-iq4_xs: 657 / 663 / 645 at 4K/16K/32K — flat, and ~2× its own 0.44.1 value from #3032
  (where it was the slow prefiler: 322–355 tok/s vs 543–615 for iq3_xxs then).
- iq3_xxs: 604–637 depending on variant — also flat.
- qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q6_k_xl: 579–596 at 4K already the lowest, and it degrades with length:
  483 at 16K, 373 at 32K (TTFT 85 s for one 32K prompt). Its chat decode is the suite leader (50.5 tok/s),

issues.title: [Other] FP4-Local prepare: the pack step's memmap sweep charges its full 64 GB of reads to the process working set on Windows
issues.author: jerry78424
issues.body:
## Area
`[Other]` (tools/nvfp4_local_pack.py, the FP4-Local prepare step)

## Desktop app, Terminal or source?
Source install (git clone, SETUP.bat) on Windows

## What happened

`nvfp4_local_pack.py prepare` fails mid-pack with no traceback:

```
  layer 24  NVFP4   /NVFP4   blob  2764816  at 31.64 GiB
prepare: D:\...\app\tools\nvfp4_local_pack.py failed (exit 1)
```

The pack python dies between its layer-24 and layer-32 prints (50–67 % of the 68 GB experts write). On my 187 GB machine with the serving model loaded (135 GB baseline), system "used RAM" climbs **+41 GB in five minutes** while the process's own committed memory is ~3.5 GB — and the run dies at ~11 GB free. Unload the model first and the same prepare completes in ~10 minutes, exit 0. The step's real RAM demand is a few GB; it **presents as ~64 GB to every free-RAM observer** (Task Manager, psutil, `os.freemem`), so `prepare` cannot run next to a loaded model on any machine without ~60 GB to spare.

Timeline (manager diag sampler, `ram_used = total - available`, ~10 s cadence; pack started 12:38:43):

```
12:37  135 GB  baseline        12:41  158 GB  rd 250 MB/s
12:39  143 GB  wr 892 MB/s     12:42  166 GB  wr 963 MB/s
12:40  150 GB                  12:43  176 GB  -> run killed by watchdog (~11 GB free left)
12:44  135 GB  -> all 41 GB back within a minute: nothing leaked
```

(The watchdog that ended the run is a personal tool of mine, unrelated to this repo — beside the point: every observer of free RAM saw the climb as real usage.)

## The cause

`Checkpoint.raw()` (`tools/nvfp4_local_pack.py:86-88`) maps each shard with `np.memmap(..., mode="r")` and caches the mapping for the process's life (`self._mm`, never closed). The pack pass reads **64.36 GB of distinct expert bytes** (header parse: 48 layers x 3 roles x 512 experts x weight + CSF pair + scale_2 + input_scale; expert->shard assignment rotates per layer, so every layer touches 13–14 of the 15 expert shards). On Windows every faulted page is charged to the **process working set**, and `ullAvailPhys` (= psutil `available` = `os.freemem` = our own `ram_used`, `serve/telemetry.py:624-625`) counts it as used until the OS trims under pressure. The sweep inflates "used RAM" ~1:1 with the read rate: when the run died, 50–67 % of 64.36 GB = 32–43 GB faulted — bracketing the +41 GB (private commits ~3.5 GB). Reclaimable, but "reclaimable" is not "available".

A/B on the live checkpoint, the pack's exact read order (layers 0–2 x gate/up/down x experts 0–511 = 4.03 GB): `np.memmap` grows the process working set **+3.75 GB** (93 % of bytes touched; charges even from a warm cache) in 2.7 s; cached sequential `readinto` of the same bytes grows it **+0.00 GB** in 2.3 s — both hash-identical. PR #3378 does this: same bytes, ~1.2x faster, flat working set.

## Workaround that works now

Run the FP4-Local setup with the serving model unloaded (or ~60 GB free: observed 41 GB climb + margin).

## Reproduction status
Reproduced on this PC: the failed run with the diag sampler timeline (2026-10-20, source install - `nvfp4_local_pack.py` there is byte-identical to the revision below; no newer upstream commit touches it), the A/B working-set measurements above run at the revision below, and the fix verified end to end (full pack, byte-identical output, flat working set).

## Strata version
e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta-12)

## Graphics card, memory and system
Windows 11 26200, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 187 GB RAM, RTX 5090 (driver 617.42), NVMe, model `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local`

## Not verified / limits

- The death point (50–67 % written) is bracketed between two progress prints, not measured.
- Working-set inflation from mapped clean pages is Windows accounting behavior (GlobalMemoryStatusEx semantics); the timeline arithmetic is consistent with it but was not decomposed with RAMMap-level counters. The fix covers the checkpoint reader only; `pack` still memmaps `dense.gguf` (~6 GB file, ~1.5–2.5 GB faulted, `iq_pack.py:161,218,324`) and `convert` ~4 GB via `LocalTensor.mmap_bytes` (`gguf/utility.py:286`) — bounded residuals.

issues.title: [Engine] serve: a temp cleaner that removes the idle vision encoder's work dir makes every later start fail ([WinError 267])
issues.author: smallmj
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine] (the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (the repo's `serve/server.py`, started by our own launcher/router)

### What happened

With `idle_unload_s` set, after the model had stayed unloaded for a while (overnight), the first request that loaded it again failed with a 503 whose message was:

```
the vision encoder failed to start: [WinError 267] The directory name is invalid. ; the next request restarts it
```

Every client retry failed the same way, seconds apart, for as long as the server process lived — only restarting the whole server healed it. The console showed a tight loop of full load attempts (the `before_load` hook ran, the free-VRAM check passed, then the vision start failed immediately; the engine was never reached):

```
[strata] model unloaded after 1800 s idle; the next request loads it again
[router] unload <other model>: 200 {"status": "not loaded"}
[strata] starting the vision encoder ...
[router] unload <other model>: 200 {"status": "not loaded"}
[strata] starting the vision encoder ...
... (x17, seconds apart, until a manual restart)
```

The engine's log had no trace of any of these attempts — no `engine started` lines (those are written before the spawn), no encoder stderr: the encoder process was never even spawned. Expected: the vision encoder starts again like it does after any other unload.

### Root cause

`Vision.work_dir()` runs once, at the server's start (`Vision.__init__`), and creates `%TEMP%\strata-vision-*`. The spawn uses `cwd=self.dir` and nothing ever checks that the directory still exists (`_start_reader()` at current HEAD; the single spawn path in earlier versions). `restart()` reuses the stale path.

While the model is unloaded, that directory sits **empty and unheld** in the temp directory — exactly what Windows' Storage Sense ("Delete temporary files that my apps aren't using", enabled on the affected machine) removes during a long idle window. The next request's `popen(cwd=<removed dir>)` raises `OSError [WinError 267]`, which `ensure_loaded` wraps as `EngineDied("the vision encoder failed to start: ...")` → 503 → the client retries → the identical failure, forever. `#914` made `shutdown()` the only remover of the dir, but nothing defends it against external removal.

Ruled out on the affected machine while diagnosing:

- **not VRAM**: with the engine resident and only ~850 MiB of VRAM free, a manually spawned `strata-vision.exe --gpu` with the config's real arguments started fine (mmproj load, warm-up, READY);
- **not a crash**: the Windows Event Log has no strata crash entries, and the encoder leaves no stderr at all — it never ran;
- the engine itself is never started during the loop.

### Smallest steps that reproduce it

1. Start the server `--lazy` with a vision config.
2. Delete the `strata-vision-*` directory in the temp directory.
3. Send any completion request (the encoder starts with the model load, not with a picture) → the 503 loop above, until the server is restarted.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally (twice on the affected machine, on different days; the second time with the client error text and the console loop captured).

### Strata version

engine 0.1.45 · serve/server.py from this repo (the deployed checkout was unmodified; the bug is confirmed present at current main by reading the code, e88ee39d)

### Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 3090 24 GB · 64 GB RAM · Windows 11 Pro

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S · 512K context (yarn ×2, k8v4 KV) · pictures on (`--vision`, GPU encoder)

### Fix

In `Vision._start()` (the wrapper at HEAD, so the CPU-fallback path is covered too), recreate the dir when it is gone and drop the cache — the encoded-image files lived in that dir, and the cache-hit branch of `encode()` returns paths without checking they exist:

```python
if not self.dir.exists():                       # a temp cleaner (Windows' Storage Sense, systemd-tmpfiles)
    self.dir = self.work_dir()                  # can remove the idle encoder's dir while the model is
    self.cache.clear()                          # unloaded: every start would then fail on the cwd, and the
                                                # cache's files went with the dir
```

PR #3372 carries the fix and a regression test (`serve/test_vision_dir.py`).

issues.title: [GUI] Optional Local Model Extension That Survives App Updates
issues.author: medking82
issues.body:
### Area

GUI

### What do you want to do?

Use an already running local Strata model in the desktop App without copying its GGUF files into the App's prepared-model library. Keep the official Model Catalog, recommendations and updater while an optional companion adds Current Model, Connected Local Models tiles in Manage Models/Storage, and explicit Use In Chat.

### Proposed scope

A separate opt-in tool under `tools/local-model-extension/`, outside the installed App. Its versioned, integrity-checked UI package can be enabled, disabled and rolled back. A bounded Node preload supports the 0.2.x host only and leaves the official frontend/API/updater path unchanged when absent or incompatible.

The optional managed Tray in #3365 remains the only server owner. A user-enabled local file protocol supplies its confirmed model/context/idle state and admits explicit context, idle, preload and unload requests through the Tray's existing drain boundary. The Extension does not create a second server. It takes arbitrary configured physical model IDs and loopback ports, without a personal model allowlist, private paths or a Codex dependency. Reasoning Effort remains the official composer control; #3363 addresses the direct API forwarding bug separately.

### Scope agreement and validation limits

This is a request for maintainer scope agreement, accompanied by a draft candidate for inspection at the user's request. No maintainer approval is assumed. Default App, server and engine files stay byte-identical; native prepared counts and directories are not fabricated or rewritten.

The existing private implementation was exercised in the Windows 0.2.0-beta App for connected tiles and actual Chat model selection. The portable candidate will have its own anonymous fixture screenshots and tests. Such screenshots represent simulated state, not GPU inference, capacity or timing measurements. Real GPU behavior and generic App/Tray hardware acceptance remain separate checks.
