issues.body:
I use Strata for arround 5 days now and do not really know what is possible.

I am running Strata with an RTX4090 on an amd epyc 32cores + 196GB RAM.

So fare it was a real improvement to the QWen 3.8 27B I ran befor.

I am working on a very tight ai factory. Claude suggested me to run a second small model for speculative decoding next to the big qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-q8_0. 

Claude said there could be a gain up to 1.5–2× on all model writing, which sounds really good.

Here the exact text:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Speculative decoding is a way to make the model on Strata write faster, without changing what it writes.

Why the model writes slowly: a language model writes one token (about one word piece) at a time. For each single token, the GPU has to read the model’s whole weights from memory. That memory read is the bottleneck; the GPU’s compute mostly waits. Whether it checks 1 token or 5 at once costs almost the same.

The trick: a second, much smaller model (the “draft” model, e.g. a 1-billion-parameter model of the same family) quickly guesses the next 5–8 tokens. The large model then checks all these guesses in one pass. 

Guesses that match what the large model would have written anyway are kept, so several tokens for the price of one;
at the first wrong guess, the large model’s own token is used from there on, and guessing starts again.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I think Claude doesn't know Strata, so I thaught I just ask here.

Is this possible? 
Would it really bring this improvements?
How would I have to make the setup?

issues.title: [Engine] q36 (qwen35moe) KV cache is always fp32: --kv / --kv-resident are not parsed, so 256K context OOMs on a 16 GB card
issues.author: conlododo
issues.body:
---

**Area:** `[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)`

**Desktop app, Terminal or source?** `Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)`

---

### What happened

With the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (arch `qwen35moe`) own-engine path, raising `--max-context` fails at model load once the fp32 KV cache no longer fits. `--max-context 262144` OOMs on a 16 GB card, while 32768 and 100000 start and serve normally on the same card and model.

The q36 engine allocates its K/V cache as plain fp32 (`dalloc()` is `cudaMalloc(n * 4)`), and unlike the generic Flash-Next path it has no KV-quantization option: `--kv`, `--kv-resident` and `--spec` are not parsed at all (passing them is ignored with "not an option of this engine"). So a `qwen35moe` model cannot trade KV precision for context length, and 256K is unreachable on 16 GB even though the same model does 256K on a 32 GB card.

I expected `--kv int8` / `--kv k8v4` (as documented for the generic path, and as used by an IQ3_S Flash-Next pack at 1M context) to work for this architecture too, or at least to be documented as unsupported for `qwen35moe`.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```bash
# Strata 0.1.45 built from source, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf (753 tensors, 22 GB, 5.15 BPW)
./engine/strata --serve --native <model>.gguf --max-context 262144 --prefill auto --mtp 2
```

Observed (16 GB card, 30 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04):

```
strata-q36: <model>.gguf: 753 tensors (layout checked), 4.40 GiB on the GPU in 1.3 s
strata: K-quant prompt kernels from .../libstrata_kq.so (STRATA_MMQ_KQ=1)
strata-q36: prompt experts on MMQ (int8)
strata-q36: cudaMalloc(&p, n * 4) failed: out of memory   (src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:1127)
```

The same command with `--max-context 32768` and `--max-context 100000` starts fine. Passing `--kv k8v4` in addition changes nothing (it is reported as "not an option of this engine").

### Reproduction status

`Reproduced locally`

### Strata version

`strata 0.1.45` (built from source with setup.py; engine/strata reports "strata 0.1.45")

### Graphics card, memory and system

`RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB · 30 GB RAM · Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 7.0.0-38)`. Also reproduced the same 256K limit on `RTX 4080 SUPER 32 GB · 62 GB RAM` only insofar as 32 GB *does* fit it; the 16 GB card is where it fails.

### Model, size and settings

`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL · UD-Q4_K_XL (Unsloth Dynamic, 22 GB, 753 tensors, 5.15 BPW) · context swept 32K / 100K / 256K · pictures off · --mtp 2 · --prefill auto`

Metadata of this file: `n_head_kv = 2`, `key_length = value_length = 256`, `block_count = 41`, `full_attention_interval = 4`, `nextn_predict_layers = 1`.

### Logs

```
# 32K — starts, 7.63 GiB VRAM free after load
strata-q36: context 32768 cells, prompt chunk 1024, MTP block loaded, 7.63 GiB of VRAM free
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 78 of 256 per layer in VRAM (5.71 GiB), all 18.75 GiB in pinned host memory, ...
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 1271565 of 1561160 batch entries on the GPU (81.5%), 289595 on the CPU pool in 7680 ms, 7629 slot replacements

# 100K — starts, 3.93 GiB VRAM free after load
strata-q36: context 100000 cells, prompt chunk 2048, MTP block loaded, 3.93 GiB of VRAM free
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 28 of 256 per layer in VRAM (2.05 GiB), all 18.75 GiB in pinned host memory, ...
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 40221 of 137472 batch entries on the GPU (29.3%), 97251 on the CPU pool in 1928 ms, 2265 slot replacements

# 256K — dies before the first request
strata-q36: <model>.gguf: 753 tensors (layout checked), 4.40 GiB on the GPU in 1.3 s
strata-q36: cudaMalloc(&p, n * 4) failed: out of memory   (src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:1127)
```

Measured KV slope between the two working points: −3.7 GiB for +67,328 cells ≈ 59 MiB per 1K cells → ≈15.5 GiB at 262,144 cells. Plus 4.40 GiB dense and ~0.80 GiB for the MTP block, that is ≈20.7 GiB, over the 16.3 GiB the card reports.

For reference, the same model on this card decodes at 126–133 tok/s at 32K (MTP drafts accepted 237/324, 229/342) and 91–94 tok/s at 100K, so the engine itself is fine — only the KV budget is the wall.

### What would fix it (for whoever picks this up)

1. Parse and honour `--kv int8|q4_0|k8v4` in the q36 engine (`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`), storing K/V in the quantized form the generic path uses (`src/program/generate.cpp:2336`); the quantized attention kernels already exist in the tree (`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/kv_stream.hpp`).
2. Optionally `--kv-resident N` streaming, as for Flash-Next, so the cache can live partly outside VRAM.
3. If either is out of scope for now, a line in the docs that `qwen35moe` has no KV compression (and therefore a ~160K ceiling on 16 GB) would save the next person the same experiment.

Side note that may be worth documenting separately: a LoRA merged with `llama-export-lora` comes back with the touched tensors as F16, which the native MMVQ rejects (`blk.0.attn_qkv.weight is F16, which the native MMVQ does not take`). Re-quantizing only those tensors back to their original per-tensor types (taken from the base file) produced a byte-size-identical file that loads normally.

issues.title: [TUI] Windows: owner-only check fails for the built-in Administrator (SDDL alias LA) and blocks the engine test start
issues.author: BoogeAI
issues.body:
**Problem:** On Windows, when the Terminal runs as the built-in Administrator account (RID 500, here renamed), the owner-only check rejects a folder whose ACL this code has just set itself. `strata update` verifies engine 0.1.45.3 and then fails its test start with `ProfileError: runtime directory must be owner-only (mode 0700)`; the engine is rolled back. A managed start on the same account fails the same way.

**Environment:**
- Strata Terminal 0.2.0-beta (build 0.1.45.3), Windows x86_64, RTX 5080 (driver 617.42), no model serving during the update.
- Account: built-in Administrator, renamed; `whoami /user` shows SID `S-1-5-21-<domain>-500`.
- Engine offered: 0.1.45.3 windows-x86_64-cuda-cuda13 (signed feed sequence 101, manifest sha256 `68fa0ee7c23bb0343e57f2e7b1db61a0f44aa7835f421b396df94502859d78af`).

**Reproduce:**
1. Use an account whose SID is the built-in Administrator's (`…-500`).
2. Run `strata update` with no engine installed.
3. The package downloads, unpacks, and passes the signature and per-file check. The test start then fails:
   `Engine none NOT changed: The new engine 0.1.45.3 did not pass its test start (ProfileError: runtime directory must be owner-only (mode 0700)).`
4. The same error occurs outside the updater whenever `runtime.runtime_dir()` creates the runtime folder.

**Expected:** The test start passes; the folder is owner-only already and only this account can reach it.

**Actual:** `ProfileError`, update not installed.

**Evidence (reproduced locally, not static analysis):**
- A fresh `STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR` created through `runtime.runtime_dir()` reports this DACL:
  `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)`.
- `Get-Acl` on that folder resolves the single ACE to `<machine>\<user>`, SID `S-1-5-21-<domain>-500`, FullControl; `icacls` shows `<machine>\<user>:(OI)(CI)(F)`. `restrict_to_current_user()` did what it promises.
- `private_files.current_user_sid()` returns `S-1-5-21-<domain>-500`.
- `private_files.is_private()` and `is_unshared()` split the SDDL text and compare the ACE principal (`fields[5]`) with that string. Windows renders the RID-500 account as the SDDL alias `LA`, so the comparison is `"LA" == "S-1-5-21-<domain>-500"` and returns False — including immediately after this module set the protected DACL itself. `runtime.runtime_dir()` raises, so the update test start never reaches the engine.
- A local change in the installed Control package that treats `LA` as the current SID when the SID ends in `-500` makes `is_unshared()` return True; `strata update` then installs 0.1.45.3 and reports `tested: started, answered one token, stopped`.

**Suggested fix:** resolve SDDL aliases (at least `LA`) or compare binary ACE SIDs with `EqualSid` instead of comparing SDDL text. `owner_transport` calls `is_private()` and is affected the same way on such an account.

**Reproduction status:** reproduced locally on the machine described above.

issues.title: [Benchmark] 2x RTX 3080 20 GB + RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB (mixed sm_86/sm_89), IQ3_S, 3-card layer split: 0.2.0-beta
issues.author: Songokou1983
issues.body:
Reported from `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges) on an
existing `serve/server.py` install. Full `results.json` (per-request data) is available on
request; it is not pasted here to keep the issue readable.

A note on this machine's shape: the three cards are **2x sm_86 (RTX 3080) + 1x sm_89
(RTX 2000 Ada)**, so it is a *mixed-architecture* layer split. The 0.2.0 sm_86 speed table does
not apply here (`generate.cpp` requires every visible card to share one compute capability), and
the start-up log does not say so — separate feature request on that.

---


Measured on 2026-10-20 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080, 20 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) W-2195 CPU @ 2.30GHz (18 cores, 36 threads); installed RAM: 123.2 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: 595.99.02; CUDA: 13.2

## Model and configuration

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)

issues.title: Windows app: Qwen3.6 install reported as "files missing" (--mtp 2 checked as a folder) and Gyro-S low-RAM prep fails (missing --compat-bf16)
issues.author: daktuno

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

issues.body:
Versions: Strata desktop 0.2.0-beta, strata-control / engine 0.1.45.3 (windows-x86_64-cuda-cuda13), bundled Python 3.12.15 PC: Windows 11, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GB (driver 617.42), 31 GB RAM, Ryzen 7 9800X3D

There are two separate bugs here. Both block a model from starting in the app, and the Diagnostics panel only shows a generic error for each.

Bug 1: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL always shows "Some model files are missing"
What happens: Setup finishes (strata-mcp: setup ended with exit code 0, "All set."). Every start attempt then fails with:

Some model files are missing. Use Download / repair to restore them.

Download / repair runs, succeeds, and the same error comes back. Deleting the model and downloading it again (23 GB) doesn't help.

Cause: The Qwen3.6 run config written by setup passes --mtp a number (the draft depth), not a folder:
```

"args": ["--native", "...\\Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf", "--max-context", "65536",
         "--prefill", "auto", "--mtp", "2", "--vision"]
strata_control/doctor.py maps "--mtp": "directory" in PATH_FLAGS, so the component check looks for a folder named 2 relative to the control directory:
```
```

{"name": "mtp", "status": "missing", "path": "...\\Strata\\control\\2", "kind": "directory", "required": true}
strata models list then reports component_status: "missing_or_invalid" / COMPONENT_MISSING, so the host gets ready: false and refuses to start. strata_cli/launch/runner.py files_present() has the same issue for --mtp.

strata_control/discovery.py:290 (mtp.isdigit()) and presets.py:115 already treat a numeric --mtp as Qwen3.6's depth. The two path checks just don't.

```
Fix I applied locally (confirmed working): in both checks, skip --mtp when its value is all digits.
```

# strata_control/doctor.py, in the PATH_FLAGS loop after `raw = args[index + 1]`
if arg == "--mtp" and raw.isdigit():
    continue

```
```
# strata_cli/launch/runner.py, files_present(): add to the existence condition
and not (flag == "--mtp" and args[args.index(flag) + 1].isdigit())
After the change, strata models list reports qwen36-ud-q4_k_xl present [].
```

Bug 2: Gyro-S fails at step 6 with "command failed (exit 1): python.exe"
What happens: With Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Gyro) Gyro-S on a PC where setup turns on low-RAM mode automatically (--low-ram auto, 31 GB RAM), step 6 fails:

=== Step 6: preparing the model for Strata ===
  Writing the experts into one file for the low-RAM mode (one time, 26 GB) ...
  > ...\python.exe ...\tools\iq_pack.py --gguf ...\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Gyro-S-TQ1_0.gguf --out ...\packs\gyro-gyro-s --experts-bin
prism.hadamard: 48 layer(s) of Hadamard-folded experts (block 128, explicit signs): hadamard.txt, native_experts.txt v5
output_hc_down.weight is IQ4_NL, but the engine requires BF16; use --compat-bf16
output_hc_up.weight is IQ4_NL, but the engine requires BF16; use --compat-bf16
blk.0.hc_attn_down.weight is Q6_K, but the engine requires BF16; use --compat-bf16
...
... and 356 more
  [X]  command failed (exit 1): python.exe
Cause: In setup.py (around line 7920), the first iq_pack.py call passes the family's pack_args (["--compat-bf16"] for gyro). That call succeeds and writes compat-bf16.json, dense.bin and index.txt. The low-RAM --experts-bin call right after it doesn't pass pack_args. index_standalone() runs again without compat_bf16 and rejects the quantized hyper-connection tensors.

Suggested fix:

```
run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "iq_pack.py"), "--gguf", str(shards[0]), "--out", str(pack),
     "--experts-bin", *fam.get("pack_args", [])], env=env)
```
This probably affects any family with pack_args whenever low-RAM mode is on.

Smaller suggestion: In the app, both failures only show "Something went wrong" / "command failed (exit 1): python.exe" or a "files missing" message that Download / repair can't clear. The actual reason ("mtp folder ...\control\2 missing", or the --compat-bf16 lines) is only in setup.log or strata models list. Showing it in Diagnostics would have made both of these much faster to track down.

issues.title: [Engine] gfx1201 (RX 9070, 16 GB): batched prompt read stalls when 7 tokens are left; 0.1.45 and 0.1.45.3 (follow-up to #579)
issues.author: JustPowell
issues.body:
Follow-up to #579 (closed in the stale sweep; it asked for a new issue if it still happens on 0.1.44 or later). The same stall still happens here on 0.1.45 and on 0.1.45.3, and there's a very regular trigger: **every hang happens when the prompt's last batched step has 7 tokens left.**

## Pattern

The client is an automated loop. It sends short OpenAI-API requests: about 3-4K-token prompts, `max_tokens` 1500, `reasoning_effort: "none"`, no conversation reuse. Each request either finishes or hangs on the last step of the batched prompt read:

| prompt tokens | progress line when it stopped | tokens left |
|---|---|---|
| 3,898 | `reading the prompt: 3,891 of 3,898` | **7** (hung) |
| 4,012 | `4,005 of 4,012` | **7** (hung) |
| 3,079 | `3,072 of 3,079` | **7** (hung) |
| 3,127 | `3,126 of 3,127` | 1 (finished) |
| 3,909 | `3,908 of 3,909` | 1 (finished) |

Every hang where I could see the prompt length had 7 tokens left, and every request I saw finish had 1 left. issues.title: [Engine] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: layer split across 2 GPUs (single GPU = 58 tok/s vs 95 with llama.cpp -sm layer)
issues.author: FernandoSPinto
issues.body:
## Context

Strata's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B path (`src/qwen35`) runs on one GPU only. Setup says it explicitly:

```
[!] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B runs on one GPU so far: using GPU 0 (Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB, 16 GB) only
```

With the 0.1.45.3 engine it now loads on 2x Tesla P100-16GB (32 GB total) — the earlier engine died at load with `cudaMalloc(&d, h.size() * 4) failed: out of memory` (q36_engine.cu:954) — but everything stays on GPU 0:

```
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 76 of 256 per layer in VRAM (5.56 GiB), all 18.75 GiB in pinned host memory, the rest of a batch of <= 128 rows on 27 CPU threads
strata serve: session 0: prompt 33 tokens ... 200 generated in 3439 ms (58.2 tok/s)
```

GPU 1 stays at 262 MiB (idle).

## The case a layer split fits

- 32 GB of VRAM in total against a 22.9 GB model (UD-Q4_K_XL): with a split every expert fits in VRAM — the case `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` calls the fast one ("every expert in VRAM"), instead of the current hybrid mode (76/256 experts in VRAM, the rest from pinned RAM / CPU).
- Pascal is already admitted on this path: `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` (2x P100 reported; 2x P40 ran the layer split in a community benchmark: IQ2_XS 19.6 tok/s on one card, 34.8 on both, #1028).
- The same GGUF on llama.cpp with `-sm layer` on these two cards: **91-95 tok/s**, against 58 with Strata today.

## Request

Port the layer split from `src/program/generate.cpp` to `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: contiguous layer ranges per GPU, each layer's dense/GDN state and KV cache on its own GPU, and an expert cache per card for its own layers. Expose it as `--gpus 0,1` (`"gpu": [0, 1]` + `"layer_split": "auto"` in the config) — the setup already accepts `--gpus` for this family and then warns that it runs on one GPU.

## Reproduce

```
./setup.sh --family qwen36 --model UD-Q4_K_XL --gpus 0,1 --context 8192
# -> [!] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B runs on one GPU so far: using GPU 0 only
# start it: loads (0.1.45.3) with 76/256 experts per layer in VRAM, GPU 1 idle, ~58 tok/s
```

## What I already checked (so this is not a duplicate)

- `docs/MULTI_GPU.md`: the split exists for Flash-Next/Coder; `--peer-device` and `--gpu-placement` are expert-cache tiers, not a layer split (`--peer-device` is refused beside `--layer-split`).
- `docs/SECOND_GPU.md`: secondary-GPU expert tiers — a different mechanism, not offered for the qwen36 family.
- `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: split-K (intra-GPU) only, nothing across devices.
- Existing issues: #2747 (OOM — fixed by 0.1.45.3), #2982 (GPU utilization), #1402 (the original qwen35moe support), #2239 (a layer-split bug on a supported model) — none asks for a layer split for this family.

issues.title: [Engine] Batch slots on Metal, so one Mac Studio can serve a small office
issues.author: unimanco
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### What do you want to do?

We help small and mid-size companies, roughly 10 to 100 people, run their AI tools on hardware they own. Strata with Flash-Next is the most interesting option we've found for that. Being able to run a model this size on a Mac at all matters a lot to companies that don't want a server room full of GPUs. And thanks for the Mac port, by the way. Going from "out of scope" to a signed .dmg in under two weeks was impressive to watch.

The one thing that holds us back is that the Metal engine handles one request at a time (docs/MAC.md, Limits). For one person that's fine. For an office, it decides how many Macs you have to buy.

Here's how it looks on paper for a 100-person company. We assume about 5 model calls per person in the busiest hour, prompts of around 6k tokens (some 24k when they pull from the knowledge base) and about 700 output tokens. Using your M5 Max numbers and a rough scale-up for M5 Ultra, one request keeps a Mac busy for 9 to 12 seconds. Put that through a simple queueing model (under 3 s of waiting on average, under 10 s for 95% of requests) and you need 5 to 6 Mac Studios, spare included. Once agents are in the mix it's 8 or 9. If each Mac could decode 2 to 4 conversations together, the way the CUDA batch slots do, our rough estimate is 30 to 45% fewer machines. For a company that size, that's the difference between "a bit expensive" and an easy yes.

So we wanted to ask whether batch slots on Metal (`"parallel": N`, opt-in, same as on CUDA/HIP) are something you'd consider.

From #2715 the gap looks known: `--batch` is accepted on Metal, and the engine exits with code 86 on the first window that has two sequences. That report lists 17 entry points without a Metal implementation yet. It was closed in the 0.2.0 reset and nobody has picked it up since. We haven't re-tested it on 0.2.0-beta ourselves (we don't have a Mac with enough memory yet), so we're not asking to reopen it as a bug.

A few questions:

1. Is Metal batching on your list for 0.2.x, or should Mac setups plan on one request per machine for now?
2. Until it exists, would it make sense to refuse `--batch` on Metal at startup with a clear message, instead of exiting on the first concurrent request?
3. If you'd accept outside help, what order would you want (the capability queries and mapped copies first, then the multi-row kernels?), and what parity evidence per kernel?

We'd be glad to help. When our Mac Studios arrive (M5 Ultra, 256 GB, UD-Q6_K_XL) we can run whatever you'd like measured and post it as [Benchmark] reports. If you agree on the scope, we're also open to porting some of the kernels ourselves in small PRs.

### What do you do today instead?

Plan for one request per Mac and put several Macs behind a router with sticky sessions, along the lines of strata-router (#772). It works, but it's the expensive way to get concurrency.

The JSC UNITE GROUP team

issues.author: yusheng227507

issues.body:
## Summary

Two community benchmark runs on **2× RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75)** with `Strata v0.2.0-beta` (commit `e88ee39d`, engine `0.1.45.3`), plus a same-machine A/B measurement of `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1` on the previous release (`v0.1.45`, engine `0.1.45`).

The A/B is the part that may be useful to you: `sm75_series.hpp` says the Turing kernels are opt-in because *"We have no sm_75 card to confirm them"*. This machine is an sm_75 card, and the measured gain is consistent: **+5.3 % (IQ3_S) and +6.2 % (IQ3_XXS) on 16K fresh prompts**, with no regression in decode.

## Hardware

- GPU: 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti, 22528 MiB each (sm_75), driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2 (engine built against `/usr/local/cuda-12.8`)
- CPU: Intel Core i7-10700K (8 cores / 16 threads), 94.1 GiB RAM
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-147-generic
- Both cards are used with `--layer-split` (`layer_split = 26`); the generated README lists the GPU model once, but the run used both cards.

## Results — v0.2.0-beta, `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1`

| Model | Context / slots | short chat decode | 4K prompt | 16K prompt | agent follow-up decode |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IQ3_S | 262144 / 3 | 70.8 tok/s | 721.2 tok/s | 1264.7 tok/s | 72.6 tok/s |
| IQ3_XXS | 262144 / 3 | 74.3 tok/s | 831.2 tok/s | 1304.4 tok/s | 79.3 tok/s |

Median of 3 runs per test (short chat: 9 requests), temperature 0, thinking off, fresh prompts tagged so the cache cannot help. Full tables, ranges, TTFT and the agent-session cache breakdown are in the two READMEs below.

## A/B: `STRATA_SM75_PERF` on sm_75 (v0.1.45, engine 0.1.45)

Same machine, same configs, same bench, run back to back (series off first, then on). The Turing kernel series was unchanged by 0.2.0, so this still applies.

| Model | Test | `SM75_PERF` off | `SM75_PERF=1` | Δ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IQ3_S | 16K prompt | 1185.9 tok/s | 1248.8 tok/s | **+5.3 %** |
| IQ3_S | 4K prompt | 707.9 | 708.6 | +0.1 % |
| IQ3_S | short chat decode | 68.4 | 70.3 | +2.8 % |
| IQ3_XXS | 16K prompt | 1224.3 | 1300.0 | **+6.2 %** |
| IQ3_XXS | 4K prompt | 801.5 | 823.8 | +2.8 % |
| IQ3_XXS | short chat decode | 72.1 | 74.9 | +3.9 % |

Notes on the measurement:
- The "on" runs came second, after ~10 minutes of load, so the GPUs were at least as hot; if anything the gain is understated.
- Ranges were tight (e.g. 16K IQ3_S: 1183.7–1186.4 off, 1247.1–1252.0 on), i.e. far outside run-to-run noise.
- The header documents these kernels as bitwise equal to the ones they replace, which matches: no output difference was observed.

For reference, `v0.1.45 → v0.2.0-beta` with the switch on in both cases is flat within noise (16K: 1248.8 → 1264.7 and 1300.0 → 1304.4 tok/s, i.e. +0.3…+1.3 %).

## Settings (both models)

`--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --vram-reserve-mib 1500 --max-context 262144`, `parallel = 3`, MTP `rt`, vision reader on CPU (`"gpu": false`, 8 threads), `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1`. Nothing else tuned.

## Method note

The bench was run with `--url` against an already-running server because `tools/strata_bench.py --config …` currently fails with `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` ([#2864](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2864)). Model loading is not timed either way.

issues.title: [Benchmark] 2x RTX 3090 NVLink, Ryzen 9 3950X, 121 GiB: v0.2.0-beta with IQ3_S / UD-Q4_K_XL / UD-Q5_K_XL on the Q8_0 PLE table, int8 vs fp16 KV
issues.author: q8atnight
issues.body:
**Hardware:** 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), NVLink bridge (NV4, 4 links x 14.06 GB/s), each card PCIe 4.0 x8, power limit 400 W. AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (16 cores / 32 threads, AVX2, no AVX-512). 121 GiB RAM. Model files and PLE table on a Samsung 970 PRO 1 TB NVMe. Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-31, driver 595.84. Source build in a CUDA 13.0 container (`-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`), engine run in Docker.

**Engine:** `v0.2.0-beta` (tag `3d1fb480`, engine 0.1.45.3) plus:
- #1937 (conversations to disk, head `6e71ac5d`, merged; 14 conflict hunks resolved).
- #1525 (`759c8b90`, applied cleanly).
- #3022 (STRATA_HC_Q8 trim).
- The decode half of #1099 (`STRATA_SPLIT_P2P=1`: the window hand-off goes over NVLink), ported by hand.
- A small fix of ours: `--ple-gguf` may name a shard that holds **only** the PLE table and belongs to another file set. The engine used to add it to the dense shards and then refused it with "additional shard must match the architecture-validated first shard's split metadata".

**Same answers as stock:** stock 0.2.0 (plus only the PLE fix) against the build above, on the deterministic gate (`--expert-cache 3000 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --prompt-cache 0 --no-prefill-borrow`; greedy, 3 short prompts plus 2 questions on a 20K-token prompt). The output was **identical on all three quants** (IQ3_S, UD-Q4_K_XL, UD-Q5_K_XL, each with the Q8_0 table). On UD-Q4_K_XL it was also identical with `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0`, with `STRATA_SPLIT_P2P=1`, with `STRATA_HANDOFF_PIPE=4`, and with `STRATA_AUX_CPUS=auto STRATA_STAGE_PIN=1`.

### What was run

Three quants, all on the **Q8_0 PLE table** from UD-Q5_K_XL shard 3 (sha256 `34efd79a…`, the same file as UD-Q6_K_XL's shard 3). The table is passed with `--ple-gguf` and read from the SSD (`--ple-io direct`). Every expert is held in RAM; nothing is mapped from the file.
- ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_S
- unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL
- unsloth UD-Q5_K_XL

**Flags:**

```
--layer-split 24 --trim-stage-weights --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --ple-io direct --ple-gguf <UD-Q5_K_XL-00003-of-00006.gguf>
--kv int8|fp16 --kv-resident 20480 (IQ3_S: 32768) --max-context 262144 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.7 (IQ3_S: 0.8) --mtp mtp/rt
--vision (vision on the CPU, 2048 tokens) --vram-reserve-mib 400 --pipeline-windows 2 --pcie-frac 0.2
--conversation-cache-mib 16384 / 32768 / 8192 (Q4 / IQ3_S / Q5) --conversation-cache-slots 4 / 8 / 4 --conversation-disk-dir <dir>
env: STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0 STRATA_SPLIT_P2P=1 STRATA_HC_Q8=1   (the sm_86 switch table is on by default)
```

**Method:** one fresh engine per arm, arms run one after another (not interleaved).
- "Chat": 400-token answers to a code prompt, a prose prompt and a 50K-token chat. Median of 3 after 2 warm-up rounds.
- "FB": flashbench at 1K / 8K / 32K / 128K, greedy and sampled (temperature 1.0), 2 repeats.
- Prefill: fresh 1.5K / 4K / 20K real-code prompts, 2 each.
- Run-to-run noise on this box is about ±3–5 % on decode.

### Results (tokens/s)

| Setup | Chat decode code / prose / 50K | FB decode greedy 1K / 8K / 32K / 128K | FB prefill greedy 1K / 8K / 32K / 128K | 20K prefill | Expert hit | RAM free after load |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reference: our old build, 0.1.43.1 + ports, UD-Q4_K_XL, IQ4_NL table, int8 | 109.3 / 97.7 / 98.2 | 127.3 / 136.4 / 127.5 / 121.6 | 373 / 1,649 / 2,624 / 3,143 | 2,359 | 95.4 % | 37 GiB |
| IQ3_S, int8 KV | 137.3 / 128.9 / 137.7 | 140.3 / 139.9 / 138.4 / 122.8 | 908 / 2,260 / 3,618 / 4,451 | 3,285 | 99.7 % | 62 GiB |
| IQ3_S, fp16 KV | 137.6 / 135.5 / 132.6 | 144.5 / 139.7 / 137.6 / 135.6 | 843 / 1,921 / 2,996 / 3,562 | 2,751 | 99.7 % | 59 GiB |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, int8 KV | 111.9 / 105.5 / 103.6 | 126.4 / 120.0 / 115.2 / 111.2 | 366 / 1,711 / 2,621 / 3,119 | 2,119–2,355 | 95.0 % | 36 GiB |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, fp16 KV | 115.1 / 107.4 / 105.2 | 122.2 / 121.4 / 119.2 / 112.7 | 356 / 1,526 / 2,266 / 2,647 | 1,906 | 94.3 % | 33 GiB |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, its own IQ4_NL table (control) | 119.3 / 99.2 / 110.9 | 124.3 / 121.1 / 119.5 / 109.2 | 369 / 1,708 / 2,618 / 3,112 | 2,315 | 94.4 % | 37 GiB |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, int8, tail skip ON | 120.8 / 108.3 / 113.2 | 127.3 / 119.7 / 121.6 / 109.1 | 368 / 1,690 / 2,614 / 3,115 | 2,274 | 97.0 % | 37 GiB |
| UD-Q5_K_XL, int8 KV | 96.0 / 79.6 / 79.4 | 107.5 / 103.5 / 96.8 / 89.3 | 250 / 1,294 / 1,989 / 2,347 | 1,733 | 89.8 % | 16 GiB |
| UD-Q5_K_XL, int8, tail skip ON | 105.3 / 93.3 / 95.0 | 116.8 / 112.9 / 109.3 / 99.4 | 251 / 1,302 / 1,995 / 2,354 | 1,741 | 93.7 % | 16 GiB |
| UD-Q5_K_XL, fp16 KV | did not start: see below | | | | | |

A 10-question quiz (thinking on) scored 10/10 on every setup that started.

### Findings
- **The sm_86 default table on a 2-card layer split:** same answers as `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0` (gate above), and faster. UD-Q4_K_XL int8: chat decode 110.2 / 101.8 / 102.6 against 107.7 / 97.9 / 97.3 with the table off; FB greedy decode 122.2 / 115.0 / 113.9 / 114.4 against 107.5 / 109.1 / 102.4 / 103.2. That is the multi-GPU row the release notes did not have.
- **The Q8_0 table costs nothing measurable here** when it is read from the SSD: UD-Q4_K_XL with Q8_0 against its own IQ4_NL table is within noise on every column (PLE read probe 93K vs 149K rows/s).
- **UD-Q5_K_XL with fp16 KV and every expert in RAM does not fit 121 GiB.** The experts (91.6 GiB) loaded and the GPU cache filled, then systemd-oomd killed the desktop session under memory pressure and the engine exited. With int8 KV it runs and leaves about 16 GiB free.
- **The 0.2.0 build against our 0.1.43.1 build** (UD-Q4_K_XL, int8): chat decode is about 6 % faster and prompt speed is about equal. Flashbench decode is about 5–7 % slower (FB geomean 116–117 against 121–125, two runs of the old build).
- `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0=1`: the engine exits at start on this build (not investigated; it may be our #1099 port).
- `STRATA_MMQ_KQ=1`: changes the gate output, and the 20K prefill was slower here (2,187–2,225 against 2,317–2,355).
- `STRATA_HANDOFF_PIPE=4`: identical output, no measurable gain.
- `--kv-resident 32768` on UD-Q4_K_XL: the gate output changes, and the speed gain is small.
- **Route tail skip ON:** UD-Q5_K_XL decode +9–15 %, UD-Q4_K_XL +2–7 %, IQ3_S +1 % (99.7 % hit already).

**Not tested:** concurrency, needle/recall, KLD. Each arm was run once (no interleaved pairs), so read differences below about 5 % as noise.

*Everything in this report was done by Claude Opus 5.5 working as an agent on this machine: the merges, the builds, the measurements and this write-up.*

issues.title: [Other] calibrate dies with "there is no GPU 0,1" on a dual config whose gpu is the string form
issues.author: MEsfits
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (setup.sh / setup.py in a source tree at 0.2.0)

### What happened

Setup's calibration of a dual-GPU config whose `"gpu"` is the string form `"0,1"` runs all measurement rounds, then stops with:

```
  [X]  there is no GPU 0,1: 0 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, 1 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090

Setup stopped. Fix the item above and run it again - everything already done is kept and skipped.
```

Expected: the calibration completes and is saved, exactly as for the list form `"gpu": [0, 1]`. Nothing is saved, because the hardware key is what the measured rounds are saved under, and computing it is where it dies.

Cause: `hardware_key()` passes `cfg["gpu"]` to `gpu_info()` unchanged; `gpu_info()` matches one card by number (`x["index"] == pick`), so the string `"0,1"` matches nothing. Serve already splits the same string form, and list-form duals work. `recommend_remote_expert_opt()` also silently skips string-form duals (`isinstance(..., list)` check), so they never get the helper-cache recommendation.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Source tree at 0.2.0 (engine 0.1.45.3) with a dual-GPU config whose `"gpu"` is the string form `"0,1"` (serve accepts it).
2. Run setup and let it calibrate that config.
3. After "Measuring the expert tier ..." and the bench round, setup stops with the message above.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (source tree at main e88ee39d)

### Graphics card, memory and system

2x RTX 3090 (3090 Ti 24 GB + 3090 24 GB) · 59 GB RAM · Ubuntu 26.04

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S dual config · 256K context · pictures on

### Logs

```
  Measuring the expert tier every 1, 160 swaps, decay 0.97 (restarts the engine) ...[strata] starting the engine: reading the model's weights ...
[...]
    146.4 tok/s

  [X]  there is no GPU 0,1: 0 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, 1 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
```

### Notes

This was reported before (#2378 on the 0.1.45 line) and a fix was sent, but it is not in the 0.2.0 tree (`setup.py` still has the pre-fix line). The earlier issue/PR were closed without it landing, so this is resubmitted for 0.2.0.

issues.title: [Other] gfx906 (2× Radeon Pro VII): install report, 200K k8v4 + CPU vision, and a 50% CPU question
issues.author: Marczellito
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Your question

Two minor questions; everything else works:

1. **CPU use:** `top` peaks at ~50% (18 of 36 logical CPUs) on this 18C/36T Xeon. The engine log says *17 pool workers + the host thread*; `docs/AMD_HIP.md` and `docs/DETAILS.md:557` suggest one worker per physical core is deliberate and all-logical was slower on gfx1030. Is that the expected behavior on Haswell-EP too?
2. **Setup path:** the docs say setup does not build gfx906, but on v0.1.45 setup stops at its first GPU check, so the model download and pack preparation are also unreachable without patching `setup.py`. Is a **download-only** route (or clearer by-hand download instructions) planned? That was the only real install dead end I hit.

The report below is a successful end-to-end run on v0.1.45 (`477ac13c`), 2× Radeon Pro VII 16 GB (gfx906), 64 GB RAM, CachyOS kernel 7.2.3: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 200K context, `--kv k8v4`, pictures on (CPU encoder). It is also posted as a comment on #2883 (the gfx906 validation thread); #3172 tracks the gfx906 build blockers I hit. I am not asking for a new feature; I am sharing what worked and where the friction is.

### What you tried

#### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 2× AMD Radeon Pro VII 16 GB, gfx906 (Vega 20, `1002:66a1`), 190 W power limit, PCIe 3.0 (engine probe 13.8 GB/s host→device) |
| CPU / RAM | Intel Xeon E5-2696 v3, 18C/36T, AVX2; 64 GB DDR4-2133 ECC at 1866 MT/s (setup reports 63 GB) |
| OS | CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.2.3-1-cachyos, GCC 16.2.1 |
| ROCm | system ROCm 7.2.4 at `/opt/rocm`, HIP 7.2.53211, AMD clang 22.0.0; no container, no `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`. The distro package ships gfx906 rocBLAS kernels (`Kernels.so-000-gfx906-xnack-.hsaco`); the community image was not needed. |
| Strata | source v0.1.45, commit `477ac13c`, engine `0.1.45`; llama.cpp `3cf03257f` |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, two shards 54.82 + 28.80 GB; vision `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf` on CPU |
| Config | `--max-context 204800 --kv k8v4 --vision --gpus 0,1 --layer-split auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --prefill auto --expert-cache auto --vram-reserve-mib 700 --vram-reserve-later-mib 1006` |
| MTP | draft layer reused from an earlier install under `Strata-data/mtp/rt`; `tools/mtp_fetch.py verify` rc=0 |

Setup command: `./setup.sh --yes --backend hip --gpus 0,1 --family qwen --model IQ3_S --vision cpu --no-start`, then the 200K / `k8v4` choices.

Note: setup's step-2 summary prints `KV cache: 4-bit (Hadamard-rotated)` for any non-int8 choice (`setup.py:6581`); the written config is `--kv k8v4` (K 8-bit, V 4-bit). Wording only.

#### What worked

- **Build:** the documented `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906` path, with the compat layer, built the engine and the CPU vision encoder. Build time ~15 min at `-j18`. The 4-file diff is in the gist below; the CMake + cublas hunks are the same set posted in #2459, and #3172 tracks the same blockers.
- **KV parity on the cards:** `kv_hybrid_parity` **ALL PASS** (k8v4 appends/gathers, 0 bad of 786,432/24,576; mode-3 batched attention 7.82e-08 vs the dequant reference), `kv_stream_parity` k8v4 ring 0 failures, `kv_window_parity` 0 bad/0 stale, `kv_steps_parity` 120/120, `kv_q8_parity` OK.
- **End-to-end:** setup (patched) → engine → download → pack → start script; server `/health` ready; text `17*23?` → `391`; vision (64×64 red PNG) → `Red`; images on. The docs' gfx906 section lists images (`--vision`) as not done — this run verifies the CPU encoder path on Radeon Pro VII.
- **Start:** ~75–90 s to ready; 46.84 GiB of experts into RAM at 1.51 GiB/s; expert cache 5,724 slots (10.30 GiB) and, on CUDA1, 4,180 slots (8.42 GiB); 586 MiB / 768 MiB free after load.
- **200K config:** `k8v4` at 204,800 costs ~2.2 GB and stays in VRAM. KV streaming is off: it needs ~2.2 GB beside the ~62 GB of experts on a 63 GB machine. No KV-related errors.
- **Long sessions:** several chats with 23K–35K-token prompts and 22K–42K-token outputs; decode held 43.8–51.6 tok/s (table below). The requests completed; the only warnings were the VRAM notes.
- **Downloads / MTP:** 86 `download interrupted` retry lines across 13 setup attempts (mostly DNS, 12 read timeouts) on a flaky link; every resume continued from `.part`, zero corruption. MTP verify passed.

#### What did not work / known issues

**Known / already tracked**

1. **`setup.py` refuses gfx906 at step 1** — documented as "Setup does not build it yet", but the failure also makes the ~84 GB download and pack preparation unreachable through setup. Exact first-run output (before the local patch):

   ```
     Your AMD GPUs:
       GPU 0: AMD Radeon (gfx906), 16 GB VRAM - cannot be used
     [!] AMD GPU 0 (AMD Radeon (gfx906)) cannot be used: not supported - [...]
         this is gfx906
     Setup stopped. Fix the item above and run it again - everything already done is kept and skipped.
   ```

   My local `setup.py` change adds gfx906 to `AMD_ARCHS`/`AMD_NAMES` and passes the gfx906 flags (including `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=OFF`). I am **not** proposing it as the default (the docs say manual build); a **download-only** path, or clearer by-hand download instructions, would remove the dead end. This is the main friction I hit.

2. **Build blockers on 0.1.45** (reproduced locally; exact messages in `build-errors.txt` in the gist):
   - missing `cublasSgemm`, `cublasSgemmStridedBatched`, `cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx` aliases in `platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h` (qwen35 `q36_engine.cu`);
   - `strata_mmq_w4a4` compiled without `GGML_USE_HIP` → `cuda.h` not found;
   - `f16kq::*` undefined at link — missing `src/prefill/moe_f16_kq.cu` in `strata_mmq` under `STRATA_HIP_GFX906`;
   - GCC 16 `<format>` vs HIP's `__noinline__` macro (fix: `#undef __noinline__` in the gfx906 compat header);
   - stale `build-hip` cache with `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON` + `STRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON` → "enable only one"; pass `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=OFF` or use a fresh build directory.

   These are in **#3172** (open; confirmed on 0.2.0-beta) and were reported in **#2459** (closed by the tracker reset). I am adding the end-to-end result, not a new build bug.

**Rough edges found here**

3. **VRAM is tight at request start.** The first start (only `--vram-reserve-mib 700`) logged `CUDA1: 462 MiB ... LOW`; adding `--vram-reserve-later-mib 1006` removed it (768 MiB free after load). One later request still logged:

   ```
   WARNING: only 493 MiB of VRAM free at the start of this request (below 512 MiB) ... Add --vram-reserve-mib 768 ...
   ```

   The following long requests still ran at 44–52 tok/s, but if the driver starts paging, `--vram-reserve-mib 768` (or 1024) is the engine's own suggestion. The desktop here is on CUDA1; `--vram-reserve-later-mib 1006` is what fixed the CUDA1 window-capture warning.

4. **`qsa_prompt_attn mode 3` refuses on HIP** and the older kernel runs; output is correct, but if mode 3 is expected to work on gfx906 this is masking it. (Observed in the parity tests; not a correctness failure.)

5. **No hipBLASLt tuning table for gfx906** (hipBLASLt 100202): setup says the prompt's dense GEMMs use plain hipBLAS. Expected for this arch, but it is a prompt-speed opportunity.

6. **Network:** the only reason setup needed 13 attempts; not a Strata issue, but the log is full of it.

#### CPU usage: ~50% (18 of 36 threads)

`top` peaks around 50% on this 18C/36T Xeon. The engine log says:

```
strata generate: 17 pool workers on logical processors 1,...,17, the host thread on 0 (--host-core first)
strata aux cpus: ... CPUs 18 (off at start; a request's aux_cpus=1 turns it on)
```

So it uses one logical CPU per physical core (17 workers + host = 18 threads) and leaves the 18 SMT siblings alone. `docs/AMD_HIP.md` (gfx1030 report) says the default is one worker per physical core and that using all logical CPUs was slower there (27 vs 38–42 tok/s); `docs/DETAILS.md:557` documents `--pool-workers`. I think this is expected, not a bug. If a sweep on Haswell-EP would be useful, I can run `--pool-workers 8/17/24/35` with a fixed prompt, but I have not done it.

#### Not tested

- **0.2.0-beta** (`3d1fb480`): not run; #3172 says the gfx906 build still fails there. This report is v0.1.45 only.
- Full 200K prompt / needle tests; KV streaming on; concurrent requests; a 12 h soak; a formal 3-run benchmark or `tools/strata_bench.py`; vision accuracy/speed beyond one image; CUDA/SYCL builds; Windows; a fresh MTP download.
- I did not run the CUDA build. My CMake changes are inside `STRATA_HIP_GFX906`, and the cublas/`__noinline__` changes are in the gfx906 compat headers, but I cannot claim the other backends from this machine.

#### Logs

Sanitized files in one secret gist (link-only, not indexed): `setup-evidence.log` (curated; the full setup log is 1,193 lines), `engine-session-evidence.log`, `build-errors.txt`, `strata-gfx906-fixes.patch`, `config-iq3_s-sanitized.json` — https://gist.github.com/Marczellito/9e9324702246fe9f1acfb0306e868c9e. Local paths are shortened to `~`; no API keys, passwords, emails, or hostnames. Full logs on request.

### Results (optional)

From `strata-iq3_s.log` after the 1006 restart. These are engine-reported averages from one continuous session, **not** the 3-run benchmark protocol. "Prompt read" is the newly read part; the reused prefix is excluded, so the prompt speed is the speed of that read, not of the whole context.

| prompt tokens (reused + new) | prompt speed | generated | decode | drafts accepted | cache hit | end context |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23,133 (81 + 23,052) | 590.3 tok/s | 41,406 | 51.6 tok/s | 25,704 / 33,271 | 97.4% | ~64.5K |
| 31,231 (23,128 + 8,103) | 403.8 tok/s | 33,051 | 43.8 tok/s | 17,267 / 27,890 | 97.2% | ~64.3K |
| 32,910 (31,226 + 1,684) | 295.7 tok/s | 42,604 | 50.3 tok/s | 27,297 / 38,890 | 96.9% | ~75.5K |
| 34,916 (32,905 + 2,011) | 312.2 tok/s | 22,758 | 50.4 tok/s | 14,153 / 17,521 | 94.4% | ~57.7K |
| 500 (56 + 444) | 157.5 tok/s | 2,829 | 48.2 tok/s | 1,638 / 2,453 | 94.5% | — |

issues.title: [Other] 0.2.0 Linux control package: tools/iq_pack.py can't find gguf-py; the "run setup.py" hint doesn't fix it in a control-mode install
issues.author: talisp
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Other

The Linux control package (`strata-control-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`), unpacked, with its bundled packer run by hand. No desktop app.

### What happened

I ran the bundled packer by hand to make packs for six Unsloth Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUFs (UD-Q2_K_XL to Q8_0). It stops after listing the shards with:

```
llama.cpp's gguf-py was not found: run setup.py (it clones llama.cpp into third_party/), or set STRATA_GGUF_PY
```

**Cause (from reading the code)**

- The package has no `third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py`.
- `tools/_paths.py` looks only in `$STRATA_GGUF_PY`, `<control>/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py` and the dev tree's `.ref/llama.cpp/gguf-py`.
- In control mode (`STRATA_CONTROL_INSTALL=1`), `setup.py` writes `third_party/` to `home()` (`STRATA_INSTALL_DIR`), not to `ROOT`. So the hint "run setup.py" doesn't help a tool run by hand: the tool never looks in `home()/third_party`.
- `setup.py` itself is fine: it sets `STRATA_GGUF_PY` when it calls the tools (e.g. at step 6). Only a tool run directly from the package hits this.

**Workaround (works)**

Point `STRATA_GGUF_PY` at any llama.cpp `gguf-py` (I used the one from a 0.1.45 source install):

```
STRATA_GGUF_PY=<llama.cpp>/gguf-py python/bin/python3 tools/iq_pack.py --gguf ... --out ... --compat-bf16
```

With that, the UD-Q2_K_XL pack takes ~25 s. The engine starts in 39 s and serves normally on the 0.2.0 engine: ~125 tok/s decode at 8K and ~110 tok/s at 128K, with MTP on.

**Suggestion**

Any one of these would fix it:
- ship `gguf-py` in the control package;
- have `_paths.py` also check `$STRATA_INSTALL_DIR/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py`;
- change the error message to name `STRATA_GGUF_PY` as the fix for packages.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Unpack `strata-control-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (SHA-256 OK against SHA256SUMS.txt).
2. Run:

```
cd <control> && python/bin/python3 tools/iq_pack.py --gguf <model>-00001-of-0000N.gguf --out <packs>/<m> --compat-bf16
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (control and engine 0.1.45.3, Linux x86_64, engine package cuda12)

### Graphics card, memory and system

NVIDIA L40S-48Q (vGPU, sm_89, 48 GB), driver 550.127.05; 251 GiB RAM; Xeon Platinum 8580 (32 vCPU); Ubuntu 22.04

### Model, size and settings

unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF UD-Q2_K_XL (73.5 GiB, revision 766911a), `--compat-bf16`

### Logs

```
llama.cpp's gguf-py was not found: run setup.py (it clones llama.cpp into third_party/), or set STRATA_GGUF_PY
```

issues.title: [Other] 0.2.0-beta prebuilt hip-rx7900 engine on a real RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, Linux): runs, same speed as 0.1.44.1; GPU picture reader works; two packaging notes
issues.author: faf-net
issues.body:
## Problem and result

The 0.2.0-beta notes say the RX 7000 builds compile but no RX 7000 card ran them. Here is one: the prebuilt engine package `strata-engine-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64-hip-rx7900.tar.gz` (SHA-256 checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`) with the control package `strata-control-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64`, on a single **RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100)**, Linux. Everything else was kept as in my 0.1.44.1 report (#2904) so the numbers compare directly: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS native pack, MTP head `rt`, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --vram-reserve-mib 832 --pool-workers 9 --pcie-frac 0`, conversation cache 4,608 MiB, hipBLASLt table `gfx1100-hipblaslt-100200` (the engine reported "hipBLASLt tuning enabled (26 rows, gfx1100, version 100200)").

**It runs.** Load 17.7 s from the page cache; `strata doctor` exit 0; no errors in the engine log.

| `tools/strata_bench.py --long` (median, n=3/9/15) | 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`, #2904) | 0.2.0-beta `hip-rx7900` |
|---|---:|---:|
| chat decode tok/s | 63.7 | 61.3 (47.3–72.1) |
| 4K / 16K / 32K prompt tok/s | 741 / 1,195 / 1,224 | 741 / 1,207 / 1,223 |
| agent cache hit | 68.6 % | 68.6 % |
| agent decode tok/s | 74.0 | 73.2 |

`needle_bench.py` (depths 10/50/90 %): 3/3 at 32K, 3/3 at 128K, 3/3 at 250K (251,626 prompt tokens, 217–229 s each).

Our own task set (`bench.py`: code, logic, refusals, tool calls; automatic checks, one run): 27 of 29 (code 7/8, logic 9/9, tools 3/3, refusals 8/9), against 26 (0.1.44.1) and 27 (0.1.45) on this box on 2026-10-17. Short / long answer 59.7 / 64.0 tok/s, agent session (6 turns) 40.6–48.0 s.

**Fresh engines with MTP (the R9700 note in Known limits):** 24 fresh starts of this engine, each with a warm-up and then two fresh 4K prompts. 23 read at 662–684 tok/s; **one read both prompts at 420 and 427 tok/s, about 38 % slower**. Its start-up lines (memory guard, read probes, load speed, expert slots, hipBLASLt) matched the others within noise. The same test on 0.1.44.1: 0 of 24 slow (646–682 tok/s). So the effect shows up on gfx1100 too, but here in about 1 of 24 starts, not half.

**Picture reader (new in 0.2.0):** the package carries `strata-vision` (CPU) and `strata-vision-hip` (GPU). Both read all four test pictures correctly (a red square, the number 4728, three coloured squares, the number 8274 drawn large).

| | CPU reader (`gpu: false`, 8 threads, max 300 tokens) | GPU reader (`gpu: true`, max 1024 tokens) |
|---|---:|---:|
| expert cache | 8,830 slots, 14.30 GiB | **8,054 slots, 13.02 GiB** |
| "VRAM free with everything loaded" | 726 MiB | 728 MiB |
| small picture, whole request | 1.36–1.58 s | 1.33–1.42 s |
| large picture | 5.62 s (325 prompt tokens) | 3.50 s (504 prompt tokens) |

So on a 24 GB card the GPU reader costs 776 expert slots (1.28 GiB); the engine sizes the cache around it, and free VRAM stays the same. Decode speed with the smaller cache was not measured.

## Two packaging notes

1. The engine binary's `--version` prints `strata 0.1.45`, while its `BUILD.json` and `engine-component.json` and the control package's `VERSION` say 0.1.45.3.
2. The tarball holds **1,080 extra files, 423 MiB uncompressed**, next to the binaries: `strata.<n>.hipv4-amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx1100/1101/1102`, `strata.<n>.host-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-`, and the same for `strata-vision-hip` and `librocblas.so.5.*`. They look like unbundled code objects. They are not listed in `engine-component.json` (579 entries, none of them). I did not test whether the engine runs without them.

## Validation

**Passed:** everything above, on 2026-10-19, prebuilt engine 0.1.45.3 `hip-rx7900` (`build_id f6d65cb58+rocm`), kernel 6.18.15, container Ubuntu 24.04 with `/dev/kfd` and `/dev/dri`; server started with the control package's own Python (`python/bin/python3 serve/server.py --engine strata --config ...`), `STRATA_ENGINE` set to the package.
**Failed:** one 250K needle run was cut off by my own setup (the model manager in front of the server unloaded the idle model while `needle_bench.py` talked to the backend directly), not by Strata; repeated, see above.
**Not run:** the AppImage and the installer (`install.sh`), `strata launch`, the app; Windows; gfx1101/1102; the identity gate.

Machine: UGREEN iDX6011 Pro NAS, Core Ultra 7 255H, 64 GB, RX 7900 XTX over OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x4, UGOS Pro 1.19 (Debian 12 base). Raw data: #2904, folder `followup-2026-10-19/strata-0.2.0-beta/`. The hybrid-CPU worker count is a separate issue: #3262.

issues.title: [Engine] Linux hybrid CPU: LP-E cores (cpu_lowpower) counted as P-cores, and 0.2.0's 15-worker default is ~35 % slower than 9 on a Core Ultra 7 255H
issues.author: faf-net
issues.body:
## Problem and result

On an Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (Arrow Lake-H: 6 P + 8 E + 2 LP-E, no SMT) under Linux, Strata's pool planning has two effects I could measure:

1. **The two LP-E cores are treated as P-cores.** `pool.cpp` (Linux branch) decides P/E from Intel's hybrid PMU lists `/sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus` and `/sys/devices/cpu_atom/cpus`. On Meteor Lake / Arrow Lake-H the LP-E cores are in a **third** list, `/sys/devices/cpu_lowpower/cpus`, so `is_e()` returns false for them. They sort after the real P-cores (lower capacity) but before every E-core, and get workers early: with `--pool-workers 9` the engine reports `9 pool workers on logical processors 1,2,3,4,5,14,15,6,7`. `--pool-affinity measure` (0.1.45) reported "8 P-cores / 8 threads, 8 E-cores".
2. **The new 0.2.0 default (one worker per physical core but the host's) picks 15 workers here**, and that is much slower than 9 on this CPU (single `bench.py` runs, same model and settings otherwise):

| Engine | Workers | Short answer | Long answer |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 0.2.0-beta prebuilt `hip-rx7900` (0.1.45.3) | `--pool-workers 9` | 59.7 tok/s | 64.0 tok/s |
| 0.2.0-beta prebuilt `hip-rx7900` (0.1.45.3) | default → 15 (`1,2,3,4,5,14,15,6,...,13`) | 39.8 tok/s | 41.2 tok/s |

This matches an earlier sweep on 0.1.44.1 (IQ2_XS, long answer, median of 3): automatic 56.1, 5 workers 76.6, 9 workers 76.8, 13 workers 74.0 tok/s.

## Topology (sysfs, kernel 6.18.15)

```
cpu_core/cpus     0-5     cpu_capacity 1024, max 5.1 GHz, private L2, L3 24 MiB
cpu_atom/cpus     6-13    cpu_capacity  774, max 4.4 GHz, L2 shared by 4 (6-9, 10-13), L3
cpu_lowpower/cpus 14-15   cpu_capacity  312, max 2.5 GHz, L2 shared by 2, no L3 (SoC tile)
```

## What the LP-E cores cost (A/B, 0.1.44.1)

Same engine and config (IQ3_XXS, MTP, `--pool-workers 9`), container limited with `--cpuset-cpus 0-13` (B) or not (A). Three interleaved pairs, each a fresh engine, one warm-up answer, then two measured answers of 900 tokens:

| | A: CPUs 0-15 (workers on 14, 15) | B: CPUs 0-13 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Decode tok/s, 6 answers | 61.7–64.4, median 63.3 | 59.9–63.8, median 62.2 |
| 63-token prompt, prompt tok/s | 60.6–69.0, median 66.1 | 91.4–95.4, median 93.9 |

Decode is unchanged; short prompts are read about 40 % faster without the LP-E cores (first token for a short chat turn about 0.95 s → 0.67 s). Longer prompts were not part of this A/B.

## Suggested change (not tested as a patch)

Read `/sys/devices/cpu_lowpower/cpus` beside `cpu_core` and `cpu_atom`, treat those CPUs as the lowest tier (after E-cores, or excluded by default), and keep the capacity fallback (`cap * 10 < max_cap * 9`) for CPUs that are in no list. For the default worker count on a hybrid CPU, this box suggests "P-cores + a few E-cores" rather than "every physical core". I can build and measure a patch on this machine (HIP only; I cannot build CUDA or SYCL here).

## Validation

**Passed:** sysfs reads above; A/B with `--cpuset-cpus` (`folgetests.py cpu`, raw JSON lines); 0.2.0 prebuilt engine with and without `--pool-workers 9` (`bench.py --tests schreiben`); placement lines copied from the engine log.
**Failed:** none.
**Not run:** a patched engine; Windows (the Windows branch has its own detection); other Meteor/Arrow/Lunar Lake CPUs; more than one run per configuration for the 0.2.0 worker comparison.

Machine: UGREEN iDX6011 Pro NAS, Core Ultra 7 255H, 64 GB LPDDR5X, RX 7900 XTX over OCuLink x4, UGOS Pro 1.19 (Debian 12 base), ROCm 7.10 (TheRock), model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS. Benchmark report: #2904. Scripts: https://github.com/faf-net/ugreen-idx6011-egpu-llm

issues.title: Strata Benchmark Report — Qwen3.8 Flash Next (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL) on 0.1.45, with --vision=cpu, 260+ kombinations
issues.author: DrLove73

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

issues.body:
# Strata Benchmark Report — Qwen3.8 Flash Next (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL) on 0.1.45, with --vision=cpu, 260+ kombinations

**Model family:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next  
**Quantization:** Unsloth Dynamic UD-Q4_K_XL (4-bit, K-quant experts)  
**Engine:** Strata 0.1.45 (llama.cpp 3cf0325)  
**Hardware:** RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (24 GB VRAM), Intel Xeon Gold 6138, 220 GB RAM  
**Dates:** 2026-10-17 (Legacy), 2026-10-19 (Strata 0.1.45 `vision=cpu` re-run)  
**Contexts:** 128K, 256K, 384K, 512K  
**Total runs:** 200+

## Summary

Peak decode is **42.70 tok/s at 256K**. Unlike the Swift IQ3_S model, offloading the vision encoder to the CPU (`vision=cpu`) **did not improve performance** for UD-Q4_K_XL and actually slightly degraded it at 256K (39.30 vs 42.70 tok/s). This is likely because the 111 GB model footprint leaves the expert cache severely VRAM-starved regardless of the ~1.5 GB saved from the vision encoder. However, performance remains remarkably stable at ~35-40 tok/s across all contexts up to 512K.

## Sweep configuration

```
CONTEXTS         = 131072 262144 393216 524288
PARALLEL_VALUES  = 1 2 4
VISION_VALUES    = cpu / off / on
KV_VALUES        = int8 q4_0 k8v4
PREFILL_VALUES   = 32768 65536 auto
KV_RESIDENT      = 32768 65536
SPEC             = 4
ADAPT_DECAY      = 0.97
ADAPT_SWAPS      = 160
```

## Results — Best config per context

| Context | Config (kv, prefill, kvr, vision) | TTFT | Decode | run_id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | q4_0, 32768, 32768, cpu | 56.9 s | **40.20 tok/s** | 1-1-c-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 256K | q4_0, 32768, 32768, off | 124.1 s | **42.70 tok/s** | 2-1-n-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 384K | k8v4, auto, 32768, off | 303.2 s | **38.92 tok/s** | 3-1-n-k-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K | int8, auto, 32768, off | 417.3 s | **37.50 tok/s** | 4-1-n-i-a-32-4-97-160 |

## Vision Mode Impact (The anomaly)

While `vision=cpu` helped Swift, it slightly hurts Q4_K_XL due to the sheer size of the model's experts.

| Context | Best Config (kv, prefill) | vision=off | vision=cpu | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | q4_0, 32768 | 38.80 | **40.20** | +3.6% |
| 256K | int8, 32768 | **42.70** *(q4_0)* | 39.30 | -8.0% |
| 384K | q4_0, 65536 | **38.65** | 36.39 | -5.8% |
| 512K | q4_0, 32768 | **37.23** | 36.66 | -1.5% |

*Note: The VRAM savings from the CPU encoder are not enough to unlock a new tier of expert caching for a 111 GB model on a 24 GB GPU.*

## Key findings

1. **~42 tok/s peak** — Q4_K_XL is roughly half the decode speed of Swift IQ3_S at equivalent context. Expected: more bits per expert, more RAM pressure.
2. **256K is the sweet spot**, but performance is essentially flat (37–43 tok/s) from 128K to 512K.
3. **KV type shifts by context**: 
   - 128K–256K: `q4_0` (best balance of memory and speed).
   - 384K+: `k8v4` or `int8` (better streaming when VRAM is tight).
4. **prefill=32768** wins at 128K–256K; `auto` wins at 384K–512K.
5. **Parallelism hurts badly** — `batch=2` drops speed by ~20-30%, and `batch=4` by up to 45% (e.g., 42.70 down to 24.19 at 256K).
6. **Quality Check needed**: Unlike Swift, we do not have NIAH quality results for Unsloth. This should be added to verify if Q4_K_XL's higher precision justifies the ~50% speed penalty.

## Recommended production configs

| Use case | Config |
|---|---|
| Chat (128K) | `kv=q4_0, prefill=32768, kvr=32768, vision=cpu` |
| Long analysis (256K) | `kv=q4_0, prefill=32768, kvr=32768, vision=off` |
| Document QA (512K) | `kv=int8, prefill=auto, kvr=32768, vision=off` |

### Representative Results & Speed Degradation Analysis (Q4_K_XL)

| Scenario / Purpose | Date | Context | KV / Prefill / KVR | TTFT (s) | Decode (tok/s) | run_id |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **128K - Best CPU Vision** | Oct 19 | 131,072 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 56.9 | **40.20** | 1-1-c-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 128K - Best OFF Vision | Oct 19 | 131,072 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 57.9 | 38.80 | 1-1-n-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 128K - Best ON Vision | Oct 17 | 131,072 | `int8` / `auto` / `32768` | 93.3 | 35.79 | 1-1-n-i-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 128K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 17 | 131,072 | `int8` / `32768` / `32768` | 57.9 | 28.89 | 1-2-n-i-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 128K - Batch 4 Penalty | Oct 17 | 131,072 | `k8v4` / `32768` / `32768` | 69.8 | 22.64 | 1-4-n-k-32-32-4-97-160 |
| **256K - Absolute Peak (OFF)** | Oct 17 | 262,144 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 124.1 | **42.70** | 2-1-n-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Best CPU Vision | Oct 19 | 262,144 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 110.5 | 39.30 | 2-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K - CPU Vision (`q4_0`) | Oct 19 | 262,144 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 124.8 | 38.92 | 2-1-c-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Best ON Vision | Oct 17 | 262,144 | `int8` / `32768` / `32768` | 109.9 | 38.23 | 2-1-y-i-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 17 | 262,144 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `65536` | 140.4 | 34.49 | 2-2-n-q-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Batch 4 Penalty | Oct 17 | 262,144 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 145.6 | 24.19 | 2-4-n-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| **384K - Best OFF Vision** | Oct 18 | 393,216 | `k8v4` / `auto` / `32768` | 303.2 | **38.92** | 3-1-n-k-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 384K - Best CPU Vision | Oct 19 | 393,216 | `q4_0` / `65536` / `65536` | 193.2 | 36.39 | 3-1-c-q-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 384K - CPU Vision (`q4_0`) | Oct 19 | 393,216 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `65536` | 182.4 | 36.07 | 3-1-c-q-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 384K - Best ON Vision | Oct 18 | 393,216 | `k8v4` / `32768` / `32768` | 213.1 | 34.68 | 3-1-y-k-32-32-4-97-160 |
| **512K - Best OFF Vision** | Oct 18 | 524,288 | `int8` / `auto` / `32768` | 417.3 | **37.50** | 4-1-n-i-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K - Best CPU Vision | Oct 19 | 524,288 | `q4_0` / `65536` / `32768` | 262.4 | 36.66 | 4-1-c-q-64-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K - CPU Vision (`q4_0`) | Oct 19 | 524,288 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `32768` | 283.4 | 36.05 | 4-1-c-q-32-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K - Best ON Vision | Oct 18 | 524,288 | `q4_0` / `auto` / `32768` | 424.8 | 35.89 | 4-1-y-q-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 18 | 524,288 | `int8` / `auto` / `65536` | 519.6 | 24.62 | 4-1-n-q-a-64-4-97-160 |

#### Key Takeaways from Representative Data (Q4_K_XL):
*   **Vision CPU vs OFF Anomaly:** Unlike Swift IQ3_S, `vision=cpu` does *not* yield a massive speedup for this model. The 111 GB footprint means experts are starved for VRAM regardless. At 256K, `vision=off` actually wins (42.70 vs 38.92 tok/s).
*   **Severe Batch Penalties:** Adding parallel slots destroys throughput. At 256K, `batch=4` slashes decode speed by almost half (42.70 down to 24.19 tok/s).
*   **KV Cache Scaling:** `q4_0` is optimal for 128K-256K. At 384K+, `k8v4` and `int8` take over, likely due to more efficient streaming when VRAM is pushed to the absolute limit.

issues.title: [GUI] Desktop install: MTP download shows no progress ("0.0 / 0.0 GB"), and cancelling leaves mtp_fetch.py running as an orphan
issues.author: bext1998
issues.body:
> **Note:** This issue was identified and analyzed with AI assistance (Claude). The root-cause observations below were reviewed by the reporter, but the AI-assisted analysis may contain inaccuracies, so please verify against logs before acting on it.

**Versions:** Strata Desktop 0.2.0-beta, Control/Engine 0.1.45.3 (windows-x86_64-cuda13), Windows 11 26300, RTX 3060 12 GB
**Model:** Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS, `--data-dir G:\StrataLLM`

**Steps**
1. Install Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS from the Desktop app. Model download and iq_pack finish (`[ok] model prepared`).
2. Step 6 runs `tools/mtp_fetch.py fetch`. The app shows "Preparing your model for Strata… IQ2_XS: 0.0 / 0.0 GB" with no progress for the ~5 GB MTP download.
3. Assuming it is stuck, cancel (or close the app), then retry.

**Actual**
- `native-jobs.json` reports the model part as `done_gb:0,total_gb:0` for the whole MTP download.
- After cancel, setup.py exits 1 (`strata-mcp: setup ended with exit code 1`), but its child `mtp_fetch.py` keeps writing. setup.log shows progress lines after the exit line, and `mtp-manifest.json` was written 4 minutes after the job was marked failed.
- On retry, a new mtp_fetch appends to the same tensor file while the orphan is still running. The orphan then dies with
  `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor` at `mtp_fetch.py:285/288` (`open(path, "ab")` / `f.write`).
- The job never reaches step 7, so no `strata-*.json` run config is written and Settings → Storage shows "No downloaded models" even though all GGUF shards are verified.

**Expected**
- MTP download progress is shown (it already prints per-tensor % to stderr).
- Cancel ends the whole process tree (`proc_kill_tree` uses `taskkill /T /F`, yet the grandchild survived here), or mtp_fetch holds a lock so two instances cannot append to the same file.
- Storage indicates "downloaded, preparation incomplete" instead of "No downloaded models".

**Workaround:** Run the install again without cancelling. Shards (`.done`) and the pack are skipped, and the MTP tensors pass `mtp_fetch.py verify`.

issues.title: [Engine] 0.1.45 and 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3): decode −10% and prefill −20% on A100 40GB (sm_80); 0.1.44.1 unaffected
issues.author: t-sm0
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine] (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (engine built from source inside Docker per release tag).

### What happened

On an A100 40 GB (sm_80), **0.1.45 loses ~10 % decode and ~20 % prefill against 0.1.44.1, and 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3) inherits the regression unchanged** — same args, same pack, fresh engine per arm. 0.2.0's new sm_86/sm_60 decode tables (+10–14 % there) again skip sm_80.

Identical fixed prompts per arm, one request at a time, engine restarted per arm, decode read from the engine's own `timings.predicted_per_second`:

- **tetris probe**: fixed prompt, seed 42, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, max_tokens 16384 (every arm length-caps at 16384, so wall time is directly comparable).
- **sand probe**: same envelope with a second fixed prompt, also 16384-token runs.
- **prefill**: fixed ~15.1k-token prompt (repeated pattern with a fresh `[run i]` prefix so nothing is cached), `max_tokens 8`, temp 0, `cache_n = 0`, median of 2 runs, tok/s from `timings.prompt_per_second`.

| engine | tetris decode (t/s) | sand decode (t/s) | prefill 15.1k (t/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.1.43.1 | 111.4 | 106.3 | 3,043 |
| 0.1.44.1 (reference) | 111.3 | 104.9 | 3,056 |
| 0.1.45 | 100.8 (−9 %) | 94.2 (−10 %) | 2,436 (−20 %) |
| 0.2.0-beta / 0.1.45.3 | 100.2 (−10 %) | 71.2 (−32 %) | 2,434 (−20 %) |

In the beta arm the sand run's output also broke format (no fenced HTML, ~10 KB vs the usual ~31 KB) — noted in passing, not measured systematically.

**Config difference, ruled out as the cause**: the 0.1.4x arms carry the experimental-speed-projection control vector; the 0.2.0-beta arm cannot (the cvec launch flags were renamed/removed in 0.1.45.3 — the launch dies with `unknown argument: project` on `--cvec-mode project`). ESP measured ±0 % decode in an earlier A/B on this box.

**Suspects**

1. The MMVQ/IL shared table: per #1842, `native_mmvq_il_rows_for` has only a `kIlRows_70` entry; every sm_80+ card inherits `kIlRowsShared`, measured on an RTX 3060 (sm_86) and RTX 5070 (sm_120). The A100 uses the same guess — same class of gap as the 0.2.0 sm_86/sm_60 tables that skip sm_80.
2. The 45-line decode kernel defaults (route-tail-skip is already the 44.1 default, so the delta vs 44.1 is something newer).
3. The prefill path — −20 % with identical args points at the prompt side too. #3204's `f3be9743` warm-up regression is HIP-only; a CUDA-side equivalent or the prefill chunk-path changes are candidates.

**Ruled out on our side**: CUDA arch is explicitly 80 in all four builds (no other GPU in the box); identical pack, args, expert-cache size (14322 slots / 27.2 GiB) and VRAM budget across arms; ESP (±0 %); no storage-tier involvement (everything resident, `ple-io ram`).

**Questions**

1. Was sm_80 in the identity/perf test set for the 0.1.45 kernel changes? (The release notes list sm_60/sm_86/gfx1201/Intel/M4 — no Ampere.)
2. Which no-rebuild switches should we A/B on 0.2.0-beta to localize it — `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_ROWS=…`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, prefill switches? Happy to run any set on this box and report numbers; all four images stay tagged, and this box stays on 0.1.44.1 meanwhile.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Build each tag with `docker build --build-arg CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80` (the image's engine args below otherwise identical across arms).
2. Serve: `--pack <packs>/iq3_s --native <models>/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf <models>/…-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile <data>/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <data>/mtp/rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --ple-io ram --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700`.
3. Run the tetris and sand probes (envelope above), then the 15.1k prefill twice; read decode/prefill tok/s from the engine timings. Compare against the same probes on 0.1.44.1.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally (all four arms, three probes each, fresh engine per arm).

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta (`3d1fb48`, engine 0.1.45.3) · 0.1.45 (`c4074a70`) · 0.1.44.1 (`b3e02db`) · 0.1.43.1 (`2d70b1bf`) — all built from source.

### Graphics card, memory and system

NVIDIA A100-PCIE 40 GB (sm_80, driver 615.78.08) · 125 GB RAM · i5-11600K (6C/12T, AVX2 only) · Arch Linux.

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (native pack + 2 GGUF shards, PLE in RAM, MTP drafter) · 262K context · int8 KV · pictures on · expert cache 14322 slots / 27.2 GiB · args in the repro block above.

### Logs

Per-arm probe numbers are in the table above; the engine's per-request `timings.predicted_per_second` / `prompt_per_second` values are the source of every cell. Raw per-request JSON for all arms available — say the word and I will attach them as a gist.
