issues.body:
Is there a technical reason not to support STRATA's mechanism of clever expert memory-management to run on CPU + RAM + NVME only?

1. Only CPU, RAM and NVMe means less complexity. Fewer moving parts.

2. CPU only means: longer time for token generation - more time to pre-fetching upcoming experts from NVME to RAM.

Especially with smaller models like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. They often fit easily into RAM but if you want super long context, a Strata-Like reduction of resident RAM would help A LOT!!

issues.title: [Engine] Linux: "exit code -9" with no OOM when started from a PipeWire desktop without rtkit (RLIMIT_RTTIME hard limit 0)
issues.author: vthomasino
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

The engine sometimes dies at load (while it builds the RAM copy) or during a request:

```
[strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -9). The usual cause is running out of RAM: Linux then ends the biggest program (check: sudo dmesg | grep -i -E 'killed process|out of memory'); ...
```

It was never RAM. There was no OOM kill in dmesg, `oom_kill` in /proc/vmstat did not move, systemd-oomd logged nothing, and auditd rules on kill/tkill/pidfd_send_signal saw no process send the signal. Since #215 the RAM hint only shows when the OS killed the engine; here the kernel did kill it, but for a different reason.

**Cause, as far as I traced it**

1. The engine inherits `RLIMIT_RTTIME` = **0 / 0** (soft / hard) from the shell. Every terminal on this desktop has it (`ulimit -R` prints 0, and `/proc/<pid>/limits` shows 0/0 for bash and pi).
2. It comes from PipeWire's client module (`libpipewire-module-rt`). With rtkit not installed, the desktop portal answers for it, and the module lowers the limit: `mod.rt: clamping rt.time.soft from 18446744073709551615 to 0 because of RTKit` (PipeWire 1.6.8, xdg-desktop-portal 1.22.1). The desktop shell is a PipeWire client, so everything started from it inherits 0/0. With `rtkit.enabled = false` and `rtportal.enabled = false` in a copy of client.conf, a client keeps `unlimited`; `rlimits.enabled = false` alone does not change it.
3. With a hard limit of 0, the kernel's `check_thread_timers()` (kernel/time/posix-cpu-timers.c) sends SIGKILL as soon as it checks a thread with an armed per-thread CPU timer: `rt.timeout` is 0 for a normal thread, and `0 >= 0` passes. The thread does not need to be real-time. A tracefs `signal:signal_generate` trace caught one engine death: `sig=9 errno=0 code=128 comm=strata`, sent from inside the process by `posix_cpu_timers_work <- task_work_run <- exit_to_user_mode_loop`, not by another process.
4. A 15-line test program reproduces it outside Strata (`rttime-thread-timer.c` in the gist below). It calls `timer_create(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)` with `SIGEV_SIGNAL`, arms 100 ms and spins for 2 s. From this shell it is killed with signal 9 (exit 137); under `systemd-run --user` (unlimited) it exits 0. With `SIGEV_NONE` it survives.

**Not found yet:** which code in the engine process arms the per-thread CPU timer. Strata's sources do not call `timer_create`. Among the engine's loaded libraries, only libc imports it. In one traced session (load plus a 15K-token prompt), no engine thread called `timer_create` or `timer_settime`, and the engine survived. The deaths are intermittent: 4 in about 24 hours with UD-Q6_K_XL (during a 155K-token prefill, after a short reply, at load, and on a 16K-token prompt). `ulimit -r` is 0 too, so no thread can switch to SCHED_FIFO, and 900 samples of every thread's scheduling class during a 16K prefill showed none real-time. I have a trace of timer_create/timer_settime with user stacks running, and will add the caller here when it shows up.

**Workaround used here:** start the server as a systemd user service, which takes the user manager's limits (unlimited) instead of the shell's. No -9 since (about 4 hours of use and A/B runs so far).

```
systemd-run --user --collect --unit=strata -p LimitRTTIME=infinity -- .venv/bin/python serve/server.py ...
```

Installing rtkit should also work (it answers 200 ms instead of 0). I did not test that.

**Suggestion:** on Linux, when the engine ends with -9, check `resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_RTTIME)` in `serve/server.py` before printing the RAM hint. If the hard limit is finite, say so and name the fix (rtkit, or start Strata outside the desktop session's limits). A warning at start-up in the same case would catch it before the first crash. When the limit is unlimited, neither changes anything. I can send this as a small PR if it is wanted.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. On a PipeWire desktop without rtkit, open a terminal and check `ulimit -R` (0 here).
2. Build and run `rttime-thread-timer.c` from https://gist.github.com/vthomasino/aef6f8e2413733cbe149a91178e889d8 : it is killed with signal 9. Run it again with `systemd-run --user --wait`: it exits 0.
3. The engine itself dies only now and then; it took long UD-Q6_K_XL sessions to see it (4 times in about 24 hours).

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (tag v0.2.0-beta, b73dbce3); the deaths were on 0.1.45, the limit and the workaround are the same on 0.2.0-beta

### Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 5090 Laptop 24 GB (driver 610.57.04) · 62 GB RAM · Core Ultra 9 275HX · Linux 7.2.5 (Omarchy/Arch, Hyprland), PipeWire 1.6.8, no rtkit

### Model, size and settings

unsloth UD-Q6_K_XL · 256K context · pictures on · `--resident-budget-gib 38`

### Logs

Kernel stack of the kill (tracefs, signal:signal_generate with stacktrace):

```
strata-371087  [006] dN.1. 307833.524553: signal_generate: sig=9 errno=0 code=128 comm=strata pid=371087 grp=1 res=0
 => trace_event_raw_event_signal_generate
 => __send_signal_locked
 => send_signal_locked
 => posix_cpu_timers_work
 => task_work_run
 => exit_to_user_mode_loop
 => do_syscall_64
 => entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe
```

issues.title: [Engine] Linux file tier: the room rule still picks the file cache on 0.2.0-beta, 2x slower prefill and 3-4x slower decode than unbuffered reads
issues.author: vthomasino
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

On 0.2.0-beta, with a model whose file tier is much larger than the free RAM, the automatic choice (`file_tier_unbuffered`, the #1194 room rule) reads the experts through the page cache. On this machine that path reads prompts at about half the speed of `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1` and decodes at a third to a quarter of its speed, and the OS reads up to 3x the expert bytes from the drive. #1682 and #2344 reported this on 0.1.4x (#2344: +43% prefill unbuffered on an RTX 4070 SUPER with 32 GB). Both were closed in the 0.2.0 reset, so this is the re-test on 0.2.0-beta.

What the engine chose by default:

```
strata generate: the file tier reads through the file cache (46.2 GiB available, 38.0 GiB of it still to be taken by the RAM copy, 63.7 GiB of experts read from the files: the file cache can keep the ones that come back)
strata generate: the file tier reads through the file cache (re-checked with the RAM copy built (38.00 GiB): 6.4 GiB available, 0.0 GiB of it still to be taken by the RAM copy, 63.7 GiB of experts read from the files: the file cache can keep the ones that come back)
```

**Results**, round 1 / round 2 (each arm a fresh server, page cache dropped before it, round 2 in reversed arm order; 2026-10-19 12:03-12:19):

| arm | prefill ~4.5K tok/s | decode tok/s | prefill ~13K tok/s | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default (file cache) | 184.9 / 179.0 | 5.0 / 6.0 | 274.4 / 258.4 | 3.4 / 5.8 |
| `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1` | 372.8 / 365.6 | 19.2 / 19.2 | 601.0 / 622.8 | 18.3 / 19.1 |

Per-request lines from the engine log:

- default: `the OS read 180282.2 MB from storage (222370 major faults) for 60804.5 MB of expert reads; page cache held 38535.4 MB at the read` (round 2: `91715.3 MB ... (68704 major faults) for 31969.8 MB`). Every logged request had 10,615 to 222,370 major faults.
- unbuffered: the OS read matches the expert reads within 0.5%, for example `124989.5 MB ... (0 major faults) for 124529.8 MB`, with 0 to 3 major faults per request.

**Expected:** with 6 GiB free after the RAM copy and a 63.7 GiB read set, the cache holds about a tenth of what is read. #1194 measured the cache winning when it holds a twentieth or more of a skewed read set; on this drive and model it loses at about a tenth. (The opposite case, #577 on a 96 GB PC where the cache holds the whole read set, should keep the cache.)

**A possible fix, offered, not assumed.** I carry a local, opt-in check, `STRATA_FILE_TIER_PROBE=1`. It runs only where the room rule picks the cache but the cache cannot hold the whole read set. It times the drive's direct reads (depth 8) and cached-path reads (depth 3) once at load, then reads unbuffered when the cache holds under 30% of the read set, or 30-50% with direct reads at least 1.5x faster. Here it logged `the cache holds 13% of the read set, direct reads 8.18 GB/s at depth 8, cached-path reads 4.93 GB/s at depth 3 (1.66x)`, chose unbuffered, and measured:

| arm | prefill ~4.5K | decode | prefill ~13K | decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `STRATA_FILE_TIER_PROBE=1` | 377.7 / 366.4 | 20.9 / 17.8 | 605.3 / 573.8 | 15.0 / 17.5 |

The thresholds come from runs on this one machine with UD-Q4_K_XL and UD-Q6_K_XL, unthrottled and with the drive capped by systemd's `IOReadBandwidthMax` down to 250 MB/s (on 0.1.45). If it is wanted, I can open it as a draft PR. It builds for CUDA; I have no HIP or SYCL toolkit, so those builds are not run. If a different rule fits better, the numbers are yours to use.

**Not tested:** AMD/HIP, Windows, ext4, a slower drive on 0.2.0 (the throttled runs were on 0.1.45), a page cache warm from an earlier run.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Start UD-Q6_K_XL from source with `--resident-budget-gib 38` on a 62 GB PC, with no file-tier variable set. The start log says `the file tier reads through the file cache`.
2. Send a fresh ~4.5K-token prompt and then a fresh ~13K-token prompt, 256 output tokens each.
3. Repeat with `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1`.

The script, the config and the raw output of both rounds: https://gist.github.com/vthomasino/aef6f8e2413733cbe149a91178e889d8

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 · tag v0.2.0-beta (b73dbce3) plus one local commit of opt-in code (STRATA_FILE_TIER_PROBE, STRATA_FILL_SPANS, a debug trace), not active in the default and unbuffered arms

### Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 5090 Laptop 24 GB (driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.2) · 62 GB RAM · Core Ultra 9 275HX · Samsung 9100 PRO 2 TB PCIe 5.0, btrfs · Linux 7.2.5 (Omarchy/Arch)

### Model, size and settings

unsloth UD-Q6_K_XL (158 GB GGUF read in place) · 256K context · pictures on · `--resident-budget-gib 38 --kv int8 --kv-resident 131072 --spec 4 --mtp --pool-workers 15 --vram-reserve-mib 1700`, env `STRATA_MMQ_KQ=1 STRATA_HC_Q8=1`

### Logs

The engine's choice and per-request lines for every arm are in `ab-q6-020.out` in the gist above.

issues.title: [Other] FP4-Local setup dies at step 6: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'transformers'
issues.author: Yunado
issues.body:
**Area**: `[Other]` (setup.py, the source installer)

**Desktop app, Terminal or source install**: source install (git clone, SETUP.bat) on Windows

**What happened**
Choosing the NVIDIA FP4-Local (QAD) model in SETUP.bat on a Python env that lacks the converter's packages dies at step 6. `tools/nvfp4_local_pack.py prepare` converts the n-gram table (~20 minutes of the 102 GB checkpoint), then reaches the dense weights, where `install()` imports llama.cpp's converter (`third_party/llama.cpp/conversion/base.py`: `from transformers import AutoConfig`) and the whole prepare exits with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'transformers'`. `setup.py`'s package step only installs `requirements.txt`'s eight runtime packages; torch, transformers and safetensors appear nowhere in it. The user must find and install the three packages by hand and re-run.

**Smallest steps or command that reproduces it**
1. fresh clone (or any clone whose `.venv` lacks torch/transformers; check with `.venv\Scripts\python -m pip list`)
2. `SETUP.bat`, pick Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, pick the NVFP4 FP4-Local (NVIDIA QAD) model
3. step 6 prints the PLE shard progress, then the traceback above, exit 1

**Reproduction status**: reproduced on this PC (0.1.45, full timestamped log; the first prepare attempt of 2026-10-19). Static check on e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta-12): `requirements.txt` and `setup.py` still do not mention torch/transformers, so the fresh-env path still dies.

**Environment**: Strata source install @ 477ac13c (v0.1.45), engine package 0.1.45, Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, Python 3.12.0 venv, RTX 5090 + RTX 3070, 96 GB RAM, model `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` revision b9ce18a

**Workaround that worked here**: `.venv` `pip install torch transformers safetensors`, re-run SETUP: the prepare completed (dense.gguf 6.0 GB, experts.bin 63.28 GiB, ple-nvfp4.gguf 320001536 x 90 B marked `nvfp4x16`, mtp/rt) and the model serves.

**Fix**: the linked pull request installs a pinned `requirements-nvfp4-local.txt` through the existing `pip_install` immediately before a prepare that actually runs, and makes the tool name the missing package when it is run by hand.

issues.title: [Engine] SYCL AOT build for bmg-g31 fails on 0.2.0-beta with IGC 2.36.3 (ICE in the int8 prompt-expert kernels); fine with the current base image
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

The SYCL AOT build for the Arc Pro B70 (`AOT=bmg-g31`) of 0.2.0-beta fails at the final `strata` link when the device compiler in the build image is IGC 2.36.3 (Compute Runtime / ocloc 26.22.38646.4). ocloc reports `IGC: Internal Compiler Error: Floating point exception` / `Build failed with error code: -11` on 77 device images, then `icpx: error: gen compiler command failed with exit code 245`. Every failing image is one of the new int8 prompt-expert kernels in `strata::prefill::i8` (`TagGu`, `TagDn`, `TagGuW`, `TagDnW`, `SwigluTag`, `QuantTag`; `sycl/src/prefill/esimd_moe.dp.cpp`). It is deterministic: the same 77 images fail on every run, and re-running ocloc on one saved image fails 4 of 4 times. The same images compile with the ocloc in the current base image (`llama-sycl-b70:stable`: ocloc 26.35.39758.10, IGC 2.41.5): 12 of 12 that I tried passed, and the whole AOT build then links.

How a user ends up with the old compiler: docs/INTEL.md says to run `docker build -t strata-sycl-dev sycl/tools` again only when `sycl/tools/Dockerfile` changes. `FROM ...llama-sycl-b70:stable` is a moving tag, though, and `docker build` reuses a locally cached base unless it gets `--pull`. A `strata-sycl-dev` image built a few weeks ago can therefore still carry an older IGC. (Ours was IGC 2.36.3 because we had swapped in the host driver's packages, so our exact image is not the stock one; I have not tested which older stock bases are affected.)

issues.title: [Engine] Current GGML override omits precision arguments in the trellis MMQ overlay
issues.author: Tsury
issues.body:
Using a current upstream GGML through `STRATA_GGML_DIR`, the new trellis MMQ overlay still emits calls from the older precision API. The CUDA build fails before any model starts.

Environment: Strata `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (engine 0.1.45.3), upstream llama.cpp `0ce8cd11416c8840498e6701bcbe39ad4b858c2b` (b11739), Linux, CUDA 13.3, SM120.

This was reproduced in a maintained build with existing adapters for the other current-GGML MMQ callers. It is an override-compatibility report, not a claim that Strata's pinned `3cf03257` default is broken. No weights are required to reach the compile error.

The remaining callers are in `cmake/strata_ggml_tq_overlay.cmake` and `third_party/ggml-tq/tq-mmq-tiles.cuh`:

- Generated DP4A and MMA write-back callbacks omit `prec_src1`.
- The generated `ggml_cuda_mmq_vec_dot_q8_0_16_q8_1_mma` callback omits `prec_src1`.
- The trellis loader calls `ggml_cuda_mmq_get_nthreads`, `ggml_cuda_mmq_get_I`, and `ggml_cuda_mmq_get_sram_stride` without the new precision argument. The current upstream IQ2_XS loader uses `GGML_PREC_Q8` for these three calls.

Representative errors:

```text
mmq.cuh: error: no instance of constructor ggml_cuda_mmq_util_funcs matches the argument list
  argument types are: (int, <unknown-type>, <unknown-type>, <unknown-type>)
tq-mmq-tiles.cuh: error: too few arguments in function call
  ggml_cuda_mmq_get_nthreads(type, J, fallback)
```

Locally, passing `prec_src1` to the three generated callbacks and `GGML_PREC_Q8` to the three loader helpers, alongside the existing adapters, lets the current-GGML text-engine target build. All failed attempts were retained. Both text and vision builds now complete. Selected native text, image-history recovery, Pi/Hermes image/tool writes, all eight tool-sanity cases, and 122K-input dispersed retrieval pass on this maintained SM120 build. These are brief checks; the selected model does not use trellis weights. HIP/SYCL builds, trellis inference, and compatibility with the pinned GGML remain untested. No performance claim follows.

A useful upstream fix could adapt the overlay to the actual GGML signature, or reject an incompatible override clearly during configuration. The current text anchors accept this source but do not catch the later signature mismatch.

issues.title: [GUI] Control Vector arguments are removed when loading a model
issues.author: joneric-scratch
issues.body:
## Description

I'm experiencing an issue with **Control Vector arguments in the new Strata Desktop GUI**.

I use **Expert Mode** and its **JSON editor** to manually add the Control Vector parameters directly inside the existing `"args": [...]` array of my model configuration.

The JSON syntax is valid, and the arguments are placed in the correct section.

However, every time I click **Load Model**, Strata regenerates the JSON configuration and removes the Control Vector arguments.

**Other model settings appear to persist correctly. The issue seems specific to Control Vector arguments.**

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Strata Desktop.
2. Select an installed model.
3. Switch to **Expert Mode**.
4. Open the **JSON editor**.
5. Add the following arguments inside the existing `"args": [...]` array:

```json
"--control-vector-scaled",
"C:\\path\\to\\control-vector.gguf:1.0",
"--control-vector-layer-range",
"4",
"44",
"--cvec-mode",
"project",
"--cvec-dir",
"per-layer"
```

6. Save the JSON configuration.
7. Click **Load Model**.
8. Reopen the JSON configuration.

## Actual behavior

The configuration is regenerated, and the Control Vector arguments disappear from the `"args"` array.

Other model parameters appear to be preserved.

Consequently, the model starts without the requested Control Vector configuration.

## Expected behavior

Control Vector arguments entered through **Expert Mode > JSON** should be preserved when loading or reloading a model.

Since the engine already supports these arguments, I would expect the Desktop GUI to retain them in the generated configuration.

## Suggested improvement

Ideally, the Desktop GUI should either:

- Preserve Control Vector arguments entered through Expert Mode.
- Provide dedicated Control Vector settings in the advanced model configuration.

## Environment

- **Strata Desktop:** 0.2.0-beta
- **Engine:** 0.1.45.3
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 5080, 16 GB VRAM
- **RAM:** 64 GB

## Additional information

The same Control Vector arguments worked with my previous standalone Strata installation.

I would prefer to keep using the new Desktop GUI rather than switching to the CLI/TUI.

Is this the intended behavior of Expert Mode, or should Control Vector arguments be preserved when the GUI regenerates the model configuration?

Thanks for your work on Strata <3 !

issues.title: [Engine] Forced 1536 MiB VRAM reserve overwrites user config on 0.2.0-beta, dropping decode speed from 80 to 50 tok/s
issues.author: mesosomeso
issues.body:
Problem:
On Strata 0.2.0-beta (Windows 11), the engine/launcher forcibly resets and overwrites `--vram-reserve-mib` to `1536` during model loading, ignoring user configuration (`0` or lower values). On a dedicated compute GPU (where the display is driven by the CPU iGPU), this unnecessary 1.5 GB VRAM reserve truncates the expert cache and drops decode throughput by ~37%.

Environment:
- Strata version: 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3)
- OS: Windows 11
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 7700 (Display connected to motherboard; iGPU handles all desktop rendering & DWM)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 12GB (Dedicated compute GPU, 0% display overhead)
- RAM: 64 GB DDR5
- Model: `swift1.5-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-IQ3_S`
- Relevant settings: `--vram-reserve-mib 0`, Vision disabled

Reproduce:
1. Configure `swift1.5-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-IQ3_S` on Windows 11.
2. In the model config JSON (`strata-*.json`), explicitly set `--vram-reserve-mib 0` (or `256` / `512`) to maximize VRAM expert cache, and ensure vision is disabled.
3. Launch the model via `strata launch` or the Strata 0.2.0 app.
4. Check the startup log and the JSON configuration during/after loading.

Expected:
The explicit `--vram-reserve-mib 0` setting is respected and kept without being overwritten, allowing the entire 12 GB VRAM to be utilized for the expert cache (achieving ~80 tok/s as in 0.1.45).

Actual:
During model loading, the reserve is forcibly recalculated/overwritten to `--vram-reserve-mib 1536`. 1.5 GB of VRAM is permanently locked away, reducing expert cache capacity and dropping decode speed from ~80 tok/s down to ~50 tok/s. Disabling vision does not reclaim this memory.

Evidence:
- Strata 0.1.45 (full VRAM utilized for expert cache): ~80 tok/s decode
- Strata 0.2.0-beta (1536 MiB forced reserve): ~50 tok/s decode (~37% regression)
- Config JSON is modified back to 1536 upon launch.

Reproduction status:
reproduced locally

issues.author: wycoconut
issues.body: GeForce RTX 5060 Ti · 16 GB graphics Memory · 56 GB RAM Windows 11 My installation folder is in E:\Strata\Strata-Data. **Problem** Stuck at "Setup step 6/7: preparing the model for Strata" Error Message : The model could not be installed. command failed (exit 1): python.exe. **Things I tried** Checked powershell command python.exe is working. Checked powershell command nvidia-smi shows CUDA UMD 13.3. Run the powershell as administrator and run the `strata launch` again, still error. Suspect it is something to do with downloading the mtp tensor files. It seems to timeout for a reason. **Workaround** I just keep pressing r to retry the download a few times, and I finally made it to the Tuning Step. **Some clues for long term solution / fix** Prior to version 0.2.0, I have encountered this issue where in the same stage, it was trying to download the tensors from huggingface.co, but timeout. issues.title: [Engine] 0.2.0-beta: prompt reading ~25% slower on a two-GPU HIP layer split (gfx1151 + gfx1201) since f3be9743; STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0 restores it
issues.author: jiayeZhu
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

On a layer split across a Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Strix Halo iGPU) and a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), 0.2.0-beta reads
long prompts about 25% slower than 0.1.45: 1,250 against 1,710 tok/s at 64K. That is about the speed of the 8060S
alone, so the second GPU stops helping. I expected 0.1.45's speed.

A `git bisect` between v0.1.45 and v0.2.0-beta lands on **f3be9743**, "prefill: warm the first BF16 and FP16 hipBLAS
products on a thread at start (STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0 skips)". Setting **`STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0`** on 0.2.0-beta brings
prompt reading back to 0.1.45's speed. Decode is not affected.

The 8060S alone (R9700 hidden with `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) is not affected either: 0.1.45 and 0.2.0-beta both read 64K
at about 1,220-1,230 tok/s there. So this looks specific to the multi-GPU split.

Prompt reading in tok/s, two runs each, one request at a time:

| Version (two-GPU split) | 64K | 128K | 211K | Decode (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1.43.1 | 1,694 / 1,682 | 1,604 / 1,563 | 1,484 / 1,463 | 45-52 |
| 0.1.45 | 1,718 / 1,705 | | | 47-50 |
| 0.2.0-beta | 1,262 / 1,244 | 1,215 / 1,208 | 1,162 / 1,163 | 44-50 |
| 0.2.0-beta + `STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0` | 1,720 / 1,709 | 1,658 / 1,618 | 1,559 / 1,548 | 43-51 |

With the warm-up off, 0.2.0-beta is a little faster than 0.1.43.1 at 128K and 211K (+4-5%). A second 64K pair on the
same engine, with prompts it had not seen, read at 1,709 / 1,677.

Ruled out on 0.2.0-beta:

- **The new Linux file-tier defaults.** With `STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP=0 STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=0 STRATA_IO_PF_GATE=0`, 64K
  averaged 1,261 tok/s against 1,244 with them on (two fresh engines each).
- **The known "R9700 + MTP: about half of fresh engines read 10-23% slower" limit.** Six fresh 0.2.0-beta engines all
  read 64K at 1,193-1,275 tok/s, so the drop is not random from engine to engine.

Workaround: set `STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0`. The only cost is the one-time hipBLAS load (1-2.5 s) on the first request.

Not tested:

- Windows.
- Other two-GPU combinations (two gfx12 cards, or NVIDIA).
- Whether the slowdown depends on the order of the GPUs (here the 8060S is GPU 0).

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Build one engine for both GPUs, out of tree:
   `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1151;gfx1201"`, HIP flags
   `-DSTRATA_W_LB=8`, ggml at the pinned 3cf03257.
2. Start `serve/server.py` with a two-GPU layer split: 8060S first, `layer_split` 30 (layers 0-29 on the 8060S, 30-47 on
   the R9700), 4 slots. The engine arguments:

   ```
   --pack <packs>/unsloth-ud-iq4_xs --native <models>/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf
   --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <mtp>/rt
   --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --mmap-experts --mtp-window 8192 --no-prefill-borrow
   --prefill 4096 --conversation-cache-mib 24576 --conversation-cache-slots 24 --trim-stage-weights
   --batch-groups 1 --batch-mtp --vision
   ```

   The environment:

   ```
   STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1151-hipblaslt-100401.txt
   STRATA_PF_FUSED=1  STRATA_PF_GEMM=1  STRATA_PA_FAST=1  STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1
   STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1  STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1  STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=64
   ```

   The experts are 100% resident: the engine reports "layer split: 100% of the experts resident".
3. Send a 16K warm-up request, then a 64K prompt: Python standard-library source cut to 64K tokens, plus a short question.
   Temperature 0, 600 tokens out, one request at a time.
4. Compare the prompt reading speed with and without `STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0`, each on a fresh engine. Prompt tok/s is
   prompt tokens divided by the time to first token, measured on the client. These figures match the engine's own
   "strata serve: prompt N tokens ... read in X ms" lines.

Every build in this report carries one small local patch, needed for this split on every version tested. Without it the
gfx1201 stage exits on the first prompt with "prefill gemm: a padded X (ldx 6208, K 6144) needs STRATA_PF_PAD's path".
The cause: `STRATA_PF_PAD` is a gfx1151 default, applied process-wide from GPU 0, but the padded GEMM exists only for
gfx11. The patch asks the current device instead (8 lines, 4 files: `Gemm::native`, the two `ld_y` / `ld_a` sites in
`Prefill::run_impl`, and `strata_pf_pad_device()` in `wmma_gemm`). Without the patch, `STRATA_PF_PAD=0` is the
workaround, at 2-3% slower prompts. Happy to send the diff.

**Bisect.** Each step: build the commit (with the PF_PAD patch above), start a fresh engine with the launch above, then
read 64K twice. A step is good if its best run is at least 1,450 tok/s. There were no ambiguous steps and none were
skipped.

| Commit | Date | Subject | 64K (tok/s) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 417cbab4 | 10-17 | packaging: the engine package carries strata-vision when the build has it | 1,696 / 1,617 | good |
| 83cde2ca | 10-18 | Merge f-151-b70 (c765c5f87) into f-split-int2 | 1,266 / 1,239 | bad |
| 80e6d91a | 10-17 | Merge commit 'a6759787c' into f-split-int | 1,722 / 1,666 | good |
| 83aa59fd | 10-18 | setup: say why the page waits while the bundled engine unpacks | 1,714 / 1,619 | good |
| af3770c6 | 10-18 | Merge f-148-amd (2053388dc, without the IQ2 fused default) into f-split-int2 | 1,722 / 1,567 | good |
| 0e58a652 | 10-18 | tests: iq_multi_parity under STRATA_KQ_SPLIT=1 ... | 1,269 / 1,238 | bad |
| 3980a5ce | 10-18 | HIP: virtual memory ranges ... so --kv-grow can run on ROCm 6+ | 1,273 / 1,245 | bad |
| aef32e22 | 10-18 | prefill timing: the hyper-connection write-back on its own line | 1,260 / 1,253 | bad |
| f3be9743 | 10-18 | prefill: warm the first BF16 and FP16 hipBLAS products on a thread at start | 1,248 / 1,237 | **bad (first bad)** |
| 79ac3164 | 10-18 | gfx12: STRATA_HIP_WMMA=auto ... | 1,719 / 1,708 | good (last good) |

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta (tag v0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3), built from source. First bad commit: f3be9743. Last good: 79ac3164.

### Graphics card, memory and system

Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 1 GB carve-out + 120 GB GTT) + Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201, as an eGPU; the engine's PCIe probe: 7.2 GB/s host to device) · 128 GB RAM · Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-38, ROCm 7.14.1 built for both architectures, hipBLASLt 1.4.1 (version 100401)

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS (unsloth, native pack) · 262K context · int8 KV · MTP drafter · 4 slots · pictures on (CPU reader)

### Logs

With the warm-up on, every start prints this sequence:

```
prefill gemm: hipBLASLt tuning enabled (90 rows, gfx1151, version 100401)
strata prefill: warmed the BF16 and FP16 GEMM libraries on GPU 0 in 2396 ms (STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0 skips)
prefill gemm: tuning architecture mismatch: file=gfx1151 runtime=gfx1201; using hipBLASEx
prefill gemm: tuning architecture mismatch: file=gfx1151 runtime=gfx1201; using hipBLASEx
strata prefill: warmed the BF16 and FP16 GEMM libraries on GPU 1 in 1048 ms (STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0 skips)
prefill gemm: hipBLASLt tuning enabled (90 rows, gfx1151, version 100401)
```

`STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` at 64K shows where the time goes. The two stages report differently: one reads in 4,096-token
chunks, the other in blocks of about 32K tokens (two per 64K prompt). These figures compare 0.1.43.1 with 0.2.0-beta, so
other changes between those versions are in them too:

| Per ~32K block | 0.1.43.1 | 0.2.0-beta (warm-up on) |
|---|---|---|
| GPU timeline | 17.2-17.5 s | 24.5 s |
| hc read | 2.7 s | 9.0 s |
| hc write (its own line since aef32e22) | n/a | 1.1 s |
| gemm gate/up | 5.3 s | 5.3 s |
| gdn | 1.7 s | 2.0 s |

With 0.2.0-beta, the 4,096-token chunk lines dropped from about 1.55 s to 0.49 s each. The ~32K-block stage became the
bottleneck instead, and most of its growth is in `hc read`.

On the 0.2.0-beta engine run with timing, the first 64K request after the start also spent 72.8 s in "ple" (525 tok/s);
its second request read at 1,207 tok/s. The other fresh 0.2.0-beta engines read their first 64K at their usual ~1,250.
Not checked whether this is related.

I did not find the mechanism. As far as I can see, the hipBLASLt tuning state is per `Gemm` (`create_hipblaslt_state`),
so the obvious shared-state suspect does not seem to apply. Where the warm-up is called:

- `warm_gemm_libraries()` in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`.
- A `std::thread` in `src/program/generate.cpp`, started before the expert arena loads.
- The end of `Prefill::init` (once per device).

issues.title: [GUI] Strata path encoding breaks on Windows 11 Russian localization (Mojibake and question marks in UI/model loading)
issues.author: almirus
issues.body: There is a critical path resolution and encoding issue on Windows 11 with Russian localization when user folders are managed by OneDrive. Strata fails to handle localized Cyrillic paths properly, breaking both folder creation and model loading. 1. Folder creation issue: Instead of using the local execution path, the application attempts to prepare data in a corrupted legacy path with Mojibake characters: C:\Documents and Settings\RobotComp\OneDrive\ 㬥 \Strata 2. UI & Model loading issue: Inside the application Settings, when Strata actually tries to load the model, the path encoding breaks even further. The Chinese characters change into question marks (???), making the model completely inaccessible and preventing it from loading. What causes this: • Encoding Mismatch: The Chinese character 㬥 appears because the Russian system folder name "Документы" (Documents) in ANSI/CP1251 gets incorrectly interpreted as UTF-8. • Question Marks (???): When the application subsequently attempts to read or display this invalid path during model loading, the fallback text processing replaces the unmappable characters with literal question marks, breaking the file handler. • Environment: This behavior is highly specific to Windows 11 systems running strict Russian locale settings combined with OneDrive synchronization. Environment: • OS: Windows 11 (Pure Russian localization) • Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB VRAM), 32 GB RAM • Model used: IQ3_S (Downloaded locally at C:\Users\RobotComp\Strata\Models\IQ3_S, but failing to prepare) Steps to reproduce: 1. Use a Windows 11 PC with Russian system locale and active OneDrive backup for the "Documents" folder. 2. Launch Strata and attempt to point it to or load the local model. 3. Observe the 㬥 characters in the generated filesystem path, which then turn into question marks (???) in the settings/logs when model loading is initiated. Suggested fix: Enforce strict Unicode/UTF-8 path translation across the entire Windows API boundary in the engine, and avoid using legacy Documents and Settings or localized cloud-synced folders by default.

issues.title: [Engine] NUMA-split CPU expert pool: +10 to +14 % decode on a dual-socket Xeon, measured, opt-in
issues.author: baptisterajaut
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### What do you want to do?

Hi, in #2242 you wrote that a dual-socket owner reporting a measured decode gain would be worth revisiting. Here is one, with a different approach from #2242, so I would like your read on scope before opening a PR.

**Box:** HP Z6 G4, 2x Xeon Gold 6226 (12 cores each), 64 GB DDR4-2933 (32 GB per NUMA node, 4 of 6 channels per socket), one RTX 3090 on PCIe 3.0. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored IQ4_XS at 262K context with MTP, v0.2.0-beta. Same tuning in every arm: `--adapt-async 1`, `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=200`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`.

**Server decode**, interleaved starts, expert profile frozen:

| Arm | Workers | Median tok/s | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2.0 default | 11, one socket | 52.6 | 51.0-53.3 |
| no split | 22 | 50.25 | 40.5-53.2 |
| split | 12 (6+6) | 51.5 | 49.9-54.4 |
| **split** | **22** | **60.0** | **57.8-61.6** |

Prompt speed and VRAM hit rate (74 %) are unchanged.

**What the split does**, behind `STRATA_NUMA_SPLIT=1`:
- the CPU pool gets one task slice per NUMA node, with its own counter and barrier;
- the rows of every CPU-side expert are cut in two at load, each half first-touched on its node by pinned threads.

Each socket then reads only local weights and never waits on the other socket's counters. #2242 binds the complement to the GPU's node; this keeps both nodes' memory and both sockets' cores in use. With the variable unset, the default path is unchanged.

These numbers agree with #674 and #707: more workers across sockets are slower on their own. The gap with the split would point at the cross-socket synchronisation rather than the core count.

Would a PR along these lines be in scope? The branch is ready with tests (pool_plan_test, pool_tasks_test including 192 bitwise comparisons in split mode, file_expert_source_test) and the full protocol. Limits up front: Linux only, 2 nodes, native expert layers only, measured on this one CUDA box.

### What do you do today instead?

The 0.2.0 default: 11 pool workers on the host socket, the other socket's 12 cores idle (before 0.2.0, `numactl --cpunodebind=0` for the same effect).

issues.author: Kiwzi
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090

Measured on 2026-10-19 with `tools/<key>_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: AMD EPYC 7443P 24-Core Processor (24 cores, 24 threads); installed RAM: 251.5 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 6.12.113+deb13-amd64; GPU driver: 615.71.09; CUDA: not read
- <key>: project 0.1.45, commit not a git checkout; engine 0.1.45
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs
- Context: 100000 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
<key> --pack unsloth-ud-iq4_xs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --max-context 100000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700
```

Environment of the config: `<key>_HC_Q8=1`, `<key>_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`

## Method

Run by `python tools/<key>_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a <key> server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | 103.8 (96.2-108.3) | 0.30 (0.25-0.33) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 (4019-4019) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 1943.9 (1937.7-1945.6) | not measured | 2.09 (2.09-2.09) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 3493.6 (3490.3-3501.1) | not measured | 4.63 (4.62-4.63) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14590 (14556-14612) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 117.9 (91.9-138.4) | 2.16 (2.03-2.35) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.6 % (68.5-68.7); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 74 (73-145) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13718 (13717-13721) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 0.90 s (0.87-0.91).

| Turn (run 1) | Prompt tokens | Reused | Read | Prompt tok/s | First token (s) | Decode tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 609 | 0 | 609 | 696.0 | 0.895 | 80.6 |

| 3 | 8723 | 5353 | 3370 | 1566.8 | 2.169 | 103.0 |
| 4 | 11649 | 8716 | 2933 | 1259.1 | 2.348 | 132.7 |
| 5 | 14612 | 11712 | 2900 | 1355.4 | 2.163 | 107.1 |

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details come from the server, `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` and the OS; background load and power limits are not recorded. Total time of the suite: 78 s.

issues.title: [Benchmark] BENCH.bat / strata_bench.py crashes with NameError when it starts the server
issues.author: IVoyt
issues.body:
## Area

[Benchmark] (measurements and reports)

## Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

## What happened

`tools/strata_bench.py` crashes with a `NameError` as soon as it has to **start** the server itself — which is the default path and the one `BENCH.bat` uses:

```
PS D:\Strata> .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\strata_bench.py --config D:\Strata\strata-swift-iq3_s.json --out D:\Strata-data\ab\old --runs 3 --long
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 1037, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 990, in main
    say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...")
                                            ^^^^
NameError: name 'port' is not defined
```

The name `port` is never assigned in `main()`; only `a.port` and the local `base` exist. Three lines use the undefined name:

- `tools/strata_bench.py:987` — `print(f"Port {port} is used by something that is not Strata: pass --port N.", ...)`
- `tools/strata_bench.py:990` — `say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} ...")`
- `tools/strata_bench.py:991` — `proc = start_server(cfg_path, port, a.gpu, log_path)`

Line 990 is reached on every run that starts a server, so the tool fails immediately, before the model is loaded and before any measurement.

## Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```
python tools\strata_bench.py --config <a config with an installed model>
```

(or `BENCH.bat`, which calls the same tool with the same arguments). `--url http://127.0.0.1:<port>` works, because that path never reaches the broken lines.

## Reproduction status

Reproduced locally.

## Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta (build 0.1.45.3), git `3fa1b524` (v0.2.0-beta-7), source checkout.

## Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 5090 32 GB - 96 GB RAM - Windows 11 (10.0.26300), i7-12700KF, driver 617.42, CUDA toolkit 13.1 (nvcc 13.1.115), Python 3.13.12.

## Model, size and settings

Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 524288 context, pictures off.

## Expected behavior

The tool starts the server on the config's port (or `--port`), waits for the model, runs the suite and writes the results folder.

## Actual behavior

`NameError: name 'port' is not defined` at `tools/strata_bench.py:990`, immediately.

## Suggested fix

Bind the port once and use it in the three places:

```python
port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), port)
```

and use `port` at lines 987, 990 and 991.

## Additional context

- The same three lines are unchanged since at least v0.1.45, so this is not a regression of the 0.2.0 work; it is a long-standing break of the default benchmark path.
- The tool's own tests never reach it: every `main()` test in `tools/test_strata_bench.py` calls the tool with `--url` (line 216: `argv = ["--url", srv.base, "--out", out_dir, "--runs", "2", "--quiet", *extra]`), so the "start the server" branch is never executed by the suite. A test that starts the server on a free port would have caught this.
- The same branch also writes the engine log excerpt (`engine-log-excerpt.txt`); with `--url` that file is not produced, so the workaround loses the log excerpt as well.
- Unrelated, found while running the suite: `python tools\test_strata_bench.py` fails on a PC whose account name is `user`, because the redaction placeholder is `<user>` and the test asserts the account name is absent from the redacted text (`tools/test_strata_bench.py:186-187`, `len(user) >= 4`). The test needs a name that is not a substring of the placeholder, or the placeholder needs to differ.

issues.title: [Benchmark] engine calibrate --measure loses the whole sweep when the report directory does not exist
issues.author: IVoyt
issues.body:
## Area

[Benchmark] (measurements and reports)

## Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

## What happened

`strata engine calibrate --measure` ran the full decode sweep (8 engine starts, 177 measurements, ~19 minutes) and then threw the whole result away with:

```
strata: report output directory does not exist
```

The output directory is only checked **at the very end** of the sweep, in `_write_new()` (`strata_control/calibration.py`), which is called after the measurement has finished:

- `calibration.py:303` — `result = execute(runner_cfg, say=say)` — the sweep, ~19 minutes
- `calibration.py:329` — `_write_new(output, _report_bytes(report))` — the write
- `calibration.py:231-232` — `if not path.parent.is_dir(): raise ProfileError("report output directory does not exist", 5)`

The report path's *existence* check is done up front (`calibration.py:291`, "calibration report path already exists"), but the check that the **parent directory exists** is at the end. A missing directory therefore costs the whole measurement.

The measured numbers survive only in the engine log, not in a report; the sweep's own output was on the console.

## Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Pick a run config whose model is installed: `strata-swift-iq3_s.json`.
2. Run the measurement with an output path whose **parent directory does not exist**:
   ```
   strata engine calibrate --profile D:\Strata\strata-swift-iq3_s.json --measure --exclusive --out D:\Strata-data\does-not-exist\iq3_s.json
   ```
3. Wait for the whole sweep (8 engine starts, ~19 minutes here).
4. The run ends with `strata: report output directory does not exist` and no report file.

The same happens with a path whose parent exists but is not a directory.

## Reproduction status

Reproduced locally.

## Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta (build 0.1.45.3), git `3fa1b524` (v0.2.0-beta-7), source checkout.

## Graphics card, memory and system

RTX 5090 32 GB - 96 GB RAM - Windows 11 (10.0.26300), i7-12700KF, driver 617.42, CUDA toolkit 13.1 (nvcc 13.1.115), Python 3.13.12.

## Model, size and settings

Swift 1.5 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 524288 context, pictures off.

## Logs

The sweep's console output (it completed; only the write failed):

```
    round 1/3 PCIe share: 0 127.9  0.2 133.6  0.35 122.5  0.55 120.4  0.75 119.3  0.9 108.9  1 137.6
    ...
    PCIe share, median of 3: 0: 129.5 (127.9-132.7), 0.2: 126.2 (119.5-133.6), 0.35: 124.5 (122.5-126.0), 0.55: 118.7 (118.1-120.4), 0.75: 119.3 (115.2-120.4), 0.9: 110.2 (108.9-113.6), 1: 136.5 (133.0-137.6) -> best 1
    draft floor, median of 3: 0.3: 129.0 (127.8-138.2), 0.5: 137.9 (133.2-139.2), 0.7: 149.5 (140.7-151.5) -> best 0.7
  Measuring with 11 CPU workers (restarts the engine) ...
    11 workers: 154.7 tok/s
  Measuring with 7 CPU workers (restarts the engine) ...
    7 workers: 158.6 tok/s
  Measuring with 6 CPU workers (restarts the engine) ...
    6 workers: 163.0 tok/s
  Measuring with 3 CPU workers (restarts the engine) ...
    3 workers: 162.4 tok/s
  Measuring the expert tier (the engine default) (restarts the engine) ...
    138.1 tok/s
  Measuring the expert tier every 1, 80 swaps, decay 0.97 (restarts the engine) ...
    168.0 tok/s
  Measuring the expert tier every 1, 160 swaps, decay 0.97 (restarts the engine) ...
    167.7 tok/s
strata: report output directory does not exist
```

## Expected behavior

The run should refuse **before** the sweep, the way it already refuses an existing report path:

```
strata: report output directory does not exist
```

or write the report where it can.

## Suggested fix

Check the output's parent directory in `_measure_locked()` next to the existing "report path already exists" check (`calibration.py:291`), so the refusal happens in a second rather than after 19 minutes of measurement:

```python
if not output.parent.is_dir():
    raise ProfileError("report output directory does not exist", 5)
if output.exists() or output.is_symlink():
    raise ProfileError("calibration report path already exists", 2)
```

## Additional context

- Not a crash and not a wrong answer: the measurement itself is fine, only the report is lost. The numbers are still in the engine log (`strata-<model>.log`), and the console shows them, but there is no report for `--review-result` / `--apply-result` to consume.
- The same late check applies to `setup.py --calibrate` (it writes its own record, so it does not fail, but it also has no up-front check).
- The mistake is easy to make: the `--out` path is free text, and nothing checks the directory until the very end.

issues.author: Rui995
issues.body:
Sharing measurements from an RX 7700 XT system, following docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7700 XT, 12 GiB VRAM, gfx1101
- CPU: Ryzen 7 5700X3D, 8 cores / 16 threads, AVX2
- RAM: 64 GB installed, 63.9 GiB reported
- OS: Windows 11, build 10.0.26300
- GPU driver: 32.0.31041.1004
- Engine: official prebuilt Windows HIP 0.1.45
- Repository commit: 477ac13c
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XS

A separate RAM-using background server and the desktop client remained open. Background load, clocks and power were not controlled.

## Configuration

- Configured context: 262144 tokens
- KV: int8, streaming with 32768 resident cells
- One serving slot
- Prefill: auto:8192
- MTP enabled; speculative decoding: 4, spec-min-p: 0.5
- Conversation cache: 8192 MiB, 4 slots, minimum 8192 tokens, 2560 MiB free-memory floor
- prompt-cache-spread enabled

Opt-in environment settings:

STRATA_PF_FUSED=1
STRATA_PF_GEMM=1
STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=4096
STRATA_PF_PAD=1
STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1
STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto
STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX=3072

## Method

Measured on 2026-10-19 using tools/strata_bench.py against an already-running local server.

Thinking was off and temperature was 0. Three runs per test; short chat used three questions per run, giving nine requests. Fresh prompts had unique tags and reported zero reused tokens.

This is a speed measurement, not a correctness or recall benchmark. Model loading was not timed.

## Results

| Test | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Median speed | Median time to first token |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Short chat, 9 requests | 43–51 | 0 | Decode 42.0 tok/s | 0.74 s |
| Fresh 4K | 4019 | 0 | Prefill 412.7 tok/s | 9.78 s |
| Fresh 16K | 16058 | 0 | Prefill 760.4 tok/s | 21.16 s |
| Agent follow-up turns | About 14.5K at final turn | 68.8% aggregate reuse | Decode 37.1 tok/s | 8.90 s |
| Fresh 32K supplement | 32050 | 0 | Prefill 665.7 tok/s | 48.207 s |

The main suite took approximately 307 seconds.

### Separate 32K supplement

Only the official Suite.calibrate() and Suite.run_prompt(32768, "32K") paths were added: two tiny calibration requests followed by three fresh prompts, capped at 24 output tokens. The other tests were not rerun.

| Run | Prompt tokens | Reused | Prefill tok/s | TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32050 | 0 | 689.2 | 46.564 s |
| 2 | 32050 | 0 | 665.7 | 48.207 s |
| 3 | 32050 | 0 | 665.1 | 48.245 s |

## Runtime conditions and limitations

- Both engine starts accepted 2 MiB large pages.
- The main suite used 2650 PROFILE expert slots, 3.57 GiB VRAM, and automatic prefill chunks of 5376 tokens.
- The 32K supplement followed a Strata-only restart enabling effort_position=end. The new process selected 2560 expert slots, 3.45 GiB VRAM, and 5120-token chunks.
- These are separately labelled measurements, not a controlled before/after comparison.
- Windows commit limit was 124.6 GiB. Before the 32K supplement, available commit headroom was 46.7 GiB.
- An earlier log warning showing only 6.5 GiB commit headroom belonged to an older engine start. The page file had already been enlarged online before these measurements.
- No Windows reboot or controlled large-pages-off/on comparison was performed.
- Low-VRAM warnings occurred. GPU paging was not instrumented.
- No correctness, recall, 128K/200K sweep, or different-build A/B comparison was performed.

The main suite needed PYTHONUTF8=1 because project_version() read the UTF-8 BOM in CMakeLists.txt using the Windows default encoding. The local fix matches existing PR #3092; no duplicate fix PR is proposed.

Measured on 2026-10-19 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: AMD Radeon, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor (6 cores, 12 threads); installed RAM: 92.2 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: 6.19.14.31400100; CUDA: not read

## Model and configuration

issues.title: Strata Benchmark Report — Swift 1.5 Flash Next (GSQ-RCO IQ3_S) on 0.1.45, with --vision=cpu, 100+ kombinations
issues.author: DrLove73
issues.body:
<!-- Failed to upload "_summary.csv" -->
<!-- Failed to upload "_speed_summary.csv" -->

# Strata Benchmark Report — Swift 1.5 Flash Next (GSQ-RCO IQ3_S) on 0.1.45, with --vision=cpu, 100+ kombinations

**Model family:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Swift 1.5 variant)  
**Quantization:** GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (3-bit)  
**Engine:** Strata 0.1.45 (llama.cpp 3cf0325)  
**Hardware:** RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (24 GB VRAM), Intel Xeon Gold 6138, 220 GB RAM  
**Dates:** 2026-10-15 (legacy `vision=on`) and 2026-10-19 (Strata 0.1.45 `vision=cpu`)  
**Contexts:** 128K, 256K, 384K, 512K, 1M  
**Total runs:** 100+

## Summary

Strata 0.1.45 with `vision=cpu` is a massive leap for long-context inference. Peak decode is **76.71 tok/s at 256K**. By offloading the vision encoder to the CPU, we free up critical VRAM for the expert cache. This eliminates the VRAM bottleneck at 384K and 1M contexts, resulting in **up to +160% performance gains** on long contexts compared to the older `vision=on` builds. 

## Sweep configuration (and run_id legend)

```
CONTEXTS         = 131072 262144 393216 524288 1048576 (run_id 1,2,3,5,5 respectively)
PARALLEL_VALUES  = 1 (2 for select runs) (run_id 1,2 respectively)
VISION_VALUES    = cpu (0.1.45) / on (legacy) (run_id c,y,n respectively)
KV_VALUES        = int8 q4_0 k8v4 (run_id i,q,k respectively)
PREFILL_VALUES   = 32768 65536 auto (run_id 32, 64, a respectively)
KV_RESIDENT      = 32768 65536 (run_id 32, 64 respectively)
SPEC             = 4
ADAPT_DECAY      = 0.97
ADAPT_SWAPS      = 160
```

## Results — Best config per context (Strata 0.1.45, `vision=cpu`)

| Context | Config (kv, prefill, kvr) | TTFT | Decode | run_id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | int8, 32768, 65536 | 55.8 s | **70.72 tok/s** | 1-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K | int8, 65536, 65536 | 124.8 s | **76.71 tok/s** | 2-1-c-i-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 384K | int8, 65536, 65536 | 185.9 s | **67.67 tok/s** | 3-1-c-i-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 512K | q4_0, 32768, 65536 | 257.3 s | **70.35 tok/s** | 4-1-c-q-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 1M   | int8, 32768, 65536 | 630.2 s | **54.19 tok/s** | 5-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |

## Version Comparison: Legacy (`vision=on`) vs 0.1.45 (`vision=cpu`)

The jump in performance is most dramatic at contexts above 256K, where VRAM starvation previously crippled the expert cache.

| Context | Old Best (Oct 15) | New Best (Oct 19) | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | 65.54 tok/s | **70.72 tok/s** | **+7.9%** |
| 256K | 72.94 tok/s | **76.71 tok/s** | **+5.2%** |
| 384K | 38.92 tok/s | **67.67 tok/s** | **+73.8%** |
| 512K | 66.34 tok/s | **70.35 tok/s** | **+6.0%** |
| 1M | 52.06 tok/s (q4_0) | **54.19 tok/s** (int8) | **+4.1%** |

*Note: At 384K, older versions suffered a severe VRAM bottleneck forcing the engine to swap experts. 0.1.45 with `vision=cpu` completely resolves this.*

## Key findings

1. **`vision=cpu` is mandatory for 384K+**. It frees the ~1.5 GB of VRAM previously used by the image encoder, allowing the KV cache to stay resident and the expert cache to function without thrashing.
2. **256K is the absolute sweet spot** at 76.71 tok/s.
3. **1M context is now stable**. In previous builds, 1M required aggressive `q4_0` KV quantization. In 0.1.45, `int8` KV now works flawlessly and is faster (54.19 tok/s) than `q4_0` was before.
4. **KV type scaling**:
   - **128K to 384K**: `kv=int8` is fastest.
   - **512K**: `kv=q4_0` edges out int8 (70.35 vs 66.99) because the smaller footprint leaves more VRAM for experts.
   - **1M**: `kv=int8` is surprisingly optimal again when paired with `vision=cpu`.
5. **Prefill tuning**: `prefill=65536` is better for 256K–384K. `prefill=32768` works better for 512K and 1M.
6. **kv-resident=65536** consistently outperforms 32768 across all contexts.
7. **Quality (NIAH 512K)**: 3/3 pass across all KV types. No quality degradation observed from the vision offload.

## Recommended production configs (Strata 0.1.45)

| Use case | Context | Config |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive Chat | ≤128K | `kv=int8, prefill=32768, kvr=65536, vision=cpu` |
| Long Analysis | 256K | `kv=int8, prefill=65536, kvr=65536, vision=cpu` |
| Document QA | 512K | `kv=q4_0, prefill=32768, kvr=65536, vision=cpu` |
| Massive Docs | 1M | `kv=int8, prefill=32768, kvr=65536, vision=cpu` |

## Reproducing

```bash
./strata_sweep.sh configs/swift-1.5-iq3_s.conf
```

### Representative Results & Speed Degradation Analysis

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 128K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 15 | 131,072 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 59.9 | 53.96 | 1-2-y-i-32768-64-4-97-160 |
| **256K - New Best** (`vision=cpu`) | Oct 19 | 262,144 | `int8` / `65536` / `65536` | 124.8 | **76.71** | 2-1-c-i-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K - New alt (Prefill 32K) | Oct 19 | 262,144 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 116.0 | 73.60 | 2-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K - New alt (`q4_0` KV) | Oct 19 | 262,144 | `q4_0` / `65536` / `65536` | 135.2 | 74.22 | 2-1-c-q-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Old Best (`vision=on`) | Oct 15 | 262,144 | `k8v4` / `auto` / `32768` | 155.0 | 72.94 | 2-1-y-k-a-32-4-97-160 |
| 256K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 15 | 262,144 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 128.3 | 54.92 | 2-2-y-i-32768-64-4-97-160 |
| **384K - New Best** (`vision=cpu`) | Oct 19 | 393,216 | `int8` / `65536` / `65536` | 185.9 | **67.67** | 3-1-c-i-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 384K - New alt (Prefill 32K) | Oct 19 | 393,216 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 200.9 | 62.55 | 3-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 384K - New alt (`q4_0` KV) | Oct 19 | 393,216 | `q4_0` / `65536` / `65536` | 195.7 | 59.26 | 3-1-c-q-64-64-4-97-160 |
| **512K - New Best** (`vision=cpu`) | Oct 19 | 524,288 | `q4_0` / `32768` / `65536` | 257.3 | **70.35** | 4-1-c-q-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 512K - New alt (`int8` KV) | Oct 19 | 524,288 | `int8` / `65536` / `65536` | 268.0 | 66.99 | 4-1-c-i-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 512K - Old Best (`vision=on`) | Oct 15 | 524,288 | `int8` / `32768` / `32768` | 265.3 | 66.34 | 4-1-y-i-32768-32-4-97-160 |
| 512K - Batch 2 Penalty | Oct 15 | 524,288 | `int8` / `auto` / `65536` | 343.5 | 47.23 | 4-2-y-i-a-64-4-97-160 |
| **1M - New Best** (`vision=cpu`) | Oct 19 | 1,048,576 | `int8` / `32768` / `65536` | 630.2 | **54.19** | 5-1-c-i-32-64-4-97-160 |
| 1M - New alt (`q4_0` KV) | Oct 19 | 1,048,576 | `q4_0` / `65536` / `65536` | 634.1 | 50.41 | 5-1-c-q-64-64-4-97-160 |
| 1M - Old Best (`vision=on`) | Oct 15 | 1,048,576 | `q4_0` / `auto:64` / `32768` | 662.5 | 52.06 | 5-1-y-q-a64-32-4-97-160 |

#### Key Takeaways from Representative Data:
*   **Batch Penalty:** Adding a second parallel slot (`-2-` in run_id) at high context (256K+) causes a severe drop in decode speed (e.g., from 65.64 to 54.92 at 256K), proving that parallel execution starves the expert cache of VRAM.
*   **Vision Offload Impact:** At 384K, the Oct 15 run with `vision=on` suffered a catastrophic drop (38.92 tok/s, not shown in the top block but present in raw data), whereas the new Oct 19 runs with `vision=cpu` hold steady at 67.67 tok/s. 
*   **KV Cache Scaling:** While `int8` is best up to 384K, at 512K the `q4_0` KV becomes the winner (70.35 tok/s) because its smaller memory footprint allows more expert weights to stay in VRAM. At 1M, `int8` retakes the lead when paired with `vision=cpu`.

issues.title: v0.1.45 HIP/gfx1100: verify timeout during ~54K-token request with MTP enabled (single RX 7900 XTX)
issues.author: peterhon168
issues.body:
## Summary
On a single Radeon RX 7900 XTX, Strata v0.1.45 (Linux HIP) serves a short MTP request successfully, but a long agent request of about 54,316 input tokens stalls shortly after decode starts. The request eventually returns HTTP 503 and the engine exits with code -15. The backend reports a native verification timeout at layer 18. This appears related to the long-context HIP verify watchdog reported in #2449, though this case uses v0.1.45 and only one GPU.

## Environment
- GPU: one AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100)
- Strata: v0.1.45, HIP backend
- ROCm: 7.2.4
- Kernel: 6.8.0-139-generic
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S
- Context limit: 262144; int8 KV cache
- Expert resident cache: 36 GiB
- MTP: enabled with `--spec 2`
- Prefill: `--prefill auto:32768`
- `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` was already set (the workaround discussed in #1705).

## Observed behavior
1. Start the server with the above configuration and MTP enabled.
2. A short test request succeeds (HTTP 200; 14 draft tokens offered, 10 accepted).
3. Send a long, multi-turn agent request with approximately 54,316 input tokens. Prefill completes, and about 444 output tokens are generated before progress stalls.
4. After roughly 126.8 seconds, the request fails with HTTP 503. The engine reports:

```text
Unrecoverable native verification failure: verify: timed out at layer 18; its GPU waits were released and the GPU finished (#267)
```

The engine is then observed to stop with exit code -15. The client sees the engine-stopped error on its next request.

## Expected behavior
The request should finish or fail with a recoverable error without terminating the inference engine. A watchdog should not misclassify a completed GPU operation as an unrecoverable verify failure.

## Control / limitations
With MTP disabled, short requests pass, and one earlier long Pi agent call completed. This was not a strict A/B reproduction with identical prompt and load, so I cannot yet conclude that MTP is the sole cause. The short MTP success shows that enabling MTP itself does not immediately fail. No private prompts, local paths, addresses, or unredacted logs are included here.

Could you advise whether this is the same verify-wait issue as #2449, and whether there is a fix or a specific diagnostic trace that would distinguish a HIP watchdog problem from an MTP/long-context interaction?

issues.title: [Benchmark] 2x MI50 16 GB (gfx906) + Ryzen 7 5700X: IQ3_XXS at 128K, --pipeline-windows 2 gives +36% decode
issues.author: romeo5353535353-ui
issues.body:
Measured on 2026-10-19 by a machine owner (reported here for the project). This is
**Strata v0.1.43.1** (`a0116b2`), the gfx906 HIP build, with the original
Flash-Next **IQ3_XXS** at the model's full **131,072-token context**.

The point of this report is not a single throughput number but a **tuning result**:
on this two-card gfx906 split, `--pipeline-windows 2` lifts decode by **+36%**
(49.2 → 66.9 tok/s) with prompt throughput unchanged, and `--trim-stage-weights`
adds another **+5%** on prompt reading. Both options are off by default, and
neither is mentioned in `docs/AMD_HIP.md` for gfx906.

## Hardware and software

- 2× AMD Instinct MI50 16 GB (Vega 20, gfx906, wave64). The VBIOS reports
  `1002:66af`, so `lspci` and the engine print "Radeon VII"; the cards are sold as
  MI50 16 GB. 16 GiB BAR each (Re-Size BAR on).
- ASUS ROG Strix X570-E Gaming, BIOS 5055; Ryzen 7 5700X (8C/16T, no AVX-512);
  64 GB DDR4-3600 (2×32 GB, FCLK 1:1) — see the RAM section below.
- Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel `6.8.0-147-generic` (amdgpu from the kernel).
- ROCm from the community image `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
  (rocBLAS/hipBLAS with gfx906 kernels; hipBLASLt is not used).
- Engine built in that image with
  `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906`,
  clang from `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin`. Container runs with
  `--device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1`.
- Power limit 200 W per card (`power1_cap`, 80% of the 250 W default).
- Model on NVMe; pack and MTP built with `tools/iq_pack.py` / `tools/mtp_*.py`.

Note: **0.1.44+ does not build for gfx906** on this machine (separate issue): a
`cublas*` symbol error in `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` and a `cuda.h`/`cuda_bf16.h`
error in the `strata_mmq_w4a4` target. `v0.1.43.1` builds cleanly, so that is
what the measurements use.

## Model and configuration

`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`, revision
`ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09`, IQ3_XXS (71 GB, two shards).

Base configuration (everything below is one change against it):

```
--pack packs/iq3_xxs --native <shard1> --ple-gguf <shard2>
--expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto
--prefill 2048 --mtp mtp/rt --max-context 131072
--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --layer-split 27
--spec 3 --spec-min-p 0.9 --vram-reserve-mib 1024
```

The engine reports 918 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded; the prompt path
borrows cache slots across both cards.

## Method

Two measurements per configuration, both served through `serve.server`, greedy
(`temperature 0`), one request at a time:

- **decode**: a fresh 1,647-token prompt (a unique nonce in every run, so nothing
  is reused), `max_tokens 128`; the number is the engine's own
  `predicted_per_second`.
- **prompt**: the same request's `prompt_per_second`.
- **short chat**: "Explain in three sentences what a CPU cache does",
  `max_tokens 256`; note that its length varies (83–133 tokens), so it is noisier.

Each configuration: one discarded warm-up pass, then **7 long and 5 short runs**,
median reported. A configuration change means a full container restart and model
reload (38–42 s, so the VRAM tier is rebuilt from the same profile).

## Results

Medians of 7 long / 5 short runs; tok/s.

| Configuration | decode (1.6K prompt) | prompt read | short chat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| base | 49.2 | 353.1 | 51.5 |
| `STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_QUERY_SWIZZLE=1` + `STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_REDUCE12=1` | 49.4 | 356.1 | 53.4 |
| `--prefill 4096` | 48.9 | 353.3 | 51.6 |
| **`--pipeline-windows 2`** | **66.9** | 352.3 | **74.1** |
| **`--trim-stage-weights`** | 50.1 | **370.8** | 52.9 |
| `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1` | 49.7 | 352.1 | 51.4 |
| **`--pipeline-windows 2 --trim-stage-weights`** | **66–68** | **371** | **73–74** |
| `... --trim-stage-weights` + the two attn switches | 69.5 | 377.7 | 72.4 |

- `--pipeline-windows 2`: **decode +36%**, prompt unchanged. On a two-stage layer
  split it overlaps the verify windows (stage 0 computes the next window while
  stage 1 verifies the current one), which is exactly the decode path here.
- `--trim-stage-weights` (with the explicit `--layer-split 27`): **prompt +5%**,
  decode +2%. It frees dense weights of foreign layers and the cache grows.
- The two attn switches add a further ~1.5–2% (69.5 / 377.7), which is at this
  machine's run-to-run noise; not adopted because they change the attention
  summation order.
- `--prefill 4096` and `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1`: no measurable change (the latter
  also makes the model load 98 s instead of ~38 s).
- Combined result against the tuple measured before tuning: decode **48.0 → 66–68
  tok/s (+38%)**, prompt **352.5 → 371 tok/s (+5%)**.

## Concurrency (`--batch`)

Four requests fired at once, 128 tokens each, aggregate tokens / wall time:

| Configuration | 1 request | 2 concurrent | 4 concurrent |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| no `--batch` | 20.2 | 20.6 | 21.1 |
| `--batch 2` | 20.4 | 23.0 | 21.6 |
| `--batch 4` | 20.0 | 22.5 | 21.8 |

Aggregate throughput barely moves while per-request decode collapses (70 → 11–37
tok/s at `--batch 2`/`4`). For a single interactive user batching is a net loss on
this machine, so it is off.

## `--kv-resident` sweep

Short context (the 1.6K prompt): `0` (all K/V in VRAM), `20480`, `32768`,
`49152`, `65536` — decode 65.4–67.3 tok/s and prompt 370.9–371.4 tok/s for every
value, i.e. inside the run-to-run noise. At 1.6K tokens nothing streams at any
setting, so the only effect is VRAM taken away from the expert cache.

Deep context (~31.3K prompt tokens, 64 tokens out):

| `--kv-resident` | prompt tok/s | decode tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 (all in VRAM) | 712.7 | 50.9 |
| 20480 | 706.0 | 51.4 (4 runs: 50.9 / 52.0 / 51.4 / 73.7) |
| 32768 | 704.5 | 53.2 (3 runs: 51.8 / 73.7 / 53.2) |
| 65536 | 704.1 | 52.5 |

A 73.7 outlier appeared once per configuration and did not reproduce; it is MTP
draft acceptance, not the KV setting. Net effect: **no measurable difference**, so
