issues.title: [Windows/AMD 26.9.2] exception 0xC0000005 IQ3_S
issues.author: angelonger
issues.body:
### Summary

I'm troubleshooting an issue with Strata on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT under Windows. I've tried several environment-variable changes, adjusted the VRAM reserve, disabled HIPBLASLt-related settings, and replaced the bundled amdhip64_7.dll with the copy from C:\Windows\System32.

The issue remains unresolved after these troubleshooting attempts.

I'm sharing the hardware configuration and changes tested to help determine whether this is related to the Windows HIP backend, HIPBLASLt, VRAM allocation, or a runtime DLL compatibility issue.

### System Configuration

9070 XT with 9800X3D & 64 GB of DDR5 / 6400. Driver version: 26.9.2 at Strata 0.1.45

### Troubleshooting performed

1. Removed HIPBLASLt tuning

Removed the HIPBLASLt tuning setting from the environment configuration to test whether the tuning path was contributing to the problem.

2. Changed the VRAM reserve

Tested different values for --vram-reserve-mib:

2048

1536

The purpose was to test whether changing the amount of VRAM reserved for the engine would affect the issue.

3. Disabled HIPBLASLt-related settings

Added the following environment parameters:

{
  "ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT": "0",
  "STRATA_HIPBLASLT": "0",
  "STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS": "0"
}

These settings were tested to see whether disabling HIPBLASLt-related paths and GFX12-specific defaults would change the behavior.

4. Increased workspace stack sizes and enabled WDDM budget handling

Added the following environment parameters:

{
  "ROCBLAS_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE": "33554432",
  "HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE": "33554432",
  "STRATA_WDDM_BUDGET": "1"
}

These changes were tested to investigate whether workspace allocation or Windows GPU memory-budget handling was contributing to the problem.

5. Replaced the bundled HIP runtime DLL

Replaced:

Strata-main\engine\amdhip64_7.dll

with the copy located at:

C:\Windows\System32\amdhip64_7.dll

This was tested to check whether the bundled HIP runtime DLL was involved.

### Current status

The above configuration changes and troubleshooting steps have been attempted, but the issue is not yet resolved.

I have not established which setting, if any, affects the underlying cause.

Log attached.

[strata-iq3_s.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33642648/strata-iq3_s.log)

issues.title: vhotseat: Strata and ComfyUI take turns on one GPU, so a local agent can render video on the same card it runs on
issues.author: wandermyz
issues.body:
vhotseat is a small tool that runs next to Strata and ComfyUI on the same PC. It makes them take turns on VRAM *and* RAM, so a local agent served by Strata can queue image and video renders on the card it runs on, with no out-of-memory errors. ComfyUI is just the example: any other GPU job (a training run, a simulation, a script) can take turns with Strata the same way by running it as `vhotseat hold NAME -- COMMAND`. Linux and NVIDIA, Python 3.10+, one dependency (PyYAML), MIT: https://github.com/wandermyz/vhotseat

**The problem.** On a 16 GB card, Strata holds ~14.7 GB of VRAM and ~44 GB of RAM for Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, and a MiniMax H3 video render needs ~14 GB of VRAM. When the agent queues a render, one of them runs out of memory.

**How it uses Strata.** Strata's `before_load` hook runs `vhotseat gate strata`. Strata's lazy load and idle unload do the rest:

- **The agent queues a render.** A small custom node in ComfyUI runs `vhotseat switch comfy` before every job. It waits for any answer Strata is writing, then unloads Strata.
- **The agent asks its next question.** Strata's `before_load` hook asks vhotseat first. While ComfyUI still has jobs queued or running, it refuses, and the agent's harness retries the 503. Once ComfyUI is idle, vhotseat frees its models (and restarts it if its leftover RAM is in the way), then lets Strata load.
- **Running work is never interrupted.** That covers an answer Strata is writing and a render in progress.

Nothing else is changed in Strata: only the `before_load` key in the run config. Any client is covered (the agent, its scripts, the ComfyUI web page, curl), because nobody calls vhotseat; each side asks for the GPU right before it loads.



## Demo

Setup: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, 64 GB RAM, Linux. Strata serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at 128K context, [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) as the agent, MiniMax H3 (int8 `fl2va`) in ComfyUI.

The prompt to pi:

> Make two 3-second anime-style clips of a cat on a windowsill with MiniMax H3, then tell which one looks better. Continue working on a clip of the cat jump from windowsill to catch a bird. Concat this two clips into a single video file.

pi did it unattended, in two render rounds.

![pi: the prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-1.png)

**Round 1.** pi wrote the job files and rendered two takes (two seeds) in one batch, which took 3 min 41 s. Strata was unloaded for the batch.

![pi: round 1 rendered in one batch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-2.png)

**Review.** Strata loaded again. pi built a contact sheet of both takes, looked at it with Flash-Next's vision, and picked take A, because "B substitutes a butterfly for the bird".

![pi: reviewing the round 1 contact sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-3.png)

**Round 2.** pi took the last frame of take A as the first frame of the jump and rendered two takes, which took 5 min 38 s.

![pi: round 2 rendered in one batch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-4.png)

**Review and finish.** Strata loaded again. pi picked the take with a real leap, then joined the two clips with ffmpeg.

![pi: reviewing the jump takes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-5.png)
![pi: summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/pi-6.png)

That's four GPU handovers, and no OOM.

The final video (6.8 s, 1344×768):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dc4e40d-caa6-4433-b654-718713c981cd

`vhotseat web` shows the same session. The GPU goes to ComfyUI at 02:10 and 02:16, and comes back to Strata at 02:14 and 02:21. Each time Strata loaded, vhotseat freed ComfyUI's 13.9 GB of models first. Strata's RAM goes from ~44 GB down to almost nothing while ComfyUI renders, then back.

![vhotseat dashboard for the demo session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/f7521060f1765f147dfee20d34ba900c4297d5e7/vhotseat-demo/dashboard.png)

## Try it

```sh
uv tool install vhotseat      # or: pipx install vhotseat
```

Or give this sentence to a coding agent on the PC where Strata runs:

> Set up vhotseat so my local LLM agent can drive ComfyUI on this GPU without running out of memory. Follow https://github.com/wandermyz/vhotseat/blob/main/docs/guides/quickstart-strata-pi-comfyui.md, adapting it to the servers and paths on this machine, and run each step's check before going on.

`vhotseat doctor` checks the config, the GPU and both gates; `vhotseat status` shows who holds the GPU.

It writes only to Strata's run config (the `before_load` key) and its own config. The ComfyUI side is one custom node.

Not tested: Windows (designed for, not done yet), AMD, Intel and Macs. Other servers (another LLM server, a TTS server, a training run) can join through a config entry or a small driver.

Feedback is welcome here or in the vhotseat repository, especially reports from other cards and setups.

issues.title: Community Benchmark: RTX 4050 Laptop (6GB VRAM) + 48GB RAM
issues.author: chanton1984-lgtm
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU

Measured on 2026-10-19 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU, 6 GiB VRAM
- CPU: 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13620H (10 cores, 16 threads); installed RAM: 47.7 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200); GPU driver: 610.74; CUDA: not read
- Strata: project 0.1.45, commit not a git checkout; engine 0.1.45
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-q2_0
- Context: 32000 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata.exe --pack q2_0 --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --max-context 32000 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 0 --kv q4_0
```

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (started by the benchmark from the install configuration); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 8 | not measured | 21.4 (17.4-30.0) | 1.55 (1.32-24.24) |

issues.title: Community benchmark: RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB + Core Ultra 7 255HX, native IQ3_XXS experts pack, Strata 0.1.44 (tuned 12 GB fork)
issues.author: zsariboga
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU

Measured on 2026-10-18 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU, 12 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 255HX (20 cores, 20 threads); installed RAM: 63.4 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200); GPU driver: 617.42; CUDA: not read
- Strata: project 0.1.44, commit 01fc2c80; engine 0.1.44
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen38-uncensored
- Context: 262144 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | 108.8 (92.7-122.7) | 0.41 (0.35-0.45) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 (4019-4019) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 1571.8 (1569.7-1643.8) | not measured | 3.01 (2.91-3.03) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 2180.0 (2162.9-2214.2) | not measured | 16.90 (16.89-16.96) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 15265 (15265-15266) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 108.7 (90.5-125.7) | 2.15 (1.35-2.63) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 70.6 % (70.6-70.7); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 143 (73-143); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 1.35 s (1.35-1.79).

Per-request data: `results.json`.

## Build measured (the part that differs from a stock install)

This machine runs a locally built engine, not a stock download, so the numbers above are not a stock-install expectation. Everything is public:

- Fork: **https://github.com/zsariboga/Strata**, branch `laptop-12gb`; the tuning write-up is in `docs/LAPTOP_12GB_TUNING.md` there.
- Source tree this report was generated from: commit `01fc2c80` (branch `loopbrk-0441`); the running engine is the locally built `v0.1.44-lb2`.
- Patch set on top of upstream: cache-aware routing (`STRATA_CAR_THRESHOLD/BUDGET/SCOPE`), `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR` (+ map / keep-p), `STRATA_TYPICAL_MARGIN/ANSWER`, `STRATA_HC_HOST=1` + `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`, `STRATA_LOOP_BREAK=1`, `STRATA_ADAPT_*` (every 1, 160 swaps, decay 0.9), `STRATA_QSA_SPLIT_ATTN=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`.
- Experts: a **native-experts pack** (`swift-iq3_xxs`, `experts.bin`, built with `tools/iq_pack.py` from the Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next abliterated IQ3_XXS GGUF, iMatrix-calibrated source; mixed per-layer IQ2_XS/IQ2_XXS/IQ2_S/IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS gate/up and Q2_0/IQ4_NL down), so the experts are read from the pack, not from the GGUF.
- Draft: MTP `rt-tr-v2` with the `dv-wide` draft vocabulary, `--mtp-window 4096`, `--mtp-q4 all`.
- KV: `--kv int8`, `--kv-resident 20480`.

## Steady-state decode on longer answers (not part of the suite)

The suite's chat test caps answers at 100 tokens, which is dominated by warm-up (the same machine measured 86.4 tok/s in an earlier run of the same suite, 108.8 here). For a steady-state figure, 30 fixed questions were sent with `max_tokens 6144` and the decode rate was taken from the engine's own `generated in N ms` lines:

- **143.3 tok/s** (6710 tokens over 46.83 s of engine-reported generation), per-request mean 141.3, median 140.1, range 112.9-164.3.
- Correctness on that set: 30/30.

Method and caveats: the questions and the scorer are local to the fork (not part of `tools/strata_bench.py`), so treat this as a same-machine steady-state reference, not as a comparable community row.

## Limitations

- A browser and an editor were open during the run; `strata_bench.py` asks for a quiet machine and this one was not fully quiet. The same suite measured 86.4 tok/s and 108.8 tok/s in two runs 20 minutes apart, which is the size of the noise here.
- Windows power plan was "Balanced" (CPU max 100 % on AC), not a high-performance plan.
- No correctness suite ran with the benchmark; only the local 30-question check above.
- Not tested: `--clients` (concurrency), `--long` (32K prompt), other quantizations, and any comparison against a stock build on this machine.

issues.title: hc_persist_parity.cpp calls POSIX setenv/unsetenv: target does not build with MSVC, ctest reports 2 tests Not Run
issues.author: gputier
issues.body:
## Context

On `main` at 477ac13c (2026-10-16), tag v0.1.45, the Windows build (Release, CUDA 13.4, sm_120, RTX 5090) fails to compile `src/kernels/hc_persist_parity.cpp` with MSVC. Lines 55-56:

```cpp
if (off) unsetenv("STRATA_HC_PERSIST"); else setenv("STRATA_HC_PERSIST", "1", 1);
```

`setenv` and `unsetenv` are POSIX functions. MSVC does not declare them. The compiler reports:

```
hc_persist_parity.cpp(55): error C3861: 'unsetenv': identifier not found
hc_persist_parity.cpp(56): error C3861: 'setenv': identifier not found
```

## Consequence

The `hc_persist_parity` target does not build on Windows. ctest marks `hc_persist_parity` and `hc_persist_default_off` as "Not Run" (CMakeLists.txt lines 1115-1119). The engine itself is not affected, since `STRATA_HC_PERSIST` is off by default. The test was added by cea3d61b, after 0.1.42.

## Proposed fix

The repository already handles this case elsewhere. `set_env` in `src/kernels/decode_cluster_parity.cpp` lines 46-52 calls `_putenv_s(name, value)` under `_WIN32` and `setenv(name, value, 1)` on other platforms. The same guard applies here. On Windows, `_putenv_s` with an empty value removes the variable (documented behavior), so the `--off` case maps to it:

```cpp
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (off) _putenv_s("STRATA_HC_PERSIST", "");
    else _putenv_s("STRATA_HC_PERSIST", "1");
#else
    if (off) unsetenv("STRATA_HC_PERSIST");
    else setenv("STRATA_HC_PERSIST", "1", 1);
#endif
```

issues.title: The prompt-cache pin protects the oldest checkpoint, which is not the system-prompt root when the system prompt is longer than --prompt-cache-every
issues.author: mikhashev
issues.body:
> Strata 0.1.45 (`--serve`, Windows), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, default `--prompt-cache 6`, `--prompt-cache-every 16384`, `--prompt-cache-root 2048`. Read from the 0.1.45 sources and observed in our engine log.
>
> **What the code intends.** `conv_cache.hpp:12-24` describes the chain's root as "in practice the end of the system prompt", pinned so that every new chat of the same client mounts through it. The root checkpoint is placed at the first turn boundary at or after `--prompt-cache-root` on a read from token 0 (`generate.cpp:13313-13325`).
>
> **What the code does.** `eviction_victim` pins index 0, the oldest chain item (`conv_cache.hpp:35-41`). On a read from token 0, the periodic checkpoints are taken during the read (`on_chunk`, `generate.cpp:9265-9325`), before the read reaches the system-prompt end where the root is saved. So when the system prompt is longer than `--prompt-cache-every`, index 0 is the first grid checkpoint (16,384), the pin protects it, and the real root is an ordinary entry that rotates out under least-recent-use.
>
> **Observed.** Our agent client's system message is longer than 16,384 tokens. Over a long conversation, 7 of 7 turn boundaries resumed from exactly 16,384 tokens and re-read 76K–119K tokens (21–35 s each at ~3,500 tok/s). `--prompt-cache-spread` fixed the turn-start case for us (the turn-start checkpoint now survives the turn), so this is not blocking — but the pin still guards a grid point rather than the shared prefix it was written for, and a new chat or a session reset with the same system prompt falls back to 16,384.
>
> **Request.** Pin the checkpoint saved at the system-prompt root explicitly (for example by marking it when it is saved), rather than by position in the chain — or, if the current behaviour is intended, adjust the comment at `conv_cache.hpp:12-24`, which assumes index 0 is the root.
>
> Related: #3088 (same deployment).

issues.title: Per-expert overlay for a native pack, and content hashing for saved sessions
issues.author: mikhashev
issues.body:
> We run Strata 0.1.45 (`--serve`, Windows) with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS as a supervised child of our own agent platform. We want to test whether individual experts carry measurable behaviour — disable or rescale a handful of `(layer, expert)` slots and see what changes. Two things we cannot do ourselves. Everything below is read from the 0.1.45 sources and from our own pack; we have not run a patched model.
>
> **What we found**
> - Our pack has no `experts.bin`, so experts are read from the model's GGUF shard at absolute offsets (`generate.cpp:5408`) and a same-size replacement needs no repack.
> - `native_experts.txt` v3 can name a shard per layer, v4 a different one per role (`gate,up,down`) — an overlay at layer and role granularity already exists.
> - One expert is **three separate byte ranges**, not one blob: `gate_off`, `up_off`, `down_off` are three stacked tensors at unrelated offsets (layer 47: 46.36, 46.69 and 45.89 GB inside the same 47.04 GB shard). `blob_bytes` is their exact sum — the loader refuses any mismatch with the formats (`expert_layout.cpp:439`), so there is no padding to preserve.
> - The load path checks that every `(file, offset)` is the tensor the pack claims, of the pack's type and size (`expert_source.cpp:4602`); nothing hashes the expert bytes at load.
> - The session fingerprint is size + first and last MiB of every file, plus its role name (`conversation_file.cpp:938-987`). In our shard no expert byte falls inside either sample: the earliest expert tensor starts at 755 MB and the last one ends 26 MB before the tail sample. A same-size in-place expert edit is therefore invisible to a saved session.
>
> **Ask 1 — overlay at `(layer, expert)` granularity.** Either extend the shard column, or take a separate file listing `(layer, role, expert) → byte range`, applied over the shard at load, with a printed count of what was replaced. We can patch bytes by hand today; what we cannot do is declare it reproducibly, undo it, and see that it happened.
>
> **Ask 2 — content hashing for saved sessions, for the in-place case only.** A shard named through the shard column, or an added file, is already noticed — by name, size and samples, and through `native_experts.txt` itself. What is not noticed is an edit inside an existing shard that keeps its size. We would like the fingerprint (or an opt-in flag) to cover an overlay manifest and the ranges it touches, so a session saved across an in-place weight edit is refused rather than resumed.
>
> **Question:** is the shard column meant as the supported way to substitute weights, or only for splitting the model across files?

issues.title: My experience updating from 0.1.43.1 to 0.1.45 and possible lessons from it
issues.author: njcray2
issues.body:
System: AMD 7900X, 64GB RAM, RTX 4070 Ti Super (16GB)

I upgraded from 0.1.43.1 to 0.1.45 expecting a performance improvement or no change similar to previous upgrades and so I was surprised when the decode rate fell from 85-95 tokens/s to about 65-75 tokens/s. Still very good compared with other servers but not what Strata had already shown me was possible.

The root cause turned out to be that I need to increase `--vram-reserve-mib` from 700 to about 1600. This reduced the number of experts that can fit in VRAM but restored the performance. The hint to do this was in the log but not immediately obvious unless you have a problem and start looking for it.

And it made me realise that Strata is running on a delicate balance of many options which I am sure many of us cannot keep up with, and some people may be running sub-optimally without even knowing it because Strata can give good-ish results even when misconfigured. I had previously been right on the brink and this release pushed me over the edge.

After that I asked Qwen to read the Strata log and the docs and it came up with many additional good suggestions for my circumstances and gave me an in-depth explanation of what the `--vram-reserve-mib` message meant. It also proactively compared my results against logged community benchmarks to check I was back "in tune".

As Strata gains more and more options and flags it is getting more delicately balanced - especially as everyone has their own different blend of RAM/VRAM/GPU make/SSD performance and so each release can upset something unexpected even with all the pre-release testing.

So here are a couple of suggestions:

1. Provide a prompt as part of the "getting started" info that users can give to their model once it is running that guides it to read the Strata log and the documentation in Strata/docs and offers warnings and suggestions about whether performance is running comfortably (without thrashing/paging etc). This would augment what `--calibrate` can do for you.
 
2. Provide an .md file in the docs folder specifically to help agents do this kind of diagnosis. (Arguably it is not needed given how well they can already diagnose Strata issues from DETAILS.md but the code authors might see ways it is not picking things up from the existing documents that could be very succinctly explained to agents rather than humans. This file could also give actions or references to other docs for each message in the log.)

issues.title: Community benchmark: Strata 0.1.41 vs llama.cpp's new MoE expert cache (--moe-cache-mib), same Coder IQ1_M files, V100-PCIe 32 GB + 16 GB RAM
issues.author: christopherrobertbrooks-tech
issues.body:
llama.cpp added a VRAM expert cache in October (`--moe-cache-mib`, PR #29887), which is close to what Strata does, so I ran both on the same card with the **same two Coder IQ1_M GGUF files** and the same client.

**Hardware:** Tesla V100-PCIe 32 GB (sm_70), PCIe Gen3 x4 (3.3 GB/s), i7-13700KF, 16 GB RAM, model on NVMe. Strata 0.1.41 (resident RAM mode, `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`, `--spec 4` MTP). llama.cpp b11718 (`547208dca`), sm_70, CUDA 12.9.

**Method:** one streaming client for both. Temperature 0, presence_penalty 0, thinking off, 256 tokens out. Prompts of 256/1000/4096 tokens, each with its own first line so neither engine can reuse a prompt. A cold start per setup, 3 runs per size, and the repeats agree within 1%.

| setup | experts on the card | write tok/s (256/1000/4096) | first token, 4096-token prompt |
|---|---|---|---|
| llama.cpp, whole model on the GPU (no cache) | 100% | 42.9 / 42.4 / 41.7 | 9.8 s |
| llama.cpp, `--cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 24000` | 100% (cache) | 35.2 / 37.5 / 37.3 | 13.2 s |
| Strata, no vision, `--spec 2` without the MTP drafter | 100% | 70.9 / 66.7 / 60.4 | 3.4 s |
| Strata, everyday (vision on the GPU) | 95% + 5% RAM | 92.4 / 88.5 / 84.8 | 3.4 s |
| Strata, no vision | 100% | 101.2 / 98.5 / 98.0 | 3.4 s |

- Like for like, Strata writes about 2.4× faster and reads prompts about 2.9× faster. Even without the MTP drafter it writes about 1.5× faster. llama.cpp has no drafter for this model: no MTP head ships in llama.cpp format.
- llama.cpp's cache costs it about 10% against loading normally: 50 graph splits per token against 2.
- llama.cpp cache-size sweep: flat down to 20 GB (83% of the experts, 99.1% hit rate), then a cliff. At 16 GB the hit rate is 96.4% but the traffic is 4×, and writing drops to about 23 tok/s. At 8 GB it falls to about 5 tok/s.
- One model, one card. llama.cpp does better elsewhere (e.g. #2464).

Full data, scripts and per-run replies: https://github.com/christopherrobertbrooks-tech/strata-vs-llamacpp

issues.title: [Question]: GPU-access daemon for sandboxed assistants (bwrap/DSH) — wanted upstream?
issues.author: ken2425pm
issues.body:
Proposal first — the code stays out of the tree until maintainers want it, so this is a question, not a PR.

**The problem**

Assistants running inside a bubblewrap sandbox (DeepSeek Harness / DSH, or any bwrap invocation that mounts a minimal `/dev` on top of a read-only host bind) can never open the GPU: the shadowing tmpfs has no `/dev/kfd` and no `/dev/dri/renderD*`, the sandbox has no capabilities (`CapEff=0`) so the device nodes cannot be recreated and the tmpfs cannot be removed, and the host's real devtmpfs underneath is unreachable. The one thing the sandbox shares with the host is the workspace bind — including Unix sockets created inside it.

**The proposal**

A small host-side daemon that listens on a Unix socket in the shared workspace and

- executes a **whitelist** of GPU binaries on request — each run's combined stdout+stderr lands in a log file inside the same workspace, which the sandbox reads directly;
- additionally manages a resident Strata HTTP server (spawned detached; the sandbox reaches its API over the shared loopback) via a `serve_start` / `serve_stop` / `serve_status` action trio, with per-instance configs and isolated pidfiles.

The daemon's socket lives inside the workspace bind (local to the sandbox pair); the managed HTTP server stays on 127.0.0.1 unless `--api-key` is set, per AGENTS.md.

**Status**

Implemented locally and validated end-to-end on a 2x MI50 (gfx906) box running a ROCm 6.3.3 build — the serving measurements in #3077 (build + runtime + the 12 h split-config soak) were collected through it. It works both from inside a repo checkout and from a copy sitting next to one; every path it resolves comes from its own location and the environment.

**Questions for maintainers**

- Is this in scope for the repo, or better kept as a separate project next to it?
- If in scope: any constraints on the whitelist shape, socket permissions, or whether the serve lifecycle belongs in the daemon vs `serve/`?

issues.title: serve: a tool call is parsed and returned even when the request declares no tools (content state, frontend.py:1285)
issues.author: riverhh76
issues.body:
## Environment

- Strata `main` @ `477ac13c` (fetched 2026-10-19), `--engine strata`, OpenAI-compatible serve
- Models: `swift-1.5-iq3_xxs` and the `qwen3.8-flash-next` family — **model-independent** (see
  "Another observation, not part of the fix")
- Sampling: `{"temperature": 0, "top_p": 1.0, "presence_penalty": 0}` — greedy
- Reproduces on **every** model tested; also present in the released `0.1.45` container image

---

## Summary

`OutputParser` scans the answer for `<​tool_call>` in two states. The scan in the
**reasoning** state is gated on whether the request declared tools; the scan in the
**content** state is not. So a request with **no `tools` field at all** still yields
`message.tool_calls` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` whenever the model writes that
XML — and the function name is never checked against the declared set (there is no
declared set).

A client that does the normal thing — `if (msg.tool_calls): run(msg.tool_calls)` — then
executes calls for tools it never offered. When the client instead *ignores* them because
it offered none, it gets `content: ""` back, i.e. **an empty answer**.

---

## Minimal reproduction

No GPU, no model, no server — the parser alone.

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "serve")
import frontend as F

def call(name, **params):
    body = F.FUNC_START + name + ">\n"
    for k, v in params.items():
        body += F.PARAM_START + k + ">\n" + str(v) + "\n" + F.PARAM_END + "\n"
    return F.CALL_START + body + "</function>" + F.CALL_END

# exactly what the model wrote in the incident below
out = call("get_indicators", curr_date="2026-10-15", indicator="close_10_ema", symbol=600076) \
    + call("get_indicators", curr_date="2026-10-15", indicator="close_50_sma", symbol=600076)

p = F.OutputParser(thinking=False, tools=None, stream_tools=False)
events = p.feed(out)
print([e.call.name for e in events if e.kind == "tool_call"])
print("".join(e.text for e in events if e.kind == "content"))
```

Actual output — `tools=None` was passed:

```
['get_indicators', 'get_indicators']
''            # content is empty
```

`tools=[]` behaves the same. The streaming path reproduces it too: over HTTP with
`stream: true` and `stream_tools` always on (`server.py:4216`), all four subtests of the
regression test below fail on the unpatched tree.

---

## Observed behaviour matrix

Same parser, same model output, varying only what the request declared:

| Request declared | `tool_calls` emitted | `content` |
|---|---|---|
| nothing (`tools` absent) | **2** | **empty** ← wrong |
| `tools: []` | **2** | **empty** ← wrong |
| `tools: [get_indicators]` | 2 | empty (correct — they are real) |
| `tools: [some_other_tool]` | **2** ← names `get_indicators` | **empty** ← wrong |

The last row is a second, independent gap: a request that *does* declare tools still
gets a call to a function that is not in the set. The guard proposed below does not cover
it; it is written up separately under "A second, related gap" because the obvious patch
for it does not work.

---

## Root cause

One line, sitting next to the guarded twin of it:

```python
# :1246  reasoning state — gated
tool = self.buf.find(CALL_START) if self.schemas else -1

# :1285  content state — NOT gated   ← this line
i = self.buf.find(CALL_START)
```

With no tools, `self.schemas == {}` (built at `:887`), yet the content state still
transitions into `"call"` and runs `_finish_call`, which builds the `ToolCall` at `:872`
without ever comparing `name` with the declared names (`:1448-1451` does
`self.schemas.get(name)`, which is `None` and is accepted).

**Why this reads as an oversight rather than a decision.** Every neighbouring path in the
same parser checks something the content path does not:

| path | line | gated on declared tools? |
|---|---|---|
| `rcall` state (a call quoted in the reasoning) | `:1203` | yes — `if name in self.schemas` |
| reasoning-state opener scan | `:1246`, `:1258` | yes — gated on `self.schemas` |
| `json_tool_call` (the `recover` path) | `:829-830` | yes — `obj["name"] not in schemas → None` |
| **content-state opener scan** | **`:1285`** | **no** |

The JSON sibling of the same feature validates the name; the XML path does not.

This also runs against the principle the parser has already been fixed to hold elsewhere:
a `<​tool_call>` that is *quoted* is text, not a call — #1058, #2039, and #700 ("serve: a
`<​tool_call>` named in prose before the real call is content, not a malformed call"). The
rule those fixes established is that text which looks like a tool call is text. Here the
inverse holds: a tool call naming a function that was never declared is still a tool call.

---

## Real-world impact

Production agent (`TradingAgents`) on 600076.SH, 2026-10-15. The technical analyst ran
four tool rounds, then sent a convergence turn that deliberately **omits `tools`** and
appends *"tool call rounds are exhausted, you must not call any more tools"*. The
response was:

```json
{"content": "", "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
 "tool_calls": [{"name": "get_indicators", "arguments": {"curr_date": "2026-10-15",
                    "indicator": "close_10_ema", "look_back_days": 30, "symbol": 600076}},
                {"name": "get_indicators", "arguments": {..., "indicator": "close_50_sma", ...}}],
 "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 7328, "completion_tokens": 172}}
```

The agent writes `content` only when `tool_calls` is empty, so the analyst's report became
the empty string, the data-quality gate graded it **F**, and the final research document
shipped a section reading *(empty)*. A production research pipeline produced a report with
a silent hole in it.

This is not rare, and it predates the current release: our own bench logs from **2026-10-04**
(Strata 0.1.38/0.1.39) already recorded `finish=tool_calls` on requests that carried no
`tools`, twice, noted then as *"occasional tool_calls hallucination"* and attributed to the
model. It is the parser.

Anyone whose convergence/final-turn pattern is "stop calling tools" is exposed — that is a
common and reasonable agent design.

---

## Test gap

`serve/test_server.py:4313 test_auto_absent_and_none_leave_the_tools_to_the_model` is the
test for this case, and it only checks the **prompt** side:

```python
offered = "search the web" in self.tok.decode(self.engine.prompts[0])
self.assertEqual(offered, extra.get("tool_choice") != "none")
```

Its fake engine never emits tool-call XML, so the answer side is never exercised. There is
no test anywhere asserting that a request which declared no tools cannot come back with
`tool_calls`.

---

## Suggested direction

Mirror the guard that already exists at `:1246`:

```python
# :1285
i = self.buf.find(CALL_START) if self.schemas else -1
```

That one line is the whole fix for this report. Measured with the repo's own
`serve/test_server.py` inside the 0.1.45 image (jinja2 3.1.6):

| | result |
|---|---|
| baseline `477ac13c`, with the new regression test | **4 subtests fail** (`nothing declared` and `tool_choice none`, streaming and not) |
| with the guard | **4 subtests pass** |
| full suite, baseline | 337 passed, 482 subtests passed |
| full suite, with the guard **and** the new test | **338 passed, 486 subtests passed** |

The new test is `ForcedToolChoice.test_a_call_the_request_never_offered_stays_text`: a model
that, after `</think>`, writes a complete well-formed call naming a tool the request never
offered. Today that comes back as `tool_calls` with an empty content; with the guard the
whole answer comes back as text, call and all.

The test also pins the case where the request declared *other* tools and `tool_choice: none`
— both must produce text, and both do today only by accident of the first guard being absent.

---

## A second, related gap: an undeclared name, with tools declared

When a request *does* declare tools but the model names a function that is not among them,
the call is emitted anyway:

| request declared | model writes | result today |
|---|---|---|
| `[some_other_tool]` | a call to `get_indicators` | `tool_calls: [get_indicators]`, content empty |

This one is **not** fixed by the guard above, and I want to be precise about why, because the
obvious patch does not work.

`Service.run` always constructs the parser with streaming on (`server.py:4216`,
`stream_tools=True`). With streaming on, the call is consumed by `_scan()` **before**
`_finish_call()` runs (`frontend.py:1395-1408`):

- `_scan()` hits `<function=NAME>` at `frontend.py:1078-1087`, builds
  `ToolCall(name=name, arguments={})` with **no membership check** — `self.schemas.get(name)`
  at `:1085` is used only to read declared parameter *types* — and immediately emits
  `tool_start`, so the client is already told about the call.
- `finish()` (`:1428-1431`) emits the final `tool_call` for that already-announced call.

Adding a name check inside `_finish_call` therefore changes nothing observable over the wire:
by the time it runs, the `tool_start`/`tool_args` chunks are already on the wire and the
client has assembled the call. I confirmed this by measurement — with such a check added, the
response carried **both** the text and a `tool_calls` entry.

The right place is `_scan()` at the `ss == "name"` step (`:1083`): the name is complete there
and nothing has been emitted yet, so an undeclared name can still be refused and the raw text
returned as content. That is a real change to the streaming state machine, so I would rather
raise it than guess at it. Flagging it as a separate item rather than folding it into the
one-line fix above — happy to work on it if you want it in the same PR.

---

## Another observation, not part of the fix

`serve/chat_template.jinja:130-157` renders an assistant message's `tool_calls`
**unconditionally** — that loop sits *outside* the `{%- if tools ... %}` block at `:72`. So a
request that declares no tools, but whose history contains tool-calling turns, puts verbatim
tool-call demonstrations into the prompt:

```
<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

<​tool_call>
<function=get_indicators>
<parameter=indicator>
rsi
</parameter>
...
</function>
</​tool_call><|im_end|>
```

Measured on `swift-1.5-iq3_xxs` with the repo's own tokenizer
(`tools/strata_tokenizer.py` over `/data/packs/swift-iq3_xxs/tokenizer`):

| conversation | `tools=None` | `tools=[one tool]` |
|---|---|---|
| 5-message demo (1 historical call) | 396 tokens | 641 tokens (the tools block adds 245) |
| the real 13-message incident payload | **7364 tokens, 4 verbatim call demonstrations** | — |

The prompt then ends with an **already-opened assistant turn** (`<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n`),
after a final user turn that reads *"Tool call rounds are exhausted. You must not call any
more tools. Write the final report now."*

Greedy decoding on that context continues the demonstrated pattern. That is expected, and it
is not the bug — a model writing `<​tool_call>` after being shown four examples is behaving
reasonably. The bug is that **the parser treats the result as a real call**.

Worth noting that the reasoning-state equivalent is already handled: a call quoted inside the
thinking stays reasoning text (`rcall` at `:1194-1212`, guard at `:1203`/`:1246`). The answer
of a non-thinking turn, or the part of a thinking turn after `</think>`, was not. I confirmed
that split by measurement: the same XML before `</think>` stays text today; the same XML after
it becomes a call.

I am not proposing a change here — the history rendering cannot simply be dropped without
corrupting the conversation — but the trigger is prompt hygiene, not the weights, so
swapping models does not remove it.

---

## What I did not test

- Only the `Content` → `call` path was exercised directly. The `rcall` (reasoning) path
  already gates correctly and was left alone.
- No end-to-end run against a live engine for the fix; the regression data above is the
  parser plus the full serve suite, not a served request.
- Vision and MCP paths u

issues.title: [Windows/NVIDIA 0.1.45] engine 0xC0000005 at strata.exe+0x535c60 (Q4_K CPU dot product reads past a weight buffer), UD-Q4_K_XL with --batch-mtp on a RAM budget
issues.author: dnnspaul
issues.body:
### Summary

`strata.exe` 0.1.45 (ready-made Windows release, CUDA 13.0) crashed twice within three minutes with an
access violation (`0xC0000005`, server: "the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 3221225477)"). The
faulting offset was the same both times. The fault is a **read past the end of an expert weight buffer
inside the CPU Q4_K x Q8_K dot product**, while serving Unsloth `UD-Q4_K_XL` with `--batch-mtp`
on a RAM budget.

### Setup

- Windows 11 Pro, RTX 5090 32 GB (driver 617.14), Ryzen 7 9800X3D (AVX-512), 96 GB DDR5
- Engine 0.1.45 release (`BUILD.json`: cuda 13.0, archs 75/86/89/120, vision gpu), repo at tag `v0.1.45` (477ac13)
- Model: Unsloth Qwen3.8-Flash-Next `UD-Q4_K_XL` (rev 38bb39e), `--compat-bf16` pack, MTP draft layer, vision on
- Engine args: `--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ... --max-context 262144
  --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 1212 --resident-budget-gib 57 --batch-mtp --batch 3`
  (`"parallel": 3`), env `STRATA_HC_Q8=1 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` (written by setup)

### What happened

- Load log with `--batch-mtp`: `strata verify: window up to 8 tokens` (6 without it), and
  `FileExpertSource: WARNING: 91 of 1276 lendable slots (7%) will read their experts from the pack during a long prompt`
  (39 of 1276 without it), `the mapped view of the experts is closed (3 GGUF shards unmapped; every expert outside RAM and VRAM is read unbuffered)`,
  `only 673 MiB of VRAM free at the start of this request (below 1024 MiB)`.
- About 4 h of single-user agent traffic, all on the solo path (no `strata batch` lines at all): sessions of
  ~110-127k tokens with cached follow-ups and resumed prompts of ~50k new tokens.
- Crash 1: the engine log ends after a normal request (`prompt 121481 tokens = 121386 reused + 95 read ... 4125 generated`)
  with no error line; the server restarted the engine on the next request.
- Crash 2: about 2 minutes after that restart, again silent, again after a ~127k-token request.
- Windows Application log, both crashes: `Application Error` 1000, faulting module `strata.exe`
  (timestamp `0x6ad2b51e`), exception `0xc0000005`, **offset `0x0000000000535c60`**.

### Dump analysis (two WER minidumps, available on request)

- Exception record: **read** access (`ExceptionInformation[0] = 0`) at `0xe308e0000` (crash 1) and
  `0xca7168000` (crash 2), both page-aligned, i.e. the read ran from a valid page into an unmapped one.
- Disassembly at RVA `0x535c60` is the Q4_K x Q8_K dot product (ggml-cpu style: `and 0x3f3f3f3f`,
  `0x0f0f0f0f`, `0x30303030` scale unpacking). The faulting load is `vmovdqu ymm5, [rbx+0x20]`, where `rbx` walks
  the **weight** block (`d`/`dmin`/`scales` at `rbx-0x4e..-0x44`). So a CPU expert kernel read a Q4_K expert
  through a buffer that ends early, or through a stale pointer.

### What did not reproduce it

- A scripted repro of the same pattern on the same `--batch-mtp` config: 10 rounds and 49 requests (cold 105-118k
  prefills, cached follow-ups, +50-85k resumed prefills up to 246k). No crash.
- About 3 h of heavier benchmarks without `--batch-mtp` that morning (257k cold prefills, 3-4 concurrent ~240k
  sessions) also had no crash.

### Memory situation at the time (may matter)

The Windows commit limit was 125.6 GiB: 94 GiB RAM plus a 33 GB system-managed page file that never grew.
`strata.exe` held about 106 GiB of private bytes. The engine logged `Windows commit: 4.3 GiB left` at start, and
during our repro requests commit free was **only 0.3-0.8 GiB**. We cannot tell from the dumps whether the faulting
page was part of a mapping, because the WER minidumps have no MemoryInfoList. So a failed allocation or file-view
map whose NULL/short result is not checked is also possible, as distinct from the `0xC0000409` commit-limit exit (#1607).
We have since set a fixed 64-96 GB page file (commit free now ~34 GiB while serving).

### Guess

Something on the solo path that `--batch-mtp` changes, either the 8-token verify window or the larger
uncovered lend region (91 instead of 39 slots read from the file), leaves a CPU expert pointer or length that
does not match the blob actually staged. We have reverted `--batch-mtp` for now (10 rounds of the repro pattern on the reverted config: no crash).
A short `--batch-mtp` re-check with the larger page file (1-4 x 2k, 2-3 x 32k) also ran clean. If more logging would help
(`STRATA_TRACE`, `--stats`), tell us which switches to run with.

issues.author: sroller
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080

Measured on 2026-10-18 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl
- Context: 131072 tokens; parallel slots: 1

issues.title: Decode 2x slower under agent frontends (Windows, RTX 3060 12GB): GPU downclocks to P0 during MoE expert misses — locking clocks recovers ~60%
issues.author: ahsvel
issues.body:
## What do you want to do?
Report a performance finding + workaround for agent-frontend users, and suggest a docs note. Related to #1910 (same family, disk side).

## Setup
- RTX 3060 12GB, Windows 10, 48GB RAM, NVMe
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_xxs (27GB MoE + PLE), engine 0.1.42 (0.1.45 also tested)
- Frontend: Hermes Agent (~12K-token system prompt, tool-heavy multi-turn)

## Symptom
- Web panel decode: ~31 tok/s. Same engine under the agent: 15-16 tok/s.
- MSI Afterburner: core clock jumps to ~2000 MHz during prefill ("reading prompt"), but drops to 850-900 MHz (P0 base clock) during decode, ~15W.
- `--ple-io direct / ram / mmap`: no difference on this NVMe rig. 0.1.45 behaves same as 0.1.42.

## Diagnosis
With a long system prompt, decode is dominated by MoE expert misses: the engine pulls experts from RAM/disk over PCIe, SMs starve, the driver sees low utilization and downclocks to P0 — then every kernel runs ~2x slower. The clock drop is an amplifier of the starvation, not the root cause.

## Workaround
Before launching the engine (admin shell):

    nvidia-smi -lgc 2000,2000

Result: decode 15 -> 25 tok/s (+60%), clocks stay at 2000 MHz during decode, power ~35-80W.
Reset: `nvidia-smi -rgc`; the lock also resets on reboot.

## Suggestion
Worth a note in the Windows setup docs (or an optional launcher flag) for agent-frontend users: if decode is much slower than prefill implies, watch the core clock during decode — locking it may recover most of the gap.

## Caveats
- Single-rig data point.
- This treats the symptom; the root cause is expert-fetch bandwidth (see #1910 for the disk side of the same problem).
- Not recommended for laptops / hot chassis.

issues.title: [Feature]: Windows low-RAM mode (--mmap-experts): let STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT work there - prompt reads are page-fault bound (opt-in patches and measurements)
issues.author: As7656431
issues.body:
**Goal:** on a Windows PC whose RAM cannot hold the experts (low-RAM mode, `--mmap-experts`), read prompts without millions of page faults, and keep the decode's cached experts in RAM afterwards. I have three opt-in changes for this, measured on one PC, and would like to know whether you would take them as pull requests, or prefer another approach.

**The PC:** RTX 5070 12 GB, i5-14600KF, 31.8 GiB DDR4-3600, Windows 10 22H2, model files on an aigo P2000 NVMe (about 1.4-1.6 GB/s). Original Flash-Next IQ2_XS (35.5 GB of experts), `--mmap-experts`, 32K context, `--kv int8`, MTP. Results-only report for 0.1.45 on this PC: #3063.

## What happens

- A 4K prompt reads at 58 tok/s and a 16K prompt at 128 tok/s (0.1.45, `tools/strata_bench.py`); agent follow-up turns wait 48 s for the first token and then decode at 6.4 tok/s.
- With Windows performance counters during a 20K-token prompt (0.1.39), the drive read only 0.2-0.5 GB/s while about 300 MB of RAM stayed available: the stager's copies out of the mapped `experts.bin` are page faults, not drive-bound reads. They also push the decode's cached experts out of RAM, so the answer after a long prompt decodes at 13-19 tok/s, against about 70 tok/s for a warm chat.
- #2004 (RTX 4060 8 GB, 32 GB, Windows 10, IQ2_XS low-RAM) describes the same thing: about 31-36 tok/s on a 9.7K prompt, one stall "with heavy paging of expert file pages". #1520 attacks it from another side (releasing the copied pages).

## Why the existing switches do not cover it

- `STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` is read only in the RAM-budget branch of `generate.cpp`, and `FileExpertSource::open_prompt_direct` is Linux only ("NTFS serves unbuffered reads of a mapped file one at a time").
- `FileExpertSource::prefetch` returns at once unless `staged()`, so a plain mapped `experts.bin` gets no batch prefetch in decode; each CPU expert faults in page by page.
- A RAM budget (`--resident-budget-gib 8` / `14`, 0.1.44.1) reads a 20K prompt in 80 s instead of about 170 s, but decodes at about 14 tok/s on this PC, so it is not an alternative here.

## The changes (on 0.1.44.1; every one off by default)

1. **`STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` on Windows and without a RAM budget.** A Windows branch in `open_prompt_direct` (a second handle on `experts.bin` with `FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`; `read_direct` uses these handles when the tier itself is not unbuffered), the switch honoured in the mmap mode without a budget, and a new `ExpertSource::prompt_reads()` so the stager hands unpinned blobs to `copy_blobs` (8 per batch) without touching `transient()`: the decode and the prompt CPU share behave exactly as before.
2. **`STRATA_PREFILL_DIRECT_RAM=3`.** In that `copy_blobs` path, a blob whose pages are all in the process working set (`QueryWorkingSetEx`) is copied from the mapping; the rest are read through the file cache as merged runs of neighbouring blobs (the standby list still holds many of them). On this PC about 70-77% of the prompt's expert bytes came from the working set and none had to be read unbuffered.
3. **`STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH=2`.** For a plain mapped `experts.bin`, the layer's CPU experts go to `PrefetchVirtualMemory` as one batch on a helper thread (the call costs about 0.2 ms even when every page is resident, so the decode thread does not wait for it).

Together with two switches that already exist: `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=8193` (stream only the routed experts for chunks up to 8,192 tokens) and `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S=180`. About 300 lines in `expert_source.cpp/hpp`, `prefill.cpp` and `generate.cpp`. Built and tested only with CUDA on Windows; the new code is Windows file I/O, not GPU code, but I have not built HIP or SYCL.

## Measurements (same PC, same day, the same settings apart from the switches)

`tools/strata_bench.py` (the 0.1.45 tool as the client), 0.1.44.1 against 0.1.44.1 with the switches, medians of 3:

| | 0.1.44.1 | with the switches |
|---|---|---|
| 4K prompt | 70.7 tok/s, first token 56.9 s | 978.5 tok/s, first token 4.1 s |
| 16K prompt | 95.7 tok/s, first token 167.9 s | 1455.9 tok/s, first token 11.1 s |
| agent follow-up turn, first token | 49.1 s | 5.7 s |
| agent decode | 10.9 tok/s | 66.1 tok/s |
| short-chat decode | 63.9 tok/s | 61.8 tok/s |

The tool's prompts are generated word lists, which probably route to fewer experts than real text and so flatter `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN`. With a real 20K-token English document (four versions in one run, four rounds, a different version first in each round; averages of the four rounds):

| | 0.1.39 | 0.1.44.1 | 0.1.44.1 with the switches |
|---|---|---|---|
| read the 20K document | 173.6 s | 162.5 s | 33.1 s |
| decode right after it | 13.3 tok/s | 17.4 tok/s | 42.0 tok/s |
| a short question after it | 26.0 tok/s | 40.1 tok/s | 65.0 tok/s |
| warm short chat | 54.2 tok/s | 71.3 tok/s | 74.4 tok/s |
| first request after a start | 31.6 tok/s | 41.2 tok/s | 48.1 tok/s |

`STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH=2` alone, four interleaved rounds: first request after a start +22% (4 of 4 rounds faster), a short question after the long document +11% (3 of 4), warm chat +7% (4 of 4), prompt reading unchanged.

## Correctness

The switches change where the bytes come from, not what is computed. Checked with `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` (the logits after the prompt) on an 8K document and a 300-token prompt:

- 8K document: all six runs with switches 1 and 2 (alone and with the existing switches) were bit-identical to one of the two official runs.
- 300-token prompt: the four runs with switches 1 and 2 were bit-identical to the official runs. One of the runs with all switches gave an output no official run gave, but so did the official binary with only the existing `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN` / `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S` switches, and the official binary alone gave three different outputs in seven runs. The extra output is within that spread (KL up to 1.8e-4 against the official outputs, which differ from each other by up to 2.1e-4); the first choice was the same in every run.
- `STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH` only asks the OS for pages ahead of time, so the bytes the pool reads are the same.

So one thing I noticed on the way: the official binary itself is not bit-reproducible between runs on this PC (two runs of the 8K document differ by a KL of 2.4e-3).

## Not tested

Linux; other GPUs; a fast NVMe (your note in `read_direct` measured unbuffered reads of a mapped file at 3.4 GB/s on a PCIe 5 drive; on this drive they still beat the page faults, but on a fast drive the official path is already much faster, see #2791); a RAM budget together with the switches; GGUF-in-place packs; HIP and SYCL builds; output quality beyond the logits check (no change is expected, since the computation is the same).

If this is welcome, I would send three separate PRs (1, 2, 3 above) on top of current main, each off by default with the default path unchanged.

issues.title: Community benchmark: R9700 vs RTX 5060 Ti — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0 at 256K on HP Z4 G4; 3945WX server results
issues.author: AloeKing
issues.body:
Community benchmark report for the same HP Z4 G4 with two GPUs. At approximately 260K input, the R9700 measured 2.75× prefill and 1.50× decode versus the historical RTX 5060 Ti result. The later tuning sweep did not establish a further overall full-window speed improvement.

Benchmark orchestration, data processing, report preparation and sampled static code review were assisted by Codex. The evidence includes per-request measurements, exact paired prompts, generated answers, settings, checksums and review findings.

Measured 17–18 October 2026. I tested both cards in the same HP Z4 G4: i9-10940X (14 cores / 28 threads), 192 GB DDR4-2666 across four memory channels. The R9700 ran at PCIe 3.0 x16; the 5060 Ti ran at PCIe 3.0 x8. This is a host-specific Strata comparison, including CPU/RAM offload.

The deployed model is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0, with a configured 262,144-token total context, int8 KV streaming and 32,768 resident KV cells. Strata 0.1.45 was pinned to commit 477ac13cbe8e582c20484871ce459d20d82df09d; AMD used ROCm 7.2.4. The R9700 results below use a 270 W ceiling. The service retained a 24-logical-core CPU quota, 148 GiB memory cap and no swap. Model weights were unchanged; no expert pruning was enabled.

## Matched comparison — medians of three fresh requests per size

| Input | 5060 Ti prefill t/s | R9700 prefill t/s | 5060 Ti decode t/s | R9700 decode t/s | First token, NVIDIA / AMD (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short | 70.0 | 50.9 | 22.4 | 37.0 | 2.90 / 3.92 |
| ~4K | 217.9 | 472.4 | 21.9 | 34.9 | 18.81 / 8.70 |
| ~16K | 407.0 | 1477.9 | 21.4 | 34.7 | 40.41 / 11.22 |
| ~32K | 536.8 | 1932.4 | 21.8 | 35.2 | 61.22 / 17.06 |
| ~260K | 635.2 | 1744.0 | 20.6 | 31.0 | 409.67 / 149.39 |

The same saved request payloads were used on both GPUs: thinking off, greedy generation, maximum 768 output tokens, natural stopping and zero cached input tokens. Output lengths vary. NVIDIA results are historical measurements on this HP, rather than interleaved reruns.

At about 260K input, the R9700 achieved 2.75x prefill and 1.50x decode; first-token latency fell from 6m 50s to 2m 29s. At about 32K, the ratios were 3.60x and 1.61x. These are per-request phase averages, not dashboard peaks.

## Actual full-window tests with 10,000 output tokens

Each measured request used 252,136 input + 10,000 output tokens, leaving eight tokens within the 262,144 capacity. Input and output share the context window. Three paired requests were completed for each configuration, with zero prompt-cache reuse.

| Configuration | Pooled prefill t/s | Pooled decode t/s | Median first token | Mean total time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Existing 13-worker configuration | 1793.3 | 36.20 | 146.62 s | 417.06 s |
| 21-worker tuning candidate | 1718.1 | 36.74 | 146.94 s | 419.21 s |

The existing configuration completed the three full requests in 402.09–424.94 seconds (mean 6m 57s). Its individual decode averages were 36.7, 35.9 and 36.0 t/s. Pooled throughput means total tokens divided by total measured phase time; it is not an average of instantaneous samples.

The tuning candidate used 21 workers, 192 tasks and adapt-every 8, plus short-chunk CPU sharing. It had slightly higher pooled decode but about 0.52% worse mean total completion time. It was rejected. Forty eligible three-request 65K screening trials were completed, but their apparent winner did not establish an overall full-window improvement. Two trials overlapping a large file copy were excluded and repeated after the copy finished.

These 10K-output requests use synthetic retrieval records followed by long Python reference generation, with temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5 and seed 42. Thinking was disabled and EOS was allowed. They are a different workload from the short-output matched GPU table, so 36.20 t/s must not be divided by the NVIDIA table's 20.6 t/s to claim another matched speedup.

## A useful short-prompt improvement

On the original 13-worker configuration, STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto with STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_MAX=1024 reduced median first-token latency from 3.93 s to 1.58 s. All three paired short requests improved, and all six passed the automatic checks. Mean latency reduction was 59.1%. The inputs were 195–196 tokens and answers were 219–251 tokens. Median total response time fell from 10.19 s to 7.80 s, although output lengths differed. Median decode was 37.0 versus 36.3 t/s: the gain was prompt latency.

Three 252,136-input/1,500-output follow-up screens also completed with that flag. Final confirmation with another three 10K-output requests was cancelled when I stopped testing to return the card. This remains a measured short-prompt improvement, not a fully validated combined replacement configuration.

## Correctness, images and operating limits

All six full-window 10K-output requests passed transport, token count, retrieval/arithmetic, repetition and complete-code syntax checks. Sampled manual review covered 18 initial code examples plus middle/end excerpts and found semantic errors: incorrect edge-case handling, an incorrect interval-intersection assertion, and inaccurate complexity claims. Generated code was not executed. The final incomplete entry at the 10K limit is expected truncation.

Earlier image validation passed four fresh-image tests, one cached image follow-up and two image-plus-long-context requests. A separate earlier document test passed 5/6 requests and 26/27 checked fields; one arithmetic answer was wrong. This shows usable context and image support, with ordinary model accuracy limitations.

At 300 W, one earlier long-context workload reached a 101 C hotspot and triggered the configured 100 C guard; subsequent reported comparison runs used 270 W. The earlier 270 W validation recorded peaks of 75 C edge / 96 C hotspot / 86 C memory and 76 C CPU. Those figures describe that validation interval, not an eight-hour thermal soak. No clocks, voltage or firmware were overclocked.

CPU usage could be raised above the observed 54% by adding workers, but that did not guarantee better completion time. A sampled 25-second full-window generation interval with 21 workers used about 23 logical cores on average without quota throttling. More CPU activity alone was not a reliable optimization target. AMD's missing live PCIe-traffic counter also did not imply a slow link: the saved startup transfer probe was about 13.7–13.8 GB/s on Gen3 x16; it is not an in-request bandwidth measurement.

## Additional server result: RTX 5060 Ti on Threadripper PRO 3945WX

A separate worker completed testing on the owner's AMD Threadripper PRO 3945WX server with 256 GB installed RAM and an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB. AMD here identifies the CPU; the GPU is NVIDIA. Inference ran in a dedicated VM with GPU passthrough and 160 GiB allocated RAM. The service retained a 16-logical-core-equivalent CPU quota, 152 GiB memory limit and 148 GiB memory-high threshold. The benchmark exports do not independently establish the PCIe link mode, so no Gen4 attribution is made here.

The model was again Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0 on Strata 0.1.45, with 262,144 total context, int8 KV and 32,768 resident KV positions. Each full trial processed **251,681 input + 10,000 output tokens**, with zero prompt-cache reuse. There was **one full request per configuration**; model loading was excluded and a short warm-up followed each restart.

| Server configuration | Prefill t/s | Decode t/s | Total elapsed seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| long-baseline | 1040.2 | 25.0 | 642.14 |
| long-candidate | 758.9 | 25.3 | 727.26 |
| long-refined | 1071.2 | 26.5 | 612.95 |

The selected recorded run took **10m 13s**, versus 10m 42s for its baseline: **4.55% less elapsed time** in these single trials. Its launch settings included five CPU workers, prefill 14,848, spec-min-p 0.85, spec 4 and a 1,024 MiB VRAM reserve. The 16,384-prefill candidate was reduced by the engine to 8,192 because its buffers did not fit, and its full-request time regressed.

Earlier short-context confirmation used one 512-output-token request each for coding, explanation and fiction. The geometric mean decode rate rose from **26.51 to 27.66 t/s** (+4.3%) with five workers and spec-min-p 0.7. That earlier profile was subsequently superseded by the long-context 0.85 profile.

**Comparability:** these server trials used different synthetic prompts, temperature 0, a fixed seed and benchmark-only EOS suppression. The HP 10K-output suite used temperature 0.7, allowed natural EOS and had three runs per configuration. The server results are therefore a separate observation, not a controlled HP-vs-server or R9700-vs-5060 Ti speedup. Changes in CPU, VM allocation, PCIe, runtime settings and prompt content are not isolated. The 1,863-entry synthetic input recovered all three check values in each full trial, but the generated handbook was not comprehensively fact-checked. Image support was disabled on this server.

issues.title: RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75) x2: STRATA_SM75_PERF=1 verified bitwise; prefill +46% from 0.1.43.1 to 0.1.45
issues.author: jiuyinssf
issues.body:
## Hardware

- **2× GeForce RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB** (modded VRAM, Turing **sm_75**), PCIe 3.0, **NVLink 2 bridged** (`nvidia-smi topo -m` reports `NV2`: 2 links x 25.781 GB/s = 51.56 GB/s each way, P2P read OK)
- Intel Xeon E5-2673 v3 (12C/24T, **AVX2 only — no AVX-512**), 62 GB DDR3-1866 ECC (quad channel)
- Xuanan X99-TF, Ubuntu 22.04.5, NVIDIA driver 580.167.08, CUDA 13.0

## Software

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Strata | 0.1.43.1 (`a0116b27`) | **0.1.45 (`477ac13c`)** |
| Build | from source, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75` | same flags |
| Toolchain | CUDA 13.0, GCC 12.3, Ninja | same |
| llama.cpp pin | `3cf03257` | `3cf03257` (unchanged) |

The engine was rebuilt for sm_75 with the recorded setup flags; `third_party/ggml` is tree-identical between the two
revisions (`0893b23e`), and the packed model below is accepted by both versions unchanged.

## Model

`SC117/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-GGUF`, **IQ3_XXS** native IQ pack — shard 1 **47.34 GB**, shard 2
28.8 GB. MTP draft layer, BF16 mmproj on the GPU. Context 262144, `--kv int8`, `parallel: 1`.

## Configuration

```
--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <rt>
--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 960 --layer-split auto
```

`env`: `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1`, `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1`

The server raised `--vram-reserve-mib` from 896 to 960 by itself after a low-VRAM warning; with 960 the start reports
**621 / 557 MiB free**, no warnings during the runs below.

## Main result: `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1` is bitwise on a real sm_75 card

The docs say the Turing kernels are *"bitwise equal to the kernels they replace"* but **"nobody on the team has an
sm_75 card to confirm them"**. This is that confirmation.

**Method.** 10 prompts × 3 greedy runs (`temperature: 0`), engine 0.1.45, everything identical except
`STRATA_SM75_PERF`. One engine start per arm.

**Result: 30 of 30 outputs are byte-identical between the two arms, and 30/30 are correct in both.**

Prompts covered single-step arithmetic (23×17, 12×12, 999+1, 1000−1, √144, counting the "r" in *strawberry*), recall
(capital of France, largest planet by volume, mean days per month) and an open-ended explanation of floating point.

### A note on what this test can and cannot show

A fully deterministic baseline is **not reachable with this pack**: the native IQ pack refuses to run without
`--spec ≥ 2` (`this pack is a native (IQ) pack: it needs --native SHARD1, --spec T (T >= 2) and --prefill CHUNK`),
so MTP cannot be switched off. Greedy output therefore varies run to run in a few near-tie positions.

I first suspected the Turing kernels because 1234×5678 changed answer once after enabling them. A control run with
`STRATA_SM75_PERF` **off** reproduced the same instability (`7022752` / `7022772` vs the correct `7006652`), and the
same wrong value appears in both arms. So 4-digit × 4-digit multiplication is unstable at temperature 0 with or
without the Turing series — a near-tie effect, not a kernel difference. I am reporting this because it may interest
you independently of sm_75.

## Speed

Prefill, tokens/s. Each request carried a unique prefix so no prompt cache could help; `max_tokens=1`.

| prompt tokens | 0.1.43.1 baseline | 0.1.43.1 + `BF16_TC`+`SELECT_SIMT` | 0.1.45 + both | **0.1.45 + both + `SM75_PERF`** |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ~2.36 K | 816 | 905 | 913 | **932** |
| ~9.16 K | 1,014 | 1,203 | 1,238 | **1,299** |
| ~36.4 K | 1,669 | 2,051 | 2,120 | **2,254** |
| ~77.2 K | 1,791 | 2,367 | 2,451 | **2,614** |

vs the original baseline: **+14 % / +28 % / +35 % / +46 %**. At 77 K that is 43.1 s → 29.5 s to read the prompt.

`STRATA_SM75_PERF=1` alone adds **+2.1 / +4.9 / +6.3 / +6.7 %** over 0.1.45 with the other two switches — growing
with depth, as the docs predict.

Decode: 63–70 tok/s before, 67–79 tok/s after. **Sample counts here are small (2–5 runs per arm) and the spread
within an arm is as large as the difference between arms, so I would not claim a decode gain.** The docs' +5–6 %
figure is plausible but unconfirmed by my data.

Expert-cache decode hit rate stayed at 99.4–99.9 % throughout.

## Suggestion

1. The bitwise claim for the Turing series holds on real sm_75 hardware for the workloads above. If you want a
   second data point before changing a default, consider asking for more reports; otherwise making
   `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1` the default on 7.5 cards looks safe on this evidence.
2. `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` still lists only `STRATA_BF16_TC=1` for the RTX 20 row, even though `STRATA_SM75_PERF` is
   documented in `DETAILS.md`. A pointer from the support matrix would help people find it.
3. Two sm_75 cards with a layer split work well: 99.4 %+ cache hit, 262 K context, 621/557 MiB VRAM free.

## Reproduction

```sh
cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
      -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75 -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc \
      -DCUDAToolkit_ROOT=/usr/local/cuda-13.0 -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=third_party/llama.cpp
cmake --build build --target strata -j 12
# then the config above, with and without STRATA_SM75_PERF=1 in the config's "env" object
```

Build time on this machine: **2 min 55 s** (153 targets, 12 threads). Binary 0.1.45 is 79 MB vs 0.1.43.1's 59 MB.

issues.title: serve: lifetime token totals + a Codex-style daily activity heatmap in the monitor
issues.author: wangzc1997
issues.body:
The monitor is genuinely lovely. Two small additions around it would let it answer the question I keep getting asked: "how much have I been using this machine?" They share one mechanism — persistent per-day counters — so filing them together.

**1. Lifetime token totals (across restarts)**

The monitor already shows a per-session line under the request list ("Since <boot>: N requests · X prompt tokens read (Y reused) · Z written"), and `/metrics` `totals` matches it — but both restart from zero every time `serve` starts. For a machine that runs Strata 24/7 across many restarts, the number I actually want is the lifetime total: how many tokens this install has served so far.

Suggestion:
- Persist counters in a small JSON in the instance's state directory (prompt_tokens, output_tokens, reused_tokens, requests, plus per-day buckets), merged at startup.
- Expose as `totals_lifetime` in `/metrics` next to the existing session totals; current fields unchanged.
- Show a "Total since install" line in the monitor.

The increment site already exists where `totals` is maintained; the new work is mainly flushing the counters on shutdown / SIGTERM (including Windows terminate).

**2. A Codex-style daily activity heatmap**

The Codex CLI shows a token activity grid: one square per day, weeks as columns, shaded by that day's token count, with 每天 / 每周 / 累计总量 (daily / weekly / cumulative) toggles. It makes usage patterns obvious at a glance, and with the per-day buckets from (1) the data is already there.

![codex-style activity grid for reference](C:/Users/admin/AppData/Local/hermes/cache/images/img_17457ea30be4.png)

**Context**

Until now I reconstruct both by parsing "[strata] done: N tokens" and "prompt N tokens = ..." log lines — workable, but older logs omit the prompt field for small prompts, so those can only be estimated. A first-class counter would be far more reliable, and the heatmap would make the monitor even better than it already is.

Environment: v0.1.44.1, Windows 11.

issues.title: OCm 多进程共享注册主机内存崩溃问题 — 求助描述
issues.author: weakspark
issues.body:
OCm 多进程共享注册主机内存崩溃问题 — 求助描述
环境
硬件:4 × AMD RX 7900 XTX(gfx1100,RDNA3),单颗 EPYC 7K62(48核96线程),128GB DDR4-3200 ECC,NVMe
系统:Ubuntu 24.04.5,内核 6.8.0-147,amdgpu 内核驱动(系统自带,四卡识别正常)
ROCm 用户态:TheRock pip 轮子(装在 venv 内),先后试过 7.10.0a20251120 和 7.14.0a20260612,均复现
应用:Strata 推理引擎 0.1.45(https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata,C++/HIP),LLM MoE 推理,64GB 共享专家池
相关配置:BIOS 未动,内核已试过 iommu=pt ttm.pages_limit=67108864 ttm.page_pool_size=67108864 + amdgpu gttsize=262144(无效)
想做什么(业务目标)
4 个独立引擎进程(数据并行,每个进程独占一张卡)共享同一份 64GB 专家权重:权重放在一个 MAP_SHARED 文件(/dev/shm/tmpfs,也试过 NVMe 上的普通文件)里,每个进程 mmap 后用 cudaHostRegister(hipHostRegister)(base, 64GB, Portable|Mapped) 注册给自己的 GPU,供 PCIe DMA 零拷贝直读。这是 Strata 引擎自带的 --shared-expert-arena 功能(带魔数+哈希头校验,首个进程创建,后续进程验证后映射同一物理页)。

现象
1 个或 2 个进程这样注册 + 跑推理:完全正常(2 进程实测 50.6 tok/s/进程,连续稳定服务)
4 个进程:每个进程都注册成功、装载完成、打印 "session is up",随后在启动尾声(验证窗口/首个 GEMM 分配处)SIGSEGV,四个进程几乎同时崩,受害者随机
3 进程未单独测;2 与 4 之间是分界
没有 3 进程同时就不行的硬证据,但 4 进程是确定性崩溃(多轮复现)
崩溃证据
dmesg(四个进程同一指令偏移,空指针):


text
strata[...]: segfault at 8 ip ...b71c9 ... error 6 in libamdhip64.so.7
gdb backtrace(ROCm 7.10 版,7.14 同样崩但未再符号化):


text
#0-#5  libamdhip64.so.7 内部(无符号,同一偏移 b71c9)
#6  strata::core::Verifier::init(...)   ← 引擎在初始化验证窗口(分配 device buffer / pinned host buffer)
#7  main ()
已排除(全部无效)
去掉 cudaHostRegisterPortable 标志(自打引擎补丁,每进程只向自己的卡注册)→ 仍崩
STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB=27 削减每进程注册量到 25GB(4×25=100GB < 2进程×56=112GB 已验证安全的总量)→ 仍崩(排除"注册总字节超限")
HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0 → 仍崩
tmpfs(/dev/shm) vs NVMe 普通文件做映射后端 → 都崩
ROCm 7.10 → 7.14 升级 → 仍崩
内核 iommu=pt + GTT 256GB(ttm.pages_limit/amdgpu.gttsize)→ 仍崩
RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=infinity 已设;无 OOM(dmesg 干净);内存余量充足(总占用 ~74GB/125GB)
我们的判断
进程内视角 2 进程与 4 进程完全相同(同样的映射+注册+装载),所以触发条件在系统级全局资源上:嫌疑集中在 amdgpu/KFD 驱动对"多个进程注册同一批物理页"的处理——某个内部查找返回 null 未被运行时检查。KFD 每进程队列/doorbell、GTT 表项、IOMMU 映射都查过或调过参,均未命中。

想请教的问题
有没有人见过 ROCm 下多进程 hipHostRegister 同一共享内存映射的类似崩溃或已知限制(进程数阈值)?
KFD/amdgpu 有没有未文档化的参数与此相关(如每进程绑定数、共享绑定上限)?
有没有推荐的诊断手段能进一步定位(amdttd/ROCr tracing、KFD debug 接口等)?
旁路建议:除了"每进程私有拷贝"(内存不够)之外,还有什么办法让 4 个进程零拷贝共享一份大权重给各自 GPU?(GPU一侧的shared memory/peer access不适用——每进程各用一张不同的卡)
English summary (for AMD/ROCm communities)
SIGSEGV in libamdhip64 when 4 processes hipHostRegister the same 64GB MAP_SHARED region (2 processes fine)

4x RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), EPYC 7K62, 128GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-147
ROCm userspace from TheRock wheels: 7.10.0a20251120 and 7.14.0a20260612 both affected
Data-parallel engines, one process per GPU, sharing one 64GB expert-weight pool backed by a MAP_SHARED tmpfs file (also tried a regular file): each process mmaps it and calls cudaHostRegister(hipHostRegister)(Portable|Mapped) on the whole range for zero-copy PCIe reads
With 1-2 processes: registration succeeds, inference runs stable for hours. With 4 processes: all four register OK, reach "session is up", then SIGSEGV almost simultaneously at the next allocation phase (Verifier::init → 5 internal HIP frames → fault at address 8, identical instruction offset in libamdhip64.so.7 in every process, victim varies per run)
Ruled out: Portable flag (registered per-device only — still crashes), registration size cap (4x25GB < proven-safe 2x56GB — still crashes), HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0, tmpfs vs file backing, ROCm 7.10→7.14, kernel iommu=pt + GTT enlarged to 256GB (ttm.pages_limit + amdgpu.gttsize), RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=infinity, OOM (none; plenty of free RAM)
Suspicion: a KFD/amdgpu-side limit or race when N≥3-4 processes register the same physical pages, leaving a null internal descriptor that the runtime dereferences
Questions: known limitation or threshold for multi-process hipHostRegister of shared pages? Undocumented KFD knobs? Recommended tracing to pin it down? Alternative ways for 4 processes (one GPU each) to zero-copy share one large host weight buffer?

issues.title: [Other] Conversation-cache metrics skip events in large log backlogs
issues.author: oscarlius
issues.body:
### Area

Other — Python source server / metrics observer.

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source checkout with the repository CPU fixture/mock engine and a loopback HTTP server.

### What happened

When unread log output exceeds one MiB, the observer advances to the final MiB and loses earlier complete events. A restore followed by enough ordinary output leaves stale parked occupancy.

Expected: Read all complete events after the committed cursor in bounded chunks, retain trailing partial lines, and process appends beyond the captured EOF on the next poll.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally on unmodified upstream production files, then fixed by PR #3338. This is a deterministic source-derived fixture reproduction, not a new real-model failure.

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta, upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`. Fixed candidate: `90ca8acc79242e18f954e71a4c570a4ee8887f41`.

### Graphics card, memory and system

Windows CPU-only regression. No graphics card, VRAM allocation or model weights are needed for the fixture. Python 3.14.3.

### Reproduction

In a disposable checkout of PR #3338, retain the PR's regression tests and restore only its production file(s) to upstream main:

```sh
git restore --source e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211 -- serve/server.py
python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog -v
```

The baseline produces the failure described above. Restore the fixed production file(s) and run the same command:

```sh
git restore --source HEAD -- serve/server.py
python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog -v
```

The candidate passes. Full results, exact tested revision and limitations are in PR #3338. Original reproduction history is retained in the GitHub edit history; this update re-tests the same problem on 0.2.0-beta after the tracker reset.

### Limits

Tests start fresh Python/mock-server processes and use temporary local logs. They do not restart or qualify a live model deployment, induce native allocation/non-finite failures, or establish performance or cross-backend compatibility.
