issues.title: [Bug]: PleReader initialization failures can wait forever for nonexistent reads
issues.author: j-luwierski
issues.body:
### What happened

`PleReader::open()` can hang in its error cleanup before any read has been submitted. Two CPU-only reproductions on freshly fetched upstream main `477ac13cbe8e582c20484871ce459d20d82df09d`:

1. Make `DirectFile::alloc_aligned()` return null by wrapping `posix_memalign` to return `ENOMEM`. `open()` sets `max_inflight` before allocating the slab, then calls `close()` on failure. The free-slot vector is still empty, so `close()` waits indefinitely in `file.wait(..., -1)`. The expected `cannot allocate read buffers` error never returns.
2. Successfully open a reader, close it, then open the same valid file with a table range extending beyond EOF. `close()` cleared the free slots but retained the previous `max_inflight`; the second open reaches the bounds error and hangs in cleanup. Calling `open()` directly on an already open reader has the same problem because it closes first.

Expected: return false with the existing error, close the file, permit repeated close and a later valid open/read.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Latest upstream main checked directly against Niko1221/Strata: `477ac13c` (0.1.45). Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0. Synthetic 16 KiB file and real DirectFile I/O; no GPU or model weights.

### Engine log

The lifecycle regression was compiled against unchanged upstream source and run with a two-second subprocess timeout:

```text
reads caller exit 0
reads threaded exit 0
reopen caller TIMEOUT after 2 seconds
reopen threaded TIMEOUT after 2 seconds
alloc caller TIMEOUT after 2 seconds
alloc threaded TIMEOUT after 2 seconds
```

These are deterministic API/error-path reproductions, not a claim that ordinary model loading exhausts memory. The proposed change delays publishing the slot count until initialization completes and resets it on close.

Searched open issues and PRs for PleReader, initialization, allocation and close. Related #2991 concerns colliding temporary files in a different selftest; #2623 concerns prefetch matching. Neither covers this initialization bookkeeping.

issues.title: [Bug]: strata-gguf --check returns success for invalid architecture and wrapped tensor bounds
issues.author: j-luwierski
issues.body:
### What happened

On upstream main `477ac13c`, `strata-gguf FILE --check` returns exit status 0 for failed checks:

- With `general.architecture=llama`, it prints `architecture guard: FAIL` but returns 0. Missing architecture metadata has the same result.
- For a single F32[1] tensor in a four-byte payload, offset `UINT64_MAX - 3` wraps `payload - offset` to 8. The geometry bracket reports zero failures and returns 0.
- Changing that tensor dimension to `2^62` wraps the F32 byte count to zero and also passes the bracket.

Expected: status 1 for failed architecture checks, out-of-file known tensor payloads and overflowing tensor byte counts.

A regression invoking the real C++ CLI entry point on synthetic GGUFs fails in these four cases on upstream and passes with the proposed fix. It also covers valid files, ordinary truncation and inspection without `--check`.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Upstream main `477ac13c` (0.1.45), Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0. CPU-only reproduction; no model weights or GPU required.

### Engine log

```text
unsupported architecture: FAIL (exit 0, expected 1)
missing architecture: FAIL (exit 0, expected 1)
offset that wraps the last gap to eight bytes: FAIL (exit 0, expected 1)
tensor byte count that wraps to zero: FAIL (exit 0, expected 1)
```

Searched open issues and PRs for strata-gguf, gguf_reader.cpp, architecture checks and offsets. Related #2288 covers the Python reader and #2475 covers the Metal reader; this report concerns only src/artifact/gguf_reader.cpp CLI validation.

issues.title: [Engine] Windows/WDDM: parked-conversation snapshot copies corrupt at 262144 -> all-logits NaN (#879 symptom, separate trigger)
issues.author: denis-1337
issues.body:
### Area

Engine

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Terminal (`serve/server.py` + engine); the fix is built from source.

### What happened

With `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto` and the default checkpoints/prompt cache, after roughly 6–10 unique prompts have parked, the engine logs

```
checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument
```

and every later request fails with "the model's output became non-finite (NaN)". Same config at `--max-context 196608`: clean. Same 262144 with `--prompt-cache 0`: clean. The same model files and settings on Linux on this PC: clean. A reference PC with the same GPU, driver and Windows runs this config on auto without problems, so this is the allocation map on this machine, not a broken driver.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Windows 11, RX 9070 XT, Strata 0.2.0-beta, IQ3_S model.
2. `serve/server.py --engine strata --port 1235 --config <cfg>` with engine args `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4` (default checkpoints/prompt cache, tuning table `tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`).
3. Send 11 unique ~1.5k-token prompts sequentially.

Expected: 11/11 OK. Actual: `OK=0 ERR=11`, engine log shows the checkpoint copy error, 43 non-finite events.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally. Re-tested on 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-19): still reproduces, both on the official install (prebuilt engine) and on a HIP build of the 0.2.0-beta source: `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43.

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (prebuilt HIP engine 0.1.45; the 0.2.0-beta source is engine 0.1.45.3, `src/core/conversation_state.cpp` unchanged from 0.1.45). Also reproduced on 0.1.45.

### Graphics card, memory and system

AMD RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201), i7-8700K (PCIe 3), 64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro build 26300, AMD driver 32.0.32015.2008 (2026-09-28), Intel iGPU drives the desktop.

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S (GSQ-RCO pack), `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4`, hipBLASLt tuning table enabled.

### Logs

Engine: `checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument`. A copy probe added to a 0.1.45 build shows the refused transfer: `conv copy fail: dst=0x275B65060 src=0x400374200 bytes=117669888: invalid argument` — the 112 MB GDN running state, device→host. The error is sticky: the next capture reports `invalid argument` even though the failing call already returned.

### Root cause and fix (PR #3037)

The GB-scale synchronous snapshot copies use heap destinations. On Windows/WDDM the HIP runtime misclassifies C++ heap pointers as pinned host memory: the direct copy is refused (the error above) or, when accepted, interleaves with expert H2D streaming on the copy engine — bytes land wrong, decode windows read garbage as expert weights, and the grouped GEMM writes NaN. PR #3037 stages every synchronous snapshot copy through a real pinned 16 MiB buffer (device→pinned via the copy engine, pinned→destination via memcpy) and passes the copy direction explicitly instead of relying on pointer classification. Opt-out: `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0`.

### Verification on 0.2.0-beta (this rig)

- Unpatched HIP build of 0.2.0-beta source (`main` @ e88ee39d): park-unique 11 prompts → `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43 (bug present).
- Same build with the PR patch: park-unique rounds `OK=11 ERR=0`, 0 non-finite (see PR #3037 Validation for exact rounds).

Note: this issue and the accompanying PR were prepared by an AI agent (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, served by Strata itself) together with the account owner.

issues.title: community test suite reports, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Windows 11)
issues.author: mistral13
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, gfx1151)

Measured on 2026-10-16 / 2026-10-17 by `mistral13`. This is a **configuration-comparison suite**: the same machine
runs three quantizations of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (IQ3_XXS, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, Coder IQ1_M) across many engine
variants, and the variants are ranked against each other. It is a **speed-only** suite — no correctness or recall
check was run. The main limitation is that other programs were running on the machine during the suite (the exact
background load was not recorded), and the storage type and the ROCm/driver version were not captured.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics (Strix Halo APU, `gfx1151`), unified memory: 64.0 GB BIOS carve-out
  + 32 GB shared with system RAM, **108 GB usable by the GPU**. There is no discrete PCIe GPU link — the CPU and the
  iGPU share one memory pool.
- CPU: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395 w/ Radeon 8060S (16 cores / 32 threads, AVX-512)
- Installed RAM: 128 GB  unified memory (64GB RAM; 64GB VRAM)
- Storage: not yet verified (model files are read from disk for the mmap / SSD-backed variants)
- PCIe link: not applicable (APU, unified memory)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Driver / ROCm: not recorded (HIP backend; the prebuilt gfx1151 AMD engine was used)
- Strata: release **0.44.1** (engine 0.1.44.1), **prebuilt release binary** (`engine/strata.exe`, llama.cpp `3cf0325`),
  not a source build
- Background workloads and power limits: other programs were running during the suite; no power limit was set on the
  APU. Background load was not otherwise controlled.

> Version note: the separate report `bench/2026-10-14-community-cpu-qwen3-8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4-xs-2` was made
> with Strata **0.43.0**. Everything in this folder (`2026-10-16_2310`) was made with **0.44.1**.

## Model and configuration

- Models and quantization (GGUF filenames, no repository/revision recorded):
  - `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs` — `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf` + `-00002-of-00002.gguf`
    (the second file is loaded as `--ple-gguf`)
  - `qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs` — `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf` … `-00003-of-00003.gguf`
  - `qwen3.8-flash-next-coder-iq1_m` — Coder IQ1_M pack
- Vision encoder: off (images disabled). Custom profile: `data/expert-profile.bin` (expert-use profile).
- Context: 262144 tokens (256K). KV type: `int8`. KV streaming: on by default (KV cache lives in RAM); the
  `kv-streaming off` variants turn it off. Expert cache: `auto`, sized from the memory the OS can give back.
- Low-RAM mode: `auto` by default; variants use `--low-ram resident` (experts the GPU cannot hold are copied into RAM
  once) or `--low-ram mmap` (experts read through the OS file cache). Unsloth default keeps ~36 GiB of experts in RAM.
- MTP: draft layer `rt` (`--mtp rt`), `--spec 4`. Reasoning/thinking: **off** for the suite. Sampling: temperature 0.
- Calibration: run per model (`START-HERE.bat --calibrate`), which sets `--pcie-frac`, `--spec-min-p`,
  `--adapt-every`, `--adapt-swaps`, `--adapt-decay`. Experimental speed projection: **not used**.

Exact launch commands (paths shortened to the Strata folder; no credentials). Each variant edits these; the exact
per-variant command is in that variant's `config-used.json` and its own `README.md`.

```text
# iq3_xxs — install default (strata-iq3_xxs.json, as START-HERE left it)
strata.exe --pack packs/iq3_xxs \
  --native models/IQ3_XXS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf \
  --ple-gguf models/IQ3_XXS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf \
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto \
  --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp mtp/rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8
  env: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt

# unsloth-ud-iq4_xs — install default
strata.exe --pack packs/unsloth-ud-iq4_xs \
  --native models/unsloth-UD-IQ4_XS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto \
  --spec 4 --mtp mtp/rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 \
  --resident-budget-gib 36 --spec-min-p 0.5
  env: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt

# example variant: iq3_xxs --pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts (low-ram mmap)
  ... --pcie-frac 1.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97 \
  --pool-workers 6 --mmap-experts
  env: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1151-hipblaslt-100500.txt, STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1
```

## Method

Driven by a test suite I wrote (`suite/`, `suite/strata_suite.py` + `suite/suite.toml`), which is included with this
report. For every model the suite runs `START-HERE.bat` (setup, `--no-start`), then `START-HERE.bat --calibrate`
(per-model tuning, 15–30 min), then `BENCH.bat --long` against the HTTP API of a Strata server started from that
variant's config. Model loading is not timed. There is a 90 s cooldown between runs, and a stale engine is killed
before each step.

`BENCH.bat` runs `tools/strata_bench.py --long`: 3 runs per test, medians with ranges. Speeds are the engine's own
timings (`prompt_per_second`, `predicted_per_second`); first-token time and latency are measured by the client over
HTTP. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt carries a unique tag, so the fresh-prompt
tests never get help from the conversation cache.

- short chat: three questions, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K / 32K prompts: fresh word-list prompts (~4,096 / 16,384 / 32,768 tokens), 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt + four tools, then 5 turns that each add ~1,500 words of a project file and continue
  from the model's own earlier answers (how agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions;
  cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)

Peak RAM and peak GPU memory are sampled by the suite during the run (Windows only, includes model load): `peak_ram_gib`
is process RAM, `peak VRAM` is the GPU's dedicated memory, `expert cache GiB` is the GPU expert-cache size. The
memory/utilization notes below are separate Task Manager readings taken by hand during representative runs.

## Results

Ranked by chat decode (primary). `*` = variant that changes numerics (output not bit-identical — quality not verified).
Per-run detail (actual prompt tokens, reused tokens, generated tokens, runs, medians and ranges, TTFT, agent cache)
is in each variant folder's `README.md` and `results.json`; engine start-up lines are in `engine-log-excerpt.txt`.

| # | run | chat tok/s | agent tok/s | 4K pp | 16K pp | 32K pp | 32K TTFT s | peak RAM GiB | peak VRAM GiB | expert cache GiB |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts low-ram mmap | 38.2 | 42.7 | 548.1 | 565.2 | 550.9 | 58.3 | 41.5 | 53.1 | 40.0 |
| 2 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts | 37.7 | 42.3 | 548.5 | 566.9 | 547.6 | 58.6 | 41.5 | 53.1 | 40.0 |
| 3 | iq3_xxs:--mmap-experts | 35.5 | 37.5 | 593.0 | 615.1 | 549.7 | 58.4 | 41.6 | 53.3 | 40.0 |
| 4 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 | 35.5 | 40.8 | 566.5 | 597.2 | 579.2 | 55.4 | 41.5 | 29.2 | 16.0 |
| 5 | iq3_xxs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 host-core last | 35.4 | 60.9 | 552.6 | 571.1 | 558.0 | 57.5 | 41.4 | 29.2 | 16.0 |
| 6 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--pool-workers 6 | 33.3 | 32.2 | 323.9 | 348.7 | 339.4 | 94.5 | 12.5 | 62.3 | 55.4 |
| 7 | iq3_xxs:low-ram mmap | 33.1 | 35.6 | 544.7 | 565.9 | 551.2 | 58.2 | 41.5 | 53.3 | 40.0 |
| 8 | iq3_xxs:--mmap-experts mmap | 33.1 | 33.7 | 543.1 | 561.5 | 546.1 | 58.8 | 41.5 | 53.3 | 40.0 |
| 9 | iq3_xxs:low-ram resident | 32.9 | 36.9 | 549.4 | 564.6 | 549.4 | 58.4 | 4.1 | 53.3 | 40.0 |
| 10 | iq3_xxs:low-ram mmap host-core last | 32.7 | 35.4 | 552.2 | 573.9 | 558.5 | 57.5 | 41.5 | 53.3 | 40.0 |
| 11 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 | 32.4 | 37.7 | 348.7 | 354.9 | 343.2 | 93.5 | 12.5 | 62.1 | 55.4 |
| 12 | unsloth-ud-iq4_xs:resident-budget-gib 36 | 32.0 | 34.7 | 318.0 | 351.4 | 340.5 | 94.2 | 12.5 | 62.3 | 55.4 |

`pp` = prompt tok/s at that prompt length. Full ranking views (by 16K prompt, by agent decode, by peak RAM) are in
`ranking.md` / `ranking.csv`; variant-vs-default diffs are in `comparisons/`.

### Memory and utilization observations (Task Manager, hand-read during representative runs)

These are my own readings, not engine timings. "Shared GPU Memory" is the system-memory-backed GPU allocation,
"VRAM" is dedicated GPU memory. CPU figures are per-core load during prefill vs generation.

| Config | RAM used | Shared GPU mem | VRAM | Prefill (CPU / GPU / disk) | Generate (CPU / GPU / disk) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iq3_xxs default (install config) | ~80% | 41 GB | 26 GB | core 0 100%, small use on 2–7 & 10–15 / ~90% / none | even cores 0,2,…,30 100%, odd cores 1,3,…,31 0% / ~90% / none |
| iq3_xxs --pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts | ~80% | 1 GB | 50 GB | core 0 100%, peaks 2–7 & 10–15, rest 0% / ~95% / none | core 0 100%, peaks 2–7 & 10–15, rest 0% / ~95% / none |
| iq3_xxs --pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 host-core last | ~80% | 40 GB | 27 GB | core 0 0%, some on 1, peaks 2–7 & 10–15, rest 0% / ~95% / none | peaks on 0–15, rest 0% / ~98% / none |
| iq3_xxs low-ram mmap | ~80% | 1 GB | 51 GB | core 0 100%, higher peaks 2–7 & 10–15, rest 0% / ~98% / none | core 0 100%, peaks 2–7 & 10–15, rest 0% / ~80% / small |
| unsloth-ud-iq4_xs default | ~10 GB | 10 GB | 63 GB | core 0 100%, all 1–31 100% with short 0% dips (incl. hyperthreads) / ~98% / small | core 0 100%, peaks 2–15 (and 2–7 & 10–15), rest 0% / ~80–85% / small |

decode almost single-threaded on core 0; the resident / `host-core last` variants keep the expert cache in shared
memory (high shared, low VRAM) and spread load across cores. Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS fills VRAM (~62–63 GB) and uses little
process RAM (~10–12 GiB).

- Fastest chat decode: `iq3_xxs` with `--pool-workers 6 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 --mmap-experts` (38.2 tok/s chat,
  42.7 tok/s agent).
- Best agent decode: `iq3_xxs ... host-core last` (60.9 tok/s) — moving the host core to the last core helps the
  agent (cache-heavy, multi-turn) workload most.
- Fastest prompt ingestion by far: `coder-iq1_m strix-prefill-switches` (842 / 940 / 950 tok/s at 4K/16K/32K, 32K
  TTFT 33.8 s) — but it changes numerics, so quality is unverified.
- Lowest process RAM: `iq3_xxs low-ram resident` (4.1 GiB) — experts copied into RAM once, no mmap churn.
- Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS is the slowest to prompt (322–355 tok/s, 32K TTFT ~94–100 s) because most experts come from disk.

issues.title: serve: disk durability for parked conversations (saved conversations)
issues.author: whitespades
issues.body:
**The ask**: make the conversation cache durable - write each parked conversation's state snapshot to disk (opt-in path) and load it back at start-up, so an engine restart costs seconds instead of a full prompt re-read.

**Why it matters (live setup: RTX 3090, IQ3_S, 262k context, engine 0.1.45)**: an agent client (DSH) is stateless and resends the conversation every turn; conversations run 100-140k tokens. Parking + restore works superbly: 131k tokens restored in ~1 s, 93% of all prompt tokens reused across 30 requests, 1 conversation parked. But the snapshot is RAM-only and dies with the engine. Every config change, engine update, reboot pays a full read: `prompt 102104 tokens = 0 reused + 102104 read in 51247 ms (1992 tok/s)`, and 62 s for 132,828. Long agent sessions start from zero after every restart.

**Why it fits Strata**: the pieces already exist. Parking already serializes exactly the state that matters (KV block tier, GDN conv history and recurrent state, position, live tokens + image keys), and the KV streaming tier already moves whole blocks between VRAM and system RAM. The durable version swaps the RAM arena for files - the match rules (live tokens, image keys, min-tokens) can stay as they are.

**Prior art**: llama.cpp's slot-state save/load, shipped as "Saved conversations" in professorpalmer/mirai-s-ada (bundle-20261017b): with `MIRAI_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` set, a 245k-token conversation is back in ~10 s instead of a 524 s re-read, a 128k document answers in 6.7 s after a restart (199 s cold), the saved K/V (VRAM part + pinned-RAM part + draft state) reloads in seconds and reads only the new turn, same answers byte for byte; the file set is pruned above 20 GB. vLLM's prefix-cache CPU/disk tier follows the same shape.

**Rough sketch**:
- Opt-in in the config's args: `--conversation-cache-save PATH` (save at park and/or on shutdown; a `--conversation-cache-save-max-gib N` quota pruning the oldest files, as the 20 GB rule does).
- File content: the parked snapshot (int8 KV blocks, GDN history/state, position, live tokens, image keys) plus a model/engine fingerprint so a stale or mismatched file is refused at load.
- At start-up: warm the slots from disk in the background; a request whose prompt extends a saved prefix restores from disk like from a park (the "1 s for 131k" path).
- Size on this family: int8 KV is cheap - 12 attention layers x 2 x 256 B/position ~ 6 KB/position, plus a few MB of GDN state per conversation: 131k tokens ~ 0.8 GB, 262k ~ 1.6 GB; NVMe load ~1-2 s. Fits the RAM budget the conversation cache already uses.

**What it does not solve** (worth stating so expectations stay right): a prefix rewrite. A client that rewrites its history at the head of the conversation invalidates every stored K/V after the change point (the vectors encode the old content), and no storage tier changes that - the spread prompt cache covers shallow rewrites; durability covers restarts. The two features are complements.

issues.title: Tensor parallel (--tp 2) on 2× RTX 3080: patch attached, correct but not usable yet (~2 % of the layer split's prefill) — open for pickup
issues.author: ZeaMQ
issues.body:
> **Status: not usable yet.** `--tp 2` is correct on every path that works, but it runs at **~2 % of the layer
> split's prompt throughput**, and its fast path (860–990 tok/s) produces `non-finite logits` from the first QSA
> layer on. **Do not run this in production.**
>
> This is an **open handover, not a submission**: the perf breakdown and the correctness bug are the useful part,
> and what is left is written down below. It is **not** a request to the maintainers — #156 was closed as *not
> planned*, and these numbers support that decision. It is a starting point for anyone who wants to continue it.

**Patch:** branch `tp2-wip` — https://github.com/ZeaMQ/Strata/tree/tp2-wip (head `e771f5cb`, on top of `296b59d2`, engine 0.1.44.1)
**Write-up:** `docs/TP2-HANDOVER.md` (English) / `docs/TP2-HANDOVER.zh-CN.md` (中文)

**If you want to pick it up, read [The three steps I would try next](#the-three-steps-i-would-try-next) first.**

---

# TP=2 (tensor parallel) is correct but slower than the layer split; its fast path is broken — handing over



I spent a long session adding `--tp 2` to a CUDA build of 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`) on 2x RTX 3080 20 GB and I am

posting this as a **half-finished** attempt rather than a PR, because the honest result is: it works, and it is

slower than what you already have.



## Relation to #156



This follows up **#156** ("support tensor parallelism for multi gpu setup"), closed 2026-09-30 as *not planned

for now: decode is limited by the experts, so tensor parallelism of the dense part gains little here*. I built

it to get the measurement that thread did not have, and **the numbers support that decision**: the correct TP

path lands at about 2 % of the layer split's prefill throughput (37–52 vs 2 114.8 tok/s), with host grouping

at 47.8 % of the TP prefill and the TP reduce at another 16.2 %. So please read this as evidence for closing

it, plus the two real bugs found on the way — not as a request to reopen it.



## What happened



- `--tp 2` with the prompt read through the two-rank verify windows is **correct at every length I tried**

  (108 / 3 458 / 6 856 / 14 060 prompt tokens, all read in full, no non-finite logits), and VRAM lands at

  **19 909 / 19 867 MiB**, the same as the layer split on this pack.

- But prompt throughput on that correct path is **37–52 tok/s**, against **2 114.8 tok/s** for the layer split

  on the same machine, same pack, same day. Decode 43–58 tok/s against 99.3.

- The fast path (one batched prefill, `STRATA_TP_FASTPROMPT=1`) does reach **860–990 tok/s** but produces

  `non-finite logits (#879)` from the first QSA layer on, for any prompt larger than one KV page. So it ships

  disabled, with the windows as the TP default.



## Strata version, GPU, OS



Strata **0.1.44.1**, base commit **`296b59d2`** (2026-10-14) · 2x RTX 3080 20 GB (PCIe 4.0 x8) + Quadro P1000

for vision · Windows 11 (10.0.26200) · Ryzen 9 5900X, 80 GiB · CUDA source build.



**Provenance:** AI-assisted, not human-reviewed; the fast path below survived thirteen fix attempts unsolved.

This is a bug report with a patch attached, not a submission.



## Engine log



```

strata serve: non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window at position 6851 (row 0): its tokens are not emitted

strata serve: prompt 6856 tokens = 0 reused + 6851 of 6856 read in 7972 ms (859.4 tok/s), 0 generated

strata dbg gdn: layer 3 qsa attn       583872 of 635904 non-finite (max |x| 2.288e+06)

strata dbg gdn: layer 3 qsa bo(reduce) 527360 of 529920 non-finite

strata dbg gdn: layer 3 staged=1 kv_mode=1 page_size=4 s.n_head_kv=2

```



## Where I got to



- Queries are fine (`qsa q(in)` clean); the attention output is not, so the QSA layer reads wrong KV cells.

- The GDN block's own counts and state offsets are correct; the MoE non-finite is downstream.

- `page_size` is 4 (not 64) and `staged=1` — the prompt attention reads the staged pool with `m.ident_table`.

  I had assumed 64 for most of the session, which invalidated a dozen hypotheses.

- Page-stride changes in both directions were tried and reverted: writer `page*2` / reader `page*1` gives

  92 % non-finite, writer `page*1` / reader `page*1` gives 100 % - so the write side is not the lever.

- Two real defects were found and fixed on the way: the QSA query stride (packed at `qh*256`, read at the

  model's 6144) and the expert-cache sizing (fixed 3/4 shrink threw away 1.83 GiB; that fix alone is what

  puts the card at 19.44 GB).

- `STRATA_GDN_KEYHEAD=0` is currently **required** in TP: `gdn_rec_kh_kernel` is not parameterised and still

  uses the model's full HV/HK.



## The three steps I would try next



1. Print `kv_append_kernel`'s `row_id` for the first 8 staged cells and `prompt_attn_kernel`'s `r` for the same

   cells, and diff them.

2. Dump `m.ident_table` (`prefill.cpp:1204`) and confirm `ident[i] == i`.

3. Re-derive with `page_size == 4`.



## What I did not test



CUDA only — no HIP or SYCL build (AGENTS.md asks for all three). One machine, one pack, one model. No

50K–100K measurement, no recall/needle suite, no bitwise single-card regression against `HEAD`, no soak.



## Licence and prior art



Strata is MIT (c) 2026 Niko1221 and the Strata contributors; this report asserts no warranty and claims no

fitness. Model weights / native pack / expert profile are separate artifacts and are not included. No

credentials are included.



This work's tensor-parallel rules were written against **llama.cpp / ggml**, which Strata already carries as

a pinned, gitignored dependency (`third_party/`, `.gitignore:31`). Both are verbatim **MIT**, copyright

(c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors, and neither is redistributed with the source. Strata cites them inline with

`file:line` — `shard.hpp` cites `handle_mul_mat:600-603`, `GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_PARTIAL:591-593` and the

qwen4exp shapes at `qwen4exp.cpp:242-247`. If review finds a function that is an adaptation rather than a

reimplementation, the ggml notice goes beside it.

issues.title: Official v0.1.45 runs NVFP4 but is ~17% slower than the strata-nvfp4 branch (type-40 experts not covered by EXPDEC/B6; no w4a4x2 prefill)
issues.author: wangzc1997
issues.body:
## Summary

Official Strata v0.1.45 runs our existing NVFP4 GPTQ model out of the box (no re-download/conversion, all three APIs + tool calling pass), but decode throughput sits **~17–21% below the community `sergqwer/strata-nvfp4` branch**, and the 5 CUDA toggles only recover ~5.8% on the 32K-prefill case. Two kernel-coverage gaps explain most of it:

1. **EXPDEC / B6 expert kernels do not cover type-40 (NVFP4) experts.** EXPDEC gate/up currently covers IQ types (16/17/18/21/22…), and our model's NVFP4 experts are type 40 — the engine log literally prints `gate/up type 40 not covered`, `down type 40 not covered`, falling back to the stock NVFP4 expert kernels. See [iq_kernels.cu#L3288](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/v0.1.45/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu#L3288) and [native_mmvq.cu#L1315](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/v0.1.45/src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.cu#L1315).
2. **No `w4a4x2` Blackwell prefill path.** The branch defaults to a two-FP4-product `w4a4x2` MoE prefill on Blackwell ([moe_mmq.cu#L257](https://github.com/sergqwer/strata-nvfp4/blob/v0.1.44.1-nvfp4.2/src/prefill/moe_mmq.cu#L257)); official offers only w4a8/w4a4/fp16 with w4a8 default ([setup.py#L201](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/v0.1.45/setup.py#L201) confirms the model itself is officially supported).

So newer version ≠ strict superset in performance for NVFP4 models.

## Environment

- Windows 11, RTX 5090 32GB (single GPU), Core Ultra 9 285K, 192 GiB DDR5-5600
- Model: `Maximilian228/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-GPTQ-Strata` (dense GGUF + FP8 PLE + BF16 embedding + NVFP4 experts.bin, type 40), same files reused across all three runs
- Runs compared: **A)** community branch `v0.1.44.1-nvfp4.2` (current daily driver), **B)** official v0.1.45 with settings migrated from A, **C)** official + the 5 CUDA toggles (`STRATA_ATTN_DAILY`, `STRATA_QSA_ROWS`, `STRATA_SIDE_MIXER`, `STRATA_EXPDEC`, `STRATA_B6_MMVQ_ROWS`)
- Method: temp 0, fixed seed, thinking off, prompt cache cleared per request, 512 output tokens, n=3 per case. First pass with automatic PCIe split showed official still warming up (fraction drifted 0.25→0.5), so the re-run below fixes `strata_tune.pcie_frac=0.5` after warm-up on both Chinese and English.

## Results (medians of 3, warmed, PCIe fraction fixed at 0.5)

| Case | Branch (A) | Official (B) | Official+CUDA (C) | C vs B | C vs A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short zh decode | 162.1 | 132.0 | 133.9 | +1.4% | −17.4% |
| Short en decode | 157.6 | 124.3 | 124.1 | −0.2% | −21.3% |
| zh decode after ~32K prefill | 161.2 | 126.2 | 133.5 | +5.8% | −17.2% |
| 32K prefill speed (tok/s) | 7,793.5 | 6,339.0 | 6,339.3 | ~0% | −18.7% |

## Feature requests

- Extend EXPDEC / B6 coverage to type-40 NVFP4 expert tensors (gate/up/down), so `STRATA_EXPDEC` actually applies to officially-supported NVFP4 models instead of silently logging `type 40 not covered`.
- Port the `w4a4x2` Blackwell MoE prefill (or an equivalent two-FP4-product path) into official, since 32K prefill is ~19% behind the branch today.
- Optional: a short note in [docs/NVFP4.md](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/v0.1.45/docs/NVFP4.md) listing which toggles do/don't affect type-40 experts, so users don't expect IQ3_S gains on NVFP4.

## Caveats

This is a whole-stack A/B/C comparison, not a per-kernel ablation: the community engine is built with CUDA 13.3 vs official 13.0, prefill paths, default fusions and auto expert-cache slot counts differ. Benchmarks run with thinking disabled; daily medium-thinking behavior may differ. Compatibility (not quality) was verified across OpenAI Chat / Anthropic Messages / Responses + tool calls on all three runs; image input and full task quality were not A/B'd.

issues.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 2x RX 7900 XT layer split + --resident-experts (0.1.45,Q2_0):16K–100K prompt prefill stalls (watchdog #29), GPU reset / device lost
issues.author: Wuqiyang312
issues.body:
### What happened

Running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 on two RX 7900 XT cards with `--resident-experts` and a layer split. Short prompts work; **every long prompt I tried hangs during prompt prefill** (16K, 40K and 100K tokens). Two outcomes:

1. The prompt watchdog fires and the engine stops itself:
   `no progress for 60 s ... waiting for the GPU (attention, router) at layer N of the prompt chunk from token M` (issue #29).
2. The kernel then tries to reset the GPU and fails: `MES failed to respond ...` -> `GPU reset begin!` -> `device lost from bus!` -> `GPU reset end with ret = -19` / `GPU Recovery Failed: -19`. Both cards can end up in this state; only a host reboot recovers them.

The same model and engine on **one** card are stable at 128K, including a 100K-token prompt.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

- Engine **0.1.45** (HIP backend)
- 2x AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (Navi 31, gfx1100, 20 GB each); an RTX 4060 Ti is present but not used by Strata
- Debian 13, kernel **6.12.113+deb13-amd64**, ROCm **7.1.1**, HIP 7.1.52802
- Container: `rocm/pytorch:rocm10.1.0_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.14.0`
- CPU/RAM: Ryzen 5 7500F, 30 GiB RAM, 178 GiB swap
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 (62 GB model + 38 GB expert pack + 6.5 GB MTP), `--resident-experts`

### Exact flags (conservative run that still failed)

```text
--serve --pack <.../packs/q2_0> --native <...Q2_0-00001-of-00002.gguf>
--ple-gguf <...Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf>
--expert-profile <.../data/expert-profile.bin> --expert-cache auto
--prefill 4096 --pcie-frac 0 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <.../mtp/rt>
--max-context 65536 --vram-reserve-mib 1024 --kv int8 --resident-experts
--layer-split auto
```

Config: `"gpu": [0, 1]`, `"layer_split": "auto"`, `"backend": "hip"`,
`"STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN": "0"`, `"HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM": "0"`.
The engine started with layers 0-24 on CUDA0 and 25-47 on CUDA1; the two caches
held 11606 and 10550 experts; 6.65 GiB were resident in RAM (pageable); 798 MiB
(CUDA0) and 846 MiB (CUDA1) of VRAM were free.

Two earlier runs used the same setup without the conservative flags:
`--prefill auto`, no `--pcie-frac`, no `--vram-reserve-mib`, `--max-context 131072`.
The first of those had 21894 cached experts (11503 + 10391, ~99.7% of the routed
mass), 10.00 GiB resident, and 474/522 MiB free.

### Reproduction

1. Start the server with the config above.
2. Send a short prompt: it answers normally.
3. Send a prompt of ~16K tokens (the conservative run) or ~40K/100K (the 128K runs).
4. At some point during prefill the engine stops making progress. After 60 s the
   watchdog aborts it; in the 128K runs the kernel then fails to reset the GPU.

I used generated filler text (`"the " * N`) with a short question at the end, sent
through `/v1/chat/completions`; nothing else was running on the box.

### Logs

Full engine log and server log are available (63 KB `strata-q2_0.log`, 2 KB
`server.out`); the key lines are below. dmesg timestamps are UTC.

**Conservative run (64K, 16K-token prompt):**

```text
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched):
waiting for the GPU (attention, router) at layer 29 of the prompt chunk from token 0)
- stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
```

**128K run, 40K-token prompt (memlock raised to unlimited):**

```text
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched):
waiting for the GPU (attention, router) at layer 12 of the prompt chunk from token 16384)
- stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
```

**Kernel, 128K run with a 100K-token prompt:**

```text
amdgpu: init_user_pages: Failed to get user pages: -1   (846 times at engine start)
[gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:24 vmid:8 pasid:126)
  in process strata pid ... thread strata pid ...
  in page starting at address 0x00007fcb300be000 from client 10
GCVM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_STATUS:0x00801031
  Faulty UTCL2 client ID: TCP (0x8)
  PERMISSION_FAULTS: 0x3
MES failed to respond to msg=SUSPEND
failed to suspend all gangs
MES might be in unrecoverable state, issue a GPU reset
GPU reset begin!
device lost from bus!
GPU reset end with ret = -19
GPU Recovery Failed: -19
```

The engine printed the matching userspace error:

```text
Memory access fault by GPU node-1 ... on address 0x7fcb300be000.
Reason: Page not present or supervisor privilege.
```

**Kernel, 128K run, 40K-token prompt** (after `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` was raised to
`unlimited`; `init_user_pages` still failed 1814 times at start):

```text
SMU: response:0xFFFFFFFF ... message:TransferTableSmu2Dram?
Failed to export SMU metrics table!
MES failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE
failed to remove hardware queue from MES, doorbell=0x1008
MES might be in unrecoverable state, issue a GPU reset
GPU reset begin! / device lost from bus!   (14 reset + device-lost pairs)
```

### What I tried / ruled out

- **P2P:** `rocm-smi --showtopoaccess` reports `GPU0 -> GPU1 = False`; RDNA3
  consumer cards do not expose P2P here. The cards are behind a Broadcom
  PEX880xx PCIe Gen4 switch sharing one x16 uplink, so card-to-card traffic
  also has to go through the host. The engine's link probe reports
  `CUDA0 link -1.0 GB/s -> miss cost x1.00` (same for CUDA1).
- **memlock:** raised the server process to `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=unlimited`; the
  watchdog/GPU failure persisted and `init_user_pages` kept failing.
- **PCIe pressure:** `--pcie-frac 0` (no PCIe expert fetches) did not help.
- **Prefill chunk:** `--prefill 4096` did not help; the stall moved from
  layer 12/token 16384 to layer 29/token 0.
- **VRAM pressure:** `--vram-reserve-mib 1024` left 798/846 MiB free; still hung.
- **Host-page reclaim workaround:** `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` (as in #1705)
  did not help on this machine.

### Single-GPU baseline (same model, same engine)

- 128K context, one card: a 100,078-token prompt is accepted and answered
  correctly; prefill 92.3 s (1084 tok/s); decode 69.7-72.8 tok/s; a repeat of
  the same prompt hits the prompt cache (100,073 tokens reused, 0.96 s).
- Short chat: ~49.8 tok/s end to end.

So the Q2_0 pack, tokenizer, MTP, 128K context and the single-GPU path are fine.

### Related issues

- #1705 (closed): gfx1100 prefill "no progress" from host-page reclaim;
  `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` fixed it there. In a comment, HackityAnn reports
  the same class on 2x RX 9070 XT with `--resident-experts` + layer split where
  HSA did not help, but **`GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576` did**.
- #1407 (closed): gfx1200 2x RX 9060 XT layer split prompt stalls (watchdog #29).
  A comment traces it to GFXOFF + SDMA adaptive expert swaps and reports
  **`STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1`** and **disabling GFXOFF** as fixes.
- #2637 (closed): gfx1100 2x 7900 XTX, `--pipeline-windows 2` + MTP, exits on an
  18K prompt; fixed by `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0=1`. My config does not use
  `--pipeline-windows`, but the hardware and prompt length are close.

### Question

Is this the same class as #1705 / #1407? Before I keep experimenting, would you
recommend trying `GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576`,
`STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1`, and/or disabling GFXOFF on 0.1.45? I can run
them one at a time and report back with the engine log and dmesg for each arm.

I am currently back on one card at 128K (stable). I can attach the full
`strata-q2_0.log`, `server.out` and the dmesg excerpts from the three runs.

issues.title: qwen35 (Qwen3.6): --mtp N is silently inert in serve mode unless --batch N --batch-mtp are also passed; setup's own config omits them
issues.author: FlyoverBlind
issues.body:
## Summary

On the qwen35 path (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), `--mtp N` alone does nothing in serve mode. MTP only activates when `--batch N` (≥ 2) **and** `--batch-mtp` are also passed — and even then only for greedy requests. No warning or error is printed when it is silently inactive. The config that setup.py itself generates for qwen36 sets `--mtp` but omits both flags, so the out-of-the-box path runs without MTP and gives no indication.

## What I measured

Same machine, same model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf), Strata v0.1.45, single session, decode speed from the `strata serve:` engine log line, steady state:

| serve flags | request | engine log | decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no MTP flags) | normal (server default sampling) | — | 34–37 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4` | normal (server default sampling) | `drafts accepted 0 of 0` | 39.0 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp` | normal (server default sampling) | `drafts accepted 0 of 0` | 39–42 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp` | greedy (temperature 0, penalties zeroed) | `drafts accepted 97 of 106` | 55.9–56.6 tok/s |

The headline is the log line, not the speed: with `--mtp 4` alone the draft model is loaded but `drafts accepted 0 of 0` shows it is never used. With the full flag set and a greedy request it engages (~91% acceptance, ~+45% decode vs. baseline on this machine).

## Where in the code

`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`:

- L3883: `E.bmtp = (batch_mtp || (std::getenv("STRATA_BATCH_MTP") ...)) && E.n_sess > 1 && E.mtp_d > 0;`
- L3351–3355: `if (E.bmtp && E.mtp_d > 0) { ... window_mtp(); return; } window_plain();`
- L1192: `int mtp_d = 0; // MTP drafts per speculative step (0: none; greedy requests only)`

So in serve mode `--mtp N` only sets `mtp_d`; without `--batch ≥ 2` → `n_sess == 1` → `bmtp == 0` → every request takes `window_plain()` and `mtp_d` is never consulted. In generate mode `mtp_d` works on its own, which makes the serve-mode asymmetry easy to miss.

There is a second silent gate worth mentioning: even with the flags right, MTP only runs for greedy requests (`needs_logits()` at L3013 — any nonzero temperature or penalty disables it), and server.py's `MODEL_CARD_SAMPLING` defaults for `qwen35moe` (temperature 0.7, presence_penalty 1.5, L6779–6786) make ordinary chat requests non-greedy by default. MTP engaged for me only after zeroing penalties and setting temperature 0.

## Why this looks like a footgun

1. setup.py's own qwen36 family config (`OWN_PATH_FAMILIES["qwen36"]`) sets `mtp: 2` but does not add `--batch` / `--batch-mtp` — the shipped path is MTP-less with no indication.
2. No startup warning: with `--mtp N` in serve mode and `bmtp == 0`, nothing says the draft path is loaded but unused. `drafts accepted 0 of 0` in the log is the only clue.
3. The user-visible flags (`--mtp`) and the activation preconditions (`--batch`, `--batch-mtp`, greedy, server default penalties) live in three different layers; each one alone silently disables MTP.

## Suggested fixes (any one would help)

a) Print a startup warning in serve mode when `mtp_d > 0 && !E.bmtp`: "MTP requested but inactive: needs --batch N --batch-mtp (and greedy requests)".
b) Allow `window_mtp()` with `n_sess == 1` so `--mtp N` works without `--batch`/`--batch-mtp`.
c) Have setup.py add `--batch-mtp` (and a suitable `--batch`) to the generated qwen36 config whenever `mtp` is set.

## Measured on

- Windows 11, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, 32 GB RAM
- Strata v0.1.45 (release engine, BUILD.json v0.1.45)
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf, sha256 starts with `55983c5a`
- Speeds from the `strata serve:` log line, single request, steady state

## Not tested

- Linux / other GPUs
- The `STRATA_BATCH_MTP` env route (should behave the same by the code path)
- More than 2 sessions
- Whether single-slot (`n_sess == 1`) MTP actually runs correctly if the `n_sess > 1` gate is lifted — I only verified the gate exists, not that the window handles one slot

MTP only activates when `--batch N` (≥ 2) **and** `--batch-mtp` are also passed — and even then only for greedy requests. No warning or error is printed when it is silently inactive. The config that setup.py itself generates for qwen36 sets `--mtp` but omits both flags, so the out-of-the-box path runs without MTP and gives no indication.

## What I measured

Same machine, same model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf), Strata v0.1.45, single session, decode speed from the `strata serve:` engine log line, steady state:

| serve flags | request | engine log | decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| (no MTP flags) | normal (server default sampling) | — | 34–37 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4` | normal (server default sampling) | `drafts accepted 0 of 0` | 39.0 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp` | normal (server default sampling) | `drafts accepted 0 of 0` | 39–42 tok/s |
| `--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp` | greedy (temperature 0, penalties zeroed) | `drafts accepted 97 of 106` | 55.9–56.6 tok/s |

The headline is the log line, not the speed: with `--mtp 4` alone the draft model is loaded but `drafts accepted 0 of 0` shows it is never used. With the full flag set and a greedy request it engages (~91% acceptance, ~+45% decode vs. baseline on this machine).

## Where in the code

`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`:

- L3883: `E.bmtp = (batch_mtp || (std::getenv("STRATA_BATCH_MTP") ...)) && E.n_sess > 1 && E.mtp_d > 0;`
- L3351–3355: `if (E.bmtp && E.mtp_d > 0) { ... window_mtp(); return; } window_plain();`
- L1192: `int mtp_d = 0; // MTP drafts per speculative step (0: none; greedy requests only)`

So in serve mode `--mtp N` only sets `mtp_d`; without `--batch ≥ 2` → `n_sess == 1` → `bmtp == 0` → every request takes `window_plain()` and `mtp_d` is never consulted. In generate mode `mtp_d` works on its own, which makes the serve-mode asymmetry easy to miss.

There is a second silent gate worth mentioning: even with the flags right, MTP only runs for greedy requests (`needs_logits()` at L3013 — any nonzero temperature or penalty disables it), and server.py's `MODEL_CARD_SAMPLING` defaults for `qwen35moe` (temperature 0.7, presence_penalty 1.5, L6779–6786) make ordinary chat requests non-greedy by default. MTP engaged for me only after zeroing penalties and setting temperature 0.

## Why this looks like a footgun

1. setup.py's own qwen36 family config (`OWN_PATH_FAMILIES["qwen36"]`) sets `mtp: 2` but does not add `--batch` / `--batch-mtp` — the shipped path is MTP-less with no indication.
2. No startup warning: with `--mtp N` in serve mode and `bmtp == 0`, nothing says the draft path is loaded but unused. `drafts accepted 0 of 0` in the log is the only clue.
3. The user-visible flags (`--mtp`) and the activation preconditions (`--batch`, `--batch-mtp`, greedy, server default penalties) live in three different layers; each one alone silently disables MTP.

## Suggested fixes (any one would help)

a) Print a startup warning in serve mode when `mtp_d > 0 && !E.bmtp`: "MTP requested but inactive: needs --batch N --batch-mtp (and greedy requests)".
b) Allow `window_mtp()` with `n_sess == 1` so `--mtp N` works without `--batch`/`--batch-mtp`.
c) Have setup.py add `--batch-mtp` (and a suitable `--batch`) to the generated qwen36 config whenever `mtp` is set.

## Measured on

- Windows 11, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, 32 GB RAM
- Strata v0.1.45 (release engine, BUILD.json v0.1.45)
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf, sha256 starts with `55983c5a`
- Speeds from the `strata serve:` log line, single request, steady state

## Not tested

- Linux / other GPUs
- The `STRATA_BATCH_MTP` env route (should behave the same by the code path)
- More than 2 sessions
- Whether single-slot (`n_sess == 1`) MTP actually runs correctly if the `n_sess > 1` gate is lifted — I only verified the gate exists, not that the window handles one slot

issues.title: [Engine] The Mac (Metal) engine ignores a request's sampling (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed, penalties) and drops logit_bias
issues.author: oceanio
issues.body:
### Area

Engine

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (`./setup.sh` on a Mac builds the Metal engine)

### What happened

On the Mac engine every request decodes greedily, whatever it asks for. `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`,
`seed`, `repetition_penalty`, `frequency_penalty` and `presence_penalty` reach the engine (they are on its `GEN` line)
but change nothing. Different seeds at temperature 1.0 give the same text, and it is the temperature-0 text.
`logit_bias` is dropped too: a token banned with -100 is still picked.

Three consequences:

1. **Sampling settings do nothing on a Mac.**
2. **The model card's defaults from 0.1.45 (#2685) do not take effect on a Mac.** The server now sends
   temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20 and presence_penalty 1.5 (instruct) when the request and the config give
   none. The Mac engine answers those requests greedily, so Mac users still get the greedy decoding that #2685 was
   about.
3. **`logit_bias` is dropped on Metal.** `Verifier::set_logit_bias` (`src/core/verify.cpp`) returns before it stores
   the bias when `le_ < g_->n_layers`. The Metal init returns before `le_` is set to the layer count, so `le_` stays
   -1 and every bias is treated as belonging to a later stage. The request gets no error.

Expected: the same behaviour as the PC engine. The settings act in the CUDA sampler's order, a fixed seed gives the
same text again, another seed gives another text, temperature 0 (or none, without the card's defaults) is greedy, and
a banned token is never picked.

The cause is that the Mac decode window always takes its own argmax (`argmax_part` / `argmax_final` in the window's
head), and `Verifier::run`'s Metal branch returns that token. The host-side sampling that the CUDA path runs after
its window is not ported. Nothing in the log or the response says that the settings were ignored.

#### Reproduction

Re-checked on 0.2.0-beta (`main` 3fa1b524, built from source); first found on `main` 477ac13c plus #2895 (the 0.1.45 Mac build fix).
I used the official two-file Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S (SC117's abliterated build), resident, as written by
`./setup.sh`. Start the server on a free port with the model's config, then send the same chat request with
different sampling:

```
python3 serve/server.py --engine strata --config strata-<model>.json --port 8197 &

ask() {  # the same prompt, thinking off, 40 tokens; $1 = extra JSON fields
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8197/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
    "model": "strata", "max_tokens": 40, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write one sentence about the sea."}] '"$1"' }' |
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])'
}
ask ', "temperature": 0, "presence_penalty": 0'      # greedy
ask ', "temperature": 0'                              # the card adds presence_penalty 1.5 (#2940)
ask ', "temperature": 1.0, "seed": 1'
ask ', "temperature": 1.0, "seed": 2'
ask ', "temperature": 1.0, "seed": 3'
ask ', "temperature": 1.5, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.95, "min_p": 0.01, "seed": 7, "presence_penalty": 0'
ask ''                                                # no sampling fields: the model card's defaults
ask ', "temperature": 0, "presence_penalty": 0, "repetition_penalty": 1.5, "frequency_penalty": 1.0'
ask ', "temperature": 0, "presence_penalty": 0, "logit_bias": {"760": -100}'   # 760 = "The", the greedy first token
```

(760 is the first token of the greedy answer with this model's tokenizer; use the first token of your greedy answer.)

Every line prints the same sentence.

#### Measured

M5 Max (128 GB), macOS 26.7.1, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, resident, `--spec 2` with MTP,
`--max-context 262144`, 2026-10-18. These are the answers to the requests above, all in one server run:

| Request (besides the prompt) | Answer |
|---|---|
| `temperature 0, presence_penalty 0` (greedy) | The vast, endless sea stretches to the horizon, its rhythmic waves whispering ancient secrets to the shore. |
| `temperature 0` (the card adds presence_penalty 1.5, #2940) | the same |
| `temperature 1.0, seed 1` | the same |
| `temperature 1.0, seed 2` | the same |
| `temperature 1.0, seed 3` | the same |
| `temperature 1.5, top_k 50, top_p 0.95, min_p 0.01, seed 7` | the same |
| no sampling fields (the model card's defaults: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5) | the same |
| `temperature 0, repetition_penalty 1.5, frequency_penalty 1.0` | the same |
| `temperature 0, logit_bias {"760": -100}` (760 = "The", the greedy answer's first token) | the same, starting with "The" |

The engine reported `0.1.45-metal` in `/v1/status`. An earlier run that day, with nearly the same requests, gave
the same: every answer equal to the greedy one.

With a port of the CUDA sampler's chain to the Mac engine (on the host, over the window's logits in unified
memory; I will open it as a PR once #2895 is merged), the same requests give a different answer for every row but
the first. Seed 1 gives the same text each
time it is sent, seeds 2 and 3 give other texts, and the banned token is not picked ("Beneath the shimmering
surface, ...").

At the engine protocol, a test I wrote for that port (`tools/metal_sampling_test.py`, run against my Metal branch
without the port) fails 12 of 18 checks. Seeds 1 and 2 give the greedy text. 100 one-token draws at temperature 1.0, top_k 40,
top_p 0.95 all give the greedy token, which has probability 0.81 on those logits; 15 of the 100 picks differ from what
a reference sampler written from the CUDA kernels draws with the same seeds. Greedy with `penalty_repeat 1.5` gives the same tokens as
without it. A token banned by `logit_bias` is still picked first.

#### Not tested

- The PC engines (CUDA, HIP, SYCL): not built here. The reference behaviour is read from their code
  (`src/kernels/cuda/sampler.cu`, `Verifier::run`) and from the test's reference sampler written from it, not run.
- Other Macs and chips, models that stream their experts from the SSD, other packs (Q2_0, IQ3_XXS, Unsloth's),
  vision requests. The cause is in code that all of them share, so I expect the same result.
- Thinking on. The requests above use thinking off; the card's thinking defaults (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95,
  top_k 20) should be ignored the same way.

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (`main` 3fa1b524, built from source). First seen on 0.1.45 (`main` 477ac13c + #2895).

### Graphics card, memory and system

Apple M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory (Metal) · macOS 26.7.1

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally on 0.2.0-beta (`main` 3fa1b524): the script below prints the same sentence for 9 of 9 requests. A fix is in #3301.

### Engine log

Not attached. Nothing in it mentions sampling: the engine prints no line about the settings it ignored.

issues.title: bench: community report, 4x Tesla T4 (sm_75, Linux, Docker): UD-Q6_K_XL on 0.1.45, +17% decode vs 0.1.42, 128K context verified with a 93K prompt, and the per-request VRAM warning that `--expert-cache auto` sets off by itself
issues.author: ericoh88
issues.body:
**Headline:** 0.1.45 decodes at **21.7 tok/s** on 4x T4 with UD-Q6_K_XL, compared with 18.6 on 0.1.42 (+17%). Prefill is unchanged at about 173 tok/s on a 1.7K prompt. At `--max-context 131072`, a **93,111-token prompt** was read at **220.8 tok/s** (433 s), then decoded at 18.6 tok/s, and the model answered a needle question correctly. The only rough edge: the "only ~448 MiB of VRAM free at the start of this request (below 512 MiB)" warning (#2065) fires on every request, even though the auto expert cache sized the cards itself. T4 sm_75 is now stable for us (the #1577 verify-window stall is gone).

## Hardware and software

- **GPUs:** 4x Tesla T4 16 GB (sm_75), PCIe Gen3 x16, power limit 70 W each, driver 615.71.09
- **CPU / RAM:** Xeon Silver 4314 (32C/64T), 251 GiB RAM
- Linux, rootless Docker, image built from the repo Dockerfile, CUDA 13.0 base
- **Strata v0.1.45, commit `477ac13c`.** Engine built from source for sm_75:
  `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75 -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`. This build is bind-mounted as `/custom`, with `STRATA_SM75_PERF=1`.
- **Model:** `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q6_K_XL`, six shards (~169 GB), packed with `--pack`

## Configuration

```
strata --serve --pack /data/packs/ud-q6_k_xl
       --native .../Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q6_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf
       --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto
       --prefill 512 --spec 2 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp /data/mtp/rt
       --max-context 131072 --kv q4_0 --vram-reserve-later-mib 1208 --layer-split auto
```
One slot, temperature 0. All numbers below come from the server's own `/metrics` per-request fields (`prompt_ms`, `decode_tok_s`), not from counting streamed chunks, because spec/MTP makes chunk counting undercount.

## Results

| Engine | Context | Decode tok/s (300-tok output, median of 3) | Prefill tok/s (1.7K prompt, median of 3) | Expert cache |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1.42 | 2,048 | 18.6 | 175 | ~35.5 GiB |
| **0.1.45** | 2,048 | **21.7** (20.1 to 21.9) | 173.2 | 35,479 MiB |
| 0.1.45 | 131,072 | 19.9 | 165.2 | 32,683 MiB |
| 0.1.45, **93,111-token prompt** | 131,072 | 18.6 | **220.8** | 32,683 MiB |

- Draft acceptance on 300-token outputs at 2K: 114 to 131 of 153 to 168 offered (74 to 85%). The expert hit rate is about 0.96 on short prompts, 0.85 on the 1.7K prompt, and **0.60** on a separate 48K prompt.
- Caveat: the 0.1.42 baseline used a similar but not identical prompt set. The 0.1.45 rows all use the same script.
- Going from 2K to 128K costs about 2.8 GiB of expert cache and about 8% decode on short prompts.
- Long-prompt scaling on T4: 48K at 222 tok/s (216 s), 93K at 221 tok/s (433 s). Prefill stays flat as the prompt grows, so for interactive use the practical limit on this rig is time, not memory.

## The VRAM warning

At 2K with no reserve flag, both 0.1.42 and 0.1.45 print:
```
strata serve: CUDA3: 260 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded - LOW ... add --vram-reserve-later-mib 1208
strata serve: WARNING: only 448 MiB of VRAM free at the start of this request (below 512 MiB) ... (#2065)
```
With `--vram-reserve-later-mib 1208` as suggested, the load-time message becomes `CUDA1/2: 1052 MiB, CUDA3: 768 MiB free with everything loaded`. **But the per-request warning still fires at 448 to 450 MiB on every request.** We have not seen paging or a hang: decode stays at 18 to 22 tok/s, including on the 93K prompt.

Questions:
1. Should `--expert-cache auto` keep the 512 MiB per-request margin by itself, so a default config doesn't warn against its own sizing?
2. On 16 GB T4s with `--layer-split auto`, is `--vram-reserve-mib 768` the recommended setting, or is there a better one?
3. At about 450 MiB free with no slowdown, is this just a precaution, or should we expect the #2065 hang under sustained load?

Happy to run test builds or `tools/strata_bench.py --long` on this box if useful.

issues.title: [Engine] ple_reader_selftest can crash or hang when two runs share the temp directory
issues.author: thc1006
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

`ple_reader_test --selftest` writes its test tables under fixed names in the temp directory (`ple_format_selftest.gguf`, `ple_reader_selftest_90.bin` and `ple_reader_selftest_110.bin`), and the ctest entry, `add_test(NAME ple_reader_selftest COMMAND ple_reader_test --selftest)`, passes no `--dir`. Two runs at the same time on one machine, for example ctest in a CUDA build and in a HIP build, overwrite and delete each other's tables while they are open.

I started two copies of the 0.2.0-beta selftest (`3d1fb48`, built for the CPU only) with the same `TMPDIR`, six times, the second one 0, 0.3, 1, 2, 4 or 6 s after the first. In all 6 pairs, at least one run failed:

- In two pairs, one run died with SIGBUS.
- In two pairs, one run printed `collect failed: PleReader: short read inside the table` and then hung, with all its threads waiting on futexes, until it was killed after 182 and 186 s. A run alone takes about 13 s.
- In the pair with no delay, both runs failed with `mapped open: PLE table size mismatch`. In the 6 s pair, both failed, one with `collect failed: PleReader: short read inside the table` and the other with `open: DirectFile: cannot open`, as did the second run of the 4 s pair.

With a separate `TMPDIR` for each run and the same six delays, all 12 runs passed. With 0.1.45 (`477ac13`), 5 of the 6 pairs failed, with SIGBUS, hangs and `cannot open` as here; those scripts and their output are in [`ple-selftest-shared-tmp-20261018.txt`](https://github.com/thc1006/strata-p100-deployment/blob/main/results/ple-selftest-shared-tmp-20261018.txt).

Adding `--dir ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}` to the `add_test` line would give each build its own files.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

Built for the CPU only from 0.2.0-beta's `src/kernels/ngram.cpp`, `src/ngram/ple_reader.cpp`, `src/platform/direct_file.cpp` and `src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp`:

```sh
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -pthread -Iinclude -Isrc src/kernels/ngram.cpp src/ngram/ple_reader.cpp src/platform/direct_file.cpp src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp -o ple_reader_test
```

Then, for each delay, two runs with the same `TMPDIR` (the file above has the whole script, `race.sh`; a run still alive after 180 s was killed):

```sh
( TMPDIR=$PWD/a nice -n 19 ./ple_reader_test --selftest > out_a.txt 2>&1; echo $? > rc_a ) &
sleep $off
( TMPDIR=$PWD/a nice -n 19 ./ple_reader_test --selftest > out_b.txt 2>&1; echo $? > rc_b ) &
wait
```

The first FAIL line of each run with the shared `TMPDIR` (rc 135 is SIGBUS, 143 the kill after 180 s):

```
delay 0    a rc=1    FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:287: mapped open: PLE table size mismatch: 499 rows x 90 B = 44910 at offset 0, but the file holds 24660 from data_start 160
delay 0    b rc=1    FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:287: mapped open: PLE table size mismatch: 2000 rows x 170 B = 340000 at offset 0, but the file holds 41480 from data_start 160
delay 0.3  a rc=135
delay 0.3  b rc=0
delay 1    a rc=135
delay 1    b rc=0
delay 2    a rc=143  FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:65: bulk: collect failed: PleReader: short read inside the table
delay 2    b rc=0
delay 4    a rc=143  FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:65: decode: collect failed: PleReader: short read inside the table
delay 4    b rc=1    FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:358: open: DirectFile: cannot open <work>/r/shared-4/a/ple_reader_selftest_90.bin
delay 6    a rc=1    FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:65: keep-alive, caller thread: collect failed: PleReader: short read inside the table
delay 6    b rc=1    FAIL src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp:358: open: DirectFile: cannot open <work>/r/shared-6/a/ple_reader_selftest_110.bin
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (`3d1fb48`)

### Graphics card, memory and system

issues.title: [Other] sycl/tools/build.sh exits 1 after a successful build and 0 after a failed compile
issues.author: thc1006
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

`sycl/tools/build.sh` sets `pipefail` and has no `exit`, so the script exits with the status of its last pipeline:

```sh
grep -E '^FAILED' $b/build.log | sed 's#.*/##' | sort | uniq | head -60
```

After a successful build this `grep` finds nothing and returns 1. After a failed compile it finds ninja's `FAILED:` lines and returns 0. The `BUILD EXIT` line that the script prints is correct.

With the script from 0.2.0-beta (`3d1fb48`), which is byte-identical to the one in 0.1.45 (`477ac13`):

- With `BUILD_DIR` set to the build directory of a small CMake project that builds, it printed `BUILD EXIT 0` and `errors: 0`, and exited with 1.
- With `BUILD_DIR` set to the same project with a compile error, it printed `BUILD EXIT 1` and `errors: 1`, and exited with 0.

With 0.1.45 it also exited with 1 in a SYCL build directory with nothing left to build, after printing `BUILD EXIT 0` and `errors: 0`.

The image's entrypoint is `bash -lc`, so in `docker run ... strata-sycl-dev "cd /work/$H && bash sycl/tools/build.sh strata" && <next step>`, the next step is skipped after a good build and runs after a failed compile. `docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md` already notes the first case and says not to chain tests behind the script.

Saving `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` right after the build and ending the script with `exit` on that value would fix it.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

Two small CMake projects with one target named `strata` (Ninja, g++ 11.4), configured with `cmake -G Ninja`: `src-good/main.cpp` is `int main() { return 0; }`, `src-bad/main.cpp` is `int main() { return x; }`. Then, for each:

```sh
REPO=<work> BUILD_DIR=<work>/b-$kind bash sycl/tools/build.sh strata; echo "### build.sh exit status: $?"
```

Output with the script from 0.2.0-beta (sha256 `a5f95ab736c072b9160d523456454c8689791750cfae91f82f03e2a97374b122`, the same as 0.1.45's):

```
### good build:
[2/2] Linking CXX executable strata
BUILD EXIT 0
errors: 0
### build.sh exit status: 1
### bad build:
FAILED: [code=1] CMakeFiles/strata.dir/main.cpp.o
<work>/src-bad/main.cpp:1:21: error: ‘x’ was not declared in this scope
ninja: build stopped: cannot make progress due to previous errors.
BUILD EXIT 1
errors: 1
main.cpp.o
### build.sh exit status: 0
```

The 0.1.45 runs, the SYCL build directory included, are in [`sycl-build-sh-exit-20261018.txt`](https://github.com/thc1006/strata-p100-deployment/blob/main/results/sycl-build-sh-exit-20261018.txt).

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (`3d1fb48`); `sycl/tools/build.sh` is unchanged since 0.1.45 (`477ac13`)

### Graphics card, memory and system

No Intel GPU (the script ran outside the strata-sycl-dev image) · 4× Tesla P100 16 GB · 62.8 GiB RAM · Ubuntu 22.04.5
