issues.title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL: Low GPU utilization, limited generation speed, and MTP acceptance concerns
issues.author: cinetube
issues.body:
Hi Strata team,

I'm trying to get the best performance out of **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL** on my system, but so far the results have been disappointing. I'd appreciate some guidance on the recommended configuration for this model, particularly regarding MoE expert offloading, GPU utilization, and MTP speculative decoding.

### Hardware and model

- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, 16 GB VRAM
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, 16 cores
- **System RAM:** 62 GB
- **NVIDIA driver:** 617.42
- **Model:** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
- **Quantization:** UD-Q4_K_XL
- **Context:** 65,536 tokens
- **Vision:** Enabled, using mmproj-F16.gguf

### Results with Strata

My current configuration uses:

- `--pool-workers 4`
- `--max-context 65536`
- `--prefill auto`
- `--mtp 2`
- `--vision`

The startup log reports:

- 4.40 GiB of model tensors on the GPU
- 42 of 256 experts per layer in VRAM
- Approximately 18.75 GiB of expert weights in pinned host memory
- CPU-side processing for the remaining experts
- 4.94 GiB of free VRAM after loading

In my testing, generation speed is approximately **60–77 tokens/s**, while GPU utilization is generally around **50–60%**.

I also tried increasing `--pool-workers` to 6 and `--mtp` to 4, but performance became worse, so I returned to 4 workers and MTP 2.

One thing that concerns me is that the logs report `MTP block loaded`, but Strata's session logs repeatedly show:

`drafts accepted 0 of 0`

I cannot tell whether MTP is actually participating in generation, whether these counters are expected for this model, or whether my configuration is missing something.

### Comparison with llama.cpp

I tested the same GGUF with a recent prebuilt CUDA-enabled llama.cpp build, using a 65,536-token context, CPU MoE offloading, and `--spec-type draft-mtp`.

The server reported:

- **Generation:** approximately 55.4 tokens/s
- **Prompt processing:** approximately 87 tokens/s
- **Draft acceptance:** 73.4% (1,082 accepted out of 1,474 generated draft tokens)
- **Mean accepted draft length:** 2.24

This confirms that speculative decoding can work with this model in llama.cpp, although its generation speed was still lower than my better Strata runs.

For comparison, my Qwen3.8 Flash-Next setup in Strata reaches approximately **100 tokens/s** on the same PC.

### Questions

1. Is my current Strata configuration appropriate for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL on a 16 GB GPU?
2. Is there a recommended way to improve GPU utilization and reduce the CPU-side MoE bottleneck without increasing VRAM usage beyond what this GPU can handle?
3. Does `drafts accepted 0 of 0` indicate that MTP is not functioning, or is this expected behavior for Qwen3.6 in Strata?
4. Are there recommended MTP settings for this model? Increasing the value from 2 to 4 did not improve performance on my system.
5. Are there any known limitations or optimizations for Qwen3.6's hybrid MoE architecture, especially when most expert weights reside in pinned host memory?

I'm not looking to rebuild or compile Strata myself. I'd like to understand whether this performance is expected for my hardware or whether there is a known configuration or implementation issue that could improve it.

Thanks for your work on Strata. Any specific recommendations or clarification about the MTP logs and hybrid expert offloading would be appreciated.

issues.title: serve: /v1/chat/completions ignores llama.cpp's n_predict, so a client's n_predict: 0 follow-up call regenerates the whole answer with no limit (~20k tokens, ~4–5 min of GPU time per reply)
issues.author: DanGTG
issues.body:
## Summary

`/v1/chat/completions` ignores the llama.cpp-native field `n_predict`. The answer limit is read only from `max_completion_tokens` / `max_tokens`, and a missing or 0 value means "the rest of the context" (`serve/server.py:5942` on `main` at `477ac13c`; `:5819` in 0.1.44.1, in `_openai`). Still the case on `main` as of 2026-10-17.

llama.cpp's own web UI (and possibly other llama.cpp-compatible clients) sends a follow-up request after every reply. The request carries the conversation so far, ending with the assistant's answer, plus `n_predict: 0` and `stream: false`. In llama.cpp, `n_predict: 0` means "generate nothing": the client only wants the prompt processed, e.g. to measure context or warm the cache. Strata generates with no limit instead. The model answers the whole task again from scratch, and the client discards the result.

Because Strata serves one request at a time, any other client of the server waits behind this request for those minutes. The chat user can cut it short: sending a new message cancels it (seen twice; it fits the client dropping its pending call, and Strata cancelling a request whose client disconnects). But that has a second cost. The follow-up never completes as a prompt-only call, so the conversation is never cached, and the user's next message re-reads the whole conversation from scratch. Strata already reports `n_predict` in `/props` (`default_generation_settings.params.n_predict`), so llama.cpp clients reasonably expect it to be honoured on requests.

## Environment

- Strata 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`, git clone). It first appeared on a `main` ZIP snapshot from 2026-10-04 (bundled engine 0.1.39) and is still there after updating, so it isn't a regression in 0.1.44.x. The same limit line is in both versions (`serve/server.py:3368` in the 2026-10-04 snapshot).
- Windows 10, `backend: hip`, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB), 96 GB RAM
- Happens after every reply in that client, across several days and on four packs: `iq3_s`, `coder-iq1_m`, `unsloth-ud-iq4_xs` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `swift-iq3_s` (Swift-1.5). The cases below are the ones captured in logs. The code path is in the shared request layer, so it does not depend on the model.
- Client: **llama.cpp's built-in web UI ("llama-ui")**. Its chat requests carry `return_progress`, `timings_per_token`, `backend_sampling` and `reasoning_format`; after each reply it sends the `n_predict: 0` call. Strata's own web app never sends `n_predict` and doesn't trigger this.
- How it ended up talking to Strata: llama-ui installs itself as a PWA with a service worker. It was installed from llama-server at `127.0.0.1:8080`, llama-server's default port and also Strata's. When Strata later served that address, `--open` brought up the cached llama-ui shell instead of Strata's page (its icons and bundle 404 against Strata), and llama-ui worked against Strata's llama.cpp-compatible API without any visible sign. Anyone who has used llama-server on 8080 can hit this without choosing that client.

## Minimal repro

Same prompt, non-streaming, against an idle server:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 40, one number per line. No thinking."}],
 "stream":false, "n_predict": 8}
```

| Limit field | completion_tokens | finish_reason |
|---|---|---|
| `"n_predict": 8` | 155 | `stop` |
| `"max_tokens": 8` | 8 | `length` |
| `"max_tokens": 0` | 153 | `stop` |

## What it looks like in practice (captured with `"api_monitor": true`)

1. The user's chat request: `stream: true`, prompt 1,081 tokens, 29,263 tokens generated.
2. 0.05 s after it finished, the client's follow-up: `stream: false`, `n_predict: 0`. The messages are exactly [user prompt, the previous answer as an `assistant` message]. Prompt 5,763 tokens, 0 reused. Live metrics showed `max_tokens: 518517`. It finished with **21,683 tokens in 292 s**: about 64k characters of reasoning plus a full second answer.

An earlier session the same day showed the same shape: chat prompt 1,081 → 39,593 tokens, then the follow-up at 7,468 prompt tokens, 0 reused, **20,181 tokens in 232 s**. In an earlier occurrence, on the `coder-iq1_m` pack, the user sent a new message about 200 s in, and that ended the follow-up.

### Interrupting it (`swift-iq3_s`, from the server log)

| # | Request | Prompt | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | User's chat | 1,081 | 20,201 tokens, `stop` |
| 2 | Follow-up (`n_predict: 0`) | 8,030, 0 reused | cancelled after 4,681 tokens / 46.6 s, when the user sent a new message |
| 3 | User's new message | 21,294, **0 reused** (24.7 s to read) | 30 tokens, `stop` |
| 4 | Follow-up again | 21,014, **0 reused** (23.9 s to read) | 31 tokens, `stop` |

Two things show here:
- **It fires after every reply.** The cost scales with the length of the previous answer: minutes after a long one, 31 tokens after a short one.
- **Nothing is ever reused.** Every resend re-reads the full conversation, because the call that would leave it cached never completes as intended. With `n_predict: 0` honoured, request 2 would have taken about 10 s of prompt reading, and request 3 could have reused most of its prompt.

## History

No version has read `n_predict` from a request. What changed over time is the cost:

- `01529aaa` (2026-09-24, first commit): the limit comes from `max_completion_tokens` / `max_tokens`, with a default of 1024 if neither is set. An `n_predict: 0` call was ignored, but capped at 1,024 tokens.
- `656a8356` (2026-09-26, "treat unset/-1 max_tokens as remaining context, not 1024"): the default became the rest of the context, so the same call now has no limit.
- `08f8d591` (2026-09-29, "add llama.cpp-compatible discovery endpoints"): `/props` started reporting `n_predict`, so llama.cpp clients treat Strata as compatible.

`656a8356` was a sensible change for real chat requests. It just made the missing `n_predict` handling expensive.

## Suggested fix

Honour `n_predict` in `_openai` when neither `max_completion_tokens` nor `max_tokens` is set. Note that this can't reuse the existing `int(... or 0)` pattern. For `max_tokens`, 0 deliberately means "the rest", so passing `n_predict` through it would keep `n_predict: 0` unlimited. llama.cpp's semantics are:

- `n_predict: -1`: no limit
- `n_predict: 0`: process the prompt and generate nothing. Return an empty completion (`completion_tokens: 0`) once the prompt has been read; the client presumably wants the prompt cached.
- `n_predict: N > 0`: same as `max_tokens: N`

Happy to test a fix on gfx1201.

Related: #2141 (same family: `thinking_budget_tokens`, llama-server's name, is ignored, so llama.cpp clients get unbounded thinking). Together, a llama.cpp client that tries to bound a request by either length or thinking gets no bound at all.

issues.title: Layer split + `--batch`: slots decode without MTP drafts, and `--batch-mtp` is slower on 4 stages. Could pipelined groups draft?
issues.author: JacobSussan
issues.body:
## Summary

On a 4-GPU layer split, a request alone decodes fast on the solo path (MTP + suffix drafts), but as soon as several requests share the batch slots, each one decodes without drafts (the pipelined `--batch-groups` path has none). `--batch-mtp --batch-groups 1` brings one draft per slot back, but the serial windows cost more than the drafts gain: 4 concurrent streams lose 30-40% of their total throughput against the pipelined default.

The gap is largest on copy-heavy work, which is most of what coding agents do: a file edit decodes at 174 tok/s alone with 98% of drafts accepted, and at 44-69 tok/s per stream when four run together.

Would it be possible for the pipelined groups to run MTP drafts per slot (even one proposal per slot per window), so a 4-stage split can pipeline and draft at the same time?

## Setup

- Strata 0.1.45, `main` at `477ac13c`, built from source by setup (sm_86, CUDA 13.2), Linux (Debian 13), driver 595.71.05
- 4x RTX 3090 24 GB, each on PCIe 3.0 x8; 2x Xeon Gold 6126 (2 NUMA nodes); 376 GB RAM
- Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL (revision `38bb39e`), every expert in RAM, 94% of experts resident in VRAM, decode expert-cache hit rate 100%
- `"parallel": 4` (`--batch-groups auto`: 4 groups of 1 slot), `"layer_split": "11,24,36"`, `--trim-stage-weights`, `--max-context 262144`, `--kv fp16 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pcie-frac 0.35` (the last two from `--calibrate`), `--ple-io ram`, `--conversation-cache-mib 65536 --conversation-cache-slots 32`, `--vram-reserve-later-mib 1300`
- env: `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1 STRATA_MMQ_KQ=1 STRATA_HC_Q8=1 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0 STRATA_SLOT_COPY_DIRECT=1 STRATA_SLOT_COPY_BATCHSYNC=1 STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1 STRATA_QSA_SLOTS=1`

## Measured

Requests to `/v1/chat/completions`, `reasoning_effort: none`, 900-token answers, a random tag at the start of every prompt so nothing is reused. Three workloads: write a new Python module (code), return an 11 KB PHP file with one method renamed (edit), write a short story (prose). "1 user" is the mean of two sequential requests; "4 users" is four concurrent requests, total output tokens over wall time, with each stream's own decode rate in brackets. A fresh engine for each arm; one round per arm.

| tok/s | code: 1 user / 4 users | edit: 1 user / 4 users | prose: 1 user / 4 users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default (pipelined groups, no slot drafts) | 139 / 209 (56-62 each) | 174 / 129 (44-69 each) | 95 / 210 (56-62 each) |
| `--batch-mtp --batch-groups 1` | 141 / 144 (38-41 each) | 177 / 99 (28-40 each) | 97 / 127 (33-34 each) |

Draft acceptance on the solo path: code 85-87%, edit 98%, prose 63-65%.

For completeness, on the same rig and workloads, none of these moved the 4-stream totals beyond run-to-run noise: `--spec 3` (191 / 122 / 193), `--spec 5` (203 / 129 / 212), `--lookup-chain 4` (192 / 121 / 201).

## Why it matters here

The workload is coding agents: 1-4 requests at once about 99% of the time (14 days of request logs), most turns either writing code or returning files with small edits. Those are exactly the requests where the solo path's drafts pay most (98% acceptance on edits) and where they disappear as soon as a second agent is busy.

`docs/BATCHING.md` notes `--batch-mtp` has only been run on two stages; on four it looks like the serial windows leave three of the four cards waiting, which outweighs the drafts.

Happy to test a branch on this rig and report numbers in the same format.

issues.title: [GUI] Web app: page overflows sideways on phones when a tool call appears
issues.author: TitanMamo
issues.body:
### Area

[GUI] - the web app (the phone/browser UI served by the engine, `serve/web`)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (the web app served by the engine; re-tested on the v0.2.0-beta web assets)

### What happened

On a phone (412 px viewport) the web app's page grows wider than the screen as soon as a tool call appears in an answer: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is 770 where the viewport is 412. Content spills off-screen - the tool row's name/preview run past the right edge, and the header renders at the viewport width while everything below it is laid out wider.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

A page with the 0.2.0-beta `serve/web/app.css` and the exact DOM `toolHtml()` renders (`.st-msg .st-bubble > details.st-collapse.tool-call > summary` with `.tool-call__name`, `.tool-call__preview`, badges), opened at a 412 px viewport.

Expected: the page stays at the viewport width (`scrollWidth` 412).
Actual: `scrollWidth` 770 on the 0.2.0-beta CSS (same on 0.1.45).

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally: 0.2.0-beta web assets, static reproduction of the tool row (headless browser, 412 px viewport). The live app on 0.1.45 showed the same behavior in a real session (MCP web-search tool call).

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3) - re-tested on the v0.2.0-beta web assets

### Graphics card, memory and system

NVIDIA RTX 3060 12 GB; 31 GB RAM; Void Linux (kernel 6.18); phone viewport 412 px (Chrome)

### Model, size and settings

Any model; the tool row appears for MCP tool calls (e.g. the firecrawl web search)

### Evidence

Headless measurement at a 412 px viewport, 0.2.0-beta `app.css`:

| | scrollWidth |
| --- | --- |
| 0.2.0-beta as-is | 770 (overflows) |
| + `.view { min-width: 0 }`, `.tool-call > summary { overflow: hidden }`, `.tool-call__name { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis }` | 412 (fits) |

Root cause (unchanged in 0.2.0-beta):

1. `.view` is a flex item of `main { display: flex; }` and keeps the default `min-width: auto`, so its min-content - raised by the `white-space: nowrap` tool name - makes the whole panel and the page wider than the viewport.
2. `.tool-call > summary` has `min-width: 0` but no `overflow: hidden`.
3. `.tool-call__name` has `white-space: nowrap` without `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`.

(The preview already has that treatment.)

@ctr-137's PR #3156 carries exactly these three rules for this issue.

issues.title: [Engine] expose optional pricing for client usage estimates
issues.author: lindestad
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine] (the server and API)

### What do you want to do?

I run Hermes and OpenCode against Strata and want to compare their usage using the same simulated external API rates. Hermes can discover rates from the endpoint's model listing, but Strata does not publish them.

Allow an optional top-level `pricing` block in the run config and report it in `/v1/models` and `/models`, including aliases. The rates would follow OpenRouter's USD-per-token convention, with an optional per-request fee. Clients would calculate their own estimates. Existing configs without pricing would need no changes.

### What do you do today instead?

I use a local Strata patch to expose the rates to Hermes. PR #2970 contains that change, with validation, documentation and regression tests. Comparing estimates with OpenCode is my use case; this request does not assume OpenCode reads prices from `/v1/models`.

### Re-test on 0.2.0-beta

Reproduced locally on unmodified main `e88ee39d` using the mock engine: a config with a pricing block still produces model listings without pricing. The rebased patch `901c7be0` publishes the configured values. Without pricing, both endpoints return byte-identical bodies to main for no config file, an empty config, a model config and aliases.

Environment: CachyOS Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.14, 91 GiB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 5080 (16 GB VRAM, driver 615.78.08). These are mock-engine HTTP checks; GPU inference was not run. Current test commands and results are in PR #2970.

issues.title: [Engine] Windows HIP, one RX 7900 XTX: about 1 engine start in 10 answers long prompts and pictures wrong (KV streaming 0 block reads), still in 0.2.0-beta
issues.author: jerem91150
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Other: the engine from the release packages, `strata.exe --serve` started by a small script (the full command is at the top of each log below).

### What happened

Re-tested on 0.2.0-beta: **still there**.

Some engine starts come up in a bad state. In that state the answers have nothing to do with the prompt (`Based on the image provided, ...` with no image sent, or generic Chinese text), while the prompt is read in full (`0 reused`) and the speed looks normal. It is decided at start: a bad start stays bad for all its requests, a good one stays good. With `--kv-resident 32768` the log shows which start is bad, because the KV streaming counter stays at zero from the first request on:

```
strata serve: prompt 20 tokens = 0 reused + 20 read in 322 ms (62.2 tok/s), 20 generated in 359 ms (55.8 tok/s), drafts accepted 9 of 14, 1 checkpoints
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: prompt 26319 tokens = 0 reused + 26319 read in 31822 ms (827.1 tok/s), 20 generated in 405 ms (49.4 tok/s), drafts accepted 6 of 8, 2 checkpoints
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
```

A good start, same config, same run:

```
strata serve: prompt 20 tokens = 0 reused + 20 read in 334 ms (59.9 tok/s), 20 generated in 371 ms (53.9 tok/s), drafts accepted 10 of 19, 1 checkpoints
strata serve: KV streaming: 96.45% of 3384 block reads hit VRAM, 0.5 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: prompt 26319 tokens = 0 reused + 26319 read in 28090 ms (937.0 tok/s), 6 generated in 114 ms (52.4 tok/s), drafts accepted 6 of 6, 2 checkpoints
strata serve: KV streaming: 79.41% of 92436 block reads hit VRAM, 76.7 MiB read from RAM
```

Expected: the right answer (`18802`, a number that is in the prompt) on every start.

**Counts on 2026-10-20**, `--kv-resident 32768`, 0.1.45.3 and 0.1.44.1 alternated, 30 fresh starts, nothing else changed:

| engine | starts | counter `100.00% of 0 block reads` | wrong 26K answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1.45.3 (0.2.0-beta) | 20 | 1 | 1 |
| 0.1.44.1 | 10 | 1 | 1 |

The two always go together: every bad start gave a wrong answer, every good start the right one (30 of 30). On the bad 0.1.45.3 start the 26K answer was Chinese, about "the picture you provided".

With the runs from the original report and the days after:

| engine | starts | bad starts |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1.44.1 | 35 | 4 |
| 0.1.45 | 19 | 0 |
| 0.1.45.3 | 20 | 1 |

So roughly 1 start in 10 to 15, on every version I have; the 0 of 19 on 0.1.45 was most likely luck.

**It is not tied to `--kv-resident 32768`.** My original workaround (`--kv-resident 131072`, all K/V in VRAM) does not avoid it, it only hides the counter. The same night, on that production config:

- speed bench, 0.1.44.1: 1 session of 4 answered the fresh 26K prompt with `Based on the image provided, here is a breakdown of the text and its meaning:`;
- vision run, 0.1.45.3 with `--vision` (CPU encoder): in 1 session of 4 all three picture questions got answers about some other picture (`Based on the image provided, here is a description of its content: ... a screenshot of a digital interface`, then generic Chinese). So it also hits short prompts of a few hundred image tokens, not only long ones.

That makes 2 bad sessions out of 8 on the production config that night.

Startup logs of bad and good starts differ only in timings: same slots, same residency, same probe results, same `verify` captures without errors. One difference I noticed: on the bad 0.1.44.1 start the 26K prompt read at 228 tok/s instead of ~930; on the bad 0.1.45.3 one at normal speed (827 tok/s).

Possibly related to #2594 (`0 block reads` on a layer split), but here it is one card, only some starts, and the answers are wrong.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Start the engine with the command at the top of the logs (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --spec 4 --mtp ... --expert-cache auto --vision --vram-reserve-mib 1536`).
2. Send a 20-token question, read the `KV streaming` line.
3. Send a fresh ~26K-token prompt (Python source files) ending with "which port does the router listen on (the PORT variable)? Answer with the number only". Right answer: 18802.
4. Stop the engine and start it again. About 1 start in 10 to 15 gives `100.00% of 0 block reads` at step 2 and a wrong answer at step 3.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta · engine 0.1.45.3 (`strata-engine-0.1.45.3-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3.tar.gz`, BUILD.json commit 18f7b90ca), and 0.1.44.1 (`strata-windows-x64-hip.zip`)

### Graphics card, memory and system

AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100) · Ryzen 9 7900X3D · 64 GB RAM · Windows 11 Pro 26100

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (native pack iq3_xxs) · 131072 context · `--kv int8`, `--kv-resident 32768` (and 131072) · MTP `--spec 4` · pictures on (`--vision`, CPU encoder)

### Logs

Four bad sessions and one good one from the same run, in the comment below.

---

<details><summary>Original report (0.1.44.1, before the tracker reset)</summary>

Native Windows 11, one RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 64 GB RAM, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, 0.1.44.1 HIP build, `--max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, MTP draft (`--spec 4`), `--expert-cache auto`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1536`.

**What happens.** Some engine starts answer every long prompt wrong. The prompt is read in full (`0 reused`), the speed looks normal, but the answer has nothing to do with it. The test is a fresh ~66K-token prompt (Python source files) ending with "which port does the router listen on (the PORT variable)? Answer with the number only", then a fresh ~113K one with the same question. The answer is in the text (18802). Good starts answer `18802` both times. Bad starts answered things like:

```
Based on the image provided, here is a description of the scene: ...
### 优化后的提示词 ...
The following analysis provides a comprehensive and structured response to the user's query ...
```

(no image was sent), and the follow-up in the same conversation went "the code visible in the image is incomplete".

**It is decided at start, and the log shows which start is bad.** In the bad starts the KV streaming counter reads zero from the first request on:

```
strata generate: KV streaming: 32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM, the K/V in 1.55 GiB of pinned RAM
strata serve: prompt 20 tokens = 0 reused + 20 read in 320 ms ...
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: prompt 65960 tokens = 0 reused + 65960 read in 58660 ms (1124.4 tok/s) ...
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
```

while a good start, same config, same prompts:

```
strata serve: KV streaming: 96.30% of 3240 block reads hit VRAM, 0.5 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: prompt 65960 tokens = 0 reused + 65960 read in 58132 ms (1134.7 tok/s) ...
strata serve: KV streaming: 74.40% of 92424 block reads hit VRAM, 95.3 MiB read from RAM
```

Startup lines are the same in both (same expert cache: `17.89 GiB free ... -> 7472 slots`, same residency line).

**Counts, 16 fresh starts today, alternated:**

| config | starts | starts with `0 block reads` | starts with wrong answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--kv-resident 32768` (K/V past 32K in RAM; 2 of these with `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1`, both good) | 10 | 2 | 2 (the same two) |
| `--kv-resident 131072` (all K/V in VRAM) | 6 | - (no streaming) | 0 |

So for us the wrong answers and the zero counter go together 10 out of 10 times. Short prompts (we never saw a wrong answer under ~27K) look fine even in a bad start, so it only shows once a conversation goes past the resident part.

This looks related to #2594 (`0 block reads` on a layer split), except here it is one card, it only happens on some starts, and the answers are wrong, so it is not just the counter.

Workaround for now: `--kv-resident 131072`. On this card it costs ~2% on fresh long prompts (66K: 59.0 against 58.1 s, 113K: 103.7 against 101.8 s), decode at 113K the same.

I can send full engine logs of a good and a bad start, or run a build with extra logging.

</details>

Speed | Expert Cache Hit | | :--- | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 32k | 10% | FOUND | 32,792 | 53 s | 17.4 tok/s | 25.9% | | 32k | 50% | FOUND | 32,792 | 52 s | 20.8 tok/s | 27.2% | | 32k | 90% | FOUND | 32,793 | 52 s | 15.9 tok/s | 33.9% | | 128k | 10% | FOUND | 127,535 | 199 s | 12.7 tok/s | 41.8% | | 128k | 50% | FOUND | 127,533 | 200 s | 11.1 tok/s | 46.9% | | 128k | 90% | FOUND | 127,533 | 176 s | 14.2 tok/s | 57.1% | | 256k | 10% | FOUND | 261,213 | 392 s | 13.3 tok/s | 58.1% | | 256k | 50% | FOUND | 261,213 | 392 s | 16.0 tok/s | 64.7% | | 256k | 90% | FOUND | 261,214 | 392 s | 20.0 tok/s | 66.1% | | 520k | 10% | FOUND | 517,676 | 863 s | 19.2 tok/s | 68.7% | | 520k | 50% | FOUND | 517,676 | 863 s | 18.1 tok/s | 64.9% | | 520k | 90% | FOUND | 517,677 | 862 s | 18.4 tok/s | 68.1% | ## Correctness and limitations Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details come from the server, `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` and the OS; background load and power limits are not recorded. Total time of the suite: 656 s. ## MSI Monitor Eco + Normal ------------------------ ### Technical Summary: NVFP4 Integration & Constraints on Consumer Rigs (Strata v0.1.45) - **Expert Cache Reduction (`--expert-cache 2048`):** Active MCP servers (`filesystem`, `Understory`, `Exa`) and system prompts inject heavy token payloads (~4k+ tokens per turn) containing JSON schemas. This spikes memory pressure during prefill and MTP verification (`verify: instantiate: out of memory`). Lowering the cache from +- 3000 to 2048 reclaims ~1.6 GB VRAM headroom. - **Orca Tokenizer Reuse:** The `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` architecture shares an identical BPE vocabulary structure (152k tokens). Reusing asset files (`vocab.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `merges.txt`) from the Orca IQ3_XXS pack satisfies `server.py` validation without redundant file duplication. - **Windows WDDM Commit Accounting vs Physical RAM:** The model (63.3 GiB) + 524k KV cache (3.38 GiB) fit entirely within 96 GB physical DDR4 RAM, leaving ~16 GB free. However, the CUDA runtime and WDDM demand a high virtual memory commitment threshold (*Commit Charge*). A static pagefile acts purely as a virtual "accounting receipt" satisfying `Commit Charge`, while pages remain hardware-locked in physical RAM via `SeLockMemoryPrivilege` and `VirtualLock` (ensuring zero SSD I/O thrashing). issues.title: [Bug]: default `--pipeline-windows 2` costs ~25% decode on 2x R9700 with every expert resident (v0.1.45)
issues.author: justincinmd
issues.body:
### What happened

v0.1.45 turns `--pipeline-windows 2` on by default for a two-stage layer split. On a pair of R9700s that hold every expert, it makes decode about 25% slower, and up to 2.7x slower at long context. `STRATA_PIPELINE_AUTO=0` brings the speed back.

Setup: 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), Linux, ROCm 7.2.4, v0.1.45 built with setup's flags, Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--layer-split 26` (26 / 22 layers), every expert in VRAM on both stages, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, one request at a time. The engine logs `--pipeline-windows 2 is on by default for a layer split of 2 stages` and `284 MiB of CUDA0 kept out of the expert cache`; the residency check still reports 100% on both cards.

Same binary and config, only the switch differs:

| | default (pipeline on) | `STRATA_PIPELINE_AUTO=0` |
|---|---:|---:|
| decode, greedy (tok/s) | 89.5 | 117.7 |
| decode, sampled (tok/s) | 79.4 | 109.8 |
| prompt read 4K / 16K / 64K (tok/s) | 1354 / 2067 / 2548 | 1425 / 2176 / 2681 |
| decode at 32K / 96K / 160K context (tok/s) | 44.3 / 36.5 / 58.9 | 99.8 / 99.7 / 86.7 |

We saw the same direction on 0.1.40 with `--pipeline-windows 2` set by hand on this rig (slightly slower, all experts resident), so it looks like the pipeline only pays when stages wait on expert misses.

Could the auto default stay off when every expert is resident on both stages, or be gated on a measured gain? Happy to run a candidate fix on this box.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.45 · 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 32GB (gfx1201) · Ubuntu 24.04, ROCm 7.2.4

issues.title: Qwen3.6 2-bit GSQ-hybrid (Q2_0 experts) crashes 0xC0000005 in the hybrid CPU expert pool; Windows HIP (RX 7800 XT)
issues.author: wanlemur
issues.body:
I wanted to test whether Strata can run the 2-bit GSQ quant of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (chitsgit/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2Bit-GSQ-hybrid-GGUF, Q2_0 routed experts). The engine already runs Q2_0 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and Qwen3.6 is the same model family/architecture, so the q36 path should handle it too.

It loads and works when every routed expert fits in VRAM, but crashes with 0xC0000005 in ~7 threads whenever the engine runs it in hybrid mode (some experts on the CPU pool). The same engine, machine, and config run the official UD-Q4_K_XL in hybrid mode without any problem, so this looks specific to Q2_0 experts in the q36 hybrid CPU path.

**Note:** the GGUF loads in Strata only after I patched its metadata by hand, so the file is NOT byte-identical to what chtisgit published. Two things the engine did not accept from the stock file:

1. The file has no MTP/nextn tensors, but the engine's GGUF checks for `qwen35moe` require `qwen35moe.nextn_predict_layers`. I added it with value 0.
2. `ffn_gate_inp_shexp.weight` is stored as `[2048, 1]`; the layout check wanted a plain `[2048]`. I rewrote the shape.

After the patches, the engine reports 733 tensors (layout checked).

## The crash: only in hybrid mode

At `--max-context 65536` the engine keeps the packed Q8_0 decode copies and runs hybrid mode:

```
strata-q36: context 65536 cells, prompt chunk 4096, 4.72 GiB of VRAM free
strata-q36: hybrid experts: 107 of 256 per layer in VRAM (3.53 GiB),
all 8.44 GiB in pinned host memory; the rest of a batch of <= 128 rows
on 7 CPU threads, bigger prompt chunks streamed (0.42 GiB staging)
strata-q36: 6.1 s
```

Then `Exception Code: 0xC0000005` (x7):

- Deterministic: identical stack offsets across runs (+0x2F4F0A, +0x2E0DC2, +0x2D990E, ... in strata.exe).
- Reproduces with `--prefill auto:16384` and `--prefill 4096`, and with different hybrid splits (155/256 in VRAM in one run, 107/256 in the other), so it does not look like a VRAM/staging fit problem.
- 7 exceptions ≈ the expert pool's threads + the host thread: the CPU half of the hybrid MoE, not the GPU side.
- The crash comes right after the `hybrid experts:` line, during load warm-up, before any `warmed up` line.

One-flag repro: at `--max-context 32768` the engine itself avoids hybrid mode ("the packed Q8_0 decode copies (1.75 GiB) given back so that every routed expert fits in VRAM") and everything runs. So hybrid on = crash, hybrid off = works.

##

Same GSQ-hybrid file, all experts in VRAM (`--max-context 32768`, the engine gives back the packed copies) — fully working, benchmarked:

| test | result (median, range) |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | 96.9 tok/s (94.3–97.2), TTFT 0.26 s |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 1,268.6 tok/s (1,258.6–1,273.2) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 1,057.7 tok/s (1,057.3–1,058.9) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 78.4 tok/s decode (66.2–89.8) |

.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (gfx1101), 16 GB
- CPU / RAM: Ryzen 7700, 32 GB RAM
- Strata: 0.1.45

##

issues.title: [Feature]: Optional rootless Apple Silicon Monitor sensors
issues.author: mjhagen
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Show Apple Silicon GPU temperature, GPU power and GPU clock in the web Monitor without running Strata or powermetrics as root. The PCIe card should show a useful platform-specific measurement, and shared-memory allocations should be labeled clearly.

This extends the basic IORegistry GPU load/memory work in #2360. The existing macOS reader remains the default; the additional sensors can be opt-in through `STRATA_MACOS_TELEMETRY=1`, using the optional `macmon` helper. Missing or stale sensors should stay unavailable rather than appearing as zero.

The implementation has been verified on an M3 Pro with macmon 0.10.0. It adds Python telemetry and dashboard support, with no native engine or build changes.

issues.title: 0.1.45: non-thinking requests inherit the card's presence_penalty 1.5 (temperature 0 too), ~25% slower decode
issues.author: Cass67
issues.body:
Since 0.1.45 (a8091f4d, #2685) a request with thinking off picks up the model card's instruct set under the config's sampling block, so presence_penalty 1.5 ends up on every non-thinking request that doesn't send one. That includes temperature 0 requests, which I'd expect to be plain greedy, and a config sampling block with temperature/top_p/top_k still inherits the card's presence.

On 4x 7900 XT (UD-Q4_K_XL, layer split 12,24,39, --pipeline-windows 2, MTP) it cost me about a quarter of decode: code prompt 89 -> 65-72 tok/s, prose 51 -> 44. STRATA_DECODE_TIMING shows the windows going from 32 to 47 ms, with draft and commit no longer hidden. Same request with an explicit presence_penalty 0 is back to 91-96. It looked like an engine regression at first, but the 0.1.44 engine binary was just as slow under the 0.1.45 server.py.

Maybe temperature 0 should skip the card set, and a config sampling block should replace it rather than merge on top? Setting presence_penalty 0 in the config works around it for now.

issues.title: 4× Tesla T10 (Turing, layer split): single-stream decode stays ~39 tok/s with 99.9% of experts in VRAM — same as 2× T10
issues.author: demon851113
issues.body:
**Hardware**
| | |
|---|---|
| Motherboard | Huananzhi H12D-8D (single socket SP3), BIOS 2.2 (2026-01-06), no BMC |
| CPU | AMD EPYC 7452, 32 cores / 64 threads (Zen 2), 1 socket, 1 NUMA node |
| RAM | 4 × 32 GB Samsung DDR4-2400 RDIMM (M386A4G40EM2-CRC) = 128 GB, 4 of 8 memory channels populated |
| GPUs | 4 × Tesla T10 16 GB (TU102, sm_75, VBIOS 90.02.41.00.01), passive cooling, power limit 100 W each (default 150 W) |
| PCIe | every card on its own CPU root port, Gen3 x16 (LnkCap 8 GT/s x16); `nvidia-smi topo -m`: NODE between all pairs; P2P works with `iommu=pt` (10–13 GB/s per pair) |
| Storage | Crucial T500 1 TB NVMe (model files on it) |

**Software**
- Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, kernel parameter `iommu=pt`
- NVIDIA driver 595.91.07 (server, open kernel modules), CUDA 13.2 toolkit
- Strata v0.1.45 (477ac13c), engine compiled locally with CUDA 13.2 (no ready-made engine for v0.1.45: releases/latest returned 404)
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 262144`, `"gpu": [0,1,2,3]`, `"layer_split": "auto"`

**What the log says**
- `layer split auto: K=14,26,38 - predicted 44.8 ms per decode window; the caches hold 21931 of 24576 profiled pairs (~99.9% of the routed mass)`
- `CUDAn 56 SMs at 1.40 GHz -> 0.93 ms per layer`, every link probed at 13.1 GB/s (pcie_frac 0.36)
- `adaptive overlap: off: not on a layer split`
- After load: CUDA3 has 341 MiB VRAM free and gets the "LOW ... add --vram-reserve-later-mib" warning
- MTP draft acceptance on 300-character Chinese answers: roughly 95–119 of 166–203 drafts (~55–65%)

**Measured** (6 Chinese prompts, ~300 characters each, no thinking, temperature 0, warm-up + median of 3 rounds)

| | tok/s |
|---|---|
| single stream decode | 39.3 |
| same, with `"parallel": 4` | 38.9 |
| 2 concurrent (`parallel` 4) | 36.5 / 38.9 per stream |
| 4 concurrent (`parallel` 4) | 27–32 per stream, 104 total |
| prompt read, 2.6K / 10K tokens | 527 / 723 |

For comparison, #2007 reports 44.2 tok/s on **2×** T10 with v0.1.40.1 and 40.5 on 0.1.43 (the regression between 0.1.40.1 and 0.1.40.2 noted there). Our 4-card result is below both, even though four cards hold almost every expert.

**Questions**
1. With nearly all experts resident, single-stream decode looks bound by the four stages running one after another (~0.93 ms per layer × 48 layers ≈ the predicted 44.8 ms window). Is there a way to overlap the stages for one stream on 3+ NVIDIA cards (`--pipeline-windows` mentions two GPUs / AMD gfx12 only), or is 4-way split simply not expected to beat 2-way for a single user?
2. Is the 0.1.40.1 → 0.1.40.2 slowdown from #2007 still present in 0.1.45 on Turing? We can run an A/B (0.1.40.1 vs 0.1.45) on this box if useful.
3. Would `--prefill-pipe` or a manual `layer_split` be worth trying for prompt reading here (723 tok/s at 10K tokens)?

Happy to run any flag combination or a debug build — the box is free for testing.

issues.title: Community benchmark: RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100), Ryzen 9 9950X, 96 GB DDR5-6400 — 0.1.45 HIP source build, IQ3_S, 262K
issues.author: destroyor
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100)

Measured on 2026-10-18 on EndeavourOS (Arch), Linux kernel 7.2.10, ROCm 7.2.4, with a
HIP source build of Strata 0.1.45 and a custom abliterated IQ3_S pack. Single card, one
request at a time.

## Hardware and software

- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, `gfx1100`), 23.98 GiB VRAM;
  **PCIe 4.0 x16** (`LnkSta: Speed 16GT/s, Width x16`). A Radeon 610M iGPU is also present
  and unused.
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, 16 cores / 32 threads.
- **RAM:** 96 GB (2×48 GB DDR5-6400, 1DPC, dual channel); `MemTotal` 91.7 GiB.
- **Storage:** SIX X7400 953.9 GB NVMe.
- **OS:** EndeavourOS (Arch), kernel `7.2.10-arch1-1`.
- **Runtime:** ROCm 7.2.4 (`hipcc` 7.2.53211), GCC 16.2.1.
- **Strata:** v0.1.45, commit `477ac13c`; HIP source build (`STRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON`,
  `STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF`, `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1100`, `Release`).
- **Background:** no other GPU workload; desktop idle. No power limit applied.

## Model and configuration

- **Model:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, GSQ-RCO-abliterated, IQ3_S native pack.
  - `...-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf`: 55,063,448,064 bytes
  - `...-IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf`: 28,800,138,432 bytes
- **Vision:** `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf`, 907,542,944 bytes, `--vision` with the
  encoder on the CPU.
- **Expert profile:** `data/expert-profile.bin` (24,576 ranked pairs).
- **Context:** 262,144. **KV:** `--kv k8v4`, `--kv-resident 32768`.
- **Expert cache:** `--expert-cache 7700` → 9,048 slots, 17.16 GiB VRAM.
- **VRAM reserve:** `--vram-reserve-mib 700`.
- **Prefill:** `--prefill auto:32768`.
- **Conversation cache:** `--conversation-cache-mib 16384`, `--conversation-cache-slots 8`,
  `--conversation-cache-min-tokens 32768`.
- **Speculative:** `--mtp ... --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`.
- **Other:** `--pcie-frac 0`, `--adapt-every 0`, `--pool-workers 15`,
  `--prompt-cache 16 --prompt-cache-every 16384`.
- No calibration run, no experimental speed projection.

```text
strata --serve --pack <pack> --native <IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf>
  --ple-gguf <IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf> --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin
  --expert-cache 7700 --prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <rt>
  --max-context 262144 --kv k8v4 --kv-resident 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 700
  --adapt-every 0 --pcie-frac 0 --pool-workers 15 --vision
  --prompt-cache 16 --prompt-cache-every 16384
  --conversation-cache-slots 8 --conversation-cache-mib 16384
  --conversation-cache-min-tokens 32768
```

## Method

- Prompts: one repeated English paragraph with a unique 2-character tag prefix per run, so
  every run is a **cold** prompt (`0 reused`). Output cap 256 tokens (98K, 260K) or 512
  (short); `temperature: 0`.
- Timing: the engine's own log lines, e.g.
  `prompt 97961 tokens = 0 reused + 97961 read in 54136 ms (1809.5 tok/s), 256 generated in 3253 ms (78.7 tok/s)`.
- Repetitions: 3 runs at 1,457 and 97,961 prompt tokens; the 259,508-token point is a
  **single run** (about 2.5 minutes of prefill each).
- The model was already loaded; loading is not included. Nothing else was running.
- Requests are non-streaming, so **TTFT was not measured by a client**; the prefill
  duration in the table is the closest available proxy (the first token follows prefill
  immediately).
- VRAM was sampled from `/sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_vram_used` during the
  260K run.

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused | Generated | Runs | Prompt tok/s (median, range) | Decode tok/s (median, range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| short | 1,457 | 0 | 512 | 3 | **521.0** (494.1–521.5) | **82.5** (82.0–83.5) |
| ~98K | 97,961 | 0 | 256 | 3 | **1809.5** (1795.7–1810.5) | **77.4** (75.8–78.7) |
| ~260K | 259,508 | 0 | 256 | 1 | **1479.6** | **79.9** |

Raw engine lines:

```text
prompt 1457 tokens   = 0 reused + 1457 read in 2794 ms (521.5 tok/s), 512 generated in 6132 ms (83.5 tok/s), drafts accepted 262 of 377
prompt 1457 tokens   = 0 reused + 1457 read in 2796 ms (521.0 tok/s), 512 generated in 6203 ms (82.5 tok/s), drafts accepted 252 of 343
prompt 1457 tokens   = 0 reused + 1457 read in 2949 ms (494.1 tok/s), 512 generated in 6247 ms (82.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 246 of 330

prompt 97961 tokens  = 0 reused + 97961 read in 54108 ms (1810.5 tok/s), 256 generated in 3307 ms (77.4 tok/s), drafts accepted 128 of 166
prompt 97961 tokens  = 0 reused + 97961 read in 54136 ms (1809.5 tok/s), 256 generated in 3253 ms (78.7 tok/s), drafts accepted 129 of 170
prompt 97961 tokens  = 0 reused + 97961 read in 54554 ms (1795.7 tok/s), 256 generated in 3376 ms (75.8 tok/s), drafts accepted 125 of 178

prompt 259508 tokens = 0 reused + 259508 read in 164691 ms (1575.7 tok/s), 256 generated in 3128 ms (81.8 tok/s), drafts accepted 149 of 214
```

**Memory.** VRAM peak 24,545 of 25,753 MiB during the 260K request (as low as 14–18 MiB
free, no failure). RAM: expert arena 46.84 GiB; about 72 GiB used of 91.7 GiB while a
conversation was parked. No OOM, no paging, no stalled window; the engine logged its
"below 512 MiB" warning twice, which is a cross-platform guard (see below).

## Correctness and limitations

- **Not a quality test.** No needle/recall run, no coding task, no tool-call check in this
  report. Speed only.
- **Single machine, single quantization.** IQ3_S only; no other quantization or context
  length, no multi-GPU, no `--batch`.
- **The 260K point is one run.** Prefill at that length takes about 2.5 minutes.
- **`--pcie-frac` costs decode here.** With `--pcie-frac 0.5` (about 11% of experts read
  over PCIe and computed on the GPU) decode measured **48.6 tok/s against 78.3** at
  `--pcie-frac 0`, i.e. -38%, on the same prompt. PCIe 4.0 x16 is roughly 25 GB/s against
  the card's 960 GB/s of VRAM bandwidth, so sending the missed experts to the GPU instead
  of computing them on the CPU is the slower path on this box.
- **`--vram-reserve-mib 700` is tight.** Free VRAM was 368 MiB at request start for 98K and
  236 MiB for 260K. On this Linux/AMD box that produced no slowdown; issue #2065 (NVIDIA
  WDDM paging GPU memory to system RAM, decode collapsing to a few tok/s) did **not**
  reproduce even with 14 MiB free. A larger reserve is safer on other platforms.
- **`--batch 2` gave no throughput gain here.** Two concurrent 1.5K-token requests decoded
  in 12.8 s serial vs 12.8 s batched (512 windows at 25.05 ms each, `avg 1.99 rows`):
  strictly linear, compute-bound. Two 98K prompts were prefill-serialized.
- Prompt throughput at 1,457 tokens (521 tok/s) is lower than at 98K (1,810 tok/s) because
  the fixed per-request overhead dominates at that size.

## Correction

An earlier revision of this report said the card runs at PCIe **x8**. That was wrong: it
came from reading `current_link_width` over every PCI device with an AMD vendor ID, which
also matched an upstream PCIe bridge (`01:00.0`, class `0x060400`, x8) and the iGPU. The
GPU's own link is `Speed 16GT/s, Width x16`. The `--pcie-frac` note above was rewritten
accordingly.

issues.title: Metal build broken on current main (v0.1.45-metal): 3 separate defects in the perf-merge sync
issues.author: DarkJoll
issues.body:
# Metal build broken on current main (v0.1.45-metal): 3 separate defects in the perf-merge sync

## Summary

A fresh install on an Apple Silicon Mac (`git clone` + `./setup.sh`, following `docs/MAC.md`) fails to build the engine at commit `477ac13c`. Three separate defects, all introduced because the f-145 perf-PR group merges (`5a6f4ed5`, `8bdef963`, `df6262f2`, `21c57972`, `b277412e`, `cbc6e3d8`, `e8b1edbc`, `f260925a`) and the #2666 peer-experts work changed the shared host code and the kernel headers without re-syncing the Metal side:

1. The Metal compat shim (`metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h`) lacks six names the shared host code now uses → **compile errors**.
2. The generated stub file (`metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`) is stale: one stale signature (member → hard compile error) and 21 entry points that are referenced but undefined → **link failure**.
3. One of the 21, `strata::kernels::fused_gr_persist_init`, is called **unconditionally** from `Verifier::init` (src/core/verify.cpp:646), so even with the stub the engine would stop at start-up (exit 86, "no Metal implementation yet").

The Metal target (`metal/CMakeLists.txt`) is a separate CMake project that never compiles in the CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds, so none of the PC-side changes were caught: the perf group is measured on RTX 2080 Ti / R9700 / gfx12 hardware only.

## Environment

- Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 27.0, Command Line Tools (Apple clang)
- `git clone https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata`, commit `477ac13c` (v0.1.45-metal)
- `./setup.sh` → step 4 (engine build) fails; the model download never starts

## Defect 1 — shim missing six names

`src/core/peer_experts.cpp` (added by #2666; `e6ad6c81` fixed the *HIP* compat for exactly this, "peer_experts.cpp did not compile on HIP in f-145-int", but not the Metal one):

```
peer_experts.cpp:72:13:  error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaMemcpyPeer'
peer_experts.cpp:157:29: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess'
peer_experts.cpp:158:34: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess'
```

`src/core/verify.cpp` (sm75/cuda86 group):

```
verify.cpp:285:54: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor'
verify.cpp:286:54: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor'
verify.cpp:859:17: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange'
verify.cpp:860:17: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cudaStreamCreateWithPriority'
```

(`cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess` is called with one argument at verify/peer_experts sites; the real CUDA signature has a defaulted `flags`, so the shim needs the default too.)

## Defect 2 — stale generated stubs

After the shim is fixed, compilation passes and the link fails with 21 undefined symbols (ld64):

```
strata::kernels::wait_handoff                     strata::kernels::hc_q8_to_bf16
strata::kernels::handoff_publish                  strata::kernels::gdn_step_norm_groups
strata::kernels::wait_flag_ge_stamped             strata::kernels::fused_gr_persist_init
strata::kernels::fused_gr_read_persist            strata::kernels::qsa_block_scores_rows
strata::kernels::qsa_decode_attn_split            strata::kernels::native_quantize_q8_1_il
strata::kernels::wait_copy_i32_from_mapped        strata::kernels::qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows
strata::kernels::copy_rows_from_mapped_after      strata::kernels::cpu::iq256_gu_rows_exact_one
strata::kernels::res_patch                        strata::prefill::f16_range_read
strata::prefill::gemm_f16_range_read              strata::prefill::gr_norm
strata::prefill::gr_norm_rs                       strata::prefill::gr_write_norm_rs
strata::prefill::gr_write_cvec_norm_rs            strata::prefill::Gemm::bf16 (stale signature)
```

All referenced from the shared host objects (`verify.cpp.o`, `prefill.cpp.o`, `mtp.cpp.o`, `native_expert.cpp.o`, `generate.cpp.o`) — the same calls run on every backend, and the last stub regeneration predates the perf group, so none of them have a Metal implementation or a stub.

The stale-signature part: `Gemm::bf16` gained a trailing `bool x_f16` (`8bdef963`, sm75 series), so the committed 9-parameter out-of-line stub no longer matches the declaration:

```
stubs.cpp:328:29: error: out-of-line definition of 'bf16' does not match any declaration in 'strata::prefill::Gemm'
```

The same drift, in its quiet form, hit four free functions: the committed stubs of `gr_norm` / `gr_norm_rs` / `gr_write_norm_rs` / `gr_write_cvec_norm_rs` are one parameter short of the current `prefill/kernels.hpp` declarations. Free functions make that *compile* (it becomes a dead overload), but the 9/9/12/16-parameter versions the host code now references are what the link needs — and the dead overloads are a latent landmine (an 8-argument call would silently bind to the stub).

## Defect 3 — `fused_gr_persist_init` stops the engine at start

`Verifier::init` calls `strata::kernels::fused_gr_persist_init();` unconditionally (src/core/verify.cpp:646, no `#if`). The feature is `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`, a HIP-only read variant: the non-HIP CUDA build compiles an empty body for it (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu:3030`, `#else` branch), and on Metal the .cu is not built at all. So on Metal the call reaches the stub and `missing()` stops the engine (metal/src/engine/missing.cpp: "no Metal implementation yet", exit 86) on *every* start, regardless of model or settings. The Metal side needs the same empty body the CUDA build has (the project already does this for the sibling `fused_gr_check()` at metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp:59).

## Runtime reachability of the 21 (so the stubs never fire on a default Mac)

Audited each call site: 20 of the 21 sit behind opt-in or PC-only gates and are not reached on a default Apple Silicon run —

| entry point | gate |
|---|---|
| `fused_gr_read_persist` | branch requires `fused_gr_supported()`, which on Metal is the stub → `false` |
| `native_quantize_q8_1_il` | `qil` = `STRATA_QIL` env or `device_is_sm75()` (Turing; false on Apple silicon) |
| `gdn_step_norm_groups` (×2) | `STRATA_BATCH_GDN_GROUPS=1` (opt-in) |
| `qsa_block_scores_rows`, `qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows` | `STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS=1` (opt-in) |
| `qsa_decode_attn_split` | `STRATA_QSA_SPLIT_ATTN=1` (opt-in) |
| `wait_copy_i32_from_mapped`, `copy_rows_from_mapped_after` | `fuse_wait_on()`: `STRATA_FUSE_WAIT` on non-HIP, off by default |
| `wait_flag_ge_stamped` (×3) | `m_bal_ != nullptr` (`set_pcie_balance`, multi-GPU) or the fused-wait branch |
| `wait_handoff`, `handoff_publish` | `hflag_*_d_ != nullptr` (overlapped layer split, multi-GPU) |
| `res_patch` | `drive.d.res_dirty`, set only with `STRATA_ADAPT_EVICT_SYNC` |
| `iq256_gu_rows_exact_one` | `STRATA_CPU_IQ_ALL_EXACT1` **and** `ggml_cpu_has_avx2()` (never true on arm64) |
| `gr_norm`, `gr_norm_rs`, `gr_write_norm_rs`, `gr_write_cvec_norm_rs`, `f16_range_read`, `gemm_f16_range_read`, `hc_q8_to_bf16` | all called only from `Prefill::run_impl` / `bf16_proj`; under `STRATA_GPU_METAL`, `Prefill::run` returns via `metal_engine::prompt_run` first (src/prefill/prefill.cpp:4814) |

Only `fused_gr_persist_init` (defect 3) is reached on the default path. A stub that stops the engine is the project's documented behavior for "never expected to be called here", so the 20 are correct as stubs; the one needs the no-op body.

## The fix (5 files, all under `metal/`)

Everything is inside the Metal-only project (`metal/` is a standalone CMake target, "never part of the CUDA / HIP / SYCL builds" — metal/CMakeLists.txt:1-2; the CUDA/HIP builds never include `metal/include`), so the PC builds are unaffected by construction. 58 insertions, 6 deletions:

- **`metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h`** — add the six names, forwarding to `strata::gpu` like every other name in the file.
- **`metal/include/strata/gpu/runtime.hpp`** + **`metal/src/gpu/runtime.cpp`** — the six `strata::gpu` functions, each following the file's existing pattern:
  - `device_cc_major/minor`: `*v = 0; return fail(kErrorUnsupported)` — the same pattern as `device_sm_count` / `device_clock_khz` ("Apple reports no core count"). Effect: `device_is_sm75()` (src/core/verify.cpp:276) gets `ok = false` → `per_dev = 1` → `false`. Correct: an Apple GPU is not a Turing card, and `strata::sm75_default(0, 0)` is `false` anyway.
  - `cudaMemcpyPeer` → one-GPU: a plain device-to-device copy (`memcpy_sync`), `kErrorInvalidValue` for a non-zero device ordinal. Never actually run on a single-GPU Mac (`p2p_` stays false: `device_enable_peer_access` fails).
  - `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess` → `fail(kErrorUnsupported)`, the same as `device_enable_peer_access`; the caller clears the last error right after.
  - `stream_priority_range` → `(0, 0)`, `stream_create_with_priority` → `stream_create(s, f)`: one priority level, i.e. the default — matching the existing precedent in `mtp.cpp:438` ("HIP, Metal: the default priority"). Only reachable with `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1` (opt-in), so default behavior is unchanged.
- **`metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`** — regenerated with the project's own `metal/tools/gen_stubs.py` from the link log: the `bf16` stub updated to the current 10-parameter signature, the four `gr_*` stubs updated to their current signatures, the 16 remaining new entry points added (21 minus `fused_gr_persist_init`, which moves to the no-op below), plus the eight headers the regenerated set includes that the old file lacked.
- **`metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp`** — `void fused_gr_persist_init() {}` next to the existing `fused_gr_check() {}` (defect 3); the corresponding line is *removed* from stubs.cpp to avoid a duplicate definition.

### Full patch

```diff
diff --git a/metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h b/metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h
index eb64243e..66c1937f 100644
--- a/metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h
+++ b/metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h
@@ -46,7 +46,9 @@ inline constexpr unsigned cudaEventDisableTiming = strata::gpu::kEventDisableTim
 inline constexpr unsigned cudaEventBlockingSync = strata::gpu::kEventBlockingSync;
 inline constexpr unsigned cudaStreamNonBlocking = strata::gpu::kStreamNonBlocking;
 enum cudaStreamCaptureMode { cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal = 0, cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal = 1, cudaStreamCaptureModeRelaxed = 2 };
-enum cudaDeviceAttr { cudaDevAttrClockRate = 13, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount = 16, cudaDevAttrIntegrated = 18 };
+enum cudaDeviceAttr { cudaDevAttrClockRate = 13,
+                      cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor = 75, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor = 81,
+                      cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount = 16, cudaDevAttrIntegrated = 18 };
 
 // ---- errors, devices
 inline cudaError_t cudaGetLastError() { return strata::gpu::get_last_error(); }
@@ -65,11 +67,14 @@ inline cudaError_t cudaDeviceGetAttribute(int* v, cudaDeviceAttr a, int d) {
         case cudaDevAttrIntegrated: return strata::gpu::device_integrated(v, d);
         case cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount: return strata::gpu::device_sm_count(v, d);
         case cudaDevAttrClockRate: return strata::gpu::device_clock_khz(v, d);
+        case cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor: return strata::gpu::device_cc_major(v, d);
+        case cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor: return strata::gpu::device_cc_minor(v, d);
     }
     return strata::gpu::compat_detail::bad();
 }
 inline cudaError_t cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer(int* v, int d, int p) { return strata::gpu::device_can_access_peer(v, d, p); }
 inline cudaError_t cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess(int p, unsigned f) { return strata::gpu::device_enable_peer_access(p, f); }
+inline cudaError_t cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess(int p, unsigned f = 0) { return strata::gpu::device_disable_peer_access(p, f); }
 
 // ---- memory and copies
 template <class T> inline cudaError_t cudaMalloc(T** p, size_t n) { return strata::gpu::malloc_device(p, n); }
@@ -93,10 +98,17 @@ inline cudaError_t cudaMemcpy2DAsync(void* d, size_t dp, const voi

issues.title: [sm_86 / RTX 3090] 0.1.43→0.1.44 decode regression = commit 661ff29 (STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP default flipped ON→OFF); =1 restores 0.1.43; 0.1.45 breakdown forthcoming
issues.author: oven1231231234
issues.body:
# [sm_86 / Xeon E5-2680 v4] 0.1.45: decode -20-27% vs 0.1.43 on a single RTX 3090; build pins and CPU expert pool both ruled out — points at 0.1.45 source changes esxi8.0

## Setup

- Single RTX 3090 24 GB, 88 GB RAM, expert arena fully pinned (zero disk reads)
- CPU: **Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4 @ 2.40 GHz** (12C/24T, 2016; AVX2 + FMA + F16C, **no AVX-512 / no AMX**)
- Driver 580.178.04; 350 W power limit
- Toolchain, identical for all four arms: CUDA 13.0 (`/usr/local/cuda-13.0`), gcc 13.3, `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`, ninja
- **llama.cpp submodule identical for all four arms** (one checkout, commit `296b59d`)
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, 262K context, KV int8, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --ple-io ram --kv-resident 32768`
- Strata source: 0.1.43 at `e568e70371a3d2e0` (built by the repo's own `setup.py` flow — the production binary), 0.1.45 at `477ac13` (tag `v0.1.45`)
- Bench: same prompts, 5 runs x 3 warmups, narrative ~600-1200 tok and code ~450-800 tok; engine swapped between arms, service restarted, ready-poll + smoke test each time

## Observation: four arms, A/B/A'/D

| arm | Strata | Q6K_EXPERTS / MMQ_KQUANTS | narrative decode | code decode | CPU pool / expert | GPU W |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A  | 0.1.43 | OFF / OFF (production build) | 102.6 | 118.4 | 82 us | 182 |
| A' | 0.1.43 (retest) | OFF / OFF | 103.2 | 115.9 | 82 us | - |
| B  | 0.1.45 | ON / ON (release pins) | **78.6 (-23%)** | **96.6 (-18%)** | 96-102 us | 166 |
| D  | 0.1.45 | OFF / OFF (rebuilt to match A exactly) | **79.4 (-23%)** | **86.3 (-27%)** | 82-85 us | - |

A vs A' agree within 1%, so positional/thermal bias is not the cause.

## What is ruled out

1. **Build pins.** Arm D is 0.1.45 compiled with `Q6K_EXPERTS=OFF` and `MMQ_KQUANTS=OFF` — the same cmake configuration as the 0.1.43 production binary (verified against `setup.py`: `host_compiler_defs` / `toolkit_root_defs` / `engine_defs` are all identical for sm_86 + CUDA 13; no `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60`, no `STRATA_ISA_FLOOR` on an AVX2 CPU). Arm D still regresses, and its CPU pool reads 82-85 us/expert — the same as 0.1.43. **The pins are not the cause.**
2. **CPU expert pool throughput / PCIe.** Arm D's "PCIe share" probe reports 82-85 us per missed expert (24.0-24.8 GB/s of expert bytes), identical to 0.1.43, and the PCIe probe reads 11.3 GB/s host->device on every arm. Yet decode is still 20-27% slower. **The per-expert CPU cost is not the cause either.**

## Added: 0.1.44.1 A/B on this same rig (2026-10-16, same method, clean build)

The 0.1.43 -> 0.1.45 delta contains an intermediate release. I A/B'd v0.1.44.1 on the identical rig, same toolchain (CUDA 13.0/gcc 13.3/arch 86/Release), same llama.cpp submodule, same model/config. Build note: the 0.1.44.1 cmake command carried no `STRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS`/`STRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS` flags (those only appear as explicit `=ON` in the 0.1.45 setup.py), so it is built with both OFF — the same build configuration as the 0.1.43 production binary, i.e. a pure source delta.

| run (2026-10-16 CST) | engine | narrative decode | code decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20:55 pre baseline | 0.1.43 (production) | 103.30 (CV 3.4%) | 118.46 (CV 1.7%) |
| 21:16-21:21 | rebuilt to 0.1.44.1 (cmake 145/145, version gate PASS, service restarted, ready ~160s) | - | - |
| 21:28 first post (cold expert cache) | 0.1.44.1 | 77.56 (CV 5.9%) | 94.20 (CV 9.2%) |
| 21:35 warm re-run | 0.1.44.1 | 91.15 (CV 4.5%) | 104.86 (CV 4.2%) |
| 21:52 clean re-run | 0.1.44.1 | 96.99 (CV 1.8%) | 109.25 (CV 1.7%) |
| 22:37 `--adapt-async 1` | 0.1.44.1 | 99.54 (CV 2.5%) | 104.45 (CV 6.2%) |

Fair comparison = the warm/clean re-runs (the first post run is a cold expert-cache artifact, same pattern seen when swapping engines): **0.1.44.1 is ~-6% narrative / -8% code vs 0.1.43**, and `--adapt-async 1` recovers only the narrative side (99.54 vs 103.30). Two implications:

1. **The regression starts at 0.1.44, not 0.1.45.** 0.1.45's -23%/-27% is additive on top of the 0.1.44 drop (that half-range also changed the build pins and default flags, so it carries one extra variable — see `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE`).
2. This further implicates the 0.1.44 "pipelined-decode and latency work" as the primary suspect — the first release in the range already shows the drop on an otherwise identical build.

Bisect range refined: `e568e70371a3d2e0..7dfd34378bd2d32a` (0.1.43 -> 0.1.44.1) is the clean half; `7dfd34378bd2d32a..477ac13` (0.1.44.1 -> 0.1.45) is the additive half. Re-running with the pipelined-decode work disabled (or `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE=0`, `--mtp` off) is offered as before.

## What that leaves

With toolchain, submodule, config, argv and PCIe all matched, the delta is **Strata source between `e568e70371a3d2e0` (0.1.43) and `477ac13` (0.1.45)**. Prime suspects from the 0.1.44/0.1.45 release notes, all CPU/decode-scheduling side:

- "the pipelined-decode and latency work" (0.1.44)
- `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7` default on CUDA (0.1.42) interacting with the newer scheduler
- the MTP router guard (0.1.40.3) under `--mtp rt`
- `pcie_frac` self-adaptation converging to a different point (0.20 on 0.1.43 vs 0.20-0.25 on 0.1.45) even though the measured pool speed is the same

Corroborating signals on the regressed arms: GPU power drops 182 W -> 166 W (the GPU waits, it does not compute slower) while host CPU busy rises 50.2% -> 56.9% for the same token count.

## Related reports

- #2932 (gfx906, 2x Radeon Pro VII): 0.1.45 vs 0.1.43.1 — 32k decode ~13% slower **and 12/12 greedy texts differ**; `STRATA_TOPK_OLD=1` gives a third set of texts.
- #2711 (Strix Halo, 0.1.41): default CPU pool workers steal package power from the GPU; decode +14-30% with fewer workers. Same "CPU busier, GPU starved" shape.
- 0.1.45 release notes: "Moved to 0.1.46: the Volta/Pascal series. Together it made default decode on an RTX 3060 about 4% slower after a long prompt; we are finding the cause before it ships."

Happy to bisect the refined ranges above (the 0.1.43 -> 0.1.44.1 half is the clean one), or re-run with `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE=0`, `--mtp` off, or any specific switch on this box.

issues.title: [Bug]: Long sessions: parking evicts every conversation and still refuses (freed memory stays in glibc's heap)
issues.author: alfre2v
issues.body:
### What happened

After a server has been busy for a while, an agent's main conversation gets **read again from scratch** after a subagent switch, although parking is on and the budget isn't full. On my box, a 214K-token conversation took 90 s to re-read instead of 11 s. A freshly started server doesn't show it; it appears once many conversations have been parked and evicted.

The engine log shows it like this:
```
strata serve: conversation cache: skip parking (physical RAM admission; need 1483 MiB plus 3072 MiB floor, 4501 MiB available, source meminfo; evicted 3, 0 still parked)
strata serve: prompt 214234 tokens = 0 reused + 214234 read in 90425 ms (2369.2 tok/s), ...
```
`evicted 3, 0 still parked`: the RAM check threw away every parked conversation and still refused. A milder form appears too: `evicted 3 parked conversations to admit this snapshot`, where 1 would have been enough. Another conversation then loses its context for nothing.

**Cause:**
- parked conversations are 16 MiB `std::vector` segments (`conversation_buffer.hpp`);
- glibc's mmap threshold is dynamic: once a large mapped block has been freed, later 16 MiB segments come from the heap, and freeing them doesn't give the memory back to the OS;
- the RAM check reads `MemAvailable`, so evicting a conversation never shows up as free RAM.

The comments at `generate.cpp:8322-8324` and `conversation_cache.hpp:279-281` (v0.1.44.1) assume the opposite.

**Fix:** proposed in #2253 (`malloc_trim` in the RAM check). Independent test results on this box are in [my comment on #2253](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2253#issuecomment-6236955827): it fixes the gate in all three runs, with no prefill cost on short prompts.

**Workaround until a fix is released:** add one line to the `env` block of your run config (`strata-<model>.json`; the server passes it to the engine), then restart the server:
```json
"GLIBC_TUNABLES": "glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=4194304"
```
- 4 MiB or 8 MiB fix it on this box. 16 MiB fixes it only partly; 32 MiB or unset don't.
- Cost here: fresh-prompt reading 4-9% slower at 4K, about 3% at 32K, 2-3% at 120-250K. Decode is unaffected.
- Linux/glibc only. Setup re-runs keep `env` entries.

**To reproduce:** start the server with parking on (here `--conversation-cache-mib 8192 --conversation-cache-slots 4 --conversation-cache-min-free-mib 3072`). Send fresh prompts that park and evict several large conversations (here 32K-250K tokens), then run an agent session where a main conversation grows past about 190K tokens while alternating with subagents. The refusal comes at the main conversation's park. It reproduced on every unpatched run of that sequence.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`, engine built locally with CUDA 13.0) · RTX 3090 24GB, Ryzen 9 3900X, 64 GB RAM · Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35) · Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-grow`

### Engine log

The relevant lines are above. The full test data (ladder, soak and engine logs for unpatched, the workaround and #2253) is summarised in [my comment on #2253](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2253#issuecomment-6236955827).

issues.title: [gfx906] 0.1.45: Flash-Next answers differ from 0.1.43.1 and 32k decode is ~13 % slower; the wide top-k (#1749) and STRATA_TOPK_OLD=1 give different outputs
issues.author: petski3
issues.body:
**Setup:** 2x Radeon Pro VII 16 GB (gfx906, wave64), Ryzen 9 3950X, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, ROCm 7.14 in a docker build image (clang 23), ggml at the pinned 3cf0325.
Build as in docs/AMD_HIP.md: `cmake -DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=...`, targets `strata strata-device`.
Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S native pack, layer split 27 over both cards, `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1`, `--pcie-frac 0`, MTP spec 4, KV int8 + `--kv-resident 32768`.

Built from v0.1.45 (477ac13) with the three gfx906 build fixes from #2459 (we hit the same breaks: the cublas maps, `GGML_USE_HIP` on `strata_mmq_w4a4`, and `moe_f16_kq.cu` in the gfx906 `strata_mmq`). With them it builds and serves (`strata 0.1.45`).

## Observed, not localised: answers and 32k decode change on gfx906 (0.1.43.1 -> 0.1.45)

Interleaved A/B (old, new, old, new; same config, fixed-nonce bench + 6 greedy prompts x 768 tokens x 2; `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` on both):

| | prompt 4k / 32k tok/s | decode 4k / 32k (256 tok) | decode bench | hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1.43.1 (two arms) | 395 / 557, 393 / 551 | 43.1 / 51.3, 42.9 / 51.3 | 44.3, 44.7 | 89.5 % |
| 0.1.45 (two arms) | 394 / 564, 393 / 557 | 43.9 / 44.8, 43.7 / 44.8 | 43.7, 44.0 | 89.9 % |

- Each version reproduces itself exactly, arm to arm, but **12 of 12 greedy decode-bench texts differ between the versions**, from character 9-259. The release notes say Flash-Next answers are byte-identical; the identity gates listed are RTX 3060 / P100 / R9700 / A750, not gfx906.
- 32k: the 256-token reply to the same prompt takes 6258 vs 5227 ms with 229 vs 208 verify windows (drafts accepted 139 vs 162), so roughly +9 % per window on top of the different text.
- `STRATA_TOPK_OLD=1` on 0.1.45 gives a **third** set of texts (matches neither version), although #1749's docs say the wide and the original top-k give the same ids. On gfx906 they do not, possibly a wave64 issue in the wide kernel. It does not explain the whole difference.
- Separate good news: `--pipeline-windows 2` with `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1` no longer stalls on 0.1.45 (it stalled on 0.1.41 / 0.1.43.1 with "verify window (pipelined): the CPU experts of layer 22"), but it gives no decode gain on the mmap arena here (43.0 vs 44.0).

Happy to run any parity test or switch you want on the cards.
