issues.title: [Bug] conversation cache skips snapshot restore under RAM pressure: parked -> next request does a full 310-372K re-prefill (4/4), same sequence recovers normally when RAM is plentiful
issues.author: xzphot
issues.body:
> All numbers below are from a single production log (`strata-iq3_s.log`, v0.1.44) over 2026-10-17, quoted verbatim.

Related: #2228 (coarse-checkpoint fallback for a fast client — same family, mild form: 6.8K-47K re-reads; this report is the heavy form with a RAM-pressure variable), #2316 (slow replay on cache hit), #2409/#2408 (restore-path OOMs).

One more observation: the leftover `reused` value is always exactly **16384** — the default `--prompt-cache` grid step — which matches #2228's 32,768-grid finding (their rig sets `--prefill auto:32768`). So under RAM pressure the engine seems to fall back to the first grid checkpoint (or skip restore entirely) and re-prefill everything since.

## Environment

- Strata v0.1.44, win32, 79.9 GB physical RAM, RTX 3090 24 GB
- Single client (one ZCode window), single long session, port 8080
- Flags: `--max-context 524288 --kv int8 --conversation-cache-mib 12288 --conversation-cache-slots 3 --conversation-cache-min-free-mib 2048`
- Session grew 321K → 388K tokens over ~2.5 hours of continuous agent work

## Symptom

4 times tonight, the first request after a successful `parked` did **not** recover the snapshot and instead did a **full re-prefill** (310K–372K tokens read, 233–285 s at ~1300 tok/s):

```
prompt 325540 tokens = 325109 reused + 431 read ... 3129 generated
conversation cache: parked 328669 tokens in 2278.5 ms; parked=2 bytes=11511460824 evictions=42
prompt 330755 tokens = 16384 reused + 314371 read in 233714 ms (1345.1 tok/s), 195 generated   <-- full re-read
conversation cache: skip parking (physical RAM admission; need 5613 MiB plus 2048 MiB floor, 5840 MiB available)
conversation cache: restored 325535 tokens (checkpoint) in 1227.0 ms
prompt 328860 tokens = 325535 reused + 3325 read in 6281 ms   <-- normal
```

The re-read request is just snapshot + ~2K new tokens (`330755 = 328669 + 2086`), so the recovery path should have hit. Same pattern at 335593 (cancelled after 233 s re-read), 336411, and 388629:

```
conversation cache: parked 386540 tokens in 1338.4 ms; parked=1 bytes=6735893912 evictions=48
prompt 388629 tokens = 16384 reused + 372245 read in 284937 ms (1306.4 tok/s)   <-- full re-read
conversation cache: skip parking (snapshot 6457 MiB exceeds available budget)
```

All 4 re-reads follow a `parked` within one log line. Zero re-reads happened in any other situation tonight.

## Control group (same day, ~8 hours earlier, RAM not yet tight)

Same sequence — parked, then next request — recovers and hits normally even at 449K tokens:

```
conversation cache: parked 449168 tokens in 2936.3 ms; parked=1 bytes=7692905940 evictions=4
prompt 448985 tokens = 442368 reused + 6617 read in 8979 ms (737.0 tok/s)   <-- recovered, normal
```

Restore latency comparison, same magnitude snapshots:

| RAM state | restore | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| plenty | 134.9 ms | 69583 |
| plenty | 477.6 ms | 285205 |
| tight | 20481.9 ms | 332285 |
| tight | 5187.7 ms | 386625 |

So under RAM pressure snapshots page out, and the engine appears to skip the recovery path entirely and re-prefill from scratch — 4-5 minutes instead of seconds.

## Secondary observation

`--conversation-cache-mib 12288` cannot hold two snapshots of a 380K-token session (7.0–7.7 GB each):

```
conversation cache: parked 386540 tokens ... bytes=6735893912
conversation cache: skip parking (snapshot 6457 MiB exceeds available budget)
```

## Question

Is skipping recovery under RAM pressure intentional (avoid page-in death spiral), or should the engine prefer restoring the snapshot? Even with a slow page-in (~5-20 s), restoring beats a 285 s re-prefill by an order of magnitude. Either way, a log line explaining *why* recovery was not attempted would help diagnosis.

Also: is 12 GB a reasonable default budget for `--conversation-cache-mib` on a 79.9 GB machine running ~400K-token sessions, given one snapshot alone is 7+ GB?

issues.title: [Bug]: Intel Arc telemetry keeps an idle-unloaded server GPU awake
issues.author: pankleks
issues.body:
### What happened

On Intel Arc / xe, an idle-unloaded Strata server can keep the GPU awake even though there are no inference requests and the engine has exited. The Monitor displayed about 41 W, but that is not an independent power measurement.

The server starts `Telemetry._loop` for its lifetime, sampling once per second. `_XeGpu.read()` continues reading hwmon temperature/energy/power-cap and PCIe sysfs attributes after the model unloads. Closing the browser is not sufficient to stop this background sampler.

Reproduction:
1. Serve a model using the SYCL wrapper with `idle_unload_s=600` and Linux GPU `power/control=auto`.
2. Wait for `loaded:false`, no in-flight requests, and no DRM clients (also reproduced after explicit `/v1/unload`).
3. Observe only the driver's software PM counters, without sampling GPU sensors.

Expected: the unloaded server does not poll hardware and prevent runtime suspend; CPU/RAM/server metrics remain available.

Observed before the patch: `runtime_status=active`, `runtime_usage=0`, with +15,002 ms active and +0 ms suspended over a quiet 15-second interval. Stopping only Strata for 120 seconds yielded +14,422 ms active / +105,582 ms suspended, ending `suspended`.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Strata 0.1.45 / commit `477ac13cbe8e`, Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (ASRock, GSC 31.1062), Linux `7.0.14-24-pve`, unprivileged Linux container, IQ3_XXS at 262,144 context. No driver, firmware, model or power-policy change was needed for the reproduction.

### Engine log

The server logged `model unloaded after 600 s idle; the next request loads it again`. At a later check, request count was unchanged, `loaded:false`, `in_flight:0`, and the last inference was about 79 minutes earlier. No raw configuration or private logs are attached.

Prepared a small fix to pause SYCL GPU telemetry while `Service.loaded()` is false, keep non-GPU telemetry running, and reset the Intel reader's energy baseline before resuming. A check based only on transient Linux runtime-PM state was not sufficient; it is not part of the proposed final patch.

issues.title: strata_bench.py: NameError: name 'port' is not defined when it starts the server itself (0.1.45, since #2330)
issues.author: K8nsch
issues.body:
**What happens**

With no Strata server running, `tools\strata_bench.py --config strata-iq3_s.json --long` stops at once:

```
  File "C:\Tools\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 990, in main
    say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...")
NameError: name 'port' is not defined
```

**Cause**

69fe4055 (#2330, PR #2362) replaced

```python
port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
```

with `base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080)))`, so `port` is no longer bound, but lines 987, 990 and 991 (`start_server(cfg_path, port, ...)`) still use it. Only the path where the bench starts the server is affected; against a running server (or with `--url`) it works.

**Fix (suggestion)**

```python
port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), port)
```

(`port` is only needed in the branch with a config, which is the only branch that reaches line 987.)

**Setup:** Windows 11, 0.1.45 release zip (`strata-windows-x64.zip`), repo at 477ac13c. Worked around by starting the server first; the bench then uses the running server.

issues.title: [Bug]: reasoning_loop_recovery: recover never fires for a low or medium request (focused_recovery_prompt only matches the template's xhigh sentence)
issues.author: BoogeAI
issues.body:
### What happened

With `"reasoning_loop_recovery": "recover"` in a model config, a reply whose thinking repeats whole passages **is detected and then does nothing**: the server logs the detection and the thinking carries on to `reasoning_budget_tokens` (or to `max_tokens` when no budget is set). The reply is not continued with the low-effort instruction, and nothing says why.

Measured on 0.1.44.1 and again on 0.1.45, a community qwen4exp fine-tune (RVN abliterated IQ3_S), `reasoning_effort: low`, one prompt that makes the model re-verify the same facts, `max_tokens` 8192, `reasoning_budget_tokens` 8192 then 4096:

| run | budget | detection | what happened next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 8192 | `repeated reasoning detected at 3072 tokens (coverage=0.277)` | thought on to 6144, then the budget wrapped it up |
| 2 | 8192 | `repeated reasoning detected at 3072 tokens (coverage=0.289)` | the same |
| 3 | 4096 | `repeated reasoning detected at 3072 tokens (coverage=0.343)` | thought on to 4096, then the budget wrapped it up |

So the detector works (it is the log line above); the recovery step is what never runs.

### Why

`focused_recovery_prompt()` (`serve/server.py:196` in 0.1.45) builds the spliced prompt by replacing **the template's own xhigh sentence** (`HIGH_EFFORT`, line 160) in the first system message with the low one, and returns `None` when that sentence is not there as whole tokens:

```python
old, new = tok.encode(HIGH_EFFORT, parse_special=False), tok.encode(LOW_EFFORT, parse_special=False)
for i in range(len(head) - len(old) + 1):
    if head[i:i + len(old)] == old:
        return ids[:i] + new + ids[i + len(old):] + list(generated)
return None
```

With `"effort_position": "start"` (the default) a request that asks for **low** or **medium** is rendered with *that level's* sentence at the top of the first system message, so the xhigh sentence is absent and the function returns `None`. The caller only acts on a non-None result:

```python
recover_prompt = focused_recovery_prompt(self.tok, ids, raw_ids)
if recover_prompt is not None:
    break
```

`recover` is therefore a silent no-op for every low/medium request — which is the common case as soon as a config sets `"reasoning_effort": "low"` (as mine does, to keep a local model from burning its output budget on thinking) or a client picks Low in its own selector. `"reasoning_loop_recovery": "stop"` is unaffected (it does not use this function and did end the reply in my runs).

### How I checked it (no engine needed)

Rendering one request both ways with the server's own functions and then calling `focused_recovery_prompt` on it:

```
--- effort_position="start" (default)
    prompt tokens                : 63
    xhigh sentence in the prompt : False
    low   sentence in the prompt : True
    focused_recovery_prompt()    : None -> the recover branch cannot fire
--- effort_position="end"
    prompt tokens                : 105
    xhigh sentence in the prompt : True
    low   sentence in the prompt : True
    focused_recovery_prompt()    : 93 ids -> it can fire
```

Script: build the tokenizer and the `ChatTemplate` from a pack's `tokenizer/` exactly as `main()` does, then

```python
low_text  = tpl.render(msgs, reasoning_effort="low", add_generation_prompt=True)          # start
hist      = tpl.render(msgs, add_generation_prompt=False)                                 # end, default (xhigh)
full      = tpl.render(msgs, reasoning_effort="low", add_generation_prompt=True)
mine      = tpl.render(msgs, reasoning_effort="low", add_generation_prompt=False)
end_text  = hist + EFFORT_TURN.format(EFFORT_TEXT["low"]) + full[len(mine):]
for t in (low_text, end_text):
    print(focused_recovery_prompt(tok, tok.encode(t, parse_special=True), []))
```

### Workaround I use now

`"effort_position": "end"` in the model config: the history is then rendered with the template's default (xhigh) and the real level follows in a short system turn before the answer, so the xhigh sentence is in the prompt and the recovery can splice it. With it, the detection line is followed by `resuming the same output with the low-effort instruction (reasoning_loop_recovery)` (measured twice, coverage 0.277 and 0.343).

Two honest notes on that: the nudge is not a cure — in both runs the model went on thinking for another ~1000-3000 tokens to the budget — and `effort_position: "end"` is a separate opt-in with its own behaviour (the engine checkpoints in front of the tail turn).

### Suggested fix

Pass the request's level into `focused_recovery_prompt()` and look for *that* sentence (the template knows `low`, `medium`, `xhigh`; `high` maps to xhigh), or fall back to the low sentence when the level's own is not found. If neither is found, print one line saying the recovery was skipped and why, instead of failing silently — the current behaviour costs a full thinking budget with no hint.

### Environment

0.1.44.1 and 0.1.45, prebuilt CUDA 13.0 engine (sm_75/86/89/120) · RTX 5080 16 GB · Windows 11 26200 · Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 95 GB RAM. Config: `reasoning_effort: low`, `reasoning_budget_tokens: 4096/8192`, `reasoning_loop_recovery: recover`, `reasoning_close_retry: true`.

### Not tested

AMD HIP and SYCL (CUDA only here); a high/xhigh request under `effort_position: "start"` (that one renders the xhigh sentence at the top, so the recovery should fire — I did not run it); the Anthropic route's `output_config.effort` path; and whether the model's repetition after the nudge would end on its own with a different prompt.

issues.title: setup: SHA-256 check is wrong for large shards and deletes correct files
issues.author: Astemiir
issues.body:
## Summary

The SHA-256 check in `setup.py` is wrong for large files (the failures we see are 43–50 GB shards): it rejects a correct file, deletes it, downloads it again, and the next attempt fails the same way. Small files hash fine, so the bug only shows on the big model shards.

## What happens

```
checking Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00002-of-00003.gguf (SHA-256, 49.8 GB) ...
[X] ... has the wrong SHA-256 (cd6e40937ddf0f39d68748f1f086b423565fcb8a6d0a32f4ac52a5be35d8f744,
    expected 577a38a2392b40ca2193cea502e1d92f60b8cd370675d308e0ec21885d9daaa7): deleted
```

After a fresh 49.8 GB download the check reports another value (`ec899c68…`); shard 3 (43.8 GB) fails the same way (`e2f8d605…` vs expected `d4634e6d…`).

## Proof that the bytes are fine and the check is not

* Same file, external hasher (`certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256`): **`577a38a2…`** — exactly the `lfs.oid` the Hub publishes for `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`, both on `main` and on the commit pinned in `setup.py` (`38bb39ee…`).
* Shard 3, same external hasher: **`d4634e6d…`** — its Hub oid. Setup's own check on those same bytes said `e2f8d605…` and deleted the file.

Environment: Windows 10 19045, Python 3.13.13, Strata 0.1.45.

## Correct way to verify these files

Use an external hasher instead of `hashlib`:

* Windows: `certutil -hashfile "<file>" SHA256`
* macOS / Linux: `shasum -a 256 "<file>"`

and compare the result with the file's `lfs.oid` from the Hub API
(`https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<dir>?expand=true`).

## Also: do not delete on a mismatch

Rename the file to `<name>.bad` and keep it. Then a mismatch costs a re-check, not another 50 GB download, and the user still has the bytes for a manual verification.

## Workaround for users today

Put `<file>.done` next to the file containing `sha256 <expected>` — `verify_sha256` then skips the check. The `whole (checked against its own tensor directory)` form written by `whole_shard` is not enough for a pinned hash: it still re-hashes.

issues.title: [Other] Swift 1.5 on a Mac (opt-in --family swift, IQ3_S)
issues.author: oceanio
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]  (anything else, including setup and installation)

### What do you want to do?

Run Swift 1.5 on a Mac. On 0.2.0-beta, docs/MAC.md still says "The Swift and Coder releases are not set up on Mac
yet", and `metal/setup_mac.py` only takes `--family qwen|unsloth`.

**What blocks it.** Swift's two shards cut through a layer: in IQ3_S, layer 14's gate is in shard 1, and its up and
down are in shard 2. Its shard 1 also holds the n-gram table. The Metal engine maps one file (`window.cpp` wraps
shard 1), so it cannot read Swift as it is.

**What already works.**
- `metal/tools/metal_repack.py` (written for Unsloth's 4-6 shards) works on Swift's 2 shards as they are.
- `tools/iq_pack.py` already handles Swift's layout. It writes the 96 F32 routers as BF16, and all 96 are exact.
- The Metal gemv has IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS, which Swift uses for `attn_output`, `ssm_out` and `ffn_down_shexp`.
- The router read takes F32.
- The engine needs no change.

**What I propose (opt-in).** `./setup.sh --family swift` sets up Swift 1.5 IQ3_S: setup repacks it like Unsloth's
files, and leaves images off. Without `--family swift` nothing changes, including the size menu, the original model
and Unsloth's files. Only IQ3_S is offered, because it is the only size I could measure. I have this on a branch:

issues.title: [Feature Request] Opt-in LaTeX-safe JSON recovery for json_object responses (LightRAG VLM)
issues.author: BoysGameStudio
issues.body:
## Summary

When a vision-language model generates JSON containing an unescaped LaTeX
backslash, Strata's `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` validation
rejects the completion with HTTP 502 (`structured_output_failed`).

This breaks LightRAG's multimodal PDF ingestion because LightRAG already
implements tolerant JSON parsing and LaTeX escape recovery, but Strata
rejects the response before LightRAG can access the generated text.

The issue has been reproduced using the same image and prompt.

## Environment

- Strata v0.1.44.1 (Strata-NVFP4 fork)
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4
- GPU vision enabled
- LightRAG v1.5.7
- MinerU PDF pipeline
- OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API

## Minimal Reproduction

Model-generated content:

```text
{"name":"alpha coefficient","type":"diagram","description":"Coefficient \alpha_0"}
```

The sequence `\a` is not a valid JSON escape.

This can also be reproduced directly against Strata's validator:

```python
from serve.structured import _ObjectOnly, validated_json

raw = r'{"name":"alpha coefficient","type":"diagram","description":"Coefficient \alpha_0"}'

print(validated_json(raw, _ObjectOnly(), "stop"))
```

### Actual Behavior

- Strict JSON parsing fails.
- Strata returns HTTP 502 (`structured_output_failed`).
- The original generated response is unavailable to LightRAG.
- LightRAG retries the failed provider request.
- The document eventually enters the FAILED state.

### Expected Behavior

An optional recovery mode could repair unambiguous LaTeX escaping errors
before strict validation.

For example:

```json
{"name":"alpha coefficient","type":"diagram","description":"Coefficient \\alpha_0"}
```

The repaired output should still pass strict JSON validation before
being returned to the client.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce an opt-in, conservative JSON recovery mechanism for
`response_format=json_object`.

Suggested behavior:

1. Preserve existing strict validation by default.
2. Attempt limited LaTeX-aware repair when explicitly enabled.
3. Validate the repaired JSON using the existing validator.
4. Return canonical JSON only after successful validation.
5. Continue returning HTTP 502 for unrecoverable output.
6. Preserve existing `json_schema` behavior.

The implementation must also account for LaTeX commands such as:

- `\alpha`
- `\beta`
- `\frac`
- `\tau`
- `\nabla`

Some commands conflict with valid JSON escape sequences, so simply
doubling every backslash is unsafe.

Regression tests should cover legitimate JSON escapes, already-correct
LaTeX escaping, duplicate keys, invalid constants, and truncated output.

## Related Issues and PRs

- Strata #2368 — Grammar-Constrained Sampling
- Strata #1328 — Token Masks for JSON Formats with MTP
- LightRAG PR #3238 — Repair LaTeX Escape Damage in LLM JSON Responses
  https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/pull/3238
- LightRAG PR #3242 — Retry Malformed Multimodal Analysis JSON
  https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/pull/3242

Constrained decoding may prevent syntactically invalid JSON, but it does
not necessarily preserve LaTeX semantics when a model emits JSON-valid
escape sequences.

This feature would improve compatibility with LightRAG and other
applications processing mathematical or technical documents.

issues.title: [Engine] unbatched replicas still cross DONE ownership on 0.2.0-beta
issues.author: dynaxbill
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine] (the Python server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source: CPU-only protocol replay against the official 0.2.0-beta Python server. No model started.

### What happened

Re-tested after the tracker reset: the two request-ownership failures remain in release `3d1fb48`. An early-closed replica child can release the pipe lock before its DONE is drained; a successor can receive zero tokens or the predecessor's frames. Independently, shared DONE statistics can be overwritten after unlock. Expected: finish native cleanup before handoff and report only the caller's own DONE.

The official added replica-selected callback updates request telemetry; it does not close the child or snapshot DONE. PR #2886 now preserves that callback and repairs both ownership failures. This is a serving correctness fix, not a GPU kernel/default/performance change.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

```sh
git clone --single-branch --branch fix/replica-done-ownership-20261017 https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata.git
cd Strata
# Install the Python runtime requirements in an isolated environment first.
python tools/replay_replica_lifetime.py --output ./replica-v020-controls-new
python -m unittest -v serve.test_replica_lifetime
```

Choose an unused output directory. The replayer compares the pinned official release with close-only and full A using the actual repository reader/pump. It never loads a model or uses a GPU. Fetch `3d1fb48090e8f2cefc22d7b5845fb7f5b71f33fa` in shallow checkouts or supply its replicas.py via `--baseline-file`.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally: CPU protocol fixtures, including real OS pipes. This is not a new GPU/model reproduction.

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta release `3d1fb48090e8f2cefc22d7b5845fb7f5b71f33fa` (release engine package 0.1.45.3, not executed here). Refreshed repair tested on main `f57c0adcb31c00f3f216550c004dac4e713a9f70`. Those two upstream Python files equal the release before applying A.

### Graphics card, memory and system

Current replay: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0, CPython 3.12.14; no GPU/VRAM or model used. The replay PC's RAM was not recorded; no memory/performance claim. Historical GPU evidence only: 2x RTX 3090 24 GiB, dual EPYC 7663, VM 64 vCPU/384 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04, driver 610.43.02 on engine 0.1.44.1. Do not treat those historical runs as 0.2.0-beta GPU qualification.

### Model, size and settings

New reproduction: deterministic synthetic native protocol producer, not an LLM. Affected path is unbatched replicas with concurrent callers routed to the same native engine; both resident-KV and KVGROW can use it. Historical model was GSQ-RCO IQ3_S. No claim that every batched C4 request fails.

### Logs

| Current CPU control | Passed / 18 |
|---|---:|
| Official v0.2.0-beta | 9 |
| Close only | 16 |
| Full A, official callback preserved | 18 |

102/102 selected CPU serving tests also pass, including the official callback/telemetry tests. [Commands, actual logs, environments and limits](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/tests/data/replica_lifetime/v020-beta/README.md), [control results](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/tests/data/replica_lifetime/v020-beta/controls.json), [manifest](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/tests/data/replica_lifetime/manifest.json).

**Failed (intentional red controls):** official source9/18 and close-only 16/18. An earlier close-only15/18 run is retained; no fixed assertion was relaxed. Two initial missing-module/dependency setup failures are also retained and explained.

**Not run:** new-release GPU/model execution, native CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds, GPU performance, full-logits/KL and long-soak testing. Existing historical evidence and the original investigation remain linked in #2886.

issues.title: strata_bench.py records a layer-split run as single-GPU (card list and VRAM total)
issues.author: kristoffern
issues.body:
### What happened

A benchmark of a two-card layer split (RTX 3090 + RTX 4080 SUPER) produces a report naming only the first card:

```json
"gpu": ["NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090"], "gpu_vram_mib": 24576
```

while the server reports both correctly:

```json
"machine": {"gpu": {"name": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER",
                    "total_mib": 40952}}
```

and the engine log says `layer split: layers 0-28 (CUDA0), 29-47 (CUDA1), one hand-off per window`.

Cause, `tools/strata_bench.py:614-616`:

```python
elif len(used) > 1 and static.get("gpu_name"):
    named = [g for g in used if g["name"] == static["gpu_name"]]
    used = named[:1] or used[:1]
```

With a split, `static["gpu_name"]` is `"A + B"`, so no single card equals it, `named` is empty, and `used` is truncated to the first card. `gpu_vram_mib` is then summed over that one card (lines 627-628), overriding the server's correct total. The `" + "` form is already parsed 20 lines below (#2001), but that branch only fires when the served cards are *not* all local (the other-vendor case), so a split across two local NVIDIA cards never reaches it.

The branch is only reached when `cfg` is None, i.e. with `--url`. On current main that is the only way to benchmark at all, because `bench.sh` crashes when it starts the server itself (#2872). So at the moment every layer-split run benchmarked with the tool is reported as single-GPU, in both the card list and the VRAM total.

To reproduce: a config with `"gpu": [0, 1]`, start the server, then `./bench.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. The generated `README.md` and `results.json` name one card.

Suggested fix: match each name the server gives, keeping the count.

```python
elif len(used) > 1 and static.get("gpu_name"):
    served_names = [n for n in static["gpu_name"].split(" + ") if n and n != "?"]
    named = [g for g in used if g["name"] in served_names]
    used = named[:len(served_names)] or used[:1]
```

Checked against this machine's values: the split case becomes `["RTX 3090", "RTX 4080 SUPER"]` / 40952 MiB, and both single-card-of-two cases are unchanged.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Engine 0.1.45, main at 477ac13c (these lines unchanged on main today). RTX 3090 + RTX 4080 SUPER, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 base), engine compiled from source.

issues.title: [Other] gfx906 / MI50: reproducible Linux releases and community validation
issues.author: romeo5353535353-ui
issues.body:
### Area

[Other]

## What do you want to do?

I am planning a local API server with AMD Instinct MI50 (gfx906), primarily running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. The application will extract GPU mining benchmark records into JSON from Discord message text and locally generated OCR text. Reliable repeated requests and correct extracted values matter more to this workload than peak token throughput.

Thank you for keeping the community gfx906 path available. I understand that it is an opt-in wave64 build, that setup does not install it automatically, and that the maintainers do not have a gfx906 card. I have not built or benchmarked v0.1.45 on this hardware yet.

Could we establish a small, reproducible Linux validation path for current releases?

1. **A pinned build recipe and a compile smoke check per release.** Pin the ROCm/gfx906 image or toolchain and llama.cpp revision, and build the actual `strata` serving executable. An optional community-maintained recipe or container would already help; automatic installation could follow later. This would make build regressions such as #2459 easier to catch.
2. **Documented starting configurations and support limits.** A tested baseline for one or two MI50 cards, distinguishing 16 GB and 32 GB boards, model/quantization, KV format, context, MTP and layer split. Please mark options measured only on RDNA/CUDA separately from those validated on gfx906, and state whether Qwen3.6 and CPU vision are supported on this path.
3. **A maintainer-agreed community test checklist.** We can contribute reports covering exact versions and configuration, self-tests, fresh-prompt processing, decode, first-token latency, long-context correctness, repeated API requests and one versus two clients. Results should include warm-up, repeated measurements, errors and answer correctness, not only tokens/s. What is the smallest useful test set for contributors without access to your other GPU backends?

Related work:

- #641: the original gfx906 port and the maintainers' preference for a separate opt-in build.
- #2459: the existing v0.1.44.1 build regression report. Any reproduced build failure should be followed up there rather than duplicated here.
- #1923: expert-cache policy experiments; the reported offline hit-rate improvement is not yet an end-to-end speed measurement.
- #2461: multi-GPU settings whose gains did not transfer to a fully resident gfx906 workload.

For v0.1.45, source inspection still shows the missing cuBLAS aliases discussed in #2459 in `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h`, while `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` uses those names. This is a static observation, not a claim that I reproduced a v0.1.45 build failure.

Would a community-maintained Linux recipe plus this validation checklist be a useful first contribution? Which of these steps would you prefer us to start with?

---

## Re-test on 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-19)

- **Version:** v0.2.0-beta, commit `3d1fb480`
- **Hardware:** 2x AMD Instinct MI50 16 GB (gfx906, the driver reports `1002:66af`), Ryzen 7 5700X, 64 GB DDR4-3600, ASUS ROG Strix X570-E
- **System:** Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-147, ROCm from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete` (the image `docs/AMD_HIP.md` names)
- **Build:**
  ```sh
  cmake -S . -B build-906 -G Ninja -DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 \
        -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++
  ninja -C build-906 strata
  ```

**Result: the gfx906 build still fails on 0.2.0-beta**, with the same errors as 0.1.44+:

```
src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:1555:13: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cublasSgemm'; did you mean 'hipblasSgemm'?
src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:1958:29: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx'
src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:1972:29: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx'
```

The `qwen35` targets are still added unconditionally in `CMakeLists.txt` (around line 730), and
`include/strata/platform/hip_compat/strata_hip.h` still has no `cublasSgemm` / `cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx`
mapping. `generate.cpp` already guards every use with `#if defined(STRATA_HAVE_QWEN35)`, so wrapping that block in
`if(NOT STRATA_HIP_GFX906)` is enough for the engine to build and link (verified locally by applying exactly that
patch to 0.1.45).

**What works today:** the same machine builds and runs **v0.1.43.1** (`a0116b2`) with `STRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON`, 2x MI50,
Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at the full 131,072-token context. Measured decode 66-68 tok/s with `--pipeline-windows 2`
(+36% over the default) and 371 tok/s prompt reading; report in #3173 and PR #3175.

So the gfx906 path is usable, but only by pinning the checkout to 0.1.43.1. A build fix for the qwen35 block (or a
`-DSTRATA_SKIP_QWEN35=ON` switch) would let MI50 owners follow `docs/AMD_HIP.md` on a current release again.

issues.title: bench.sh crashes with NameError when it starts the server itself (regression from #2330)
issues.author: kristoffern
issues.body:
### What happened

`./bench.sh` (with no `--url`) crashes before it starts the model:

```
  File "tools/strata_bench.py", line 990, in main
    say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...")
NameError: name 'port' is not defined
```

Commit 69fe4055 (#2330) replaced

```python
port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
```

with `base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080)))`, but `port` is still used at lines 987, 990 and 991 (`start_server(cfg_path, port, ...)`). Every run where bench.sh starts the server hits this. Running with `--url` against an already running server works, because it skips that branch.

To reproduce: a set-up install with no server running, then `./bench.sh`.

Suggested fix: keep the variable.

```python
port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), port)
```

Workaround until then: start the model with `./run-<model>.sh`, then `./bench.sh --url http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Engine 0.1.45 (main at 477ac13c, still present on main today). RTX 3090, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 base), engine compiled from source by setup.

issues.title: Windows HIP: limit the #1630 prefill cap and warning to the affected archs (gfx1030 is stable at 8192+)
issues.author: ByteJuggler
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1630 (closed in the 3-day clean-up): another data point, on a different AMD card:

**On an RX 6900 XT (gfx1030) on Windows 11, chunks of 8192 tokens and above have been completely stable, never slower, and up to 12% faster on long prompts.**

So the crash in #1630 may be specific to gfx1100 or its prompt path, not to Windows HIP or AMD Radeon as a whole.

**Setup**
- Engine 0.1.44.1, ready-made HIP zip (ROCm 10.2.0a20260930).
- RX 6900 XT 16 GB, gfx1030, AMD Software 26.8.1. *gfx1030 has no hipBLASLt table, so the plain hipBLAS path runs.*
- Windows 11 Pro 23H2.
- i7-5930K, 128 GB DDR4-2133 (64 GB and 92 GB for some earlier runs), 32 GB page file.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0, IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS.
- Flags: `--kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --vram-reserve-mib 1024 --pool-tasks 36`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, `--max-context` 131072 up to 262144.

**Stability**
- 45 engine starts in tuning sweeps with `--prefill` at 8192, 10240, 12288 or 16384, plus the servers started by hand for the long-context tests.
- Prompts from 4K up to 255K tokens, with 8192 and 12288 as the usual settings.
- No crashes and no 0xC0000409.
- Commit charge stayed flat. During a run of 64K–248K prompts at `--prefill 12288` and 262144 context (IQ3_XXS), the system commit peaked at 75.4 GB and the engine's working set at 45.3 GB, sampled every 30 s.

**Speed** (prompt tok/s, Q2_0 at 131072 context, compared with 8192; decode unchanged)

| `--prefill` | 4K | 16K | 32K | 60K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | −18% | −18% | −19% | −20% |
| 7168 | 0 | −12% | 0 | −2% |
| 10240 | 0 | +7% | −1% | +2% |
| 12288 | 0 | +3% | +11% | +5% |

- IQ3_S, 150K prompt: 895 tok/s at the default `auto` (capped at 6144), 1,007 tok/s at `--prefill 12288` (+12%).
- At 262144 context with 12288 chunks, 255K prompts read at 950–990 tok/s.

**Suggestion**

On gfx1030, *the `auto` cap of 6144 and the warning at every start cost about 10% on long prompts*, for a crash that hasn't shown up on this card.

**So,** could the cap and the warning apply only to the archs where it was seen (gfx1100, or the hipBLASLt prompt path if that's where it comes from)?

I can run a build with the cap lifted for gfx1030 and measure plain `--prefill auto`, if that would help.

issues.title: [Bug]: chat/completions stream ignores stream_options.include_usage (usage stays on the finish_reason chunk)
issues.author: Eranicus30666
issues.body:
### What happened

OpenAI's streaming contract: with `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}`, the last chunk before `[DONE]` has `"choices": []` and carries `usage`; the other chunks carry no usage. `/v1/chat/completions` ignores `stream_options` and always puts `usage` on the same chunk as `finish_reason`.

In my setup (LiteLLM in front of Strata), LiteLLM does not read the usage from that chunk and recounts the tokens itself, lower than the engine's count. A client that uses this number to decide when to compact its context then compacts too late.

Expected: with `include_usage: true`, the usage in its own last chunk with `"choices": []`; unchanged without the option. A PR with a fix follows.

Related: #2278 adds the legacy /v1/completions endpoint and says its final chunk already carries the usage; this issue is only about /v1/chat/completions.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.45 · 2x NVIDIA A2 16GB (sm_86) · Debian 13, CUDA 13.4

issues.title: tools/strata_bench.py: NameError: name 'port' is not defined — bench cannot start a server (regression from 69fe4055 / #2330)
issues.author: yusheng227507
issues.body:
## Summary
`tools/strata_bench.py` is broken in **v0.1.45 (477ac13c)**. Any run that starts its own server (i.e. `--config` without `--url`) dies immediately with `NameError: name 'port' is not defined`. Passing `--url` (pointing at an already-running server) still works, so the failure is confined to the "start the server" path.

## Environment
- Strata: `v0.1.45` / commit `477ac13c`
- OS: Ubuntu (Linux), Python from the project `.venv`
- Hardware: 2x RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75)
- Config: the standard `strata-*.json` with `"port": 8080`, `"host": "0.0.0.0"`
- No server running on the port at the time (so the "start our own server" branch is taken).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Make sure nothing is listening on the config's port (e.g. `8080`).
2. Run the bench without `--url`:
   ```
   .venv/bin/python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-iq3_s.json --out bench/results/x
   ```

## Actual result
It fails before loading the model (and therefore before any measurement):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/yusheng/strata/tools/strata_bench.py", line 1037, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
             ^^^^^^
  File "/home/yusheng/strata/tools/strata_bench.py", line 990, in main
    say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...")
                                            ^^^^
NameError: name 'port' is not defined
```
Exit code 1.

## Expected result
The bench starts the server on the configured port, waits for readiness, and runs the suite (as it did in v0.1.44.1 and earlier).

## Root cause
Commit **`69fe4055`** ("tools: poll the server address the config binds, not loopback (#2330)") replaced

```python
        port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
        base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
```

with

```python
        base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080)))
```

That removed the only assignment of the local name `port`, but three later uses in the same `else` branch still reference it (the "port is used by something that is not Strata" message, the "Starting ... on port {port}" message, and `start_server(cfg_path, port, ...)`). The `--url` path skips the branch, so it never trips.

The new test added by that commit (`tools/test_bench_host.py`) only exercises `server_base()` in isolation, so it does not catch the missing local.

## Suggested fix
Restore the local name (keeping the new `server_base` host handling):

```python
    else:
        port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))
        base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), port)
```

## Workaround (no source change)
Start the server yourself and point the bench at it, which bypasses the broken branch:
```
.venv/bin/python serve/server.py --engine strata --config <cfg>.json --port 8080 &
.venv/bin/python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --out bench/results/x
```

issues.title: macOS Metal build broken: CUDA-only symbols missing from metal_compat and Metal stubs (compile at 477ac13, link at a2de744)
issues.author: maverns
issues.body:
Machine: Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 27.0.1, Command Line Tools 27.0.0 (Apple clang 21.0.0), SDK 27.0.

Command: ./setup.sh --model UD-Q4_K_XL --vision no --no-browser --no-start --context 196608 --yes. It stops at step 4 with "the Metal engine did not build".

At 477ac13 (current main), the compile fails. Six symbols are missing from metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h:
- src/core/verify.cpp: cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor and cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor (added in 88a1c23f), plus cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange and cudaStreamCreateWithPriority (added in bc90e1ac).
- src/core/peer_experts.cpp: cudaMemcpyPeer and cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess (added in 33150724, #2666).

At a2de744 (parent of bc90e1ac), everything compiles but the link fails. The undefined symbols are strata::kernels::gdn_step_norm_groups, qsa_block_scores_rows and qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows. They are called from verify.cpp (Verifier::record_window, capture_commit_batch), but there is no Metal definition and no entry in metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp. They were introduced by f629fb04 ("Batch decode: one launch for all rows…").

Possible fix: guard these call sites the way src/core/mtp.cpp already guards its stream-priority calls (#if … && !defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)), or add Metal stubs.

issues.author: BBQ2077
issues.body:
## Summary

Sharing measurements from my tuned Q2_0 setup for others with similar hardware, especially a 32 GiB RAM system.

Short-chat decode reached a median of 64.7 tok/s. Three longer generations, each producing 1,024 tokens, measured 64.2 / 64.9 / 69.1 tok/s. Fresh 16K and 32K prompts took about 73 and 105 seconds to the first token, respectively. Follow-up conversations benefited from prefix reuse.

Measured on 2026-10-17. These results describe the combined configuration below.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070, 16 GB, gfx1201; engine reports 16,304 MiB.
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5700, 8 cores / 16 threads, AVX2.
- RAM: 4 x 8 GiB DDR4, configured at 2666 MT/s; 31.80 GiB OS-visible.

- OS: Windows 11 Home, build 26300.

- Bundled ROCm: 10.2.0a20260930; hipBLASLt: 100500.
- Python: project .venv, 3.14.6.
- Normal desktop background workload; no power-setting changes during the test.

## Model and settings

Original Flash-Next GSQ-RCO Q2_0, with these source files:

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00001-of-00002.gguf
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf

Actual startup allocation:

- CPU pool: 7 workers plus the host thread, with --host-core last.
- Active RDNA4 defaults logged: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 and STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7.

STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0.5 biases expert selection toward resident experts, and the projection changes residual activations; both are part of the measured setup.

## Results

Median (min–max). Prompt/decode speeds are from API engine timings; time to first token (TTFT) is measured by the client.

| Workload | Requests | Actual prompt tokens | Output tokens | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Short chat | 9 | 43–51 | 100 | 105.5 (45.8–118.7) | 64.7 (36.8–72.2) | 0.480 (0.425–0.960) |
| Fresh 4K prompt | 3 | 4,019 | 24 | 187.8 (143.2–193.2) | 42.3 (32.8–45.9) | 21.434 (20.843–28.093) |
| Fresh 16K prompt | 3 | 16,058 | 24 | 219.8 (217.4–245.1) | 39.6 (37.0–43.1) | 73.106 (65.580–73.901) |
| Fresh 32K prompt | 3 | 32,049 | 24 | 304.6 (290.1–305.6) | 46.5 (41.9–57.7) | 105.273 (104.915–110.545) |
| Agent follow-up | 15 | 3,741–14,557 | 5–64 | 226.4 (184.0–429.3) | 63.1 (41.4–100.6) | 12.791 (4.645–17.266) |
| Longer generation | 3 | 97 | 1,024 | 72.1 (47.9–85.5) | 64.9 (64.2–69.1) | 1.368 (1.156–2.050) |

Short-chat decode medians by round: 37.6 / 66.6 / 64.7 tok/s. All three rounds are included in the overall result.

Agent prefix reuse was 68.72% (68.69–68.74%) per session. Only 2–4 old-conversation tokens were re-read per session. On the final follow-up turn, total context was about 14.5K tokens, with 2,899 fresh tokens; median TTFT was 6.825 seconds.

## Method and checks

- Ran tools/strata_bench.py with --runs 3 --long.
- One server session, one GPU, sequential requests, temperature 0, thinking off.
- Four warm-up/calibration requests excluded from the measured results; model loading also excluded.
- Fresh prompts had unique tags and zero reused tokens. Expert-cache state and OS file-cache state were retained within the session.
- Agent workload: three sessions, each with one initial turn and five document-addition turns; tool schemas were supplied, with instructions not to call tools.
- Additional long-output test: three requests for a detailed local-inference performance guide, each capped at and producing 1,024 tokens.
- Official suite: 0 failed requests, 0 skipped tests.
- Arithmetic, Chinese arithmetic and JSON-format checks: 3/3 passed.
- Official needle_bench.py, --lengths 4k --depths 10,50,90: 3/3 found; actual prompt lengths were 3,327 / 3,327 / 3,328 tokens.

Whole-system telemetry sampled approximately every five seconds showed RAM usage up to 31.56 GiB. The engine startup log reported 23.6 GiB of mapped expert pages for CPU prefill sharing versus 22.7 GiB of free RAM. The configuration was kept unchanged throughout the test.

The practical result on this machine is roughly 65 tok/s for generation, with longer initial waits for fresh documents and shorter waits when continuing a cached conversation. The allocated context was 64K; fresh-prompt measurements reached about 32K.

issues.title: [Feature]: Monitor: one widget per batch slot, so several requests at once each show their own speed
issues.author: street-tripy
issues.body:
When `"parallel": N` is set, I want to see at a glance that the requests are really decoding
*together*, each with its own rate — and which slot is reading, decoding or free.

Today the Monitor only shows one request's number: the header pill reads `Generating · 79.8
tok/s` (the newest request) and the Model state card shows one request's progress and rate. With
two coding agents running I cannot tell from the page whether they are interleaved or one after
the other, so I end up watching the engine log's `strata batch: ... avg 2.00 rows, ... ms/window`
line instead — which is a strange thing to have to do to answer "is it busy?".

What I would like: one widget per batch slot in the Monitor — `Worker 1`, `Worker 2`, … — each
with the slot's state (Reading / Decoding / Free), its own live tok/s, how many tokens it has
written and how long it has been in the slot, and that slot's context fill. The header pill
would name every decoding stream when more than one is decoding (`2 decoding · 80.4 + 76.1
tok/s`).

Workaround I use today: `curl /metrics` and read `live.slots` by hand, or the engine log. The
data is already there — `live.slots` has carried `slot`, `state`, `prompt_tokens`, `generated`,
`elapsed_s` and `tok_s` per slot since #465; the page simply does not show it.

It should stay out of the way for everyone else: the card only appears when `/metrics` reports
`live.parallel`, i.e. when the run config sets `"parallel": N`. Without it the Monitor is
exactly what it is today.

I have a patch ready for this (4 files, 98 insertions: `index.html`, `app.js`, `app.css`, plus
the same page test as `test_the_card_is_on_the_page` in `test_monitor.py`) and will open a PR
against it if that is welcome.

issues.body:
**What happened.** An install built for a Tesla V100 (engine and `strata-vision` for sm_70, Docker image based on `Dockerfile.v100`) was started on two Tesla P40s (sm_61) with `GPUS=0,1`. Setup noticed the new architecture and recompiled the engine:

```
Compiling the engine for sm_61, sm_70 (a card it had no code for; 10-20 minutes, once) ...
[ok] engine compiled: /opt/strata/engine-cuda12/strata
```

but it did not rebuild the image encoder. The server then stopped at start:

```
loading the vision encoder ...
RuntimeError: the vision encoder did not start:
```

The message after the colon is empty: the encoder exits without printing anything (compute mode was `Default`, so it is not the #1445 case).

**Cause.** `cuobjdump --list-elf` on the two binaries:

```
engine-cuda12/strata         62 sm_61, 62 sm_70
engine-cuda12/strata-vision  139 sm_70
```

`BUILD.json` then listed `archs [61, 70]` and `vision: gpu`, while `strata-vision` still had sm_70 code only.

**Workaround.** Rebuilding the encoder with the same call as `Dockerfile.v100` (`setup.cmake_build(ROOT/"tools"/"vision", ..., "strata-vision", [..., "-DSTRATA_VISION_CUDA=ON", "-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=61;70", ...])`) and copying it to `engine-cuda12/` fixes it; the server starts with vision on both P40s.

**Suggestions.** When setup recompiles the engine for a new architecture, rebuild `strata-vision` for the same list (or check its architectures, e.g. via `vision_src`/archs in `BUILD.json`); and when the encoder exits without a line, name the likely cause (no kernel image for this GPU) instead of an empty message.

Environment: Strata 0.1.44.1, CUDA 12.8 toolkit, driver 580.178.04, Linux 7.0, Docker. Benchmark of this setup: #2854.

issues.title: Mac mini M6 (16 GB): Q2_0 streaming works - measured 11.7->27.2 tok/s + arena fix for sub-32 GB Macs
issues.author: hansong80
issues.body:
First data point for a **sub-32 GB Mac**, following up on MAC.md's "smaller Macs are untested".

**Machine:** Mac mini, Apple M6, 16 GB unified memory, macOS 27.0.1, ~185 GB free disk.
**Setup:** `git clone` + `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com ./setup.sh --yes` (mainland China network — direct huggingface.co connected but transferred 0 bytes; the mirror fixed it at ~70 MB/s). Selected pack: **Q2_0**, SSD expert streaming, MTP auto-off, context 32768. Engine built from source with the stock `./setup.sh` (Metal).

### Result

The server starts and serves, but **every inference fails** on a 16 GB Mac out of the box:

```
[strata] the engine reported an error: metal prompt: no arena region for the prompt buffers
```

Cause: at the moment the arena is sized, `vm_stat` shows only ~200 MB free, and the default "keep 7 GB for macOS" rule (MAC.md) leaves nothing for the prompt buffers.

### Fix

In `strata-q2_0.json` -> `env`:

```json
"STRATA_METAL_KEEP_FREE_GB": "3",
"STRATA_METAL_ARENA_GB": "8"
```

Restart with `./run-q2_0.sh`. Everything then works.

### Measured (engine's own "done:" lines, Q2_0, 32K ctx)

| Condition | tok/s |
|---|---:|
| Cold cache (first request after start) | 11.7 |
| Warmed up (subsequent short requests) | 14.6 – 27.2 |

So a 16 GB M6 is usable — close to the 32 GB M4 mini's documented ~14 tok/s.

### Minor note

`"enable_thinking": false` in the request is ignored (reasoning_content still generated); `reasoning_budget_tokens` is the working knob, as the server log helpfully says. Could MAC.md mention the KEEP_FREE_GB/ARENA_GB combination as the first thing to try below 32 GB? That would have saved me the debugging.

issues.title: 5700xt use IQ3_S mistake
issues.author: niupkk
issues.body:
# RDNA1 (gfx1010, RX 5700 XT): GPU page-fault floods, card resets and host freezes — three findings, one fixed

**Engine**: Strata 0.1.44.1, locally built HIP engine (`source: local-hip`, `archs: ["gfx1010"]`, `src: 7dfd34378bd2d32a`)
**Card**: AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT, Navi 10, gfx1010, 8 GB, 40 CU — the card `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` lists as "built by hand"
**Status**: usable, with a hard context ceiling. One of the three findings has a one-line fix that I believe other RDNA1 users need.

I am reporting this because `AGENTS.md` says a report from hardware the maintainers do not have is welcome. All
numbers below are measured on this machine; nothing is estimated. Everything I tried and measured — including what
did **not** help — is listed in §6 so you do not have to re-run it.

---

## 1. Summary

| # | Finding | State |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | The expert arena is larger than the kernel's default amdgpu **GTT window**, so the GPU is handed host addresses it cannot translate → page-fault flood → `GPU reset begin!` → **`VRAM is lost`, the desktop dies with it** | **Fixed** by `amdgpu.gttsize=57344` (one line + `update-initramfs -u` + reboot) |
| **B** | The **batched prompt path** stalls at "waiting for the GPU (attention, router)" and resets the card | Unfixed; worked around with `--short-read` |
| **C** | A prompt **longer than ~5,000 tokens** completes reading, then the first generation step fails with `verify: ... never rang` while the GPU accesses **fabricated addresses in the 92–124 GiB range** on a machine with 70 GiB of memory total | Unfixed; worked around with a small `--max-context` |

Finding A is the important one for other users, and I think it is a *documentation* bug at least, because its
arithmetic covers a large group of machines (§3.4).

---

## 2. What to record — machine, model, settings

**Hardware**

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (Navi 10, gfx1010), 8 GB VRAM (7.98 GiB), 40 CU, PCIe **4.0 x16 at full speed**
  (16.0 GT/s, width 16), power cap 180 W, 53 °C at idle and 54–56 °C under load. `gfx1010:xnack-`.
- CPU: Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4 (28 threads, AVX2, **no AVX-512**)
- RAM: 62 GiB (DDR4 ECC; per-module speed/type not captured — `dmidecode` needs root)
- Motherboard: X99-D8I, Intel VT-d / IOMMU active
- Storage: KIOXIA KXG70PNV2T04 2 TB NVMe (models on it)

**Software**

- Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel **7.0.0-38-generic**, amdgpu (open source, no amdgpu-pro)
- Strata 0.1.44.1, release tarball, engine compiled locally for gfx1010
- ROCm **7.14.0a20260612** from TheRock's `https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx101X-dgpu/` index, installed **inside the project venv** (no system ROCm)
- llama.cpp pinned commit `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d` (the `LLAMA_CPP_COMMIT` of 0.1.44.1)
- Build options: `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON`, `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1010`

**Model**

- `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`, **IQ3_S**, 2 shards, 83,617,662,656 bytes, both SHA-256 verified (fetched from ModelScope — HuggingFace is unreachable from this network)
- MTP draft layer: `mtp/rt/dense.bin` 116,099,072 bytes, `mtp/rt/experts.bin` 707,788,800 bytes, `mtp-q2_0.gguf` 889,017,216 bytes
- Engine reports the expert region as **46.84 GiB**, loaded at 2.48–2.55 GiB/s
- `docs/MODELS.md` / `setup.py` list the IQ3_S arena as **50.3 GB**

**Settings (the configuration all measurements below use)**

```
--pack <IQ3_S pack> --native <shard1> --ple-gguf <shard2>
--expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto
--spec 2 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <mtp/rt>
--max-context 5120 --short-read 5120 --kv fp16 --vram-reserve-mib 1024
env: HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0, GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576
```

Serving with `host: 0.0.0.0`, `port: 8080`, API key set. `vm.min_free_kbytes` raised from 66 MiB to 1 GiB.

**Getting the gate open.** I mirrored your own `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1103` opt-in rather than editing defaults —
4 additions in `setup.py` (`ROCM_INDEXES`, `ROCM_FAMILY_PINS`, `AMD_ARCHS`, `AMD_NAMES`) plus
`GFX1010_OPT_IN = os.environ.get("STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1010") == "1"`. With it set, `./setup.sh --backend hip
--check` reports `[ok] GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT ... 8.0 GB VRAM` / `IQ3_S needs ~62 GB RAM: fits`.
If you want this upstream I am happy to open it as a one-change PR; it leaves the default path byte-identical.

---

## 3. Finding A — the expert arena does not fit the default GTT window (**fixed**)

### 3.1 Symptom

A request that sustains work for more than ~20 s produced this, every time, and took the desktop down with it:

```
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:24 vmid:8 pasid:19)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000000000000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: GCVM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_STATUS:0x00801031
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:          Faulty UTCL2 client ID: TCP (0x8)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:          PERMISSION_FAULTS: 0x3
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: gmc_v10_0_process_interrupt: 188 callbacks suppressed
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: GPU reset begin!. Source:  1
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!
```

The `pasid` in the fault header shows a **host/userptr** address space — the faults are against memory the engine
pinned in RAM and handed to the GPU, not against VRAM.

### 3.2 The arithmetic

```
amdgpu's default gttsize = half of system RAM
                         = 31.31 GiB   (on 62 GiB;  confirmed via
                                        /sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_gtt_total)
IQ3_S expert arena       = 50.3 GB     (46.84 GiB as the engine reports it)
```

The arena is **1.6× the window**. Anything the GPU touches past the window cannot be translated.

### 3.3 The fix and its measured effect

```sh
echo 'options amdgpu gttsize=57344' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/amdgpu-gtt.conf   # MB => 56 GiB
sudo update-initramfs -u          # amdgpu loads from the initramfs on Ubuntu; the file alone did not change it
sudo reboot
```

After the reboot `mem_info_gtt_total` reads **56.00 GiB** and system RAM is unchanged (so `gttsize` here is a limit,
not a preallocation — worth confirming on your side).

Same request, before and after (short prompt + 1,200 generated tokens, identical settings otherwise):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| result | **GPU reset at 23.7 s, desktop frozen** | **completes in 62.8 s** |
| decode | — (crashed) | **20.0 tok/s** |
| GPU page faults | every request | **none** |
| card access beyond the window | yes | none |

A 4,554-token prompt that previously died with `verify: layer 44 never rang` also then completed
(`prompt=4554 tokens at 26.4 tok/s`).

### 3.4 Why I think this matters beyond my card

The rule "default GTT = RAM/2" means the threshold is `RAM >= 2 × arena`. Against your own `MODELS` table:

| model | arena | RAM needed for the default GTT to fit |
|---|---|---|
| IQ1_M (Coder) | 23.4 GB | 47 GB |
| Q2_0 | 34.0 GB | 68 GB |
| IQ2_XS | 35.5 GB | 71 GB |
| IQ3_XXS | 42.9 GB | 86 GB |
| **IQ3_S** | **50.3 GB** | **~101 GB** |

So **any Linux AMD machine under ~101 GB of RAM running IQ3_S has the default window too small** — including every
64 GB machine, which is what `docs/MODELS.md` recommends as the IQ3_S minimum ("needs a 64 GB PC"). It does not bite
on CUDA (no GTT) or on Windows, which may be why it has not shown up.

**Asks:**
1. Can you confirm on an AMD Linux box with a known-small `gttsize` whether the arena exceeding the window is the
   same root cause behind other "device wedged"/reset reports? A one-line check is `mem_info_gtt_total` vs the
   arena size.
2. `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` asks RDNA1 users to build by hand. I would suggest adding one line there: **check
   `mem_info_gtt_total` against the model's arena before the first run, and raise `amdgpu.gttsize` if it is
   smaller.** It cost me several hours and one hard power cycle to find.
3. If the engine can read `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/mem_info_gtt_total` at startup and warn (or refuse) when
   the arena exceeds it, that would catch this class of machine before the freeze.

---

## 4. Finding B — the batched prompt path stalls and resets the card (**unfixed**)

Your own watchdog reports it (issue #29), verbatim:

```
no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): waiting for the GPU
(attention, router) at layer 32 of the prompt chunk from token 0) - stopping the engine so
the server starts it again (issue #29) - please report it at github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues.
```

Kernel side, at the same moment:

```
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: [gfxhub] page fault (src_id:0 ring:24 vmid:8 pasid:19)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000300000000 from client 0x1b (UTCL2)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000000000000000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x000000003f78a000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x000000003f787000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x00007f0935df5000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: GPU reset begin!. Source:  1
```

**It is not fixed by finding A's change** — it still stalls and still resets the card with the 56 GiB window.
`--short-read <ctx>` routes prompts through the decode path and is a clean workaround (measured: a 2,000-character
prompt went from "must crash" to success in 46.9 s, `prompt=1182 tokens at 27.3 tok/s`).

Only a handful of attempts; I stopped once the workaround held, so I cannot say how reproducible the batched path
is on other layer numbers (I saw it at layer 32, and the same class of failure at layers 1, 3, 7, 13, 35, 39, 44, 45).

---

## 5. Finding C — prompts above ~5,000 tokens fail with fabricated high addresses (**unfixed**)

### 5.1 Measured boundary

Fresh prompts, one run each, `--max-context` raised to 24576 for the first two so they were not truncated:

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 1,182 | ✅ `prompt=1182 tok at 27.3 tok/s`, correct answer |
| **4,554** | ✅ `prompt=4554 tok at 26.4 tok/s` |
| 6,801 | ❌ `verify: unspecified launch failure` |
| 20,846 | ❌ `verify: layer 7 never rang (unspecified launch failure)` |

The engine **reads the whole prompt** (`reading the prompt: 20,846 tokens, 270 s so far`) and then fails on the
**first generation step**. So the prompt path itself completes; the failure is at the prompt→decode handover.

### 5.2 The addresses are not real memory

First failure in this class:

```
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000001700000000 from client 0x1b (UTCL2)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000001800000000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:   in page starting at address 0x0000001900000000
... 0x0000001a00000000, 0x0000001b00000000, 0x0000001c00000000, 0x0000001d00000000,
    0x0000001e00000000, 0x0000001f00000000
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: GCVM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_STATUS:0x00801031
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0:          Faulty UTCL2 client ID: TCP (0x8)
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: GPU reset begin!. Source:  1
amdgpu 0000:04:00.0: VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!
```

**Nine consecutive addresses, exactly 4 GiB (`0x1_00000000`) apart, spanning `0x17_00000000` – `0x1f_00000000`
= 92 – 124 GiB.** This machine has 62 GiB of RAM and 8 GB of VRAM — 70 GiB of addressable memory in total. A
regular 4 GiB stride, and a range that is suspiciously close to **2× the 46.84 GiB arena**, is what I would expect
from a base-plus-offset computation that goes wrong rather than a permission problem.

The IOMMU sees the same thing from the host side:

```
DMAR: [DMA Write NO_PASID] Request device [04:00.0] fault addr 0x1fda40000
      [fault reason 0x05] PTE Write access is not set
```

I want to be explicit about one thing: **I did not "fix" this by disabling VT-d, and I would ask other users not
to.** Turning the IOMMU off does not repair a bad pointer, it removes the check and lets the GPU write into
arbitrary physical RAM — on a machine holding a 47 GiB model, that converts a diagnosable crash into silent
corruption. I mention it only because it is the obvious-looking knob in the BIOS f

issues.title: Community benchmark: 2x Tesla V100 16 GB (SXM2 + PCIe), i9-9820X, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S
issues.author: tomcoolss
issues.body:
First dual-V100-16GB entry I think - layer split across V100-SXM2-16GB + V100-PCIE-16GB with KV streaming, `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`. Ran `./bench.sh` (suite 1) against the running server, 2026-10-17.

Context: this box also runs a production agent workload; daily logs show decode weighted ~74-77 tok/s with 94% prompt-cache reuse, consistent with the suite agent-session figures.

# Community benchmark on Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB + Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB

Measured on 2026-10-17 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB + Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB, 32 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9820X CPU @ 3.30GHz (10 cores, 20 threads); installed RAM: 123.2 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: 580.178.04; CUDA: 13.0
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s
- Context: 262144 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack iq3_s --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --remote-expert-opt --vram-reserve-mib 768 --vram-reserve-later-mib 1105 --spec-min-p 0.5 --vision
```

Environment of the config: `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | 66.5 (54.1-79.4) | 0.49 (0.42-0.57) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 (4019-4019) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 821.3 (805.1-821.5) | not measured | 4.92 (4.92-5.02) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 1579.4 (1569.7-1579.5) | not measured | 10.20 (10.20-10.27) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14567 (14555-14581) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 71.0 (62.1-88.7) | 5.14 (4.68-5.46) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.6 % (68.6-68.8); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 74 (4-74) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13728 (13728-13728) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 3.33 s (3.31-3.35).

| Turn (run 1) | Prompt tokens | Reused | Read | Prompt tok/s | First token (s) | Decode tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 609 | 0 | 609 | 185.5 | 3.306 | 53.0 |
| 1 | 3743 | 623 | 3120 | 592.1 | 5.296 | 62.1 |

| 5 | 14555 | 11656 | 2899 | 560.9 | 5.203 | 68.4 |

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details come from the server, `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` and the OS; background load and power limits are not recorded. Total time of the suite: 175 s.

issues.title: Community benchmark: Apple M1 Max 64 GB (Metal) — Q2_0 decode 26.7 tok/s, 4K/16K prompts, agent session; 245K needle at 262144 context; Metal OOM note
issues.author: abssoul
issues.body:
Thanks for asking for more Mac data in `docs/MAC.md` — here is the first **Apple M1 Max 64 GB** report (the chip class between your M4 mini and M5 Max measurements). Everything below is from a quiet machine, engine's own timings, `tools/strata_bench.py` suite 1.

## Hardware and software

- **Apple M1 Max** (10-core CPU, 32-core GPU), **64 GB** unified memory, internal SSD, macOS 27.0.1
- Strata project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2, engine **0.1.44.1-metal**, built from source by `setup.sh` on the Mac
- Resident mode: pack mapped via `--mmap-experts`, `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`

> Note: the auto-generated report below mislabels the hardware as "CPU only / arm 10 cores / VRAM not read" — that is the Metal engine on the M1 Max GPU; `strata_bench.py`'s hardware probe does not read the GPU on Darwin. The folder name picked up `community-cpu` for the same reason.

## Benchmark report (verbatim, suite 1: short chat / 4K / 16K / agent)

Measured on 2026-10-17 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

### Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-q2_0
- Context: 32768 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged (metal backend); thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack q2_0 --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache 64 --prefill auto --spec 2 --mtp rt --max-context 32768 --mmap-experts
```

Environment of the config: `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`

### Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | **26.7 (25.4-38.7)** | 1.10 (0.85-1.23) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 | 24 cap | 3 | **226.0 (222.0-228.8)** | not measured | 17.83 (17.60-18.14) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 | 24 cap | 3 | **234.1 (228.2-235.3)** | not measured | 68.65 (68.28-70.42) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14520 at the last turn | up to 64 | 3 | 184-216 per turn | 28.6 (18.4-31.8) | 13.83 (7.13-16.06) |

Agent session: cache hit 68.7 % over follow-up turns; first turn (nothing cached) first token 3.21 s. For comparison on your M5 Max 128 GB table (Q2_0, same defaults): decode 119.5/108.2 and 4K prompt ~1430 tok/s — the M1 Max lands at ~4.5× slower decode and ~6.3× slower prompt.

## Extra measurements beyond the suite

**Context beyond 32K (your "measured up to 32K" open question).** Ran with `--max-context 262144` (the model's full window), then `tools/needle_bench.py`:

- 64,902 prompt tokens, code word at 90 % depth: **FOUND**, 314 s total
- 246,976 prompt tokens, code word at 90 % depth: **FOUND**, 1116 s total (~221 tok/s effective, prefill+decode; warm file cache)
- The KV cost held: engine RSS 40.3 GB at 32K config → 43.3 GB at 262144 config, swap unchanged. Memory is not the limit on 64 GB; prefill time is (a fresh ~247K prompt is ~19 minutes to first token).

**Quality spot checks (greedy, informal):** 4/4 correct — bat-and-ball (5 with correct algebra), palindrome function, a two-leg average-speed arithmetic problem (63 min), wolf-goat-cabbage (full 7 crossings including taking the goat back). Same answers as a 35B MoE we run locally gets on these.

**Startup:** "decode window … ready in 26759 ms" from engine start; ~65 s from a cold `run-q2_0.sh` to the HTTP API answering.

## A Metal OOM observation (exit code 5, reproducible)

The engine reports "6331 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded" at startup — ~42 GB wired through Metal for pack+KV+buffers on a 64 GB machine. If another GPU process then wires a large block (in our case a second local inference server loading 17-20 GB of weights), the next Strata request dies with:

```text
mtl: command buffer failed: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
```

and the engine exits with code 5. Two notes that may be useful:

1. After this exit, the server's "the next request restarts the engine" path did not recover: the engine aborted again during restart in the same memory state. A full stop/start of the server (with the other process's memory released first) was needed every time.
2. Our workaround is to release the other server's weights (its `/v1/memory/release`) before each Strata request. Since then: three consecutive requests with a growing conversation, stable 28.8 tok/s, no exits.

Happy to open a PR with the `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-cpu-qwen3-8-flash-next-q2-0/` folder (results.json + engine-log-excerpt.txt included) if that is preferred — the folder name just carries the misdetection above.

I'd like the Qwen3.6 path to reuse the conversation prefix between requests, the way the Flash-Next engine does with its conversation-cache checkpoints (DETAILS.md, "Conversation cache"). Today every request on Qwen3.6 re-reads the whole conversation from token 0, which makes agent clients slow.

**Measured with BENCH.bat on the same PC** (RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, Ryzen 9 7900, 32 GB, Windows 11, engine 0.1.44.1, repo `296b59d`):

| | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL, 128K | Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M, 64K |

| agent cache hit % | **0.00** | 68.71 |

| agent turn first token | **6.69 s** (2.64–10.97) | 1.32 s |
| chat decode | 70.2 tok/s | 69.1 tok/s |
| 16K prompt read | 1,425 tok/s | 3,235 tok/s |

**In practice:** with Claude Code (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`), the system prompt and tool list are about 24K tokens and get read again on every turn. The same 10-section document task took 35 minutes on Qwen3.6 (17 turns) against 8 minutes on the Coder (20 turns). Decode speed is fine; the prompt re-reading is what costs the time.

As far as I can tell, `src/qwen35/q36_main.cpp` has no checkpoint or snapshot code yet. Since qwen35moe mixes Gated DeltaNet layers with a few attention layers, I assume it needs the same state checkpoints the Flash-Next path uses, rather than KV-prefix reuse alone.

**Workaround today:** I use the Flash-Next Coder for long agent sessions and Qwen3.6 for chat. Related but different: #2693 / #2698 / #2742 (int8 KV cache for this path).
