issues.title: Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151, Ryzen AI Max+ 395): hipMemGetInfo reports only the carve-out's free space, and the gfx1151 arch defaults never apply
issues.author: moweishun
issues.body:
# Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151, Ryzen AI Max+ 395): hipMemGetInfo reports only the carve-out's free space, and the gfx1151 arch defaults never apply

## Hardware and software

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, `gfx1151`, wave32, 40 CUs), Windows 11
  (build 26100), Adrenalin driver 32.0.31041.1004, 96 GB LPDDR5X (BIOS carve-out settable).
- Strata v0.1.44.1 (also reproduced on main 296b59d), ready-made Windows HIP engine
  (`strata-windows-x64-hip.zip`, ROCm 10.2.0a20260930), and a self-built engine from the same tree
  (`tools/hip/build_windows.bat`, `STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1151`).
- Model: ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, 200K or 32K context, int8 KV, MTP on.

## Finding 1: `device_free_bytes()` is not unified-memory aware on Windows

`cudaMemGetInfo` on this APU reports the free space of the BIOS's dedicated carve-out (what the
desktop has not taken of it), not what the unified memory can host. The Linux-only correction in
`src/core/expert_cache.cpp` (`#if defined(__linux__)` → MemAvailable minus
`STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB`) does not apply, so the auto expert cache sizes from a tiny figure.

Measured free figure (after the session's allocations), by BIOS carve-out, 32K context unless said:

| carve-out | free figure | what happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 GB | ~0 | auto refuses; forced `--expert-cache N` shrinks to 0 slots |
| 16 GB | 0.37 GiB | auto refuses: "needs at least 241 slots (611 MiB), about 757 MiB more than this card has free" |
| 32 GB | ~1.1 GiB | 32K works: 438 slots, filled from the profile, 96% hit rate, ~29 tok/s decode with MTP |
| 64 GB | 6.69 GiB (200K) | sizes 19339 slots, but the 200K prompt paths crash (below) |

Consequences of the small figure, all reproduced:

- auto: "expert cache auto: 0.00 GiB free → 0 slots" → "no VRAM is left for the expert cache".
- forced `--expert-cache N`: the sizing pass sets `expert_cache = 0` (keep_bytes ≤ 0), so the cache
  opens with no slots and the profile fill reports "pre-filled 0 of 0 slots from the profile"; the
  server then exits because the MTP verify tier needs the profile-filled VRAM expert tier. An IQ
  pack cannot drop MTP (`it needs --native SHARD1, --spec T and --prefill CHUNK`), so there is no
  working fallback: a catch-22.

A patch that applies the same unified-memory correction on Windows (integrated GPU →
`GlobalMemoryStatusEx().ullAvailPhys` minus the same headroom) fixed all of it here: at 16 GB
carve-out and 200K context, the auto cache sized 19339 slots (36.84 GiB), filled 19336 of them from
the profile, and served 40-45 tok/s decode at 96.9% hit rate. I will send it as a PR.

## Finding 2: the gfx1151 arch defaults never apply on Windows HIP

`src/program/generate.cpp` (the `#if defined(STRATA_USE_HIP)` block) applies
`apply_arch_defaults(ad.gcnArchName)` only when `cudaGetDeviceProperties` succeeds, and swallows the
error otherwise. On this machine (Windows HIP 10.2.0a20260930 wheels) it fails, so the 18 exact
speed switches silently stay off — no "strata: gfx1151 (Strix Halo): N exact speed switches" line
at startup. Setting the 18 switches as environment variables directly (same values the table sets)
took decode from 26 tok/s to 40-45 tok/s at 200K, byte-identical answers as documented. A fix would
either retry the property query, log the failure, or apply the defaults when the device query
cannot run.

## Finding 3: at 200K on Windows, the prompt/verify paths crash whenever the cache is large

With the probe reading larger figures (64 GB carve-out, pre-patch; or any large cache), each
configuration died in a different subsystem, all in the `unspecified launch failure` (719) family:

- `--prefill auto` (auto → 6144) + auto cache: `strata serve: cannot create the refill stream` /
  `Hip error 719` inside hipblaslt.cpp:468;
- the same with `STRATA_GFX1151_DEFAULTS=0` (portable path): `strata serve: verify: stream create
  failed`;
- forced cache that lends slots to the prompt path: `prefill: the token id buffer (unspecified
  launch failure)`, and at 32K with a large borrowed region: `prefill: setting the FP16 activation
  image failed`;
- with a small cache that cannot lend (no borrowing): no GPU crash at all, but then verify's tier
  is missing (finding 1) and the server exits.

32K with the stock defaults on the 32 GB carve-out (cache 438 slots, prompt path borrowing only
310 of them) is the one configuration that served stably — which is what makes me suspect the
borrowed-region path breaks once the borrowed region (or the cache) crosses some size on this
driver, though I could not pin the threshold and did not test beyond what is listed.

## Also noted

- The engine's own `--prefill 8192` warning (#1630) matches: with a forced `--prefill 8192` the
  commit charge jumped ~60-70 GB and the process died; `--prefill 6144` and below were stable here
  too. A bare `--prefill auto` stopping at 6144 on Windows is what kept the working 32K setup safe.
- BIOS carve-out interacts with everything above through finding 1; on Windows, unlike the Linux
  guide's advice, a LARGER carve-out helps (it is the only thing that grows the reported figure).

## What I did not test

- Any Linux build; the SYCL port; multi-GPU; images (`--vision cpu` was configured but unused);
  other model sizes; `--kv q4_0` / `k8v4`; the CUDA backend (no NVIDIA GPU).
- Long-running stability at 200K beyond a benchmark session (hours), and 256K/384K/512K contexts.

Happy to test builds or run more configurations on this machine — it is currently serving 200K at
40-45 tok/s decode with the patch and the 18 switches set explicitly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
The full report:

# Community benchmark on AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX

Measured on 2026-10-17 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, VRAM not read
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (8 cores, 16 threads); installed RAM: 63.1 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200); GPU driver: not read; CUDA: not read
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads: not recorded; power limit and clocks: see "Added by hand" below

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs
- Context: 262144 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration (hip backend), tuned for this machine (see "Settings kept" below) and not changed by the benchmark; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata.exe --pack iq3_xxs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --pcie-frac 0
```

Environment of the config: `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=gfx1100-hipblaslt-100500.txt`, `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1`, `STRATA_PF_GEMM=1`, `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=4096`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7`

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py --long` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (started by the benchmark from the install configuration); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |

| agent session, follow-up turns | 14602 (14587-14611) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 104.8 (84.8-117.6) | 4.21 (4.08-4.23) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.8 % (68.8-68.8); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 4 (3-4) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13729 (13728-13731) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 3.52 s (3.47-3.56).

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details come from the server, `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` and the OS; background load and power limits are not recorded. Total time of the suite: 187 s.

## Added by hand (what the tool could not read)

- GPU: RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (Sapphire Nitro+), AMD Adrenalin driver 32.0.31041.1004 (2026-08-17); the engine's bundled ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 (official prebuilt Windows HIP zip). A second card (RTX 5080) is installed but not used by this run.

- Tuning (Adrenalin, owner's settings): core 2,800 MHz, VRAM 2,800 MHz, 1,000 mV, power limit +15%. Not stock clocks.

- Page file: 32-48 GB on the NVMe in addition to 4 GB on C:, commit limit 99 GB. It is needed for `--prefill auto:32768`: engine 0.1.44.1 warns that prompt chunks of 8K and more crashed RX 7900 XTX engines on Windows through a commit-charge jump (#1630). With the large page file nothing crashed.

### Settings kept (changed from setup's defaults)

| Setting | What it does here |

issues.title: Report: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S works on dual V100-SXM2-16GB (sm_70) with driver 550 / CUDA 12.6 (0.1.44.1)
issues.author: atollerus-tm
issues.body:
This is a separate report from #971 (that one covers L40S vGPU on driver 550). Here: **dual Volta (sm_70)**, which I don't think has been reported working with 0.1.44.1 yet.

### Hardware

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 2× Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB (sm_70, 16 GB each, bare metal) |
| Driver | 550.144.03 (exposes CUDA 12.4, intentionally not upgraded) |
| CUDA toolkit | 12.6 (installed alongside 12.1, only the toolkit — driver untouched) |
| CPU | 2× Intel Xeon E5-2640 v4 (2 sockets, 24 threads total) |
| RAM | 64 GB |
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Strata | upstream 0.1.44.1 |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S (GSQ-RCO, 78 GB, 2 shards) |
| MTP | fetched from original Qwen checkpoint (~5 GB) |

### Setup command

```bash
STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=1 \
./setup.sh --setup --family qwen --model IQ3_S --gpus 0,1 \
  --port 8085 --api-key test-v100 \
  --gguf-dir <repo>/IQ3_S \
  --cuda 12 --vision gpu --build --no-start --yes
### Ref

#971 — driver 550 / CUDA 12 on L40S vGPU. Same `--cuda 12` mechanism, different hardware.
Notes:

STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=1 is required for sm_70 (engine built with -DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON).

System cmake is 3.22.1, CMakeLists requires ≥ 3.24. Used the venv's cmake 4.4.3 via PATH=<repo>/.venv/bin:$PATH.

--cuda 12 picked /usr/local/cuda-12.6/bin/nvcc (the 12.6 toolkit, not the driver's 12.4 ceiling) and lowered the driver floor to 525, as documented.

Results
Layer split across GPUs [0, 1] works; both V100 busy, one strata process per card.

VRAM (text only): ~15.5–15.8 GB used on each V100.

VRAM (with --vision gpu):

GPU 0: 1428 MiB (strata-vision) + 14128 MiB (strata) = 15556 MiB

GPU 1: 306 MiB (strata-vision) + 15376 MiB (strata) = 15682 MiB

RAM: ~46.8 GiB experts loaded.

Expert cache: 94–98% hit rate on long agent runs.

Decode: 50–71 tok/s (text), 75–80 tok/s on 1700-token generations with vision.

Prompt eval: 69–86 tok/s on short prompts; ~3 s for a 10K-token prompt (~3300 tok/s prefill).

MTP: acceptance rate 69–71%.

KV int8, context 65536.

Calibration results (./setup.sh --calibrate)
Median of 3 rounds for each value:

PCIe share (--pcie-frac):

Value	tok/s
0	70.5
0.2	70.6 (best)
0.32	69.2
0.55	67.4
1.0	56.3
Draft floor (--spec-min-p):

Value	tok/s
0.3	67.5
0.5	69.7
0.7	71.2 (best)
CPU workers:

Workers	tok/s
3	60.2
5	63.3
6	64.4
7	62.0
11	67.7 (best of tested)
Expert tier (adaptive):

default: 66.8

every 1, 80 swaps, decay 0.97: 73.9 (best)

every 1, 160 swaps, decay 0.97: 72.0

Final: 73.9 tok/s (vs 70.5 before calibration).

Real workload (agent use)
After calibration, ran an agent with tool calling (ask_user, search_web, write_note, update_memory) over the OpenAI API. Context grew from ~10K to ~17K tokens.

Tokens generated	tok/s
2526	68.6
2841	64.7
3656	74.3
1721	66.6
Average ~69 tok/s. Expert cache hit rate 94–98%.

Tool calling, streaming, multi-step agent loops all work on 2× V100-SXM2-16GB.

Vision
After adding --vision gpu, the encoder (strata-vision) loads on both cards (see VRAM numbers above). A screenshot of a Russian-localized Total Commander was correctly described. Decode with vision: 75–80 tok/s on ~1700-token generations.

Pitfalls worth knowing for other Volta users
Fork Hardin22/Strata-DualGPU (Strata 0.1.38) does NOT build on CUDA 12. Its src/core/mtp.cpp uses CUDA 13 API signatures (cudaGraphAddNode with edge data, cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo with 7 args). Error is cannot convert cudaGraphEdgeData** to size_t*. This is an API mismatch, not "Volta unsupported".

In 0.1.38 MIN_DRIVER = 580 blocked startup even with STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=1 — there is no --cuda flag and no conditional floor. Upstream 0.1.39+ fixed this with --cuda 12. Confirms what's written here.

Installing CUDA 12.6 via apt flips the update-alternatives cuda symlink to 12.6. If another service (e.g. llama.cpp) relies on /usr/local/cuda → 12.1, restore it: update-alternatives --set cuda /usr/local/cuda-12.1. Otherwise a restart of that service may load the wrong runtime.

--pool-workers 5 tip from setup is not universal. On this machine (2× Xeon E5-2640 v4, equal cores per socket), 5 workers is worse than 11 or even 6:

3 → 60.2

5 → 63.3

6 → 64.4

7 → 62.0

11 → 67.7

Calibration picked 11 as the best of the tested set. Worth mentioning in docs/OLDER_GPUS.md that the "fewer workers on dual-socket" tip is hardware-specific and can hurt on equal-core systems.

Prompt > context is rejected, not truncated. With --max-context 65536, a 77 187-token prompt returns 400: request exceeds the context window: ... requests are never truncated. That is by design, but worth documenting for users with long histories — they either trim the client-side history or rebuild with a larger context.

Thanks
--cuda 12 works out of the box on Volta with 0.1.44.1, including vision and agent tool calls. Great work on the older-GPU path.

Ref
#971 — driver 550 / CUDA 12 on L40S vGPU. Same --cuda 12 mechanism, different hardware.

issues.title: [Linux, 2x RTX 3060, 32 GB RAM, SATA SSD, 0.1.44] `--prefill auto` picks 8192 by VRAM alone; lent slots + file tier exceed the page cache, so a 28.7K prompt re-reads 28-45 GB (TTFT 164-287 s); `--prefill 4096` fits: 0.9-1.4 GB read, TTFT 36-38 s
issues.author: jds1-ai
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** `0.1.44` (ed4773eb, built from source with `STRATA_PORTABLE=ON`, CUDA 13.0, sm_86) · 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 12 GB, layer split auto (K=39), CUDA0 at 01:00.0 Gen3 x16, CUDA1 at 02:00.0 Gen2 x4 (chipset slot) · Linux 6.8.0-147-generic, Intel i7-4790K (4C/8T, no AVX-512), 32 GB RAM (MemTotal 32,043 MB), 8 GiB swap, one PNY 250 GB SATA SSD (ext4, model and swap on it) · NVIDIA open kernel module 580.178.

**Model and flags.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XS, native pack, GGUF shards in place (36.53 GiB + 26.82 GiB, no experts.bin):

```
--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <rt> --max-context 32768
--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --resident-budget-gib 12 --layer-split auto
```

Every run below is the same binary and the same three prompts: a 7,718-token warm-up as request 1 on a fresh engine, nine ~105-token requests, then a 28,683-token prompt (repeats use 28,679 and 28,709 tokens), 256 completion tokens each. Only `--prefill`, `--resident-budget-gib` and `--ple-io` change between rows.

### Summary

With `--prefill auto` the engine picks an 8192-token chunk and lends the prompt path 5,532 GPU cache slots (its own line: `the split stages lend 5532 slots to the prompt path: 0 keep their experts in RAM too`). Those lent experts are read from the GGUF on every chunk. On this box the bytes a long prompt reads from the files (the experts outside the GPU cache and the RAM copy, plus the lent slots) are larger than the RAM left for the page cache, so the set cycles through the cache and the drive serves 28-45 GB per 28.7K-token prompt. `--prefill 4096` lends 2,966 slots, the set fits, and the same prompt reads 0.9-1.4 GB once the cache is warm. The auto scan only tests VRAM (slot count and the lend percentage); it does not look at RAM. The one RAM-aware clamp in the tree is the gfx12-only #2090 step from 16384 to 8192.

### Measurements

Long prompt, time to first token and bytes read from the drive during the request (`/proc/diskstats` sectors read on `sda`, sampled at the stamps before and after each request; swap is on the same drive, so swap-in is included, and the sector deltas run 1-7% above the engine's own storage counter. `pswpin` sampled per request: 4-84 MB per rep in the five fixed-chunk cells, except 0.58 GB on rep 1 of the 4096/12 and 6144/12 cells; 0.73-0.93 GB per long prompt on the `auto` rows (2.3 GB across each `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=0` cell's three), about 2-3% of their 28-45 GB):

| `--prefill` | budget GiB | PLE | rep 1 (cold) TTFT | reps 2-3 TTFT | prefill tok/s, reps 2-3 | drive GB per prompt, reps 1 / 2 / 3 | cell |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto (8192) | 12 | direct | 277.0 s | | 104 | 40.2 | `n4d-d-auto-s10-1016T144018` |
| auto (8192) | 12 | direct | 189.6 s | | 151 | 31.1 | `...-drop-1016T145417` |
| auto (8192) | 18 | direct | 171.3 / 182.9 / 236.7 s (3 starts) | | 121-167 | 29.3-31.6 | `...-b18-*` |
| auto (8192) | 12 | direct, `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=0` | 276.0 s | 204.6 / 196.8 s | 140-146 | 37.7 / 34.4 / 39.5 | `...-nola-1016T151848` |
| auto (8192) | 12 | direct, `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=0` | 200.8 s | 163.9 / 286.8 s | 100-175 | 27.9 / 28.5 / 45.2 | `...-nola-r2-1016T160734` |
| 2048 | 12 | direct | 69.3 s | 53.0 / 50.9 s | 542 / 565 | 5.7 / 0.8 / 0.6 | `...-pf2048-reps-1016T195949` |
| 2048 | 12 | mmap | 69.9 s | 54.5 / 51.3 s | 526 / 560 | 6.3 / 0.9 / 0.6 | `...-pf2048-mmap-reps-1016T203603` |
| 4096 | 12 | mmap | 91.0 s | 38.2 / 37.4 s | 751 / 768 | 8.9 / 1.4 / 0.9 (rep 1 includes 0.58 GB swap-in) | `...-pf4096-mmap-reps-1016T205114` |
| 6144 | 12 | mmap | 107.3 s | 40.0 / 35.2 s | 718 / 816 | 12.5 / 2.8 / 1.2 (rep 1 includes 0.58 GB swap-in) | `...-pf6144-mmap-reps-1016T210420` |
| 4096 | 16 | mmap | 59.1 s | 37.4 / 36.1 s | 767 / 796 | 7.1 / 1.2 / 1.0 | `...-b16-pf4096-mmap-reps-1016T211559` |

The 7,718-token warm-up as request 1: 126-198 s on the five `auto` starts (198.5, 197.1, 170.9, 146.4, 126.4), 103.5 s at 4096/12, 54.7 s at 4096/16.

Across 11 long prompts on seven `auto` starts at two budgets, TTFT is 164-287 s and the drive serves 28-45 GB per prompt. At 2048, 4096 and 6144 the steady state is 35-55 s and 0.6-2.8 GB. The budget does not change which chunk fits: at `auto` the drive serves 28-45 GB per prompt at budget 12 and 29-32 GB at 18, and at 4096 it serves 0.9-1.4 GB at 12 and 1.0-1.2 GB at 16.

### What the engine lends per chunk

Read off the `lend sizing` line of one start per chunk (`n4d-lend-pf2048-1016T195329`, `n4d-lend-pf4096-1016T195628`, the 6144 and auto cells above):

| chunk | slots lent | GiB (at the engine's 7.54 GiB for 5,532) |
|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 1,688 | 2.3 |
| 4096 | 2,966 | 4.0 |
| 6144 | 4,246 | 5.8 |
| 8192 (auto) | 5,532 | 7.5 |

Linear: 0.626 slots per token plus 406. The engine's own startup lines on this box (the s10 start; the 12-GiB starts read 28.0-28.6 and 15.4-16.0 GiB across the campaign): `28.4 GiB available, 12.0 GiB of it still to be taken by the RAM copy, 21.0 GiB of experts read from the files: the file cache can keep the ones that come back`, re-checked after the copy as `15.6 GiB available`, and `RAM budget 12.00 GiB: 9021 of the 19.18 GiB of experts the GPU cache does not hold, by profile rank; the rest are read from the files`. The GPU caches hold 5,573 slots on CUDA0 (7.39 GiB) and 4,586 on CUDA1 (6.45 GiB), and the lend draws from both (at 4096: 1,526 + 1,440). So the file tier at decode is 19.18 - 12.0 = 7.2 GiB; the `21.0 GiB` figure is every expert outside the RAM copy, including the two GPU caches (19.18 + 13.84 - 12.0). During a prompt the lent slots are streamed from the files again, so the set a long prompt reads is 7.2 GiB + lend(chunk) + ~0.35 GiB of PLE pages: about 15.1 GiB at 8192, 13.3 at 6144, 11.6 at 4096. The page cache that was actually available to hold it, measured as the cgroup's file total at steady state, was 14.5-14.6 GiB at budget 12 (MemAvailable after the copy reads ~1 GiB higher, 15.4-16.0). 8192 does not fit, and the reads say so; 6144 fits by about 1.2 GiB and reads 2-3x the bytes of 4096 at the same TTFT, which is the edge; 4096 fits by about 3 GiB.

### Where the choice is made (ed4773eb)

- `src/program/generate.cpp:6669-6748`: `plan_lend` / `biggest_chunk` bisect the chunk against `k + 128 <= xcache.slots() && k * 100 <= kAutoLendPct * xcache.slots()` (`:6733`), where `k = lend_slots(chunk)`. The test is VRAM slots only. The layer-split path has its own copies of the same test per stage (`:4024`, `:4066`, `:7350`, against `parts[i].cnt` / `p.cache->slots()`); this box is a split, so one of those is the test that ran here, and they are VRAM-only too.
- `src/program/generate.cpp:6631-6660`: the #2090 clamp drops the gfx12 ceiling from 16384 to 8192 when `avail_mib < pin_mib + extra_mib + 6144`. It is the only RAM test in the scan; it runs for gfx12 only and stops at 8192.
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp:512-537` and `include/strata/platform/memory.hpp:54`: `file_cache_keeps(avail, arena, read, 1 GiB, 0.05, 1.5 GiB)` decides buffered vs unbuffered reads at load. With `hot_fraction` 0.05 it asks whether a twentieth of the file tier fits; that is the decode question (#1194), not the prompt one, where the lent slots are read once per chunk, in full.
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp:3241-3246`: the split-lend line prints `0 keep their experts in RAM too (... not enough RAM for them)`; the #1389 WARNING at `:3227-3236` is inside the single-GPU `lend` branch (`lend` at `:2746` requires `additional_gpu_pairs.empty()`, and this box has 4,586 of them), so on a split nothing warns that every lent slot will be re-read from the files.

### Proposed change

In the auto scan, at every backend and every step, keep only a chunk whose prompt-time file set fits the RAM that will be available after the RAM copy is built, with a margin:

```
file_set(chunk) = (experts the GPU caches do not hold - RAM budget) + lend_bytes(chunk)
fits(chunk)     = file_set(chunk) + margin <= RAM available for the page cache after the copy
```

Both terms already exist as log lines: the first from `N of the M GiB of experts the GPU cache does not hold` (M - budget; not the `21.0 GiB ... read from the files` line, which counts the GPU caches too), the second from `lend sizing`. On this box, against the 15.4-16.0 GiB MemAvailable after the copy, a margin of 1-2 GiB picks 6144 (13.3 + 2 = 15.3 is still under 15.4) and 4096 needs a margin of about 2.5 GiB; against the ~14.5 GiB the page cache actually held, 2 GiB picks 4096 (13.3 + 2 = 15.3 > 14.5). The measurements say the margin should be the larger one: 6144 fits by the arithmetic but reads 2-3x the bytes of 4096 at the same TTFT and costs 16 s more on the cold first fill, so "largest chunk that fits" should be "largest chunk that fits with 2-3 GiB to spare", or 2 GiB against the page cache the box can actually hold after the copy (MemAvailable overstates it here by ~1 GiB). 8192 would be left to an explicit `--prefill 8192`. On a box where the 8192 set fits with that margin, nothing changes. A second, smaller change: print the #1389 warning on the split path too when `stage_lent < offered`.

### Not tested

One GPU; other quantizations; prompts over 32K; Windows; `--resident-experts` (the full RAM copy). `--ple-io mmap` is used from the 2048-mmap row on because `--ple-io direct` tripped the #29 watchdog on this box (reported separately on #2797); the 2048 direct and 2048 mmap rows differ by under 2 s, so the PLE mode does not move the chunk result.

Logs for every cell (engine log, argv, per-request JSON, diskstats and `/proc` stamps) are available on request.


---
Filed by jds1-ai. Measurements and the /proc instrumentation run by an agent (Fizz, Claude model); source reading, pre-registered scoring and this write-up by a second agent (Fable, Claude model); reviewed by the account owner before filing.

issues.title: [Engine] Let short requests interrupt a long single-engine response
issues.author: Zcg2021
issues.body:
## Area

Engine

## What do you want to do?

Let a short interactive request interrupt a long response on a single native engine, then resume the original stream with its accepted tokens and tool-call identity intact. The feature remains opt-in. The workaround today is waiting, cancelling/retrying, or using batch slots. Batch admission priority is distinct from yielding a request that is already decoding.

## Reproduction on 0.2.0-beta

Re-tested the unmodified server at `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (the relevant server/native/tokenizer trees match tag `v0.2.0-beta`) with the beta's official CUDA13 engine asset version 0.1.45.3. The binary itself prints 0.1.45; asset SHA256 is recorded in the linked report.

Environment: Windows 11 build 26100, Ryzen 9 5900X, RTX 3090 24 GiB, 128 GiB RAM, original non-abliterated Qwen3.8 Flash Next ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S. Context 262144, 32 GiB conversation cache / 8 slots, int8 KV, spec 4, one native engine. No SC117 in these measurements.

Steps: warm a 127788-token synthetic archive; start a long response capped at 3072 output tokens; after 7 seconds submit a short exact-JSON request with priority 1. Repeat three times. The report includes the fixture generator, benchmark command, settings and individual runs.

Actual: all three short requests waited until the long response finished. Short TTFT was 20.784 / 20.542 / 21.129 seconds. The requested behavior is for an explicitly enabled scheduler to yield safely while preserving the long stream. This is reproduced native hardware behavior, not a code-reading hypothesis.

## Proposed scope and evidence

The existing implementation in #2822 has been rebased and adapted to beta queue deadlines, cancellation and terminal telemetry. It changes only the Python server, keeps the option off by default, and uses the existing STOP/DONE and RAM conversation cache. Cold prefill and cache restore can still delay short requests. The original parser stays alive; generated code/tools are not executed by the benchmark.

A matching three-arm trial compares unmodified beta, patch off and patch on. Median short TTFT with the option on was 0.610 seconds versus 20.523 off; median aggregate throughput was 107.88 versus 111.29 tok/s. This is a small same-machine sample, not a universal speed claim. All nine fact audits and short JSON outputs matched.

Maintainer agreement on feature scope is still requested here. The PR will remain draft while that and validation on other backends are outstanding. This updates the existing proposal; it does not create a competing submission.

The one-hour multi-conversation revalidation completed 424 requests (410 completions, 14 intentional cancellations), 100 tool round trips and 30 exact audits without validation failures or unexpected transport errors. There were 290 preemptions and no paused-prefix misses. Short TTFT p50/p95/max was 0.923/6.545/46.663 s; the maximum came from partial-cache-hit prefill, so this remains a cooperative scheduling feature with documented latency limits.

## Reproducible report

[Full beta revalidation report, settings and raw results](https://github.com/Zcg2021/Strata/blob/4312dd7aa7cc87b6a84e2b3a7363dbdff9afc372/bench/results/2026-10-19-solo-priority-v020-beta/README.md).

issues.title: [Feature]: images on the Intel (SYCL) port through setup, with the CPU image encoder as on AMD
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Send pictures to Strata on an Intel Arc, through the setup the port already has: `./setup.sh --backend sycl
--vision cpu`, the way `--vision cpu` works on AMD since #304.

docs/INTEL.md's comparison table says images are "not yet" on the SYCL port, and `sycl/setup_intel.py` makes it
so: it forces `--vision none` (`install()`), maps every `--vision` choice to "none" (`S.hip_vision = lambda asked:
"none"`) and drops the config's `"vision"` section in `to_sycl()`. But the engine side is there: the SYCL engine
takes `--vision` (the GENI request with the encoder's embeddings, the per-cell M-RoPE position table in
`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`), and the image encoder (`strata-vision`, `tools/vision`: llama.cpp's mtmd and the
model's mmproj file) is a CPU program with no SYCL in it - the very build the AMD path makes for the CPU, run by
`serve/server.py` on the host.

The workaround I use today: build `tools/vision` for the CPU by hand (`cmake -S tools/vision -B build-vision -G
Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_DIR=<pinned llama.cpp> -DSTRATA_PORTABLE=OFF`), then add the `"vision"`
section (`exe`, `mmproj`: `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf`, `model`: shard 1, `threads`) and `--vision` to the
config by hand. With that, on two Arc Pro B70s (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA IQ3_XXS), a 448x448 picture of four
coloured quadrants is answered correctly through `/v1/chat/completions`: on `main` 296b59d2 with `--layer-split 30`
("Red, Green, Blue, Yellow" in the asked order), and on a development tree (expert parallel) also next to a
concurrent code request; the encoder takes 1.2 s for a 256x256 test picture on 8 CPU threads (64 image tokens) and no
VRAM; text decode speed is unchanged with `--vision`
(140.9 vs 140.5 tok/s on a 512-token reply, a development tree with the same vision path as `main`).

What I would like: setup does the above for `--backend sycl --vision cpu` (compile the encoder for the CPU, get
the mmproj file, write the vision section and `--vision`), the docs say images work on the port and what was
measured, and nothing changes for a setup run without `--vision cpu`. `--vision yes` (the GPU encoder) can stay off
with a note, as on AMD. A pull request that refers to this issue does that in `sycl/setup_intel.py`,
`tools/test_setup_sycl.py` and `docs/INTEL.md`; `setup.py` itself is not touched.

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the analysis, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

issues.title: Community benchmark: RTX Pro 4000 Blackwell, qwen3.8-flash-next Unsloth Q8_0
issues.author: DrLove73
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell

Measured on 2026-10-16 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6138 CPU @ 2.00GHz (60 cores, 60 threads); installed RAM: 220.5 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64; GPU driver: 580.105.08; CUDA: 13.0
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-q8_0
- Context: 131072 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack unsloth-q8_0 --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0-00001-of-00006.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --ple-io ram --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700 --pcie-frac 0.20 --spec-min-p 0.50 --pool-workers 39 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --adapt-decay 0.97
```

Environment of the config: `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (started by the benchmark from the install configuration); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 (43-51) | 0 | 100 (100-100) | 9 | not measured | 14.6 (12.2-18.4) | 2.27 (1.90-2.64) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 (4019-4019) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 436.1 (426.9-436.6) | not measured | 9.29 (9.29-9.51) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 849.1 (834.0-849.9) | not measured | 19.01 (18.99-19.36) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14559 (14546-14580) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 16.3 (11.9-24.9) | 9.45 (9.18-9.57) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.7 % (68.6-68.7); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 3 (2-74) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13728 (13728-13729) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 5.36 s (5.20-5.45).

| Turn (run 1) | Prompt tokens | Reused | Read | Prompt tok/s | First token (s) | Decode tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 609 | 0 | 609 | 113.3 | 5.448 | 9.0 |
| 1 | 3741 | 621 | 3120 | 333.4 | 9.444 | 13.4 |
| 2 | 5274 | 3734 | 1540 | 166.0 | 9.364 | 13.8 |
| 3 | 8718 | 5337 | 3381 | 358.2 | 9.55 | 16.4 |
| 4 | 11644 | 8781 | 2863 | 303.6 | 9.557 | 24.9 |
| 5 | 14580 | 11681 | 2899 | 310.0 | 9.467 | 15.5 |

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details come from the server, `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` and the OS; background load and power limits are not recorded. Total time of the suite: 396 s.

issues.title: [Feature]: SYCL: a two-kernel hyper-connection read (norm + down + reduce in one launch) for Intel Arc, opt-in
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Spend less of the decode window on the hyper-connection read on Intel Arc. On the Arc Pro B70 the SYCL port's default
read is four launches per layer half (the norm per token and stream, the sliced down projection, its reduce, the up
projection): 5.8 + 22.7 + 2.7 + 30.2 us at T = 6 rows, and the down / up kernels grow ~1.7 / 3 us per extra row. The
weights are 13.2 MB a read, so at T = 6 that is ~210 GB/s of a 600 GB/s card: the cost is kernel latency and per-row
issue, not bytes. Per decode cycle the verifier's ~100 reads are ~6 ms.

What I want: an opt-in read (`STRATA_GR_FUSED=1`, default off, the default read byte-identical) that does the norm,
the down projection and its partial reduction in one kernel - one row per 16-lane sub-group lane with the activations
uniform across the sub-group, the last work-group of a row group finishing it (an arrival counter, nothing waits, so
it is safe inside a SYCL graph) - and the up projection in a second kernel with K split over the sub-groups. The same
BF16 bytes, the default read's per-element arithmetic, another summation order: lo / rs / mixed differ at FP32
rounding level, R_out (the pending write) is bitwise. It is the structure of the Q8_0 read of `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` on
SYCL (the bug-fix PR this builds on) applied to the BF16 weights, for the cases that keep BF16: an exact read is
wanted, or the Q8_0 copies' 0.63 GiB do not fit.

Measured (2x Arc Pro B70, upstream main 296b59d2 vs the branch, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, two-card layer split, 65536
context, a fixed prompt with a 512-token greedy reply, 3 runs): the verify window 39.4 / 39.5 / 39.7 -> 38.8 / 38.1 /
38.7 ms (-2.5%); decode 81.8 / 79.5 / 78.7 -> 86.8 / 79.0 / 88.3 tok/s (the spread is draft acceptance of the changed
output); per read at the kernel level 38.7 -> 34.8 us at T = 1, 62.0 -> 47.1 at T = 6. The PR has the details.

Workaround today: none on SYCL; `STRATA_GR_V3=1` (upstream's two-kernel read) is 4-6% SLOWER on the B70
(docs/INTEL.md, the 0.1.31 merge), and `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS` / `STRATA_GR_UP_COLS` are worse there too (each extra
group recomputes the lo prologue).

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

issues.title: [Bug]: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 does nothing on the SYCL (Intel) build: the Q8_0 copies are loaded but never read
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What happened

`STRATA_HC_Q8=1` is documented (docs/QUANTS.md, docs/STRIX_HALO.md, docs/MAC.md) as the hyper-connection read from
the GGUF's own Q8_0 projections (or, for a BF16 pack, a Q8_0 copy quantized at load): the verify window's
hyper-connection down / up projections are read as Q8_0 instead of BF16 - an output-changing, measured speed-up on
CUDA, the default on AMD gfx12 and Mac. On the SYCL build (`sycl/`, Intel Arc) the flag never reaches a Q8_0 read: the hyper-connection
read only ever takes the BF16 weights, so the flag cannot change the output or the speed.

What I saw: on a development tree whose loader already makes the Q8_0 copies from the BF16 tensors (start-up line
`strata: STRATA_HC_Q8=1: 0.63 GiB of Q8_0 hyper-connection projections for the verify read`), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA
IQ3_XXS on two Arc Pro B70s, decode speed with `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` was the same as without it, and a GPU trace of the
decode window showed the same BF16 kernels (the sliced `gr_down`, `gr_down_reduce`, `gr_up_multi_kernel`) with the
flag on and off: the 0.63 GiB was never read. Reading `main` explains it (below). I did not run `main` itself with
the flag; from the source, on an ISTA (BF16) file it uploads nothing, and on a file with Q8_0 projections it makes
the copies and never reads them.

What I expected: the Q8_0 read, as on CUDA - the projections read as Q8_0 (the file's own, or quantized at load from
BF16), decode faster, answers differing slightly.

Why, from the source on `main`:

- CUDA has the whole path: `src/core/native_dense.cpp:46-69` (`hc_q8_env`), `:384-409` (a GGUF's own Q8_0
  projections), `:411-446` (a BF16 pack's projections quantized to Q8_0 at load), `:448-466` (the dequantization
  scratches for the prompt path), `src/program/generate.cpp:3062-3065` (the BF16 copies dropped on a single GPU). The
  read: `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu:1351-1358` (`gr_down_q8_kernel` / `gr_up_q8_kernel`), dispatched at
  `:1981-1982` when `a[0].q8_down != nullptr && a[0].q8_up != nullptr`; the argument check at `:1965` accepts
  `(w_down && w_up) || (q8_down && q8_up)`.
- The SYCL port has only the loader's first half: `sycl/src/core/native_dense.cpp:321-358` keeps a Q8_0 copy only for
  a tensor of GGUF type 8 (`:327`), so a BF16 tensor (type 30) is skipped and nothing is uploaded; there is no
  quantize-at-load and no `add_hc_skip` / `hc_bf16_view` (the comment at `:110`: the port "only needs the env switch").
- The SYCL read never looks at the Q8_0 pointers: `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp:1770-1786`
  `fused_gr_read_multi` requires `x.w_down && x.w_up` and never reads `x.q8_down` / `x.q8_up`; every branch below it
  takes the BF16 weights, and its last line says so (`:2051`: "the Q8_0 reads (S23 STRATA_HC_Q8) are not built").
  The callers do set the pointers (`sycl/src/core/verify.cpp:982-983`, `:1549-1563`), so for a GGUF with Q8_0
  projections the copies are allocated and then ignored.

Steps to reproduce: build `sycl/` (docs/INTEL.md), run a Flash-Next GGUF with and without `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` on a
fixed prompt at temperature 0: from the code above the outputs should be identical (the BF16 read runs either way).
A pull request that refers to this issue makes the flag take the Q8_0 read on SYCL; with it the output changes and the verify window gets 5% shorter
on the setup above.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

main 296b59d2 (0.1.44.1, the `sycl/` build) - 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB - Ubuntu, kernel
7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1

### Engine log

The development-tree run (loader already making the copies, read unchanged), the only line the flag adds:

    strata: STRATA_HC_Q8=1: 0.63 GiB of Q8_0 hyper-connection projections for the verify read

issues.title: [Feature]: SYCL: read prompts faster on Battlemage by attending over the union of neighbouring positions' selections
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
<!-- Feature request form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml). Title: see ISSUE_TITLE.txt. -->

### What do you want to do?

Read long prompts faster on the SYCL port on an Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage) with INT8 KV.

Today the QSA prompt attention on SYCL runs the FP32 decode kernel (`qsa_decode_attn_batch`), 32 prompt positions per
launch, and every position gathers its own ~2,051 selected K/V cells. The XMX port of the tensor-core kernel
(`STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1`) is correct but slower than that fallback: it is gather-bound and only 12 of its 16 matrix
rows are real heads (docs/INTEL.md, "XMX prompt attention v2"). docs/INTEL.md also measured that 8 consecutive
positions of an 80K prompt select 3.3x one position's cells between them, and left a kernel over that union "not
built" because it multiplies the arithmetic.

What I would like: an opt-in kernel that takes 8 neighbouring positions together, gathers the union of their selected
cells once, runs the products for all 8 x 12 heads on XMX (every matrix row a real head, the extra arithmetic on the
matrix units), and masks per position so each one still attends to exactly its own cells. The default path stays as
it is.

Workaround today: none; the default FP32 attention is the fastest prompt attention on this card.

I have a working version. On upstream main with 2x Arc Pro B70 (layer split, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS,
INT8 KV) it reads 4K and 32K prompts 15-16% faster (1,189 -> 1,382 and 1,956 -> 2,246 tok/s) and cuts the first token
of a turn with 40,796 tokens of context from 23.28 to 20.39 s; decode is unchanged. The output is not bitwise (FP16
inputs to the products, about 1e-3 of the output scale against FP64). Details and the parity test in the pull request.

issues.title: [Feature]: SYCL: decode QSA selection and attention in fewer, shorter launches (opt-in, same bits)
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Decode Flash-Next faster on an Intel Arc Pro B70 (the SYCL port), with several streams and at long context, without
changing a single output bit.

With MTP, every verify window runs the QSA selection (block scores, top-k) and the attention for each attention layer.
On the B70 these are small, latency-bound launches, and four of them do more serial work than they need to:

1. A batch window (`--batch`, `"parallel"`) runs the scores, top-k and attention one row at a time, because each slot
   has its own K/V: four launches per row and layer. The kernels already take several rows, each with its own step
   record. So a slot's rows could share one scores launch, and the whole window could share one top-k launch and one
   attention launch over every slot's pools.
2. The wide top-k kernel (a capacity above ~135K cells, e.g. `--max-context 200000`) finds each radix pass's digit
   with one thread walking 256 bins while the other 1,023 wait.
3. The decode block scores run a separate 5-step shuffle reduction for every (query, head) of every block.
4. The attention merge walks every chunk of the capacity, including the chunks with no selected cell. The MTP
   drafter's 32K window is 512 chunks, one dependent load chain per thread, even at a 1K context.

I would like an opt-in switch for each, off by default. Each should give exactly the bits of the path it replaces,
checked by a parity test against the existing kernels, so it can be measured and turned on where it pays.

Kernel times from a working implementation, one B70 (synthetic layers: 24 q heads, INT8 K/V, a 200,000-cell capacity;
graph replay, us):

- a window of 2 slots x 2 rows, selection + attention per layer: 184 -> 78 (1K), 365 -> 138 (16K), 498 -> 205 (64K)
- the wide top-k, one query: 36.3 -> 19.5 (16K), 57.9 -> 42.1 (64K)
- the block scores of four queries: 18.7 -> 14.1 (16K), 63.1 -> 43.2 (64K)
- the MTP drafter's attention call: 86.9 -> 41.0 (1K), 460.9 -> 335.9 (64K)

Workaround today: none.

I have an implementation that touches only `sycl/**` and `docs/INTEL.md`, and will open a pull request that
references this issue.

issues.title: [Feature]: SYCL: faster small-batch decode GEMVs for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS on the Arc Pro B70 (opt-in)
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Decode faster on an Intel Arc Pro B70 with the SYCL port by making the dense GEMVs of a decode window
(`native_mmvq` at 1-8 columns: the projections, the shared expert, the verify window and the 248,320-row output
head) read their weights closer to the card's memory bandwidth.

What I see today (one B70, `native_mmvq` called directly with random weights, distinct weight copies per graph so
L2 never holds a matrix):

- On the large matrices (2560 x 6144 / 10240 / 12288, 6144 x 2560, the head) the Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K kernels stream
  31-72% of the card's 608 GB/s at 1-2 columns and 18-41% at 6 columns; IQ4_XS 41-54% and 30-34%.
- The Q5_K head (2560 x 248,320) takes 1,063 us at 1 column and 2,691 us at 6.
- The time is not memory-bound: with the matrix held in L2, Q4_K 2560 x 10240 at 6 columns still took 82 us against
  94 us from DRAM. The wide kernels re-read every column's activations for every row (at 6 columns about 10x the
  weight bytes in L1 loads, issued one at a time), so they are bound by instruction issue at 4-6 columns.

What I'd like: an opt-in SYCL kernel family for these four formats that loads each column's activations once per
work-group and streams rows against them, with the default path left exactly as it is. A version of this on two
B70s (upstream main, `--layer-split 30`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--spec 4 --mtp`, one slot)
decodes 79.5 -> 95.0 tok/s (median of 3), with the K-quant matrices at 74-97% of bandwidth at 1-2 columns and the
head at 759 us (1 column) and 1,175 us (6 columns). It is not bitwise equal to the default kernels (another FP32
summation order), but a multi-column call stays bitwise equal to one-column calls.

Workaround today: none. The existing switches do not move decode: `STRATA_MMVQ_WIDE_K_RPW=2` measured 54.31 ->
54.00 tok/s (commit 2a0d2f55), and the SIMD16 builds (`STRATA_MMVQ_SG`) gave no gain beyond noise (docs/INTEL.md).

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

issues.title: [Feature]: SYCL: cheaper IQ weight decodes in the grouped expert kernels (opt-in, same bits)
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
## What do you want to do?

Decode faster on Intel cards whose expert kernels are instruction-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.

On an Arc Pro B70 (SYCL port, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, two cards with a layer split) an ISA dump of the
lane kernels that read the routed experts (`native_gu_kernel` / `native_down_kernel` in
`sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`) shows 280-480 instructions per 32-weight part for the part's 8 dp4a: the
Q2_0 down dot spends ~300 of its 476 on the dpct per-byte emulation of `byte_level_permute`, the IQ4_NL dot ~100 of
279 on the compare/select codebook lookup, and every format pays popcount/multiply ksigns unpacking and 64-bit
`kbx * sizeof(block)` address products each iteration. The kernels read the experts at 19-44% of the card's DRAM
bandwidth, so decode is slower than the memory system allows.

I would like an opt-in flag (`STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1`) that switches the seven IQ expert formats to kernels
producing exactly the same bits with fewer instructions: table-driven ksigns masks, the signed grid byte in one xor
and one add, Q2_0 fields spread by shifts and masks, the IQ4_NL codebook through small position tables, a loop that
walks block pointers, two rows per lane in 16-lane sub-groups, and a multi-entry form for IQ2_XXS.

Measured on two B70 (32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1), main against a branch with
these kernels, `--layer-split 30 --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4` with the BF16 draft layer, greedy, a fixed
512-token coding reply: decode 79.5 -> 85.6 tok/s median (+7.7%), 76.0 -> 81.4 at a 40,796-token context, output
tokens and draft acceptance counts identical, prompt speed unchanged. A grouped-call microbenchmark on one card put
the Q2_0 down product at 63.7 -> 26.4 us per call and the IQ2_XXS/Q2_0 layers at 114.8 -> 59.8.

Workaround today: none; the kernels are what they are. The default path should stay byte-identical, so the change
must be opt-in and come with a parity test (`native_grouped_parity --iq`) that compares the new kernels against the
current ones bit for bit on random blobs for every IQ gate/up and down format.

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

issues.title: [Bug]: SYCL, 2x Arc Pro B70 layer split: --pipeline-windows 2 fails the first verify window (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED)
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
## What happened

With `--pipeline-windows 2` on a two-card layer split, the SYCL engine loads, captures all of its verify window
graphs without an error, reads the prompt, and then fails the first verify window. The request ends with
`verify: error` and the engine stops with a SYCL exception:

```
strata serve: --pipeline-windows 2: two verifiers per stage, the stages overlap across windows (decode too; the GDN snapshots beside the window)
strata verify: captured the 1-token window (upload no error, sync no error)
... (16 captures: 1-4 tokens, two verifiers, two stages, all "no error")
strata trace: read 24 tokens (windows) in 347.1 ms
strata serve: verify: error
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'sycl::_V1::exception'
  what():  level_zero backend failed with error: 37 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED)
```

The same build without `--pipeline-windows 2` (the same flags otherwise, at `--max-context 65536` and the default reserve) serves normally (deterministic output across
restarts, coherent replies, per-card health checks pass after each stop). The cards stay healthy after the crash
(per-card health check passes, no reset needed).

Command (the server's engine line, upstream main 296b59d2 built for bmg-g31; the last three flags were appended
to make the experts fit next to the second verifier, see below):

```
strata --serve --pack <ista-gsq-rco-iq3-xxs pack> --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf
  --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf --ple-io direct --stream-experts
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile-sycl.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill 8192 --no-prefill-borrow --kv int8
  --spec 4 --mtp <mtp rt> --spec-min-p 0 --conversation-cache-mib 32768 --conversation-cache-slots 4
  --suffix-draft 0 --lookup-chain 0 --mtp-max-t 4 --layer-split 30
  --pipeline-windows 2 --max-context 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 512
```

Container environment as in docs/INTEL.md (`STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1`,
`STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=12`, `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:*`).

Steps: start the server with the line above, send one chat completion (any short prompt, `max_tokens` 128). Both
starts that loaded failed this way at the first request: this one on main 296b59d2, and one earlier the same day
on a build of main plus an unrelated GDN change (`--max-context 200000`, `--prefill 8192`, same split).

What I expected: decode with the two verifiers overlapping, as the flag describes.

Side note (not the bug): at `--max-context 200000 --vram-reserve-mib 1024` the second verifier's 303 MiB means
909 experts no longer fit, and the engine refuses to start with the clear "REFUSED: ... experts are neither in
VRAM nor mirrored" message; at 32K context and a 512 MiB reserve everything fits. Without
`--pipeline-windows 2`, `--max-context 65536` with the default 1024 MiB reserve fits all 24,576 experts.

Possibly related: #1980 ends in the same `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED` abort at the first verify window on 2x B60,
but there it follows a `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` with experts missing from VRAM. Here every expert is resident, no
DEVICE_LOST is logged, and the run without `--pipeline-windows 2` is fine.

Not tested: a single B70, other Intel cards, other models, `--pipeline-windows 1`. I did not look for the failing
call inside the verify path.

issues.title: [Linux, RX 7900 XTX gfx1100, 0.1.44.1, ntfs3] --ple-io direct's PLE reads run at ~950 IOPS (3.7 MiB/s) while the same file does 70,406 IOPS from another process; boot probe says "fine", and the #1407 I/O allowance cannot fire for small random reads
issues.author: frankwang1130
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** `0.1.44.1` · AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100, ROCm 7.2.3,
HIP) · Linux 7.0.0-38-generic, Intel B760M D5 (no AVX-512), 20 CPUs, 62.6 GB RAM

**Summary.** On Linux + HIP (RX 7900 XTX, gfx1100, engine 0.1.44.1, stock config) the default
`--ple-io direct` PLE read path delivers **~950 random 4 KiB reads/s (3.7 MiB/s)** while a
prompt chunk is read, so layer 1 of one chunk never finishes inside the 60 s watchdog and the
engine aborts itself (exit -6, `server.py` restarts it, clients see 503). Five occurrences in
two engine sessions.

**The drive is not the limit, and it is not the Windows unbuffered path.** The model GGUF is on a
non-rotational NVMe, and a standalone process reading the *same file* with the *same* random
4 KiB `O_DIRECT` pattern reaches **70,406 IOPS / 275 MiB/s / 0.22 ms**, measured at the block layer
(`/sys/block/nvme0n1/stat`), not in userspace. That run overlapped the engine's stalled window:
while the engine's 16 pool threads sat in state `D` and `/proc/<pid>/io` advanced at ~3.7 MiB/s, a
second process doing identical reads on the same file still got 45–91k IOPS.

**The startup probe gives a false all-clear.** On this machine the boot probe prints

```
strata generate: PLE direct read probe: 34667 rows/s (fine)
```

(above the 15,000 rows/s bar in `generate.cpp:3314`), so no warning is printed. But that is ~36x
what the same process, same `PleReader`, same `DirectFile` pool delivers later at runtime. The
probe measures 4096 rows in ~0.12 s at boot, before the GPU work and the CPU expert pool exist; it
does not predict the prompt path.

## Environment

- **Engine:** 0.1.44.1, HIP, ROCm 7.2.3, stock config (no `STRATA_*` env set)
- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB
- **Host:** Linux 7.0.0-38-generic, Intel B760M D5 (no AVX-512), 20 CPUs, 62.6 GiB RAM, 0 MiB swap
- **Disk:** ZHITAI Ti600 1 TB NVMe on `nvme0n1p4`, **NTFS mounted with `ntfs3`**, rotational=0,
  the 44.9 GB GGUF is heavily fragmented (`filefrag` shows many extents)
- **Model:** Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S, PLE table **320,001,536 rows x 90 B = 28.8 GB**,
  `--ple-gguf` pointing at the same shard as `--native`
- **Config:** `--prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp ... --max-context 262144 --kv q4_0 --vision
  --vram-reserve-mib 1024 --pool-workers 9 --conversation-cache-mib 4096 ...`
- `--ple-io` left at the default (`direct`); `STRATA_IO_THREADS` unset

## What the engine logs

```
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): layer 1 of the
prompt chunk from token 8104) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.44.1): stage "reading the prompt (batched): layer 1 of the
prompt chunk from token 8104" for 60 s; 0 layers served since the last finished step
  VRAM free when this request began: 912 MiB
  expert pool: epoch 0, batch epoch 0: 0 of 0 jobs claimed, 0 done; 9 of 9 workers parked, 9 sleeping
  expert pool threads: w0..w8=sleeping; host idle for 192230 ms
  verify window: 0 tokens at position 0, host at layer step 1; the GPU rang 0
  threads waiting on the disk (state D): 16 of 37 (blk_io_schedule x16)
  memory: 49390 MiB resident, 0 MiB in swap, 8768 MiB RAM available; 7 major page faults so far
```

Stages seen across the five stalls: `layer 1 of the prompt chunk from token 0`, `... from token 8104`,
and one `waiting for the GPU (attention, router) at layer 1`. VRAM was never low (743–912 MiB free),
so this is not the #2065 card-full class. `dmesg` has no I/O errors, no timeouts, no hung-task
warnings; `nvme_core.io_timeout` is 30.

## Measurements (2026-10-17, same day, same machine, same file)

| what | random 4 KiB O_DIRECT | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| standalone process, 16 threads, 10 s | **70,406 IOPS, 275 MiB/s, 0.22 ms** | block-layer counters, `/sys/block/nvme0n1/stat` |
| standalone process, 16 threads, 15 s | 67,545 IOPS, 264 MiB/s, 278 ms max | userspace timing |
| standalone process, 64 threads | 75,269 IOPS, 294 MiB/s, 5.7 ms max | userspace timing |
| the engine's boot probe | 34,667 rows/s ("fine") | `ple_direct_rows_per_s`, `generate.cpp:1778` |
| **the engine, during the stall** | **~950 IOPS, 3.7 MiB/s, ~16.8 ms/read** | `/proc/<pid>/io` sampled every second; 16 threads in D |

The per-read latency is ~76x worse inside the engine than from a standalone process on the same file.

## Three things I think are wrong, independent of the root cause

1. **The #1407 I/O allowance can never engage for this read pattern.** `generate.cpp:9640` treats the
   file tier as busy only when `majflt + (read_bytes >> 20)` grows by **>= 16 in one second**. A PLE
   gather is a large number of *small* random 4 KiB reads: at ~950 reads/s that is ~4 MiB/s, and the
   whole run had **7 major page faults**. So the allowance (up to `STRATA_WATCHDOG_IO_S`, default 600 s)
   never starts and the engine is *guaranteed* to abort at 60 s even when it is making steady I/O
   progress. #1425 asked "should an I/O-bound prompt read be able to trip the 60 s no-progress
   watchdog?" and this looks like the answer is: it cannot be helped today, by construction. A read
   counter (reads/s or reads outstanding) would catch this shape; MiB/s does not.

2. **`STRATA_IO_THREADS` is capped at 16 on Linux but `ple_inflight` defaults to 256.** On POSIX each
   pool thread does one blocking `pread`, so the thread count *is* the queue depth
   (`direct_file.cpp:319`, `io_threads(16)`), while `generate.cpp:402` defaults `ple_inflight` to 256
   and comments that 64 "left the SSD half idle". So 256 jobs are queued and only 16 can ever reach
   the drive. `docs/INTEL.md` already documents 16 -> 64; the default still disagrees with the
   comment that justifies it.

3. **Neither documented mitigation is usable on a 64 GB machine running IQ3_S.** `--ple-io mmap`
   needs page cache for a 28.8 GB table and `--ple-io ram` needs 28.8 GB of RAM, but the expert arena
   is already 46.84 GiB resident (and pinned via `cudaHostRegister`), leaving **8768 MiB** available.
   So the log's advice (`#605: --ple-io ram`, `--ple-io mmap`) cannot be followed, and there is no
   supported workaround for this configuration.

## Questions

1. Is the ~76x per-read gap between the engine's runtime path and the boot probe on the same pool
   expected, or is something in the request path (the `aux_cpus` pinning that switches on per request,
   or `--native` mmap and `--ple-io direct` sharing one GGUF file on `ntfs3`) serialising the reads?
2. Would a read-count based file-tier signal (rather than MiB/s + major faults) be the right fix for
   the watchdog allowance?
3. Does anyone have a measurement of `--ple-io direct` on `ntfs3` specifically? All the earlier
   reports I could find (#1425, #1629, #2040, #1407) are Windows, ext4, or loop devices.

## What I did not test

- I did not move the model to an ext4 filesystem, so I cannot separate `ntfs3` from the engine's own
  read path. That is the cheapest next test and I can run it.
- I did not sample `/sys/block/nvme0n1/stat` *during* a stall. That single measurement splits the two
  remaining hypotheses: device IOPS ~950 means the requests reach the drive and are slow there;
  device IOPS ~0 with 16 threads still in `D` means they are stuck above the drive. I can reproduce
  and capture this, plus `gdb -p <pid>` backtraces for the 16 blocked threads.
- Three older stalls in my log are a different class (0 threads in state D, VRAM free 448-450 MiB,
  #2065); I am not claiming them here.

## Related

#1425 (closed for 0.1.42; the maintainer invited a 0.1.44 re-report), #1629, #1407, #2040, #1984,
#605.

issues.title: [Bug]: A `</think>` the model quotes inside a code block in its reasoning still ends the reasoning, and the turn's tool call is lost (follow-up to #1526)
issues.author: KarlGrier
issues.body:
### What happened

This is the same family as #537 / #1526 (a quoted `</think>`) and #2026 (a quoted `</tool_call>`, fixed in 0.1.43.1). The model quotes a tag while it thinks, and the server takes the quote for the real tag. #1526's rule (v0.1.42) treats a `</think>` written right after a quote or backtick, and followed by anything but a line break, as reasoning text. That rule misses a tag the model writes as Python source with escapes inside a fenced code block, which is common when an agent works on code that renders the chat template:

````
I will add this test:
```python
    self.assertIn("<think>\n\n</think>\n\n", prompt)
```
````

(`\n` here is the two characters of the escape.) The character before the quoted `</think>` is the `n` of `\n`, so `OutputParser` ends the reasoning there. What follows:

- **The answer:** the rest of the thinking comes back as answer text, including the model's real `</think>`.
- **The tool call:** the real call after the real `</think>` reads as quoted, because fence tracking restarts at the answer and the closing ``` of the quoted block opens a "fence".
- **The client:** it gets `finish_reason: "stop"`, part of the reasoning as the answer, and no tool call, so an agent ends the session.

**How often.** We ran one real task on Strata's own `serve/` code 9 times, across four agent harnesses, over both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`. The task was to make the config's `reasoning_effort` default apply to every API; it involves `"none"` and so the `<think>\n\n</think>` prompt. **All 9 sessions ended at this point.** Whether the task got solved depended only on whether the fix was complete by then (3 of 9 were not). 18 sessions on plain coding tasks never hit it.

**Parser-only reproduction** (from the repo root, no model needed):

```python
from serve.frontend import OutputParser
tools = [{"name": "read", "parameters": {"properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}}}]
p = OutputParser(thinking=True, tools=tools)
text = ('I will add this test:\n```python\n    self.assertIn("<think>\\n\\n</think>\\n\\n", prompt)\n```\n'
        'Now read the file.\n</think>\n\n'
        '<tool_call>\n<function=read>\n<parameter=path>\nserve/x.py\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>')
evs = p.feed(text) + p.finish()
print("tool calls:", [e.call.name for e in evs if e.kind == "tool_call"])
print("content:", repr("".join(e.text for e in evs if e.kind == "content")[:70]))
```

On v0.1.44.1 this prints `tool calls: []` and a content that starts with the rest of the quoted test (`'\\n\\n", prompt)\n```\nNow read the file.\n</think>\n\n<tool_call>...'`). Expected: `tool calls: ['read']` and an empty content.

**A fix we tested.** Inside a code fence (``` or ~~~) of the reasoning, a `</think>` is quoted text, the same way #804 / #1058 already treat `<tool_call>`. A fence the model never closes must not swallow the real end of the thinking, so the fix has a safeguard:

- From a fenced `</think>` on, the text is held until the fence closes. Then the held text was reasoning, and it is released and read again as reasoning.
- If the turn ends with the fence still open, the last `</think>` held is the end of the thinking.
- Only the reasoning / answer / tool-call split can change; the generated tokens do not. Streaming of the reasoning pauses only while a fenced tag waits for its fence to close.
- Inline code (an odd backtick count in the paragraph) is left out on purpose. Counting it misfired once in our data, on a real end of thinking after the model wrote "escape backticks with \`".

How we checked it:

- **Replay:** all 503 recorded tool-enabled turns from those sessions went through `OutputParser`, as shipped and patched. The patched parser recovers the **7** lost tool calls (one for each session that was cut mid-task) and gives the **same events for the other 496 turns**. Its events are the same whether the text arrives 1 character, 7 characters or all at once.
- **Unit tests:** five new tests, covering a fenced tag followed by a call, the hold ending when the fence closes, an unclosed fence with a real `</think>`, an unclosed fence with a quoted and then a real tag, and a turn cut inside an unclosed fence. The existing `serve.test_reasoning_tools` tests pass, and so does the full serve suite.
- **Server level:** 10 recorded agent requests (7 of them the turns that lost their call) went greedy through two servers on the same engine, one as shipped and one patched. The prompt's CPU share was off, which makes repeated runs identical. The raw generated text and the token counts were identical in all 10. The split differed in 3 requests, where the patched server returned the tool call and the shipped one returned none.
- **End to end:** the same real task, 4 more sessions on the patched server (two of the harnesses, 2 each). All 4 ran to the end and solved it (hidden tests and the full suite), with no lost or unparsed tool call.
- **The patch:** 54 lines in `serve/frontend.py` plus the tests. Happy to open it as a PR if that helps.

**Not covered:** in one session the model wrote `"<think>\n\n` and then a `</think>` with real line breaks around it, and ended its turn 12 tokens later. That looks like the model emitting its real end-of-thinking token, the #1814 / #2731 shape, which no parser rule can recover.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Strata 0.1.44.1 server code. `serve/frontend.py` is unchanged from the tag, and main had no newer change to it on 2026-10-16. Our build carries local engine patches that do not touch `serve/`.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, RTX 5080 16 GB and RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB, Linux.

### Engine log

Not attached: the parser-only reproduction above shows the problem without a model.

Measured and drafted with Claude Code.

issues.title: tools/strata_bench.py: UnicodeDecodeError reading CMakeLists.txt on non-UTF-8 Windows (GBK/cp932), before any measurement
issues.author: Lithivm
issues.body:
`tools/strata_bench.py:564` (`project_version`) reads `CMakeLists.txt` with `Path.read_text()` and **no `encoding=`**, so it decodes with the OS locale code page. On a Chinese or Japanese Windows (GBK / cp932) the file's UTF-8 BOM makes the read fail and `BENCH.bat` dies **before any measurement**:

```
$ python tools/strata_bench.py
Starting strata-iq2_xs.json on port 8080 (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...
  still loading (2 s) ...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 1028, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 989, in main
    pre = collect_machine(base, key, cfg, a.gpu)
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 639, in collect_machine
    "strata_version": project_version(), "strata_commit": git_commit(),
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 564, in project_version
    m = re.search(r"project\(strata VERSION ([\d.]+)", (ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text())
  File "C:\Users\...\lib\pathlib.py", line 1135, in read_text
    return f.read()
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbf in position 2: illegal multibyte sequence
```

`CMakeLists.txt` starts with the UTF-8 BOM `EF BB BF`; `0xbf` at offset 2 is the third BOM byte. Note it leaves the server it started behind, and the process exits with a traceback rather than a message.

`setup.py:4649` reads the same file with `encoding="utf-8"`:

```python
m = re.search(r"project\(strata VERSION ([\d.]+)", (ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
```

so this looks like a `strata_bench.py` omission rather than an intentional locale dependency. Other `read_text()` calls in the file that read repository files are likely to hit the same thing on those systems.

**Workaround** (no source change needed): run with UTF-8 mode on.

```
set PYTHONUTF8=1
BENCH.bat
```

Verified: the suite then runs to completion (420 s) and writes a normal report.

**Suggested fix:** pass `encoding="utf-8"` at that call (and audit the other `read_text()` calls in the file), or read with `errors="replace"` — the value only needs to match `project(strata VERSION x.y.z)`.

Environment: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Python 3.10.11, Strata 0.1.44.1 (release engine). A benchmark report produced on this machine is in #2791, which mentions this bug.

issues.title: [Feature request] 16-bit KV cache option above 8K context (to A/B against int8)
issues.author: mbaaku
issues.body:
**What:** an opt-in `--kv f16` (or `bf16`) for contexts above 8K. Today the choices there are `int8` (default), `k8v4` and `q4_0`; full precision is used only up to 8K.

**Why:** with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M (v0.1.44.1, SYCL, Arc Pro B60, `--kv int8`, `--max-context 131072`) as the model of a coding agent, tool-call formatting degrades with prompt length:
- the first broken calls appear around 15–25k prompt tokens;
- at ~79k we saw a streak of calls with an empty body (`<function=Bash></function>`, no parameter), 48 in 40 minutes against 19 well-formed ones;
- at ~100k a reply looped in its reasoning until max tokens.

The broken calls are already in the raw model output (`STRATA_DEBUG=1`), so this is generation, not parsing. It may be the weight quantization alone, but the KV cache is the other quantized part that grows with context, and there is currently no way to rule it out. `docs/DETAILS.md` measures q4_0 against int8 (perplexity +8–12% on long documents); a 16-bit option would allow the same comparison one step up.

**What we would measure:** the share of malformed tool calls per 10k prompt tokens over the same agent workload with `int8` vs `f16`, from the `STRATA_DEBUG` raw output. Happy to post the numbers here.

**Cost we understand:** twice the KV memory of int8, so fewer experts in VRAM or a shorter context. It would be an opt-in for diagnosis and for cards with room to spare, not a new default.
