issues.title: [Feature] Third-party qwen4exp GGUFs via tools/iq_pack.py — measured report (OrcaRouter Uncensored IQ3_XXS, YaRN to 1M)
issues.author: emiltsoi
issues.body:
[Feature] Third-party qwen4exp GGUFs via tools/iq_pack.py — measured report (OrcaRouter Uncensored IQ3_XXS, YaRN to 1M) and a supported-path question

**Summary.** `tools/iq_pack.py --compat-bf16` repacked a third-party `qwen4exp` GGUF
(`orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF`, IQ3_XXS, 2 shards, ~85 GB) into a
working native pack with no source changes. The v0.1.44.1 release binary runs it
end-to-end, including YaRN x4 to a 1,048,576-token window. Question at the end:
is there appetite for documenting this repack path, or a curated `SUPPORTED_GGUFS`
entry for third-party repositories? Happy to PR whichever is preferred.

**Hardware and software.**

- RTX 5090 32 GB; Ryzen 9 9950X; 96 GB RAM; NVMe
- Windows 11, driver 581.xx, release binary `strata 0.1.44.1` (source at 296b59d)
- Model: `orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF` — IQ3_XXS
  (`...-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf`, `-00002-of-00002.gguf`).
  Expert mix: routed gate/up IQ3_XXS, routed down IQ4_NL; PLE table IQ4_NL.
- Draft: official MTP chain (`mtp_fetch.py` → `mtp_pack.py` → `mtp_rt.py`, Q2_0).
  The repo's `MTP-draft.gguf` uses llama.cpp `blk.48.*` names and does NOT feed
  `mtp_pack.py`; the official path worked.

**What was done.**

```
python tools/iq_pack.py --gguf <shard1> --out pack-unc-iq3xxs --compat-bf16
```

Pack: 1,079 tensors indexed, 303 served natively from the GGUFs, 459 dense-side
conversions (96 exact, 363 rounded, max abs err ~0.0144); expert and PLE bytes
untouched. Then:

```
--pack pack-unc-iq3xxs --native <shard1> --ple-gguf <shard1>
--expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto
--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <mtp rt dir>
--max-context 1048576 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4
--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 1664 --resident-experts
```

**Note relevant to #2396:** the same files run on the native-pack path without
touching the `compress_ratios` check in `read_geometry` — consistent with that
regression being specific to the `--gguf` loader, not the weights.

**Measured** (single runs per depth; corpus haystack with two synthetic needles at
~30% and ~88% positions; `reasoning_effort: xhigh`; engine-reported timings):

| Stage | Window | YaRN | Prompt tok | Decode tok/s | Draft acc | Needles |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| baseline | 262,144 | — | 252.0K | 150.5 | 82% | 2/2 |
| A | 524,288 | x2 | 497.6K | 110.2 | 67% | 2/2 |
| B | 1,048,576 | x4 | 907.1K | 107.7 | 74% | 2/2 |

Across 15 probes (5 per stage): 15/15 clean `stop` finishes, zero repetition flags,
early needle 10/10, late needle 7/10 (misses at all scales — a positional effect,
not a depth cliff). Prompt ingest ~2–2.5K tok/s at depth (~7 min TTFT at 907K).
Over-window requests are rejected, never truncated.

**Not tested:** vision (`strata-vision.exe` + the repo's F16 mmproj not wired),
`--batch`, agentic multi-turn trajectories, quality delta vs the official quants,
and anything below ~119K prompt depth. Needle tests measure retrieval on these
inputs only; single-sample misses are stochastic.

**Ask.** Would you like (a) a docs page documenting `iq_pack.py` repacking for
third-party `qwen4exp` GGUFs (prereqs: `gguf-py` checkout, per-type kernel
coverage, the `--spec`/`--prefill` requirement, MTP fetch), (b) orcarouter quants
in `SUPPORTED_GGUFS` once sha256s are reviewed, or (c) neither — keep it unofficial?
I can PR (a) or the bench-results folder; whichever you prefer.

issues.title: sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell): mmvq_il_parity --emit-table over 7 runs, decode +1.3% in the engine; the table would also apply to the RTX 5070
issues.author: brocktice
issues.body:
## Card

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (sm_120, 96 GB, 300 W), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.2, Linux. Strata v0.1.43 built with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120 -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`.

## mmvq_il_parity --bench --emit-table

Seven runs on an otherwise idle card; every run ends `mmvq_il_parity: OK (every case, T 1-4, rows 1/2/4 and the table, bitwise)`. Several cells flip between runs, so the block below applies `emit_table`'s rule (worst shape of a cell under 0.97 of native_mmvq, else 0; a class with no shape copies its lower neighbour) to the **median** of the seven runs per shape, token count and rows choice:

```cpp
    {23, {{0, 1, 1, 2, 1}, {0, 4, 2, 4, 4}, {0, 2, 2, 2, 2}}},   // IQ4_XS
    {12, {{0, 0, 1, 2, 2}, {0, 2, 2, 4, 4}, {0, 2, 2, 2, 2}}},   // Q4_K
    {13, {{0, 0, 1, 4, 4}, {0, 1, 2, 4, 2}, {0, 2, 2, 2, 2}}},   // Q5_K
    {14, {{0, 0, 1, 4, 4}, {0, 0, 2, 4, 1}, {0, 2, 2, 2, 2}}},   // Q6_K
    {11, {{0, 1, 2, 2, 4}, {0, 2, 2, 4, 2}, {0, 2, 2, 2, 2}}},   // Q3_K
// one column:
    {23, {0, 0, 1, 0, 2}},   // IQ4_XS
    {12, {0, 0, 1, 1, 1}},   // Q4_K
    {13, {0, 0, 1, 1, 1}},   // Q5_K
    {14, {0, 0, 0, 0, 0}},   // Q6_K
    {11, {0, 0, 2, 2, 2}},   // Q3_K
```

Summed over every measured shape at 2-4 columns, these rows take 13.9% less time than `kIlRowsShared`'s picks on this card (median times): IQ4_XS -7.0%, Q4_K -7.3%, Q5_K -3.8%, Q6_K -8.4%, and Q3_K -34%, which the shared table leaves on native_mmvq (-38 to -49% at 6144-12288 rows, -12 to -20% at 2560, none below 2048).

The full output of run 1 is below; I can attach all seven.

## Decode A/B in the engine

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, all experts resident, `--batch 4 --batch-mtp --spec 4 --kv int8`, one card, greedy, thinking off. Each arm is a fresh server; four fixed prompts (256 tokens, the median of the 2nd and 3rd pass), one ~8K-token prompt, and the four prompts at once. Arm B sets `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_ROWS` to the 2-4 column rows above (not the one-column rows); A is unset.

| pair (A/B interleaved) | solo decode B/A | 4 at once B/A | long prompt B/A |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.013 | 1.026 | 0.997 |
| 2 | 1.011 | 0.999 | 1.002 |
| 3 | 1.015 | 0.987 | 0.999 |

A ran at 226-229 tok/s solo. All answers are byte-identical between the arms (and between every A run). With the one-column rows as well, a single screening run gave no extra gain. That is 3 pairs, not the 10 the doc asks for; I can run more if useful.

## The catch: sm_120 is also the RTX 5070

`kIlArch` is keyed by compute capability, so a `kIlRows_120` from this card would also replace the RTX 5070's half of `kIlRowsShared`. I have no 5070 to check it on, which is why this is an issue and not a PR. If a 5070 run of `--bench` exists, applying the same worst-of-both-cards rule to the two would give a table for both; the Q3_K row alone would not conflict with anything, since the shared table has none.

issues.title: [BUG] Engine crashes with 0xC0000005 in hipModuleLoad on first request — AMD RX 9070 XT (gfx1201) on Windows, Strata 0.1.44.1
issues.author: jx839842046
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows + AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), the engine starts cleanly to `session is up` but crashes on the first user request with an access violation (0xC0000005) inside `amdhip64_7.dll` → `libtensilelite-host.dll` → `libhipblaslt.dll hipblasLtMatmul` → `rocblas_gemm_ex`. The crash is at the `hipModuleLoad` boundary on every code-object load — not specific to one kernel. The bundled ROCm (`engine/amdhip64_7.dll`, `engine/rocm/bin/*`) appears to have a Windows + gfx1201 incompatibility in the hipBLASLt / TensileLite path.

## Environment

- **Model**: `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq2_xs` (the recommended `--family qwen --model IQ2_XS` on 48 GB RAM)
- **Strata version**: `0.1.44.1` (latest on `main` at the time of this report; `MIN_ENGINE = (0, 1, 44, 1)`)
- **GPU**: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, 16 GB GDDR6, gfx1201 (RDNA4)
- **Driver**: `32.0.31036.15` — AMD Software: PRO Edition 26.Q3 (released 2026-08-12). This is the latest PRO Edition for this card; the consumer Adrenalin 26.9.2 (Optional) is also available but I have not installed it.
- **CPU**: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (8C/16T, AVX-512)
- **RAM**: 48 GB DDR5 (system shows 47 GB usable)
- **OS**: Windows 10 64-bit (the "Windows 10 - 64-Bit Edition" download section on amd.com)
- **Other GPU on the box**: integrated `AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics` (gfx1036, the Ryzen APU) — not used by Strata (it's not in the engine's gfx list); `engine/strata-device.exe --list-devices` correctly picks GPU 0 (9070 XT).

## Repro steps

1. Fresh install with `START-HERE.bat --yes --family qwen --model IQ2_XS --no-start`.
2. Run `run-iq2_xs.bat`. Engine starts, reaches `session is up (engine 0.1.44.1)`.
3. Open the web UI (`http://127.0.0.1:8080`) and send any message (e.g. "hello").
4. Engine dies mid-first-request. Web UI shows `the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 3221225477)` (= 0xC0000005 in signed form).
5. Server auto-restarts the engine. The same prompt hits the same crash on every restart.

## Crash stack (verbatim, from `strata-iq2_xs.log`)

0x00007FF7BC679C6C, .../engine/strata.exe(0x00007FF7BBF00000) + 0x779C6C
0x00007FFF38517374, KERNEL32.DLL, BaseThreadInitThunk() + 0x14
0x00007FFF38FBCC91, ntdll.dll, RtlUserThreadStart() + 0x21
```

The same stack appeared earlier as `hipModuleUnload failed: unspecified launch failure` + `Exception Code: 0xC00000FD` (stack overflow) — that's the same path before `ROCBLAS_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE` was raised; the underlying fault is in `hipModuleLoad`, not in stack exhaustion. Once the rocBLAS worker threads had enough stack, the crash turned into the clean 0xC0000005 in `hipModuleLoad` itself.

## Engine output before crash

```
strata generate: GPU 0: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201)
strata generate: HIP runtime E:\AI\Strata\engine\amdhip64_7.dll
strata generate: expert arena: locked 10901 MiB via working-set minimum + VirtualLock; cudaHostRegister of the whole arena FAILED (invalid argument); 33 slices pinned (22 GiB); large pages refused for 35456548864 B (GetLargePageMinimum=2097152, VirtualAlloc error 1450); using 4 KB pages
strata generate: expert cache 6472 slots, 8.67 GiB of VRAM
strata serve: 2289 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
... crash before any "prompt X tokens" line ...
```

The engine always reaches "VRAM free with everything loaded" then dies before the first prefill. Speed numbers are reachable only via the first request of an engine instance — i.e. never, in practice.

## Things I tried (none helped)

1. Removed the `--control-vector-scaled ... --cvec-mode project` lines from `strata-iq2_xs.json` (no longer needs the `data/Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-refusal-direction-r.gguf` steering vector). Same crash, different stack frame ordering but same `hipModuleLoad` top.
2. Reduced `--max-context` from 131072 to 32768. Same crash.
3. Set `ROCBLAS_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE=33554432` and `HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE=33554432` in the config's `"env"` field (passed through `serve/server.py:child_env` → `strata.exe`). The earlier `Exception Code: 0xC00000FD` (STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW) disappeared and became the `0xC0000005` you see above. So the rocBLAS stack fix does work; the remaining crash is inside `hipModuleLoad` itself.
4. Set `STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS=0` in `"env"` — confirmed by `arch_defaults.cpp` reading `getenv("STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS")` (engine no longer prints the `"5 exact speed switches on by default"` line). The five `STRATA_GDN_*` / `STRATA_CVEC_FUSE` defaults are now off. No effect on the crash.
5. Set `STRATA_WDDM_BUDGET=0`. No effect on the crash (used ~11 GiB of expert cache regardless).
6. Verified `engine/strata-device.exe --list-devices` sees the card correctly:

   ```
   device 0: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
     arch gfx1201, 15.9 GiB, wave32
   ```

   (device 1 is the integrated gfx1036 APU which the bundled ROCm was not built for, as expected — Strata picks device 0 only.)

## Side observations

- `expert arena: large pages refused for 35456548864 B (GetLargePageMinimum=2097152, VirtualAlloc error 1450); using 4 KB pages` — the bundled ROCm explicitly falls back to 4 KB pages on Windows. This may contribute to the code-object load path being exercised on every request (no in-RAM code cache shared across invocations?).
- The 0xC00000FD → 0xC0000005 transition after raising the rocBLAS worker-stack size strongly suggests the bundled `engine/rocm/bin/*` does deep template instantiation in `rocblas_internal_gemm_grouped_batched_ex_template<H>` which on Windows + gfx1201 is right at the limit of the 8 MiB default thread stack. Even with `ROCBLAS_WORKSPACE_STACK_SIZE` raised, the launch eventually falls over inside `hipModuleLoad`.
- On a previous session before I disabled `STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS=0`, the crash surfaced as `prefill mmq: iota: unspecified launch failure` (a different failure point but in the same launch family) — toggling the gfx12 defaults moves the failure around but does not eliminate it.

## Suggestion

The bundled ROCm (`engine/rocm/bin/*`, `engine/amdhip64_7.dll`, `libtensilelite-host.dll`, `libhipblaslt.dll`, `rocblas.dll`, `hipblas.dll`) on Windows appears not to be combined with a shipped code-object cache (the equivalent of `~/.cache/hipblaslt` on Linux). On Windows + gfx1201 this means every first request of every engine instance triggers a fresh `hipModuleLoad` → TensileLite JIT path. If there is an opt-in env var to disable hipBLASLt and force a non-JIT path on Windows, or to keep the code-object cache warm across requests, that may be the fix.

## Files / logs

- `E:\AI\Strata\strata-iq2_xs.log` — approximately 1840 lines, multiple crashes; the last crash block ends at the line before the next `[strata] ... engine started:`.
- `E:\AI\Strata\strata-iq2_xs.json` and `E:\AI\Strata\run-iq2_xs.bat` — the config I ran.

[strata-iq2_xs.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33553651/strata-iq2_xs.log)
[strata-iq2_xs.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33553671/strata-iq2_xs.json)

## Environment summary one-liner

`Win10 64-bit · AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT · 32.0.31036.15 (PRO 26.Q3) · Strata 0.1.44.1 · Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS · crash in hipModuleLoad on first request`

issues.title: Batched prompt read stalls (#1118 family) + prefill copy_i32 illegal memory access, engine 0.1.44
issues.author: zy15617
issues.body:
Engine: 0.1.44 (BUILD.json → version: 0.1.44; the stall dump's PDB path is C:\Users\AI-Server\Desktop\Strata\GitHub\wt-144-rel\build-release-zip\strata.pdb, i.e. the official release build)
Server: serve/server.py from the same release
OS: Windows 11, WDDM
GPU: single RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) - no layer split, no --pipeline-windows, no --resident-experts
CPU: Threadripper 3970X, 32 physical cores, no AVX-512; 96 GiB DDR4-3200
Model: Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, tools/iq_pack.py native pack

---

Summary

Two separate problems, found while benchmarking --pool-workers:

1. A long prompt stalls in reading the prompt (batched) when another slot is decoding. The #29 watchdog fires at 60 s and stops the engine; the server reloads the model (~2–3 min). Root cause identified and a workaround confirmed - it is #1118.
2. prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access was encountered on the third round of 16K prompts at --batch 2. The engine is then left at live.state = "unloaded" for 6+ minutes and does not recover on its own. Not resolved.

---

1. Long-prompt stall in the batched reader - same family as #1118

Symptom

A ~16K-token prompt stops advancing partway through the read. The log repeats the same line every 10 s for 130 s+:

[strata] reading the prompt: 14,757 of 14,764 tokens, 131 s so far
[strata] answering: 3 of max 192 tokens, 0.0 tok/s

The watchdog (#29) then stops the engine:

strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched), done up to token 14757) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.44): stage "reading the prompt (batched), done up to token 14757" for 60 s; 0 layers served since the last finished step (0 = stopped, more = slow)
  wrote the thread stacks to H:\Strata\strata-stall-28168.dmp (attach it to the issue)

From the outside: the port stays listening, the request hangs forever, and the server reloads the model.

A second occurrence stalled at token 7,304 (strata-stall-34384.dmp) - so it happens at different offsets, not one fixed position.

Reproduction

The trigger is one slot decoding while a long prompt is being read - exactly what #1118 describes. Note this made it easy to misdiagnose: a *bare* single 16K request with no other traffic in flight completes fine. It stalls when the harness has another request (a warm-up, or a second concurrent request) running alongside. Read as a pair, the two ingredients are:

- "parallel": 2 (--batch 2)
- one request decoding in a slot while a second, long prompt is admitted and read

Workaround that works: STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE=0

Adding it to the config's env block fixes it on this machine:

| 16K-token prompt | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| single, no other traffic | stalls 130 s+ | 11.6 s, prefill 1600 tok/s |
| two concurrent | stalls → engine unloaded | 23.2 s, prefill 1613–1630 tok/s |

Re-measured a second time: single 16K in 11.8 s, prefill 1605 tok/s. Consistent.

The cost is the one #1118 already documents: while a prompt is read, the other slot's decode drops to 5–11 tok/s. Acceptable here.

One detail worth flagging: this box already had STRATA_BATCH_YIELD_CHUNKS=0 set in the config, and that alone did not prevent the stall. STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE is a *different* variable - setting the yield-chunk count to 0 is not a substitute for turning the decode share off.

Binary strings confirm both variables and the log templates exist in 0.1.44:

STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE
STRATA_BATCH_YIELD_CHUNKS
BSTOP / BYIELD
strata batch: the prompt read gives way at %lld of %lld tokens; slot %d holds it (copied in %.1f ms)
strata batch: BYIELD %d not taken at %lld of %lld%s%s

Question

Is STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE meant to be user-facing, or is it an internal knob that happened to be the right lever here? If the latter, would the signal path in the yield window be worth hardening so that a prompt read cannot wait on it indefinitely (rather than requiring the variable)?

---

2. prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access at --batch 2 (unresolved)

With problem 1 worked around, a new failure shows up on the third back-to-back round of two concurrent 16K prompts:

strata verify: captured the batch window over slots 0,0,1,1
strata batch: 116 windows, avg 3.28 rows, 39.05 ms/window = run 35.17 (CUDA0 GPU-reach wait 31.15 + CPU experts 1.80) + commit 1.38 + emit 2.32 + adapt wait 0.18; per stage (ms/window): CUDA0 wait 31.15 + pool 1.80; per layer-window: CPU experts 0.59, VRAM hits 39.48, PCIe 0.00; routed entries per window: VRAM 1894.9 (98.5%), PCIe 0.1 (0.0%), CPU 29.2 (1.5%); adaptive tier (async): 116 rounds started, 419 experts swapped in; 27.6 rows/s over 13828 ms of wall time (admissions included)
prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access was encountered

After that: live.state = "unloaded", and it stayed there for 6+ minutes while I polled /metrics every 10 s (40 polls, all unloaded). Both in-flight requests got HTTP 503. The server did not restart the engine on its own; I had to kill the processes and relaunch.

The same log also shows the adaptive tier running far off its steady state:

strata serve: asynchronous adaptive tier: 322 rounds, 3888 experts swapped in, 1449.5 ms per round (start to flip, between windows) (arena, copy-in only, batch 0, wait 1, pick inline 0.10 ms/round)

Steady state on this box is ~20 ms/round; 1449.5 ms/round suggests it was not converging.

Relation to existing reports

- #1341 - your reply there notes prefill copy_i32 is the sticky cudaGetLastError() mis-attribution (src/kernels/cuda/qsa.cu:77) and names no real kernel.
- #2157 - you note prefill.cpp:4678 is only the catch of the whole prompt run, so it names no kernel either.

This box is single card, no layer split, no --pipeline-windows, so it is neither of the multi-GPU paths above. It looks like a third manifestation, on the batched path, at --batch 2 with --kv-resident 32768. Not deterministic: 2 of 3 rounds passed, the third failed. 8K prompts at --batch 2 did not trigger it in ~20 runs.

Question

Would STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1 or STRATA_KV_WIDE_HOST=0 be worth trying here (both were levers in #1407 / #2157), or is there a more targeted STRATA_* switch for the batched prefill path you would rather see tried first? Happy to run any reproducer you name.

---

Config

--pack <swift-iq3_xxs> --native <IQ3_XXS gguf> --ple-gguf <same file>
--expert-profile <expert-profile.bin> --expert-cache auto
--prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --mtp <rt>
--max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768
--vision --vram-reserve-mib 1664
--spec-min-p 0.90 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --adapt-decay 0.97 --adapt-async 1
--pcie-frac 0.15 --batch-mtp --batch 2
env: STRATA_BF16_TC=1, STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1, STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT=1,
     STRATA_BATCH_YIELD_CHUNKS=0, STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE=0   (last one added as the workaround)

/metrics at idle: pool_workers=31, expert_slots=6918, batch_slots=2, batch_groups=1, version=0.1.44.

Engine start lines of note:

strata generate: expert arena read unbuffered (0 of 32 probe reads from the file cache; 8.7 GiB available, 70.7 GiB of files)
strata generate: R4 hit path ON - resident experts are computed on the GPU
strata generate: token graph hit path: 6918 resident experts, decided on the device

Not an all-resident / zero-doorbell session: zero-doorbell appears 0 times in the engine log, so #1025's doorbell fix is not in play here.

---

Dumps available

- strata-stall-28168.dmp (399,852 B, 2026-10-16 20:16:47) - single 16K, stalled at token 14,757
- strata-stall-34384.dmp (399,012 B, 2026-10-16 20:04:50) - stalled at token 7,304

Happy to attach either or both.

---

Two notes that cost me time, in case they help the docs

1. The stall report and the dump path are written to strata-<model>.log, not to the server's srv.out. I read srv.out first, saw no no progress line, and concluded the watchdog had never fired - it had, with the full stall report and dump path, in the engine's own log.
2. live.state = "unloaded" for 6+ minutes is not self-recovering on this box. Every client times out and the engine only comes back after a manual kill + relaunch. If that is expected behaviour after this class of error, a note in TROUBLESHOOTING.md would save someone the same minutes.[

[strata-stall-28168.dmp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33552047/strata-stall-28168.dmp)
[strata-stall-34384.dmp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33552048/strata-stall-34384.dmp)
[strata-swift-iq3_xxs.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33552049/strata-swift-iq3_xxs.log)

](url)

issues.title: [Feature]: Experimental native RX 580 / gfx803 support for Qwen3.6 on Linux
issues.author: minkiboo
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B through Strata on an AMD Radeon RX 580 (8 GiB, native gfx803) with system-RAM expert offload on Linux, without architecture spoofing. An explicit experimental, build-from-source option would make this older hardware usable without implying that every Polaris card or model is qualified.

The current workaround is a project-local port using isolated ROCm 6.3.4 and a separately built gfx803 rocBLAS/Tensile library. Draft PR #2765 proposes the narrow enablement changes: build selection, compatibility/kernel fallback, bounded uploads from pageable memory, and conservative hybrid prompt batching. Q8 KV, independent CPU speedups and startup caching are intentionally separate.

On the tested RX580 / 32 GiB RAM system, the bounded path passed a real API tool round-trip, stream cancellation/recovery and process restart. Streamed expert/MMQ prompt batches faulted and remain excluded; historical model-logit differences are unresolved. The draft documents these limits and does not claim general numerical or long-context qualification.

This issue tracks the requested experimental hardware support and discussion of its acceptance requirements. The draft still needs affected-backend build checks and evidence for the repository's unchanged-default-path requirement before maintainer review/merge readiness. No automatic setup, driver installation or broad supported-hardware claim is requested in this first change.

issues.title: [Bug]: --rope-scaling and the other rope flags are resolved (for linear/yarn logged as active) on the Mac (Metal) engine but change no rotation
issues.author: oinani0721
issues.body:
### What happened

On the Metal engine, the rope flags that docs/DETAILS.md:1427-1430 lists (`--rope-scaling`, `--rope-scale`, `--rope-freq-base`, `--rope-freq-scale`, `--yarn-*`) and a model file's `rope.scaling.*` keys are resolved, and for linear and yarn the engine logs the scaling as active (`strata generate: rope scaling yarn, factor 4 ...`, src/program/generate.cpp:3002-3008). But no rotation on a Mac reads them:

- `rope_table_set` does nothing on Metal (metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp:151, "the window keeps its own table");
- every RoPE rotation on Metal is in `qsa_prep`, which reads only the decode window's own cos/sin table (metal/kernels/qsa.metal:74);
- `Window::init` builds that table without scaling, from the model file's `rope.freq_base` (metal/src/engine/window.cpp:468-475).

So, by the code, `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4` gives the unscaled rotation, and a context past the trained 262,144 tokens runs with the stock angles.

Expected: the flags change the rotation on a Mac as they do on the PC.

On an Apple M5 Max (128 GB), main 296b59d's Metal build gave the same tokens, the same timing-free DONE fields and byte-identical first-window logits for 86 requests (a question, 64 tokens of a fixed text forced one per request, 20 prompts of 256 to 1,000 tokens and 128 tokens of a story), and byte-identical log-probability rows (the target token's and the top 64, `STRATA_METAL_LOGPOS`) at every position that the next one-token window continued (the 64 forced tokens and the story), with and without `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --yarn-orig-ctx 262144` (the other rope flags were not run), with one-token decode windows (no MTP draft layer, no suffix drafts). On setup's default config its 6 requests gave identical tokens, DONE fields and first-window logits with and without `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --yarn-orig-ctx 262144` too.

The model was Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_S (two shards, revision eec4e10a of its Hugging Face repository), greedy, thinking off. I have a change that makes the window build its table with `build_rope_table` under the resolved scaling, with a CPU-only test, and will open it as a pull request that references this issue.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1-metal (main 296b59d) · Apple M5 Max, 128 GB · macOS 27.0.1

### Engine log

```

```

issues.title: [Engine] Windows x64 HIP 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3) on Strix Halo (gfx1151): default expert-cache mode still dies with 'the embedding buffer failed'; --mmap-experts works
issues.author: ppcckk
issues.body:
## Re-tested on Strata 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3) — 2026-10-20

**Strata version tested: 0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3** (`strata-engine-0.1.45.3-windows-x86_64-hip-rdna3.tar.gz`).
Same Windows 11 x64 HIP build on the same Strix Halo / gfx1151 box, same model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S), same flags.

**Result on 0.2.0-beta: the default path still fails.** With `--expert-cache auto` and no `--mmap-experts` the engine prints
`session is up (engine 0.1.45.3)` and then dies with `strata generate: the embedding buffer failed` (exit 1) — identical
signature to 0.1.44.1. With `--mmap-experts --vram-reserve-mib 512` the same 0.1.45.3 engine starts normally and prints
`READY 131072` (`expert_slots=24576`, `51611 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded`).

Full logs of all three runs, the issue-form answers, and an analysis of why this is not genuine VRAM exhaustion are in the
comment below: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2766#issuecomment-6281712768

The 0.1.44.1 report follows, unchanged.

---
# Windows x64 HIP (0.1.44.1) on Strix Halo / gfx1151: default start exits with "the embedding buffer failed" — `--mmap-experts` runs

**TL;DR** — On a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151) under Windows 11, the ready-made
`strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` (0.1.44.1) **starts, loads the model, prints `session is up`, and then dies**
with `strata generate: the embedding buffer failed` (that is a **10 KB** `cudaMalloc` in `generate.cpp:6018`).
The expert cache is sized from **5.41 GiB of "free" VRAM → 1087 of 24576 slots** in that mode.
Adding `--mmap-experts` (plus `--vram-reserve-mib 512`) makes the same install run correctly, and in that
mode the process happily uses **~57.5 GB of dedicated VRAM**. Details, logs and a hypothesis below.

---

## 1. Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | Six United AXB35-02 mini-PC |
| APU | AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S, **gfx1151**, 20 CUs, wave32 |
| Memory | 128 GB LPDDR5X-8532 (8 × 16 GB); **BIOS "UMA Frame Buffer" = 64 GB** → Windows sees **63.6 GB** |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro, build **26200** (25H2) |
| GPU driver | **32.0.31021.5001** (2026-06-28) |
| Radeon software | Adrenalin 26.6.4 |
| Engine | `strata-windows-x64-hip.zip`, v0.1.44.1, sha256 `e40bce7a2cfe47ea42d3f2af1e0adb92d14b8c02a29107c5a309b2cb518f5f52` (matches `SHA256.txt`) |
| `engine/BUILD.json` | `source=prebuilt, backend=hip, platform=windows-x64, version=0.1.44.1, rocm=10.2.0a20260930, hipblaslt_version=100500`, archs incl. `gfx1151`, `vision=none` |
| Python | 3.14.4 (venv created by `START-HERE.bat`) |
| Model | `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`, rev `ed59f920`, **IQ3_S**: shards `54,817,524,224` + `28,800,138,432` B, `mmproj` `907,543,008` B (all sha256-verified) |

`engine\strata-device.exe --list-devices` / `--selftest` (with `engine\rocm\bin` on PATH) are healthy in both modes:

```
device 0: AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics
  HIP arch            gfx1151 wave32 (compiled for gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1200,gfx1201,gfx1030,gfx1151)
  multiprocessors     20
  VRAM total / free   107.647 GiB (115585384448 B) / 107.496 GiB (115422916608 B)
  driver / runtime    71726391 / 71726391
  HIP runtime         E:\Strata-win\engine\amdhip64_7.dll
  memory plan  --max-context 20480 … plan + KV vs free   FITS
selftest: over-allocation refused as required
strata-device selftest OK
```

---

## 2. Install path that works end-to-end

1. **Layout.** The three Windows zips on the release page are **engines only** — `START-HERE.bat`,
   `setup.py`, `serve/`, `tools/` are *not* in them. I took the scripts from the source zip of `main`
   (`codeload.github.com/Niko1221/Strata/zip/refs/heads/main`, 21.6 MB) and unzipped
   `strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` into `engine\` (contents: `strata.exe`, `strata-device.exe`, `rocm\`,
   `amdhip64_7.dll`, `amd_comgr.dll`, `rocm_kpack.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `vcruntime140*.dll`, `BUILD.json`).
   → **Suggestion:** mention on the release page that the HIP zip is the engine and where the scripts come from.
2. `START-HERE.bat` → venv (Python 3.14.4) → `setup.py`.
3. ```
   setup.py --family qwen --model IQ3_S \
     --gguf-dir <folder with the two IQ3_S shards + the mmproj> \
     --context 131072 --vision no --backend hip --yes
   ```
   * engine: `[ok] ready-made AMD engine already installed`
   * model: `[ok] model files present` (no re-download), pack → `Strata-data\packs\iq3_s`
     (`302` canonical tensors served natively, arena 1.43 GiB; experts are read from the GGUF in place,
     so `Strata-data` is only ~7.9 GB on disk)
   * MTP: 31 tensors / 5.214 GB fetched → `mtp-q2_0.gguf` (0.889 GB) → runtime dir
   * start script written with `--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp … --max-context 131072 --kv int8`

> Note (not a bug, but it costs an hour): the venv `pip install` needs a reachable index. With the
> Tsinghua mirror one pinned wheel 403'd (`numpy==2.5.3` `cp314-win_amd64`); Tencent/aliyun/USTC/pypi.org
> all served it. Setup's `--quiet` makes that step look frozen.

---

## 3. Bug: default (resident expert arena) start dies

Command (exactly what setup generated, no extra flags):

```
engine\strata.exe --serve --pack E:\Strata-data\packs\iq3_s \
  --native …-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf …-00002-of-00002.gguf \
  --expert-profile E:\Strata-win\data\expert-profile.bin \
  --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 \
  --mtp E:\Strata-data\mtp\rt --max-context 131072 --kv int8
```

Engine log (verbatim, one line per entry):

```
strata: gfx1151 (Strix Halo): 18 exact speed switches on by default (…): GDN_HEAD GDN_PP GDN_CONVL2 GDN_NOY
        CVEC_FUSE HCD_EXACT PF_PAD Q8_PACKED Q6_PACKED MMVF_ROWS ATTN_LANECELL EXPERT_V2 TSUM LFUSE GDN_SPLIT QFUSE PLE_BATCH SH_STREAM
strata generate: memory guard: limit 63.6 GiB (source: meminfo), current 16.1 GiB, reclaimable cache credited 0.0 GiB;
        available 47.5 GiB (MemAvailable 47.5 GiB), floor 2560 MiB
strata generate: native pack: … experts (largest blob 2.66 MB), token embedding IQ4_XS in mapped host memory (322 MiB, 0.3 s)
strata generate: 300 native projection matrices, 2018.88 MiB of weights, in 2.7 s
strata generate: PLE on, table 320001536 rows of …-00002-of-00002.gguf
strata mtp: draft layer loaded, 950 MiB of VRAM (experts 675, dense 111), files read in 0.21 s
strata: STRATA_Q6_PACKED=1 packed the output head (248320 x 2560, +497.3 MiB)
strata generate: GPU 0: AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics (gfx1151)
strata generate: HIP runtime E:\Strata-win\engine\amdhip64_7.dll
strata generate: expert arena read unbuffered (0 of 16 probe reads from the file cache; 0.6 GiB available, 51.1 GiB of files)
strata generate: expert arena: cudaHostRegister PORTABLE ok; large pages refused for 50295996416 B
        (GetLargePageMinimum=2097152, VirtualAlloc error 1314); using 4 KB pages
strata generate: loaded 46.84 GiB at 2.03 GiB/s
strata generate: expert cache auto: Windows keeps 2560 MiB free after the cache on a card this size …
strata generate: expert cache auto: 5.41 GiB free, 2560 MiB reserved (+218 MiB for the draft head) -> 1087 slots
strata generate: pre-filled 0 of 0 slots from the profile in 0.0 s (0 MB/s); slot 0 verified
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.44.1)
strata generate: the embedding buffer failed          ← exit code 1
```

`the embedding buffer failed` is the **10 KB** allocation at `src/program/generate.cpp:6017-6021`:

```cpp
float* d_emb = nullptr;
if (cudaMalloc(&d_emb, (size_t) g.n_embd * 4) != cudaSuccess) {   // g.n_embd = 2560 → 10 KB
    std::fprintf(stderr, "strata generate: the embedding buffer failed\n");
    return 1;
}
```

### Reproduced twice, and it is **not** a system-RAM shortage

| run | `memory guard` reading | expert-cache line | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | `current 16.1 GiB`, `available 47.5 GiB` | `5.41 GiB free, 2560 MiB reserved -> 1087 slots` | `the embedding buffer failed` |
| #2 | `current 11.3 GiB`, `available 52.4 GiB` | `5.41 GiB free, 2560 MiB reserved -> 1087 slots` — **identical** | `the embedding buffer failed` |

Freeing 4.8 GB of system RAM (closing background apps) changed the guard reading but produced the
**same 5.41 GiB / 1087 slots** and the same failure, so the number the cache is sized from is not
"free system RAM" on Windows.

---

## 4. Workaround that works

```
--mmap-experts --vram-reserve-mib 512
```

```
[strata] mapping the experts from the model files (about 55 GB, --mmap-experts): they are not loaded into RAM …
[strata] filling the GPU's expert cache (24576 experts, 46.84 GiB of VRAM) …
ready: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1  (OpenAI: /v1/chat/completions, Anthropic: /v1/messages, context 131072 tokens)
```

In this mode Windows Task Manager reports **57,521 MB dedicated** + ~1.7 GB shared for the process,
and `strata verify: capturing the … window (51573 MiB of VRAM free)`.
So the card is not out of memory — the failure above is specific to the **resident-arena** path.

---

## 5. Hypothesis (please sanity-check — I have not built the engine)

* `src/core/expert_cache.cpp:28 device_free_bytes()` returns `cudaMemGetInfo(&free,&total)` and adds a UMA
  correction **only under `#if defined(__linux__)`**: `/proc/meminfo` `MemAvailable` minus
  `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB` (default 6). On Windows that correction is compiled out, so the expert-cache
  sizing uses HIP's free number as-is.
* `src/platform/memory.cpp:112 gpu_shared_memory_budget()` (DXGI
  `QueryVideoMemoryInfo(0, DXGI_MEMORY_SEGMENT_GROUP_NON_LOCAL)`) exists, but a repo-wide search finds its
  **only caller in the SYCL backend** (`sycl/src/core/pinned.dp.cpp:328`) — the Windows HIP path does not
  use it.
* On WDDM, host memory the GPU can reach is charged to the process's **non-local (shared)** budget, while
  the 64 GB BIOS carve-out is a separate **dedicated** segment. The resident arena is registered with
  `cudaHostRegister(…, PORTABLE)` (46.84 GiB). If HIP's `cudaMemGetInfo` free on a UMA adapter tracks that
  shared budget, then after registration the reported "free" collapses to ~5.4 GiB although the dedicated
  segment is nearly empty — which would explain both `1087 slots` and the later 10 KB allocation failure.
* Possible directions (yours to judge): exclude the registered arena from the sizing reading on
  Windows/UMA; use the DXGI non-local budget (or a `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB`-equivalent) there; or
  allocate the arena from the dedicated segment; or make the automatic choice fall back to
  `--mmap-experts` on Windows when it would otherwise fail.

---

## 6. Speed, same machine, same model — and the Linux comparison

Windows (this install, `--mmap-experts --vram-reserve-mib 512`, IQ3_S, context 131072, KV int8),
from the engine's own `strata serve: prompt …` lines:

| prompt tok | prefill | generated | decode | MTP drafts accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 53 | 660 ms (80.3 tok/s) | 40 | 36.5 tok/s | 22 / 34 |
| 57 | 780 ms (73.1) | **1898** | **40.7 tok/s** | 1050 / 1531 |
| 58 | 705 ms (82.3) | 97 | 34.0 | 45 / 83 |
| 82 | 993 ms (82.6) | 600 | 38.0 | 312 / 515 |
| 588 | 1758 ms (334.5) | 748 | 30.7 | 269 / 551 |
| 2221 | 3772 ms (588.8) | 24 | 38.1 | 15 / 24 |
| **7261** | **11032 ms (658.2)** | 16 | 46.6 (too short to be meaningful) | 11 / 12 |

`strata serve: expert tiers: GPU 0 hits this request; since the start RAM 0 blobs, files 0 blobs 50294.7 MB read
(the GGUF in place)` — the byte counter only crept up (50,294.7 → 50,604.7 MB over several requests), i.e. the
cache looks like it is hitting, not thrashing.

Linux reference on the **same box and model** (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0, engine built locally for gfx1151,
default placement, same context): decode **47.2 / 47.4 / 47.5 / 48.9 / 55.2 tok/s**
(`done: 736 tokens in 17 s (48.9 tok/s)` … `done: 33 tokens in 1 s (55.2 tok/s)`).
`docs/STRIX_HALO.md` lists IQ3_S at 8K: **1,242 prompt / 59.7 decode**.

So on Windows I measure roughly **53 % of the documented prefill** (658 vs 1,242 tok/s) and
**~30–41 tok/s decode vs 47–60 on Linux/docs**. Question:

issues.title: [Bug]: 0.1.44.1 / HIP 2×7900 XTX — 186k-token conversation: cold read OK, every re-read dies in the pipelined verify window (exit −6, then #879); 11/11 clean without the tuning flags
issues.author: dinesh-chander
issues.body:
### What happened

A **long-context conversation cannot be served on 2× AMD RX 7900 XTX (HIP)**: the cold read of a ~185.6k-token document succeeds, and then *every* request that carries that context dies.

The run below is the 13-request conversation an agent actually produces at that context — cold read → 5 continuations → a compaction request → the post-compaction turn → an over-context probe → an "is it alive" probe → 2 concurrent re-reads — against the config I run daily (full args below):

| # | step | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | calibration (1,560 tok) | 200 |
| 1 | **cold read, 185,601 tok** | **200** — but only on the *second* document: the first one ended in #879 after 261 s (the harness re-sends the same size with different words). ttft 136.0 s, prefill 1,364.7 tok/s, 128 gen @ 62.8 tok/s |
| 2 | continuation 1/5 | **200** — prompt-cache hit, 1.4 s |
| 3 | continuation 2/5 | **503** — 67.7 s, `the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6)` |
| 4 | continuation 3/5 | **503** — 583.6 s, `#879 non-finite` |
| 5 | continuation 4/5 | **503** — 430.3 s, `#879` |
| 6 | continuation 5/5 | **503** — 485.0 s, `#879`, engine restarted |
| 7 | compaction request | **503** — 336.4 s, `#879` |
| 8 | post-compaction turn | **200** — 224.8 s (after a reload) |
| 9 | over-context probe | **400** — correct |
| 10 | alive probe | **200** |
| 11 | concurrent re-read 1/2 | **503** — 253.9 s, `#879` |
| 12 | concurrent re-read 2/2 | **503** — 582.4 s, `the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6)` |

**5 of 13 requests OK, 5 engine restarts.** It reproduces on every config variant I tried: `--prefill auto:16384` (5/13, ttft 99.6 s), `--prefill auto` (above), and `--adapt-every 0` (5/13, 3 restarts) — always the same shape: **the cold read is served, the first re-read that carries the 185.6k context kills the engine, everything after that is #879.** The two client-visible errors:

```
503 {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6); the next request restarts it"}}
503 {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"the model's output became non-finite (NaN) twice in a row (#879); the engine has dropped its cached state - send the request again"}}
```

### The stall the engine reports before the kill

The kill is the engine's own 60 s no-progress watchdog, and its stall report names the stage ("issue #29" in the message): the **pipelined verify window**, at the very tail of the 185,756-token re-read.

```
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (verify window (pipelined): the CPU experts of layer 22) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.44.1): stage "verify window (pipelined): the CPU experts of layer 22" for 60 s; 0 layers served since the last finished step (0 = stopped, more = slow)
  VRAM free when this request began: 2806 MiB
  expert pool: epoch 4644, batch epoch 4644: 42 of 42 jobs claimed, 42 done; 13 of 13 workers parked, 13 sleeping; mode 0
  expert pool threads: w0=sleeping w1=sleeping w2=sleeping w3=sleeping w4=sleeping w5=sleeping w6=sleeping w7=sleeping w8=sleeping w9=sleeping w10=sleeping w11=sleeping w12=sleeping; host idle for 60819 ms
  verify window: 6 tokens at position 185615, host at layer step 23; the GPU rang 24; flags: served 23, plan (A) 23, copies (B) 23
  threads waiting on the disk (state D): 0 of 43
  memory: 81016 MiB resident, 0 MiB in swap, 4402 MiB RAM available; 0 major page faults so far
  2 s later:
  (the same lines, host idle for 62819 ms)
strata: released the verify window's GPU waits (#267): the GPU finished in 0 ms
strata: released the verify window's GPU waits (#267): the GPU did not finish within 5 s
```

Note what the stall report itself says: the **expert pool is idle** (42/42 jobs done, all 13 workers parked, host idle for 60 s) and **no thread is waiting on disk** (0 of 43 in state D). The verify window sits at position 185,615 of 185,756 — the last window of the prompt — with the GPU on ring 24 while the host has served 23. This is a GPU-synchronisation hang in the *pipelined* verify window, not expert or I/O starvation.

The #879 NaNs then arrive **after** the first kill, on requests that re-read the same context from token 0 after the reload:

```
strata serve: non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window at position 185591 (row 0): its tokens are not emitted, the request ends (DONE nonfinite) and the next request reads its prompt from token 0
strata serve: prompt 185756 tokens = 0 reused + 185591 of 185756 read in 125969 ms (1473.3 tok/s), 0 generated in 0 ms (0.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 0 of 0, 6 checkpoints (cancelled)
strata serve: after non-finite logits (#879): dropped the live session, 6 checkpoints, 0 parked conversations and 0 idle slots; reading this prompt from token 0
```

So in this workload the NaN looks like it follows the crash/reload rather than being independent of it — the *first* failure in every run is the watchdog kill.

### Control: the same conversation is clean when the optional flags are dropped

Same box, same model, same 186k context, same 13-request shape. The only difference is the set of *optional* engine flags: I removed `--short-read 260 --pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 13 --adapt-every --adapt-async --adapt-swaps --adapt-decay --conversation-cache-mib --pipeline-windows --layer-split` and all `STRATA_*` env vars, keeping only what the engine needs to load a native (IQ) pack and fit the model (`--pack --native --expert-profile --expert-cache --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp --max-context 200000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 3072` — the engine refuses to start without `--spec/--prefill` for this pack, so a literally flag-free run does not exist here).

| | shipping args | engine-required args only |
|---|---|---|
| requests served (200/400) | 5 of 13 | **11 of 11** |
| engine restarts | 5 | **0** |
| first re-read after the cold read | 503, 67.7 s | **200, 2.9 s** |
| cold read | 200, 185,601 tok, ttft 136.0 s, 1,364.7 tok/s | 200, 186,071 tok, ttft 186.2 s, 999.5 tok/s |
| continuations | 503 ×4 (#879) | 200 ×5, 2.9–4.6 s each |
| compaction request | 503, #879 | **200**, 6.3 s |
| post-compaction | 200 (after a reload) | 200, 4.3 s |
| decode | 62.8 tok/s | 43.1 tok/s |

Every request in that run returned 200 except the intentional over-context probe (400). **So it is not "2 AMD cards cannot do long context"** — the same conversation, on the same two cards, completes with the pipeline and the optional knobs out of the picture. (It is slower: 1,000 vs 1,365 tok/s prefill without the pipeline.)

For completeness, a cross-backend control: the identical 13-request conversation on the same model (NVFP4, single NVIDIA GPU, same box) is **13/13, zero restarts** (cold read 185,598 tok, ttft 82.2 s, 2,257.5 tok/s).

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Strata | **0.1.44.1** (git `296b59d2`, tag `v0.1.44.1`) — HIP source build |
| Engine | `serve/server.py` from the repo, engine `strata --serve` |
| GPUs | 2× AMD RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, gfx1100), 24 GB each, `--layer-split 24` (also tried `auto`, same failure) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, **UD-Q4_K_XL native pack** (`unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl`), `--spec 4 --mtp`, vision on CPU |
| CPU / RAM | Intel Core Ultra 7 265K / 96 GB DDR5 |
| OS | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel `7.0.0-38-generic` |
| HIP | `7.16.26385-0000000` |

Engine args (shipping config):

```
--pack <data>/packs/unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl
--native <cache>/qwen38-flash-next-gguf/UD-Q4_K_XL/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf
--expert-profile <data>/expert-profile.bin
--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --short-read 260 --spec 4 --mtp <data>/mtp/rt
--max-context 200000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 3072
--pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 13
--adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97 --conversation-cache-mib 8192
--pipeline-windows 2 --layer-split 24
```

env: `STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1`, `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0=1` (so this is not #2637, which is why `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0` is set), `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1`, `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=<…>gfx1100-hipblaslt-100401.txt`.

### How to reproduce

Two requests. Any prose document of ~185.6k tokens (my filler is ~1.09 tokens/word) reproduces it; the second request is the one that dies, and a single first request never fails.

```python
import requests

doc = open("185k-document.txt").read()          # ~185.6k tokens
ask = "Continue from the last point and add one short paragraph."
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1/chat/completions"
def ask_model(messages, n=128):
    return requests.post(url, timeout=3600, json={
        "model": "local", "messages": messages, "max_tokens": n,
        "temperature": 0, "stream": False, "reasoning_effort": "none"})

r1 = ask_model([{"role": "user", "content": doc}])
print(r1.status_code, r1.json()["timings"])      # 200, prompt 185,598, ~130-190 s

r2 = ask_model([{"role": "user", "content": doc},
                {"role": "assistant", "content": r1.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]},
                {"role": "user", "content": ask}])
print(r2.status_code, r2.text)                   # 503 "the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6)"
```

After the 503 the engine is reloaded (~2–4 min on this box) and the next request that re-reads the prompt returns the #879 NaN instead. The full harness (13 requests, including the compaction turn) is `loadtest180k.py`; the JSON artifacts and the full engine log for every run above are available if you want them attached.

### Things I checked so I would not send you a red herring

* `--prefill auto:16384` → same failure (5/13). `--prefill auto` → same.
* `--adapt-every 0` (adaptive tier off) → same failure (5/13, 3 restarts). The tier is not it.
* `STRATA_PF_GEMM` on and off → same.
* `--layer-split auto` and `--layer-split 24` → both fail at long context (`auto` also produced #879 at position 39,613 on a 32k prompt).
* `--vram-reserve-mib 2048` → `3072`: no change for this failure (the known #267 mitigation is already in place).
* Client-side timeouts are not involved: the client waits 3600 s; the 503 bodies above are produced by the server.
* 8k / 32k paged conversations on the same config: every request returned 200 in this whole campaign — the failure is specific to *re-reading a long context*, not to the 2-GPU arrangement as such.

### What I think is happening (and what I am testing next)

The dying stage is literally named `verify window (pipelined)`, i.e. a stage that only exists while the prefill pipeline is on — so **`--pipeline-windows 2` is my first suspect**, possibly together with the VRAM budget at that context (`--kv-resident 32768` + `--conversation-cache-mib 8192` + `--vram-reserve-mib 3072` left 2,806 MiB free when the failing request began). This is a different stage from the decode-side pipeline stall fixed in v0.1.42 by #1741 (that one was the device switch in the decode poll loop; this one is the verify window at the tail of a long prompt), and it is on Linux/HIP, not Windows/CUDA.

I am running the single-variable version now — the shipping config with **only** `--pipeline-windows` changed to `0` — and will post the result as a comment. If it passes, that is the fix for my config; if it fails, I will bisect the remaining knobs and report which one it is.

### Related

* #267 — the verify-window watchdog this fires (already mitigated here with `--vram-reserve-mib 3072`, which is not enough at 185k with the pipeline on)
* #2449 — the same watchdog on long-context decode
* #2452 — #879 non-finite logits at a fixed prompt position
* #879 — the non-finite logits tracker
* #1740 / #1741 — the pipelined **decode** stall on Windows, fixed in v0.1.42 (different stage)
* #2637 — `--pipeline-windows 2` needing `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0=1` on gfx1100 (set here)

issues.title: [Feature]: Add opt-in Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B support
issues.author: BColsey
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Run **Meta Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B** through Strata's local inference engine, with expert offloading rather than requiring the whole checkpoint in GPU memory.

Model: https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B
Available GGUF conversions: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF

Spark Open has 816B total / 42B active parameters, gated grouped-query attention, and 256 routed experts with top-8 routing. It requires a model-specific execution graph; accepting its model name or repacking tensors alone would not provide inference support.

### Initial scope

- Opt-in **text inference** for Muse Spark Open, without changing Strata's defaults or existing model behavior.
- Validate model metadata, tensor shapes, quantization support and memory requirements before allocating or downloading large files.
- Reuse Strata's expert offloading where compatible, with explicit errors for unsupported features or formats.
- Correct tokenizer/chat-template handling and API generation, with regression coverage.
- Deterministic small-shape reference/parity tests, followed by CUDA validation and clearly separated full-checkpoint evidence.

Vision/audio, performance claims and automatic installation as a recommended model are not part of the initial text-only implementation.

### Hardware available for testing

Linux x86-64, Ryzen 9 3900X, 64 GB installed system RAM (about 60 GiB usable), RTX 3080 10 GiB + RTX 2080 Ti 11 GiB + RTX 3060 12 GiB. These cards have separate allocations, not a single 33 GiB device.

The smallest currently published Unsloth GGUF is approximately 176 GB, so full-checkpoint execution on this hardware would require storage-backed offloading; it is **not yet demonstrated to fit or run at usable speed**. Small CUDA tests are not evidence of successful 816B inference.

I am investigating an implementation and will link a PR with the exact validation performed and any outstanding limitations. AI-assisted development and independent review will be disclosed in that PR.

issues.title: Second server start should fail fast: PID lock before model loading
issues.author: ver9118-droid
issues.body:
## Problem

Starting a second Strata server on the same port does not fail fast. `main()` checks the port (`Server((host, port), ...)` probe) and binds only **after** the model is loaded, so two simultaneous starts (e.g. Windows autostart + `START-HERE.bat` + an agent script at boot) both pass the probe, each maps ~39 GB of experts, and they fight over RAM for minutes on a 32 GB PC before the loser finally fails at bind.

On Windows `allow_reuse_address` is already `False`, so the bind itself is safe — the hole is the check-then-bind race combined with minutes of loading in between.

## Proposed fix

Take a PID lock file (next to the model config, `.strata-<port>.lock`) right after arg/config resolution, before tokenizer/engine loading. Second start exits in <1s with the owner's PID. Stale locks (hard kill, no atexit) are detected via PID-liveness check and taken over.

Tested locally on Windows 11 + RX 9070 XT, engine 0.1.44.1:

- duplicate start: `server.py: error: another Strata server is already starting/serving port 8081 (PID 7204)` in **0.2 s**, no model touched
- hard-killed owner leaves a stale lock; next start detects the dead PID, takes over, and serves normally

## Patch (against 0.1.44.1 `serve/server.py`)

Add after `listen_problem` (~line 107):

```python
def _pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
    try:
        import ctypes
        h = ctypes.windll.kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, False, pid)
        if not h:
            return False
        ctypes.windll.kernel32.CloseHandle(h)
        return True
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - unknown platform: assume taken (safe side)
        return True


def take_server_lock(ap, a) -> None:
    """One server per port: a PID lock taken before the minutes of model loading,
    so a second start (autostart + START-HERE + agent at boot) exits in <1s instead
    of mapping ~39 GB for minutes and then failing at bind."""
    import atexit
    try:
        base = Path(a.config).parent if a.config else Path(tempfile.gettempdir())
    except (OSError, TypeError):
        base = Path(tempfile.gettempdir())
    lock = base / f".strata-{a.port}.lock"
    try:
        fd = os.open(lock, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
    except FileExistsError:
        pid = 0
        try:
            pid = int(lock.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip().split()[0])
        except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError):
            pid = 0
        if pid > 0 and _pid_alive(pid):
            ap.error(f"another Strata server is already starting/serving port {a.port} (PID {pid}): "
                     f"use it instead of starting a second one")
        try:
            lock.unlink()
        except OSError:
            pass
        try:
            fd = os.open(lock, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
        except FileExistsError:
            ap.error(f"port {a.port} is already in use - is Strata (or another server) already running?")
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"[strata] WARNING: cannot take the start lock ({e}): continuing without duplicate protection",
                  flush=True)
            return
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"[strata] WARNING: cannot take the start lock ({e}): continuing without duplicate protection",
              flush=True)
        return
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
        f.write(str(os.getpid()))

    def _release(path=lock):
        try:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        except OSError:
            pass
    atexit.register(_release)
```

And call it in `main()` right after the `a.host = ...` line:

```python
    take_server_lock(ap, a)                       # one server per port: fail fast before loading
```

Environment: Windows 11, RX 9070 XT 16 GB, 32 GB RAM, IQ2_XS + Coder IQ1_M configs, port 8080.

issues.title: [Bug]: NVFP4 2-GPU layer split + STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1: deterministic non-finite logits (#879) on 1024..3276-token single-chunk prompts (PeerPrefill omits tail_off scales)
issues.author: sankerXD
issues.body:
### What happened

When running an NVFP4 pack (`Maximilian228--Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-GPTQ-Strata`) with a 2-GPU layer split (`--layer-split 23`), `--prefill auto` (chunk 8192), and `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1`, every single-chunk prompt segment whose uncached length `T` falls in `1024 <= T <= 3276` deterministically fails with `non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window`.

When `#879` fires:
1. The engine drops the live session and all KV checkpoints (`after non-finite logits (#879): dropped the live session, 6 checkpoints ... reading this prompt from token 0`).
2. `server.py` automatically retries the request from token 0.
3. On the retry from token 0, the full prompt (`13K` to `86K` tokens) spans multiple 8192-token chunks (`single_chunk == false`), so `bind_stage_helper` does not activate and the retry succeeds after re-reading the entire 13K–86K prompt from scratch.

In a single multi-turn coding/agent session (growing from 11K to 86K tokens), this triggered **9 times** (at prompt deltas of `1189`, `1292`, `1292`, `1297`, `1738`, `1288`, `1289`, `1289`, `1296` tokens — every single one in `[1024, 3276]`), wiping the KV cache each time. Setting `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=0` completely resolves the issue.

#### Root cause in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`

1. **Activation condition (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1571-1579, 1624-1633, 2125-2126`)**:
   - `Prefill::bind_stage_helper(int64_t T)` activates only when `single_chunk` (`n <= m.T`), `T >= stream_all_min()` (`1024`), and `split_help_frac(T) >= 0.3` (`T <= 3276`).
   - `bind_stage_helper` checks `mmq_plan()` and `fused::native_supported()`, but does **not** check `lay.fmt[l].tail_off != 0`.
2. **Missing NVFP4 `tail_off` global scales in `PeerPrefill` (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:3626-3657` and `3707-3732`)**:
   - On NVFP4 packs, each expert blob carries a 16-byte tail `{s_gate, s_up, s_down, 0}` (`f.tail_off != 0`, each scale `~1e-4`).
   - The primary card's MMQ path (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:3888-3930`) gathers `f.tail_off` into `m.grp_tail`, runs `mmq::swiglu_scaled` (applying `s_gate` and `s_up`), and writes `s_down` into `m.row_sd` via `mmq::down_row_scales` before `moe_combine` (`line 4055-4056`) multiplies all `T * K` rows by `m.row_sd`.
   - However, `PeerPrefill` (`P.compact` at lines `3626-3657` for `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1`, and `!P.compact` at lines `3707-3732` for `--peer-device`) calls `mmq::gather_native` **without** `f.tail_off` / `grp_tail`, runs unscaled `mmq::swiglu` instead of `mmq::swiglu_scaled` (leaving hidden activations `~1e8x` too large), and **never writes `m.row_sd[rows_local .. rows_local + rows_peer)`** (leaving those entries uninitialized/stale when `moe_combine` reads `m.row_sd` across all `T * K` rows).

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1 · RTX 4070 Ti 12GB (CUDA0) + RTX 2080 Ti 22GB (CUDA1) · Debian 13 Linux 6.12.111 (Driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.1)

issues.title: iq_embed_rows: missing the >65535-row guard - fixed --prefill 65536 fails deterministically at a 64K chunk (invalid argument)
issues.author: daifeiya
issues.body:
Environment: Windows 11, RTX 4090 48GB (non-D), driver 617.42, engine/project 0.1.44.1 (source tree), NVFP4 pack (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-GPTQ-Strata).

Symptom: with a FIXED `--prefill 65536`, every launch fails when the 131072-token tier is requested: the engine's last log line is `iq_embed_rows: invalid argument`, the request returns HTTP 503, and the engine stops serving (the Python server stays up). Reproduced 3/3 launches (deterministic). The same config completes every tier up to 65536 (actual 65527 tokens).

Log excerpt (run 1 of 3, tune/logs/r4-1.log; identical shape in runs 2 and 3 at lines 86 and 85):

    strata serve: prompt 65527 tokens = 0 reused + 65527 read in 12706 ms (5157.2 tok/s), 223 generated in 1651 ms (135.1 tok/s), drafts accepted 131 of 206, 1 checkpoints
    strata serve: decode expert cache hit rate: 99.3% (143966 hits / 144957 lookups); 3 more read by the GPU over PCIe or from another GPU (0.0% of all 144960 routed)
    strata serve: KV streaming: 95.89% of 1885524 block reads hit VRAM, 312.4 MiB read from RAM
    strata serve: suffix drafts: 5 windows, 19 of 21 drafts accepted
    iq_embed_rows: invalid argument

The failing request (the next tier, 131072 tokens) produced no `prompt ... read` line at all - the failure is at prompt ingestion, before any chunk progressed.

Analysis: `iq_embed_rows` launches one row per prompt token. Three sibling kernels guard the same CUDA grid-y limit of 65535 (src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu:1168 `grid.y > 65535`; native_rope.cu:191,223 rows > 65535; sampler.cu:1196 tokens > 65535), but the iq_embed_rows path has no guard or row tiling - a 65536-row launch exceeds grid.y (max 65535). Consistent with this: a FIXED chunk of 61440 (below the limit) completes a full 9-tier x 3-run ladder on the same machine/config with zero occurrences of the error (prompt-path borrow 23.70 GiB vs 9988 slots at 65536, proportional).

Suggestion: add the guard + row tiling (or clamp) to the embedding upload path, like the sibling kernels.

Secondary: `--prefill auto:NN` silently clamps to 32768 for NN >= 32768 (src/program/generate.cpp:2041-2049); I first tried `auto:65536` expecting a larger chunk and got 32768 with no notice. Documenting (or reporting) the ceiling would help.

Happy to paste the full three run logs if useful.

issues.title: NVFP4 prompt modes on a 96 GB Blackwell card (every expert in VRAM): w4a4 reads fresh prompts 9-13% faster than w4a8
issues.author: alphastorm
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`, release engine `strata-windows-x64.zip`, its CUDA 13.0 build) · RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition 96 GB (sm_120, PCIe 5.0 x16), driver 616.92 · Windows 11 (26200) · i9-14900K, 192 GB DDR5-5200

[docs/NVFP4.md](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78/docs/NVFP4.md) keeps `w4a8` the default "until a 96 GB+ RTX 50 PC measures the others". On this card the engine logs `every expert is in the GPU cache (24576 of 24576)` (63.29 GiB), so no prompt waits for RAM or the SSD.

**Setup.** `--family nvfp4 --model NVFP4` (the GPTQ pack, `Maximilian228/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-GPTQ-Strata` @ `640a1db9`, every file at setup's pinned SHA-256) with setup's plan for this card: `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --expert-cache auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --pool-workers 15`, `--parallel 4`, and the two settings setup recommends, `--prefill auto:32768 --conversation-cache-mib 8192`; text only. The `w4a4` arm is the same config with `"env": {"STRATA_PREFILL_NVFP4": "w4a4"}` (its log has no W4A8 fallback note). Reference: IQ3_S (ISTA GSQ-RCO) with the same settings. Each arm started cold on an idle GPU, then `python tools/strata_bench.py --long --clients 4` ran against it: 3 runs per test, medians with ranges, engine timings.

| | IQ3_S | NVFP4, `w4a8` (default) | NVFP4, `w4a4` | w4a4 vs w4a8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4K prompt tok/s | 5,272 (5,175-5,281) | 4,957 (3,804-4,965) | 5,603 (4,218-5,698) | +13.0% |
| 16K prompt tok/s | 7,345 (7,259-7,365) | 7,010 (5,951-7,024) | 7,683 (6,480-7,735) | +9.6% |
| 32K prompt tok/s | 7,622 (7,620-7,821) | 7,289 (7,287-7,303) | 7,974 (7,828-7,983) | +9.4% |
| agent follow-up turn, first token (s) | 0.72 | 0.76 | 0.64 | -15.5% |
| short chat decode tok/s | 219.4 | 207.6 | 196.5 | -5.3% |
| agent turns decode tok/s | 220.4 | 204.8 | 212.4 | +3.7% |
| 4 clients, total tok/s | 167.6 | 157.9 | 155.8 | -1.3% |

The two decode rows move in opposite directions between the NVFP4 arms, which differ only in the prompt path, so I read them as run-to-run spread (MTP acceptance varies with the answer).

Longer prompts, from an earlier window on 2026-10-14 (the same three arms, each from a cold start, one request per depth through our own client, prompt tok/s as the server reports it):

| prompt tokens | 6.6K | 26K | 52K | 89K | 130K | 179K | 244K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `w4a8` | 3,752 | 6,921 | 7,622 | 7,758 | 7,695 | 7,541 | 7,349 |
| `w4a4` | 4,072 | 7,492 | 8,308 | 8,487 | 8,404 | 8,239 | 8,008 |
| w4a4 vs w4a8 | +8.5% | +8.3% | +9.0% | +9.4% | +9.2% | +9.3% | +9.0% |

**A first-request cost on both NVFP4 arms.** The first fresh 4K prompt and the first fresh 16K prompt read 15-25% slower than the next two of the same size (`w4a8`: 3,804 then 4,957 / 4,965 at 4K, 5,951 then 7,024 / 7,010 at 16K; `w4a4`: 4,218 then 5,698 / 5,603, and 6,480 then 7,683 / 7,735). IQ3_S's first runs were within 2% of its later ones, and the 32K test, which runs after both, had no slow first run on any arm.

**Not covered.** `docs/NVFP4.md` also describes `w4a4x2` and `STRATA_PREFILL_X2_MIN_K`, but this engine accepts only `w4a8`, `w4a4` or `fp16` ([moe_mmq.cu#L188-L196](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78/src/prefill/moe_mmq.cu#L188-L196); `main` is at the same commit), so neither ran. Nothing here measures `w4a4`'s answers (the doc's KL figures stand); `fp16` and NVIDIA's own pack were not run; Windows only.

issues.title: 2x2080Ti 44G  64G RAM UD-IQ4 512K 配置 KV 复用
issues.author: lingopen
issues.body:
# Strata 配置留档（2026-10-16，主机 192.168.1.6:/home/sunny/Strata）

> 升级 Strata 后需要恢复的三样东西：
> 1. 配置 JSON 里的两个缓存参数（下文已标注）
> 2. 启动脚本的调优环境变量（脚本一般不会被升级覆盖，确认即可）
> 3. **serve/frontend.py 的键序规范化补丁（升级会覆盖此文件，必须重打！）**

---

## 一、引擎配置 strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.json

{

  "--conversation-cache-mib", "20480",

  "--conversation-cache-min-free-mib", "2048",
  "--conversation-cache-min-tokens", "8192",
  "--aux-cpus", "auto",
  "--resident-experts"
 ],
 "cwd": "/home/sunny/Strata",
 "tokenizer": "/home/sunny/Strata-data/packs/unsloth-ud-iq4_xs/tokenizer",
 "model_name": "qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs",
 "log": "/home/sunny/Strata/strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.log",

}
```

### KV 复用相关的关键参数（升级后重点核对）

| 参数 | 值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `--conversation-cache-min-free-mib` | **2048**（默认 4096 太保守） | parking 内存准入底线，保证 ~3.7GB 的对话快照能 park 进 RAM |
| `--conversation-cache-min-tokens` | **8192**（旧版无此参数，默认 0） | 小于 8192 token 的请求不占缓存槽，防止小请求驱逐大对话 |
| `--conversation-cache-mib` | 20480 | 缓存总预算 |
| `--conversation-cache-slots` | 8 | 最多同时 park 8 个对话 |
| `--kv-resident` | 32768 | 常驻 KV 窗口 |

---

## 二、启动脚本 run-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.sh

```sh
#!/bin/sh
cd "/home/sunny/Strata"
# Turing/NVLink 调优开关（#1349/#2239 实测）
export STRATA_SPLIT_OWN=0
export STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1
export STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1
export STRATA_BF16_TC=1
export STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1
export STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1
export STRATA_SPLIT_RING=384
exec "/home/sunny/Strata/.venv/bin/python" "/home/sunny/Strata/serve/server.py" "--engine" "strata" "--config" "/home/sunny/Strata/strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.json" "--port" "8000"
```

启动方式：`cd /home/sunny/Strata && setsid nohup ./run-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.sh > /tmp/strata-run.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &`

---

## 三、serve/frontend.py 补丁（升级必重打！）

升级会覆盖 `serve/frontend.py`，KV 复用的根因修复在里面。重打方法：

在 `/home/sunny/Strata` 下执行：

```sh
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p = '/home/sunny/Strata/serve/frontend.py'
src = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()

helper = '''def _canonical_tools(obj):
    """Rebuild dicts with sorted keys, recursively.  Clients (Trae, Codex) reshuffle tool JSON property
    order between requests of one conversation while the content stays the same; the rendered prompt must
    not follow it, or the engine's conversation cache loses its whole prefix.  Lists keep their order:
    only object key order is unstable."""
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: _canonical_tools(v) for k, v in sorted(obj.items())}
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return [_canonical_tools(v) for v in obj]
    return obj


'''
if 'def _canonical_tools' in src:
    print('already patched')
else:
    assert src.count('class ChatTemplate:') == 1
    src = src.replace('class ChatTemplate:', helper + 'class ChatTemplate:', 1)
    sig = '               **kwargs) -> str:\n'
    assert src.count(sig) == 1, 'render signature not found'
    src = src.replace(
        sig,
        sig + '        if tools is not None:                            # render client key-order shuffles stably\n'
              '            tools = _canonical_tools(tools)\n',
        1,
    )
    open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(src)
    print('patched OK')
PYEOF
python3 -m py_compile serve/frontend.py && echo COMPILE_OK
```

补丁位置参考（2026-10-16 版本 frontend.py）：
- 第 40-50 行：`_canonical_tools()` 模块级函数（在 `class ChatTemplate` 之前）
- 第 71-73 行：`ChatTemplate.render()` 开头，`**kwargs) -> str:` 之后加两行，对 `tools` 做规范化

### 验证补丁生效

```sh
# 重启后跑一轮对话，看日志：
grep -E 'prompt [0-9]+ tokens = ' strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.log | tail -1
# 期望: prompt N tokens = (N - 几百) reused ...  即 reused 接近 prompt 大小
```

- `serve/frontend.py.bak-20261016`（补丁前原始版）
- `strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.json.bak-20261016-opt`（改配置前原始版）

issues.title: [Engine] a reply that ends inside its thinking still returns an empty answer on 0.2.0-beta (the #1814 shape)
issues.author: 47Hunter47
issues.body:
Problem: a reply that ends inside its thinking with no answer comes back empty and nothing says why. The turn ends on the turn-end token just as the model is about to write its closing thinking tag, so `finish_reason` is `stop`, `content` is empty, and the reasoning stops mid-sentence.

Environment: Strata `v0.2.0-beta` (`3d1fb480`), a stock checkout of the tag - its own `serve/`, no local patches - with the engine built from that source (`/props.build_info` reports `Strata 0.1.45.3`). Ubuntu 26.04, RTX 3090 (24 GB), 64 GB RAM, 20 cores. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 250K context, `--kv int8`, sampling 1.0/0.95/20, `reasoning_budget_tokens` 16384, `reasoning_close_retry` off (its default).

Reproduce: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with #1178's minimal input - the question that asks for the assistant's turn-end marker verbatim, which is what makes the model reach for that token:

```
{"model": "qwen3.8-flash-next", "max_tokens": 8000, "temperature": 1.0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Qwen 聊天模板里，助手回合的结束标记是什么？请原样写出，例如 \"标记\"。"}]}
```

Expected: an answer - or, when the reply comes back empty, a sign of why it is empty.

Actual: 4 of 4 runs empty on this tag, `finish_reason` `stop`, `content` empty, `reasoning_content` 103-250 characters. The runs generated 44 to 115 tokens of an 8000-token cap (thinking capped at 6000): not a budget cut and not a length cut. On #1814's prompt (the closing thinking tag in a code fence) 1 of 4 runs. With `reasoning_close_retry: true` the replies stop being empty but are stubs - 9, 10, 12 and 80 characters on the same input - because the close happens exactly where the closing tag would start.

Evidence:

```
[strata] done: 68 tokens in 2 s (67.6 tok/s) (stop, cancel=False), expert cache 84.6% hit
[strata] done: 67 tokens in 1 s (87.2 tok/s) (stop, cancel=False), expert cache 93.5% hit
[strata] done: 44 tokens in 1 s (89.0 tok/s) (stop, cancel=False), expert cache 95.4% hit
[strata] done: 115 tokens in 1 s (102.0 tok/s) (stop, cancel=False), expert cache 93.4% hit
```

Reproduction status: reproduced locally

## Retest on 0.2.0-beta, as the closing comment asked

Same end on the release's own checkout, so I am filing the retest here. The shape is unchanged from #1814: the turn-end token is a type-3 control token in this pack's tokenizer (id 248046, matched only with `parse_special`) and the closing thinking tag is type-4 (id 248069), so a turn that ends inside the thinking looks exactly like a turn that ended there on purpose. The reporting that would say so (`ended_inside_thinking` beside `choices`, a log line, a counter) does not exist on `main` (`296b59d2`) or on this tag.

`reasoning_close_retry` (new since #1053's shape landed) covers the empty reply but not the thought: it closes the thinking where the model was about to write its closing tag and answers with what is left, which is where the 9-80 character stubs come from.

The fix in #1840 was closed in the tracker reset; I reopened the same work on this base as #3207 - the marker's text goes back as ordinary text where the model was writing it (#1178), the thought continues from there, and the close is the fallback for the other shapes, all behind the same opt-in flag.
