issues.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 (RX 7900 XT 20 GB, 31 GiB RAM): amdkfd SVM restore hangs and kswapd order-0 alloc failures persist with HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0; suspend with the SVM mapping active never resumes
issues.author: Smuggz69
issues.body:
## What happened

Four kernel-level events on one box, all in the amdkfd/SVM restore paths, on a 31 GiB RAM / 20 GB VRAM machine. Two of them are evidence the published workaround does **not** cover: `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` removes the amdkfd hang, but not the reclaim pressure behind it, and suspend/resume with the SVM mapping active never returns.

This is a second machine for the mechanism in #1705 (that box had 125 GiB RAM and the env var ended everything there). We are filing a new issue that links it, per the closing note there, because the new evidence below is not in #1705. Related: #750, #920, and the compaction-stall docs section being added in #2413.

### Environment

- Engine **0.1.43.1**, HIP backend (`build-hip`, archs `gfx1100`), args `--resident-experts --vram-reserve-mib 3072 --kv int8`
- **AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100)**, one GPU, also drives the desktop (Wayland)
- **CachyOS** (Arch), kernel `7.2.9-2-cachyos` PREEMPT, **31 GiB RAM**, zram swap, zswap off, model files on NVMe
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 131072 ctx, expert pool 14.2-20.6 GiB held as one paged SVM region (`STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=0`, per the ~32 GB box guidance in TROUBLESHOOTING #649)
- One long-lived engine process; expert pages migrate RAM<->GPU under normal inference load

### Events 1 and 2 - 2026-10-12, before the env var was set

**1. `12:38:28` - `kworker` in D state inside `svm_range_restore_work`, then the box died** (boot ended 12:38:47, manual reboot 12:42):

```text
Workqueue: events_freezable svm_range_restore_work [amdgpu]
Call Trace:
 ? walk_pgd_range+0x460/0xea0
 ? walk_page_range_mm_unsafe+0x149/0x330
 ? hmm_range_fault+0x78/0xb0
 ? amdgpu_hmm_range_get_pages+0xcb/0x160 [amdgpu]
 ? svm_range_validate_and_map+0x633/0x18c0 [amdgpu]
 ? svm_range_restore_work+0xe1/0x370 [amdgpu]
 ? process_scheduled_works+0x1fa/0x690
```

followed by `warn_alloc` / `kswapd0: page allocation failure: order:0`.

**2. `19:32:25` (also `13:03:10`, `15:48:59`) - hung task, engine unkillable until reboot:**

```text
INFO: task kworker/1:67:15296 blocked for more than 122 seconds.
Workqueue: events_freezable amdgpu_amdkfd_restore_userptr_worker [amdgpu]
Call Trace:
 __schedule+0x753/0x2270
 schedule+0x55/0x810
 schedule_preempt_disabled+0x30
 __mutex_lock+0x1e9/0x5d0
 amdgpu_amdkfd_restore_userptr_worker+0x82/0xad0 [amdgpu]
```

The mutex is held by `svm_range_restore_work` -> `amdgpu_hmm_range_get_pages` -> `hmm_range_fault` -> `filemap_fault` -> `folio_wait_bit`: **the GPU's SVM expert restore waits inside a model-file page fault.** At user level that is the prompt watchdog plus a 60-162 s freeze, then SIGABRT:

```text
reading the prompt (batched): waiting for the GPU (attention, router) at layer 21
host idle 242 s, 7/7 workers parked, 24/24 jobs done, 0 threads on disk
no progress for 60 s during a request (issue #29)
```

The engine then exits `-6` and the server restarts it. ~10 stalls/day on the Q2_0 tier.

### Event 3 - 22:46:26, suspend with the engine loaded never resumed

```text
Oct 12 22:46:26 systemd-logind[697]: suspend requested from client PID 1531 ('org_kde_powerde')
Oct 12 22:46:26 kernel: PM: suspend entry (deep)
```

Nothing after - no resume line, no amdgpu line. The box needed a hard power cycle (reboot 22:51:35). Third time suspend/resume with the Strata SVM mapping active has failed to come back, same class as event 1. **This one is independent of the env var**, so we stop the engine before suspend via a system-sleep hook.

### Event 4 - 2026-10-13 12:53:52, WITH the workaround set

`HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` and `GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576` were both in the engine's `env` block for this run, and the reclaim pressure is still there:

```text
Oct 13 12:53:52 kernel: kswapd0: page allocation failure: order:0,
  mode:0xc0de0(GFP_KERNEL|__GFP_HIGH|__GFP_ZERO|__GFP_COMP|__GFP_NOMEMALLOC)
Oct 13 12:53:52 kernel: PID: 141 Comm: kswapd0 Tainted: G U 7.2.9-2-cachyos
  warn_alloc <- __alloc_pages_slowpath <- __alloc_frozen_pages_noprof
  <- folio_alloc <- isolate_lock_cluster <- cluster_alloc_swap_entry
  <- folio_alloc_swap <- shrink_folio_list <- evict_folios <- kswapd
```

Same boot: coder tier (IQ1_M, expert pool 17.14 GiB, `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=8`, `--kv int8`), **0 file-tier expert reads**, MemAvailable 10 GiB, swap 0 used. 31 order-0 allocation failures in that boot. So on this box the env var removes the amdkfd hang (events 1-2 have not recurred with it set) but not the RAM side of the same subsystem.

### What we would like upstream

1. A note in the `docs/AMD_HIP.md` reclaim section that on a ~31 GiB box the env var ends the *hang* but not the order-0 reclaim failures, and that suspend with the SVM mapping active is a separate failure class - so people do not read "set the env var" as a complete fix.
2. If it is cheap: a load-time warning when the resident expert complement plus headroom exceeds usable RAM, which is exactly the condition that produced events 1, 2 and 4 here.
3. Nothing here is a request for new engine behaviour on the GPU side - the traces are kernel-side, and our box is now stable on the coder tier (0 file reads, 0 stalls).

### Notes for triage

- All four traces are in the SVM/amdkfd restore paths (`svm_range_restore_work`, `amdgpu_amdkfd_restore_userptr_worker`) - one subsystem.
- The paged pool is one large SVM region (tens of GiB); page-ins/outs happen under normal inference load, not only during fault storms.
- Bisect hint: events 1-2 predate `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0`; event 3 is the suspend path and is independent of it; event 4 is with it set.
- We are on 0.1.43.1, not 0.1.44 - happy to re-test on 0.1.44 and reopen/comment here if any of the four classes still reproduces.

issues.title: [Feature]: Offline conversion of FP4-Local CSF checkpoints
issues.author: hagope
issues.body:
## What do you want to do?

Convert the text weights of [`nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local) for Strata's existing NVFP4 expert path.

This checkpoint stores routed-expert block scales as CSF fixed/exception streams, dense weights as mixed MXFP8/NVFP4, and the PLE table as NVFP4. The existing `nvfp4_convert.py` path does not decode these streams and formats. The shard index also places files under `tensors/`.

The proposed change is an explicit offline converter: losslessly expand/repack routed-expert scales, decode dense weights before the existing BF16/F16/Q8_0 policy, and stream the PLE table to the existing BF16 reader. The installer, runtime, default converter and engine backends stay unchanged. Vision and MTP conversion are outside this change.

A bounded experiment has already checked nine real expert projections against an uncompressed reference and the pinned converter, and three converted expert blobs passed Strata's CUDA expert parity test on an RTX 5090. Full-model serving, answer quality and throughput remain untested. A draft PR with CPU tests and the bounded real-tensor conversion check will follow.

Related format work: [vLLM #60646](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60646). [Strata #1859](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1859) is a separate native safetensors source; this proposal uses offline conversion instead of adding a native weight backend.

issues.title: --prefill-head-alias: 3x slower cold prefill on a 16GB card, and the safety stop aborts the request at the end of prompt read
issues.author: ShaggyDragon
issues.body:
## Environment

- Strata **0.1.44.1**, `--serve`, single GPU
- RTX 5080 **16 GB**, dual Xeon Platinum 8176 (56C/112T), 256 GB RAM, Linux (Unraid, docker)
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (79 GB pack: 52 GB main + 27 GB PLE), `--expert-cache auto`, `--ple-io ram`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 16384`
- `--prefill-head-alias` enabled (from the initial setup recommendation)

## 1. Cold prefill is ~3x SLOWER with the flag on a 16 GB card

A/B on the same config, one flag changed, 35K-token cold prompt, same engine generation:

| | with `--prefill-head-alias` | without |
|---|---|---|
| Cold prefill (35K tok) | 60 s (~505 t/s) | **21 s (~1,650 t/s)** |
| Fork/resume of same prompt | 60 s | **5.4 s** |
| Decode steady state | 88–96 t/s | 89–92 t/s (unchanged) |

With the flag on, the prompt path appeared forced into ~2048-token chunks that borrowed expert-cache slots (engine log slot accounting); without it, chunks went to the normal size and experts loaded once per chunk. The docs describe the flag as paying off on small (8 GB) cards — on 16 GB it looks like pure cost.

**Suggestion:** auto-enable only when the prompt-path buffers don't fit alongside the expert cache, rather than leaving it to users to discover the regression by A/B.

## 2. The safety stop aborts the whole request — always at the very end of prompt read

4 occurrences in one engine generation. The pattern is consistent: the error fires at **96–99 % of prompt read**, i.e. the head layer appears to be reloaded (address moved) *during* prefill, and the captured verify graphs then fail at decode start:

```
[strata] reading the prompt: 26,845 of 26,850 tokens, 9 s so far
[strata] the engine reported an error: --prefill-head-alias: the output head was reloaded at another address, so the captured verify graphs would read freed memory
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 10 s (0.0 tok/s) (error, cancel=False)

[strata] reading the prompt: 56,354 of 56,429 tokens, 42 s so far
[strata] the engine reported an error: --prefill-head-alias: the output head was reloaded at another address, so the captured verify graphs would read freed memory
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 44 s (0.0 tok/s) (error, cancel=False)

[strata] reading the prompt: 90,338 of 90,343 tokens, 47 s so far
[strata] the engine reported an error: --prefill-head-alias: the output head was reloaded at another address, so the captured verify graphs would read freed memory
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 48 s (0.0 tok/s) (error, cancel=False)
```

The guard itself is right — reading freed memory would be worse — but the cost is brutal: the entire prefill (up to 48 s of work) is discarded, the client gets an error, and in our case the retries plus engine restarts wiped the adaptive tier, making every following request stone cold. That's how a "safety stop" turned into 100 s+ perceived cold starts.

**Suggestion:** when the moved head is detected, drop the alias for that request and decode via the non-aliased path (or re-capture the verify graphs) instead of failing the request — the prefill is already done at that point, everything else is throwaway.

Happy to run further A/Bs or capture the engine log around the reload events if useful.

issues.title: Strata Profile Studio: a page that shows what limits Strata on your PC, and whether a tune helped
issues.author: qiuzan2001
issues.body:
Strata Profile Studio is a small web page that runs next to Strata on the same PC. It shows which part of the PC limits Strata (disk, RAM, CPU, PCIe, VRAM, GPU), where the time of each request goes, and whether a change of settings made Strata faster, measured against the noise of your PC. It uses Python 3.11+ and the standard library only, and no GPU of its own: https://github.com/qiuzan2001/strata-profile-studio

![20-second tour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qiuzan2001/strata-profile-studio/v0.1.0/docs/screenshots/tour.gif)

To install it, give this sentence to a coding agent on the PC where Strata runs:
`Install Strata Profile Studio on this computer and open it in my browser: https://github.com/qiuzan2001/strata-profile-studio (follow docs/AI_SETUP.md)`

To look first without Strata: `git clone https://github.com/qiuzan2001/strata-profile-studio && cd strata-profile-studio && python3 studio.py --demo` (recorded data of one PC, not yours).

What it measured on my PC (RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, Ryzen 7 5800X3D, 80 GB DDR4, Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, 0.1.44.1): a calibration (`setup.py --calibrate`) removed `--pcie-frac 0.35` and `--spec-min-p 0.70` because its short-chat test saw no 3 % gain, and set `--adapt-swaps 80`. The profile before and after it (run 5 to run 6): agent turns -5.2 %, 6 of 6 turns slower (sign test p = 0.031); chat +0.4 % and long context -2.7 %, inside the noise. With 0.35 / 0.70 put back, a second calibration changed only `--adapt-swaps 160` to `80` (run 8 to run 9): agent turns +5.1 %, 6 of 6 faster (p = 0.031). The calibration's test is three short chats of 128 and 512 tokens; it does not see agent turns. The Studio shows the calibration's result and the profile side by side, so you can keep or go back.

Not tested: Windows, macOS and AMD cards. The readers for them come from the documentation of each tool. If you try it there, `python3 studio.py --host-probe --config <your strata-<model>.json>` prints what it can read, and a "works on" issue in the Studio's repository with that output is welcome.

It writes only Strata's run config (after a dialog, with a `.bak` copy) and its own state file.

issues.title: [Feature]: an opt-in setting to refuse a request whose model is not the loaded model
issues.author: BoogeAI
issues.body:
### What I want to do

When a client asks this server for a model name it does not serve, the chat routes answer anyway with whatever model is loaded, and the reply reports the server's own name. I would like an opt-in setting that refuses such a request instead — the same `model not found` `/props` already gives — so a client pointed at the wrong local model fails loudly instead of being answered by the wrong weights.

### The case that made me look

I run two local models through one port: the base **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S** (`strata-iq3_s.json`) and a community fine-tune (**RVN abliterated**, `strata-rvn-iq3_s.json`). They are mutually exclusive on `127.0.0.1:8080` — I stop one and start the other (~47 GiB against ~53 GiB of experts in RAM). My agent front-end has both declared as two models on one OpenAI-compatible route.

The picker said "RVN", the answers came, and I assumed I was talking to the fine-tune. I was not: the base model was loaded and it answered everything. The fine-tune's style and its (abliterated) refusals never appeared, and nothing in the response said so — `model` in the reply is always the server's own. I only found out by reading `/health` next to the picker.

The documented "any model name" behaviour is good for a one-model install and for clients that hardcode a name (`docs/AI_SETUP.md` §8: "any model name"), so I do not want the default changed.

### What the server does today

Measured on 0.1.44.1 (prebuilt CUDA 13.0 engine), RTX 5080 16 GB, Windows 11 26200, base model loaded, `model` set to a deliberately nonsense name (`完全不存在-的模型名`) and 8 output tokens:

| route | result |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | 200, `model` in the reply = `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s` |
| `POST /v1/messages` (Anthropic) | 200, `model` in the reply = the same |
| `POST /v1/responses` | 200, `model` in the reply = the same |
| `GET /props?model=<anything else>` | 404 `{"error": {"message": "model not found"}}` — this one does check (`serve/server.py` `_props`, the `model not in svc.model_names()` branch) |

`POST /v1/load` / `/v1/unload` check too, but only for the local page. The three routes a client actually talks to do not.

### What I would like

An opt-in config key, for example

```json
"strict_model": true
```

so that a request whose `model` is neither the served name nor its alias is refused with the 404 body `/props` already uses, on the three client routes. Absent or false keeps the current path exactly as it is.

A list spelling would be fine too (`"accept_model_names": ["strata", "<the model name>"]`) if an alias should keep working; I have no preference between them.

### Workaround I use today

- Split the front-end's provider into one route per local model, with a display name that says which server must be running, and only that model's id in each route's list.
- Read `/health`'s `model` field (my own launcher prints it as a status line) before trusting a picker.

### Scope and what I did not test

Server only (`serve/server.py`); no engine, kernel or setup change. If a mismatched name is refused before the request reaches the engine, nothing an accepted file does can move.

Not tested: AMD HIP and SYCL (this PC is CUDA only); the Anthropic and Responses routes beyond the one mismatch request each above (the three routes share the request path, so one check would sit there); and `POST /v1/embeddings` — it answered 404 to the fake name, but I did not send the served name to it, so that 404 is not evidence either way.

issues.title: `--batch` on the Metal backend is accepted at boot and exits the engine with code 86 on the first request that runs two sequences together
issues.author: alvarorsouza-arch
issues.body:
## What happened

`--batch` is accepted on the Metal backend, allocates its slot sessions at boot, and then stops the engine the first time a request actually decodes two sequences together. On a Mac that is worse than a refusal, because the server restarts the engine between requests and the rest of the run fails the same way.

What I ran: setup's own config for the IQ3_S pack plus `--batch N` in `--serve`, then the repo's burst client.

```bash
python3 tools/serve_load.py http://127.0.0.1:8012 --clients 1,4 --rounds 3 --max-tokens 256
```

The boot is happy, and it announces itself with the CUDA device name on a Mac build:

```text
strata generate: --batch: 4 slot sessions on CUDA0 (1.73 GiB each); 95.16 GiB free
strata generate: --batch 4: the slot sessions take 6.91 GiB of VRAM on CUDA0 that the expert cache would otherwise hold
strata verify: batch windows of up to 4 sequences (layers [0, -1))
```

The first concurrent round then writes two lines and the process is gone:

```text
strata batch: slot 0 takes 67 tokens (copied in 12.7 ms)
strata metal: strata::kernels::pdl_supported has no Metal implementation yet
```

`metal/src/engine/missing.cpp` documents what follows that message, verbatim: `Default: say which one and stop (exit code 86), so a run never continues on outputs nobody wrote.` The server's side:

```text
[strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 86). ... The next request starts the engine again.
[strata] the engine had stopped (exit code 86); starting it again (a minute or two) ...
```

In my engine log the restarts after these exits are 6, 25 and 74 s apart. Same at `--batch 2` and `--batch 3`.

Measured with `tools/serve_load.py`, three rounds, 256 tokens out, one engine boot per row:

| `--batch` | one client, total tok/s | that many clients, total tok/s | first token p50/p95, seconds |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2 | 43.3 | 0.4 | 5.12 / 5.21 |
| 3 | 43.3 | 0.3 | 5.19 / 5.23 |
| 4 | 44.2 | 0.4 | 5.26 / 5.29 |

One client is normal decode; from two sequences onward the number is the restart cycle, not throughput.

## Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1-metal, source build of `main` at `296b59d` · Apple M3 Max, 40-core GPU, 128 GB unified memory · macOS 26.6, high power mode. Model: original Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--max-context 65536`, experts resident with `--mmap-experts`, `--spec 2` with the MTP draft layer, everything else at setup defaults.

## Engine log

The two relevant lines are quoted above, and the version line in the same log reads `strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.44.1-metal)`. The full measurement set for this machine is in #2649.

## Why it stops at that call

`src/core/verify.cpp:901` decides the batch window with `pdl_window(G == 1 && pdl_supported())`. `pdl_supported()` is a capability query rather than a kernel, and on Metal it is one of the entry points listed in `metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`, so it runs `missing()` and exits.

## How far the batch route is from working on Metal

`STRATA_METAL_STUBS=log`, which that same file describes as `for listing which entry points a code path reaches, never for answers`, shows what a four sequence run touches. Seventeen entry points:

```text
pdl_supported, pdl_scope
fused_gr_read_multi, gdn_conv_l2_multi, gdn_ab_multi, gdn_step_norm_multi, shared_expert_multi, broadcast_streams
native_quantize_q8_1, native_mmvq, native_router_top10, quantize_q8_1_rows, iq_embed_rows, bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf
doorbell_publish_res, copy_from_mapped, copy_i32_from_mapped
```

Two capability queries, the multi row family a batched window needs, the native helpers, and the expert pool side, which Metal does not use because it reads experts in place from the mapped file.

## What I would suggest

- Refuse `--batch` on Metal at boot, the way `--kv int8` already stops there with `strata metal: strata::kernels::kv_block_bytes has no Metal implementation yet`, instead of allocating 1.73 GiB per sequence and exiting 86 mid-request.
- If the intent is to reach batch on Metal, `pdl_supported` returning false in the stubs moves the stop from a capability query to the kernels that matter, which is where the list above becomes a checklist.
- `docs/MAC.md` still names `--parallel` (batch slots) as not ported. The flag today is `--batch` (and `--slots`), so a Mac reader can miss the line, and the boot line's `on CUDA0` does not help.

issues.title: [Feature]: let a coding agent's own heavy jobs have the GPU and RAM, then continue the conversation without re-reading it
issues.author: page1
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

I run coding agents (opencode, Claude Code) against Strata on one PC. Their work often includes running a program that needs the same GPU and RAM the model holds: a simulation, a training run, an ML pipeline. What I want:

1. **The model gets out of the way while the job runs.** It gives back the RAM and the VRAM, and stays out: nothing loads it back over the job, not even another agent's request. With several agents running jobs, it stays out until the last job ends, however each one ends (a crash or a kill included).
2. **The model comes back and continues the same conversation efficiently.** The agent then reads the results and carries on where it was. These conversations are long (100K-250K tokens with tool output), and today a restart reads each one again from token 0.

Measured on an RTX 3090 24 GB, Core Ultra 9 285K, 95 GB DDR5-6800, Windows 11, Flash-Next IQ3_S at 262K context, with a ~100K-token conversation, timed from the moment the model is asked back to the first answer of the continued conversation:

| | Back with the conversation |
|---|---|
| today (start the engine, then read the whole prompt again) | 53.2-53.8 s |
| #1937's disk tier + the latch (`POST /load`, the conversation from the disk) | 18.1-18.7 s |
| + the start-up PRs (#2672, #2673) and other local start changes | **12.9-13.2 s** |

Giving the machine to the job: 4.2-4.5 s. In use on the whole PC before -> after: RAM 81.2 -> 28.0 GB (of 95.5; the rest is other programs), VRAM 23.2 -> 1.0 GB (of 24).

**Why a fast start matters for this, and not much otherwise.** For a server that stays up all day, the engine start happens about once a day, and a few seconds there are worth little. In this workflow the start is part of every iteration: the agent hands the whole machine to a job and takes it back, many times a day, and every return waits for a full engine start. Once the conversation itself comes back from the disk in a second or two, the start is most of what is left: here about 11 s of the 13 s (`POST /load` returned after 10.9-11.0 s), and the engine start went from 17.0 s on v0.1.44.1 to 11.9 s (median of 6 starts each).

How it's built locally:
- the persistent disk tier of #1937, with a small fix for reading back under tight RAM: xrip/Strata#1, a PR against #1937's branch (the conversation comes back in 2.4 s instead of being read again in 39 s when free RAM is close to the floor);
- a 503 "latch": `POST /unload {"save": true}` saves and ends the engine, and requests answer 503 until `POST /load` (xrip/Strata#2, a PR against #1937's branch);
- "holds": process ids that keep the model out until they end;
- a CLI and opencode commands to wrap a job.

The latch is open as xrip/Strata#2 (server-side, about 115 lines with 9 tests); holds would follow on top of it. If #1937 does not land, the same can be built standalone on the session files. I'd like to know whether you want this in Strata, and in which shape.

issues.title: let Cascade Lake CPUs (AVX512F/BW/VL/DQ + VNNI, no VBMI) use the AVX-512 i-quant kernels
issues.author: zhai-hello
issues.body:
My CPU is an Intel i9-10940X (Cascade Lake-X, 14 cores). It has AVX512F, AVX512BW, AVX512VL, AVX512DQ, AVX512CD and AVX512-VNNI. It does **not** have AVX512-VBMI — VBMI came in on Cannon Lake, and Cascade Lake is Skylake-X plus VNNI.

`cpu_avx512_ok()` asks for all five bits, so the engine prints

> this CPU has no AVX-512: the expert kernels run on AVX-2 (multi-token for the i-quant gate/up rows)

and the i-quant gate/up rows run on the AVX-2 kernel. What I want is for the gate to accept CPUs that have F/BW/VL/DQ + VNNI but not VBMI, at least on builds where nothing in those translation units can emit a VBMI instruction.

**What it changes:** on the Windows/MSVC build, CPUs of this class (Skylake-X/Brookdale, Cascade Lake-X, Cascade Lake-SP with VNNI) would run the AVX-512 i-quant kernels instead of the AVX-2 ones.

**What it leaves alone:** the default path on Ice Lake / Zen 4 and newer stays byte-identical, and the GCC/Clang build keeps asking for VBMI (reason below).

## Why I think it is safe on the MSVC build

- `/arch:AVX512` is set on the sources (CMakeLists.txt:1326 for `iq_avx512.cpp` and `nvfp4_avx512.cpp`, :1219 for `expert.cpp`), and MSVC's `/arch:AVX512` covers F/CD/BW/DQ/VL — the compiler will not emit a VBMI instruction from it.
- The AVX-512 sources use no VBMI intrinsic. I searched `src/` for the VBMI intrinsics (vpermb / vpermi2b / vpermt2b / vpmovb2m …): the only byte-or-word permute in them is `_mm512_permutexvar_epi16` at iq_avx512.cpp:47, which is AVX512BW. The VNNI intrinsic `_mm512_dpbusd_epi32` is used (expert.cpp:183, nvfp4_avx512.cpp:120) — that is why the gate needs VNNI, and this CPU has it.
- nvfp4_avx512.cpp:9 already states the kernels' own requirement: "Needs AVX512F/BW/VL and VNNI - what cpu_avx512_ok() checks before anything here is called." VBMI is extra on top of what the kernels use.
- There is already a narrower gate for the same kind of gap: `cpu_avx512bw_ok()`, documented at include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert_layout.hpp:47 as "AVX-512F + AVX-512BW + AVX-512VL + AVX-512DQ (e.g. Skylake-X i9-9920X)".

## Why the gate asks for VBMI anyway

On GCC/Clang those same sources are compiled with `-mavx512vbmi` explicitly (CMakeLists.txt:1224, :1339), so on that build a CPU without VBMI can reach a VBMI instruction and take an illegal instruction — which is what the comment at expert_layout.cpp:300 is guarding against. So the fix probably has to be build-aware (relax the bit only where the build cannot emit VBMI), or `tools/check_isa_guard.py` should show the AVX-512 objects are VBMI-free.

## How I checked, and what I have not measured

- numpy's runtime CPUID detection on this machine: AVX512F, BW, VL, CD, DQ, VNNI = true; AVX512VBMI = false.
- The engine's own check passes OSXSAVE and the XCR0 test and fails only on the VBMI bit.
- **I have not measured any speed difference** — I have no build with the relaxed gate. The direction is that the CPU pool does all the missed experts here (`--pcie-frac 0.00`), so a faster CPU kernel should matter more on this box than on a box that streams from PCIe, but I am not claiming a number.

## Machine, and I can test it

i9-10940X (Cascade Lake-X, 14C/28T, an ES part, stepping B1), RTX 3090 24 GB, 64 GB DDR4, Windows 10 21H2, engine 0.1.44.1, model Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS (native pack, `--pcie-frac 0.00`, `--spec-min-p 0.70`).

If you put out a test binary with the relaxed gate, I will run the same-day comparison the way docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md asks and post the numbers.

Similar reports in other projects, for what they are worth: [ollama #14435](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14435) (Enable AVX512_VNNI for Cascade Lake CPUs), [ik_llama.cpp #2409](https://github.com/ikawrakow/ik_llama.cpp/issues/2409) (Optimizing the AVX-512 codepath on Intel Cascade Lake).

issues.title: Community report: Strix Halo (gfx1151, Windows): default 15 pool workers vs 6 + STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1, 32.0 -> 41.7 tok/s in one ~120 W budget
issues.author: yoheier
issues.body:
### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.41 · Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI Max+ 395) · Windows 11

### Your question

On a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 the CPU cores and the GPU share one package power limit. During decode Strata runs the CPU expert pool and the GPU at the same time. With the default pool size (15 workers, chosen by the engine when `--pool-workers` is not given) the CPU takes most of the power and the GPU clock drops to about 1.77 GHz while decoding. With fewer workers the GPU stays near 2.8 GHz, and `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` alone lifts it to about 2.3 GHz. Decode is 14-30% faster in those settings. I recorded HWiNFO64 sensors (2 s steps) during the same 7-step smoke test for each setting (table below).

1. Is the default pool size (15 workers here) meant to be that high on a Strix Halo? Fewer workers leave more of the shared power for the GPU, and in my runs 4 workers (36.4 tok/s) was no better than 6 workers (36.6 tok/s). I saw #1351, where 4 workers beat the default of 15 on an RTX 4080 SUPER, so this may be the same effect with a power limit on top. Could the default on gfx1151 be lower (for example 6), or be chosen from the power limit?
2. `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` alone gave +19% with 15 workers (GPU clock 1770 -> 2340 MHz, CPU busy 58% -> 50%), and +14% on top of 6 workers. What does it change? I suspect it makes the CPU workers wait instead of spinning, which frees power for the GPU. That looks like the same mechanism as #2174 (waiting workers spinning and taking GPU power), but I have not checked. As far as I know `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT` needs a WAITPKG CPU, and I do not know whether the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 has it. If it does not, is there a non-diagnostic way to get the same effect? I have not yet run a long soak test with `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` on.
3. Could the log or Monitor tab show instantaneous tok/s as well as the running average? On Windows there are no GPU power or clock readings in About.

### Results

| run | setting | avg tok/s (smoke test) | busy CPU (total %) | CPU clock (MHz) | GPU clock while decoding (MHz) | DRAM read (GB/s) | package power (W) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | default, 15 workers | 32.0 | 58 | 2860 | 1770 | 101 | 120 |
| B | 15 workers + `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` | 38.1 (+19%) | 50 | 2380 | 2340 | 121 | 120 |
| C | `--pool-workers 6` | 36.6 (+14%) | 31 | 1565 | 2830 | 117 | 120 |
| D | `--pool-workers 4` (same conditions as C, without `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE`) | 36.4 (+14%) | 25 | 1270 | 2870 | 119 | 119 |
| E | `--pool-workers 6` + `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` | 41.7 (+30%) | 23 | 1150 | 2855 | 127 | 117 |

HWiNFO columns are means over the decode samples after the first 8 s of each run, averaged over the whole smoke test. In the prefill steps of the same runs the CPU is nearly idle and the GPU holds 2790-2860 MHz in all five runs, so the GPU can run at about 2.85 GHz inside the same 120 W. The tok/s of A, B, C and E come from the smoke test summaries; the GPU clock figures I noted at the time were about 1,610 / 2,240 / 2,500 / 2,750-2,800 MHz with slightly different averaging.

In run E the log shows one verify window taking about 46-51 ms (about 60-65 ms in run A), with the GPU wait about 30-33 ms. The CPU part of the window is slower (about 3.5-4.8 ms), but the faster GPU more than pays for it. Expert cache hit rate stays at 92-95% and KV VRAM hit rate at 99% or more.

**Power and limits seen in the logs**

- The package power is about 138 W for the first 8-16 s of a run (PPT FAST limit about 99%), then falls to about 120 W when the PPT SLOW limit reaches 100%. STAPM stays below 60% of its limit and there is no thermal throttling flag, so PPT SLOW is the binding limit. That is also why a long answer starts fast and then slows down: on one 512-token answer the running average went from 49.5 tok/s in the first second to 33.1 tok/s at the end.
- Prompt reading is steady at about 700 tok/s in repeated runs (spread about 2%), because it is GPU-bound and the CPU pool is idle then.

**Environment**

- Machine: EVO-X2 mini PC, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 96 GB visible RAM + 32 GB BIOS carve-out
- OS: Windows 11, AMD driver 32.0.31041.1004; HWiNFO64 sensors
- Strata 0.1.41 for the five HWiNFO runs (2026-10-10), before I updated to 0.1.43. The same 15-worker default also appears in my 0.1.43 logs.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--expert-cache auto`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ...`, int8 KV, `--max-context 131072` for these measurements (I raised it to 196608 and later 262144 for other tests, and saw no meaningful change in tok/s)
- `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`: the attached log of run E shows `strata decode timing` lines, so it was on for E. I have no logs for A-D, so I cannot confirm it was on there. It is not set in my current config. I have not checked how much overhead it adds.
- Power mode: "Performance" mode of the EVO-X2 (the only power setting the BIOS offers on this machine; I did not change any TDP/power limit values). HWiNFO shows the limits actually in force: PPT SLOW about 120 W (the package power settles there and the "PPT SLOW Limit" reading is 100%), PPT FAST about 140 W (package power peaks at 138-140 W at about 99% of "PPT FAST Limit").

**Not measured yet (I can add these later if useful)**

- A longer soak test (20-30 min) of setting E, to check that tok/s does not fall and nothing crashes.
- The same comparison on the latest release (0.1.44.1), with a pause between runs so each starts cool.
- Optional: 8 or 10 workers, to see where the GPU clock starts to fall.

**Attached**

- `hwinfo_smoke_runs_A-E.zip`: the five HWiNFO64 CSV files (runs A-E, 2 s steps).
- `strata_engine_log_runE_0.1.41_cleaned.log`: engine log of the run E session (engine 0.1.41, 6 workers, `--max-context 131072`). I removed the AMD COMGR compiler output and my Windows user name; the Strata lines are unchanged. No logs are available for A-D.

[hwinfo_smoke_runs_A-E.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33520527/hwinfo_smoke_runs_A-E.zip)

[strata_engine_log_runE_0.1.41_cleaned.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33520540/strata_engine_log_runE_0.1.41_cleaned.log)

issues.title: [Bug]: --pipeline-windows is silently clamped to 2; values above 2 are accepted and ignored
issues.author: kietq8684-design
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** 0.1.42 (61b3fb5) · Radeon VII 16GB (0x66af) + Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 16GB (0x66a1), gfx906, layer split · Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-146-p2p, ROCm HIP 7.14 (mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete), HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6

`--pipeline-windows` is hard-clamped to `[0, 2]`, and the clamp is **silent**: a value above 2 is accepted, the
engine uses 2, and nothing on stderr or in the log says the requested value was out of range.

#### 1. The clamp, in source

`src/program/generate.cpp:1991`:

```cpp
else if (a == "--pipeline-windows") o.pipeline_windows = std::max(0, std::min(2, std::atoi(next("--pipeline-windows"))));
```

#### 2. The engine's own log shows "3" and "2" side by side, with no warning in between

Same run, same startup log (`--pipeline-windows 3` requested):

    [strata] 2026-10-15 06:03:34 engine started: /src/build-906/strata --serve --pack ... --layer-split 27
             --prefill 4096 --spec 2 --spec-min-p 0.7 --mtp /data/mtp/rt --pcie-frac 0 --ple-row-cache 8388608
             --pipeline-windows 3 --max-context 32768
    strata generate: --pipeline-windows 2: 290 MiB of CUDA0 kept out of the expert cache (the second verifier, the GDN snapshots)
    strata serve: --pipeline-windows 2: two verifiers per stage, 2 stages overlap across windows (decode too; the GDN snapshots beside the window)

The engine's argv says 3; every line the engine then prints says 2. There is **no** line announcing the clamp:
`grep -icE "clamp|out of range|capped|ignoring"` over that startup log returns **0**.

#### 3. It is measurably a no-op: 3 is indistinguishable from 2, while 1 vs 2 clearly differ

Controlled sweep, one fresh container per value, both cards sampled from the host
(`/sys/class/drm/cardN/device/mem_info_vram_used`; idle = median of 12 samples after a 20 s settle,
peak = max over 160 samples at 0.5 s while a 16K-token request was in flight). Same config otherwise.

| requested | idle card0 / card1 (GiB) | peak card0 / card1 (GiB) | engine's structural report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--pipeline-windows 1` | 14.712 / 15.348 | 14.778 / 15.457 | **6912 slots / 12.57 GiB** |
| `--pipeline-windows 2` | 14.716 / 15.436 | 14.784 / 15.547 | **6889 slots / 12.53 GiB** |
| `--pipeline-windows 3` | 14.718 / 15.436 | 14.785 / 15.547 | **6889 slots / 12.53 GiB** |

Row 3 is row 2 within sampling noise (≤ 2 MiB) and **byte-identical** on the engine's own expert-cache line
(6889 slots / 12.53 GiB). Row 1 is 88 MiB and 23 slots away — so the knob does have an effect at 0/1/2;
3 just never runs.

#### Why this cost us real time (the actual impact)

We ran a boundary sweep over this flag and included a `--pipeline-windows 3` arm. It was a **no-op identical to the
baseline**, and we only found out by reading the engine's structural log line by line — the sweep's own summary
table looked like a normal result. We had already written "PW3" up as a data point before catching it. Anyone
tuning this flag can spend hours on an arm that never ran, and the engine gives them no hint.

#### What we'd like (deliberately small)

1. **A one-line notice when the value is out of range.** The codebase already has exactly this "say it once"
   pattern for the *off* path — `src/program/generate.cpp:3279`:
   ```cpp
   std::fprintf(stderr, "strata generate: --pipeline-windows %d is off: %s\n", o.pipeline_windows, off);
   ```
   So something like `strata generate: --pipeline-windows 3 is above the maximum 2, using 2` would match the
   existing style. (An `exit(2)` would be fine too, but we assume the clamp is intentional and just want it said.)
2. **State the range in the docs.** `--help` (`src/program/generate.cpp:784-786`) says
   "`--pipeline-windows N ... 1 = the prompt's short reads, 2 = decode as well`" — it describes 1 and 2 but never
   says N is capped at 2. `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` (the section "One conversation with both cards busy") likewise
   describes 1 and 2 only. A single "(0-2)" would close it.
3. *(optional, same root cause)* the other silently clamped numeric flags in the same parsing chain:
   `--lookup-chain` (`std::clamp(..., 0, 7)`, `generate.cpp:1994`), and `--suffix-draft` / `--mtp-max-t` /
   `--prompt-cache` (floored at 0). Same silent-truncation shape, lower stakes.

#### What we are NOT claiming

- **Not** that the cap of 2 is wrong. Two windows in flight is evidently the design maximum ("two verifiers per
  stage"), and the allocation-failure hint points at `--pipeline-windows 0` rather than higher.
- **Not** a functional defect: with a valid value (0/1/2) the flag behaves as documented, and we saw no wrong output.
- **Not** a performance claim about 2 vs 1 — we only used those two rows to show the knob is live.

issues.title: Metal: --kv fp16 is accepted and reported, but the QSA cache always stores int8
issues.author: Boundlessmolson
issues.body:
**Summary**
On the Metal engine, `--kv fp16` is accepted and the serve banner reports `kv=fp16`, but the Metal QSA
kernel always stores K and V as int8 with an fp16 scale per 64 values. The flag is silently ignored
for the QSA cache.

int8 looks like a deliberate choice for this kernel, so this is mainly about the mismatch: the banner
says fp16 while the cache is int8.

**Steps to reproduce**
Any Metal run with `--kv fp16`, for example:

```sh
env STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0 STRATA_HC_Q8=0 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0 \
  STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window \
  ./build-metal/strata --serve \
  --pack "$HOME/Developer/Strata-data/packs/q2_0" \
  --native "$HOME/Developer/Strata-data/models/Q2_0/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00001-of-00002.gguf" \
  --ple-gguf "$HOME/Developer/Strata-data/models/Q2_0/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf" \
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin \
  --expert-cache 64 --prefill auto --spec 2 --suffix-draft 0 \
  --max-context 4096 --mmap-experts --kv fp16 --adapt-every 0
```

The banner reports:
```
INFO ... context=4096 kv=fp16 kv_resident=0 ... engine=0.1.44.1-metal
```

**Where it comes from (at 296b59d)**
- `generate.cpp:9596` prints `kv=` from the flag string (`o.kv`).
- `metal/kernels/qsa.metal:135-147` (in `qsa_prep`) quantizes every K and V append to int8 with an
  fp16 scale per 64 values (`kq`/`vq` are `device char*`, `ksc`/`vsc` are `device half*`). Nothing in
  the kernel reads `--kv`.
- The file's own contract comments say the same: lines 6-7 (int8 KV append, fp16 scale per 64) and
  line 48 (the `kq/vq ... int8, ks/vs ... half` cache layout).

**Why it matters**
It changes numerics compared with CUDA's fp16 KV, which matters when comparing the two engines or
chasing drift over long contexts. Someone passing `--kv fp16` to rule out KV quantization would
reasonably believe they had.

**Suggestion**
Either honor `--kv fp16` in the Metal QSA path, or print what the Metal cache actually uses (for
example `kv=int8 (Metal QSA)`) and warn when another type was requested.

**Environment**
- Strata `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78` (engine `0.1.44.1-metal`)
- Mac Studio (Mac17,14), Apple M5 Max, 36 GB unified memory
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO Q2_0, native IQ pack, streamed experts

issues.title: [Engine] STRATA_HC_UPMIX on a gfx11 + gfx12 layer split corrupts prefill on the gfx12 stage (gr_upmix caches its arch check from the first device); still on 0.2.0-beta
issues.author: jiayeZhu
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

On a layer split across a Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Strix Halo iGPU, first stage) and a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201,
second stage), `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` gives wrong prefill results on every layer that runs on the gfx1201 stage. Nothing
crashes and nothing is logged; generation stays fluent, so it is easy to miss. It shows up as worse answers: on BFCL
parallel function calling the model emits one call where it should emit several.

**Re-tested on 0.2.0-beta (tag v0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3) on 2026-10-19: still there, same numbers.**
`gr_upmix()` in `src/prefill/kernels.cu` (line 2523 on v0.2.0-beta) is unchanged: it decides "is this gfx11?" once, in
a function-local `static`, from whichever device calls it first, and then launches `gr_upmix_kernel` on the gfx1201
device too. That device's code object was compiled with the non-gfx11 branch of `um_wmma()`, which is `return c;`,
so the WMMA step does nothing.

The engine's own check (`STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK=400`, which runs the default pair beside the fused kernel and reports
the difference of `mixed`) on 0.2.0-beta, three prompts of 364 / 372 / 443 tokens, two halves each, six checks per layer:

| layers (device) | checks | mixed rel RMS, min-max | max \|diff\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-29 (8060S, gfx1151) | 180 | 7.6e-08 - 3.3e-07 | 1.5e-05 |
| 30-47 (R9700, gfx1201) | 108 | 0.425 - 0.702 | 16.7 |

Every one of the 18 gfx1201 layers is in the 0.43-0.56 range on all six checks (layer 43 reaches 0.70, 44 reaches 0.57).
Sample lines:

```
strata: STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK layer 0 half 0 T 443: mixed rel RMS 1.651e-07, max |diff| 6.440e-06 (upmix)
strata: STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK layer 30 half 0 T 443: mixed rel RMS 4.615e-01, max |diff| 8.700e+00 (upmix)
strata: STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK layer 43 half 1 T 443: mixed rel RMS 7.017e-01, max |diff| 4.290e+00 (upmix)
```

Effect on output, 0.2.0-beta, the same 38 BFCL v4 `parallel` / `parallel_multiple` items as below (the exact BFCL
OpenAI-FC request: tools, the "Python 3 syntax" hint, temperature 0.001, 4 at once; each correct answer needs 2 or
more tool calls), one fresh engine per row, `STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0` on both (#3204, unrelated):

| 0.2.0-beta, the split | responses with 2+ tool calls |
|---|---|
| `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` (with the check on) | **2 / 38** |
| without `STRATA_HC_UPMIX` | **28 / 38** |

The earlier versions gave the same picture: v0.1.43.1 (`a0116b27`) and v0.1.44 (`ed4773eb`) 3/38 against 28/38, with
the per-layer check at ~1e-7 on layers 0-29 and 0.42-0.74 on layers 30-47; still present on v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`).

Workaround: unset `STRATA_HC_UPMIX` on a mixed-architecture split. (On the 8060S alone it is fine and stays on here.)

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

1. Build one engine for both GPUs: `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON
   -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1151;gfx1201"`, HIP flags `-DSTRATA_W_LB=8`, ggml at the pinned 3cf03257.
2. Run any gfx11 + gfx12 layer split with the gfx11 device first (here: `"gpu": [<gfx1151>, <gfx1201>]`,
   `"layer_split": "30"` through `serve/server.py`, 4 slots) with `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1 STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK=400`
   in the environment. The engine arguments:

   ```
   --pack <packs>/unsloth-ud-iq4_xs --native <models>/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf
   --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <mtp>/rt
   --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --mmap-experts --mtp-window 8192 --no-prefill-borrow
   --prefill 4096 --conversation-cache-mib 24576 --conversation-cache-slots 24 --trim-stage-weights
   --batch-groups 1 --batch-mtp --vision
   ```

   The rest of the environment:

   ```
   STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1151-hipblaslt-100401.txt
   STRATA_PF_FUSED=1  STRATA_PF_GEMM=1  STRATA_PA_FAST=1  STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1
   STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1  STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1  STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=64
   ```
3. Send any chat request. Any prompt length works, since `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T` defaults to 0 and
   `hc_upmix_min_t()` is 0 on HIP.
4. `grep STRATA_HC_UPMIX_CHECK engine.log`: ~1e-7 on every gfx1151 layer, ~0.4-0.7 on every gfx1201 layer.

Every build in this report carries one small local patch elsewhere in the prefill path (the `STRATA_PF_PAD` per-device
check that the gfx1201 stage needs in order to start; see #3204). It does not touch `gr_upmix` or its call site.

**Root cause.** `src/prefill/kernels.cu` on v0.2.0-beta:

```cpp
// 1745 (v0.1.44.1) - the gfx12 code object's um_wmma is a no-op
__device__ __forceinline__ um_f8 um_wmma(um_b16 a, um_b16 b, um_f8 c) {
#if defined(__gfx1100__) || defined(__gfx1101__) || defined(__gfx1102__) || defined(__gfx1103__) || defined(__gfx1150__) || defined(__gfx1151__)
    return __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32(a, b, c);
#else
    (void) a; (void) b; return c;   // not a gfx11 device pass: never launched (runtime gate)
#endif
}

// 2523 (v0.2.0-beta)
bool gr_upmix(...) {
#if defined(__HIPCC__)
    static const bool gfx11 = [] {                       // <- evaluated once per process,
        int dev = 0;                                     //    on whichever device calls first
        cudaDeviceProp p;
        if (cudaGetDevice(&dev) != cudaSuccess || cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p, dev) != cudaSuccess) return false;
        return strata::kernels::gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma(p.gcnArchName);
    }();
    if (!gfx11 || T <= 0) return false;
    gr_upmix_kernel<<<...>>>(...);                       // <- also launched on the gfx1201 stage
```

The call site in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` (line 3149 on v0.2.0-beta) has no per-device check either:
`if (wu->q8_scale == nullptr && hc_upmix() && T >= std::max(pf_switch_min_t(), hc_upmix_min_t()) && !gr_unfused() && ...)`.

With the gfx1151 stage first, `gfx11` is cached as `true`, and the "runtime gate" the `um_wmma` comment relies on
lets the gfx1201 launch through. With the gfx12 device first the cache would hold `false` and the fused path would be
skipped on both GPUs: slower but correct (not tested).

Other device-specific checks in the tree already cache per device: `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()` in `wmma_gemm.cu`
(`std::atomic<int> cache[64]`), `sel_gfx12_device()` in `qsa_select.cu`, and the `arch[dev]` lookup in
`qsa_prompt_attn.cu`. The same `gr_upmix` pattern is mirrored in `sycl/src/prefill/kernels.dp.cpp`.

**Suggested fix.** Cache per device, the way `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()` does:

```cpp
bool gr_upmix(...) {
#if defined(__HIPCC__)
    static std::atomic<int> cache[64];   // 0 unknown, 1 gfx11, 2 not
    int dev = 0;
    if (cudaGetDevice(&dev) != cudaSuccess || dev < 0 || dev >= 64) return false;
    int c = cache[dev].load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (c == 0) {
        cudaDeviceProp p;
        c = cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p, dev) == cudaSuccess && strata::kernels::gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma(p.gcnArchName) ? 1 : 2;
        cache[dev].store(c, std::memory_order_release);
    }
    if (c != 1 || T <= 0) return false;
    ...
```

Or have the call site in `prefill.cpp` ask the stage's device. As a defensive extra, the non-gfx11 branch of
`um_wmma` could trap (`__builtin_trap()`) instead of `return c`, so a launch that slips past the gate fails loudly
instead of computing wrong numbers.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta (tag v0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3), built from source; re-tested 2026-10-19. Also reproduced on
v0.1.43.1 (a0116b27), v0.1.44 (ed4773eb) and v0.1.44.1 (296b59d2).

### Graphics card, memory and system

issues.title: gfx1150 (Radeon 890M): confirmed build+run, isystem build fix, --expert-cache auto UMA pitfall
issues.author: Influx934Threads
issues.body:
## Summary

**Confirmed: a second gfx1150 (Radeon 890M) machine builds Strata clean, passes 64/64 meaningful ctest cases, and
serves correct chat completions end-to-end** — IQ3_XXS + MTP, extending the report in `docs/AMD_HIP.md` #1217. This
isn't just "it technically runs": below is a build fix for a header-shadowing bug that can silently corrupt the HIP
compat shim, and a reproducible `--expert-cache auto` pitfall on unified-memory AMD APUs that's undocumented for
non-"budget" model families — everything needed to get a Strix Point box running the same way.

Full write-up, raw benchmark JSON, and the sanitized config: **https://gist.github.com/Influx934Threads/493b031121ee940570aff8561e5e49c4**

## Hardware/software

AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (Radeon 890M, gfx1150), 92 GiB RAM, Debian 13, TheRock ROCm 7.14.1 built isolated for
`gfx1150` only, Strata v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`). `setup.sh` refuses this chip outright, so the pack build, MTP draft
layer, and server config were all done by hand with `tools/iq_pack.py` / `tools/mtp_fetch.py` / `tools/mtp_pack.py` /
`tools/mtp_rt.py`, reverse-engineering what `setup.py` would have generated.

## 1. Build fix: stale system HIP headers can win over the isolated SDK

On a distro with both a system HIP/ROCm package (Debian/Ubuntu ship HIP 5.x at `/usr/include/hip/`) and a separate
isolated ROCm/TheRock prefix, clang passes `--rocm-path`'s include dir with `-idirafter` (lowest priority) — so the
*older* system header can win, reporting `HIP_VERSION_MAJOR 5`. Strata's compat shim branches on exactly that
(`#if HIP_VERSION_MAJOR < 7`), so the build silently takes the wrong code path with no error. Fix: an explicit
`-isystem $SDK/include` ahead of `--rocm-path` in `CMAKE_HIP_FLAGS` (full command in the gist). ctest: 64/64
meaningful tests pass after the fix.

## 2. `--expert-cache auto` can OOM a UMA GPU — gap in setup.py's existing RAM-safety logic

`auto` sizes the GPU-side expert cache from RAM that's free *after* this model's ~40 GiB resident expert arena is
already loaded — fine on a discrete GPU (cache lives in VRAM), but on a UMA APU that arena and the "free RAM" figure
share the same pool, and the sizer doesn't discount for it. The engine does print a warning, but not a refusal; it
OOM-killed both this process and an unrelated already-running llama.cpp service here. `setup.py`'s own
`uma_expert_cache()` RAM-budget logic exists for this exact shape of bug, but only applies to Unsloth "budget"-family
models by its model table — IQ3_XXS has no `"budget"` flag, so that protection doesn't engage for it. Fix used here:
an explicit `--expert-cache 8192` (~17.8 GiB) instead of `auto`. Engine log excerpt and full explanation in the gist.

## 3. Numbers

Warm decode 23.1-24.8 tok/s, 95-98% MTP draft acceptance (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`), deterministic sampling,
thinking disabled. Faster than the one existing gfx1150 data point in the docs (15-19 tok/s, no MTP breakdown) — not
a controlled A/B, just a second machine's numbers. Full table and raw JSON responses in the gist.

## Worth the few extra lines in setup.sh to support gfx1150 natively?

With two independent machines now confirming a correct build and correct output on gfx1150 (#1217 and this one),
and the kernel guards + hipBLASLt table already shipped, this looks like a small, bounded change to let
`setup.sh --backend hip` accept it (even kept unvalidated) instead of refusing outright. Happy to test a patch
against this hardware, or to fold this into `AMD_HIP.md` myself if that's preferred — just say which.

issues.title: [Bug]: Metal (M1 Ultra): engine stalls at token 0 reading an 8.7K-token prompt — "no progress for 60 s", exit -6 (0.1.44.1, stock config)
issues.author: beettlle
issues.body:
### What happened

On Apple Silicon (Metal backend), the engine stalls at **token 0** while reading a longer prompt (8,722 tokens). After 60 s the watchdog stops it with exit code -6 and asks for a report under #29. A short prompt (58 tokens) on the same install completes, but slowly: prefill runs at 1.6 tok/s and decode at 2.3 tok/s.

This happened on 2 of the 4 engine starts in the log, once with `--max-context 32768` and once with `--max-context 65536`. Everything else is the stock `setup.sh` config (`--expert-cache 64`, `--prefill auto`, `--mmap-experts`, `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1`). This is a different bug from #2671: no flags were changed, and the engine stalls instead of exiting with code 1.

**Steps**
1. Clean `./setup.sh` install of v0.1.44.1 (commit `296b59d`), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S.
2. `./run-iq3_s.sh`, then wait for `ready: http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1`.
3. Send a chat request with a prompt of about 8.7K tokens.

**Console output**
```
ready: http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1  (OpenAI: /v1/chat/completions, Anthropic: /v1/messages, context 65536 tokens)
[strata] reading the prompt: 8,722 tokens, 10 s so far
...
[strata] reading the prompt: 8,722 tokens, 61 s so far
[strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6). The engine stopped itself because it had stopped making progress - a hang it caught. Its log line: strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt, from token 0) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29) ...
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 62 s (0.0 tok/s) (error, cancel=False)
```

**Stall report**
```
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.44.1-metal): stage "reading the prompt, from token 0" for 59 s; 0 layers served since the last finished step (0 = stopped, more = slow)
  VRAM free when this request began: 42037 MiB
  expert pool: epoch 0, batch epoch 0: 0 of 0 jobs claimed, 0 done; 19 of 19 workers parked, 19 sleeping; mode 0
  expert pool threads: w0..w18=sleeping; host idle for 112309 ms
  verify window (last window, not the current stage): 0 tokens at position 0, host at layer step 1; the GPU rang 0; flags: served 0, plan (A) 0, copies (B) 0
  memory: 0 MiB resident, 0 MiB in swap, 0 MiB RAM available; 0 major page faults so far
strata: released the verify window's GPU waits (#267): the GPU finished in 0 ms
```

**What the log shows**
- No work was dispatched: 0 layers served, 0 expert jobs, every pool worker asleep, and the GPU never rang. This looks like a hang rather than slow progress.
- `host idle for 112309 ms` is longer than the 60 s watchdog window. The host thread was already idle before this request started.
- No major page faults, so the engine wasn't waiting on the disk.
- The memory line reads 0 for everything. At startup the log also says `memory guard: the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore are refused`. On macOS the stall report's memory figures may never be filled in.
- `the arena is small: the prompt's 1.63 GB of buffers are their own allocation, not a region of its slots`, and `the prompt path allocates its own buffers (too few cache slots to borrow)`.
- `PCIe probe failed -> pcie_frac default 0.55`. This is expected on unified memory, but it shows up on every start.

**Setup notes**
- The model files are on an external **USB** SSD (`/Volumes/NVMe`, APFS). The expert arena fill reads at about 0.90 GB/s.
- No `strata-stall-*.dmp` file was written. That dump is Windows-only, as far as I can tell.

I'm happy to run a debug build, try environment variables (for example `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` or `STRATA_METAL_WIRE_ARENA=0`), or test a patch on this machine.

### Strata version, GPU, OS
0.1.44.1-metal (commit 296b59d) · Apple M1 Ultra, 64 GB unified memory · macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)

### Engine log
(attach `strata-iq3_s.log`)

issues.title: Feature request: KV cache quantization (`--kv int8` / `--kv q4_0`) for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (strata-q36) path
issues.author: TorBere
issues.body:
The q36 path keeps its KV cache in fp32 (`src/qwen35`; 45,056 B per context cell). On a 12 GB card that is the wall for long contexts: at `--max-context 131072` the KV alone takes ~5.9 GB, so **no routed expert stays in VRAM at all** (engine log: `0 of 256 per layer in VRAM`). The Flash-Next path already offers `--kv int8` / `--kv q4_0` / `k8v4`; on the q36 path, setting `--kv int8` changes nothing (same KV size, same placement).

Setup: RTX 3060 12 GB, Ryzen 7 5800XT, 64 GB RAM, Windows 10, Strata 0.1.44.1 (ready-made CUDA 13 engine), `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF` UD-Q4_K_XL (setup's pinned file, SHA-256 checked), config as setup writes it (`--native <gguf> --max-context N --prefill auto --mtp 2`).

Measured (greedy, 120-token answers, warmup + 2 runs each, after a fresh start):

| context | decode | experts in VRAM | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 65,536 | ~46 tok/s (45.5–47.1) | 18 of 256 per layer (1.32 GiB) | rest on the 8-thread CPU pool |
| 131,072 | ~34 tok/s (33.7–34.8) | **0 of 256 — nothing fits** | fp32 KV ~5.9 GB |

- MTP (`--mtp 2`) is worth +40–44% here (46 vs 32 tok/s at 64K; 34 vs 24 at 128K) — it stays on.
- In long filled conversations decode drops further (~30 tok/s; GPU ~50% utilised, memory controller ~36% — the bottleneck is the CPU/offload side plus the KV traffic).
- On the same PC, llama.cpp (via LM Studio, Q4_K_M, 128K context, quantized KV) holds ~43 tok/s at 128K — the KV format is the visible difference.

Why this fits the existing code: Qwen3.6's `head_dim` is 256 — the exact size of the FWHT-256 rotation used by `--kv q4_0` (PR #21). With int8 (1,056 B per cell) or q4_0 (576 B per cell) the 128K KV shrinks from ~5.9 GB to ~1.4 GB / ~0.76 GB: ~4.5–5.1 GB back for experts at 128K and 3–6x less KV traffic per decoded token (related: #2464, where decode falls with context on a V100).

Happy to run A/Bs (int8 vs q4_0 vs fp16, several contexts) on the 3060 if that helps.

---

issues.title: [Bug]: Chrome page translation jitters back to English - the web app rewrites the UI once a second by polling /metrics
issues.author: MrKop-git
issues.body:
## What happened

The Monitor tab (and the header pill) update by **polling**: `serve/web/app.js` runs `async function poll()` and re-arms itself with `setTimeout(poll, 1000)` (line 158-176), i.e. one `GET /metrics` per second; `serve/web/monitor.js` does the same every 2 s. Every tick replaces text that Google Chrome's built-in page translation is also rewriting.

With Chrome's translate feature on ("translate this page"), the UI text flips back and forth between the translated language and English — it "jitters"/flickers into English on every poll, one shift per second on the Monitor tab. The numbers on the Monitor are unreadable while it happens.

Expected: the page should keep the translated text stable while it updates its own values.

**Steps:** open `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` in Chrome with a UI language other than English, let Chrome translate the page (or right-click > "Translate to ..."), open the Monitor tab, watch the header pill and the metric cards.

**Cause (as far as I can see in the source):** Chrome's translation is a DOM mutation pass. Rewriting the same text nodes from a timer once per second makes Chrome's translation state and our own updates fight over the same nodes, so the freshly written English string shows before the translation pass re-applies. A push from the server (a single long-lived response the server writes to, e.g. SSE / a streamed `/metrics`), or updating only the parts that changed, removes the per-second full rewrite.

## Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1 · GTX 1080 Ti 11GB (+ GT 710 for display) · CachyOS Linux 6.18.55 · Chromium 142 (Chrome's translate feature)

## Engine log

(not engine-related — the web app's own polling; no engine log lines)

issues.title: Strata serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with strange behavior - really bad results
issues.author: tamascogustavo
issues.body:
# Strata serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next dumber than llama.cpp: tool-call loops + engine nondeterminism

Hardware: RTX 5070 12 GB, 60 GB RAM (only one 46 GB instance fits at a time), driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2.
Pack: IQ3_S (`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ3_S`), Strata native pack.
Reference server: `llama serve -hf ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ3_S -c 110000 -np 1
-fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -b 4096 -ub 1024 --load-mode none --no-mmproj --port 8080 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 2048`

## 1. Observed behavior (the complaint)

Same model, same prompts, two servers:
- Via Strata: tool calls fail most of the time (malformed args, hallucinated tools:
  `Bash`/`exec`/`WebFetch`/`registry`/`search`, OpenCode-style args like `file_path`, `limit`/`offset`
  that don't exist in the offered schema). Failures trigger agent retry loops. Also "dummy loops":
  very short thinks followed by the same command over and over (`list_files` x3-x5, `ls -la` x5).
- Via llama.cpp (`llama serve`, same quant): noticeably better reasoning, working tool calls.
- Result: Strata not usable as daily driver.

## 2. Issues found AND fixed (config)

**2a. Greedy-by-default sampling.** `strata-iq3_s.json` had no `sampling` block, and
`serve/server.py` only forwards `temperature>0` / `top_p<1` etc, so the engine ran greedy
(temperature 0). Greedy decoding is the classic cause of repetition loops.
**Fix applied** to `strata-iq3_s.json` (backup `strata-iq3_s.json.pre-fix.bak`):
`sampling {temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20}`.

**2b. `tool_call_recovery` off.** Absent from config = False (`server.py:3102,6864`;
`docs/DETAILS.md:845` quotes 92.9% vs 98.3% tool-call success on 1462 turns).
**Fix applied**: `tool_call_recovery true`.
Parser proof (GPU-free): synthetic 5-shape check 1/5 recovered without the flag, 5/5 with it;
`serve.test_server.ToolCallRecovery*` 12/12 pass.

## 3. Agentic evals (controlled, same harness)

Harness (`evidence/dailydriver*.py`): agentic loop over a slide-generator repo
(`/home/gustavo/Testes/lol/slide_test`: ppt.js, deck_claude.js, styles.css, pdf_text.txt,
binary pptx/pdf), tools `list_files`/`read_file`/`grep`, full call trace, keyword scoring.
- v1 (5 runs/arm, max_tokens 1024): 0/10 summaries, mostly `finish=length` (harness flaw: 1024
  starves xhigh thinking).
- v2 (max_tokens 4096, 8 turns, 5 runs/arm): old-greedy arm loops 4/5, fixed arm loops 2/5 +
  hallucinations 2/5. **Both arms 0/10 task completions.**
- Same harness vs llama.cpp (arm C, port 8083): **5/5 clean, 14-15/15 valid calls, zero loops.**
- v3 (fixed config, temp 0.6, 3 runs): **0/3 usable** — same disease (list_files loops, binary reads,
  hallucinated `write_file`). Config fix did NOT cure it.
- Ruled out prompt rendering: Strata `chat_template.jinja` byte-identical to llama.cpp `/props`
  template (183 lines, empty diff); Strata-rendered vs llama-tokenized prompt ids IDENTICAL
  (516/516 turn 1, 562/562 turn 2, tools block included). Difference is engine-side (logits)
  and/or sampling RNG (harness sends `seed`; Strata seed-honoring untested).
- Single-request continuation test: Strata 1/6 full reads + Bash hallucination + partials;
  llama 6/6 correct progress.
- Near-greedy (temp 0.01, seeds 111x2+222): llama 3/3 bit-identical; Strata nondeterministic
  **with the same seed**. <-- this redirected the whole investigation to the engine.

## 4. Engine nondeterminism hunt (the deep part)

Method (`evidence/run_determ.sh`): canonical engine args (pack iq3_s, native+ple GGUFs,
expert-profile.bin, cache auto, prefill auto, spec 4, mtp, max-ctx 110000, kv int8, pcie-frac 0,
spec-min-p 0.75, vram-reserve 896) + `--tokens-file prompt609.txt` (609 ids) + `--max-new 24` +
`--window-hashes`. Two fresh processes, compare hashes. Baseline: DIFFER from prefill-tail
window 0 (residual hash 2df94610 vs 8860bf2c, argmax 9764 vs 40; 20 vs 26 windows).

Still differed after each of (one factor at a time): MTP removal, `--pool-workers 1`, reasoning
budget, `--prompt-cache 0`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, `--no-coupled-draft`,
`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`, `--sync-every-layer`, `--adapt-every 0`,
`--expert-cache-cpu-order`, `--ple-io ram`, `--no-host-worker`, `STRATA_PREFILL_ISSUER=0`,
`STRATA_PF_STEP_SYNC=1`, `--pcie-frac 0` (partial: window-0 argmax identical, diverges token 3).
`--dump-routing`: records 0-2 identical, record 3 differs. `--dump-logits` writes empty files
(broken); `--dump-residual` all zeros; `--dump-layers` OOMs (~1.2 GB dump buffers).

Per-layer ground truth via the research hook `STRATA_DBG_FEAT` (+`_LAYERS`, `prefill.cpp:2948`;
parser `evidence/featparse.py`): layers 0 AND 1 bit-identical (ids, weights, hidden states),
layer 2+ differ hugely (~1.5M/1.55M values, magnitudes ~0.9-1.7). Onset varies run to run
(layer 1 vs 2). Layer-1 MoE fp32 input bit-identical. **Decisive: `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` runs are
bit-IDENTICAL** (hashes byte-equal, streamed/resident counts exactly equal) => the divergence
is inside the MMQ expert-compute path; attention/routing/tokenizer/server/sampling cleared.

Cleared by experiment: same-process back-to-back greedy server requests DIFFER (live race, not
just process state); VRAM-poison P0-vs-P1-vs-P0b all differ (not uninitialized memory);
`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` still diverges at layer 2 (not a GPU overlap race; prefill completes,
then hangs at verify capture — known issue #1341); CPU-share=0 still diverges (pool truly idle:
`PoolHold` gating, `cpu_maybe`); CLB+SHARE=0 still diverges (both jointly cleared);
stream_all-forced path still diverges (STAGE-ring cleared); tiny prompts T=2,4,8 all diverge
(shape theory dead); near-all-streamed (`--expert-cache 32` + SHARE=0) still diverges;
no-MTP (`--spec 2`, `+0 MiB for the draft head`) still diverges (draft cleared).
Cleared by audit: staging-slot protocol, upload rings (all single-stream `m.cs`), host grouping
tables (per-layer full sync), stager + file sources (thread-safe libaio/OVERLAPPED),
static residency (`host_res` built once at startup; full 48x512 table verified identical),
no float atomics anywhere, combine (same call both modes), vanilla unmodified llama.cpp MMQ
headers (third_party git-clean), deterministic J-loop / stream-K / launch selection.

## 5. The paradox (where the hunt stands)

Custom uncommitted debug patch `STRATA_DBG_MOE_TENSORS` (`prefill.cpp` ~4082) dumps layer-1
Xq/GU/Dm/bo + gathered blobs + bounds + cnt/off + residency + row map. Across runs, EVERY
gate/up-product input is bit-identical (activations, all 16 group blob slots, device bounds
nbound=957, counts, offsets, static residency, ids 0..N) yet gate/up products differ on ALL
6080 rows (resident and streamed experts alike). Standalone replay harness
(`evidence/replay.cpp`): the kernel is deterministic in isolation (15/15 identical) — but its
bits don't match the engine's (fidelity gap; the pack's actual gate/up type value is unverified).
compute-sanitizer synccheck hung at the #1341 verify capture and was killed (inconclusive).

## 6. What persists / next steps

- Root cause UNKNOWN. Air-tight paradox: identical inputs + deterministic kernels + different
  outputs is logically impossible, so one verified claim must be false (fidelity gap in what the
  engine actually launches) or the sm_120 kernel build misbehaves. Next: close the replay
  fidelity gap (actual `gu_type`, launch params), then per-group launch-param dump.
- Workaround with evidence: `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` is the only flag that gave bit-identical
  runs. Agent-quality validation (3x repo test, fixed config + MMQ=0) was running when this was
  written — see `evidence/dailydriver4.jsonl` / `dailydriver4.log`, results appended below.
- Still owed regardless: greedy temp-0 3x test (workaround check), Strata seed-honoring check.

## Appendix A. Validation: MMQ=0 as daily-driver workaround

Apples-to-apples with v3 (B-fixed config, temp 0.6, same repo/task/harness, 3 runs), plus
`STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` in the server environment (`evidence/dailydriver4.py`).

### Results (runs completed 2026-10-15)

| run | turns | tool calls | executed | loop | empty turns | think chars | SUMMARY | kw/10 |
|-----|-------|-----------|----------|------|-------------|-------------|---------|-------|
| 0 | 8 | 14 | 14 | no | 0 | 1785 | none (still exploring at turn cap) | 0 |
| 1 | 8 | 14 | 14 | no | 0 | 1625 | none (still exploring at turn cap) | 0 |
| 2 | 8 | 13 | 13 | no | 0 | 1740 | none (still exploring at turn cap) | 0 |

All 41 tool calls executed (no parse failures, no hallucinations: no `Bash`/`exec`/
`WebFetch`/`registry`, no OpenCode-style `file_path`/`limit`/`offset` args). Every run did
productive exploration — `list_files`, then `read_file` of all four real repo files
(`deck_claude.js`, `ppt.js`, `pdf_text.txt`, `styles.css`) plus targeted `grep`s
(`writeFile`, `SLIDE \d+`, `FONT_*`, `MASTER_`, ...). Zero dummy loops, zero empty turns.

Verdict: **MMQ=0 cures the loop/hallucination disease** (v3 with MMQ on: 0/3, dummy
`list_files` loops + hallucinated tools/args). But **task completion is still 0/3** by the
harness metric: no run produced a SUMMARY within the 8-turn cap (all were still gathering).
Caveats: (a) server stdout/stderr went to DEVNULL, so no prefill-timing numbers and MMQ=0
is confirmed only via env inheritance (the same mechanism as the bit-identical NOMMQ engine
runs); (b) 8 turns may be too tight — the MMQ=0 runs spent their turns reading instead of
looping, so a longer cap or a nudge-to-summarize might complete; (c) determinism does not
imply quality — this validates stability, not that summaries are good.

issues.title: [Performance]: NUMA-local binding on a dual-socket PC gives +37-40% prompt throughput (GTX 1080 Ti, 2x Xeon E5-2696 v4)
issues.author: MrKop-git
issues.body:
## What happened

On a dual-socket PC, the engine's pinned expert arena and its CPU pool spread across both NUMA nodes by first-touch. The GPU sits on one socket, so roughly half of its DMA and half of the CPU expert reads cross the inter-socket link. Binding everything to the GPU's node made prompt throughput **37-40% faster** and first-token times **27-32% shorter**, with no engine change.

## Hardware

- GPU: **NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (GP102, sm_61), 11 GiB GDDR5X, PCIe Gen3 x16** — on **NUMA node 1**
- CPU: **2x Intel Xeon E5-2696 v4** (22 cores / 44 threads each, 44c/88t total, Broadwell-EP, **no AVX-512**)
- RAM: 125.8 GiB (64 GiB per node); NVMe SSD
- Expert cache on this card: **1,513-1,514 slots** (hit rate 16-42%), so **58-84% of routed experts are computed on the CPU pool (AVX-2)** — the CPU side dominates decode
- A tiny GT 710 handles the display on NUMA node 0; the 1080 Ti at `84:00.0` does the compute

## The change

```bash
numactl --preferred=1 --cpunodebind=1 python serve/server.py ...
```

- `--preferred=1`: the 46.84 GiB pinned expert arena + 3.09 GiB pinned K/V land on node 1 (the GPU's node). Node 1's 64 GiB holds it beside ~6 GiB of system use.
- `--cpunodebind=1`: the expert pool's workers run on node 1's 22 cores (44 threads). This halves the available cores (22 vs 44 spread) — and is still **faster**, because the 44-core spread paid the 2.1x remote-memory penalty (NUMA distance 10 vs 21) on half its reads.
- Additionally we moved 184 non-Strata processes to node 0 and reserved node 1 for the engine (`AllowedCPUs=22-43,66-87` in a systemd drop-in), so the desktop does not steal cycles from the pool.

Also on this box: `vm.nr_hugepages` was 24000 (46.9 GiB reserved for MAP_HUGETLB). The engine needs 23,983 pages but found 8,221 already reserved, so MAP_HUGETLB failed every start and fell back to THP while the idle pool was invisible to normal allocations — the fallback load then tripped systemd-oomd (the unit was killed and restart-looped). Setting `vm.nr_hugepages = 0` removed the trap; the engine loads with THP + regular pages.

## Measured (the same suite, same card, same day)

| Metric | before (no binding) | **after (preferred=1 + cpunodebind=1)** |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4K prompt, fresh | 202.4 tok/s (201.1-202.8) | **276.3 tok/s (273.1-280.0)** (+36.6%) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 194.6 tok/s (193.5-196.7) | **272.6 tok/s (272.3-277.8)** (+40.1%) |
| 4K first token | 19.92 s | **14.62 s** (-26.6%) |
| agent turn first token | 25.60 s | **17.47 s** (-31.6%) |
| chat decode | 27.4 tok/s | 24.9 tok/s (within noise) |
| agent decode | 23.6 tok/s | 21.5 tok/s (within noise) |
| agent cache hit | 66.0% | 68.8% |

Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are client-side over HTTP; `tools/strata_bench.py` suite, 3 runs per test. Decode is unchanged because it is bound by the AVX-2 expert compute itself (local now, but the same 22 cores), not by memory locality.

The PCIe link (Gen3 x16, probe 11.6-11.9 GB/s) carries only ~200-257 MB/s during prompts — the interconnect is not the limiter either way; the win is the CPU-side reads hitting local DDR4 (4 channels ≈ 68 GB/s) instead of UPI (~19 GB/s shared).

## What this suggests for setup

A dual-socket PC whose GPU is on one socket gains from a start-time binding to that socket. Setup could read the GPU's `numa_node` sysfs attribute and, when it is >= 0 and the node has RAM for the arena, mention or apply the equivalent of `numactl --preferred=<gpu_node> --cpunodebind=<gpu_node>`. The engine already knows the arena size and the CPU topology. A `--numa auto|off|<node>` knob would make this a first-class option instead of a wrapper script.

## What was not tested

- The CPU-only side in isolation (binding memory but not CPUs, or vice versa) — we changed both at once and measured the combination.
- Whether `--cpunodebind=1` alone hurts on a PC whose GPU is on node 0 (the mirror case).
- AMD/EPYC (different interconnect and distances).
- Long-run stability (thermal, cache drift) under the binding — one suite, ~11 minutes.
- The hugepage trap's fix (`nr_hugepages=0`) on a PC that actually needs MAP_HUGETLB.

issues.title: [Feature]: fail the test build when a release-engine CUDA kernel spills or uses local memory (re-file of #1758, with the PR)
issues.author: Avicennasis
issues.body:
### What do you want to do?

Re-filing #1758, which the 2026-10-13 sweep closed as older than three days. The ask is unchanged; the difference is that the PR is filed right behind this issue and names it (`Resolves #…`), so both exist inside the three-day window.

A build-time check that fails `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS` when a CUDA kernel in the release engine spills registers to local memory or keeps a per-thread array there, per architecture in `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`.

**Why.** Strata carries per-architecture kernel tables and has found two defects that were compiler-output facts rather than source facts: #1522 (`gdn_l2_kernel` compiles without the fma the fused kernel spells out on CUDA 13.3 / sm_120) and #1469 (Pascal decode regression). A register spill is the same kind of fact: it shows up in the compiler's resource report and nowhere in the source, it varies by toolkit and `sm_`, and it costs decode throughput silently. Nothing in the tree reads that report today.

**Shape (what the PR does).** `tools/check_cuda_spills.py` reads the built kernel libraries with `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` and fails when a kernel's STACK or LOCAL bytes exceed what an exceptions table in the script allows for that (kernel, `sm_`) pair; the message names the kernel, the `sm_` and the two numbers. It is registered as the CTest `cuda_spill_guard` under `STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA AND STRATA_BUILD_TESTS` (not under HIP, where there is no `cuobjdump`), skips with 77 where `cuobjdump` or Python is missing, and mirrors `tools/check_isa_guard.py` in shape. No build-flag change: it reads the objects that were built anyway, and it needs no GPU at test time. The vendored llama.cpp ggml kernels (`mul_mat_q`, `quantize_*`) are skipped — they are the only kernels with no namespace, and they are llama.cpp's to gate. This is how DeepGEMM gates its kernels (`DG_JIT_CHECK_NO_SPILLS` / `DG_JIT_CHECK_NO_LOCAL_MEMORY`).

**Measured on `296b59d2` with CUDA 13.1 (nvcc V13.1.80), Release, `sm_86` and `sm_120`:** 1351 Strata kernels (359 once template instantiations are collapsed) across the eight kernel libraries; 150 (kernel, `sm_`) entries carry a stack frame — 61 are register spills in 21 distinct kernels (the largest `block_topk_reg_kernel`, 196 B of spill stores / 284 B of loads on sm_120 at the 64-register cap of its launch bounds; then `native_mmvq_il_kernel` 60/60 B and `native_gu_multi_kernel` 56/64 B) and 89 are spill-free per-thread arrays (`attn_chunk_kernel`'s 384-byte score tile the largest). LOCAL is 0 everywhere: on CUDA 13.1 both arrays and spills land in STACK. The exceptions table carries exactly those numbers — 37 entries, 53 (kernel, `sm_`) allowances, one line each saying what the array is or what spilled — so the first run documents the current state rather than failing on it; a later change that adds a spill or grows a local array is a red test naming the kernel. The spills themselves are findings, not fixed in the PR.

**Not measured:** sm_75 and sm_89 (the table is per-`sm_`; entries for them come from the first build on such a box), HIP and Windows, any timing or GPU behaviour, and why ptxas settles on different register counts per arch (e.g. `gr_down_q8_kernel<7>`: 128 registers + spills on sm_86, 206 registers and clean on sm_120).

If you would rather have the capture elsewhere (a CMake option, a CI step over the build log), say so on the PR and I will move it.
