issues.title: [sm_120 / RTX 6000D] native Q5_K head dequant crashes on long requests: "unspecified launch failure"
issues.author: mikesse
issues.body:
# GitHub Issue: native Q5_K head dequant crashes on long requests — "unspecified launch failure" on RTX PRO 6000D (Blackwell, sm_120)

> Copy-paste ready. Paste into https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/new

---

## Summary

On an **RTX PRO 6000D** (GB202, Blackwell 2.0, compute capability **12.0 / sm_120**), the **native Q5_K output head** dequant kernel crashes with:

```
dequant launch: unspecified launch failure
```

on **long requests**. Short requests (≤ ~10 tokens) work fine; anything from ~128 tokens up crashes the engine every time. The crash is tied to the native head dequant kernel (`native_q5_k_f32`), and it is **worse on newer engine versions** — an original (non-abliterated) native IQ pack that ran long requests cleanly on **v0.1.40.2** for days starts crashing at just **128 tokens on v0.1.44.1**.

This looks like the same class of architecture-guard bug already seen in your `#371` (qsa_prompt_attn_batch on sm_70): a kernel guard that checks only the compute-major version, so a kernel that is wrong for the actual device gets launched, and only fails on the larger grid / higher-memory path that a long request triggers.

## Environment

- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000D (Blackwell 2.0, GB202, compute capability 12.0)
- **CUDA Toolkit:** 13.3
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04
- **Pack:** native IQ pack — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S (IQ3_S), loaded with `--native SHARD1` (required; the pack refuses to start without it)
- **PLE:** `--ple-gguf` provided
- **Engine versions tested:** v0.1.40.2 (original pack runs cleanly), v0.1.44.1 (crashes)
- **Config flags:** `--expert-cache auto --prefill auto:16384 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <mtp>/rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --batch 6 --batch-mtp --vram-reserve-mib 15000`

## Reproduction

A native IQ pack with `--native` loads the native head (log line: `experimental native Q5_K head, 521472000 bytes, in 0.1 s`) and then `session is up`. After that:

- short prompt → OK
- long prompt (≥ ~128 tokens) → engine dies, last log line: `dequant launch: unspecified launch failure`

The engine exits with status 1; the next request restarts it.

## Test data (RTX PRO 6000D, native IQ IQ3_S pack, `--native`)

### Engine **v0.1.40.2** — original (non-abliterated) IQ3_S pack — all requests OK

| Request | gen tokens | decode speed (tok/s) | prompt speed (tok/s) | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| short (10) | 10 | 99.8 | 246 | 200 |
| medium (128) | 128 | 134.3 | 266 | 200 |
| long (512) | 512 | 151.0 | 559 | 200 |
| very long (1024) | 1024 | 161.1 | 553 | 200 |

### Engine **v0.1.44.1** — same original IQ3_S pack — crashes from medium up

| Request | gen tokens | decode speed (tok/s) | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| short (10) | 10 | 125.9 | 200 |
| medium (128) | — | — | **503** |
| long (512) | — | — | **503** |
| very long (1024) | — | — | **503** |

So v0.1.44.1 is a **regression** relative to v0.1.40.2 on this card: the native head dequant that used to survive long requests now fails at 128 tokens.

## Why I think it's an architecture-guard / sm_120 issue

1. Your own history of `unspecified launch failure` issues is dominated by **architecture-guard bugs** — e.g. `#371` (qsa_prompt_attn_batch on sm_70: the host guard compared only the major version 7 while the kernel needs sm_75, so a Turing kernel was launched on a V100 and hit `__trap()`). The native Q5_K head dequant (`native_q5_k_f32`, `native_head.cpp`) is a dedicated CUDA kernel; if its launch guard similarly checks only the major compute version, sm_120 could slip through and run a kernel whose PTX/instructions are not valid on Blackwell.
2. llama.cpp upstream has the same class of problem on Blackwell: `ggml-org/llama.cpp#19662` reports MXFP4 template instances failing to assemble for sm_120 with `"Instruction 'mma with block scale' not supported"`, and MMQ/dequant kernels crashing on sm_120 until built with a correct `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120` and a matching CUDA toolkit.
3. The **short-request OK / long-request-crash** pattern matches a kernel that is fine at small grid / low shared-memory but trips a hardware limit or unsupported instruction only on the larger launch path that a long context requires.

## Suggested fixes to look into

- Check whether the native Q5_K head dequant launch guard consults the **minor** compute version (like the `#371` fix did) and whether sm_120 needs a dedicated kernel path or a fallback to the canonical head.
- Verify the native head kernel is compiled for / validated on sm_120 (CUDA arch 120), same care as the Blackwell MMQ/dequant build guidance in `#19662`.
- Consider whether the native head can be disabled or routed to a portable path when the guard detects sm_120, so the canonical `output.weight` path is used instead.

## Attachments

Full engine log tail (startup → `session is up (engine 0.1.44.1)` → crash):

```
strata generate: experimental native Q5_K head, 521472000 bytes, in 0.1 s
strata generate: GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX 6000D, compute capability 12.0
...
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.44.1)
...
strata serve: 14571 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
dequant launch: unspecified launch failure
```

issues.title: [Engine] --expert-cache above the setup default kills the engine on Metal (Apple Silicon)
issues.author: ailabjeremy-ctrl
issues.body:
**Problem:** on the Metal backend, `--expert-cache` above the 64 that `metal/setup_mac.py` writes makes the engine exit 1 on any prompt shorter than the prefill chunk.

**Re-tested on `v0.2.0-beta` (engine `0.1.45.3-metal`) on 2026-10-19: still reproduces.** This is not a 0.1.45-only problem.

**Environment:** `v0.2.0-beta`, engine `0.1.45.3-metal`, built from the tag with `./setup.sh --update` and no local patches. macOS 27.0.1. Apple M1 Max, 24-core GPU, 64 GB unified memory. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 (full 512 experts, `--mmap-experts`), `--spec 2`, context 32768, `--prefill auto`.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
cd ~/Documents/AI/Strata-mac
# change only the expert cache in the shipped config
python3 -c "import json;c=json.load(open('strata-q2_0.json'));a=c['args'];a[a.index('--expert-cache')+1]='2048';json.dump(c,open('/tmp/cfg.json','w'))"
./.venv/bin/python ./serve/server.py --engine strata --config /tmp/cfg.json --port 8081
# then send any prompt shorter than the prefill chunk (it comes out at 5376 here)
```

**Expected:** the request is served. `--expert-cache 2048` is a legal value and the engine accepts it at boot (`filling the GPU's expert cache (2048 experts, 2.64 GiB of VRAM)`).

**Actual:** `POST /v1/chat/completions` returns 400, the engine exits 1, and the next request gets 503 while the server restarts it:

```
lending the prompt path its slots failed: prefill: relayout needs borrowed buffers and a chunk of at most 0
```

**Which prompts fail (this build, cache 2048, chunk 5376):**

| target tokens | actual prompt_n | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1,900 | — | 400, `lending the prompt path its slots failed ... at most 0` |
| 2,400 | — | 503 (engine restarting after the previous 400) |
| 3,000 | — | 400 (same message) |
| 3,800 | — | 503 |
| 4,800 | — | 400 (same message) |
| 7,140 | — | 503 |
| 9,000 | 7,251 | OK, prefill 174 tok/s |
| 13,000 | 10,460 | OK, prefill 284 tok/s |

The boundary is the chunk itself: below it the engine asks for a relayout and fails, above it the prompt fills the chunk and never asks. `--expert-cache 64` is unaffected and never enters that path (`the prompt path allocates its own buffers (too few cache slots to borrow)`).

**Which condition fails:** instrumenting the guard in `Prefill::relayout` names the clause:

```
DIAG relayout: clause=borrowed==false chunk=5120 T_max=0 borrowed=0 borrow_spill=0 borrow=0x178bfa1000
```

So it is `!m.borrowed`, not `chunk > m.T_max`. `borrow` is non-null while `borrowed` is 0: the caller passed the region, and `Prefill::init()` did not reach `m.borrowed = borrow != nullptr`.

**Not pack-specific:** ben0112 reports the same failure on an M5 Max 128 GB with UD-Q4_K_XL; this report is an M1 Max 64 GB with Q2_0. Different chip, memory and quant, same message and same threshold.

**A tested fix exists:** PR #3030 (a successful no-op `Prefill::relayout` on Metal, plus guarding the lend slot-marking loop; +16 lines, entirely inside `STRATA_GPU_METAL`) was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset together with this issue. It was verified on this exact configuration before the reset — cherry-picked onto v0.1.45, `--expert-cache 6144` with chunk 8192: before, a ~6,000-token prompt died 3 of 3; after, prompts of 1,235 / 2,439 / 4,043 / 4,845 / 5,648 / 6,605 / 10,462 tokens all completed with the engine up and no `at most 0` or `given back`. The Metal branch is all I can vouch for; I have not built the CUDA, HIP or SYCL backends.

**Mode 2 (`given back` SIGABRT) is not claimed as fixed.** I never reproduced it on this machine (at `--expert-cache 64` the lend path is never entered) and it did not appear in this re-test either.

**Reproduction status:** reproduced locally, on `v0.2.0-beta`, three times per prompt length, with a fresh nonce each time so `cache_n` is 0.

issues.title: Network Issues with Strata caused by AdGuard
issues.author: Adonist
issues.body:
Model and engine
Model qwen3.8-flash-next-coder-iq1_m
Engine v0.1.44.1
Context 32,768 tokens
KV cache 8-bit, all in VRAM
Experts in VRAM 1,937 (3.7 GB)
Speculation MTP drafts up to 3 tokens, prompt lookup on
Images on

PC
GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070, 12 GB
CPU Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900F, 32 threads
RAM 64 GB

OS:  Windows 11 Pro
Version: 26H2
OS Build: 26300.9457

AdGuard 8.0.2

My deployment was causing intermitent network connectivity. It kept switching between "Server Not Reachable" to "idle" and failing 1 in 3 requests.
After a lengthy troubleshooting session, turns out the my local AdGuard installation was causing the issue.
Disabling loopback filtering seems to have sorted it from: Settings -> App Settings -> Advanced -> Filter localhost.
I also added the strata and python executables in the "Exclude apps from filtering by their full path".
One of the steps to troubleshoot it was using powershell + simple python server to loop through requests and see if it failed:

1..50 | % {
curl.exe -s -o NUL -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/
 if ($LASTEXITCODE) { " FAIL exit $LASTEXITCODE" } else { "" }
} | Group-Object | Select Count, Name

Also checking providers in the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). Getting an export with:
netsh wfp show state file=C:\Temp\wfpstate.xml

Then checking for <providerKey> and <name> for anything 3rd party.

I hope this helps someone

issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 48GB and 64GB system RAM
_(Custom RTX 4090 with doubled VRAM. Should be on par with RTX 6000 Ada)_

Measured on 2026-10-15 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 48 GiB VRAM (Water Cooled)
- CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E3-1220 v6 @ 3.00GHz (4 cores, 4 threads); 
- installed RAM: 60.7 GiB (DDR4-2666); 
- storage: ADATA XPG MARS 980 (2000000 IOPS)
- OS: Linux 7.2.6-070206-generic; GPU driver: 615.71.09; CUDA: 13.3
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit not a git checkout; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads and power limits: 4090 at 300W limit

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl
- Context: 262144 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --resident-budget-gib 33 --pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 2
```

Environment of the config: `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (started by the benchmark from the install configuration); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

issues.title: Peer-expert tier (--peer-device 1) crashes on first prompt: "iq_dequant_gu_f16: an illegal memory access"
issues.author: CaptRauti
issues.body:
## Bug: two-GPU peer-expert tier (`--peer-device 1`) crashes on the first prompt — "iq_dequant_gu_f16: an illegal memory access"

**Engine:** 0.1.41 (locally built for this CPU)
**OS:** Windows 11 (WDDM)
**Hardware:** 2x NVIDIA RTX 3060 12 GB, Intel Xeon E5-2697 v2 (no AVX2), 128 GB RAM
**Model:** swift-1.5-iq2_xs (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MoE), context 128000, KV q4_0, `--kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB=26`

### Reproduction

Run on two GPUs (config `gpu: [0, 1]`) with `--peer-device 1`, so CUDA1 becomes an adaptive expert-cache tier instead of a layer split. The engine starts cleanly and fills the peer tier, but the **first** ~5.3k-token prompt crashes it deterministically:

```
strata generate: --trim-stage-weights needs a layer split across GPUs (ignored)
strata generate: expert cache 3353 slots, 4.49 GiB of VRAM; policy is
strata generate: peer GPU 1: 7723 experts, 10.36 GiB (filled in 4.5 s); with the primary's 3353 that is 11076 of 24576 on the GPUs
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.41)
strata serve: prompt chunk auto: 7936 tokens, a 96-slot ring
strata prefill: peer GPU 1 computes its experts' rows of each prompt chunk (up to 79360 rows per layer, no P2P: through mapped host memory in FP16, one weighted sum per token back, compact group buffers); 0 MiB left free on it
strata serve: 443 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
iq_dequant_gu_f16: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Crash site: `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:3679` (`iq_dequant_gu_f16` on the P6 native-pack dequant path).

### Not a VRAM-shortage (already ruled out)

All three crash identically on the same first prompt:
- `--vram-reserve-mib 700` (baseline): 443 MiB free on CUDA0, peer card 0 MiB free
- `--vram-reserve-mib 1800` (primary reserve raised): 1497 MiB free on CUDA0 — same crash
- `--prefill auto:8192` (smaller prompt chunks, per the engine's own startup hint) + `--peer-reserve-mib 1200`: same crash, peer card 679 MiB free

With no peer tier the same model+prompts run fine on the same two cards as a layer split.

### Why this matters

The peer tier is a big win for small cards: primary 3353 + peer 7723 = **11076 of 24576 experts on the GPUs**, versus ~5,700 on the two-card layer split for the same model. If the peer prefill path could run without the illegal access, small-VRAM dual-GPU boxes would get a substantial decode lift.

Repro args: `--serve --pack ... --expert-cache auto --prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ... --max-context 128000 --kv q4_0 --kv-resident 32768 --peer-device 1`

Happy to attach the full engine logs or run further diagnostics.

issues.title: Community benchmark: Apple M1 Max (24-core GPU, 32 GB), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 (Metal, streaming)
issues.author: qramo
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on Apple M1 Max (24-core GPU, Metal)

Measured on 2026-10-16 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

> Note: `strata_bench.py` probes `nvidia-smi`/`rocm-smi` for the GPU and, finding neither on macOS, auto-labelled this run "CPU only". That is a detection gap, not the actual device: the run used the **Apple M1 Max 24-core GPU via Metal** (engine build `0.1.44.1-metal`, `--mmap-experts` streaming). The hardware fields below are filled in by hand; all timing numbers are the tool's unmodified output.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: Apple M1 Max, 24-core GPU, Metal 4. No dedicated VRAM — 32 GiB unified memory shared with the system. On 32 GiB the Q2_0 pack (~37.6 GB mapped) does not fit Metal's resident share (~26 GiB), so the experts stream from the SSD automatically (`--mmap-experts`); the OS file cache serves them as the GPU's expert cache fills.
- CPU: Apple M1 Max (10 cores: 8 performance + 2 efficiency); installed RAM: 32.0 GiB unified; storage: Apple NVMe SSD (AP0512R, 500 GB, TRIM supported).
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Darwin 25.5.0, build 25F80); Metal 4; GPU driver: n/a (Metal, built into the OS).
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1-metal (built from source).
- Background workloads and power limits: desktop idle, no other GPU workload during the run; on AC power.

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-q2_0
- Context: 32768 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
- 4K / 16K prompts: generated word lists sized by a calibration request, 24 new tokens, 3 fresh prompts each
- agent session: system prompt and four tools, then 5 turns that each add about 1500 words of a project file and continue from the model's own earlier answers (the way agent clients resend a conversation), 64 new tokens per turn, 3 sessions; the cache numbers come from the answer's usage (`cached_tokens`) and timings (`prompt_n`)
- concurrency (when run): N requests sent at the same moment, total tokens over the wall time of the burst, latency over all requests

## Results

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Reused tokens | Generated tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s median and range | Decode tok/s median and range | TTFT seconds median and range |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |

| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 (16058-16058) | 0 (0-0) | 24 cap | 3 | 287.1 (285.5-287.2) | not measured | 55.99 (55.98-56.31) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14514 (14509-14532) at the last turn | see below | up to 64 | 3 | see below | 16.6 (14.1-19.6) | 11.95 (6.92-14.74) |

Ranges are the lowest and highest of the runs; `Runs` counts requests that returned a token.

### Agent session (conversation cache)

Cache hit over the follow-up turns: 68.7 % (68.7-68.7); earlier-turn tokens read again per session: 5 (5-5) (earlier turns that the cache did not hold; the 13730 (13730-13730) new tokens of the files are read once); first turn (nothing cached) first token: 3.33 s (3.32-3.34).

| Turn (run 1) | Prompt tokens | Reused | Read | Prompt tok/s | First token (s) | Decode tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 609 | 0 | 609 | 186.2 | 3.33 | 14.1 |
| 1 | 3751 | 628 | 3123 | 237.0 | 13.238 | 14.1 |
| 2 | 5284 | 3814 | 1470 | 210.4 | 7.043 | 15.3 |
| 3 | 8728 | 5347 | 3381 | 232.3 | 14.616 | 16.5 |
| 4 | 11616 | 8754 | 2862 | 240.8 | 11.946 | 18.5 |
| 5 | 14532 | 11633 | 2899 | 240.0 | 12.14 | 19.6 |

Per-request data: `results.json`. Engine log lines from the start: `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (when this run started the server).

## Correctness and limitations

Not measured: this is a speed suite. The conversation uses the model's own replies, so token counts differ a little between runs. Machine details were filled in by hand (the tool cannot read a Metal GPU); background load and power limits are as noted above. Total time of the suite: 540 s.

The 32K prompt test (`--long`) was skipped: the install's context is 32768 tokens, so a ~32K prompt leaves no room for the generation, and the tool skips it. 16K is the longest prompt measured here. The suite was run twice with closely matching numbers (chat decode 14.7 / 14.9 tok/s, 4K prompt 289 / 286 tok/s, 16K prompt 287 / 286 tok/s), so the medians above are reproducible.

For context, Strata's own `docs/MAC.md` measures Q2_0 on a 32 GB **M4 Mac mini** (streaming) up to a 4K prompt: ~14 tok/s decode and ~94 tok/s on the 4K prompt. This M1 Max 32 GB run lands at a similar ~15 tok/s decode but ~287 tok/s fresh-prompt throughput — about 3x the M4 mini's prompt speed (the 24-core GPU and wider memory bandwidth; decode stays SSD-bound, so it matches). 16K and the agent session are beyond what the official M4 mini report covers. A previously unreported Apple Silicon configuration.

issues.title: Long-session decode drift on WSL2 + RTX 3090 24 GB at 262K: 59.3 → 80.0 tok/s in the last third; --kv-grow + reserve 1216 cuts the drift from −29% to −4.5%
issues.author: david-zdw
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** engine 0.1.44.1, source build (CUDA 13.4, `sm_86`) · RTX 3090 24 GB · **WSL2** Ubuntu 26.04 on Windows, host 128 GB RAM, `.wslconfig` `memory=96GB swap=0` · AMD Threadripper PRO 3975WX (AVX2, no AVX-512)

Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO **IQ3_S**, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --expert-profile --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp … --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700`, plus the experimental speed projection on (identical in both arms). One slot, no `--batch`.

This is the long-soak arm `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` asks for ("an hour or more of back-to-back requests … shows drift"), and it found drift.

## What happened

One engine start at 17:30, back-to-back agent traffic (multi-turn tool use, contexts 10K–80K), 124 requests with the engine's own per-request `decode_tok_s`, `hit_rate` and draft counts. Splitting that run into thirds by request order:

| | decode tok/s | expert hit | draft accept | mean context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first third | 84.0 | 83.4% | 78.9% | 47,461 |
| middle third | 77.2 | 84.1% | 79.3% | 69,512 |
| last third | **59.3** | 83.1% | 74.2% | **35,765** |

Whole run: mean 73.4, median 76.3, p10 55.5, min 40.5.

The control that matters: **hit rate stayed flat** (83.4% → 84.1% → 83.1%) while decode fell 29%, and the last third ran at a *shorter* mean context than the first. So this is not content, not cache warming, and not context length.

It is not clocks either: at load the card sat at 1890 MHz / 69–70 °C / 210–287 W against a 350 W limit, and `SW Thermal Slowdown`, `HW Thermal Slowdown`, `HW Power Brake` and `SW Power Cap` were all `Not Active` in `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE`.

The tell is the engine's own line, which escalated across the first six requests:

```
strata serve: 274 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
strata serve: WARNING: only 274 MiB of VRAM free at the start of this request (below 512 MiB): … (#2065). Add --vram-reserve-mib 960 …
strata serve: WARNING: only 140 MiB of VRAM free … Add --vram-reserve-mib 1088 …
strata serve: WARNING: only   0 MiB of VRAM free … Add --vram-reserve-mib 1216 …
```

The sizer had priced the whole 262K K/V up front: `expert cache auto: 13.85 GiB free, 700 MiB reserved … -> 5224 slots`, then after shrinking `expert cache 6180 slots, 11.73 GiB of VRAM`, leaving 274 MiB on the card before any request ran.

## The change, and what it did

Two flags only, everything else byte-identical, second engine start at 21:39:

```
--kv int8 --kv-grow --vram-reserve-mib 1216      # was: --kv int8 --vram-reserve-mib 700
```

At start: `elastic K/V: 16384 of 262144 cells in VRAM (0.25 of 3.35 GiB); the expert cache (7411 slots) gives the K/V room below slot 5222 as the context grows`.

Both arms below are the **whole session** — all 124 requests before, all 54 after, no windowing:

| | before (n=124) | after (n=54) |
|---|---|---|
| expert cache | 6,180 slots / 12,012 MiB | **7,411 slots / 14,388 MiB** (+20%) |
| `vram_free_mib` at load | 274 | 803 |
| free during a request | 0–140 MiB | 587–871 MiB |
| decode mean / median | 73.4 / 76.3 | **82.8 / 81.4** |
| decode p10 / min | 55.5 / 40.5 | **73.4 / 66.4** |
| prefill aggregate (Σ read ÷ Σ prompt_ms) | 1,291 tok/s | **1,559 tok/s** |
| expert hit / draft accept | 83.6% / 77.4% | 82.6% / 73.3% |
| mean context | 50,791 | 73,102 |

Whole run, and the same split:

| | decode tok/s | expert hit | draft accept | mean context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first third | 83.8 | 80.6% | 75.5% | 44,520 |
| middle third | 84.5 | 82.9% | 76.4% | 62,617 |
| last third | 80.0 | 84.4% | 68.1% | **112,170** |

**The drift is much smaller, but it is not gone.** The before-run lost 29% from its first third to its last; the after-run loses 4.5%, and its last third runs at a **2.5× longer** mean context (112,170 vs 44,520) than its first — where the before-run's last third was at a *shorter* context. So the change bought a large level improvement and a much flatter shape, not a flat line.

Note the control now cuts the other way: hit rate and draft acceptance are **lower** after the change (83.6%→82.6%, 77.4%→73.3%) in exchange for +13% decode *and* +44% mean context. Fewer expert hits and fewer accepted drafts, still faster — so the gain is not an easier traffic mix.

## What `--kv-grow` costs, measured

During the steady climb the K/V takes ~52–57 slots per 8,192-cell step (`K/V grown to 81920 cells (1.07 GiB); the expert cache gave 56 slots for it … 6919 of 7411 slots hold experts`), and it gives them back when a session ends (`K/V grown to 16384 cells` again). It is not uniform, though: the *first* climb through a region is far more expensive than the second. Growing to 65,536 cells cost **326 slots** the first time and 56 the second, and 122,880 cells cost **218 slots** in a single move — so the cache re-learns which experts it can afford as the window moves. The cache also compacts as it goes (`7355 of 7411 slots hold experts` after a give-back). The cost is a slope, not a cliff:

| context | n | decode mean |
|---|---|---|
| 5–30K | 4 | 86.7 |
| 30–55K | 7 | 81.3 |
| 55–70K | 20 | 86.8 |
| 70–90K | 11 | 81.1 |
| 90K+ | 11 | 78.1 |

At 70–90K the `#2065` warning fires again (`only 414 MiB free`, `only 136 MiB free`) even with the 1216 MiB reserve, and decode settles at 78.1 above 90K — which is the same region the last third of the table above is measuring.

## Questions

1. **Should `--expert-cache auto` price the `--max-context` reservation differently on a card this full?** Setup wrote 262,144 with the whole-K/V default on a 24 GB card and left 274 MiB free at load. `--kv-grow`'s preconditions (one GPU, expert profile, no KV streaming, all experts in RAM) were all already true here — would it be worth defaulting it on, or having setup pick it, when they hold and the whole-K/V sizing lands under ~1 GiB free?
2. **The warning's suggested reserve climbs per request** (960 → 1088 → 1216). Could the start-up sizer begin at the value it would end up asking for, instead of discovering it over the first six requests?
3. **WSL2 has no fallback here.** `--kv-resident` is not usable (the WSL NVIDIA driver pins ~1 GB, as `docs/DETAILS.md` notes), so `--kv-grow` is the only path on WSL2 + 24 GB + a long context. Worth a line in the WSL notes, and maybe a setup warning for that combination?
4. **Is the 70–90K dip expected from ~55 slots per 8,192 cells**, or is there a cheaper place to take it from? The first-pass steps (326 slots at 65,536 cells, 218 at 122,880) look like a different regime from the steady ~55 — is re-learning the cache on the first climb through a region avoidable?

## Limits, stated plainly

- **The two arms are different traffic windows, not an interleaved A/B**, and the after-run is shorter (54 requests vs 124) while carrying a **longer** mean context (73,102 vs 50,791) — so the raw means are not a like-for-like speedup. The case for the change is the shape of the thirds plus the hit-rate/acceptance control above.
- **The client is the same engine** (this session serves the agent that ran the analysis), the same caveat as #1986.
- **Drift is reduced, not eliminated** — the after-run's last third is still 4.5% below its first, and decode keeps falling above 90K (78.1 mean). One engine session per arm; no multi-day number.
- Real agent traffic, not `BENCH.bat`: no fresh-prompt sweep, no needle recall, no quality check, no concurrency. Nothing about correctness is claimed.
- No cold-boot numbers; the OS page cache was warm in both arms. `--vision` was on in both — I did not test the vision-on-CPU change from #2406, which looks relevant on a card this full.

## Reproducing

Numbers come from the engine's own lines (`prompt … generated in … tok/s, drafts accepted …`, `hit rate: …`, `K/V grown to …`) and `GET /metrics`, never from dividing tokens by wall time. The parsing script is two regexes over `strata-<model>.log`, split at `engine started`; happy to add it as a `tools/` script or a `bench/results/` folder if that is the right shape.

issues.title: BENCH.bat crashes on Japanese-locale Windows: UnicodeDecodeError (cp932) reading CMakeLists.txt
issues.author: qramo
issues.body:
**What happens**

On Windows with a Japanese system locale (ANSI code page 932), `BENCH.bat` stops before measuring anything:

```text
Using the Strata server already running at http://127.0.0.1:8080.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 1028, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 989, in main
    pre = collect_machine(base, key, cfg, a.gpu)
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 639, in collect_machine
    "strata_version": project_version(), "strata_commit": git_commit(),
  File "D:\Strata\tools\strata_bench.py", line 564, in project_version
    m = re.search(r"project\(strata VERSION ([\d.]+)", (ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text())
  ...
UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0xef in position 0: illegal multibyte sequence
```

**Cause**

`CMakeLists.txt` starts with a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). `Path.read_text()` without `encoding=` uses the locale's code page on Windows, which is cp932 here. On English-locale Windows (cp1252) the BOM decodes without error, which is probably why this hasn't come up.

**Fix**

```python
# tools/strata_bench.py:564
(ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
```

Other `read_text()` calls without an encoding in `tools/` could fail the same way on CJK-locale Windows if they read files containing non-ASCII bytes. The ones in `strata_bench.py` at lines 448 and 471 read `/proc` and are Linux-only, so they're fine.

**Workaround**

`set PYTHONUTF8=1` before running `BENCH.bat`. With that, the benchmark completes normally.

**Environment**

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 (Japanese), Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2), Python 3.13 venv created by setup.

issues.title: layer-split auto gives an asymmetric pair 3 of 48 layers (12 GB idle, -44% prefill)
issues.author: Tworks25
issues.body:
## What happens

On an **asymmetric** two-GPU pair, `layer-split auto` assigns almost all layers to one card, leaving most of the second card's VRAM unused for the whole run.

Measured on RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB (48 layers, Strata 0.1.44.1, `296b59d2`, Flash-Next IQ3_S):

```
layer split, CUDA1: 5.50 GiB free of 11.63, room for experts 4.72 GiB
layer split: CUDA1 runs layers 18-47 ...     (with a manual split)
```

With `auto`, the engine log reports:

```
layer split auto: K=2 would give a stage fewer than 3 layers (a tiny expert cache
  there clamps the prompt chunk of every card, #1616); chose K=3 instead
layer split: CUDA1 runs layers 3-47, expert cache 4263 slots
layer split: CUDA0 runs layers 0-2
```

So the RTX 3060 got **3 of 48 layers**. Through an entire 14,564-token prefill it drew **17 W** (idle power) and sat at ~0-1 % utilisation while the 4060 Ti ran at 100 %:

```
samples (1/s) during prefill, host CPU busy% | GPU0 util,mem,power | GPU1 util,mem,power
 8  cpu_busy=9%  gpus=[0, 100, 11614, 50.58; 1, 100, 15555, 102.25;]
10  cpu_busy=19% gpus=[0, 100, 11614, 135.79; 1,   8, 15559, 100.07;]
12  cpu_busy=16% gpus=[0, 100, 11614, 138.12; 1,   0, 15730,  31.58;]
```

Host CPU was ~3 % and cross-card expert traffic measured 0.0-4.1 % of routed experts, so neither the CPU nor the PCIe link was the limit — the split itself was.

## Cost

Identical cold 14,564-token prompt, fresh server per point, only `layer_split` changed:

| `layer_split` | RTX 3060 layers | RTX 4060 Ti layers | prefill tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `auto` | 3 | 45 | 452.6 |
| 12 | 12 | 36 | 581.8 |
| 18 | 18 | 30 | 693.0 |
| 24 | 24 | 24 | 761.7 |
| **28** | **28** | **20** | **802.1** |
| 32 | 32 | 16 | 803.2 |

**`auto` costs 44 % of prefill throughput on this pair** versus split 28, where the curve plateaus. Decode improves too (41.8 → 50.4 tok/s chat median; 25.1 → 36.2 agent median), presumably because fewer layers per card lets each expert cache cover its own layers better.

## A diagnostic that may be worth documenting

With the mis-set split, prefill is **flat in prompt length** — 491.7 tok/s at 4K, 512.1 at 16K, no batching benefit. With split 28 it becomes a slope: 488.2 at 4K, 835.0 at 16K. Note the 4K number is unchanged, so **a 4K-only benchmark cannot see this**. Anyone tuning from a short prompt would conclude the install is fine.

## Which way the split should go is not intuitive

The obvious rule — give the faster card proportionally more layers — predicts the wrong direction here. What tracked the result was **memory bandwidth**, not SM count or FP32 TFLOPS: the RTX 3060 has 360 GB/s against the 4060 Ti's 288 GB/s, so it is the better host for expert-heavy layers despite fewer and slower SMs. That is an argument for a bandwidth-aware automatic split rather than a compute-aware one.

## Reproduction

```
RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB (CUDA1) + RTX 3060 12 GB (CUDA0), 48 layers
Strata 0.1.44.1, original Flash-Next IQ3_S, --max-context 262144 --kv int8
strata-iq3_s.json:  "gpu": [1, 0],  "layer_split": "auto"
```

Then set `"layer_split"` to `12` / `18` / `24` / `28` / `32` and cold-prefill one fixed long prompt against a freshly started server at each value.

## Related

Full benchmark and the sweep are in PR #2643, which adds the report under `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rtx-4060-ti-plus-rtx-3060-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-s-3/`.

## Not claiming

The `auto` heuristic avoids a real failure mode (#1616 — a stage whose tiny expert cache clamps the prompt chunk of every card). I did not observe that clamping at any split I tested, but I only tested this one pair, on one model, at one context length. If a bandwidth-aware balance would reintroduce #1616 on other hardware, the tradeoff may well be deliberate — in which case documenting "sweep `layer_split` on asymmetric pairs" would be enough.

issues.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 2-GPU `--pipeline-windows 2` + MTP: "verify: layer N never rang" (illegal memory access), engine exits on an 18k-token prompt (0.1.44.1, 2x 7900 XTX)
issues.author: dinesh-chander
issues.body:
**Setup:** 2× Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB each) on one box, Strata **v0.1.44.1** (commit `296b59d2`), Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38, HIP **7.16.26385-0000000** (`amdrocm-core10.1-gfx1100 10.1.0-3`), Intel Core Ultra 7 265K, 93 GiB DDR5. Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next unsloth **UD-Q4_K_XL**, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 200000`.

Exact flags (both runs identical except `--adapt-every`):

```
--serve --pack <pack> --native <gguf> --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin
--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --short-read 260 --pipeline-windows 2 --spec 4
--mtp <mtp/rt> --max-context 200000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision
--vram-reserve-mib 3072 --pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 13
--adapt-every 1 (run A) / 0 (run B) --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97
--conversation-cache-mib 8192 --layer-split auto
```

env: `STRATA_PF_GEMM=1`, `STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1`, `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=<gfx1100 tuning file>`. Layer split auto → K=24 (CUDA0 layers 0-23, CUDA1 24-47 + head); the pw2 cost line reports "272 MiB of CUDA0 kept out of the expert cache" (expert cache CUDA1 4933 → 4879 slots).

**Symptom.** With `--pipeline-windows 2` the pipelined decode dies on a **~18k-token prompt** (cold read, `max_tokens` 256, temperature 0):

```
strata serve: pipelined decode: verify: layer 47 never rang (an illegal memory access was encountered)
```

The engine then exits (`exit code 1`) or is reloaded, and the client sees:

| run | request | HTTP | message |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (`--adapt-every 1`) | 16384 cold r1 | 400 | `verify: layer 47 never rang (an illegal memory access was encountered)` |
| A | 16384 cold r2 | 503 | `the engine said nothing for 684 s` |
| B (`--adapt-every 0`) | 16384 cold r1 | 400 | `verify: layer 36 never rang (unspecified launch failure)` |
| B | 16384 cold r2 | 503 | `the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 1); the next request...` |

**Turning off the adaptive expert swap changes the symptom, not the outcome.** This was the obvious suspect (a synchronous adaptive swap racing a pipelined speculative window), so the same 18k prompt was run with `--adapt-every 0`: different layer (36 vs 47) and a different HIP error (`unspecified launch failure` 719 vs `illegal memory access` 700), but it still faults. The pipelined decode path itself is the trigger on gfx1100.

**Reproduce rate:** 2/2 runs, 2/2 `--adapt-every` settings, always on the first 16384-token request of the session (real prompt length 18 228 tokens, cold, no cache reuse).

**Small prompts are fine, and the payoff is large** — which is why this is worth fixing rather than just documenting:

| prompt length | result | decode, pw0 → pw2 |
|---|---|---|
| 128 / 512 / 4096 tokens (run A) | clean, 4 passes each | cold 54.5→75.2 / 53.5→80.8 / 52.5→73.5 tok/s; cached 54.5→93.4 / 53.5→82.0 / 52.5→79.6 |
| 128 and 4096 tokens (run B) | clean, 4 passes each | cold tg 87.7 / 81.6; cached tg 85.4 / 76.9 |
| **16384 tokens** (both runs) | **fault** | — |

Prefill is flat (503.8 → 504.9 tok/s at 4096): the gain is entirely decode, up to ×1.7 over pw0 — the serial stage alternation disappearing, as intended.

**Verbatim engine log, run A (`--adapt-every 1`):**

```
strata serve: suffix drafts: 1 windows, 2 of 5 drafts accepted
strata serve: conversation cache: parked 5061 tokens in 140.1 ms; ...
strata serve: pipelined decode: verify: layer 47 never rang (an illegal memory access was encountered)
strata serve: adaptive swap copy failed (layer 7, slot 3984, pinned 0): an illegal memory access was encountered
strata: released the verify window's GPU waits (#267): the GPU finished in 0 ms        (×4)
Hip error: 'an illegal memory access was encountered'(700) at /__w/rockrel/rockrel/rocm-libraries/projects/hipblaslt/library/src/amd_detail/hipblaslt.cpp:204
hipModuleUnload failed:  error: an illegal memory access was encountered             (×6)
[strata] ... engine started: ... --adapt-every 1 ...                          <- engine reload
```

**Run B (`--adapt-every 0`):**

```
strata serve: suffix drafts: 5 windows, 19 of 25 drafts accepted
strata serve: conversation cache: parked 5222 tokens in 140.2 ms; ...
strata serve: pipelined decode: verify: layer 36 never rang (unspecified launch failure)
strata: released the verify window's GPU waits (#267): the GPU finished in 0 ms        (×4)
Hip error: 'unspecified launch failure'(719) at /__w/rockrel/rockrel/rocm-libraries/projects/hipblaslt/library/src/amd_detail/hipblaslt.cpp:204
hipModuleUnload failed:  error: unspecified launch failure                           (×6)
[strata] ... engine started: ... --adapt-every 0 ...                          <- engine reload
```

The `#267` lines are the watchdog firing *after* the fault — the cause is the verify window never ringing, not the 5 s watchdog.

**Why a gfx1100 box reaches this at all.** `--pipeline-windows 2` is auto-off on gfx1100 (`decode_defaults_arch_ok()` is gfx12-WMMA-only on HIP), but passing the flag explicitly skips that gate: the `pipeline_windows > 0` validation in `generate.cpp` checks serve / layer split / MTP / `--batch` / `--peer-device` / helper caches and never the arch, so the engine starts the pipelined path with no warning that the arch's measured defaults (route tail skip, PCIe share) do not apply. `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` ("`--pipeline-windows 2` asks for it on any split") reads as "supported on any split". Either honour the gate with a refusal/warning on gfx1100, or fix the decode path there.

**Workaround:** `--pipeline-windows 0` restores stability — the identical flag set (pw0) ran the full length sweep including 65536 tokens without any verify fault. The engine is back on pw0 here.

**Related:** #2245 (gfx1030 2-GPU pw2 + MTP → #267 verify *hang*, bisected to `6126f8d`; that one stalls the MEC, this one raises a HIP fault) · #267 · #1341 (closed, >100k prompt deadlocks the pipelined verify-window reader) · #1740 (closed, Windows pw2 stall) · #1447 (closed, docs: pw2 and `--adapt-async 1` combine).

Happy to re-run with a minimal flag set (dropping `--short-read`, the `STRATA_*` env, `--vision`), to bisect the prompt-length boundary between 4.9k and 18.2k, or to try #2245's `STRATA_ATTN_LANECELL=1` on gfx11 if that is useful.

Причина найдена! На твоих скриншотах есть всё необходимое для диагностики.

Сравним локальный файл с оригиналом на Hugging Face:

| Параметр  | Локальный файл            | Hugging Face                  |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------- |

| SHA256    | `610922CD...E1B6AE4BB69F` | `610922cdb1af...e1b6ae4bb69f` |
| Результат | Совпадает                 | VERIFIED                      |

Файл скачан полностью и не повреждён. Его SHA256 совпадает с контрольной суммой оригинала.

Ошибка находится в проверке размера Strata: установщик ожидает `10 946 624` байта, тогда как официальный файл содержит `10 946 618` байт — разница ровно шесть байт.

Повторно скачивать файл не нужно.

## Как исправить Strata

Я проверил исходный код `setup.py` в репозитории Strata. Проблема находится в функции `check_shards()`: она сравнивает размер файла с вычисленным концом области тензоров. 

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://raw.githubusercontent.com\&sz=32)

GitHub



У твоей первой части GGUF, согласно метаданным на скриншоте:

- `tensor_count = 0` — файл содержит метаданные, а не веса модели.
- Вычисленное начало области тензоров находится на 6 байт дальше фактического конца файла.
- Сам файл полностью совпадает с официальным SHA256.

То есть проверка ошибочно требует наличие выравнивающих байтов, хотя в этом файле нет тензоров.

Предлагаю точечное исправление с резервной копией.

В `D:\github\Strata` выполни:

```
Copy-Item .\setup.py .\setup.py.bak

$path = ".\setup.py"
$code = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText((Resolve-Path $path).Path)

$old = "if have < need:"
$new = "if g.tensors and have < need:"

if (($code.Split([string[]]@($old), [StringSplitOptions]::None).Count - 1) -ne 1) {
    throw "Проверка встречается не один раз. Файл не изменён."
}

$code = $code.Replace($old, $new)
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Resolve-Path $path).Path, $code)

python -m py_compile .\setup.py
```

Изменение означает: проверять ожидаемый размер области тензоров только в файлах, где эти тензоры действительно присутствуют. Для остальных частей модели защита от обрезанных данных сохраняется.

После успешной проверки синтаксиса повтори:

```
.\START-HERE.bat --setup
```

Выбирай те же настройки: `4 → 3 → 4 → 1 → n`.

Это локальный обход ошибки установщика, а не официальное исправление. Если Strata всё-таки остановится на следующем этапе, пришли новый вывод — проверим уже конкретную причину, не меняя сами GGUF-файлы.

issues.title: Linux CUDA/Xid crashes on RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB: repeated short prompts and 16K+ prefill; same machine reportedly works on Windows
issues.author: fdk3r6b
issues.body:
# Linux CUDA/Xid crashes on RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB: repeated short prompts and 16K+ prefill; same machine reportedly works on Windows

## Summary

Strata v0.1.44.1 intermittently fails on short requests and repeatedly fails during longer prefill on this Ubuntu machine. NVIDIA kernel logs show Xid 11/13/31/69 across the investigation. The engine reports CUDA launch failures, sometimes an illegal memory access or cuBLAS execution failure. Text, vision and native 128K context are the intended workload; this installation is **not reliably usable** yet.

The owner reports that the same hardware, model, images and 128K workload work on Windows. The exact Windows driver/build and a matched Windows log are not yet available, so this is an owner-reported comparison, not a controlled benchmark.

**Root cause is unknown.** We are seeking guidance on distinguishing an engine bug, CUDA/driver issue, or platform interaction. We have not established a defective GPU, an unsupported CPU, a firmware defect, or an IOMMU root cause.

## Environment

| Component | Recorded configuration |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | MSI GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GB, PCI device ID 2d04 |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, Zen 2, AVX2 supported; no AVX-512 |
| Motherboard | ASUS TUF B350M-PLUS GAMING |
| BIOS | 6254; newest listed version when checked during investigation |
| RAM | 64 GB, four 16 GB DIMMs from mixed A-DATA/G.Skill kits; tested at 3000 and 2666 MT/s |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS |
| Current recorded kernel | 6.8.0-147-generic |
| Current recorded driver | NVIDIA open kernel module 615.71.09, Ubuntu package 615.71.09-0ubuntu0.24.04.2 |
| Engine | v0.1.44.1, built by official Linux setup workflow; BUILD.json records CUDA 13.0, arch 120, source 7dfd34378bd2d32a; GCC 13.3 |
| Model | ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF, IQ2_XS |
| Context | 131072; INT8 KV; KV resident 32768; vision enabled |
| PCIe | x8 negotiated width; measured host-to-device probe about 7.1 GB/s |
| BAR1 | 16 GiB after CSM disabled / Above 4G Decoding Auto; previously 256 MiB |
| Current recorded kernel arguments | ro quiet splash iommu.passthrough=1 iommu.strict=1 vt.handoff=7 |

Current configuration has an empty `env` object. `--no-ple-prefetch` remains enabled from diagnosis, but does not resolve the crashes. Other important arguments include `--expert-cache auto --prefill 512 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 896`, plus model/pack/MTP/profile paths.

## Expected / actual behavior

Expected: repeat text and image requests, including native 128K prompts, without engine termination or new NVIDIA Xids.

Actual: the model loads successfully, but requests can terminate the engine. A short request passing once does not imply stability. Some image failures were HTTP 400 or incomplete answers without a new Xid; those must be distinguished from GPU crashes.

Three service-start cycles on driver 615.71.09, BAR1 16 GiB, with `--no-ple-prefetch`:

| Cycle | Vision | ~2K prompts passed | ~8K prompts passed | ~32K prompts passed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | HTTP 400 | 1/2 | 1/2 | 0/1 |
| 2 | Incomplete answer, no new Xid | 2/2 | 1/2 | 0/1 |
| 3 | Pass | 1/2 | 2/2 | 0/1 |

32K failed on its first request in all three cycles. In separate direct-engine tests, 12K passed and 16K failed (about 64 seconds). This is an observed boundary in those runs, not a universal threshold.

One earlier 28-minute interval passed vision, 2K ×2, 8K ×2, 32K ×1 and ~130800-token prompts ×2 with no new Xid. The successful configuration did not remain reliable after reboot. The long tests checked retrieval of `START-593` and `END-827`; they are smoke tests, not comprehensive quality benchmarks.

## Direct-engine reproduction

This bypasses the HTTP server and its watchdog. Use the existing official setup-generated config; it must contain valid local pack/model/MTP/profile paths. Stop the service first to release VRAM. Run from the Strata directory in the same environment as the installation.

```bash
sudo systemctl stop strata
cd /opt/Strata
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib, subprocess, time
config = json.loads(pathlib.Path('strata-swift-iq2_xs.json').read_text())
tokens = pathlib.Path('/tmp/strata-repro-16k.txt')
tokens.write_text(' '.join(['40'] * 16000))
args = list(config['args'])
# The setup config used here contains engine args, without --serve.
assert '--serve' not in args, 'Remove serving-only options for direct mode'
cmd = [config.get('exe', '/opt/Strata/engine/strata'), *args,
       '--tokens-file', str(tokens), '--max-new', '16']
start = time.monotonic()
with open('/tmp/strata-repro-16k.log', 'w') as log:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
print('exit:', result.returncode, 'seconds:', round(time.monotonic()-start, 2))
PY
sudo journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -E 'NVRM: Xid|MMU Fault|FAULT_PDE'
```

Do **not** add a literal `generate` subcommand: direct generation is the default in this build. Supplying `generate` returned usage/exit 2. Token ID 40 repeated 16000 times is a synthetic prefill stress input; natural-text API prompts fail too. Record kernel-log timestamps or before/after counts to identify new events rather than counting old Xids.

## Error samples and sanitizer result

Earlier driver 580 runs repeatedly included addresses ending in `06837000` (other earlier events had different offsets):

```text
MMU Fault: ENGINE GR_HOST0 HUBCLIENT_ESC0 faulted @ 0x202_06837000.
Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```

On 615.71.09, recorded failures also include Xid 11/13 and:

```text
MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC2 GPCCLIENT_T1_0 faulted @ 0x0_00000000.
Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```

Engine observations under different diagnostic settings:

| Setting | Reported error |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | dequant launch: unspecified launch failure |
| STRATA_BF16_TC=2 | dequant launch: an illegal memory access was encountered |
| --sync-every-layer | prefill moe_combine: unspecified launch failure |
| CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 | prefill gemm: cublasGemmEx: cuBLAS status 13 |

CUDA errors can be asynchronous; these locations do not establish the originating operation. Launch blocking also changes behavior and is diagnostic only. `STRATA_PF_STEP_SYNC=1` produced no `pf-step` lines; this absence alone does not prove every synchronization point passed.

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on the direct 16K test reported five CUDA API errors, all `cudaErrorLaunchFailure (719)`, with the first reported at `cudaStreamSynchronize` in `strata::prefill::Prefill::run_impl`. It reported no Invalid read/write or misaligned-access diagnostic. Instrumentation required overriding `--expert-cache 500 --vram-reserve-mib 4096`; otherwise instrumentation ran out of VRAM at initialization. **This is a changed configuration and does not exclude an application bug, race, or uninstrumented failure.**

## Comparisons already attempted

These changes did not establish a stable configuration; they are not all controlled single-variable experiments, and should not be read as categorical exclusions.

| Area | Tested values / changes |
| --- | --- |
| NVIDIA driver | 570.211.01, 580.178.04, 615.71.09 |
| Kernel | 6.8.0-147, 6.17.0-42, 7.0.0-38 |
| Build | CUDA 12.9 and 13.0; engine 0.1.40.3 and 0.1.44.1 |
| Memory clock | 3000 and 2666 MT/s |
| PCI/platform | IOMMU passthrough and fully disabled; ASPM disabled; NVreg_DmaRemapPeerMmio=0; pci=nommconf |
| BAR1 | 256 MiB and 16 GiB |
| Engine | prefill auto/4096/512; VRAM reserve 700/832/896/960/4916; --pcie-mode dma |
| Diagnostics | STRATA_KV_HOST_DMA, STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0, STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1, --sync-every-layer, STRATA_BF16_TC=2 |
| Host allocation | THP request disabled; explicit 2 MiB huge pages (17000 pages), allocation confirmed in log |

`--spec 0` was rejected for this native IQ pack, so it is **not** a completed no-speculation comparison. `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1` was found in a compile-time SM60-only path, so it is **not** a valid comparison on this build. `--ple-sync-submit` produced NaNs and was removed. Experimental environment overrides and explicit huge pages were removed afterward.

The documented RTX 50/CUDA 13.2.0–13.2.1 compiler issue does not directly match the CUDA 13.0 build used here.

## Other diagnostics and limitations

- `gpu_burn 600`: no reported errors. This does not certify all GPU/VRAM/PCIe paths healthy.
- `memtester 8192M`: no reported failures in tested patterns/region. This did not test all 64 GB or exclude intermittent RAM faults.
- Recorded AER status was clean; no OOM kill was found in the inspected logs.
- Custom CUDA probes also failed outside Strata: batched small-kernel / host-transfer workloads produced Xids; per-copy-synchronized tests passed 120 seconds, including a recorded 743.87 GiB transfer/check run. A kernel-only batch probe also failed, so **large host registration or host DMA alone is not an established explanation**. The probes are custom diagnostic code, not certified hardware tests; correctness and timing effects require independent review.
- Changing driver changed fault signatures; it does not prove the driver caused the fault or that an earlier issue was fixed.
- No GPU-in-another-machine / another-GPU-in-this-machine cross-test has been completed.
- BIOS availability, Windows driver details and a matched Windows reproduction should be rechecked before drawing platform conclusions.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Does the direct 16K reproduction or these Xid signatures match a known sm_120 issue?
2. Which official diagnostic configuration/test would best distinguish engine ordering/lifetime bugs from a driver/platform failure?
3. Which logs, build metadata or NVIDIA diagnostic bundle would you like next?
4. Would a comparison with an officially supported alternate engine build help, and which build/settings should be held fixed?

Potential attachments: setup config with API keys removed, engine BUILD.json, full failing engine log, timestamped kernel log, complete sanitizer log, and custom probe source with launch parameters. Not all of those are included in this text; missing artifacts should not be implied to exist.

issues.title: Support for AMD Instinct MI100 and MI210 GPUs
issues.author: bioxuxuan
issues.body:
### Background
Currently, Strata has amazing support for many consumer and legacy AMD GPUs (like MI50/MI60), but it doesn't seem to support enterprise/datacenter AMD Instinct MI100 (gfx908) and MI210 (gfx90a) cards yet. 

### Proposed Feature
I would love to see official compilation support or runtime compatibility for AMD Instinct MI100 and MI210 GPUs. Since these cards have large VRAM capacities, they would be absolutely perfect for running Strata's high-speed local inference.

Specifically, hoping to see support for:
- **MI100** (gfx908 architecture)
- **MI210** (gfx90a architecture)

### Current Alternatives
Users with these enterprise cards currently have to stick with other backends like vLLM, but we are missing out on the incredible performance and optimizations that Strata offers.

### Future Plans & Testing
Are there any plans or roadmap milestones to bring support for CDNA-based Instinct cards (MI100/MI200 series) in the near future? 

I have access to MI100/MI210 hardware and would be more than happy to help test any experimental branches or provide logs if needed!

issues.title: [Bug]: PLE gather reissues already-prefetched reordered and duplicate keys
issues.author: hotschmoe
issues.body:
### What happened

`PleTable::gather_batch` uses positional equality for Direct-mode prefetched keys. After prefetching A,B,C,D,E,F, gathering D,E,F,A,B,C reissues 96 requested rows even though every 16-row vector is already prefetched. Prefetching A once and gathering A,A,A reissues 48 requested rows because prefetches are deduplicated while the fast path requires at least as many slots as requested tokens.

Expected: reuse existing immutable prefetched slots and decode into requested order. This is a redundant-request mechanism; no serving latency or physical disk-I/O saving is claimed.

There is also a related cleanup defect in the same successful-match branch: on the first failed collect, it clears n_prefetch without draining subsequent outstanding tickets. A narrow proposed fix drains all tickets, preserves the first error, and returns without decoding after a failure. Failure handling is source-reviewed; runtime fault injection has not been performed.

Reproduction: open a finite tiny IQ4_NL GGUF in Direct mode, call prefetch_rows for the vectors above, and compare the requested-row counter in io_report before/after gather_batch. [Exact executed fixture](https://github.com/hotschmoe/b70_ai_things/blob/fff2c71b0a1d806db428b8489b42fd248d50bebd/strata/flash-next/lowlevel_probe/ple_prefetch_cpu.cpp) and [evidence](https://github.com/hotschmoe/b70_ai_things/blob/fff2c71b0a1d806db428b8489b42fd248d50bebd/docs/20261015_strata_ple_prefetch_readiness.md). The fixture's local include path needs adjustment outside its original checkout.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Upstream main 296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78 (0.1.44.1), Linux; CPU-only PleTable/PleReader/DirectFile reproduction, g++ 13.3.0, C++17/O2/pthreads. No GPU access required. Shared PleTable with the SYCL tree's host reader/file implementation was tested; full CUDA/HIP backend builds are not claimed.

### Engine log

Both baseline and patched CPU harnesses exit 0, 44 cases per arm (88 total): 11 cases x cache 0/256 x worker off/on. All successful output bytes match an independently opened Mmap reference, and guards, finite references, logical byte accounting and request counts pass. Permutation: 96 -> 0 additional requested rows; duplicates: 48 -> 0; subset: 32 -> 0; extra-prefetch subset: 16 -> 0. Missing/over-limit/pending behavior retains expected counts. Runtime fault injection and out-of-range coverage are absent.

Searched existing issues/PRs on 2026-10-15 for PLE prefetch, gather_batch and prefetch_keys. Related PRs #1516, #2073 and #2326 touch this area but retain positional matching; no exact duplicate was found. Search is keyword-based, not an exhaustive review of every open diff.

issues.title: `gdn` state left by a fresh prefill is not bit-reproducible across runs at long prompts (2K and 40K are bit-stable, 120K is not)
issues.author: kietq8684-design
issues.body:
### Summary
Two independent runs of `tools/conversation_cache_soak.py` on the same box with the same config produced **different
`gdn` state fingerprints for the fresh-prefill (baseline) arm** at a 120K prompt, while the park/restore
(candidate) arm was bit-identical across both runs. Generation output was identical in both runs, so we saw no
semantic impact — but bit-reproducibility of the prefill path is lost. This looks like an engine-side determinism
question, not a conversation-cache defect: the cache is the *stable* side here.

### Environment
- GPU: Radeon VII 16 GB (`0x66af`) + Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 16 GB (`0x66a1`), both gfx906, layer split
- ROCm: HIP 7.14 (hipcc 7.14.60850) from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`; kernel 6.8.0-146-p2p; Ubuntu 24.04;
  `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6`
- Engine: v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`), gfx906 opt-in build (`-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON`), working tree clean
- Model: Coder IQ1_M (`--native` pack), local NVMe
- Engine args: `--serve --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072 --layer-split 27 --prefill 4096
  --pipeline-windows 2 --ple-row-cache 8388608 --pcie-frac 0 --spec 2`
- Engine env: `STRATA_STATE_HASH=1 STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1 STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1 STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1
  STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_QUERY_SWIZZLE=1 STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_REDUCE12=1`
  (all verified present in `/proc/<engine-pid>/environ` inside the container)
- Experts: 100% resident (6,889 + 5,376 = 12,265 slots), `evictions=0` throughout

### Reproduction
`tools/conversation_cache_soak.py` **unmodified**. Two runs, same config, same box, back to back:

    python3 tools/conversation_cache_soak.py --prompt-tokens 2048,40000,120000 --cycles 30 --cache-mib 8192

Each run does an A/B/A: first the baseline arm with `--conversation-cache-mib 0` (fresh prefill, no cache), then the
candidate arm with `--conversation-cache-mib 8192`. Compare the `strata serve: STATE_HASH ...` lines that the
**baseline** arm emits, run 1 vs run 2.

### Observed — `gdn` fingerprint per prompt length, both arms, both runs

| `L` (prompt tokens) | run 1 baseline | run 2 baseline | run 1 candidate | run 2 candidate | baseline across runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,026 (2K head) | `11588c1477c2b342` | `11588c1477c2b342` | `11588c1477c2b342` | `11588c1477c2b342` | identical |
| 2,062 (2K answer) | `7073c4a151834315` | `7073c4a151834315` | `7073c4a151834315` | `7073c4a151834315` | identical |
| 39,985 (40K head) | `ba8166e26a13cb48` | `ba8166e26a13cb48` | `ba8166e26a13cb48` | `ba8166e26a13cb48` | identical |
| 40,021 (40K answer) | `52f2e6a00b00ffda` | `52f2e6a00b00ffda` | `52f2e6a00b00ffda` | `52f2e6a00b00ffda` | identical |
| **119,987 (120K head)** | **`610f3b1ff5dde7ba`** | **`1dd3577d2a1918d5`** | `1dd3577d2a1918d5` | `1dd3577d2a1918d5` | **DIFFERS** |
| **120,023 (120K answer)** | **`a54d74e32544a13b`** | **`2261bd02e1845136`** | `2261bd02e1845136` | `2261bd02e1845136` | **DIFFERS** |

Every other fingerprinted component (`L`, `kv`, `ple`, `tail`, `dead`, `pooled`, `ple_prev`) is identical across
runs at every length, including 120K. `kv` in particular — the real attention K/V over `[0, L)`, including the
streamed host copy — is byte-identical across both arms and both runs at all lengths.

Also: within a single run the candidate arm emits the 120K `gdn` **10 times and always the same value**; only the
baseline (fresh prefill) differs between runs. So the non-determinism is on the prefill side, not the restore side.

### Output was identical, so this is a reproducibility issue, not (observed) a correctness one
Both runs returned the same known answers and the same continuation tokens at every length. We are not claiming
wrong output. We are claiming that "prefill the same prompt twice on the same box, same config → same `gdn`" does
not hold at 120K, which is what a bit-exactness / determinism expectation would require, and which the soak's
`state` gate implicitly assumes.

### What we ruled out, and what we did NOT establish
- **Not the conversation cache.** The candidate (park/restore) side is stable across runs; the baseline (fresh
  prefill) side is the one that moves. At 2K/40K both sides are stable.
- **`atomicAdd` in the GDN kernels: none.** `grep -c atomicAdd` is 0 in every GDN source file:
  `src/kernels/cuda/native_gdn.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gdn.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/native_gdn_preprocess.cu`,
  `src/kernels/cuda/gdn.cu`, `src/kernels/gdn_parity.cpp`, and all `gdn` headers. The only `atomicAdd` hits in any
  file with "gdn" in its name are 6 counter atomics inside `src/prefill/gdn_rec_parity.cu`, which is a parity test
  harness (`landed` / `late` / `apart` / `sitting` / `out`), not the state update.
- **`grep -i "non-determin"` over `src/`: 0 hits.**
- **We are explicitly NOT claiming the trigger is `prompt > --kv-resident`.** The 40K prompt (39,985 tokens) is
  also larger than `--kv-resident 32768`, so streaming KV is active there too, and it is bit-stable. Whatever
  distinguishes 120K from 40K is not pinned down by this data — that is an open question for you, not a conclusion
  from us.

### Confirmed code facts, for whoever picks this up
1. What the buffer is — `src/program/generate.cpp:3484`:
   ```cpp
   auto gdn_snapshot_bytes = [&](const strata::core::SessionState& s0) -> size_t {
       return (size_t) s0.gdn_alloc * ((size_t) g.ssm_state_size * g.ssm_v_heads * g.ssm_state_size +
                                       (size_t) g.ssm_conv_channels * (g.ssm_d_conv - 1)) * sizeof(float);
   };
   ```
   i.e. per GDN layer: the recursive matrix plus the conv rolling window, ×4 B, × `gdn_alloc` layers
   (21 here, the layer-split 27 carve).

2. The same buffer is already treated as containing non-semantic bytes by your own test —
   `src/core/conversation_snapshot_test.cpp:202`:
   ```cpp
   cuda_check(cudaMemset(ss.gdn_state,91,sizes.gdn));
   ```
   a canary fill, which is the reason we did not immediately call the mismatch a cache bug.

3. The per-layer debug hash already exists on both paths: `src/program/generate.cpp:11789` (serve) and
   `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:4096` ("the GDN states as the prompt path leaves them"), gated on
   `STRATA_STATE_HASH_GDN`.

### Suggested next step
Run the same prompt twice through the **prefill** path above the resident window with `STRATA_STATE_HASH_GDN=1` and
diff the per-layer hashes; if it reproduces, the `gdn` comparison in `conversation_cache_soak.py` /
`conversation_cache_parity.py` should compare **cross-run stability of the restore side** rather than equality to a
single baseline sample, in the streamed region. We can run this on our box if you want a second data point, but we
did not want to file a mechanism claim we cannot support.

issues.title: Windows + AMD: dashboard GPU tiles stay blank (telemetry is Linux-sysfs only) — fixed locally via ADL, incl. a PCIe link-speed pitfall
issues.author: bigbrid2023
issues.body:
Follow-up to #2523, from the same Windows + RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) machine (Strata 0.1.44.1, Windows 11 26H2, Adrenalin 26.8.1).

**Symptom:** on Windows with an AMD card, the dashboard's GPU load / VRAM / GPU temp / Power / PCIe tiles always show "—". The NVIDIA path works; AMD never does.

**Root cause:** `serve/telemetry.py`'s AMD reader only reads Linux amdgpu sysfs paths, so on Windows every `gpu_*` field comes back empty.

**What I run locally (fixed, in daily use):** a Windows AMD reader next to the sysfs one, built on the AMD Display Library (`atiadlxx.dll`):

- Utilization / temperature / board power / clocks via PMLog (`ADL2_New_QueryPMLogData_Get`, sensor IDs per the official ADL SDK enum)
- VRAM total via `ADL2_Adapter_MemoryInfo_Get`; VRAM used via `ADL2_Adapter_DedicatedVRAMUsage_Get` — note this is WDDM committed-dedicated memory: it pulses with requests (~0.1 GiB idle, ~21.3 GiB during generation on this 24 GB card; cross-checked against Windows PDH GPU counters)
- ADL context created once, ~1 Hz cache, every failure degrades to `None` so the telemetry endpoint never errors

**One pitfall worth its own paragraph — the PCIe link generation.** The PMLog link channels do *not* report the negotiated link speed on this driver. They read "Gen3" while the slot was BIOS-forced from Gen3 to Gen4 and both GPU-Z ("PCIe x16 4.0 @ x4 4.0") and the Windows device property confirmed Gen4 — at idle *and* at 93% generation load, the PMLog value never moved. I now read the generation from the Windows PnP property `DEVPKEY_PciDevice_CurrentLinkSpeed` (via cfgmgr32), filtering to the started instance (this machine also carries a disconnected phantom instance of the same card, left by a Windows feature update). Related trap: the DEVPKEY link-*width* properties are not the negotiated width either — they report the card's wiring (16 for the XTX sitting in an x4 slot; 8 for an RTX 5060 Ti) — so the width stays on PMLog, which agrees with the physical x4.

**No equivalent found:** PCIe RX/TX throughput — nothing in the full PMLog table exposes it, so that sub-line of the tile stays blank rather than showing a made-up number.

**Validation:** idle 0% / 39 °C / 6.0 W; during generation util 71→97%, power up to 299 W, VRAM used ~21.3 GiB; after the link-source correction the PCIe tile reads "Gen4 x4", matching GPU-Z.

Happy to turn this into a PR with the reader code if that's useful — just say the word.

issues.title: Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060
issues.author: mbock-ai
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060

Measured on 2026-10-15 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (8 cores, 16 threads); installed RAM: 62.7 GiB; storage: not measured
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: 595.99.02; CUDA: 13.2
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s
- Context: 65536 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack iq3_s --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.70 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97
```

## Method

Run by `python tools/strata_bench.py` against the HTTP API of a Strata server (already running); model loading is not timed. One warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Every prompt starts with a unique tag, so the conversation cache cannot help the fresh-prompt tests.

- short chat: the three questions of `tools/ab_engine.py`, up to 100 new tokens, 3 runs
