issues.title: [Feature]: degrade the conversation cache across levels instead of deleting the oldest (RAM -> fast M.2 -> cold disk, each level switchable)
issues.author: shahrokhzargarpour
issues.body:
## What exists today

The conversation cache's disk tier has exactly one full policy:

- `--conversation-cache-spill-when-full` accepts two values, `evict-oldest` (the default) and `reject`.
- With `evict-oldest`, the GC **deletes** the oldest entry to make room. There is no pin, no protected set, and no
  second (colder) level to move it to.
- Start-up line from the boot we run today:

```text
strata serve: conversation cache: spill dir ready (20 conversations, 20225 MiB, when-full=evict-oldest, max-age=0 d, spill-on=park, divergence=4096 tok, park-throttle=0 s, 0 oversized kept, 58 stale kept, 0 foreign kept, 0 orphans kept, 0 disk evictions, 0 age evictions)
```

- We have seen the FIFO work: 101 disk evictions counted in a measurement window on 2026-10-14, and the log's
  cumulative `evictions=` counter reaches 132. (In the boot above the counter is 0 because the budget, 460,800 MiB,
  is far above what is in use, 20,225 MiB.)

## What we ask: a cascade that degrades instead of deleting

The entry that leaves a level **enters the next one**; only the last level discards.

| level | destination | switch | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RAM | `--conversation-cache-mib X` (`0` = off) | hot |
| 2 | fast M.2, a few GB | `--conversation-cache-disk-mib` (`0` = off) | warm |
| 3 | cold M.2/SATA SSD, hundreds of GB | `--conversation-cache-cold-dir` + `--conversation-cache-cold-mib` (`0` = off) | cold |
| - | floor | `--conversation-cache-min-free-mib` | **stays as it is** |

Two properties we care about, and they are the whole request: **each level can be switched off independently**, and
the RAM floor is not part of the cascade (it protects the rest of the machine, it is not a parking level).

## Why the existing `archive` cannot be the cold level

The archive we already run (`--conversation-cache-archive-mode state`, `--conversation-cache-archive-keep 4`) is
history with a contract: an archived state is never a reuse candidate — it exists so the state is not lost, not to
make a reload cheap. Level 3 has to be a real tier: its own GC, its own match index, and a restore path.

```text
strata serve: conversation cache: archive ready (state, 9 archived, 7461 MiB, mib=8192, keep=4, max-age=0 d, 0 archive evictions [0 by age])
```

To be explicit about the source of that claim: it is our reading of the archive path, not a quote from your docs. If
the archive *is* meant to be a reuse source, say so and this section is moot.

## Design by media type, not by drive letter

Level 2 should be the volume the setup bench measures as the fastest with room; level 3 the next by sequential
speed, or the one with the most free space. On Windows the setup already probes disks, so an `auto` that reads
volumes (sequential read/write, free space, bus type NVMe/SATA) is the piece that assigns the levels — not a
hand-written list. Re-running it when a disk is added should be automatic.

We are not asking you to design that part blind; here is what it looks like on this machine, for scale:

- `D:` is a 1.9 TB NVMe SSD with ~597 GiB free, measured filling the expert arena at 6.03 GiB/s and restoring
  2.9 GB in 274 ms (the latter assisted by the OS file cache).
- `C:` has ~44 GB free and hosts the pagefile, so it is not a candidate for a warm level.
- The operator's `F:` is excluded by policy.

So today levels 2 and 3 would land on the same volume — the cascade degrades inside one disk until a second medium
exists. That is fine as a design, but it belongs in the docs, and it is why we would rather have two switchable
levels than one level plus an assumption.

## Why we ask (what the numbers buy today)

- The tier is not decorative here: 1,294 restores and ~90.5 M tokens restored between 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-14, the
  largest a 171,516-token context in 656.9 ms against 158.6 s cold (24x).
- `evict-oldest` deletes exactly the copy that makes the next reload cheap. The entry goes to the archive only when
  the archive is enabled, and per the contract above that copy is not reusable.
- A smaller warm budget is the realistic setting on a workstation that shares the disk with everything else, and
  under a small budget every restart silently trades history for the newest few conversations.

## What we owe you as a counter-argument

With a large disk budget (450 GiB in our config) the FIFO already keeps the same hot set plus everything else, and a
second level buys nothing. The cascade matters when the fast volume is small, when the two media differ in speed, or
when the operator wants history kept without it competing with the hot set. **We are not claiming a measured
regression from `evict-oldest`** — this is a design request with an operator-side motivation, not a bug report.

## What we do not claim

- Not implemented, not benchmarked, and we are not sending code for it.
- `--conversation-cache-cold-dir` / `--conversation-cache-cold-mib` do not exist in our build.
- The 101 evictions are a count, not a cost: we did not measure how much prefill the current eviction policy caused.
- Windows only.

## What we ruled out (checked before opening this)

- **#47** (closed/completed) `Spill kv-cache to nvme` — the origin of the disk tier.
- **#847** (closed/completed) `Allow system ram to be used instead of SSD when available.` — the RAM/disk ordering.
- **#661** (closed/completed) `Proposal: save and restore a conversation to disk` and **#1444** (closed/not planned)
  `can kvcache be saved and reused on disk?` — the save/restore path itself.
- **#1572** (closed/completed) reclaiming disposable host caches on SAVE, and **#1347** (closed/completed) evicting
  to pass the physical-RAM gate instead of dropping the snapshot — both are *eviction to pass a gate*, not
  *demotion between levels*.
- **#2033** (open) `MADV_COLD` for swap and **#1900** (open) NUMA cold pools — colder placement, not a cascade.
- **#2275** (open) and **PR #2050** — the read path that stops the machine while a cold read runs. A cascade that
  pushes reads onto a slower medium makes that path longer; same direction, different fix, and worth knowing before
  adding a level.
- Searched for `evict`, `when-full`, `demote`, `cascade`, `cold tier`, `second tier`, `spill`: none of the above
  asks for "the entry that leaves level N enters level N+1, and only the last level discards".

## What we did not test

- No implementation, so no measurement of the cascade.
- We did not measure the cost of the current eviction on reload (we have the count, not the price).
- We did not test the disk tier under a small budget for long enough to see the FIFO delete a conversation we then
  wanted back; the 101 evictions come from the monitor we run, not from a reload experiment.

issues.title: KV streaming on a layer split reports `0 block reads` (0.1.43 `7695859a`, IQ2_XS, RTX 3090 + RTX 3060), while the same config on one card reports 215k-252k
issues.author: TurtleFlyRU
issues.body:
## What happens

On a layer split the engine's per-request counter reads `KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB
read from RAM` for every request, at every context size and with every KV format. The start line says three
quarters of each QSA layer's cells are not in VRAM, so the RAM copy should be read. The same machine, build, model
and `--kv-resident 32768` on the 3090 **alone** reports real reads for the same residency line.

Start line, split:

```text
strata generate: KV streaming: 32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM, the K/V in 0.13 GiB of pinned RAM
```

Start line, one RTX 3090, same `--kv-resident 32768`:

```text
strata generate: KV streaming: 32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM, the K/V in 1.55 GiB of pinned RAM
```

Per request, split (131072 context, a 4019-token prompt):

```text
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
```

Per request, one RTX 3090 (same context, the same 4K prompt in the same suite):

```text
strata serve: KV streaming: 89.58% of 246456 block reads hit VRAM, 103.5 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: KV streaming: 85.45% of 215652 block reads hit VRAM, 126.4 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: KV streaming: 87.18% of 252636 block reads hit VRAM, 130.4 MiB read from RAM
```

The split also reports 0 reads at `--max-context 262144` with prompts of up to 255,433 tokens, and with
`--kv k8v4` and `--kv q4_0`, so it is not one format, one context size or one prompt.

## Why I think something is off

With 32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM, 98304 cells per layer are not, and a 64K-256K prompt has to
attend to them. If the host copy holds them, those blocks have to be read from RAM. The split reports 0 such reads
in every run we made; the single card reports 200k-250k per request for the same residency. Either the split does
not stream K/V blocks at all, or the counter is not wired for the split path - I cannot tell which from the
outside.

A second thing I cannot explain and would like to understand: `1.55 / 0.13 = 12`. If the single card's number is
the whole model's host copy (12 QSA layers) and the split's number is one QSA layer's share, the two are the same
1.55 GiB and only the counter differs. If both numbers are the same quantity, then on a split the host copy is 12x
smaller, which would explain 0 reads but would mean the split keeps the K/V somewhere else. Which is it?

## Configuration

Split (both cards), port 8092:

```text
strata --serve --pack Strata-data/packs/iq2_xs
  --native .../Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XS-00001-of-00002.gguf
  --ple-gguf .../Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XS-00002-of-00002.gguf
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto
  --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp Strata-data/mtp/rt
  --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700
```

`"gpu": "0,1"`; the engine reorders to `card order 1,0`, so CUDA0 is the RTX 3060 (layers 0-2, 1536 slots,
2.06 GiB) and CUDA1 the RTX 3090 (layers 3-47, 12927 slots, 17.32 GiB). `--layer-split auto` chose K=3.

Single card: the same file with `"gpu": 1` (the 3090), everything else identical.

## How to reproduce

```bash
python tools/strata_bench.py --config <the split config> --port 8092 --api-key <key> --long --huge
python tools/strata_bench.py --config <the 3090-only config> --port 8092 --api-key <key> --long --huge
```

The counters are the `strata serve: KV streaming: ...` lines in the engine log, one per request, and the
`strata generate: KV streaming: ...` line at start. `tools/ctx_sizes.py --sizes 170000,262144` shows the same
thing at 262144.

## System

- Strata 0.1.43, commit `7695859a`, source build (engine 0.1.43)
- 2 GPUs: RTX 3090 24 GB (PCIe 4.0 x16, 250 W) + RTX 3060 12 GB (PCIe 3.0 **x4**, 130 W); driver 580.178.04, CUDA 13.0
- AMD Ryzen 7 7700X, 122.6 GiB RAM, Linux 7.0.0-31
- Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS (native pack), 24576 experts, shipped expert profile

## What I ruled out

- Not the KV format: int8, k8v4 and q4_0 all report 0 reads on the split.
- Not the context size: 131072 and 262144 both report 0 reads; the prompts were up to 255,433 tokens.
- Not the cache: the split's expert-cache hit rate over the same suite is 91-99%, the same as the single card's.
- Not `--kv-resident` being ignored: the start line does report `32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM` in
  both cases, and raising it to 65536 costs 294 slots on the 3090, so the option is read.

## What I did not test

- Another split (the same pair in the other order, or a pair of equal cards) - I can send those logs if they help.
- Windows, WSL and AMD.
- `STRATA_SPLIT_TIMING=1` on a long request, which is probably the next step - I can run it on request.
- Whether the 3.4 GB/s link of the 3060 (Gen3 x4) is involved.

## Related

- #2415 (kv_stream page-pool eviction) - same subsystem.
- #2007 (256K + KV streaming on a 2x T10 layer split): their prefill moves between engine versions with
  `--kv-resident 32768` on a split, so I would expect the streaming path to be active there; they do not quote
  the block-read counter.
- #2418 (x16+x4 link-gap rig class) - our rig has the same 4x-ish link gap, 26.8 vs 3.4 GB/s probed.
- #2450 (open PR: no KV streaming when one card holds every expert and the whole K/V) - that is the opposite
  case, a card that should not stream; this report is about the counter on a split.

I have per-run JSON, engine logs and the full configs for everything above and can attach them.

issues.title: UD-Q5_K_XL shard 1 rejected: check_shards and UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS disagree on expected size
issues.author: DrLove73
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

setup.sh rejects Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf with an inconsistent error. The verification logic in setup.py compares the file against two different expected sizes depending on the check.

**To Reproduce**

    Download Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL via ./setup.sh.

    The download of shard 1 completes.

    Run ./setup.sh again to continue the installation.

    Setup stops with the following error:
    text

[X]  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf is short: 10,946,618 of 10,946,624 bytes (6 missing)

Following the suggested fix (truncate -s 10946624 <file>), the file size becomes exactly 10,946,624 bytes.

Run ./setup.sh again. A new, different error appears:
text

[X]  Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf is 10,946,624 bytes, not 10,946,618

**Expected behavior**

Setup should accept the shard as valid and continue the installation. The file size is correct according to both the GGUF header and the UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS dictionary.

**Analysis / Root Cause**

There is an inconsistency in setup.py between two sources of truth for the expected file size:

    The check_shards() function (around line 1958) calculates the expected size (need) by reading the GGUF header and summing the tensor data offsets. For this file, it computes 10,946,624 bytes.

    The UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS dictionary (around line 335) defines the expected size for the same file as 10,946,618 bytes.

The file on disk, as downloaded from Hugging Face, matches the size in UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS (10,946,618 bytes). However, the GGUF header inside the file declares a data size of 10,946,624 bytes, likely due to missing alignment padding at the end of the last tensor. Because check_shards does not tolerate this small discrepancy, it rejects the file. After manually padding the file to 10,946,624 bytes to pass check_shards, a subsequent, different check (using UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS) now fails because the file is larger than the declared size.

This makes it impossible to satisfy both checks simultaneously with a single file size.

**Suggested Fix**

The verification logic should be made consistent. One of the following changes would resolve the issue:

    Update UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS: Change the expected size for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf from 10,946,618 to 10,946,624 bytes to match the GGUF header. This is the most robust solution.

    Add a tolerance in check_shards(): Modify the check_shards function to allow a small tolerance (e.g., up to 32 bytes) when have < need, accounting for alignment padding. The condition could be changed to if have < need - 32: or similar.

Either fix would allow the setup to proceed.

**Environment**

    **OS**: Linux (RHEL-based, kernel 6.12.0-211.49.1.el10_2.x86_64)

    **Strata Version**: 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2)

    **Model**: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Unsloth) UD-Q5_K_XL

    **GPU**: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell

**Workaround**

None, as the two checks are mutually exclusive. A code fix is required.

issues.title: Report: UD-IQ4_XS and IQ3_XXS on RTX 3090 + Haswell-EP Xeon (AVX2, no AVX-512), NVMe vs HDD
issues.author: basiceconomypublishing-create
issues.body:
Thanks for Strata. You asked for UD-IQ4_XS numbers on NVIDIA, so here are ours, plus IQ3_XXS for reference.

**Setup**
- HP Z440 workstation, Xeon E5-2683 v3 (14 cores, Haswell-EP, AVX2, no AVX-512), 62 GB DDR4-2133 ECC (4 channels)
- 1× RTX 3090 24 GB, PCIe 3.0 x16 (engine's probe: 11.2–11.9 GB/s), driver 595.58.03, CUDA 12.8
- Model files on a Samsung PM981 NVMe, ext4; Linux (Proxmox LXC, Debian 13)
- Engine 0.1.39 (6f32ec0), built from source via the UnbiasedStrata fork (engine sources identical to yours), ctx 65536, `--threads 14` unless noted (8 turned out best — see below)
- Card at 220 W with clocks locked at 1600 MHz (`nvidia-smi -lgc 1600,1600`) unless noted
- Benchmark: 2,847-token Polish prompt with a unique tag (no cache reuse), up to 600 output tokens, temperature 0.6, 1/3/5/8 concurrent requests (served one at a time), second of two repeats

**Results (single user unless noted)**

| Variant | aggregate tok/s | decode tok/s | TTFT | prefill tok/s | experts on GPU | experts in RAM | from files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **IQ3_XXS, `--threads 8`**, `--ple-io direct --resident-experts` | **39.8** | **56.5** | 3.0 s | 948 | 10,326 slots (16.75 GiB) | 26.6 GiB pinned | 0 |
| IQ3_XXS, same, `--threads 14` | 32.4 | 40.2 | 3.1 s | 930 | 10,326 slots (16.75 GiB) | 26.6 GiB pinned | 0 |
| IQ3_XXS, same, ctx 131072 | 28.9 | 38.0 | 3.1 s | 908 | 9,744 (15.79 GiB) | 27.5 GiB | 0 |
| IQ3_XXS, unlocked clocks (1920 MHz) | 34.3 | 41.9 | 3.0 s | 944 | — | — | — |
| **UD-IQ4_XS** (pack `--compat-bf16`), `--ple-io direct --resident-budget-gib 36` | **16.6** | **20.9** | 7.4 s | 387 | 6,911 (15.58 GiB) | 36 GiB of 39.85 | ~3.9 GiB (773 GB read over 27 min) |
| IQ3_XXS, "RTX 3060-like" (`--vram-reserve-mib 12288`, core 600 MHz, mem 5001 MHz on the 3090) | 14.0 | 17.4 | 5.5 s | 517 | 3,327 (5.43 GiB) | 37.9 GiB | 0 |

- UD-IQ4_XS: packs and runs fine on NVIDIA (Ampere). Tool calls and reasoning work. Decode expert-cache hit rate 84.4 %. Aggregate stays ~14 tok/s at 3/5/8 users (one request at a time).
- Long prompts (47k tokens, single request): IQ3_XXS TTFT 28.9 s (prefill 1,628 tok/s), decode 22.6 tok/s; UD-IQ4_XS TTFT 60 s (prefill 784 tok/s), decode 12.2 tok/s. IQ3_XXS at 118k tokens (ctx 131072): TTFT 75 s, decode 38.7 tok/s.
- MTP draft acceptance on Polish text: ~41–45 %; on tool calls / numbers: ~80 %.
- On this box the CPU side is the limit: 1920 vs 1600 MHz on the GPU gives only ~6 %.
- **Thread count matters a lot** (IQ3_XXS, 64k, single user, aggregate / decode): 4 threads 28.0 / 34.4, **8 threads 39.8 / 56.5**, 14 threads (= physical cores) 32.4 / 40.2, 28 threads (Hyper-Threading) 29.5 / 37.3 tok/s. 28 threads were also 7–22 % slower than 14 on 128k, UD-IQ4_XS and the 3060-like run. With 8 threads: 3 users 39.2, 8 users 39.5 tok/s aggregate; CPU package 25 W idle, 62–64 W under load (RAPL). Looks memory-bandwidth bound (4 × DDR4-2133): beyond ~8 workers the expert pool only adds contention. Maybe worth a hint in the docs that the default (all physical cores) is not always best on older many-core Xeons.

Full tables (all variants, power draw, long documents, thread counts) and a comparison with vLLM on 4× RTX 3090: https://www.local-ai.company/geeks-only.html#strata-engine — benchmark page: https://www.local-ai.company/benchmark.html

**HDD confirmation of #605**
Before the NVMe drive, the model sat on a 7200 rpm HDD with `--ple-io ram` + `--mmap-experts` (62 GB RAM, so experts could not be resident): 0.13 tok/s, and the default 60 s watchdog killed the engine on the first request (stall report: threads in state D, millions of major faults). `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S=900` let it finish. The warning in the docs is right — an SSD is effectively required when RAM cannot hold the experts.

issues.title: update: an engine binary without its BUILD.json is never updated, and nothing says why (follow-up to #2054)
issues.author: qiuzan2001
issues.body:
Follow-up to #2054 (the maintainer asked for it as its own issue). Related: #2159 (an interrupted update that
leaves `BUILD.json.prev`, PR #2161), which covers one way this state happens.

**What happens.** With `engine/BUILD.json` gone (a user "cleaning up", or #2159's interrupted update) and the engine
binary still there, `./update.sh` / `UPDATE.bat` neither downloads nor compiles an engine and says nothing about
why. In #2054 it only printed the binary's old version and finished. There is no state in which the update offers to
rebuild.

**Where.** `setup.py:3612` (`update_installed_engine`, `296b59d2`): `if not info.exists() or not (eng /
EXE).exists(): return`.

**Possible change.** Treat a binary without its stamp as of unknown origin and offer to replace it (a download of
the ready-made engine, or a compile with `--build`). Or at least print one line saying that `BUILD.json` is missing,
so the engine is not updated, and how to get a new one.

issues.title: setup: a build folder configured without the engine target fails twice with "unknown target 'strata'" and is not reconfigured (follow-up to #2054)
issues.author: qiuzan2001
issues.body:
Follow-up to #2054 (the maintainer asked for it as its own issue).

**What happens (from the post-mortem in #2054).** A `build-cuda12/` folder that had been configured without the
engine's definitions (an interrupted earlier attempt, plus a manual `cmake -S . -B build-cuda12`) made the engine
build configure "successfully" and then stop at `ninja: error: unknown target 'strata'`. The build is tried a
second time, which fails the same way, and the last message does not point at the build folder. Deleting the folder
and running setup again fixed it.

**Where.** `setup.py:3827` (`cmake_build`, `296b59d2`) configures the existing folder, then runs the build twice.
Since 0.1.43.1, `build_engine` (`setup.py:3962`) says "the build folder ... may be configured for something else:
delete it and run this again" when the build finishes without a new engine. It does not reach that line when the
target does not exist, because `cmake_build` stops first.

**Possible change.** After configuring, check that the target exists (`cmake --build <dir> --target help`, or
`ninja -t targets`). If it does not, configure a fresh copy of the folder once before giving up, the way
`isa_floor_defs` (`setup.py:3868`) already deletes `CMakeCache.txt` when the ISA floor changes. Or name the folder
in the error.

Not reproduced here: I did not find which cached setting removes the `strata` target, since setup passes
`-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON` on every configure.

issues.title: setup: a default g++ newer than the CUDA toolkit accepts stops the engine build; an installed older g++ is not tried (follow-up to #2054)
issues.author: qiuzan2001
issues.body:
Follow-up to #2054 (the maintainer asked for it as its own issue).

**What happens.** On a rolling distribution the system `g++` can move past what the installed CUDA toolkit accepts.
In #2054, gcc went from 14 to 16 on CachyOS with CUDA 12.8, and the engine build stopped in CMake's CUDA compiler
check with nvcc's `#error -- unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 14 are not supported`, although
`g++-14` was installed. The same build had worked the day before.

**Where.** `setup.py:3876` (`host_compiler_defs`, `296b59d2`) passes `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` / `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` /
`CMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER` only when the user sets `CC` / `CXX` / `CUDAHOSTCXX` (#1645). Otherwise CMake takes the
default `g++`, and nothing tries an older one.

**Workaround (from #2054).** `CC=gcc-14 CXX=g++-14 CUDAHOSTCXX=g++-14 ./update.sh`.

**Possible change.** When none of the three is set and the default `g++` is newer than the toolkit accepts, look for
an installed `g++-N` / `gcc-N` the toolkit does accept (newest first) and pass it as the host compiler, saying so.
Or, at least, catch nvcc's "unsupported GNU version" and print the workaround.

Not reproduced here: this box (Ubuntu, CUDA 13.1, gcc 15.2) builds with its default compiler.

issues.title: [Feature]: Skip low-rank missed experts on Metal when streaming from the SSD

Get faster decode on a Mac that streams experts from the SSD. On my Mac Studio (M4 Max, 36 GB, 512 GB SSD, UD-Q4_K_XL, 16 GB wired arena), decode is about 11 tok/s. issues.title: [Bug]: Metal: IQ2_XS (GSQ-RCO) fails to load — 6 IQ1_M expert tensors have no Metal path; oversized wrap exits instead of falling back to streaming
issues.author: cuijs2026
issues.body:
### What happened

The GSQ-RCO **IQ2_XS** file cannot run on a Mac: the Metal engine dies during load, and after working around that it dies again on a Metal buffer limit. IQ2_XS is not offered by `metal/setup_mac.py` (`MAC_MODELS`), so this is about manual installs of a size the PC path supports (CUDA/HIP have IQ1_M kernels) but the Metal port does not.

**Step 1 — IQ1_M has no Metal path.** With the stock files from ISTA-DASLab's repo (pinned revision `ed59f92`), the engine exits while loading shard 1:

```
strata serve: the prompt path allocates its own buffers (too few cache slots to borrow)
ref: unknown type 29
```

Type 29 = IQ1_M. The file is mixed-precision; 6 expert tensors use it:

```
blk.8.ffn_gate_exps.weight   IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
blk.8.ffn_up_exps.weight     IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
blk.13.ffn_gate_exps.weight  IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
blk.13.ffn_up_exps.weight    IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
blk.37.ffn_gate_exps.weight  IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
blk.37.ffn_up_exps.weight    IQ1_M [2560, 640, 512]
```

`metal/src/ref_quant.cpp` (`block_bytes`) prints `ref: unknown type 29` and `std::exit(2)`; `metal/kernels/moe.metal` has no `T_IQ1_M` instantiation either (`GU_SET` covers Q2_0/IQ3_XXS/IQ2_XXS/IQ2_XS/IQ2_S/IQ3_S/IQ4_XS/K-quants/Q8_0). The CPU kernels note the same gap: `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx512.cpp` says *"IQ1_M stays on ggml-cpu (no shipped model has IQ1_M expert rows)"* — this IQ2_XS file does ship them, so the assumption no longer holds for the GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS release. CUDA has it (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu` `dq_iq1_m`), so the same file runs on PC.

**Step 2 — single-buffer wrap limit.** As a workaround I converted those 6 tensors offline to Q8_0 (dequantized with ggml's `dequantize_row_iq1_m`, re-quantized with the q8_0 reference rule; all other tensors copied byte-identical; pack rebuilt with `tools/iq_pack.py`). With `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0` (as on a resident Q2_0) the larger shard 1 (43,472,687,392 bytes) then fails to map as one MTLBuffer:

```
strata serve: the prompt path allocates its own buffers (too few cache slots to borrow)
mtl: wrap 43472699392 failed
```

`Context::wrap` (`metal/src/mtl_rt.mm`) exits(4) instead of falling back. `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1` avoids it (experts stream from the SSD), which is presumably why `setup_mac.py` chooses stream by size — but a wrapped start on an oversized file should either fall back to streaming or fail with a message that says so.

### What I expected

- Either the Metal port runs IQ2_XS as-is (add IQ1_M to `ref_quant.cpp` + the moe/prompt expert kernels, like CUDA), or
- `setup_mac.py` offers IQ2_XS with the conversion done at setup time, or at least fails with "this size needs IQ1_M, which Metal does not have" instead of a bare `ref: unknown type 29`.
- A wrap that exceeds Metal's buffer limit should fall back to streaming (or say to set `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1`) rather than `exit(4)`.

### Workaround (works, measured below)

1. Rewrite shard 1 with the 6 IQ1_M tensors as Q8_0 (`ref`-exact IQ1_M dequant → q8_0 reference quantize; ~+4.2 GB file size; verified: 1223 tensors, names/order unchanged, every other tensor byte-identical, `iq_pack.py` rebuilds cleanly).
2. `"env": {"STRATA_METAL_STREAM": "1"}` in the config.
3. IQ2_XS does not need its own MTP layer: `mtp_pack.py --experts q2_0` output is shared (the Metal loader reads `<mtp dir>/../mtp-q2_0.gguf`).

### Measurements (M4 Pro 64 GB, macOS, engine 0.1.44.1-metal)

Both sizes, same machine, `tools/strata_bench.py` (thinking off, medians):

| | IQ2_XS (streamed) | Q2_0 (resident) | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| chat decode tok/s | 26.6 | 33.1 | Q2_0 +24% |
| 4K prompt tok/s | 211.8 | 264.7 | Q2_0 +25% |
| 16K prompt tok/s | 223.4 | 273.5 | Q2_0 +22% |
| agent decode tok/s | 25.7 | 32.1 | Q2_0 +25% |

Note the comparison also mixes two differences: IQ2_XS streams (its pack does not wrap) while Q2_0 stays resident, and Q2_0's `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0` is the faster path on this Mac. Long-context recall (`tools/needle_bench.py`, 32K, depths 10/50/90): **3/3 found for both sizes**. Memory with IQ2_XS running: engine RSS 35.4 GB, no swap growth, 128K context (`--max-context 131072`) held a 124K-token prompt at 246.8 tok/s prefill.

Also worth noting for the "6 IQ1_M tensors" case: they are only in layers 8/13/37, gate+up; downs are Q2_0 like every other layer — a per-tensor fallback (dequant those rows once at load) would also cover it.

### Engine log

```
[mapping/expert-cache lines from startup]
ref: unknown type 29
```

and, after the workaround:

```
[strata metal: decode window ...]
mtl: wrap 43472699392 failed
```

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows: a second NVIDIA GPU halves the largest pinned allocation, so the RAM-budget complement silently falls back to pageable memory (CUDA counterpart of #2485)
issues.author: KLOP09
issues.body:
### What happened

On Windows, adding a second NVIDIA card (a GTX 1650 that drives no display and is hidden from CUDA with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<RTX 5070 UUID>`) made the low-RAM resident mode stop page-locking its RAM copy. Same config, same engine, before and after:

```
# GTX 1650 enabled
FileExpertSource: allocating 14.00 GiB page-locked cache complement
FileExpertSource: locked resident cache complement ready: resident 14.00 GiB, pinned 0.00 GiB; page-locking refused (out of memory); locked 14335 MiB via working-set minimum + VirtualLock

# GTX 1650 disabled in Device Manager (nothing else changed)
FileExpertSource: mapped pinned cache complement ready: resident 14.00 GiB, pinned 14.00 GiB; page-locked and mapped
```

**Cause: the largest single pinned allocation is halved, the total is not.** Measured with the CUDA driver API (`cuMemHostAlloc`, `PORTABLE | DEVICEMAP`, the same flags as the complement), only the RTX 5070 visible, ~26 GB RAM available:

| | GTX 1650 enabled | GTX 1650 disabled |
|---|---|---|
| largest single allocation | **7.344 GiB** (7.375 fails at once) | **14.719 GiB** |
| total held in 0.5 GiB pieces | 14.0 GiB | 14.5 GiB |
| 4 + 4 + 4 GiB held at once | the third one fails | — |

It looks like two ~7.3 GiB regions instead of one ~14.7 GiB region. Logging out does not change it (7.344 / 14.0 GiB again). With both GPUs visible to CUDA, and with the `default` flags, 6 GiB is granted and 8 GiB refused, as with only the 5070 visible. Windows reports 15,945 MB of shared GPU memory per adapter (half of 31.1 GB). Before the 1650 went in, a 14 GiB complement was pinned on this PC and a 19.8 GiB one was refused.

**Why the engine is hit:** on Windows, `FileExpertSource::pin_cache_complement` (v0.1.44.1, the same file on main today — read, not run) still asks for the whole complement with one `cudaHostAlloc(Mapped | Portable)`. The stepped registration of #1250 is only switched on inside `#if defined(__linux__)`, and `STRATA_PARTIAL_PIN` registers a single prefix. So with the default settings the whole 14 GiB stays pageable, the prompt path streams it through the stager, and the decode's PCIe share is off. `STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED` is in `ArenaExpertSource::open` only.

**Suggested fix:** #2485 does this for the SYCL port (2 GiB chunks, `complement_at()`), as `GgufExpertSource::mirror` already does. A CUDA counterpart would fix it here, with two changes for this kind of limit:
- 2 GiB chunks would reach only about 12 GiB here (three per 7.34 GiB region), so chunks of 1 GiB or less (or one per layer, as the arena does).
- keep the chunks that were granted, hottest experts first, and lock only the rest, rather than all-or-nothing.

### What it costs (0.1.31, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS, `--resident-budget-gib 14`, 64K, MTP, the same agentic tasks on two runs, logged in both times)

| medians, same task stage | complement pageable (1650 on) | complement pinned (1650 off) |
|---|---|---|
| decode, short-context tasks (replies ≥ 1,000 tokens) | 46.5 tok/s | 48.0 tok/s |
| decode, long-context repo tasks | 40.2 tok/s | 42.2 tok/s |
| new-session prompt read (8–10K tokens), short-context tasks | 229 tok/s | 233 tok/s |
| new-session prompt read (8–10K tokens), repo tasks | 230 tok/s | 254 tok/s |

So pinning is worth 3–5 % in decode and 2–10 % in prompt reading here: modest. The bigger reason is the next part.

**Possibly related to #879/#606 (not proven):** the all-NaN signature hit twice in the pageable run, 2 of 30 new sessions. Replies were `!` only, with the expert-cache hit at 99.1–99.9 % and decode at 74–127 tok/s. In the first event 14 requests in a row each ran to 32,000 tokens, until we stopped the server; the second was cut by a watcher after 61 s. Both times it struck the first request of a new session right after a ~31K-token session ended. That request read its 8.5–9.4K-token prompt from token 0. In the first event a dozen tokens came out normal and then the run collapsed; the fresh prompts that followed (also read from token 0) did the same, so the poisoned state was not only the conversation's K/V. With the complement pinned it was 0 of 233 new sessions before the 1650 went in. A replicate the next morning with the 1650 disabled gave 0 of 28 new sessions, 8 of them right after a ≥ 29K-token session. 2 of 30 against 0 of 28 alone is not significant (one-sided Fisher p ≈ 0.26). Against all pinned runs it is 0 of 261 (p ≈ 0.01, mixed conditions). The second GPU and a Windows update arrived on the same day, but pinned vs. pageable is the one engine-side difference we found.

**Workarounds (not yet measured):** disable the second card while Strata runs; `--resident-budget-gib 7` (fits one region); `STRATA_PARTIAL_PIN=1 STRATA_PARTIAL_PIN_GIB=7` (half pinned).

<details><summary>Probe script (Python, ctypes, CUDA driver API)</summary>

```python
import ctypes, os
cuda = ctypes.WinDLL('nvcuda.dll'); cuda.cuInit(0)
dev = ctypes.c_int(); cuda.cuDeviceGet(ctypes.byref(dev), 0)
ctx = ctypes.c_void_p(); cuda.cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain(ctypes.byref(ctx), dev); cuda.cuCtxSetCurrent(ctx)
def alloc(n):
    p = ctypes.c_void_p()
    return p if cuda.cuMemHostAlloc(ctypes.byref(p), ctypes.c_size_t(n), ctypes.c_uint(3)) == 0 else None  # PORTABLE|DEVICEMAP
lo, hi = 1, 16 * 32                      # 1/32 GiB steps
while hi - lo > 1:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    p = alloc(mid * 2 ** 25)
    if p: cuda.cuMemFreeHost(p); lo = mid
    else: hi = mid
held = []
while len(held) < 64:
    p = alloc(2 ** 29)
    if not p: break
    held.append(p)
print(f'largest single allocation {lo/32:.3f} GiB | total in 0.5 GiB pieces {len(held)*0.5:.1f} GiB')
for p in held: cuda.cuMemFreeHost(p)
```
</details>

### Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.31 (the code path above is the same in v0.1.44.1 / main) · RTX 5070 12 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16) + GTX 1650 4 GB (PCIe 3.0 x4, no display, hidden from CUDA) · Windows 11 Pro 26H2 build 26300.9711 · NVIDIA 617.14 · HAGS on · Ryzen 7 9800X3D · 32 GB

issues.title: Strata Deck — a web control panel add-on (Linux, battle-tested)
issues.author: CamTechLinear
issues.body:
Hi Niko — first off, Strata is brilliant. Getting Qwen3.8-Flash-Next running on a 12GB RTX 3060 with this kind of throughput felt like magic in my shop, so thank you.

I built **Strata Deck**, an independent web control panel for Strata hosts, and it's been running production workloads (including live AI-agent traffic) on Linux for a while now. MIT-licensed, no engine internals touched — it drives Strata through its own `run-<model>.sh` / `setup.py` scripts and the `/v1/status` API.

**Repo:** https://github.com/CamTechLinear/strata-deck

What it does:
- **Dashboard** — engine status, GPU/VRAM, RAM, model disk, live timings
- **Model management** — start/switch/stop, install new quants via `setup.py` (resumable), tuner for `strata-<model>.json` with `.bak` safety
- **IN USE guard** — uses the engine's own `activity` counters to block stop/restart while sessions are live, with recent-consumer hostnames shown before you pull the trigger. Built this after learning the hard way that stopping the `serve/server.py` proxy kills client sessions even when the engine stays loaded — a failure invisible to GPU monitoring
- **Stale-path detector** — flags configs pointing at moved/deleted data dirs (the classic post-`--data-dir`-migration footgun)
- **cgroup-safe launches** — models start in their own `systemd-run` units so restarting the panel never touches the serving chain
- **Audit log** — every control action records caller, decision, engine state, consumers

A few ideas in there (stale-path detection, validate-before-stop switching, the proxy-vs-engine distinction) might be worth stealing into the engine itself — happy to help if useful.

Would you be open to linking it as a community add-on in the README? And if there's appetite, I'd like to map out Windows/macOS support — currently it's Linux + systemd user services.

Screenshots are in the repo README. Feedback welcome — and thanks again for Strata.

issues.title: RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) on Windows, v0.1.44.1: --adapt-async +6.2%, STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 +8.5% (cumulative 64.8 → 79.2 tok/s)
issues.author: bigbrid2023
issues.body:
Sharing measurements from a Windows + RX 7900 XTX setup, since I understand Windows AMD coverage is limited. All numbers are from the current release, v0.1.44.1, single GPU, IQ3_S pack.

**System**
- GPU: RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro
- CPU / RAM: i9-13900KF, 128 GB DDR4-3200
- Engine: Strata v0.1.44.1 (release build)

**Method**
Fixed fixture for every configuration: 72-token prompt, 256 output tokens, 1 warmup + 3 measured runs, fresh process per run, `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`. Each change was compared against a control re-run in the same batch (batch-to-batch drift on this machine is up to ~±4%). A gain is only reported as confirmed when it exceeds 3% and the run ranges do not overlap.

**Results (median tok/s)**

| Configuration | tok/s | Note |
|---|---|
| Stock defaults (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`) | 64.8 | |
| `--spec-min-p 0.7` | 67.1–67.6 | ~+4% |
| + `--adapt-async 1` | 72.4 | +6.2% vs same-batch control (68.2); adapt wait 2.84 → 0.38 ms/window |
| + `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7` | 79.2 | +8.5% vs same-batch control (73.0); host CPU experts 4.79 → 2.38 ms/window; VRAM residency 90.7% → 95.1%; MTP acceptance 75.1% → 74.6% |

Two notes that may be useful upstream:

1. **ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP default on gfx1100.** As far as I can tell from the source, the tail-skip default is enabled on HIP only for gfx1200/1201 (`decode_defaults_arch_ok`), and gfx1100 starts with it off. On this card `=7` was worth +8.5% with a negligible acceptance change (−0.5 pt). If the gfx1100 exclusion is not based on a known correctness issue, enabling the same default for gfx1100 would give every 7900 XTX user this gain out of the box. (Understood that outputs differ slightly with it on, as documented.)
2. **Negative results, for the record:** `--kv k8v4` was unstable here (median +7.5%, but one run dropped to 68.8, overlapping the control range, and it added nothing on top of ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP); `--spec 3` was −3.8% vs spec 4; `STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED=1` showed no decode gain. Tuning `--adapt-every / -decay / -swaps` around the defaults also showed no further gain, so the defaults look well chosen.

Happy to provide full timing breakdowns or test other settings on this hardware if useful.

issues.title: gfx1201 (R9700, HIP): the `!` degeneration is #879 — GDN state overflow (max |x| 2.26e+32) at 16K–93K; 0.1.44.1's guard catches and recovers it on this box
issues.author: aiworkeryuan-chuxi
issues.body:
Following the maintainer's note in #1468 ("if this still happens on 0.1.44, leave a comment here … a new issue that links this one works too"). This is a single-card gfx1201/HIP data point, and it comes with a mechanism trace plus a confirmation that 0.1.44's NaN guard catches this fault **on a machine where your own 1,870-request R9700 run could not fire it**.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 1x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4), 32 GB |
| Host | 62 GiB RAM, Linux 6.17, NVMe; no swap in use during any run |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS** (`ISTA-DASLab/…`, rev `ed59f920`; shard 1 47,039,860,096 B, sha256 `219ea929900dfa9ef091f3aa473fdba6874b65fcb36526d7d851ac9e95856d15`) |
| Build | local HIP build against the **ROCm 7.10 "TheRock" userspace** (setup's venv wheels, not system ROCm) |
| Versions | most measurements on **0.1.42**; the guard confirmation below is on **0.1.44.1** (same box, same build chain, upgraded today) |
| Args | `--max-context 131072 --kv int8 --prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --vram-reserve-mib 1000` |
| Env | `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0`; WMMA off; `STRATA_PF_FUSED` unset (0.1.42 default) / explicitly `=0` on 0.1.44.1 |

## 1. The `!` degeneration is the non-finite family — traced here on 0.1.42

`STRATA_DBG_NAN=1` already exists in 0.1.42, so no guard is needed to see it. Same config, two 16K requests, one degenerate and one clean:

```
# degenerate (reply = 40 x '!')
strata dbg: layer 0 (mmq 1, types 17/20, 0 experts): non-finite GU 0 H -1 Dm 0 bo 33226240 of T 17075
strata dbg: prompt end: last residual row 10240 non-finite (max |x| 0); PLE history 0 non-finite (max |x| 21.1);
            GDN state 0 9264 non-finite (max |x| 2.26e+32)
strata dbg: verify window at position 17075, row 0: 248320 of 248320 logits non-finite (token out 0)

# clean request, same config
strata dbg: prompt end: last residual row 0 non-finite (max |x| 5.13); PLE history 0 non-finite (max |x| 12.4);
            GDN state 0 0 non-finite (max |x| 3.34)
```

- **`248320 of 248320 logits non-finite`** — the same count the reporter in #1208 got on gfx1030 (whole vocab).
- **`GDN state … 9264 non-finite (max |x| 2.26e+32)`** — the recurrent state's magnitude has run away to 1e32 before the residual goes non-finite; the clean request prints **0** for both fields. So here the chain is: *GDN state overflow → residual row non-finite → all logits NaN → sampler collapses to token 0 (`!`)*.
- This fires at a **16K** prompt, while the same box reads 63K/76K/85K cleanly — so on this hardware it is not a context-capacity effect.
- Cost of the instrument, for anyone reusing it: `STRATA_DBG_NAN=1` takes a 16K-prompt prefill from ~1,400 tok/s to ~310 tok/s (~4.5x), and it prints informational (all-zero) lines on passing requests too.

## 2. On 0.1.44.1 your guard catches exactly this, and the retry recovers it

Interleaved arm, 40K cold needle prompts, fresh nonce per request, engine restarted per arm, with our amplifier `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` (see §5):

```
non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window at position 38621 (row 0): its tokens are not emitted,
the request ends (DONE nonfinite) and the next request reads its prompt from token 0
non-finite logits (#879): dropped the live session, 2 checkpoints, 0 parked conversations and 0 idle slots …
```

The three probes in that arm **all returned the correct answer** (via the retry), and the log line names the position. On 0.1.42 the same fault was emitted as 40 `!` characters with no log line at all, so from a user's point of view the guard turns silent corruption into a visible, recoverable event. Thank you for #1892.

## 3. Server-side behaviour worth documenting

After a degeneration, re-sending the **same** prompt is served from the prefix cache (`prompt 38438 tokens = 38431 reused + 7 read in 38 ms`) and **degenerates again**; a **different** prompt sent immediately after, same engine, answers correctly. So the poisoned state follows the conversation/prefix rather than the engine — consistent with #2452's retry-from-0 and with #879's "session-scoped, not engine-global". Users may be wasting a full re-read by retrying the same request; a new conversation recovers without a reload.

## 4. Two levers that do nothing here (so other 32 GB / gfx12 users don't spend the time)

- **`STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`** (#1208's fix on gfx1030): interleaved 8 rounds x 2 arms, 40K, `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` in both arms, on 0.1.42 — **3/8 vs 2/8, Fisher one-tailed p = 0.50**. It does not transfer to single-card gfx1201.
- **`STRATA_KV_STAGE_OWN=1`**: `take_stage()` returns unless the session is KV-streaming, so on a **KV-resident** config the variable has no object at all (our logs never contain `KV streaming:`). We then built the condition it needs (`--kv-resident 32768`) and first verified the lever acts — `the prompt path borrows 8066 → 7988 CUDA0 cache slots (13.14 → 13.01 GiB)`, the 13.01 GiB being exactly the resident-run figure your comment in `prefill.cpp` predicts — and the A/B is **null: 1/8 vs 1/8 (Fisher p = 0.77)**, 0 engine faults in the 21 requests of that configuration. Worth a line in the docs: on a 32 GB card with resident KV this arm can only produce a false negative.

## 5. The amplifier, for anyone trying to reproduce

`STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` (0.1.42, opt-in there): at 40K it raises the degeneration rate from 0/8 (baseline) to **3/8 (37.5%)** in an interleaved arm — consistent with our earlier 6/18 vs 0/8. That is why we pin `STRATA_PF_FUSED=0` in production and why the fact that 0.1.43 turned it on by default for IQ3_XXS matters to us.

## 6. And the other signature, for the record

`prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access` at ~93K tokens (91,511, frozen at `65,536 of 91,511`), ≈1/13 requests on 0.1.42 with the production config; 63K/76K/85K read cleanly. We have only one 93K pass on 0.1.44.1 so far, so we cannot say anything about whether that changed.

## 7. What we could not test

Our engine is built against the **TheRock 7.10 wheels**. The follow-up comment in #1208 reports the default batched MMQ path as finite on ROCm 10 system packages and NaN with the TheRock 7.10 wheels, which points at the ROCm side rather than the engine. We have not A/B'd ROCm userspaces here (this box also serves two other engines that depend on the current setup). If that comparison is worth having, say which userspace and we will build it.

We can also bisect, or dump token ids around a failing position, or run any specific env/arm on gfx1201 — the config above is the exact one. If `STRATA_DBG_NAN`-style counters at the GDN update are easier than at the logits, that would localise the overflow source faster than we can from outside.

issues.title: SYCL, Arc A770 (i915): serve-mode SIGSEGV at the first graph-replay window (dies after layer 0); STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1 avoids it
issues.author: afterthought325
issues.body:
**Hardware:** Arc A770 16 GB (Alchemist, **i915**), LXC container (Debian forky/sid) with the card passed through from a Proxmox host running kernel 7.0.14-20-pve. oneAPI 2026.1, NEO (`libze-intel-gpu1`) current. Ryzen 9 5900X, 64 GB RAM.
**Build:** `v0.1.44.1` (`296b59d2`), `build-sycl`, engine banner `session is up (engine 0.1.44.1)`.
**Model:** UnitySC Swift 1.5 (qwen4exp arch) IQ2_XS native pack, MTP head, PLE, `--resident-experts --spec 4 --mtp --max-context 32768 --kv k8v4 --expert-cache auto` (2579 slots, 3.47 GiB), `--no-prefill-borrow --prefill 4096`. Env: `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0`, `IGC_EnableDPEmulation=1`, `NEOReadDebugKeys=1`, `OverrideDefaultFP64Settings=1`.

What happens
------------

Through `serve/server.py`, every request dies the same way: the engine exits with **SIGSEGV (exit code -11)** about 12.5 s after the request starts, before emitting any token. The startup capture itself succeeds:

    strata verify: window up to 6 tokens, 56.9 MiB of device buffers
    strata serve: 6330 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
    strata verify: captured the 6-token window (upload no error, sync no error)

and the first `GEN` line kills it. With `STRATA_VERIFY_DEBUG=1` the ladder localizes it to the **first window replay, right after layer 0**:

    verify dbg: captured; staging
    verify dbg: staged; launching
    verify dbg: launched
    verify dbg: layer 0 rang
    <process dies>

Reproduced standalone without the HTTP server (same argv captured from the live engine, `GEN 16 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8` piped to stdin after READY): same death after `layer 0 rang`.

Bisect
------

* **The one-shot (non-serve) path with the same args and model does NOT crash** (14.95 tok/s decode, clean DONE). serve-vs-one-shot is the axis.
* `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1` **fixes it**: the standalone repro completes (`DONE 16 8 12749.9 4140.3 ...`), and serve mode has been stable since at 18.3-19.5 tok/s decode, 56% expert-cache hit rate.
* No change from: `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=20000000`, `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1` (with and without), `--no-prefill-borrow`, and dropping `--resident-experts` (still crashes).
* `--no-capture` could not be used to isolate the replay path: it refuses to start with `--resident-experts` ("session_token has NO CPU expert-pool hook").
* Kernel side is clean: host `dmesg` shows nothing from i915/DRM around the crashes — no GT reset, no job timeout. Pure userspace SIGSEGV.

Note this is a different failure from #2194 (queue never drains, hang): here the process segfaults, and `STRATA_WINDOW_SYNC` is already at its i915 default of 1, so the drain-before-window fix from 0.1.44 is active and does not prevent this.

Question
--------

Is there an i915-specific assumption in the captured graph-replay window path (the one-shot path and the stepped path both survive; only the serve-mode graph replay dies, at the first MoE layer after the dense layer 0)? Curious whether the capture records something the i915 backend re-resolves differently on replay.

Happy to run a debug build, `ZE_DEBUG`, ASAN, or a candidate patch against this box — the standalone repro takes one load (~4 min) and one `GEN` line.

issues.title: KV compaction and hot-swappable KV sessions (two proposals)
issues.author: shahrokhzargarpour
issues.body:
Two forward-looking KV ideas, split clearly from what we already run.

## What already exists (our fork)

The conversation-cache disk tier we run saves by stage as content-addressed segments, dedups the `Sys` between conversations (same `head = H(model||config)`), and has a prefix restore ladder. Measured on Windows: reload of a 171.5k context in 657 ms vs 158.6 s cold, and 1,294 real restores over 8 days with about 90.5 M tokens not re-prefilled. A PR for this disk tier is being prepared from our fork.

## (a) KV compaction

Today the tier saves per stage, but the stationary KV components - the system prompt and fixed headers - are still carried inside every image. The missing piece: compact those stationary components as independent, deduplicated KV segments (their own content-addressed blocks) instead of dragging them through every park/restore. Related: #1090 and #1331 (system-prompt prefix on disk), #1962 (share identical KV prefix blocks across concurrent conversations).

## (b) Continuous KV sessions

Store KV as detachable fragments that can be dropped and re-attached in place - a dynamic context window guided by RAG (fragments retrieved by embedding + reranking) instead of re-prefilling. Related: #2351 (prefix mount, splices, checkpoint ladder), #2431 (prefix reuse falls back to root-ck), #1269/#1511/#1164 (session restore and prefixes), and #2434 (KV page-pool policy measurement).

## Not proven

- The stationary-KV compaction is not implemented or measured.
- No RAG-guided fragment retention/retrieval has been built or benchmarked - section (b) is aspirational, not a claim.
- These are Windows-only measurements; the maintainer noted there is no Windows test box on their side (#2185/#1412).

issues.title: Metal: an MTP draft layer with Q4_0 experts stops the engine at the first request ("no function moe_gu_2_32_1_4")
issues.author: joesinvestments
issues.body:
### What happened

`tools/mtp_pack.py` offers `--experts q2_0 | q4_0 | q8_0` (its header names `mtp-q4_0.gguf` the acceptance comparison
arm). On the Metal engine a Q4_0 draft layer loads, then the engine exits with code 3 at the first request, on every pack
we tried (IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, UD-Q4_K_XL). The Q2_0 layer that setup writes and a Q8_0 layer built the same way both work.

The log names the cause: the Metal library has no MoE gate/up kernel for that expert type and tile:
`mtl: no function moe_gu_2_32_1_4 Function moe_gu_2_32_1_4 was not found in the library`.

If Q4_0 is not meant for Metal, a refusal at load (as for Qwen3.6) would be friendlier than an exit at the first request.

```
.venv/bin/python tools/mtp_pack.py --src <Strata-data>/mtp --experts q4_0 --out <Strata-data>/mtp/mtp-q4_0.gguf
STRATA_METAL_MTP_GGUF=<Strata-data>/mtp/mtp-q4_0.gguf  (config args: --mtp <Strata-data>/mtp/rt --spec 3)
```
Then any chat request. With `mtp-q8_0.gguf` the same config answers normally, and its output equals the no-MTP output
token for token on our three test prompts.

issues.title: Metal: a short side request drops the conversation cache (parking is refused, then "invalid checkpoint running-state payload")
issues.author: joesinvestments
issues.body:
### What happened

On the Metal engine a single short request from another conversation (an agent's "give this chat a title" call) drops the
main conversation, and its next turn reads the whole prompt again. Same symptom as #1920 on CUDA, but on a Mac the
documented fix (`--conversation-cache-mib`) cannot work, for two reasons we found in v0.1.44 (still the same on `main`
296b59d2):

1. **The memory guard has no macOS reading.** `sample_host_memory()` in `src/core/conversation_memory.cpp` has branches
   for `_WIN32` and `__linux__` only and returns nothing elsewhere, so every Mac start logs
   `memory guard: the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore are refused`.
   (`src/core/expert_source.cpp` already reads macOS memory with `host_statistics64`.) A small PR for this follows.
2. **With the guard fixed and the cache turned on, parking still fails on every request:**
   `conversation cache: skip parking (conversation snapshot: invalid checkpoint running-state payload)`.
   As far as we can read the code: `conversation_checkpoint_save` / `_restore` have `STRATA_GPU_METAL` branches
   (`window_checkpoint_save` / `_restore`, `conversation_state.cpp` ~167-194), but the parking path validates with the
   host layout every time (`view_validate()` ~line 85 and the snapshot check ~line 360 call
   `conversation_checkpoint_validate()`), while `Window::checkpoint_save` (`metal/src/engine/window.cpp` ~1375-1398)
   packs the GDN state and history its own way and leaves `block_pos` empty. So the size check cannot pass on Metal.

Also: `docs/MAC.md` does not mention the conversation cache, and `metal/setup_mac.py` does not print the
`--conversation-cache-mib` tip that `setup.py` prints on a PC.

**Repro (one request at a time, greedy, thinking off):** a ~16K-token prompt of real code, two follow-up turns, then a
60-token unrelated request, then a fourth turn of the first conversation. UD-Q4_K_XL streamed from the SSD:

| step | prompt tokens | reused | time to first token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| turn 1 | 15,680 | 0 | 22.1 s |
| turn 2 | 15,961 | 15,675 | 0.86 s |
| turn 3 | 16,239 | 15,956 | 1.32 s |
| side request | 60 | 0 | 1.11 s |
| turn 4 | 16,519 | **0** | **22.4 s** |

Identical with (a) the release engine, (b) the guard fixed, and (c) the guard fixed plus `--conversation-cache-mib 4096
--conversation-cache-slots 4`. IQ3_XXS behaves the same. We have not tried a Metal snapshot ourselves.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Strata v0.1.44 (ed4773eb) built from source with `./setup.sh`, Metal engine. Mac Studio M5 Max (40-core GPU), 64 GB,
macOS 27.0.1, `iogpu.wired_limit_mb=58000`. Packs: Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL and IQ3_XXS (GSQ-RCO), both streaming their experts
from the SSD (`STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1`). `--spec 3` with the MTP draft layer, `--prefill auto`, `--max-context 32768`.

### Engine log

Release engine:
```
strata generate: memory guard: the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore are refused
strata serve: prompt 15680 tokens = 0 reused + 15680 read in 22122 ms (708.8 tok/s), 256 generated in 6344 ms (40.4 tok/s), drafts accepted 120 of 272, 1 checkpoints
strata serve: prompt 15961 tokens = 15675 reused + 286 read in 856 ms (334.2 tok/s), 256 generated in 5527 ms (46.3 tok/s), drafts accepted 140 of 232, 2 checkpoints
strata serve: prompt 16239 tokens = 15956 reused + 283 read in 1316 ms (215.1 tok/s), 256 generated in 5562 ms (46.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 140 of 230, 3 checkpoints
strata serve: prompt 60 tokens = 0 reused + 60 read in 1112 ms (53.9 tok/s), 16 generated in 282 ms (56.7 tok/s), drafts accepted 11 of 12, 1 checkpoints
strata serve: prompt 16519 tokens = 0 reused + 16519 read in 22424 ms (736.7 tok/s), 256 generated in 5348 ms (47.9 tok/s), drafts accepted 137 of 238, 2 checkpoints
```
Guard fixed, `--conversation-cache-mib 4096 --conversation-cache-slots 4`:
