issues.title: Long generation ratchets to !×256 at the default 20,000 spin bound — 2× Arc Pro B60 (xe), 4,331 host-served experts, engine 0.1.44
issues.author: MaineTim
issues.body:
The server's repeat-stop message points at #606; this is a different failure — the #606 tell is
checked in the signature below.

## What happens

On a two-card layer split with 4,331 experts served by the host, long generations collapse into a
single-token repeat: initial lucid output, partial draft-accept throughout, then `!`×256 at some window, ended
by `repeat_stop_tokens`. Short requests in the same session are clean. The outcome follows the config,
not the drive or the card state — same box, same boot, same model:

| engine config | result |
|---|---|
| `--ple-io direct`, default 20,000 bound | garbage from the first window, **6/6 requests over two days**, byte-identical fingerprint; drafts accepted 100% (124/124, 126/126); 21.7–43.5 tok/s |
| direct, `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=200000` | clean: 334 + 4,876 tok, 65.9/66.4 % accepted, 15.3/28.3 tok/s |
| direct, `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=40000` | clean: 2,705 tok (541 windows), 65.9 %, 24.7 tok/s |
| direct, `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=30000` | req 1 clean (637 tok); req 2 lucid to ~5,688 tok, then `!`×256 (5,944 total; 31.5 tok/s) |
| `--ple-io mmap`, default 20,000 bound, short | clean: 635 + 483 tok, 65.9/66.4 %, 17.3/26.4 tok/s |
| `--ple-io mmap`, 20,000 bound, long (3 requests) | req 1 clean (810 tok, 72.2 %); req 2 lucid to ~3,000 tok, then `!`×256 (3,037 total; 30.8 tok/s; 68.5 %); req 3 ("continue" on the ratcheted conversation) lucid to ~2,660 tok, then `!`×256 (5,889 total; 34.4 tok/s; 69.9 %) |
| `--ple-io mmap`, 20,000 bound, long, second independent run (3 requests) | req 1 clean (564 tok, 67.0 %); req 2 lucid to ~6,004 tok, then `!`×256 (6,260 total; 31.2 tok/s; 69.0 %); req 3 ("continue") lucid to ~1,176 tok, then `!`×256 (1,432 total; 36.5 tok/s; 73.0 %) |

Token positions are exact (server CLI log); window counts are estimates at ~5 tok/window, so: first
ratchet at window 1 (direct 20k), ~608 and ~1,200 (mmap 20k, two independent runs), ~1,138 (direct 30k),
0 over 541 windows (direct 40k).
Single events, so the rates are wide-bracket estimates, not a CDF.

## Signature (why this is not #606)

- Lucid prefix, then a step into the repeat; draft-accept stays partial (68–72 %) up to the ratchet —
  not the 100 %-of-everything collapse.
- **A fresh short prompt answers cleanly before and after** — the #606 tell. The q8_1 clamps are in
  0.1.44.
- The ratchet is per-conversation: continuing a ratcheted conversation ratchets again (req 3 above); a
  fresh conversation starts clean.
- Drive state exonerated within the measured range: the drive was in its fast state (PLE random 4 KiB
  65,267–66,155 rows/s) in every run, garbage included. The one slow-state observation (13,955 rows/s,
  cold) predates all of them.
- mmap does not remove the tail: two independent long runs, first ratchet at ~window 608 and ~1,200 vs
  ~1,138 at direct 30k — so it is not only PLE direct-IO drive contention. I have not attributed the
  residual.

## Environment

- 2× Intel Arc Pro B60 24 GB (8086:e211), xe driver, `--layer-split 25` (card 0: layers 0–24; card 1:
  25–47 + head). PCIe probes at start: 3.1 GB/s (card 0), 14.0 GB/s (card 1).
- Ryzen 5 5600XT (AVX2-only — engine line "this CPU has no AVX-512 … run on AVX-2"), 64 GB DDR4.
- NVMe: WDC WDS100T2B0B (WD Black SN770 1 TB), DRAM-less. Measured: PLE random 4 KiB 13,955 rows/s
  (slow, once, cold) / 65,267–66,155 (fast, every run); expert shard fill 0.45–0.62 GB/s.
- CachyOS, kernel 7.2.9-1-cachyos. Compute runtime (NEO) 26.35.39758; `sycl-ls`:
  `[level_zero:gpu] Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics 20.1.0 [1.17.39758]` on both cards;
  oneAPI/SPCL 2026.21.7.0.24_160000. rusticl 26.2.4-arch3.1 present, not selected.
- Engine **0.1.44 at `ed4773eb`**, SYCL AOT build (`bmg-g21`), `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, one slot.

Engine config (the long run; the baseline differs only in `--ple-io direct` / the spin bound):

```
--pack …/pack-ud-iq4_xs --native …/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf
--expert-profile …/expert-profile-ud-iq4_xs.bin --expert-cache auto --stream-experts
--ple-io mmap --layer-split 25 --prefill auto --max-context 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 1024
--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp …/mtp/rt
```

env: `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1 STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0 STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1
STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=12 SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=0 ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:*`
(no `STRATA_SPIN_MAX` in any mmap run)

Load: 8,036 slots / 18.08 GiB on card 0; 4,764 of the missing experts mirrored in 10.63 GiB pinned
host memory; 7,445 of 11,776 profiled pairs on card 1; **4,331 experts served by the host**;
1,633 MiB of VRAM free; verify windows captured, no faults before the first request.

All runs under one boot (`uptime -s` 2026-10-09 19:37:32); `dmesg` clear and no devcoredump through
the last run.

Prompts (identical first prompt in every run, same thinking setting): "Tell me about the seven seas."
/ "Expand, and be detailed." / "continue".

## Not tested

Slow drive state; `--ple-io mmap` + `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=40000`; 40k over more than 541 windows; one card.

## Notes

1. The verify path has no per-window "wait ran to its bound" report (contrast `ep_check` in #1798):
   the first expired window here was silent, and everything above was reconstructed from the output.
   A one-line report, or an env switch to enable one, would make this class self-diagnosing.
2. For a layout with a large host-served share on xe, is `STRATA_SPIN_MAX=40000` a sound permanent
   setting, or should the bound follow the host-served count / mirror size?

Full engine logs and per-request server CLI output for every row of the table are available on request.

All test configs run natively and data collected on host. Data collated and summarized by Qwen 3.8.

issues.title: [Bug]: BENCH.bat / strata_bench.py crashes on Windows with a non-UTF-8 locale (UnicodeDecodeError reading CMakeLists.txt)
issues.author: hasifumi
issues.body:
### What happened

`BENCH.bat` (`tools/strata_bench.py`) stops right after it finds the server on Windows with a Japanese locale (ANSI code page cp932). It never runs the suite:

```
Using the Strata server already running at http://127.0.0.1:8080.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<strata>\tools\strata_bench.py", line 1028, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File "<strata>\tools\strata_bench.py", line 989, in main
    pre = collect_machine(base, key, cfg, a.gpu)
  File "<strata>\tools\strata_bench.py", line 639, in collect_machine
    "strata_version": project_version(), "strata_commit": git_commit(),
  File "<strata>\tools\strata_bench.py", line 564, in project_version
    m = re.search(r"project\(strata VERSION ([\d.]+)", (ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text())
  File "...\Python311\Lib\pathlib.py", line 1059, in read_text
    return f.read()
UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0xef in position 0: illegal multibyte sequence
```

**Steps:** a v0.1.44.1 checkout on Windows 11 (Japanese), then `BENCH.bat` (or `.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080`).

**Cause:** `CMakeLists.txt` starts with a UTF-8 BOM (`ef bb bf`). `project_version()` calls `read_text()` with no encoding, so Python uses the locale's code page (cp932 here). The `except OSError` around it does not catch `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`), so the whole run stops instead of reporting no version. Other non-UTF-8 code pages (cp936, cp949, cp1252...) should hit the same error. Linux and English Windows usually read UTF-8, which is probably why it has not shown up.

**Workaround:** `set PYTHONUTF8=1` before `BENCH.bat`. With it, the run finishes normally.

**Possible fix:** `(ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")`, and/or `except (OSError, ValueError)` so that a version that cannot be read never stops the benchmark. I only checked this one call. The `/proc` reads in the same file are Linux-only, so they are not affected.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

Strata v0.1.44.1 (engine 0.1.44.1, CUDA 13.0 ready-made), RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, Windows 11 Pro 26200 (Japanese), Python 3.11

### Engine log

Not relevant: the engine runs fine, and only the benchmark client fails.

issues.title: calibrate's --pcie-frac 0.00 recommendation wedges the served engine at boot on AMD gfx1201 (ROCm)
issues.author: bhodgens
issues.body:
# Strata calibrate recommendation wedges the served engine at boot on AMD (gfx1201)

**Strata version:** v0.1.44 (`ed4773e`)
**Backend:** HIP/ROCm, built from source for **gfx1201** (Radeon AI PRO R9700)
**Host:** Ubuntu, ROCm 7.2.1, AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 + R9700 (discrete)
**Model:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, served native, `--shared-expert-arena /dev/shm/strata-arena`, `--adapt-async 1`

## Problem

`tools/calibrate.py` recommended `--pcie-frac 0.00` and `--spec-min-p 0.70`, and its own interleaved measurement showed ~23% decode gain (65.8 vs 53.4 t/s). But applying those settings to the **served** config wedges the engine during startup.

## Repro

1. Start flashnext from a config whose args end with:
   ```
   ... --kv k8v4 --ple-io ram --shared-expert-arena /dev/shm/strata-arena --adapt-async 1 --pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70
   ```
2. Engine prints up to `strata generate: GPU 0: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201)` then produces **no further log output**, indefinitely.
3. Process state is `D` (uninterruptible sleep) + `L` (memory-locked), CPU at 2-5%, for 6+ minutes (we killed it; may never complete).
4. Removing `--pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70` (back to the pre-calibrate config, `--spec-min-p 0.5`, no explicit `--pcie-frac`) boots normally and serves ~70 t/s.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: calibrate's recommended settings load and serve like any config.
- Actual: the engine hangs at/just after `GPU 0: ...` device enumeration when `--pcie-frac 0.00` is present.

## Additional notes

- `--spec-min-p 0.70` alone is likely safe (it is just the MTP draft-confidence floor and measured near-neutral); we isolated the hang to the full calibrate settings, not to `--spec-min-p` alone. We did not binary-search which flag causes it.
- `--pool-workers 15` (the default on this host) was already optimal per calibrate; no issue there.
- The calibrate harness measures the engine in-process (`StrataEngine.generate`) rather than the served path, so a setting that measures well can still fail the served bootstrap. It would help to have the served path covered too, or a note that calibrate results are engine-only.

This is on a discrete AMD card (gfx1201, ROCm) — not a Mac/Metal or NVIDIA path.

issues.title: [Engine] serve drops the connection when the engine program cannot be started
issues.author: devYRPauli
issues.body:
### Area

[Engine]  (speed, kernels, models, the server and API)

### Desktop app, Terminal or source?

Source (START-HERE.bat, setup.sh or a build)

### What happened

When the server cannot start the engine program, the request that starts the engine gets no HTTP answer. The client sees a closed connection with no status line. This happens on a lazy first load and on a restart after the engine stopped.

Any `OSError` from `subprocess.Popen` takes this path. Three examples:

- The engine program is missing (`FileNotFoundError`).
- The file is not executable (`PermissionError`).
- Windows blocks the program (#735, WinError 4551 or 1260). I simulated this case with an `OSError` at the `subprocess.Popen` boundary.

Expected: a 503 with the reason. An engine that exits before READY already gets one (#1527). The comment above `raise EngineDied` in `StrataEngine.__init__` asks for the same result.

I re-tested each of the three cases on 0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480) with 6 requests: chat, messages and responses, streamed and not.

- All 18 requests end with `RemoteDisconnected`.
- The server prints the `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError` or `OSError` traceback for each request.
- `/health` still reports `status: ok`.
- Each failed start leaves one start narrator thread alive. After 6 requests, 6 narrator threads are alive.
- The engine log handle of the last failed start stays open.

Cause: `StrataEngine.__init__` calls `popen()` with no handler. The `OSError` passes through `restart()`, which catches only `RuntimeError`, and through `Service.ensure_loaded()`. The request handler's `except OSError` branch records `disconnected` and re-raises, so `socketserver` closes the socket. On this path `__init__` also never sets the `loading` event and never closes `self.log`.

PR #2497 fixes this and contains 0.2.0-beta. I ran the same 18 requests on its head (e7680b9d7). All 18 get a 503 with the reason, for example `the engine could not be started: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/strata'`. No narrator thread stays alive, and the log handle is closed.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

Save this as `repro.py` in the repo root and run `python repro.py`. It needs no GPU and no engine build.

```python
import json
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from serve.server import ByteTokenizer, ChatTemplate, Service, StrataEngine, serve

eng = StrataEngine("/no/such/strata", [], log="strata-test.log", lazy=True)
svc = Service(eng, ByteTokenizer(), ChatTemplate(Path("serve/chat_template.jinja")))
httpd = serve(svc, port=0)
url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{httpd.server_address[1]}/v1/chat/completions"
body = json.dumps({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "max_tokens": 8}).encode()
try:
    urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}))
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, getattr(e, "code", ""), e.read().decode() if hasattr(e, "read") else e)
```

On 0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480) the script prints this line:

```
RemoteDisconnected  Remote end closed connection without response
```

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally

### Strata version

Strata 0.2.0-beta, tag v0.2.0-beta, commit 3d1fb480. serve/ only, no engine build.

### Graphics card, memory and system

No GPU used (the engine never starts). Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB RAM, macOS 27.0.1, Python 3.12.14

### Model, size and settings

None. The failure happens before a model loads.

### Logs

The server output for one request on 0.2.0-beta:

```
[strata] loading the model again (it was unloaded) ...
[strata] starting the engine: reading the model's weights ...
...
  File "serve/server.py", line 3831, in ensure_loaded
    self.engine.restart()
  File "serve/server.py", line 1253, in restart
    self.__init__(*self.spawn)
  File "serve/server.py", line 997, in __init__
    self.proc = popen("the Strata engine", [exe, "--serve", *args], cwd=cwd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
  File "serve/lifeline.py", line 256, in popen
    child = subprocess.Popen(args, **kw)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/strata'
```

issues.title: STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 vs 0 on an RTX 5080 16 GB (0.1.44, UD-IQ4_XS, 352K real conversation): +6% warm decode, prefill unchanged; the decode hit rate excludes skipped experts
issues.author: enkynakamura
issues.body:
### Setup

- RTX 5080 16 GB (sm_120), Xeon w7-2475X, 128 GB DDR5, Windows; engine **0.1.44** (not 0.1.44.1)
- Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, `--kv int8`, `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 3 --max-context 786432`, `--expert-cache auto` (2401 slots, 5.40 GiB), `--vram-reserve-mib 1420`, `--spec 5 --spec-min-p 0.8`, `--suffix-draft 0`, `--pcie-frac 0.33`, `--resident-budget-gib 55`
- env: `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 STRATA_IQ_GATHER=1 STRATA_IQ_PREFETCH=4096 STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=8 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`
- The two arms differ only in `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP`: `0` vs unset (the engine logs `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 is ON (default)`).

### 1. Fixed-token benchmark: 352,130-token real conversation, temperature 0, 512 tokens

A conversation exported from Jan (the desktop chat app, jan.ai, which I use as the OpenAI-compatible client for Strata): 109 messages, Italian, code, tool calls, plus a fixed question; fresh engine, one cold read, then runs that reuse the 352,123-token prefix (decode only). All numbers below are from the engine's own `strata serve: prompt ...` lines.

| arm | prefill tok/s (cold) | decode tok/s (cold) | decode tok/s (warm runs) | drafts accepted (warm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TAIL_SKIP=0, session 1 | 2271.6 | 56.7 | 57.2 | 221 / 307 |
| TAIL_SKIP=0, session 2 | 2282.8 | 52.8 | 55.8 | 221 / 307 |
| TAIL_SKIP=7 | 2283.5 | 54.0 | 58.2, 62.0, 59.9 | 223/345, 224/348, 210/333 |

- Warm decode: mean 60.0 vs 56.5 tok/s, **+6.2%** (60.03 / 56.5). All three skip runs are above the best no-skip run.
- Prefill: unchanged (2283.5 vs 2271.6 / 2282.8), consistent with the skip acting only in verify windows.
- Cold decode: 54.0 sits between the two no-skip values (52.8 / 56.7), so no readable difference.
- Limits: only two no-skip warm runs (one per session) and three skip runs.

### 2. Real chat use (Jan desktop app as client, temperature 1, long answers)

Requests with more than 4K output tokens, from the same logs:

| arm | context at start | output tokens | drafts accepted | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| skip | 200K | 18,189 | 86.2% | 67.7 |
| skip | 224K | 13,526 | 83.3% | 60.7 |
| skip | 239K | 20,947 | 83.6% | 58.3 |
| skip | 260K | 6,023 | 87.5% | 60.4 |
| skip | 266K | 7,488 | 79.5% | 64.4 |
| no skip | 191K | 31,754 | 84.8% | 62.3 |
| no skip | 224K | 7,775 | 87.4% | 58.1 |
| no skip | 232K | 4,739 | 71.9% | 59.0 |

Same context (224K): 60.7 vs 58.1 (+4.5%) with lower draft acceptance on the skip side. Content differs between requests, so this is only consistent with section 1, not a measurement of its own.

### 3. The decode hit rate is not comparable between the two settings

In `decode expert cache hit rate: X% (hits / lookups); N more read ... (Y% of all R routed)`, the `routed` total is a multiple of 480 in **129 of 129** request lines with `TAIL_SKIP=0`, and in **0 of 16** lines with `TAIL_SKIP=7`. My reading (not checked in the code) is that skipped experts are dropped from both `lookups` and `routed`. The hit rate then rises because the denominator shrinks, not because the cache serves more experts. On the 352K benchmark it reads 63-66% with the skip and 56-58% without.

This matters whenever hit rates are compared across settings (as in the original #2441 report). Reporting skipped experts in the same line (or computing the hit rate over all routed experts) would make them comparable.

### 4. Output quality (anecdotal)

Two paired generations at temperature 1 (same prompt, one per arm): a ~477K-context conversation summary checked number by number against the conversation, and a 4-part test (two exact-answer math questions, a look-ahead bug in a pandas z-score, and a hardware question with no available data), judged blind. I saw no degradation in either pair. This only rules out an obvious problem, not a small one.

### Summary

On a 16 GB card at 200-350K context, the default `TAIL_SKIP=7` gave roughly +4-9% decode in use and +6% on the fixed-token run, with no visible quality loss. I am keeping it on. Happy to run more A/B on this machine if useful, for example several no-skip warm runs within one session, or other ranks.

issues.title: CPU prefill share stays unarmed on a 32 GB machine; forcing it gives 1.8-2.2× prompt speed with no failures
issues.author: Dongli99
issues.body:
RTX 3080 Laptop 8 GB, 32 GB RAM, Linux, Strata 0.1.44.1, Coder IQ1_M, setup's config (`--prefill auto`, resident low-RAM mode), two starts from a cool GPU on the same day:

| | setup's config | + `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4K prompt tok/s (3 runs) | 294 (282-295) | 541 (538-571) |
| 16K prompt tok/s (3 runs) | 283 (282-289) | 628 (611-633) |
| 16K first token | 56.8 s | 25.6 s |
| chat decode tok/s (9) | 24.0 (22.7-29.0) | 25.3 (22.3-35.0) |
| failed requests | 0 | 0 |

Without the env, the log says `the CPU prefill share is not armed by default: the experts it would read are 2.9 GiB of file pages and only 4.3 GiB of RAM is free to keep them`. With it, the engine warns that the share `can slow prompts or fail on a machine this short of memory` (1.0 GiB of file pages, 3.6 GiB free), then runs at the speeds above.

The resident set is decided the same way. Over three starts with the same config, `resident RAM mode` kept 19.43, 21.30 and 23.10 GiB of experts (the last with `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=3`). The first start warned `the whole resident RAM mode does not fit (... resident complement 22.33 GiB exceeds available RAM (23.68 GiB) minus the 4 GiB safety headroom; 24.4 GiB of the RAM is file cache ...)`. We could not separate a decode effect of the resident size (one start each, overlapping ranges).

On a 32 GB machine, prompt speed therefore depends on what ran before the start. Is the free-RAM threshold for the share conservative for the resident mode? Could setup measure the share once and record `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto` when it helps?

issues.title: 8 GB card: setup's config leaves ~420 MiB of VRAM free, below the 512 MiB that `serve` warns about (#2065)
issues.author: Dongli99
issues.body:
RTX 3080 Laptop 8 GB, Linux, Strata 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`), Coder IQ1_M with setup's config (`--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp ... --max-context 32768 --kv int8 --resident-experts`), nothing else on the GPU (15 MiB used before start).

The start log says `expert cache auto: 1.99 GiB free, 700 MiB reserved (+218 MiB for the draft head) -> 441 slots`, then `expert cache 566 slots, 1.09 GiB of VRAM`. After loading, `serve` reports `423 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded`. The first request prints `WARNING: only 423 MiB of VRAM free ... (below 512 MiB) ... Add --vram-reserve-mib 832`, and a later one warns at 291 MiB and suggests 960. Three starts gave 417-423 MiB free. IQ2_XS with its setup config (mapped): 481 MiB free after load, warnings at 481 and 335 MiB.

We saw no paging stall: 0 failed requests in four bench runs, and no request decoded below 13 tok/s. On 0.1.43.1, `--vram-reserve-mib 832` gave 553 MiB free and 502 slots with no measurable decode change (not repeated on 0.1.44.1).

Questions: should `auto` on a small card leave the room its own warning asks for, so setup's config starts without the warning? And is it expected that `auto` computes 441 slots but the cache ends with 566?

issues.title: Setup fails GGUF shard validation for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q5_K_XL
issues.author: popken-it
issues.body:
First issue report ever. Working solution provided with chatgpt below. 
I am not technical (ordinairy user), so follow questions will be very hard for me to answer.

# Setup fails GGUF shard validation for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q5_K_XL

## Summary

During setup of **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Unsloth) UD-Q5_K_XL**, the first GGUF shard is rejected as being 6 bytes too short, even though the downloaded file matches the size and SHA-256 hash declared in `setup.py`.

This appears to be related to the GGUF validation logic in `check_shards()` in `setup.py`.

## Environment

- **OS:** CachyOS Linux
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 7950X
- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT, 16 GB VRAM
- **System RAM:** 128 GB
- **Strata version:** v0.1.44.1
- **Model:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Unsloth) UD-Q5_K_XL
- **Model repository:** [[unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out Strata v0.1.44.1.
2. Select Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Unsloth) UD-Q5_K_XL during setup.
3. Run `./setup.sh`.
4. Allow setup to download or detect the existing model shards.

## Expected behavior

Setup should validate the downloaded GGUF shards and continue if their contents and integrity are valid.

## Actual behavior

The original setup reports:

```text
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf is short:
10,946,618 of 10,946,624 bytes (6 missing)
```

The relevant entry in `UNSLOTH_BIG_SHARDS` in `setup.py` declares the following expected size and SHA-256:

```python
"Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf": (
    10946618,
    "610922cdb1afe1094e95d7a3e86b12ee33317ebbf7320ac9344e21b6ae4bb69f",
),
```

The downloaded file has exactly the declared size and hash:

```text
File size: 10,946,618 bytes
SHA-256:   610922cdb1afe1094e95d7a3e86b12ee33317ebbf7320ac9344e21b6ae4bb69f
```

Downloading the file again from the Hugging Face repository produced the same size and hash.

## Technical observations

Using `GGUFFile` from `tools/gguf_reader.py`, I inspected the first shard and obtained:

```text
Actual file size:          10,946,618
Calculated minimum size:   10,946,624
Number of tensors:         0
Data start:                 10,946,624
```

The current `check_shards()` implementation calculates the minimum required file size using:

```python
need = g.data_start + max(
    (t.offset + (t.expected_bytes() or 0) for t in g.tensors),
    default=0,
)
```

When the parsed shard contains no tensors, the `default=0` means the calculated minimum size is simply `g.data_start`. In this case, that aligned offset is 6 bytes beyond the end of the file.

The size and hash declared in `setup.py` agree with the downloaded file, but the structural validation rejects it before setup can finish.

## Additional test

After modifying the validation locally to skip the tensor-size check when `g.tensors` is empty, setup proceeded to SHA-256 verification of the model shards:

```text
=== Step 5: downloading Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Unsloth) UD-Q5_K_XL ===
[ok] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf already downloaded
[ok] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00002-of-00006.gguf already downloaded
[ok] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00003-of-00006.gguf already downloaded
...
checking Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf (SHA-256, 0.0 GB) ...
checking Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00002-of-00006.gguf (SHA-256, 0.7 GB) ...
checking Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00003-of-00006.gguf (SHA-256, 54.4 GB) ...
```

**Note:** At the time of writing, the full SHA-256 verification and subsequent model loading have not yet been confirmed to complete successfully.

## Questions

1. Is the first shard intentionally a metadata-only or otherwise special GGUF shard with no tensors?
2. Should `check_shards()` handle an empty tensor list differently, rather than treating the aligned data offset as the minimum file size?
3. Is there an upstream fix or a recommended workaround for this model/version combination?

A robust fix should preserve validation of genuine truncated shards while correctly handling valid GGUF files that contain no tensor payload.

Thank you!

issues.title: [Bug]: json_object silently discards elements from array-root output
issues.author: bettercallcaleb
issues.body:
### What happened

With `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}`, an array-root model response can be accepted as a successful JSON object. `_extract_json()` selects the first balanced `{...}` inside the array and drops the remaining elements.

Reproduced on unmodified `main` (`296b59d`):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from serve.structured import _ObjectOnly, validated_json
raw = '[{"answer":1},{"answer":2}]'
print(validated_json(raw, _ObjectOnly(), "stop"))
PY
```

Actual: `{"answer":1}`. The mock HTTP endpoint also returned 200 with that truncated object.

Expected: reject an array-root response with `structured_output_failed` (HTTP 502 for non-streaming requests), not silently reinterpret it as an object. Existing support for an object inside prose or a Markdown code fence (#762) should remain intact.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

`main` at `296b59d` · Ubuntu 24.04 LTS · Python 3.12 · GPU not used (parser-only and MockEngine HTTP reproduction).

issues.title: Follow-up to #2378: --calibrate saves values contradicting its own round winners
issues.author: MEsfits
issues.body:
## Follow-up to #2378: `--calibrate` completes on string-gpu duals, but saves values contradicting its own measurements

Found while verifying the #2378/#2380 fix (which works — no more crash, tuning runs to completion on `"gpu": "0,1"`). The save step writes a config that matches neither the round arrows nor the previous file. Engine `0.1.44.1` + setup `01cb90dc`, dual RTX 3090, IQ3_S 262K, `strata-iq3_s-dual-iso8.json`.

**1. PCIe share: arrow says 1, file says auto.**
Rounds (median of 3): `0: 125.8 (123.9–129.4), 0.2: 127.2, 0.35: 127.8, 0.55: 127.4, 0.75: 127.5, 0.9: 125.7, 1: 129.5 (126.4–131.7) -> best 1`. Every value overlaps; fine. But the file ends up with `--pcie-frac` **removed** (→ auto). Either the best should be written, or the verdict should say the race was tied and it kept auto — currently arrow and file disagree.

**2. Draft floor: arrow says 0.7, file says 0.5.**
`0.3: 119.8, 0.5: 129.8, 0.7: 132.1 -> best 0.7`, yet the file carries `--spec-min-p 0.5`. This one is unambiguous: the measured winner was not saved.

**3. Expert tier: raw numbers say 1-160, verdict says default.**
`default 112.5, every-1-80 111.1, every-1-160 114.9` → `[ok] default settings are already the fastest`, adapt flags stripped. The verdict contradicts its own raw table (114.9 > 112.5). If a margin/significance rule flips this, it should be printed; as-is it reads as a bug.

**Impact:** after a clean calibrate run the config matches nothing the run measured, and a user comparing arrows to file (as I did) cannot tell which to trust. Suggest either saving exactly what the arrows name, or printing the verdict rule (tie margin, cost preference) whenever it overrides a round winner.

issues.title: [Engine] Qwen3.6-35B-A3B decode falls with context (V100: 109 to 14.6 tok/s at 114K on 0.2.0-beta); llama.cpp holds ~90

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.2.0-beta, temperature 0 (no drafts: #2940) | 109.3 | 104.7 | 85.7 | 59.7 | 40.3 | 23.4 | 14.6 |
| 0.2.0-beta, `presence_penalty: 0` (MTP drafts on) | 156.9 | 157.2 | 117.0 | 57.7 | 34.6 | 19.6 | 11.6 |
| llama.cpp 5e03bdd, same file (0.1.44 run below) | 92.2 | 92.1 | 91.3 | 87.3 | | | |

Prefill: 1,169 / 1,734 / 1,795 / 1,607 / 1,360 / 984 / 602 tok/s. The answers are correct; it is only the decode speed.

@kirinriki7777-sys sees the same shape on an L4 (sm_89) in the hybrid mode on 0.2.0-beta (comment below), so it is not Volta-only.

An int8 K/V cache helped a lot on this card: #2698 (`--kv int8`, closed in the reset, not merged) decoded 52.5 tok/s at 65,536 vs 17.3 on its base (296b59d), and #3084 (FP16 K/V by default) gave +8% at 65,536. Neither is in 0.2.0-beta: the q36 engine still stores the K/V cache in FP32.

### Smallest steps or command that reproduce it

`./setup.sh --family qwen36 --model UD-Q4_K_XL`, then the engine with `--native <gguf> --max-context 131072 --prefill auto --mtp 2` (setup's config) and any prompt of 16K tokens or more; compare decode with a short prompt.

### Reproduction status

Reproduced locally on 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-19), and by @kirinriki7777-sys on an NVIDIA L4.

### Strata version

0.2.0-beta (3d1fb48, engine 0.1.45.3)

### Graphics card, memory and system

Tesla V100-PCIe-32GB (sm_70), i7-13700KF, 16 GB RAM, Linux, CUDA 12.9, driver 580.173.02

### Model, size and settings

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (setup's pinned file from unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF @ 5bc3e238), `--native --max-context 131072 --prefill auto --mtp 2`, every routed expert in VRAM (19.31 GiB free after load).

### Original report (0.1.44)

Tested v0.1.44 (ed4773e) with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (setup's pinned file from unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF @ 5bc3e238, SHA-256 checked) on one Tesla V100-PCIe-32GB (i7-13700KF, 16 GB RAM), CUDA 12.9, built with `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON` and `libstrata_kq.so` next to the engine. Config as setup writes it: `--native <gguf> --max-context 131072 --prefill auto --mtp 2`. Every routed expert fit in VRAM (18.75 GiB, after "the packed Q8_0 decode copies (1.78 GiB) given back"). Greedy, 256-token answers, the same benchmark.py prompts as our other V100 reports, 3 runs per size, medians. Decode tok/s, with time to first token in brackets:

| prompt | `--mtp 2` | `--mtp 0` (decode) | llama.cpp, same file |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 153.8 (0.23 s) | 111.3 | 92.2 (0.55 s) |
| 1,000 | 154.2 (0.60 s) | 106.3 | 92.1 (1.54 s) |
| 4,096 | 114.8 (2.38 s) | 86.3 | 91.3 (6.01 s) |
| 16,384 | 56.5 (10.56 s) | 59.2 | 87.3 (25.38 s) |

llama.cpp = mainline 5e03bdd built for sm_70, `-ngl 99 -fa on`, the identical request bodies (thinking off), streamed.

Short prompts are great on this card: MTP drafts are accepted 69% of the time and decode is ~1.7x llama.cpp's. But decode falls with context with and without MTP, while llama.cpp's barely moves, so at 16K Strata decodes ~35% slower than llama.cpp on the same card (it still reads the prompt 2.4x faster). Our guess is the full-attention layers' decode on sm_70, but we haven't profiled it, and we know Volta is experimental. HumanEval (thinking off) was 155/164 in 4.0 min, the same score as our earlier llama.cpp test of this model.

Happy to run variants (`STRATA_Q36_KEEP_PACKED=1`, longer contexts) if that helps.

issues.title: Layer-split auto (0.1.44.1): a 2x link gap is no longer priced, so a 4090 x16 + 3090 x8 pair picks K=45 and runs ~25% slower; STRATA_SPLIT_LINK_ABS=1 restores 0.1.43.1
issues.author: alphastorm
issues.body:
**Strata version, GPU, OS:** 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`, release engine) · RTX 4090 24 GB (CUDA0, PCIe Gen3 x16, probe 12.4 GB/s) + RTX 3090 24 GB (CUDA1, Gen3 x8, probe 6.2 GB/s) · Windows 11, driver 617.42 · i9-7900X (X299, so Gen3 is the ceiling), 128 GB DDR4-3200

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S with setup's plan for this pair: `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --conversation-cache-mib 8192 --pipeline-windows 2`, layer split auto (CUDA0 then CUDA1; #1576 keeps that order).

### What happened

On this pair 0.1.44.1's auto split runs layers 0-44 on the 4090 and only 45-47 on the 3090, where 0.1.43.1 ran 0-31 and 32-47. Decode drops by about a quarter and long prompts read at about half speed. `STRATA_SPLIT_LINK_ABS=1` on 0.1.44.1 brings back K=32 and 0.1.43.1's numbers.

Measured back to back on the same host: same flags and pack, each arm from a cold start on idle GPUs, 512 output tokens per depth through the API, one request per depth, prompt and decode rates as the server reports them.

| | 0.1.43.1 | 0.1.44.1 | 0.1.44.1 + `STRATA_SPLIT_LINK_ABS=1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| miss cost CUDA0 / CUDA1 | x1.62 / x3.24 | x1.00 / x1.00 | x1.62 / x3.23 |
| auto K (layers on CUDA0 / CUDA1) | 32 (0-31 / 32-47) | 45 (0-44 / 45-47) | 32 (0-31 / 32-47) |
| CUDA1 expert cache | 8,185 slots, 16.50 GiB | 1,536 slots, 3.42 GiB | 8,183 slots, 16.50 GiB |
| profiled pairs held (routed mass) | 17,512 (98.9%) | 10,580 (97.4%) | 17,510 (98.9%) |
| predicted per decode window | 18.6 ms | 16.6 ms | 18.6 ms |
| decode tok/s at ~60 / 8K / 32K / 64K / 100K | 173 / 206 / 197 / 194 / 184 | 113 / 151 / 154 / 148 / 148 | 164 / 196 / 196 / 189 / 187 |
| prompt tok/s at 8K / 32K / 64K / 100K | 1,583 / 3,120 / 3,506 / 3,599 | 1,222 / 1,784 / 1,916 / 1,868 | 1,605 / 3,123 / 3,519 / 3,604 |
| TTFT at 100K | 28.6 s | 55.0 s | 28.6 s |

0.1.44.1's default also prints:

```
strata generate: layer split auto: K=47 would give a stage fewer than 3 layers (a tiny expert cache there clamps the prompt chunk of every card, #1616); chose K=45 instead (16.6 ms per decode window, not 16.5)
strata generate: layer split auto: NEAR TIE - K=42 is predicted 16.7 ms per decode window, within 0.7% of K=45 (16.6 ms); the cards differ, so the prediction may not rank them (it prices decode, not the prompt). To try the other: --layer-split 42
strata serve: WARNING: prompt chunk 5888 tokens, not 8192: CUDA1 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090) has 1536 expert-cache slots, and a 8192-token chunk borrows 1536 of them (it must keep 128, and lend at most 85%) - prompts read slower than on CUDA0 alone (#448)
```

### Why

#2007's `link_miss_scale` ([split_rules.hpp#L77-L98](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78/include/strata/program/split_rules.hpp#L77-L98)) scales a stage's miss term only from a 4x gap against the fastest link. At 12.4 against 6.2 GB/s both stages get x1.00 ([generate.cpp#L3846-L3855](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78/src/program/generate.cpp#L3846-L3855)), and the search then holds 6,932 fewer profiled pairs (97.4% of the routed mass instead of 98.9%). The comment there expects a gap below 4x to matter less than the probe's noise and the formula's fit. On this rig it is the largest effect, perhaps because the slower link is also on the slower card (82 SMs at 1.75 GHz against 128 at 2.52).

So the 0.1.41 rule is right on this pair, the 2x Tesla T10 rig in that comment needed it gone, and #2418 (a 4.2x gap, x16 + x4) asks for a uniform cost. The link ratio alone does not seem to separate the three rigs.

issues.title: 2026-10-14: Radeon VII 16 GB + Radeon Pro VII / MI50 16 GB (gfx906, mixed pair), Ryzen 7 3700X, 62 GB RAM
issues.author: kietq8684-design
issues.body:
Partial benchmark data point (full COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS PR to follow after the 32K/128K sweep + needle checks).

Source build of v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`) on the gfx906 opt-in path, HIP 7.14 from the community image
`mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`, Coder IQ1_M native pack, layer split 27 across both cards,
`--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--max-context 32768`.

This closes the Radeon VII half of the `docs/AMD_HIP.md` "Not done: … MI60 and Radeon VII (the same gfx906 ISA;
not run)" line. The pair is a Radeon VII (`0x66af`) with a Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 (`0x66a1`) — same ISA,
mixed cards. HIP names both "AMD Radeon VII", so the existing MI50 report's hardware line is ambiguous in the
same way.

`STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1` puts **all 12,265 experts resident** (6,889 + 5,376 slots), which reproduces the MI50
report's "all 12,288 experts in VRAM" on a mixed pair.

Two configuration results that differ from the published gfx906 report (which used `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`):

- **`--spec-min-p 0.7` instead of 0.5** — two independent scans, n=7 per value: 4K decode 68.6 → 71.5 (+4.2%),
  16K 65.5 → 67.6 (+3.2%). 0.5 is the worst value tested; the minimum spans 0.2–0.9 and 0.7 ties with 0.8.
- **`--spec 2` instead of 4** — interleaved A/B, 18 samples: 4K decode median 73.40 → 77.50 (+5.6%, mean +6.9%),
  and the spread narrows from sd 2.2 to 0.73. Draft acceptance 77.9% → 94.3%. Note `--spec N` expands to
  `mtp_max_t = N` with verify window `min(N+2, 8)` (suffix drafting defaults to 3), so the window goes 6 → 4.

Also measured on this pair: `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1` gives prefill +2.0% / +2.3% / +2.3% at 1.5K / 3K / 4K
(sd < 0.5 over 3 restarts), and `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1` gives decode +3.2% (4K) / +5.9% (16K) with `route tail skip`
misses falling from ~1,400 to ~19.

### Not done / limits
- Prompt sweep is 4K and 16K only; no 32K or 128K, no needle check, no TTFT table. `--max-context 32768` bounds
  the current config.
- Measurements are controlled short-prompt bench (256 generated tokens, greedy, one request at a time), not
  production mixed traffic — do not compare them against the mixed-traffic numbers in the MI50 report.
- Model is on local NVMe. Storage is a first-order variable on this box: the same model on JuiceFS over a

issues.title: gfx906 + 100% expert residency: `STRATA_SPLIT_OWN=1` costs decode, `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1` does nothing
issues.author: kietq8684-design
issues.body:
### Summary
On a gfx906 box whose experts are 100% resident in VRAM, two of the opt-in switches documented in `MULTI_GPU.md`
do not pay off, and one of them is actively negative. The published numbers for both were taken on other
architectures (`SPLIT_OWN`: R9700 + RX 9070 XT; `PREFILL_HELP`: 2x RTX 3090) and neither section states that
residency changes the outcome. Reporting so the sections can carry a precondition.

### Environment
- Radeon VII 16 GB (`0x66af`) + Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 16 GB (`0x66a1`), Ryzen 7 3700X (AVX2, no AVX-512),
  62 GB RAM, kernel 6.8.0-146-p2p
- HIP 7.14 from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`; engine v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`), gfx906 build
- Coder IQ1_M (`--native` pack), `--layer-split 27`, `--prefill 4096`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`,
  `--max-context 32768`, `--pcie-frac 0`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--ple-row-cache 8388608`,
  `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.7`
- `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1 STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1 STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_QUERY_SWIZZLE=1 STRATA_GFX906_ATTN_REDUCE12=1`
- Startup: 6,889 + 5,376 = **12,265 experts, 100% resident**, prompt path borrows 1,040 + 937 slots, ring 96 slots

### Method
Interleaved A/B (`A1 B1 A2 B2 A3 B3`), one independent restart per arm, 3 runs per arm per prompt length,
n=9/arm/length, 4K = 4,589 prompt tokens, 16K = 18,010 prompt tokens, `temperature=0`, unique nonce per request.
Interleaving is necessary on this box: two runs of the *same* binary 1.5 h apart differ by ~2%. Prefill is kept
as a control column (it should not move). Reported values are medians.

### `STRATA_SPLIT_OWN=1` — prefill barely moves, decode drops
Structural evidence: the expert cache falls from **6,889 to 5,353 slots (−22%, −2.82 GiB)**, because each card now
keeps its own ~3,264 MiB prompt buffers.

| | default | `SPLIT_OWN=1` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 4K (tok/s) | 469.5 | 479.9 | +2.2% |
| prefill 16K (tok/s) | 735.2 | 741.1 | +0.8% |
| **decode 4K (tok/s)** | **75.50** | **72.80** | **−3.6%** |
| **decode 16K (tok/s)** | **70.10** | **66.40** | **−5.3%** |

`MULTI_GPU.md:80` reports 2K 1,450 / 16K 2,227 tok/s there with "decode unchanged". On gfx906 the prefill gain is
+0.8–2.2% instead of ~+14%, and the cache it costs is what decode needs. Decode is the primary metric for this
deployment, so we leave it off. Suggestion: state in that section that the flag trades expert cache for prompt
buffers, and that on a card whose cache is the binding constraint the decode cost can exceed the prefill gain.

### `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1` — no effect at all
1.5K prefill **415.1 vs 419.7 tok/s (−1.1%)**, 3K **460.1 vs 460.0 (flat)**, n=3/arm. The decode deltas
(+4% / −4.5%) contradict each other and the flag only touches the prompt path, so they are noise.

Mechanism as we understand it: the flag hands "a share of its **streamed** experts" to the idle card
(`MULTI_GPU.md:85`). With `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1` every expert is resident, so the prompt path streams essentially
nothing — the work it is meant to offload does not exist. Suggestion: add "requires non-resident (streamed)
experts" as a precondition to that section, next to the existing MMQ/`--peer-device` notes.

### For completeness, `STRATA_GR_SPLIT=1`
`AMD_HIP.md:494` gives it "~3% per window". End to end we measure 4K +0.8% / 16K −1.6% (prefill flat, n=9) —
within noise. That may just be a per-window vs end-to-end distinction rather than a disagreement, so flagging it
only as a data point.

### Not a claim
This says nothing about the flags on the architectures they were measured on; it is one gfx906 box with a fully
resident expert cache.

issues.title: gfx906/HIP build broken on v0.1.44.1: two compile blockers (platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h missing three cublas maps, and the new strata_mmq_w4a4 target missing GGML_USE_HIP)
issues.author: kietq8684-design
issues.body:
### Summary
`-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON` no longer builds on the latest tag. v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`) builds clean; v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`)
fails with two independent blockers, both introduced after 0.1.42. `docs/AMD_HIP.md:472` says the gfx906 engine
"is checked to compile for gfx906", so this is a regression rather than a missing feature. A 9-line patch makes
`ninja -C build-906 strata` finish with 149/149 linked, exit 0.

### Environment
- GPU: Radeon VII 16 GB (`0x66af`) + Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 16 GB (`0x66a1`), both gfx906
- ROCm: HIP 7.14 (hipcc 7.14.60850) from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
- Kernel: 6.8.0-146-p2p, Ubuntu 24.04, `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6`
- Build: `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=/llama
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++`, Ninja
- llama.cpp at the pinned commit (`3cf03257f`)
- `git describe` on the tree: v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`) builds; worktree at v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`) fails

### Blocker 1 — `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h` is missing three mappings

`include/strata/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h` gained `cublasSgemm`, `cublasSgemmStridedBatched` and
`cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx` between 0.1.42 and 0.1.44.1, and `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` (new in 0.1.44.1) uses
them. But that file is **not on the gfx906 include path**: `CMakeLists.txt:60` says the cuBLAS names are mapped by
`include/strata/platform/hip_compat/`, lines 138/141/142 attach it `BEFORE INTERFACE`, and the only strata-side
`-I` in `compile_commands.json` is `-I/src/include/strata/platform/hip_compat`. That second file still maps
`cublasGemmEx` only, so the three names are undeclared.

Fix — add to `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h`:

```diff
 #define cublasGemmEx hipblasGemmEx
+#define cublasSgemm hipblasSgemm
+#define cublasSgemmStridedBatched hipblasSgemmStridedBatched
+#define cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx hipblasGemmStridedBatchedEx
```

### Blocker 2 — the new `strata_mmq_w4a4` target has no `GGML_USE_HIP`

```
FAILED: CMakeFiles/strata_mmq_w4a4.dir/src/prefill/mmq_nvfp4_w4a4.cu.o
/llama/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/cuda.h:4:10: error: 'cuda.h' file not found with <angled> include
/llama/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/cuda.h:6:10: fatal error: 'cuda_bf16.h' file not found
```

`mmq_nvfp4_w4a4.cu` includes llama.cpp's `common.cuh`, which selects `vendors/hip.h` only under
`#if defined(GGML_USE_HIP)` and otherwise pulls `vendors/cuda.h` (`<cuda.h>`, `<cuda_bf16.h>` — absent in a HIP
environment; `platform/hip_compat/` provides only `cuda_fp16.h`, `cuda_runtime.h`, `math_constants.h`).
`CMakeLists.txt:1791` sets `GGML_USE_HIP` on `strata_mmq` for the gfx906 branch and `:1576` has the `=1` form for
gfx11, but the `strata_mmq_w4a4` target added at `:1449-1457` was missed. Its sibling `mmq_nvfp4_w4a8.cu` has the
define and compiles (877 KB `.o`), which is what identifies this as an omission rather than a design choice.
CUDA builds are unaffected — they want `vendors/cuda.h`.

Fix — in `CMakeLists.txt`, after `target_link_libraries(strata_mmq PRIVATE strata_mmq_w4a4)`:

```diff
     target_link_libraries(strata_mmq PRIVATE strata_mmq_w4a4)
+    # gfx906 / HIP: this unit includes ggml-cuda's common.cuh, which only takes vendors/hip.h when
+    # GGML_USE_HIP is defined (strata_mmq gets it in the HIP branches below).  Without it the CUDA
+    # vendor headers (<cuda.h>, <cuda_bf16.h>) are pulled in and the HIP build fails.
+    if(STRATA_HIP_GFX906 OR STRATA_ENABLE_HIP)
+      target_compile_definitions(strata_mmq_w4a4 PRIVATE GGML_USE_HIP)
+    endif()
```

### Result with the patch
`ninja -C build-906 strata` → **149/149 linked, exit 0**, `build-906/strata` = 26,224,152 B (v0.1.42 is 21 MB).
Patch total: 9 lines (`cublas_v2.h` +3, `CMakeLists.txt` +6). The 0.1.42 tree is untouched.

### Note (not a blocker, just a build-time observation)
`strata_mmq_w4a4` is a unit that the gfx906/HIP path does not use at all, so an alternative to the define above
is to skip the target on this branch entirely — either way the HIP build should not be pulling CUDA vendor headers
for it.

issues.title: 0.1.44 on HIP/gfx1030 (RX 6950 XT, Windows): IQ3_S output turns to garbage, Q2_0 fine, 0.1.43.1 fine
issues.author: 0xPiPo
issues.body:
Hi, and thanks for Strata, it's been running really well on my card.

After updating to 0.1.44, the IQ3_S pack of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next started giving me nonsense on my RX 6950 XT. A reply would start out roughly on topic and then drift into stray tool-call tags, random Chinese, or loop on the same phrase until it hit the token limit. Nothing in the log looks wrong. The engine starts, the verify windows pass, it just says the wrong things.

What I checked:

- Same machine, same 0.1.44 engine, the Q2_0 pack answers normally. So it isn't the whole engine on this GPU.
- I rolled back with `START-HERE.bat --rollback-engine` to 0.1.43.1. Same IQ3_S files, same config, and the output is correct again.
- On a small eval set I use (12 domain questions), IQ3_S scored 11/12 on 0.1.43.1 and 0/12 on 0.1.44.

Something in the logs that might help: on 0.1.44 the replies were much longer and drafts were accepted a lot, for example `196 generated ... drafts accepted 99 of 146`. On 0.1.43.1, similar prompts give `36 generated ... drafts accepted 23 of 28` and `40 generated ... 26 of 33`. That fits the looping I was seeing. Startup looks the same on both versions apart from the version line (expert cache 3437 slots, R4 hit path ON, MTP draft layer loaded).

I haven't tried turning off MTP, speculative decoding or the expert cache on 0.1.44 to narrow it down. I still have 0.1.44 in `engine\.previous`, so I'm happy to run whatever combination would help.

**Setup**

- Windows 11 Enterprise, build 26300
- AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT (gfx1030), 16 GB, driver 32.0.21045.5002, 64 GB RAM
- Prebuilt HIP engine. Both builds report rocm `10.2.0a20260930` with gfx1030 in `archs`

```
backend hip, gpu 1
```
</details>

issues.title: [Benchmark] Snakes and Ladders in 3D: Comparing Strata Variations + Ollama and llama.cpp — RTX 5060 Ti 16GB + 96GB RAM
issues.author: okets
issues.body:
**On my machine, Strata-served models produced substantially better games than the non-Strata setups I tested on the same application-building task.** My best Strata build scored **94.8/100**. The best scored non-Strata builds reached **65.1** for GLM-5.3-Flash via llama.cpp, **59.9** for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B coding via Ollama, and **33.3** for Qwen3-Coder-Next via llama.cpp.

This is a comparison of complete local setups—model, quantization, inference backend, context, and agent—not a controlled measurement of the inference engine alone. All full-task comparisons used **Claude Code as the harness**, with inference supplied by the selected local model. No Anthropic model performed the tested coding work. Claude helped create the benchmark and reviewed code separately.

> **Low results from the tested non-Strata setups:** Qwen3.6 coding via Ollama averaged **59.1/100**, GLM via llama.cpp averaged **52.0/100**, and Qwen3-Coder-Next via llama.cpp scored **33.3/100**. Their average game ratings were only **33.0, 19.5, and 18.0**, respectively. Every fully scored Strata game in this dataset finished above the best scored non-Strata result.

## Same task, different local setups

Every full-task run started from the same seed repository and specification: build a **3D snakes-and-ladders game** in TypeScript, three.js, and Vite, across six milestones. The agent had to produce a working application, not just answer coding questions.

The table includes only full-task builds with all three scoring components present. Averages pool the tested settings for each model; they are descriptive summaries, not matched-condition estimates.

| Local model / backend | Scored full-task builds | Mean function | Mean code | Mean game rating | Mean total | Best total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL / Strata | 5 | 100.0 | 83.6 | 84.0 | **90.3** | 92.8 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS / Strata | 4 | 100.0 | 81.5 | 85.5 | **90.1** | **94.8** |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S / Strata | 9 | 99.1 | 80.6 | 74.0 | **86.0** | 91.5 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M / Strata | 3 | 100.0 | 69.7 | 68.0 | 81.3 | 89.5 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Swift IQ3_XXS / Strata | 3 | 100.0 | 79.3 | 54.0 | 80.0 | 88.5 |
| **Non-Strata: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B coding / Ollama** | 2 | 91.6 | 42.0 | **33.0** | **59.1** | **59.9** |
| **Non-Strata: GLM-5.3-Flash E256 Q2 / llama.cpp** | 4 | 66.5 | 65.1 | **19.5** | **52.0** | **65.1** |
| **Non-Strata: Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-IQ4_XS / llama.cpp** | 1 | 44.2 | 34.0 | **18.0** | **33.3** | **33.3** |

The difference appeared in the finished applications as well as the code reviews. Ollama's Qwen runs scored fairly well on automated function checks, but much lower on code quality and my game ratings. The GLM runs were weaker in game quality, and some gave up or looped. The single Qwen3-Coder-Next run ended with substantially lower function, code, and game scores.

The gap was not just a comparison against Strata's single best result: IQ3_S averaged **86.0** over nine full-task builds, and both larger Unsloth variants averaged about **90**. In contrast, the two Ollama builds scored **59.9 and 58.4**. Even the best scored GLM build, **65.1**, remained below every scored full-task Strata build in this dataset; the lowest Strata total was **72.8**. This is a consistent separation within these saved runs, although the conditions and number of trials are unequal.

**Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct UD-Q4_K_XL was also tested via llama.cpp**, at 192K context. Its function score is 44.2 and my game rating is 18.0, but its code review is missing. It therefore has **no final total** and is excluded from the ranking above.

### Low non-Strata results: individual runs and score gaps

Even when comparing each non-Strata setup's **best scored run** with Strata's **best scored run**, the gaps were substantial:

| Non-Strata setup | Best total / 100 | Points below the best Strata build (94.8) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GLM-5.3-Flash E256 Q2 / llama.cpp | **65.1** | **29.7** |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B coding / Ollama | **59.9** | **34.9** |
| Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-IQ4_XS / llama.cpp | **33.3** | **61.5** |

These are descriptive score gaps between the tested setups, not percentage improvements or isolated engine effects. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B remains unranked because its code score is missing.

| Model | Context | Effort | Build labels | Individual totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B coding / Ollama | 256K | low | T, X | 59.9, 58.4 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash E256 Q2 / llama.cpp | 256K | low | AE, AI | 37.2, 50.2 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash E256 Q2 / llama.cpp | 256K | high | AF, AJ | 55.5, 65.1 |
| Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-IQ4_XS / llama.cpp | 256K | high* | AL | 33.3 |
| Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct UD-Q4_K_XL / llama.cpp | 192K | high* | AM | Not yet fully scored |

GLM's low-effort runs averaged **43.7**; high-effort runs averaged **60.3**. AE and AF gave up, AI looped, and AJ completed. Additional GLM max-effort attempts were stopped or hit an infrastructure error and have no final totals.

**Important qualification for GLM:** AE and AF each recorded **121 server errors** and **10 automatic resumes**. Their results reflect backend/session problems as well as the generated code, so the four-run GLM mean must not be interpreted as a clean measurement of model ability. Later runs AI and AJ recorded zero server errors and scored **50.2 and 65.1**. AJ is marked complete but its telemetry also flags a loop; these fields describe different aspects of the run.

*The Qwen3-Coder models are marked `high` in the lab configuration, but the backend identifies both as non-thinking models. This label should not be read as equivalent to a thinking model's high-effort setting. GLM E256 Q2 is the pruned, 2-bit expert variant recorded by the lab, not an unquantized GLM result.*

## Hardware and environment

- Intel Core i9-13900K
- 96 GB installed RAM (approximately 94 GiB available to the host)
- NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GB VRAM
- Strata running in Docker on Unraid
- Original Strata run: v0.1.40.3, commit `d5ea713`; Claude Code 2.1.280, Qwen Code 0.24.5, Pi 0.87.1, Ollama 0.40.2, as recorded in the benchmark notes
- Non-Strata models were served through Ollama or llama.cpp's `llama-server`; the local launcher pins `server-cuda-b11552`

The first Strata series ran on October 9–11, 2026; the saved dataset also contains later non-Strata comparisons. The results and screenshots here were retrieved on October 14, 2026.

The benchmark notes record stopping competing model servers and Plex/Jellyfin during the original Strata lab run to give it the GPU and RAM. I have not independently established identical background-load conditions for every later comparison, so that remains a reproducibility limitation.

## What the game task actually required

The specification deliberately combined rules, rendering, interaction, and polish. Finishing a rules module alone was not enough:

| Milestone | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Rules and test hook | Pure TypeScript rules, seeded randomness, forced dice sequences, a text interface, and rule tests |
| 2. 3D board | A correctly numbered 10×10 board, alternating tiles, lighting, soft shadows, an orbit camera, and resizing |
| 3. Die and tokens | A tumbling 3D die showing the actual roll, tokens hopping square by square, and sensible placement when tokens share a square |
| 4. Snakes and ladders | 3D ladder rails and rungs, curved snakes with heads, and movement along their paths |
| 5. Game flow | Configurable 2–4 human/computer players, start screen, turn banner, computer turns, winner celebration, and restart |
| 6. Polish | Camera follow, generated sound effects, mute and keyboard controls, phone layout, reduced motion, and no console errors |

The rules include nine fixed ladders and ten fixed snakes, an extra roll on a six, exact landing on 100 to win, and bouncing back when a roll overshoots. A bounce can land on a snake: **97 + 5 lands on 98, then slides to 78**. These edge cases help distinguish a plausible-looking board from a correct game.

The required `window.__game` hook exposes state and a promise-returning roll operation. URL parameters control the random seed, dice sequence, player count, and instant animations. This lets the external grader play repeatable games and compare actual state transitions, rather than trusting the agent's final message.

The seed contained installed tooling and the specification, rather than a completed game to edit. Packages were fixed—TypeScript, Vite, three.js, Vitest, Playwright, and ESLint—with no network access to install additional dependencies or download art. Audio had to be generated with the Web Audio API.

## Method and scoring

I first checked three harnesses against the same Strata IQ3_S model at 256K context and high effort. This check covered **milestones 1–2 only**, rather than the complete game:

| Harness | Automated function/code score | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Claude Code | 92.7 | 18.4 minutes |
| Qwen Code | 94.2 | 84.1 minutes |
| Pi | 93.8 | 43.2 minutes |

All three passed the rule checks. Claude Code reached a similar automated score fastest in this check, so it was used for the remaining tests.

In this one harness check, Qwen Code took approximately **4.6×** Claude Code's wall time and Pi took **2.3×**. Their output-token totals were about **201K**, **94K**, and **49K**, respectively. This supports the harness choice for this experiment; it is not a general claim that Claude Code is always the fastest harness.

### How a full run proceeded

1. The lab selected a model, configured context window, effort, and backend, then prepared the local model server.
2. The agent started in a fresh sandbox from the common seed repository and task specification.
3. It was instructed to work through the milestones in order, run tests/type checks/lint/build before each milestone commit, and inspect screenshots after visual milestones.
4. A relay routed inference to the local backend and recorded requests, tokens, tool failures, errors, context use, compactions, and timings.
5. The external grader checked the generated application, and the lab retained the code, metrics, screenshots, and run outcome.
6. A blind code review and my game ratings supplied the remaining scoring components.

The orchestrator could send a fixed continuation message when an agent stopped early, up to ten times within the run's time limit. This was automatic continuation, not bespoke human debugging. Most configurations had an eight-hour limit; UD-Q4_K_XL and the tested GLM configuration had sixteen-hour limits. The exported `resumes` field is zero for the scored Strata runs and ten for GLM AE and AF.

Configuration selection was staged rather than an exhaustive sweep. IQ3_S served as the anchor; context and effort were explored, other Strata variants were added, and selected larger windows and higher efforts were requested afterward. Some low-scoring settings received a second run. The winner is therefore the best **observed** build in this search, not an estimate of the best possible configuration.

Full-task scores combine:

- **40% function:** hidden scripted gameplay checks, build/test checks, stability, and milestone completion.
- **30% code:** a blind Claude review against a fixed rubric covering architecture, readability, tests, correctness, and hygiene.
- **30% game rating:** my manual scores for gameplay, visuals, animation, controls, and bugs.

The dashboard's automatic score uses function and code only, weighted 4:3. **This report ranks by the total that includes my game rating.** The gallery rounds scores to whole numbers; the tables retain the exported one-decimal values.

### What each score measures

For a fully scored build, **total = 0.40 × function + 0.30 × code + 0.30 × game rating**. The winning build Z therefore scores `0.40 × 100 + 0.30 × 82.5 + 0.30 × 100 = 94.75`, displayed as **94.8**.

issues.title: [Bug]: elastic image encoder wakes on every turn when the client re-sends pictures it already encoded
issues.author: jerry78424
issues.body:
## What happened

With the elastic image encoder (`vram_elastic: true` + vision `"elastic": true`), every turn whose messages contain an image takes the encoder's start - even when every one of those images is already in the hash cache. `Vision.unload()` keeps `Vision.cache` and the `.sve` files (that is the documented design), so an already-encoded picture needs no encoder process at all - but `prepare()` never asks the cache: on any image turn it takes the encode FIFO and calls `_vision_up()` unconditionally, and only afterwards does `encode_all` find that everything is a hit.

This is not a corner case: most clients re-send the whole conversation - pictures included - on every turn. So after the first idle stop, **every subsequent turn pays the start again, forever**, including pure-text follow-ups.

Repro (any elastic setup, no rebuild):
1. Start a model with `vram_elastic: true` and vision `{"elastic": true, "elastic_idle_s": 10}`.
2. Send a message with an image -> encoder starts, answer arrives.
3. Wait past `elastic_idle_s` (log: `the image encoder stopped after 10 s without a picture`).
4. Send a text-only message while the client re-sends the picture from step 2.

Actual: the log shows `the expert cache keeps ... free` + `the image encoder started ...` before the answer - and the same on every later turn.
Expected: a turn whose images are all cached answers from the cache without waking the encoder. A new picture (alone or alongside cached ones) should still wake it.

Measured on RTX 5090 32 GB, Windows 11 (build 26200), engine 0.1.44.1, nvfp4 quant, `elastic_idle_s: 10`, a client that re-sends history images every turn. Before the change, one chat session's engine log (verbatim, one session file):

```
[strata] images: the image encoder started in 5.8 s, 2085 MiB of VRAM
[strata] images: the image encoder stopped after 10 s without a picture; the expert cache took its VRAM back (22528 of 22909 MiB)
[strata] images: the image encoder started in 2.3 s, 2085 MiB of VRAM
[strata] images: the image encoder stopped after 10 s without a picture; ...
[strata] images: the image encoder started in 2.3 s, 2085 MiB of VRAM
```

Per-turn wall time with a scripted client, one conversation, the same machine - before the change every image-bearing turn after an idle stop was preceded by such a start line in the engine log; with the fix:

| turn | before | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| new picture A | 4213 ms, encoder starts | unchanged: starts (3979-4213 ms) |
| text-only, picture re-sent in history | a 2.3 s start line before the answer, 2085 MiB taken from the expert cache | 722 ms, no start line, no VRAM change |
| same picture re-sent again | another start line | 1277 ms, no start line |
| new picture B | starts | starts (3979 ms) |

The `2.3 s` and `2085 MiB` are the steady-state re-start cost on this card (5.1-5.8 s on the very first start).

## Strata version, GPU, OS

0.1.44.1 · RTX 5090 32 GB · Windows 11 (build 26200)

## Engine log

Excerpt above is verbatim from `strata-nvfp4-nvfp4.log`.

## Fix

serve/server.py only, no native files: `Vision.key_of()` / `Vision.cached()` (hash lookup that works with the process down), and `prepare()` maps the turn's images through the cache first - when every one is a hit the turn skips the FIFO, `_vision_up()` and the encode entirely. A miss keeps today's path exactly.

`serve/test_vision_cache_wake.py` (new, CPU-only, no engine): a re-sent picture does not wake a stopped encoder, a new picture alongside cached ones still wakes it, and the cache lookup answers with the process down. The whole `serve` suite passes with the change here (348 tests, 3 skipped).

What I did not test: AMD/HIP and layer-split machines (on a layer split `--vram-elastic` is refused anyway, and the start there is covered by #2435), non-elastic vision (path untouched), and the CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds (no native file changes).

I'll open a PR with the fix + the test referencing this issue.

issues.title: Windows/NVIDIA performance regression: v0.1.42 ~69 tok/s vs v0.1.44.1 ~55–58 tok/s on RTX 5060 Ti
issues.author: Celica4101
issues.body:
Hi, I am seeing a fairly large decode performance regression on Windows/NVIDIA after updating Strata.

## System

- OS: Windows 11
- CPU: Intel Core i9-14900K
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
- RAM: 128 GB
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
- Quant: IQ3_S
- Context: 64K
- KV cache: int8
- Images: OFF
- Experimental Speed Projection: ON

I have not manually changed the tuning parameters from the values generated by Strata setup.

## Performance

### Full v0.1.42 checkout

I cloned the `v0.1.42` tag into a separate directory and started it from there.

Observed:

- RAM usage: about 64 GB
- Decode speed: **69.2 tok/s**

The runtime log for this run shows:

- `session is up (engine 0.1.42)`
- `expert cache 4269 slots, 8.14 GiB of VRAM`
- `2078 generated in 30043 ms (69.2 tok/s)`
- `decode expert cache hit rate: 91.1%`
- `KV streaming: 99.93%`

I have attached this v0.1.42 runtime log.

### Full v0.1.44.1 checkout

After updating my normal Strata checkout to v0.1.44.1, I repeatedly observed:

- RAM usage: about 68 GB
- Decode speed: approximately **55–58.8 tok/s**

This was repeatable across multiple generations.

Before the update, v0.1.43.1 on this same machine was also running in roughly the same performance range as v0.1.42 (around 67–69 tok/s).

## Engine rollback test

I also tried:

`python setup.py --rollback-engine`

This restored engine v0.1.43.1 while keeping the newer Strata checkout.

In that configuration:

- RAM usage decreased slightly to about 66 GB
- Decode speed remained around 55–58 tok/s

So rolling back only the engine binary did not restore the previous performance.

When I instead ran the complete v0.1.42 checkout, RAM usage returned to about 64 GB and decode performance immediately returned to 69.2 tok/s.

This makes me wonder whether the regression may involve something outside the engine binary itself, such as generated configuration, expert/memory placement, or another change in the surrounding Strata tree.

## PCIe check

I also monitored the GPU PCIe link while generating.

The RTX 5060 Ti remained at **PCIe Gen5 x8 under load**, so I do not appear to be seeing the Gen1 link-drop behavior reported in another issue.

## Logs

Attached:

- `strata_full_0.1.42_69.2tps.log`
  - Full v0.1.42 checkout
  - 69.2 tok/s run

- `strata_newtree_0.1.44.1_rollback_0.1.43.1.log`
  - Contains the v0.1.44.1 runs at approximately 55–58.8 tok/s
  - Also contains the subsequent engine-only rollback to v0.1.43.1, which remained in the same slower performance range

issues.title: 0.1.44/HIP: deterministic non-finite logits (#879) at a fixed prompt position on long-context request; retry-from-0 reproduces
issues.author: dinesh-chander
issues.body:
On 0.1.44 the engine emits non-finite logits at a fixed prompt position, deterministically: the server's automatic retry-from-token-0 reproduces it at the identical position. No private prompt content is attached; the signature alone should be actionable.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Strata | 0.1.44 (HIP source build, gfx1100+gfx1100) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, UD-Q4_K_XL native pack |
| Engine args | `--max-context 200000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --vision --vram-reserve-mib 2048 --pool-workers 13 --conversation-cache-mib 2048 --conversation-cache-slots 8 --conversation-cache-min-tokens 2000 --layer-split auto` |
| GPUs | 2x AMD RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), layer split 24/24, ROCm/HIP |
| OS | Linux, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic |

## What happened

Server log:

```
[strata] reading the prompt: 102,369 of 102,374 tokens, 8 s so far
[strata] the engine's logits became non-finite before the first token (#879); it dropped its cached state: sending the request again once
[strata] reading the prompt: 8,192 of 102,374 tokens, 18 s so far
... (full re-read) ...
[strata] reading the prompt: 102,251 of 102,374 tokens, 83 s so far
[strata] the engine's logits became non-finite again on the retry (#879): the request ends with an error
```

Engine log (both attempts, identical position):

```
strata serve: non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window at position 102369 (row 0): its tokens are not emitted, the request ends (DONE nonfinite) and the next request reads its prompt from token 0
strata serve: prompt 102374 tokens = 98673 reused + 3696 of 3701 read in 8966 ms (412.2 tok/s), 0 generated in 0 ms (0.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 0 of 0, 6 checkpoints (cancelled)
...
strata serve: after non-finite logits (#879): dropped the live session, 6 checkpoints, 0 parked conversations and 0 idle slots (0 running slots not kept after their reply); reading this prompt from token 0
...
strata serve: non-finite logits (#879) in a prompt window at position 102369 (row 0): ...
strata serve: prompt 102374 tokens = 0 reused + 102369 of 102374 read in 75865 ms (1349.4 tok/s), 0 generated in 0 ms (0.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 0 of 0, 6 checkpoints (cancelled)
```

## Key properties

- **Deterministic in content, not transient.** First attempt (98,673 tokens reused from cache) and retry (full cold re-read from 0) fail at the identical position 102369 of 102374 — 5 tokens from the prompt tail. Resending is futile.
- **Healthy session otherwise.** Prior requests in the same session decoded at 44–53 tok/s with 87–94% expert-cache hit rates. Engine stayed loaded throughout; no restart needed.
- **Expensive retry.** The automatic retry-from-0 burned a ~76 s full prefill of a 102k prompt to reproduce the same failure. For a deterministic #879, that retry is pure waste — consider skipping the re-read when the first failure is at (near-)the same tail position, or capping auto-retry to transient-looking cases.

## Notes

- The triggering bytes are in the user's private session content, so no prompt is attached. The tail region (last few tokens: newest tool result / message + chat-template closing) is where to look; typical suspects are odd byte sequences from tool output, but that's unverified.
- Related: #2449 (verify-window watchdog on this same box), #267, #251.
- Happy to run a bisection or dump token IDs around the failing position if you describe a safe way to extract them (the raw session can't leave the machine).

issues.title: ### More data for #1431: wrong parameter syntax inside an otherwise valid call (Coder IQ1_M on an Arc Pro B60)
issues.author: mbaaku
issues.body:
**Hardware note:** this is an **Intel Arc Pro B60** (`bmg-g21`, SYCL backend, built with `AOT=bmg-g21`). The startup banner says the SYCL backend was tested on an Arc Pro B70 and an Arc A750, so the B60 counts as untested. I have no B70 or CUDA card to check whether the rate is backend-specific, so treat that as an open question. **Setup** - Strata v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`), SYCL backend, 1× Intel Arc Pro B60 (24 GB), Debian Linux 13 , Docker 29.8.1 (`ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0`, `STRATA_EXPERT_SPLIT=1`) - Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Coder IQ1_M** (`--kv int8`, `--max-context 131072`, 1 slot) - Run config: `"tool_call_recovery": true`, `"fit_max_tokens": true`; reasoning effort left at the model default - Client: Continue CLI (`cn`) through LiteLLM, OpenAI chat completions, streaming, **21 tools** (built-in `Bash`, `Read`, `List`, … plus MCP tools) - Raw outputs captured with `STRATA_DEBUG=1`
Full configuration (compose environment, .env, setup command, engine arguments, run config) `compose.yaml`, service `strata` (image built from the repo's `Dockerfile.b60`), environment: ~~~yaml environment: STRATA_DEBUG: "1" AOT: bmg-g21 REPO: ${STRATA_ROOT}/Strata BUILD_DIR: ${STRATA_ROOT}/Strata/build-sycl-aot JOBS: "28" STRATA_EXPERT_SPLIT: "1" ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR: level_zero:0 SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT: "0" ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN: "1" STRATA_SYCL_ROOT: ${STRATA_ROOT} STRATA_SYCL_IMAGE: strata-sycl-b60 STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN: "1" STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST: "1" STRATA_MIRROR_MIB: "36864" ~~~ `.env` next to `compose.yaml` (`STRATA_ROOT` and `STRATA_API_KEY` omitted; the commented lines are the other quants used on the same setup): ~~~bash #STRATA_MODEL=IQ3_S #STRATA_MODEL=UD-IQ4_XS STRATA_MODEL=IQ1_M #STRATA_FAMILY=qwen #STRATA_FAMILY=unsloth STRATA_FAMILY=coder STRATA_CONTEXT=131072 ~~~ Container command (after an incremental SYCL build when the checked-out commit changed): ~~~bash exec ./setup.sh \ --backend sycl \ --family ${STRATA_FAMILY} \ --model ${STRATA_MODEL} \ --gguf-dir "${STRATA_ROOT}/models/${STRATA_MODEL}" \ --models-dir "${STRATA_ROOT}/models" \ --data-dir "${STRATA_ROOT}/data" \ --context ${STRATA_CONTEXT} \ --kv int8 \ --vision no \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8080 \ --api-key "${STRATA_API_KEY}" \ --yes ~~~ Engine arguments from `strata-coder-iq1_m.json` (paths omitted): ~~~text --pack --native --ple-gguf --expert-profile --expert-cache auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --stream-experts --vram-reserve-mib 2048 --prefill 4096 ~~~ Other run-config keys: `"backend": "sycl"`, `"tool_call_recovery": true`, `"reasoning_close_retry": true`, `"fit_max_tokens": true`.
**What happens** The model opens the call correctly (`` + ``), but writes the parameter tag in a different syntax. `parse_tool_call` only reads ``, so the call reaches the client with **empty arguments** (`{}`), even though the full value is in the output. `tool_call_recovery` does not cover these forms. It starts after roughly 15–25k prompt tokens and comes in streaks (2–3 broken calls in a row). It hits the `Bash` tool far more often than MCP tools with longer argument lists. Sampling made no difference: greedy and temperature 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / top_k 20 gave the same rate. No VRAM warnings in the log; `reasoning_close_retry` never fired. Measured: - 2026-10-13 (v0.1.43.1): 17 of 61 `Bash` calls broken in one 64-turn session - 2026-10-14 (v0.1.44.1): 35 of 45 `Bash` calls broken in the first 30 min after a restart **Tool schemas** - `Bash` (Continue built-in): required string `command`, optional `timeout` - `retry_code` (MCP): required strings `attempt_id` and `feedback` **Raw outputs (exact, from the server log)** 1. Name as an XML-style attribute, quoted (most common on 14.10): ~~~text grep -rn "correction_fit\|correction_generate\|job_type\|correction" lotto_graph/services/lstm/correction/runner.py lotto_graph/api/routes/jobs.py 2>/dev/null | grep -v __pycache__ | sed -n '1,40p' <|im_end|> ~~~ 2. Name as an attribute, unquoted: ~~~text ls lotto_graph/worker.py 2>/dev/null; grep -rln "def.*job\|job_type\|correction" lotto_graph/worker.py 2>/dev/null <|im_end|> ~~~ 3. All arguments as JSON in a nameless `` (feedback shortened here): ~~~text {"attempt_id": "bf3b0e1cb16b", "feedback": "Checked against the real repository file: `get_model` DOES exist on CorrectionRepository, so leave that call as it is. …"} ~~~ 4. Not recoverable, no value at all (observed bodies of ``): ~~~text command Bash (empty body) <｜end｜> ~~~ 5. Also seen, rarer: - `{"command": "grep -rn …"}` inside `` - `` with `` (a parameter of the `List` tool) - ``, `` Breakdown: on 13.10, 6 of the 17 broken calls carried the full value in a wrong syntax (forms 1–3) and 11 had none (form 4). On 14.10, 19 of 35 were forms 1–2, 3 were the `` JSON form and 13 had no value. **Local workaround for forms 1–3 (patch below)** A small patch on v0.1.44.1 (`serve/frontend.py`), active only with `"tool_call_recovery": true` and declared tools: - inside `…` it rewrites ``, `` and `` to ``; - it expands `{json}` into one `` per key (non-string values as JSON); - a new `ParamForms` class does this before `OutputParser` sees the text, holding a tag split across stream deltas until it is complete; - text outside a call (reasoning, answer) is untouched.
