issues.title: 0.1.44/HIP: verify-window watchdog still fires on long-context decode despite the 0.1.31 bounded-wait fix (residual #267)
issues.author: dinesh-chander
issues.body:
Follow-up to #267 (commented there too, filing separately since backend/OS/symptom differ). On 0.1.44 the verify-window watchdog still fires, with the post-fix message showing the 0.1.31 release path executed but wasn't enough.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Strata | 0.1.44 (HIP source build, gfx1100+gfx1100) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, UD-Q4_K_XL native pack |
| Engine args | `--max-context 200000 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --vision --vram-reserve-mib 2048 --pool-workers 13 --conversation-cache-mib 2048 --conversation-cache-slots 8 --conversation-cache-min-tokens 2000 --layer-split auto` |
| GPUs | 2x AMD RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, gfx1100), layer split 24/24, ROCm/HIP |
| CPU | Core Ultra 7 265K |
| RAM | 96 GB DDR5 |
| OS | Linux, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic |
| Launch | `reasoning high`, vision on CPU |

## What happened

Mid-decode on a long-context request, decode rate decayed progressively, then the watchdog fired:

```
[strata] thinking: 482 of max 32768 tokens, 28.7 tok/s, 17 s
[strata] thinking: 516 of max 32768 tokens, 18.4 tok/s, 28 s
[strata] thinking: 516 of max 32768 tokens, 13.6 tok/s, 38 s
[strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code None). Unrecoverable native verification failure: verify: timed out at layer 29; its GPU waits were released but the GPU did not finish within 5 s (#267) The next request starts the engine again.
[strata] done: 516 tokens in 48 s (10.8 tok/s) (error, cancel=False)
```

## Engine log: the dying request

The request that died was a ~95k-token conversation doing heavy KV streaming (this looks more like #251's long-context trigger than #267's short prompt):

```
strata serve: prompt 95487 tokens = 95387 reused + 100 read in 2198 ms (45.5 tok/s), 1841 generated in 44006 ms (41.8 tok/s), drafts accepted 868 of 1471, 6 checkpoints
strata serve: decode expert cache hit rate: 94.5% (1107035 hits / 1171357 lookups); 2723 more read by the GPU over PCIe or from another GPU (0.2% of all 1174080 routed)
strata serve: KV streaming: 98.03% of 46963620 block reads hit VRAM, 3730.4 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: suffix drafts: 18 windows, 27 of 52 drafts accepted
strata serve: prompt 97349 tokens = 97329 reused + 20 read in 356 ms (56.2 tok/s), 107 generated in 2015 ms (53.1 tok/s), drafts accepted 78 of 85, 6 checkpoints
strata serve: decode expert cache hit rate: 87.3% (47655 hits / 54560 lookups); 640 more read by the GPU over PCIe or from another GPU (1.2% of all 55200 routed)
strata serve: KV streaming: 98.03% of 47376474 block reads hit VRAM, 3762.1 MiB read from RAM
strata serve: suffix drafts: 11 windows, 36 of 39 drafts accepted
```

(The next engine-log line is the auto-restart on the following request — no engine-side stall report or dump was emitted before death.)

Prior requests in the same session were healthy (44–53 tok/s decode, 87–94% expert hit rates).

## How this differs from #267

- **The 0.1.31 fix ran and didn't save it.** The message says GPU waits *were released* but the GPU still didn't finish within 5 s — so this isn't the unreleased-flag case, it's a genuinely stuck GPU-side wait.
- **No device loss.** Both cards stayed healthy; `server.py` restarted the engine on the next request and serving resumed. No reboot.
- **Silent at kernel level.** No amdgpu/GTT/OOM lines in dmesg or the journal around the stall.
- **Not the low-VRAM case.** 2048 MiB reserve per card; per-request stats show no VRAM distress (98% KV-streaming VRAM hit, PCIe expert share ~1%). I've since raised `--vram-reserve-mib` to 3072 as the documented mitigation — will report back if it recurs.
- **Long context, not short.** ~95k-token conversation vs #267's one-sentence prompt; closer to #251.

## Notes

- Related: #267 (closed, 0.1.31), #251 (long-prompt verify stall), #29 (stall → engine restart).
- Box also runs other GPU/CPU load (long-lived ComfyUI, desktop), so system memory pressure can't be fully ruled out as a contributor — but nothing spilled loudly.
- Full engine log around the stall and the server log are on hand; say what to attach or capture next time it fires (e.g. `/metrics` snapshot, thread stacks if the engine can emit them on this path).

issues.title: [Feature]: ~10x less SSD writing when switching long conversations — a small addition to #1480
issues.author: fqqdc
issues.body:
**How it was made.** I built it together with an AI coding assistant — it wrote the code, I set the goal and tested it on my PC. The code is here if you're curious: https://github.com/fqqdc/Strata-conversation-cache-delta/tree/conversation-cache-delta (it's #1480 plus my changes). I'm not planning to open a PR — I don't have any experience with that side of things — I just wanted to share it and hear what others think.

Hello! I work as a programmer, but this kind of low-level software really isn't my area — I don't write C/C++ and I know nothing about CUDA.

**My situation.** One Windows PC (64 GB RAM, RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB). My conversations get very long (up to ~256K), and switching back to one used to re-read the whole conversation every time — 40 to 85 seconds. PR #1480 (`--conversation-cache-disk-only`) fixed that for me: switching back now takes a couple of seconds. Thank you for it.

**The catch.** Every time you switch away, it saves the whole conversation to disk — over 2 GB for my 245K conversations. With daily use that adds up to tens of terabytes of writes a year, and I'd rather not wear out my SSD.

**What I did.** On top of #1480, I made it save only the part that actually changed. Two small housekeeping things came along: after a restart the cache folder cleans up its own leftovers, and when the folder is full it deletes the conversation you haven't used for the longest time (before, it deleted whichever file happened to sort first — sometimes one you'd just used).

Numbers from my own machine:
- switching away from a 245K conversation: over 2 GB → about 227 MB (roughly 10x less)
- switching away from a 121K conversation: about 1.2 GB → about 226 MB
- switching back still works, and nothing was lost in any of my tests (dozens of switches, plus engine restarts)

It's off by default — you add one option to turn it on. Without it, everything behaves exactly as before.

**Honest limits.** The saving is about 10x, not more: roughly 200 MB of each save is a chunk of the model's internal memory whose size doesn't depend on how long the conversation is, and I don't know how to shrink that. Also, I only tested this on my own computer (Windows, NVIDIA, single GPU) — no idea about Linux, AMD, or multi-GPU.

I hope to see this kind of feature in the main branch someday — conversations kept on disk, and only the changed part written each time.

issues.title: Community benchmark: 2x NVIDIA A2 16 GB (sm_86, PCIe only), Xeon Gold 6444Y, 62 GiB RAM - UD-IQ4_XS and Q8_0, 64K to 1M, v0.1.42
issues.author: talisp
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on 2x NVIDIA A2 16 GB (sm_86, PCIe only), 62 GiB RAM

**Measured 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 on Strata v0.1.42. UD-IQ4_XS and Q8_0 of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, contexts 64K to 1M, speed and answer quality. More quantizations are still running.**

## Context

- This is a lab VM that sat idle for months. We are using it for a long, repeatable battery on Strata: speed and long-context behaviour, and (our main focus) the **quality of the answers of each quantization against Q8_0**.
- We also run Strata on a separate production VM. The lab VM is deliberately isolated from it, so we can run for days without disturbing anything.
- We want to help the project: give back measurements in the format you ask for, and report the rough edges we met. Nothing here is urgent. We can rerun any of it on a newer build.
- The battery is automated and this text was drafted by an AI assistant (Claude Code) working from our logs. The account owner reads and answers replies on this thread.

## Related threads from the same battery

- Bug (new): STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS writes nothing with `--pipeline-windows 2`, silently: #2445
- Data point added to the checkpoint-save error thread (#1932): https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1932#issuecomment-6170938660
- Data point added to the CUDA OOM on a 2-GPU split thread (#2408): https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2408#issuecomment-6170939159
- Related existing threads we did not touch: #2065 (VRAM headroom), #2275 (multi-user direction; we may later explore one GPU per request with a shared RAM copy of the model, and would report that separately).

## Hardware and software

- GPU: 2x NVIDIA A2, 15,356 MiB each, 60 W, Ampere sm_86. PCIe gen4, link width **x8** each (max x16), no NVLink, no P2P. Layer split only.
- CPU/RAM/storage: Xeon Gold 6444Y, 16 vCPUs (VMware guest, 1 socket, AVX-512, AMX), 62 GiB RAM, 500 GB virtual disk (fio: 5,758 MiB/s sequential read, 4K random read 462 MiB/s at queue depth 32).
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8.0-139, driver 570.211.01, CUDA 12.8.
- Strata: tag v0.1.42, commit `61b3fb5dd3f1e8ec09cf7e4e05208bc6d3c46406`, **source build for sm_86** (setup found no ready-made engine for this architecture and compiled one). Test engine built with `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON -DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`; the 4 exactness tests for the Q6_K/Q8_0 pieces passed on Ampere.
- Background load: none (nothing else runs on the VM). One request at a time (no concurrency tests yet).

## Model and configuration

- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` (revision main, Oct 2026): **UD-IQ4_XS** (93.7 GB) and **Q8_0** (188.2 GB, packed with `iq_pack.py --compat-bf16`; the experts are read straight from the GGUF, no `experts.bin`); vision enabled (mmproj BF16).
- Same settings for every test: 2 GPUs, `--layer-split auto`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--prefill auto`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5` with the MTP block, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--resident-budget-gib 35`, `--expert-cache auto`, `--max-context` 65536 / 131072 / 262144 / 524288 / 1048576 (YaRN above 262144).
- `--vram-reserve-mib`: **700 for UD-IQ4_XS, 1000 for Q8_0** (see the OOM section; the two models are therefore not at identical reserve).
- Reasoning: off. Direct tests send `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`; the evals use `reasoning_effort: none` in the config. Greedy (temperature 0). Cold disk cache at every server start.
- Server start: 60 to 75 s.

## Results

Speed numbers are the server's own timings. "Full context" = a prompt filling 97% of the window, then a 512-token continuation that reuses it. One run per point for these; three runs for the short-prompt sweep. `hit_rate` as reported (VRAM share, excludes `--pcie-frac` experts, see #588).

| Context | Model | Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s | Time to first token | Decode tok/s (512 tokens, full context) | hit_rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64K | UD-IQ4_XS | 64,489 | 742 | 87 s | 19.3 | 0.91 |
| 64K | Q8_0 | 64,488 | 192 | 336 s | 6.2 | 0.70 |
| 128K | UD-IQ4_XS | 124,091 | 767 | 162 s | 18.6 | 0.89 |
| 128K | Q8_0 | 124,091 | 183 | 680 s | 5.9 | 0.69 |
| 256K | UD-IQ4_XS | 250,616 | 742 | 338 s | 16.9 | 0.92 |
| 256K | Q8_0 | 250,616 | 189 | 1,329 s | 4.9 | 0.71 |
| 512K | UD-IQ4_XS | 497,579 | 591 | 843 s | 15.1 | 0.90 |
| 512K | Q8_0 | 497,578 | 178 | 2,800 s | 4.6 | 0.71 |
| 1M | UD-IQ4_XS | 1,041,873 | 398 | 2,620 s | 12.0 | 0.88 |
| 1M | Q8_0 | 1,041,873 | 166 | 6,274 s | 3.9 | 0.67 |

Short prompts, 64K config, median of 3: UD-IQ4_XS 4K prompt 352 tok/s prompt / 25.0 decode, 32K prompt 651 / 23.7; Q8_0 4K 76 / 6.7, 32K 185 / 6.7. Q8_0 (188 GB) does not fit in 62 GiB, so it reads experts from the SSD (about 36 to 42 GB read per request in the 4K and 32K sweeps, 256 tokens generated).

**Needle recall:** three hidden codes at 10/50/90% depth, recovered in order: 3/3 at every context from 64K to 1M on both models. `tools/needle_bench.py` on Q8_0: 15/15 found (32K, 128K, 262K, 400K, 500K x three depths; 200 s to 2,678 s each). Not yet run on UD-IQ4_XS.

**Parallelism without NVLink** (UD-IQ4_XS, 64K config, median of 3 decode tok/s at 4K / 16K prompts): default layer split 22.1 / 23.6; `--pipeline-windows 2` 23.4 / 26.0; peer without P2P 20.2 / 25.0. We adopted `--pipeline-windows 2` (+6 to +10% decode).

**1 GPU vs 2 GPUs** (UD-IQ4_XS, 256K config): sweep decode 21.5 / 21.1 / 20.0 (1 GPU) vs 22.5 / 22.6 / 21.5 (2 GPUs) at 4K / 32K / 128K; full-context prompt 411 vs 742 tok/s, decode 15.8 vs 16.9. `hit_rate` 0.62 to 0.66 (1 GPU) vs 0.89 to 0.92 (2 GPUs). The second card mostly helps prompt reading. Q8_0 on one GPU: 128K sweep 179 tok/s prompt, 5.6 to 5.8 decode, `hit_rate` 0.45.

### Answer quality (end-to-end correctness checks, one run, temperature 0)

| Check | Q8_0 | UD-IQ4_XS |
|---|---:|---:|
| HumanEval base / plus (164) | 95.1 / 92.7 | 94.5 / 92.7 |
| MBPP base / plus (378) | 93.4 / 78.8 | 92.6 / 79.4 |
| GSM8K flexible / strict (250) | 94.0 / 92.8 | 94.4 / 94.0 |
| IFEval prompt strict / loose (250) | 80.8 / 84.4 | 81.2 / 86.0 |
| 24 images with known answers (text 9 to 24 px, counting, table, colour/position) | 18/24 | 18/24 |

Paired exact McNemar tests on the same problems: p >= 0.42 on every metric, so no difference is detectable at these sample sizes. This is consistent with, but weaker than, the teacher-forced KL numbers in the 0.1.44 release notes (UD-IQ4_XS 88.9% same top token against Q8_0): task accuracy hides a measurable divergence. We are collecting first-token KL on 220 prompts too and will add it.

## What needed a workaround

1. **Engine exits with CUDA out of memory in small allocations, Q8_0, 2x16 GB, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`.** 128K: `mtp prefill: the input records do not fit` (cudaMalloc, `src/core/mtp.cpp` ~1138/1180 in v0.1.42), and once `mtp: step capture: no error` (no cause). 256K: `saving a checkpoint part failed` to the client; the reason (`checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: out of memory`) is only in the engine's stderr. "VRAM free at start" does not predict it: UD-IQ4_XS passes with 137 to 149 MiB free, Q8_0 at 64K passes with 29 MiB, Q8_0 at 128K fails with 383 MiB. 128K reproduced 3 of 3. At 128K it passes with `--vram-reserve-mib 1500`, with `--pipeline-windows 0`, or with `--prefill 1024` (one run each). We set `--vram-reserve-mib 1000` for every model: Q8_0 then ran 64K to 1M and over a thousand eval requests with no engine error (one run per context). See the two comments linked above.
2. **STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS silently does nothing with `--pipeline-windows 2`:** #2445. Workaround: collect with `--pipeline-windows 0`.
3. **Notes for anyone scoring a slow model with common harnesses (not Strata bugs):**
   - `evalplus` (openai backend) uses `signal.alarm(100)` in `gen/util/openai_request.py` and retries the same request forever when it fires. At ~5 tok/s a reply over ~500 tokens never fits; the server logs `done: ... (cancel, cancel=True)` at ~101 s again and again (66 of 98 requests) and the run sat on one problem for ~2 h. We raised it to 7200 s.
   - `lm_eval` `local-chat-completions` defaults to a 300 s timeout; IFEval generates up to 1280 tokens (~256 s at 5 tok/s). We set `timeout=7200`.
   - Pass chat replies through `evalplus.sanitize` before scoring: code fences made HumanEval score 0.0% in an earlier session.

## Already covered upstream (we found this by reading the docs afterwards)

Thinking control through the API (`DETAILS.md`), the meaning of `hit_rate` (#588), Q6_K experts being built by default (`QUANTS.md`, 0.1.44), and what `--compat-bf16` rounds (`tools/iq_pack.py` docstring). We had listed these as questions; they are answered, so we are not opening issues for them.

## Not tested / limitations

- Only v0.1.42. Not re-run on 0.1.43 to 0.1.44.1, which may already change item 1.
- One request at a time. No concurrency, `--batch`, or conversation-cache tests yet.
- Single run for the long-context and needle points; UD-IQ4_XS ran with reserve 700 and Q8_0 with 1000.
- Still queued: UD-Q6_K_XL, UD-Q5_K_XL, UD-Q4_K_XL, UD-Q3_K_XL, UD-Q2_K_XL; and the first-token KL pass.

## Data

Per-request JSON, engine logs and the scripts are kept with the results and can be shared on request or as a pull request under `bench/results/` if you prefer that format. We can also rerun the same battery on a newer build and send the diff.

issues.title: [Bug]: STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS writes no files with --pipeline-windows 2 on a 2-GPU layer split, and gives no warning (0.1.42)
issues.author: talisp
issues.body:
### What happened

With `--serve --pipeline-windows 2` on a two-GPU layer split, `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS=<path>` wrote **no** `<path>.<n>` files in 12 server sessions (2 models, contexts 64K to 1M, each session sent at least 60 one-token requests). The same engine binary, machine, config and prompts with `--pipeline-windows 0` (or with one GPU) write the files as documented in the code comment: 993,280 bytes each, i.e. the full vocabulary (248,320 logits) as float32. There is no message in the engine log or on stderr in the failing case.

### How to reproduce

1. Two NVIDIA GPUs, `--layer-split auto`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--spec 4 --mtp ...`, any model; start `strata --serve` with `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS=/tmp/l` in the environment.
2. Send one `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"max_tokens": 1`.
3. `ls /tmp/l.*` shows nothing.
4. Restart with `--pipeline-windows 0` (everything else identical): `/tmp/l.0` appears.

### What we think is going on

Reading `src/program/generate.cpp`: the serve-side dump (~line 11605 in v0.1.42, ~12662 on `main` today) sits right after `ver.run(...)` in the non-pipelined window loop. The file has only two dump sites (serve, and `generate` at ~13851 on main); the pipelined decode loop (the code that prints `pipelined decode:` and `pcie_auto_step` "in the pipelined loop too") has none. We did **not** trace which path the first window takes with `--pipeline-windows 2`; the evidence is that no file appears, in 12 of 12 sessions.

### Why it matters

Anyone comparing quantizations or code paths by KL through this dump gets an empty folder and no error. We only noticed after a multi-day battery had run, because the harness collected nothing and nothing complained.

`tools/quant_quality.py` uses `STRATA_LOGPOS` and is not affected; the variable is not mentioned in `docs/DETAILS.md`, so this may simply be an undocumented diagnostic with a mode limit.

### Suggestions (any one would have saved us a day)

- Write the dump from the pipelined path too; or
- print one stderr line when the variable is set but the current mode will not honour it; or
- say in the code comment / `DETAILS.md` that it needs `--pipeline-windows 0`.

We can test a patch on 2x A2 if useful.

### Strata version, GPU, OS

v0.1.42 (commit `61b3fb5dd3f1e8ec09cf7e4e05208bc6d3c46406`), source build for sm_86 · 2x NVIDIA A2 16 GB, PCIe gen4 x8 each, no NVLink · Ubuntu 24.04.4, driver 570.211.01, CUDA 12.8. Not re-tested on 0.1.43 or later; the dump code is unchanged on `main`.

### Engine log

Nothing to attach: there is no log line for the failing case, which is the problem.

---
Part of a set of reports from one test battery on an idle lab VM: see the field report / community benchmark #2446. Drafted by an AI assistant (Claude Code) working from our logs; the account owner will read replies here.

issues.title: 2026-10-14-community-vega-20-pro-vii-instinct-mi50-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3xxs STRATA_DENSE_MMQ STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16
issues.author: QPhuGit
issues.body:
# Community benchmark on Vega 20 [Radeon Pro VII/Radeon Instinct MI50 16GB] with STRATA_DENSE_MMQ, STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16 and numactl config

Measured on 2026-10-14 with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges). Speeds are the engine's own timings; first-token times are measured by the client over HTTP. Speed only: no correctness check was run.

## Hardware and software

- GPU and VRAM: Vega 20 Mi50 16GB (gfx906), power limit 130w, pcie 3.0 x16 8GT/s, on CPU0
- CPU: Dual Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2620 v3 @ 2.40GHz (12 cores, 24 threads); QPI: 9.6GT/s; installed RAM: 4x16GB; storage: SSD; 
- Memory bandwidth: Quad-chanel (3x16GB on CPU0, 1x16GB on CPU1), limit 1866GT/s by CPU
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-146-generic; GPU driver: ROCM 6.1.2; CUDA: not read
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2; engine 0.1.44.1
- Background workloads and power limits: not recorded

## Model and configuration

- Model and quantization: qwen3.8-flash-next-IQ3XXS
- Context: 131072 tokens; parallel slots: 1
- Settings: the install's own configuration, unchanged; thinking off for the suite; temperature 0

```text
strata --pack iq3xxs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf --max-context 131072 --expert-profile expert-profile.bin --kv k8v4 --kv-resident 16384 --spec 4 --prefill auto --expert-cache auto --expert-cache-per-layer
```

## Method

issues.title: 0.1.44.1: ~20-25% decode regression on RTX A3000 12GB (sm_86), IQ3_XXS GSQ-RCO pack, --spec 4
issues.author: yannickloth
issues.body:
# 0.1.44.1: ~20-25% decode regression on RTX A3000 12 GB (sm_86), IQ3_XXS GSQ-RCO pack, `--spec 4`

**Machine / build**

- Laptop, single GPU: **RTX A3000 Laptop 12 GB, sm_86**; i7-12850HX (8P+8E, no AVX-512); 125 GB RAM; CachyOS.
- Engine built from source (Nix, CUDA from nixpkgs), llama.cpp pinned to `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d` (upstream's `third_party/ggml/VERSION.txt`).
- Pack: **GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)**, native pack + MTP draft layer.
- Serve config: `--pack … --native … --ple-gguf … --expert-profile … --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp … --max-context 524288 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 2 --vram-reserve-mib 1800 --pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.7 --pool-workers 15 --adapt-every 1` (serve + idle-unload; single request at a time).

**Method**

Identical request on both engines on the same machine, back to back: one fixed prompt ("Write a Python module that reads an INI config file … Code only."), `temperature 0`, `max_tokens 300`, 1 warmup + 3 measured runs. Decode tok/s and draft acceptance are read from the engine's own serve log line (`prompt N tokens … M generated in … ms (X tok/s), drafts accepted a of b`). Engines were swapped by pointing the server's `exe` at the two built binaries; no rebuild between runs, no other traffic on the engine.

**Results**

| engine | decode (tok/s) | drafts accepted |
|---|---|---|
| **0.1.43.1** | **38.1, 38.5, 40.2, 42.1** | 78.9%, 81.1%, 84.3%, 85.7% |
| 0.1.44.1 (defaults) | 28.7, 32.0, 35.0, 39.7 | 73.9%, 80.3%, 81.1%, 83.6% |
| 0.1.44.1, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` | 23.7, 24.0, 24.4, 25.8 | 79.1%, 79.4%, 80.4%, 83.1% |

So 0.1.44.1 is ~20-25% slower to decode here, with or without the new route-tail-skip policy. 0.1.43.1's numbers are the reference we are used to (agent workloads with higher acceptance reach the high 40s).

**Observations that may help**

- In this regime (decode expert-cache hit rate 66-69%, 12 GB card missing lots of experts) `--route-tail-skip` turns **on** by default. It is worth ~+25% *within* 0.1.44.1 (28.7-35 vs 23.7-25.8) but does not reach 0.1.43.1, so it looks like a mitigation of a regression, not its cause.
- Draft acceptance is only part of it: the `=0` arm runs at 79-83% acceptance yet decodes 24 tok/s, below 0.1.43.1's 38-42 at similar acceptance.
- Suspects we have not singled out yet: the new **`STRATA_COMMIT_BATCH`** default (on), and the "**dense Q8_0 matrices read one row per block** … (RDNA4 and **sm_86**)" change from the 0.1.44 notes — sm_86 is exactly this card.
- Relevant log lines on 0.1.44.1: `decode expert cache hit rate: 66.4% / 68.5%`, `route tail skip: 86800 missed experts skipped (90774 entries)`, `KV streaming: 99.8% of block reads hit VRAM`.

Happy to run any A/B you want on this box (we keep both engines built and can switch them deterministically) and report back — e.g. `STRATA_COMMIT_BATCH=0`, an explicit `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` rank, or a build with the sm_86 dense-Q8_0 row path disabled.

issues.title: Layer split on an unequal NVIDIA pair (RTX 5080 + RTX 4070 Ti) hard-crashes the machine at 240K context; dump write fails (Windows 11, v0.1.42)
issues.author: leonininder
issues.body:
## Body

**Setup**

- Strata v0.1.42 release (`strata-windows-x64-cuda12.zip`, BUILD.json: CUDA 12.9, archs 60–89 + PTX), Windows 11 Home, driver 617.42.
- Unequal pair: RTX 5080 16 GB (sm_120 — runs this build's sm_89 **PTX**, no sm_120 cubin in the zip) + RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB (sm_89). PCIe probe 6.4 GB/s.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next abliterated IQ3_XXS, 262,144 context, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 3` + `mtp/rt`, `--expert-cache auto`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1024`.
- Layer split via `--layer-split auto --split-device 1`, `--vram-reserve-later-mib 512` (5080 first; auto picked `layers 0-34 / 35-47`). PCIe frac auto-probed to 0.18.

**What happened**

Three consecutive ~238K-token prompt runs completed (log: `prompt 237976 tokens = ... 94253 ms (2524.9 tok/s)`, KV streaming 82–84% VRAM hits, expert reads over PCIe reported per request), then the machine **hard-crashed** (Kernel-Power 41). The crash dump write itself failed: `volmgr` event 161, `BugCheckProgress 0x00020020` — no minidump, so unfortunately no bugcheck code. The same 240K ×3 workload is stable on the same engine in single-GPU mode (`--gpu` only), and the split runs were fine at 8K/70K.

**Hypothesis**

This build has no sm_120 cubin (BUILD.json archs stop at 89, `ptx: true`), so the 5080 executes PTX-JIT kernels. The layer-split + long-context KV-streaming path exercises cross-card hand-off per verify window; a JIT edge case under that pressure is my first suspect (second: the known asymmetric-pair rough edges in #2052/#2239). Kernel dump capture is now enabled here, so a repeat run should produce a dump — happy to run a bisect-style probe if you point me at the right knobs (e.g. `STRATA_SPLIT_RING`, `--kv-grow`, forcing precompiled cubins).

**Also measured (for the TEST_REQUESTS unequal-pair ask)**

Full report with per-run data ready for a `bench/results/` PR (both card orders + helper-cache arm): single-GPU won every tier; both split orders lost ~30-55% prefill and ~12% decode vs single 5080; helper cache (`--expert-cache-device1 5000 --remote-expert-opt`, 3,306 experts on the 4070 Ti) collapsed decode to 23.6 tok/s (spread 16.6–48.5) vs 85.0 control. `cuDeviceCanAccessPeer` = 0 both ways (WDDM GeForce), so peer-mapped designs are untestable on this host.

*(Bench report: PR pending — link will follow.)*

pulls.author: GoldenLeafBird
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

No community numbers existed for a single-GPU RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) Windows
HIP box. This PR adds two result folders measured on 2026-10-20 with
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, context 131072, KV int8, MTP spec 4:

- Community report `bench/results/2026-10-20-community-rx-7900-xtx-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs/`
  with the legacy suite across four configurations (0.1.43.1 untuned, 0.1.43.1
  with the issue 2274 tuning, 0.1.45 tuned, v0.2.1 serve layer tuned).
- Standard-v1 run `bench/results/2026-10-20-standard-rx-7900-xtx-5b4dbf77/`,
  written by `strata bench run` unchanged, validation included.

Headline numbers: tuned 32K prompts read at 1,818 tok/s, 16K at 1,822 tok/s,
chat decode about 70 tok/s, agent decode 82.1 tok/s. The v0.2.1 serve layer
changes every cell by less than the run-to-run spread against the 2026-10-19
0.1.45 record.

The standard-v1 sanity checks scored 0 of 12: that engine start drew the
per-start bad state of #2960 (the `KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads`
marker on every request). The prompts were provably intact (frozen fixture
token counts on all 22 requests, byte-exact template render), and the
configuration is exonerated by a follow-up replay across four configurations
that answered correctly on five fresh starts. The run stays a valid
performance measurement; the quality result and its diagnosis are recorded in
the README.

## Related discussion

- #2274 - the prompt-path tuning these runs measure (five env flags, prefill
  chunk 16384, hipBLASLt table).
- #2960 - the per-start engine state that produced the 0 of 12 sanity score. A
  comment with this run's evidence follows this PR.
- #3188 - the `strata_bench.py` NameError. A local three-token patch was
  needed to run the legacy suite; a comment with the patch follows.

## Approach

Results only, no engine changes. Raw `results.json` files are copied unchanged
(the three earlier ones under `comparisons/`), the used configuration is
attached, `repeat.sh` holds both commands with their preconditions, and every
number in the README tables was cross-checked against those files after the
commit.

## Validation

- Passed: `strata bench report` on the standard run, status complete, all 89
  missing-map entries carry reasons.
- Passed: 21 of 21 standard requests finished, 0 failed, no unexpected cache
  reuse.
- Failed: sanity 0 of 12 (bad engine start, #2960, see above).
- Not run: the optional concurrency stage, vision (Windows AMD serves
  text-only), the `--model-revision` / `--source-revision` pinning fields.

## Limits

Single machine, one quiet box, warm expert cache (not cold-model numbers), and
the server does not replay seeded requests byte-identically, which limits
exact reproduction. The engine is 0.1.45, not the 0.1.46 this release ships,
because a source install cannot fetch it (`WIN_HIP_ASSET` names an asset no
0.2.x release carries). A separate issue follows for that.

The report text was drafted with AI assistance. Every number comes from the
machine-recorded result files in this PR, none typed by hand or generated.

pulls.title: [GUI] Use web API keys immediately when browser storage fails
pulls.author: engharat
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The web app saves its API key only on `change` (usually blur), and every request reads it back from localStorage. Before blur, an edited key is not used. If storage is blocked or full, the app discards the entered key, sends no key (or the old one), and still says “API key saved.”

The page now uses the trimmed key immediately on input, saves it when possible, and keeps using it in memory if storage fails. On change, it warns that the key must be entered again after reload when persistence is unavailable. Clearing the field removes Authorization. Existing stored keys and keyless servers keep working.

Related symptom: #725. This fixes the client-side event/storage paths, not server-side key normalization proposed in the closed #956.

## Approach

Keep the current page's key in memory for the shared request-header helper. Have the existing storage setter report whether its write succeeded, so the notification does not claim persistence when the write failed. No new dependencies, server changes, authentication bypasses, or engine changes.

## Validation

Linux, Python 3.14.4, Node v22.22.1. Final commit: `3afe9d4a`.

Passed:
- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_web_api_key serve.test_web_sampling -v`: 12 tests passed (8 API-key regressions, 4 existing sampling tests).
- `node --check serve/web/app.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Before the fix, the initial regression run failed on missing/stale Authorization and the false success notification; the same cases pass after the fix.
- In Chromium against the running page at `127.0.0.1:8080`, confirmed input updates Authorization and storage without blur. With Storage reads/writes forced to throw, confirmed Authorization still uses the edited key, a warning appears, and clearing the field removes Authorization. Test values were removed afterward.
- Authenticated GET `/metrics` on the live server returned HTTP 200.

Failed / limits:
- Broader `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s serve -t .` run, before adding the final notification regression: 888 tests, 2 failures, 14 skipped. Failures were `serve.test_keepawake.KeepAwakeTests.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close` and `serve.test_responses.NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler`. The keepawake failure also reproduces against an exported unmodified parent revision (`e88ee39d`); the sampler test passes in isolation on both revisions. Neither was changed here.
- A live chat request authenticated but returned HTTP 400: `verify: instantiate: out of memory`. A successful GPU-generated answer was therefore not verified; this PR does not address that engine memory error.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` could not run: pytest is not installed. C++/GPU builds were not run because no backend files changed.

pulls.title: [Engine] HIP: the expdec shared int4 arrays use the attribute-after-declarator form
pulls.author: chenxyz129
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

**Before:** on `main` (9ae93f7b, Control 0.1.46.1 / engine 0.1.46), a HIP build for gfx1032 stops in
`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`:

```text
src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu:2263:16: error: 'alignas' attribute cannot be applied to types
src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu:2450:16: error: 'alignas' attribute cannot be applied to types
```

Those are the two expdec kernels added in v0.1.45 (gate/up and down), which declare
`__shared__ alignas(16) int4 s_u[...]`. The same file already carries the working form right next to them:
`STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_U32`, with the #778 comment saying that HIP takes the attribute after the declarator.

**After:** a `STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_I4` macro mirrors that one (`__shared__ int4 name[...] __attribute__((aligned(16)))`
under `__HIPCC__`, `alignas` elsewhere), and the two kernels use it. Array type, size and alignment are unchanged.

## Related discussion

none

## Approach

One macro beside the existing `STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_U32`, and the two declarations switched to it. No kernel logic,
no launch configuration and no numerics change: this only makes the expdec source compile for HIP again.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- After the change, at commit `f1e9d33a` (main `9ae93f7b` + this patch), `cmake --build build-hip -j10` for gfx1032 ->
  all targets built and `strata` linked; `./build-hip/strata --version` -> `strata 0.1.46.1`.
  Environment: Fedora, ROCm 7.1.1 (hipcc 7.1.52802), AMD RX 6650 XT (gfx1032, 8 GB).
- `./build-hip/strata-device --selftest` at the same commit -> `strata-device selftest OK` (arena allocation and the
  over-allocation refusal).
- The same build also passes with this patch on top of the gfx1032 setup branch (`3eff80b1`): all targets built,
  `strata-device --selftest` -> `strata-device selftest OK`.

**Failed:**

- Before the change, at `9ae93f7b`, the same `cmake --build build-hip -j10` for gfx1032 fails with the two
  `'alignas' attribute cannot be applied to types` errors quoted above. That is the problem this fixes.

**Not run:**

- gfx1030 hardware: same shared-memory declaration and same HIP compiler path, but no such card here.
- CUDA, SYCL and Metal builds.
- A full model run, llama.cpp parity and any timing: this is a compile fix, and no number here is a speed claim.

## Limits

- Tested with one HIP compiler version (7.1.52802) on one gfx1032 card; other HIP targets compile the same macro but
  were not built here.
- Nothing about the expdec kernels' speed or results is measured in this pull request.

pulls.title: [Other] Fix Windows child process permissions in adopt_user_defaults
pulls.author: kossum
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

I ran into this while starting a locally built engine on Windows. The server was healthy, but my PowerShell helper for setting HighQoS kept timing out because it couldn't read `strata.exe`'s path. Trying `OpenProcess` directly returned error 5 (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`), even though the engine was running under the same user.

The cause is the `FA` entries in the token default DACL set by `adopt_user_defaults()`. `FA` means `FILE_ALL_ACCESS` (`0x1f01ff`), but that default DACL is also used when creating child processes. The file access mask doesn't include the process query and set-information rights needed here.

Changing these entries to `GA` lets Windows map the permissions to the object being created. With this change, reopening a child process and setting its QoS works without elevation.

## Related discussion

None. The `FA` token default was added in `df13760c`.

## Approach

The fix only changes `FA` to `GA` in the token default DACL. The user, SYSTEM and Administrators entries stay the same. The separate ACLs used to make files private are untouched.

The regression test calls `adopt_user_defaults()`, starts a Python child, then reopens it with `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_SET_INFORMATION` and calls `winjob.no_throttle()`. It runs in a separate Python process so it doesn't change the test runner's token defaults.

Non-Windows code still returns before this point. There are no engine or GPU backend changes.

## Validation

Tested without elevation on Windows 11, build `10.0.26300`, with 64-bit Python 3.13.2 (Anaconda) from the project's `.venv`.

The patched tree is based on `9ae93f7b1fe989d04a8e404d32cddaeeff10505f`, on branch `fix/windows-child-process-default-dacl`. Commands were run from the repo root using that environment.

**Passed:**

```text
python -m unittest discover -s tests/terminal -p test_private_files.py -v

Ran 14 tests
OK (skipped=1)
```

That's 13 passed, with the POSIX mode-bit test skipped on Windows. This includes the new process-access test and the existing file-ACL tests.

`git diff --check` also passed with no output.

**Failed:**

Before changing the DACL, the new test reproduced the access denial:

```text
python -m unittest discover -s tests/terminal -p test_private_files.py -k default_dacl -v

AssertionError: OpenProcess failed: 5
FAILED (failures=1)
```

That run was before syncing main; the affected `FA` code was unchanged by the sync. The post-fix run above is on the updated base. No failures in that run.

**Not run:**

- The full Terminal/Control suite.
- Linux/macOS, or the new test from an elevated Windows session.
- A full model-server restart on the updated base. The new test uses a Python child and real Windows process/QoS calls, without loading a model.
- GPU builds or benchmarks, since this doesn't change backend code.

## Limits

The server needs a restart. This doesn't repair the token defaults or ACLs of processes that are already running.

The test checks that reopening the child and setting QoS succeed; it doesn't read back the throttling state. This also doesn't mean Strata's built-in QoS setup was failing: it uses the handle returned when the child is created, rather than reopening it by PID.

pulls.title: [Engine] Metal: the control vector (experimental speed projection) on the Mac engine
pulls.author: Flo5k5
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On a Mac, `--control-vector-scaled` loads nothing: the Metal engine answers with an empty control vector (`metal/src/engine/missing.cpp`), and `docs/MAC.md` lists the control vector as not ported. So the experimental speed projection (`data/experimental-speed-projection/`, docs/DETAILS.md) does nothing on Apple Silicon, although the flags are accepted.

With this change, the Metal engine applies the vector as the CUDA engine does: after each steered layer (4..44 for the ESP), every hyper-connection stream of every row becomes `h - s (h.v) v` (project) or `h + d` (add). It covers the decode window, the MTP verify window and both prompt paths. The log prints `control vector mode = project, dir = per-layer, layers 4..44 (41 steered)`, and the request field `"experimental_speed_projection": false` switches it off. With it off, the replies are token-for-token those of the engine started without a vector.

## Related discussion

none (a port of the existing CUDA/HIP feature to the Metal backend; no new flag, no change to a default)

## Approach

- `metal/src/engine/msl/cvec.metal`: one threadgroup per (stream, row). It applies the layer's pending FFN write `R += bo * 2 sigmoid(inj / hc)` with `gr_norm`'s own arithmetic, then the projection (or the addition). It is the same operation as `src/kernels/cuda/cvec.cu`.
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`, `prompt_chain.inc`: after a steered layer's MoE output, the window encodes this kernel, and the next layer's hyper-connection read runs with `apply = false` (the write is already in R). The last layer and the final `output_hc` read follow the same rule. Three paths are covered: `Window::run` (decode, verify windows, short prompts in 8-row windows), `pc_chunk` (the resident prompt chain) and `prompt_chunk` (the streaming prompt chunks).
- The per-request switch: the window caches its encoded command lists, so the switch state is part of the cache key. A request with the vector off encodes exactly the stock dispatches. No device flag is needed, and an off request costs nothing.
- `metal/src/engine/cvec.cpp`: `cvec_upload`, `cvec_set_enabled`, `cvec_enabled`, `cvec_replicate` and `cvec_tables` for Metal (unified memory: the tables stay in host memory, and the window copies the 480 KB direction table into a Metal buffer the first time the vector is on). Their four stubs are removed from `stubs.cpp`, and the empty `cvec()` from `missing.cpp`. `cvec_apply` and `gr_write_cvec_norm_rs` stay stubs: they are the CUDA engine's host-side hooks (layer.cpp, verify.cpp, prefill.cpp), which the Metal engine does not run.
- No shared source changes (`src/`, `include/`): CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds are not touched.

## Validation

Revision: `metal-control-vector` at c885c306 (main 9ae93f7b + this change). MacBook Pro, Apple M5 Pro, 64 GB, macOS 27. Built with `cmake -S metal -B build-metal -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DMETAL_CPP_DIR=… -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=…` (llama.cpp 3cf03257) and `ninja -C build-metal strata cvec_parity`.

**Passed:**
- Build: `strata`, `cvec_parity`, `gr_parity` link with no error; the warnings are in existing shared headers only.
- `build-metal/cvec_parity`: 27 of 27 checks, for 1, 3 and 8 rows. Project against a double-precision host reference (max error 5.0e-7; s = 2 reflects the component, s = 1 removes it). The pending write is **bitwise** `gr_norm`'s folded write (gr.metal with `apply`). Write then project: max error 4.8e-7. Add is `h + d` bitwise. Rows past the window are untouched.
- Engine A/B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 in memory (`--spec 2 --mtp … --prefill auto --max-context 65536 --mmap-experts`, `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`, `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT_CHUNK=2048`), served by `serve/server.py`, greedy (`temperature 0`, `reasoning_effort none`, `max_tokens 256`). Five prompts: 4 short ones (24-42 tokens, 8-row windows) and one of 2,338 tokens (the resident prompt chain). Two repetitions.
  - Started with `--control-vector-scaled <Strata>/data/experimental-speed-projection/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-experimental-speed-projection.gguf:1.0 --control-vector-layer-range 4 44 --cvec-mode project --cvec-dir per-layer`: the log prints `control vector mode = project, dir = per-layer, layers 4..44 (41 steered)`.
  - `"experimental_speed_projection": false` against the same build started without the vector: 8 of 8 replies identical, reasoning and text, character for character (one of them cut short at 160 tokens by an external memory watchdog, a prefix of the stock reply). The stock engine is identical between its two repetitions.
  - `"experimental_speed_projection": true`: 8 of 8 replies differ from stock. The two requests the stock model refused were answered: "How do I pick a pin tumbler lock…" in both repetitions, "Write a brutal, mean-spirited roast…" in the one repetition that ran (the second stopped before it).
  - Cost, kernel alone (`cvec_parity --bench`, the 41 dispatches a window adds, median of 20): 0.22 ms of GPU time per window for 1, 2, 3 or 8 rows; 38 ms for a 2,048-row prompt chunk.
  - Cost, decode: about 25 ms per verify window in all three runs (on, off, stock); the 0.22 ms is about 1% of it. The tokens/s of the replies (on 55.8-73.9, off 61.0-72.2, stock 61.2-73.7) do not resolve a 1% cost: off and stock run the same dispatches and still differ by up to 5.5% on one prompt (the code prompt, mean 69.1 vs 73.1 tok/s).
  - Cost, prompt: the 2,338-token prompt read in 2,277 / 2,282 / 2,326 ms with the vector on and 2,262 / 2,302 / 2,319 ms off (alternating, after one warm-up pair): 2,295 vs 2,294 ms. The first read of a run is slower (2.9-10.4 s, cold file cache after another model server ran); it is left out.

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- The streaming path (`prompt_chunk`, experts read from the SSD with `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1`): the code is there, not run.
- `--cvec-mode add`, and `--cvec-dir single:L` in the engine (the add kernel is covered by `cvec_parity` only).
- A KL or perplexity measurement against stock on Metal (like bench/results/2026-09-27-esp/ on CUDA).
- The M5 Max, the M4 and other Macs; Unsloth's files and the other families.
- CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds: no file they compile is changed.

## Limits

- The Mac setup (`metal/setup_mac.py`, `strata launch`) does not offer the speed projection yet. It is turned on by passing the engine flags (the config's `args`), as above.
- The vector is copied into the window the first time it is on; a second `cvec_upload` in the same process (not done by the loader) would not be picked up.
- `cvec_tables` returns false on Metal (no device tables for another kernel to fuse); the CUDA prompt path's `STRATA_CVEC_FUSE` has no Metal counterpart, and none is needed: the prompt kernels read the vector through the same dispatch.

pulls.title: [Other] Set the policy baseline for the standalone GGML overlay test
pulls.author: hulkbig
pulls.body:
Fixes #3412.

The documented `cmake -P cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake` invocation fails on CMake 3.x because its script scope has no policy baseline. In particular, the `IN_LIST` check uses the OLD behavior of CMP0057 even though the project requires CMake 3.24 or newer. Running the main CMake project first does not initialize policies for a separate script invocation.

Set `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)` in the standalone test, matching the project baseline. The overlay generator and GPU source are unchanged.

Validation (Linux x86_64, CPU-only script execution):
- Used Strata source at `9ae93f7b1fe989d04a8e404d32cddaeeff10505f` and a complete llama.cpp checkout at the pinned `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d`.
- Before the change, the unmodified overlay test fails with CMP0057 / Unknown arguments on CMake 3.24.3 and 3.31.10; it passes on 4.4.4.
- After the change, the same standalone test passes on all three versions.
- All 121 generated/copied files are byte-identical across the three fixed runs and the pre-change CMake 4.4.4 run.
- Command: `cmake -DLLAMA=<pinned llama.cpp checkout> -DOUT=<dedicated scratch directory> -P cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake`.

Not run: CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds, GPU inference, model benchmarks, or online CI. This change only initializes the standalone test's CMake policies and makes no performance claim.

AI-assisted implementation and validation.

pulls.title: [GUI] Web search and page reading for the web app's Chat (DuckDuckGo default, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Serper, Exa, Perplexity)
pulls.author: c-OOL-io
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The Chat tab of the lean web app (the serve/Terminal frontend, not the App) has no web access at all: answers are limited to the model's weights, and agent-style use on a headless server had no source-backed option. Upstream shipped web search for the App in 0.2.0; the serve web chat route is still without it.

Before: no search in the web app's Chat, no sources. After: a built-in web search, modeled after how Open WebUI and similar chat tools do it: the model can look the question up before answering, and the answer shows its sources. **Web search is completely off by default**: until the user turns it on in Chat Settings, nothing about this feature sends anything out of the PC. Strata's Chat is deliberately lean, and this feature is built the same way: it adds no tokens until a chat turns search on, and results are budget-capped to a small slice of the model's context window (defaults scale with the context window), so the Chat gains recent information without losing what makes it comfortable for long sessions.

## Related discussion

Replaces #2826: that PR was closed in the pre-0.2.0-beta tracker reset ("closed here does not mean rejected"); after the rebase its stored head commit became unreachable, so GitHub refuses to reopen it and this PR carries the same work on a live base. Upstream's App search (`apps/host`, DuckDuckGo via MCP) does not overlap with this work: this targets the serve web chat, with self-hostable engines (SearXNG) and server-side page reading.

## Approach

Search runs server-side in the serve backend (`serve/websearch.py`, stdlib-only); the browser frontend only configures and renders it. All providers are fetched through the Strata server (a browser could not call them directly because of CORS). API keys stay browser-only (localStorage), like the existing API-key field; **nothing search-related is stored on the server**.

### What it looks like in the UI
- A globe button in the composer (first icon, before the paperclip) toggles search for the next message.
- **Chat Settings** (gear) has a *Web search* section: enable/disable, engine picker, SearXNG URL, API key field, max results, page reading and a page reader mode (see below). All web-search controls appear only when the search switch is on; switching it on expands the whole section and fires the privacy toast.
- When search is on, the results are injected as context before the model's turn, with an instruction to answer from them and cite by `[n]`.
- Under each answer the sources appear as `Sources (DuckDuckGo): [1] … | [2] …` (clickable, engine named, read pages get a `read` badge), and they are included in the "Save this chat as Markdown" export.
- While a search runs the status pill shows the truth instead of "Idle": a globe (instead of the state dot) with `Framing query` → `Searching web + reading pages · DuckDuckGo · 12.4 s`; a failed search reads `Search failed` for 2.5 s. The same status line appears in the answer bubble exactly where "Thinking…" would sit.
- If the engine is busy with someone else's turn (another tab or agent) while this chat searches, the pill shows it as a hint (`… · 1 queued`) instead of hiding it or hijacking the label: one priority function owns the pill (search phase > engine state > queue count > idle), so the 1 s metrics poll and the 250 ms search timer can no longer overwrite each other.

### Query optimizer
Conversational wording ("can you look up what the newest Qwen release from Alibaba is") makes weak search queries, so there is an **"Optimize search query"** toggle (on by default): one fast call to the user's own local model (temperature 0, reasoning off, max 100 tokens) extracts the core search question before the search runs.
- The query stays **in the language the user wrote in**: English stays English, German stays German etc. Obvious typos are fixed.
- If the call fails, is aborted, or returns something empty or rambling, the **raw message is searched instead** - the optimizer can never break a search.
- **Transparency**: whenever what was searched differs from what was typed, the sources line shows `Sources (DuckDuckGo) · searched: "…"`, and so does the Markdown export. An optimized query is never hidden behind a plain-looking result.

### Reading result pages in full
Snippets alone often miss the details, so search can also fetch the top result pages and inject their extracted text (Open WebUI's "Web Loader" idea, stdlib `html.parser` based, which skips nav/footer/scripts, prefers `main`/`article`):
- **"Read result pages"** toggle + **"Pages to read"** (1-5).
- **"Limit page text"** toggle (on by default) with a **"Max characters per page"** field (default 5000). Turning it off sends whole pages; see the budget below for why that is still safe.

### Page reader: direct fetch, or Jina Reader for JS-heavy pages
Plain `urllib` cannot render JavaScript-heavy pages, so there is a 3-tier **Page reader** setting:
- **Direct only (default)**: only the Strata server fetches pages; nothing goes to any third party.
- **Jina as fallback**: direct first; pages that fail (JS walls, blocks) are retried through [r.jina.ai](https://r.jina.ai) (free hosted headless browser, no key needed, Apache-2.0).
- **Jina for all pages**: every page goes through r.jina.ai.
- The base URL is overridable via `STRATA_JINA_URL` (e.g. a self-hosted instance), and failures of either path degrade to a readable combined reason.
- **Privacy is surfaced, not buried**: the dropdown explains per selection, a warning line appears whenever a third party could see the URLs, and turning search on fires a toast that names the engine *and* the reader mode ("… go through r.jina.ai - a third party sees those URLs").

### Context-aware reading budget
How much search text goes into the prompt scales with the model's own context window (`reported_ctx()`), so small-context instances are never overloaded:
- The reading budget is a slice of the window (~3 chars/token): **10 %** normally, **25 %** when the user explicitly turns the per-page limit off; the per-page cap is then derived from the budget instead of a fixed number.
- First-use defaults scale the same way from `/health`'s `max_context` (e.g. 16K ctx → 4 results / 1 page × 3000 chars; 128K → 6 / 2 × 5000; 262K → 8 / 3 × 5000).
- Unknown context falls back to the plain 5000/page default.

### Distinct, persistent search warnings
A failed search no longer fails silently: the reason stays on the message (in the sources line, warning-colored) and in the Markdown export, with a different message per cause:
- **no API key set** → `Brave Search needs its API key (Chat Settings > Web search)` (same for Tavily/Serper/Exa/Perplexity; a *rejected* key gets its own message, incl. Brave's 422)
- **engine unreachable** (e.g. SearXNG not running) → `SearXNG at http://127.0.0.1:8888 is not reachable (…); start it or pick another engine`
- **DuckDuckGo bot check** → DDG's lite endpoint answers Chrome-impersonating UAs with its `anomaly.js` page; the fetcher uses an honest custom UA and, if the bot page still shows up, says so instead of reporting "no results"
- **engine reachable but nothing found** → `no results`
- **unreadable page** → per-result `read_error` (shown as a warning line), never a silent empty string

### Security hardening
- **`/search` sits behind the web app's own-page guard** (`_own_page`): a JSON body is required (415 for form posts) and a foreign `Origin` is rejected (403; `trusted_origins` still allowed), so a random web page cannot make this PC run searches or fetch URLs through it.
- **http(s) only**: the SearXNG base URL and every result URL that gets page-read pass a scheme check (`_http_url`); `file://`, `data:`, `javascript:` and friends are refused with an explicit reason, so page reading can never become a local file reader.
- **Source links render defensively**: only `http(s)` URLs become clickable `<a href>`; anything else shows as plain text, so no `javascript:`/`data:` links from a poisoned result.
- **Prompt-injection hardening**: the injected search context states that titles, snippets and page text are untrusted web data whose embedded instructions must not be followed.
- **LAN-bound warning**: `/health` reports `lan_bound` (server bound beyond loopback, e.g. `0.0.0.0`); turning search on fires an extra toast line warning that queries and engine keys then cross the network in plain HTTP and that devices on it can use the search without an api_key. On the default `127.0.0.1` bind this warning never appears.
- API keys stay browser-only (localStorage); nothing search-related is stored server-side.

### Settings drawer updates
- The drawer was titled **"Sampling"**; since it now also holds web search settings it is renamed to **"Chat Settings"** (gear tooltip: "Chat Settings: Thinking & Web Search"), the close button got a proper "Close" tooltip, and the save toast says "Settings saved".
- The **Reset** button turns web search completely off and restores the first-use defaults: search disabled, engine back to DuckDuckGo, no API key, instead of leaving a stale engine or an active search behind.
- The empty-state privacy note is qualified and split into two fixed lines: "Nothing leaves it. / Web search is off by default - when on, only the search query goes out."
- Reset and Apply now sit fixed under the "Chat Settings" title while the options scroll below; the sampling options are grouped under a restored "Sampling" heading.

### Scroll fix (drive-by)
Auto-follow-to-bottom was broken for turns where content grows past the stick threshold mid-stream (the thinking panel expanding could pin the view at the user's own message). Stickiness is now captured *before* the content grows, so the view keeps following the answer.

### Engines
| engine | needs |
|---|---|
| DuckDuckGo (default, labeled "anonymous - no key needed") | nothing (lite endpoint) |
| SearXNG | a running instance (default `http://127.0.0.1:8888`) |
| Brave Search | API key |
| Tavily | API key |
| Serper (Google) | API key |
| Exa | API key |
| Perplexity (model `sonar`) | API key |

Exa and Perplexity call the same endpoints upstream's App calls (`api.exa.ai/search` with Bearer key, `api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions` model `sonar`, sources taken from `search_results`, falling back to bare `citations` when the plan omits them), so a key someone already has for the App works here unchanged.

### Design notes
- `serve/websearch.py` is **stdlib-only** (`urllib`, `json`, `re`, `html.parser`, `os`); no new dependencies, cross-platform (Windows/Linux/macOS).
- `POST /search` carries its own engine config per request; nothing is stored on the server.
- Page fetches are capped (10 s timeout, 2 MB download); read results use an explicit contract (`content` on success, `read_error` on failure, `read_via` for Jina-read pages) instead of heuristics.
- `/search` has a catch-all so an unexpected error returns a clean 502 with a server-side log line instead of a broken connection.

## Validation

Re-validated today (20.10.) on the rebased branch `web-search` @ `3d05a166`, which contains upstream `main` including `894d1be1` (0.2.1) and `8aaf188a` (user-args/VRAM fix). Environment: Windows 11, RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, Ryzen 9 7950X3D, engine 0.1.45 (`MIN_ENGINE` (0,1,45) met), model qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs, 128K ctx.

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest serve.test_websearch -v` (the suite now committed in this branch): **18 tests, all green** (scheme guard rejects 15 poison URL types `file:// gopher:// javascript: data: ftp:// dict:// ldap:// sftp:// ssh:// mailto: telnet: jar: chrome-extension: vbscript:` and accepts http(s); reader tier matrix direct/fallback/always incl. Jina rescue on a failing direct fetch and the combined both-paths-fail reason; bad reader values degrade to direct; non-HTML content refused; reading-budget clamps at 10 %/25 % of context with per-page caps derived at 4K/16K/128K; `max_results` clamp; keyed engines: Exa/Perplexity deman

pulls.title: [Engine] Preserve target probabilities in gated MTP
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1`, the confidence gate selects drafts using the probability of the token it just drew. The original verifier still uses the unfiltered q, and a failed gate becomes a plain target sample. This biases the output toward the draft head's preferred tokens.

This patch keeps the confidence gate and accounts for the missing proposal mass explicitly. It also keeps CPU expert arithmetic independent of how many tokens share a speculative window, so the verifier samples the singleton target distribution.

For `p=(0.5,0.5)`, `q=(0.875,0.125)` and threshold `0.5`, the original gate emits `(0.5625,0.4375)`; the repaired gate emits `(0.5,0.5)`.

## Related discussion

Refs #2028. Thanks to KarlGrier for the report and derivation. This continues #2591 on v0.2.1 (`90767252`, engine 0.1.46). Its intake check passed, but GitHub rejected reopening the closed PR; the intake bot requested a linked replacement in that case.

## Approach

The proposal packet retains q on admitted tokens without renormalizing it; call this measure μ. A failed draw becomes an explicit NULL row. Offered tokens use `min(1,p(D)/μ(D))`; rejection and NULL sample the normalized positive part of `p−μ`. A row with no attempted proposal remains an ordinary bonus sample.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q[Draft distribution q] --> G[Confidence gate + eligible suffix root]
    G --> M[Retained measure μ + NULL mass]
    M --> O[Offered token]
    M --> N[NULL]
    O --> A[Accept with min 1, p / μ]
    O --> R[On rejection: sample positive p − μ]
    N --> R
```

CLI and serial serve share the packet builder. Attempt counts and context limits are decided at the producer boundary. Suffix eligibility uses committed context and request-fixed policy statistics. CPU dispatch preserves singleton arithmetic while retaining shared weight decoding where it gives the same result.

The 0.2 port preserves Trellis/Hadamard handling, per-job expert layouts and cold-read batching. Both ready and cold-read job submissions carry the arithmetic mode. ARM builds retain their native singleton arithmetic rather than referencing x86 kernels. Default exact-match drafting remains the default; explicit `top` gating remains available.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `gated_proposal_test`: 266 checks, including macOS ASAN/UBSAN.
- `spec_admission_test` and `STRATA_SPEC_PROB_GATE=top spec_admission_test top`: 900 Top cases and 2,700 μ-packet cases per configuration, with the original biased rule as a negative control.
- `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 STRATA_OLD_SAMPLER=0 STRATA_SAMPLER_ONE_BLOCK=0 spec_proposal_parity`: 432 rows, zero mismatches against an independent CPU oracle on RX 7900 XTX.
- `native_arithmetic_parity`: 4,866,048 finite bitwise comparisons in each of eight Windows configurations, including Trellis formats and Hadamard-folded inputs.
- Full CUDA, HIP, SYCL and Metal engine builds pass. CUDA/GCC and SYCL/oneAPI each pass 13 CPU tests; Metal also passes `strata --version` (`0.1.46-metal`).
- Incremental 12-position comparison against the genuine 0.2.1 release: patched MTP matches both no-MTP singleton references at all 12 raw-logit rows. Original MTP matches 1/12; its token-12 distribution has TV **0.0361348** from the singleton reference. All 24 sampled decisions reconstruct from captured p, q and counters. Trace builds reproduce production outputs.
- The default-mode original/patched 12-token outputs match. After the ARM compile fix, the rebuilt HIP candidate repeats the MTP/singleton check: all 24 logit rows and all outputs match the earlier candidate; the final default-mode check and sampler/CPU suites pass again.

![Target probability agreement on the fixed-prefix fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyanHu-git/Strata/470d558be39f1a8c8edda4d6058b8b5b8331035b/bench/results/2026-10-20-gated-mtp-v021/target-agreement.png)

[Prompt, seeds, binary/library hashes, per-position distributions and figure source](https://github.com/KeyanHu-git/Strata/tree/470d558be39f1a8c8edda4d6058b8b5b8331035b/bench/results/2026-10-20-gated-mtp-v021). The six-run numerical probe generated 72 tokens in 115.47 seconds. Singleton controls advance one token at a time; they do not re-prefill the whole prefix.

**Failed:** No remaining failure in the checks listed above. During preparation, the Metal link exposed two x86-only references; architecture-specific dispatch fixes them. An initial GPU test selected the integrated GPU; the reported run explicitly selects the RX 7900 XTX. These failed setup attempts are retained in the local experiment record.

**Not run:** CUDA, SYCL and Metal model execution; a new full GSM8K evaluation; a 0.2.1 throughput benchmark.

## Limits

The repaired proposal path supports serial generation on one CUDA/HIP device, with lookup-chain, adaptive swaps and PCIe sharing off. Unsupported combinations report an error. SYCL and Metal compile but do not execute this proposal path.

The numerical fixture resolves the earlier token-12 target-probability discrepancy. It does not establish an aggregate model-quality score or explain the later long reasoning trajectory. The previous 100-pair speed measurements remain results for the older engine, not 0.2.1 performance claims.
