pulls.title: [Engine] NUMA-split CPU expert pool, on by default on dual-socket Linux boxes
pulls.author: baptisterajaut
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On a dual-socket box the CPU expert pool either stays on one socket (the 0.2.0 default, 11 workers here) or spreads across both and gets slower, as the benchmarks behind the 0.2.0 default (#674, #707) found. With the split, both sockets' cores pay off. As agreed in #3201, it is on by default when the pool's CPUs span 2 NUMA nodes, and `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` turns it off.

Box: 2x Xeon Gold 6226, 64 GB (32 GB per NUMA node), RTX 3090 on PCIe 3.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored IQ4_XS at 262K context, kernel booted with `iommu=pt`. Server decode:

| Arm | Workers | Median tok/s | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2.0 default | 11, one socket | 54.05 | 50.7-54.8 |
| no split | 22 | 43.25 | 41.0-47.4 |
| split | 12 (6+6) | 51.45 | 50.0-52.9 |
| **split** | **22** | **59.3** | **57.1-61.9** |

+9.7 % over the default. Two earlier sessions, with the IOMMU translating DMA (the Debian default), gave +14 % and +11.5 %: the default gained from the faster bus, the split did not move (details below). A split without the placement (diagnostic build, earlier session) gave 51.0 against 53.1 for the default. Neither more cores, nor local memory at 12 workers, nor the per-node pool slices without the placement explains the gain: it takes both halves at 22 workers. Prompt speed and VRAM hit rate are unchanged. A machine with one NUMA node runs exactly as before: same worker count, no log line. A test checks it; no single-socket machine was at hand, so it ran on this box with the process bound to one node (`numactl --cpunodebind=0`), which the pool's topology detection follows.

## Related discussion

https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3201 (scope agreed: on by default with two NUMA nodes, `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` to turn it off). #2242 took a different route, binding the complement to the GPU's node, and was declined for lack of dual-socket measurements.

## Approach

- **Pool:** one task slice per NUMA node in the native gate/up and down phases, each with its own claim counter and barrier, so a worker claims and waits only within its own node's slice.
- **Placement:** the rows of every complement expert in a native layer are cut in two (gate/up on n_ff, down on n_embd, so no partial-sum reduce), and each half is first-touched on its node by threads pinned there, after the page cache of the model files, the pack's files and the MTP head is released. Releasing only the GGUF maps left the pack and MTP pages read at start in the cache, and a 32 GB node fell under 95 % of its slices. Placement is checked after registration with move_pages samples and reported per node.
- **Workers:** under the split the default covers both sockets' physical cores, minus the host core and the usual spare core, capped at 32 (22 here); an explicit `--pool-workers N` alternates sockets. The default spans both sockets only when the split will follow (Linux, exactly 2 nodes, pinned threads, no `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1`), since 22 workers without the split are the slowest arm above.
- **Refusals:** a node count other than 2, `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1`, unpinned threads and a lopsided worker layout turn the split off, with the reason in the log; the pool then runs as in 0.2.0.
- **Test mode:** `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=test` builds the same slices on any machine, without placement.
- **Docs:** docs/DETAILS.md, next to `--aux-cpus`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Rebased on 0.2.1, CUDA 13.2 build on the box: `pool_plan_test` OK; `file_expert_source_test` PASS; `pool_tasks_test` "360 bitwise comparisons passed, 192 of them in NUMA-split mode", and its default check: unset 22 workers split on, `1` 22 workers split on, `0` 11 workers.
- Single-node machine, simulated: `pool_tasks_test` under `numactl --cpunodebind=0` on the same box: unset 11 workers split off, `1` 11 split off, `0` 11; the unset runs log nothing, `1` logs "NUMA split off: the pool's CPUs span 1 NUMA node(s)". Not run on a real single-socket machine.
- Server start on 0.2.1 with this branch, same box and model: unset gives `NUMA split on: slice 0 = node 0 (12 threads), slice 1 = node 1 (11 threads)`, 22 workers, placement 100.0 / 99.6 %; `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` gives 11 workers on socket 0 and no split line. One start per arm, a functional check, not a speed comparison.
- Opt-in version on v0.2.0-beta, CUDA 13.2 build on the box (Linux, RTX 3090, sm_86) at ca1dafbd: `pool_plan_test` OK; `pool_tasks_test` "360 bitwise comparisons passed, 192 of them in NUMA-split mode", 20 runs out of 20; `file_expert_source_test` PASS.
- Host-only g++ build (CUDA, HIP and SYCL off) on a single-socket laptop: no warnings, `pool_plan_test` and `pool_tasks_test` pass.
- Server decode, protocol below (opt-in version on v0.2.0-beta, same pool and placement code): default 54.05 tok/s, split 59.3, 22 workers without split 43.25, split at 12 workers 51.45. Placement 95.8 to 100 % per node on every split start (95.2 to 100 % in the earlier sessions).

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**
- HIP, SYCL, Metal and MSVC builds: no toolchains here. The Linux-only calls (move_pages, sched_setaffinity, madvise, /sys reads) sit behind the guards the files already use; on other platforms the split stays off (`STRATA_NUMA_POOL=1` logs "NUMA split off: the split needs Linux").
- The split in pool modes 0 to 4: the test exists but needs AVX-512 VBMI, which the 6226 lacks, so it skips here.
- Other dual-socket hardware, more than 2 NUMA nodes, AMD NPS modes. A single-socket CPU exposing 2 nodes (SNC2, NPS2) would get the split by default, unmeasured.
- The split against the default with upstream's default tail skip (7) and pool spin (20 ms): every arm here ran with the tuning in the notes below.
- End-to-end output identity: greedy CLI outputs already differ between runs with the split off, because the CPU/GPU expert routing depends on timing. Correctness rests on the bitwise pool tests.

## Limits

- Linux, exactly 2 NUMA nodes.
- Only native expert layers are split; ArenaExpertSource and the cudaHostAlloc path are not (the engine logs it for the arena path).
- Each node needs room for its half plus 2 GiB. On this box node 0 is tight: the "NUMA placement at risk" warning fires on every start. Before the pack and MTP drop a node landed at 95.2 to 95.8 % on some starts, just above the 95 % FAILED line; with it, three starts placed 100 % on both nodes.
- On by default from one box's measurements. Tworks25 plans to report on a 2x E5-2690 v2 box (#3201).

<details><summary>Test protocol</summary>

Box: HP Z6 G4, 2x Xeon Gold 6226 (12 cores each, 2 NUMA nodes), 64 GB DDR4 (32 GB per NUMA node) on 4 of 6 channels per socket, RTX 3090 on PCIe 3.0 x16, CUDA 13.2, Debian 12 kernel 6.1 booted with `iommu=pt`. Engine at ca1dafbd on v0.2.0-beta, server config: `--pack orca-iq4_xs --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-IQ4_XS --expert-cache auto --resident-budget-gib 55 --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp mtp/rt --mtp-max-t 2 --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --vram-reserve-mib 844 --adapt-async 1`, expert profile frozen (md5 checked before every start, profile saving off). Every arm ran with the same config env: `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=200`, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`. Harness, configs and raw logs: https://gist.github.com/baptisterajaut/0cd495f3e548be4964406f1198119e28

Arms: measured before the switch became `STRATA_NUMA_POOL` and on by default. D = default (split off, 11 workers); S = split on (22 workers); X = split with `--pool-workers 12`; N = split off with `--pool-workers 22`. Server starts in the order D1 S1 D2 S2 X1 N1 S3 X2 N2 S4, no drop_caches between them (production-like). Per start: a 60K-token passkey prompt twice (prompt speed, passkey checked), then 3 decode samples of a fixed prompt (Python LRU cache with type hints plus 5 design bullets, max_tokens 3000, reasoning_effort low, sampled), decode speed read from the server's `timings.predicted_per_second`, VRAM hit rate from the server's done line. A split start below 95 % placement on a node would have been discarded; none was.

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Start 3 | Start 4 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 54.0 54.1 54.7 | 50.7 54.8 53.8 | | | 54.05 (50.7-54.8) |
| N: no split | 22 | 43.5 42.5 47.4 | 43.0 41.0 45.2 | | | 43.25 (41.0-47.4) |
| X: split | 12 (6+6) | 50.8 50.0 50.8 | 52.1 52.9 52.7 | | | 51.45 (50.0-52.9) |
| S: split | 22 | 57.1 58.2 59.7 | 58.2 60.1 59.9 | 61.2 58.2 61.9 | 58.4 60.6 58.9 | 59.3 (57.1-61.9) |

Prompt speed 1282 to 1341 tok/s across all arms, passkey found in all 20 prompt runs, VRAM hit rate 72 to 79 %. N streams 4.0 to 4.7 % of the routed experts over PCIe against 1.2 to 2.4 % in the other arms.

Earlier sessions, same protocol and binary, IOMMU in translated mode (`DMA-FQ`, pinned H2D 7.7 to 9.2 GB/s against 12.3 with `iommu=pt`). First, order D1 S1 X1 D2 S2 X2 N1 S3 N2 S4:

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Start 3 | Start 4 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 51.0 53.3 53.3 | 51.0 53.1 52.1 | | | 52.6 (51.0-53.3) |
| N: no split | 22 | 40.5 50.4 50.1 | 45.3 50.7 53.2 | | | 50.25 (40.5-53.2) |
| X: split | 12 (6+6) | 50.4 52.3 51.9 | 49.9 51.1 54.4 | | | 51.5 (49.9-54.4) |
| S: split | 22 | 57.8 61.0 60.1 | 58.3 58.0 60.0 | 60.0 58.6 58.1 | 60.0 60.7 61.6 | 60.0 (57.8-61.6) |

Second, order A1 S5 D3 A2 S6, A = split with the placement skipped by a throwaway switch on a diagnostic build (not in this PR):

| Arm | Workers | Start 1 | Start 2 | Median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: default | 11, one socket | 52.7 54.3 53.1 | | 53.1 (52.7-54.3) |
| A: split, no placement | 22 | 50.5 48.7 51.3 | 50.7 56.6 56.8 | 51.0 (48.7-56.8) |
| S: split | 22 | 60.5 58.4 59.2 | 58.8 59.2 60.2 | 59.2 (58.4-60.5) |

Prompt speed 926 to 1037 tok/s across all arms of both sessions, passkey found in all 20 prompt runs of the first. VRAM hit rate 71 to 77 %.

</details>

## Misc. notes: tuning on this box

Every arm ran with the same tuning, set before this work for reasons unrelated to the split:
- `--adapt-async 1`: the adaptive tier's VRAM/RAM expert swaps happen between windows instead of inside them. On 0.1.45, 34.5 to about 54 tok/s on the LRU prompt (single runs), the swaps' cost per window from 24.5 to 2.7 ms.
- `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=200`, for heat: an idle worker sleeps after 200 µs instead of `kSpinBeforeSleep` 20 ms (pool.hpp:264). With ~30 ms windows and work at each of the 48 layers, the default kept every pool core spinning. No visible cost on CPU expert time (16.7 to 18.3 ms per window against 17.8).
- `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, to judge the quant without the lossy default skip (docs/QUANTS.md:158-162). It costs speed in every arm.
- `--resident-budget-gib 55` instead of the 40 setup.py gives on 64 GB (it leaves 24 GB beside the budget, setup.py:548): the box is headless and idles at about 4 GB, so the ~44 GiB complement fits in RAM and nothing is read from the NVMe.
- `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1` only adds timing log lines.
- `iommu=pt` on the kernel command line, for the main table only: Debian's kernel translated every DMA (`DMA-FQ`), which held pinned H2D at 7.7 to 9.2 GB/s on PCIe 3.0 x16; passthrough gives 12.3 GB/s and about +30 % prompt speed. It is a gen3/gen4 matter: on xrip's PCIe 2.0 x16 box (#3201) the copy speed is the same in both modes, and `iommu=pt` broke the GSP boot of a card on a patched driver there.
- A degraded inter-socket link makes the one-socket default much worse, and the split barely notices. On this box the UPI link between the two Xeons falls back to half width after some hours of uptime (machine-check log: "COR Phy lane failure, recovery in x8 width" on both ends). The main table predates it: no such error in that boot until 11 hours after the last start. After a fallback this morning, with 0.2.1 and this branch, one start per arm: the default (11 workers, one socket) gave 38.8 to 45.0 tok/s, against 56.6 and 57.4 with the split;

pulls.title: perf(cuda): enable Volta defaults with dual V100 benchmark evidence
pulls.author: koshikawa-masato

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

pulls.body:
## Change

V100 (sm70) currently receives no table from `nv_default_env`, even though manually enabling a subset of the newer CUDA optimizations improved decode on my dual V100 PCIe 32 GB system. Add that six-switch table for sm70, retain explicit user overrides, and provide `STRATA_SM70_PERF=0` to opt out. Existing homogeneous-device gating remains unchanged.

The table enables SIDE_MIXER=2, GR_UP75=1, B6_MMVQ_ROWS=1, GU_SWIGLU=1, QSA_ROWS=1 and ATTN_DAILY=1 (all `STRATA_`-prefixed). It does not change sampling, VRAM reserves or CPU-expert settings.

## Measurements

Ryzen 9 9950X / 128 GB RAM / 2 × V100 PCIe 32 GB at 150 W each, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, MTP4, 32K context, INT8 KV. Official v0.2.0-beta engine; same binary/config/model in all arms. Three repeats per workload, baseline → stack → baseline, then stack after long-context stress.

| Arm | Japanese decode | Code decode |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline before | 74.23 tok/s | 108.40 tok/s |
| Six-switch stack | 78.63 tok/s | 116.77 tok/s |
| Baseline after | 74.40 tok/s | 108.70 tok/s |
| Stack after stress | 78.70 tok/s | 116.87 tok/s |

Approximately **+5.8% Japanese / +7.6% code** versus pooled baseline. All nine output texts matched in every arm (hashes included). Two concurrent 32,000-token inputs + 512 generated tokens, repeated twice, passed both sentinel checks without GPU errors. Long-context pair latency remained ~44.3 seconds; no improvement claimed there.

Included report, per-request measurements/output hashes and exact short-prompt measurement script under `bench/results/2026-10-20-v100-sm70-defaults/`.

## Validation and limits

- New CPU-only `nv_defaults_test` passes on macOS and Linux with C++17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: architecture dispatch, opt-out, explicit user overrides, idempotency, and existing sm60/sm86 dispatch. Registered with CTest.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Source patch is against current main; GPU measurements were on the stated release, not a full GPU rebuild of this main commit.
- Combined-stack experiment only, no per-switch ablation. Decoded-text equality is not a token-ID/logit/exact_pp identity gate.
- Single V100, 16 GB cards, SXM2 and other models remain unmeasured. Additional hardware validation before broad rollout would be welcome.
- Both arms used later-GPU reserve 650 MiB to retain all 12,288 expert pairs / zero-doorbell graph. Minimum GPU1 free memory was 267 MiB. This is deliberately not proposed as a global memory default.

These are community diagnostic measurements, not the standard benchmark protocol. No private prompts or credentials are included.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] community report: RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GiB (Windows 11, 32 G…
pulls.author: hqlhqlhqlhql
pulls.body:
## What this adds

`bench/results/2026-10-20-community-rtx-4060-laptop-gpu-qwen3-8-flash-next-q2-0/`: the `README.md` the suite wrote, `results.json` with every request and the machine facts, and the engine start-up log. Nothing else in the tree is touched.

## Why it may be useful

- **This is the smallest VRAM tier in `bench/results`.** The smallest existing entry is a 12 GiB RTX 3060 (`2026-10-09-community-rtx-3060-0141`); 8 GiB is the tier where the expert cache holds about 6% of the (layer, expert) pairs - the GPU holds the dense weights, the draft head and the streamed KV window too, leaving 1,487 cache slots.
- **The host has 32 GB of RAM**, the tier `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` asks for ("a host with 32 GB of RAM or less", because the expert file tier and the resident mode depend on how much of the model fits in RAM). This one has 31.7 GiB visible.
- The CPU has **no AVX-512**, so the expert kernels run on AVX-2 - the same constraint the closest existing entry had.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GiB (sm_89), PCIe Gen4 x8, 12.8 GB/s measured host->device; 80 W limit
- CPU: i7-14700HX (8 P-cores + 12 E-cores, 28 threads), no AVX-512
- RAM: 32 GB (31.7 GiB visible); Windows 11 10.0.26200; driver 580.97; CUDA 13.0
- Strata: engine 0.1.45.3 (0.2.0-beta), source build from upstream main `3fa1b524` plus three local patches: three SSE keep-alive events in `serve/server.py`, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=Shared` in `setup.py`, and the MSVC `tq_avx2.cpp` unroll fix (Gyro only; Q2_0 does not use it)

## Suite medians

`tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-q2_0.json --runs 3 --long`, thinking off, the install's own configuration (Q2_0 pack, `--kv q4_0 --kv-resident 20480`, `--resident-experts`, `--pool-workers 19`, 131,072 context):

| Test | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| short chat (3 questions, 100 tokens) | - | **37.4 (29.9-49.7)** | 0.97 (0.64-1.08) |
| 4K fresh prompt | **266.5 (244.0-267.7)** | - | 15.17 (15.09-16.54) |
| 16K fresh prompt | **282.2 (279.0-283.4)** | - | 56.99 (56.78-57.64) |
| 32K fresh prompt | **289.4 (288.6-296.9)** | - | 110.93 (108.05-111.19) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 228.7 (last turn) | **27.5 (9.8-39.2)** | 12.40 (10.31-14.47) |

The agent session hit the conversation cache 69.2% of the time; the last turn carries 14,536 prompt tokens.

## The one axis the suite does not cover: free RAM at start

The expert cache is sized from the RAM available when the engine starts, and on a 32 GB host that number moves with what else is loaded. Across starts on this box the complement ranged 13.15-18.62 GiB of the 29.73 GiB of experts the VRAM cache does not hold (44%-62.7%), and Q2_0's decode stayed in the same 24-28 band - so for this quant the coverage in that range was not the limit; closing other programs before the start still buys the largest complement, and this run had it (62.7%).

## Closest sibling

`2026-10-06-community-rx-6800m`: 12 GiB RX 6800M, 31.4 GB RAM, no AVX-512, Q2_0, `--resident-experts` with `--kv-resident`, a self-built HIP engine. It measured **9-27 tok/s decode and 50-114 tok/s prompt** (its own README names the same two causes: the experts do not fit in RAM and are streamed, and the CPU has no AVX-512). Here: **24-28 decode on longer generations (37.4 on the short chats) and 266-289 prompt**. The differences - CUDA on sm_89 against HIP on gfx1031, 12.8 against 7.0 GB/s PCIe, i7-14700HX against 5900HX, KV 20,480 of 131,072 cells in VRAM against 32,768 of 65,536 - are consistent with the gap.

## Not tested

- correctness or quality (the suite is a speed check, not a quality test)
- vision (enabled, not exercised)
- concurrency (`--clients`), a long soak, and a second GPU
- power limits and background load (not recorded by the suite)

## How to rerun

```text
python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-q2_0.json --runs 3 --long
```

The folder holds `README.md`, `results.json` and `engine-log-excerpt.txt`. `--config` is required here because the suite's default picks the newest `strata-*.json` of the folder, and this install also has configs for other quants.

pulls.title: [TUI] Fix the owner-only check for the built-in Administrator (SDDL alias LA)
pulls.author: jackbapa
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On Windows the built-in Administrator (RID 500) cannot start the engine or finish an engine update. `runtime_dir()` raises `ProfileError: runtime directory must be owner-only (mode 0700)` even though the directory ACL is exactly what `restrict_to_current_user()` wrote. The same check gates the activity lease and the engine test start, so the application stops there.

`restrict_to_current_user()` writes `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;<current SID>)`. When Windows renders that DACL back, it replaces the SID of RID 500 with the SDDL alias `LA`, so `is_private()` compares `"LA"` with `S-1-5-21-...-500` and returns False. `is_unshared()` has the same problem.

After the change the alias is resolved to its string SID before the comparison, `runtime_dir()` returns the directory, and an ACL that names another account is still rejected.

## Related discussion

https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3302 - reported the same failure and suggested resolving the SDDL alias (or comparing with `EqualSid`). This PR follows that approach.

## Approach

A new `_as_sid()` helper runs `ConvertStringSidToSidW` + `ConvertSidToStringSidW` and returns the string SID, or the input unchanged when it is not a resolvable alias. `is_private()` and `is_unshared()` normalise the trustee field through it.

Alternatives considered: adding `LA` to `_PRIVILEGED` would accept the built-in Administrator on every machine, including ones where the current user is someone else - that relaxes `is_unshared()` instead of fixing the comparison, so it is not done here.

No change to how the ACL is written; the same DACL is now recognised. POSIX behaviour is untouched (`_as_sid` returns its input when `WINDOWS` is false).

Two existing tests compared the raw SDDL text with `current_user_sid()`; they now compare through the same normalisation, otherwise they fail on every RID 500 host. Two Windows-only tests cover the alias and check that it does not authorise a different account.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest tests.terminal.test_private_files -v` on a Windows x86_64 host signed in as the built-in Administrator (renamed locally, SID `S-1-5-21-...-500`), Python 3.13.9, revision d67b749: 16 tests, `OK (skipped=1)` (the POSIX test). Without the source change the same suite failed on that host, including five assertion failures that compared the raw SDDL text.
- Manual, with a fresh `STRATA_RUNTIME_DIR`: `runtime.runtime_dir()` returns the directory, `dacl_sddl()` is `D:PAI(A;OICI;FA;;;LA)`, `is_private()` and `is_unshared()` are True, `current_user_sid()` is the RID 500 SID.

**Failed:**

none observed.

**Not run:**

- POSIX (Linux/macOS): no machine available; `_as_sid` is a no-op there and the POSIX branches are unchanged.
- Other Windows accounts: covered by the mocked test (`LA` entry, different current SID -> False) rather than a second real account.

## Limits

Only trustee fields are normalised. An account whose SDDL alias cannot be resolved by `ConvertStringSidToSidW` keeps the previous literal comparison.

pulls.title: [Other] macOS setup: install cmake and ninja before a compile
pulls.author: Flo5k5
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Fixes #3403. Since a242537 moved `cmake` and `ninja` to `requirements-build.txt`, `./setup.sh` on a Mac no longer installs them: `metal/setup_mac.py` still installs only `requirements.txt` and expects the build tools to come with it. On a fresh `.venv` without `ninja` on `PATH`, the Metal engine build stops at CMake's `'ninja' '--version'`.

With this change, the engine and image encoder builds install the missing pinned helpers from `requirements-build.txt` into `.venv` first, and then build.

## Related discussion

#3403 (focused fix, no change of defaults)

## Approach

`build_tools()` in `metal/setup_mac.py` does what `setup.py`'s `cmake_build()` already does on a PC: it looks for each helper on `PATH` or next to the venv's Python (`find_tool`), installs only the missing pins with `pip_install`, and fails with the same workaround message if they are still not there. It runs right before a compile (`build_engine`, `build_vision`), and not when the engine is current, so the runtime install stays free of the build helpers, as a242537 intended. A `cmake` or `ninja` already on `PATH` (Homebrew, for example) is used as before. The step 3 message, the module docstring and `docs/MAC.md` no longer say that step 3 installs cmake and ninja.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_mac` on 3c316c7 (macOS 27.0.1, Python 3.15.0): 28 tests OK. The 4 new `BuildTools` tests check that a fresh venv gets both pins, that only the missing helper is installed, that `requirements.txt` carries neither, and that both builds call `build_tools()` before anything else. On 9ae93f7's `setup_mac.py`, 3 of them fail (no `build_tools`).
- Apple M5 Pro, 64 GB, macOS 27.0.1, fresh checkouts with no `.venv`, `./setup.sh --update --yes` (`llama.cpp` and `metal-cpp` copied into `third_party/` from an existing checkout at the same pins, `STRATA_SETTINGS_FILE` and `--data-dir` pointed at a scratch folder):
  - 9ae93f7, `ninja` not on `PATH`, Homebrew `cmake` on `PATH`: fails, `build-metal/build.log` as in #3403 (`'ninja' '--version'` ... `no such file or directory`).
  - 0aa3c59 (this change before line wrapping), same `PATH`: step 4 installs `ninja==1.13.2` only and builds `build-metal/strata`.
  - 3c316c7 (this PR), `PATH` reduced to `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` plus a `python3` link, so neither `cmake` nor `ninja`: step 4 installs `cmake==4.4.3 ninja==1.13.2` and builds `build-metal/strata`. A second run reports `Metal engine: ... (built for this source)` and installs nothing.

**Failed:**

None observed.

**Not run:**

- `build_vision()` on hardware: `--update` returns before the image encoder step. Only the unit test covers its call to `build_tools()`.
- The full setup (model download, pack, start): unchanged by this PR and not needed for the failure.
- CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds: not touched (only `metal/setup_mac.py`, `tools/test_setup_mac.py` and `docs/MAC.md` change).

## Limits

An older `.venv` that already has cmake and ninja behaves as before. The desktop app's Control mode does not run `setup_mac.py` (its test asserts it), so it is not affected.

pulls.title: [Engine] conversation cache: drop an older copy of the conversation rewritten turns back (#342 follow-up)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`ConversationCache::drop_superseded` (#342) drops a parked copy of the outgoing conversation only when the outgoing checkpoint chain holds that copy's deepest checkpoint. That covers a client that re-renders the last reply. It misses a client that rewrites its last turns a few turns back (agents trim tool output and thinking): the copy's deepest checkpoint is past the rewrite, and once the conversation has grown, the chain's spread checkpoints (8 here) no longer hold anything near the copy's end. The stale copy then stays parked: it takes the byte budget (5.7 GB of an 8 GiB budget for a 300K-token copy here) and is evicted later in place of another conversation, or, with a disk tier, written out.

- **Before:** on my box one 120K-326K-token agent conversation left two such copies (120,236 tokens, rewritten after token 116,787; 248,844, rewritten after 246,337). At the next switch both were evicted, and with the disk tier of #1937 the park waited 41.4 s for their writes.
- **After:** a parked copy that is shorter than the outgoing conversation and has at most a tenth of its tokens not shared with it is dropped as superseded, like the copies #342 drops.

## Related discussion

Follow-up to #342 (closed), whose rule this keeps. Found while running the disk tier of #1937; this change does not depend on it.

## Approach

- `superseded_at()` (new, private) holds the rule for `drop_superseded()` and `parked_prefix_tokens()`, which had the deepest-checkpoint test twice: first #342's rule unchanged, then the new one (`std::mismatch` for the shared tokens).
- Kept, as before: an entry without checkpoints, another conversation that shares only the system prompt with the outgoing one, and an equal or longer entry (a branch the client may go back to).
- No new option. Without the conversation cache nothing changes.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `conversation_cache_test` (CPU build, `-DSTRATA_BUILD_CONVERSATION_TESTS=ON`, GCC 14 in `nvidia/cuda:13.3.0-devel-ubuntu24.04`): 4,774 checks, among them the new case (a copy rewritten 4 of 40 tokens from its end is dropped, 5 of 41 is kept, with the outgoing chain thinned to the root) and every existing #342, borrowing and park-gain check. `conversation_file_test`: 201 checks.
- The rule against the stale copies in my box's log: 3,449 of 120,236, 2,507 of 248,844, 3,049 of 322,930 and 330 of 76,492 tokens not shared, all dropped by it; sub-agents sharing only the ~16K-token system prompt are kept.
- Live in my fork (on 0.2.1, 2x CMP 50HX, Ubuntu 24.04.4, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, conversation cache 8 GiB / 16 slots) since 2026-10-20 12:35: a conversation rewritten at 177,146 tokens dropped its previous copy, and that park took 4.1 s with nothing evicted. The log line does not say which of the two rules dropped it.

**Failed:** none.

**Not run:**
- A live A/B of the two rules over a full day; I will add the counts here.
- HIP, SYCL, Metal and Windows builds (a header-only change with no platform code).

## Limits

- The tenth is a judgment: a client that goes back to a dropped copy reads again from the nearest checkpoint still held, against the budget the copy holds while nobody comes back to it.
- One box and one agent client (Claude Code) measured.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: [Other] preserve Windows child identity after adopting user defaults
pulls.author: midhatn
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On Windows, `serve.server.main()` calls `adopt_user_defaults()` before starting children. Its token-default DACL grants `FA` (`FILE_ALL_ACCESS`), but that default also applies to new process objects. The file access mask omits `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION`, so a live child can become unreadable to `procs.start_token()` and its ownership record cannot be written.

This surfaced as two lifecycle failures after an earlier test entered `main()`. The same lifecycle tests passed alone. A new isolated regression reproduces the actual cause: adopt the defaults, start a real sleeping child, and try to identify and record it.

Use `GA` in the **token default** so Windows maps the access mask for each newly created object type. The existing principals—current user, SYSTEM and Administrators—are unchanged. File-specific ACL code still uses file rights.

## Related discussion

Discovered while checking the current release for #1493, but this fix is independent of adaptive inference and changes no model behavior. I searched open and closed items for `default DACL`, `adopt_user_defaults`, and child/access-denied reports before opening this.

## Approach

One access-mask correction plus a Windows-only regression in a disposable interpreter. The test does not change the test runner's token defaults and always stops its own child.

References used for the correction:
- [Microsoft: process security and access rights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-security-and-access-rights): default process ACLs come from the creator's token; limited process queries require `0x1000`.
- [Microsoft: ACE strings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/ace-strings): `FA` is file-all access; `GA` is generic-all access.

## Validation

Windows 11, Python 3.11. Base `c093ac263f8175307e67b7fd7eeeaa2e73ceaded`; fixed revision `841476cdcc566dcdcf750121ef235749efc06375`.

**Passed:**
- New regression on the fixed revision: live child identified and recorded.
- Combined new regression, `tests/terminal/test_private_files.py`, `tests/terminal/test_procs.py`, and `serve.test_lifeline`: 27 tests run, 24 passed, 3 platform skips, in 7.226 seconds.
- `git diff --check`.

The new regression can be run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests/terminal -p test_default_object_access.py -v`. The combined run used `unittest` discovery for the three terminal files plus `serve.test_lifeline`, with TEMP/TMP in a private directory declared under STRATA_STATE_DIR.

**Failed:**
- Expected before-fix regression on the unchanged base: `live child became unreadable after adopting user defaults`.
- An initial private-file test run under a shared, non-profile temporary directory had one failed assertion and two errors because that fixture did not meet those tests' private-inheritance/repair-root assumptions. Repeating under a private declared state root passed; no repair boundaries were relaxed.

**Not run:**
- Full repository suite on this public branch, model inference, Linux/macOS, CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds. No native engine files changed.

## Limits

This restores access for the same existing token-default principals; it does not grant access to other users or bypass ownership verification. It does not establish a model performance gain or general adaptive-runtime qualification.

pulls.title: [Engine] propose DSpark speculative decoding plan
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Open issue [#3304](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3304) asks whether Strata can use speculative decoding with a separate drafter. Strata currently offers MTP and DFlash/DFlash2 but has no DSpark artifact or runtime path. This PR proposes an initial implementation plan so maintainers can agree on a checkpoint, target model, and backend before feature work starts. The PR itself changes no runtime behavior; if the plan is accepted, the proposed result is an opt-in DSpark drafter that leaves the current MTP default and target-only path unchanged.

## Related discussion

- [Issue #3304](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3304) asks about speculative decoding in Strata.
- Existing DFlash and DFlash2 support provides a runtime and artifact reference. DSpark adds a semi-autoregressive Markov head and a confidence head; confidence-scheduled verification is an additional system-level step.

## Approach

1. **Agree on the first supported artifact and scope.** Select a published DSpark checkpoint compatible with a Strata target, pin its revision and hashes, document its tensor/feature contract, and agree on the initial target model and backend before implementation.
2. **Add artifact conversion and validation.** Extend the existing DFlash artifact path to recognize DSpark-only tensors and metadata, reject unsupported geometry or mismatched target/tokenizer combinations, and add converter/loader fixtures.
3. **Implement the drafter.** Reuse the parallel DFlash backbone where contracts match, then add DSpark's Markov head for intra-block dependencies and confidence head for per-position acceptance estimates. Compare intermediate outputs against the reference implementation.
4. **Integrate proposal verification behind an opt-in setting.** Preserve the existing MTP default and target-only behavior. Start with fixed-length proposals and the current verifier; verify accepted-prefix commits, rejection replacement, context limits, rewind, and prompt/conversation snapshot behavior.
5. **Add confidence scheduling as a separate milestone.** First evaluate a static confidence cutoff. Then consider a load-aware prefix scheduler only after its decisions can be shown causal and its benefit can be measured under concurrent serving.
6. **Validate and measure.** Add deterministic parity, malformed-artifact, cache/rollback, and output-equivalence checks. Compare target-only, MTP, DFlash/DFlash2, and DSpark on the same prompts, build, hardware, and settings. Report acceptance by draft position, accepted tokens per verifier pass, latency, throughput, memory use, and all unrun backends separately.

## Validation

**Passed:** On Linux, git fetch origin main updated origin/main to c093ac26; git switch --create codex/dspark-plan origin/main created this branch from that revision; git commit --allow-empty -m '[Engine] propose DSpark speculative decoding plan' created 6edb36b; and git push --set-upstream fork codex/dspark-plan pushed it. For PR #3397, the title-area and intake checks passed and GitHub reports no base-branch conflicts. Repository issue/PR searches found the related open issue #3304 and no DSpark PR.

**Failed:** None observed.

**Not run:** No code or tests changed, so no engine build, unit test, parity check, GPU run, or performance measurement was run. Compatibility with any Strata target or backend remains unverified.

## Limits

This is a plan-only draft with one empty commit and no changed files. Maintainer agreement is requested on the first checkpoint/target pair and backend scope before implementation. No default change or performance claim is proposed.

pulls.title: [Engine] Add opt-in Galahad session storage
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Strata's existing slot API can persist its current conversation to a local file. Users who need encrypted, durable named sessions on supported NVIDIA systems have no integrated storage backend. With this opt-in change, the same API saves and restores complete Strata session images through Galahad; the existing file backend and default inference path stay unchanged.

## Related discussion

Previous closed submission: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1761. The maintainer asked for a rebase on current main, a title prefix and the current PR template. After updating the old submission, the `/reopen` check passed but GitHub refused to reopen it and instructed us to open a new pull request. This PR contains that rebased update.

## Approach

Add a separate Galahad adapter for full session images, configuration and CLI options, size/error handling, and user documentation. Galahad remains an optional import and requires a separately installed licensed package. Session operations remain explicit, limited to slot 0, and unavailable with parallel requests or the ordinary file backend. The rebase preserves the current session-save retry behavior. Galahad shutdown is guarded against duplicate close calls from normal shutdown and `atexit`.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `.venv/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_galahad serve.test_slots serve.test_security` — 67 tests passed on Linux x86-64, Python 3.13, at revision `7e3494582faecba5934c1d43b692b98ecfe080e1`, based on main `5bda973a`.
- `.venv/bin/python serve/server.py --help` — Galahad options are present.
- `git diff origin/main --check` — no whitespace errors.

**Failed:**

- None observed.

**Not run:**

- Licensed native Galahad save/restart/restore, GPU output parity, and performance checks: this environment has no licensed NVIDIA setup.
- CUDA, HIP, and SYCL builds: no engine or backend kernel files changed.

## Limits

Requires Linux x86-64, a licensed NVIDIA GPU, and `galahad-kv==1.31.5`. Names are immutable, only slot 0 is supported, and the feature does not add automatic prefix caching. Mock tests establish the adapter and HTTP contract, not native persistence, encryption, GPU correctness, or performance.

pulls.title: [Other] preserve Chat Completions tool result order
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When an OpenAI Chat Completions request contains multiple tool calls and the client returns their tool results in a different order, the serving layer drops the call IDs before rendering the prompt. The model then sees anonymous results in arrival order, even when the results belong to calls with the same function name. The fix restores the call order for complete, unambiguous result runs before removing the temporary IDs.

## Related discussion

This follows the closed tracker-reset submission [#2952](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2952). The new branch is based on current main; the v0.2.0-beta tag is an ancestor of the base revision.

## Approach

The Chat Completions conversion retains call IDs only while normalizing a request. It reorders a result run only when call and result IDs are nonempty unique strings with matching sets and counts. Missing, duplicate, unknown, or incomplete IDs keep their received order. IDs are removed before prompt rendering. No engine, template, Anthropic, Responses, or default behavior changes.

## Validation

Environment: Linux, Python 3.12.14, dependencies from the repository's pinned requirements.txt.

**Passed:**

- Reproduction on unmodified main at 5bda973a4331212494d74cf35927ada7f0e063e7: /tmp/strata-pr2952-venv/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_chat_tool_results -q ran 7 tests and reproduced 4 failures, including reversed same-function results and the HTTP-to-engine prompt order.
- Fixed revision 7b87be62201245a8747f248cd58b006c7ed9b92d: /tmp/strata-pr2952-venv/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_chat_tool_results serve.test_frontend serve.test_server serve.test_responses -q ran 415 tests; **OK (skipped=1)** in 128.991 seconds.
- git diff --cached --check passed before commit.

**Failed:**

- None on the fixed revision.

**Not run:**

- GPU/model inference and CUDA, HIP, SYCL, or Metal builds. This change touches only Python serving code and its tests.

## Limits

Only complete, unambiguous tool-result runs are reordered. Incomplete or ambiguous histories preserve their incoming order.

pulls.title: [Engine] make strata-gguf --check reject invalid files
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On current `main` (`5bda973a`), `strata-gguf FILE --check` prints an architecture failure but returns status 0. Its geometry check can also accept an out-of-file tensor offset when unsigned subtraction wraps, and a tensor whose byte count overflows. After this change, these checks return status 1. Inspection without `--check` remains unchanged.

## Related discussion

Rechecked after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset: [#3043](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3043) and [#3044](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3044). The maintainer noted that closure during the reset does not mean rejection.

## Approach

Use the existing overflow-safe `tensor_payload_bytes()` helper, validate the payload offset before subtracting, and return failure when the architecture guard reports an error. Add a CPU-only CTest that invokes the actual CLI entry point on synthetic GGUFs covering valid and invalid inputs.

## Validation

Environment: Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0. Tested on current `main` `5bda973a4331212494d74cf35927ada7f0e063e7` plus candidate `a2aee5fb`.

**Passed:**
- `cmake -S . -B build-pr3044 -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_WERROR=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=OFF -DSTRATA_ENABLE_SYCL=OFF`: configured successfully.
- `cmake --build build-pr3044 --target strata-gguf gguf_cli_test gguf_reader_test gguf_split_test gguf_geometry_test model_family_test -j2`: all targets built.
- `ctest --test-dir build-pr3044 --output-on-failure -R '^(gguf_cli_test|gguf_reader_test|gguf_split_test|gguf_geometry_test|model_family_test)$'`: 5/5 passed.
- `git diff --cached --check`: clean.

**Failed on unchanged base (expected regression evidence):**
- Compiled and ran the new CLI regression test against `5bda973a`. It exited 1 because unsupported and missing architecture, a wrapped out-of-file offset, and an overflowing tensor byte count returned 0 instead of 1. The valid file, inspection-only mode, ordinary out-of-file offset and truncation cases behaved as expected.

**Not run:**
- Full repository suite, model inference, Windows/macOS runtime, and CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds. The change is confined to the standalone host CLI and its CPU-only test.

## Limits

The check still reports unknown tensor types separately; this change only makes known invalid payload bounds and architecture failures affect the exit status.

pulls.title: [Other] setup: reject invalid explicit RoPE scale factors
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On current `main`, setup accepts an explicit `--rope-scale` of `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`, zero, or a value below 1. For example, `resolve_rope(1048576, "yarn", float("nan"))` returns `("yarn", nan)`; setup can then pass the invalid value into the generated engine arguments. The engine requires a finite factor >= 1.

After this change, setup rejects every explicit non-finite factor and every factor below 1 before it writes configuration, and the error names `--rope-scale` and the valid range. Valid factors remain unchanged.

## Related discussion

This is the rebased follow-up to #2950, which was closed during the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset rather than declined. Its fix was not present on current `main`.

## Approach

Validate the explicit factor at the start of `resolve_rope()` with `math.isfinite()` and the engine's >= 1 lower bound. Update `--help` to state the accepted range. Add regression coverage across contexts below, at and above 262144, with omitted, `none`, `linear` and `yarn` scaling methods.

Automatic scaling, valid explicit overrides, model inference and backend code are unchanged. This does not change YaRN quality or require the factor to cover the requested context.

## Validation

Revision: `b7c8ede5`, based on `main` `5bda973a`. Linux, Python 3; no GPU or model downloads.

**Passed:**
- Reproduced on unmodified `5bda973a`: the resolver accepted NaN, both infinities, -1, 0 and 0.5 for contexts 131072, 262144 and 1048576 with linear and yarn.

pulls.title: [Engine] add opt-in advisory VRAM plan
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Before the expert cache takes the remaining VRAM, users have no diagnostic estimate of the prompt buffers or cache size the current sizing rules will choose. This adds a warnings-only advisory plan, enabled with `STRATA_ADVISORY_PLAN=1`. The unset default retains the existing startup output and runtime path. The existing sizing, loan scan, and error paths remain authoritative; the planner does not allocate, resize, or refuse startup.

## Related discussion
Continuation of the closed [#1133](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1133), closed during the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset rather than declined. It implements part C of [#796](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/796), with scope previously agreed in that discussion: no startup refusal, runtime contract, or second allocator. Related foundational discussion: [#765](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/765).

## Approach
The planner estimates owned-prefill buffers and the auto-loan/cache plan from the same pricing and sizing inputs. It then re-derives the estimate after cache open and reports runtime differences as warnings. It is opt-in to preserve the default path.

## Validation
Tested submitted tree `39f98ea1` based on current `main` `90767252`, on Linux, CUDA 13.4.92, CUDA arch 89, NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (16 GiB), IQ3_XXS.

**Passed:**
- `cmake -S . -B build-advisory -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89` — configured successfully.
- `cmake --build build-advisory --target strata vram_plan_test -j 12` — engine and planner test built successfully.
- `ctest --test-dir build-advisory -R '^vram_plan_test$' --output-on-failure` — 1/1 passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Runtime, same model/config and a 12,288-ID prompt file, once with `STRATA_ADVISORY_PLAN` unset and once with `STRATA_ADVISORY_PLAN=1`: both exited 0, processed 12,287 prompt tokens in two chunks, chose an 8,192-token chunk and 2,489 loan slots, opened a 5,537-slot (8.98 GiB) cache, and generated token 198. The enabled run predicted those chunk, loan, and cache values exactly and emitted no mismatch warning. The unset run emitted no advisory diagnostics. One run per mode is not a performance comparison.

Runtime command (with `DATA` pointing to the local model data directory and `/tmp/strata-pr1133-prompt.txt` containing `198 ` repeated 12,288 times):
```sh
./build-advisory/strata --pack "${DATA}/packs/iq3_xxs" \
  --native "${DATA}/models/IQ3_XXS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf" \
  --ple-gguf "${DATA}/models/IQ3_XXS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf" \
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto \
  --spec 4 --mtp "${DATA}/mtp/rt" --max-context 32768 --max-new 1 --kv int8 \
  --tokens-file /tmp/strata-pr1133-prompt.txt
```

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** HIP and SYCL builds (their compilers are unavailable in this environment); multi-GPU and Windows/WDDM runtime checks; full CTest suite.

## Limits
Hardware execution covers one single-GPU CUDA configuration. The advisory is diagnostic and does not guarantee that a configuration will avoid allocation failure. No performance claim is made.

pulls.title: [Engine] preserve prompt loan residency without token graph
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On current main (0.2.1, 90767252), a profile-filled IQ3_XXS native pack with --prefill auto and --no-token-graph could not borrow the expert cache. The residency table was only built for the token-graph hit path, so the prompt path tried to allocate its own 8192-token buffers and failed with 23 MiB free while requesting an 80 MiB buffer.

The fix builds the residency table whenever prefill borrowing is available, independently of token-graph capture. On the same RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, the updated build borrowed 2489 cache slots, refilled them after the prompt, processed 12,287 tokens, and generated one token. A token-graph control also completed and produced the same token.

## Related discussion

- Original report and maintainer scope agreement: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1131.
- Parent context: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/796.

## Approach

The residency decision covers borrowing availability and a positive prefill chunk. The table is staged for either reader: the token-graph hit path or the prompt loan. Graph hit wiring remains gated by graph capture. A borrowing-only staging failure warns and disables borrowing for that run; graph staging failures retain their existing fatal behavior. Loan/refill trace lines report the slot range and any slots still lent.

## Validation

Tested revision: 70660fa3 on 90767252. Environment: Linux, NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GB, CUDA 13.4.92, CUDA arch 89, Ryzen 9 5900X, 125 GiB RAM. Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS native pack, int8 KV, 32K context, MTP spec 4. The prompt file contained 12,288 copies of token ID 198.

**Passed:**

- cmake --build build-repro --target strata -j 12 — CUDA Release build passed.
- cmake --build build-repro --target borrow_residency_test -j 12 and ctest --test-dir build-repro -R '^borrow_residency_test$' --output-on-failure — passed.
- Baseline --prefill auto --no-token-graph reproduction on 90767252: exited 1 at prefill initialization with 23 MiB free while the 8192-token chunk requested an 80 MiB buffer.
- Same run on 70660fa3: completed the 12,287-token prompt and generated token 198; the log reported an 8192-token chunk, 2489 borrowed cache slots, and all 2489 slots refilled.
- Token-graph control on 70660fa3: completed the same prompt and generated token 198.
- git diff --check — passed.

Runtime prompt setup: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; Path("/tmp/strata-pr1131-prompt.txt").write_text("198 " * 12288)'. The engine command used --pack $DATA/packs/iq3_xxs, the IQ3_XXS native GGUF shard pair, --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin, --expert-cache auto, --prefill auto, --spec 4, --mtp $DATA/mtp/rt, --max-context 32768, --max-new 1, --kv int8, --no-token-graph, and --tokens-file /tmp/strata-pr1131-prompt.txt.

**Failed:**

- Baseline reproduction on 90767252 failed as described above; no failure was observed on the tested final revision for the supported run.

**Not run:**

- HIP and SYCL builds: hipcc, icpx and dpcpp are unavailable, so this PR is a draft.
- --no-capture: current main rejects this native-pack configuration because session_token has no CPU expert-pool hook; the suggested --no-pool combination was not tested.
- Multi-GPU, two-request serve run, and full CTest suite.

## Limits

The hardware run covers one CUDA GPU and one IQ3_XXS pack. It makes no performance claim and does not establish HIP, SYCL, multi-GPU, or repeated-serve behavior.

pulls.title: [Engine] reject duplicate GPUs in automatic replica groups
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On the current upstream `main`, `gpu_groups()` accepts overlapping GPUs when a numeric replica count derives groups from the configured GPU list. Reproduced before the fix: `{"gpu":[0,0],"replicas":2}` returns `[[0],[0]]`; `{"gpu":[0,1,1,2],"replicas":2}` returns `[[0,1],[1,2]]`. The server can then start independent replica engines on the same card. After this change, these configurations raise `ReplicaConfigError` before replica engines start.

## Related discussion
[PR #2953](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2953) was closed during the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, not declined. The original change was revalidated against current `main`. Search of open and closed issues and PRs for `gpu_groups`, duplicate cards and replica GPU grouping found no other fix for this case.

## Approach
Build numeric groups and pass them through the same non-empty and duplicate-card validation used for explicitly named groups. Add regression coverage for duplicate GPU IDs in list and comma-separated forms, normalized duplicate IDs, explicit groups, preserved card order, and disabled replica counts. Valid group ordering and the no-replica path remain unchanged. No engine backend or defaults are changed.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- Reproduced the issue on upstream `main` at `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`, Linux Debian 13, Python 3.13.5: duplicate GPU configurations returned overlapping groups instead of raising an error.
- `uv run --with-requirements requirements.txt python -m unittest serve.test_replicas serve.test_parallel -q`, on the change based on `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`, Linux Debian 13, Python 3.13.5: **64 tests passed** in 71.163 seconds. These tests use fake engines; no model or GPU was used.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

**Failed:**
- The initial `python3 -m unittest serve.test_replicas serve.test_parallel -q` attempt could not import `jinja2` from the system Python. The same suite then passed when run with the pinned repository requirements in a temporary `uv` environment.

**Not run:**
- Multi-GPU inference and CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal builds; this change touches only Python server code and was verified with fake engines.

## Limits
This validates configuration handling and fake-engine server behavior. It does not establish GPU runtime behavior or performance on hardware.

pulls.title: [Engine] avoid hanging on PleReader initialization failures
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On current upstream main, `PleReader::open()` still hangs during cleanup if read-buffer allocation fails or if a reader is reopened with a table range beyond EOF. The failed `open()` never returns its existing error. After this change, it closes cleanly and a later valid open/read succeeds.

## Related discussion

Retested the report in [#3045](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3045), which was closed during the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original PR [#3046](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3046) was also closed in that reset.

## Approach

Publish the in-flight slot count only after the buffers and free-slot list are ready, and reset the count when closing. Add Linux CPU-only lifecycle coverage for normal reads, failed reopen, and injected allocation failure in caller-thread and I/O-worker modes. The allocation failure uses link-time `posix_memalign` wrapping and does not add production fault-injection behavior.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0, CUDA 13.4.92, NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; base revision `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`, candidate revision `9f4b65fc`.

**Passed:**
- CPU: `cmake -S . -B build/ple-reader-beta -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_WERROR=ON`; `cmake --build build/ple-reader-beta --target ple_reader_lifecycle_test direct_file_async_test -j2`; and `ctest --test-dir build/ple-reader-beta --output-on-failure -R '^(ple_reader_(reads|reopen|alloc)_(caller|threaded)|direct_file_async_test)$'`: targets built and all 7 tests passed.
- CUDA: `cmake -S . -B build/ple-reader-cuda -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_WERROR=OFF -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-13.4/bin/nvcc`; `cmake --build build/ple-reader-cuda --target strata ple_reader_lifecycle_test direct_file_async_test -j2`: all targets built.
- CUDA CTest: `ctest --test-dir build/ple-reader-cuda --output-on-failure -R '^(ple_reader_(reads|reopen|alloc)_(caller|threaded)|direct_file_async_test)$'`: all 7 tests passed.
- Reproduced on unchanged base revision `e88ee39d`: both read controls passed; `reopen` and injected `alloc` cases timed out after 2 seconds in caller and threaded modes (4 hangs).
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

**Failed:**
- With `STRATA_WERROR=ON`, the CUDA build command `cmake --build build/ple-reader-cuda --target strata ple_reader_lifecycle_test direct_file_async_test -j2` stopped on `-Werror=misleading-indentation` in unchanged `src/core/layer.cpp`. The CUDA build passed with WERROR disabled; warnings are outside this change.

**Not run:**
- HIP and SYCL builds: `hipcc`, `dpcpp` and `icpx` are unavailable.
- Windows runtime checks and real model inference.

## Limits

The reproduction uses a synthetic file and real DirectFile I/O on Linux; it verifies initialization and recovery behavior, not a production memory-pressure incident or model inference.

pulls.title: [Engine] run Mirai's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-S (QNS trellis) packs
pulls.author: alesha-pro
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Mirai published Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-S, a trellis build of Flash-Next (routed experts 1-5 bits each, 2.4 on average; backbone and head 5 bits), packed for Strata: `trymirai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-S-strata-experimental`. Until now it runs only on v0.1.43 with Mirai's `strata-qns.patch`. This PR ports that patch to 0.2.0: the S and S-small packs load and run on one card and on a layer split, with MTP and the refusal projection. Every other model takes the same path as before, checked on IQ3_S below.

## Related discussion

Scope: I am writing to @Niko1221 directly to agree it. The QNS format, the CUDA and AVX2 kernels and the packer support are Mirai's work, from their `strata-qns.patch`.

## Approach

Mirai's code is taken unchanged from their HF repo (2026-10-15, which already has the layer-split rotation fix). What the merge with 0.1.44-0.2.0 needed:

- **Pack version.** 0.2.0 uses `native_experts.txt` v5 for Hadamard-folded experts, and the patch used v5 for QNS layers. QNS packs are v6 here. v5 keeps its meaning (hadamard.txt is required for v5 only). A v5 QNS pack from the old patch is refused with "repack with tools/iq_pack.py"; repacking takes ~20 s and gives the same files except the header line. The packer skips the Hadamard spec for QNS.
- **MTP head on another card** (0.1.44 moved the drafter to the first stage): the trellis head's subset rows and their row scales are gathered on the head's card and copied over, like the non-QNS path.
- **New side-stream paths** that read dense weights directly now take the trellis GEMV for `kQnsDenseType`: the GDN gate projection (`side_proj`) and the QSA query chain on a branch stream.
- Expert cache sizing uses `slot_stride(expert_bytes(l, e), slot_guard)`; `expert_bytes` is the layer's blob for non-QNS packs.
- The CPU pool keeps 0.2.0's per-layer widths and rounds QNS row ranges to whole 8-row blocks.
- `docs/QNS.md`: how to pack and run.

All new code is behind `expert_layout().qns()` or `kQnsDenseType`.

## Validation

Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.8, 4x RTX 3090 at 300 W, EPYC 7642 (AVX2), 125 GB RAM. Branch head 8e75f6f (engine sources identical to the tested build).

**Passed**
- CUDA build: `cmake -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF`, `--target strata`. No new warnings in the touched files.
- `tools/iq_pack.py` on S and S-small: v6 packs; `qns_offsets.bin`, `qns_rotation.bin`, `dense.bin`, `index.txt` and every layer row byte-identical to the v0.1.43 patch's packs.
- Six greedy probes through `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking off, 32K context, MTP on, the refusal vector on: a sum, a Python function, a Russian answer, a tool call, a 6,210-token document with a hidden code, a lock-picking question.
  - S-small, 1 card and 2 cards (layer split): all answers correct; the code is found; the tool call is right; no refusal. Against v0.1.43 + Mirai's patch on the same cards: 5 of 6 answers identical, the sixth parts on a near-tie after 10-55 words (v0.1.43 itself gives a different text on 1 and 2 cards there, from about 120 words on).
  - S (full), 1 card and 2 cards: all six correct.
  - On 2 cards MTP drafts are accepted (117 of 170 on a 200-token answer), no errors in the engine log.
- **Default path:** IQ3_S (ISTA GSQ-RCO) on 2 cards, the same flags, stock 0.2.0-beta (3d1fb48) against this branch: all six greedy answers byte-identical, same token counts; decode per request within 3.1%.
- Decode, server tok/s per request (one run each, indicative): S-small 47-106 (1 card) / 83-166 (2 cards); S 35-81 / 60-125. v0.1.43 + patch on the same S-small requests: 45-92 / 75-143.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run**
- HIP build: no ROCm toolchain here. The new `.cu` files are compiled for HIP by the existing glob, so this needs a HIP build (or a CUDA-only guard) before review. Help welcome.
- SYCL and Metal: not touched. Windows / MSVC: not built.
- Long contexts (above 32K) and vision on QNS: not run in this PR (vision ran on v0.1.43 with the patch).

## Limits

- NVIDIA CUDA and the AVX2 CPU pool only, as in Mirai's patch.
- Setup and the Terminal do not offer these models; they start from a hand-written config (`docs/QNS.md`).
- Kept as a draft until the HIP build is checked.

pulls.title: [Engine] STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_BATCH=1 (opt-in): the prompt's CPU share with --batch, for a read while no slot decodes; short reads -21% to -31%
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The prompt path's CPU share (`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE`) is off whenever `--batch` is set: generate.cpp sets `share_pool = o.batch <= 0 && !o.no_pool`, so with `"parallel": 2` the variable has no effect. The server runs with batch slots for concurrency, so a short read there always waits on the GPU alone: below the full-streaming chunk size (`stream_all_min`, here 2048) a chunk copies only its routed experts over PCIe, and on this machine that wait is about half of a 1-2K-token read.

With `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE_BATCH=1` the pool is handed to the prompt path as it is without batch slots, and before each read the serve loop checks the slots: a read while any slot is decoding takes no share (the slots' verify windows use the pool), a read with none does. The existing CPU-share rules then decide as before (which chunks, how many experts).

Result on 2x RX 6900 XT (below), 10 interleaved cold-start pairs: real-text reads under 2,048 tokens -28.8% (median), a 1,733-token one -20.9%, conversation continuations adding 455/781 tokens -30.7%, a 34K read -2.3% (its last chunk, 1,378 tokens); reads of 2,048 tokens and more unchanged. Without the variable the default path is byte-identical.

## Related discussion

None found. I could not find a stated reason for `batch <= 0` in the code or history; this keeps it as the default and only adds the opt-in.

## Approach

- generate.cpp: `share_pool = (o.batch <= 0 || share_batch) && !o.no_pool`, with one line at load when the variable applies; a `share_gate()` before each read (in `read_part`'s run and before the concurrent reader starts) calls `Prefill::set_share_blocked(busy > 0)` from the slots' `active` flags, and prints the decision for the first 4 reads.
- prefill.cpp: `set_share_blocked()` sets an atomic that the chunk's existing pool-hold test also checks (`!g_share_blocked`).
- The share still needs the CPU share itself enabled (`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto` or `1`; on a layer split it is not on by default).

## Validation

Environment: 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, 16 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8 each), Ryzen 5 5600X (6 cores), 128 GB DDR4-3200, Ubuntu 26.04 (kernel 7.0.0), ROCm 10.0.0. Revision: main e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta + 12 commits) and this branch on it. Built with setup.py's HIP options (`-DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`, gfx1030, the pinned ggml, Release). Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, layer split over both cards.

**Passed:**

1. Default path byte-identical: deterministic config (`parallel` 1, no pipeline windows, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`, `STRATA_LOGPOS` top-256 log-probabilities), 8 chats of real text, 4,067 scored positions: main and this branch without the variable `cmp` identical.
2. Speed: `parallel` 2 (`--batch 2`), `--pipeline-windows 2 --batch-mtp`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=2048`, `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1`, a rocBLAS table via `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING`. The same binary with and without the variable, 20 cold starts alternating A B A B; each arm sends the same 33 requests one after another (so no slot is decoding during a read): 27 single real-text prompts of 430-3,521 tokens (English prose, Chinese prose, C++), then a 34K-token conversation and 5 continuations of it adding 455-3,168 tokens. `prompt_ms` from /metrics. Median over the 10 pairs of each group's mean change:

   | reads | median change | faster |
   |---|---|---|
   | 15 single prompts under 2,048 tokens (430-1,542) | -28.8% (pairs -28.6 to -29.0) | 10/10 |
   | 1 single prompt of 1,733 tokens | -20.9% | 10/10 |
   | 11 single prompts of 2,048+ tokens | -0.0% (pairs -0.2 to +0.1) | - |
   | 34,146-token first read (4 chunks of 8,192 + one of 1,378) | -2.3% | 10/10 |
   | 2 continuations adding 455 / 781 tokens | -30.7% | 10/10 |
   | 3 continuations adding 2,136-3,168 tokens | +0.0% | - |

   e.g. a 430-token Chinese prompt 1,722 -> 1,146 ms, a 455-token continuation 1,722 -> 1,168 ms. The `=1` arms printed `CPU share for this read: on (0 slot(s) decoding)`, the others no such line; 0 stalls.
3. `ctest` (STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON; the engine binary is the same one, sha256 unchanged): 137 tests, 131 passed. The 6 failures are the same 6 on main e88ee39d built the same way: `ple_parity` (needs a Q2_0 GGUF this machine does not have), `hip_prefill_mmq_parity` (SEGFAULT on main too), `native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` ("this ggml has no trellis types"), `isa_guard_check` (`tq_rows_avx512` not listed). The branch adds no test: the change is a scheduling condition; item 2 checks it end to end (the per-read confirmation line).

4. CUDA compile only (no NVIDIA GPU here): CUDA 13.2.2 (nvcc 13.2.86) with GCC 15.2, `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`: the engine builds; the one warning in generate.cpp (line 11576, an unused variable) is there on main too, none from the changed lines.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**
- Reads beside a decoding slot on this revision: by design they take no share; I measured that two concurrent requests are unchanged on 0.1.45 with this patch, not on 0.2.0.
- Output quality with the share on: the CPU computes some experts, so the bits differ from the GPU-only read and depend on timing, as with the CPU share without batch slots today; I did not measure KL for it on this revision.
- CUDA execution (compiled only, item 4), the SYCL and Metal builds (no toolkits here; SYCL builds its own copy of prefill.cpp, Metal compiles this one, and the new `Prefill::set_share_blocked` is defined in it, so no stub is needed - not verified by a Mac build), a single-GPU setup, Windows, other GPUs.

## Limits

- Opt-in; it only lifts the `batch <= 0` condition, the CPU-share rules themselves are unchanged.
- The gate is taken when a read starts: a slot that begins decoding during a long read does not take the pool back from it.
- The gain is for reads below the streaming chunk size on a machine where those wait on PCIe (here 2x x8, 45% of the experts in VRAM); a box with the experts resident would see little.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on the machine described here.

pulls.title: [Engine] STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_RDNA2=1 (opt-in, gfx103x, INT8 KV): prompt QSA attention without the decode kernel's split and merge, -3.5% prompt time at 32K and 119K
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On gfx103x the prompt's QSA attention has no kernel of its own. `qsa_prompt_attn_batch` returns false (the matrix-core kernels are RDNA4/CUDA), so prefill.cpp falls back to the decode path: `attn_chunk_kernel_pre75` 32 queries at a time, each query's ~2,051 selected cells split into 64-cell chunks over many blocks, then `attn_merge_kernel`. The split is there to fill the card with one decode query; a prompt chunk already has thousands of queries.

With `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_RDNA2=1`, one block per (query, KV head) walks all of the query's chunks with an online softmax: no per-chunk scratch and no merge pass. The score phase is `attn_chunk_kernel_pre75`'s, unchanged. The value phase takes 4 dimensions per thread (one 4-byte load of int8 codes feeds 48 FMAs instead of 12), and each chunk is summed from zero and folded into the running sum with one fma, so the summation is blocked like the split path's.

Result on 2x RX 6900 XT (below): prompt time -3.49% at 31K and at 119K tokens, 10 of 10 interleaved cold-start pairs each; the kernel itself 1.36-1.68x faster in the synthetic parity test; error against FP64 no larger than the split path's, on synthetic and on real data. Without the variable the default path is byte-identical (checked, below).

## Related discussion

None. It is opt-in and limited to gfx103x with INT8 K/V; nothing changes for other cards or without the variable.

## Approach

- `qsa_prompt_attn_rdna2()` (qsa_decode_attn.cu) runs only when the variable is 1, `pre75_attn()` holds (gfx103x, or `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75=1` on another wave32 card), K/V are INT8 (not Q4_0 / FP16), head_dim 256 with 12 query heads per KV head, and n_q <= 65535; otherwise it returns false and prefill.cpp keeps its current path. `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_OLD` still wins.
- HIP only: the kernel is compiled under `#if defined(__HIPCC__)` (inside the existing `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75_BUILT` block, which CUDA builds also define), the entry point is a stub returning false elsewhere, and prefill.cpp calls it only under `STRATA_USE_HIP` - so the CUDA, SYCL and Metal engines never reference it (Metal links root `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` against generated stubs; SYCL builds its own migrated copies).
- Not bit-identical to the split path: the chunks fold into one running maximum instead of the merge's two passes (FP32-level differences, quantified below).
- Test: `hip_prompt_attn_rdna2` is `qsa_prompt_attn_parity.cpp` built with `STRATA_PARITY_RDNA2` - the same checks the RDNA4 kernel has (`hip_prompt_attn_wmma`): against an FP64 host reference and against the decode kernel; it skips (77) off gfx103x.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, 16 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8 each), Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GB DDR4-3200, Ubuntu 26.04 (kernel 7.0.0), ROCm 10.0.0. Revision: main e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta + 12 commits) and this branch on it. Built with setup.py's HIP options: `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1030`, the pinned ggml, Release. Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, layer split over both cards, `--kv int8`.

**Passed:**

1. `hip_prompt_attn_rdna2 32768 2048 3` (synthetic, GPU 1):

   | case | max abs error vs FP64: split / new | new vs split (of output scale) | ms per chunk: split -> new |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | ctx 32768, 2048 queries | 2.13e-6 / 2.00e-6 | 6.3e-7 | 19.30 -> 14.22 (1.36x) |
   | ctx 1500, 1500 queries (every cell) | 1.78e-6 / 1.90e-6 | 5.1e-7 | 6.48 -> 3.85 (1.68x) |
   | ctx 2100, 256 queries (identity-to-sparse edge) | 2.03e-6 / 1.54e-6 | 5.9e-7 | 2.43 -> 1.68 (1.45x) |

   RMS error vs FP64 (an extra print, not in the test): new / split = 0.94, 0.93, 0.94. An earlier version that rescaled one running sum every chunk passed the test's bounds too but had 1.16-1.41x the split path's RMS error; the blocked fold costs ~1.6% kernel time.
2. `ctest` (STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON): 138 tests, 132 passed (including `hip_prompt_attn_rdna2`, 3.8 s). The 6 failures are the same 6 on main e88ee39d built the same way (137 tests): `ple_parity` (needs a Q2_0 GGUF this machine does not have), `hip_prefill_mmq_parity` (SEGFAULT on main too, with PREFILL_MMQ=ON), `native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` ("this ggml has no trellis types"), `isa_guard_check` (`tq_rows_avx512` not listed).
3. Default path byte-identical: deterministic config (`parallel` 1, no pipeline windows, `--short-read 640 --adapt-every 100000`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`), `STRATA_LOGPOS` with top-256 log-probabilities at every scored position: 8 chats of real text (first message 6K-105K tokens read through the prompt path, then ~580 tokens of continuation scored), 4,067 positions. main and this branch without the variable: `cmp` identical.
4. Quality, same harness, against a local build of the same kernel in double (scores, softmax and sums in FP64; not part of this PR). Mean over the 8 chats, criteria fixed before the run (KL <= 1.5x main's, argmax agreement >= main's - 2 points):

   | | mean KL to the FP64-attention reference | argmax agreement |
   |---|---|---|
   | main | 0.0334 | 94.81% |
   | this branch, `=1` | 0.0325 | 95.88% |

   Per chat the two differ in both directions; each has one chat well above its mean (main: the 14K chat, 0.066; this branch: the 65K chat, 0.131, also high in a second build). For that 65K chat a local diagnostic build re-ran the last 512 queries of every one of the 96 attention calls through the split path and the FP64 kernel on the real inputs: new/split RMS error 0.829-0.924 (median 0.883), the same distribution as the 14K control chat (median 0.893), no call above 1.2x. So the chat's higher KL is downstream amplification (QSA's top-k selection is discrete), not a larger attention error; I am reporting it rather than averaging it away.
5. Speed: production-like config (`parallel` 2, `--pipeline-windows 2 --batch-mtp`, `--kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=2048`, a rocBLAS table via `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING`), the same binary with and without the variable, 20 cold starts alternating A B A B, each reading two real-text prompts with max_tokens 1, `prompt_ms` from /metrics (0 tokens reused):

   | prompt | without (median, range) | `=1` (median, range) | per pair | median | faster |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 31,039 tokens | 19,126 ms (19,112-19,151) | 18,453 ms (18,448-18,481) | -3.43% to -3.59% | -3.49% | 10/10 |
   | 119,290 tokens | 62,639 ms (62,617-62,666) | 60,456 ms (60,419-60,501) | -3.44% to -3.55% | -3.49% | 10/10 |

   The `=1` arms all printed the confirmation line, the others none; 0 stalls.

6. CUDA compile only (no NVIDIA GPU here): CUDA 13.2.2 (nvcc 13.2.86) with GCC 15.2, `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`: the engine and every test target build, including `qsa_prompt_attn_parity` with the changed source; no warning from the changed files (the build's 261 warnings are all in files this PR does not touch). The HIP engine binary is byte-identical before and after adding the `STRATA_USE_HIP` guard (sha256 unchanged), so items 1-5 hold for the submitted commit.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**
- CUDA execution (compiled only, item 6), other CUDA architectures than sm_86, and the SYCL and Metal builds (no toolkits here). SYCL compiles its own copies of the changed files; Metal compiles the changed prefill.cpp, where the new call is under `STRATA_USE_HIP`, so it needs no new stub - not verified by a Mac build.
- Other gfx103x cards (RX 6800 / 6700, W6800, V620) and Windows: not tested.
- gfx11 / gfx12: the dispatch keeps their path (`pre75_attn()` is false there unless `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75=1`); not executed.

## Limits

- Opt-in, gfx103x with INT8 K/V and the Flash-Next attention geometry (head_dim 256, 12 query heads per KV head) only; Q4_0 or FP16 K/V keep the split path.
- Only the prompt path; decode is unchanged.
- Quality is "not worse" by the measurements above, not "more accurate": FP32-level differences against the split path, which is itself not bit-identical to FP64.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on the machine described here.
