pulls.title: [Other] serve: an all-cached image turn never wakes the elastic encoder
pulls.author: jerry78424
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
An elastic image encoder is woken (seconds of start, VRAM the expert cache gives up) on every turn that re-sends pictures it has already encoded - which is what most clients do on every turn. A turn whose images are all in the hash cache needs no encoder process at all.

Measured on RTX 5090 32 GB, Windows 11 (26200), engine 0.1.44.1, nvfp4, `elastic_idle_s: 10` (table and verbatim log lines in #2454): before - a text-only turn with a re-sent picture cost a 2.3 s start + 2085 MiB taken from the expert cache; after - 722 ms with no start line. A re-sent-picture turn: 1277 ms, no start. New pictures unchanged (3979-4213 ms, still start).

## Related discussion
Resolves #2454. Follows #2455 (same branch and author; closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, and GitHub would not reopen it after the rebase force-push). Independent of the #2641 successor (the tool-picture wake lands in this same method - textual overlap only; the two changes conflict in neither order, verified by cherry-pick).

## Approach
- `serve/server.py`: `Vision.key_of()` / `Vision.cached()` - a hash-cache lookup that answers with the process down (the cache and its .sve files survive an unload, as before) and marks a hit most recently used, as `encode()` does on its hit path. `prepare()` maps the turn's images through the cache first, for an elastic encoder only: when every one is a hit the turn skips the encode FIFO, `_vision_up()` and the encode. A miss - alone or alongside hits - keeps today's path byte-for-byte: FIFO, make-room, start, encode.
- `serve/test_vision_cache_wake.py` (new, CPU-only, no engine): a re-sent picture does not wake a stopped encoder; a new picture alongside cached ones still wakes it; the lookup answers with the process down and keeps the re-sent picture from aging out of the 64-entry cache; a non-elastic turn keeps today's path even when every picture is cached.
- `docs/VRAM_ELASTIC.md`, `docs/DETAILS.md`: both halves of the elastic rule - a picture's turn starts the encoder, a turn of pictures the cache knows takes neither the turn nor a start.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Every new behavior fails on a tree without the code that provides it.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_vision_elastic serve.test_vision_busy serve.test_vision_cache_wake serve.test_images`: the vision four 36 OK - at `e88ee39d` (v0.2.0-beta-12), rebased 2026-10-20, Windows 11 26200, Python 3.12 venv, CPU-only tests.
- Full serve suite: 791 OK (15 skipped).
- With #2641 cherry-picked on top: the files stay 19 + 19 OK.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** AMD/HIP and layer-split machines (a layer split refuses elastic anyway; its start failure is #2435). No native files are touched, so no native builds are required.

## Limits
- What it leaves alone: non-elastic vision, the start/stop/idle lifecycle itself, the encode path, and every native file (no CUDA/HIP/SYCL build needed).
- The measured numbers are one machine (RTX 5090, nvfp4); the mechanism - no process start for an all-cached turn - is hardware-independent, but the saved seconds are not claimed for other machines.

pulls.title: [Other] serve: a tool's picture starts the elastic encoder, and its turn counts
pulls.author: jerry78424
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
`_note_unreadable_tool_images` - the method that promises "a picture a tool returned that this server cannot read becomes a short note in its place instead of a 400" - encodes the picture without starting the elastic encoder first. Once the idle sweep has stopped the encoder (`elastic_idle_s` without a picture, default 120 s), the tool's picture writes to a pipe that no longer exists: the `AttributeError` on the `None` proc escapes the `except (ValueError, OSError)` filter and the route's body-shape filter, and the request dies as a **400 "the request is malformed (AttributeError...)"** - the opposite of what the method exists to do. And because clients re-send the whole history every turn, every later request of the conversation dies the same way at this method's own line: the conversation stays broken until a picture from another conversation (or a restart) starts the encoder.

Reproduce: `"elastic": true` + `"vram_elastic": true`; send one picture, let the encoder idle-stop (log: `[strata] images: the image encoder stopped after N s ...`); then send a `tool` message whose content carries an `image` block (Claude Code's Read of a picture - the exact input 3709c15f added this method for). Expected per the method's own docstring: a `[image omitted: ...]` note. Actual: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'stdin'` (inside `Vision.encode`'s `self.proc.stdin.write`) surfaces as a 400.

After the change the tool picture starts the encoder first, the note is written as documented, and the conversation survives.

## Related discussion
Follows #2641 (same branch and author; closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, and GitHub would not reopen it after the rebase force-push). Fixes #3171. The prepare() path does not have this problem - its encode block calls `_vision_up()` inside the FIFO turn; the tool path (3709c15f, wrapped into `_turn` by 873a0d66) never got the wake, and the elastic idle stop made the missing wake fatal. Related: #2435 (the sibling: a start that fails on the prepare path), #2343 (MCP picture results will send more traffic through this exact path). Independent of the #2455 successor (its `cached()` skip lands in this same method later - textual overlap only). #3174 is a parallel PR with the core wake alone; this one is the same fix plus the two sides that adding a wake to this path brings.

## Approach
- `serve/server.py`: inside the tool path's turn, `_vision_up()` before the encode (the caller holds the FIFO, as prepare does); the turn's end updates `last_image_at` in a `finally` - without it the idle sweep judges the just-started encoder by the previous picture's timestamp and reclaims it at once, and a tool-picture-only conversation never moves the timer; `start()`'s `RuntimeError` joins the filter, so a failing start becomes the documented note, not a dead request.
- `serve/test_vision_elastic.py`: two cases - a tool picture wakes a stopped encoder, and the turn holds it across the idle check; a start that raises becomes the note.
- Compatibility: the widened filter matches what can still raise (`encode()`'s own pipe death already becomes ValueError/OSError internally - #1317's read timeout raises ValueError, a write to a dead pipe is OSError - and `ClientGone` is a bare Exception, so a client that left still propagates). No native files touched.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Both new cases fail on the base tree at the fake's "a picture reached an encoder that was not started" assert (the bug's exact signature), and a real `Vision` with the proc unloaded raises the `AttributeError` verbatim.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_vision_elastic serve.test_vision_busy` (CPU-only, no engine): 13 OK; `python -m unittest serve.test_images`: 19 OK - at `e88ee39d` (v0.2.0-beta-12), rebased 2026-10-20, Windows 11 26200, Python 3.12 venv. On the previous base `f57c0adc` the same files were 9/9 + 32 OK.
- With #2455 on top (cherry-picked, auto-merge clean): the three files stay 19 + 19 OK - the two PRs conflict in neither order.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds (no native files touched); the live GPU end-to-end is #3171's reporter's log, reproduced here by the two CPU tests' fail-on-base/pass-after signature.

## Limits
- The wake reuses the same FIFO turn the encode already runs in, so a tool picture now costs the encoder start (~seconds, logged) on an idle-stopped encoder - the same cost the user-picture path already pays; it is what the note path cannot afford to skip.
- No native files touched; nothing here changes non-elastic behavior.

pulls.title: [Other] tools: read the FP4-Local checkpoint with cached sequential reads, not a process-lifetime np.memmap
pulls.author: jerry78424
pulls.body:
Fixes #3377. Related: #3227 / #3228 (a different failure of the same step; no hunk overlap — that PR touches the overlay gens around `:191-211`, this one the `Checkpoint` class at `:48-91`).

## The problem and the result

`prepare` fails mid-pack on Windows: the pack python dies at 50–67 % of the experts write, exit 1, no traceback, while its own committed memory is ~3.5 GB. `Checkpoint.raw()` maps every shard with `np.memmap(..., mode="r")` for the process's life; the pack pass reads 64.36 GB of distinct expert bytes, and on Windows every faulted page is charged to the process working set, which `ullAvailPhys` (= psutil `available` = `os.freemem` = our own `ram_used`, `serve/telemetry.py:624-625`) counts as used until the OS trims — the step presents a ~64 GB RAM demand for a few-GB real one (issue: +41 GB in five minutes, run dead at ~11 GB free).

With this change the same reads return hash-identical bytes, run ~1.2x faster warm, and the working set stays flat — a full 68 GB pack run to a scratch dir with the serving model loaded (the scenario that failed): exit 0, byte-identical `experts.bin`, working set 3.3–5.3 GB bounded (externally sampled), free RAM never below ~53 GB.

## The approach

`Checkpoint.raw()` reads the tensor's byte range through a cached file handle with `seek` + `readinto` into a fresh buffer; the kernel's pages then live in the system file cache (standby: counted as available) instead of the process working set.

- The returned array keeps `array()`'s `.view().reshape()` contract (buffers >=8-byte aligned; U8/U16/U32/F32 all used); it is writable where `mode="r"` was read-only — no consumer writes (all produce fresh outputs; a mutator would previously have raised through numpy or faulted through a torch view) — and `raw()` shares one handle per shard, so it is not thread-safe, unlike the memmap it replaces; all call sites are single-threaded.
- Unmapping per shard would bound the working set to ~one shard (~5 GB) but re-fault ~64 GB per pass (13–14 of the 15 expert shards are open per layer anyway); sequential `readinto` bounds it to ~0. Within a shard the order walks three ascending streams (exceptions, weights, CSF-fixed) expert-ascending. np.memmap has no Windows lever (no `FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN`/madvise equivalent).
- No API or call-site changes; at most one open read handle per shard, same count as the replaced memmaps. Residual memmaps elsewhere are bounded and untouched: `iq_pack.py:161,218,324` (~6 GB dense.gguf) and `LocalTensor.mmap_bytes` in convert (~4 GB).

## Validation

- **passed**: `python -m pytest tools/test_nvfp4_local_pack.py`: 13 — the 11 existing (they never construct `Checkpoint`) plus 2 added here: a synthetic two-shard checkpoint (byte-exact reads at a tensor's range, `array()` dtype/shape views, repeat reads, truncated shard -> `EOFError` instead of a silent short view).
- **passed**: A/B on the live checkpoint, the pack's read order (4.03 GB): old path +3.75 GB working set (93 % of bytes touched; charges even warm) in 2.7–4.1 s, this path +0.00 GB in 2.3 s, both hash-identical. Extrapolation: the failed run had faulted 50–67 % of 64.36 GB = 32–43 GB, bracketing its observed +41 GB.
- **passed**: full pack to a scratch `--out` with the serving model loaded: exit 0, `experts.bin` size identical (67,948,118,016 bytes), SHA-256 match `1e124ee94b7c921a7c895d2898bfa4ddc2d8111f3fd3e8b94207759c363291a5`; externally sampled working set 3.3–5.3 GB bounded, free 53.3–60.0 GB throughout (in-run 15 s sampler; pre-patch signature: +41 GB in 5 min).
- **failed**: none.
- **not run**: `ple`/`mtp`/`verify` individually (same class, different call sites, covered by the new class tests); Linux/AMD (OS-neutral file I/O; the inflation mechanism is Windows-specific).

## Limits

- `readinto` returns short only at EOF (the buffering layer absorbs partial raw reads); the added `EOFError` names a truncated shard instead of the old silent short memmap view — a behavior change only for corrupt checkpoints.

**Environment**: tested at e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta-12), Windows 11 26200, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 187 GB RAM, RTX 5090 (driver 617.42), NVMe, model `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local`.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RX 9070 XT on Windows 11, Coder IQ1_M at 64K, engine 0.1.45.3 built on the PC
pulls.author: facundopanizza
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`docs/AMD_HIP.md` asks for reports of a Windows AMD card running a model ("The ready-made zip itself has not run a model on a discrete card yet - please report", and "Reporting a Windows AMD run"). This is one: an **RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201) on Windows 11**, Ryzen 9 9950X, **31 GB RAM**, running the **Coder IQ1_M at 65,536 context** in the low-RAM mode. The engine (0.1.45.3) was built on this PC with `tools\hip\build_windows.bat` because no ready-made AMD engine was published for 0.1.45.3.

Results only, no code change. Medians and ranges from one `tools/strata_bench.py --long` suite on a fresh server:

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| chat decode | **46.9 tok/s** (42.5-58.8, n=9), first token 0.64 s |
| fresh prompt 4K / 16K / 32K | 909 / 1,271 / 1,237 tok/s (n=3 each), first token 4.5 / 12.7 / 26.0 s |
| agent session, follow-up turns | decode 60.5 tok/s (25.2-69.1, n=15), cache hit 69.6 %, first token 3.4 s |

**The experimental speed projection was on** (chosen in setup); there is no run without it. Full report: `bench/results/2026-10-20-community-rx-9070-xt-qwen3-8-flash-next-coder-iq1-m/README.md`, with per-request data (`results.json`), the engine's start-up lines (`engine-log-excerpt.txt`) and the device checks (`strata-device.txt`). One entry added to the list in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

## Related discussion

- The `docs/AMD_HIP.md` request above (#325 is the Windows AMD thread it names).
- #3235: the `strata_bench.py` start-up `NameError`, reproduced here (see Failed).

## Approach

Measured with the repository's own `tools/strata_bench.py`, unchanged. Because its self-start path fails (#3235), the server was started with the tool's own `start_server()` in a separate process and the suite run with `--config strata-coder-iq1_m.json --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --long`. The tool's report was kept as written; the hardware, build, storage, low-RAM and speed-projection facts it marks "not recorded" were filled in from Windows (WMI) and the engine log. Paths in the added files are replaced by `<HOME>`, `<STRATA>`, `<DATA>`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `engine\strata-device.exe --list-devices` (PATH: `engine\rocm\bin` first), e88ee39d build: lists device 0 (integrated Radeon, gfx1036, "cannot run") and device 1 (RX 9070 XT, gfx1201).
- `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 engine\strata-device.exe --selftest`: `strata-device selftest OK` on the RX 9070 XT.
- `tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-coder-iq1_m.json --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --long`: `failures: []` and `skipped: {}` in `results.json`, suite 239 s; numbers above.
- Files checked for user names, host name, home paths, IP addresses and the server's API key: none present.

**Failed:**
- `engine\strata-device.exe --selftest` without `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, as `docs/AMD_HIP.md` gives it: exits 1 because it tests device 0, the integrated GPU (output in `strata-device.txt`).
- `python tools/strata_bench.py --long` (the self-start path `BENCH.bat` uses): `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` at `tools/strata_bench.py:990`, as in #3235.

**Not run:**
- A run without the experimental speed projection, and `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` (off by default on Windows).
- RAM at its rated speed: the DDR5-5600 modules ran at 4800 MT/s (EXPO off).
- More than one suite or server start; needle or other correctness checks; the ready-made 0.2.0 `rx9070` package.

## Limits

One machine, one suite run, with the Windows desktop and other apps open. The engine warned that the Windows commit limit had 4.7 GiB left at start (#1607); no crash happened. The numbers include the speed projection and the low-RAM mode on 31 GB, so they are not comparable to a run with more RAM or without the control vector.

pulls.title: [Engine] verify_q8: fix the CUDA 12.0/12.1 build (host call to device-only __half_as_ushort)
pulls.author: yudhanjaya
pulls.body:
Fixes #3368 (also reported in the closed #2926).

**What it changes:** `verify_q8` (the `STRATA_Q36_VERIFY=1` debug path in `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`) printed the half bits with `__half_as_ushort(...)`. That function is `__device__` only in CUDA 12.0/12.1, so nvcc rejects the call from host code and the whole engine fails to build. The bits are now copied out of the `__half` with `memcpy`. Same value, same output.

**What it leaves alone:** only the debug print in that one function. No kernel, no default path, no other backend file is touched; the default path is byte-identical (the changed lines run only with `STRATA_Q36_VERIFY=1` and a mismatch).

**How I checked:** nvcc 12.0.140, Ubuntu, `arch=compute_86` and `compute_89` (RTX 3060 + RTX 4080 SUPER): `./update.sh` rebuilt the engine without error and reports engine 0.1.45.3.

**Not tested:** HIP and SYCL builds; running with `STRATA_Q36_VERIFY=1`; CUDA 12.1+ (the error is the same one in #2926).

pulls.title: [GUI] Add Opt-In Local Model Extension Outside The App Installation
pulls.author: medking82
pulls.body: ## Problem and result A Strata server managed outside the App can be usable through an API connection while **Manage Models** and **Storage** show no native downloads. Customizing bundled frontend files to expose that connection also conflicts with App updates. This opt-in companion adds **Current Model** and isolated **Connected Local Models** cards while retaining the official catalog, download library and component updater. It uses the managed Tray as the sole lifecycle owner. No model files are moved or copied, and connected models do not become native prepared/downloaded rows. ## Related discussion Scope proposal #3369; depends on the optional owner protocol in #3365. **Ready for review. Scope agreement has not yet been obtained; review is requested alongside that discussion.** It changes no defaults. Reasoning effort stays in the official composer; the separate API effort fix is #3363. ## Approach All changes are new files under `tools/local-model-extension/`, based on `main` at `e88ee39d`. Existing engine, server, frontend, setup, installer and updater files are byte-identical to that base (`git diff e88ee39d -- . ':!tools/local-model-extension'` is empty). An explicit external launcher adds a Node preload only to its App child. It checks the exact host entrypoint and listening port, preserves existing `NODE_OPTIONS`, and serves one versioned Shadow DOM/iframe UI package through a separate namespace. Package hashes, inventory, App 0.2.x and Bridge API 1 are checked before injection. Missing, disabled, corrupt or incompatible packages leave the original host listener in place. Activation, disable and rollback are outside the App install folder. The companion accepts configurable loopback ports and physical model IDs, with optional display labels. It cross-checks the fresh owner snapshot with live API metadata. Context choices come from the actual native catalog; selected and effective values remain distinct. Idle choices are Never/5/10/30 Minutes. Explicit context, idle, preload and unload requests enter the existing Tray serial worker via atomic file IPC, with execution-time identity checks and durable acknowledgments. The companion never starts an inference server or bypasses owner drain/authentication through direct HTTP load/unload calls. **Use In Chat** requires one existing App connection with the same API URL and physical ID. It preserves authentication and unrelated rows, updates confirmed display/capacity metadata, then selects the exact official picker entry after an explicit action. It does not change effort, Fast, permissions or client settings. The package contains no private model allowlist, Codex dependency, account details or local user paths. ## Examples Anonymous simulated fixtures, rendered from the production extension assets and the actual `NativeModels` / `SettingsStorage` React components. These are UI render examples, **not evidence of inference, actual memory fit or an installed App update**. Original user screenshots were not uploaded. Captions identify the simulated state; no private paths, credentials or model IDs are present. **Current Model** **Manage Models** — the native dialog is scrolled to the connected card's actions. **Storage** — native directories and download counts remain unchanged. [Current Model opened inside the App fixture](https://github.com/medking82/Strata/blob/98f8da6aa2de0587e9346f73e1fac213f928399f/tools/local-model-extension/examples/current-model-in-app.png). Generation source and setup instructions are in the added README; no original personal screenshot is used. ## Validation Windows x64, Node 24.18.0, Python 3.12; candidate `98f8da6a` on base `e88ee39d`. Commands below omit the local windowless-runner wrapper. **Passed:** - `node --test tools/local-model-extension/owner_api.test.mjs tools/local-model-extension/extension_bridge.test.mjs tools/local-model-extension/host-preload.test.mjs tools/local-model-extension/package/ui.test.mjs`: **70 tests passed**, zero skipped, using the Tray candidate at `ff69390e` through `STRATA_TRAY_SOURCE`. Covers real loopback HTTP and file IPC, cross-language consumption/acknowledgment, matching/stale identities, actual host preload in disposable Node child processes, default/failure fallback, package compatibility, exact picker selection, cancellation, context/idle confirmation and unchanged native model counts/directories. - `python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/local-model-extension -p test_*.py`: **13 tests passed**, including immutable package activation, disable, rollback, inventory/hash validation and launch-plan isolation. - `node tools/local-model-extension/examples/render.mjs`: four actual UI render images; official eight catalog choices verified, external requests blocked, zero model mutations and zero browser page errors. Chrome ran headless with GPU disabled. Every image was visually inspected. - Final UI-only checks passed again after anonymizing fixture names and paths. `git diff --check` passed; changed paths are confined to the new tools directory. No original application or runtime configuration was changed. **Failed:** - None unresolved in the final checks. **Not run:** - Installed Windows App launch/update and end-to-end real model inference, native GPU allocation, memory-fit limits, physical load/unload or idle timing for this portable candidate. No model download or GPU workload was launched. No CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal code is touched; those builds were not run. ## Limits Scope agreement and targeted Windows acceptance remain outstanding. This is a narrowly version-gated external companion, not a general plugin platform or guaranteed compatibility with future App DOM layouts. Requires the managed Tray candidate and a matching existing App model connection. File IPC state must remain private to the local account. Interrupted commands are not replayed; manual inspection is needed before recovery. The public README documents opt-in, normal-launch bypass, disable and rollback.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: recreate the vision encoder's work dir when a temp cleaner removed it
pulls.author: smallmj
pulls.body:
**[Engine] — the title above starts with the area.**

## Problem and result

An idle encoder's work dir (`%TEMP%\strata-vision-*`) sits empty and unheld in the temp directory for as long as the model stays unloaded, and Windows' Storage Sense (or any temp cleaner) removes it there. Every later start then failed on the encoder's cwd with `[WinError 267] The directory name is invalid`, on every client retry, until the whole server was restarted: `work_dir()` runs once at the server's start and `restart()` reuses the stale path.

After the fix, `Vision._start()` recreates the dir (and drops the encoded-image cache, whose files lived in it) before either the GPU or the CPU-fallback reader is spawned, so an unload/load cycle survives an external removal of the directory.

## Related discussion

#3370 (the full evidence chain: production timeline, ruled-out causes, minimal reproduction).

## Approach

The check lives in `_start`, the wrapper, so both the GPU reader and the CPU fallback start against an existing dir. The cache is dropped along with the dir because the cache-hit branch of `encode()` returns paths without checking they exist — stale entries would hand the engine paths into a directory that no longer exists. No compatibility effects outside the broken case: a dir that exists is left untouched, and `work_dir()` is the same #480-selected space-free path as before.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python3 -m serve.test_vision_dir` — both cases (removed dir recreated + cache dropped; intact dir kept with its cache), at e88ee39d + this patch, Ubuntu, CPython 3.12
- `python3 -m serve.test_vision_busy` — the existing vision-start tests, no regression (4/4)
- the equivalent one-line fix has run on the affected production machine (Windows 11, RTX 3090, engine 0.1.45) since 2026-10-20: `py_compile` clean; the load-after-idle path had been failing daily before the fix

**Failed:**

- none observed

**Not run:**

- a real GPU encoder start against a removed dir on Windows (the production machine has the fix and has not hit the condition since; the unit test covers the logic with the spawn mocked)
- CUDA / HIP / SYCL / Metal builds of the engine — the change is serve-side Python only

## Limits

The recreated dir is a new directory: anything holding a path into the old one goes stale. The server itself holds no such paths (the cache is dropped with the recreation), and the encoder is spawned fresh in the new dir — so nothing inside the server can observe the switch.

pulls.title: [Engine] allow CPU vision to load on demand without elastic VRAM
pulls.author: keylimesoda
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With a CPU picture reader (`vision.gpu: false`), `vision.elastic: true` is currently disabled unless the text engine also enables `vram_elastic`. As a result, starting the text model starts the CPU encoder too, even when every request is text. Enabling elastic VRAM merely to defer a CPU process is unnecessary and changes the text engine's memory policy.

This allows the existing opt-in on-demand lifecycle for a CPU encoder without elastic VRAM: text leaves it unloaded, the first picture starts it, and idle unload stops its process. Set `"elastic": true` in an existing CPU `"vision"` section; `"elastic_idle_s"` keeps its existing default of 120 seconds.

## Related discussion

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for CPU vision, elastic encoders and on-demand loading; found no duplicate CPU-specific fix. Related GPU lifecycle work: #2196. The tool-returned-image path in #3174 is separate and is not changed here. No changes to defaults or engine architecture; this is a focused extension of the existing opt-in lifecycle.

## Approach

Allow CPU elastic startup independently of `vram_elastic`, and skip the VRAM reserve and free-VRAM probes when starting that CPU reader. Reuse the existing FIFO, idle timer and unload/restart paths. GPU readers still require `vram_elastic` and retain their existing reserve behavior. Without `vision.elastic: true`, eager and lazy startup remain unchanged.

Regression checks cover text-first loading, first/repeated pictures, idle unload and reload, no CPU VRAM calls, eager startup, and GPU eligibility/reserve behavior. The docs explain the CPU settings and load-time tradeoff. No personal configuration, model files, engine code or dependencies are included.

## Validation

Tested revision: `0fd7a70725de94e9fb847039666ad0973e7df781`, based on current `main` at `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta).
Environment: x86-64 Linux (Omarchy/Arch), Python 3.14.8, Ryzen 9 9950X, 60 GiB RAM, RTX 4090 24 GB. The hardware smoke used the released 0.1.45.3 picture reader in **CPU mode**, existing IQ3_S model shards and BF16 mmproj, 8 encoder threads, and synthetic 128×128 PNGs.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_vision_elastic serve.test_lifecycle serve.test_vram`: 26 tests, OK.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server serve.test_runconfig`: 350 tests, OK.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `python /tmp/strata-cpu-vision-http-smoke.py`, with `STRATA_TEST_CONFIG` pointing to the existing CPU-vision config: a local HTTP harness using the real `Vision` reader and the existing `VramEngine` text-engine fixture. A text request left `Vision.proc` unset; a red-square image started the real CPU reader and encoded; advancing `last_image_at` beyond the configured 120-second threshold and invoking the idle check stopped that process; another text request left it unloaded; a distinct blue-square image started a new process and encoded. Both `engine.vram()` and `Service.free_vram_mib()` were patched to raise on any call. Neither was called. All test processes were shut down.

Observed smoke output (request/timing lines omitted):

```text
PASS: first HTTP text request left CPU encoder unloaded
PASS: first HTTP image started and encoded on CPU
[strata] images: the CPU image encoder stopped after 120 s without a picture
"first_text_keeps_vision_unloaded": true
"idle_stops_process": true
"vram_resize_and_telemetry_calls": 0
"encoder_stopped_at_end": true
```

The unittest runs emitted ResourceWarnings for telemetry fixture files, HTTP errors and sockets; both runs completed with OK.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** full text-model image-answer generation or quality checks; GPU vision hardware execution; CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds (no engine or compiled-backend sources changed). The real smoke verifies CPU encoding and lifecycle with a fake text engine, not backend hardware compatibility or answer quality. No performance claim is made.

## Limits

The first picture after unload pays the encoder's load time. With the existing idle polling, a 120-second timeout normally unloads after about 120–150 seconds, later if a request owns the FIFO. Unloading ends the encoder process; existing embedding caches and reclaimable OS file cache may remain. This does not change tool-returned-image handling or fix the separate issue in #3174.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: the hyper-connection read's reduce keeps 8 loads in flight, its up step writes lo once
pulls.author: deriknel
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On the Arc Pro B70, the hyper-connection read (`gr`, 2 sites per layer) is one of the largest kernel classes in decode. Its reduce issues one load at a time, and its up step writes `lo` on every iteration. The variants that keep 8 loads in flight and write `lo` once already exist, but only behind `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS`, which bundles them with two layouts that run slower on the B70. This change makes the two variants the default without the slower layouts. Same output bits; decode about 0.7% faster here.

## Related discussion
none. A focused kernel change, no defaults outside these two kernels.

## Approach
`sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`, two launches:
- the down step's reduce launches `gr_down_reduce_kernel<true>`: the same 80 adds in the same order, with 8 loads issued ahead instead of waiting on each L2 load in turn;
- the up step launches `gr_up_multi_kernel<C, false, true>`: the per-token `lo` values are written by block 0 instead of by all 160 blocks (the same values).

Both variants were only reached under `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS` (on by default for the A-series), which also switches in a 480-group down kernel and an 8-column up step; together those lost 2% on two B70s, so they stay where they are. `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS` keeps its meaning.

## Validation
Setup for every run: `main` e88ee39d built for SYCL (AOT `bmg-g31`, oneAPI 2026.1, Compute Runtime 26.35.39758.10, IGC 2.41.5) in a container; host CachyOS, kernel 7.2.11, `xe`. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, layer split 26, Swift 1.5 Flash-Next IQ3_S with every expert in VRAM, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.6`, `--prefill 4096`. Each build has only this PR's commit on top of `main`. Greedy check: 5 fixed prompts (prose, code, maths, an edit, a story), temperature 0, 400 tokens, thinking off, compared character by character. Pipeline windows off; `main` and this change alternated on fresh engines, two runs each.

**Passed:**
- Decode, bench medians: `main` 83.2 / 82.8 (prose), 106.6 / 106.6 (code); this change 83.7 / 83.7 and 107.4 / 107.3 (+0.8% / +0.7%).
- Greedy text on the 5 prompts identical to `main`'s, both runs.
- `ctest` on both cards: the same 3 failures as on `main` (`gr_parity` among them, failing the same way without this change); `iq_parity` with fixtures, 0 failures.

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and Metal builds: the change is in `sycl/` only.

## Limits
A small gain. `gr_parity` fails on `main` as well (its `STRATA_QFUSE` case), so it does not check this change.

We investigated (myself and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code) and I reviewed the findings and ran every test on my two Arc Pro B70s on my CachyOS machine.

pulls.title: [Other] Let a trusted LAN serve without an API key via STRATA_ALLOW_KEYLESS_BIND env variable
pulls.author: dsenchankau
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Since v0.2.0-beta, the server started on `0.0.0.0` refuses with `a non-loopback bind requires an inference API key` and exit 2; Although `0.0.0.0` is not loopback, it's my local network, behind a firewall, and nothing else reaches it.

Now, if you set `STRATA_ALLOW_KEYLESS_BIND=1` in the environment where strata starts, both `strata serve` and `launch` checks let the keyless bind through. The server prints a warning at startup so a stray env var stays visible: `STRATA_ALLOW_KEYLESS_BIND is set: anyone who can reach this port can use the model`. Unset or empty, nothing changes, same refusal, same message.

## Approach

One helper, `keyless_bind_allowed()`, next to `api_key_of` in `serve/server.py`. Both gates call it: the server startup check and `_launch_plan` in `strata_cli/cli.py`, which already imports from `serve.server`. The gate checks the effective host, so it doesn't matter whether the host comes from the run config or from `--host`. It is an env var rather than a flag: the check runs in the process that starts the server, and a flag would need plumbing through launch, the TUI and the app. It is only read when the bind is non-loopback and no key was configured.

## Validation

Passed:

- `.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.terminal.test_profiles` — 22 tests, `OK`. The new `test_keyless_non_loopback_bind_needs_the_opt_in_env` plans a profile with `host=0.0.0.0`, expects the refusal, and expects the plan to pass with the env var set.
- `.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.terminal.test_launch` — `OK`.
- `.venv/bin/python -m py_compile serve/server.py strata_cli/cli.py` — no output (compiles).
- `STRATA_ALLOW_KEYLESS_BIND=1 python serve/server.py --engine strata --config <run config> --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1337` — the server started, no `[strata] a non-loopback bind requires an inference API key` error.

Failed:

- None observed.

Not run:

- N/A

## Limits

- The config JSON's `env` field doesn't help: it feeds the engine subprocess, the gate reads the server's own environment at startup.
- If the owner-host daemon starts the server, set the var in the daemon's environment.
- No `--allow-keyless` flag, nothing in the app or TUI.

pulls.title: [GUI] Add Optional Windows Tray For Local Model Control On 0.2.0
pulls.author: medking82
pulls.body: ## Problem and result Windows users need quick access to their local Strata server without keeping a console or browser open. This opt-in Tray adds a read-only client and a separately configured managed mode for model profiles, context, idle unload and explicit Preload/Unload. It is not installed or started by the default installer. ## Related discussion #2034. Continuation of #2035 after the tracker reset: GitHub refused to reopen the closed PR even after restoring its previous head, and the reset bot suggested a replacement. This candidate is rebased onto 0.2.0-beta `main` (`e88ee39d`). **Ready for review. Scope agreement for the managed feature is still requested.** The earlier issue proposed a narrower read-only client. No maintainer agreement on the expanded scope is assumed. The separate Local Model Extension scope is #3369. This Tray provides its optional single-owner protocol; the Extension UI stays in #3373. ## Approach All files are isolated under `tools/windows-tray/`. Existing engine, server, frontend, setup and default installation files are byte-identical to the base revision (`git diff e88ee39d -- . ':!tools/windows-tray'` is empty). The Tray forwards client authentication unchanged and owns only the processes in its private Windows Job. Lifecycle changes close admission and drain admitted requests before acting; occupied ports are refused. Startup and restart stay lazy. Managed mode uses the official context choices (8K, 32K, 64K, 128K, 200K, 256K, 384K, 512K), and Never/5/10/30-minute idle unload, preserving original profiles and saved settings. Selected/effective settings remain distinct. An optional `desktop_app` path adds Open Strata App and a separate App update metadata check using the official feed. App installation and signature verification stay in the App. Legacy engine staging is retained only for legacy assets; signed 0.2 component releases defer to the official component updater. The current official desktop icon is embedded. Production menu construction is shared with a native fixture renderer so the examples below come from real WinForms controls, not a recreated mockup. No personal configuration, model ID, private path or original user screenshot is included. This generic candidate has no Codex dependency or client-capacity synchronization. `app_extension` defaults to false and publishes no companion IPC files unless opted in. When enabled, it publishes fresh allowlisted owner metadata and claims one UUID/physical-model-bound context, idle, load or unload command into the existing serial worker. Identity is checked at execution. Durable terminal acknowledgments precede claim removal; interrupted claims are never replayed. The companion has no independent inference process or HTTP lifecycle bypass. ## Examples **These are anonymous simulated menu states**, rendered offscreen by the production `ManagedMenu` through WinForms `DrawToBitmap`. The fixture starts no Tray controller, server, App, updater or inference. Submenus are placed beside the main menu for readability. Captions and the official icon sit outside the controls. These images do not establish server health, installed updates or GPU behavior. **Managed Menu** **Official Context Choices** **Idle Unload** **Engine Updates** — signed component installation belongs to the official updater. **App Updates** — checks App metadata and opens the App to install. The added `screenshots/README.md` and `MenuExamples.cs` document reproducible generation. All five PNGs were visually inspected and have no text/EXIF metadata. ## Validation Windows x64, .NET Framework compiler v4, Python 3.12; candidate `ff69390e` on base `e88ee39d`. Commands below omit the local windowless-runner wrapper and use a disposable output/dependency directory. **Passed:** - Production, test and example WinForms executables compiled from the same production sources, manifest and official icon. `TrayTests.exe`: **81 checks passed**, including actual PerMonitorV2, loopback parsing, auth/redirect boundaries, diagnostic privacy, App metadata checks, menu/control states, all eight context choices and lifecycle disable states. - `TrayMenuExamples.exe --out `: five native PNGs generated and inspected, with anonymous fixture data. No runtime or model launched. - `python -B tools/windows-tray/managed/test_extension.py`: **15 new tests passed**, covering opt-in defaults, exactly-once file claims, queue/execution identity, all context/idle values, drain behavior, acknowledgment ordering, duplicates, interrupted recovery and truthful loaded/unknown states. - `python -B -m unittest -v test_managed.ConfigTests test_managed.UpdateTests test_managed.LifecycleTests.test_lazy_start_restart_and_update_do_not_preload test_managed.LifecycleTests.test_development_version_starts_but_update_requires_exact_version` from `tools/windows-tray/managed`: **12 affected existing tests passed**, with no server process launched. - The separate Extension's cross-language test consumed Node-produced commands through this exact Python IPC and observed terminal state without repeating commands. - The preceding `d2303a53` revision's full managed suite had **16 tests passed** using the base's unmodified official MockEngine and disposable streaming fixtures. This is prior evidence, not a newly rerun full suite. MockEngine always reports loaded and fixed 32768 context. - `git diff --check` passed; all changed paths are below `tools/windows-tray/`. **Failed:** - None unresolved in the final checks. The preceding full mock run initially needed the base's `jinja2` and `regex` dependencies; that run passed after adding those official dependencies in an isolated test directory, without changing production Python. **Not run:** - The four existing cases that launch a mock server were not rerun for this IPC/menu update. Real GPU cold load, generation, unload/idle timing or upgrade; Windows reboot/autostart; cross-monitor transitions; configured-App launch and App installer interaction remain unverified. No inference or model download was submitted. ## Limits Scope agreement and targeted Windows hardware acceptance remain outstanding. Signed component installation belongs to the official updater. This Tray does not provide a general upstream plugin API or native prepared-model registration. Read-only mode accepts no API key and reports authentication required for protected servers. Optional companion IPC state must remain private; stale running markers block replay until manually inspected.

pulls.title: [GUI] Forward Composer Effort To Supported API Models
pulls.author: medking82
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Manual chat with a saved reasoning API model displays the composer's selected effort, but `runRemoteTurn` drops it before constructing the outgoing request. The official Off/Low/Medium/High/Max choice now reaches supported OpenAI-chat models. Models with false or unknown reasoning support retain the provider default.

## Related discussion

None required for this focused host bug fix. Existing reasoning checks cover native/agent paths; this change covers direct saved-API chat.

## Approach

Carry `thinking` through the direct-chat path and use saved capability metadata or the host's cached server probe. Ignore capability claims supplied in a client selection. OpenAI-compatible requests map Off to `none` and Max to `high`; OpenRouter reuses the existing official `OPENROUTER_EFFORTS` mapping and `reasoning: { effort }` format, including Max to `xhigh`. No new UI levels are introduced. Authentication, history and cancellation remain in the existing request path.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- Windows, Node 24.18.0, base `e88ee39d`, submitted changes through `ab57c5da`: `node --test tests/api-reasoning-effort.test.mjs tests/model-providers.test.mjs tests/openrouter-reasoning.test.mjs` from `apps/host`, plus a separate successful rerun of `tests/model-providers.test.mjs` with the Windows PowerShell module path corrected. Combined result: 18 passed, 1 Harness-dependent test skipped.
- Direct API fixtures exercise all five choices, provider defaults, saved false/unknown capability, host-owned probes, ignored client capability overrides, OpenRouter's wire format, and unchanged Responses/Anthropic payloads. A disposable real host and mock API exercise 20 composer/model combinations without acquisition or live-model calls.
- Existing `tests/thinking-direct.test.mjs` checks passed; its implementation is unchanged.

**Failed:**

- Baseline regression: selecting Off reached the API without `reasoning_effort` instead of `none`.
- Follow-up regression exposed the direct OpenRouter format mismatch; the final patch uses the existing agent mapping.
- The Windows ACL helper initially failed under an inherited PowerShell 7 module path. The same check passed with the process-local Windows PowerShell module path; no repository or system policy was changed.

**Not run:**

- Live cloud or GPU inference. The real Harness integration test was skipped because a built Harness is not configured. No engine backend code changed.

## Limits

This applies to OpenAI-chat connections whose saved or probed metadata declares reasoning support. Responses and Anthropic keep their current defaults. Thinking budgets are not added to external API requests.

pulls.title: [GUI] Reuse Legacy Model Libraries Through A Valid Native Data Root
pulls.author: medking82
pulls.body:

## Related discussion

Related storage feedback: #3292. This fix addresses the retained legacy HOME/models path specifically; it does not resolve every imported-model recognition problem in that report.

## Approach

Translate only an existing legacy model library, including a saved or environment-selected copy of that exact path. Use a Windows junction or directory symlink for the native layout. Refuse a conflicting destination. Explicit custom libraries and fresh defaults keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

No model files are moved, copied or downloaded by this fix. Existing arbitrary custom directories remain subject to native setup's existing rules. The alias requires permission to create a directory link at the chosen Strata home.

pulls.title: [Other] setup: lock the n-gram table in RAM only when the experts still fit
pulls.author: dsenchankau
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

Since v0.2.0-beta setup sometimes writes `--ple-io ram` on SSD PCs: the model's n-gram table is locked in RAM so a new prompt does not wait for its table rows from the disk. It only does this when a RAM check says there is room, but for the two 4-bit Unsloth files (`UD-IQ4_XS`, `UD-Q4_K_XL`) that check used the wrong number. It counted the model with its minimum requirement: the RAM it needs when part of its experts live on disk. On those same machines setup had just chosen the mode that keeps every expert in RAM, so both together do not fit.

I hit this myself on my 96 GB machine (`ram_gb()` sees 94) with UD-Q4_K_XL: fully loaded, with every expert resident, RAM sits at 91.5 GB — there is plainly no room for the 29 GB table on top. The engine then streamed experts from the model files and decode dropped from roughly 40 t/s to 15-20 t/s. A 96 GB machine gets the wrong flag with both 4-bit files, a 128 GB machine with UD-Q4_K_XL. After this change those machines read the table from disk and keep the experts in RAM.

The rotating-disk version of the rule had the same wrong number and pushed the experts onto the slowest storage possible, so I fixed it the same way.

### Approach

Both rules now work out what the install puts in RAM the same way the code above them does when it picks the all-in-RAM mode: the whole expert set plus the usual allowance beside it. If the table and the existing spare do not fit on top of that, setup leaves the table on disk.

Nothing changed for the other model families, their numbers were already right, and the Windows path never reaches this code. The bigger Unsloth files move by under a GB, which changes nothing.

Machines that were already set up by v0.2.0-beta keep the flag they got: run setup again, or drop `--ple-io`, `ram` from the config's args by hand.

### Validation (Linux, Python 3.12.3)

**Passed**

- Unit tests (mocked PC, no GPU needed):

  ```
  python3 -m unittest tools.test_setup_choices             # 55 tests, all OK
  python3 -m unittest tools.test_setup_risk tools.test_setup_menu tools.test_setup_sycl   # all OK
  python3 -m unittest tools.test_setup_qwen36 tools.test_setup_gyro                       # all OK
  ```

  The new tests cover both 4-bit files on machines from 32 to 192 GB, on an SSD and on a hard disk, and they finally show the rule the big sizes' real 54 GB table (before, every test took the 29 GB fallback). I also checked the tests actually catch the bug: copied onto the commit before the fix they fail (UD-IQ4_XS on a 96 GB machine wrongly gets `--ple-io ram`), and they pass here.

- Ran `setup.sh` on my own PC (96 GB) for both UD-IQ4_XS and UD-Q4_K_XL. The configs they write no longer have the wrong `--ple-io ram` entry, and the rest of the config is unchanged — still the mode that keeps every expert in RAM. With the fixed config decode is back to roughly 40 t/s, against 15-20 t/s before. My machine, everyday use, not a formal benchmark run.

- Engine test suite (C++, untouched by this PR, ran it as a regression check):

  ```
  ctest --test-dir build-tests --output-on-failure
  ```

  151 of 157 passed (96%), exactly the same as the latest master commit on this machine. Same six failures with and without my change (`ple_parity`, `ggml_tq_overlay`, `native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2`, `isa_guard_check`). Same one skip (`expert_multi_test`). 215 s.

**Failed**

Nothing among the commands above.

**Not run**

- The other quant sizes on real hardware — the RAM check change is the same code for all of them, but I only ran mine.
- Windows and WSL — the code does not run there.
- The golden-config suite fails the same on master in our fork (a fork-local difference), so I did not count it either way.

### Limits

The check is still an estimate.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RX 7900 XT 20 GB, UD-Q5_K_XL: v0.1.44.1 vs v0.2.0-beta
pulls.author: loeeeee
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Results-only benchmark report from an RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100) on Linux with Unsloth UD-Q5_K_XL at 262K, all experts in RAM. This PR was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; I rebased it on current `main` and re-ran the measurements on v0.2.0-beta as the reset message asked. It now carries two reports:

- `2026-10-15-community-rx-7900-xt-ud-q5-k-xl` (v0.1.44.1): setup's default configuration vs the same plus `--vram-reserve-mib 1024 --prefill auto:32768`, same day. Unchanged from the original submission.
- `2026-10-20-community-rx-7900-xt-ud-q5-k-xl-0.2.0-beta` (new): the tuned configuration measured the same day on v0.1.44.1 and then on v0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3), `tools/strata_bench.py --runs 3 --long`, medians:

| | v0.1.44.1 | v0.2.0-beta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4K / 16K / 32K prompt, tok/s | 226 / 833 / 902 | 828 / 1,153 / 1,050 |
| short-chat decode, tok/s | 16.2 | 18.6 |
| agent follow-up first token, s | 5.79 | 5.67 |

Prompt throughput at 16K and 32K is higher and steadier on v0.2.0-beta (+38 % / +16 % in the medians); decode and agent turns are not different beyond the run ranges. The v0.1.44.1 4K run was noisy (172-311 tok/s) and well below the 2026-10-15 result on the same build (577), so the 4K difference is not a speedup claim.

## Related discussion
Continues #2705, which the maintainer closed in the 0.2.0-beta reset ("closed here does not mean rejected"). GitHub would not reopen it after the rebase, so this is the same branch as a new PR. Results-only, as `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` describes; no engine changes.

## Approach
New report folder with a comparison README, the tool's own README and `results.json` for each build, one `COMMUNITY.md` row and one `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` entry. The tool's output was edited in two places only: the GPU name (it printed "AMD Radeon") and the service user name that its sanitizer replaced in the Strata version line.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --runs 3 --long` against the running server, once on v0.1.44.1 and once on v0.2.0-beta, same machine and configuration, 2026-10-20. No failed requests in either. Per-request data in each folder's `results.json`.
- Update to v0.2.0-beta via `setup.sh --backend hip` (source build, ROCm 7.2.4): server loaded, engine log "session is up (engine 0.1.45.3)".
- Hand-run pilot of `docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md` (draft; schedule, settings, fixtures and scoring followed by hand with `protocol-pilot/scripts/pilot.py`), two complete runs on a freshly restarted engine each, v0.2.0-beta only: **12/12 sanity checks in both runs** (4 JSON, 4 retrieval at 4K/16K, 4 tool calls), no failed requests, 0 reused prompt tokens in the performance requests, 7 min required stages. Optional concurrency on the one-slot server (queued, aggregate 18-20.5 tok/s, equal to one stream).
- `tools/needle_bench.py` at 32K and 124K prompts, depths 10/50/90: 6/6 found in both runs.
- Memory/clock telemetry sampled every ~2 s across run 2 (574 rows): VRAM 19.3 of 20.0 GiB steady, host RAM 97-98.5 of 128 GiB, shader clock median 2.56 GHz, PCIe Gen4 x16, power median 210 W.

**Failed:**
- First v0.2.0-beta setup link failed (`undefined reference: sqrtf@GLIBC_2.43` from librocblas) because the CMake cache in `build-hip` still pointed at the previous ROCm (7.2.3) and glibc. Moving `build-hip` aside and rerunning fixed it. Noted in the report; I did not investigate whether setup should detect a changed ROCm root.
- A second setup run failed copying into `engine/strata` ("Text file busy") while the server was running; stopping the server first fixed it.

**Not run:**
- The draft protocol as a conforming run: no runner, approved fixture bundle or JSON schema exists yet, so the pilot is explicitly nonconforming (deviations listed in `protocol-pilot/README.md`: unpinned tokenizer/template, resolved server config and seed handling not verified, model file hashes not recorded, flat result structure).
- The protocol pilot on v0.1.44.1, so the pilot supports no before/after claim; 262K prompts; telemetry for run 1 (sampler PATH bug, fixed for run 2); other backends (this is one AMD box, and no engine change is proposed, so no builds beyond the HIP one above).

## Limits
The before/after comparison is one session per build, not a controlled A/B; the protocol pilot (v0.2.0-beta only, two replicate runs on the same machine) is nonconforming and not a hardware replication. The OS update moved nixpkgs ROCm 7.2.3 -> 7.2.4 between the two runs, so the Strata tag and ROCm are changed together. The machine is shared with coding agents, background load was not controlled, and the cause of the baseline's noise is unknown.

pulls.title: [GUI] Add a paired iPhone companion for Mac conversations
pulls.author: jorge123255
pulls.body: ## Problem and result Strata's Mac conversations currently cannot be opened and continued from a native iPhone app. This adds an optional SwiftUI companion using Strata's emerald, charcoal and white palette. After pairing, the phone shows the Mac's existing history, expandable Thinking, ordered progress and browser/tool activity, and can continue that same conversation, answer approvals or Stop its work. Inference remains on the Mac or its configured provider. ## Related discussion Scope proposal: #3346. **Runtime dependency: #3347**, which supplies opt-in Mac pairing and the shared-conversation API. This branch contains the native client only, starts from the same upstream base, and does not duplicate that PR's Mac changes. Maintainer agreement is pending; both submissions remain drafts for scope and implementation review. ## Approach - Pair with a five-minute, one-use QR invitation or manual entry. Pin the exact TLS certificate before sending credentials, reject redirects, and save the connection in the device-only Keychain. Camera access is optional; local-network access is required. - Reopen and continue Mac conversations with their existing model, workspace and permission mode. New conversations use the Mac's default workspace and ask before actions. Earlier private phone-only conversations retain their text-only continuation path. - Refresh the selected chat in the foreground; show Thinking, reply paragraphs, progress groups, browser/tool cards and pending approvals in their recorded order. Keep Mac work running when the phone leaves the app. Discard stale responses after switching or disconnecting. - Include a portable synthetic fixture using the real HTTPS bridge and authentication, plus unit/UI coverage. No personal signing team, provisioning profile, pairing credentials or local deployment reports are included. Build and signing instructions are in `apps/ios/README.md`. ## Validation Fresh checks at **680bc505ba318ab75367be25efc579132f1d538a**, based on upstream **e88ee39d**, using the Mac bridge at **818ecf4c**. Subsequent changes on this branch are documentation and a public synthetic UI preview only; application code, project settings, fixture and tests are unchanged. Environment: **macOS 26.5 arm64, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Node 26.0.0, iOS 26.5 Simulator / iPhone 17 Pro**. **Passed:** - Simulator build through XcodeBuildMCP `build_sim({})`: zero warnings or errors. Effective defaults: project `apps/ios/StrataMobile.xcodeproj`, scheme `StrataMobile`, Debug configuration, iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5 selected by its local simulator ID, and DerivedData `apps/ios/build`. - Full unit target through XcodeBuildMCP `test_sim`, with `extraArgs: ["-only-testing:StrataMobileTests", "-parallel-testing-enabled", "NO"]`: **26 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the explicitly optional live TLS test without an invitation. - The repository's portable fixture command below: **1 full workflow passed, 0 failed**; test body 76.839 seconds. It verified actual TLS pairing, saved history, live Thinking and its recorded panel, ordered progress, browser activity, Allow/Deny, continuation, Stop and relaunch. The wrapper's XCTest environment forwarding and owned-process/temporary-key cleanup also completed successfully. ```sh # Set MAC_CHECKOUT to the separate Mac PR checkout, then run from this checkout. STRATA_TEST_BRIDGE_MODULE="$MAC_CHECKOUT/apps/companion-bridge/bridge.mjs" \ STRATA_TEST_DERIVED_DATA=apps/ios/build \ node apps/ios/test-support/shared-conversation-fixture.mjs --test \ 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' ``` The measured fixture run selected that simulator by its local ID; the command above uses its portable name and substitutes the matching checkout path. The fixture supplies synthetic host data and does not start a real model, browser or desktop agent. See `apps/ios/test-support/README.md` for the reproducible workflow and simulator-pairing side effect. Preview captured from that synthetic workflow: **Failed:** None in these fresh checks. **Not run:** Physical iPhone interaction or camera pairing against this sanitized branch; iOS 17 or iPad runtime acceptance; App Store/distribution signing; real-model inference or real browser control. Earlier development installation of the complete fork on an iPhone is separate from acceptance of these split upstream revisions. ## Limits Requires the Mac support in #3347 and iOS 17 or later. Initial pairing uses the same trusted local network. Foreground polling does not provide background notifications or relay access. Browser cards report actions/results; they do not stream the Mac's screen. The app inherits the paired Mac conversation's permissions, including a trusted phone's ability to answer approvals. Contributors must select their own signing team/profile for device installation.

pulls.title: [GUI] Add opt-in Mac pairing and shared iPhone conversations
pulls.author: jorge123255
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A Mac conversation currently cannot be securely reopened and continued by a paired native iPhone client. This adds opt-in **Pair iPhone** in the sidebar and Settings, plus shared history, existing-session continuation, visible Thinking/progress, browser/tool activity, approvals and Stop. Closing the phone leaves the Mac's work running.

## Related discussion

Scope proposal: #3346. Maintainer agreement is pending; this PR is a draft for scope and implementation discussion. The native iPhone client is submitted separately in #3348 and depends on this API. Both branches start from the same upstream base so their diffs can be reviewed independently; the client needs this Mac support at runtime.

## Approach

- Keep the inference host on loopback. Start the companion's authenticated HTTPS listener only after explicit enablement; use certificate-pinned, expiring one-use invitations and revocable per-device token hashes.
- Import desktop history after opt-in and persist a shared catalog independently of any connected screen. Stable chat/message IDs, revision checks, deletion tombstones and turn-bound callbacks prevent stale caches or delayed work from replacing a newer turn. A conversation already running before first enablement is imported when that response finishes.
- Continue with the Mac chat's existing model, folder and permissions. Expose only bounded controls and display data; omit provider configuration, raw tool arguments and runtime protocol. Existing private phone-only routes remain compatible. Paired devices are trusted to read the shared catalog and answer its pending approvals.
- Stage the bridge and a local Core Image QR helper through normal desktop builds. Packaged Python disables bytecode writes to preserve signed application contents; source Python behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

Fresh checks at **818ecf4c**, based on upstream **e88ee39d**, on **macOS 26.5 arm64, Node 24.12.0, Xcode 26.6**. Host dependencies matched the existing lockfile installation.

**Passed:**

```sh
/Applications/Strata.app/Contents/Resources/node/node --test apps/companion-bridge/test/*.test.mjs
# 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

STRATA_HARNESS_DIR=/Applications/Strata.app/Contents/Resources/harness \
  /Applications/Strata.app/Contents/Resources/node/node --test \
  apps/host/tests/conversations.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/conversation-migration.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/conversation-agent.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/conversation-events.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/conversation-routes.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/companion.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/companion-routes.test.mjs \
  apps/host/tests/packaged-python-cache.test.mjs
# 48 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

npm --prefix apps/host run typecheck
npm --prefix apps/desktop run build:ui
git diff --check
```

The focused host run includes real shipped Harness session continuity/detach with scripted inference, private event/origin restrictions, no capture before opt-in, migration during an active response, stale-turn/Stop races, reasoning timing, and real bundled-Python cache isolation. The UI build also compiled and signed the QR helper. Its existing large-chunk warning remains.

**Failed:**

None in the fresh checks above. Earlier broad full-feature development runs had nine failure locations reproduced on their clean dependency-matched baseline; this PR does not claim a clean complete host suite.

**Not run:**

The full host suite on this split revision; fresh Tauri app/installer packaging, Developer ID signing or notarization; Windows/Linux desktop acceptance; physical iPhone interaction against this exact split branch; native local-model inference. No engine/GPU backend code changes or performance claims are included.

## Limits

Initial support is local-network Mac pairing. Polling follows the selected conversation while the phone is active. Browser cards show actions and results rather than browser pixels. Earlier installed full-feature fork checks are separate from acceptance of these split upstream revisions. Release packaging and the permission/API boundary need maintainer review before this draft is ready.

pulls.title: [Engine] rocBLAS table for gfx1030 with rocBLAS 5.4.0 (TheRock gfx103X-all 7.13 wheels): short follow-up prompts 12% faster
pulls.author: elightcap
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The rocBLAS tables in `tools/hip` cover gfx1030 with rocBLAS 5.6.0.8d1ae90e (ROCm 10.0.0) only. An RX 6000 engine built
against TheRock's `gfx103X-all` 7.13.0a20260515 wheels - what setup installs into `.venv` when the PC has no system
ROCm 7 (`ROCM_FAMILY_PINS`), and what the `rx6900` package of #3329 carries - loads rocBLAS 5.4.0.ad84daa81c, so with
`STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` the engine logs

```
prefill gemm: cannot open rocBLAS tuning file (.../tools/hip/gfx1030-rocblas-5.4.0.ad84daa81c.txt); rocBLAS's default kernels run
```

This adds that table, made with `tools/hip/tune_rocblas` on an RX 6900 XT against that rocBLAS, and names it in
docs/AMD_HIP.md. With it a 268-395-token follow-up on a cached conversation reads 11.7% faster (median), every pair
10-13%; longer fresh prompts change little (numbers below).

Related: #3329 (the package; independent of this PR). Its docs sentence "The package's rocBLAS (5.4.0) has no table in
`tools/hip` yet" becomes stale once both are merged; I will update whichever lands second.

## Approach

Data only: the engine already picks `<arch>-rocblas-<version>.txt` from `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING` for its own rocBLAS
build and refuses any other, and setup already points `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING` at `tools/hip` when a table for the
card's arch exists. Nothing changes for an engine on another rocBLAS build (it keeps refusing this file) or without
`STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` (the table serves that route only). The packaged engines do not carry `tools/hip` tables
yet, so a Terminal user gets it only with `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING` set by hand until packaging includes the tables.

`tune_rocblas` was built from this tree against the wheels' rocBLAS and run with the rx6900 package's libraries
(`LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<package>`; `ldd` shows its `librocblas.so.5` and `libamdhip64.so.7`). It ran one token bucket per
process (`--tokens 256`, ..., `--tokens 4096`) and the 8192 bucket one shape per process (`--case 8192,N,K,N` for the
14 default shapes), with pauses between runs; every row is one shape at one bucket, so the parts were merged in the
tuner's own order under one header. 112 rows (the same shape/bucket keys as the 5.6.0 table), 79 with a solution,
33 `default`.

## Validation

RX 6900 XT 16 GB (gfx1030), Ryzen 9 5950X, 128 GB DDR4, Arch Linux; engine 0.1.45.3 (e88ee39d), the rx6900 package of
#3329 (rocBLAS 5.4.0.ad84daa81c from `rocm[libraries,devel]==7.13.0a20260515`).

**Passed**

- `hip_prefill_rocblas_gemm` built from this tree against the same rocBLAS, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`:
  `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1030-rocblas-5.4.0.ad84daa81c.txt` and `=tools/hip` (the engine's own pick): 4 of
  4 cases PASS, "outputs match hipBLASEx within FP16 rounding" (relative_l2 0.000208, max_abs 0.00196, 4 ulp = 0.0156),
  exit 0. With the 5.6.0 table: "tuning table rejected: rocBLAS version mismatch: file=5.6.0.8d1ae90e
  runtime=5.4.0.ad84daa81c", exit 0.
- The engine with the table: `prefill gemm: rocBLAS tuning enabled (112 rows, 79 with a solution, gfx1030, rocBLAS
  5.4.0.ad84daa81c)`.
- A/B on the server, UD-Q4_K_XL, the same settings in both arms except `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING=tools/hip`
  (`STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1 STRATA_SH_STREAM=1 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto
  STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1`, `--resident-budget-gib 71 --pcie-frac 0.35 --mtp-draft-vocab data/draft_vocab_en.bin
  --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072 --spec 4`). Arms in the order without, with, with, without, each on
  a fresh server; per arm 3 rounds of a fresh prompt, a follow-up on it and a fresh longer prompt, different text per
  round, the same text in both arms. Server prompt times in ms:

  | prompt | without the table | with the table | median |
  |---|---|---|---|
