pulls.title: [Engine] conversation cache: park and restore conversations through session files (--conversation-cache-disk-mib)
pulls.author: dsenchankau
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

I took this PR idea from [Maya](https://github.com/mw00/project-maya), a GLM5.3-Flash fork of Strata, where the disk conversation cache is on by default.

Right now the conversation cache has 2 options: keep it in RAM, or don't use it at all.

RAM is fine with a smaller quant (IQ3_S) and plenty of system RAM (96GB with that quant). It gets tight with a bigger quant like UD-Q4_K_XL, or with less system RAM.

UD-Q4_K_XL's experts are way bigger, and after startup the OS overhead + model + engine + coding harness have already eaten (almost) all the RAM. That leaves you two bad options: offload some experts to disk and lose decode and prefill speed, or skip the RAM cache and re-process the prompt over and over (slower the bigger the model gets).

For performance, the better move is to move the conversation cache to disk and keep more of the model's experts in RAM.

Without a cache, a conversation that comes back re-reads its whole prompt. With the cache on disk it's read back from its file and picks up where it left off. The re-reading gets worse the longer the session runs, but reading from the file stays about as cheap no matter how long it's been, so the disk cache pays off across a working session. You notice it most when you're using subagents a lot and bouncing between the main session and side ones. I measured the park/restore part (see Validation); I didn't run a reprocessing-vs-restore timing test, so I'm not putting a speedup number on it.

With this change, `--conversation-cache-disk-mib N` parks conversations into `conv-*.sess` files under `<pack>/conversation_cache`, and the budget counts the file bytes, so a lot more stay parked than would fit in RAM. A conversation that comes back on a later turn (same run, or after a restart) is read back from its file and continues from its own state instead of re-reading its prompt. It's off by default, the way the repo wants new features.

## Approach

- `include/strata/core/conversation_cache.hpp` - disk mode: `enable_disk`, `put_disk` (budget counts file bytes), the slim folder-index entry, and the budget check that refuses an oversized entry before it touches anything already parked.
- `src/core/conversation_file.{hpp,cpp}` - meta-only read (`session_file_read_meta`) and the startup folder scan (`conversation_cache_index`) that keeps this model's fresh `conv-*.sess` and deletes foreign, stale or unreadable files. Reuses the session-file format that's already there.
- `src/program/generate.cpp` - the park and restore calls in the serve loop, plus the guards that skip parking (snapshot bigger than the whole budget, and RAM admission).
- `include/strata/core/{conversation_snapshot.hpp,session_save_reclaim.hpp}`, `src/core/conversation_state.cpp` - the meta/checkpoint plumbing the index and restore need.
- No `serve/` change: the engine flags go straight through the run-config `args`, so `server.py` is untouched.
- Tests: a disk-mode budget-refusal check in `conversation_cache_test.cpp`; `conversation_file_test.cpp` already covers the meta-only read and the folder scan.
- `docs/DETAILS.md` - the flag and the measured numbers.

## Validation

Revision `1aa35f01`. Environment: Linux `home-pc 7.0.0-38-generic #38~24.04.4-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC x86_64`, RTX 4080 SUPER (driver 615.71.10), CMake 3.28.3, Ninja 1.11.1, CUDA 13.4, Python 3.12.3.

Passed:

- Build (CUDA backend only; the change is common code, no backend sources or `#ifdef`):

  ```sh
  cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build-tests -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_CONVERSATION_TESTS=ON \
    -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89
  cmake --build build-tests -j "$(nproc)"
  ```

- The disk-cache unit tests (CPU-only), 5/5: `conversation_cache_test` (4789 checks), `conversation_file_test` (217 checks), plus `conversation_split_failure_test`, `conversation_memory_test` and `session_save_reclaim_test`:

  ```sh
  ctest --test-dir build-tests -R 'conversation_(cache|split_failure|memory|file)_test|session_save_reclaim_test' --output-on-failure
  ```

  5/5 passed, 1.46s.

- The engine conversation tests, 3/3. `conversation_snapshot_test` uses the GPU (passed in 1.11s on an idle card; it skips with code 77 when it can't get one). `conversation_validation_test` and `conversation_transfer_test` run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`:

  ```sh
  ctest --test-dir build-tests -R 'conversation_(snapshot|validation|transfer)_test' --output-on-failure
  ```

  3/3 passed, 1.17s.

- Full suite. `ctest --test-dir build-tests --output-on-failure` on the branch gives the same result as master: 96% passed, 6 failed out of 157, 1 skipped (`expert_multi_test`). Those 6 are the usual environment/hardware ones on both branches (`ple_parity` and `tq_cpu_parity` want fixtures that aren't in the published source; `ggml_tq_overlay`, `native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` want AMD/trellis hardware; `isa_guard_check` is a no-ISA check). So nothing new broke. Run this on a free GPU, or `conversation_snapshot_test` OOMs on whatever else is using the card.

- Engine run on one RTX 4080 SUPER, IQ3_S pack, greedy. I launched the model the normal way from its config, adding only `--conversation-cache-disk-mib 16384` to the run-config `args`:

  ```
  .venv/bin/python serve/server.py --engine strata --config strata-iq3_s.json --port 1337
  ```

  It parked `1962 tokens to disk (266,114,352 bytes)`, I restarted it, and it took back the same 1962 tokens from disk. The next turn only read the new part (`cached_tokens 1962`, `prompt_n 17`). The guards hold too: a snapshot bigger than the whole budget is refused and the folder stays empty, foreign files and a hand-edited `conv-hacked-9.sess` are deleted at startup, and `--conversation-cache-days 0` empties the folder.

- serve suite:

  ```sh
  PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s serve
  ```

  881 run, 14 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure (`test_lifeline`: "the child outlived a killed server") is a process-watcher timing race. It's not from this change: `git diff upstream/main HEAD -- serve/` is empty, so I touched no serve file, and the test fails the same on master.

Failed: nothing here is caused by this change. The 6 C++ failures above are the same environment/hardware ones master has, with or without the branch, and the serve `test_lifeline` failure is a watcher race in a file this PR doesn't touch.

Not run: HIP and SYCL, build and run - I don't have AMD hardware. The change is common code only (no backend sources, no `#ifdef`), so it should be backend-agnostic, but that's me reading the code, not a build - call it unconfirmed static analysis. Someone with that hardware should build it, and run it once on each if they can. Metal I didn't build or run. The park/restore numbers above are NVIDIA/CUDA only.

## Limits

The park/restore measurement is one pack on one card (RTX 4080 SUPER). I'm not claiming a speedup on other hardware or quants beyond the reasoning above. The disk cache is opt-in, and I didn't change the RAM cache path or how its budget is counted. HIP and SYCL are unverified because I have no hardware for them.

pulls.title: [Other] serve: accept pi's three thinking-budget field names as aliases
pulls.author: shizhx
pulls.body:
Problem and result: pi's `compat.thinkingTokenBudgetField` only allows
`thinking_token_budget` (vLLM), `thinking_budget` (Qwen/DashScope/SGLang) and
`thinking_budget_tokens` (llama.cpp), but #123's thinking budget was only readable
from `reasoning_budget_tokens`, so a pi client's budget was silently ignored - the
model thought its full length instead of being wrapped up at N tokens. After this
change all three names work exactly like `reasoning_budget_tokens` on the three
chat routes. Related: issue #123 #984.

## Summary

```diff
_post (serve/server.py)
  req = json.loads(body)
  if path in chat routes:
    self.record = svc.begin_request(path, req)
+   if req.get("reasoning_budget_tokens") is None:
+     first of thinking_token_budget / thinking_budget / thinking_budget_tokens
+       -> req["reasoning_budget_tokens"]
  dispatch -> _responses / _openai / _anthropic
    svc.reasoning_budget(req)      # existing: reads the native name, 400 on a non-integer
```

One commit, 3 files, +49/-1 (`serve/server.py` alias copy, `serve/test_server.py`
4 tests, `docs/DETAILS.md` the budget bullet). A request that sends none of the
three names goes through the added lookups unmodified: no mutation, no config,
engine or response change, so the default path is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on base e88ee39d the three names are silently ignored

  ```text
  # fake-engine suite: the new tests against the unpatched server
  FAIL: test_the_budget_alias_field_names
  AssertionError: 'Let me think step by step about two plus two. ...' !=
                  'Let me think step by\n\nI have thought about this long enough ...'
  FAIL: test_a_bad_alias_is_a_400
  AssertionError: 200 != 400 : ('thinking_token_budget', 1.5, ...)
  Ran 23 tests in 13.215s - FAILED (failures=2)
  ```
- **After:** e88ee39d + this commit

  ```text
  test_the_budget_alias_field_names               red -> green
  test_a_bad_alias_is_a_400                       red -> green
  test_the_request_s_own_budget_wins_over_the_aliases   green (precedence guard)
  test_the_alias_field_order_wins                 green (precedence guard)
  Ran 23 tests in 13.231s - OK                    # serve.test_server.ThinkingBudget
  Ran 885 tests in 377.483s - OK (skipped=14)     # full serve suite, CI's command
  ```

  live on :4000 (real IQ3_S model, 2x RTX 2080 Ti), prompt "What is 17*23? ...",
  budget 20:

  ```text
  no budget (baseline)  200 finish=stop reasoning_chars=183, no wrap-up
  native                200 finish=stop wrapped=True reasoning_chars=181 answer='17 × 23 = 391'
  thinking_token_budget 200 finish=stop wrapped=True reasoning_chars=134 answer='17 × 23\n...'
  thinking_budget       200 finish=stop wrapped=True reasoning_chars=178 answer='17 × 23:...'
  thinking_budget_tokens200 finish=stop wrapped=True reasoning_chars=134 answer='...'
  bad alias (1.5)       400 reasoning_budget_tokens=1.5: expected a whole number of tokens
  ```

  Each alias wraps the thinking at 20 (wrap-up marker, answer after, finish stop)
  exactly like the native field; the response shape is unchanged.

## Approach

The alias copy happens once, at the request entry (`_post`, after `begin_request`,
before dispatch), so every downstream read - `Service.reasoning_budget` on all
three routes, including `/v1/responses` - sees the native name and keeps the
existing whole-number validation (a bad alias is the same 400). Precedence is
deterministic: the request's own `reasoning_budget_tokens` wins over all aliases;
among the aliases the fixed order `thinking_token_budget` > `thinking_budget` >
`thinking_budget_tokens` does. The patch applies verbatim onto e88ee39d: `do_POST`'s
body moved to `_post` and the req parse now happens after `reserve_inference`, but
the insertion point and the budget's read path are unchanged.

## Validation

Revision e88ee39d + 2b336465, Python 3.13.5,
Linux x86-64, 2x RTX 2080 Ti, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S:

- Passed:
  - `.venv/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_server.ThinkingBudget -v` - red
    before (the alias-wrap and bad-alias-400 tests fail on base; the two
    precedence tests pass since the native field already wins when the aliases
    are ignored) / green after, 23 OK
  - `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'` (CI's
    command): 885 OK (14 skipped)
  - live requests on :4000 (`strata serve --profile strata-iq3_s.json`, the
    patched tree): see Evidence
- Failed: none observed
- Not run: no C++ backend is touched (serve/ Python only), so no CUDA/HIP/SYCL
  builds; the live check used the OpenAI route - the Anthropic route and
  `/v1/responses` are covered by the suite's fake-engine tests only

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way - revert the one commit; no data, schema, config or feed
migration.

**Blast Radius:** request handling on the three chat routes. A client that sends
none of the three names is unaffected (lookups only, no mutation); the only
behavior change is that a previously-ignored field now does what its name says.

## Limits

- Several aliases at once: the first of the fixed order does (documented in
  DETAILS.md).
- The aliases apply on all three chat routes, so an Anthropic body carrying a
  top-level `thinking_budget` is aliased too, same as the native field's
  behavior there.
- The live check covered one model (IQ3_S) and one prompt family; the routes and
  response shapes are covered by the suite.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 4090 Laptop: EXL3 2-bit worker comparison
pulls.author: delirious6423
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Community measurements for a 16 GB RTX 4090 Laptop + i7-13700HX running EXL3 `2.05bpw_h8`: ten versus seven CPU workers on the same modified fork binary.

- Fixed-prompt median decode: **+3.3–11.4%**; built-in agent follow-ups: **48.0 → 53.4 tok/s**.
- Short chat regressed: **30.1 → 28.9 tok/s**. Prefill changed little.

[Report and per-request evidence](bench/results/2026-10-20-community-rtx-4090-laptop-exl3-2bit/README.md).

## Related discussion

#1764 supplies the EXL3 context; it closed unmerged during the tracker reset. This is new benchmark evidence, not a request to merge that engine proposal.

## Approach

Adds one results folder only: a 903-word report, sanitized measurements/logs/configurations, provenance and reproduction inputs. Source patches are historical evidence inside that folder, not applied engine changes. No default, engine or headline-performance changes.

## Validation

**Passed:** Offline checks on Linux against the staged report: all 25 files match the reviewed draft; artifact hashes match; all 90 fixed-suite summary statistics recomputed from 30 measured requests; fixed/HTTP table values agree with saved data; links resolve; private-path/common credential-pattern scan clean. Evidence patch was also applied to a temporary archive of `fa21db8` and reproduced the modified source; temporary tree removed.

Recheck artifact hashes from the report directory:

```sh
python3 -c 'import hashlib,json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("."); m=json.loads((p/"provenance.json").read_text()); assert all(hashlib.sha256((p/n).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==v["shared_sha256"] for n,v in m["exports"].items()); print("PASS: artifact hashes")'
```

**Failed:** No report-consistency failures remain. Historical larger-cache/miss-sharing candidates failed the equivalence gate and are excluded from the selected results. Greedy generation matched only **2/15** control traces, despite matching the fixed-set quality checks.

**Not run:** No inference, GPU builds or VM/app tests during report preparation; this changes evidence/docs only. Original measurements are dated 2026-10-20 on fork `fa21db8` plus recorded patches, engine `0.1.45`—not current upstream.

## Limits

Q8 dense projections, INT8 KV and MTP; not all-EXL3. Three repeats per fixed length, uncontrolled background state, workload-dependent continuations; no significance or task-accuracy claim. Original MTP preparation details and full prompt-logit arrays are not included. Reproduction gaps are explicit. This is not a result under the draft standard benchmark protocol.

pulls.title: [Other] Read conversation-cache log backlogs without dropping events
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Issue #3048 can drop earlier conversation-cache events when more than one MiB arrives between monitor polls. The observer now advances through a captured end of file in bounded chunks, commits only complete lines, and retains a partial line for the next poll.

## Related discussion

Continues #3050 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original passed the new format check, but GitHub refused to reopen the rebased branch; [the reset bot](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3050#issuecomment-6282596517) explicitly suggested a new linked pull request.

Fixes #3048.

## Approach

- Replace the last-MiB seek with bounded sequential chunks in `serve/server.py`.
- Commit the byte cursor only through complete lines so interrupted writes and read errors retry safely.
- Add local backlog, chunk-boundary, interrupted-read, and local HTTP regression coverage in `serve/test_cache_log_backlog.py`.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `90ca8acc79242e18f954e71a4c570a4ee8887f41` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_cache_log_backlog.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.
 `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog` (7 tests); `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_server serve.test_prometheus` (357 tests, 3 skipped); `python -m py_compile serve/server.py`; `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:** Red reproduction used `git restore --source=e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211 -- serve/server.py`, then `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog`, then `git restore --source=HEAD -- serve/server.py`. The test ran 7 tests and failed 8 assertions, covering lost early events, chunk crossings, partial-line retry, and local `/metrics` catch-up.

**Not run:** Native backend builds and real GPU/model tests. Only Python observer code changed. The Python 3.14.3 test environment had no Ruff; the separate Python 3.12.7 lint comparison above completed successfully.

## Limits

One poll may process a large accumulated backlog; each underlying read remains bounded by `READ_MAX`. Validation used local file fixtures and a local MockEngine HTTP server; it did not use a real engine or a production service.

pulls.title: [Other] Synchronize cache metrics after completed recovery clears
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:

pulls.title: [Other] Exclude refused batch admissions from completion metrics
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A request refused by every BGEN slot returns HTTP 503, but its history row is still (finish, prompt_tokens, prompt_read) = (length, 51, None), and successful completion/token/latency metrics include it. This fix records an error history row with zero processed prompt tokens and excludes this pre-admission rejection from successful completion and latency totals. The regression also checks Retry-After, Prometheus metrics, slot cleanup and a later successful request.

## Related discussion

Continues #3042 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original passed the new format check, but GitHub refused to reopen the rebased branch; [the reset bot](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3042#issuecomment-6282593730) explicitly suggested a new linked pull request.

Closes #3040. This is an accounting follow-up to #1994; admission and retry policy stay the same.

## Approach

Classify GpuBusy as a pre-admission refusal only when no DONE segment has settled and no output token was emitted. Preserve accounting for settled or partly generated work.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_parallel.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 21 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- Windows, Python 3.12.7: `python -m unittest serve.test_parallel.ParallelService.test_bgen_refused_for_good_is_a_retryable_503_and_frees_the_slots -v` — 1 passed on `23a4f428d78655b92b05048620570465469533b1`.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_parallel serve.test_prometheus -v` — 48 tests, passed; final test result `OK`.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_parallel.py` and `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211...HEAD` passed.

**Failed:**
- Expected red baseline: with exact upstream `serve/server.py` at `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta), the same focused test fails: `('length', 51, None) != ('error', 0, None)`. No candidate test failure observed.

**Not run:**
- Real model generation, CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds or hardware execution. This patch touches only Python server code and its CPU fake-engine tests.

## Limits

Fresh Python processes and loopback HTTP prove the server accounting behavior, not native engine admission or model quality. No runtime default is changed.

pulls.title: [Other] Serialize conversation-cache log polling
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Concurrent `/metrics` readers could read the same conversation-cache log range and replay an event. This change serializes access to the shared log cursor, so direct and HTTP metrics readers count each event once.

## Related discussion

Continues #3041 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original passed the new format check, but GitHub refused to reopen the rebased branch; [the reset bot](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3041#issuecomment-6282591930) explicitly suggested a new linked pull request.

Closes #3039.

## Approach

Guard the existing log-poll operation with the cache object's lock and add direct-reader and local loopback `/metrics` concurrency regressions. Cache parsing and native inference behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `04796fa0427beaa6b8628d6e2ab914c7059ca8c0` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- `python -m unittest -v serve.test_monitor serve.test_prometheus` — 18 tests passed.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py`.
- `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:**
- With the exact base production file restored, the direct concurrency test replayed the park event twice. The initial two-test run also had one environment error before the local `regex` dependency was installed. The subsequent fresh loopback HTTP `/metrics` red test failed as expected with `(parks, restores) = (2, 0)` instead of `(1, 0)`.

**Not run:**
- No GPU, native backend, model download, or hardware inference test.

## Limits

The proof covers concurrent Python readers, the repository mock engine, and a local loopback HTTP server. It does not exercise a real model process or hardware runtime.

pulls.title: [Docs] Explain cache settings for long-context batch handoffs
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The batching guide still omits the cache settings needed to reuse a solo request's live prefix when it moves into a batch slot. Add a minimal handoff configuration, separate its memory cost from parked-conversation budgets, and explain why in-flight requests do not establish concurrent cold-prompt prefill.

## Related discussion

Continues #3035 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original passed the new format check, but GitHub refused to reopen the rebased branch; [the reset bot](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3035#issuecomment-6282591198) explicitly suggested a new linked pull request.

None required for this documentation clarification. This updates the original PR after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset.

## Approach

Only `docs/BATCHING.md` changes. Document `--prompt-cache 1 --prompt-cache-every 0 --prompt-cache-root 0`; keep an existing conversation-parking budget when already enabled. Explain observed slot/status checks without claiming all configured slots remain resident.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta), candidate `91e5a5d5b6e52c5b4951655ab7f66f2627de6ec7`. Windows, Python 3.12.7.
- Confirmed this guidance is absent from the base document and appears once in the candidate.
- Parsed the example argument fragment as JSON after removing its explicit ellipsis placeholder; all four flags exist in the current native argument parser.
- Checked the current `o.prompt_cache > 0` live-prefix reuse gate and per-slot cached-state gates in `src/program/generate.cpp`; the prose matches them.
- Checked new-section relative links and `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211...HEAD`; only `docs/BATCHING.md` differs.

**Failed:**
- None observed in these documentation checks.

**Not run:**
- A new native handoff generation, model/GPU test or backend build. No runtime source or default changes, and no speedup is claimed.

## Limits

This is documentation and source-consistency validation, not measured handoff or hardware-capacity evidence.

pulls.title: [Other] Refresh conversation-cache metrics after refused parking
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

After a refused conversation-cache park, the Monitor and `/metrics` could retain a prior occupancy. This change records only the remaining count where the refusal establishes it, marks unknown bytes and cumulative evictions as unknown, and hides occupancy bars until a later authoritative event.

## Related discussion

Continues #3034 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. The original passed the new format check, but GitHub refused to reopen the rebased branch; [the reset bot](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3034#issuecomment-6282589985) explicitly suggested a new linked pull request.

Closes #3033.

## Approach

Parse physical-pressure, minimum-length, and other refusal log lines in the server observer. Add regression coverage for log replay, the local loopback `/metrics` endpoint, and the Monitor card. The native cache policy and inference paths are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `8d0a488f5a4ba8c06afae70f1739121345bcbab0` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- `python -m unittest -v serve.test_monitor serve.test_prometheus` — 24 tests passed.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py`.
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`.
- `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:**
- With exact base production files restored, the pressure regression set failed (8 tests; 10 assertion failures and one environment error before the local `regex` dependency was installed). The fresh loopback HTTP `/metrics` red test then failed as expected: stale `(parked, bytes)` remained `(1, 104857600)` instead of `(0, 0)`.

**Not run:**
- No GPU, native backend, model download, or hardware inference test.

## Limits

The proof covers the Python observer, local mock engine, loopback HTTP server, and Monitor JavaScript rendering. It does not measure a real engine's memory-admission behavior.

pulls.title: [Other] add legacy /v1/completions for raw-prompt clients (#2277)
pulls.author: kossum
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Clients that build their own prompts need `/v1/completions`, but Strata has no legacy completions endpoint. Sending those prompts through the chat API would apply the chat template again.

This adds `/v1/completions` for string prompts, with streaming and non-streaming responses in the OpenAI `text_completion` format, including token usage.

## Related discussion

#2277, #2278.

This replaces #2278 after the tracker reset. The `/reopen` format check passed twice, but GitHub returned "Validation Failed" both times. The bot suggested opening a new PR and linking the old one. The earlier review and fixes are in #2278.

## Approach

The handler reuses the existing generation path without rendering a chat template. `max_tokens: 0` or a negative value uses the remaining context.

If the caller explicitly disables thinking, the handler appends the template's no-thinking tail. Otherwise it leaves the prompt alone.

Streamed text is sent once. With `echo: true`, the prompt goes out once at the start, and the finish chunk has empty text. The tests concatenate the chunks and compare them with the non-streaming reply, with echo on and off.

The structured-output error handler stays in the chat endpoint. A failed streamed response sends an SSE error followed by `[DONE]`, rather than a second HTTP response inside the stream. Engine errors after streaming starts are also returned as SSE errors.

## Validation

Tested `7e08755f`, rebased onto main `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta).

**Passed:**

On Windows with Python 3.13.2 and jsonschema installed:

```sh
uv run --no-project --with regex --with jinja2 --with jsonschema python -m unittest serve.test_server serve.test_structured serve.test_monitor
```

368 tests, OK, 3 skipped.

On Linux in a Python 3.11 Docker container, using a dedicated venv with only the pinned `requirements.txt` packages:

```sh
python tools/minimal_server_smoke.py --report /tmp/minimal-server-smoke.json
```

The smoke test reported `"passed": true`.

`git diff --check upstream/main` passed too.

**Failed:**

In the same Linux venv:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'
```

888 tests, 2 failures, 18 skipped. The failures were:

- `test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed`: the test still sees the child after killing the server.
- `test_server.VisionTempFiles.test_work_dir_has_no_space_when_temp_has_one`: the temporary path contains a space.

I reran both tests on clean main `e88ee39d` with the same container and dependencies. Both failed with the same assertions there. This PR doesn't change either path.

**Not run:**

- Live-model tests on this revision. The live checks mentioned in #2278 were on an older revision.
- CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal builds; no native backend source is changed.
- A byte-for-byte comparison of the existing endpoints against the release.

## Limits

The endpoint accepts one string prompt and supports only `n=1` and `best_of=1`. Suffix and logprobs are rejected.

`stream_options` accepts only `include_usage`, with streaming enabled. Usage is still on the finish chunk rather than a separate `choices: []` chunk, so the OpenAI streaming-usage format isn't fully implemented.

pulls.title: [Engine] Linux RX 6000 engine package: build_hip_linux.sh variant rx6900 (gfx1030, gfx1031)
pulls.author: elightcap
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On Linux the Terminal and `strata update` have no engine for an RX 6000 card. The 0.2.0-beta feed has HIP packages for
gfx1100-1102, gfx1151 and gfx1200/1201 only, so `strata launch` on an RX 6900 XT stops with:

```
The model is ready, but Strata can't start it yet: it couldn't find an engine for this computer (This build of Strata is
for AMD RX 7000 and RX 9000 and Ryzen AI Max cards. This computer has an AMD RX 6000 card (gfx1030). Ask for the RX 6000 build).
```

#3296 reports the same on an RX 6700 XT (gfx1031). The engine itself runs on these cards (the RDNA2 section of
docs/AMD_HIP.md); only the package is missing.

This adds an `rx6900` variant to `packaging/build_hip_linux.sh` (gfx1030 and gfx1031), puts it in the release matrix
test and adds a note to docs/AMD_HIP.md. With the package in the components folder, `strata launch` picks it and serves.

Related discussion: #3296

## Approach

The same script and steps as the `rx9070`, `rx7900` and `halo` packages; only the variant's arch list is new. ROCm is
TheRock's `gfx103X-all` 7.13.0a20260515, the version setup pins for this family (`ROCM_FAMILY_PINS`, #1103). That
library set has rocBLAS kernels for gfx1031 of its own (142 files for each of gfx1030 and gfx1031), so a gfx1031 card
runs its own code and needs no `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION` (which #3145 needed for ROCm 7.1.1). hipBLASLt has no gfx103x
kernels, as before.

Compatibility: no existing package, default or code path changes. The feed offers the package only after a maintainer
builds and publishes it. The release matrix test now lists `rx6900` for linux-x86_64 and expects gfx1030 and gfx1031
on Linux to get it; Windows still has no RX 6000 package, and gfx1030 moved from the "no engine" list to that new test.

## Validation

Machine: RX 6900 XT 16 GB (gfx1030), Ryzen 9 5950X, 128 GB DDR4, Arch Linux (kernel 7.2.5, glibc 2.44, GCC 16.2.1,
CMake 4.4.4). Source e88ee39d plus this change; llama.cpp at setup's `LLAMA_CPP_COMMIT` (3cf03257).

Built with:

```sh
VARIANT=rx6900 LLAMA=<llama.cpp> HP=<venv>/_rocm_sdk_devel CORE=<venv>/_rocm_sdk_core \
  LIBW=<venv>/_rocm_sdk_libraries_gfx103X_all packaging/build_hip_linux.sh
```

(`rocm[libraries,devel]==7.13.0a20260515` from https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx103X-all/; 950.7 MiB, 314 files.)

**Passed**

- `python packaging/binary_deps.py <package>`: every imported library is bundled or belongs to the OS / GPU driver.
- `python packaging/package_engine.py --verify <package>`: ok (313 files).
- `llvm-objdump --offloading`: `strata` 66 gfx1030 + 66 gfx1031 code objects, `strata-vision-hip` 138 + 138, no other arch.
- `env -i <package>/strata --version`: `strata 0.1.45.3`.
- `strata launch --model ud-q4_k_xl --family unsloth --context 128k --yes --no-tui` with the package in
  `~/.local/share/strata/components/engine/`: the Terminal picks it and serves; the engine and `librocblas.so.5` load from
  the package folder.
- `strata connect <app> --check` for opencode, codex, claude-code and pi: prompt and tool call PASS (8 of 8).
- Both picture readers from the package (`strata-vision-hip` on the card, `strata-vision` on the CPU) read a 640x480
  test picture correctly ("STRATA 6900", a red rectangle and a blue circle): 8.2 s and 9.3 s per request.
- Same engine version, same settings, one fresh 48,453-token UD-Q4_K_XL prompt each: the package 722 tok/s (an earlier
  gfx1030-only build of it: 725), engine 0.1.45.3 built by hand against the system ROCm 7.2.4 with its rocBLAS table
  733 tok/s. Settings: `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1 STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING=tools/hip STRATA_SH_STREAM=1
  STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1`, `--resident-budget-gib 71
  --pcie-frac 0.35 --mtp-draft-vocab data/draft_vocab_en.bin`, the rest as `strata launch` writes it (`--kv int8
  --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072 --spec 4`). One run per cell.
- `python -m pytest tests/terminal/test_release_matrix.py`: 11 passed.

**Failed**

- `python -m pytest tests/terminal` in this checkout: 848 passed, 16 skipped, 6 failed. None comes from this change:
  five also fail on a clean origin/main worktree on this machine (`test_discovery.py::GuiLayout` x2,
  `test_launch_tui.py::AccessStep::test_cloudflare_without_the_helper_says_how_to_install_it_and_does_not_block`,
  `test_private_files.py::...not_strictly_private`, `test_procs.py::...engine_orphan...`). The sixth,
  `test_discovery.py::GuiLayout::test_list_and_the_wizard_agree_on_the_install`, fails only because this checkout is
  itself a setup install (`/home/.../Strata != /tmp/strata-discovery-.../install`); with this diff applied to the clean
  worktree it passes, together with the release matrix tests (12 passed).

**Not run**

- A gfx1031 card (RX 6700 XT / 6750 XT): the gfx1031 code is built and in the package, not executed.
- Another distribution: the package above was built on Arch and needs glibc 2.43 / GLIBCXX 3.4.35, so it was only run
  here. The published packages are built in an Ubuntu 22.04 chroot; that build was not made.
- A Linux AppImage installer for RX 6000, a Windows RX 6000 package, CUDA and SYCL builds (no file of theirs changes).

## Limits

- `tools/hip` has no rocBLAS table for the package's rocBLAS (5.4.0.ad84daa81c), so the engine logs that it cannot open
  `gfx1030-rocblas-5.4.0.ad84daa81c.txt` and runs rocBLAS's own kernels. Making one with `tools/hip/tune_rocblas` is
  follow-up work.
- The package reaches users only once a maintainer builds and publishes it in the feed.

Measured and written with Claude Code.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 4090 with the model in the page cache: experts read in place from the GGUF cost 21-57% prompt, 19-24% decode (file tier of #149)
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

This machine keeps the whole model in the page cache (40 GiB of experts, 46 GiB of RAM), so the file tier
of #149 is off: the engine reads experts from a packed `packs/iq3_xxs/experts.bin` and says
`experts via mmap (--mmap-experts; the A/B arm of R2.1)`. The pack also carries `native_experts.txt` with
the offsets inside the GGUF, so switching to the tier is a one-line change. We measured the switch.

Result: **the file tier costs 21% to 57% of prompt reading and 19% to 24% of decode here, and 0 of 2
interleaved pairs favoured it.** The pack stays. This is a boundary-of-feature measurement, not a bug
report: the tier is for machines that cannot hold the file set in memory, and this one can - the plan
line of the engine itself says `file set 31.7 GiB fits the page cache 40.1 GiB -> about 0.0 GB read from
the drive per 32768-token prompt`, so the mechanisms have nothing to overlap.

Two related numbers are in the same folder: `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1` on the packed file (the opt-in that
does exist for a pack) makes decode slower in 3 of 3 pairs (median -6.2%), so it stays off; and the drive
speed the prefill plan assumes (`drive 1.50 GB/s (assumed)`) is 2-8x below what this NVMe actually does
(3.6-12 GB/s in six direct-access reads), which does not change this plan but would matter where the file
tier is the bottleneck.

## Related discussion

none (a results-only submission; no engine change is proposed). Follows the engine A/B PR of the same
day for the same machine, where the same configuration and the same instruments are described.

## Approach

`def` is the working configuration; `gguf` is the same configuration with `packs/iq3_xxs/experts.bin`
temporarily renamed away, which makes the engine read the experts in place from the GGUF and turn the tier
on. Nothing else differs; the script puts the pack back. The change is verified from the engine's own
output and from the files it actually mapped:

```text
def : experts via mmap (--mmap-experts; the A/B arm of R2.1)      -> maps packs/iq3_xxs/experts.bin
gguf: experts via mmap (--mmap-experts; the GGUF shards in place, no experts.bin)
      file tier (Linux defaults, the GGUF read in place): … (STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP=4, io prefetch on 8 I/O threads, STRATA_IO_PF_GATE=1)
                                                                  -> maps models/IQ3_XXS/…-00001-of-00002.gguf
```

Two interleaved pairs, a freshly started engine per arm, 3 runs per case, medians; the auto-chunk is
8192 tokens / 96 slots in both arms, so the two sides are comparable token by token.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- the A/B above on commit `e88ee39d` (engine 0.1.45.3, source build, arch `[89]`), Ubuntu 26.04.1,
  NVIDIA 615.71.09, RTX 4090 24 GB, Ryzen 9 7950X, 46 GiB RAM. Observed medians, pack vs GGUF-in-place
  (prompt tok/s | decode tok/s): 4K 1972.7 vs 844.9 | 127.4 vs 97.5; 32K 3309.7 vs 1879.6 | 131.9 vs
  100.8; 128K 3285.5 vs 2567.2 | 127.1 vs 103.5; 194K 3249.9 vs 2553.7 | 131.7 vs 101.3;
  generation-only 297.6 vs 130.5 | 157.4 vs 124.8. TTFT grows 1.3-2.8x. The gap narrows with prompt
  length (x0.43 at 4K, x0.78 at 194K) and never closes; 0 of 2 pairs in favour of the tier on any case.
- draft acceptance did not change (942/1393 vs 983/1329 in the 4K case, inside the run-to-run spread), so
  the same tokens are produced through a worse data path, not a different routing.
- `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1` against the same-session baseline, 3 interleaved pairs: prompt 32K x1.003
  (2/3 pairs), 4K x0.914, decode slower in 3/3 pairs (159.1 -> 148.3, 149.6 -> 140.3, 148.6 -> 143.3).
- `dd iflag=direct` on `experts.bin`, six samples: 3.6-12 GB/s on an ADATA LEGEND 960 (raw output in
  `drive-read.txt`).

**Failed:** none observed beyond the numbers above; nothing here is a failing test or a crash.

**Not run:** the case where the tier should actually pay - a cold start with an empty page cache, and a
host with 16-32 GB of RAM where the 31.7 GiB file set does not fit. We do not have such a host: our
second machine (4x Tesla V100-SXM2 32 GB) keeps 98% of the experts resident, so it is not the target
regime either. Other `STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP` / `STRATA_IO_PF_*` values than the defaults, and
`--pcie-frac` variants, were not swept.

## Limits

One quant (IQ3_XXS), one pack, one machine with the model fully cacheable; our own prompt suite (the one
described in the engine A/B PR of the same day), not the repository's suite, so these ratios are not
directly comparable with other community reports - the two arms are identical instruments of the same
suite. The conclusion is about the regime "model fits the page cache", not about the tier in general.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 4090 24 GB: engine 0.1.45 vs 0.1.45.3 changes nothing measurable at 16K-32K; short prompts not attributable
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The engine of this machine was updated from 0.1.45 to 0.1.45.3 (0.2.0-beta). Two folders of measurements
answer one question: does the update change what this machine feels?

Result: **no, within +-1% at 16K and 32K tokens.** Prompt reading and the conversation cache are
unchanged; the short-prompt column and the decode column cannot be attributed to the engine at all on
this machine. We propose no engine change - this is a results-only submission, and the negative half of
it is the useful part: our own earlier reading of a long-context table (+0.5…+1.7%) does not survive the
repository's own suite.

## Related discussion

none required (a results-only submission, no behaviour change proposed). For continuity: our 0.1.45
measurements for this same machine were PR #3109, closed by the tracker reset on 2026-10-19; the numbers
here re-measure part of that baseline on the old binary in the same session, so the comparison does not
depend on the old thread.

## Approach

Two engines, one machine, everything else identical (same server config, same model files, same
arguments): 0.1.45 kept as `engine/strata.0145.bak` and 0.1.45.3, both **built from source on this
machine by `update.sh`** (CUDA arch `[89]`), never downloaded. The auto-selected prompt chunk is the
same in both (8192 tokens, 96-slot ring), so the runs are comparable token by token.

The measurements are ordered so that the version is separated from the state of the machine:

- `python tools/strata_bench.py --runs 3 --long` against a freshly started server, run **twice per
  engine with the order of the pair reversed** (pair 1: 0.1.45 then 0.1.45.3; pair 2: the reverse). This
  machine drifts like the one in #1332: the same setting gave 1294-1924 tok/s at 4K across four runs, so
  one pair cannot separate drift from a real difference. What is claimed below is what agrees in both
  pairs; what does not is named as not established.
- a control run of the same 0.1.45.3 binary again in the same session, which gives the noise band of the
  second instrument (prompt +-0.0…0.7% at 32K and above, decode +-0.6…6.6%);
- an interleaved binary A/B (2 pairs, both binaries alternating inside one session) with the second
  instrument, and a supplementary suite at 128K-200K, because the tool stops at 32K while this
  configuration's whole point is the 204,800-token context.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --api-key <key> --runs 3 --long`, four times
  (2 pairs x 2 engines), commit `e88ee39d` / engine 0.1.45.3 and the kept 0.1.45 build; Ubuntu 26.04.1,
  kernel 7.0.0-38, NVIDIA 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4, RTX 4090 24 GB, Ryzen 9 7950X, 46 GiB RAM. Observed,
  pair 1 / pair 2: 16K prompt -0.1% / -0.8%, 32K prompt +0.1% / -0.9%, conversation-cache hit 69.4% in
  all four runs, TTFT at 16K/32K within +-1%; 4K prompt -12.7% / -20.8% (the two pairs disagree about
  which engine is faster); `chat decode` +2.6% / +9.1% and `agent decode` -4.0% / +8.7% - the sign flips
  with the order, so no decode claim is made.
- the recall check (needle at 32K and 128K, depths 10/50/90) passed 6/6 on both engines; draft
  acceptance over the whole long-context suite 4615/6415 (71.9%) -> 4567/6241 (73.2%).
- the long-context suite (4K…200K, 3 runs each, warm-up, control run of the same binary, and the 0.1.45
  baseline of the short cases measured on the old binary in the same session): +0.5…+1.7% at 32K and
  above in one session, x1.010 in the interleaved A/B, and 0…-1.3% in the repository's suite. Taken
  together we report **no** prompt improvement.

**Failed:**

- the full unit-test run at this commit: 1881 tests (1012 `tools/`, 869 `serve/`), 57 not passing, against
  1703 tests / 16 not passing at 0.1.44.1. Every delta was traced to this machine or to the tests
  themselves, none to the engine or the server; the counts and the names are in
  `tests-0.2.0-beta-summary.txt` in the folder, and the two test-side problems are filed as a separate
  issue.
- an attempt to compare the two builds by their answers (fixed prompts, temperature 0, thinking off) did
  not work as a gate: the control arm - the same configuration started twice - differs in 4 of 6
  prompts. That is filed as a separate observation, because it affects how "bit-identical" can be
  demonstrated at all.

**Not run:**

- concurrency (`--clients`), cold start with an empty page cache, vision requests, the 0.2.0
  application-layer features;
- any other machine or backend: this is one RTX 4090 (sm_89) with a source build; HIP, SYCL and Metal
  were not built here;
- the opt-in switches of the release (`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED`, the sm_86 switch set, `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH`)
  and the file tier of #149: measured on this card, reported in a separate PR, not in this one.

## Limits

The long-context supplement uses our own prompts and lengths and is not comparable with other community
reports; the numbers of `tools/strata_bench.py` are. The 4K column is dominated by session state on this
machine in both directions, and the decode column is inside the band of repeated runs - both are reported
without conclusions. No claim is made about other quants, other contexts or other cards.

pulls.title: [Engine] support the official Flash-Next DFlash2 checkpoint
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The official `incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2` checkpoint requires five attention layers with 128-wide heads, raw HC-mean target features, dynamic convolution and a predecessor-conditioned selector. This change implements that checkpoint contract and supports original BF16 weights plus Q8_0, Q5_0 and Q4_0 backbone quantizations, using the full shared target output head. This PR resolves the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next speculative-decoding gap tracked in [issue #3304](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3304) by adding opt-in DFlash2 support and setup integration. The measured results do not establish the suggested 1.5–2× gain across workloads; performance depends on target, prompts, hardware and configuration, as detailed below.

Setup offers MTP (default), experimental DFlash2, or no model drafter. DFlash2 selection enables the local CUDA build, pinned download/conversion and artifact-specific calibration. Weights, private KV pools and attention scratch are accounted for before auto-sizing the expert cache, including the configured context length and elastic growth. MTP and DFlash2 cannot be selected together.

## Related discussion

Explicit maintainer confirmation of the expanded official-checkpoint/setup scope remains pending. This remains a draft while that scope and missing backend validation are resolved.

## Approach

DFlash2 is opt-in behind `STRATA_ENABLE_DFLASH2=ON`. The converter validates the checkpoint geometry and preserves all 45 norm, convolution and selector tensors in BF16; the 36 backbone matrices can be quantized. Setup offers BF16, Q8_0 and Q4_0; Q5_0 is also supported by the converter/runtime and included in the measurements below.

Prompt and conversation snapshots retain the draft context. Cache controls enforce matching actual expert placement before checking output. The shared runtime includes the infrastructure required for proposal verification, a fix for state publication on the opt-in QFUSE path and a fix for the CPU-only loader-test build dependency. The existing default drafter stays MTP.

## Tuned long-prompt result (2026-10-20)

The final same-executable comparison now puts DFlash2 ahead on the PR's 2425-token long fixture. RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GiB, Ryzen 9 5900X, Linux, CUDA 13.4 / SM89; greedy seed 1234, 96 output tokens, one warmup and three measured repeats per task. Medians exclude prefill/startup.

| Drafter | Code, 27 input tokens: median [range] tok/s | vs MTP | Long, 2425 input tokens: median [range] tok/s | vs MTP |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP, floor 0.5 | 38.46 [38.34–38.60] | reference | 55.31 [53.50–55.42] | reference |
| DFlash2 Q8_0, block 7, floor 0.7 | **50.86 [50.82–50.87]** | **+32.23%** | **56.77 [56.76–57.13]** | **+2.64%** |

Long-prompt measured repeats (decode tok/s; one warmup excluded):

| Drafter | Repeat 1 | Repeat 2 | Repeat 3 | Median |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP | 55.3091 | 55.4209 | 53.5028 | 55.3091 |
| DFlash2 Q8_0 | **57.1327** | **56.7611** | **56.7678** | **56.7678** |

Final profile and long-request measurements:

| Metric | MTP | DFlash2 Q8_0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum proposals / verifier capacity | 3 / 4 | 7 / 8 |
| Probability floor | 0.5 | 0.7 |
| Actual target expert slots | 3143 | 3188 |
| Allocation reserve, MiB | 480 | 480 |
| Long accepted / offered proposals | 64 / 68 | 68 / 71 |
| Long verification windows | 32 | 28 |
| Median long prompt reading, s | 61.40 | 50.96 |
| Median full long client request, s | 63.14 | 52.64 |

Full request timings include prompt reading and architecture/cache-placement effects; decode throughput excludes prompt reading and startup. Math/prose and a new four-task aggregate were not measured for this final profile.

Every measured DFlash2 long sample exceeds every MTP sample. Both arms use the same final executable and opt-in shared-head flags, with prompt/conversation caches, CPU prompt sharing, PCIe sharing, adaptive swaps and suffix/lookup drafting off. Context/resident 8192, prefill 256, reserve 480 MiB; actual target expert slots are fixed at 3188 for DFlash2 and 3143 for MTP. DFlash2 uses block 7 / verifier capacity 8; MTP retains up to three proposals / capacity 4. MTP floor was swept, but its width was not independently tuned. This is a result for this fixture and configuration, not a general long-context speedup claim.

The remaining costs were repeated paged-attention address work and a missing interleaved Q8_0 output-head path. The patch reuses pool-row addresses, uses paired FP16 value loads for aligned long windows, adds exact Q8_0 interleaved head dispatch, and fixes preparation for more than four head rows. The head optimization is strictly opt-in through STRATA_MMVQ_IL_Q8_HEAD=1, with STRATA_DFLASH_HEAD_IL=1 for DFlash2; both flags were enabled for MTP too. Selecting the measured Q8_0 backbone and block/floor reduces long verification windows to 28 versus MTP's 32. The actual shared target head is Q8_0; the old Q5_K log label was hardcoded and has been corrected.

Passed: CUDA extension ON/OFF builds; 8 selected CTests with the head flag off, the same 8 with it on, and 3 extension-OFF CTests. All warmed/measured outputs match target-only controls exactly (192/192 fixture token IDs, no near-tie exemption). Expanded head parity and three paired graph-replay attention comparisons pass, with all 286720 FP32 attention outputs byte-identical per comparison. Earlier negative runs and the initial failed wide-head preparation attempt are retained in the evidence.

[Final raw runs, reproducible commands, source/executable hashes, tuning history and limits](https://github.com/j-luwierski/Strata/blob/27b65cc8b4c42c83da65bbed605c8ab6bba8171b/bench/results/2026-10-20-dflash2-long-tuned/README.md).

Not run: HIP/SYCL/Metal/Windows, multi-GPU, concurrent requests, held-out long-prompt suite or full 128K prompt sweep. No new-head CI success is claimed. The PR remains a draft pending backend validation and scope agreement. The historical measurements below remain intact.

## Historical baseline: MTP versus DFlash2 (2026-10-19)

These tables describe the earlier block-3 benchmark, before the final head/attention optimizations and tuning above. They are retained for comparison and are not the current performance result.

Fresh same-source runs on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GiB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 125.7 GiB RAM, Linux, CUDA 13.4 / SM89. Target: local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 pack, BF16 embeddings, FP8 PLE, shared Q8_0 output head, INT8 KV. Context 8192, prefill 256, auto expert cache, allocation reserve 512 MiB. All arms fill available VRAM; smaller draft allocations permit more target experts.

Greedy seed 1234, 96 new tokens, four fixed prompts (27/54/33/2425 input tokens), one warmup per prompt and three measured repeats per speculative arm. MTP at floor 0 is run before and after all four DFlash2 variants. An additional MTP run at setup's floor 0.5 follows those series and is the table reference; this sensitivity check was added after the initial series to avoid comparing only against an untuned zero-floor baseline. Both MTP settings remain in the raw evidence.

DFlash2 uses three proposals (verifier capacity 8, fixed block 3); MTP uses up to three proposals (verifier capacity 4), probability floor 0 in the fixed-budget series, plus the separate MTP setup-floor 0.5 control. The DFlash2 block length is fixed; the study does not independently tune each drafter.

CPU prompt sharing, PCIe sharing, adaptive swaps, suffix/lookup drafting and prompt/conversation snapshots are off. Engines run sequentially, with no build or other benchmark during measurements. Values are medians of native decode throughput; prefill/startup are excluded. Geomean weights all four task medians equally.

| Drafter | Code tok/s | Math tok/s | Prose tok/s | Long tok/s | Geomean tok/s (vs MTP) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP (setup floor 0.5) | 38.05 | 44.84 | 39.94 | 55.19 | 44.04 (reference) |
| MTP (floor 0, pooled) | 36.81 | 43.68 | 36.26 | 48.61 | 41.03 (-6.8%) |
| DFlash2 BF16 | **43.25 (+13.7%)** | 43.16 (-3.7%) | 36.40 (-8.9%) | 41.77 (-24.3%) | 41.05 (-6.8%) |
| DFlash2 Q8_0 | **45.08 (+18.5%)** | 44.45 (-0.9%) | 37.05 (-7.2%) | 44.58 (-19.2%) | 42.65 (-3.1%) |
| DFlash2 Q5_0 | **45.19 (+18.8%)** | 44.87 (+0.1%) | 33.71 (-15.6%) | 43.89 (-20.5%) | 41.62 (-5.5%) |
| DFlash2 Q4_0 | **47.11 (+23.8%)** | **45.36 (+1.2%)** | **40.66 (+1.8%)** | 43.52 (-21.1%) | 44.10 (+0.1%) — tie |

Q4_0 has the best observed DFlash2 aggregate, 44.10 versus MTP's 44.04 tok/s (+0.1%). Their per-repeat geometric-mean ranges overlap: treat this as an overall tie. Its clear code advantage is +23.8%; math/prose improve by 1.2%/1.8% in this sample, while the long prompt regresses by 21.1%. Q8_0, Q5_0 and BF16 are slower in aggregate.

Per-repeat geometric means span 43.00–44.10 tok/s for MTP floor 0.5 and 44.07–44.20 tok/s for DFlash2 Q4_0. Bold task cells mean every measured DFlash2 sample exceeded every MTP floor-0.5 sample for that task; percentages are relative to MTP for that column. The bracketing zero-floor MTP's end/start geomean changed by -0.49%. Three samples per DFlash2/default-floor MTP task and six pooled zero-floor MTP samples are too few to establish a general speedup. Non-overlapping observed throughput ranges: bf16/code, Q8_0/code, Q5_0/code, Q4_0/code, Q4_0/math, Q4_0/prose. These are descriptive ranges, not confidence intervals.

| Drafter | Initial runtime MiB | Extra draft-head MiB | GPU expert slots | Minimum GPU free MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP floor 0, start | 801.0 | 275.7 | 3140 | 182 |
| DFlash2 BF16 | 1354.6 | 0.0 | 3038 | 130 |

The initial runtime column is the engine's load counter, not total process VRAM. MTP subsequently allocates another 275.7 MiB of selected output-head rows, plus index/sampling buffers. DFlash2's counter includes its weights, private KV pools and scratch, and it shares the full target output head without another head-weight copy. Expert slots and GPU-free snapshots show the practical final placement.

[Raw runs, ranges, memory and output controls](https://github.com/j-luwierski/Strata/blob/86af7286254d1efb148cf0aa8c9a96868d4e9f09/bench/results/2026-10-19-dflash2-pr-performance/README.md).

## Historical intermediate: confidence-gate fix (2026-10-20)

The earlier long-case loss used DFlash2 at floor 0 against MTP at setup's floor 0.5. A controlled Q4_0 follow-up isolates the gate in one process at the same actual expert placement. Fixed-block manual DFlash2 launches now also default to `--spec-min-p 0.5`; an explicit floor, including zero, still wins. Fresh same-hardware runs at `c7bebe215a6feb754e08dfbc02a3ac12d38fa55f`: three measured repeats per cell after warmup, 96 generated tokens, the same 27/2425-token code/long fixtures, context 8192, prefill 256, auto expert cache and 512 MiB reserve. pulls.title: [Benchmark] bind the port so strata_bench.py can start its own server
pulls.author: victorgabr
pulls.body:
Closes #3188. Also covers the crash reported in #2864, #2872, #2908 and #3130.

## Problem and resulting behavior

`tools/strata_bench.py` dies with `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` on every run that has to **start the server itself** - the default path, and the one `BENCH.bat` and the setup "Run a quick benchmark now?" prompt use:

```
File "tools/strata_bench.py", line 990, in main
    say(f"Starting {cfg_path.name} on port {port} (loading takes 1-3 minutes; the PC may be slow meanwhile) ...")
NameError: name 'port' is not defined
```

After this change the tool starts the server on the config's port (or `--port`), waits for the model, runs the suite and writes the results folder; the "port is used by something that is not Strata" message also prints the real port instead of crashing.

## Why this approach

Commit 69fe4055 (#2330) replaced `port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))` + `base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"` with `base = server_base(cfg.get("host"), a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080)))` and left the three remaining uses of `port` (lines 987, 990, 991) unbound. The fix restores the assignment the line used to carry and uses it in all three places - the same shape suggested in #3188. The `--url` path is untouched.

The suite never caught it because every `main()` test passes `--url`, so the start-server branch is never executed; that gap is called out in #3188. One new test (`test_the_start_server_branch_knows_its_port`) reaches the branch with a stubbed `start_server`: it asserts the config's port reaches the starter and the not-ready path returns 1, and that a non-Strata port occupant returns 2 with the port named in the message.

## Validation

On `upstream/main` `e88ee39d`, Linux, Python 3.14.7, branch exactly as submitted:

**Passed**
- `python tools/test_strata_bench.py` with the fix: `Ran 18 tests ... OK` (17 existing + the new one).
- The new test fails **without** the fix (fix reverted, test kept): `FAILED (errors=1)`, with the real traceback `NameError: name 'port' is not defined`, `line 990, in main`.
- End-to-end with the fix, no CI, on hardware: `python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-iq3_s.json` on Linux (TITAN RTX, engine 0.1.45.3) started its own server, ran the suite and wrote a full results folder - the path the change unblocks. Two paired runs this way produced the A/B evidence posted alongside this bug report's thread dates.

**Failed**
- none.

**Not run**
- Windows path (`BENCH.bat`) - the changed code is platform-independent Python and reproduces identically on Windows per #3188 and #3130, but I ran it only on Linux.
- No CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds needed: no compiled file is touched.

## Limits

The new test stubs `start_server`, so it proves the branch binds and passes the port, not that a real engine boots. The port-free check still relies on `/health` probing (unchanged behavior).

pulls.title: [Engine] Calibrate: survive an engine dying mid-measurement; adaptive gate: say where the copies stopped (#1337, #2188)
pulls.author: dsenchankau
pulls.body:
Issue: extends #1337 (shipped in 0.1.41); diagnostics for #2188 (still open)

## Problem and result

--calibrate restarts the engine for every setting it measures. Since 0.1.41, a candidate whose engine won't start just skips that candidate and keeps what was measured so far (#1337). But an engine that starts fine and then dies during its own measurement still fails the whole calibration.

I hit this on a UD-Q4_K_XL run: --adapt-swaps 80 measured fine, then the --adapt-swaps 160 engine died at the adaptive tier's copy gate (the same error as #2188). About twenty minutes of --pcie-frac and --spec-min-p results were lost.

After this change a dead engine drops only its own candidate. The earlier settings survive and the winner is picked from what actually measured; in my run 80 swaps beat the default by 10% and was still written even though 160 died. The engine's timeout line for that gate now also prints how far the copies got, which is what's missing in #2188.

## Related discussion

#1337 (closed; this extends its rule from failed starts to mid-measurement deaths) and #2188 (open; the engine part here is diagnostics only, it fixes nothing). I don't think this needs a scope agreement first: a calibration where nothing dies behaves exactly as before, and the new C++ code only runs after a wait has already timed out.

## Approach

Steps 4, 5 and 6 (worker counts, expert tier, the AMD shared-expert fork) already had the failed-start rule through restart() and failed_starts. I routed a mid-measurement death through the same path and folded the three nearly identical blocks into one restart-and-measure helper. Step 6 had no mid-measurement protection at all and failed the whole run the same way. The first start (steps 1-3) still fails the run; nothing has been measured yet, so there is nothing to keep.

On the engine side, when the adaptive gate's wait times out the message now carries the gate's reached counter, its atomic, and the copy stream's pinned value, and says that the #267 release drains the window's own streams and never the tier's copy stream. With STRATA_VERIFY_TRACE=1 it also dumps the window's trace. Nothing changed for the case where the wait succeeds.

## Validation

Revision eb07e553. Ubuntu 24.04, i7-13700F, RTX 4080 SUPER (sm_89), CUDA 13.4 (nvcc V13.4.92, cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0). I re-ran everything on the upstream main commit this branch is rebased on, as a baseline, and the failing lists below are the same on both.

**Passed:**

```
cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build-tests -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89
cmake --build build-tests -j "$(nproc)"
ctest --test-dir build-tests --output-on-failure
```

Build is clean. ctest: "96% tests passed, 6 tests failed out of 149". expert_multi_test skips itself on this CPU (no AVX-512). The six failures (ple_parity, ggml_tq_overlay, native_hadamard_test, tq_cpu_parity, tq_cpu_parity_avx2, isa_guard_check) are the same six on the baseline, same command, same build dir. Nothing new fails on this branch.

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python tools/test_calibrate.py
```

33 tests, OK. The baseline has 30; the three new ones cover the cases above: a tier candidate dies and the faster candidate still wins, a worker count dies and the rest still measures, a fork candidate dies and the run still returns.

```
for t in tools/test_*.py serve/test_*.py bench/test_*.py; do
  PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "FAILED: $t"
done
```

Six failures, the same six on the baseline: test_iq_pack, test_nvfp4_local_pack, test_setup_download, test_setup_engine_hash, test_setup_golden, test_gfx906_qsa_query_swizzle_guard. All environmental, none caused by this change.

**Failed:** the ctest and python failures listed above. Every one of them reproduces the same way on the baseline, so none comes from this change.

**Not run:**

- HIP compile of src/core/verify.cpp, I don't have an AMD card. The new block is ordinary C++ in the file CUDA and HIP share, and it compiles on its own under -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2, but that's a static check, not a HIP build. Could someone with a HIP setup compile this one file?
- Actually seeing the new timeout line. It needs the real #2188 stop (GPU + adaptive tier + STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1), and the STRATA_TEST_VERIFY_STALL hook stalls the window's flag waits, not the gate, so it can't fake it either. The #2188 reporters: a rerun on this branch with STRATA_VERIFY_TRACE=1 would give the evidence the thread needs.
- SYCL. The sycl tree has no adaptive gate at all (no adapt_gate_wait there), so this file is not built for SYCL.

## Limits

The python tests exercise calibrate.py against a fake engine; nothing crashes a real engine end to end in the tests. And this doesn't fix #2188, it only prints the values its diagnosis needs.

pulls.title: [Engine] the MMQ scratch now comes out of the prompt loan
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2835) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, rebased onto current `main` (`e88ee39d`); the conflict with `warm_gemm_libraries` beside the MMQ loan in `prefill.cpp` was resolved. It replaces the closed #2835, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

llama.cpp's `mmq.cuh` allocates its stream-k fixup tiles lazily through `ggml_cuda_pool`, which this build backs with a `cudaMalloc` on whatever is free at that moment - a few MB on a card the expert cache has filled, at the one moment a prompt is running. A malloc that fails there aborts the engine mid-read instead of failing the request. After this change, `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` (opt-in) takes those tiles from the loan's unused tail instead of free VRAM. A layout does not use the whole loan: the carve is a bump, so everything from its stop to the loan's end is the prompt's own memory, provably (a loan is whole cache slots and the top one is only partly needed).

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2835 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `bf844d5`.

## Approach

The pool takes the tiles from the loan's tail in **size classes** (a power of two, 128 KiB floor). The classes are load-bearing: MMQ's J search picks a different J per launch, so a cache keyed on the exact size holds one buffer per J - 32 buffers, 31.5 MiB on a 579-token chunk in the Maya checkout's measurement - where a class bounds the pool to a few MB.

Three guards make it safe, all load-bearing: it is published per layout keyed on the tail's **address** (a request whose chunk moves `used` moves the tail and the pool drops the old buffers); `Prefill::run` drops it once the prompt is read, before the caller refills the borrowed slots; and the loan is the participant's own expert cache `cudaMalloc`ed on this device, so the tail is this card's memory to write. A tail that is empty (the layout used the whole loan, or spilled into owned buffers) publishes nothing, and the pool allocates as it always did.

Unset (the default), the pool stays on free VRAM exactly as before: `lend_mmq_scratch` publishes nothing and `mmq::pool_slab` is not given a slab. The size classes are part of the slab path only (they bound the slab's pool); with the knob off there is no slab to bound. Default path unchanged by construction.

## Validation

Tested revision: `78d0e621`, one commit on current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2 (V13.2.86), `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the build machine is the Q8_0 4-way rig (2x RTX 3060 12 GB, 2x RTX 5060 8 GB).

**Passed:**
- `git rebase e88ee39d` - the conflict in `prefill.cpp` with `warm_gemm_libraries` beside the MMQ loan was resolved; the branch's diff is this feature only.
- `ninja -C build strata` at `78d0e621` - exit 0 (CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`).
- `-fsyntax-only` on `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean.
- `src/prefill/ggml_cuda_host.cu` and `src/prefill/moe_mmq.cu` compiled clean with the build's nvcc flags (CUDA 13.2, `compute_86` and `compute_120`).
- Maya checkout, local commit `bf844d5` (not this engine, not run by us here): it hit the failure at a 16,384-token chunk on a 5060 (3.4 MB free of 7,707.7 MB, 1.2 MB wanted) and measured the slab costing 42-47 more lent experts per part with no change to the chunk arithmetic, on its live split (5060/5060/3060/3060).

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- A served run with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` at this head: the start's check line and a prompt reading to completion have not been observed here.
- Serving the rebased head: only the build was re-run after the rebase; no GPU run was made at `78d0e621`.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. The device files this touches are the CUDA MMQ target's; the slab plumbing in `prefill.cpp` has no per-backend branch.

## Limits

- No speedup is claimed. What the start's check line shows is whether the slab is in use on a given rig: `strata prefill mmq: CUDA%d the scratch pool takes a new N MiB buffer` prints for a buffer of 4 MiB or more; with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` and a loan that has a tail it should not appear.
- The slab only exists when the layout leaves a tail; a layout that used the whole loan, or spilled into owned buffers, publishes nothing and falls back to free VRAM.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the slab plumbing has no per-backend branch.

pulls.title: [Docs] --prompt-cache-every does not set the prompt piece size
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2834) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, based on `477ac13c`, and GitHub reports that it merges cleanly with current `main` (`e88ee39d`). It replaces the closed #2834, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

Readers can take `--prompt-cache-every` for a piece-size dial, as it is in the Maya checkout, where its marks bound the segments the prompt path reads and every segment pays a fill and a drain of the part chain. In this engine a periodic mark is saved at a chunk boundary and the run carries on, so no piece ends at it. After this docs change, `docs/DETAILS.md` says that, gives the Maya checkout's numbers with what they were measured on, and names the cuts that actually split a fresh long read here.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2834 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The numbers quoted are the Maya checkout's, local commit `3095719` (2026-10-15).

## Approach

A docs bullet for `--prompt-cache-every` in `docs/DETAILS.md`: the knob is **not** a piece-size dial in this engine. What the bullet records:

- The Maya checkout's numbers for its `STRATA_GLM_CKPT_EVERY` (same 16384 default), local commit `3095719`, on a 100,535-token fresh read (Maya-L split, 8192-token chunks, one 580-token warm prompt before each arm, engine restarted between arms): `16384` cut the read into 5 pieces read in 148.8 s, `32768` into 4 in 134.9 s (-9.3%), `0` into one of 13 chunks in 93.2 s (-37.4%) - that checkout's numbers on its rig, a piece fitting ~14.6 s + 6.5 s a chunk there.
- Why they do not carry over here: a periodic mark is saved at a chunk boundary and the run carries on, so no piece ends at it. What cuts this engine's read into runs is the cut list - a re-read (`STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`), the system-prompt root, a message boundary (`STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY`), the start of the last turn and a pinned prefix - and each of those is one fill and drain.
- So `--prompt-cache-every 0` here skips the periodic marks and the near-tail one (a `--prompt-cache-tail` mark needs `--prompt-cache-every` above 0), while the root, the last turn, a message boundary and a pin are still saved - the same trade the Maya checkout documents for its `0`: a client that rewrote a turn *before* the last one mounts a farther mark. The lever for a fresh long read here is those cuts, not this cadence.

Documentation only: not one line of code or default changes.

## Validation

Tested revision: `4a5fa03f`, one commit on `477ac13c`; not rebased, and GitHub reports it merges cleanly with current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux; docs-only, so there is no build or GPU run.

- The default the bullet cites is the one the engine prints: `src/program/generate.cpp:900`, `--prompt-cache-every N ... (default 16384, 0 = off)`.
- The bullet's Maya numbers are quoted with what they were measured on (that checkout's rig, Maya-L split, the warm prompt, the restarts between arms). No number is claimed for this engine.

**Failed:**

## Limits

- The numbers are the Maya checkout's, not this engine's. They are there to show why the cadence was a dial there and is not one here.

pulls.title: [Engine] choose how many expert slots a prompt loan keeps
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2833) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, rebased onto current `main` (`e88ee39d`); the conflict with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner in `generate.cpp` was resolved. It replaces the closed #2833, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

When a prompt chunk borrows the expert cache's tail, the auto lend caps what it borrows at 90% of the cache. On a small cache that cap, not the number of slots the prompt needs left resident, picked the chunk, and there was no way to choose it. After this change, `STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP=N` (128 by default) is the one reader of the slots a loan must leave resident: on the Q8_0 four-way's 691- and 937-slot stages it leaves 563 and 809 slots where the cap would leave 621 and 843. Unset, every use is 128, exactly as before.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2833 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `71c1ca7` (2026-10-15).

## Approach

`STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP=N` (**128 by default**): the expert-cache slots a loan must leave resident while a prompt chunk borrows the cache's tail. On a small cache it is this number, not the auto lend's 90% cap, that picks the chunk. `STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_KEEP` is accepted as the same knob.

**The clamp is up, not down**: a lend has to leave the elastic K/V a region to grow into (its floor is `STRATA_KV_GROW_FLOOR`, 128 by default), so a smaller `N` is clamped to that floor and the start says so - lower both together to lend more of the cache and let the chunk grow at the K/V's expense. A larger `N` keeps more experts resident for the prompt's own tokens and buys a smaller chunk.

The number is the same one the auto scan, the per-stage lend regions, the serve loan, the smallest cache a start accepts and the vram-elastic reserve used before; this change routes all of them through one reader of the variable.

Unset, every use is 128, exactly as before - this is by construction, not a measurement, and this PR's default run is byte-identical on that path. With the variable set to 128 (its default) the numbers are also unchanged.

## Validation

Tested revision: `badfccd7`, one commit on current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2 (V13.2.86), `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the build machine is the Q8_0 4-way rig (2x RTX 3060 12 GB, 2x RTX 5060 8 GB).

**Passed:**
- `git rebase e88ee39d` - the conflict in `generate.cpp` with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner was resolved; the branch's diff is this feature only.
- `ninja -C build strata` at `badfccd7` - exit 0 (CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`).
- `-fsyntax-only` on `src/program/generate.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code. This was run before the rebase; the full build above covers the rebased head.
- Maya checkout, local commit `71c1ca7` (not this engine, not run by us here; `STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB=400`, a four-way split, a 99,758-token conversation): the binding part reached an 8192-token chunk; a 49,152-token piece went 61,762 -> 57,507 ms (-6.9%) and a whole five-piece read 161,291 -> 158,938 ms, on the live split (5060/5060/3060/3060). It was not a free win there either: a 16,384-token piece that went from three chunks to two lost 3% (28,716 -> 29,651 ms), since the parts run a chunk as a chain and there is less left to overlap.

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- A binding-cap A/B on our rig at a `STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP` other than 128: the four-way Q8_0 runs so far used 128, which is this default.
- Serving the rebased head: only the build was re-run after the rebase; no GPU run was made at `badfccd7`.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both builds compile the same change.

## Limits

- No number is claimed for our rig; the measurement above is the Maya checkout's, on its split and its rig.
- Lowering `N` below `STRATA_KV_GROW_FLOOR` does nothing unless the floor is lowered too; the start says when it clamps.
- A larger `N` buys a smaller chunk, so it trades prompt throughput for expert residency.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the file has no per-backend code.
