pulls.title: [Engine] warm up the prompt path once before READY
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2832) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, rebased onto current `main` (`e88ee39d`); the conflict with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner in `generate.cpp` was resolved. It replaces the closed #2832, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

A session's first prompt pays what no later prompt pays: the first chunk carries every kernel's first launch, the prompt path's own allocations and the tiers' first reads. After this change, `STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=N` (off by default) reads one synthetic N-token prompt through the whole part chain **before the engine says READY**, so the first real request does not pay it. Unset or `0`, the block is skipped and the engine says READY exactly as before.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2832 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `cc58309` (2026-10-14).

## Approach

`STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=N` (`--serve`): one synthetic prompt of N tokens (32 if you ask for less) is read through the whole part chain before READY. `STRATA_GLM_WARM_PROMPT` is accepted as the same knob.

The synthetic ids are spread over the vocabulary (`100 + (i * 131) % 20000`), so the routes are not one expert's. It takes the same loan a request takes (the slots the prompt path is laid out in go non-resident and are refilled from the arena afterwards), and every participant's state is zeroed before and after it, so no conversation can see it. A prompt path that cannot run prints why and the first prompt pays it; the start never fails because of it.

Unset or `0` (the default), the whole block is skipped and the engine says READY exactly as before. Nothing outside the block changes; this is by construction.

## Validation

Tested revision: `af867e73`, one commit on current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2 (V13.2.86), `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the build machine is the Q8_0 4-way rig (2x RTX 3060 12 GB, 2x RTX 5060 8 GB).

**Passed:**
- `git rebase e88ee39d` - the conflict in `generate.cpp` with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner was resolved; the branch's diff is this feature only.
- `ninja -C build strata` at `af867e73` - exit 0 (CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`).
- `-fsyntax-only` on `src/program/generate.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code. This was run before the rebase; the full build above covers the rebased head.
- Reported by blange48 on 4x RTX 5080 16 GB (2026-10-17; not run by us; Linux, layer split 12,24,36, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 8 --batch-groups 4`, v0.1.45 + this PR + #2673, one run per case, warm page cache): time to READY 102 s unset vs 101 s at `STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=512`; first request (a ~325-token prompt) time to first token 1.00 s unset vs 0.72 s at 512; later requests were unaffected.
- Maya checkout's issue #8 reported 95-133 ms/token on a first prompt against 23-44 warm - that checkout's number on its rig.

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- Our own hardware: the reported run above is not ours.
- More than one run per case, and a start with a cold page cache.
- Serving the rebased head: only the build was re-run after the rebase; no GPU run was made at `af867e73`.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both builds compile the same change.

## Limits

- The report is one run per case, so its 0.28 s first-token gain is not a distribution.
- The reported build also carried #2673, whose different-greedy-answers issue is being looked at there; this PR was off in those comparisons, so it does not look involved.
- On this engine the knob is how you measure it: the first request's time to first token, or its `PP` line, with the variable set and unset is the A/B.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the file has no per-backend code.

pulls.title: [Engine] an optional line showing where each prompt chunk's time goes
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2831) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, based on `477ac13c`, and GitHub reports that it merges cleanly with current `main` (`e88ee39d`). It replaces the closed #2831, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

Without a stage line, a prefill change can only be judged by the prompt's ms/token, which mixes the chunk size, the copy lane, the host and the GPU's phases. After this change, `STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=1` (opt-in; unset is off) prints one line a stage a chunk showing where the chunk's wall went, so those parts can be told apart. It also turns the phase timer on. It is a diagnostic and claims no speedup.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2831 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `a34f57c`, with its fixes `04b8d65` (the line's events are destroyed with the prompt path) and `63b3690` (the line reads only the events its chunk recorded). Its spelling `STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_STAGES` is accepted as the same knob, so a config written for that checkout runs unchanged.

## Approach

`STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=1` turns on the chunk's stage line: **one line a stage a chunk** with where the chunk's wall went - the chunk's wall, the copy lane's own span split into what ran before it (lead), the lane itself and what ran behind it (tail), the bytes it moved and the bytes the chunk's consumers waited on (the difference is the ring's read-ahead), the hand-off a later stage of a layer split paid, the GPU's own phases over the chunk, and the experts and host time it spent. It also turns the phase timer on.

Unset (the default), `stages_on()` is false: no line is printed, the phase timer is not read for it, and no extra sync is taken for it. The syncs the line does add when on wait only on copies the compute stream has already waited for (the issuer is joined when the chunk ends), so `STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=0` beside a `--bench` A/B is how you check it costs nothing. The default path is unchanged by construction.

## Validation

Tested revision: `782433f6` (one commit on `477ac13c`; not rebased, and GitHub reports it merges cleanly with current `main` `e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2; the development branch carries `sm_86` + `sm_120` builds.

**Passed:**
- `-fsyntax-only` on `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean.
- The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- A full `ninja -C build strata` at this exact head: only the syntax check above was run at `782433f6`; the full build was of the development branch carrying the same change.
- A served run with `STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=1` at this head: the line has not been observed here, so its output and its cost are unverified.
- The set-vs-unset `--bench` A/B that prices the line. The design keeps the cost at zero by waiting only on work already joined, but that is reasoning, not a measurement.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. The change adds no backend-specific branch; it uses the same stream/event API the file already used, and the events are only created when the knob is on.

## Limits

- This is a diagnostic; it makes no claim to speed anything up.
- Its own cost is unmeasured here. The set-vs-unset A/B under `--bench` is the check.
- The three Maya fixes are carried, but no Maya measurement is quoted for this engine.

pulls.title: [Engine] a long prompt can borrow the MTP drafter's memory while it reads
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2830) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, based on `477ac13c`, and GitHub reports that it merges cleanly with current `main` (`e88ee39d`). It replaces the closed #2830, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

A long prompt's ring is bounded by the VRAM the prompt path can borrow, so on a full card the read waits on the ring. The MTP drafter's 512 routed experts are 708 MB (675 MiB) that only the **decode** reads - a prompt's passes run the draft layer's dense tensors and its K/V - so while a request that **reads** enough tokens is being read, that block can become the prompt path's ring. Before: the ring is whatever the layout could free elsewhere. After: `STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=TOKENS` (opt-in) lends the block in place for such a request and takes it back before the first decode window; a turn that reuses a cached prefix and reads only a few hundred tokens does not take the room or pay its two 675 MiB DMAs.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2830 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commits `7df369c` (`STRATA_GLM_ROOM_MIN`), `d4d0792` (the tail's slots rounded up to the largest blob) and `5ccf9a4` (the in-place shape, for the MTP config's NextN block). Counting what a request reads, rather than the whole prompt, is this port's change, made after the report below.

## Approach

`STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=TOKENS` (`--serve` with `--mtp`): a request that reads at least TOKENS prompt tokens (`0`: every request) uses the MTP drafter's 512 routed experts as the prompt path's ring while it is read. TOKENS counts the tokens this request reads, not the whole prompt: a turn that reuses a cached conversation prefix and reads a few hundred tokens gains nothing from the room. The prompt path's ring is pointed **at the block itself**: `slot i = experts_base + (i - rule) * MAXBLOB` (135 slots on a Q8_0 pack, whose largest blob is 4.98 MiB). Opening and closing a room moves the ring count alone (`Prefill::set_ring_room_active`): the block is never freed, never allocated again and never moves, so no prompt path is laid out again, the decode's captured round/step graphs stay valid (nothing is dropped), and what comes back before the first window is the decode's own bytes (`MtpDrafter::experts_reclaim`). In the measured shape's successor this is two 675 MiB DMAs around the read.

The room is opened after the reused prefix is known (`read_from`) and immediately before `lend()`, so a relayout still re-carves with the room; a request that must be re-read from 0 (`STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`) counts all of its tokens.

Limits, refused with the reason at start: `--serve` only, `--mtp` needed, `--batch` not supported (its slot drafters share the solo drafter's weights). A layer split is fine (the room goes to the prompt path on the drafter's card), `--pipeline-windows` is fine (the room closes before the request's first window), and `--prefill-head-alias` is fine.

Unset (the default) `mtp_room_min` is `-1` and not one line of the room runs; the prompt path is laid out exactly as before. The new code is reachable only behind that check. This is by construction, not by a measurement. `=0` keeps the behaviour that was measured: every request takes the room (the 2026-10-19 control did, on 7-token continuations).

## Validation

Tested revision: `41bff1d3` (three commits on `477ac13c`; not rebased, and GitHub reports it merges cleanly with current `main` `e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the Q8_0 4-way rig is 2x RTX 3060 12 GB and 2x RTX 5060 8 GB.

**Passed:**
- `ninja -C build strata` on the parent engine and on `41bff1d3` - both exit 0; the two binaries differ by this work.
- First shape on our Q8_0 4-way rig (2026-10-16): the room opened, the 675 MiB really went into the ring, the block came back before the first window and the decode ran unchanged. It bought no time at 3,080 or 14,859 tokens and cost 3.4-4.0 s per roomed request, which is why the in-place shape replaced it.
- In-place shape and read threshold on our Q8_0 4-way rig (2026-10-19): two engines from the same branch (the parent commit against this one), one start each, `STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=1024`. One 5,042-token chat and three continuations that echoed the answer back. The parent lent the room for the whole 5,096-token prompt on continuations that read 61, 7 and 7 tokens (lend ~102 ms + reclaim ~104 ms); this commit lent nothing. Read time 2,054 -> 1,813 ms, 360 -> 153 ms, 344 -> 152 ms; time to first token 2.110 -> 1.869 s, 0.409 -> 0.203 s, 0.390 -> 0.199 s. A `MIN=0` control on this binary still opened the room on the 7-token continuations (time to first token 0.432 / 0.415 s), so `=0` is unchanged and the difference is the room, not the binary. The cold request still took the room in both arms.
- Reported by merbanan on an 8 GB RTX 2060 SUPER (2026-10-18; a port onto a 0.1.45-based branch, not run by us): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--serve --mtp` (Q2_0 drafter, 675 MiB), `--resident-budget-gib 40`, `--kv k8v4 --kv-resident 20480`, `--prefill auto`. The auto chunk was 6,656 tokens with a 96-slot ring; the room added 303 slots (399 in all), chunk unchanged. `STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=0` against the same build unset (paired A/B, 3 pairs, prompt tok/s): 4K 448.4 -> 527.2 (+17%), 16K 558.9 -> 658.1 (+17%), 32K 584.0 -> 719.7 (+23%); decode moved -0.27 / +1.42 / -0.17 (noise). The lend cost 107 ms per roomed request. `STRATA_PREFILL_RING` alone showed the ring was the limit (192 slots: +9.8% / +6.2% / +2.3%, decode -3.1 to -3.6 tok/s). First-token logits after a 15,521-token prompt were bitwise equal to the unset run (two runs per arm, all four identical), the 48-token greedy replies matched, and the drafter's acceptance after reclaim was normal (27 of 34).

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both builds compile the same change.
- More than one run per timing on our rig, and `--prefill-head-alias`.
- A run against a revision based directly on `e88ee39d`: this head is based on `477ac13c` and was not rebased; GitHub reports it merges cleanly.

The measurements above are listed with what they were measured on. No blanket speedup is claimed: the knob is how you measure it, the same prompt with the variable set and unset, `PP` line against `PP` line. `7df369c` records the room as not yet measured, with its standing baseline 89.5 s (1,123 tok/s) on its byte-identical 100,535-token read.

## Limits

- The ring gain appears where the ring is the limit (the 8 GB card above) and is nil where it is not (our Q8_0 rig).
- The read threshold's gain is separate and does not depend on the ring: it removes the room's own DMA from turns that reuse a conversation, about 0.2 s per short turn on our rig.
- `--serve --mtp` only; `--batch` is refused because its slot drafters share the solo drafter's weights.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the file has no per-backend code.

pulls.title: [Engine] each GPU can choose its own prompt chunk size
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
> **Why this PR was recreated.** The original (#2829) was opened from the `gopinath87607/Strata` fork. Deleting that fork deleted its branches, and GitHub closes every pull request whose branch lived in a deleted fork - a closed PR whose source branch is gone cannot be reopened. This is the same work from a new fork, rebased onto current `main` (`e88ee39d`); the conflict with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner in `generate.cpp` was resolved. It replaces the closed #2829, which was closed by the fork's deletion, not by a maintainer.

## Problem and result

Strata's layer split is one prompt path: every stage reads prompt chunks of the chain's size. A card whose expert cache cannot fund that chunk therefore pulls every stage down to its number (the `#448` warning), even when the other cards could read more. After this change, `STRATA_PREFILL_MAX` gives each prompt-path participant its own opt-in ceiling: a capped stage lays out at `min(chain, its cap)` and reads each larger hand-off in its own steps, while the other stages keep the chain's chunk. A ceiling only lowers a stage and never raises one. Unset, no number changes.

## Related discussion

The original pull request and its discussion: #2829 (closed when its fork was deleted; this PR replaces it). The work comes from the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `ef3b6e7` (2026-10-15).

## Approach

`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,4096,8192,8192"` - an opt-in ceiling on the prompt chunk of each prompt-path participant, in the split's order. Entry 0 is the first card's path (it reads the chunk's embeddings and hands its rows on), entry *i* the *i*-th stage; `0` or an absent entry is no ceiling, and values are multiples of 256. `STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_MAX` is accepted as the same knob.

The ceiling is the other choice to one grid: a capped stage lays out at `min(chain, its cap)` and `Prefill::run_impl`'s `c0 += m.T` loop reads each larger hand-off in steps of its own, forwarding each sub-step, while the other stages keep the chain's chunk.

Every chunk-pricing site prices a part at its own chunk: the auto scan (`fits_one`, `ring_room`, the old candidate list), the serve loan (`lend`), the resident-RAM lend regions, stage init (at the stage's own maximum - `relayout` requires `chunk <= T_max`), the init retry, split-small's extra slots, the own-buffers headroom test and the head-alias candidates. The start prints one line per capped entry: `strata serve: prompt chunk: CUDA%d reads N tokens a step (STRATA_PREFILL_MAX N)`, with `, inside a larger chain chunk` when the cap is below the chain's.

Unset, not one number changes: the list is empty, `part_chunk` / `part_ceiling` return the chain chunk, `max_head` is 0, and the new print loop runs zero times. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Validation

Tested revision: `7a4175d5`, one commit on current `main` (`e88ee39d`). Environment: Linux, CUDA 13.2 (V13.2.86), `sm_86` + `sm_120`; the build machine is the Q8_0 4-way rig (2x RTX 3060 12 GB, 2x RTX 5060 8 GB).

**Passed:**
- `git rebase e88ee39d` - the conflict in `generate.cpp` with upstream's `chunk_vram` prompt planner was resolved; the branch's diff is this feature only.
- `ninja -C build strata` at `7a4175d5` - exit 0 (CUDA 13.2, `sm_86` + `sm_120`).
- `-fsyntax-only` on `generate.cpp` with the build's own flags - clean; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code. This was run before the rebase; the full build above covers the rebased head.
**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- The binding-cap A/B on our rig (`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,8192,8192,2048"`, expecting the chain to rise toward CUDA0's own 6912 while CUDA3 reads its hand-offs in 2048-token steps). Not run; no speedup is claimed.
- Serving the rebased head: only the build was re-run after the rebase; no GPU run was made at `7a4175d5`.
- HIP and SYCL builds: no toolchain on this machine. `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both builds compile the same change.

Measured elsewhere: the Maya checkout's local commit `ef3b6e7` (not this engine, not run by us here) measured moving every part as a loss - 94,840 ms for the capped 16k/16k/8k/7k shape against 91,718.9 ms for 13 equal chunks of 7,744, on its byte-identical 100,535-token read (an earlier nesting took 98,568.1 ms). That negative result is why the ceiling only lowers a stage and why it is opt-in.

On the start log of the four-way Q8_0 rig this was written for: the chain settles at 4096 because CUDA3's 690 slots cannot fund 6912 (`WARNING: prompt chunk 4096 tokens, not 6912 ...`, `#448`). That is the case the knob is for; the A/B that would price it has not been run.

## Limits

- The knob only helps when one participant's cache is the binding limit. The one measurement we have says capping every part is a loss on its rig.
- No number is claimed for this engine; the A/B above is how the gain or loss on a given rig is measured.
- HIP and SYCL are unverified beyond the fact that the file has no per-backend code.

pulls.title: [Other] fix(setup AMD): engine probes get the engine's lib_dirs on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux (the PATH-only #2372 env made strata --families exit 127, so setup falsely refused Qwen3.6)
pulls.author: xxxliqu1dxxx
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Setup's own engine probes (`strata --families`, `strata-device --list-devices`) only got the
engine's ROCm `lib_dirs` on `PATH` (#2372), which the dynamic loader only honors on Windows.
On AMD Linux the probes exited 127 on `libhipblas.so.3`, so `./setup.sh --backend hip` Step 4
falsely said "this engine does not run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B yet" while the local HIP engine does
run it. After the change, on POSIX the `lib_dirs` are prepended to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (existing
value preserved); on Windows the `PATH` behavior is byte-identical. The probes exit 0.

## Related discussion

Resubmission of #2914, closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset (its head branch was force-pushed, so GitHub
would not reopen it — this one links that PR). Follow-up to #2372 (commit 093108c). No open issue. Focused fix,
no scope agreement needed.

## Approach

`engine_env` only: on POSIX, `lib_dirs` are prepended to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` instead of `PATH`;
on Windows the `PATH` prepend is unchanged. Mirrors `serve/server.py`'s existing
`"PATH" if os.name == "nt" else "LD_LIBRARY_PATH"` choice. Left alone: the engine binary, the
build, the server launch env, the `engine_families` fallback, `hip_lib_dirs`, prebuilt Windows
engine handling.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python tools/test_setup_amd.py` — revision d409ec38 (rebased on main, 0.2.0-beta), local
  Windows PC (no GPU needed): 42 tests OK. Covers `EngineLaunchEnv`: the Windows `PATH`
  behavior (pinned to `os.name = "nt"`), the new `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` test (lib dir first,
  existing value preserved, `PATH` untouched), and the two probe tests.
- Live check on an AMD Linux box (Radeon RX 9060 series, gfx1200, 16 GB VRAM, 31 GB RAM,
  local HIP engine 0.1.45): `env = setup.engine_env(Path('engine'))` +
  `engine/strata --families` → rc 0, prints `qwen4exp qwen35moe` (previously exit 127).

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** multi-GPU, Windows live run (no Windows AMD box), NVIDIA/CUDA paths (untouched by
the change).

## Limits

Only affects the two setup probe commands' environment on non-Windows. No behavior change on
Windows, in the engine, the build, or the server.

pulls.title: [Engine] metal: the request's sampling on the Mac engine (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, seed, penalties, logit_bias)
pulls.author: oceanio
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On the Mac (Metal) engine every request decodes greedily. `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `seed` and the
penalties reach the engine on its `GEN` line but change nothing, and `logit_bias` is dropped. Since 0.1.45 the server
also sends the model card's sampling when a request gives none, and on a Mac that has no effect either. Nothing in the
log or the response says so (#3006).

With this PR the Mac engine samples as the PC engine does: the same chain and order (logit_bias, penalties, top_k,
top_p, min_p, temperature), one Philox draw per token keyed by the seed and the position, so a fixed seed repeats its
text and another seed gives another. Temperature 0 (or none) stays greedy and gives the same tokens as before.

## Related discussion
#3006 (the bug, reproduced again on 0.2.0-beta; see Validation). A focused fix, so no scope issue first.

## Approach
`Verifier::run`'s Metal branch returned the window's argmax. The CUDA path samples on the host after its window; this
PR does the same on the Mac, on the CPU, over the window's head logits, which are already in unified memory (no copy).
A request that is greedy and has no penalties and no `logit_bias` keeps the window's argmax, so its tokens are exactly
the old ones. The MTP drafts stay greedy and a draft is kept when the sampled token equals it, as on the PC.

- `metal/src/engine/host_sampler.cpp` / `.h`: the CUDA sampler's chain with the kernels' float/double arithmetic and
  tie order. 9-46 µs per row on 248,320 logits (M5 Max), so no GPU kernel.
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`: an accessor for row t of the last window's head logits.
- `src/core/verify.cpp`: the sampling after the Metal window (inside `#if defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)`), and one line in
  `set_logit_bias` that every backend compiles: `if (le_ >= 0 && le_ < g_->n_layers) return true;`. The Metal init
  leaves `le_` at -1, which the old test read as "an earlier stage" and so never stored the bias. The CUDA, HIP and SYCL
  inits set `le_` to `n_layers` when it is -1 (`verify.cpp`, `init`), so after init the condition is the same for them.

## Validation
Environment: M5 Max 128 GB, macOS 26.7.1, Command Line Tools 27.0 (Apple clang 21). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S
(SC117's abliterated build, the official two-file layout), resident, `--spec 2` with MTP, `--mmap-experts`,
`--max-context 262144`. Base = `main` 3fa1b524 (0.2.0-beta + 7 commits), built from the same tree.
Rebased since onto `main` e88ee39d (2026-10-20; its 5 new commits change no engine, Metal or server file): the
3 commits build again with all Metal targets, `host_sampler_parity` passes again; the runs below are on 3fa1b524.

**Passed:**
- `ninja -C build-metal` (all Metal targets), at each of the 3 commits: 0 errors, no new warnings.
- `build-metal/host_sampler_parity` (CPU): 592 picks, all equal a serial transcription of the CUDA kernels
  (`sampler_parity.cpp`'s mirror); Philox matches 4,096 draws.
- `python3 tools/metal_sampling_test.py --exe build-metal/strata --config <cfg>`: 13 of 13 pass. On the base build the
  same script fails 11 of 13 (every seed gives the greedy text; penalties and `logit_bias` change nothing). 208
  one-token requests drew exactly the token a reference sampler (written in the test from `sampler.cu`) draws from the
  same dumped logits.
- #3006's reproduction through `serve/server.py` (9 requests, the curl script in the issue): base, 9 of 9 print the
  greedy sentence; this PR, the greedy request prints the same sentence as the base, and the other 8 (seeds 1-3 at
  temperature 1.0, top_k/top_p/min_p, the card's defaults, penalties, `logit_bias` 760:-100) each print another
  sentence; the banned first token is not picked.
- Greedy unchanged: temperature 0 through the server on a 28-, a 2,257- and a 16,180-token prompt, identical text to
  the base build.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds (no such toolchains on a Mac). The only line they compile is the `set_logit_bias` test
  above. Asking for a build on one of them before this leaves draft.
- Other Macs and models; Swift / Unsloth packs; batch slots (Metal has none on `main`, #2715).
- Not ported: the opt-in draft schemes `STRATA_SPEC_COUPLED`, `STRATA_SPEC_PROB`, `STRATA_SPEC_GUMBEL` (the Mac drafts
  greedily).

## Limits
- Sampled decode is a little slower than greedy: 74.8 / 72.9 / 68.8 against 76.3 / 83.3 / 78.3 tok/s over 3 runs
  (4 short prompts, 256 tokens, MTP; `--bench`), because fewer drafts are kept (0.70 against 0.72) and the texts
  differ. The pick itself costs under 0.05 ms a token.
- The card's presence penalty now applies on a Mac too: a client that wants the old greedy text sends
  `temperature: 0` and `presence_penalty: 0` (documented in docs/MAC.md).

pulls.title: Metal: run Gyro (trellis TQ2_T/TQK6/TQK7) models on Apple Silicon
pulls.author: mnott

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

pulls.body:
Gyro-M now runs on the Metal engine. Until now Metal refused Gyro files at load ("no trellis kernels").

**This PR builds on #3231** (Mac conversation cache). Its first 4 commits are that PR; the 5 Gyro commits follow.

## What's in it

- **Kernels.** TQ2_T (the type Gyro-M uses for gate, up and down), TQK6 and TQK7 (Gyro-S): decode GEMV, the v2 prompt expert GEMMs, and the Hadamard rotation. The CPU reference is `src/kernels/cpu/tq_cpu.cpp`.
- **Engine.**
  - `native_expert_supported` accepts types 144-146.
  - The Hadamard rotations are wired into the decode window and the prompt chain.
  - The trellis gate/up tile uses 16 lanes, because 80 units per row do not split evenly across 32.
- **Single-GGUF Gyro.** The PLE table (`per_layer_token_embd`, ~54 GB, contiguous) sits inside the model file. It is now excluded from the wrapped GPU buffers: only the head and tail ranges are wrapped (37.6 of 92 GB), with no read-ahead on the table. The table is still read with direct I/O. Files with a separate PLE shard (IQ3_S) keep the old path; `STRATA_METAL_WRAP_PLE=1` forces it.
- **Tests.** `metal/tests/tq_parity`: 81/81 PASS (rel L2 ~1e-7 against the exact dot; the Hadamard rotation is bit-identical to `hadamard_rotate`). `moe_mm_parity` PASS. `docs/GYRO.md` updated.

## Measured (M5 Max, 128 GB)

| | IQ3_S | Gyro-M |
|---|---|---|
| Engine footprint | ~61-65 GB RSS | 23-26 GB + 37.6 GB weights mapped |
| 20k prompt decode, prose / edit | 84 / 121 tok/s | 73-79 / 110 tok/s |
| Per-layer expert GEMV (top-10) | 57.6 us, 405 GB/s | 65-67 us, 190-194 GB/s |
| Agent coding task (3 parts), one agent | 7.4 min | 8.1 min |
| Same task, quality gates (tsc, build, full tests) | all pass | all pass |

- **Two engines on one Mac.** Because the mapped weights are shared, two Gyro-M engines fit in 128 GB (2 x 24 GB + 37.6 GB). Running one agent each did 1.28x the work of a single engine; per-engine decode drops to 56-69 tok/s on the shared GPU.
- **Where decode could get faster.** It is ALU-bound on the trellis hash/lookup; an int8 LUT is the obvious next step.

## Not covered

- TQK6/TQK7 have not run on a full model (no Gyro-S file).
- `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=1` is encoded for trellis but untested.
- The kernel source path is compiled in; `STRATA_METAL_KERNELS` overrides it.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: temperature 0 stays greedy - no model-card penalties on a greedy request (#2940)
pulls.author: christopherrobertbrooks-tech
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Since a8091f4d (#2685) the server merges the model card's sampling under every request. A request that asks for
`temperature: 0` keeps its temperature but still gets the card's `presence_penalty: 1.5` (Flash-Next when not
thinking; Qwen3.6 in both thinking states). The engine then samples from penalized logits: the answer is not the
greedy one, and on the Qwen3.6 engine the MTP drafts never run (`spec` needs `!smp.needs_logits()`), so every
temperature-0 request shows `drafts accepted 0 of 0`. Still the case on 0.2.0-beta.

With this change, when the request, the shared Chat settings or the config's `sampling` block (the first of them
that sets a temperature) asks for temperature 0, the card's penalties are left out. The rest of the card (top_p and
top_k, which greedy decoding ignores) and any penalty the request or the config sets itself still apply. `/props`
reports the same. Requests that do not ask for temperature 0 are unchanged.

## Related discussion

Replaces #3119 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset; GitHub can't reopen it after the rebase). Resolves #2940: its first suggestion (temperature 0 skips the card's set). The second (a config `sampling` block
replacing the card instead of merging over it) is left alone.

## Approach

`model_card_sampling(arch, thinking, greedy=False)` drops `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty` and
`repetition_penalty` when `greedy` is set; `asks_greedy(*layers)` says whether the first layer that sets a
temperature sets 0. `_run` and `/props` pass it. One sentence in `docs/DETAILS.md` after "Greedy is only for who
asks for it". Rebased on main (e88ee39).

## Validation

Revision: this branch (main e88ee39 + one commit). GPU runs: the v0.2.0-beta tag (3d1fb48, engine 0.1.45.3) with
this commit applied to its `serve/server.py`, built for sm_70 with CUDA 12.9. Tesla V100-PCIe-32GB, i7-13700KF,
16 GB RAM, Linux. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (setup's pinned file),
`--native --max-context 131072 --prefill auto --mtp 2`, every routed expert in VRAM, `reasoning_effort: none`.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_model_card_sampling`: 8 tests OK. The two new ones
  (`test_greedy_gets_no_card_penalty`, `test_asks_greedy`) fail on main (ImportError: `asks_greedy`).
- All 52 `serve/test_*.py` files on main and on this branch: the same result for every file (see Failed).
- The same prompt at `temperature: 0`, 0.2.0-beta vs this branch; "true greedy" = the same request with
  `presence_penalty: 0` added:

| request | server | text = true greedy | drafts accepted | decode |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| prose | 0.2.0-beta | no | 0 of 0 | 114.3 tok/s |
| prose | this branch | **yes** | 115 of 166 | **166.4 tok/s** |
| code | 0.2.0-beta | no | 0 of 0 | 111.6 tok/s |
| code | this branch | **yes** | 260 of 280 | **193.5 tok/s** |

- `strata-bench-v100/benchmark.py` (temperature 0, fresh prompts filled to each size, 256-token answers, engine
  `/metrics`, 3 runs per size, medians), decode tok/s:

| prompt tokens | 256 | 1,000 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 32,768 | 65,536 | 114,688 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.2.0-beta (no drafts) | 109.3 | 104.7 | 85.7 | 59.7 | 40.3 | 23.4 | 14.6 |
| this branch (3,103 of 4,540 drafts accepted) | **156.5** | **156.4** | **116.7** | 57.6 | 34.6 | 19.6 | 11.6 |
| 0.2.0-beta + config `"sampling": {"presence_penalty": 0}` | 156.9 | 157.2 | 117.0 | 57.7 | 34.6 | 19.6 | 11.6 |

  Prefill is the same in all three (1,168 / 1,733 / 1,793 / 1,606 / 1,360 / 984 / 602 tok/s).

**Failed:** `serve/test_responses.py` `NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler` (a thread count:
`1 != 2`), on main and on this branch alike, and on and off on 0.1.45 too.

**Not run:** the Flash-Next engine live, AMD (HIP), Intel, Mac, and the batch path (`--batch N`). This changes the
Python server only, so there is no backend to build.

## Limits

From 16K up the drafts cost on this card with the default FP32 K/V cache (11.6 vs 14.6 tok/s at 114,688). That is
MTP's own trade-off, the same as before a8091f4d, not something this change adds; the long-context decode itself
is #2464.

pulls.title: [GUI] serve: a Chinese / English language switch for the web app (adapted to 0.2.0-beta)
pulls.author: hogtinbao
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The web UI in `serve/web/` is English-only. On a Chinese Windows install the settings page, the sampling drawer, the monitor table and even the server's own validation errors are unreadable to the person running the model, and there is no hook to translate them without editing `app.js` / `monitor.js` — files upstream rewrites regularly.

This PR adds a self-contained translation layer that is opt-in at runtime: one new file `serve/web/i18n-zh.js` plus one `<script>` line in each page. A `Language` control in the header switches between **English**, **简体中文** and **中英文** (Chinese with the English original in small type beneath it). The default stays English, so anyone who never touches the control sees the current UI. Model output is never rewritten — chat bubbles, thinking, code blocks and tool-call payloads are in the skip list.

## Related discussion

This replaces #1836 — the earlier revision of this change (adapted to v0.1.45), closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, not on merit. `/reopen` on that PR failed with `Validation Failed` after the branch was force-pushed to this revision, so this is a fresh pull request with the same change, rebased onto `e88ee39d` and re-verified there.

## Approach

- One new file, no build step, no edits to `app.js`, `monitor.js` or `app.css`; each page gets a single script tag. If the file is absent the pages behave exactly as today.
- A dictionary for static strings plus regex rules for text that carries numbers (`56.9 tok/s`, `3,201 tokens · 12.3 tok/s`, `Saved (…); the earlier file is ….bak`). A `MutationObserver` translates nodes the pages create later, and `title` / `placeholder` / `aria-label` / `<option>` text is translated too.
- Both languages stay in the DOM and CSS picks one, so switching back to English restores the original page (attributes and option labels included).
- Only user-visible chrome is translated; config **values** posted to `/config` remain English (only the option text is translated), so the layer cannot change what the server stores.
- No new dependency, no network access, ~40 KB, MIT, same license header as the rest of the repo.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'` on this branch — Windows 11, Python 3.12, revision `78e13ae` rebased on `e88ee39d`: `Ran 881 tests in 334.4s ... FAILED (errors=1, skipped=20)`. The one error is `serve/test_winjob.py::test_children_end_with_a_killed_server` (see **Failed**).
- `python -m unittest serve.test_winjob -v` on pristine `e88ee39d` in a clean worktree — the same error, 1 of 3 tests, so it is pre-existing on the base revision, not caused by this change.
- Real server on this branch: `serve/server.py` started with the layer attached; `/health` returned `{"status": "ok", "loaded": true, "images": true, "image_generation": true, ...}`; a `/v1/chat/completions` request with `reasoning_effort: "none"` answered normally (18 tokens, `finish_reason: "stop"`) — the API path is untouched.
- `curl /` and `curl /api-monitor` return the pages with the added script tag; `curl /web/i18n-zh.js` serves the file with HTTP 200.
- `node --check serve/web/i18n-zh.js` — no syntax errors.
- Server error strings round-trip: `POST /config {"set": {"lazy_load": true}}` returns the 400 message `lazy_load: lazy loading is text-only, and this model reads images ("vision")`; that exact string, and the other seven validation messages from `serve/runconfig.py`, are matched by the layer's rules (checked by evaluating the file's own dictionary + rules in node, and by POSTing the failing values).
- Manual use on this PC since v0.1.40: chat, monitor, image page and the settings page, in all three language modes, light and dark; switching back to English restores the original UI.

**Failed:**

- `serve/test_winjob.py::test_children_end_with_a_killed_server` — `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable` at `test_winjob.py:32` (the job-object query returns nothing on this machine). Reproduces on `e88ee39d` without this branch, so it is environmental.

**Not run:**

- No automated browser test. Rendering was checked by eye (Edge and Chrome on Windows, 1366×768 and 1920×1080, light and dark, three language modes). Headless `--dump-dom` hangs against the live page on this machine because it streams `/metrics`, so there is no scripted UI check in this PR.
- No Linux or macOS check of the pages. The file is plain DOM code with no platform branches, but I did not run it there.
- No check of the desktop app (`apps/host`) — it has its own strings and is untouched here.

## Limits

- Covers the web UI only, not the Tauri app.
- The translations live in one file that needs a refresh whenever upstream rewords a string; an unmatched string simply stays English (no runtime error). The file is organised by upstream version, so the diff for such a refresh is small.
- Not a general i18n framework — no locale files, no plural rules. If upstream later wants first-class i18n, this should be replaced by it rather than extended.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: report timings on /v1/responses
pulls.author: pschaub
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
/v1/chat/completions returns top-level `timings` (#107), but /v1/responses (#451) does not, although server.py already computes them for every request. Now the final `response.completed` / `response.incomplete` event and the non-streaming reply include the same `timings` object.

## Related discussion
Follow-up to #107 (based on #83) for /v1/responses.

## Approach
`_with_timings` in serve/responses.py copies `done["timings"]` onto the final event; `collect()` keeps it on the non-streaming reply. Nothing else changes.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` on this branch (one commit on main e88ee39), Windows 11, Python 3.12: 882 tests OK, 20 skipped. The same command on main e88ee39 without the change: 881 tests OK, 20 skipped.
- The new `UsageAndStatus.test_responses` fails without the change.
- Live check on main e88ee39 (Windows 11, CUDA): the final event of streamed /v1/responses requests carries timings; without the change it does not.

**Failed:**
none observed

**Not run:**
- Linux and macOS.
- The non-streaming /v1/responses reply was checked by the unit test only; the live check used streaming.
- No CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal build: the change is Python only.

## Limits
`response.failed` carries no timings.

---
Created with Claude Opus 5.5. The result was verified by a human (me) in llama-swap: prompt and decode speeds now show for /v1/responses requests.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] 3x GPU (RTX 5060 Ti + 2080 Ti + 3080 Ti): 0.2.0-beta, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at 262K
pulls.author: wronglebowsk
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A community benchmark report measuring Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE, IQ3_XXS, ~3.4 bpw) running across a heterogeneous 3-GPU desktop setup using Strata 0.2.0-beta (`project 0.1.45.3`, engine `0.1.45`, commit `e88ee39d`) with MTP speculative decoding (`--spec 4`, `--spec-min-p 0.65`) at native context 262,144 tokens.

The pull request adds `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-rtx-5060-ti-plus-rtx-2080-ti-plus-rtx-3080-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs/`: the tool-written `README.md` and the per-request `results.json` (`schema: 1`).

### Hardware and Software
- **GPUs:** 3 NVIDIA GPUs (~39.8 GiB total VRAM)
  - Stage 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GiB (`sm_120`, Blackwell)
  - Stage 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti 11 GiB (`sm_75`, Turing)
  - Stage 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti 12 GiB (`sm_86`, Ampere + MTP head)
- **Host CPU:** Dual Intel Xeon E5-2683 v4 (32 cores / 64 threads, NUMA interleave)
- **RAM:** 184.5 GiB DDR4
- **OS / Drivers:** Linux 7.2.6-generic, NVIDIA Driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4
- **Engine / Branch:** Strata 0.2.0-beta (`origin/main` commit `e88ee39d`), native unified CUDA build (`sm_75`, `sm_86`, `sm_120`)

### Configuration
- **Model:** `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_XXS`
- **Context:** 262,144 tokens (`--kv k8v4`)
- **Parallel Pipeline:** `--layer-split 17,29` across GPUs `[1, 0, 2]`
- **Speculative Decoding:** `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.65 --mtp rt`
- **Vision:** `--vision` sidecar enabled

### Results Summary (3 runs each, medians with ranges)
- **Short Chat Decode:** 81.1 tok/s median (76.0 – 102.5 tok/s, n=9), TTFT 0.44 s (0.41 – 0.47 s)
- **4K Prompt Prefill:** 1,035.1 tok/s median (1,025.0 – 1,047.7 tok/s), TTFT 3.91 s
- **16K Prompt Prefill:** 2,052.6 tok/s median (2,042.6 – 2,059.9 tok/s), TTFT 7.86 s
- **32K Prompt Prefill:** 2,814.2 tok/s median (2,797.2 – 2,815.6 tok/s), TTFT 11.44 s
- **Agent Session:** 99.3 tok/s median decode (79.1 – 125.0 tok/s), 69.3% cache hit rate, first-turn TTFT 1.95 s, turn TTFT 3.47 s across 6 turns.

## Approach

Results only: one folder `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-rtx-5060-ti-plus-rtx-2080-ti-plus-rtx-3080-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs/` containing the tool-generated `README.md` and `results.json`, per `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` "Submit a report" guidelines. No engine or documentation modifications.

## Validation

Passed:
- Suite executed via `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --config strata-sc117-abliterated.json --long` on `main` at `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta).
- All requests completed with 0 errors / 0 failures across short chat, 4K/16K/32K prompts, and 6-turn agent sessions.
- `results.json` validates with `schema: 1`.

Failed:
