pulls.title: [Engine] conversation snapshot: stage parked-state copies through pinned memory on Windows/WDDM
pulls.author: denis-1337
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #3036

Supersedes #3037 (closed by the tracker reset; its head commit became unreachable when the branch was rebased on `main`, so GitHub could not reopen it - the reopen check itself passed).

## Problem and result

On Windows/WDDM, parked-conversation snapshot copies at `--max-context 262144` are refused or corrupted: the engine logs `checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument`, and every later request returns non-finite (NaN) output. After this change the synchronous snapshot copies are staged through a real pinned buffer, and the same workload runs clean on the same rig.

## Related discussion

#3036 (reproduced on 0.2.0-beta and 0.1.45). Bug fix, no defaults changed. Review feedback from @midhatn applied in the second commit.

## Approach

All synchronous running-state copies in `conversation_state.cpp` are staged first through a pinned 16 MiB buffer (device→pinned via the copy engine, pinned→destination via memcpy), because on Windows/WDDM the HIP runtime misclassifies C++ heap destinations as pinned host memory: the direct copy is refused, or when accepted it interleaves with expert H2D streaming on the copy engine and corrupts the bytes (decode then reads garbage as expert weights and the grouped GEMM writes NaN). The save call also passes the copy direction explicitly instead of relying on pointer classification, and the sticky `invalid argument` is consumed and retried once. `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0` restores the old path for A/B. Linux is unaffected (the direct path works there; staging is harmless). Cost: one memcpy hop per snapshot copy; measured decode unchanged (~55 tok/s).

## Validation

Tested on `main` @ e88ee39d (0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3), Windows 11 Pro build 26300, AMD RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), driver 32.0.32015.2008, model IQ3_S, `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4`, tuning table `tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`. The rebased branch file is byte-identical to the file built and tested here.

**Passed:**
- Official 0.2.0-beta install (prebuilt engine 0.1.45), 11 unique ~1.5k-token prompts via `serve/server.py` (park-unique script): `OK=0 ERR=11`, 43 non-finite events — bug reproduces on 0.2.0-beta.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d, unpatched, same script: `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43 — bug present in the 0.2.0-beta source.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d + this patch, same script: 2/2 rounds `OK=11 ERR=0`, 0 non-finite.
- Production constellation (same config, port 1234): 22/22 requests OK, 0 non-finite since engine start, prompt-cache reuse active, decode ~55 tok/s.
- On 0.1.45 (same rig, same scripts): baseline rounds nf=35/41/17 → patched 5/5 rounds nf=0; tuning-table constellation also clean.

**Failed:** none observed with the patch applied.

**Not run:** CUDA, SYCL and Metal builds — no CUDA/SYCL toolchain and no Apple hardware on this machine. The change uses only the CUDA-shaped API already used in this file (`cudaHostAlloc`, `cudaMemcpyAsync`, `cudaStreamSynchronize`, `cudaFreeHost`); it compiles and runs on hardware under HIP. CUDA compilation stays unverified. The `cudaHostAlloc` failure path and the stream-sync failure path are inspection-only (no fault injection), as noted by @midhatn in review.

## Limits

Staging adds one memcpy hop per snapshot copy (a few ms per parked conversation). `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0` restores the old path for A/B. The misclassification itself lives in the WDDM/HIP layer; this PR avoids it on the checkpoint path rather than fixing the classification.

Note: this issue and the accompanying PR were prepared by an AI agent (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, served by Strata itself) together with the account owner.

pulls.title: [Engine] Metal: the #879 guard reads the argmax sentinel where the device row check cannot run
pulls.author: catalinb13
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On the Metal engine a non-finite logits row (#879) reaches the user as a crash instead of a recovery. The #879 guard reads per-window flags that `logits_nonfinite_rows` raises on the device beside the greedy pick, but the Metal port has no kernel of that name — it is a trap stub (`metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`) — so the flags stay zero and `nonfinite_hit` reports a clean window. What a row that is *all* NaN leaves behind is Metal's sampler sentinel: `metal/kernels/sample.metal` seeds the argmax at `bi = 0x7fffffff` and skips NaN elements, so the row keeps the sentinel, `pl_finish` copies it out, and the engine prints `T 2147483647`. The serve loop then dies twice: the detokenizer raises a raw `IndexError: token id 2147483647 is outside the vocabulary (248320)` and kills the request thread, and the engine feeds the sentinel into the drafter and the embedding and segfaults (exit -11) shortly after.

Measured on an M1 Max (macOS, engine built from `main` at `e88ee39d`, Qwen3.8 vocabulary 248320), reproduced when the machine is under enough memory pressure for a row to go NaN.

After this change the sentinel takes the existing #879 recovery, on both sides:
- the engine marks that row non-finite at the pick read, emits none of the window's tokens, and answers `DONE … nonfinite` — the cached state is dropped before the sentinel can reach the drafter, so the follow-on segfault goes away;
- the server raises `EngineNonFinite` if a sentinel id appears in the token stream anyway (an engine binary without this fix), so the request gets the normal path: retried once when nothing went out yet, ends as `"length"` mid-reply, a clean error after a second pass — never a traceback.

## Approach

`Verifier::note_nonfinite` takes the picks that were just read beside it and marks the row of any pick holding `INT32_MAX`. That reading is true on every platform: the id is past every vocabulary, so a pick that holds it is exactly the fact #879 records. All five pick-read sites pass their buffer (`run`, `run_slot_rows`, `run_slots`, `batch_poll`, `pl_finish`). Where the device check already runs, the scan can only agree with it; on Metal it is the whole guard.

The server's arm is one test in `_run` before the detokenizer, raising the same `EngineNonFinite` the `DONE … nonfinite` line raises, so it needs no new recovery code.

## Validation

Passed:
- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_server.NonFiniteLogits serve.test_server.SentinelToken` — 7/7 on this branch off `main` (`d986ecbc`). Two new mock tests: a sentinel before the first token is retried once and answers normally; a sentinel mid-reply ends the reply as `"length"` with the text up to it. The five existing #879 tests still pass.
- Metal engine builds clean; `ctest` 2/2 (`runtime_hello`, `window_cells_test`) on the M1 Max.

Not run:
- the sentinel path with the real model on Metal: it needs an all-NaN row, which only appeared under memory pressure and cannot be provoked on demand (and `STRATA_NAN_INJECT` reports the row through the flags, beside this path). The engine-side arm is therefore compile-and-static evidence; the server-side arm is proven by the tests and by this machine's own crash tracebacks.

Failed: none.

## Limits

- A row with *some* NaN logits still samples its best finite pick on Metal (the sampler skips NaN per element); only an all-non-finite row leaves the sentinel, and that is the case this guard catches.
- The default CUDA/HIP path keeps its byte-identical behaviour unless a pick holds `INT32_MAX`, which on those platforms the device check already reports.

pulls.title: [Engine] session: support multi-GPU layer-split save/restore (format v3)
pulls.author: LuckyKo
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When running Strata with `--layer-split auto` across multiple GPUs, `POST /slots/0?action=save` answers 400: "session files do not support --layer-split". The save was either refused or produced an incomplete file that couldn't be restored. This made `--slot-save-path` unusable for the most common multi-GPU configuration, which is exactly where long-context session persistence matters most (the RAM cost of re-reading a 30K+ token prompt).

After this PR: save and restore work on multi-GPU layer splits. A 94K-token session saves in ~5.5 s and restores in ~3.7 s after an engine restart (vs. 147 s to re-read the prompt from scratch).

## Related discussion

none

## Approach

Introduce **format v3** for session files that carries per-stage data. Version 2 is reserved for PR #2247's BF16 state codec; this build rejects it explicitly at the version gate.

- **Write:** `put_payload` serializes stage 0 (as before), then — only when `stage_images` is non-empty — a count followed by one block per later stage. Each block holds that stage's running state, K/V parts, and checkpoint. The file header version is set to `kVersionStages = 3`.
- **Read:** `get_payload` reads stage 0 identically to v1, then checks the version. For v3 files it reads the stage count (bounded by `limits.max_stages`) and each subsequent stage block, validating geometry and layer range per stage. A v1 file has no stage section; a v2 file is refused at the version gate (not silently misparsed as v1).
- **Save guard:** if `conversation_checkpoints_split` routes any checkpoint to `cs.rest` (incomplete for the split), the save is refused rather than silently dropping it.
- **Read-limit hardening:** `SessionReadLimits` gains `max_stages` and a per-stage `stage_limits` vector. The serve loop populates these from the live engine's stage carves before calling `session_file_read`, so a file from a different split is refused before any allocation.
- **Backward compatible:** v1 files read unchanged. A v3 file opened by old code is refused at the version check.

Supersedes #2590 (closed by mass-cleanup, same branch).

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `build-win-cuda13\conversation_file_test.exe` — 208 checks (rev `94f55cd6`, CUDA 13.4, Windows 11, 2× RTX 5060 Ti sm_120)
- `build-win-cuda13\conversation_snapshot_test.exe` — 4027 checks
- `build-win-cuda13\conversation_cache_test.exe` — 4219 checks
- `build-win-cuda13\conversation_memory_test.exe` — 25 checks
- `build-win-cuda13\conversation_split_failure_test.exe` — 36 allocation-failure cases (stages 1–3)
- `build-win-cuda13\session_save_reclaim_test.exe` — 119 checks
- Smoke test: engine starts on dual-GPU layer-split, chat completion responds, session save/restore round-trip works
- Independent test on Linux (2× NVIDIA A2, sm_86, Debian 13): 23K and 94K token sessions, save/restore verified, invalid files properly refused (by @Eranicus30666, rev `75e7df6b`)

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- `--batch` / parallel slots (no multi-slot test harness)
- Restore with a different GPU split than the save (unit tests cover the refusal path)
- Full-disk / near-full-VRAM restore (see #2409)
- HIP, SYCL, Metal builds (CUDA-only development environment)

## Limits

- Does not support `--batch` (parallel slots) — the stage layout is per-slot and the save format assumes a single active slot.
- A v3 file is not readable by pre-0.2.0 engines (refused at the version check, no data loss).
- The one-clause reply difference observed at 94K tokens by @Eranicus30666 is decode non-determinism (floating-point accumulation order between a fresh prompt pass and an incrementally-built restored state), not a serialization bug.

pulls.title: [Other] Honor STRATA_INSTALL_DIR when locating gguf-py
pulls.author: hulkbig
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When `STRATA_INSTALL_DIR` points to an existing Control installation, standalone tools still fail to find its `third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py` directory unless `STRATA_GGUF_PY` is also set. Control-mode setup writes that dependency beneath its install home, but `_paths.py` only checks the explicit GGUF override, source tree and development tree.

The helper now checks the configured install directory. An isolated reproduction using empty temporary directories goes from the reported missing-gguf-py `SystemExit` to returning the installed path.

## Related discussion

Refs #3269. This implements the report's suggestion to check `$STRATA_INSTALL_DIR/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py`.

## Approach

Keep `STRATA_GGUF_PY` first, then check `STRATA_INSTALL_DIR`, followed by the existing source/development fallbacks. A candidate still needs a `gguf` directory. With `STRATA_INSTALL_DIR` unset or empty, the existing lookup order is unchanged.

The new stdlib-only tests load `_paths.py` directly and use temporary directory trees and process-local environment patches. They require no gguf package or model files.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.14. Base: `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`. Tested candidate tree: `20c39f7e709d092363fb5918e70695ab1b5b8eac`.

**Passed:**

- `python3 -I -S -B tools/test_paths.py -v`: 10/10 on the candidate.
- `python3 -I -S -B -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_paths.py -v`: 10/10 on the candidate.
- `git diff --cached --check`: clean.

**Failed:**

- The identical test file alongside the unmodified base helper, run with `python3 -I -S -B tools/test_paths.py -v`: 7 passed, 1 assertion failure and 2 `SystemExit` errors. All three failures concern the configured install directory: finding it alone, selecting it before source/development copies, and falling back to it from an absent explicit GGUF path.
- No failures on the candidate.

**Not run:**

- `iq_pack.py`, setup, actual gguf imports, model conversion, packaged-Control integration or the full repository suite.
- Windows/macOS execution and backend builds. No backend code changed.

## Limits

`STRATA_INSTALL_DIR` must be set. This does not automatically discover a default per-user installation when the variable is absent, so it does not claim to fix every unpacked-package case in #3269. Setup already supplies `STRATA_GGUF_PY` to its preparation subprocesses; this change concerns standalone discovery.

AI-assisted implementation and test preparation.

pulls.title: sm_70: keep the CUDA layout for the IQ4_NL down projection under Volta mode 8
pulls.author: aleesposito85

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

pulls.body:
sm_70: keep the CUDA layout for the IQ4_NL down projection under Volta mode 8

## What

On Volta (sm_70) with the mode-8 expert layout (`STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`), `native_expert_grouped`
routes the down projection through `native_down_lds_kernel` for both `IQ4_NL` (20) and `Q2_0` (42).
`native_expert_bench` on an IQ3_S pack's `iq2_s`/`iq4_nl` layers shows that choice is a loss for
IQ4_NL — the CUDA layout is faster — while mode 8 keeps its win on gate/up.

This mirrors the existing `sm75_down_em()`: a new `sm70_down_em(em0, d_type)` returns mode 0 for
`d_type == 20` on compute capability 7.0.  `Q2_0` (42), every other type and every other arch keep
their mode, and `STRATA_EXP_MODE` still wins when set.

## Measured

Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, CUDA 12.8, `native_expert_bench`, real rows of the IQ3_S pack, 10 groups,
medians of 300.  `all` is the per-layer expert call (gate/up + fused SwiGLU + q8_1 + down).

| layer | types | T=1 before | T=1 after | T=4 before | T=4 after |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3 | iq2_s / iq4_nl | 63.9 us | **59.1 us (-7.5%)** | 94.7 us | **87.1 us (-8.0%)** |
| 40 | iq3_s / iq4_nl | 59.1 us | **54.0 us (-8.6%)** | 87.7 us | **76.6 us (-12.7%)** |
| 10 | iq2_s / q2_0 | 54.0 us | 54.3 us | 84.2 us | 84.4 us |
| 20 | iq3_xxs / q2_0 | 46.7 us | 46.7 us | 75.9 us | 75.8 us |

The down phase alone on the IQ4_NL layers: 25.8 -> 20.7 us (T=1), 39.2 -> 28.3 us (T=4); gate/up is
untouched (36.3 us at T=1, 55.0 us at T=4, the mode-8 win that stays).

Every row is **bitwise equal** to the reference mode (the bench checks every cell), so this changes
speed only.

## Tests

- `native_expert_bench` … bitwise equal on all rows above.
- Builds with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70 -DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON` (CUDA 12.8).

pulls.title: [Engine] add request-scoped prefill VRAM loans
pulls.author: c3c
pulls.body:
This the rebased version of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1581 for the VRAM loaning part of the PR.
Reopened PR of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105 as I couldn't use /reopen.

## Problem and result

Current main can borrow expert-cache storage for prompt buffers, and
`--prefill-head-alias` can reuse the native output-head allocation. On a tight
8 GiB serve configuration, however, verifier, native-head, and MTP decode
resources still prevent the automatic planner from selecting a large prompt
geometry.

This PR adds a manual request-scoped transaction that releases those
decode-only resources during prefill, grows the elastic expert cache, and
restores all resources and runtime state before generation. It also supports
repeating the transaction for later long messages.

On an RTX 2080 Super Max-Q, enabling the loan in the same binary changed the
automatic plan from a 2,304-token chunk to 5,376 and increased median prefill
from 513.6 to 774.8 tokens/s (+50.9%). Median generation was 30.9 tokens/s in
both arms. The default path is unchanged when the master switch is absent.

## Approach

Example full configuration:

```json
{
  "STRATA_PREFILL_ELASTIC_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_MTP_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_HEAD_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_RETAIN_STARTUP_CHUNK": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_MIN_TOKENS": "50000"
}
```

All six variables are introduced here, but they are not six independent
requirements:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_ELASTIC_LOAN` | Master opt-in; required |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_MTP_LOAN` | Also defer MTP routed experts and draft head |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_HEAD_LOAN` | Also defer the native output head and verifier |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_RETAIN_STARTUP_CHUNK` | Keep the startup planner geometry for the first request |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_LOAN` | Repeat the transaction for later substantial prompts |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_MIN_TOKENS` | Unread-token threshold for repeats; default 1,024, minimum 256 |
| `--vram-elastic`, `--serve`, `--mtp`, `--spec` | Existing upstream options used by the transaction; not introduced here |

The existing `--vram-elastic` option supplies the segmented expert-cache
backend. Startup loans cannot use a prompt-length threshold because the first
request is not known at initialization; the repeat threshold applies only to
later prompts.

Current main already loans expert-cache slots to prompt workspace. This PR
extends the lifetime transaction to resources that are needed only for decode:
the verifier arena/graphs, native output head, MTP routed experts, and MTP draft
head. Reload restores PCIe balancing, adaptive-overlap gating, residency
pre-launch synchronization, logit bias, and MTP draft sampling before decode.

## Safety and supported configurations

The feature is admitted only on the serialized, one-GPU NVIDIA CUDA serve path.
It requires `--serve`, `--vram-elastic`, and CUDA virtual-memory segments of at
least 64 MiB. Startup rejects batch slots, pipeline windows, layer split,
helper/remote/peer caches, HIP, and `--prefill-head-alias`. MTP/head loans
require `--mtp` with `--spec >= 2`; the head loan also requires a native output
head. Invalid combinations fail before resources are deferred.

Multiple conversations are supported when requests are processed sequentially
by one server. Concurrent batch sessions are deliberately rejected. Separate
Strata processes sharing a GPU are not coordinated and must not take loans
concurrently.

The transaction does not change the routing algorithm. A larger cache and a
different chunk geometry can change which experts execute on GPU and the order
of floating-point operations, so generated tokens are not promised to be
bit-identical to a loan-off run.

## Validation

Tested revision: `cf14700f`, based on upstream `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta). The
combined build used this branch plus the separate SM75 native-IQ branch at
`db02a533`.

### Passed

- Windows Release CUDA production build with CUDA 13.4, MSVC 19.51, and SM75
  SASS.
- Three fresh-engine end-to-end runs per configuration, serialized on the same
  machine. The production server was stopped during each run and restored and
  health-checked afterward.
- A default-off A/B against the exact upstream executable: the combined
  rebased binary with every new flag absent measured 513.6 PP median versus
  514.6 PP for current main (-0.2%, within the run ranges), and selected the
  same 2,304/226 plan.
- A later-message lifecycle run: after a short warm-up request, a 31,258-token
  prompt released verifier, native-head, and MTP resources; retried smaller
  geometries when necessary; restored all resources; and generated all 256
  requested tokens without a CUDA/runtime failure.

### Failed

- The repository-wide test build did not complete on Windows because current
  upstream `src/kernels/gdn_chunk_parity.cpp` calls POSIX `setenv`. The
  production target compiles and the end-to-end loan paths run; that unrelated
  current-main test compile failure remains.

### Not run

- HIP and SYCL builds.
- Multi-GPU, batch, pipeline, helper, remote-cache, and peer-cache execution;
  the feature rejects these configurations at startup.
- Other GPU generations after this current-main rebase.
- Full visible-answer parity: the throughput requests reached their 256-token
  reasoning cap, so these runs validate lifecycle and rates, not complete
  answer equivalence.

## Benchmark configuration

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Super Max-Q, 8 GiB, 105 W, compute capability
  7.5.
- CPU/RAM: Intel i7-10875H, 64 GiB RAM.
- PCIe host-to-device probe: approximately 12.2--12.3 GB/s.
- Windows, CUDA 13.4, MSVC Release build with SM75 SASS.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS native GGUF plus IQ3_XXS expert pack.
- Runtime: 65,536 context, Q4_0 KV, 24,576 resident KV cells, MTP `--spec 4`,
  `--short-read 0`, experimental speed projection, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, and
  `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_Q4_TC=1` held constant.
- Request: 31,258 fresh prompt tokens, 256 generated tokens, fresh process for
  every repetition. Values below are medians of three engine timing lines.

## Results

| Configuration | Prompt chunk / ring | PP median (range) | TG median (range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact current-main executable | 2,304 / 226 | 514.6 (513.6--516.1) | 29.9 (29.7--30.0) |
| Combined rebased executable, every new flag absent | 2,304 / 226 | 513.6 (512.8--514.5) | 30.9 (30.7--31.0) |
| Loan flags enabled; SM75 native-IQ extension off | 5,376 / 227 | **774.8** (772.7--779.9) | **30.9** (30.2--31.9) |
| Loans plus [separate SM75 native-IQ extension](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3104) | 4,864 / 512 | 859.4 (859.1--860.5) | 30.9 (30.7--32.6) |

The same-binary isolated loan effect in this workload is +50.9% PP. The
combined row is included to show composition, not attributed to this PR alone;
the [SM75 native-IQ PR](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3104) adds a
separate +10.9% over loans, and the combined gain over current main is +67.0%.

For comparison, current main with `--prefill-head-alias` selected a
1,536-token chunk and measured 370.3 PP median on this exact workload. That is
not a general claim against head alias; it explains why its existing narrower
loan did not replace this transaction on this memory-constrained setup.

The later-message lifecycle run selected 4,352 tokens after bounded retries,
completed prefill at 841.0 PP, restored the deferred resources, and generated
at 28.0 TG. Compared with the 30.9 TG fresh-request median, that is a 9.4%
reduction and remains inside the 10% decode-regression limit used for this
experiment.

## Additional qualification evidence

### Fixed-geometry mechanism check

A matched 2,304/227 experiment held prompt geometry constant to distinguish
the transaction cost from the planner benefit:

| Configuration | Prompt plan | PP | TG |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Loan flags off | 2,304 / 227 | 424.7 | 29.8 |
| Loan flags on, same plan | 2,304 / 227 | 425.1 | 29.3 |

The +0.1% PP difference is noise. The loan is not a faster kernel; its value is
allowing a larger cache/chunk geometry to fit. Benefit therefore depends on
prompt length and on whether releasing the decode resources crosses a useful
planner threshold.

### Cross-GPU loan qualification

The transaction is not SM75-specific. An earlier qualification used an RTX
4070 Ti (12 GiB, SM89), INT8 KV, a 196,608-token context, and a 512-slot staging
ring. These measurements were made on an older v0.1.41 source revision, so they
support the cross-GPU mechanism but are not current-main performance numbers.
Loan-off and loan-on runs were interleaved, serialized, and used fresh engine
processes. The 36k result is a three-run median and the 72k result is a five-run
median; completions were capped at 512 tokens.

| Fresh prompt | Loan | Prompt chunk | PP | TG | GPU prefill |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 36,061 tokens | Off | 8,448--8,960 | **2,562.9** | **54.8** | 13.811 s |
| 36,061 tokens | On | 15,104 | 2,539.4 | 52.9 | **12.987 s** |
| 72,061 tokens | Off | 8,960 | 2,617.0 | 54.1 | 27.271 s |
| 72,061 tokens | On | 15,104 | **2,680.9** | **54.9** | **25.772 s** |

At 36k, loans reduced GPU prompt work by 6.0%, but the fixed resource-reload
cost left engine PP 0.9% lower. At 72k, they reduced GPU prompt work by 5.5%
and improved engine PP by 2.4%. The five-run 72k PP ranges were
2,604.3--2,633.7 off and 2,501.1--2,696.3 on; four of the five loan-on runs
were at least 2,673.5 PP, with one retained slow outlier. This crossover is why
the feature remains a manual opt-in rather than a default.

pulls.title: [Engine] --ple-gguf: accept a table-only PLE shard from another file set (Q8_0 table beside IQ3_S / UD-Q4_K_XL)
pulls.author: q8atnight
pulls.body:
**Problem.** Passing `--ple-gguf` with the PLE table of a *different* file set stops the engine at start-up:

```
strata generate: native dense projections: native dense: additional shard must match the architecture-validated first shard's split metadata
```

The use case: running a smaller quant (ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL) with the **Q8_0** n-gram/PLE table that unsloth ships as UD-Q5_K_XL / UD-Q6_K_XL / Q8_0 shard 3. That table is read from the SSD, so it costs no RAM. UD-Q5_K_XL shard 3 holds exactly one tensor, `per_layer_token_embd.weight`, and has the same sha256 (`34efd79a…`) as the UD-Q6_K_XL shard 3 listed in docs/UNSLOTH_Q6.md.

**Cause.** With `--native`, generate.cpp appends `o.ple_gguf` to `o.native_dense_gguf` unless the file is a `strata-ple` table. A foreign shard then fails native_dense's split-metadata check, even though it holds no projections at all.

**Fix (4 lines, src/program/generate.cpp).** A PLE file whose only tensor is `per_layer_token_embd.weight` is treated like a `strata-ple` table: it is used for the table and not added to the dense shards. Nothing else changes. When `--ple-gguf` is not given, or names one of the model's own shards, the code path is the same as before.

**Validation (passed).**
- Hardware: 2x RTX 3090 (sm_86, layer split 24), Ryzen 9 3950X, 121 GiB RAM, Linux, CUDA 13.0 build.
- Base: v0.2.0-beta `3d1fb480` with this commit.
- IQ3_S and UD-Q4_K_XL start with `--ple-gguf <UD-Q5_K_XL-00003-of-00006.gguf>`. The log shows `PLE on, table 320001536 rows of …UD-Q5_K_XL-00003-of-00006.gguf`.
- Without the commit, the same configs refuse to start with the error above.
- Deterministic gate (greedy; 3 prompts + 2 questions on a 20K-token prompt): stock v0.2.0 and v0.2.0 with this commit give **identical output** on IQ3_S, UD-Q4_K_XL and UD-Q5_K_XL. Every model was run with the Q8_0 table in both arms.
- Speed, UD-Q4_K_XL int8 KV, Q8_0 table against its own IQ4_NL table: within noise on decode and prefill (flashbench 1K–128K). Full numbers in #3278.

**Not run.** HIP and SYCL builds (the change uses only `GgufFile::tensors()`, no backend code). The branch sits on `85b75dcb` (my fork cannot push the newer workflow files). The same commit cherry-picks cleanly onto current main `e88ee39d`. It was built and tested on the v0.2.0-beta base above, not on main.

**Limits.** The check is by tensor list: a one-tensor shard that holds only the PLE table. A foreign table shard that also carried projections would still be refused, which is correct.

*Written, built and tested by Claude Opus 5.5 working as an agent on this machine.*

pulls.title: [Engine] extend native-IQ prefill dispatch to SM75
pulls.author: c3c
pulls.body:
This the rebased version of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1581 for the native-IQ prefill part of the PR.
Reopened PR of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3104 as I couldn't use `/reopen`.

## Problem and result

Strata already has fused native-IQ prompt-expert kernels, but on SM75/Turing the
native path only admits the Q2_0/Q2_0 pair. Native expert packs using IQ2, IQ3,
or IQ4 gate/up tensors therefore fall back to the ordinary MMQ prompt path.

This PR adds a separate, manual A/B switch for the additional SM75 format
pairs. On an RTX 2080 Super Max-Q with an IQ3_XXS pack, enabling the extension
on top of the same [VRAM-loan configuration](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105) increased median prefill from 774.8
to 859.4 tokens/s (+10.9%). Median generation remained 30.9 tokens/s.

The default path is unchanged when the new switch is absent.

## Approach

Enable the extension with:

```json
{
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED": "1",
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75": "1",
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75": "1"
}
```

`STRATA_PF_FUSED` and `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75` already exist. This PR introduces
only `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75`; it is deliberately separate so existing
SM75 users who enabled the Q2_0 path do not silently opt into new arithmetic.
`STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE` remains the existing global native-path A/B disable.

| Variable | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED` | Existing upstream fused-expert opt-in; still required |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75` | Existing upstream SM75 Q2_0 opt-in; still required |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE` | Existing upstream native-path A/B disable; unchanged |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75` | New manual gate for the additional SM75 IQ formats |

The new SM75 coverage is:

- Gate/up: IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, and IQ4_XS.
- Down: Q2_0 and IQ4_NL.

Admission checks the actual CUDA capability, the specific format pair, and
kernel occupancy. The admitted SM75 formats use the qualified 128-row Turing
shape. Unsupported pairs continue through MMQ. SM80+, SM120, HIP, and decode
dispatch are unchanged.

The path keeps the same selected experts, routing weights, and weighted scatter
order. It does change prompt expert arithmetic and may therefore change prompt
state or generated tokens slightly; it is not claimed to be bit-identical to
MMQ.

The implementation updates the SM75 capability description, native-IQ public
contract and CUDA dispatch in `include/strata/core/sm75_series.hpp`,
`include/strata/prefill/moe_fused_iq.hpp`, and
`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`. The corresponding format matrix is covered in
`tests/cuda/prefill_fused_iq_test.cpp`, and `docs/DETAILS.md` documents the new
manual gate.

## Validation

Tested revision: `44500122`, based on upstream `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta). The
combined end-to-end build used the same native commit plus the separate
[VRAM-loan branch](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105) at `db02a533`.

### Passed

- Windows Release CUDA build with CUDA 13.4, MSVC 19.51, and SM75 SASS:
  `strata.exe` and `prefill_fused_iq_test.exe`.
- The focused native-IQ CUDA suite passed on the RTX 2080 Super Max-Q for every
  admitted gate/up and down pair listed above, plus the existing Q2_0/Q2_0
  pair. In its reference cases, fused-versus-MMQ relative RMS was
  `3.5e-5`--`4.0e-4`; the large timing cases also passed, with relative RMS
  `1.2e-4`--`2.1e-4`.
- Three fresh-engine end-to-end runs per configuration, serialized on the same
  machine. The production server was stopped during each run and restored
  afterward.
- With every new flag absent, the combined rebased binary measured 513.6 PP
  median versus 514.6 PP for the exact upstream binary (-0.2%, within the run
  ranges), with the same 2,304/226 plan.

### Failed

- The repository-wide test build did not complete on Windows because current
  upstream `src/kernels/gdn_chunk_parity.cpp` calls POSIX `setenv`. The
  production and focused native-IQ targets compile and run; that unrelated
  current-main test compile failure remains.

### Not run

- HIP and SYCL builds.
- Other GPU generations and multi-GPU configurations.
- Full visible-answer parity: the throughput requests reached their 256-token
  reasoning cap, so these runs validate execution and rates, not complete
  answer equivalence.

## Benchmark configuration

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Super Max-Q, 8 GiB, 105 W, compute capability
  7.5.
- CPU/RAM: Intel i7-10875H, 64 GiB RAM.
- PCIe host-to-device probe: approximately 12.2--12.3 GB/s.
- Windows, CUDA 13.4, MSVC Release build with SM75 SASS.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS native GGUF plus IQ3_XXS expert pack.
- Runtime: 65,536 context, Q4_0 KV, 24,576 resident KV cells, MTP `--spec 4`,
  `--short-read 0`, experimental speed projection, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, and
  `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_Q4_TC=1` held constant.
- Request: 31,258 fresh prompt tokens, 256 generated tokens, fresh process for
  every repetition. Values below are medians of three engine timing lines.

## Results

| Configuration | Prompt chunk / ring | PP median (range) | TG median (range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [VRAM loans](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105), SM75 native-IQ extension off | 5,376 / 227 | 774.8 (772.7--779.9) | 30.9 (30.2--31.9) |
| Same configuration, extension on | 4,864 / 512 | **859.4** (859.1--860.5) | **30.9** (30.7--32.6) |

The isolated net effect in this workload is +10.9% PP. This is an end-to-end
feature A/B rather than a kernel-only number: native-IQ changes the supported
expert execution path and the planner admits a different chunk/ring geometry.

The separate [request-scoped VRAM-loan PR](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105)
is not an algorithmic requirement. It was needed on this 8 GiB configuration
to free enough prefill VRAM for the useful native shape. A larger-memory GPU
may admit the native path without it.

The SM75 native-IQ extension itself is independent of upstream
`--prefill-head-alias` and can be used with it. The separate VRAM-loan PR
rejects head alias because both features manage the native output-head
allocation at the prompt/decode boundary.

pulls.title: [Other] setup: calibrate a dual config whose gpu is the string 0,1
pulls.author: MEsfits
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Setup's calibration of a dual config whose `"gpu"` is the string form `"0,1"` (accepted and split by serve) dies after all measurement rounds with `[X] there is no GPU 0,1: 0 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, 1 = NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090`. Nothing is saved, because the hardware key the rounds are stored under cannot be computed.

`hardware_key()` passed the raw value to `gpu_info()`, which matches one card by number (`x["index"] == pick`), so the string matched nothing. List-form duals (`[0, 1]`) worked; only the string form died. `recommend_remote_expert_opt()` had the same blind spot: its `isinstance(cfg.get("gpu"), list)` check skipped string-form duals, so they never got the helper-cache recommendation.

After the fix the same config keys and calibrates exactly like the list form.

## Related discussion

Fixes #3275. The identical fix was sent earlier for the 0.1.45 line (#2378) and did not land; the 0.2.0 tree still had the pre-fix line. Focused bug fix, no scope agreement needed.

## Approach

- `gpu_sel(value)`: a config's `"gpu"` as a list of card numbers -- `0`, `[0, 2]` and the string form `"0,2"` (which serve splits the same way); `[]` when it names none.
- `hardware_key()`: string-form selectors go through `gpu_sel()` before `gpu_info()`.
- `recommend_remote_expert_opt()`: `len(gpu_sel(...)) < 2` instead of the `isinstance(..., list)` check.
- Regression test in `CalibrationKey`: `"0,1"` keys exactly like `[0, 1]`; `gpu_sel("0,1") == [0, 1]`, `gpu_sel("0") == [0]`.

The NVIDIA key format is unchanged (the existing test asserts it). No behavior change outside setup; serve and the engine are untouched.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_amd.CalibrationKey` on 3f52b2d7 (0.2.0 tree, e88ee39d) -- 8/8 tests OK, including the new `test_nvidia_string_dual_keys_like_the_list`.
- Real dual config on 2x RTX 3090 (3090 Ti + 3090), Ubuntu 26.04, engine 0.1.45.3: `hardware_key(cfg)` with `"gpu": "0,1"` now returns `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090|48GB|AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor|59GB|<model>|262144|images`; before the fix the same call died with `there is no GPU 0,1`.

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Full calibrate round-trip after the fix (the failing call itself is covered; the re-run on the reporting box is the next check).
- No engine rebuild: the change is `setup.py` only (pure Python); CUDA/HIP/SYCL/CPU binaries are untouched.

## Limits

- Executed on Linux/NVIDIA only; the code path is platform-agnostic but Windows and macOS were not run.
- Only `hardware_key()` and `recommend_remote_expert_opt()` are covered; the other `gpu_info()` callers already pass card numbers.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB in a KVM guest with Docker: 0.2.0-beta against 0.1.43
pulls.author: moneymikeMD
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A results-only benchmark report for a card with no other report here: one RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB (sm_86) in a KVM guest with
GPU passthrough, served from Docker. Re-run on 0.2.0-beta as asked when the tracker was reset; it replaces the 0.1.42
report this PR carried before.

The 0.2.0-beta image (engine package 0.1.45.3) and the 0.1.43 image were run in alternation on the same model files at
context 262,144, a fresh container per sweep, three runs per cell:

- IQ3_S decode 76.4 / 77.1 / 68.4 tok/s on 0.1.43 against 97.0 / 92.2 / 81.8 on 0.2.0 at 4K / 32K / 128K (two sweeps
  each; every 0.2.0 sweep beat every 0.1.43 sweep). Prompt speed within 4%. With `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0` 0.2.0 gives
  83.5 / 79.6 / 73.8, so the new sm_86 table is worth 14 / 14 / 10% here. `TUNE=quick`: "already fastest".
- Swift 1.5 IQ3_S: 77.2 / 77.4 / 63.2 against 96.0 / 97.1 / 85.6.
- UD-IQ4_XS: with 0.2.0's own settings the engine was killed for lack of RAM on this 94 GiB guest in 4 of 4 starts
  (kernel lines and engine log included). Reading `setup.py`, `unsloth_budget()` keeps every expert in RAM when the RAM is
  at least the experts plus 16 GiB, which does not count the PLE table locked in RAM or the KV streamed to RAM at this
  context; 0.1.43's setup wrote `--resident-budget-gib 55` for the same file. With that budget given by hand, 0.2.0 reads
  prompts 46 / 31 / 13% slower than 0.1.43 and decodes 21 / 7 / 11% slower; `STRATA_PREFILL_HOST_PLAN=0` changed nothing.
- Needles 9 of 9 at 32K, 128K and 262K on 0.2.0 IQ3_S.

## Related discussion

Replaces #2005, closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; `/reopen` passed its check but GitHub would not reopen it because the branch was re-pushed with the new report. No scope agreement needed (benchmark report).

## Approach

New folder `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-rtx-3080-ti-kvm-docker-0.2.0/` (README, every run as JSON lines, the run
configs with the key removed, the 0.2.0 engine logs, the scripts as run) and one entry in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.
No code changes.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `docker/build.sh --flavor cuda --engine <package> --tag strata:0.2.0-beta-cuda13 --base public.ecr.aws/docker/library/ubuntu:24.04`
  at v0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480) with the released `strata-engine-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64-cuda-cuda13.tar.gz` (SHA-256 matches
  `SHA256SUMS.txt`), after adding `docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md` to the script's `paths=` list (below); the build's own checks passed.
- `sweep.py` (in the folder) and `tools/needle_bench.py` against both images on 2026-10-19, Ubuntu 26.04.1 guest, driver
  615.71.09, Docker 29.9.0; the numbers above are from those runs (`sweep-*.jsonl`, `needles-iq3_s-0.2.0.json`).
- The `STRATA_SET` values of each arm show up in that arm's engine log.

**Failed:**

- `docker/build.sh` unchanged at v0.2.0-beta: `missing payload item: docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md` (its build-context list has
  `docs/MANAGEMENT_PROTOCOL.md` but not `docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md`, which `packaging/package_terminal.py` requires; the
  line is the same on `main` at f57c0adc). Not fixed in this PR.
- 0.2.0 UD-IQ4_XS with its own settings: OOM-killed, 4 of 4 starts, as above.

**Not run:**

- A bare-metal run of the same machine (VM and Docker cost not measured).
- The 0.1.42 comparison is one sweep, after the others, not interleaved.
- Generated tokens were not compared between versions; no quality check beyond the needles.
- Vision, concurrent requests, a soak, agent sessions.

## Limits

Three runs per cell and two sweeps per interleaved arm. The 0.1.43 and 0.1.42 images are sm_86-only source builds; the
0.2.0 image uses the released engine package. The cause of the slower UD-IQ4_XS prompt read with the budget was not found.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: opt-in peer prompt row reduction and PUSH return for --expert-parallel-device (stacked on #2205)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `--expert-parallel-device` (#1798, prompt path #2205), the peer card returns one FP32 row per routed expert of every prompt token over IPC, and the primary combines them. On two Arc Pro B70s that return dominates the prompt read: at 32K tokens the engine reads 720 tok/s, against 2,078 for a plain two-card layer split of the same model.

Two opt-in switches, both off by default:

- `STRATA_EP_PREFILL_REDUCE=1`: the peer sums its routed experts per token first and returns one FP32 row per token; the primary adds its own routed sum and the shared expert. Changes the FP32 addition order (text can change).
- `STRATA_EP_PREFILL_PUSH=1` (with the reduction): the sum region lives on the primary and the peer writes it through the IPC mapping (posted writes, system-scope fences), instead of the primary reading it from the peer. Transport only: bitwise the reduction's output.

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, prompt tok/s at 4K / 32K: unset 635 / 720, reduce 993 / 1,264 (+56% / +76%), reduce + push 1,148 / 1,514 (+81% / +110%). Decode unchanged.

## Related discussion

Stacked on #2205 (which builds on #1798), at @recutita's request in recutita/Strata#1. **Only the top three commits are this PR**; the four below them are #1798 and #2205 rebased onto 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d (the only conflict was in `docs/INTEL.md`; `git range-diff` shows #2205's commit unchanged against its current head 4805fa9a). Opened as a draft until #1798 / #2205 have their two-card gate. No maintainer agreement on scope yet.

## Approach

- `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: the reduce path when the env is set (rows for the peer's experts summed on the peer with the routing weights, one row per token returned), the push variant allocating the sum region on the primary with the peer as importer. One stderr line when the reduction is on.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/ep_kernels.dp.cpp`, `sycl/include/strata/kernels/ep_kernels.hpp`: the reduce kernel and its posted-write form, a system-scope fence per producer work item before the existing host peer wait.
- `sycl/probe/ep_prefill_reduce.cpp` (new): a two-card probe against an independent FP32 FMA oracle in the original router order.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: one section with the numbers and the probe commands.

Unset: the existing per-expert rows and combine run as before (the env is read once at setup; the unset arm below is this binary with nothing set, not a separate build of the stack below).

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d + #1798 + #2205 (rebased) + this PR, head 1da1f265 (engine built at 86d8ed20; the top commit is docs only). 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, SYCL AOT `bmg-g31` built with the repository dev image. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--expert-parallel-device 1 --prefill 8192 --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts --expert-cache auto`, Docker `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE`, one slot, greedy, a fresh engine per arm, two fixed 512-token coding replies, then fresh 4K and 32K prompts.

**Passed:**

- `ep-prefill-reduce-probe` and `ep-prefill-reduce-probe --push` (both cards): `PASS cases=26 max_abs=9.53674316e-07` each.
- Engine A/B:

| | 4K read tok/s (ms) | 32K read tok/s (ms) | decode tok/s, two prompts |
|---|---|---|---|
| unset | 635 (5,947) | 720 (42,031) | 80.0 / 81.3 |
| `STRATA_EP_PREFILL_REDUCE=1` | 993 (3,802) | 1,264 (23,934) | 80.6 / 83.8 |
| `+ STRATA_EP_PREFILL_PUSH=1` | 1,148 (3,286) | 1,514 (19,975) | 80.2 / 83.4 |

- Push vs reduce: output SHAs and draft counts identical on both prompts. Reduce vs unset: coherent, text differs (addition order). The engine log shows `EP row reduction enabled` in both reduce arms. Coherence true and per-card health passed after every stop.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** the `mg_norepeat` / `exact_pp` gate at 4096 and 20000 tokens (offered on #1798; happy to run it on this stack); two slots and `--max-context 200000`; a soak or stability run; CUDA/HIP (no file touched outside `sycl/` and `docs/`).

## Limits

- Even with both switches, expert-parallel prompt reading here (1,514 tok/s at 32K) stays below a plain layer split on 0.2.0 (2,078); expert parallelism's gain is decode (80-84 vs 71-74 tok/s on the same prompts).
- PUSH prints no line of its own; the reduction's line shows either mode.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: [Other] opt-in gfx1010 in setup (RX 5700 XT) plus a community bench
pulls.author: Gedankenn
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Setup refused an RX 5700 XT (gfx1010) even though the HIP arch gate already compiles that card as unvalidated. With `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1010=1`, setup treats gfx1010 like the gfx1103 opt-in: TheRock `gfx101X-dgpu` wheels, the card is usable, default AMD list unchanged. Unset, setup still refuses it.

## Related discussion

Continues https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2283 (closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, not rejected; `/reopen` passed the check but GitHub would not reopen that number). Earlier notes: HIP already accepts gfx1010 as unvalidated (#996 / #1142). Review on #2283: `test_setup_rocm_pins` KeyError on `gfx101X-dgpu`, and `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` hardcoded.

## Approach

Same opt-in shape as gfx1103 / gfx1150: index in `ROCM_INDEXES` always, arch in `AMD_ARCHS` only when the env is set. `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is now the chosen card's HIP index, and only when another unsupported AMD device is listed (typically an iGPU). It is in `SETUP_ENV` so a re-run without the sibling drops it. CUDA, the default `AMD_ARCHS` list, ready-made engines, and every other HIP architecture are unchanged.

Community bench folder from this machine is included (engine 0.1.43.1; not a rerun of the 7600X numbers already in OLDER_GPUS.md).

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_amd tools.test_setup_rocm_pins tools.test_setup_start_gpus_amd` on 266413610431f127f6bb0a07dcaee31a39025d8d (rebased on current main). 67 tests, 0 failures. Includes `Gfx1010OptIn` (refuse without opt-in, index present, opt-in admits the card, ROCR index vs iGPU / lone card / supported sibling). `test_setup_rocm_pins` skips `gfx101X-dgpu` the same way it skips gfx1150 (no saved listing).
- Hardware (older revision, not this SHA): RX 5700 XT 8 GB (desktop) + Renoir iGPU hidden, Ryzen 5 4600G, 46 GB RAM, Linux, HIP source, TheRock 7.10.0a20251120, Coder IQ1_M, 32K, `--spec 4`, int8 KV, engine 0.1.43.1. Chat decode 18.0 tok/s (16.7–22.7, n=9); 4K prompt 163.7 tok/s; 16K prompt 162.1 tok/s; agent decode 17.4 tok/s. Report: `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-rx-5700-xt-coder-iq1_m/`.

**Failed:**
none observed on the unit tests above.

**Not run:**
- HIP rebuild / `./bench.sh` / needle / 30K prompt / ctest on the card against this SHA (0.2.0-beta tree). The numbers above are 0.1.43.1. Niko already noted the engine target compiles for gfx1010 on the then-current tree.
- CUDA / SYCL / Windows HIP.

## Limits

Opt-in, unsupported. No hipBLASLt table for gfx1010. `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is set only when an unsupported AMD sibling is present; a lone 5700 XT is left alone. Default path without the env is unchanged.

pulls.title: [Engine] LoRA adapter support with per-request on/off switch
pulls.author: agrogov
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Strata cannot apply a LoRA adapter, so a fine-tuned variant of the model needs a merged GGUF. This adds optional LoRA support in the CUDA engine (llama.cpp's adapter GGUF format) with a per-request on/off switch.

- `--lora FILE` / `--lora-scaled FILE:SCALE[,...]` load a llama.cpp LoRA GGUF (`general.type = adapter`, `adapter.type = lora`; f32/f16/bf16). It is applied to the mixer output projections: `ssm_out` on GDN layers and `attn_output` on QSA layers. For each adapted layer, `y += s·B(A·x)` with `s = scale·alpha/rank`; several files stack their ranks.
- **Per request:** the engine key is `lora=0|1`, and the server takes `"lora": true|false` in the request body (OpenAI and Anthropic APIs) or `"sampling": {"lora": ...}` in the config. The switch is a device flag the kernels read, so captured CUDA graphs serve both states with no re-capture. Turned off, the output is bit-identical to the engine without an adapter (checked, see Validation).
- **State:** the conversation cache, batch slots and session files are keyed by the switch, next to `cvec`. Session files stay backward compatible (a new bit in the existing flag word; the fingerprint changes only when an adapter is loaded). While batch slots are decoding, a request for the other state is refused.
- **Not adapted:** the MTP draft layer (it only drafts; the verified tokens are the adapted model's).

Without `--lora` nothing changes: the feature is opt-in.

## Related discussion

Continues #1523, closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. `/reopen` passed its check but GitHub would not reopen it (the branch was rebased and force-pushed after it was closed), so this is the same change, not a competing attempt. No separate scope issue.

## Approach

Six commits: kernels (+ the `lora_parity` test); core hooks in decode, verify and the prompt path; conversation cache/session keying; `generate` loader, CLI flags and request key; `serve` request field + unit test; the decode/verify up kernel as a programmatic dependent launch (rank > 64 and HIP use the plain launch).

Rebased on `main` `f57c0adc` (0.2.0-beta). Conflicts were in `layer.cpp`, `conversation_state.cpp`, `conversation_cache.hpp` and `generate.cpp`; `main`'s changes were kept and the LoRA lines re-added, including the LoRA switch in the #879 slot checkpoint move and the donor take-over.

## Validation

Revision tested: this branch's code (`799c0c17`) as built in a Docker image from `0e320510`, which has the same source files (it differs only in docs/bench files kept out of this PR). Engine on `main` `f57c0adc` base. One NVIDIA RTX 5090, CUDA 13, driver 615.71. Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M (`--native`, `--spec 4`, `--expert-cache auto`), adapter `ara-trial9-lora-F32.gguf`: 48 layers adapted, 79.8 MiB.

**Passed:**
- `lora_parity` (synthetic, GPU): `lora_parity: all ok`. Error against double precision 3.0e-7 to 7.9e-7 for 1, 3, 8 and 300 tokens, fp32 and fp16 activations. Switched off: bitwise unchanged for 1, 8 and 300 tokens and from a graph captured while on. Switching back on re-applies through the same graph. Kernel time, rank 50, 6144 -> 2560: 3.7 µs (1 token), 7.6 µs (4), 10.5 µs (8), 31.7 µs (300); in a captured 48-layer graph 3.71 µs per layer at 1 token and 10.49 µs at 8 tokens.
- End to end (`bench/e2e.py`-style, greedy, 48 tokens, 2 prompts, with and without MTP): `lora=0` gives the same tokens as an engine without an adapter; `lora=1` repeated gives the same tokens. On these two short prompts `lora=1` and `lora=0` also gave the same tokens, so this run does not show the adapter changing the output; over the API, 120-token answers did differ between `lora: true` and `lora: false`.
- Over the Anthropic API on the running container (`/v1/messages`, `temperature 0`): a request without the field behaves as `lora: true`; `lora: false` differs from it; after a `lora: true` request, a `lora: false` request reads 0 cached tokens (the cache is keyed by the switch) and a repeat in the same state reads the cached prefix.
- Multi-GPU layer split, same revision and engine as above, with an RTX 4090 as the second card over Thunderbolt: `--layer-split 24 --split-device 1`, `--spec 4`, with and without MTP, same two prompts, greedy, 48 tokens. The log shows `layers 0-23 (CUDA0), 24-47 (CUDA1), one hand-off per window` and `LoRA: 1 file, 48 layers adapted, 79.8 MiB per device`. Results as on one card: `lora=1` repeated gives the same tokens, and `lora=0` gives the same tokens as an engine without an adapter. As on one card, `lora=1` and `lora=0` gave the same tokens on these short prompts, so this run shows the adapter loads on both cards and the switch is bit-neutral, not that the second card's layers change the output. Speed on the split was not measured.
- Speed (3 runs per setting after one warm-up, prompts of about 2,500-2,900 tokens, 256 generated tokens):

| | decode, MTP | decode, no MTP |
|---|---|---|
| no adapter | 271.8 tok/s | 164.0 tok/s |
| loaded, `lora=0` | 269.9 (-0.7%) | 161.9 (-1.3%) |
| loaded, `lora=1` | 272.4 (+0.2%) | 158.6 (-3.3%) |

The MTP differences are within the run-to-run noise of a single benchmark process per setting. Prompt read is not compared: each setting reads its own texts (2,527 to 2,880 tokens), so its times are not comparable.
- Earlier measurements on a B200 (sm_100, Qwen4Exp IQ2_XS, `main` v0.1.40.4, rank 50) are in the first revision of this PR: decode -3.3% (MTP) and -5.5% (no MTP) with `lora=1`, `lora=0` -1.3% and -2.8%; they were taken before the rebase and are not repeated here.

## Limits

No SYCL/HIP port, no web UI toggle, no VRAM accounting in the layer-split auto planner (80 MiB at rank 50). The MTP draft layer is not adapted. Docs (`docs/DETAILS.md`) and benchmark scripts/results are kept out of this PR.

pulls.title: [Engine] logit_bias: accept it with --batch (one bias table per slot)
pulls.author: qni-live
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`logit_bias` is refused whenever the engine runs with `--batch`. That makes the Han/Kana/Hangul ban (docs/LOGIT_BIAS.md) unusable on a 4-slot server, which is the setup for several parallel agents.

Result: each batch slot can carry its own bias table, and a bias reaches only its own request. A slot that is reused by a request without a bias carries nothing over. `--batch-mtp` still refuses it.

This PR is rebased on `main` for 0.2.0-beta (`e88ee39d`, tag `v0.2.0-beta`); it applies without conflicts. #1891 is already in `main`, so nothing of it is repeated here.

## Related discussion

Replaces #2977 (GitHub would not reopen it after the rebase).

No issue and no scope agreement: none. There is no open issue; `--batch` answers `logit_bias` with HTTP 400 today. It is a focused change that lifts one refusal and adds no new request field.

## Approach

- `include/strata/core/verify.hpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`: `Verifier::set_slot_logit_bias(slot, bias, err)` and `slot_has_bias(slot)`. Only the final stage allocates a table (one float per vocabulary entry, about 1 MB for 248,320 tokens) and copies it, and only when it changed. `set_slot_sampling` keeps the slot's table pointer. `init_slots` frees and clears the tables.
- `sample_rows`: a greedy row whose slot has a table is drawn on the last stage like a sampled row, because the graph's argmax does not know the bias. Rows without a table take the same path as before.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the bias is set at admission, before `set_slot_sampling`; an empty one clears the slot. `--batch-mtp` still answers `ERR logit_bias: --batch-mtp does not take it yet`. `INFO` advertises `logit_bias_batch=1`.
- `serve/logit_bias.py`: the server refuses `--batch` only when the engine does not advertise `logit_bias_batch=1`, so older engines keep the clear 400.
- Tests: `tools/batch_test.py --bias-han` (every second prompt carries the ban and asks for Chinese) and the new `tools/batch_bias_reuse_test.py` (3 waves, banned and free prompts swap slots every wave; a slot's tokens must equal its solo tokens). `docs/LOGIT_BIAS.md` and `serve/test_logit_bias.py` updated.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 GB each), Linux 7.0.0-38, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.4 source build (sm_120) of `main` e88ee39d plus this commit (a7026916), Swift IQ3_XXS, `--batch 4 --trim-stage-weights --pipeline-windows 2`, layer split 25, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000`, 64 new tokens, 65,842 banned tokens (all Han/Kana/Hangul). Each test compares a slot's tokens with the same request run alone. Run on 2026-10-19; log `pr2977-tests-lauf.log`.

**Passed:**
- `python3 tools/batch_test.py ... --batch 4 --n 4 --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000 --batch-groups 1"`, no bias anywhere: 4 of 4 slots identical to solo.
- same with `--bias-han`, ban on 2 of 4 slots, greedy, `--batch-groups 1`: 4 of 4 identical, 0 Han/Kana/Hangul characters in the banned slots.
- same, `--batch-groups` auto: 4 of 4 identical, 0 CJK characters in the banned slots.
- `python3 tools/batch_bias_reuse_test.py ... --waves 3`, greedy: 12 of 12 slot rows identical to solo, RESULT: PASS.
- same, sampled (`temperature=0.7 top_k=20 seed=7`): 12 of 12 identical, RESULT: PASS.
- `python3 -m pytest serve/test_logit_bias.py`: 12 passed, 19 subtests passed.
- `cmake --build build -j 40`: builds (CUDA).

**Failed:**
none observed on this revision. My first run of the series used a relative `--exe` that resolved to an older build and answered `continuous batching is not supported`; I discarded it and reran with an absolute path. The results above are from the rerun only.

**Not run:**
- HIP and SYCL builds: the change touches `src/core/verify.cpp` and `src/program/generate.cpp`; only CUDA was built and run.
- Throughput cost and the CJK rate over 150 prompt pairs in batch: measured on the 0.1.45 base for the earlier version of this PR (10 of 150 answers in Chinese script without the ban, 0 of 150 with it; -1 to -3 % batch throughput; +21 ms fixed cost per request), not repeated on 0.2.0-beta.
- A byte comparison of the default path (no bias, `--batch`) against the packaged 0.2.0-beta engine 0.1.45.3. The no-bias slots equal their solo run on the changed build; I did not diff them against the release binary.
- `--batch-mtp` with a bias after the rebase (it is unchanged by this PR), the Qwen3.6 engine path, layer splits over three or more GPUs, and a start with the Windows or Mac engine.

## Limits

- `--batch-mtp` still refuses `logit_bias`.
- Tested on two GPUs, CUDA only, four slots, 64-token requests.
- Written with Claude Code (AI-assisted); I ran and checked every test above on my hardware.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] Experts in VRAM ahead of time: oracle run 3.0x prose, 4.1x code decode, same output
pulls.author: toel1234
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On this machine most of a decoded token's time is the CPU computing experts that are not in VRAM: 46.9 of 60.0 ms per token, with 69.7% VRAM cache hits (Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS, RTX 5070). This PR measures how much faster decode gets when the right experts are already in VRAM, as a ceiling for a possible lookahead expert prefetcher. Nothing in Strata changes.

Oracle run: the VRAM cache pre-filled with exactly the experts the continuation routes to, adaptive tier off.
- Prose, 32 tokens: 12.68 → **38.05 tok/s (3.00×)**; hits 58.4% → 88.5%
- Code, 24 tokens: 10.41 → **42.34 tok/s (4.07×)**; hits 46.8% → 88.4%
- All 12 runs' output IDs equal the greedy reference. A control arm (adaptive tier off, normal profile) equals the normal arm, so the gain is from which experts are in VRAM.

Also recorded: a perfect lookahead prefetcher would copy 39–84 experts per token at 16–64 tokens ahead (2–4 ms at the measured 28.4 GB/s host→device), distinct experts per window up to 64 tokens, and the prompt-path cost of 4- to 64-token chunks as an estimate of larger verify windows.

## Related discussion
Follows from the NCM study, #3247 (NCM predicts a rough picture of a block of future text; the experts a block uses are that kind of picture). No NCM model is used here. Benchmark report only; no feature or default change proposed in this PR.

## Approach
- `docs/EXPERT_LOOKAHEAD.md`: plain summary first, then settings, the five measurements, what it does and does not show, how to repeat.
- `docs/benchmarks/expert-lookahead-2026-10-19-rtx5070/`: every run's stdout/stderr, results JSON, the two routing traces and prompt/reference IDs used (inputs, 0.8 MB total), PCIe benchmark output, profile and engine SHA-256. Local paths rewritten.
- `tools/expert_lookahead_bench.py`: `unions`, `simulate` and `oracle-profile` run without a GPU on the committed traces; `oracle-runs` and `prefill-sweep` drive the engine.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- RTX 5070 (12 GB), Ryzen 9 7900X, 61 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-38, driver 610.43.02; existing engine 0.1.45 binary, checkout e88ee39d; saved run config with context 4096, KV residency 0, `--mmap-experts`, greedy reference mode (`--spec 2 --spec-corrupt 1`, no MTP).
- Oracle runs: 3 arms × 2 prompts × 2 repeats in alternating order; repeats within 3%; 12/12 output IDs equal the reference.
- Chunk sweep: 9 runs, repeats within 2%.
- The tool reproduces the recorded results: identical union and simulation output, byte-identical oracle profiles (SHA-256 in the PR), and the same engine argument lists as the recorded runs (all 12 oracle runs and the sweep, compared without running the engine).
- `git diff --exit-code main -- src include serve strata_cli strata_control apps requirements.txt` returns 0.

**Failed:**
none observed. A first cold T=8 chunk run (263.1 ms vs 221.8 ms) is kept separately and left out of the table.

**Not run:**
- A real prefetcher or predictor; copying experts during decoding (the oracle experts were loaded at start-up, 1.2 s, untimed).
- Long answers: only 24–32 tokens' experts fit in 4,866 slots. Normal arms are slower in short runs (79–96 ms/token) than over 64 tokens (60 ms), so the gain over long answers is likely smaller.
- The saved 64K configuration, MTP or prompt lookup on top, other machines, HIP/SYCL/Metal.
- No engine code changed, so no backend builds.

## Limits
Two prompts, one machine, diagnostic settings, short runs. This is a ceiling for a perfect predictor, not a speed-up of Strata. A real predictor's misses cost roughly 17 ms per token per 10% of routed experts missed (estimate from these runs).

pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): optimize MTP draft, shared expert, and verify/sampler head kernels on RDNA4
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #3069 (closed during the `0.2.0-beta` tracker reset), rebased onto `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`).

During speculative decode and verification on RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`), six bottlenecks in the MTP drafter, shared expert, S2 routed experts, and verify/sampler head operations accounted for significant per-window overhead while having **100% bitwise-identical** replacements:
1. `multi_block_head_ops()` and `argmax_rows_wanted()` in `src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu` unconditionally returned `false` under `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`, forcing `argmax_rows` (`T x 248,320` logits) and `row_top_prob_split` onto single-WGP (`<<<n_rows, 1024>>>`) launches instead of 128-block (`argmax_rows_kernel`) and 32-block (`row_top_prob_split_kernel`) wave32 kernels (`402.0 -> 35.1 us` at `T=5`, **11.45× speedup**).
2. `quantize_q8_0_scaled` in `src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu` used a 1-thread-per-block serial 32-element loop under `#if defined(__HIPCC__)` instead of the warp-per-block shuffle-reduction kernel (`quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel`).
3. `moe_hit_grouped_s2`, `moe_hit_grouped_s2_dev`, and `moe_hit_grouped_s2_multi` in `src/kernels/cuda/s2_expert_grouped.cu` launched `swiglu_kernel` and `quantize_q8_0_scaled` separately instead of the fused `swiglu_quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` already used by `moe_grouped_s2`, and `gu_grouped_t_kernel`/`down_grouped_t_kernel` allocated 25 KB / 6.25 KB LDS (`GMAX=8`) even for `cap_entries <= 16` (`T=1` MTP draft), capping occupancy at 2 blocks/WGP.
4. `MtpDrafter::forward_body` (`src/core/mtp.cpp`) and `Verifier::forward_range` (`src/core/verify.cpp`) quantized `mixed` to `Q8_1` twice per layer (once in `fused_gr_read_multi` / `native_quantize_q8_1` for routed experts, and a second time inside `shared_expert`), and `fused_gr_read_multi` declined `q8_mixed` when `q8_cnt == nullptr` (`STRATA_QFUSE_HC_LOCAL=1`).
5. `Verifier::forward_range` issued up to 8 separate `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., cudaMemcpyHostToDevice)` calls per layer to copy pinned expert blobs for misses instead of a single batched `copy_from_mapped_multi` device kernel reading mapped host pointers.

Every optimization in this PR is **100% bitwise identical** (`0` differing bits across all outputs).

## Related discussion

Supersedes #3069 (includes the `copy_from_mapped_multi_fallback` alignment-safe scalar fallback for `bytes % 4 != 0` or `4 mod 8` pointers and the `verify_parity` unaligned fallback tests from review on #3069).

## Approach

- Enable wave32 `argmax_rows_kernel` (`128` blocks/row) and `row_top_prob_split_kernel` (`kTopBlocks = 32` single-warp blocks/row) on RDNA HIP (`p.warpSize == 32`, cached per device in `arch[64]`) in `src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu`.
- Enable warp-per-block `quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` on HIP in `src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu` (`STRATA_OLD_Q80_SCALED=1` fallback).
- Route `moe_hit_grouped_s2{,_dev,_multi}` through `launch_hit_swiglu_q8`, specialize `gu_grouped_t_kernel<1>` / `down_grouped_t_kernel<1>` for `cap_entries <= 16` (reducing LDS from 25 KB to 3.125 KB), and use `s2_sync_lds()` in `src/kernels/cuda/s2_expert_grouped.cu`.
- Reuse pre-quantized `x_q8_1` across routed and shared experts in `src/kernels/cuda/shared_expert.cu`, `src/core/mtp.cpp`, and `src/core/verify.cpp`, and allow counter-free `q8_mixed` in `fused_gr_read_multi` (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`) when `q8_cnt == nullptr`.
- Add `copy_from_mapped_multi` in `src/kernels/cuda/elementwise.cu` (with alignment-safe fallback for non-8B-aligned pointers/sizes) to batch mapped-host miss expert copies in `src/core/verify.cpp`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `cmake --build build-copilot-hip --target strata verify_parity gr_parity shared_expert_parity s2_expert_grouped_parity arch_defaults_test -j16`: revision `d79fe8e8` on `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`), AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, Linux `7.2.9-2-cachyos-server`, ROCm `10.2.0a20260914`), clean build & link.
- `./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test`: revision `d79fe8e8` (`0.2.0-beta`), `arch_defaults_test: OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/verify_parity`: revision `d79fe8e8` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `argmax_rows, row_top_prob_split: bitwise equal`, `copy_from_mapped_multi: bitwise equal (multi=1 and fallback=0, aligned + 1025w + 4B-aligned)`, `quantize_q8_0_scaled: bitwise equal`, `verify_parity: PASS`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/gr_parity --selftest`: revision `d79fe8e8` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `fused GR counter-free q8_1 (q8_cnt == nullptr), T 1..8, direct/graph + LOCAL=0 guard: pass`, `gr_read/gr_write: 0 failures`, `gr_parity OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/shared_expert_parity`: revision `d79fe8e8` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `native shared x_q8_1 reuse: byte-identical`, `shared_expert: 0 failures`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/s2_expert_grouped_parity` (default, `STRATA_S2_SWIGLU_Q8=0`, and `STRATA_OLD_Q80_SCALED=1`): revision `d79fe8e8` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, all 14 cases bitwise identical (`s2_expert_grouped_parity: 0 failures`, `PASS`).

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Target-device runtime execution on `gfx11` / `gfx906` and CUDA hardware (no `gfx11`/`gfx906` or NVIDIA GPU in this host).
- SYCL and Metal builds (changes are in CUDA/HIP kernels and engine verify/MTP paths).

## Limits

- Wave64 `gfx906` keeps the single-block `row_top_prob` and `sampler_greedy_kernel` paths (`#if !defined(STRATA_HIP_GFX906)` and `p.warpSize == 32` check).

---

## Summary

This PR enables and optimizes several bitwise-identical paths across the MTP draft layer, the verify/draft head greedy sampler & top-probability kernels, the S2 grouped expert kernels, and the shared expert on RDNA HIP (`gfx1201`):

1. **Wave32 multi-block `argmax_rows` and `row_top_prob_split` on RDNA HIP (`src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`):**
   - `argmax_rows_kernel` and `row_top_prob_split_kernel` were previously compiled out under `#if !defined(__HIPCC__)`, forcing wave32 RDNA GPUs (`warpSize == 32`) onto the single-block `sampler_greedy_kernel<<<n_rows, 1024>>>` and `row_top_prob_kernel<<<n_rows, 1024>>>` (1..5 blocks total across 48 WGPs to scan 425 KB..4.97 MB of logits).
   - Guards the wave32 multi-block kernels with `#if !defined(STRATA_HIP_GFX906)` (keeping wave64 `gfx906` on the one-block kernels) and enables `multi_block_head_ops()` / `argmax_rows_wanted()` per device on HIP when `p.warpSize == 32` (`STRATA_MULTI_BLOCK_ARGMAX=0` and `STRATA_ARGMAX_ROWS=0` force them off).
   - Sets `kTopBlocks = 32` (`32` threads = 1 warp/block across 32 WGPs, avoiding intra-block `__syncthreads()` barriers when `blockDim.x == 32`) and adds `#pragma unroll 8` to the stride-1024 reduction loop in `row_top_prob_kernel` and `row_top_prob_split_kernel` (preserving exact per-thread summation order while overlapping 8 global loads in flight).
   - Enables the `verify_parity` target on HIP (`STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA OR STRATA_ENABLE_HIP`) and extends `verify_parity` with `copy_from_mapped_multi`, `quantize_q8_0_scaled`, and `--bench` checks.

2. **Fused HC `q8_mixed`, `STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI`, and shared-expert `x_q8_1` reuse in MTP and Verify (`src/core/mtp.cpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/shared_expert.cu`):**
   - Allows `fused_gr_read_multi` (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`) to write `q8_mixed` without a `q8_cnt` buffer when `qfuse_hc_local() && a[0].s_down == nullptr` (`gr_up_q32_kernel` and `gr_up_q8_q32_kernel` assign one warp per 32-column `q8_1` block and never touch `q8_cnt`).
   - Enables `STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI` by default on `gfx12` in `verify.cpp` and `mtp.cpp` (`STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI=0` disables), replacing the 4-launch `gr_read` fallback on the MTP final mixer with `fused_gr_read_multi`.
   - Passes `q8_mixed = xq_ + t * (N / 32) * 36` to all 3 `fused_gr_read_multi` calls in `MtpDrafter` (`attn_hyper_connection`, `mlp_hyper_connection`, and `hyper_connection_mixer`) and to the final `output_hc_*` `fused_gr_read_multi` in `Verifier`, skipping redundant standalone `native_quantize_q8_1` launches when `fused_gr_read_multi` writes `xq_`.
   - Updates `shared_expert()` (`src/kernels/cuda/shared_expert.cu`) to honor `native->x_q8_1` (set by `MtpDrafter` when `q8_mlp && T == 1`), matching `shared_expert_multi`.

3. **S2 grouped expert `<1>` specialization, LDS-only barriers, and fused SwiGLU+Q8_0 on hit paths (`src/kernels/cuda/s2_expert_grouped.cu`, `src/kernels/s2_expert_grouped_parity.cpp`):**
   - Adds `s2_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`; `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx1030`/`gfx11xx`) for LDS-only staging barriers.
   - Adds `MAX_E = 1` template specializations `gu_grouped_t_kernel<1>` (`LDS = 3,200 B`, `VGPR = 85` vs `<8>`'s `LDS = 25,600 B`, `VGPR = 89`) and `down_grouped_t_kernel<1>` (`LDS = 800 B`, `VGPR = 47` vs `<8>`'s `LDS = 6,400 B`, `VGPR = 40`) dispatched when `cap_entries <= 16` (covering single-token MTP `T = 1, K = 10`).
   - Uses `swiglu_quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` in `moe_hit_grouped_s2`, `moe_hit_grouped_s2_dev`, and `moe_hit_grouped_s2_multi` when `fast && x_scales != nullptr && swiglu_q8_on()` (`STRATA_S2_SWIGLU_Q8=0` disables), matching `moe_grouped_s2`.

4. **Warp-per-block `quantize_q8_0_scaled` and `copy_from_mapped_multi` on HIP (`src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/elementwise.cu`, `src/core/mtp.cpp`):**
   - Enables the warp-per-block `quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` on HIP (`STRATA_OLD_Q80_SCALED=1` restores the thread-per-block kernel).
   - Enables `copy_from_mapped_multi_kernel` on HIP (`STRATA_MTP_MULTI_COPY=0` restores individual copies) and uses `copy_from_mapped_multi` in `MtpDrafter::capture_round` and `MtpDrafter::capture_step`.

---

## Verification & Parity Evidence (AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 `gfx1201`)

All 7 parity and self-test suites pass with **0 failures** and 100% bitwise equality:

```text
$ ./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test
arch_defaults_test: OK

$ ./build-copilot-hip/verify_parity --selftest --bench
argmax_rows, row_top_prob_split: bitwise equal to the one-block kernels (ties, NaN, -inf, 1-8 rows on one scratch)
copy_from_mapped_multi: bitwise equal to individual mapped copies (multi=1 and fallback=0, aligned + 1025w + 4B-aligned)
quantize_q8_0_scaled: bitwise equal to CPU act_quant_q8_1 reference (zero, .5 ties, normal)
  V=106299 rows=1: greedy 1-blk  24.39 us -> argmax_rows   7.87 us (x3.10) | top_prob 1-blk  22.43 us -> split  11.24 us (x2.00)
