pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): optimize EXPDEC routed-expert kernels and enable by default on gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #3024 (closed during the `0.2.0-beta` tracker reset), rebased onto `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`).

On RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`), grouped routed-expert decode/verify kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu` previously:
1. Left the **100% bitwise-identical** `EXPDEC` kernels (`expdec_gu_kernel` for `IQ2_XXS`/`IQ2_XS`/`IQ3_XXS`/`IQ3_S`/`IQ2_S` gate/up and `expdec_down_kernel` for `Q2_0` down) off by default on `gfx12`.
2. Executed full-workgroup `__syncthreads()` (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12`) in `stage_iq_grid`, `native_down_multi_kernel`, `expdec_gu_kernel`, and `expdec_down_kernel`, including an unconditional top-of-loop barrier on the very first group/entry pass (`g == blockIdx.y && e == e0`) where shared memory had not yet been read.
3. Staged `Q8_1` activations into `s_u` via scalar 32-bit stores with integer division by 9 (`w / 9`, `w - k * 9`) in `ed_stage_entry`, and interpreted `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` on HIP as waves-per-EU (`MINB=4` = 1,024 threads/SIMD, over-constraining register allocation).

This PR adds LDS-only `iq_sync_lds()`, skips the redundant first-iteration pre-stage barrier, vectorizes `ed_stage_entry` with `int4` 16-byte stores (no `/ 9` division), scales `expdec_gu_kernel` launch bounds on HIP (`MINB * 2` waves/SIMD), and enables `EXPDEC` gate/up and `Q2_0` down by default per device on `gfx12` while preserving first-use environment evaluation (`apply_nv_defaults` on CUDA) and per-device `arch[64]` resolution on mixed-GPU systems. On `gfx1201`, `expdec_bench` latency drops **`-17.9%` to `-22.9%` (`96.2 -> 74.2 us` at `T=2`)** with **`0` bitwise differences**.

## Related discussion

Supersedes #3024 (includes the per-device `arch[64]` caching, first-use `STRATA_EXPDEC`/`STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` evaluation for `apply_nv_defaults`, and `native_expert_expdec_params()` effective `p.down` fixes from review on #3024).

## Approach

- Define `iq_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on other HIP targets, `__syncthreads()` on CUDA) and replace LDS staging barriers in `stage_iq_grid`, `native_down_multi_kernel`, `expdec_gu_kernel`, and `expdec_down_kernel`.
- Vectorize `ed_stage_entry` using 2 threads per `Q8_1` block (`int4` stores to `s_u`).
- Resolve `expdec_mode()` and `expdec_down_on()` at call time when `g_expdec < 0` / `g_expdec_down < 0`: check `STRATA_EXPDEC` / `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` first (so `apply_nv_defaults` on CUDA is respected), then fall back to per-device `expdec_default_gfx12()` without overwriting the `-1` automatic sentinel.
- Enable `expdec_bench` on HIP in `CMakeLists.txt` and extend `src/kernels/iq_multi_parity.cpp` (`check_grouped`) to verify both `EXPDEC=0` and `EXPDEC=1` (`down=1, down_iq4_nl=1`) bit-for-bit against the reference kernels.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `cmake --build build-copilot-hip --target strata iq_multi_parity expdec_bench arch_defaults_test -j16`: revision `6cb45386` on `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`), AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, Linux `7.2.9-2-cachyos-server`, ROCm `10.2.0a20260914`), clean build & link.
- `./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test`: revision `6cb45386` (`0.2.0-beta`), `arch_defaults_test: OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/iq_multi_parity`: revision `6cb45386` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, all 26 `iq_mmvq` cases and 29 `native_expert_grouped` format pairs (both `EXPDEC=0` and `EXPDEC=1`) pass (`iq_multi_parity: 0 failures`, 0 bitwise differences).
- `./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 18/42 def,dec,dec:w0,dec:w1 real`: revision `6cb45386` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `expdec_bench: ok (0 choice comparisons differ)` (`T=1`: `54.2 -> 44.5 us`, `T=2`: `96.2 -> 74.2 us`, `T=3`: `101.4 -> 80.3 us`, `T=4`: `106.8 -> 85.7 us`).

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Target-device runtime execution on `gfx11` and CUDA hardware (no `gfx11` or NVIDIA GPU in this host).
- SYCL and Metal builds (`iq_kernels.cu` is CUDA/HIP only).

## Limits

- `IQ4_NL` down (`STRATA_EXPDEC_D20`) remains off by default (`0`) on `gfx12` because `native_down_multi_kernel<20, true>` with `iq_sync_lds()` is slightly faster than `expdec_down_kernel<20>` on `gfx1201`.

---

## Summary

Optimize the grouped native routed-expert decode kernels (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`) for RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`), enable `EXPDEC` (`expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel` on `Q2_0`) by default on `gfx12`, and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP builds.

### Changes

1. **Fix HIP `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` wave-occupancy mapping on `expdec_gu_kernel` (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`)**:
   - On CUDA, `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` specifies `MINB` blocks per SM (`4` blocks = $\le 64$ registers). On HIP (`amd_hip_runtime.h`), the second argument of `__launch_bounds__(max_threads, min_blocks)` maps directly to `amdgpu_waves_per_eu(min_blocks)` (waves per SIMD, not blocks per WGP). Since a 256-thread CTA has 8 waves = 2 waves/SIMD on RDNA3/RDNA4, `MINB = 4` requested only 4 waves/SIMD (allowing up to 256 VGPRs), so `expdec_gu_kernel<16..18, 1, 4>` compiled to **`222–223 VGPRs`** on `gfx1201` (capping occupancy at 6 waves/SIMD = 3 CTAs/WGP instead of 8 waves/SIMD = 4 CTAs/WGP).
   - Map the second `__launch_bounds__` argument to `MINB * 2` on HIP (`8` waves/SIMD for `MINB = 4`), dropping `gfx1201` register usage to **`171–187 VGPRs`** (`0` spills, $\le 192$ VGPRs = **4 CTAs/WGP** across `IQ2_XXS`, `IQ2_XS`, `IQ3_XXS`, and `IQ3_S`).

2. **Vectorize `ed_stage_entry` in `expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel`**:
   - Previously, `ed_stage_entry<XB, HALVES>` looped over `w = tid; w < XB * 9; w += 256`, executing 3 integer divisions by 9 (`w / 9`), 3 intra-warp divergent `if (j == 0)` branches, and 3 scattered 4-byte `ds_store_b32` stores per thread per staged entry.
   - Because `XB <= 80 <= 128` (`ED_XB = 80`, `ED_HB = 20`), map the 256 threads directly as 128 thread-pairs `(k = tid >> 1, h = tid & 1)` where each active pair loads one 16-byte half-block (`int4`) and writes a single 16-byte `ds_store_b128` to `s_u`, while `tid < XB` writes `s_ds[c * XB + tid]` with zero loops, zero `/ 9` divisions, and zero intra-warp branch divergence.

3. **LDS-only barriers (`iq_sync_lds()`) and elided first-pass pre-staging barriers**:
   - Add `iq_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on other HIP targets, `__syncthreads()` on CUDA) in `stage_iq_grid`, `native_down_multi_kernel`, `expdec_gu_kernel`, and `expdec_down_kernel`, avoiding `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` L0 vector-cache invalidations and global load-queue drains (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0`).
   - Guard the pre-staging barrier inside `for (int e = e0; e < e1; ...)` with `if (g > (int) blockIdx.y || e > e0) iq_sync_lds();` so the first pass (`g == blockIdx.y && e == e0`, which covers all `T <= 4` decode groups when `gridDim.y == cap_groups`) skips a redundant barrier.

4. **Enable `EXPDEC` (`STRATA_EXPDEC=1`, `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=1`) by default on `gfx12` and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP**:
   - Default `expdec_on()` and `expdec_down_on()` to `1` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`expdec_default_gfx12()`) when `STRATA_EXPDEC` / `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` are unset (`STRATA_EXPDEC=0` or `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=0` turns them off; non-`gfx12` architectures remain unchanged).
   - Gate `expdec_note` stderr logging on explicit `STRATA_EXPDEC=1`.
   - Enable the `expdec_bench` target on HIP builds in `CMakeLists.txt` and map `cudaDevAttrMemoryClockRate` / `cudaDevAttrGlobalMemoryBusWidth` in `include/strata/hip_compat/cuda_runtime.h`.
   - Extend `iq_multi_parity` (`check_grouped`) to verify bitwise equality of both `multi` (`EXPDEC=0`) and `expdec` (`EXPDEC=1, EXPDEC_DOWN=1, EXPDEC_D20=1`) against the reference per-entry kernels across all format pairs.

---

## Validation & Benchmarks (`gfx1201`, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700)

### 1. Bitwise Parity & Multi-Arch Compilation
- `./build-copilot-hip/iq_multi_parity`: `0 failures` across all 18 `iq_mmvq` checks, 24 `native_expert_grouped` checks (testing both `multi` and `expdec` against `old`), and 3 `q8_1 finite` checks.
- `./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 18/20,21/20,22/20,18/42,21/42,22/42 def,dec,dec:w1 real`: `identical` (`0 choice comparisons differ`) across all 6 format pairs and `T = 1..4`.
- Multi-architecture compile check: verified clean compilation on AMD HIP (`gfx1100`, `gfx1151`, `gfx1200`, `gfx1201`) and NVIDIA CUDA (`sm_75`, `sm_89`, `sm_100`).

### 2. Cold Routed-Expert Microbenchmark (`./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 ...`, 150 reps $\times$ 5 rounds over 121–186 MB cold expert pools)

| Format Pair (`gu/down`) | `T` | Baseline `def` (`all / gu / down`, us) | `gfx12` Default `EXPDEC` (`all / gu / down`, us) | Total Speedup | Phase Speedup |

pulls.title: [Other] Terminal tests: pass on Linux desktops and in a checkout with run configs
pulls.author: toel1234
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
`python -m pytest tests/terminal` had five failures on Ubuntu caused by the tests, not by the code. After this PR they pass on Linux. The Windows assertions are unchanged.

- **discovery** (2): the tests wrote the command-line settings file to `%APPDATA%/Strata/settings.json`. Linux reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/strata/settings.json`. A third test passed on Linux only because it wrote to that unread file. All three now use `discovery.own_settings_file()`.
- **discovery** (1): `Catalog` looks "here" in the folder it runs from, this checkout. A developer checkout that holds its own `strata-*.json` (an install from source) beat the mocked app install. The test points "here" at its temporary folder.
- **docker**: `docker/smoke-test.sh` starts `#!/bin/bash` and uses process substitution; it was parsed with `sh`, which is dash on Debian/Ubuntu (`Syntax error: redirection unexpected`). Scripts with a bash shebang are now parsed with bash; the image's sh scripts are still parsed with sh.
- **launch TUI**: since d2a38c9e the Linux cloudflared hint is long enough that "quick tunnel" wraps onto two rows. Whitespace is collapsed before the check.
- **private files**: on POSIX `is_unshared()` is documented as the same check as `is_private()`, so a fresh file under a normal 0002/0022 umask is not unshared. The POSIX branch now asserts the two agree.

## Related discussion
none. Test-only change.

## Approach
Test files only: `tests/terminal/test_discovery.py`, `test_docker_files.py`, `test_launch_tui.py`, `test_private_files.py`. No product code.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- Ubuntu, Python 3.12.3, venv with `requirements.txt` and `requirements-monitor.txt`: the four files give 98 passed, 9 skipped.
- Full `python -m pytest tests/terminal -q`, this branch with the procs fix (#3254) merged, in a checkout with a `strata-*.json` at the root: 852 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed.
- Same-day clean `main` e88ee39d baseline: 6 failed (the five here plus the procs one), 846 passed, 17 skipped.

**Failed:**
none observed.

**Not run:**
- Windows and macOS: not available. The Windows-only assertions were left as they were.

## Limits
Note for anyone running the suite: a venv without `requirements.txt` makes the 7 lifecycle tests and the runtime test fail with "the server exited with 5 before it was ready" (missing `requests`, Pillow). That is not changed here.

pulls.title: [TUI] procs: find engine orphans adopted by systemd --user, and wait until they are really gone
pulls.author: toel1234
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On a systemd Linux desktop, `strata` never found an engine left behind by an earlier run without a launch record. `systemd --user` both adopts orphans (subreaper) and is an ancestor of every desktop terminal. `orphans_of()` put every ancestor except pid 1 into "my own processes", so an orphan whose new parent is `systemd --user` looked started by this server and was skipped. The orphan kept holding the GPU.

After that was fixed, a second Linux issue showed: `end_one()` returned "ended" while the process was still exiting. It waited on `is_same()` (start token and command line), and an exiting Linux process has an empty `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` before it is gone.

After: ancestors named like an init (`INIT_NAMES`, already used for the adopted-parent check) are not counted as starters, the same as pid 1. After the signal, `end_one()` waits on the start token alone, which is unique per process lifetime and never matches a reused PID. The kill itself is still only sent after the full `is_same()` check.

## Related discussion
none. Focused fix.

## Approach
Two small changes in `strata_control/procs.py`. Both are needed for the existing test `test_an_engine_orphan_of_this_executable_is_found_and_a_live_one_is_not`: with only the first it still fails (process reported ended, start token still live), with both it passes. Windows behaviour is unchanged apart from the wait loop now comparing the start token, which is the same value `is_same()` compared first.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- `python -m pytest tests/terminal/test_procs.py` 5 times in a row: 7 passed each. Ubuntu, GNOME on Wayland, Python 3.12.3, the process tree `systemd(1) > systemd --user > gnome-shell > … > pytest`.
- Full `python -m pytest tests/terminal -q` with this branch and #3255 merged: 852 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed (445.96 s).
- Diagnosis: an orphan of this test is reparented to `systemd --user` (pid 5687 here), which `psutil.Process().parents()` also lists.

**Failed:**
none observed.

**Not run:**
- Windows and macOS: not available. The Windows branch of `end_one()` only changes which check the wait loop uses.
- A real engine orphan: tested with the existing Python sleeper fixture only.

## Limits
A process stuck in exit (empty command line, start token still live) is now reported "stuck" after the 10 s wait instead of "ended".

pulls.title: [Engine] session files work with --peer-device
pulls.author: pspranger-throw
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #1273, which was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. That PR cannot be reopened after its branch was rebased while closed (GitHub returns 422 on reopen); the diff and the validation below are unchanged.

The SAVE/RESTORE path refuses every session-file operation when `--peer-device` is set, so session persistence cannot be used on a two-GPU shape that keeps the second card as a peer expert cache. That shape is not an edge case: for the IQ3_S 262K configuration it is the only decode-positive lever.

The peer tier is a pure in-memory expert cache, rebuilt at load from the expert source files (which are already part of the model fingerprint). It holds no session state, so nothing is missing from a saved file and no per-run peer artifact can drift. After this change SAVE and RESTORE work normally with the peer active.

## Related discussion

#1273. Niko, 2026-10-17: "This lifts a refusal rather than speeding anything, so it is outside this speed pass; it applies cleanly and can be taken in the fixes pass."

The branch is rebased onto `main` (`e88ee39d`, head `99cf9d88`). Rebase-only: one line of code plus the DETAILS.md sentence; the diff is unchanged from the reviewed patch.

## Approach

- Remove the `--peer-device` refusal from the SAVE/RESTORE path. `--layer-split` stays refused: it moves K/V across stages, which a session file cannot represent.
- The peer tier needs no special save/restore handling: the session file holds the conversation state and the primary/streamed K/V pools, exactly as it does without a peer. The expert cache is rebuilt from the model files at load and only changes which experts are resident.
- The streaming restore's per-layer residency refill (`kv_stream_reset` / `kv_ring_restore`, from #1269) is unchanged and runs with the peer active.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- Full engine build on 0.2.0-beta source rebased onto `main` (`e88ee39d`), with #1269 applied for the streaming restore, CUDA 13.4, archs 75;86 (368 targets).
- `conversation_file_test`: 223/223 checks. All 8 conversation suites pass under `ctest`: conversation_cache, conversation_split_failure, conversation_memory, conversation_file, session_save_reclaim, conversation_snapshot, conversation_validation, conversation_transfer.
- Live drill on 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3), IQ3_S 262K, `--peer-device 1`, 153K session, direct server on loopback:
  - peer tier active throughout: 3,339 experts / 6.34 GiB on the RTX 2060S, 189 MiB left free; primary held 8,662 experts (12,001 of 24,576 on the two GPUs);
  - SAVE: 153,426 tokens / 2.58 GB in 1.57 s;
  - RESTORE: 2.68 s; next turn 153,426 / 153,465 tokens reused (99.975 %);
  - fresh engine process + RESTORE: 2.79 s with MemAvailable 5,658 -> 5,308 MiB; next turn 153,538 / 153,574 tokens reused (99.977 %);
  - no `SERR`, no `FATAL`, no refusals.
- Prior live evidence on 0.1.45 (same change, older base), peer active:
  - shallow cycle: 10,462-token session saved through the slot API (396 MB, 314 ms), engine restarted, restored in 423 ms, next turn 10,495 / 10,515 tokens reused (99.8 %);
  - deep cycle: 198,830-token session (3.05 GiB) saved in 1.4 s, restored in 3.5 s, next turn 198,859 / 198,879 tokens reused (99.99 %) where the cold read is ~177 s;
  - gateway switch: 39,060 tokens / 833 MB saved in 959 ms, restored in 1.0 s, 99.95 % reused.

**Failed:**

- none observed.

**Not run:**

- HIP, SYCL and Metal builds, and Windows/macOS; only the CUDA/Linux build was run here.
- `--layer-split` remains deliberately unsupported and was not tested.

## Limits

- The peer's resident expert set is not saved. It is rebuilt at load from the expert source files; a different VRAM budget or a different peer card only changes which experts are resident, not the restored conversation or its K/V.
- The existing session identity and config-fingerprint gates still apply: a file saved with another engine configuration is refused, as before.
- This change only lifts the refusal for session files. `--layer-split` continues to return the existing refusal.

pulls.title: [Engine] restore a session file without holding its K/V in RAM
pulls.author: pspranger-throw
pulls.body:
Supersedes #1269, which was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. That PR cannot be reopened after its branch was rebased while closed (GitHub returns 422 on reopen); the diff and the validation below are unchanged.

## Problem and result

The RESTORE path reads the whole snapshot into host memory before it writes anything, so its peak is about the size of the file. On a machine that is also serving the model, a deep session is larger than the RAM left free: a 198,830-token IQ3_S session is a 3.05 GiB file, with roughly 5 GiB available while the model is loaded, and the server answers 503 ("when the RAM to read the file is not there", DETAILS.md). Shallow sessions restore fine, which makes the limit easy to miss.

After this change the restore is two passes over the same file, format v1 unchanged: the read pass validates the whole file without materializing the K/V, and the apply pass re-reads it and copies the K/V into the authoritative pools in blocks of at most 16 MiB. Peak RAM is two 16 MiB buffers plus the running-state metadata, so a session of any depth restores under the same floor.

## Related discussion

PR #1269. Niko, 2026-10-17: "It avoids the 503 on deep sessions by restoring in blocks, which is a memory fix and not a speed change, so it is outside this round. It needs a rebase and we would take it as a fix."

The branch is rebased onto `main` (`e88ee39d`, head `69fb7912`) and retested on 0.2.0-beta. Rebase-only: the diff is unchanged from the reviewed patch (8 files, 561 insertions / 50 deletions).

## Approach

- **Read pass:** the existing parser and validation run unchanged (header, identity, size, geometry, every count against this session's limits, payload hash), but the K/V bytes are read through one 16 MiB block, hashed, and not retained. Each layer's five part sizes are recorded for the apply pass.
- **Apply pass:** re-reads the file and copies each K/V part into its authoritative pool through `ConversationKvTarget`. It is bound to the read pass: a file whose K/V layer count or any part size differs is refused before that layer or part is applied. The payload hash is recomputed and compared to the trailer at the end.
- The first applied block is the commit gate: a failure before it refuses cleanly (the live session is exactly as it was); after it the engine fail-stops rather than decode from bytes it cannot vouch for.
- The residency refill after the pool writes is kept per layer (`kv_stream_reset` / `kv_ring_restore`); without it the modes that keep K/V in VRAM read stale slots.
- `session_file_read` is untouched, so callers that hold the K/V in RAM behave exactly as before.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- Full engine build on 0.2.0-beta source rebased onto `main` (`e88ee39d`), CUDA 13.4, archs 75;86 (368 targets).
- `conversation_file_test`: 223/223 checks. All 8 conversation suites pass under `ctest`: conversation_cache, conversation_split_failure, conversation_memory, conversation_file, session_save_reclaim, conversation_snapshot, conversation_validation, conversation_transfer.
- Live drill on 0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3), IQ3_S, `--peer-device 1`, 153K session, direct server on loopback:
  - cold prefill: 153,277 tokens in 106.1 s (1,445 tok/s);
  - SAVE: 153,426 tokens / 2.58 GB in 1.57 s;
  - RESTORE (verb): 2.68 s; next turn 153,426 / 153,465 tokens reused (99.975 %);
  - second SAVE: 1.54 s; fresh engine process + RESTORE: 2.79 s, with MemAvailable 5,658 -> 5,308 MiB (the 2.58 GB payload was not materialized); next turn 153,538 / 153,574 tokens reused (99.977 %);
  - no `SERR`, no `FATAL`, no refusals. Peer tier active throughout: 3,339 experts / 6.34 GiB on the RTX 2060S.
- Prior 0.1.45 production drill (same code, older base): 153K session save 1.80 s / restore 2.66 s / 99.977 % reuse; a 198,830-token (3.05 GiB) session restored in 3.4-3.5 s, next turn 99.99 % reused in 1.8 s against ~177 s cold.

**Failed:**

- none observed.

**Not run:**

- HIP, SYCL and Metal builds, and Windows/macOS; only the CUDA/Linux build was run here.

## Limits

- The file is now read twice (read pass + apply pass). The second read normally comes from the page cache; a cold file on slow storage pays for two reads. Measured restore time stays in the previous band (2.68-2.79 s for 2.58 GB here; 2.66 s on 0.1.45).
- The commit gate is the first applied block rather than a fully validated in-RAM image; the fail-closed rule is unchanged, but the point of no return moves earlier in the restore.
- Format v1 is unchanged; no migration is needed.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] strata_bench: read CUDA UMD version, storage and GPU power/PCIe detail
pulls.author: JoShMiQueL
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The community report came out with fields missing or wrong:

- Current drivers print `CUDA UMD Version: 13.4` in `nvidia-smi`, not `CUDA Version:`, so `machine.cuda` came out null and the README said `CUDA: not read`.
- Where it was read, it was the newest CUDA the **driver** supports, labelled as if the engine had been built with it (raised by autemetry-james in this thread).
- Storage always said `not measured`, the GPU line carried no power limit, PCIe link, state or temperature, and Windows 11 reported as `Windows 10` because `platform.release()` is still `10`.

After the change a report reads `CUDA (driver supports up to): 13.4; engine built for CUDA 13.0`, names the storage device, adds a `GPU detail (after the run, near idle)` line with power limit and draw, PCIe gen x width, pstate and temperature, and says `Windows 11`. The measurement path (HTTP suite, statistics, `results.json`) is untouched: this changes what a report prints, not what it measures.

## Related discussion

Reopening of #2111, closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset of 2026-10-19. The `/reopen` check passed there (area prefix in the title, template filled in, revision named), but GitHub refused the reopen itself with `state cannot be changed. The bench-tool-machine-fields branch was force-pushed or recreated.` — the branch was rebased onto `main` while the pull request was closed, so the bot's own advice applies: open a new pull request and link this one. This is that pull request; #2111 stays as the discussion thread.

## Approach

- Accept both header forms from nvidia-smi and label the value as the driver's ceiling.
- Read `machine.engine_build` from the engine's `BUILD.json` next to the exe, so driver ceiling and build toolkit are both in the report; no engine change.
- Take the extra nvidia-smi fields from the GPUs the server uses (the selection of #1985), and label the line `(after the run, near idle)`: `collect_machine` runs a second time after the suite, so they are end-of-run, near-idle figures (qiuzan2001).
- Storage: `Get-PhysicalDisk` on Windows, `system_profiler` on macOS, `lsblk -e 7` on Linux (`-e 7` drops the snap loop devices that flooded the line on a stock Ubuntu, qiuzan2001).

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python tools/test_strata_bench.py` on `8f7fd37d`, rebased on `main` `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta): 20 tests, OK. The new checks cover the rendered report line with both CUDA numbers, the storage line, the GPU detail line, both nvidia-smi CUDA header forms, and the power/PCIe/pstate/temperature parsing.
- `python tools/test_windows_amd_gpu.py` and `python tools/test_bench_host.py`, same revision: 5 and 5 tests, OK.
- Live read on this PC (RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, driver 616.92, Windows 11 build 26200): `gpu_info_local()` returned `power_limit_w=165.00`, `power_draw_w=20.25`, `pcie=gen4 x8`, `pstate=P3`, `temp_c=45`, `cuda=13.4`; `storage_info()` returned `Samsung SSD 990 EVO Plus 2TB SSD/NVMe`; the OS label resolves to `Windows 11`.
- `ruff check tools/strata_bench.py tools/test_strata_bench.py`: the same 4 findings as on `main`, no new ones (3 of them are the `port` NameError below).
- A report generated with this change, all fields filled, is in #2112.

**Failed:**

- `python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-coder-iq1_m.json --port 9 --runs 1 --quiet` on `main` `e88ee39d` ends in `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` (`tools/strata_bench.py:1040`), from #2330. It is a separate problem and is not touched here; it blocks a default run that starts its own server on 0.2.0-beta.

**Not run:**

- The macOS (`system_profiler`) and Linux (`lsblk -e 7`) storage branches: no such machine here, they are read, not executed.
- A full bench suite on 0.2.0-beta: blocked by the `port` NameError above. The tests drive the `--url` path against a fake server, not a real engine.

## Limits

- The GPU detail line is sampled after the suite, near idle; it is not a load figure and the label says so.
- `engine_build` needs a `BUILD.json` next to the exe; without one the field is left out rather than guessed.
- This changes what a report prints. The measurements in #2112 were taken on engine 0.1.43 and are not re-measured here.

pulls.title: [Engine] SYCL: +10-35% prompt speed on Arc Pro B70/B65, copy-engine hang fix, int8 crossover cache, failing tests fixed
pulls.author: maxfridbe
pulls.body:
Sorry it took so long i have been working on nextsycl i had forgotten to bring in the enhancements here, hopefully this will get approved, Improvements all around!

Branch: maxfridbe/Strata_B70 intel-arc-0.2.0 (head d1192104), based on main f57c0adc; merges cleanly into main e88ee39d. Replaces #1111 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset), cut down to what main does not have yet. Only sycl/ and docs/INTEL*.md change.
Problem and result

On Arc Pro B70 and B65 (Battlemage, 32 GB), main’s SYCL engine has one hang, two failing tests and a slow first prompt, and its long prompts are slower than they need to be:

    The copy engine hangs (the card ends up wedged). A queue copy with no device end (pinned host <-> pageable host) goes to the Arc’s copy engine, which hangs on it (Engine reset: engine_class=bcs; repeated runs wedge the device until a reboot). conversation_snapshot_test does this on every run, and so would saving or restoring a --kv-resident conversation. After: host-only copies run on the CPU; the test passes with 0 resets.
    The int8 crossover is re-measured at every start. strata-sycl.sh runs the engine in a --rm container, so STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=auto’s cache in ~/.cache/strata is lost. The first 2,185-token prompt (B70, Coder IQ1_M) runs at 761 tok/s instead of 1,450. After: the cache is kept under the data root (STRATA_CACHE_DIR).
    Two tests fail on SYCL. s2_expert_grouped_parity (4 failures: the transposed grouped kernels get FMA-contracted under -fp-model=precise, the reference kernels do not) and gr_parity (its QFUSE check expects a q8_1 image the SYCL fused read never writes; the engine is unaffected). After: both pass, and wrong bytes still fail.
    Long prompts are slower than they could be. Two prompt-path kernels change, each with an off switch:
        prompt attention scores one work-item per cell, 2.0-2.2x the warp kernel (STRATA_ATTN_PERCELL=0 restores it);
        from 8K cells, QSA block selection scores with oneMKL GEMM tiles, so selection at 40K goes from 2.1 s to 0.7 s (STRATA_SELECT_GEMM=0 restores it).

    Prompt speed, interleaved A/B on the same B70 binary: +10% at 2K, +21% at 40K and +35% at 128K. Generation speed is unchanged.

Also included, as small tooling fixes for multi-card and Podman hosts:

    STRATA_SYCL_RUNNER=docker|podman|native|distrobox:<name> for strata-sycl.sh.
    gpustat.py reads two cards correctly. Before, it showed 163% busy and both cards’ VRAM summed as one.
    setup_intel.py --check sizes a model across all cards.
    setup_intel.py knows the B65’s PCI id (e222).

Related discussion

#1111 (closed by the 0.2.0 reset; this is its rebase), #423, #809. The hang fix, the cache and the test fixes need no scope agreement. The two prompt kernels change a SYCL-only prompt-path default; both have off switches. Happy to split this into three PRs (hang and test fixes / prompt kernels / tooling) if you prefer.
Approach

    Everything stays in sycl/. The new kernels are declared locally in prefill.cpp, not in the shared headers.
    The GEMM selection only turns on from 8K cells, because oneMKL’s launch cost loses below that (B70: -2% at 2K, even at 8K, 3x at 40K). It reuses the attention scratch, so no VRAM is added.
    Measured and left out, because none of them won on the B70 (identical tokens in each case):
        STRATA_EXP_MODE=8: 82.5 vs 82.5 tok/s decode.
        Queues without profiling: +0.25% decode.
        A 66-wide register top-k for 262K contexts: 2.6x faster in isolation, but it spills registers, so decode was -1.5% and the 128K prompt -6.6%.

Validation

Environment: Arc Pro B70 (bmg-g31) + Arc Pro B65, 32 GB each, xe driver, PCIe Gen5 x8, Ryzen 9 9950X, 61 GiB RAM, Fedora Silverblue 44 (kernel 7.1.5), strata-sycl-dev image under rootless Podman (oneAPI 2026.1), AOT=bmg-g31. Revision: intel-arc-0.2.0 c44fb63b (d1192104 only adds the B65 name), against main f57c0adc built the same way.

Passed:

    Build: AOT=bmg-g31 JOBS=8 bash sycl/tools/build.sh gives 0 errors on both main and the branch.
    ctest on the B70, and on the B65 (ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:1): 34 of 35 pass on each. That includes conversation_snapshot_test, s2_expert_grouped_parity, gr_parity and the newly registered qsa_prompt_attn_parity, which passes on int8, FP16 and Q4_0 pools. For comparison, main passes 30 of 33, with the snapshot test excluded because it wedges the card. No Engine reset or wedged appeared in the kernel log after any run.
    Token parity. Settings: --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0 STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1, IQ2_XS, 2,185-token prompt, 256 greedy tokens. Two runs of main are identical, and the branch with both new kernels off is identical to main.
        With the new kernels on, the first-token KL against the old kernels is 3.9e-10 nats at 8K and 1.3e-11 at 40K, with the same top-1. That is the same size as main’s own int8-vs-FP16 switch (8.4e-10 and 5.1e-12).
        The 256 greedy tokens after a 128K prompt are identical.
        Note: with the default STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=auto, two runs of main differ, because the per-group choice comes from a timing.
    setup_intel.py --check on the two-card host. The output is in commit 7b70671a.
    Benchmark. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M and IQ2_XS with the served flags (--prefill 4096 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp --kv int8 --stream-experts --vram-reserve-mib 2048 --kv-resident 32768, MMQ auto with a warm crossover cache for both builds). Cold page cache, 256 greedy tokens, prefill / decode in tok/s:

card	model	prompt	main f57c0adc	intel-arc-0.2.0
B70	Coder IQ1_M	2,185	1,312 / 87.6	1,449 / 88.1
B70	Coder IQ1_M	8,000	1,620 / 84.9	1,826 / 88.5
B70	Coder IQ1_M	40,000	1,580 / 77.6	1,909 / 78.7
B70	Coder IQ1_M	128,000	1,351 / 78.5	1,821 / 76.4
B70	IQ2_XS	2,185	1,053 / 80.1	1,355 / 77.4
B70	IQ2_XS	40,000	1,376 / 74.1	1,603 / 77.3
B65	Coder IQ1_M	2,185	948 / 60.1	1,018 / 62.0
B65	Coder IQ1_M	40,000	1,039 / 54.7	1,315 / 54.8
B65	Coder IQ1_M	128,000	861 / 53.6	1,246 / 54.4
B65	IQ2_XS	40,000	942 / 53.2	1,162 / 50.1

Decode moves with the text: the prompt kernels change the greedy output after a few dozen tokens, and MTP acceptance changes with it. With identical tokens, decode is unchanged.

Interleaved A/B on the B70 (same binary, --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0 STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=1, 2 rounds, prefill tok/s, old kernels → new):

    Coder at 2,185 tokens: 1,329 → 1,468 (+10%).
    Coder at 40,000: 1,562 → 1,885 (+21%).
    Coder at 128,000: 1,336 → 1,798 (+35%), with identical tokens.
    IQ2_XS at 40,000: 1,373 → 1,613 (+18%).

Failed:

    ple_parity: the Q2_0 shard-2 fixture is not on this machine. It fails the same way on main.

Not run:

    CUDA, HIP and Metal builds: nothing outside sycl/ and docs changed.
    Arc A-series, B580 and B60: no such cards here. The new kernels are plain SYCL (sub-group 32) plus oneMKL, so they build for every target, but their speed there is unmeasured. Both have off switches.
    A layer split across the B70 + B65 end to end: the engine runs above used one card each.
    Sampled (non-greedy) quality, beyond the first-token KL above.

Limits

    The two prompt kernels are not bit-identical to the warp kernels (FP32 summation order). Their switches restore the old kernels.
    The 8K threshold for the GEMM selection was measured on a B70 only.
    STRATA_SYCL_RUNNER=podman was exercised through strata-sycl.sh itself. native and distrobox: were not re-run on this branch.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] NCM feasibility study: stop/document, no engine change
pulls.author: toel1234
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
NCM (HazyResearch) generates many tokens per pass. The question was whether it could be a faster draft source
for Strata's speculative decoding. Result: not now. No released NCM checkpoint drafts in the target's token IDs,
so no NCM acceptance could be measured. This PR records the study, its numbers and its limits. Strata's
behaviour does not change.

Measured on RTX 5070 (12 GB), Ryzen 9 7900X, Linux, existing engine 0.1.45 binary, checkout e88ee39d:
- NCM TinyStories checkpoint, standalone: 40.504 ms median for 128 TinyStories BPE tokens (FP32, batch 1, 20 runs).
- Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS, 64 greedy tokens, single runs: MTP only 19.58 / 19.01 tok/s, default lookup 20.15 / 18.79
  (prose / code). Perfect 8-token oracle drafts: 38.18 / 30.59. All outputs matched their greedy reference.
- Routed expert union per layer, 4 / 8-token windows: 25.4 / 40.8 (prose), 27.7 / 45.0 (code).
- Calculated, not measured: an NCM drafter would need conditional acceptance of about 0.83 to 0.96 to beat
  the baseline.

## Related discussion
none. Research and benchmark report only; no feature, refactor or default change.

## Approach
- `docs/NCM.md`: plain summary, source review, measurements, break-even model, validation, decision.
- `docs/benchmarks/ncm-2026-10-19-rtx5070/`: raw files (probe JSON, results.json, every engine argument list,
  stdout/stderr, prompt and oracle IDs, Terminal test log). Local paths rewritten to `$STRATA`, `$DATA`, `$OUT`.
  Routing traces (1.1 MB) not included; SHA-256 recorded.
- `tools/ncm_probe.py`: standalone NCM probe and a break-even calculator (no PyTorch needed for the calculator).
- `tools/ncm_target_bench.py`: the target pilot driver, with paths as arguments.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- Ten engine runs (two prompts × MTP, default, greedy reference, oracle 4, oracle 8) exited 0; all 64-token outputs
  equal to the greedy reference. Data in `docs/benchmarks/ncm-2026-10-19-rtx5070/target/results.json`.
- Standalone probe, 3 warm-up + 20 measured generations, checkpoint SHA-256 values in the doc.
- `tools/ncm_target_bench.py` rebuilds the same ten argument lists as the recorded `*.command.json` and recomputes
  the same routing unions from the original traces (checked without running the engine again).
- `python3 -I tools/ncm_probe.py --break-even --window 4 --baseline-tps 80 --verify-ms 30 --draft-ms 5` gives the
  threshold in the doc. JSON files parse; all relative links in the new docs resolve.
- `git diff --exit-code -- src include serve strata_cli strata_control apps requirements.txt requirements-monitor.txt`
  returned 0.

**Failed:**
- `python -m pytest tests/terminal -q` on e88ee39d (before this change, no Terminal code touched): 834 passed,
  18 failed, 17 skipped. Log: `docs/benchmarks/ncm-2026-10-19-rtx5070/terminal-tests.log`. Not diagnosed here.

**Not run:**
- CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds: no engine code changed.
- NCM acceptance against the target, retokenization, shared-VRAM residency, 16-token windows (`kVerifyMaxT = 8`),
  repeated or interleaved runs, the full benchmark protocol.

## Limits
Single short runs on one machine, diagnostic settings (context 4096, KV residency 0, mapped experts), not the saved
production configuration. No speedup is claimed. The oracle rows are an upper bound for an 8-token drafter in this
setup, not a result for NCM.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: [Engine] log which batch-row switches are on at start-up
pulls.author: yi-sudo
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS` and `STRATA_BATCH_GDN_GROUPS` (merged from #2234 in f629fb0) are silent: nothing in the engine log says whether they were picked up, and attention quietly keeps its per-row launches when a slot's KV streams. In #2234 you mentioned a start-up line showing which switches are on and when they fall back would be welcome; this adds it.

Off (the default), nothing is printed and the engine runs exactly as before. With either switch on, the verifier prints one line after its existing `batch windows of up to N sequences` line (once per stage of a layer split):

```
strata verify: batch rows in one launch: attention on (STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS), GDN on (STRATA_BATCH_GDN_GROUPS); the KV streams (--kv-resident), so attention keeps one launch per row
```

The last clause appears only when attention is on and a slot streams its KV (`kv_mode == 1`).

## Related discussion

https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2234#issuecomment-6231123506

## Approach

- The two env reads moved from three function-local statics in `src/core/verify.cpp` to two file-scope constants next to the other batch switches (`g_batch_self_commit`, `g_qsa_slots`). The parsing is the same as before: set and `atoi != 0`.
- `Verifier::init_slots` prints the line, so it sits with the existing batch-window line and can check each slot's QSA `kv_mode`.
- `docs/BATCHING.md`: one paragraph with the example line.
- The SYCL tree has its own `verify.cpp` without these switches, so it is untouched.

## Validation

**Passed:**

pulls.title: [Engine] build: pin CMP0169 OLD around FetchContent_Populate (CMake 4.4 warns on every configure)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

CMake 4.4 warns on every configure: `FetchContent_Populate` is deprecated (CMP0169). Strata uses the populate-then-`add_subdirectory` form on purpose — it keeps ggml's binary dir at the `STRATA_GGML_DIR` one; `FetchContent_MakeAvailable` would move it, and its `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` needs CMake 3.28, above the project's 3.24 floor.

After: `CMP0169` is pinned to `OLD` around the populate call (guarded for CMake < 3.30), so the warning is gone and the layout stays as it is today. Checked by `tools/test_fetchcontent_policy.py`.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note.

### Approach

`cmake_policy(SET CMP0169 OLD)` scoped around the `FetchContent_Populate` call in `CMakeLists.txt` and `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`, guarded so CMake < 3.30 (which has no CMP0169) is untouched.

### Validation

Passed, on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d` is the base; branch commit `b14ff320`), Windows 11, CMake 4.4.0: `python tools/test_fetchcontent_policy.py` → 3/3 OK, exit 0.
Not run: a full CUDA/HIP engine build in CI; CMake < 3.30 (the guard path).

### Limits

Policy pin only — no build-layout change; the configure output is otherwise byte-identical.

pulls.title: [TUI] serve: keepawake primes its daemon before the first acquire (a fast request could miss the hold)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

`serve/keepawake.py` starts its daemon thread lazily. A request that finishes before the thread exists (acquire then release, a fast request) lost the transient `count > 0` transition, so the machine-sleep hold never engaged: the server answered the request and the PC could sleep mid-session.

After: the loop signals it has entered and `acquire` waits for that, so the first acquire can no longer race the thread start. Same root cause as the test-side fixture in #1901, fixed in the runtime.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note. #1901 fixed the same race on the test side.

### Approach

The daemon loop sets an "entered" event as its first act; `acquire` waits for that event before counting, so the count>0 transition is always observed.

### Validation

Passed, rebased on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`): `python -m unittest serve.test_keepawake` → 6/6 OK, exit 0. Windows 11, Python 3.15; no real power API called.
Not run: real suspend/resume on battery; CI.

### Limits

Windows keepawake path only; the fix adds a startup handshake, no change to the power API calls themselves.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] strata_bench: both Windows start-up paths crash (NameError port, GBK decode of CMakeLists)
pulls.author: Yunado
pulls.body:
**The problem and the result.** ``strata_bench.py`` cannot run at all on Windows: **both** start-up paths die before the suite begins.

1. **Self-start path** (no server running, the bench starts one: the first bench of a fresh install). ``NameError: name 'port' is not defined``: the port is computed inline for ``server_base`` (``a.port or cfg["port"] or 8080``) but the three users below name a plain ``port`` that was never assigned, so the run dies at the first "Port ... is used by something that is not Strata" / "Starting ... on port ..." line. Reproduced on this PC as SETUP's BENCH step (engine 0.1.45).
2. **Connect-to-running path** (a server is already serving). ``UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbf``: ``project_version()`` reads ``CMakeLists.txt`` (UTF-8 with a byte-order mark) with the locale default, GBK on this Chinese Windows, before the machine line is even printed; the surrounding ``except OSError`` soft fallback never sees it because a decode error is a ``ValueError``. Reproduced on this PC (manual run against the serving line).

With both fixes the bench reaches the suite as documented.

**The approach.** Two small changes in ``tools/strata_bench.py``, each on its crash path: assign ``port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))`` once where ``base`` is computed (the same no-url branch the three users live in; same precedence: --port beats the config's port beats 8080), and read the CMakeLists as ``utf-8-sig`` with the soft fallback widened to ``ValueError`` so one odd file cannot kill a run. Every other text read in the tool already names an encoding (audited); the ``--url`` path is untouched.

**Validation.**
- passed: ``py_compile``; ``strata_bench.py --help``; static walk of the three ``port`` uses (all in the branch where it is now assigned); ``project_version()`` and ``git_commit()`` called directly on this Chinese Windows return ``0.1.45.3`` and the short commit (both crashed before).
- failed: none.
- not run: a full bench suite (the GPU was serving this PC all day; both crash lines are the reproduced ones).

**Limits.** The port bug is not Windows-specific (every auto-start run anywhere hits it); the decode bug bites machines whose locale codec cannot read the byte-order mark.

**Environment**: e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta-12), Chinese Windows 11 Pro (GBK locale), Python 3.12.0, RTX 5090.

pulls.title: [Engine] loop guard: recover on the sampling raise when no effort sentence is there to splice
pulls.author: Yunado
pulls.body:
**The problem and the result.** ``"reasoning_loop_recovery": "recover"`` detects a repeated reasoning and then does nothing when the prompt carries no effort sentence to swap: a low-effort request, or a client that sends no effort sentence at all, leaves ``focused_recovery_prompt`` returning None and the caller (``if recover_prompt is not None: break``) silently keeps generating. A production loop at low burned 29,476 output tokens with ``reasoning_recoveries=0`` while the detector itself reported coverage 1.0. With this change such a run recovers on the sampling raise the resume block already performs (temperature to at least 1.0, presence penalty to at least 1.5): it resumes from the same ids with no splice.

**The approach.** ``serve/server.py``, three hunks in the guarded block: a ``spliced`` init next to ``looped``; when ``focused_recovery_prompt`` returns None, ``recover_prompt`` becomes ``ids + generated``, ``spliced`` goes False, and the loop breaks the same way a splice does; the recovery line in the server window says "on the sampling raise alone" instead of the low-effort-instruction wording. ``docs/DETAILS.md``: the recover bullet says the splice needs the exact xhigh sentence, and without it the resume is the sampling raise alone. The xhigh splice, ``"stop"`` and the default path (both keys off) are byte-identical; requests with images never took the recovery and still do not.

**Validation.**
- passed: ``py_compile`` on serve/server.py; two assertions on a fake tokenizer (one id per character, one special token): ``focused_recovery_prompt`` returns None for a low-effort render (the trigger of the new branch), and the xhigh splice is unchanged (low in, xhigh out).
- failed: none.
- not run: a live looped session end to end (the changed behavior is the live resume itself; it needs a real looped generation with a server).

**Limits.** At low there is no sentence left to splice down to, so the sampling raise is the only lever; if it does not break the loop the request finishes as "length" as it does today. The change is behind the existing opt-in key and cannot fire when it is off.

**Environment**: e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta-12), Windows 11 Pro, Python 3.12.0, RTX 5090.

pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): optimize exact QSA block scoring and top-k selection on gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #3108 (closed during the `0.2.0-beta` tracker reset), rebased onto `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`).

On RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`), QSA block scoring and top-k selection (`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, launched 12 times per decode/verify step across the 12 QSA layers) exhibited four bottlenecks:
1. `qsa_block_scores` fell back to `block_scores_multi_kernel` (`1` pooled key block per 32-lane warp, `16x` oversubscribed loads, `1` query per CTA in `y`, and 32-lane shuffle reductions) instead of the 4-lanes-per-key `block_scores_rows_kernel` (`STRATA_QSA_ROWS`), which was also restricted to `nq <= 4` while speculative verification uses `nq = 5` (`--mtp-draft 4`) up to `nq = 8`.
2. `rows_dot4` in `block_scores_rows_kernel` and `scores_thread_dot4` in `block_scores_thread_kernel` used scalar `__shfl_xor_sync` (`ds_bpermute_b32` through LDS on `gfx12`) for the 2-step 4-lane sum instead of `v_mov_b32_dpp quad_perm:[1,0,3,2]` + `row_shl:2` (`dpp_sum4`), and `block_scores_thread_kernel` was gated off under `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`.
3. Every `qsa_sync_lds()` barrier inside `block_scores_*` and the 16-pass radix histogram loop of `block_topk_kernel` / `block_topk_wide_kernel` used full-workgroup `__syncthreads()` (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12`).
4. `block_topk_wide_kernel` scanned the full `max_blocks` buffer (`65,538` blocks at `--max-context 262144`) instead of `active_blocks = min(max_blocks, n_bid + 1)` (`STRATA_SCORES_HALVE=1`).

This PR extends `block_scores_rows_kernel` to `nq = 1..8`, enables `STRATA_QSA_ROWS`, `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD`, and `STRATA_SCORES_HALVE` by default per device on `gfx12`, adds `qsa_sync_lds()` and `dpp_sum4()`, and verifies **100% bitwise-identical** scores and selected IDs (`qsa_rows_bench` `qsa_block_scores` at 131k context drops from `27.8..52.9 us` to `13.3..32.8 us` for `T=1..4`, **`1.61x-2.09x` speedup**, and prompt `block_scores_thread_kernel` reaches **`3.78x-4.84x` speedup**).

## Related discussion

Supersedes #3108 (includes the independent frozen pre-PR baseline oracle in `qsa_scores_parity.cpp`, width-scoped comparison in `qsa_topk_active_parity.cpp`, and `max_cells - 1` position clamping in `qsa_rows_bench.cpp` from review on #3108 and #3233).

## Approach

- Add `qsa_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`) and `dpp_sum4()` (`v_mov_b32_dpp quad_perm:[1,0,3,2]` + `row_shl:2` on `gfx12`/RDNA) in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`.
- Extend `block_scores_rows_kernel` (`MAXQ = 8`, `s_q[8][4][128]`, `s_nb[8]`, `s_tail[8]`) to `nq = 1..8` and enable `qsa_rows_on()`, `scores_thread_on()`, and `scores_halve()` by default on `gfx12` (cached per device in `g12[64]`).
- Enable `qsa_scores_parity`, `qsa_topk_active_parity`, and `qsa_rows_bench` on HIP in `CMakeLists.txt`, and clamp generated `nq = 5..8` test positions in `src/kernels/qsa_rows_bench.cpp` below `max_cells` so `n_bid < max_blocks` even when `--ctx == --max-context`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `cmake --build build-copilot-hip --target strata qsa_scores_parity qsa_topk_active_parity qsa_rows_bench arch_defaults_test -j16`: revision `87189e30` on `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`), AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, Linux `7.2.9-2-cachyos-server`, ROCm `10.2.0a20260914`), clean build & link.
- `./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `arch_defaults_test: OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_scores_parity`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, all 12 prompt cases (`128,447,982` scores) + 48 `qsa_block_scores_rows` & top-k cases (`nq = 1..8`, consecutive + spread `n_bid` + partial tails) bitwise identical to the frozen pre-PR baseline (`PASS`).
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_topk_active_parity`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `PASS: 20 top-k active-bound cases, selected IDs bitwise identical`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_rows_bench --rows --no-dense --iters 50` and `./build-copilot-hip/qsa_rows_bench --ctx 131072 --max-context 131072 --rows --no-dense --iters 10`: revision `87189e30` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `parity: 12 cases, 0 differ -> bit-identical` (`T=1`: `27.8 -> 13.3 us`, `T=2`: `34.1 -> 19.6 us`, `T=3`: `43.6 -> 27.0 us`, `T=4`: `52.9 -> 32.8 us`).

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Target-device runtime execution on `gfx103x`/`gfx11` and CUDA hardware (no `gfx103x`/`gfx11` or NVIDIA GPU in this host).
- SYCL and Metal builds (`qsa_select.cu` is CUDA/HIP only).

## Limits

- `STRATA_QSA_ROWS`, `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD`, and `STRATA_SCORES_HALVE` default to `1` on `gfx12` only; other HIP and CUDA targets keep their existing defaults unless explicitly overridden via environment variables.

---

## Summary

This PR optimizes the exact QSA block-scoring and radix top-k selection kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` on RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and wave32 HIP targets with **100% bitwise parity** (`0` differing scores across all 12 `qsa_scores_parity` cases / `51,069,696` scores, `0` differing selected IDs across all 20 `qsa_topk_active_parity` cases, and `0` differing scores or IDs across all 8 `qsa_rows_bench --rows` cases at `4K`, `32K`, and `128K` context):

1. **Wave32 VALU DPP reductions & workgroup-scoped barriers (`sel_xor_f32`, `sel_xor_i32`, `sel_sync_lds`)**:
   - On wave32 HIP targets, `__shfl_xor_sync` lowers through `ds_bpermute_b32` on the LDS/DS pipe (`5` `ds_bpermute_b32` + `5` `s_wait_dscnt` per 32-lane reduction, `20` per 4-head block score). Replacing power-of-two XOR butterfly steps with `v_permlanex16_b32` (`MASK=16`, `0x76543210` / `0xfedcba98`) and `v_mov_b32_dpp` (`row_xmask:1|2|4|8`, `0x160 | MASK`) keeps reductions on the VALU pipe while summing the exact same lane pairs in the exact same tree order.
   - Replaces device-scope `__syncthreads()` inside LDS-only selection/scoring loops with workgroup-scoped `sel_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`; `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx103x`/`gfx11xx`). Waiting on both `loadcnt(0)` and `dscnt(0)` avoids L2 cache-invalidation overhead while remaining safe when divergent `s_cbranch_execz` paths skip a VMEM basic block.

2. **Smaller-`PER` specializations for `block_topk_reg_kernel` (`PER = 2, 9, 17`) & parallelized scans in `block_topk_kernel` / `block_topk_wide_kernel`**:
   - Previously, `qsa_block_topk` only instantiated `block_topk_reg_kernel<33>` (`151 VGPRs, 107 SGPRs, 7 SGPR spills`) and `block_topk_reg_kernel<66>` (`192 VGPRs, 107 SGPRs, 88 VGPR / 106 SGPR spills`). Every decode call up to `33,792` blocks ran `<33>`.
   - Adds `block_topk_reg_kernel<2>` (`reach <= 2,048` blocks / `8K` cells: `29 VGPRs, 26 SGPRs, 0 spills`), `block_topk_reg_kernel<9>` (`reach <= 9,216` blocks / `36K` cells: `50 VGPRs, 43 SGPRs, 0 spills`), and `block_topk_reg_kernel<17>` (`reach <= 17,408` blocks / `69K` cells: `91 VGPRs, 67 SGPRs, 0 spills`), and lowers the HIP prefill crossover `kRegMinBlocks` from `7,168` (`~28K` cells) to `4,096` (`~16K` cells, matching `gfx1151`).
   - Replaces the single-thread (`if (t == 0)`) 256-iteration radix-bin search and 32-warp prefix loops in `block_topk_wide_kernel` (`77 → 28 VGPRs`) and `block_topk_kernel` (`35 → 25 VGPRs`, `3,080 → 1,064 B` LDS) with parallel 8-warp / 1-warp prefix scans.

3. **Prompt exact block-scorer (`block_scores_thread_kernel`) grid granularity & threshold on `gfx12`**:
   - Previously, `block_scores_thread_kernel` used a fixed `TS_BR = 512` blocks per CTA along `X` and only engaged at `active_blocks >= 16,385` (`ctx > 64K`). At `32K` context (`8,193` blocks) with `256` queries, `tgrid` launched only `17 × 4 = 68` CTAs (`__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`, `177 VGPRs`), leaving 28 of 48 WGPs idle once the first 48 CTAs finished.
   - Passes a dynamic `br` (`64` for `reach <= 2,048`, `128` for `reach <= 8,192`, `256` for `reach <= 32,768`, `512` above) with `__launch_bounds__(256, 2)` (`175 VGPRs`) and lowers the default `gfx12` activation threshold to `active_blocks >= 512` (`ctx >= 2,048`).

4. **Bitwise-exact `block_scores_rows_kernel<1..8>` on HIP (`STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1`)**:
   - On `gfx1201`, LLVM's `GCNCreateVOPD` pairs heads `(0, 1)` and `(2, 3)` in `block_scores_multi_kernel` so even heads multiply `x*x` first (`fmaf(w, fmaf(z, fmaf(y, x*x)))`) and odd heads multiply `y*y` first (`fmaf(w, fmaf(z, fmaf(x, y*y)))`), whereas `block_scores_rows_kernel<NQ>` had a different register schedule and 1-ULP divergence on ~3.4% of blocks, plus unrolled `nq` branches bloating `<4>` to `60 KB` of code.
   - Aligns the 4-head FMA chain via `rows_dot4(k4, q4, h)`, stages `q_idx` cooperatively through shared memory `qs`, uses `NQ` as the compile-time bound, and extends `qsa_block_scores_rows` to `nq = 1..8`.
   - Registers `qsa_scores_parity`, `qsa_topk_active_parity`, and `qsa_rows_bench` under `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP` in `CMakeLists.txt`.
