pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): vectorize HC_Q8 prefill dequant and enable gfx12 Q8_0 gr_upmix
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Supersedes #2988 (closed during the `0.2.0-beta` tracker reset), rebased onto `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`).

When `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` is active (the default on RDNA4), each prefill chunk previously launched 192 scalar `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` calls (1 `int8` element per thread, 2-byte stores, `601.5 GB/s` on `gfx1201`) and dequantized both `wd` and `wu` before `gr_norm_rs`, evicting `wd` (`6.55 MB`) from the 8 MB L2 / 64 MB Infinity Cache before `bf16_proj(wd)` read it. In addition, the opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` path was gated off on `gfx12` (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and required materializing `wu` in global BF16 scratch before running.

This PR:
1. Vectorizes `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`8` `int8` elements per thread, `uint4` 16-byte stores, **bitwise identical** across all `16,777,216` `(fp16 d, int8 q)` pairs), adds pair-fused `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`3.204 ms -> 1.646 ms`, **`1.95x`** across 192 matrices), elides same-stream `cudaStreamWaitEvent` calls, and moves `hc_bf16_view(*wd)` / `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` immediately before their consumers.
2. Ports opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` (`gr_upmix_kernel`) to `gfx1200`/`gfx1201` (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32_gfx12`, **`1.57x-1.63x`** vs `hipBLASLt + gr_mix_r`) and fuses direct `Q8_0` `w_up` dequantization into shared memory `sB` (**bitwise identical** to pre-dequantized BF16 `gr_upmix` across all 21 token counts `T = 1..32768`), reducing 397B `--serve` prefill wall time on `gfx1201` by **`-14.0 ms` (`T=2048`)** and **`-21.8 ms` (`T=4096`)**.

## Related discussion

Supersedes #2988. Scope is limited to `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` prefill dequantization (bitwise-identical default path) and opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` on `gfx12`.

## Approach

- Vectorize `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`64` `Q8_0` blocks per 256-thread CTA) and add `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair` + `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view_pair` / `hc_bf16_release_pair`.
- Port `gr_upmix_kernel` and `gr_upmix` to `gfx1200`/`gfx1201` with optional direct `Q8_0` `w_up_q8` shared-memory dequantization, while preserving the ten/eleven-argument signature across SYCL (`sycl/src/prefill/kernels.dp.cpp`) and Metal (`metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`).
- Guard `can_upmix` with `!m.f16_io` so `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` remains on the FP16 GEMM path, and retry `gr_upmix` with materialized BF16 weights when direct `Q8_0` upmix is declined (preserving CUDA `sm_80+` fused upmix under `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`).

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `cmake --build build-copilot-hip --target strata gr_parity gr_upmix_parity arch_defaults_test -j16`: revision `67d3b105` on `0.2.0-beta` (`e88ee39d`), AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, Linux `7.2.9-2-cachyos-server`, ROCm `10.2.0a20260914`), clean build & link.
- `./build-copilot-hip/arch_defaults_test`: revision `67d3b105` (`0.2.0-beta`), `arch_defaults_test: OK`.
- `./build-copilot-hip/gr_parity --selftest`: revision `67d3b105` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, `fused GR Q8_0 dequant (vec8 + pair), finite/Inf/NaN scales: pass`, `gr_read/gr_write: 0 failures`, `gr_parity OK`.
- `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt ./build-copilot-hip/gr_upmix_parity --bench`: revision `67d3b105` (`0.2.0-beta`), `gfx1201`, all 21 token counts (`T = 1..32768`) pass (`gr_upmix_parity: 0 failures`, 0 bitwise diffs between direct `Q8_0` `w_up_q8` and pre-dequantized BF16 `w_up`; `T=2048` `0.508 -> 0.324 ms` `1.57x`, `T=8192` `1.935 -> 1.207 ms` `1.60x`, `T=32768` `7.794 -> 4.784 ms` `1.63x`).
- `clang++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -Iinclude/strata/hip_compat -Iinclude -I/opt/rocm/include -D__HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__=1 metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`: syntax check passed (`0 errors`).

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- Target-device runtime execution on `gfx11` and CUDA `sm_80+` hardware (no `gfx11` or NVIDIA GPU in this host).
- Full SYCL and macOS Metal toolchain link builds (no Intel oneAPI / macOS Metal SDK on this Linux host; updated `sycl/src/prefill/kernels.dp.cpp` and `metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp` signatures verified via header/stub syntax check).

## Limits

- `hc_down` (`wd`) in prefill still dequantizes `Q8_0 -> BF16` into scratch slot 0 (`6.55 MB` per half) and runs `hipBLASLt`.
- `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` remains opt-in (`hc_upmix()`) because its 16-element WMMA accumulation order differs slightly from `hipBLASLt` (`mixed max |diff| / max |value| ~ 1.1e-7..1.9e-7`).

---

## Summary

Optimizes the `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` hyper-connection (`hc_down` / `hc_up`) prefill read path on RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) and CUDA/HIP in two complementary steps:

1. **Default path (`STRATA_HC_Q8=1`, bitwise-identical):**
   - Vectorizes `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`) from 1 `int8` element per lane (`global_load_u8/i8` + `global_store_b16`) to 8 `int8` elements per lane (`dequant_q8_0_vec8_item` + `bf16x2_from_f32_finite` with `uint4` 16-byte stores, 64 `Q8_0` blocks per 256-thread CTA), and adds pair-fused `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair`) plus `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view_pair` / `hc_bf16_release_pair` (`src/core/native_dense.cpp`).
   - Tracks the last recording stream per scratch slot (`g_hc_ev_stream[dev][slot]`) so same-stream `cudaStreamWaitEvent` calls are elided during single-stream prefill chunks.
   - Moves `hc_bf16_view(*wd)` after `gr_norm_rs` (immediately before `bf16_proj(wd)`) and `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` after `gr_silu` (immediately before `bf16_proj(wu)`) in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` so `gr_norm_rs` (`125.8 MB` at `T=2048`, `251.7 MB` at `T=4096`) and `wu` do not evict `wd` (`6.55 MB`) from the 8 MB L2 / 64 MB Infinity Cache before `bf16_proj(wd)` reads it.

2. **Opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` path on `gfx12` (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) + fused `Q8_0` `w_up` dequantization:**
   - Extends `gr_upmix_kernel` and `gr_upmix()` (`src/prefill/kernels.cu`) to `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32_gfx12`, 8-element `um_b16` fragments per lane, `t = t0 + 8 * hi + i` wave32 output row mapping, and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1`).
   - Adds an optional `const uint8_t* w_up_q8 = nullptr` parameter to `gr_upmix` so that when `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` and `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` are active (`wu->data == nullptr && wu->hc_q8 != nullptr`), `gr_upmix_kernel` dequantizes each CTA's 64 `w_up` rows (`64 × 320` = 640 `Q8_0` blocks) directly into shared memory `sB` once per CTA. `prefill.cpp` skips `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` entirely, eliminating all 96 `wu` full-matrix dequantizations (`1.26 GB` of BF16 scratch write+read per chunk) in addition to eliminating the `m.gated` (`T × 10,240` FP32 = `16.1 GB` at `T=2048`, `32.2 GB` at `T=4096`) global memory round-trip across all 96 halves.
   - Enables `gr_upmix_parity` (`src/prefill/gr_upmix_parity.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`) on HIP (`gfx11` / `gfx12`) and adds a bitwise parity check verifying `gr_upmix(..., d_wu_q8)` matches `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0 + gr_upmix(..., d_wu_deq)` bit-for-bit across all 21 token counts (`T = 1 .. 32768`).

---

## Root cause

1. **`STRATA_HC_Q8=1` prefill dequantization overhead and cache eviction (`src/core/native_dense.cpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`):**
   - When `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` is set (`NativeDense::add_hc_skip`), the BF16 hyper-connection matrices (`blk.*.attn_hc_down/up.weight`, `blk.*.ffn_hc_down/up.weight`) are skipped at load (`w.data == nullptr`), leaving only `w.hc_q8` (`Q8_0`, `320 × 10,240` = `3,276,800` elements / `102,400` blocks per matrix).
   - On every prefill chunk (`prefill.cpp:2943`), each of the 96 halves called `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view` twice (`192` launches of `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel`), where each thread loaded a single `int8` quant (`global_load_u8`, `global_load_u8`, `global_load_i8`) and issued a 2-byte `global_store_b16` (`601.5 GB/s` on `gfx1201`).
   - Worse, `prefill.cpp` dequantized both `wd` (`6.55 MB` BF16) and `wu` (`6.55 MB` BF16) before `gr_norm_rs`. Running `gr_norm_rs` (`251.7 MB` of `m.R` read + `m.xn16` write at `T=4096`) between dequantization and `bf16_proj(wd)` evicted the freshly dequantized BF16 scratch from the 8 MB L2 / 64 MB Infinity Cache before `bf16_proj` read it.

2. **`STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` gated off on `gfx12` (`src/prefill/kernels.cu:2112, 2398`):**
   - `gr_upmix()` checked only `gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma(p.gcnArchName)`, returning `false` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201`. Furthermore, `prefill.cpp:2972` required `wu->data != nullptr` before calling `hc_bf16_view`, or else required dequantizing `wu` (`6.55 MB` per half) into global BF16 scratch first.
   - As a result, `gfx1201` always fell back to `hc_bf16_view(wu)` + `hipBLASLt` (`wu` GEMM) + `gr_mix_r`, writing and re-reading `T × 10,240` FP32 `m.gated` (`80 MB` per half = `7.68 GB` read + `7.68 GB` write at `T=2048`; `30.7 GB` total at `T=4096`).

---

## The change

- `include/strata/kernels/fused_gr.hpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`:
  - Add `bf16x2_from_f32_finite` and `dequant_q8_0_vec8_item` (8 elements per thread, handling both 2-byte aligned and arbitrary unaligned pointers, using round-to-nearest-even finite packing when `(d_u16 & 0x7C00u) != 0x7C00u` and falling back to `bf16_from_f32` for `±Inf`/`NaN` scales).
  - Update `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`64` `Q8_0` blocks per 256-thread CTA, `uint4` 16B stores) and add `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair`).
- `include/strata/core/native_dense.hpp`, `src/core/native_dense.cpp`, `src/core/layer.cpp`:
  - Add `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view_pair` and `NativeDense::hc_bf16_release_pair`, plus `g_hc_ev_stream[64][2]` tracking to elide redundant same-stream `cudaStreamWaitEvent` calls.
- `include/strata/prefill/kernels.hpp`, `src/prefill/kernels.cu`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`:
  - Port `gr_upmix_kernel` and `gr_upmix` to `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32_gfx12`, wave32 `gfx12` fragment/row layout, `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1`).
  - Add `const uint8_t* w_up_q8 = nullptr` to `gr_upmix` so `gr_upmix_kernel` dequantizes `w_up_q8` (`Q8_0`) directly into shared memory `sB`, and wire `prefill.cpp` to skip `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` when `gr_upmix` runs.
  - Move `hc_bf16_view(*wd)` after `gr_norm_rs` and `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` after `gr_silu` in `prefill.cpp`.
- `src/kernels/gr_parity.cpp`, `src/prefill/gr_upmix_parity.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`:
  - Add bitwise parity self-test for `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0` and `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair` across finite, subnormal, `±0`, `±Inf`, `qNaN`, `sNaN` scales and aligned/unaligned pointers in `gr_parity --selftest`.
  - Enable `gr_upmix_parity` on HIP (`gfx11` / `gfx12`) and verify that `gr_upmix(..., d_wu_q8)` is bitwise identical to `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0 + gr_upmix(..., d_wu_deq)` across all 21 token counts (`T = 1 .. 32768`).

---

## Evidence

### 1. Standalone Kernel Microbenchmarks & Parity (`gfx1201`)

#### A. `gr_dequant_q8_0` (`192` matrices per chunk, `1.93 GB` total read+write traffic on Radeon AI PRO R9700 `gfx1201`)
- Exhaustive bitwise check across all `65,536 × 256 = 16,777,216` `(fp16 d, int8 q)` pairs (`±0`, subnormals, normals, `±Inf`, `qNaN`, `sNaN`): **0 bitwise mismatches** vs scalar `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel`.

| Kernel variant | Launches / chunk | Median GPU time (192 matrices) | Effective bandwidth | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (scalar 1B loads, 2B store) | 192 | `3.204 ms` | `601.5 GB/s` | `1.00×` |
| Vectorized `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`vec8`, 16B `uint4` store) | 192 | `1.701 ms` | `1,132.7 GB/s` | `1.88×` |
| Pair-fused `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`pair_vec8`) | 96 | **`1.646 ms`** | **`1,170.7 GB/s`** | **`1.95×` (`-1.56 ms`)** |

#### B. `gr_upmix_parity --bench` on `gfx1201` (`STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`)
- All 21 token counts (`T = 1, 7, 16, 31, 32, 33, 48, 63, 64, 65, 96, 126, 127, 128, 129, 600, 1000, 2048, 4099, 8192, 32768`) pass (`gr_upmix_parity: 0 failures`):
  - `mixed max |diff| / max |value|`: `7.10e-08 .. 1.86e-07` vs `hi

pulls.title: [Other] serve: support IPv6 bind addresses
pulls.author: purrsec
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Starting Strata with an IPv6 bind address such as `--host ::` failed before model loading because the HTTP server always used an IPv4 socket. `Server` now selects `AF_INET6` when the bind address is an IPv6 literal, binds `::`, serves requests through `::1`, and formats IPv6 URLs with brackets. IPv4 behavior remains unchanged.

## Related discussion
Supersedes closed PR #1326: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1326

## Approach
Set `self.address_family = socket.AF_INET6` directly in `Server.__init__` when the bind address contains `:`, so both the startup preflight check and the running server use the right socket family without extra wrapper classes. Advertise the loopback URL as `[::1]` for `--host ::`, bracket IPv6 literals in printed URLs, and document the IPv6 option. No default or authentication behavior changes; an API key remains required when listening beyond loopback.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python3 -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_security.py setup.py` at `7aea86c1` on macOS.
- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_security -v`: 28 tests passed, including `Server` address family selection and a real `::` bind and `/health` request through `::1`.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP, SYCL and Metal builds; this change only touches the Python server, setup help, tests and documentation.

## Limits
IPv6 support depends on the host OS having IPv6 enabled. Listening beyond loopback still requires an API key in normal startup.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RX 7900 GRE (gfx1100, 16 GB): IQ2_XS production serving measurements at 262K context
pulls.author: lsunay
pulls.body:
[Benchmark] RX 7900 GRE (gfx1100, 16 GB): IQ2_XS production serving measurements at 262K context

Community benchmark report, no code change. Adds a long-context gfx1100 data point: the 0.2.0 release notes list RX 7000 cards as untested on the 0.2.0 builds, and the earlier RX 7900 GRE report (#740) measured at 65,536 context.

**Method, stated plainly:** these are production serving measurements from the engine's own per-request log over six days of real agent traffic with reasoning enabled — not a controlled bench. 1,004 request lines, 168 with `reused = 0` (fully fresh prompt). Only the fresh lines are aggregated. Output lengths vary per request and `generated` includes thinking tokens, so the decode medians are not comparable to #740's greedy 128-token arm.

Median over the 168 fresh-prompt lines:

| Prompt size | n | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| < 1,000 | 61 | 198.2 | 52.1 |
| 1,000 - 8,000 | 25 | 777.8 | 53.5 |
| >= 8,000 | 82 | 965.9 | 52.5 |

Prefill holds ~950-990 tok/s up to 114K fresh prompt tokens on this card at 262K context.

Two settings decided on this machine, confirmed in use:
- `--vram-reserve-mib 832` - decode crashed when VRAM filled at long context before it was added (2026-10-13); no crash in six days of continuous serving after.
- `fit_max_tokens` - removed the 400 "request exceeds the context window" error when a client sent `max_output_tokens: 32768` at long context.

Environment: Strata 0.1.43.1 source build, commit `a0116b2`, HIP/gfx1100, hipBLASLt gfx1100 table 100200 (26 rows), Ryzen 5 5600X (no AVX-512), 64 GB RAM, `vm.nr_hugepages = 0`, Debian 13. Full config, per-request CSV, aggregates, sanitized log and SHA-256 manifest are in the report folder.

Limitations: one machine, one card, no cross-engine or cross-GPU baseline; no needle test, no TTFT, no greedy arm; ROCm runtime version is not printed in the engine log and could not be confirmed on this host, so only the tuning table version is recorded. The log is a snapshot taken 2026-10-19 while the engine was still serving.

Reproduction status: all numbers come from the log produced on this machine.

pulls.title: [Engine] a reply that ends inside its thinking is continued and reported (#1814)
pulls.author: 47Hunter47
pulls.body:
Fixes #1814. #1178's turn-side case is the same end and is covered by the same flag. This is the work #1840 carried (closed in the tracker reset), rebased onto `main` and extended by one test commit.

## Problem and result

A reply that ends inside its thinking with no answer comes back empty, and nothing says why: `finish_reason` is `stop`, `content` is empty, the reasoning stops mid-sentence. I retested the end on a stock `v0.2.0-beta` checkout (`3d1fb480`, engine built from that source, `/props.build_info` reports `Strata 0.1.45.3`), RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 250K context, `--kv int8`, sampling 1.0/0.95/20, `reasoning_budget_tokens` 16384:

| prompt | runs | empty replies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #1178's minimal input (asking for the turn-end marker, verbatim) | 4 | 4 of 4 (reasoning 103-250 chars, 44-115 tokens generated of an 8000-token cap) |
| #1814's prompt (the closing thinking tag in a code fence) | 4 | 1 of 4 |

With `reasoning_close_retry: true` the replies stop being empty (0 of 8) but are stubs: 9, 10, 12 and 80 characters on #1178's input, because the close happens exactly where the closing tag would start.

With this change, behind one opt-in flag: 0 of 14 empty over two batteries of the same two prompts. The marker's text goes back into the reply as ordinary text where the model was writing it (2 of 3 trigger-prompt runs contain the exact 10-character marker text, which is what that prompt asks for), the thought continues from there (the code-fence prompt answers in full, 1120 and 1211 characters), and the end is reported: one log line, `totals.ended_inside_thinking`, and `"ended_inside_thinking": true` beside `choices`.

## Related discussion

#1814 (the shape this fixes), #1178 (the turn-side case, covered here), #2731 (my retest of this end on 0.2.0-beta, reopened with the numbers above), #1840 (the same work before the tracker reset), #1053 and #123 (the close this falls back to), #931 (the plain spans the write-back uses), #728 (the loop this deliberately does not touch).

## Approach

In this pack's tokenizer the token that ends the turn is a type-3 control token (id 248046, matched only with `parse_special`) and the closing thinking tag is a type-4 token (id 248069). The turn ends on the control token itself, so no character of any marker reaches the stream, and a turn that ended there on purpose looks exactly the same - which is also why the parser cannot catch it.

Behind `"literal_think_guard": true` in `strata-<model>.json` (or `STRATA_LITERAL_THINK_GUARD=1`), like #1053's `reasoning_close_retry`:

1. The end is reported: one log line per reply, `totals.ended_inside_thinking` exposed as `strata:totals_ended_inside_thinking_total` on both `/metrics/prometheus` and `/metrics` with `Accept: text/plain`, and `"ended_inside_thinking": true` beside `choices` and in the stream's last chunk.
2. The token that ended the turn is given back as text where the model was writing it (#1178), as ordinary text through the tokenizer's `plain` spans (#931's mechanism), in the reply and in the next pass's prompt. With the real pack tokenizer: encoding the marker with `parse_special=True` is the single control token 248046, while the same string marked `plain` is the same six ordinary text tokens as the unparsed string, which is what makes the next pass carry on instead of stopping at once. Capped per reply (`LITERAL_MARKER_WRITES = 2`); a thought that repeats whole passages is #728's loop, not a marker it mentions, and goes to the close.
3. Otherwise the thinking is closed the way #123's wrap-up closes it and the reply is continued, capped per reply (`LITERAL_THINK_RETRIES`).

The write-back runs before `reasoning_close_retry`'s close, so a server with both on keeps the thought that was writing the marker. With the flag off a default server is unchanged: no log line, no counter, no response field, and unit checks cover the field and the counter being absent.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest serve.test_literal_think_guard serve.test_prometheus` - 27 tests, OK (this head `791e7b0e`, Ubuntu, RTX 3090).
- Full suite `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` - 902 tests, 14 skipped, the failures listed below.
- Both fork workflows on this head: `Portable monitor client` and `Minimal serving runtime`, green.
- Two live batteries with the guard on (8000 max_tokens): 0 of 14 empty, the marker's text back as ordinary text where the model was writing it, `ended_inside_thinking: true` on the 7 runs that ended inside.
- Two live batteries on the stock `v0.2.0-beta` tag without the change: 5 of 8 empty (the table above), and 0 of 8 empty but 9-80 character stubs with `reasoning_close_retry: true`.

**Failed:**
- `test_keepawake.KeepAwakeTests.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close` - every full run on this machine, and the same on a detached `v0.2.0-beta` worktree (881 tests, 1 failure, that test).
- `test_responses.NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler` - 2 of 3 full runs here. It passes alone (3 of 3) and right after this PR's own module, and it also fails on older trees of this suite on this machine, so I read it as the thread-racy sampler counting this suite already has, not this patch. I did not fix it here.

**Not run:**
- Other engines than this box's CUDA build (HIP, SYCL, Metal, CPU-only), other models and packs, and streaming clients other than the plain non-stream calls in the batteries. The unit tests run against mock engines.

## Limits

- Capped per reply (two write-backs, two closes). A longer pathology is #728's loop, not this end.
- The reporting sits behind the same flag, so a client that did not opt in is told nothing; the counter in `/metrics` is what an operator sees.
- The marker's text goes back as the tokenizer's plain spans, so the reply mentions the marker as text. Nothing else about the stream changes.
- One of this PR's tests needed an adaptation on this base: the length-cut specimen ends on `max_tokens`, but 0.1.45's answer room caps the thinking at 3/4 of `max_tokens` and wraps it up and answers before the cut is reached. The test turns the answer room off so the turn is the one that was recorded.

## History

#1840 carried this work and was closed in the tracker reset. The branch is 8 commits (the 7 of #1840 plus the test adaptation above); the diff is +549/-2 in 6 files, the stat #1840 reported plus that test commit. The first push was based on the `v0.2.0-beta` tag and both fork workflows went red on it: the tag's `tools/minimal_server_smoke.py` summary regex predates `fcca2ccb` and rejects `OK (skipped=N)`, and the monitor client smoke wants the packaging preflight that landed after the tag. Rebasing onto `main` fixed both without touching the diff.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] calibrate checks the output directory up front (#3187)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
## The problem

`strata engine calibrate --measure` checks the report path up front, but not the directory it should land in. That check only ran in `_write_new`, after the sweep, so a full measurement (8 engine starts, 177 measurements, ~19 minutes on the reporter's machine) ended with `report output directory does not exist` and no report for `--review-result` / `--apply-result` to consume.

## What it does

The parent-directory check now runs in `_measure_locked` next to the existing "report path already exists" check, so the refusal happens in a second instead of after the sweep. Same message, same exit code (5). `_write_new` keeps its check as the last word. Nothing is created: the tool still refuses rather than making a directory.

## Validation

Environment: `main` @ `f57c0adc` (the branch base), Windows 11, Python 3.14.7.

- New test `test_measure_refuses_a_missing_output_directory_before_the_sweep` in `tests/terminal/test_calibration.py`: one case for a missing directory, one for a parent that is a file. It uses a runner that fails if the sweep starts, so it only passes when the refusal comes first.
- That test fails on the unpatched tree with `calibration measurement failed (AssertionError); config unchanged` instead of the refusal, which is the sweep having run and only the write failing.
- `tests/terminal`: 701 tests with the change, 700 without, and the same 24 problems in both runs (7 failures, 17 errors) — the two lists are identical. Those are this machine's pre-existing Windows problems in the process and liveness tests plus loader errors, not the change. `pytest` is not installed here, so I ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests/terminal`.
- Not run: no CUDA, HIP or SYCL build, as this file is Python only. No GPU, no model files, no engine start, no measured numbers.

## Limits

- Only `strata engine calibrate --measure`. The issue also names `setup.py --calibrate`, which writes its own record and does not fail; I left it alone.
- No new behaviour and no default changed: the message, the exit code and the report writing are as they were, only earlier.

Fixes #3187

pulls.title: [Engine] OpenAI logprobs / top_logprobs / allowed_token_ids for the CUDA/HIP engine
pulls.author: xiezhipeng-git
pulls.body:
Problem and result. `/v1/chat/completions` on the CUDA/HIP engine accepted `logprobs` / `top_logprobs` and returned HTTP 200, but `choices[0].logprobs.content` was always `[]`. A client that ranks candidate tokens from the model's own distribution — constrained decoding, candidate scoring, tool-choice re-ranking — silently got nothing: the request succeeds, the content is correct, only the field is missing, so the failure is invisible unless the caller asserts on the field. After this change, `logprobs: true` with `top_logprobs` 0..20 (the legacy completions form `logprobs: N` is also accepted) returns one entry per token with its top alternatives, and `allowed_token_ids` returns a distribution renormalised over exactly the ids the caller named.

Related discussion. This supersedes #2254, which the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset closed. GitHub will not reopen it (`state cannot be changed. The feat/openai-logprobs branch was force-pushed or recreated.`), so this PR carries the same single commit, rebased onto `main`. #1916 proposed the same feature for CUDA/HIP and is closed. This implementation follows the protocol the SYCL port already speaks (835d30b1) and the Metal port (31f26683), so one server-side reader serves all three backends.

Approach.

- Engine half, `src/program/generate.cpp`: `logprobs=K` and `allowed=a,b,c` are two extra keys on the `--serve` GEN line (an engine that predates them skips them as unknown), and one `LP <logprob> [id:logprob ...]` line is written after each `T <id>` in the same flush. The value comes from the verify window's head logits **before** sampling, penalties and temperature, so it is the model's distribution rather than the sampler's. Off by default: a request without `logprobs` produces the previous output byte for byte, and the per-token cost is one integer compare.
- Server half, `serve/server.py`: `sampling_keys` appends the two keys only when asked; `generate` reads each token's `LP` line before yielding the token (a held line is consumed before the next read, so an engine without LP lines loses no lines, and a `DONE` read while looking for one still ends the request); `LogprobEntries` decodes token bytes incrementally so the entries joined spell the reply; `allowed_token_ids` keeps the named ids and renormalises over them; `structured_chunks` re-aligns the entries when `response_format: json_schema` rewrites the content and returns **no** logprobs rather than a set that does not match.
- Compatibility: additive and opt-in. A request that does not ask for logprobs gets the same bytes as before, and no default changes.

Validation.

Rebased onto `upstream/main` `e88ee39d` (which contains `v0.2.0-beta` `b73dbce3`); head `104becfd`. The diff is 3 files, +570/−8, unchanged by the rebase.

Passed:

- Full CUDA build and link, revision `104becfd`: `cmake --build build-lp --target strata` — Release, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89`, CUDA 13.3 (V13.3.73), MSVC 14.41, Windows 11, RTX 4090. `[154/154] Linking CXX executable strata.exe`, exit 0.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_logprobs` — 17 tests, OK, on `104becfd`.
- Hardware run, same revision and engine (`strata.exe` built from it, model Swift-1.5 IQ3_XXS, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`), `max_tokens: 1`, `temperature: 0`, `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false`:
  - non-streamed, `top_logprobs: 20` → `logprobs.content` length 1, `top_logprobs` width 20; entry token `A` at -0.1028 with `B -3.121`, `C -3.201`, `D -5.1109`.
  - the same request with `tools` and `tool_choice: "auto"` → entries present, width 20, labels `A/D/C/B`.
  - `stream: true` → the delta carries `logprobs.content` (1 entry, token `A`, -0.0801, top width 20).
- An external client (a separate project) that scores 5 candidate labels from this endpoint: 7 scoring requests in a 30k-token session, 0 errors, 0 disabled calls. Run against the same commit before the rebase (`80494788`); the endpoint behaviour it depends on is the same code path exercised above.

Failed: none observed.

Not run:

- HIP backend build. `src/program/generate.cpp` is shared by the CUDA and HIP builds; only the CUDA configuration was built here (no AMD GPU or toolchain on this machine).
- SYCL backend build. It carries its own implementation (`install_logprobs` in `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`) and this change does not touch it; no Intel GPU or toolchain here.
- `--batch` mode: see Limits.

Limits.

- `--batch` does not return logprobs. `generate_batched` never reads `LP` lines; only the solo/serial path (`generate`) does, so a server started with `--batch` answers `logprobs.content: []`. Giving the batched path the same read-before-yield step is the remaining work if that combination is wanted.
- The reported logprob describes the model's distribution before penalties and temperature, not the post-sampling one.
- With `response_format: json_schema` the returned content may not be spelled by the tokens; in that case no logprobs are returned, by design.
- CUDA/HIP only; the SYCL and Metal implementations are untouched.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: per-layer expert routing metrics for /metrics ("routing_counts", opt-in)
pulls.author: blange48
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Which experts do the requests actually use? Today the only way to see it is a `--dump-routing` trace (~4 KB per generated token, rewritten at every start) and an offline script. This PR adds a cheap view of the same data on `/metrics`, so Prometheus and Grafana can show it.

- **Before:** no routing information on `/metrics`.
- **After, with the opt-in key:**
  - the JSON `/metrics` gets an `experts` section: per layer, the experts seen, the top 32's share, the entropy in bits and the top 10 experts;
  - the Prometheus text gets `strata:expert_routed_total`, the per-layer gauges `strata:expert_seen`, `strata:expert_top32_share` and `strata:expert_entropy_bits` (label `layer`), and `strata:expert_routed_by_expert_total` for each layer's 8 most routed experts (labels `layer`, `expert`). That is ~530 series, not 24,576.
- **Without the key** nothing is counted, written or reported.

## Related discussion

#1547, closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset. The `/reopen` check passed there, but GitHub would not reopen it after the rebase force-push, so this is the same branch as a new pull request. The earlier review (SuperDistance, Windows builds included) is in #1547.

## Approach

- **Engine** (`--routing-counts PATH`, `--routing-counts-every MIN`): one `uint64` counter per (layer, expert), incremented where the routing trace reads the ids (`drive_pool` / `drive_pool_multi`, every layer of every decode window, drafted tokens included; prompt reads are not counted). Nothing is written per token. The counts are saved as JSON every minute between requests (the same spot as the expert-profile save) and on QUIT, through a temporary file renamed over the last one with `std::filesystem::rename`, so it replaces the old file on Windows too. A 48 × 512 file is ~55-85 KB.
- **Server** (`"routing_counts": "<path>"`, optional `"routing_counts_every"`): passes the flags, and `GET /metrics` reads the file, cached on its mtime.
- **Docs:** `docs/DETAILS.md`, and an Experts row in `docs/monitoring/grafana-strata.json`.
- Compatibility: off by default; no change to any other metric or to the engine's work when the key is absent.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python serve/test_prometheus.py` on this head (47e57d95, rebased on main): 8 tests OK (summary with counts, entropy, an empty layer, a missing file; gauges; per-expert counters, at most 8 per layer; config key to engine flags). macOS, Python 3.
- Engine and server built from v0.2.0-beta plus this PR (CUDA 13.0, `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`, Linux, docker), then `pytest serve` in that image: 864 passed, 18 skipped, 1 failed: `test_lifeline.py::test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed` (the POSIX watcher path inside a container; this PR does not touch it, I have not checked whether it fails on v0.2.0-beta alone).
- In production since 2026-10-08 on 0.1.40.3 to 0.1.45 builds: 4× RTX 5080, layer split 12,24,36, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 8 --batch-groups 4`. 384 `strata:expert_routed_by_expert_total` series exported at every release check, a Grafana row on top. Throughput with and without the key, 1 / 4 / 8 clients (T=0.7, 300 tokens, warm pass): 147 / 269 / 394 against 143 / 268 / 392 tok/s, within run-to-run noise. The counts agreed with a `--dump-routing` trace of the same traffic (layer 0's top experts 382, 300, 324 in both; every layer counted the same number of times).

**Failed:**
- none observed in this PR's code (the lifeline test above is outside it).

**Not run:**
- The runtime check on this exact head with 0.2.0-beta on the 4× RTX 5080 box: scheduled for tonight with our release gate; I will add the numbers here.
- Windows and HIP builds of this head (SuperDistance built an earlier revision on Windows for CUDA sm_120 and HIP gfx1100, which is how the rename bug was found and fixed).

## Limits

- Counts restart at zero with the engine (a Prometheus counter handles that). The first file appears at the first request a minute after the start.
- Prompt reads are not counted, only decode windows.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 5090: the 0.1.45 to 0.1.45.3 engine change is worth +9.5 % on a 16K prompt
pulls.author: IVoyt
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Two folders with measurements from one RTX 5090, taken with the standard bench suite
(`tools/strata_bench.py`): the install's own report for the current engine, and an **engine A/B**
that measures what the **0.1.45 → 0.1.45.3** engine change is worth, with the variables
controlled one at a time.

The result: **the engine change is worth +9.5 % on a 16K prompt and +10.7 % on a 32K prompt**,
measured with the same CUDA toolkit, the same build flags, the same runtime libraries, the same
model and the same configuration on both sides. Time to first token falls 9-10 % at 16K/32K and
8 % on the agent turns. **The CUDA toolkit makes no difference** (13.0.0, 13.1 and 13.2.2 of the
same source agree within ±0.3 %), and the **0.1.45.3 → 0.1.46 step adds nothing** for a single
RTX 50 — which matches the 0.2.1 release notes, where the new defaults are for AMD, Linux,
Intel, integrated GPUs and two-card setups.

## Related discussion

none (a results-only submission; no engine change is proposed)

## Approach

**Nine arms**, every one a local build of a known tree, the same model, the same run
configuration (byte-identical `args`), the same runtime libraries and the same six `STRATA_*`
switches; only the engine binary differs:

| arm | engine | tree | compiler |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 0.1.45 | v0.1.45 | published release build (CUDA 13.0, portable, multi-arch + PTX) |
| B1, B2 | 0.1.45 | v0.1.45 | 13.1, local, sm_120 |
| C | 0.1.45.3 | v0.2.0-beta-7 | 13.1, local, sm_120 |
| D | 0.1.46 | v0.2.1 | 13.0.0, local, sm_120 |
| E1, E2 | 0.1.46 | v0.2.1 | 13.1, local, sm_120 |
| F1, F2 | 0.1.46 | v0.2.1 | 13.2.2, local, sm_120 |

The same build is measured more than once, because this box moves 8-28 % between engine starts
at an unchanged setting (#1332) and a single old-vs-new pair cannot separate that from a real
difference. The 0.1.45 arms were built from a `git worktree` of tag `v0.1.45`, so the code
change is measured with the toolkit and the flags held constant.

The first version of this report compared the published 0.1.45 release binary against a local
0.1.45.3 build, which confounds the engine change with the toolkit and the build flags. That
comparison is kept as arm A, and the controlled series replaces it as the evidence.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:<port> --api-key <key> --runs 3 --long`
  against each of the nine servers, on Windows 11, driver 617.42, RTX 5090 32 GiB, i7-12700KF,
  95.8 GiB RAM, Python 3.13.12, Visual Studio 2022 Community 14.34. The tool's own reports are in
  the folder (`bench-report-*.md`), every request in `results-*.json`, the engine logs beside them.
- the tool's own comparisons: `python tools/strata_bench.py --compare <old> --compare-only <new>`.
  The three that matter are in the report: **B1 → C** (the engine change, same toolkit and flags),
  **E2 → D** and **E1 → F1** (the toolkit alone, same source).

**Failed:**

- none observed

**Not run:**

- **No correctness check.** No needle test, no HumanEval, no tool-call check, and the answers of
  the arms were not compared token by token. The 0.1.45.3 change alters the default prompt path on
  sm_120 (the fused int8 prompt experts, the fused gate/up SwiGLU launch), which the project's own
  notes describe as slightly different answers at the same quality; this report does not measure
  that difference.
- **Decode is not resolvable at this machine's noise level.** The two arms of the same build differ
  by 0.2-1.2 % at 16K/32K, so anything smaller than that is not a result here. The decode figures
  in the report are given as measured, with no claim attached.
- **One machine, one model, one configuration** — a 24 GiB card, another quantisation or another
  tree may land elsewhere.
- Background load and power limits were not recorded; the drive model is not in the report.

## Limits

The A/B folder is a report, not a change: no engine, tool or documentation file is touched, and the
README's headline performance claims are left alone. The `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` index is
not edited here — that entry is the maintainer's to add if the report is accepted.

The bench tool's own "start the server" path raises a `NameError` (`port` is undefined at
`tools/strata_bench.py:990`), so the server was started by hand and the bench pointed at it with
`--url`; that is issue #3188, reported separately. With `--url` the tool does not write
`engine-log-excerpt.txt`, so the engine logs are included here instead.

The CUDA toolkits were installed from NVIDIA's redistributable components into `D:\cuda-13.0.0` and
`D:\cuda-13.2.2` rather than with the Windows installer, so the layouts are the redistributable
ones (`bin/`, `include/`, `lib/x64/`, `nvvm/`) rather than `C:\Program Files\...\CUDA\v13.x`. The
compiler and its libraries are the same bits, and the build found the root through the same
`-DCUDAToolkit_ROOT` the setup uses.

pulls.title: [Engine] arena: hand back the block for layers a GPU holds whole (opt-in, saves 21.7 GiB of RAM)
pulls.author: weituotian

labels.name: needs-format
labels.description: Title or template does not follow CONTRIBUTING.md yet

pulls.body:
## Title

Issue: Resolves # (no issue filed — this grew out of a private investigation on a 3090 + V100 rig; happy to open one if you prefer the change tracked there)

## Summary

On a **layer split**, the layers a GPU stage holds *whole* — every one of its experts resident in that card's cache — are never read from the CPU expert arena. Today they are still copied into the arena and paid for in RAM/commit for the whole run. This adds an opt-in path that loads those layers into a **separate `PinnedArena`** and hands the whole block back to the OS once the residency table proves the claim.

Enabled with `STRATA_ARENA_RELEASE_BLOCK=1`. **Default off: one block, byte-identical to today.**

```
strata generate: arena-skip: layers 27-47 are fully resident: 21.71 GiB of the expert arena handed back to the OS
```

Why a second allocation and not `madvise` / `MEM_DECOMMIT`: `release()` already exists and is already called for every VRAM-resident pair, but it only acts on the **file-backed** arena (`STRATA_ARENA_MMAP`), where dropping a page just means faulting it back from the file. The default arena is anonymous **2 MiB large pages**, so (a) a range cannot be decommitted — `MEM_DECOMMIT` on a `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` allocation fails, the region must go back whole — and (b) a released anonymous page reads back as **zeros**, i.e. silent corruption. Making the releasable layers their own allocation is what keeps the large pages.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `include/strata/core/pinned.hpp` | `load_experts_ranges`: `dst_bias` (the file offset that maps to `dst[0]`) |
| `src/core/pinned.cu` | the write path honours `dst_bias` (`dst + off - dst_bias`) |
| `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp` | `load_experts_gguf`: `dst_bias` **and** a layer range `[l0, l1)`. `ArenaExpertSource`: `set_split_layer()`, `split_layer()`, `release_tail()`, `tail_released()`, and the tail block's members |
| `src/core/expert_source.cpp` | the second `PinnedArena`, its load (`dst_bias = boundary_off_`), the `blob_at()`/`blob()` branch, `release_tail()` (one `MEM_RELEASE`), `close()` |
| `src/program/generate.cpp` | `set_split_layer(split_at.front())` behind the switch; after `host_res` is built, the per-layer "all 512 experts resident" check and the release, with the log line |

`load_experts_gguf` needed **two** things, not one: it wrote at `dst + lay.blob_offset(...)` (a second allocation cannot be served by that) **and** it walked all `lay.n_layers`, so a block would otherwise fill all 48 layers.

## Extra Notes

**Why it is safe.** The block is released only when *every* pair of those layers has `host_res != kNotResident`, i.e. all 512 experts of all 21 layers sit in the V100's cache. A layer with all 512 experts resident has **no spare slot** to `admit()` another one, so the adaptive tier can never evict one of them; hence no CPU-pool read can ever land in the released block. And if that reasoning were ever wrong, `blob_at()` answers **nullptr** for those layers, which the pool turns into `d.failed = "the expert source could not produce a blob"` — a loud error, not zeros.

**Why the release waits for `host_res`.** Sizing it up front from free VRAM was rejected: on the test machine the V100 has only **0.26 GiB** of headroom over its layers' experts (21.70 needed vs ~21.96 available after the prompt buffers, KV residency and the reserve), so an estimate that is 1 % off would release a layer that can still miss. `host_res` is the first point where the residency is known exactly.

**Concretely, on the machine it was written for** — RTX 3090 (24 GB, x8) + Tesla V100 (32 GB, x8), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO **IQ3_S**, 48 layers × 512 experts = 24,576 pairs, `--max-context 262144`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--prefill 4096`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--spec-min-p 0.7`, `--conversation-cache-mib 4096`, Windows 11. `--layer-split auto` prices decode and picks **K=27** (best of 46 placements; K=31 is a 0.2 % near tie):

| | RTX 3090 (CUDA0) | Tesla V100 (CUDA1) |
|---|---|---|
| layers | 0–26 (27) | 27–47 (21) + head + draft |
| decode cost per layer | 0.48 ms | 0.66 ms |
| experts those layers hold | 27 × 512 = 13,824 | 21 × 512 = 10,752 |
| expert cache slots | 8,516 (15.46 GiB) → **62 %** | **10,752 → 100 %** |
| free VRAM once loaded | 1,413 MiB | 1,676 MiB |

So 21 × 512 × 2.07 MiB = **21.70 GiB** of the 46.84 GiB arena that the CPU can never read.

| Before / after, same config, same model, same boot | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `experts loaded` | 46.84 GiB | 46.84 GiB (unchanged) |
| **Windows commit free once loaded** | **0.5 GiB** | **21.4 GiB** |
| process commit | ~64.5 GiB | **~43.4 GiB** |
| VRAM hit / PCIe / CPU pool | 96.15 / 0.25 / 3.55 % | 96.70 / 0.20 / 3.10 % |
| decode tok/s (median, 10 replayed real agent requests) | 110.2 | 106.5 |
| first token (median) | 2.36 s | 3.03 s |
| `file_blobs` / `file_mb` | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The 0.5 GiB figure is why this exists: the engine warns `the Windows commit limit is 116.7 GiB and 2.9 GiB of it is left ... it can end at the limit with no message (exit code 0xC0000409)` on that machine, and a released block is the difference between "at the limit" and 21 GiB of headroom.

**On the decode / first-token deltas above** — they are not the mechanism. The released block is never touched on the decode path (proved by `file_blobs = 0` and zero errors), the two runs differ in file-cache state (the run after a fresh start pays a cold 204K-token prompt), and per-block deltas even change sign (+1.8 % / −6.3 %). A paired comparison of the same 10 requests against the 0-release arm gives **−1.2 % decode, 5 up / 5 down** = noise. 20 replayed requests: `could not produce a blob` **0**, `file_blobs`/`file_mb` **0** on every request.

**Where it works.** Both expert sources: the pack above has **no `experts.bin`** (`native_experts.txt` → the GGUF shards), so `open()` takes the `from_gguf` path. Not touched: `--mmap-experts` / `--resident-*` (they already have their own partial-residency machinery), the padded `STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED` layout, `--shared-expert-arena`, `--expert-cache-device1..3` — `open()` falls back to one block for all of them.

**Build / verify.** `build-cuda12`, `strata` target, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="70;86"`, exit 0. Smoke-tested on this rig: `session is up (engine 0.1.45)`, the release line printed, K stayed 27, and the same 10-request replay ran clean.

**Note on the base.** This branch was cut from `477ac13c` and so predates the `pin_reserve_*` sequence that now wraps `arena_src.open(...)`; that is why GitHub reports it as not mergeable against today's `main`. Rebasing is a one-place edit (keep the new `pin_reserve_take()/pin_note_arena()/pin_reserve_release_soft()` trio and insert the gated `set_split_layer()` before it) — say the word and I will rebase rather than have you resolve it.

**Design note** is in the same PR: `docs/ARCH-EXPERT-MEMORY-2026-10-19.md` — the 94 % / 96 % hit-rate breakdown, the per-miss cost of the three paths (PCIe 0.15 ms → 3090, 0.31 ms → V100, CPU pool ~1 ms), and why only the 512/512 layers qualify.

pulls.title: [Other] setup: say that --kv, --context and --vision are not applied when starting an installed model
pulls.author: victoralcazardev
pulls.body:
Problem and result: with a model already installed, `./setup.sh --kv q4_0` (or `--context N`, or `--vision no`) starts the model with its saved settings and prints nothing about the flag. The start path passes only host, API key, draft vocab, VRAM reserve and browser to `start()`; `--kv`, `--context` and `--vision` are dropped. The user believes the new setting is in use. With this change, setup prints a warning that names the ignored flags and how to apply them, and then starts as before. Behavior is otherwise unchanged.

```
  [!]  --kv, --context, --vision only apply when a model is set up: this start keeps its saved settings. To change them: ./setup.sh --setup --model NAME --kv --context --vision ...
```

Approach: a warning, following the existing `--calibrate` "said, not dropped" pattern (#2036), rather than applying the flags on start. Applying them would change what a plain start does, and the setup path already rewrites them (`--setup --model NAME --kv ...`). The check covers the two paths that start or tune an installed model without setting it up (the plain start and `--calibrate`); `--setup`, `--check`, `--model`/`--family` and `--no-start` go through setup as before.

Validation:
  Passed: `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_choices` (55 tests OK). The new `StartIgnoresSetupFlags.test_said_on_a_plain_start` fails on main (only the banner is printed) and passes with this change. `test_silent_without_them` checks that a plain start with none of these flags prints no warning.
  Passed: `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_setup_*.py'`: 688 tests. The same 50 failures occur on main (3fa1b524) without this change (48 in `test_setup_golden`, 2 in `test_setup_engine_hash`); the list of failures is identical with and without it.
  Not run: a real start on hardware. The reproduction is in the mocked harness only; I found the gap by reading the start dispatch (`setup.py`, the `have and not (a.setup ...)` branch) and confirmed it with the test. No engine code changed.
Limits: `--rope-scaling`/`--rope-scale` may have the same gap; not checked, not included.

pulls.title: [Other] setup: pass the family's pack args to the low-RAM experts.bin run (Gyro needs --compat-bf16)
pulls.author: victoralcazardev
pulls.body:
Problem and result: on a PC where setup picks the low-RAM mode, a Gyro install (`--family gyro`) stops at the second pack run. Setup packs twice: first `iq_pack.py ... --compat-bf16` (with the family's `pack_args`), then `iq_pack.py ... --experts-bin` for low-RAM mode. The second call does not pass `pack_args`, so `iq_pack.py` rejects Gyro's non-BF16 hc tensors and exits 1:

```
output_hc_down.weight is IQ4_NL, but the engine requires BF16; use --compat-bf16
blk.0.hc_attn_down.weight is Q6_K, but the engine requires BF16; use --compat-bf16
... and 356 more
  [X]  command failed (exit 1): python
```

The first run has already written `native_experts.txt`, so a rerun skips it and fails at the same point every time; the install cannot finish. With this change both runs pass the family's `pack_args`.

Approach: one-line change in `setup.py`: the `--experts-bin` run also gets `*fam.get("pack_args", [])`, like the pack run just above it. Families without `pack_args` get the same command as before.

Validation:
  Passed: reproduced on hardware: RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), Linux, 31 GiB RAM, clone at v0.2.0-beta-4-g4caf857c, `./setup.sh --setup --family gyro --model Gyro-S --backend hip --vision no --yes --no-start --context 262144 --kv int8 --vram-reserve-mib 3072`: stopped with the error above. Ran the same command setup uses, with `--compat-bf16` added (`tools/iq_pack.py --gguf <Gyro-S gguf> --out <pack> --experts-bin --compat-bf16`): wrote `experts.bin: 48 layers, 24.02 GiB`. A rerun of setup then finished ("All set", start script written).
  Passed: `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_gyro` (13 tests OK). The new `GyroLowRamPack` test fails on main (`'--compat-bf16' not found in [... '--experts-bin']`) and passes with this change.
  Passed: `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_setup_*.py'`: 687 tests. The same 50 failures occur on main (3fa1b524) without this change (48 in `test_setup_golden`, 2 in `test_setup_engine_hash`); the list of failures is identical with and without it.
  Not run: setup.py with this patch end to end on hardware (only the patched command, run by hand, as above); Gyro-S inference on gfx1100; no engine or backend code changed, so no GPU builds.
Limits: none known. The Unsloth family also has `pack_args`, but it does not reach this branch.

pulls.title: Web app: use wide windows and fit narrow screens
pulls.author: mnott
pulls.body:
The web app's views were capped at fixed widths (chat 860 px, monitor 1240 px), so on a wide window, or in a wide side panel, most of the space stayed empty. This makes the layout follow the window:

- **Wide windows:** the monitor grows up to 1920 px and its metric cards fill the row (`auto-fit`, 280 px minimum, so 1280 px keeps 4 columns); chat, composer and About grow to 1100 px while message text keeps a readable line length.
- **Narrow screens:** breakpoints at 900, 640, 560 and 480 px. The monitor row stacks, metrics drop to one column, the settings form becomes one column with full-width inputs, gauges scale instead of using fixed pixel sizes, long values (paths, model names) wrap, and touch targets are at least 40 px tall.

Only `serve/web/app.css` changes; no markup, script or token changes.

**Checked:** `document.scrollWidth <= innerWidth` on Chat, Monitor, About and the API monitor page at 360, 390, 768, 1280 and 1920 px; used live for a day on macOS (Metal build), Chrome, in a normal window and a split-view side panel.

One note for testing: the server sends the web files without cache headers, so browsers can keep the old stylesheet; a hard reload (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R) shows the change.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] 2x MI50 16 GB (gfx906): IQ3_XXS at 128K, --pipeline-windows 2 gives +36% decode
pulls.author: romeo5353535353-ui
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

There is no measured report for the gfx906 build with the original IQ3_XXS at the
full 131,072-token context, and `docs/AMD_HIP.md` does not mention the two flags
that matter most on a two-card gfx906 split.

This adds a community report: 2x Instinct MI50 16 GB + Ryzen 7 5700X, Strata
v0.1.43.1, IQ3_XXS at 131,072 tokens. The two findings worth a line in the docs:

- `--pipeline-windows 2`: decode **49.2 -> 66.9 tok/s (+36%)**, prompt rate
  unchanged (353 tok/s).
- `--trim-stage-weights` (with the explicit `--layer-split 27`): prompt reading
  **353 -> 371 tok/s (+5%)**, decode +2%.

Also measured and reported so others do not repeat it: `--batch` gives no
aggregate gain for one interactive user (per-request decode collapses), RAM
2400 -> 3600 MT/s is +2%, and `--kv-resident` from 0 to 65536 is neutral both at
1.6K and at 31K prompt tokens.

## Related discussion

https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/3173

## Approach

Documentation and data only:

- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-2x-mi50-5700x/README.md` - the report,
  following the format of the other community reports;
- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-2x-mi50-5700x/results.json` - every run,
  not only the medians;
- one bullet in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

No code, no defaults, no build changes.

## Validation

**Passed:** 12 configurations, each a full container restart plus one discarded
warm-up and 7 long + 5 short measured requests. Engine v0.1.43.1 (`a0116b2`),
Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-147, ROCm from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`,
`-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906`. About 1.5 h of
continuous load across the runs: no engine errors, no faults, `dmesg` clean, GPU
junction 45-49 C, 200 W cap per card.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** no source changes, so no CUDA / HIP / SYCL / Metal builds were made;
a single machine; the sweep prompt is 1.6K tokens with one 31K probe, not the
4K/32K/128K ladder of the harness.

## Limits

One machine, one VBIOS (the cards report `1002:66af`), MTP on, 200 W per card.
The report is measured on 0.1.43.1 because 0.1.44+ does not build for gfx906 on
this machine (#3172).

pulls.title: serve: start an elastic image encoder before encoding a tool-returned image (#3171)
pulls.author: Lithivm
pulls.body:
Fixes #3171.

## The bug

`_note_unreadable_tool_images()` encodes a picture that a **tool** returned (Claude Code's `Read` of an image file, an MCP tool returning a plot) with `self.vision.encode(src)` — but unlike `prepare()`'s own image path it never calls `self._vision_up()`:

```python
# prepare(), the request's own images — correct
with self._turn(cancel):
    self._vision_up()
    encoded = self.vision.encode_all(images, cancel) ...

# _note_unreadable_tool_images(), a picture a tool returned — no _vision_up()
with self._turn(cancel):  # the encoder takes its turn with the requests (see below)
    self.vision.encode(src)
```

With the elastic encoder (`vram_elastic: true` + vision `"elastic": true`) the encoder is not running between pictures, so `Vision.proc` is `None` and `encode()`'s `self.proc.stdin.write(...)` raises `AttributeError`. That function's `except (ValueError, OSError)` does not catch it, so it leaves `prepare()` and lands in `_post`'s generic handler, which reports any of those as a client error:

```
400 {"type": "invalid_request_error",
     "message": "the request is malformed (AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'stdin')"}
```

So an agent doing a normal tool call breaks the turn — and, because clients re-send history, possibly the turns after it as well.

## Repro (0.1.44.1, no waiting needed)

A fresh elastic session never starts the encoder (it starts with the first picture), so the first request with a tool image fails:

1. `"vram_elastic": true` and `"vision": {"gpu": true, "elastic": true, ...}`; start the server — `strata-vision` is not running (expected).
2. One request whose messages hold an image in a **tool** message (Anthropic dialect: `user` → `assistant tool_use` → `user tool_result` with an `image` block).
3. 400 as above. Measured: fails before this patch, answers normally after it, and the encoder is then started and stopped as usual (`VRAM 3584 MiB kept free: the expert cache N -> M of N slots` in the engine log).

`"elastic": false` does not hit it (the encoder runs from the start), and a *user*-sent image was always fine — only the tool-returned path is affected.

## The change

Two lines, the same call the sibling path makes. `_vision_up()` returns immediately when the encoder is not elastic or is already running (`if not getattr(v, "elastic", False) or v.alive(): return`), so nothing changes for non-elastic setups.

```diff
                         with self._turn(cancel):  # the encoder takes its turn with the requests (see below)
+                            self._vision_up()   # an elastic encoder is down between pictures: start it first, as
+                                                # prepare()'s own image path does (else encode() writes to a None proc)
                             self.vision.encode(src)
```

`\ No newline at end of file` — no; the file's LF endings are unchanged (2 lines added, 0 removed).

## Two things I did not change (see #3171)

- That function exists so an unreadable tool picture becomes `[image omitted: ...]` instead of a 400; widening its `except` to `AttributeError` would keep that promise for unexpected failures too. Kept out of this PR to keep it to the defect.
- `_post` maps any `AttributeError` raised while preparing a request to `400 invalid_request_error`. That is why this looked like a client bug; an internal error arguably deserves a 500.

## Verified

- Before: 400 with the exact message above (0.1.44.1, Windows 11 26200, RTX 5070 Ti, Q2_0, context 131072, `--mmap-experts`, `--vram-elastic`, `elastic_mib` 3584).
- After: the same request answers; regression checks pass on plain text (`/v1/chat/completions`), a user image via `/v1/chat/completions` and via `/v1/messages`, and the tool image that used to fail.

pulls.title: [Engine] kv: size the resident ring from the run's depth (opt-in, STRATA_KV_RING_ADAPT)
pulls.author: xyzzing
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The resident K/V ring is one global value (`--kv-resident`), and because the KV pool is sized by it (the pool *is* the ring), a ring chosen for depth is paid by every run. A flat raise is a measured loss at shallow depth — on 0.2.0, ring 32,768 → 49,152 at 1K costs **−40 %** of the MTP path (acceptance 207/207 → 149–156/215) and at 32K **−9.1 %** with MTP against **−1.7 %** without: the draft path pays for a ring it cannot use, not attention.

This PR sizes the ring from the run's depth, and only grows it when the ring can cover the whole context:

```
needed = prompt + max_new + one page
ring   = (needed >= cap) ? cap : 32768     // 32768 is the engine's historical default
cap    = --kv-resident
```

Opt-in (`STRATA_KV_RING_ADAPT`), default behaviour unchanged. A shallow run keeps exactly today's ring; a deep one grows into the cap.

## Related discussion

- #2450 — the "keep the K/V in VRAM when it fits" setup rule this extends to the case where it does not quite fit.
- #2630 — the streamed page pool's eviction policy; ring size is the first-order lever next to it on this card.
- #3166 — the shallow-depth drafter/ring interaction this avoids by keeping the floor at the default ring.

## Approach

- `qsa_kv_ring_adapt(g, cells_needed, cap)` in `src/core/layer.cpp` (+ declaration in `layer.hpp`): rounds the needed cells up to a page, floors at `max(qsa_kv_resident_min(), 32768)`, and **returns the floor unless `needed >= cap`**.
- The hook in `src/program/generate.cpp` runs **before** the session arena is sized and the graphs are captured, because `qsa_state_bytes` → `kv_pool_bytes` sizes the pool by slots.
- The floor is the engine's historical default ring on purpose: with the allocator minimum (20,480) an earlier version measured **−7.3 % at 1K**.

## Validation

Passed (0.2.0-beta base, same binary both arms, interleaved pairs, 256 generated tokens):
- 32K: control 82.2 → **82.3 tok/s (+0.1 %)** — the depth-only rule had lost 9.1 % here; the ring stays at 32,768, which the arm's own log line confirms (`KV ring adaptive: 49152 -> 32768`).
- 128K: 70.7 → **81.5 tok/s (+15.3 %)**, prefill 2,391/2,375 and TTFT 55.1/55.4 s unchanged.
- Against the live v0.1.45 binary: decode **+7.5 % @32K, +9.0 % @64K, +8.6 % @128K** (5 pairs at 128K, tight: prefill 2,445–2,459 vs 2,382–2,400; TTFT 53.6–53.9 vs 54.9–55.3 s), prefill −0.9/−1.4/−2.4 %, TTFT +0.7/+1.3/+2.5 %. This is a trade the maintainers may or may not want; it is stated rather than hidden.
- 1K: **−7.7 %** with the cap. This is a **same-ring** comparison — at 1K both arms print 32,768 — and the difference tracks the MTP acceptance state (207 vs 197 accepted). I do not claim it as a gain or a regression.

Failed: none observed.

Not run:
- CUDA and SYCL builds (no such toolkit on this machine). The patch is backend-neutral core code, but I have not compiled it for those backends.
- The `--serve` path: serve keeps one main session plus parked snapshots, so there is no per-request session to size a ring for; per-request sizing there needs per-conversation KV pools, noted as a follow-up, not this patch.

## Limits

- Opt-in and `generate`-path only.
- The 32,768 floor is a constant (the engine's default ring), not a configuration knob.
- Because the pool is the ring, the ring cannot be resized within a session — only chosen when the session's arena is built.
- The 64K point used a workload derived as the first 65,536 ids of a synthetic 128K prompt; provenance is in the measurement record.

## Measurement notes

One process a cell, one-shot greedy, 256 generated tokens; the intervals are the MTP acceptance state (cells moved ±8 %), so only paired medians are used. Raw rows: 32K control 74.0/82.4/…, 128K control 70.7/64.5/…, cap arm 81.5/84.2/… — the full tables are in the campaign records; I can attach a sanitized dump if useful.

pulls.title: serve: accept the three thinking-budget field names (pi's thinkingTokenBudgetField) as aliases
pulls.author: shizhx
pulls.body:
## Summary

pi's `thinkingTokenBudgetField` can be any of the other providers' names for the same budget; clients send `thinking_token_budget` (vLLM), `thinking_budget` (Qwen) or `thinking_budget_tokens` (llama.cpp). Those fields were silently ignored, so the thinking budget never applied. The serve layer now copies the first alias present into `reasoning_budget_tokens` before dispatching; the request's own `reasoning_budget_tokens` wins.

```text
on(request, for /v1/chat/completions | /v1/messages | /v1/responses)
  if request has no reasoning_budget_tokens
    copy first present of
      thinking_token_budget, thinking_budget, thinking_budget_tokens
      → reasoning_budget_tokens
  dispatch   # unchanged downstream: validation, budget, wrap-up
```

Serve layer only — 9 lines in `serve/server.py` plus tests and the DETAILS.md note. No engine change; the budget machinery itself (#123) is untouched.

## Evidence

- **Before:** parent commit `477ac13c`, same four tests — the alias is ignored, thinking runs to the end, a bad alias is not rejected:
  ```text
  FAIL test_the_budget_alias_field_names
    AssertionError: 'Let me think step by step about two plus two. ...'  (full thinking, no wrap-up)
                 != 'Let me think step by
                     I have thought about this long enough; time to give my answer.'
  FAIL test_a_bad_alias_is_a_400
    AssertionError: 200 != 400 : ('thinking_token_budget', 1.5)
  ```
- **After:**
  ```text
  test_the_budget_alias_field_names ... ok
  test_the_request_s_own_budget_wins_over_the_aliases ... ok
  test_the_alias_field_order_wins ... ok
  test_a_bad_alias_is_a_400 ... ok
  Ran 4 tests in 2.250s — OK

  python3 -m unittest serve.test_server
  Ran 341 tests in 111.677s — OK
  ```
  Measured on this PC with the mock engine (serve's tests run without a GPU or downloads). No backend files touched, so no CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds; the alias lands before the existing, separately-tested budget path.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Additive serve-layer normalization; rolling back is a revert, and nothing downstream knows the budget came from an alias. Default path stays byte-identical: a request without any of the three aliases has `reasoning_budget_tokens` left untouched.

**Blast Radius:** small — requests carrying one of the alias fields now have it applied as the thinking budget (previously ignored), and an invalid alias value now 400s like `reasoning_budget_tokens` does (previously 200 and ignored).

pulls.title: [Engine] hip: STRATA_SELECT_GRID=2 - the selection scorer's CTA order swaps for L2 (bitwise identical)
pulls.author: vlupilin
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The WMMA scorer CTA order puts all key tiles of query-tile 0 first: each of 16 query-tiles re-reads the pooled key array from DRAM because L2 (8 MiB) cannot hold it. With `STRATA_SELECT_GRID=2` the grid dimensions swap so CTAs sharing a key tile run together and L2 holds it for all of them. Output is bitwise identical (only the scheduling order of independent CTAs moves).

## Approach

Template parameter `bool XQ` mapping blockIdx to query/block tiles; opt-in env `STRATA_SELECT_GRID=0|1|2` with adaptive threshold `STRATA_SELECT_GRID_MIN` (default 8192 blocks). Default 0 = unchanged. One file: `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` (+26/-4).

## Validation

**Passed:**

Kernel benchmark (both arms same session, 5 reps, v0.2.0-beta @ 4caf857c, gfx1151 Radeon 8060S Strix Halo, ROCm 10.1, Linux 7.0.0-38-generic):
```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/lib STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1 STRATA_SELECT_GRID=0 ./build-rocm101/qsa_select_bench 32768 256 5 32768
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/rocm/lib STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1 STRATA_SELECT_GRID=2 STRATA_SELECT_GRID_MIN=0 ./build-rocm101/qsa_select_bench 32768 256 5 32768
# (repeated for 131072, 262144, 524288)
```
| context | old order | swapped | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32768 | 0.818 ms | 0.756 ms | 1.08x |
| 131072 | 2.468 ms | 2.368 ms | 1.04x |
| 262144 | 8.429 ms | 7.831 ms | 1.08x |
| 524288 | 13.316 ms | 10.669 ms | 1.25x |

Engine (interleaved 2 rounds, grid measured alone):
```
# baseline: STRATA_SELECT_GRID=0, test: STRATA_SELECT_GRID=2
# bench.py --lens 131072,262144,524288 --prod-params --salt 150
```
| depth | mainline | +grid | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 131072 | 946.8 | 946.8 | 0.0% |
| 262144 | 1002.8 | 1014.1 | +1.1% |
| 524288 | 928.1 | 944.1 | +1.7% |

Bitwise identical ids: verified 256/256 at all depths (qsa_select_bench gate).

**Failed:** none.

**Not run:** CUDA (kernel is HIP-only); gfx12 (maintainer R9700 can verify); shallow-context regression check below 8192 blocks (the adaptive threshold prevents the swap there).

## Problem and result

The QSA selection scorer on gfx11/gfx12 (the WMMA path, `STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1`) computes 6 wmma products per block. With `STRATA_SELECT_SPLIT2=1` the three products that carry the lo piece are dropped (3 wmma instead of 6): the scorer runs 1.5-2.2x faster, rounding-level accuracy change (~1.5e-5, the class upstream accepts at 254/256).

Companion to the accepted wide top-k (#1749).

## Approach

Template parameter `bool S2` on `block_scores_wmma_kernel`; opt-in env. Default off: the 6-product kernel bits are unchanged. One file: `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` (+35/-14).

pulls.title: [Other] tests: three suite gaps a live PC showed (no engine, setup, serve, or docs change)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

On a live PC (Windows 11, RTX 4090, a Strata server serving on the default port 8080) three suite gaps made the tools tests fail for reasons unrelated to the code under test:

- `tools/test_iq_pack.py` died at import on a checkout without llama.cpp's gguf-py (`_paths.gguf_py()` exits hard there). After the rebase onto current main, upstream's new `HadamardTests`/`NativeExpertsV5Tests` classes hit `NameError: name 'iq_pack' is not defined` (18 errors).
- `tools/test_strata_mcp.py`: the discovery scans were answered by the live server on 8080, not by the tests' own servers.
- six `tools/test_conversation_cache_*.py` files fail when run from the repo root (`python -m unittest`), as the suite is run, because `tools/` is not on `sys.path`.

After: the iq_pack file imports without gguf-py (`iq_pack` needs numpy + `gguf_reader` only, so it is imported unguarded), the GGUF-fixture classes (Compatibility, Conversion, SplitArtifact, NativeExpertsV5) skip with a named reason, the MCP tests see only their own servers, and the cache tests run from the repo root. No engine, setup, serve, or docs change.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note.

### Approach

Guarded import + `setUpClass` skip in `test_iq_pack.py` (`split_model`'s `gate1` default moved to runtime so the module imports without gguf-py); `DEFAULT_PORT` patch in `test_strata_mcp.py`; `sys.path` insert in the six cache tests.

### Validation

Passed, rebased on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`), Windows 11, Python 3.15:

- `python -m unittest tools.test_iq_pack` and `python tools/test_iq_pack.py`: 3 ran / 4 skipped, exit 0 (both start forms; the 4 skips are the GGUF-fixture classes on a checkout without llama.cpp).
- `tools.test_strata_mcp`: OK, exit 0.
- `tools.test_conversation_cache_disabled` / `_growth` / `_isolation`: 14 tests OK, exit 0.

Not run: the full tools suite in CI; no engine, setup, serve, or docs code touched.

### Limits

The skips are conditional on gguf-py being absent; with llama.cpp cloned the classes run as before. No behavior change for any shipped code.

pulls.title: [GUI] web: a tool call no longer widens the page on phones (#2971)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
## What it changes

`serve/web/app.css`, three rules:

- `.view` gets `min-width: 0`. As a flex item of `main` it otherwise keeps `min-width: auto`, so its min-content width — raised by a long `nowrap` tool name — makes the whole panel, and the page, wider than the viewport.
- `.tool-call > summary` gets `overflow: hidden`.
- `.tool-call__name` gets `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, so the name shrinks and ellipsizes instead of forcing the row wider.

The preview already had the same treatment.

Layout only: no markup, JS or API change, and the desktop layout is unchanged.

## Validation

Environment: `main` @ `477ac13c`, headless Edge (puppeteer-core) on Windows 11.

pulls.title: gentoo-setup: setup.py builds the CUDA and HIP engines on Gentoo
pulls.author: arabek
pulls.body:
(portage ebuilds, gcc caps, ROCm in /usr)

What changes: setup.py learns the Gentoo paths for both engine builds; the Ubuntu/Debian, Windows and other-Linux flows keep their commands. What it leaves alone: the engine sources, the ready-made engines, and every default on non-Gentoo PCs except the cmake_build build line.

Detection: is_gentoo() is /etc/os-release ID=gentoo with emerge on PATH.

CUDA: dev-util/nvidia-cuda-toolkit's ebuilds cap nvcc's host gcc (GCC_MAX_VER: 12.9 -> 14, 13.4 -> 16); a newer system gcc breaks nvcc there. gentoo_gcc_env picks the newest installed gcc at or below the cap from gcc-config -l and applies that choice's gcc-config -E environment to this process only (PATH first, so gcc, g++ and nvcc's default --ccbin use it); the system's gcc-config pick is never changed and no sudo is used. The toolkit itself installs with sudo emerge dev-util/nvidia-cuda-toolkit.

HIP: portage's ROCm ebuilds install to /usr, so rocm_root's default sysroot is /usr on Gentoo (ROCM_PATH still wins) and hipBLAS is looked for in lib and lib64 (Gentoo keeps it in /usr/lib64); the amdgcn bitcode folder is also sought at root/lib/amdgcn/bitcode. When hipcc or hipBLAS are not installed yet, main() emerges GENTOO_ROCM_EBUILDS (hip, hipcc, rocm-core, rocm-device-libs, rocBLAS, hipBLAS, hipBLASLt; emerge pulls their dependencies).

HIP compiler for CMake: CMake refuses a compiler named hipcc (CMakeDetermineHIPCompiler stops on that name); the wheels' clang is AMD's patched build that takes gfx archs in CUDA mode, while upstream clang needs -x hip for a .cu TU and the same flag on a link line makes it read the .o files as source. hipcc's driver gets both right, so it is wrapped under another name: build-hip/hip-clang++, a one-line script that turns a link call that still carries .cu/.hip sources into a compile to /dev/null.

engine_archs / engine_runs_on: a HIP engine's BUILD.json archs are gfx names, not CUDA arches: engine_archs returns None for backend hip, and an installed engine with no CUDA archs now returns False (compile) instead of True, so a HIP engine no longer passes for a CUDA card's engine, or the other way round.

place_binary: Linux refuses to open a running binary for writing ("Text file busy", errno 26), which setup hit while the server was running the old engine. The new file is copied to <name>.new beside the target and renamed over it with os.replace: the rename unlinks the old file, which is allowed while it runs, and the running server keeps its old copy until it restarts. Used for the HIP engine, the CUDA engine and the image encoder, and for the ROCm runtime binaries placed beside the AMD engine.

fresh_cache_if: CMake re-runs a configure WITHOUT the command-line -Ds when it decides the cache must go (a compiler that changed between configures - Gentoo's hipcc for a folder first configured with clang++), which drops Strata's -DSTRATA_ENABLE_* flags and leaves the target unregistered. A cache whose stored values disagree with the requested -D definitions is removed before configuring, so the next configure is a real first one.

cmake_build: the build step calls ninja directly with -j at the full core count instead of cmake --build at half.

Checked: python -m py_compile setup.py; all tools/test_setup_*.py pass except two failures in test_setup_engine_hash.py that are unchanged from the two previous commits (pre-existing, untouched by this change). The Gentoo paths themselves were ~~not~~ run on Gentoo hardware.

Attributed-to: qwen3.8-flash-next-coder-iq1_m (using Strata) + opencode

pulls.author: gt50
pulls.body:
On v0.1.45 a Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Windows 11, ROCm 10.2.0a20260930) stalls in its first verify window when gfx1151's default switches are on. The engine prints `verify: an earlier window never finished on the GPU (#267)` and "the GPU rang 0", the watchdog restarts it after 60 s, and no token comes out. It happens with a stock config and with mine. The installed 0.1.40.2 engine, with the same switches and config, does not stall.

**Cause:** f629fb04 (#2234), its `qsa_select.cu` change. `block_scores_multi_kernel` is the kernel every decode window's QSA block scores run on. #2234 gave it a by-value `QsaScoreRows` argument (16 pointers and a count) and a per-query branch for the opt-in `STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS` path. Both apply with that switch off.

**Fix:** `block_scores_multi_body` is a template on `OWN`.
- The default kernel (`OWN` false) is the pre-#2234 kernel again, with no `QsaScoreRows` argument and no branch.
- `qsa_block_scores_rows` launches a new `block_scores_multi_rows_kernel` (`OWN` true).
- One file: `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, +33/−14.

### How it was found
All on that Radeon 8060S, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, `--spec 4 --mtp`, `--kv int8`. Each trial was a fresh start, then a 14-token request with `max_tokens` 8. No answer in 30 s counted as a stall; a normal answer takes 0.4-0.7 s.

- **The switches:** 26 trials with `STRATA_GFX1151_DEFAULTS=0` and subsets turned on. `STRATA_PLE_BATCH` is on in every set that stalled. It needs `STRATA_LFUSE` and `STRATA_TSUM` or `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT` beside it, and other switches change which set is enough. With the other 18 defaults on, `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0` stops the stall.
- **Not every start stalls:** one build stalled in 6 of 7 starts (c8265fce, the commit just before v0.1.45 on main). So each step below used 3 starts.
- **Commits:** a bisect from v0.1.40.2 (good) to v0.1.45 found the first bad main-line merge, e8b1edbc "perf-PR group batch". Its parent 5a6f4ed5 answered 3 of 3. Inside the merge, the commits from f629fb04 up to f755a06d do not build on HIP (`qsa_decode_attn.cu`; f755a06d fixes that). So each part was applied alone to the merge base 296b59d2:

| On 296b59d2 | Starts |
|---|---|
| a2de7446 (PleTable lock) | 3 of 3 answer |
| f629fb04 + 739bc948 + f755a06d | stall |
| only the `qsa_decode_attn` files (f755a06d's refactor) | 3 of 3 answer |
| only f629fb04's GDN change (`verify_kernels`) | 3 of 3 answer |
| **only f629fb04's `qsa_select.cu` / `.hpp` change** | **stall** |

The f-145-fix3 merge with #2622 answered 3 of 3, so the PLE gather change is not the cause. Several 0.1.45 merges do not build on Windows HIP without e6ad6c81's 4-line `hip_compat` fix, which these tests applied.

### Checked with this change
On v0.1.45 (477ac13c) plus this commit, on the same machine:

- **The stall trial:** 5 of 5 starts answer with all 19 gfx1151 defaults on.
- **The parity tests:** `batch_rows_parity` passes (it checks `qsa_block_scores_rows` at 1, 2, 4 and 8 rows against one call per row, bitwise). So do `qsa_parity`, `qsa_topk_parity`, `hip_native_qsa_score` and `verify_batch_parity`. `qsa_scores_gfx1100_parity` builds and skips itself, since it is gfx1100 only.
- **Answers:** three greedy answers (284-344 tokens) are byte-identical to v0.1.45 with `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0`.
- **Speed:** decode 34.9 / 48.9 / 40.3 tok/s, against 34.9 / 48.5 / 40.8 with the workaround.

### Not covered
- **Other backends:** not built for CUDA or SYCL. The code uses `if constexpr`, as other `.cu` files here already do.
- **The mechanism:** why the argument and branch hang the window only beside those switches is not explained here. The tests show this change caused it, and that taking it out of the default kernel stops it.
- **Multi-row speed:** the per-row path's speed with `--batch` and `STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS=1` was not measured. Only its parity test ran.
- **Unrelated test build:** a full `tools\hip\build_windows.bat tests` stops at `hc_persist_parity.cpp`. It uses POSIX `setenv`/`unsetenv`, which this change does not touch.
