pulls.title: bench: 4x Tesla V100-SXM2 reports for 0.1.45 (IQ3_S, 262144): prompt reading unchanged, the 6-7% ru gap is measurement order, full test suite
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
## What this is

Three community benchmark reports from one update cycle on a machine that is not in the existing set: **4x NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB (sm_70) in a Minisforum MS-01**, `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s`, context 262144, comparing **0.1.45 with 0.1.44.1** with whole trees swapped in one session.

- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-4x-tesla-v100-iq3-s-262k-code/` — code-style prompts, 4K…260K.
- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-4x-tesla-v100-iq3-s-262k-ru/` — Russian-style prompts, same lengths, plus the reversed-order control.
- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-4x-tesla-v100-test-suite/` — the Python suite (118 modules, 1703 cases) and what each failure actually is.

Each folder carries `env.json`, `config.json`, `runs.json`, the same-binary control run, the 0.1.44.1 baseline, needle recall files, 2-second VRAM/RAM samples and the driver scripts.

Related: the same 0.1.45 cycle on RTX 4090 is in #3109 (branch `bench/2026-10-18-rtx4090-0145`); the previous cycle on this V100 box, 0.1.44.1 vs 0.1.43, is #2525; the NVLink/interconnect dossier for the same machine is #2905.

## The machine

A **Minisforum MS-01** mini-workstation (DMI: `Micro Computer (HK) Tech Limited`, product `Venus Series`, board `AHWSA`, BIOS `AHWSA.1.22` of 2024-03-12, chassis type 3, UEFI) — i9-13900H (20 logical CPUs, one NUMA node), 96 GB DDR5 (`MemTotal` 91.7 GiB usable), one NVMe drive SOLIDIGM `SSDPFKKW020X7` (2.05 TB, ext4 root, holds the model files), 2x Intel X710 10GbE SFP+ plus I226-V/I226-LM, Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, driver 580.178.04. No root/sudo on this box.

The GPUs are not PCIe cards: four **Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB** SXM2 modules (`GV100GL [10de:1db1]`, compute 7.0, 16384 MiB, 300.00 W limit, max clocks 1530/877 MHz, persistence enabled; serials `1323920036046`, `0324218160473`, `0323517036572`, `1422119022723`) on a third-party 4-GPU SXM2 carrier board, behind a **PLX/Broadcom PEX 8748** Gen3 switch at `0000:01:00.0`, with the cards at `03:00.0`..`06:00.0`. The host side of that switch is the CPU root port `0000:00:01.0`, and it trains as **x8 at 8.0 GT/s** (`current_link_width = max_link_width = 8`); every card also links at x8 / 8.0 GT/s. Four x8 downlinks share one x8 uplink — 4:1 oversubscription, ~7.9 GB/s per direction; measured earlier on this machine (#2905): 6.29 GB/s host→device for one card alone, 1.56 GB/s per card when all four stream. NVLink is live between every pair (`nvidia-smi topo -m` gives `NV2`; 6 links per card at 25.781 GB/s). The whole probe is reproducible with `scripts/host-probe-185.sh`, and its raw output is committed as `host-provenance.txt`.

This shape of the machine matters for the numbers: a layer-split model with most experts resident is what this box is good at, and its absolute tok/s are not comparable with a desktop card on a full x16. RAM was never a limit — the cycle peaked at 11.0 GiB of 91.7 GiB; VRAM is the limit (`CUDA3` reaches 16144 of 16384 MiB).

## Results

**Prompt reading on Volta is unchanged.** 4K…260K, code-style: −0.10…−0.39% (one case +0.14%), while the same 0.1.45 binary re-measured moved −0.17…+0.24% — every delta sits inside the control band. The two longest cases were repeated 3+3 times per version: 237483 tokens in 96.9–97.5 s and 260331 in 107.0–107.5 s in both versions. Recall: 6/6 needles at 32K and 128K in both versions, 3/3 at 249262 tokens in both.

**The 6–7% "regression" in the Russian-style run is an artifact of measurement order.** In the first ordering 0.1.44.1 (measured second) was 6.5–7.1% faster at ≥127K tokens. Both orders were then measured, which gives a 2×2 (version × seat in the session):

| actual prompt tokens | 0.1.45, first seat | 0.1.45, second seat | 0.1.44.1, first seat | 0.1.44.1, second seat |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4028 | 882.9 | 883.9 | 876.2 | 893.2 |
| 31828 | 1907.3 | 1915.4 | 1915.2 | 1986.2 |
| 64628 | 2249.2 | 2261.2 | 2255.8 | 2369.2 |
| 127228 | 2393.3 | 2390.6 | 2387.1 | 2573.1 |
| 188828 | 2433.2 | 2432.8 | 2430.1 | 2619.1 |
| 203528 | 2450.0 | 2444.6 | 2444.1 | 2630.1 |

0.1.45 is seat-independent (0.02–0.5% spread); 0.1.44.1 gains 1.9–7.8% purely by running after another engine of the same model and config. Same-seat deltas: |Δ| ≤ 0.8%. Suggested reading for anyone benchmarking long contexts on this class of machine: absolute numbers drift by up to 8% between sessions of the *same* build, so only order-reversed or interleaved A/B is trustworthy.

**Test suite: 1703 tests, 13 failures + 1 error, none from 0.1.45.** `serve.*` (836 tests) passed completely with the live production server. All failures come from `tools.test_strata_mcp` (4+1), `tools.test_setup_golden` (8) and `tools.test_setup_engine_hash` (2); the identical 14 reproduce in 0.1.44.1 with its own engine and its own venv, and the 5 `test_strata_mcp` ones disappear when this machine's production server is stopped (port 8080 is a permanent production service here).

## Two concrete things for the project

1. **`tools.test_setup_golden` cannot pass on Linux** — it compares `vision.exe` against `<T>/engine/strata-vision.exe`, while `setup` writes `strata-vision`. `normalize()` substitutes only `setup.EXE` via the `<EXE>` placeholder, not `setup.VEXE`. All 8 failing subtests in both versions start from this; in 0.1.44.1 the maxDiff output shows it as the only differing value. Fix: normalize `VEXE` the same way, or record `<VEXE>` in the fixture.
2. **0.1.45 introduces an unmocked `os.cpu_count()` dependency in setup** — 3 of the 8 golden subtests (profiles 47GB-2x16GB and 96GB-1x16GB) now get `vision.threads: 10` on a 20-logical-CPU host where the fixture expects 6 (`setup.py:5906`, `max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 8) // 2)`; 0.1.44.1 does not take this path under the same mocks). The golden profiles mock RAM and GPU cards but not the CPU count. Fix: mock `os.cpu_count()` per profile, or normalize the value.

## Notes on comparability

- Both engines are built from source on this machine for `sm_70` (`STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`) with a private CUDA 12.8 (nvcc 12.8.93) and private gcc-14 — the Linux release archive carries no engine binary, so a local build is the only path, and both versions were built identically. `BUILD.json` records this.
- Auto prompt chunk is 8192 tokens with a 96-slot ring in **both** versions, and the two run-config files (one per tree) are byte-identical, so the configuration is the same. `engine-start-lines-comparison.txt` in the code report collects the start-up self-description per session and per version: `prompt chunk auto: 8192 tokens, a 96-slot ring` and `adaptive overlap: off: not on a layer split` in every session of both versions. What does differ is the reported resident share (97% in every 0.1.45 session here, 96-99% across 0.1.44.1 sessions): it follows the memory free at the moment of start, so it is a start condition, not a version difference. That file also states a caveat: the two 0.1.44.1 sessions of this cycle left no start-up block in the shared log, so the 0.1.44.1 column there includes its sessions of 2026-10-14..17.
- `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE` is not active on sm_70 (`per_dev[]` matches sm_61/sm_86 only), so the RTX 4090 finding about it does not transfer here. The other new defaults were checked against this config: `STRATA_ADAPT_EVICT_SYNC` (no adaptive copy tier here), `STRATA_DF_QB_Q4` (q4_0 KV only), `STRATA_PIPED_*` (opt-in), `STRATA_SIMT2_TILE` (needs `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT`), `STRATA_RDNA2_SGEMM` (AMD).
- No DCGM on this machine, so there is no colouring or kernel-level profiling here. Generation columns are reported but not used for conclusions (answer lengths differ between versions). No other agent's traffic touched this server during the measurements — the agent running the cycle is served by a different box.
- The scripts are published with English comments and English log strings; every command in them is what was actually run. Text that is measurement data stays as it was sent to the model: the Russian workload paragraph, the `[метка N]` marker inside every prompt, and the Russian verification query in the swap scripts (each with an English gloss in a comment). `reverse2-run.log` keeps the Russian stage markers the machine wrote at the time.

pulls.title: report: RX 6700 XT (gfx1031 running as gfx1030) - built-in suite in two arms; STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1 reads prompts 1.76x-1.99x faster, decode unchanged
pulls.author: ljmbot
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
A community report for the card the maintainers do not have: RX 6700 XT, 12,272 MiB, `gfx1031`, run as `gfx1030`
under `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0`, which is the only way long prompts run on ROCm 7.1.1 at all (rocBLAS ships
31 `gfx1030` library files and 0 `gfx1031` ones - see the paired fix PR #3145). Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, 65,536-token context, KV
int8, one parallel slot, expert cache 2,645 slots / 5.07 GiB of VRAM.

`tools/strata_bench.py --long` (chat, 4K, 16K, agent session, 32K), three runs per test, run twice - the default
prompt GEMMs and `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` - one engine session per arm, model reloaded from cold between arms,
nothing else changed:

| prompt | default | with `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,019 tokens | 339.2 (294.1-339.5) tok/s | 595.9 (448.2-596.1) | 1.76x |
| 16,058 | 352.5 (343.2-355.7) | 692.9 (674.9-714.0) | 1.97x |
| 32,049 | 356.2 (353.8-357.4) | 707.5 (701.7-711.1) | 1.99x |

TTFT 11.90 / 45.61 / 90.05 s becoming 6.80 / 23.23 / 45.39 s. Decode is not touched: chat decode 21.7 (20.2-26.8)
against 21.0 (19.7-24.9) tok/s over 9 runs each, agent-turn decode 23.6 against 22.3. The agent session caches the
same in both arms (68.8% of the follow-up-turn tokens reused, about 2 tokens of earlier turns read again), so the
difference is the reading: turn TTFT 9.59 -> 6.16 s, and the turns that re-read about 2,900 uncached tokens ran at
207-263 against 519-552 tok/s. The whole suite took 731 s and 464 s.

## What changed
- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-rx-6700-xt/` - README.md (hardware, config, both arms, every table, correctness
  and what was not tested), METHODS.md (how the arms were separated, the suite command, the probe build line,
  sanitizing, what was not measured), `results-default.json` and `results-f16.json` (the tool's own per-request
  data, field for field), `engine-log-default.txt` and `engine-log-f16.txt` (each arm's startup lines: the arch the
  card reported, the GEMM route the engine took, the cache sizes), and `scripts/` with the two extra measurements -
  `rocblas_gemm_ex` at the prompt shapes (7.0 TFLOPS f16 in / f32 out, 21.3 f16 in / f16 out, 6.6 bf16, 11.8 f32,
  each checked against a CPU reference) and a matched 11,103-token prompt read in the same session (34.4 s and 33.9 s
  against 17.9 s, 1.90x).
- `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`: one bullet in the report list, in date order.
- `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`: one row in the index table, PR column "PR pending".

## Extra Notes
The README's arch links point at `docs/AMD_GFX1031.md`, which is in the paired fix PR #3145; the link 404s on `main` until
that one merges.

This is a speed run, not a parity run: every arm answered coherently (the chat questions, the agent turns against a
project file, the 11,103-token summary), and there is no needle test, no golden-answer parity and no HumanEval here.
The FP16 route is not bit-identical to the default (an FP16 rounding of the prompt GEMMs, which the engine says on
its startup line), so answers can differ slightly on borderline prompts.

Not tested: the 4K / 32K token-id parity between the two arms, Windows, TheRock's venv ROCm, a layer split with a
6700 XT in it, the vision encoder (`--vision` off in this config), concurrency (`--seqs 1`, no `--batch`), a long
soak, other quantisations than Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, the other `gfx1031` cards (6750 XT, 6800M), ROCm older than 7.1.1,
PCIe width (no passwordless sudo for `lspci -vv`), RAM speed, temperatures and clocks under load. One machine, one
engine session per arm, one order (default first, FP16 second), so drift between sessions is not separated out; the
chat control arm and the identical cache hit rates argue against a large drift. The engine is a source build for
`gfx1030;gfx1031` (`engine/BUILD.json`), not a release binary. The model's GGUF sits on a FUSE-mounted SATA SSD
(`fuseblk`), not compared against a native mount.

pulls.title: fix(HIP): pair gfx1031 with gfx1030 and run it as 10.3.0 - ROCm 7.1.1's rocBLAS ships no gfx1031 kernels
pulls.author: ljmbot
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
On an RX 6700 XT (`gfx1031`) the engine did not compile, and once it compiles it loads, answers a 46-token prompt at
20-27 tok/s, and dies on the first prompt of about 12K tokens. The death message looks like an out-of-memory:

```
rocBLAS error: Cannot read /opt/rocm/lib/rocblas/library/TensileLibrary.dat: No such file or directory for GPU arch : gfx1031
```

It is not memory: 62.7 GiB RAM, 12,272 MiB VRAM, 4.5 GiB VRAM free after the load. The prompt path is the only path
that calls rocBLAS (decode streams experts from host RAM and uses the CPU gemv), and ROCm 7.1.1's rocBLAS ships 31
`gfx1030` library files and 0 `gfx1031` ones (`ls /opt/rocm/lib/rocblas/library | grep -c gfx1031` is 0). So the
engine built `gfx1030;gfx1031` fixes the kernels and leaves the library unfixable, and
`HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0` is what makes rocBLAS find that library at runtime. This PR makes setup.py do both,
adds a no-GPU test for it, fixes the compile, and documents it. No new default; a card whose arch has a Tensile
library gets exactly what it got before.

Measured on: RX 6700 XT (12,272 MiB), Xeon E5-1620 v3, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-147, ROCm 7.1.1 in
/opt/rocm, rocBLAS 5.1.1, Strata 0.1.45 at commit `477ac13c`, Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, 65,536-token context, KV int8,
`--expert-cache auto`, `--spec 4`, engine built from source on this machine.

## What changed
- `setup.py` (43 added, 4 changed): `HIP_ROCBLAS_SIBLINGS = {"gfx1031": "gfx1030"}` and
  `HIP_ROCBLAS_AS = {"gfx1031": "10.3.0"}` next to `AMD_ARCHS`, with the reason and these numbers in the comment
  above them. `HIP_ARCH` falls back to the sibling when the card's own arch has no Tensile library, so a source build
  gets the gfx1030 kernels, and the run config's `env` gets `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0`, which is what makes
  rocBLAS find that library at runtime. The env entry only appears for a card whose arch has no library. `HIP_ARCH`
  and the arch list are the two points where a fat build becomes necessary; the prebuilt `strata-win-hip.zip` has the
  same hole, so the release binary alone does not cover the card.
- `tools/test_setup_gfx1031.py` (new, 77 lines): a 6700 XT gets `["gfx1030", "gfx1031"]`, the override in the config
  and in the printed export line; a 9070 XT is untouched; a 9070 XT keeps `12.0.0`. Runs without a GPU and without
  downloads.
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu` (4 added, 2 changed): `__shared__ alignas(16) int4 s_u[...]` in
  `expdec_gu_kernel` (1858) and `expdec_down_kernel` (2045) does not compile under HIP clang - "'alignas' attribute
  cannot be applied to types", the #778 pattern - so the engine did not build on this machine. The file already
  carries the answer for `uint32_t` shared arrays: `STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_U32` puts `__attribute__((aligned(16)))`
  after the declarator under `__HIPCC__` and keeps `alignas` elsewhere. This adds the same macro for `int4`
  (`STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_I4`) and uses it at those two sites. Layout identical, and nvcc accepts the CUDA form,
  which is why CUDA builds never see this.
- `docs/AMD_GFX1031.md` (new, 88 lines): the symptom, the two changes, the probe numbers, what to copy for this card,
  and the `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16` measurement. `docs/AMD_HIP.md` (9 added, 1 changed): a line pointing at it for
  cards whose arch ships no rocBLAS kernels.

How I checked:
- `python3 tools/test_setup_gfx1031.py` -> `Ran 8 tests ... OK`; `tools/test_setup_choices.py` -> `Ran 47 tests ...
  OK`; `tools/test_setup_amd.py` -> `Ran 40 tests ... OK`. No GPU, no downloads.
- the engine built from source here: `engine/BUILD.json` `"archs": ["gfx1030", "gfx1031"]`, `engine/strata`
  53,696,584 bytes (53.7 MB) against 32.5 MB for one arch, 275 s to build on this 8-thread CPU, and no run-time cost.
- the built-in suite in two arms (`tools/strata_bench.py --long`, three runs per test, in the paired report PR
  #3146): prompt 339.2 (294.1-339.5) / 352.5 / 356.2 tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K becoming 595.9 / 692.9 / 707.5 with
  `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` (1.76x / 1.97x / 1.99x), TTFT 11.90 / 45.61 / 90.05 s becoming 6.80 / 23.23 / 45.39 s,
  chat decode 21.7 -> 21.0 tok/s over 9 runs each (decode does not use these GEMMs).
- the same 11,103-token prompt in one server session: 33.9 s / 32.8 s / 34.4 s reading (327.6 / 338.1 / 322.4 tok/s)
  on the default route and 17.9 s (620.9 tok/s, 1.90x) with the switch; a 13,023-token prompt 38.6 s (337.6 tok/s);
  the second copy of the 11,103-token prompt reuses 11,098 of 11,103 tokens in 102 ms.
- `scripts/rocblas_gemm_probe.cpp` (in the report PR) at `N = 10240 x T = 1024 x K = 2560`, each type checked against
  a CPU reference: 7.0 TFLOPS f16 in / f32 out (the default route), 21.3 f16 in / f16 out, 6.6 bf16, 11.8 f32.
- the two halves are both needed: the override on a `gfx1031`-only binary SEGFAULTS (HIP then looks for gfx1030 code
  objects) and the fat binary alone leaves rocBLAS asking for gfx1031. A `ROCBLAS_TENSILE_LIBPATH` directory of
  symlinks renaming the gfx1030 files to gfx1031 is not a fix - the abort stops and every `rocblas_gemm_ex` returns
  status 6 (internal_error) and writes nothing.

## Extra Notes
What this leaves alone: no new default and no behaviour change for a card whose arch has a Tensile library (gfx1151,
gfx1201, gfx942, RDNA2, RDNA1 - gfx1151 already pairs with gfx1151, so it takes the same code path and gets the same
arch back); the CUDA path is untouched (the non-`__HIPCC__` branch of the new macro is the CUDA form, as it was); the
`iq_kernels.cu` change is a compile fix with identical layout, not a new code path; no other engine source is touched.

What is not measured here: there is no built-in-suite arm for a `gfx1031`-only build - that build dies on the first
long prompt, so the only before/after for the arch change and the override is the 11,103-token pair above and the
probe. Also not tested: 4K / 32K token-id parity between the two GEMM routes, the other `gfx1031` cards (6750 XT,
6800M), Windows, TheRock's venv ROCm, a layer split with a 6700 XT in it, ROCm older than 7.1.1, PCIe width, RAM
speed, temperatures.

pulls.title: Dashboard: show the loaded model in the top bar and on the Model state card
pulls.author: vrami-dev
pulls.body:
Screenshots of the Monitor never say which model is running. This shows it in the top bar (every tab) and next to the
Model state title:

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next · Swift 1.5 IQ3_S`

## Changes (26 lines, opt-in)

- **`serve/server.py`:** an optional config key `"display_name"`. `/metrics` reports `engine.display_name` and
  `engine.mode`, a free-form note an engine adapter can set on the Service (`svc.mode_note`, `None` here); `/health`
  reports `display_name`. Nothing changes when neither is set: the label then shows the model id.
- **`serve/web/`:** `renderModelLabel()` puts `<display_name or model id> · <mode>` in the header and on the Model state
  card (muted text, ellipsized in the header).

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 · dsx 2-bit · light routing (0.25 / 0.15)`. Here it is only the hook.

pulls.title: [GUI] web: retry a failed GET /mcp instead of hiding the MCP tools for the session (#3113)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
Issue: #3113 (the web-app half; #3135 fixed the server half)

## Summary

`loadMcp()` returned on `!r.ok` and on a fetch exception, and scheduled a retry only while a server's status was
literally `starting`. One failed `GET /mcp` - a 401 before the API key was entered, a server restart, a proxy hiccup
- disabled the MCP tools for the life of the tab: the card was hidden, `mcpInfo.tools` stayed 0, and every chat
request left `strata_mcp` off. That is the second way #3113's "the backend loaded 14 tools, the page does not use
them" can happen.

## What changed

- `serve/web/app.js`
  - A failed status fetch (network error, 5xx, 401, or a body that stops arriving) is retried after 3, 6, 12 and then
    every 30 seconds; a success resets the backoff.
  - A 404 (an older server without `/mcp`) is not retried, and it clears a stale tool list.
  - The Monitor's MCP card says why the status is missing ("MCP status needs the API key (About > Settings)", "the
    server is unreachable; retrying") instead of silently disappearing. A list from the last successful fetch stays
    visible and is labelled "last known state shown".
  - Entering or changing the API key asks again immediately instead of waiting out the backoff; turning the MCP
    toggle on does the same when no tools are known.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: one sentence on the retry schedule.
- `serve/test_web_mcp_retry.py`: a node test pins the schedule, the 404 stop, the 401 message, the success reset and
  the `starting` poll (skipped without node, like `test_web_sampling`).

## Validation

- `node --check serve/web/app.js` - syntax OK.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_web_mcp_retry serve.test_web_sampling` - **5 tests, OK**.
- **Manual, in the browser**, against a real `python -m serve.server --engine mock --port 8096 --api-key k
  --mcp-config ...` and the Streamable HTTP fake MCP server:
  - before the key: the Monitor card shows **"MCP status needs the API key (About > Settings)"**;
  - after entering the key in About > Settings: **"6 tools · 1 of 1 servers connected"** with the fake server's
    tools, without a reload.
- Regression: with `serve/web/app.js` reverted (the test kept), the node test fails (`mcpError is not defined`);
  with the change it passes.
- The full `serve` suite: **849 tests; the only error is `test_winjob.TestWinJob`** (a Windows `tasklist` call
  returning `None` here), the same one as on unmodified `main` (848 tests). `test_keepawake` is timing-flaky under
  the full run and passes alone; neither is related to this change.

## What I left alone

- The hard-coded 10 s MCP start wait is a separate change.
- A cut-off HTTP transport answer is PR #3139.
- The retry stops at a 404 on purpose: an older server has no `/mcp`, and retrying forever would only fill the
  console.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve/mcp: a cut-off HTTP answer is an error, not a TypeError on the waiting side
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
Issue: none; found in the gap analysis, related to the HTTP-bridge scenario in #3113

## Summary

`HttpTransport._post` caught `urllib.error.HTTPError`, `OSError`, `ValueError` and `McpError`, but not
`http.client.IncompleteRead` (an `HTTPException`). A Streamable HTTP MCP server that closes in the middle of its body
left the slot with `msg = None` and `error = None`; `_wait` then evaluated `"error" in None` and raised a `TypeError`.

Two user-visible consequences:

- **At startup** `McpServer._start` catches only `McpError`, so the `TypeError` escaped and the server stayed on
  `starting` forever - no `Failed` badge, no reason, and its tools simply missing. That is indistinguishable from a
  server that is still loading.
- **During a tool call** the `TypeError` escaped `McpHub.call`, whose contract is "only `McpCancelled` is raised";
  the chat ended without the `error: ...` result the model should have read.

## What changed

- `serve/mcp.py`
  - `http.client.IncompleteRead` becomes `McpError("the server's answer was cut off: ...")`.
  - Any other `http.client.HTTPException` becomes a failed-answer `McpError` instead of escaping the same way.
  - `_wait` refuses a slot that has neither a message nor an error with a clear `McpError` - the `TypeError` cannot
    come back through a future transport path either.
- `serve/mcp_fake_server.py`: `http_server(port, truncate=...)` and `--truncate METHOD` answer that method with a
  `Content-Length` longer than the body, then close. This is the deterministic reproduction of the bug.
- `serve/test_mcp.py`: two new tests (below).
- `docs/DETAILS.md` and the module docstring list "a cut-off HTTP answer" among the cases that become an `error: ...`
  result.

## Validation

`python -m unittest serve.test_mcp` - **27 tests, OK**, two of them new:

| test | result |
| --- | --- |
| truncated `initialize` | server status `failed`, error says "cut off", no tools |
| truncated `tools/list` | server status `failed`, error says "cut off", no tools |
| truncated `tools/call` after a good start | `hub.call` returns `ok=False` with `error: ... cut off`, no `TypeError` |

**Regression proof:** with `serve/mcp.py` reverted (the tests and the fake server kept), the two new tests fail:
`AssertionError: 'starting' != 'failed'` and a `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable` - 2 failures,
1 error. With the fix: 2 passed.

The full `serve` suite: **850 tests; the only error is `test_winjob.TestWinJob`** (a Windows `tasklist` call returning
`None` here), the same one as on unmodified `main` (848 tests). `test_keepawake` is timing-flaky under the full run
and passes alone; neither is related to this change. No new skips.

## What I left alone

- A cut-off answer does **not** mark the transport broken. One truncated response can be a proxy hiccup, and the next
  call may still work; a dead server already fails with the connection error. A 404 with a session id still marks it
  broken, as before.
- The web app's missing `GET /mcp` retry and the 10 s start wait are the other two paths in the same family; they are
  separate PRs.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: read llama.cpp's n_predict, including the prompt-only 0 (#2980)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
Issue: #2980

## Summary

`/v1/chat/completions` read only `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`. llama.cpp's web UI sends a follow-up with
`n_predict: 0` after every reply to evaluate the prompt into the conversation cache; Strata treated 0 as "the rest of
the context" and generated a second full answer (~20k tokens, 4-5 minutes of GPU on the reporter's R9700). Because
Strata serves one request at a time, every other client waited behind it, and the next user message re-read the whole
conversation because the prompt-only call never completed. llama.cpp's server README defines the field this way:
"When 0, no tokens will be generated but the prompt is evaluated into the cache."

## What changed

`n_predict` is honoured on `/v1/chat/completions` when the request has neither `max_tokens` nor
`max_completion_tokens`:

- **`0`** evaluates the prompt through the normal generation path and generates nothing. The answer is empty with
  `finish_reason: "length"` - the shape llama.cpp returns for this - and `usage.completion_tokens` is 0. Streaming
  and non-streaming.
- **`N > 0`** is the output cap.
- **`-1`** (or absent) leaves the rest of the context, as before.

An OpenAI `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` in the same request wins over `n_predict`, so an existing client
keeps exactly the behaviour it had. A non-integer `n_predict` (`"0"`, `true`, `1.5`) is a 400 before inference.

One engine note: `GEN` needs `max_new >= 1`, so the prompt-only call samples and drops one token. The prompt is read
through the normal generation path, which is what the client's follow-up wanted. The engine's own totals count that
one token; the API response reports 0 completion tokens, matching llama.cpp.

`docs/DETAILS.md` has one bullet under the API section.

## Validation

`python -m unittest serve.test_n_predict` - 6 tests, OK:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `n_predict: 0` | 0 completion tokens, `finish_reason: "length"`, empty content, the prompt reached the engine |
| `n_predict: 0`, `stream: true` | role chunk, final chunk with `length` and usage 0, `[DONE]`, no content |
| `n_predict: 3` | 3 completion tokens, `length` |
| `max_tokens: 2` + `n_predict: 7` | 2 completion tokens (the OpenAI field wins) |
| `n_predict: -1` | a full answer, `finish_reason: "stop"` |
| `"0"` / `true` / `1.5` / `[0]` | 400, the engine is never reached |

The full `serve` suite: **854 tests; the only error is `test_winjob.TestWinJob`** (a Windows `tasklist` call returning
`None` here), the same one as on unmodified `main` (848 tests). `test_keepawake` is timing-flaky under the full run
and passes alone; neither is related to this change. No new skips.

## What I left alone

- `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`. The report is llama.cpp's chat client, Anthropic requires `max_tokens`, and the
  Responses API has `max_output_tokens`.
- The engine protocol. A true `GEN 0` that samples nothing would be a C++ change; this stays a server-side fix with
  one sampled token.
- The `n_predict` field in `/props` was already reported; it is unchanged.

pulls.author: WillkTech
pulls.body:
mac: setup offers Swift 1.5 (--family swift) at IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS and IQ3_S

The Mac's size table is keyed by size with the family as an attribute, and
Swift's three sizes share names with the original's, so the family is resolved
before the size. model_shard_names takes the family instead of hardcoding qwen,
and model_shard1_gb prices a Swift pack for the resident-versus-streaming
decision.

Swift's shards cut through layers, so it is repacked into one file for the GPU
like Unsloth's, and its file names carry the abliterated segment the Hub uses.
Q2_0 stays refused for Swift: the pack tool cannot prepare it yet (#171).

CONTEXTS extended to 262,144 and 524,288; Swift's projector pinned by SHA-256.

Left alone: setup.py, the engine, the kernels, the CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds.
The default qwen and unsloth menus, the recommended sizes and the engine
arguments are unchanged; Swift is reachable only by asking for it.

Checked on an M5 Max, 128 GB: setup --family swift --model IQ3_S --no-start
writes the config this Mac already runs; tools.test_setup_mac 25/25,
test_setup_menu 24/24, test_setup_rope 19/19. Decode and prompt speed for
Swift on a Mac are not measured yet, and the docs say so.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: a bare MCP tool name runs the one tool that offers it, and an unoffered name becomes an error (#3113)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
Issue: #3113 (duplicate #3112; the second half of #3075)

## Summary

The MCP servers load, the server window lists their tools, and the chat still never runs one. The reproduced cause:
the model writes the tool's **bare** name (`list_directory`), while Strata offers the namespaced route
(`filesystem__list_directory`). `run_with_mcp` treated every name that is not in `mcp_names` as one of the request's
own tools, returned it as an OpenAI `tool_calls` delta - and the web chat has no handler for `tool_calls`. Nothing
ran, and nothing was shown.

Against the real `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`, with the 14 tools in the prompt:

| the model wrote | what happened |
| --- | --- |
| `<function=list_directory>` | no `strata_mcp` events, a client `tool_calls` delta named `list_directory`, nothing ran |
| `<function=filesystem__list_directory>` | `start` / `call` / `result`, the tool ran |

That is the "backend loaded 14 tools, the Web UI never uses them" report in #3113.

## What changed

- `run_with_mcp` now takes the request's own tool names (`own_names`). A call to one of those goes back to the
  client exactly as before - the request's tools still win a name clash.
- A call with a name the request did not declare is resolved against the MCP tools this request offered: if exactly
  one offered tool has that bare name, it runs under its namespaced route.
- If two servers offer the name, or no offered tool has it, the model gets an `error:` result naming the full
  `<server>__<tool>` routes, so it can correct itself; the chat page shows the block. Before, the call disappeared.
- The `tool_start`/`tool_args`/`tool_call` events of an MCP call are still kept off the client stream, and the
  continuation prompt names the route that actually ran, so the call and its result agree.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: one bullet under "Tools from MCP servers".

Only requests with `"strata_mcp": true` (the chat page's opt-in) take this path. The default API path is unchanged:
a request that declares no MCP opt-in still returns tool calls to its client exactly as before.

## Validation

`python -m unittest serve.test_mcp` - **29 tests, OK**, four of them new:

- a bare `echo` runs `fake__echo`, with `start`/`call`/`result`, no client tool call, and the result in the next
  prompt;
- an unoffered `nope` becomes an `error:` result naming `fake__echo`, and the model gets a second round;
- a bare `echo` offered by two servers is an error naming both routes (no guessing);
- a request that declares its own `echo` keeps it: the client answers, not the MCP server.

The full `serve` suite: **852 tests; the only error is `test_winjob.TestWinJob`** (a Windows `tasklist` call
returning `None` here), the same one as on unmodified `main` (848 tests). `test_keepawake` is timing-flaky under the
full run and passes alone; neither is related to this change. No new skips.

## What I left alone

Three neighbouring MCP failure modes are real and worth their own PRs, but are not this change:

- `serve/web/app.js:407-417`: one failed `GET /mcp` disables MCP tools for the life of the tab (no retry unless a
  server is literally `starting`). This can produce the same symptom as #3113.
- `serve/server.py`: the hard-coded `svc.mcp.wait(10)` in `_openai` omits a still-starting server from the first chat.
- `serve/mcp.py` `HttpTransport._post`: `http.client.IncompleteRead` is not caught, so a truncated HTTP answer can
  leave the server on "Starting" instead of "Failed".

Images returned by MCP tools (#2130) and the 10 s start wait are untouched as well.

pulls.title: Bound Qwen3.6 Windows CUDA placement by dedicated VRAM headroom
pulls.author: kbc20f11
pulls.body:
Qwen3.6 currently uses `cudaMemGetInfo` directly when sizing prompt chunks, admitting session caches and placing routed Experts. Under Windows/WDDM, the reported allocation budget can exceed the dedicated VRAM available on the adapter, so an automatic configuration can put Experts in CUDA allocations that require OS paging instead of the intended CPU/GPU hybrid placement.

An instrumented process using the same Qwen3.6 placement logic reported CUDA free memory of **12.85 GiB** while its simultaneous NVML reading showed only **0.91 GiB** of dedicated VRAM free. This was on an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF 24 GB with another process holding a touched 16 GiB allocation. The counters have different meanings; this change does not treat the CUDA API itself as defective.

The Windows CUDA path now bounds each startup free-memory estimate by `min(CUDA free, NVML dedicated free)`. NVML is loaded dynamically from System32 and the active adapter is selected by its CUDA PCI bus address, avoiding assumptions about CUDA/NVML device numbering. Missing NVML, failed queries and inconsistent counters fall back to the previous CUDA estimate. `STRATA_Q36_PLACE_DEBUG` prints the two readings and the selected value. Linux/HIP retain their existing query behavior.

The existing Expert placement algorithm, packed-weight release, MTP-only CPU placement, 768 MiB default reserve and conditional 256 MiB near-fit reserve remain unchanged. This is a startup budget correction; it cannot guarantee future residency or reserve VRAM against other applications.

Related: #1911 addresses the same Windows memory-accounting problem in the common Expert-cache path. This change covers the separate Qwen3.6 path, which that PR does not modify.

Draft status: the Windows CUDA build and the checks below passed. Other GPU backends have not been compiled, and a successful upstream real-model run remains outstanding because the installed mixed-quant GGUF is rejected by upstream before these queries. This is not ready for a final merge decision on the evidence available here.

Validation:

- Built the actual `strata-q36` target successfully with CUDA 13.2, sm120, portable AVX2 and Release configuration on Windows.
- Passed 42 host cases using the actual helper extracted from this source: clamp and zero-free handling, active-device PCI selection, driver/query failures and invalid counters, CUDA error preservation, and unchanged Linux/HIP preprocessor paths. These are deterministic host mocks, not actual Linux/HIP hardware tests.
- Attempted a bounded upstream native model probe with the installed Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS file, context 8192, chunk 512, MTP 0, no warmup and 16 GiB external pressure. Upstream rejected the file's existing mixed IQ2_S/IQ3_S Expert format during loading, before reaching the changed budget queries. **No successful upstream real-model generation or speed result is claimed.**
- Compiled and exercised the identical helper in TinyStrata with the installed Unsloth model. With a separate touched 16 GiB allocation on the 24 GB GPU, the previous CUDA-only policy placed all 10,496 routed Expert slots (11.40 GiB) on the GPU. The corrected automatic policy used 451 slots (501 MiB) in a diagnostic run and processed the remainder through the CPU pool.
- Two further TinyStrata runs retained GPU Vision at 4,096 image tokens, MTP 3 and production sampling defaults. Automatic selection kept context 64K and chunk 512. INT8 used 410 GPU slots / 455 MiB and generated at 66.30 tok/s; FP8 used 328 slots / 364 MiB and generated at 63.85 tok/s. Each run generated 768 tokens across three inputs repeated twice and recorded over 1.2 million CPU Expert entries. Available VRAM changed between fresh starts, so this is not a fixed-cache INT8-versus-FP8 comparison or an upstream performance result.
- Untimed retouching of the entire live external allocation after generation changed physical free memory by 64 MiB and 32 MiB respectively. This ruled out a large hidden eviction in that check, while not proving exact residency or emulating a physical 8 GB GPU. The 768 MiB reserve remains a placement target; later warmup allocations can reduce observed free memory below it.

Reproduction on Windows with an upstream-supported Qwen3.6 GGUF:

1. Use an NVIDIA GPU in WDDM mode and keep another GPU application actively using enough VRAM to make dedicated memory scarce. An idle allocation alone may be paged out by Windows and is insufficient to establish persistent pressure.
2. Build `strata-q36` using the project's normal Windows CUDA build procedure. Run the same supported GGUF with and without this patch. Keep the context, chunk, MTP and other options identical; leave `--expert-vram` and `--expert-slots` unset so Expert placement remains automatic.
3. In PowerShell, enable the diagnostics and run a short native generation, replacing the executable and GGUF paths with your local files:

```powershell
$env:STRATA_Q36_PLACE_DEBUG = '1'
& '.\build\strata-q36.exe' --model 'C:\models\supported-qwen36.gguf' --max-context 8192 --chunk 512 --mtp 0 --no-warmup --tokens '1,2,3' --n 16
```

4. The patched `resident VRAM budget` lines print CUDA free memory, device-wide dedicated free memory and the selected value. The selected value must not exceed either reading. The existing Expert placement log shows whether the result is all-GPU or CPU/GPU hybrid. NVML must be available for the clamp to apply; otherwise the diagnostic explicitly reports the CUDA fallback.
5. Check device-wide free memory in another terminal with `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pci.bus_id,memory.free,memory.total --format=csv`. Keep the other GPU workload live throughout the test. A separate allocation on a larger card is not a fixed physical smaller-card profile, and this correction does not prevent WDDM from paging other allocations later.

The source change introduces no external SDK or test-file dependency. Driver-failure and counter-edge cases were tested with a separate deterministic host harness; those tests are described above rather than being required to reproduce the real Windows memory-accounting discrepancy.

References:

- [CUDA Driver API: cuMemGetInfo](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/cuda_driver_api/group__CUDA__MEM.html)
- [NVIDIA explanation of WDDM CUDA memory accounting and paging](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/cudamemgetinfo-not-reporting-the-actual-gpu-memory-stats/161335)
- [Microsoft video-memory budgeting documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgi1_4/ns-dxgi1_4-dxgi_query_video_memory_info)

pulls.title: [Engine] test+guard: a call for a tool the request never offered stays text (#3075)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
## What it changes

- `serve/frontend.py` — the content state's call scan is gated on the declared tools (`#3075`), the way the reasoning-state scan already is: a request that declared nothing gets the call back as text, not as `tool_calls` with an empty `content`.
- `serve/frontend.py` / `serve/server.py` — one explicit exception. `OutputParser(passthrough=False)` and `Service.run/_run(passthrough=False)`; the responses route sets it only when `prompt_tools()` actually returned the conversation's kept tools (`shown is not tools`), i.e. the Codex compaction request, whose prompt is rendered with kept tools while the request declares none (`responses.py:361-373`). Every other tools-less request follows #804's rule.
- `serve/test_server.py` — `ForcedToolChoice.test_a_call_the_request_never_offered_stays_text`: after `</think>` the model writes a complete, well-formed call for a tool the request never offered, checked for `tools` absent, `tools: []` and `tool_choice: "none"`, streamed and not (6 subtests). On the unpatched tree all 6 fail.
- `serve/test_mcp.py` and `serve/test_parser_call_scan.py` — the two expectations that encoded the old behaviour. The MCP test now expects `stop` and the call as content; the re-scan test declares the tool it writes, because it measures the structural walk, not the no-tools rule.
- `serve/test_responses.py` — the compaction test keeps its with-metadata half unchanged: the calls still come back as `function_call` items, with no namespace/custom shape. Its without-metadata half now asserts the text the new rule produces, because without the metadata it is a plain tools-less request.

## What it leaves alone

The second gap in #3075 — a call naming a function outside a *declared* set — is not touched. As measured on review, a name check in `_finish_call` is too late (`_scan()` has already emitted `tool_start`), and `name in self.schemas` would reject Codex's flat `mcp__server__tool` spelling, which `responses.py:271` maps through `names`. That needs its own change.

## Validation

- New test: 6 subtests fail on the unpatched tree, pass with the guard.
- Full `serve` suite on Windows 11 / Python 3.14.7, CPU only: **849 tests — 1 failure and 1 error, both baseline** (`test_keepawake`'s `wait_for` and `test_winjob`'s `tasklist` returning `None`; both fail the same way on unmodified `main` here). `test_responses`' thread count, which is order-dependent, was green in this run. Nothing else changed.

pulls.title: Metal backend: fix the build on macOS 27.2 / Apple clang 21 and make fused_gr_persist_init a no-op
pulls.author: mnott
pulls.body:
## Problem

Building the Metal engine of v0.1.45 (`./setup.sh`, Metal path) on macOS 27.2 with Apple clang 21 fails, and once it builds,
serving needs a workaround.

1. `metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h` lacks `cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor/Minor`, `cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange`,
   `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority`, `cudaMemcpyPeer` and `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess`, which `src/core/verify.cpp` and
   `src/core/peer_experts.cpp` use (the HIP compat header maps them).
2. `metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp` is stale: `Gemm::bf16` lacks the `bool x_f16` parameter (compile error), and 21 kernel entry
   points (`wait_handoff`, `hc_q8_to_bf16`, `qsa_*`, `gr_norm*`, ...) are undefined at link time.
3. The serve path calls exactly one generated stub at start, `strata::kernels::fused_gr_persist_init` (`src/core/verify.cpp`, the
   opt-in HIP initialiser behind `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`). Generated stubs stop the engine (exit 86) unless
   `STRATA_METAL_STUBS=log` is set, so the server could only be started with stub logging on.

## Change

- `cuda_runtime.h`: shims for the missing calls. Compute capability and the peer calls report "unsupported" (the only
  compute-capability caller, `src/core/verify.cpp`, reads a failure as "not a Turing card"); stream priority range 0/0, a
  priority stream is a plain stream.
- `stubs.cpp`: regenerated in place with `metal/tools/gen_stubs.py` against the v0.1.45 headers (its include root is the LAST
  `-I.../include` that contains `strata/`, so `-I<repo>/include` must come after `-I<repo>/metal/include`): stale signatures
  updated (`Gemm::bf16` and the `gr_norm*` family gained their `bool` parameter) and the 21 missing entry points added. They are
  not ports: they stop the engine with the entry point's name if reached, like the existing stubs.
- `setup_host.cpp`: `fused_gr_persist_init() {}` next to `fused_gr_check() {}`, and `fused_gr_read_persist()` returning `false`,
  both removed from the generated stubs. This matches the CUDA and SYCL builds (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, non-HIP branch).
  All other stubs still stop the engine.

The build-fix parts overlap with #3114, which bundles them with RoPE scaling, a memory probe and setup changes; this PR is
only the build fix, tested on hardware, and adopts #3114's in-place stub regeneration and "unsupported" compute capability.

## Testing

Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 27.2, Apple clang 21.

- Build: `./setup.sh --yes --no-start --no-browser --family unsloth --model UD-Q4_K_XL --vision no --build` finishes and the
  engine links (exit 0).
- Serve without `STRATA_METAL_STUBS` (IQ3_S pack, 65,536 context, MTP on): the engine reaches READY and answers a short
  `/v1/messages` request and a tool-call request (`tool_use` with the right arguments, `stop_reason` `tool_use`). The engine log
  of that start has no `STUB` line, and the engine stayed up (no exit 86) until stopped. Before the change the same start logged
  `STUB strata::kernels::fused_gr_persist_init`.
- Speed, same machine: a 5-hour agentic coding run (Flash-Next IQ3_S, MTP on, thinking off, 262,144 context) served 2,843
  `/v1/messages` requests, measured from the engine's per-request log lines (prefill = newly read tokens / prefill time,
  decode = generated tokens / generation time):

| Context per request | Requests | Decode tok/s | Prefill tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| < 8k | 121 | 111.0 | 1352 |
| 8-45k | 1816 | 109.2 | 1398 |
| 45-90k | 771 | 108.6 | 1158 |
| 90-130k | 135 | 109.6 | 994 |

  Prefill counts requests with at least 4k new tokens; in the 90-130k row no request had that many (the rest of the prompt came
  from the prefix cache), so that value is from the 21 requests with 1-3k new tokens. Overall: 738,060 tokens generated at
  109.1 tok/s, prompts 98.0 % reused from the prefix cache, median context 33,100 tokens (p90 75,506, max 130,137), about 260
  tokens generated per request. Decode stays flat up to 130k context.
- Prefix cache check (5 turns, ~20k prompt): cold 25.4 s, follow-up turns 2.1-3.0 s, 93-94 % of the prompt reused.
- `/v1/messages` tool smoke (Read, Edit, Bash, Edit-after-Read): all pass.

pulls.title: conversation cache: opt-in overwrite growth for snapshot buffers
pulls.author: JumpEggKiller
pulls.body:
## Summary

Parking a long conversation grows host K/V buffers and then overwrites the new bytes with the snapshot copy. Add an opt-in overwrite growth path to avoid initializing those bytes twice. Only `STRATA_SNAPSHOT_NOFILL=1` enables it; the default still fills new bytes. Related: #2264.

## What changed

- Store each `ConversationBuffer` segment in owned raw byte storage while preserving value semantics, address stability and ordinary resize filling.
- Add `resize_for_overwrite` and use it at the snapshot capture call site under the opt-in switch. Keep the existing cache policy and snapshot format.
- Add host tests for full overwrite, retained prefixes, segment boundaries, copy/move, allocation failure, failed transfer callbacks and discard/retry.
- Include sanitized historical v0.1.45 park timings and their limits in `bench/results/conversation-overwrite/`.

## Validation and remaining work

Standalone buffer tests on this main-based candidate: 92 checks pass with MSVC 19.44, C++17, optimized build. A separate v0.1.44.1 backport builds CUDA sm_86 and passes 92 buffer checks, 4,219 cache checks and 36 checkpoint split allocation-failure cases.

The CSV is historical evidence from one patched v0.1.45 binary and two RTX 3090 cards at a 262,144-token context. It includes a slower overwrite run under host contention; it is not a current-main or backport benchmark. The README documents exactly what is timed and omitted. No model, private path, config, prompt, binary or credential is included.

**Draft: not ready for review.** Full current-main CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds remain outstanding. HIP/SYCL toolchains are unavailable on this host. Fresh same-binary backport A/B, prefix edits, two alternating long histories, HTTP error recovery, and a NOFILL-enabled 3-hour/50-request soak are not yet complete. No production binary has been replaced. There is no claim that temperature zero makes outputs deterministic or that all failure modes have been covered.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: temperature 0 stays greedy - no model-card penalties on a greedy request (#2940)
pulls.author: christopherrobertbrooks-tech
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Since a8091f4d (#2685) the server merges the model card's sampling under every request. A request that asks for
`temperature: 0` keeps its temperature but still gets the card's `presence_penalty: 1.5` (Flash-Next when not
thinking; Qwen3.6 in both thinking states). The engine then samples from penalized logits: the answer is not the
greedy one, and on the Qwen3.6 engine the MTP drafts never run (`spec` needs `!smp.needs_logits()`), so every
temperature-0 request shows `drafts accepted 0 of 0`. Still the case on 0.2.0-beta.

With this change, when the request, the shared Chat settings or the config's `sampling` block (the first of them
that sets a temperature) asks for temperature 0, the card's penalties are left out. The rest of the card (top_p and
top_k, which greedy decoding ignores) and any penalty the request or the config sets itself still apply. `/props`
reports the same. Requests that do not ask for temperature 0 are unchanged.

## Related discussion

Resolves #2940: its first suggestion (temperature 0 skips the card's set). The second (a config `sampling` block
replacing the card instead of merging over it) is left alone.

## Approach

`model_card_sampling(arch, thinking, greedy=False)` drops `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty` and
`repetition_penalty` when `greedy` is set; `asks_greedy(*layers)` says whether the first layer that sets a
temperature sets 0. `_run` and `/props` pass it. One sentence in `docs/DETAILS.md` after "Greedy is only for who
asks for it". Rebased on main (e88ee39).

## Validation

Revision: this branch (main e88ee39 + one commit). GPU runs: the v0.2.0-beta tag (3d1fb48, engine 0.1.45.3) with
this commit applied to its `serve/server.py`, built for sm_70 with CUDA 12.9. Tesla V100-PCIe-32GB, i7-13700KF,
16 GB RAM, Linux. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (setup's pinned file),
`--native --max-context 131072 --prefill auto --mtp 2`, every routed expert in VRAM, `reasoning_effort: none`.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_model_card_sampling`: 8 tests OK. The two new ones
  (`test_greedy_gets_no_card_penalty`, `test_asks_greedy`) fail on main (ImportError: `asks_greedy`).
- All 52 `serve/test_*.py` files on main and on this branch: the same result for every file (see Failed).
- The same prompt at `temperature: 0`, 0.2.0-beta vs this branch; "true greedy" = the same request with
  `presence_penalty: 0` added:

| request | server | text = true greedy | drafts accepted | decode |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| prose | 0.2.0-beta | no | 0 of 0 | 114.3 tok/s |
| prose | this branch | **yes** | 115 of 166 | **166.4 tok/s** |
| code | 0.2.0-beta | no | 0 of 0 | 111.6 tok/s |
| code | this branch | **yes** | 260 of 280 | **193.5 tok/s** |

- `strata-bench-v100/benchmark.py` (temperature 0, fresh prompts filled to each size, 256-token answers, engine
  `/metrics`, 3 runs per size, medians), decode tok/s:

| prompt tokens | 256 | 1,000 | 4,096 | 16,384 | 32,768 | 65,536 | 114,688 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.2.0-beta (no drafts) | 109.3 | 104.7 | 85.7 | 59.7 | 40.3 | 23.4 | 14.6 |
| this branch (3,103 of 4,540 drafts accepted) | **156.5** | **156.4** | **116.7** | 57.6 | 34.6 | 19.6 | 11.6 |
| 0.2.0-beta + config `"sampling": {"presence_penalty": 0}` | 156.9 | 157.2 | 117.0 | 57.7 | 34.6 | 19.6 | 11.6 |

  Prefill is the same in all three (1,168 / 1,733 / 1,793 / 1,606 / 1,360 / 984 / 602 tok/s).

**Failed:** `serve/test_responses.py` `NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler` (a thread count:
`1 != 2`), on main and on this branch alike, and on and off on 0.1.45 too.

**Not run:** the Flash-Next engine live, AMD (HIP), Intel, Mac, and the batch path (`--batch N`). This changes the
Python server only, so there is no backend to build.

## Limits

From 16K up the drafts cost on this card with the default FP32 K/V cache (11.6 vs 14.6 tok/s at 114,688). That is
MTP's own trade-off, the same as before a8091f4d, not something this change adds; the long-context decode itself
is #2464.

pulls.title: fix(serve): a cached image whose .sve was deleted is encoded again; a 500 instead of a dropped connection
pulls.author: kai-chop
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none filed

## Summary
A cached image whose `.sve` file has been deleted from the encoder's temp directory (`%TEMP%\strata-vision-*`; something cleaned it while the server ran) makes every request that carries that picture end with a dropped connection and no answer. Clients that resend the whole history (opencode, Claude Code) then fail every later request of the conversation; opencode reports only `ECONNRESET` and retries forever.

Two causes, both still on `main`:
1. `Vision.encode` treats a key in `self.cache` as a hit without checking that its file still exists, so the engine is handed a missing file.
2. The resulting `FileNotFoundError` is an `OSError`, and `_post`'s `except OSError` treats every `OSError` as a client that left: it re-raises, nothing is answered, and the cause is never visible to the client.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`, `Vision.encode`: a cache entry whose file is gone is dropped and the image is encoded again.
- `serve/server.py`, `_post`: only `ConnectionError` / `TimeoutError` are treated as a client that left (as before). `BadBody` is re-raised to `do_POST` (400 / 413, as before). Any other exception raised before the answer began is a `500` that names it (`internal server error (FileNotFoundError: ...)`), with the traceback in the log, in the same shape as the existing 400 for a malformed body; an answer already begun is not replaced.
- `serve/test_vision_cache_missing.py`: a hit with the file present is still a hit; a deleted file is encoded again. Fails without the change.
- `serve/test_internal_error_500.py`: an unexpected `OSError` and another exception are a 500; `ConnectionResetError`, `BadBody` and an answer already begun are still re-raised; `ValueError` keeps its 400. Two tests fail without the change.

## Extra Notes
- Measured on Windows 11, RTX (CUDA), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, installed from v0.1.43.1: with the `.sve` of one RGBA PNG (832x1248) deleted, a one-picture request dropped the connection in 0.02 s; the same bytes plus one trailing byte (another cache key) answered 200. With the change, the same request after deleting the file answers 200 and the `.sve` is written again; requests without pictures and with other pictures are unchanged, and a malformed body is still a 400.
- On v0.1.43.1 the full `serve` suite passes with the change (733 tests, OK, 12 skipped). On this branch (current `main`) I could only run it in a checkout of `serve/` without the native modules: 360 errors with and without the change, the same set, so none comes from this change.
- I did not find what deleted the file. Here the cache dir was under `%TEMP%` (`strata-vision-kp5r7rqe`), which Windows Storage Sense and cleanup tools may empty while a server runs for days (a guess, not verified).

pulls.title: [Engine] gpustat: give each Intel card its own VRAM readings
pulls.author: beyondcr
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Two Intel GPUs on one xe host, both behind the chipset's PCIe bridges: an Arc Pro B70 at
`0000:0d:00.0`, where the engine runs, and an Arc A770 at `0000:11:00.0`, driving the desktop.
Resizable BAR is enabled on both, both are visible in `lspci`, and the engine runs on the B70
through Level Zero, so the hardware side is not in question.

The Monitor's VRAM card read **31.2 of 56.0 GB** for the card the engine was on, which has 30.30
GiB usable. The total was almost double the card, and a sample taken with nothing loaded still read
56.0 GB, so it was not transient. Correcting the total alone then made the panel read **105
percent**, which is how the second problem surfaced.

After this change each card reports its own capacity and its own clients, and a card the sampler did
not read reports no memory rather than another card's figures.

## Related discussion

#3117 covered the first two readings and was closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset rather than on
review; this is the same problem rebased on `main` and extended to the rest of it. Issue #2001 is
the mixed NVIDIA/Intel case, where the wrong card is shown; this is two Intel cards and does not
address it.

## Approach

**The total was a bridge window.** `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<pci>/resource` holds thirteen lines: the
card's six BARs and its ROM at indices 0-6, then the bridge windows the card sits behind at 7-12. A
bridge window is sized for everything behind it and can be far larger than the card, and `max()`
over every line returned one. On this host, above 1 GiB:

```
index 0   BAR      0.02 GiB
index 2   BAR     32.00 GiB    BAR2, which maps all of VRAM with resizable BAR
index 7   bridge   0.11 GiB
index 9   bridge  56.00 GiB    what max() returned
```

Only the card's own BARs describe its memory, so the sizes now come from the first seven lines. The
module already documents the intended value as "the card's largest PCI BAR, which maps all of VRAM
with resizable BAR", and a bridge window is none of those things.

**The used figure included the other card.** `clients()` accepted any `/dev/dri` path in
`/proc/*/fdinfo` and never looked at `drm-pdev`, so with two cards fitted the used figure was both
cards summed while the total was one. Measured here before the fix:

```
B70 (engine)     32161 MiB
A770 (display)    2352 MiB
sampler "used"   34514 MiB   both cards, against a 32768 MiB total
```

A client now has to name this card in `drm-pdev`. A client that reports no `drm-pdev` is still
counted, so a kernel that does not publish it keeps the previous behaviour rather than reporting
nothing.

**Every card is sampled, and the reader takes its own entry.** `find_cards()` returns every Intel
GPU on xe, each sampled with its own hwmon directory matched by device path and its own
accumulators, and `/proc` is scanned once per sample for all of them rather than once per card. The
document keeps one entry per card under `cards`, keyed by PCI address, and still writes the first
card's fields at the top level, so a reader written before this continues to work.

The reader uses the entry for its own card. It previously applied the flat fields whatever card
wrote them, so on a two-card host one card's capacity and usage were shown for the other. When no
entry belongs to the card being read, it reports nothing for load and VRAM rather than another
card's figures.

**The name.** `card_name()` split `lspci -mm` on a quote-space-quote sequence, which mangled the
device name and swallowed the fields after it. It tokenises the fields now.

`GPUSTAT_OUT` names the JSON path, so the sampler can be run as a normal user against a scratch file
to check its output without installing it.

Neither the capacity nor the client change is specific to a card model. Both apply to any Intel GPU
whose host fits a second card, which is a property of the platform rather than of the model or the
amount of VRAM.

Compatibility: the JSON keeps its existing keys and the flat top level is unchanged on a single-card
host. No build change; both changed files are Python.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- Before and after on the same host, same program, at `main` (e88ee39d) and at this commit: running
  `sycl/tools/gpustat.py` from `main` reports `vram_total_mb` **57344**; at this commit it reports
  **32768**. Both write the same 20 top-level keys, so the change is confined to the values.
- `python3 -m unittest tools.test_gpustat_vram_total`, revision 1e770091 on `main` (e88ee39d),
  Linux 7.2.11, Python 3.14: 18 tests, OK.
- Each test fails when its fix is removed. Dropping the `[:7]` slice fails the bridge-window test;
  removing the `drm-pdev` filter fails the client test; restoring the flat read fails the
  card-matching test; restoring the old `lspci` split fails the name test; taking the first `xe`
  hwmon fails the hwmon test.
- Per-card readings on the same host: 32768 MiB and 16384 MiB for the two cards with different
  package temperatures, and the reader returns each card's own entry on three consecutive samples.
  Busy percent, power and the PCIe link still report.
- A single-card document, with `GPUSTAT_PCI` pinning one card, gives that card its entry and the
  other card nothing, rather than lending it the wrong figures.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** no CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal build, since the change is Python only and touches no
compiled code. Not run on a single-Intel-GPU host, and not on Windows, where the SYCL serve layer is
not used.

## Limits

Every Intel xe card is sampled by default and the document carries one entry per card, so the reader
takes the entry for the card it is reading without any configuration. `GPUSTAT_PCI` is still there
for a sampler limited to one card; a reader whose card the sampler did not cover reports no load or
VRAM rather than another card's figures.

Load and VRAM stay root-only across users, because another user's `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo` needs
`CAP_SYS_PTRACE`; the existing install notes already say so.

## Notes

- `serve/telemetry.py` is untouched. The sampler's document keeps its existing keys and gains one
  `cards` map; the flat top level still describes the first card.
- Busy percent becomes per-card as a side effect of the client filter, which is what it should have
  been.
- The total remains the card's largest BAR rather than usable VRAM, so it rounds up to the next
  power of two: 32 GiB for 30.30 GiB usable, 16 GiB for 15.11 GiB. That is the module's documented
  intent and this change does not alter it. `GPUSTAT_VRAM_MB` still overrides everything.
- `#2001` is the mixed NVIDIA/Intel case; this is two Intel cards and does not address it.
- Written with AI assistance, then measured and reviewed by hand on the hardware above. Every
  number here was checked against the source or against command output, and I can explain every
  changed line. Both cards are fitted here, so further checks can be run on request.
