pulls.title: bench: RTX 4090 reports for 0.1.45 (IQ3_XXS + IQ3_S, up to the 204800 limit): STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE regression at 4K, isolated by A/B; full test suite
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
Two community benchmark reports and a full test-suite report for engine 0.1.45 on one
RTX 4090 (sm_89) box. 0.1.44.1 was re-measured in the same sessions by swapping the
engine binaries; every claim below has a same-binary control in the report files.

## Summary

- **No change from 32K through the 204800 context limit**, on both IQ3_XXS and IQ3_S:
  every prompt-reading delta (+0.0% to +1.2% at 156K/185K/200K, ±3% below) sits inside
  the same-binary control band. TTFT at 200K unchanged (61.30 s vs 61.31 s on IQ3_XXS).
  Recall unchanged: 6/6 at 32K/128K (both styles), 3/3 at 192K, both versions.
- **One regression, isolated by A/B: `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE` on sm_89.** It is now on by
  default on sm_86; sm_89 is not in the release's test set. On this RTX 4090 it costs
  ~10-15% of 4K-prompt reading and makes the case unstable.
- **Full Python test suite (1703 tests): no regression of 0.1.45.** Two test-side
  defects with reproductions and suggested fixes (below).

## 1. `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE` on sm_89: 4K-prompt reading

IQ3_XXS, context 204800, code-style 4K prompt (below the chunk; the auto chunk is 8192
in both versions, so the columns are bit-comparable):

| build | 4K prompt tok/s |
|---|---|
| 0.1.44.1 | 2152 / 2163 / 2168 (tight) |
| 0.1.45, default | nine samples in three runs: 1380-2119, medians 1815-1987 (unstable) |
| 0.1.45, `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE=0` | 2107 / 2133 / 2145; control 2129-2145 (tight) |

TTFT at 4K: 1.85 s (0.1.44.1) vs 1.99-2.25 s (0.1.45 default), restored by the switch.
Other lengths are unaffected by the switch (32K: 3289-3321 off vs 3301 default; 128K:
3271-3277 vs 3280). The ru-style 4K case on the IQ3_S config shows the same direction
(-8.3%, below both the control and 0.1.44.1) but was not A/B'd there. Env delivery was
verified in `/proc/<engine>/environ`. Files:
`runs-0.1.45-no-dequant-wide*.json` in the IQ3_XXS code report.

## 2. What was measured

- `2026-10-18-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-{code,ru}` — IQ3_XXS, 204800. One session:
  warm-up -> code -> ru -> same-binary control -> 0.1.44.1 (engine swap) -> back.
  Long lengths (targets 163840/194560/209715 -> actual 156,291/185,531/200,015 tokens)
  ran in a second session of the same protocol; the report tables merge them into one
  table per style. Generation columns are inside the method's noise (±5-6% on identical
  binaries); no generation conclusion is drawn.
- `2026-10-18-community-rtx4090-iq3s-200k-{code,ru}` — IQ3_S on the same box (~50 GB
  of experts vs 48 GB RAM + 24 GB VRAM: the file tier does the work, decode hit rates
  66-88%). Same protocol, same verdict: no change at any length, recall unchanged.
  Absolute speeds are comparable only within this config.
- Not measured: the release's other opt-in switches, long lengths in the ru style
  (measured code-only this time), generation at long lengths.

## 3. Test suite: 1703 tests, 16 failures, none a regression

`2026-10-18-community-rtx4090-test-suite` (raw log included). Ten failures are the
known 0.1.44.1 baseline on this machine (the `test_setup_golden` fixture's
`strata-vision.exe` entries on Linux; two `test_setup_engine_hash` cases specific to a
locally-built engine). Four are `tools.test_strata_mcp.StartStop` seeing this box's
production server on port 8080 — the module passes 24/24 with the port free (verified).
Two are test-side defects:

1. `test_strata_bench.RedactionTests.test_paths_names_ips_and_keys` — the redactor
   rewrites the username before the literal repo ROOT, so `<strata>` never appears when
   the repo lives under `$HOME` with a matching username. Fails deterministically in
   `~/Strata`; the same module passes from a clean worktree of the same tag at `/tmp`.
   Suggested fix: substitute ROOT before the username rules, or use a synthetic ROOT.
2. `serve.test_keepawake.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`
   — the mock request finishes before `KeepAwake`'s daemon thread takes the lock, so the
   `ON` call never happens (5/5 standalone on a fast CPU; passed in a later full-suite
   run — the expectation is timing-dependent). Suggested fix: drive `KeepAwake` directly
   or make the mock generator hold briefly.

## Provenance

RTX 4090 (sm_89), Ryzen 9 7950X, 48 GB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04.1, driver 615.71.09,
CUDA 13.4, Python 3.14.4. Both engines built from source the same way
(`"source": "local"`, archs `[89]`), versions verified in `git describe`,
`engine/BUILD.json` and `/props`. The agent driving the machine works against a
different server, so no observer traffic polluted the runs. Full method, tables and
caveats in the READMEs.

pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): optimize exact QSA block scoring and top-k selection on gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
**Problem and result**
This PR optimizes the exact QSA block-scoring and radix top-k selection kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` on RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and wave32 HIP targets with 100% bitwise parity:
1. **Wave32 VALU DPP reductions & workgroup-scoped barriers**: Replaces `__shfl_xor_sync` reductions with `v_permlanex16_b32`/`v_mov_b32_dpp` to keep reductions on VALU pipe, replaces device-scope `__syncthreads()` in LDS-only selection/scoring loops with workgroup-scoped `sel_sync_lds()` (waits on both `loadcnt(0)` and `dscnt(0)` to avoid L2 cache-invalidation while safe when divergent paths skip VMEM blocks).
2. **Smaller-`PER` specializations & parallelized scans**: Adds `block_topk_reg_kernel<2,9,17>` for small block counts, lowers HIP prefill crossover `kRegMinBlocks` from 7,168 to 4,096, replaces single-thread 256-iteration radix-bin search and 32-warp prefix loops with parallel 8-warp/1-warp prefix scans in `block_topk_kernel`/`block_topk_wide_kernel`.
3. **Prompt exact block-scorer grid granularity & threshold**: Passes dynamic `br` (64/128/256/512) with `__launch_bounds__(256,2)` and lowers default gfx12 activation threshold to `active_blocks >= 512` (ctx >= 2,048).

**Related discussion**
none

**Approach**
On wave32 HIP targets, `__shfl_xor_sync` lowers to `ds_bpermute_b32` on LDS/DS pipe, causing overhead. Using `v_permlanex16_b32` (MASK=16) and `v_mov_b32_dpp` (row_xmask:1|2|4|8, 0x160|MASK) keeps reductions on VALU pipe while summing exact same lane pairs in exact same tree order. Device-scope `__syncthreads()` inside loops causes unnecessary L2 cache-invalidation; workgroup-scoped `sel_sync_lds()` waits on both `loadcnt(0)` and `dscnt(0)` to avoid L2 cache-invalidation overhead while safe when divergent `s_cbranch_execz` paths skip a VMEM basic block. Smaller `PER` specializations reduce VGPR/SGPR pressure and spills for small block counts. Parallelized scans replace inefficient serial loops with warp-level prefix sums, improving occupancy. Dynamic grid granularity (`br`) and lower activation threshold improve utilization of wavefronts at moderate context sizes.

**Validation**

**Passed:**
- `qsa_scores_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (zero bitwise differences, includes independent pre-PR baseline scorer)
- `qsa_topk_active_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (selected IDs bitwise identical)
- `qsa_rows_bench --rows`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (runs without error, validates nq=5–8 and partial tails via internal checks)
- `arch_defaults_test`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- CUDA builds (no CUDA toolchain available)
- SYCL builds (no SYCL toolchain available)
- Metal builds (no Metal support)

**Limits**
- The optimizations target wave32 HIP targets; non-wave32 HIP targets retain existing behavior.
- The grid granularity heuristic (`br`) and activation threshold are tuned for gfx1201; may require adjustment for other GPUs.
- The smaller-`PER` specializations (`PER = 2,9,17`) are limited to block counts within their respective reach; larger blocks still use existing kernels.

pulls.title: Add request-scoped prefill VRAM loans
pulls.author: c3c
pulls.body:
This the rebased version of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1581 for the VRAM loaning part of the PR.

## Summary

This PR adds a manually enabled, request-scoped VRAM loan for prompt prefill.
It temporarily lends decode-only allocations to the prompt path, then restores
the verifier, native output head, MTP experts and draft head before generation.
The repeat-prefill option applies the same transaction to later long messages.

The default path is unchanged when the flags are absent.

## What changed

Enable the feature with:

```json
{
  "STRATA_PREFILL_ELASTIC_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_MTP_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_HEAD_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_RETAIN_STARTUP_CHUNK": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_LOAN": "1",
  "STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_MIN_TOKENS": "50000"
}
```

All six `STRATA_PREFILL_*` variables above are introduced by this PR, but they
are not six independent requirements: `STRATA_PREFILL_ELASTIC_LOAN` is the
master switch; MTP/head loans are staged sub-options; and the retain/repeat
flags apply only when later prompts should repeat the transaction. A minimal
startup experiment needs only the master switch. The existing upstream
`--vram-elastic` command-line option is required as the segmented-cache
backend; it is not part of this PR.

| Variable/option | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_ELASTIC_LOAN` | New master switch |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_MTP_LOAN` | New optional MTP/draft deferral |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_HEAD_LOAN` | New optional native-head deferral |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_RETAIN_STARTUP_CHUNK` | New optional retention of startup geometry |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_LOAN` | New optional subsequent-prompt transaction |
| `STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_MIN_TOKENS` | New repeat threshold; default 1,024, minimum 256 |
| `--vram-elastic`, `--serve`, `--mtp`, `--spec` | Existing upstream options used/validated by this PR |

`STRATA_PREFILL_REPEAT_MIN_TOKENS` applies only to subsequent prompts. It is
clamped to a minimum of 256 tokens and defaults to 1,024. Startup loans are
controlled by the startup flags because the first request length is not known
when the engine initializes.

The implementation is in the serve/prefill lifecycle (`src/program/generate.cpp`)
and the verifier, native-head and MTP resource transactions
(`src/core/verify.cpp`, `src/core/native_head.cpp` and `src/core/mtp.cpp`).

As mentioned in the original PR: **benefit depends on prompt length and whether the released VRAM
crosses a useful planner threshold**. 

## Extra Notes

### Test system and method

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Super Max-Q, 8 GiB, 105 W, compute capability
  7.5.
- CPU/RAM: Intel i7-10875H, 64 GiB RAM.
- Link: PCIe 3.0 x16; measured host-to-device bandwidth approximately
  12.2 GB/s.
- Platform/build: Windows, CUDA 13.4, MSVC Release build with SM75 SASS.
- Engine: current upstream main at v0.1.45 (`477ac13c`) plus this PR.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, native GGUF plus IQ3_XXS expert pack.
- Runtime: 65,536-token context, Q4_0 KV, 24,576 resident KV cells, MTP
  enabled with `--spec 4`, and the experimental speed projection held constant.
- Benchmark request: 31,258 fresh prompt tokens and a 512-token completion
  cap. Runs were serialized with a fresh engine; PP/TG are the engine-reported
  timing-line rates.

### Guarding and supported configurations

The feature is restricted at startup to the serialized, one-GPU NVIDIA CUDA
server path. It requires `--serve`, `--vram-elastic`, CUDA virtual-memory
segments of at least 64 MiB, and rejects batch slots, pipeline windows, layer
split, helper/remote/peer caches, HIP and `--prefill-head-alias`. MTP/head
loans require `--mtp` with `--spec >= 2`; the head loan additionally requires
a native output head.
Invalid combinations fail before any decode resource is deferred.

CPU worker count does not change the ownership model. Multiple conversations
can use one server sequentially, but concurrent batch sessions are rejected.
Separate Strata processes sharing one GPU are not coordinated and must not run
concurrently with loans enabled.

### Measurements

The fixed-planner A/B isolates the transaction when geometry is held constant:

| Configuration | Prompt plan | PP | TG |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Loan flags off | 2,304 / 227 | 424.7 | 29.8 |
| Loan flags on, same plan | 2,304 / 227 | 425.1 | 29.3 |

This is effectively neutral (+0.1% PP, within run noise). The feature is not a
same-kernel speedup; its purpose is to make a larger prompt geometry fit.

With automatic planning (`--prefill auto`), the loan-only run selected a larger geometry:

| Configuration | Prompt plan | PP | TG |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Loan flags on, automatic planner | 5,376 / 227 | **780.6** | **29.7** |

The combined configuration is **11.5% faster in PP** than loans alone in this
screen. The planner also changes the chunk/ring geometry, so this is reported
as an end-to-end combined benefit rather than a loan-only percentage.

A repeat-prefill test released and reloaded the verifier, native head, MTP
experts and draft head without a CUDA/runtime error. The loan-only follow-up
completed at **742.9 PP / 30.4 TG**.

This PR is intentionally incompatible with `--prefill-head-alias`; startup
fails before a loan is taken. Use head-alias mode by itself, or remove it when
using the loan transaction.

### Cross-GPU VRAM-loan qualification

The loan is not SM75-specific. A separate test used an RTX 4070 Ti
(12 GiB, SM89), INT8 KV, a 196,608-token context, a 512-slot staging ring - but an older v0.1.41 source revision. Loan-off and loan-on runs were interleaved,
serialized, and started from a fresh engine. The 36k result is a three-run
median and the 72k result is a five-run median; both used a 512-token
completion cap.

| Fresh prompt | Loan | Prompt chunk | PP (tok/s) | TG (tok/s) | GPU prefill |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 36,061 tokens | Off | 8,448--8,960 | **2,562.9** | **54.8** | 13.811 s |
| 36,061 tokens | On | 15,104 | 2,539.4 | 52.9 | **12.987 s** |
| 72,061 tokens | Off | 8,960 | 2,617.0 | 54.1 | 27.271 s |
| 72,061 tokens | On | 15,104 | **2,680.9** | **54.9** | **25.772 s** |

The larger loan-backed chunk reduced median GPU prompt work by 6.0% at 36k
tokens and 5.5% at 72k. Loading the deferred output-head and MTP resources is
a fixed boundary cost, so the 36k request was 0.9% slower by the engine's
end-to-end PP rate while the 72k request was 2.4% faster. The five-run 72k PP
ranges were 2,604.3--2,633.7 off and 2,501.1--2,696.3 on; four of five loan-on
runs were 2,673.5 PP or higher, with one retained slow outlier. This is evidence
that the general CUDA loan works beyond Turing, but also that it should remain a
manual opt-in: benefit depends on prompt length and whether the released VRAM
crosses a useful planner threshold.

pulls.title: [Engine] extend native-IQ prefill dispatch to SM75
pulls.author: c3c
pulls.body:
This the rebased version of https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1581 for the native-IQ prefill part of the PR.

## Problem and result

Strata already has fused native-IQ prompt-expert kernels, but on SM75/Turing the
native path only admits the Q2_0/Q2_0 pair. Native expert packs using IQ2, IQ3,
or IQ4 gate/up tensors therefore fall back to the ordinary MMQ prompt path.

This PR adds a separate, manual A/B switch for the additional SM75 format
pairs. On an RTX 2080 Super Max-Q with an IQ3_XXS pack, enabling the extension
on top of the same [VRAM-loan configuration](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105) increased median prefill from 774.8
to 859.4 tokens/s (+10.9%). Median generation remained 30.9 tokens/s.

The default path is unchanged when the new switch is absent.

## Approach

Enable the extension with:

```json
{
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED": "1",
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75": "1",
  "STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75": "1"
}
```

`STRATA_PF_FUSED` and `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75` already exist. This PR introduces
only `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75`; it is deliberately separate so existing
SM75 users who enabled the Q2_0 path do not silently opt into new arithmetic.
`STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE` remains the existing global native-path A/B disable.

| Variable | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED` | Existing upstream fused-expert opt-in; still required |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75` | Existing upstream SM75 Q2_0 opt-in; still required |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE` | Existing upstream native-path A/B disable; unchanged |
| `STRATA_PF_FUSED_NATIVE_SM75` | New manual gate for the additional SM75 IQ formats |

The new SM75 coverage is:

- Gate/up: IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, and IQ4_XS.
- Down: Q2_0 and IQ4_NL.

Admission checks the actual CUDA capability, the specific format pair, and
kernel occupancy. The admitted SM75 formats use the qualified 128-row Turing
shape. Unsupported pairs continue through MMQ. SM80+, SM120, HIP, and decode
dispatch are unchanged.

The path keeps the same selected experts, routing weights, and weighted scatter
order. It does change prompt expert arithmetic and may therefore change prompt
state or generated tokens slightly; it is not claimed to be bit-identical to
MMQ.

The implementation updates the SM75 capability description, native-IQ public
contract and CUDA dispatch in `include/strata/core/sm75_series.hpp`,
`include/strata/prefill/moe_fused_iq.hpp`, and
`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`. The corresponding format matrix is covered in
`tests/cuda/prefill_fused_iq_test.cpp`, and `docs/DETAILS.md` documents the new
manual gate.

## Validation

Tested revision: `44500122`, based on upstream `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta). The
combined end-to-end build used the same native commit plus the separate
[VRAM-loan branch](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105) at `db02a533`.

### Passed

- Windows Release CUDA build with CUDA 13.4, MSVC 19.51, and SM75 SASS:
  `strata.exe` and `prefill_fused_iq_test.exe`.
- The focused native-IQ CUDA suite passed on the RTX 2080 Super Max-Q for every
  admitted gate/up and down pair listed above, plus the existing Q2_0/Q2_0
  pair. In its reference cases, fused-versus-MMQ relative RMS was
  `3.5e-5`--`4.0e-4`; the large timing cases also passed, with relative RMS
  `1.2e-4`--`2.1e-4`.
- Three fresh-engine end-to-end runs per configuration, serialized on the same
  machine. The production server was stopped during each run and restored
  afterward.
- With every new flag absent, the combined rebased binary measured 513.6 PP
  median versus 514.6 PP for the exact upstream binary (-0.2%, within the run
  ranges), with the same 2,304/226 plan.

### Failed

- The repository-wide test build did not complete on Windows because current
  upstream `src/kernels/gdn_chunk_parity.cpp` calls POSIX `setenv`. The
  production and focused native-IQ targets compile and run; that unrelated
  current-main test compile failure remains.

### Not run

- HIP and SYCL builds.
- Other GPU generations and multi-GPU configurations.
- Full visible-answer parity: the throughput requests reached their 256-token
  reasoning cap, so these runs validate execution and rates, not complete
  answer equivalence.

## Benchmark configuration

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Super Max-Q, 8 GiB, 105 W, compute capability
  7.5.
- CPU/RAM: Intel i7-10875H, 64 GiB RAM.
- PCIe host-to-device probe: approximately 12.2--12.3 GB/s.
- Windows, CUDA 13.4, MSVC Release build with SM75 SASS.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS native GGUF plus IQ3_XXS expert pack.
- Runtime: 65,536 context, Q4_0 KV, 24,576 resident KV cells, MTP `--spec 4`,
  `--short-read 0`, experimental speed projection, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, and
  `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_Q4_TC=1` held constant.
- Request: 31,258 fresh prompt tokens, 256 generated tokens, fresh process for
  every repetition. Values below are medians of three engine timing lines.

## Results

| Configuration | Prompt chunk / ring | PP median (range) | TG median (range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [VRAM loans](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105), SM75 native-IQ extension off | 5,376 / 227 | 774.8 (772.7--779.9) | 30.9 (30.2--31.9) |
| Same configuration, extension on | 4,864 / 512 | **859.4** (859.1--860.5) | **30.9** (30.7--32.6) |

The isolated net effect in this workload is +10.9% PP. This is an end-to-end
feature A/B rather than a kernel-only number: native-IQ changes the supported
expert execution path and the planner admits a different chunk/ring geometry.

The separate [request-scoped VRAM-loan PR](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/3105)
is not an algorithmic requirement. It was needed on this 8 GiB configuration
to free enough prefill VRAM for the useful native shape. A larger-memory GPU
may admit the native path without it.

The SM75 native-IQ extension itself is independent of upstream
`--prefill-head-alias` and can be used with it. The separate VRAM-loan PR
rejects head alias because both features manage the native output-head
allocation at the prompt/decode boundary.

pulls.title: batch-groups: STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH beside STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT (opt-in STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1)
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Summary

`STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1` is off beside `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1` (`STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT is off beside STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH`), because the batched draft K/V (`Prefill::draft_kv`) would allocate on the read's thread. This adds an opt-in, `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1`, that removes the allocation and lets the two run together. Off (the default), nothing changes.

## What allocates

Reading `Prefill::draft_kv`:

- its row buffers are carved from the prompt path's scratch region (`m.region`): no allocation;
- its two uploads (the bounds, 16 B; the tokens, `nb` x 4 B) go through `up_ring`, and are smaller than what `reserve_uploads` already reserves before the read (`T` x `K` x 4 B);
- the Q8_0 projections run through `mmq::Context` (llama.cpp's MMQ): the context is created at first use, and llama.cpp takes its stream-k fixup buffer from the context's pool, which grows at the first larger request.

So the MMQ pool is the one thing that can allocate. On devices whose MMQ configs do not use stream-k it never does (in the ggml we build with, all 254 RDNA2 configs have `stream_k = false`); on NVIDIA (Volta and newer) and CDNA it can.

## The change

- `mmq::Context::reserve_fixup(bytes)`: takes `bytes` from the pool and gives them back, so a later run that needs at most that much allocates nothing.
- `Prefill::reserve_draft_kv()`: creates the MMQ context and grows the pool to the largest fixup, one 128 x 128 tile of floats per SM (`nsm` x 128 x 128 x 4 B).
- In `generate.cpp`, with `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1` and `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1`, it is called on the drafter's stage before each concurrent read, beside the existing `mtp.reserve_prefill` and `sp.reserve_uploads`, with nothing in flight. It logs once: `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1: the batched draft K/V (STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH) runs beside the concurrent read; its MMQ pool is grown before each read`.
- `ConcurrentReadSetup::split_mtp_batch_reserved`: `concurrent_read_off` no longer names `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH` when it is set. `batch_read_test` covers the new case (checked that it fails when the new assertion is flipped).

## Measured

2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030), ROCm 10.0, Linux. Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, 262144 context, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, layer split with part of the experts in RAM, `--spec 3 --spec-min-p 0.7`, `"parallel": 2`, `--batch-groups 2 --batch-mtp`, greedy. This branch's binary, a fresh engine per arm. Both arms have `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1`; "with" adds `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1 STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1`.

**Stability:** 9 arms, 0 stalls. In the three full runs (two with, one without), each arm read a 64K prompt while a short request arrived (4 give-ways per arm, short TTFT 8.0-8.1 s), two streams, a hand-off, and a needle test across the yield point (6 of 6 correct).

**Prompt read**, 3 interleaved pairs (each arm's outputs are token-identical run to run, so these are the same requests):

| | 4K | 32K | 128K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| without | 951-954 | 1,723-1,724 | 1,990-1,991 |
| with | 990-991 (**+4.0%**) | 1,754 (**+1.8%**) | 2,006-2,008 (**+0.9%**) |

**The cost, which is `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH` itself and not this change:** the draft layer's K/V come from Q8_1 x Q8_0 MMQ instead of the drafter's own mmvq, so the drafts move (as `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` says). On the same requests, drafts accepted fell from 87.5% to 85.3% (and 84.5% to 82.4% in the full runs, 6 of 6 comparisons lower), and decode was about 3% lower at 4K and 32K, unchanged at 128K. On our rig the two roughly cancel, so we leave it off. On rigs where the prompt read is a larger share, or where `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH` gains more, it may be worth it.

## Not tested

The path this guards: **no NVIDIA card here**, so the stream-k fixup allocation that this change pre-grows has not been exercised. On gfx1030 the MMQ never takes from the pool, so our runs show the two coexisting, not that the reservation is sufficient on a stream-k device. A run on CUDA with `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1 STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1 STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_SMB=1` and a few long reads beside a decoding slot would settle it.

---
Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030), ROCm 10.0, Linux.

pulls.title: [Engine] perf(hip): enable wave32 QSA decode attention and MMVQ row reuse on gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
**Problem and result**
This PR combines two bitwise-exact RDNA4 (gfx12, wave32) decode/speculative-verification optimizations and enables their parity/benchmark harnesses under `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP`:
1. **D5 — Wave32 QSA decode attention**: Replaces cross-warp `__syncthreads()` with `qda_sync_lds()` to avoid stalling on global KV VMEM loads, enables wave32 `attn_chunk_kernel_pre75<M,8,true>` by default on gfx12, enables bounded `attn_merge_v2_kernel<16>` by default on gfx12.
2. **D6 — Native MMVQ cross-row fragment reuse & LDS barriers**: Replaces cross-warp partial LDS reduction barriers with `mmvq_sync_lds()` on gfx12/gfx103x, enables `v_perm_b32` IQ4 lookup path across HIP targets, extends `b6_mmvq_rows_kernel` to SmallTraits (Q8_0, IQ4_NL) with preload of activation fragments, adds `b6_default_rows_gfx12` for auto row count on gfx12.

**Related discussion**
none

**Approach**
On gfx12, the prior implementation suffered from shared-memory barriers draining in-flight global KV VMEM loads due to `__syncthreads()` emitting full system scope barriers. The workgroup-scoped `qda_sync_lds()` and `mmvq_sync_lds()` avoid L0 vector cache invalidation and global-load drain while preserving synchronization. For MMVQ, activation fragments and reusable weight-code transforms are preloaded once across output rows, reducing redundant global loads. The auto row count table (`b6_default_rows_gfx12`) selects measured optimal rows per shape on gfx12, falling back to off elsewhere.

**Validation**

**Passed:**
- `qsa_scores_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (zero bitwise differences)
- `qsa_topk_active_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (selected IDs bitwise identical)
- `mmvq_multi_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (0 bit-different with multi_exact on)
- `b6_mmvq_bench 80 0 -1`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (0 failed comparisons)
- `qsa_merge_daily_parity`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS (0 bitwise differences)
- `arch_defaults_test`: revision e88ee39d, GPU AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), observed PASS

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- CUDA builds (no CUDA toolchain available)
- SYCL builds (no SYCL toolchain available)
- Metal builds (no Metal support)

**Limits**
- One-column MMVQ (`ncols == 1`) is unchanged: `b6_launch` is only invoked from `launch_multi_n` when `ncols > 1` and `multi_exact()` is true. Evaluated `STRATA_Q6_PACKED=1` for one-column `Q6_K` heads on gfx1201, but at the default 640-block grid it regressed the 106,299-row MTP head (339.9 → 408.8 us) and 248,320-row output head (794.1 → 960.4 us) while requiring ~213–497 MiB of additional persistent VRAM; both `STRATA_Q8_PACKED` and `STRATA_Q6_PACKED` remain off by default.

pulls.title: [Engine] STRATA_PW_WITH_BATCH=1 keeps --pipeline-windows for a lone request beside --batch slots; single-stream decode +12-16% on a layer split
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `--batch` slots ("parallel" >= 2) generate.cpp turns `--pipeline-windows` off for everything ("--pipeline-windows 2 is off: not with --batch slots"), so a request that is alone - it runs the solo path, and the server goes back to it whenever a slot is left alone (#857) - loses the window overlap a layer split gets without batch slots. A server configured for concurrency is slower for the common one-request case.

With `STRATA_PW_WITH_BATCH=1` the solo path keeps `--pipeline-windows` beside the batch slots; batch windows run without it as before. Result on 2x RX 6900 XT (below): a lone request decodes +16.1% at 4K and +12.3% at 32K context (10 of 10 interleaved cold-start pairs each, draft acceptance unchanged). Without the variable the default path is byte-identical.

## Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; the same change rebased on main and re-measured on 0.2.0-beta as asked.

## Approach

One file (`src/program/generate.cpp`, +23/-5). Both parities' verifiers share the stage's session (`ver_b.init(.., gs.ss, ..)`), so when the solo request is stopped for a newcomer, `copy_to_slot` reads a whole state from `ss` after the pipeline has drained; batch windows never use the second verifiers. With `--batch-mtp` the slot drafters go where the solo drafter is (the first stage's card when `mtp_first`), as it does. The `--pipeline-windows` auto rule and `mtp_first` take `batch_blocks_pw` (= `o.batch != 0 && !STRATA_PW_WITH_BATCH`) instead of `o.batch != 0`; a line says when it stays on. Opt-in.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, 16 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8 each), Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GB DDR4-3200, Ubuntu 26.04 (kernel 7.0.0), ROCm 10.0.0. Revision: main e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta + 12 commits) and this branch on it (it merges cleanly with today's main 9ae93f7b, the 0.2.1 candidate, not re-measured), built with setup.py's HIP options (`-DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`, gfx1030, the pinned ggml, Release). Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, layer split over both cards, int8 KV.

**Passed:**

1. `ctest` (STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON): 137 tests, 131 passed; the 6 failures are the same 6 on main built the same way (`ple_parity` - a missing Q2_0 GGUF, `hip_prefill_mmq_parity` - SEGFAULT on main too, `native_hadamard_test` / `tq_cpu_parity` / `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` - "this ggml has no trellis types", `isa_guard_check` - `tq_rows_avx512` not listed).
2. Default path byte-identical: deterministic config (`parallel` 1, `STRATA_LOGPOS` top-256 log-probabilities, 8 real-text chats, 4,067 positions): main and this branch without the variable `cmp` identical.
3. Speed: `parallel` 2, `--spec 3 --spec-min-p 0.7 --pipeline-windows 2 --batch-mtp`, `--kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=2048`, a rocBLAS table. The same binary without and with the variable, 20 cold starts alternating A B A B; each arm sends one request at a time: real text of about 4K and 32K tokens + "summarize in about 400 words", greedy, max_tokens 512; `decode_tok_s` and drafts from /metrics:

   | context | unset (median, range) | `=1` (median, range) | per pair | median | faster | drafts accepted (unset / `=1`) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 4,122 tokens | 65.2 tok/s (63.2-66.6) | 75.7 (72.2-77.2) | +10.1% to +19.4% | +16.1% | 10/10 | 82% / 81% |
   | 30,321 tokens | 66.7 (64.6-67.3) | 74.2 (71.8-76.1) | +8.0% to +14.4% | +12.3% | 10/10 | 81% / 78% |

   Generated 494-512 tokens (a few natural stops at 4K), 512 at 32K. The unset arms printed "--pipeline-windows 2 is off: not with --batch slots", the others "--pipeline-windows 2 stays on for the solo path beside 2 batch slots (STRATA_PW_WITH_BATCH=1)"; 0 stalls.
4. CUDA compile only (no NVIDIA GPU here): CUDA 13.2.2, GCC 15.2, sm_86, tests on: builds.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** concurrent requests on this revision (batch windows are not changed by the patch, but a request arriving while the solo path is pipelined waits for the pipeline to drain; not measured here); a single-card setup (the gain is the layer split's window overlap); CUDA execution; SYCL and Metal (Metal compiles generate.cpp; the change is host logic only, not verified by a Mac build); other GPUs, Windows.

## Limits

- Opt-in; only a lone request's path changes.
- Output text: with pipeline windows the drafts depend on timing, so outputs are not reproducible between starts - but in this serving configuration they were not with the variable unset either (10 of 10 distinct texts in each arm: the CPU share and the adaptive expert cache already vary), so text identity is not a criterion here; the deterministic check is item 2.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on the machine described here.

pulls.title: Gfx906 exact pipeline j48 20261018
pulls.author: 0FL01
pulls.body:
## Dependent draft — builds on #2966

This is a supplement to #2966, not a replacement or a claim that its existing optimizations are new. Until #2966 lands, the main-branch diff includes its commits. Review the incremental commits starting at `744243d293d63c8647f83ece6b5621f2f84f8747`.

The new work adds exact-F16 workspace reuse, shape-aware preparation around the existing decode pipeline, and an opt-in, guarded J48 MMQ hint for local full-routing gfx906 prefill. The existing pipeline mode 2 itself is not introduced by this PR.

### Measured whole operating profile

Two Radeon Pro VII 16 GiB (gfx906), same model and expert-cache capacity; 65,536 prompt / 1,024 generated tokens, six interleaved pairs, all runs retained.

| | Baseline | Candidate | Paired change | 95% paired-log t interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PP, t/s | 644.6466 | 649.5473 | +0.7585% | −0.7457% to +2.2855% |
| TG, t/s | 55.2240 | 61.6476 | +11.6318% | +11.4085% to +11.8555% |

All 12 runs matched all 1,024 reference output token IDs. All six TG pairs were positive. This comparison includes pipeline/reserve configuration changes; it is not an isolated J48 gain or a comparison with identical speculative work. Zero PP regression is **not** established.

### Correctness and incremental checks
- J48 held-out component replay: 35 vectors, two campaigns, both GPUs; exact output/canary checks.
- 64K accepted0705→J48 ABBA: PP +0.6716%, TG +0.1926%; all four outputs exact.
- 200K/256 single pair: PP 605.4084→612.5657, TG 54.0826→54.1112; exact output. Preliminary.
- 8K repeat ON/OFF/OFF/ON: exact outputs; PP +1.5043%, TG −0.2820%. An initial 8K PP slowdown is retained and unexplained; it did not repeat.

### Why this stays Draft
- CUDA and other HIP-device builds/runtimes remain unverified. Shared host code changes include Product, verify capture, and prompt preparation ordering; this does not claim non-gfx906 host execution is untouched.
- Existing HIP build prerequisites overlap #2020, #2460 and #2459/#3083. They are documented as a reproducibility patch, **not proposed again as optimization code**. The published source is not claimed to build standalone on gfx906 without those prerequisites.
- Do not combine with #1457 workspace-lifetime changes without fresh analysis/tests.
- #3078's void cudaFree wrapper conflicts with checked frees in the inherited HC code; it is not imported.
- Fixed synthetic fixtures and token equality do not establish all model-quality, vision or agent-session behavior.
- No production deployment.

[Full report, per-run results, hashes, benchmark script and prerequisites](https://github.com/0FL01/Strata/tree/64a33632164059477146ebec0eaf2487c2ab6797/bench/results/2026-10-18-gfx906-exact-pipeline-j48)

The source and raw local test artifacts are preserved on the MI50 host; the earlier accepted +11.48% TG result is retained as a rollback.

pulls.author: gg320324492-lgtm

## What it changes
One line: `project_version()` in `tools/strata_bench.py` read `CMakeLists.txt` with the system default encoding. Nothing else. The rest of the file's reads already declare encodings (`utf-8` / `utf-8-sig`); this was the only one that did not.

## How I checked
On an RTX 5090 / Windows 11 (GBK default) box: running `python tools/strata_bench.py` against a live server failed with the decode error before the change, and completed the whole suite (chat, 4K, 16K, agent) after it.

pulls.title: monitor: show every parallel request + fixed-height slot dots (#465)
pulls.author: superlee-terry
pulls.body:
## What

Two web-monitor commits (previously part of #2738, now split out; all engine changes from that PR are dropped — see the closing comment there for the 2x3090 A/B data).

**1. Show every parallel request (#465).** With `--batch N`, the Model state card's single progress bar only ever showed the newest request, so concurrent streams were invisible. The card now renders one row per batch slot: reading progress, decoding (tokens, tok/s, elapsed), or idle with the tokens it holds for the next turn — plus solo-path / waiting-for-slot / queued counts.

**2. Slot dots on the head row.** The extra-counts line under the grid appeared and disappeared with load, so the card height jumped between single and parallel requests. It is replaced by one dot per slot on the state-card head row, right-aligned, text-free: grey = idle, blue = reading, green = generating, yellow = queued/waits, red = error; hovering a dot shows what that slot is doing. The card height is now constant.

Dot and row counts come from `/metrics`' `live.slots` (the server reports one entry per `--batch` slot), so they follow `parallel`/`--batch` dynamically — 2 slots render 2 dots, 4 render 4. `--spec` is the MTP budget and is unrelated to slots.

## Test

Live on 2x RTX 3090, batch 3: 3 concurrent streams render 3 generating rows + 3 green dots; idle returns to grey; state card height measured constant (197px) across idle/parallel transitions. `serve/web` static files only — no server, engine, or protocol changes.

pulls.title: bench: community report, Radeon VII 16 GB (gfx906), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL
pulls.author: Kaidora
pulls.body:
A speed report from hardware the project does not have: one **Radeon VII 16 GB (gfx906)** running
**Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL** on the qwen35moe path. Report-only, no engine change.

**Machine:** Radeon VII 16 GB (gfx906, Vega 20, PCIe 3.0 x16, 250 W cap), Xeon E5-2676 v4 (16 threads,
AVX2, no AVX-512), 62.7 GiB RAM, Debian 13 / kernel 6.12.111, the community image
`mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:10.0-complete` (HIP 7.15.26333, clang 23), `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6`.
Strata 0.1.45 (`477ac13c`), built from source with `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON`. 32K context, 2 slots,
`--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp --pool-workers 6`. Background load: the KDE desktop, Firefox, the DeepSeek Harness and deepseek v4.1 flash were
running during the suite; nothing else ran.

**Measured** (`tools/strata_bench.py`, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges):

| test | result |
| --- | --- |
| chat decode | 34.0 tok/s (26.3-39.7, n=9) |
| chat first token | 0.47 s |
| 4K prompt | 1,150.3 tok/s |
| 16K prompt | 1,040.9 tok/s |
| agent decode | 34.5 tok/s (30.7-38.3, n=15) |
| agent cache hit | 0.0% |

**Two things the report records, and they are the reason I am posting it:**

1. **`--pool-workers` on this path.** Changing only the worker count, at the same 32K context, the same
   slots and the same 62 of 256 experts in VRAM: **13.5 tok/s** chat decode at 15 workers against **34.0**
   at 6 (one slot: 15.4 against 35.2). 15 is the engine's own default on this 16-core CPU (one worker per
   physical core except the first; setup writes no `--pool-workers` here because all cores are alike). At
   15 workers the GPU was busy **33%** of the time and every core sat at 95-100% user (the pool's threads
   spin). At **4, 6 or 8** workers a warm 128-token request decodes at **~64-67 tok/s**; 15 lands at ~26.
   The 16-thread CPU seems to be the wrong place to split a few expert rows per layer.
2. **MTP is inert for the requests the suite (and setup's own config) send.** With
   `--mtp 4 --batch 2 --batch-mtp` the engine logs `drafts accepted 0 of 0` for a request that sends
   only `temperature: 0`. Adding `presence_penalty: 0, frequency_penalty: 0, repeat_penalty: 1` makes
   the drafts appear (`85 of 184`) and the same request decodes at **66-84 tok/s**. That matches
   #3008/#3009; the numbers here are from gfx906.

**What this does not do:** it does not change the engine. It also does not test pictures, `--clients`,
`--long`, a second build or a soak.

**Not comparable to the published Qwen3.6 numbers in one respect:** this card drives the desktop, so
the report's own run caps the experts with `--expert-vram` where needed; the folder notes which
setting each number came from, and the README carries the four configurations I ran (15 workers /
whole card / `--batch 4` / the fixed one) side by side.

pulls.title: expert source: batch-prefetch a layer's CPU experts for a plain mapped experts.bin (STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH, #3065)
pulls.author: As7656431
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #3065 (the third of the three changes described there; independent of #3072)

## Summary
`FileExpertSource::prefetch` returns at once unless `staged()` (the GGUF in place, an unbuffered file tier or Linux io prefetch). In the low-RAM mode with a pack's `experts.bin` read through the mapping (`--mmap-experts`, no RAM budget), each expert the decode's CPU pool computes is faulted in page by page. With `STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH` the layer's CPU experts go to the OS as one batch before the pool reads them. Opt-in: with the variable unset nothing changes.

## What changed
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: `prefetch_mapped` (one `PrefetchVirtualMemory` call per layer on Windows, `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` elsewhere; experts in the RAM copy are skipped) and `prefetch_async` (a helper thread; the newest request replaces one that has not started). `prefetch()` uses them when the source is not staged and the variable is set; the destructor stops the thread.
- `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: the members for the above.
- `STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH=1` issues the batch on the calling (dispatch) thread; `=2` hands it to the helper thread and returns at once (`PrefetchVirtualMemory` costs about 0.2 ms a call even when every page is resident). `=2` is what I measured.

## Extra Notes
- **Same computation.** It only asks the OS for pages ahead of time; the bytes the pool reads are the same. `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` after an 8K document and a 300-token prompt, two runs each: every run with the variable set was bit-identical to a run without it. Against the 0.1.45 release binary, with the variable unset the code path is the release's; the logits differed only as much as the release differs from itself between runs (#3065), and the first choice was the same in every run.
- **Speed**, same PC and settings as #3063 (RTX 5070 12 GB, 31.8 GiB RAM, Windows 10, Flash-Next IQ2_XS, `--mmap-experts`, 0.1.45 server), this branch with the variable unset against set, four interleaved rounds (each first twice), a short question, another, a 20K-token English document, a short question:

| | unset | `STRATA_MMAP_PREFETCH=2` | rounds faster |
|---|---|---|---|
| first request after a start | 35.4 tok/s | 47.0 tok/s (+33%) | 4 of 4 |
| warm short chat | 65.2 tok/s | 71.7 tok/s (+10%) | 4 of 4 |
| reading the 20K document | 187.5 s | 183.6 s (unchanged) | 2 of 4 |
| decode right after the document | 15.2 tok/s | 22.9 tok/s (+50%) | 4 of 4 |
| a short question after the document | 35.5 tok/s | 47.7 tok/s (+34%) | 4 of 4 |

  The gain comes when the mapped pages are not in RAM: after a start and after a long prompt has pushed the cached experts out. On top of #3072 it is smaller (in an earlier run on 0.1.44.1 with both: +22% first request, +11% question after the document, +7% warm chat), since that PR keeps the cached experts in RAM.
- Built and tested with CUDA on Windows only. I have not built or tested the non-Windows branch (`madvise`) on Linux or macOS, nor HIP or SYCL.

pulls.title: Enable IQ prefill path on sm_75 (RTX 20-series / Turing)
pulls.author: dd777mine
pulls.body:
<!-- If Applicable, reference the GitHub issue -->
Issue: N/A

## Summary
<!-- Quick Summary of changes -->
On Turing (`sm_75`, e.g. RTX 2060), `moe_fused_iq.cu` was bailing out early under the assumption that codebook formats do not fit 64 KB of shared memory at 4 warps a row. However, with `ASTAGES_DEV=2`, `IQ3_S` blocks require ~58.8 KB (cleanly fitting the 64 KB ceiling), and `IQ2_S` / `IQ2_XS` fit at 2 warps (~43.5 KB).

This PR adjusts the sm_75 gate so Turing GPUs can use the native fused MoE prefill path instead of falling back to CPU dequantization and host synchronization.

## What changed
<!-- Specifics on files changed, and what changes were made there -->
One file: `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`

* `setup_one_turing()`: registers `IQ2_S` / `IQ2_XS` at `WW=2` only; all other formats keep `WW=4` + `WW=2` (matching sm_80+).
* `dev_info()`: runs `setup_one_turing` for the codebook formats on Turing instead of restricting to `Q2_0`.
* `native_supported()`: removes the sm_75-only `Q2_0` restriction and checks `d.t75` directly so either `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` or `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75=1` activates the path.
* `experts_native()`: pins `ww=2` for `IQ2_S` / `IQ2_XS` on Turing to match what was registered.
* Fully opt-in: activates with either `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` or `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75=1`. Non-Turing (`sm_80+`) and HIP builds remain byte-identical.

## Extra Notes
<!-- Any extra notes, delete if there are none -->
### Numbers (RTX 2060 12 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S)
Tested on ~5.8K prompt tokens (clean v0.1.45 build, only this file changed):

* **Time to first token (prompt latency):** 14.1 s → **12.3 s** (-1.8 s faster)
* **Bulk prefill speed:** 509 tok/s → **606 tok/s** (+19.2%)
* **Decode speed:** identical (zero regression)

### Context & Transparency
* I run an RTX 2060 12 GB at home where prefill was the main bottleneck. I worked on tracing the gate with an AI coding agent as a second pair of eyes, and verified everything by building and running it on real hardware. I'm not a CUDA expert, and would rather say that up front.
* In my personal fork I have a few other experimental tweaks (enabling BF16 tensor cores in `gemm.cu` and GDN vectorization), which push prefill speed even further to **~760 tok/s** (10.1 s latency, **+50%** total speedup). None of that is in this PR — I wanted to keep this strictly scoped to one file and one clear fix per contribution guidelines, but happy to share or open separate PRs if interested.
* If any of the setup checks fail on other hardware, `d.ok` stays false and the engine safely falls back to the existing non-native path.
* Happy to rename things, split this down, or close if you prefer a different approach for Turing. Feedback welcome either way!

pulls.title: qwen35: FP16 K/V cache by default, int8 with --kv-q8 (262144 fits a 16 GiB card)
pulls.author: benthic-io
pulls.body:
## Title

qwen35: FP16 K/V cache by default, int8 with `--kv-q8` (262144 fits a 16 GiB card)

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary

The Qwen3.6 / `qwen35moe` engine stored its K/V cache in FP32 with no option to change it. At the model's
native 262144 cells that is **12.0 GiB** - the whole of a 16 GiB card before a single expert - so the context
had to stop at 192K. FP32 is also the wrong precision for this path, for a reason the code already made
obvious: **the prompt has always attended over FP16** while the decode of the next token read FP32.

FP16 becomes the default (6.0 GiB at 262144), matching what the main engine's `kKvF16` already does, and
`--kv-q8` stores int8 codes with one FP16 scale per 64 dims - the main engine's own `kv_q8.hpp` scheme
(`KV_Q8_GROUP`) - at 3.1 GiB.

This could not be reached with a configuration flag: **this engine path has no KV or precision option at
all.** Its parser has none of `--kv`, `--kv-resident` or anything else, and the allocation was a hardcoded
`dalloc(...)` (float) with the kernels reading `const float*` directly. There was nothing to set; the flag
and the storage had to be added together.

## What changed

`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`

- `k_attn_prep`, `k_attn_part` and `k_kv_f16` are templated on the cache format, so the FP16 path carries no
  branch and the prompt path's existing half-staging (`k_kv_f16`) becomes a pure compaction instead of an
  FP32→FP16 conversion.
- `--kv-q8` quantizes on write with `scale = fp16(max|x| / 127)`, `code = clamp(rint(x / scale), -127, 127)` -
  the main engine's scheme, so a cell is stored the same way in both engines.
- `k_attn_prep` loses its `if (i >= HD) return;` early return. The q8 group max needs a `__syncthreads()`
  that every thread has to reach, so the stores are guarded with `i < HD` instead. Behaviour on the FP16
  path is unchanged.
- `RowSel`, `Sess` and the batch rows' per-session pointer tables carry the scale arrays alongside the code
  arrays. The session-to-slot copy was sized in FP32 elements (`* 4`) and is now sized in the format's, with
  a second copy for the scales under q8.

`docs/QWEN36.md` - a section on the two formats with the numbers below.

## Extra Notes

**Why FP32 was never the right choice here.** `k_kv_f16` has always compacted `[kvh][ctx][HD]` into the
`[kvh][P][HD]` halves that the prompt chunk's Q K^T and P V GEMMs read. So a prompt attended over FP16
values while the split-K decode of the very next token read FP32. The cache format only ever gave the decode
a higher precision than the prefill sharing its sequence; FP16 makes the two agree.

**Measured**, Radeon VII (gfx906, 16 GiB), ROCm 7.1, `--max-context 262144 --chunk 4096 --expert-vram 8`,
two runs, back to back:

| cache | VRAM free | experts in VRAM | tg32 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP32 (before) | does not allocate | - | - |
| FP16 | 4.46 GiB | 49 / 256 | 41.4 / 45.0 tok/s |
| `--kv-q8` | 7.12 GiB | 91 / 256 | 49.1 / 52.6 tok/s |

q8 is both the smaller cache and the faster one, which is not the obvious outcome: the VRAM it returns goes
to the expert cache, and the q8 read also halves the bytes the split-K decode pulls across PCIe. The gap is
about +18%, with a few points of run-to-run spread.

**Parity** against an FP32 build of the same tree: 4 prompts of 4,000 tokens, greedy 96, `--mtp 0`, with both
binaries checked to place the same 81/256 experts so the comparison is the cache format and nothing else.
FP16 **383 / 384** generated tokens identical, `--kv-q8` **384 / 384**. The one FP16 difference is an argmax
near-tie at token 43 of the first prompt; no earlier token moves.

**A characteristic `--bench-pp` hides**, recorded in docs/QWEN36.md: it measures a 2,048-token prompt, nowhere
near the context's end, and throughput falls as a prompt fills the context. One 198,603-token prompt through
the server read 4,096 tokens at 1365 tok/s, 106,496 at 195, 172,032 at 72 - a steady decline that finishes,
about 17 minutes end to end. Worth knowing before filling a 262144 context in one request; irrelevant to a
conversation built up over turns.

**Not run here**: `tools/qwen35/q36_solo_gate.py` over the 10 parity prompts, `q36_batch_gate.py`, and the
vision gates. Those are the obvious next step on the project's own hardware.

pulls.title: fix(HIP compat): the Qwen3.6 engine does not compile on ROCm, and gfx906 does not link at all
pulls.author: benthic-io
pulls.body:
## Title

fix(HIP compat): the Qwen3.6 engine does not compile on a ROCm target

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary

Three separate defects, all on the AMD path, none reachable from a CUDA build:

1. `main` **does not link at all** on `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` - the Qwen3.6 / qwen35moe engine path cannot be built.
2. `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` does not compile for HIP - two cuBLAS names the HIP compatibility header does not map.
3. Two expert kernels in the shared file break any HIP build - a `__shared__ alignas(16)` the HIP host pass rejects.

None is a configuration problem. A `#define` cannot come from a CMake option or an environment variable, the
declaration syntax is fixed by the compiler, and a missing source file is missing.

## What changed

**`CMakeLists.txt`** - `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` forces `STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA ON`, so a gfx906 build takes this
`add_library(strata_mmq ...)` and not the `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ` one below it - and this list omits
`src/prefill/moe_f16_kq.cu`, which the other one does list. `moe_fused_iq.cu` calls `f16kq::covers / gate_up /
down` inside `#if defined(__HIPCC__)` with no `STRATA_PF_F16` opt-in around them, so every HIP build on this path
references symbols that are not compiled:

```
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: strata::prefill::fused::f16kq::covers(int)
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: strata::prefill::fused::f16kq::gate_up(...)
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: strata::prefill::fused::f16kq::covers_down(int)
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: strata::prefill::fused::f16kq::down(...)
```

Adding the file resolves it; `f16kq::covers()` keeps the gfx11 kernels undispatched elsewhere, so run-time
behaviour is unchanged. Guarded by `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` because a CUDA build references none of these symbols and
should not compile a gfx11 kernel file.

**`include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h`** - two missing cuBLAS-to-hipBLAS aliases:

- `cublasSgemm`, the F32 projections on the tiled split-K SGEMM (`q36_engine.cu:1555`)
- `cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx`, the prompt chunk's FP16 Q K^T and P V (`q36_engine.cu:1958`, `:1972`)

**`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`** - `STRATA_SHARED_INT4`, for the two `int4` staging arrays at `:1856` and
`:2043`. These spell the attribute out longhand where the neighbouring line uses `STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_U32`.
That macro exists for exactly this reason (#778) and its comment already records the workaround, so this follows
the established pattern. `int4` is 16-byte aligned by type, so under `__HIPCC__` the explicit attribute is
dropped - same layout, as the existing comment says for `uint32_t`.

## Extra Notes

Before, on gfx906:

```
q36_engine.cu:1555: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cublasSgemm'; did you mean 'hipblasSgemm'?
q36_engine.cu:1958: error: use of undeclared identifier 'cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx'; did you mean 'hipblasGemmStridedBatchedEx'?
iq_kernels.cu:1856: error: 'alignas' attribute cannot be applied to types
iq_kernels.cu:2043: error: 'alignas' attribute cannot be applied to types
... then, at link:
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: strata::prefill::fused::f16kq::covers(int)
```

After: `ninja strata strata-q36` is clean.

Verified on **gfx906 (Radeon VII, 16 GiB), ROCm 7.1, Fedora 44**, gcc host compiler,
`-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=<llama.cpp>`. Each file was checked
individually: it fails to compile without its change and compiles with it. The rebuilt `strata` then serves the
IQ4_XS pack (HTTP 200, correct answer, 3982 MiB free with everything loaded) and `strata-q36` runs a Qwen3.6
GGUF at 262144 cells (1329 tok/s pp2048, 49.3 tok/s tg32 with `--kv-q8`).

`src/prefill/gemm.cu` also names `cublasSgemm`, `cublasGemmAlgo_t` and `CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`, but all
three are inside `#if defined(STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60)` (the experimental Pascal path) and are not compiled in
a normal HIP build, so no mapping is added for them here.

One thing I noticed but did **not** change, since it is a design question rather than a defect: the HIP
workarounds are gated on `STRATA_USE_HIP`, which `cmake/hip_backend.cmake:98` defines for the
`strata_hip_runtime` target - i.e. the `STRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON` backend. `STRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON` instead defines
`STRATA_HIP_GFX906` and never `STRATA_USE_HIP`, so the 91 `#if defined(STRATA_USE_HIP)` sites across 12 files
are compiled out of a gfx906 build, including `STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1` (#884, the SDMA hang workaround
in `generate.cpp:259`) and `STRATA_FILE_CACHE_OLD_RULE` (#1752, a gfx906-specific stall). Only
`generate.cpp`'s outer guard at `:248` is written as `(defined(STRATA_USE_HIP) || defined(STRATA_HIP_GFX906))`.
Worth deciding whether the two backends should agree here; happy to test a patch that defines `STRATA_USE_HIP`
on the gfx906 path if that is useful.

- `tools/test_setup_amd.py` gains the gfx906 no-wheels exception cases.

**What it leaves alone**: every other card's path is unchanged; the wheel-driven default path is untouched. The card is opt-in by nature — setup lists it and points at the hand build, it does not drive one.

Verified: `python tools/test_setup_amd.py` passes (40 tests), including the new exception cases. Engine-side build/run evidence for the card is in `docs/ROCm_6_3_3.md` (#3077) on 2x MI50.

pulls.title: prefill: check both f16-range symbol writes on the reset path
pulls.author: ken2425pm
pulls.body:
One change in `src/prefill/kernels.cu` (5 lines): `f16_range_read(reset=true)` fired the two `cudaMemcpyToSymbol` writes and never looked at the result. When one failed, the symbol kept its previous value and the next read reported a stale cumulative count with nothing saying the reset did not happen.

Now both writes always run (a failed first write must not skip the second), both results are checked, and failure is reported.

**What it leaves alone**: behaviour is unchanged when both succeed — the normal path still does exactly two symbol writes and one error check, and the reads are untouched. No defaults change.

Not tested: a CUDA build (no CUDA toolkit on this box); the change compiles on the gfx906 HIP target.

pulls.title: gfx906: compile the engine on a system ROCm 6.3.3 (blockers past the cublas maps)
pulls.author: ken2425pm
pulls.body:
Complements #2460 / #2459 (the cublas name maps): with those in place, five more spots still block `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON` on a **system** ROCm 6.3.3 (clang 18, `/opt/rocm-6.3.3`, no container). This PR carries only those, so the cublas PR keeps its scope.

**What it changes**

- `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/strata_hip.h`: void wrappers for the call sites that genuinely discard their `hipError_t` result — ROCm 6.x marks the type `[[nodiscard]]`, so every unchecked call warns under `-Wall -Wextra`. The pass-through wrappers are gone; those names map straight onto `hip*`.
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: `__shared__ alignas(16) int4` does not compile on HIP (the #778 pattern) — a `STRATA_SHARED_ALIGN16_INT4` macro keeps the CUDA spelling and takes the attribute form under HIPCC.
- `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: `__ldg` does not resolve in this TU under HIP (plain deref, semantically identical on gfx906); `__half_as_ushort` is device-only on HIP (memcpy bit-cast in the host debug print); `CK()` moves into a template so the void-returning compat wrappers type-check on both toolkits.
- `src/core/remote_experts.cpp`: `cudaInitDevice` has no HIP counterpart — excluded under `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` the way Metal already is.
- `src/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_parity.cpp`: the sm_80+ Q4_0 gate must not query device attributes on a HIP build (the existing `__HIPCC__` exclusion, widened).

**What it leaves alone**: CUDA and SYCL are untouched — every hunk sits inside a HIP guard or a HIP-only macro branch, so those paths compile as `main` does by construction. No defaults change; no opt-in surface added.

**Verified** on 2x Instinct MI50 (gfx906), system ROCm 6.3.3: the `strata` target links clean with `-Wall -Wextra`, and generation runs (measurements in `docs/ROCm_6_3_3.md`, #3077).

**Not tested**: a CUDA build and SYCL (no CUDA/oneAPI toolchain on this box — stated, not skipped silently), and a `-Werror` build (`STRATA_WERROR=OFF`; the make-it-true path is measured in the report).

pulls.title: Fix crash (0xC0000005) when Qwen3.6's Q2_0 experts are offloaded to the CPU pool
pulls.author: wanlemur
pulls.body:
# Overview The 2-bit GSQ quant of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`chitsgit/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-2Bit-GSQ-hybrid-GGUF`) runs great as long as every routed expert fits into VRAM. However, whenever I tried running it in hybrid mode—offloading some of the experts to the CPU pool—it crashed immediately during warm-up with an access violation (`0xC0000005`) across all worker threads. ### Whats wrong I traced the root cause to the CPU pool activations: native 2-bit (Q2_0) CPU kernels don't read standard activations directly. Instead, they expect activations pre-quantized into a specialized layout (`ActQ`) that stores the quantized data alongside scaling factors. The `q36` engine set up the standard activation buffer for hybrid layers, but left the `ActQ` pointer uninitialized (`nullptr`). When worker threads picked up a Q2_0 expert job, they tried to read scale factors from this null pointer and crashed immediately. The Flash-Next engine already handles this case properly, but `q36` never got the equivalent logic. ### How I fixed it I mirrored the approach used in Flash-Next: before dispatching expert jobs to the pool, I check the layer's quantization format. - If the layer uses native Q2_0 kernels, I quantize the hidden states into an `ActQ` buffer on the fly and hand that pointer to the worker job. - For all other formats, I keep the standard activation path without adding extra overhead. With this in place, hybrid mode runs completely stable. On my RX 7800 XT with 155 of 256 experts per layer in VRAM (and the rest in system RAM), decode speed sits at **41.8 tok/s**—on par with UD-Q4_K_XL in the same scenario, where it previously crashed on startup. --- ### What Changed All edits `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` inside the CPU pool logic: 1. **Included headers** for the `ActQ` structures and activation quantization helpers. 2. **Added an `ActQ` buffer:** I added a vector of `ActQ` structures to the engine class and resized it alongside the existing activation allocations during expert placement. 3. **Branched by layer quantization type:** - I check if the current layer uses native Q2 kernels. - If yes: I quantize activations into the `ActQ` buffer and give the worker job the `ActQ` pointer. If no: I pass the standard activation buffer pointer as before. I didn't need to touch the pool scheduler or compute kernels: the down-projection pass already quantizes its own intermediate buffers between phases, and Qwen3.6’s layer dimensions (embedding dimension 2048, expert intermediate size 512) divide cleanly into the kernel's 64-element block size. --- ### Benchmarks **My test setup:** AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (16 GB), RAM 32GB, Ryzen 7 7700, Strata 0.1.45 + this patch. I benchmarked three configurations: 1. **UD-Q4_K_XL (Hybrid, 32K context):** At 20.2 GiB, the model exceeds 16 GB VRAM, so it always runs in hybrid mode. 2. **GSQ 2-bit (Full GPU, 32K context):** At 13.2 GiB, the model and KV cache fit entirely in VRAM with no CPU offloading. 3. **GSQ 2-bit (Hybrid, 64K context):** Doubling the context pushes the KV cache over budget, forcing 101 of 256 experts per layer into system RAM (8.44 GiB in the CPU pool). **This is the scenario that used to crash.** | Scenario | UD-Q4_K_XL
*(Hybrid, 32K ctx)* | GSQ 2-bit
*(Hybrid, 64K ctx)* | | :--- | :---: | :---: | | **Chat decode**, tok/s *(median)* | 38.8 | **41.8** | | Chat TTFT, s | 0.31 | **0.18** | | **4K prompt**, tok/s | 256 | **520** | | 4K TTFT, s | 15.7 | **7.7** | | **16K prompt**, tok/s | 242 | **453** | | 16K TTFT, s | 66.3 | **35.5** | | **Agent turn decode**, tok/s | **39.9** | 39.0 | | Agent turn TTFT, s | 38.8 | **20.7** | ### Key Takeaways: 1. **Prompt processing is ~2× faster on 2-bit GSQ.** Prefill throughput jumps from 256 to **520 tok/s** on 4K prompts and from 242 to **453 tok/s** on 16K prompts. This cuts time-to-first-token in half across both short and long contexts (**7.7s** vs 15.7s at 4K; **35.5s** vs 66.3s at 16K). 2. **Hybrid decode remains faster even with double the context.** Despite holding a 64K context window (which forces 101 of 256 experts per layer into system RAM), 2-bit GSQ decodes at **41.8 tok/s** versus 38.8 tok/s on Q4 hybrid at only 32K context, all while using a much smaller CPU pool memory footprint (8.44 GiB). 3. **Decode throughput is bound by RAM bandwidth.** In both hybrid setups, generation speed is limited by how fast offloaded expert weights are transferred across the system bus per token. With the patch eliminating the previous crash and startup stalls, the Q2_0 hybrid path demonstrates smooth, expected scaling.

pulls.title: [Engine] STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2 takes the simt2 scorer on HIP too (it silently fell back to the warp kernel); 119K prompt -6.5% on gfx1030
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`qsa_block_scores_tc`'s HIP branch read only `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1`, so `=2` (#2071's `block_scores_simt2_kernel`, 32 x 128 tiles with the next K chunk in registers) silently kept the warp scorer on AMD cards while CUDA ran it. With this change `=2` launches `block_scores_simt2_kernel<32, 128>` (and the tail kernel) on HIP as the CUDA branch does; the confirmation line names it.

Result on 2x RX 6900 XT (below): prompt time -1.35% at 31K and -6.53% at 119K tokens, 10 of 10 interleaved cold-start pairs each; the selection scorer's share grows with the context. Without the variable the default path is byte-identical; with it, two runs are bit-identical to each other on this card.

## Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; this is the same change rebased on main and re-measured on 0.2.0-beta as asked. petski3 reported run-to-run differences with `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1` on gfx906 in the earlier thread; item 3 below is the gfx1030 data point for that.

## Approach

One file (`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, +18/-5): the HIP branch parses `0/1/2` like the CUDA branch; `=2` takes the simt2 kernel with the same grid guard (`grid.y > 65535` returns false, the caller keeps its path); `=1` and unset are unchanged. Opt-in; CUDA unchanged.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, 16 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8 each), Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GB DDR4-3200, Ubuntu 26.04 (kernel 7.0.0), ROCm 10.0.0. Revision: main e88ee39d (v0.2.0-beta + 12 commits) and this branch on it; the branch merges cleanly with today's main 9ae93f7b (the 0.2.1 candidate), which was not re-measured. Built with setup.py's HIP options (`-DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`, gfx1030, the pinned ggml, Release). Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, layer split over both cards, int8 KV.

**Passed:**

1. `ctest` (STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON): 137 tests, 131 passed, including `qsa_select_bench`, `qsa_select_bench_fp32_tiled` and `hip_native_qsa_score`. The 6 failures are the same 6 on main built the same way: `ple_parity` (needs a Q2_0 GGUF this machine does not have), `hip_prefill_mmq_parity` (SEGFAULT on main too), `native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2` ("this ggml has no trellis types"), `isa_guard_check` (`tq_rows_avx512` not listed).
2. Default path byte-identical: deterministic config (`parallel` 1, no pipeline windows, `--short-read 640 --adapt-every 100000`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`, `STRATA_LOGPOS` top-256 log-probabilities), 8 chats of real text (first message 6K-105K tokens through the prompt path, ~580 continuation tokens scored), 4,067 positions: main and this branch without the variable `cmp` identical.
3. Determinism with `=2`, same harness: two runs `cmp` identical (4,067 positions). So on gfx1030 the simt2 scorer itself does not make runs differ; in the serving configuration (CPU share, adaptive expert cache) outputs differ between starts with or without it.
4. Quality, same harness: mean KL over the 8 chats to a local FP64-attention reference build (scores, softmax and sums of the QSA attention in double; not part of this PR): main 0.0334 (argmax agreement 94.81%), `=2` 0.0220 (95.75%); KL(main || `=2`) 0.0256. Not worse - the scorer only changes the summation order of the block scores.
5. Speed: production-like config (`parallel` 2, `--pipeline-windows 2 --batch-mtp`, `--kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_MIN=2048`, a rocBLAS table via `STRATA_ROCBLAS_TUNING`), the same binary without and with `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2`, 20 cold starts alternating A B A B, each reading two real-text prompts with max_tokens 1, `prompt_ms` from /metrics, 0 tokens reused:

   | prompt | unset (median, range) | `=2` (median, range) | per pair | median | faster |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | 31,039 tokens | 19,117 ms (19,105-19,382) | 18,867 ms (18,847-18,880) | -1.18% to -2.71% | -1.35% | 10/10 |
   | 119,290 tokens | 62,637 ms (62,583-62,882) | 58,554 ms (58,511-58,653) | -6.43% to -6.73% | -6.53% | 10/10 |

   The `=2` arms all printed `qsa select: FP32 tiled scorer (STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2), tiles simt2 32x128 (#2071)`, the others no tiled-scorer line; 0 stalls.
6. CUDA compile only (no NVIDIA GPU here): CUDA 13.2.2 (nvcc 13.2.86), GCC 15.2, `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`: the engine and the tests build (the file's CUDA branch is unchanged).

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** gfx906 (petski3's card), gfx11 / gfx12 (`=2` there still yields to the gfx12 WMMA scorer when that is on), other gfx103x cards, Windows; CUDA execution; SYCL and Metal (they do not compile this file).

## Limits

- Opt-in; only `=2` on HIP changes.
- Not bit-identical to the warp scorer (another summation order), so outputs differ from the default by FP32 rounding; quality item 4.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on the machine described here.

pulls.title: prompt path: STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1 on Windows, also in the low-RAM mode without a RAM budget (#3065)
pulls.author: As7656431
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #3065 (the first of the three changes described there)

## Summary
On a Windows PC whose RAM cannot hold the experts (`--mmap-experts`), the stager copies each prompt chunk's experts out of the mapped `experts.bin`: millions of page faults that read the drive slowly and push the decode's cached experts out of RAM. `STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` already reads the prompt path's blobs unbuffered on Linux, in the RAM-budget branch only. This PR makes it work on Windows, and also in the low-RAM mode without a RAM budget. Opt-in: with the variable unset nothing changes.

## What changed
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: a Windows branch in `open_prompt_direct` (experts.bin opened a second time with `FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`); `read_direct` uses these handles when the file tier itself is not unbuffered. `copy_blobs` is unchanged: it already reads through `pdirect_`.
- `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `ExpertSource::prompt_reads()` (default false; true on Windows for experts.bin with those handles open).
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: with `prompt_reads()` the stager hands unpinned blobs to `copy_blobs` (8 neighbours per request, ring of 2 x batch x threads). `transient()` is not touched, so the decode and the prompt CPU share keep their behaviour.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: on Windows, `STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` is also honoured in the mmap mode without `--resident-budget-gib`.

## Extra Notes
- **Default path unchanged / same computation.** `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` after an 8K document and a 300-token prompt, two runs each, against the 0.1.45 release binary: with the variable unset and with it set, every run of this build was bit-identical to one of the release's runs (the release's own two runs of the 8K document differ, KL 1.2e-3, as noted in #3065).
- **Speed, same PC and settings as #3063 (RTX 5070 12 GB, 31.8 GiB RAM, Windows 10, Flash-Next IQ2_XS, `--mmap-experts`), `tools/strata_bench.py`, medians of 3; the 0.1.45 numbers are from #3063, measured the same day:**

| | 0.1.45 | this PR, `STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` |
|---|---|---|
| 4K prompt | 58.3 tok/s, first token 69.0 s | 160.6 tok/s, first token 25.0 s |
| 16K prompt | 127.5 tok/s, first token 126.0 s | 310.8 tok/s, first token 51.7 s |
| agent follow-up turn, first token | 48.2 s | 25.0 s |
| agent decode | 6.4 tok/s | 51.8 tok/s |

  The agent decode gains most because the prompt no longer pushes the decode's cached experts out of RAM. From the command line, an 8K document read in 73.7 / 75.7 s with the release and 28.3 / 28.4 s with this PR.
- **Linux is unchanged**, also with the variable set: `prompt_reads()` and the new branch in `generate.cpp` are Windows only.
- On Windows, a RAM budget together with `STRATA_PROMPT_DIRECT=1` (which `open_prompt_direct` used to refuse there) now opens the handles too; I have not tested that combination.
- NTFS serving unbuffered reads of a mapped file one at a time (the note in `read_direct`) still applies; on this drive (about 1.4-1.6 GB/s) the reads run near the drive's speed, which is far more than the page faults got. Not tested on a fast NVMe, where the default path is already much faster (#2791).
- Built and tested with CUDA on Windows only. The new code is Windows file I/O, not GPU code, but the HIP build on Windows compiles it too and I have not built HIP or SYCL.

pulls.title: perf(hip): enable wave32 head ops, MTP q8_mixed/HEAD_MIX_MULTI, and S2 <1> specialization
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR enables and optimizes several bitwise-identical paths across the MTP draft layer, the verify/draft head greedy sampler & top-probability kernels, the S2 grouped expert kernels, and the shared expert on RDNA HIP (`gfx1201`):

1. **Wave32 multi-block `argmax_rows` and `row_top_prob_split` on RDNA HIP (`src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`):**
   - `argmax_rows_kernel` and `row_top_prob_split_kernel` were previously compiled out under `#if !defined(__HIPCC__)`, forcing wave32 RDNA GPUs (`warpSize == 32`) onto the single-block `sampler_greedy_kernel<<<n_rows, 1024>>>` and `row_top_prob_kernel<<<n_rows, 1024>>>` (1..5 blocks total across 48 WGPs to scan 425 KB..4.97 MB of logits).
   - Guards the wave32 multi-block kernels with `#if !defined(STRATA_HIP_GFX906)` (keeping wave64 `gfx906` on the one-block kernels) and enables `multi_block_head_ops()` / `argmax_rows_wanted()` per device on HIP when `p.warpSize == 32` (`STRATA_MULTI_BLOCK_ARGMAX=0` and `STRATA_ARGMAX_ROWS=0` force them off).
   - Sets `kTopBlocks = 32` (`32` threads = 1 warp/block across 32 WGPs, avoiding intra-block `__syncthreads()` barriers when `blockDim.x == 32`) and adds `#pragma unroll 8` to the stride-1024 reduction loop in `row_top_prob_kernel` and `row_top_prob_split_kernel` (preserving exact per-thread summation order while overlapping 8 global loads in flight).
   - Enables the `verify_parity` target on HIP (`STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA OR STRATA_ENABLE_HIP`) and extends `verify_parity` with `copy_from_mapped_multi`, `quantize_q8_0_scaled`, and `--bench` checks.

2. **Fused HC `q8_mixed`, `STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI`, and shared-expert `x_q8_1` reuse in MTP and Verify (`src/core/mtp.cpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/shared_expert.cu`):**
   - Allows `fused_gr_read_multi` (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`) to write `q8_mixed` without a `q8_cnt` buffer when `qfuse_hc_local() && a[0].s_down == nullptr` (`gr_up_q32_kernel` and `gr_up_q8_q32_kernel` assign one warp per 32-column `q8_1` block and never touch `q8_cnt`).
   - Enables `STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI` by default on `gfx12` in `verify.cpp` and `mtp.cpp` (`STRATA_HEAD_MIX_MULTI=0` disables), replacing the 4-launch `gr_read` fallback on the MTP final mixer with `fused_gr_read_multi`.
   - Passes `q8_mixed = xq_ + t * (N / 32) * 36` to all 3 `fused_gr_read_multi` calls in `MtpDrafter` (`attn_hyper_connection`, `mlp_hyper_connection`, and `hyper_connection_mixer`) and to the final `output_hc_*` `fused_gr_read_multi` in `Verifier`, skipping redundant standalone `native_quantize_q8_1` launches when `fused_gr_read_multi` writes `xq_`.
   - Updates `shared_expert()` (`src/kernels/cuda/shared_expert.cu`) to honor `native->x_q8_1` (set by `MtpDrafter` when `q8_mlp && T == 1`), matching `shared_expert_multi`.

3. **S2 grouped expert `<1>` specialization, LDS-only barriers, and fused SwiGLU+Q8_0 on hit paths (`src/kernels/cuda/s2_expert_grouped.cu`, `src/kernels/s2_expert_grouped_parity.cpp`):**
   - Adds `s2_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`; `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx1030`/`gfx11xx`) for LDS-only staging barriers.
   - Adds `MAX_E = 1` template specializations `gu_grouped_t_kernel<1>` (`LDS = 3,200 B`, `VGPR = 85` vs `<8>`'s `LDS = 25,600 B`, `VGPR = 89`) and `down_grouped_t_kernel<1>` (`LDS = 800 B`, `VGPR = 47` vs `<8>`'s `LDS = 6,400 B`, `VGPR = 40`) dispatched when `cap_entries <= 16` (covering single-token MTP `T = 1, K = 10`).
   - Uses `swiglu_quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` in `moe_hit_grouped_s2`, `moe_hit_grouped_s2_dev`, and `moe_hit_grouped_s2_multi` when `fast && x_scales != nullptr && swiglu_q8_on()` (`STRATA_S2_SWIGLU_Q8=0` disables), matching `moe_grouped_s2`.

4. **Warp-per-block `quantize_q8_0_scaled` and `copy_from_mapped_multi` on HIP (`src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/elementwise.cu`, `src/core/mtp.cpp`):**
   - Enables the warp-per-block `quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel` on HIP (`STRATA_OLD_Q80_SCALED=1` restores the thread-per-block kernel).
   - Enables `copy_from_mapped_multi_kernel` on HIP (`STRATA_MTP_MULTI_COPY=0` restores individual copies) and uses `copy_from_mapped_multi` in `MtpDrafter::capture_round` and `MtpDrafter::capture_step`.

---

## End-to-End 397B Speculative Decode A/B (Radeon AI PRO R9700 `gfx1201`)
