pulls.title: perf(hip): optimize GDN verify kernels with LDS-only barriers and enable batched commit under STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Optimizes the Gated Delta Net (GDN) speculative-verify forward and commit kernels in `src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu` while preserving **100% bit-for-bit output and state parity**:

1. **Enable 2-launch batched `gdn_commit_layers` when `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` (`verify_kernels.cu:1073`):**
   - `gdn_commit_layers` previously checked `(sp && sp[0] == '1')` (`STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1`) and returned `false`, forcing `verify.cpp:2419` to fall back to **72 per-layer kernel launches** (`gdn_conv_commit` + `gdn_state_replay_kernel` across 36 GDN layers) instead of the 2-launch 36-layer batched commit (`gdn_conv_commit_layers_kernel` + `gdn_step_commit_layers_kernel`).
   - Because `gdn_step_commit_layers_kernel` and `gdn_state_replay_kernel` share the exact same `32 × 4` column-split state layout and `red[0..3][col_local]` reduction order, their committed states are **100% bitwise identical** (`gdn_parity` Section 6: 8 `n_keep` cases × 5 layers, 0 mismatches).
   - Notably, `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` is enabled by default on `gfx1151` (`Strix Halo`) in `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp`, so `gfx1151` was silently falling back to 72 per-layer commit launches on every verify window.
   - `STRATA_GDN_COMMIT_SPLIT=0` and `STRATA_DBG_GDN=1` remain available as explicit per-layer commit overrides, and `gdn_parity.cpp` now fails if `gdn_commit_layers` is unexpectedly skipped when neither override is set.

2. **LDS-only workgroup barriers (`vk_sync_lds()`) in GDN verify kernels (`verify_kernels.cu:37`):**
   - On RDNA4 (`gfx1200`/`gfx1201`) and RDNA3 (`gfx11xx`/`gfx1030`), `__syncthreads()` compiles to a full workgroup memory fence (`s_wait_loadcnt 0x0; s_wait_storecnt 0x0; s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12`), draining all in-flight global memory loads and invalidating the shader engine's L1 vector cache at every LDS synchronization point (4× per token in `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel`, 5× per token in `gdn_step_split_kernel`, 3× per token in `gdn_step_commit_body`).
   - Since inter-thread communication in `gdn_conv_l2_body`, `gdn_step_commit_body`, `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel`, `gdn_step_split_kernel`, `gdn_state_replay_kernel`, and `gdn_out_norm_kernel` goes strictly through `__shared__` memory (LDS), `vk_sync_lds()` uses `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12` and `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`/`gfx1030` (falling back to `__syncthreads()` on CUDA and other targets).

3. **Prologue state-load ordering and unified next-token prefetch in `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` (`verify_kernels.cu:328`):**
   - Issuing the 32 per-thread state loads (`s[0..31]`) before the initial `sk[0]`/`sq[0]` LDS store allows `vk_sync_lds()` at `t = 0` to overlap all 32 global state loads with the first barrier.
   - Unifying the `rg == 0` (`sk`) and `rg == 1` (`sq`) next-token prefetch under a single predicate (`load_kq`) overlaps the global load of token `t + 1`'s `k`/`q` and token `t`'s `v`/`z` with the 32-FMA `kv` and `o` loops while reducing register pressure by **4–7 VGPRs** across all four `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` instantiations.

4. **Double-buffered 3-barrier `gdn_step_split_kernel` (`verify_kernels.cu:417`):**
   - `gdn_step_split_kernel<true>` previously used single-buffered `sk[S]`, `sq[S]`, and `red[RG][GS_COLS]`, requiring **5 barriers per token** and stalling on `ht` global loads inside the barrier pair.
   - Double-buffering `sk[2][S]` and `sq[2][S]` with separate `red_kv[RG][GS_COLS]` and `red_o[RG][GS_COLS]` (LDS `1536 B -> 3072 B`, preserving full 16-wave / 4-CTA-per-WGP occupancy) reduces the loop to **3 `vk_sync_lds()` barriers per token** and overlaps next-token `k`/`q` global loads with the 32-FMA `kv` dot product.

---

## Root Cause & RED / GREEN Verification

On `origin/main` (`477ac13c`), running `gdn_parity` with `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1` skipped Section 6 (`gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit`) because `gdn_commit_layers` returned `false`. With the tightened assertion in `src/kernels/gdn_parity.cpp`:

- **RED (`origin/main` `verify_kernels.cu` + `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 ./gdn_parity`):**
  ```text
  gdn_ab_multi T=1..8 == fused_gdn_ab        bitwise (8 cases)
  gdn_step_norm_multi T=1..8 == single-token bitwise (47 cases)
  gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit      *** NO (unexpectedly skipped) ***

  gdn: 1 failures
  ```
- **GREEN (this PR + `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 ./gdn_parity`):**
  ```text
  gdn_ab_multi T=1..8 == fused_gdn_ab        bitwise (8 cases)
  gdn_step_norm_multi T=1..8 == single-token bitwise (47 cases)
  gdn_commit_layers == per-layer commit      bitwise (8 cases, 5 layers)

  gdn: 0 failures
  ```
- `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=0 ./gdn_parity`, `STRATA_GDN_COMMIT_SPLIT=0 ./gdn_parity`, `./verify_batch_parity --selftest`, `./spec_verify_parity`, and `./arch_defaults_test` all pass with 0 failures.

---

## Code Object Resource Usage (`gfx1201`, `llvm-readobj --notes`)

| Kernel (`gfx1201`) | `origin/main` (VGPR / SGPR / LDS / Spills) | This PR (VGPR / SGPR / LDS / Spills) |
|---|---|---|
| `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel<true, false>` | `89 / 32 / 6160 B / 0` | **`83 / 32 / 6160 B / 0`** (`-6 VGPRs`) |

pulls.title: STRATA_RAM_ADAPT: copy an incoming expert out of its stage buffer instead of a second file read
pulls.author: SanghunYun
pulls.body:
## Title STRATA_RAM_ADAPT: copy an incoming expert out of its stage buffer instead of a second file read Issue: follow-up to #1837 / #1838 (in main as d7298883) ## Summary On #1838 you measured no gain on the bench and a decode loss. We reproduced it on the `strata_bench.py` normal suite (short chat −3.4% with `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8`). The option only pays off once the RAM copy has followed a conversation for a while, and every move cost a file re-read on the decode thread (~0.77 ms, 8 moves per window), so a short request ended before the moves paid back. This change makes a move a memcpy out of the stage buffer the demand read just filled (~0.1 ms). Result: the short bench no longer loses (+3.2% decode, prefill unchanged), and the long sessions this option is for gain clearly: **+33.8% decode on 120 ShareGPT requests** and +19.2% on a 47-request session, with cumulative time down 23% / 13%. ## What changed - `src/core/expert_source.cpp`, `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `replace_resident_staged()` moves a pair when the incoming blob is still in a finished stage buffer; the buffer is held under `stage_mu_` during the copy; same Foresight hold and between-window checks as `replace_resident()`. Counter `ram_staged()`. - `src/program/generate.cpp`: the `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` loop tries the staged copy first for every ranked pair (up to one per layer per window); `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=` now caps only the pairs that still need a file read (1 is enough). Pair selection, thresholds and the stage buffers' size and reuse are unchanged; still opt-in. The stats line counts staged moves. - `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: a staged move writes the exact bytes, refuses an unstaged or invalid pair and leaves the other experts untouched (pinned and pageable). - `docs/DETAILS.md`: the `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` entry. ## Extra Notes v0.1.45 + this commit, RTX 3060 12 GB, IQ2_XS, 3769 VRAM expert slots, `--resident-budget-gib 20.5` (~74% of the experts outside the GPU), NVMe. Fresh process per run, `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=1`. Engine arguments and environment, identical in every run except `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` (unset for OFF, `1` for ON): ``` strata --serve --prefill auto:16384 --spec 3 --mtp-max-t 3 --spec-min-p 0.5 --suffix-draft 0 --max-context 131072 --kv k8v4 --pool-workers 7 --ple-io direct --greedy --stop-eos --stats --mmap-experts --mtp --prompt-cache-root 1024 --prompt-cache-every 0 --conversation-cache-min-free-mib 1280 --tail-role-token 8678 --conversation-cache-min-tokens 3072 --pack --native --expert-profile --resident-budget-gib 20.5 --expert-cache 4200 --vram-reserve-mib 768 --adapt-async 1 --conversation-cache-mib 1536 --conversation-cache-slots 3 --prompt-cache 2 STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1 STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=8 STRATA_STAGER_RING=32 STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=1 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB=0 STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=0 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7 CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY ``` `--expert-cache 4200` got 3769 slots; temperature 0; `serve/server.py` behind our local logging wrapper (the kit replays against plain `serve/server.py`). | Workload | Decode tok/s
OFF → ON | Prefill tok/s
OFF → ON | SSD expert reads / token
OFF → ON | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `strata_bench.py` normal suite (15 req., short) | 38.7 → 39.9 (+3.2%, no loss) | 446 → 445 (−0.2%) | 15.9 → 9.7 (−39%) | | ShareGPT, 30 conversations × 4 turns (120 req.) | 36.6 → 48.9 (**+33.8%**) | 119 → 142 (+19%) | 22.9 → 4.5 (−80%) | | English 47-request session (in the kit) | 43.7 → 52.1 (**+19.2%**) | 277 → 292 (+5%) | 12.6 → 0.9 (−93%) | Runs were OFF, ON, OFF; OFF in the table is the run after ON. The OFF run before ON gave 38.3 / 36.5 / 44.1 decode tok/s, within 1% of the one after. ![ShareGPT 120 requests: decode ms per token, SSD expert reads per token and cumulative time saved, OFF vs STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SanghunYun/Strata/ram-adapt-replay/charts/sharegpt120-cumulative.png) In the long session ON is faster from the first requests and stays there; the cumulative saving grows to 9% after 10 requests, 16% after 30 and 23% after 120. Paired per-request decode-time ratio (ON / OFF): ShareGPT 0.747 (95% CI 0.734–0.761), English 0.839 (0.819–0.861). One run per arm. With a RAM budget below the experts outside the GPU the #669 lend-region warning is printed in every run; that is the case this option is for. Replay: requests, the ShareGPT builder, replay/summary scripts and our per-request numbers are at https://github.com/SanghunYun/Strata/tree/ram-adapt-replay Tests: CUDA sm86 Release `file_expert_source_test --rotation-gpu` passes with the new case. HIP gfx1100 Release (ROCm 7.10): engine and test build and link, host-side `file_expert_source_test` passes; no AMD GPU inference.

pulls.title: Add a gfx1101 hipBLASLt table (RX 7800 XT, hipBLASLt 1.5.0): +14/+52/+72% prompt at 1K/8K/24K
pulls.author: durikim1-cpu
pulls.body:
`docs/AMD_HIP.md` says gfx1101 has no hipBLASLt table ("make one with Tuning table and compare the prompt speed with
and without it"). This adds one, calibrated on an RX 7800 XT with the hipBLASLt shipped in the 0.1.44.1 Windows HIP
package (version 100500), plus the measurements.

## What changes

- **Adds** `tools/hip/gfx1101-hipblaslt-100500.txt` (70 rows). Setup picks it only for a gfx1101 card whose installed
  hipBLASLt reports 100500, by the existing `hipblaslt_table()` file-name rule; no code changes.
- **Adds** `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rx-7800-xt-hipblaslt-100500/`: calibration method and script, per-row
  timings, launch configs and per-run prompt-speed data.
- **Edits** `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: the "gfx1101 has none" sentence and one entry in "Shipped tables".
- **Leaves alone**: the engine, setup, every other table. Other cards and other hipBLASLt versions are unaffected.

## Measured

Prebuilt Windows HIP engine 0.1.44.1, same `strata.exe` in both arms, only `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING` differs.
Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 32K context, fresh prompts, medians of 3:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s without → with | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,060 | 161.7 → 184.5 (+14%) | 28.2 → 29.7 | 6.60 → 5.79 |
| 8,041 | 335.1 → 510.8 (+52%) | 29.6 → 29.0 | 24.07 → 15.80 |
| 24,054 | 404.6 → 695.2 (+72%) | 29.9 → 29.2 | 59.51 → 34.67 |

Per GEMM against plain hipBLAS: median 6.45x, geometric mean 5.80x, 0.81x–15.9x; all 70 rows pass the upstream
accuracy and padding gates. Correctness set 11/12 in both arms (the same arithmetic question fails in both).

## How it was calibrated

The Windows package has no `tune_hipblaslt`, so the folder includes a ctypes port of `tools/hip/tune_hipblaslt.cpp`
that calls the packaged DLLs unchanged and applies the same gates. Geometries: the 16 of `gfx1100-hipblaslt-100500.txt`
at T = 8192 / 6144 / 4096 / 1024, plus `f16 1280 2560 1280` at T = 64…8192. No solution id is copied from another GPU.

## Not checked

- `fallbacks=0` with `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_VERBOSE=1` (the summary line was not captured) and the HIP ctest
  (`hip_prefill_hipblaslt_gemm`); the prebuilt Windows package has no test binaries.
- Linux, other 1.5.0 builds (solution ids may be numbered differently), Flash-Next with only the table changed.
- One row (`bf16 1 2560 1 T=1024`) is 0.81x of hipBLAS (hipBLASLt 0.0327 ms vs hipBLAS 0.0266 ms). I kept it because the end-to-end runs
  used the full table; happy to drop that geometry's rows if you prefer.

I can run any extra check you want on this card.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RX 7800 XT (gfx1101), Windows 11, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS (0.1.41 release + private file-cache A/B)
pulls.author: durikim1-cpu
pulls.body:
Measured on 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-18 by durikim1-cpu on one native-Windows desktop. As far as I can see this is the first **Windows** report from a **gfx1101 / RX 7800 XT** card in `bench/results` (an earlier Linux validation of this card is #254 in `docs/AMD_HIP.md`). It has two parts, and they must not be read as one before/after pair:

- **A. Strata 0.1.41 as released** (prebuilt Windows HIP engine), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 64K context, fresh prompts of
  about 1K / 8K / 24K / 60K tokens, three runs each.
- **B vs C. A private build, same binary, one opt-in switch off/on.** A same-day A/B of a Windows file-read change
  (`STRATA_R6_FILE_READ_CACHE`, proposed separately in an issue) at a 60K fresh prompt, three runs each.
  **This build is not a Strata release**: it is 0.1.44.1 with local changes, listed below.

Main limitations: one machine, one model, mostly one long-prompt length for the A/B; desktop apps were open during the
runs; GPU clocks, driver and PCIe link were not captured per run; part A and part B/C differ in date, engine, KV type and
RAM budget, so the A→C difference is a history, not the effect of one change.

Results-only submission, no engine changes.

  (`STRATA_R6_FILE_READ_CACHE`, proposed separately in an issue) at a 60K fresh prompt, three runs each.
  **This build is not a Strata release**: it is 0.1.44.1 with local changes, listed below.

Main limitations: one machine, one model, mostly one long-prompt length for the A/B; desktop apps were open during the
runs; GPU clocks, driver and PCIe link were not captured per run; part A and part B/C differ in date, engine, KV type and
RAM budget, so the A→C difference is a history, not the effect of one change.

Results-only submission, no engine changes.

---

pulls.title: docs(bench): dual PCIe V100 layer split with same-engine single-card control (0.1.44.1)
pulls.author: noahark
pulls.body:
Dual-GPU layer split on two PCIe V100-class cards, measured **against the same engine on one of the same cards** — same suite, same day, n=2 per arm. The community has dual-GPU reports on DDR4 hosts (#1300, #1028) but no same-machine single-card control, so the true split gain was not separable from the platform before; this fills that gap and adds a `--pipeline-windows 2` arm on NVIDIA (opt-in there), plus the first Windows + Volta (sm_70) dual-GPU datapoint we know of.

Two things beyond the split itself are in here: a **long-context follow-up** (256K native / 512K / 1M on both tiers, H1 probes to 1.01M tokens) and a short **daily-use section** with the numbers this box turns in outside the suite — including the restart-to-restart variance that matters when benchmarking a two-node Windows machine.

## Machine
2x Tesla PG500-216 32 GB (V100-class, 1,132 GB/s HBM2), PCIe 3.0 x16 each (Gen3 x16, current = max), TCC; dual Xeon E5-2696 v3, 128 GB DDR3L-1600 (2 NUMA nodes, 2 processor groups of 36); Windows 10; official prebuilt cuda12 engine **0.1.44.1** for the split report, **0.1.45** for the long-context and daily-use sections.

## Headline numbers (decode tok/s, 4.3K-doc leg)

| | 1x | 2x split | 2x + `--pipeline-windows 2` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| IQ3_XXS (262K) | 77.0 | 108.6 (1.41x) | **129.0 (1.67x)** |
| UD-IQ4_XS (131K) | 40.0 | **79.1 (1.98x)** | - |

- Caches after the split (auto, K=24): **24,576 / 24,576 pairs (100%)** on XXS, **~99.8% of the routed mass** on UD — the DDR3L host stops mattering for decode almost entirely.
- UD gains more than XXS: its 4-bit experts are the biggest per-token host traffic, so the single card was the most host-bound.
- H1 probe (n! trailing zeros) correct in **17/17 runs** across all arms.
- With the caches full: the `--pcie-frac` sweep is flat 0→1 (92.3-92.4 tok/s), and the single-card UD tier's 20% pool-workers sensitivity disappears.
- **`--pipeline-windows 2` on NVIDIA: +15-19% on the XXS tier** (above), with an H1 short-prompt read at 21 ms. On the **Q6 tier** the same switch cost **5%** in the 0.1.45 follow-up — both with the draft layer on the last card and with `STRATA_MTP_STAGE0=1`. Opt-in on NVIDIA and clearly tier-dependent: treat the +15-19% as an XXS number, not a general one. Peak 62/60 C at the 250 W limits.

## Contents
- `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-2x-pcie-v100-ddr3l/` — README with the full method, the paired table, thermals, a **daily-use** section and 12 raw result JSONs (both rounds of every arm) plus `summarize-dual-0144.py`.
- `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-2x-pcie-v100-longctx/` — **follow-up (0.1.45):** 256K/512K/1M ladders and H1 probes on the same split.
- `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md` — index rows (one per folder).
- `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` — a Measured subsection with the paired table.

## Follow-up added 2026-10-19: how far the context goes on the split (engine 0.1.45)

Same machine, same two cards, two tiers. One restart per context form; ladders from `bench-ctxdecay256.py`
(30-paragraph document, 400-token structured summary) and the H1 probe from `h1-deep.py` (the question is asked
after a 245K-990K-token document, answer checked for `8090`).

Decode tok/s by depth (the 4.3K-leg column is the same suite as above, on 0.1.45):

| Tier / context form | 4.3K leg | 64K | 194K | 258K | 517K | 712K | 1.02M |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q6_K_XL, 256K native | 43.6 | 42.3 | 41.4 | **40.7** | — | — | — |
| Q6_K_XL, 512K (YaRN x2) | — | 30.3* | 40.9 | — | **36.6** | — | — |
| Q6_K_XL, 1M (YaRN x4) | — | — | 36.0 | — | 39.0 | — | **34.5** |
| IQ4_XS, 256K native | 82.8 | 65.9 | 59.4 | **58.8** | — | — | — |
| IQ4_XS, 512K (YaRN x2) | — | 47.0* | 52.9 | — | **49.2** | — | — |
| IQ4_XS, 1M (YaRN x4) | — | — | 53.1 | — | 50.3 | 45.7 | **41.0** |

\* first point after a fresh start: warm-up contaminated (the engine swaps the adaptive expert tier in).

- **256K native is the sweet spot.** Q6 is flat 42.3 → 40.7 (-3.8%) over 64K-258K; IQ4_XS 65.9 → 58.8 (-11%),
  and its loss is front-loaded (16K-128K costs 13%, 128K-258K only 2% more).
- **YaRN costs ~11-13% inside the trained window.** At ~194K: Q6 41.4 native vs 40.9 (x2) vs 36.0 (x4);
  IQ4_XS 59.4 vs 52.9 vs 53.1. So the 1M form is only worth it for prompts that need it.
- **Both tiers reach 1M without OOM**: Q6 34.5 and IQ4_XS 41.0 tok/s at 1.02M tokens, i.e. -15% / -30% against
  the same tier's 256K-native figure. Prefill stays 707-2,272 tok/s across all ladders (long prompts amortize).
- **IQ4_XS is 1.2-1.6x faster than Q6 at every depth**, and both pass H1: **6/6 correct up to 1.01M tokens**
  (Q6 and IQ4_XS at 245K / 507K / 1.01M), so recall does not decay with depth in this range.

## In daily use on this box (added 2026-10-19)

What it looks like outside the suite, on the same split:

- **A long answer**: 1,665 tokens at **44.1 tok/s** on Q6 with the expert cache at 96.5% hit (1,500-token
  answers: 38.4-45.5 tok/s by run, draft acceptance 57-62%).
- **The CPU is not the wall**: both sockets together burned ~**39.5 cores** during that decode, i.e.
  **0.9 core-seconds per output token**. Forcing `--pool-workers 9` (default is 35) cost **13%** of decode
  while CPU use fell to ~9 cores — the rest is spin waiting. On a dual-socket host this is the cheapest way
  to buy power and fan noise back.
- **Three conversations at once** (`parallel: 3`): **67.1 tok/s aggregate = 1.41x** one stream (23 tok/s each),
  reproducible. `--batch-mtp --batch-groups 1` does run the slot drafters (`MTP proposals accepted 933 of
  1463 (63.8%)`) but aggregates **63.6 tok/s** — 5% below the pipelined default on this tier.
- **Restart-to-restart variance**: same binary, same config, four restarts, 3x800-token probes: **43.9 / 45.5 /
  47.4 / 48.0 tok/s**. The two high runs put the expert arena on NUMA node 0, the two low ones on node 1
  (**+6.7% for node 0**), with the workers pinned across both processor groups either way. Worth recording
  which node the arena landed on (or averaging two restarts) when benchmarking this class of machine.

**If we built this again**: the cores are not what the split is limited by — `--pool-workers` 9 and the default
35 landed within 13% of each other, and during decode the CPU is ~39.5 busy cores of which most is spin. What we
would shop for next is VRAM and PCIe x16 slots (a single socket delivers both, without the two-node landing
variance above), not more CPU.

## What we are not claiming
The split's gain is measured on this host and this engine only; the 1M numbers are one run per point and the
first point of each ladder is warm-up contaminated. No needle test, no quality suite beyond H1, and no
single-card arms in the long-context folder (the parent folder is the same-machine control for the split).

Same platform family as our earlier single-card reports in #617 / #1355 (the DDR3L host whose decode sat at 33-42 tok/s single-card on the prebuilt-engine generations). Happy to run follow-ups (a third card when it arrives, `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP`, batching variants) if useful.

pulls.title: [Other] Read conversation-cache log backlogs without dropping events
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Issue #3048 can drop earlier conversation-cache events when more than one MiB arrives between monitor polls. The observer now advances through a captured end of file in bounded chunks, commits only complete lines, and retains a partial line for the next poll.

## Related discussion

Fixes #3048.

## Approach

- Replace the last-MiB seek with bounded sequential chunks in `serve/server.py`.
- Commit the byte cursor only through complete lines so interrupted writes and read errors retry safely.
- Add local backlog, chunk-boundary, interrupted-read, and local HTTP regression coverage in `serve/test_cache_log_backlog.py`.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `90ca8acc79242e18f954e71a4c570a4ee8887f41` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_cache_log_backlog.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.
 `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog` (7 tests); `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_server serve.test_prometheus` (357 tests, 3 skipped); `python -m py_compile serve/server.py`; `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:** Red reproduction used `git restore --source=e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211 -- serve/server.py`, then `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_backlog`, then `git restore --source=HEAD -- serve/server.py`. The test ran 7 tests and failed 8 assertions, covering lost early events, chunk crossings, partial-line retry, and local `/metrics` catch-up.

**Not run:** Native backend builds and real GPU/model tests. Only Python observer code changed. The Python 3.14.3 test environment had no Ruff; the separate Python 3.12.7 lint comparison above completed successfully.

## Limits

One poll may process a large accumulated backlog; each underlying read remains bounded by `READ_MAX`. Validation used local file fixtures and a local MockEngine HTTP server; it did not use a real engine or a production service.

pulls.title: [Other] Synchronize cache metrics after completed recovery clears
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Issue #3047 can leave the Monitor conversation-cache current values stale after either completed non-finite-logit recovery clear message. The observer now recognizes only the two completed engine messages and resets `parked` and `bytes` while preserving cumulative cache history.

## Related discussion

Fixes #3047.

## Approach

- Add strict full-line recognition for the two completed recovery-clear messages in `serve/server.py`.
- Reset only the current cache values, leaving eviction, park, restore, and last-event history unchanged.
- Add local file and local HTTP regression coverage in `serve/test_cache_log_clear.py`.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `bc1a4e54b722d985c9205542bfc4fe17226d7987` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_cache_log_clear.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.
 `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_clear` (4 tests); `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_server serve.test_prometheus` (357 tests, 3 skipped); `python -m py_compile serve/server.py`; `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:** Red reproduction used `git restore --source=e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211 -- serve/server.py`, then `python -m unittest serve.test_cache_log_clear`, then `git restore --source=HEAD -- serve/server.py`. The test ran 4 tests and failed 8 assertions, including the local `/metrics` fixture retaining stale cache values.

**Not run:** Native backend builds and real GPU/model tests. Only Python observer code changed. The Python 3.14.3 test environment had no Ruff; the separate Python 3.12.7 lint comparison above completed successfully.

## Limits

The parser intentionally accepts only complete known engine recovery messages. Validation used local file fixtures and a local MockEngine HTTP server; it did not use a real engine or a production service.

pulls.title: ngram: avoid draining nonexistent reads after initialization failures
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Title

Resolves #3045

## Summary

`PleReader::open()` can block forever during cleanup before submitting any reads: slab allocation failure publishes a nonzero slot count with no free slots, and failed reopen inherits the previous slot count after close cleared the free slots. Both paths wait for completions that cannot exist. Failed initialization now returns the existing error, closes the file and permits a later valid open.

## What changed

- Publish `max_inflight` only after the slab and free-slot list are initialized.
- Reset `max_inflight` when closing the reader.
- Add a Linux CPU-only lifecycle test with caller-thread and I/O-worker cases. Link-time `posix_memalign` wrapping injects a one-shot ENOMEM without adding production fault-injection settings. CTest timeouts turn the former hangs into bounded failures.

Successful row reads, page-straddling rows, close with outstanding reads, repeated close and read-after-recovery are covered. The I/O scheduling, cache, kernels, row bytes, defaults and public API remain unchanged.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0; isolated branch from directly fetched upstream main `477ac13cbe8e582c20484871ce459d20d82df09d`.

- CMake CPU build with `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON` and `STRATA_WERROR=ON`: built `ple_reader_lifecycle_test` and `direct_file_async_test`.
- CTest: all 7 selected tests passed (6 lifecycle cases and existing DirectFile async test). Successful reads are compared byte-for-byte against an independent fixture pattern.
- Compiled the same lifecycle test against unchanged upstream: both normal-read controls passed; allocation and reopen cases timed out after 2 seconds in both caller and threaded modes (4 timeouts).
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Extra Notes

Draft; no review requested. AGENTS.md requires builds of every affected backend before review. Full CUDA/HIP/SYCL engine builds have not been run; HIP and SYCL compilers are unavailable here. Windows runtime behavior and real model inference were not tested. These are injected/API error-path tests, not a measured production memory-pressure incident.

Searched open issues and PRs. #2991 concerns temporary-file collisions in another selftest; #2623 concerns prefetch matching. This change addresses initialization bookkeeping only.

pulls.title: artifact: reject invalid tensor bounds and architecture failures in --check
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Title
Resolves #3043

## Summary
`strata-gguf --check` returns success after an architecture failure, and unsigned gap/byte arithmetic can accept a tensor outside the file or a tensor whose byte count overflows. These cases now return status 1.

## What changed
- Use the existing overflow-safe `tensor_payload_bytes()` helper and check file bounds before subtracting an offset in the standalone CLI.
- Return status 1 when the architecture guard fails.
- Add a CPU-only CTest invoking the actual CLI entry point on nine synthetic cases: valid input, inspection-only behavior, unsupported/missing architecture, wrapped and ordinary out-of-file offsets, overflowing byte count and truncation.

Inspection without `--check`, the reader API, inference code, GPU kernels, unknown-type reporting and the existing padding bracket are unchanged.

## Validation
Linux x86_64, GCC 14.2.0, upstream base `477ac13c`:
- CMake build with `STRATA_WERROR=ON`: strata-gguf, gguf_cli_test, gguf_reader_test, gguf_split_test, gguf_geometry_test and model_family_test.
- CTest: all five selected tests passed.
- The new test against unchanged upstream fails for unsupported/missing architecture, wrapped offset and overflowing byte count.
- Old/new executable comparison: identical exit codes, stdout and stderr bytes for a valid file with `--check` and three inspection-only fixtures.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Extra Notes
No model inference, Windows runtime or CUDA/HIP/SYCL engine builds were run. The changed production source is the standalone host-only CLI target; GPU backend sources are untouched. Searched open issues and PRs; #2288 and #2475 address different readers.

pulls.title: [Other] Exclude refused batch admissions from completion metrics
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A request refused by every BGEN slot returns HTTP 503, but its history row is still (finish, prompt_tokens, prompt_read) = (length, 51, None), and successful completion/token/latency metrics include it. This fix records an error history row with zero processed prompt tokens and excludes this pre-admission rejection from successful completion and latency totals. The regression also checks Retry-After, Prometheus metrics, slot cleanup and a later successful request.

## Related discussion

Closes #3040. This is an accounting follow-up to #1994; admission and retry policy stay the same.

## Approach

Classify GpuBusy as a pre-admission refusal only when no DONE segment has settled and no output token was emitted. Preserve accounting for settled or partly generated work.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_parallel.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 21 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- Windows, Python 3.12.7: `python -m unittest serve.test_parallel.ParallelService.test_bgen_refused_for_good_is_a_retryable_503_and_frees_the_slots -v` — 1 passed on `23a4f428d78655b92b05048620570465469533b1`.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_parallel serve.test_prometheus -v` — 48 tests, passed; final test result `OK`.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_parallel.py` and `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211...HEAD` passed.

**Failed:**
- Expected red baseline: with exact upstream `serve/server.py` at `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta), the same focused test fails: `('length', 51, None) != ('error', 0, None)`. No candidate test failure observed.

**Not run:**
- Real model generation, CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds or hardware execution. This patch touches only Python server code and its CPU fake-engine tests.

## Limits

Fresh Python processes and loopback HTTP prove the server accounting behavior, not native engine admission or model quality. No runtime default is changed.

pulls.title: [Other] Serialize conversation-cache log polling
pulls.author: oscarlius
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Concurrent `/metrics` readers could read the same conversation-cache log range and replay an event. This change serializes access to the shared log cursor, so direct and HTTP metrics readers count each event once.

## Related discussion

Closes #3039.

## Approach

Guard the existing log-poll operation with the cache object's lock and add direct-reader and local loopback `/metrics` concurrency regressions. Cache parsing and native inference behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `04796fa0427beaa6b8628d6e2ab914c7059ca8c0` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- `python -m unittest -v serve.test_monitor serve.test_prometheus` — 18 tests passed.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py`.
- `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

**Failed:**
- With the exact base production file restored, the direct concurrency test replayed the park event twice. The initial two-test run also had one environment error before the local `regex` dependency was installed. The subsequent fresh loopback HTTP `/metrics` red test failed as expected with `(parks, restores) = (2, 0)` instead of `(1, 0)`.

**Not run:**
- No GPU, native backend, model download, or hardware inference test.

## Limits

The proof covers concurrent Python readers, the repository mock engine, and a local loopback HTTP server. It does not exercise a real model process or hardware runtime.

pulls.title: bench: community report, Radeon 890M (gfx1150) on 0.1.45: the shipped hipBLASLt table's A/B and the 17 exact switches' identity check
pulls.author: zeriyoshi
pulls.body:
## Title
bench: community report, Radeon 890M (gfx1150) on 0.1.45: the shipped hipBLASLt table's A/B and the 17 exact switches' identity check

Issue: Follow-up to #1395 (and #1217)

## Summary

The two measurements asked for in #1395, on 0.1.45 (`477ac13`), Radeon 890M, AMD TheRock ROCm 7.14.1 for gfx1150
(hipBLASLt 100401). Results only, no engine change.

1. **The shipped table** (`tools/hip/gfx1150-hipblaslt-100401.txt`, as 0.1.41+ ship it) against plain hipBLAS: prompts
   read **1.54x / 1.72x / 1.74x faster** at 1K / 3.6K / 7K tokens, decode unchanged.
2. **The 17 exact switches** (gfx1151's exact defaults less `STRATA_HCD_EXACT`, the set `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1150=1`
   writes since #2147), all off against all on: the greedy token ids of 10 short prompts plus a 4K and a 20K prompt are
   **12 / 12 identical** on two models.

## What changed

- `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-gfx1150-0.1.45/` (new)
  - `README.md`: the rig, the method, the results and what was not tested
  - `runs.csv`: every run of the table A/B (13 runs)
  - `identity.csv`: every case of the identity check (sha-256 of each case's token ids, times, draft acceptance)
  - `calibrate.json`: `tools/calibrate.py`'s output on this machine
  - `strata-gfx1150.json`: the server config the runs started from
  - `scripts/strata_ident.py`: the identity check (starts the engine directly and saves the generated token ids)
- `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`: one row for the new folder (the PR column reads `-`)
- `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`: one entry for the new folder

## Measurements

**1. The shipped table against plain hipBLAS.** GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, the 17 switches on both sides, a server restart per
run (cold prompt cache), one request at a time, the engine's own `strata serve: prompt` timings. Five rounds of the two
arms with the order alternating (H T, T H, ...) and the prompts of the 2026-10-07 README (a short chat three times, then
fresh document prompts of about 1K, 3.6K and 7K tokens); a third arm with `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` in the first three rounds
for reference.

| Prompt | plain hipBLAS | table | table + `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` (3 rounds, reference) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 987-989 tokens | 95.4 tok/s | 147.0 (1.54x) | 152.2 |
| 3,562-3,564 tokens | 128.5 | 221.5 (1.72x) | 254.3 |
| 7,009-7,010 tokens | 132.8 | 231.6 (1.74x) | 277.2 |
| decode, short chat | 15.2 | 15.2 | 15.2 |

Medians; every round gave the same order and the spreads are within ±1.5%. Every table run logged
`prefill gemm: hipBLASLt tuning enabled (144 rows, gfx1150, version 100401)`.

**2. Identity check of the 17 switches.** `ATTN_LANECELL CVEC_FUSE EXPERT_V2 GDN_CONVL2 GDN_HEAD GDN_NOY GDN_PP=2
GDN_SPLIT LFUSE MMVF_ROWS PF_PAD PLE_BATCH Q6_PACKED Q8_PACKED QFUSE SH_STREAM TSUM` (all `STRATA_`), all off against all
on, both sides with the table and without `STRATA_HIP_WMMA`. The engine is started directly (`serve.server.StrataEngine`,
as `tools/calibrate.py` does); greedy, no thinking, MTP on, one request at a time in a fixed order: 10 short prompts
(128 tokens out), then a 4,024-token and a 20,024-token prompt (this checkout's `docs/*.md`, 64 tokens out). The
generated token ids are compared.

| Model | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS | off, on, off, on | 12 / 12 identical off against on (both pairs), and each side identical to its repeat |
| OrcaRouter Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored IQ3_XXS | off, on | 12 / 12 identical |

- The HIP ctest suite with the 17 set in the environment (and the table): the same results as without them (only
  `ple_parity` fails, as always: it needs `bench/micro`)
- Speed from the same runs: decode +0-3%, the 20K prompt +2-4%

**3. `tools/calibrate.py`** run by hand on this machine (setup does not offer it on AMD) finds nothing over its 3% bar:
every expert is in the GTT pool, so the PCIe share is flat. `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` measured +2% and `--spec-min-p 0.7`
+1.2%.

## Extra Notes

- Machine: MINISFORUM N5 PRO, Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370, Radeon 890M (gfx1150, 16 CUs), 96 GB DDR5-5600, GTT 70 GiB;
  Proxmox VE 9.2 with kernel 7.0.14-24-pve, the engine in an unprivileged LXC container; engine 0.1.45 built by hand with
  `-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1150`. ctest: 71 of 75 pass (the README lists the skips and the failure).
- `--kv-grow` reports "off" on HIP because `src/core/vmm.cpp` has no HIP path (`vmm_available()` is false);
  `docs/DETAILS.md` lists its conditions without saying it is CUDA only.
- Not tested: KL or task quality (`STRATA_HIP_WMMA` changes bits and is not part of the identity check), other ROCm
  versions (#2147's `gfx1150-hipblaslt-100500.txt` was not tried), setup itself (the configs are hand-written with the
  same `env` that setup writes), identity-check prompts past 20K tokens.
- **The identity check compares the generated token ids, not dumps.** If your gate needs more before the 17 switches can
  be a gfx1150 default (the 4K / 20K residual or first-window logits dumps, for example with `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`,
  your own prompt set, longer prompts or other models), let me know and I will rerun it on this machine.

pulls.title: [Engine] conversation snapshot: stage parked-state copies through pinned memory on Windows/WDDM
pulls.author: denis-1337
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #3036

## Problem and result

On Windows/WDDM, parked-conversation snapshot copies at `--max-context 262144` are refused or corrupted: the engine logs `checkpoint save: conversation snapshot running-state copy: invalid argument`, and every later request returns non-finite (NaN) output. After this change the synchronous snapshot copies are staged through a real pinned buffer, and the same workload runs clean on the same rig.

## Related discussion

#3036 (reproduced on 0.2.0-beta and 0.1.45). Bug fix, no defaults changed. Review feedback from @midhatn applied in the second commit.

## Approach

All synchronous running-state copies in `conversation_state.cpp` are staged first through a pinned 16 MiB buffer (device→pinned via the copy engine, pinned→destination via memcpy), because on Windows/WDDM the HIP runtime misclassifies C++ heap destinations as pinned host memory: the direct copy is refused, or when accepted it interleaves with expert H2D streaming on the copy engine and corrupts the bytes (decode then reads garbage as expert weights and the grouped GEMM writes NaN). The save call also passes the copy direction explicitly instead of relying on pointer classification, and the sticky `invalid argument` is consumed and retried once. `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0` restores the old path for A/B. Linux is unaffected (the direct path works there; staging is harmless). Cost: one memcpy hop per snapshot copy; measured decode unchanged (~55 tok/s).

## Validation

Tested on `main` @ e88ee39d (0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3), Windows 11 Pro build 26300, AMD RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), driver 32.0.32015.2008, model IQ3_S, `--kv int8 --max-context 262144 --expert-cache auto --spec 4`, tuning table `tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`. The rebased branch file is byte-identical to the file built and tested here.

**Passed:**
- Official 0.2.0-beta install (prebuilt engine 0.1.45), 11 unique ~1.5k-token prompts via `serve/server.py` (park-unique script): `OK=0 ERR=11`, 43 non-finite events — bug reproduces on 0.2.0-beta.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d, unpatched, same script: `OK=0 ERR=11`, nf=43 — bug present in the 0.2.0-beta source.
- HIP build of `main` @ e88ee39d + this patch, same script: 2/2 rounds `OK=11 ERR=0`, 0 non-finite.
- Production constellation (same config, port 1234): 22/22 requests OK, 0 non-finite since engine start, prompt-cache reuse active, decode ~55 tok/s.
- On 0.1.45 (same rig, same scripts): baseline rounds nf=35/41/17 → patched 5/5 rounds nf=0; tuning-table constellation also clean.

**Failed:** none observed with the patch applied.

**Not run:** CUDA, SYCL and Metal builds — no CUDA/SYCL toolchain and no Apple hardware on this machine. The change uses only the CUDA-shaped API already used in this file (`cudaHostAlloc`, `cudaMemcpyAsync`, `cudaStreamSynchronize`, `cudaFreeHost`); it compiles and runs on hardware under HIP. CUDA compilation stays unverified. The `cudaHostAlloc` failure path and the stream-sync failure path are inspection-only (no fault injection), as noted by @midhatn in review.

## Limits

Staging adds one memcpy hop per snapshot copy (a few ms per parked conversation). `STRATA_CKPT_STAGE_FIRST=0` restores the old path for A/B. The misclassification itself lives in the WDDM/HIP layer; this PR avoids it on the checkpoint path rather than fixing the classification.

Note: this issue and the accompanying PR were prepared by an AI agent (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, served by Strata itself) together with the account owner.

## Problem and result

After a refused conversation-cache park, the Monitor and `/metrics` could retain a prior occupancy. This change records only the remaining count where the refusal establishes it, marks unknown bytes and cumulative evictions as unknown, and hides occupancy bars until a later authoritative event.

## Related discussion

Closes #3033.

## Approach

Parse physical-pressure, minimum-length, and other refusal log lines in the server observer. Add regression coverage for log replay, the local loopback `/metrics` endpoint, and the Monitor card. The native cache policy and inference paths are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta); tested candidate `8d0a488f5a4ba8c06afae70f1739121345bcbab0` on Windows, Python 3.14.3. Each test command starts a fresh local process.

**Passed:**
- `py -3.12 -m ruff check --output-format json serve/server.py serve/test_monitor.py` (Ruff 0.2.1): 10 existing diagnostics, same as unmodified main; zero new diagnostics.

- `python -m unittest -v serve.test_monitor serve.test_prometheus` — 24 tests passed.

- `node --check serve/web/app.js`.
- `git diff --check e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211..HEAD`.

pulls.title: fix(Metal): the prompt path no longer kills the engine on prompts > 6…
pulls.author: DarkJoll
pulls.body:
fix(Metal): the prompt path no longer kills the engine on prompts > 64 tokens

Addresses #2671 - the Metal failure reported there (same machine family, M1 Max 64 GB; the
follow-up comment's diagnosis, `!m.borrowed` inside `Prefill::relayout`, matches what I measured).

## What this changes

On Metal, every prompt over 64 tokens kills the engine, in two ways:

1. a ~1.6k-token prompt: `lending the prompt path its slots failed: ... at most 0`, exit 1
   (the guard inside `Prefill::relayout`, as #2671 diagnosed);
2. a 10,797-token prompt: the read completes, then SIGABRT `a copy touches a device allocation
   of 21298.5 MB that was given back` inside `ExpertCache::fill_slot_queued`, exit -6. The Metal
   arena purges host allocations >= 32 MB (`metal/src/engine/window.cpp` `stream_arena` ->
   `purge_device_allocations(32<<20)`), and the post-read refill writes into that purged region
   through the slots the lend loop marked.

One root cause under both: on Metal the prompt's buffers live in the Metal arena (`window_ensure`),
not in the host region the host code believes it is borrowing, and the Metal window never reads the
host residency table. So the relayout has nothing to re-layout, and the lend has nothing to lend.

- `Prefill::relayout`: on Metal, a successful no-op that keeps the larger chunk count (the Metal
  buffers never shrink; a large `chunk()` is one `run()` per segment).
- the `lend` lambda: the slot-marking loop is guarded out, so `p.lent` stays empty and the refill
  after the read is a no-op instead of writing to purged host memory. `p.lent_chunk = want_p` stays.

## What this leaves alone

Every added line is inside a `STRATA_GPU_METAL` / `!STRATA_GPU_METAL` guard: the CUDA / HIP / SYCL
branch is the untouched pre-fix source, byte-identical by construction. The startup line "the prompt
path borrows N CUDA0 cache slots" still logs (cosmetic on Metal) and the sizing arithmetic is
untouched. No new flags, no behaviour change on any other backend.

## How I checked

Apple M1 Max 64 GB, macOS 27.0, engine 0.1.45-metal, test arena 8 GB (`STRATA_METAL_ARENA_GB=8`):

- pre-fix repro, both modes, deterministic: ~1.6k-token prompt -> "at most 0" exit 1;
  10,797-token prompt -> "given back" SIGABRT exit -6.
- post-fix: 4,643-token prompt -> prefill 85.3 tok/s, 512 tokens generated at 9.3 tok/s, engine
  alive after; 10,797-token prompt -> prefill 179.8 tok/s, 512 generated at 6.9 tok/s, engine alive
  after. Log over both: no "given back", no "at most 0", no lending error. `/health`: loaded.
- `ninja -C build-metal` full build 0 errors; `ctest` 1/1 (`runtime_hello`); `gr_parity` ALL PASS
  (prepared planes bitwise, rel-L2 <= 3.4e-08 on the rest); `prompt_parity` ALL PASS.

**Not checked:** the CUDA / HIP / SYCL builds cannot be compiled on a Mac (no toolchains). Per
AGENTS.md a build per backend is the check before merge; the guard makes the non-Metal branch the
untouched source, but I cannot claim the builds, only the construction.

## Numbers on the shipping configuration

Same machine, the default run (`run-iq3_s.sh`, IQ3_S, expert arena ~32.5 GB, 256K context):
prefill ~220 tok/s, decode ~20 tok/s, and long prompts complete with the engine staying up. These
are read off the server's own logs during normal use, not a controlled benchmark; the 8 GB-arena
numbers above are the controlled ones (the small arena is what makes its prefill slower).

pulls.title: docs: add a Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151) deployment guide
pulls.author: HaiYunChuang
pulls.body:
## What this adds

`docs/STRIX_HALO_WINDOWS.md`, a companion to `docs/STRIX_HALO.md` for the Windows
path. `STRIX_HALO.md` documents the Linux build and the release notes mark the
Windows one as untested on a Strix Halo; this document records a working Windows
deployment on the same hardware, with measured numbers and the traps that cost
time.

## Why

The Windows HIP build has carried gfx1151 code since 0.1.40, but no Windows
configuration was documented. Three findings are worth having in writing:

- `--mmap-experts` is the single biggest lever on Windows: the default resident
  expert arena pins 46.84 GiB into host memory, which WDDM counts against the
  process GPU budget, leaving 2.25 GiB free and squeezing the expert cache to 320
  slots (28.0 tok/s). Dropping the arena for mmap over the GGUF shards takes the
  cache to 24,576 slots and decode to 37.7 tok/s (+35%).
- `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0`: the switch is on by default on gfx1151 and pays on Linux,
  but costs 13% here on Windows (34.1 -> 39.6 tok/s), matching issue #816.
- `--kv-streaming` is a `setup` option, not an engine option, and KV streaming is
  not usable at 128K on this machine at all while `--mmap-experts` is available.

## Impact

Documentation only; no code or engine change. Windows Strix Halo users get a
configuration that reaches about 40 tok/s on IQ3_S (39.6 Chinese, 42.3 English)
at 128K, within a few percent of the Linux reference (42.8 in `STRIX_HALO.md`
section 6), and 34.0 tok/s at the model's native 256K context.

## What was checked

- Every number is a median of three runs on one machine, and the doc names the
  engine build for each row (0.1.41 for the tuning rows, 0.1.45 for the context
  and version rows).
- The 0.1.43 -> 0.1.45 upgrade was A/B'd and changes nothing here (34.0 against
  32.6), consistent with the release notes: the default speed-ups in 0.1.42 and
  0.1.43 are CUDA and RDNA4 only, and 0.1.45 states it did not run on Windows.
  gfx1151's default switch count does go from 17 to 18, the addition being
  `STRATA_TOPK_REG_MIN_BLOCKS`.
- The 128K -> 256K change was A/B'd back to back: 32.6 at 256K against 30.8 at
  128K, i.e. flat, with the expert cache unchanged at 24,576 slots and about
  1.8 GiB of VRAM taken by the KV. 262,144 is the native trained length, so no
  rope scaling is involved.
- `not measured` is used wherever a value was not taken rather than estimated.
- Section 3.5 lists two upstream gfx1151 switches (`STRATA_PF_F16`,
  `STRATA_REFILL_PARTS`) and the remaining Linux-tuned defaults as leads that were
  not confirmed: the first A/B attempt was invalidated by page-cache drift (the
  engine restarts took 57 s, 70 s and 141 s to fill the expert cache), so they are
  listed as open rather than claimed.

pulls.title: setup: --skip-gguf-sha256, for a model file that is another build of the model setup pins
pulls.author: iMilnb
pulls.body:
## What this adds

One opt-in setup flag: `python setup.py --skip-gguf-sha256`. With it, `verify_sha256`
compares neither the pinned size nor the pinned SHA-256 of the model files (GGUF shards
and the mmproj), warns with the size on disk next to the pinned size and the pinned
hash prefix, and keeps the file instead of deleting it. Without the flag the default
path is byte-identical to v0.1.45.

## Why

We often want to run a variant of a model Strata officially supports instead of the
pinned repository file: for example huihui-ai's
[Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated-v2-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated-v2-GGUF)
instead of unsloth's [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)
(the same model, refusal answers edited out, re-sharded: same architecture, so the
engine runs it, but neither the file sizes nor the hashes match the pins in `setup.py`).
Today setup deletes such a file and stops, and the only workaround is editing
`verify_sha256` out of `setup.py` by hand. Same symptom from #2635 and #2346, where a
repository moved its file after the pin was taken; see also #1979 and #2842.

## What it leaves alone

- The ready-made engine keeps its own separate switch (`STRATA_SKIP_SHA256`,
  `check_engine_digest`); neither one implies the other, and a test pins that.
- `check_shards` still reads the GGUF headers, so a truncated or incompatible file is
  refused even with the flag.
- A skipped file's `.done` mark records `sha256 skipped (N bytes)`, so a later run
  without the flag hashes it again and re-arms the normal check.
- ModelScope's published-hash check, the Vulkan SDK archive and `metal/setup_mac.py`
  keep verifying as before (the Mac path does not take the flag yet).

## How I checked

- New tests in `tools/test_setup_unsloth.py`: the skip accepts a different build and
  keeps the file, skips the hashing, re-hashes a mark from an earlier skipped run, and
  `STRATA_SKIP_SHA256=1` alone does not relax the model-file check; one end-to-end test
  shows the flag reaching every pinned model file (`main()` with `--skip-gguf-sha256`).
- All 41 `tools/test_setup_*.py` suites pass on this branch, except
  `test_setup_engine_hash` (2) and `test_setup_golden` (8), which fail identically on a
  clean `477ac13c` in the same checkout (verified with the branch's changes stashed).
- Docs: one line in `docs/INSTALL.md` and the `docs/DETAILS.md` option list, plus a
  `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` entry for "setup says a model file has the wrong SHA-256,
  or the wrong size" that spells out the two separate switches.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GiB (Windows 11, 32 GB RAM), Q2_0, engine 0.1.45
pulls.author: hqlhqlhqlhql
pulls.body:
bench: community report, RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GiB (Windows 11, 32 GB RAM), Q2_0, engine 0.1.45

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-rtx-4060-laptop-gpu-qwen3-8-flash-next-q2-0/`: the README the
suite wrote, `results.json` per request and the engine log excerpt. I added a "Notes from the author"
section for the build's provenance, what was not tested, the long-context figures below, and one
measurement the suite does not cover. Nothing else in the tree is touched.

Why it may be useful: **this is the smallest VRAM tier in `bench/results` so far** — there is no single
8 GiB card (the smallest existing entry is a 12 GiB RTX 3060, then 16 and 24 GiB), and 8 GiB is the tier
where the expert cache holds about 9% of the (layer, expert) pairs. `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` also asks for
"a host with 32 GB of RAM or less" because "the expert file tier and the resident mode depend on how much
of the model fits in RAM"; this is such a host (31.7 GiB), on Windows rather than Linux.

Suite medians (3 runs each, temperature 0, thinking off, the install's own configuration):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | **30.5 tok/s** (22.9-44.1, n=9), first token 1.10 s |
| 4K fresh prompt | **220.1 tok/s**, first token 18.33 s |
| 16K fresh prompt | **220.4 tok/s**, first token 72.97 s — no decay from 4K to 16K |
| agent session, follow-up turns | decode **23.1 tok/s** (7.3-33.7, n=15), first token 16.21 s, conversation-cache hit 68.6% |

**Long context, from daily use rather than the suite** (the suite stops at 16K). This install also runs an
agent client against the same Q2_0 server; its engine log covers ten days and 1,932 requests with thinking
on and the client's own sampling, so it is not the suite's protocol:

- the longest prompt carried **113,621 tokens** (112,781 reused from the conversation cache + 840 read) at
  99.5 prompt tok/s, and generated 3,175 tokens at 24.5 tok/s decode
- 88 requests with a 64K-120K prompt: prompt median 47.0 tok/s, decode median 24.0 tok/s
- 27 requests above 96K: decode median 23.9 tok/s, i.e. no decay against the 21.2 tok/s median of the
  1,072 requests above 32K
- the longest single generation was 64,879 tokens (from a 649-token prompt) at 16.2 tok/s

So context is not what limits this machine: the KV cache keeps 20,480 of 131,072 cells per QSA layer in
VRAM with about 0.84 GiB in pinned RAM, and the conversation cache reuses most of a long prompt.

The one thing I would look at: decode here tracks how much of the expert set fits in RAM when the server
starts. Same box, same model (Flash-Next IQ2_XS), same settings, two runs on the same day: a RAM
complement of 10.53 GiB of the 31.03 GiB the VRAM cache does not hold (34%) gave a decode median of
15.5 tok/s; 16.93 GiB (55%) gave 21.6 tok/s. Only the free RAM at startup differed (a clean boot versus a
session with other work loaded).

Not tested in the suite: prompts above 16K (covered above from daily use), `--clients` concurrency,
vision, a layer split, a long soak, and any non-Windows host.

Note: the suite needed two local fixes to `tools/strata_bench.py` to run here (`port` never assigned; the
`CMakeLists.txt` read without an encoding on a Windows whose ANSI code page is not UTF-8). Those are the
sibling pull request; the measurements are unaffected.

pulls.title: perf(hip): optimize EXPDEC routed-expert kernels and enable by default on gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Optimize the grouped native routed-expert decode kernels (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`) for RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`), enable `EXPDEC` (`expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel` on `Q2_0`) by default on `gfx12`, and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP builds.

### Changes

1. **Fix HIP `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` wave-occupancy mapping on `expdec_gu_kernel` (`src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`)**:
   - On CUDA, `__launch_bounds__(256, MINB)` specifies `MINB` blocks per SM (`4` blocks = $\le 64$ registers). On HIP (`amd_hip_runtime.h`), the second argument of `__launch_bounds__(max_threads, min_blocks)` maps directly to `amdgpu_waves_per_eu(min_blocks)` (waves per SIMD, not blocks per WGP). Since a 256-thread CTA has 8 waves = 2 waves/SIMD on RDNA3/RDNA4, `MINB = 4` requested only 4 waves/SIMD (allowing up to 256 VGPRs), so `expdec_gu_kernel<16..18, 1, 4>` compiled to **`222–223 VGPRs`** on `gfx1201` (capping occupancy at 6 waves/SIMD = 3 CTAs/WGP instead of 8 waves/SIMD = 4 CTAs/WGP).
   - Map the second `__launch_bounds__` argument to `MINB * 2` on HIP (`8` waves/SIMD for `MINB = 4`), dropping `gfx1201` register usage to **`171–187 VGPRs`** (`0` spills, $\le 192$ VGPRs = **4 CTAs/WGP** across `IQ2_XXS`, `IQ2_XS`, `IQ3_XXS`, and `IQ3_S`).

2. **Vectorize `ed_stage_entry` in `expdec_gu_kernel` and `expdec_down_kernel`**:
   - Previously, `ed_stage_entry<XB, HALVES>` looped over `w = tid; w < XB * 9; w += 256`, executing 3 integer divisions by 9 (`w / 9`), 3 intra-warp divergent `if (j == 0)` branches, and 3 scattered 4-byte `ds_store_b32` stores per thread per staged entry.
   - Because `XB <= 80 <= 128` (`ED_XB = 80`, `ED_HB = 20`), map the 256 threads directly as 128 thread-pairs `(k = tid >> 1, h = tid & 1)` where each active pair loads one 16-byte half-block (`int4`) and writes a single 16-byte `ds_store_b128` to `s_u`, while `tid < XB` writes `s_ds[c * XB + tid]` with zero loops, zero `/ 9` divisions, and zero intra-warp branch divergence.

3. **LDS-only barriers (`iq_sync_lds()`) and elided first-pass pre-staging barriers**:
   - Add `iq_sync_lds()` (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on other HIP targets, `__syncthreads()` on CUDA) in `stage_iq_grid`, `native_down_multi_kernel`, `expdec_gu_kernel`, and `expdec_down_kernel`, avoiding `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` L0 vector-cache invalidations and global load-queue drains (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0`).
   - Guard the pre-staging barrier inside `for (int e = e0; e < e1; ...)` with `if (g > (int) blockIdx.y || e > e0) iq_sync_lds();` so the first pass (`g == blockIdx.y && e == e0`, which covers all `T <= 4` decode groups when `gridDim.y == cap_groups`) skips a redundant barrier.

4. **Enable `EXPDEC` (`STRATA_EXPDEC=1`, `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=1`) by default on `gfx12` and enable `expdec_bench` on HIP**:
   - Default `expdec_on()` and `expdec_down_on()` to `1` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`expdec_default_gfx12()`) when `STRATA_EXPDEC` / `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` are unset (`STRATA_EXPDEC=0` or `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=0` turns them off; non-`gfx12` architectures remain unchanged).
   - Gate `expdec_note` stderr logging on explicit `STRATA_EXPDEC=1`.
   - Enable the `expdec_bench` target on HIP builds in `CMakeLists.txt` and map `cudaDevAttrMemoryClockRate` / `cudaDevAttrGlobalMemoryBusWidth` in `include/strata/hip_compat/cuda_runtime.h`.
   - Extend `iq_multi_parity` (`check_grouped`) to verify bitwise equality of both `multi` (`EXPDEC=0`) and `expdec` (`EXPDEC=1, EXPDEC_DOWN=1, EXPDEC_D20=1`) against the reference per-entry kernels across all format pairs.

---

## Validation & Benchmarks (`gfx1201`, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700)

### 1. Bitwise Parity & Multi-Arch Compilation
- `./build-copilot-hip/iq_multi_parity`: `0 failures` across all 18 `iq_mmvq` checks, 24 `native_expert_grouped` checks (testing both `multi` and `expdec` against `old`), and 3 `q8_1 finite` checks.
- `./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 18/20,21/20,22/20,18/42,21/42,22/42 def,dec,dec:w1 real`: `identical` (`0 choice comparisons differ`) across all 6 format pairs and `T = 1..4`.
- Multi-architecture compile check: verified clean compilation on AMD HIP (`gfx1100`, `gfx1151`, `gfx1200`, `gfx1201`) and NVIDIA CUDA (`sm_75`, `sm_89`, `sm_100`).

### 2. Cold Routed-Expert Microbenchmark (`./build-copilot-hip/expdec_bench 150 0 20 ...`, 150 reps $\times$ 5 rounds over 121–186 MB cold expert pools)

| Format Pair (`gu/down`) | `T` | Baseline `def` (`all / gu / down`, us) | `gfx12` Default `EXPDEC` (`all / gu / down`, us) | Total Speedup | Phase Speedup |

pulls.title: native_dense: STRATA_HC_Q8 uploads only the stage's own Q8_0 rows on a trimmed layer split
pulls.author: havok2-htwo
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none found (searched "HC_Q8"). Related: #2427, a different leak on a split, in other lines.

## Summary
On a layer split with `--trim-stage-weights` (or `STRATA_STAGE_TRIM=1`) and `STRATA_HC_Q8` on, the loop in `src/core/native_dense.cpp` that attaches the GGUF's Q8_0 hyper-connection rows does not skip other stages' layers. A trimmed stage still has their table entries (metadata only), so every trimmed card uploads the Q8_0 rows of all 48 layers and reads only its own: 0.63 GiB per card on the rig below, 0.15-0.18 GiB with this change.

## What changed
`src/core/native_dense.cpp`, +2 lines: the loop skips a tensor when `outside(name) || !in_range(name)`, the filter the upload loop above it uses. `in_range` does the work here (stage trim sets it through `set_layer_range`; the bf16-pack quantize loop below already checks it). No value changes: each stage reads the same rows as before.

It applies only where all three hold: `STRATA_HC_Q8` is on (setup writes `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` for CUDA UD-* installs; HIP gfx12 turns it on by default), stage trim is on, and the `--native` GGUF itself stores Q8_0 hyper-connection rows (the UD-* files). A bf16 pack's rows come from the quantize loop, which already filters. CUDA0 is trimmed only with an explicit `--layer-split`; the later stages are also trimmed under `auto`, because their weights load after the split search. Without stage trim, `set_layer_range` never runs and `in_range` passes every layer, so nothing changes: the code path is the same, and with the fix and no trim each card still loads 0.63 GiB (I did not run 0.1.45 without trim, and the no-trim tokens are not compared).

## Extra Notes
Measured on 4x RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), CUDA 13.0, setup.py release flags, v0.1.45 (`477ac13c`) with and without this commit. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS (`--native` GGUF + pack), `--layer-split 12,25,37 --resident-experts --expert-cache auto --expert-profile <profile> --prefill 512 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <draft> --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 28672 --ple-io ram --batch 16`; env `STRATA_HC_Q8=1 STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1 STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1 STRATA_NAN_GUARD=0` (the last one turns off a default). All experts are resident in the two trimmed arms; without trim 87 %.

| | trim, 0.1.45 | trim, + fix | no trim, + fix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `STRATA_HC_Q8=1: ... GiB` (engine line), CUDA0/1/2/3 | 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 | 0.16 / 0.18 / 0.16 / 0.15 | 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 / 0.63 |
| free before the expert cache, GiB, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 16.01 / 16.27 / 16.43 / 15.25 | 16.60 / 16.85 / 17.02 / 15.86 | 12.86 / 13.13 / 13.19 / 11.92 |
| expert cache slots, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 6144 / 6656 / 6144 / 5632 | 6144 / 6656 / 6144 / 5632 | 5240 / 5691 / 5557 / 4835 |
| free with everything loaded, MiB, CUDA0/1/2/3 | 1507 / 1601 / 1707 / 1805 | 1325 / 1403 / 2319 / 1639 | 411 / 507 / 507 / 285 |

Free VRAM before the expert cache goes up by 0.58-0.61 GiB per card, a little more than the 0.45-0.48 GiB drop in the engine line. That line counts payload bytes only; I did not look into the difference. On this rig the expert cache already holds every profiled pair, so the slot counts stay the same. The freed VRAM changes what the prompt path borrows instead: on 0.1.45, CUDA0/1/3 lend 324-348 cache slots each to the prompt path and 2.27 GiB of RAM is pinned for them; with the fix every card keeps its own prompt buffers (0.75 GiB each) and nothing is pinned. Those own buffers are new allocations, while the loan reused cache slots, so CUDA0/1/3 end 0.16-0.19 GiB lower with everything loaded, and CUDA2, which had no loan, ends 0.6 GiB higher.

Tokens: `tools/batch_test.py --batch 16 --n 16 --max-new 128 --keys temperature=0 --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000"`, with the same expert cache on every card in both trimmed arms. 0.1.45 vs fix: solo 16/16 and batch 16/16 identical, and in both arms every slot matches its own solo run. Batch throughput is the same: 236.3 vs 236.4 tok/s; I took no other speed measurement. The no-trim arm has a smaller cache, so its tokens are not compared.

#2427 drops the bf16 copies on a split; this change drops other stages' Q8_0 copies. They change different lines. I did not run them together.

**Not tested:** only CUDA sm_86 was built and run. I have no ROCm, SYCL or Metal toolchain here, so the HIP and Metal builds of this file were not compiled. The two lines only call `outside` and `in_range`, which the same function already calls, so they add no code a backend could fail on. That still leaves the AGENTS.md build rule open, so this stays a draft until someone builds it for HIP. On HIP gfx12 with a UD-* GGUF and stage trim, this should lower VRAM in the same way under the default; the per-card `STRATA_HC_Q8=1: ... GiB` line on an R9700 split would confirm it. The SYCL copy of this loop (`sycl/src/core/native_dense.cpp`) gets the same filter in #2810, so this PR leaves SYCL alone. Also not run: long prompts (the tokens check is 16 short prompts, 128 new tokens, and the prompt path's buffers changed), 2- or 3-GPU splits, `--layer-split auto`, `--keep-canonical`, `STRATA_HC_Q8_INJECT=1`, bf16/GSQ packs, other models.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 5090, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 512K YaRN, parallel 2
pulls.author: steve8697
pulls.body:
## What this is

Results only, for one PC. No engine change.

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 32 GiB, driver 617.42, power limit 402.50 W, PCIe gen 4 x16 while busy. The desktop is not on this GPU (`display_active` Disabled).
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X. Installed RAM about 93.7 GiB. OS: Windows 11.
- Strata 0.1.45, commit 477ac13c, release engine CUDA 13.0.
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S. Context 524288 with YaRN factor 2 (`yarn-orig-ctx` 262144). KV int8, 32768 resident. `parallel` 2 (`--batch` 2). Expert cache auto (this start: 10038 slots / 19.05 GiB). `--vram-reserve-mib` 700, left there even though startup suggested more. Conversation cache 16384 MiB / 4 slots. `--pcie-frac` 0.35, `--spec` 4, `--spec-min-p` 0.50, `--adapt-swaps` 160. Thinking off for every measured request.

Folder: `bench/results/2026-10-18-community-rtx-5090-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-s/`.

## What was measured

The official suite (`tools/strata_bench.py`: chat, 4K, 16K, 32K, agent session, 2 short clients) and a long-context extension at about 64K, 128K, 256K, and a full-window prompt of about 511K tokens (the word-list estimate aimed at 523976 and landed short of that). Three runs where the process finished them. Fresh prompts, restored prompts, and two prompts at once are separate rows. Speeds are the engine's timings. A needle check covers 128K, 256K, and 480K at depths 10 and 90. All six were found.

## Limitations worth reading before quoting a number

- A cache hit is a restore in the engine log plus at least 90% of the prompt reused, after both slots were flushed. An immediate resend is not used as the cached condition.
- At 64K and 128K the single-request restore works (time to first token about 0.18 s and 0.26 s). The cached pair restored only one of the two prompts. The restored request decoded at about 33 tok/s with no draft accepts while the other request reread the prompt. That cell is not two cache hits.
- The full-window snapshot was refused on a fresh process: `skip parking (physical RAM admission; need 8243 MiB plus 2560 MiB floor, 9377 MiB available)`. The 16 GiB conversation-cache setting is not the check that fired. The resend read the prompt again.
- The same full-window length inside the long process decoded at about 26 tok/s with 0 draft accepts. A fresh process, with about 193 draft accepts, decoded that length at 180 tok/s (and 236 tok/s on the reread). Those are different rows.
- Two long prefills ran one after the other. The slower time to first token is queueing, not batched decode. There is no parallel-1 arm. YaRN is on for the short rows as well as the long ones.
- `--vram-reserve-mib` stayed 700. Startup reported 119 MiB of VRAM free and suggested a higher reserve.

`long_matrix.py` in the folder is the extension. The official suite is the repository's own tool.

pulls.title: [Other] tests: test_setup_golden pins the core count the golden output depends on
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

`setup.py` derives the CPU vision encoder's threads from `os.cpu_count() // 2`, so `tools/test_setup_golden.py`'s golden output moved with the machine it ran on: the golden baseline PC has 12 cores (6 threads), and on any other core count the golden comparison failed.

After: the test mocks `os.cpu_count` to the baseline PC's 12 cores, so the golden output is stable on every machine. Test-only change, no setup.py change.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note.

### Approach

Mock `os.cpu_count` to 12 in the golden test's fixture, matching the baseline the golden file was recorded on.

### Validation

Passed, rebased on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`): `python tools/test_setup_golden.py` → 4/4 OK, exit 0. Windows 11, Python 3.15, no GPU needed.
Not run: CI.

### Limits

Test-only; the mock pins the value the golden file was recorded with, it does not change how setup derives threads on a real machine.

pulls.title: [Other] tests: test_winjob reads tasklist in the console's OEM code page (#2331)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

Two gaps in `serve/test_winjob.py`:

1. On a non-English Windows console the test decoded `tasklist` output as text, and the console's OEM code page mangled it (#2331).
2. `TestNoThrottle` was defined after `unittest.main()`, so `python serve/test_winjob.py` ran only 2 of the 3 classes; the module form ran all 3.

After: the test reads `tasklist`'s bytes in the console's OEM code page, and the `main()` call sits at the file end, so the file form runs 3/3 like the module form already did. Test-only change.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note. #2331 is the OEM code-page report this fixes.

### Approach

Read `tasklist` output as bytes and decode with the console OEM code page; move `unittest.main()` to the file end.

### Validation

Passed, rebased on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`), Windows 11 (German locale), Python 3.15:

- `python serve/test_winjob.py` → 3/3 OK, exit 0.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_winjob` → 3/3 OK, exit 0.

Not run: CI; English-locale consoles (the OEM decode is locale-independent by construction).

### Limits

Test-only; no change to the job-object code under test.

pulls.title: [TUI] serve: keepawake primes its daemon before the first acquire (a fast request could miss the hold)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

`serve/keepawake.py` starts its daemon thread lazily. A request that finishes before the thread exists (acquire then release, a fast request) lost the transient `count > 0` transition, so the machine-sleep hold never engaged: the server answered the request and the PC could sleep mid-session.

After: the loop signals it has entered and `acquire` waits for that, so the first acquire can no longer race the thread start. Same root cause as the test-side fixture in #1901, fixed in the runtime.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note. #1901 fixed the same race on the test side.

### Approach

The daemon loop sets an "entered" event as its first act; `acquire` waits for that event before counting, so the count>0 transition is always observed.

### Validation

Passed, rebased on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`): `python -m unittest serve.test_keepawake` → 6/6 OK, exit 0. Windows 11, Python 3.15; no real power API called.
Not run: real suspend/resume on battery; CI.

### Limits

Windows keepawake path only; the fix adds a startup handshake, no change to the power API calls themselves.

pulls.title: [Engine] build: pin CMP0169 OLD around FetchContent_Populate (CMake 4.4 warns on every configure)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

CMake 4.4 warns on every configure: `FetchContent_Populate` is deprecated (CMP0169). Strata uses the populate-then-`add_subdirectory` form on purpose — it keeps ggml's binary dir at the `STRATA_GGML_DIR` one; `FetchContent_MakeAvailable` would move it, and its `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` needs CMake 3.28, above the project's 3.24 floor.

After: `CMP0169` is pinned to `OLD` around the populate call (guarded for CMake < 3.30), so the warning is gone and the layout stays as it is today. Checked by `tools/test_fetchcontent_policy.py`.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; rebased on main and re-verified per the reset note.

### Approach

`cmake_policy(SET CMP0169 OLD)` scoped around the `FetchContent_Populate` call in `CMakeLists.txt` and `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`, guarded so CMake < 3.30 (which has no CMP0169) is untouched.

### Validation

Passed, on 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d` is the base; branch commit `b14ff320`), Windows 11, CMake 4.4.0: `python tools/test_fetchcontent_policy.py` → 3/3 OK, exit 0.
Not run: a full CUDA/HIP engine build in CI; CMake < 3.30 (the guard path).

### Limits

Policy pin only — no build-layout change; the configure output is otherwise byte-identical.
