pulls.title: perf(hip): tune RDNA4 QSA prompt WMMA path (STRATA_HIP_WMMA stays opt-in)
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Optimizes the HIP `int8`-KV QSA prompt-attention matrix-core kernel (`prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` in `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu`).

**`STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` remains opt-in on every architecture (`gfx12` and `gfx11` included).** While this PR's changes inside `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` are **100% bitwise identical** to `main`'s `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>` (`NEWHASH` `2c5cab7eb6601f66` / `deb4f727fbac41af` / `2d10cd9d6d1fd5b5`), the matrix-core path itself differs in its last bits from the default FP32 fallback (`qsa_decode_attn_batch`) due to `FP16 hi + lo` splitting and reduction order. Keeping `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` out of `arch_defaults.cpp` preserves the exact-only policy of `arch_default_env("gfx1201")` and avoids process-wide enablement on `gfx11` stages in mixed-GPU runs.

1. **LDS-only workgroup barriers (`pa_sync_lds`):**
   - Replaces the `__syncthreads()` barriers inside `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel` (which synchronize only LDS `S`) with `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12` and `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11` (generic `__syncthreads()` elsewhere), avoiding the `s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0` global-load drain and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` L0 vector-cache invalidation emitted by generic `__syncthreads()` on `gfx12`.
2. **Global-load / WMMA overlap (`fetch` K-before-V + deferred FP16 scale conversion + post-`q·K` V staging):**
   - Keeps `k_scale` and `v_scale` in raw `uint16_t` registers (`Chunk::ksc_u16[2]`, `Chunk::vsc_u16`) during `fetch()` and converts them via `u16_scale()` (with an empty `asm volatile("" : "+v"(u))` barrier on AMDGPU) only at their point of use after the `q·K` WMMAs, preventing LLVM from hoisting `v_cvt_f32_f16` into the conditional global-load blocks and forcing an early `s_wait_loadcnt 0x0`.
   - Issues the `K` global loads before the `V` global loads in `fetch()`, and moves LDS `V` staging (`S.v` / `S.vs`) inside `chunk()` to *after* the `q·K` WMMAs, so `V` global loads stay in flight while the matrix cores compute `q·K`.
3. **Vectorized 32-bit LDS `V` gather + in-register DPP byte transpose (`dpp_tr4`) + VALU wave butterfly reductions (`pa_xor_u32` / `pa_xor_f32`):**
   - Replaces the 64 scalar 1-byte `ds_load_i8` reads per wave per chunk in the `p·V` loop (`S.v[warp][cb + i][d]`) with 16 aligned 32-bit `ds_load_b32` reads (`*reinterpret_cast<const uint32_t*>(&S.v[warp][cb + 4 * q4 + qs4][j * 16 + qm4])`) followed by an in-register 4×4 byte transpose across the 4 lanes of a hardware DPP quad (`dpp_tr4`: `__builtin_amdgcn_mov_dpp` quad_perm `0xb1` / `0x4e` + `__builtin_amdgcn_perm`).
   - Replaces `__shfl_xor_sync` in the `q`-max, row-max, row-sum, `row_x16`, and `V`-scale reductions with VALU lane permutations (`pa_xor_u32` / `pa_xor_f32`: `mov_dpp` quad_perm `0xb1`/`0x4e` for masks `1`/`2`, `permlane16` for `4`/`8`, `permlanex16` for `16`), avoiding `ds_bpermute_b32` traffic through the LDS pipe and cutting `gfx1201` register pressure from `191` to `168` VGPRs (`SPLIT=true`) and `160` to `147` VGPRs (`SPLIT=false`) with `0` spills (`SmemW` remains `21,648 B`).

---

## The change

Three files changed vs `main` (`477ac13c`) at `f9b11142`:

- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu` (+110/−38):
  - Adds `pa_sync_lds()`, `dpp_tr4()`, `pa_xor_u32()`, and `pa_xor_f32()` inside `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`.
  - Updates `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT>`: raw `uint16_t` scales (`Chunk::vsc_u16`, `Chunk::ksc_u16[2]`) + `u16_scale()`, K-before-V global loads in `fetch()`, V slice staged into `S.v`/`S.vs` after the `q·K` WMMAs in `chunk()`, `pa_sync_lds()` barriers, `pa_xor_f32()` butterfly reductions, and aligned 32-bit `S.v` loads + `dpp_tr4()` in `p·V`.
  - `SmemW` layout is unchanged (`uint8_t v[4][WCH][WVS]` with `WVS = 80`, `21,648 B` total).
- `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp` (+2/−0):
  - Comment-only note documenting why `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` is intentionally excluded from the `gfx12` default table.
- `src/core/arch_defaults_test.cpp` (+14/−1):
  - Asserts `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` is absent from `arch_default_env` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, clears all seven `gfx12` env vars (`STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS`, `STRATA_HIP_WMMA`, `STRATA_GDN_HEAD`, `STRATA_GDN_PP`, `STRATA_GDN_CONVL2`, `STRATA_GDN_NOY`, `STRATA_CVEC_FUSE`) before asserting `apply_arch_defaults("gfx1201").size() == 5`, and verifies that `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` stays unset by default while an explicit `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` is preserved.

---

## Evidence

All runtime measurements below were taken on commit `f9b11142` vs `main` (`477ac13c`) on an uncontended AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`, 32 GB, `strata.service` stopped).

### 1. ELF Resource Usage (`llvm-readobj --notes`)

| Target | Kernel | VGPRs (`main` → this PR) | SGPRs (`main` → this PR) | LDS (B) | Spills |

### 2. Kernel Microbenchmark & Parity: `hip_prompt_attn_wmma` (`main` @ `477ac13c` vs this PR @ `f9b11142`)

1 warmup pair + 5 interleaved pairs of separately built `hip_prompt_attn_wmma` binaries (`main` vs `f9b11142`). On HIP, `hip_prompt_attn_wmma` sets `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` in `main()` and times `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<true>` against the FP32 fallback (`qsa_decode_attn_batch`) and an FP64 host reference.

Output FNV-1a checksums (`NEWHASH`) of `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<true>` are **100% bitwise identical** between `main` and `f9b11142` across all three shapes (`FAILURES: 0`):

| `ctx 2100, 256 q` | `0.742, 0.748, 0.742, 0.743, 0.738 ms` (**`0.742 ms`**) | `0.589, 0.590, 0.595, 0.606, 0.590 ms` (**`0.590 ms`**) | **`-20.5%` (`1.26×`)** | `8.89×` (`5.25 ms`) | `2d10cd9d6d1fd5b5` (exact) |

### 3. End-to-End 397B `--serve` Prefill A/B (`Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-IQ3_S`, 60 Layers / 12 QSA Layers, `T = 4096`)

Measured via `strata --serve --kv int8 --prefill 4096 --prompt-cache 0` with `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1`, `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`, `STRATA_DENSE_MMQ=1`, `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1`, `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` (`1` warmup + `3` rotated-token trials per arm on idle `gfx1201`):

- **HIP (`hipcc` / Clang 22.0.0):** Compiled `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu` cleanly across `--offload-arch=gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1103,gfx1151,gfx1200,gfx1201` with `0` register spills.
- **CUDA (`nvcc` 13.4):** Compiled `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu` cleanly across `-gencode arch=compute_75,code=sm_75` (Turing), `-gencode arch=compute_89,code=sm_89` (Ada), `-gencode arch=compute_100,code=sm_100` (Blackwell), and `-gencode arch=compute_120,code=sm_120` (Blackwell).

---

## What this does NOT fix

- **Last-bit rounding difference vs the FP32 fallback (`STRATA_HIP_WMMA=0`):** While this PR is **bit-for-bit identical** to `main`'s `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` implementation (`2c5cab7eb6601f66` / `deb4f727fbac41af` / `2d10cd9d6d1fd5b5`), the matrix-core path splits FP32 `q` and `p` into `FP16 hi + lo` pairs (`2.64e-06 .. 3.57e-06` vs FP64, compared to `1.78e-06 .. 2.13e-06` for the FP32 fallback). For that reason `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` remains opt-in on every architecture.
- **No RDNA3 runtime measurement on this host:** `gfx11` compiles cleanly (`235` VGPRs for `SPLIT=true`, `177` VGPRs for `SPLIT=false`, `0` spills), but no RDNA3 hardware runtime measurement was taken on this host.
- **Does not change `--kv k8v4` prompt attention:** `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel` applies to `--kv int8` (`pools.k_q4 == nullptr && pools.v_q4 == nullptr`).

---

## Test plan

- [x] `arch_defaults_test` passes (`OK`, `gfx12` table = 5 exact switches, `STRATA_HIP_WMMA` opt-in)
- [x] `hip_prompt_attn_wmma` passes all 3 shapes (`FAILURES: 0`) with identical `NEWHASH` checksums to `main` on `gfx1201`
- [x] Uncontended 5-pair interleaved `hip_prompt_attn_wmma` A/B against `main` (`-16.7%`, `-16.7%`, `-20.5%`)
- [x] End-to-end 397B `--serve --kv int8` 4K prefill A/B (`qsa attn` `105 → 87 ms`, `-17.1%`; total prefill `1,414.2 → 1,397.6 ms`)
- [x] Multi-arch HIP compile check (`gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1103,gfx1151,gfx1200,gfx1201`)
- [x] Multi-arch CUDA compile check (`sm_75`, `sm_89`, `sm_100`, `sm_120`)
- [ ] CI

---

## Reproduction

```sh
cmake -B build-hip -DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1200;gfx1201" -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build-hip --target arch_defaults_test hip_prompt_attn_wmma strata -j
./build-hip/arch_defaults_test
./build-hip/hip_prompt_attn_wmma 32768 2048 5
```

pulls.title: Community benchmark: Apple M4 Pro (48 GB), Flash-Next Q2_0, 262K context streamed from SSD
pulls.author: ipriyaaanshu
pulls.body:
## Summary
Community benchmark report for the Apple Silicon Metal engine on an **Apple M4 Pro with 48 GB unified memory** — a configuration the docs list as untested (the MAC.md measurements stop at a 32 GB M4 mini and an M5 Max).

- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Q2_0** (the only size 48 GB fits), **262,144-token context**, experts streamed from SSD (setup's automatic choice + the `.experts` one-request-per-expert copy, `--mmap-experts`, expert cache 64 slots, `--spec 2`).
- Suite: `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1), 3 runs per test, engine-own timings, medians with ranges.

## Results (medians)
| Test | Value |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | **26.0 tok/s** (23.0-26.8), TTFT 1.35 s |
| 4K fresh prompt | 247.4 tok/s, TTFT 16.3 s |
| 16K fresh prompt | 280.4 tok/s, TTFT 57.3 s |
| 32K fresh prompt | 280.2 tok/s, TTFT 114.4 s |
| agent session | 68.7 % conversation-cache hit, 5 re-read tokens/session, 24.4 tok/s in-session |

Headline decode lands between the docs' 32 GB M4 mini streaming figures (~14 tok/s) and the M5 Max resident figures (108-120) — on the memory-bandwidth-limited part of the curve, as expected for an SSD-streamed pack on an M4.

## Notes for reviewers
- Engine 0.1.45-metal built **from source** (no ready-made Mac binary exists); upstream HEAD did not compile for Metal without local fixes — details are in the report's *Contributor notes* section (missing Metal-compat shims for #2666's new API, and a stale generated `stubs.cpp`).
- No correctness battery was run (speed-only submission); a real agentic workload on the same install (long-document reading) was noticeably faster end-to-end than the dense 27B it replaced, matching the prefill numbers.
- Results-only PR, no engine changes included (the compat patches are described in prose, not committed here, to keep the report self-contained).

Per docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md's submit-a-report workflow.

pulls.title: perf(prefill): port wmma_gemm and gdn_chunked WMMA kernels to RDNA4 gfx12
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Ports Strata's prefill FP16/BF16 WMMA kernels in `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` and the WY-chunked Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill recurrence in `src/prefill/kernels.cu` (`gdn_chunked`) from RDNA3-only (`gfx11`) to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`):

1. **Enables `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11=1` for `gfx12` builds (`cmake/hip_backend.cmake:105`):**
   - Previously `cmake/hip_backend.cmake` matched only `gfx11`, so on `gfx1200;gfx1201` builds `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` compiled to `return false;` stubs for `strata_wmma_gemm_f16`, `strata_wmma_gemm_bf16`, `strata_pf_gemm_f16` / `strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld`, `strata_pf_hcdown_bf16`, and `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16`.
2. **Ports `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) Wave32 16×16×16 WMMA (P3a):**
   - Extends `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()` to accept `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()`.
   - Updates `WmmaTraits<_Float16 / __bf16>`, `gemm_wmma_16x16_1w`, `gemm_wmma_64x64_4w`, `pfg::kernel`, `pfg::kernel_bk64` (`STRATA_PF_GEMM=1`), `pfg::kernel_hcdown` (`STRATA_PF_HCDOWN=1`), and `pfg::kernel_hcd_exact` (`STRATA_HCD_EXACT=1`) to use RDNA4 8-element half-wave fragments (`k = 8 * hi + 0..7`), `__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_{f16,bf16}_w32_gfx12`, contiguous half-wave accumulator row mapping (`row = 8 * hi + i`), and LDS-only barriers (`s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `gfx12`, `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`).
3. **Ports WY-chunked GDN prefill recurrence (`gdn_wmma_prep_kernel`, `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel`, `gdn_rec_wmma` in `src/prefill/kernels.cu:1513–1875`, `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1`) to RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`):**
   - On `gfx12`, the Wave32 WMMA accumulator layout `(row = 8 * hi + v, col = lane & 15)` is already identical to the B-operand fragment layout `(k = 8 * hi + v, n = lane & 15)`. Converting an accumulator tile `gw_f8` into a B-operand fragment (`gw_acc_to_b`) requires **zero cross-lane permutes** (`4× permlanex16` + `8× v_perm_b32` on `gfx11` become a direct 8-element FP32→FP16 cast on `gfx12`), keeping `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel` at `239 VGPRs` with `0` spills on `gfx1201`.
4. **Fixes host-only BF16 fixture encoding and non-finite checks in `tests/hip/prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp`:**
   - Uses `strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(value)` in `encode(value, true)` instead of `hip_bfloat16(value).data` (which in a host-only `.cpp` translation unit without `__HIPCC__` performs C++20 parenthesized aggregate initialization `(uint16_t)value` and truncated fractional BF16 inputs to zero), and rejects non-finite `delta` values (`!std::isfinite(delta) || delta > 0.0`).

---

## Root cause

1. **`cmake/hip_backend.cmake:105` & `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`:**
   - `if(CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES MATCHES "gfx11")` excluded `gfx12`, leaving `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11` undefined on RDNA4 builds so `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` compiled only the `#else` stub section (`return false;`).
   - Within `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`, device passes checked `#if defined(__gfx1100__) ...` and used RDNA3 16-element replicated fragments (`ext_vector_type(16)`) and interleaved accumulator row indexing (`2 * i + hi`), whereas RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) Wave32 16×16×16 WMMA instructions (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_{f16,bf16}_w32_gfx12`) split the 16-element K-dimension across the two half-waves (`8` elements per lane: `hi = 0` holds `k = 0..7`, `hi = 1` holds `k = 8..15`) and map accumulator elements `c[0..7]` to contiguous half-wave rows `8 * hi + i`.
2. **`src/prefill/kernels.cu:1513–1875` (`gdn_chunked`):**
   - `STRATA_GDN_WMMA` and `gdn_rec_wmma()` checked only `gfx11` targets (`gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma`), so `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` always returned `false` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` and fell back to the token-serial `gdn_rec_fused_kernel`.

---

## The change

- `cmake/hip_backend.cmake`:
  - Match `gfx11|gfx12` when defining `STRATA_WMMA_GFX11=1`.
- `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu`:
  - Define `STRATA_WMMA_DEV_GFX11`, `STRATA_WMMA_DEV_GFX12`, `WMMA_ROW(i, hi)`, `WMMA_K_OFF(hi)`, `wmma_sync_lds()`, and `pfg::pfg_sync_lds()`.
  - Support `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` in `strata_wmma_gfx11_device()`, `WmmaTraits<_Float16>`, `WmmaTraits<__bf16>`, `gemm_wmma_16x16_1w`, `gemm_wmma_64x64_4w`, `pfg::kernel`, `pfg::kernel_bk64`, `pfg::kernel_hcdown`, and `pfg::kernel_hcd_exact`.
- `src/prefill/kernels.cu`:
  - Define `STRATA_GDN_WMMA_GFX11`, `STRATA_GDN_WMMA_GFX12`, and `GW_ROW(v, hi)` for `gdn_wmma_prep_kernel` and `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel`, implement zero-permute `gw_acc_to_b` and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0` barriers on `gfx12`, and allow `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()` in `gdn_rec_wmma()`.
- `tests/hip/gdn_chunked.cpp` & `tests/hip/prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp`:
  - Enable `gfx_arch_is_gfx12_wmma()` in both test harnesses, fix `encode(value, true)` in `prefill_wmma_gemm_parity.cpp` to use `strata::kernels::bf16_from_f32(value)`, and add exact binary-fraction parity tests (with `!std::isfinite(delta)` guards) for `strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld`, `strata_pf_hcdown_bf16`, and `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16`.

---

## Evidence

### 1. ELF Resource Usage on `gfx1201` (`llvm-readobj --notes`)

All 11 device kernels across `wmma_gemm.cu.o` and `kernels.cu.o` compile on `gfx1201` with **0 register spills (`vgpr_spill_count = 0`, `private_segment_fixed_size = 0`)**:

| Object | Kernel | Threads (`Waves`) | VGPRs | SGPRs | LDS (B) | Spills |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `gemm_wmma_16x16_1w<_Float16 / bfloat16_t>` | 32 (`1w`) | 23 | 24 | 0 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `gemm_wmma_64x64_4w<_Float16 / bfloat16_t>` | 128 (`4w`) | 64 | 26 | 4,096 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `pfg::kernel<128, 32>` | 256 (`8w`) | 143 | 22 | 40,960 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `pfg::kernel<256, 64>` | 256 (`8w`) | 236 | 20 | 61,440 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `pfg::kernel_bk64` | 256 (`8w`) | 229 | 23 | 55,296 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `pfg::kernel_hcdown` | 256 (`8w`) | 191 | 25 | 36,864 | 0 |
| `wmma_gemm.cu.o` | `pfg::kernel_hcd_exact` | 192 (`6w`) | 165 | 19 | 36,864 | 0 |
| `kernels.cu.o` | `gdn_wmma_prep_kernel` | 128 (`4w`) | 133 | 16 | 3,456 | 0 |
| `kernels.cu.o` | `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel` | 256 (`8w`) | 239 | 52 | 31,360 | 0 |

### 2. Parity & Standalone Kernel Benchmarks on `gfx1201`

- **`hip_prefill_wmma_gemm_parity`:**
  - Before (`origin/main` `477ac13c`): skipped with exit code `77` on `gfx1201` (`WMMA GEMM parity SKIPPED: gfx1201 has no WMMA matrix cores`).
  - With PR: **3,529 test cases passed, 26 declined shapes skipped, 0 failures, `max_abs = 0`** across `strata_wmma_gemm_f16` (`1,760` cases), `strata_wmma_gemm_bf16` (`1,760` cases with non-zero `bf16_from_f32` inputs), `strata_pf_gemm_f16_ld` (`5` cases covering `kernel<128, 32>`, `kernel<256, 64>`, and `kernel_bk64`), `strata_pf_hcdown_bf16` (`2` cases), and `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16` (`2` cases).
- **`hip_gdn_chunked` (1 GDN layer: `HK = 16, HV = 48, S = 128`, 7-repeat median):**
  - Before (`origin/main` `477ac13c`): reported `wmma=0` on `gfx1201` (`gdn_rec_wmma` declined every `T`).
  - With PR: **`wmma=1`, `FAILURES: 0` across all 45 test cases** (`T = 0..16385`, CPU reference, chunk continuation, weak-decay, beta-zero, and guard checks).

| Token Count (`T`) | Default `gdn_rec_fused` (`--bench-default`) | WMMA `gdn_rec_wmma` (`--bench`) | Speedup (1 Layer) | 48 GDN Layers Default | 48 GDN Layers WMMA | Saved per Prompt |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `64` | `0.0814 ms` | **`0.0342 ms`** | **`2.38x` (`-57.9%`)** | `3.91 ms` | **`1.64 ms`** | **`-2.26 ms`** |
| `256` | `0.2306 ms` | **`0.0790 ms`** | **`2.92x` (`-65.8%`)** | `11.07 ms` | **`3.79 ms`** | **`-7.28 ms`** |
| `2048` | `1.8829 ms` | **`0.5159 ms`** | **`3.65x` (`-72.6%`)** | `90.38 ms` | **`24.76 ms`** | **`-65.62 ms`** |
| `16384` | `12.4872 ms` | **`4.0308 ms`** | **`3.10x` (`-67.7%`)** | `599.38 ms` | **`193.48 ms`** | **`-405.91 ms`** |
| `32768` | `24.6364 ms` | **`7.6724 ms`** | **`3.21x` (`-68.9%`)** | `1,182.55 ms` | **`368.28 ms`** | **`-814.27 ms`** |

Measured via `strata --serve --prompt-cache 0 --short-read 0` with `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` (`1` warmup + `3` timed trials per prompt length on uncontended `gfx1201`):

| Default (opt-ins off) | `4096` | `121 ms` (`7.5%`) | `149 ms` (`9.2%`) | `1605, 1610, 1611` (**`1610 ms`**) | `1647.5, 1652.1, 1653.4` (**`1652.1 ms`**) | `2,479.3 tok/s` | baseline |
| `STRATA_PF_HCDOWN=1` (P3a isolated, `--vram-reserve-mib 1024`) | `4096` | `121 ms` (`7.5%`) | **`129 ms` (`8.0%`)** | `1602, 1606, 1607` (**`1606 ms`**) | `1645, 1649, 1649` (**`1649.0 ms`**) | **`2,484.3 tok/s`** | **`hc read` `-19 ms` (`-12.8%`)** |
| `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` | `4096` | **`39 ms` (`2.6%`)** | `149 ms` (`9.7%`) | `1536, 1539, 1540` (**`1539 ms`**) | `1578.7, 1582.7, 1582.5` (**`1582.5 ms`**) | **`2,588.3 tok/s`** | **`-69.6 ms` (`+4.4%`)** |
| `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1 STRATA_PF_HCDOWN=1 STRATA_PF_GEMM=1` | `4096` | **`39 ms` (`2.6%`)** | **`129 ms` (`8.4%`)** | `1531, 1534, 1534` (**`1534 ms`**) | `1573.5, 1577.3, 1576.7` (**`1576.7 ms`**) | **`2,597.8 tok/s`** | **`-75.4 ms` (`+4.8%`)** |

*(Candidate evaluated and excluded — P3b in-kernel `Wd_q8` dequant inside `pfg::kernel_hcdown`: Under `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`, dequantizing `Wd` (`320 × 10240` BF16 = `6.55 MB`) once per half-layer via `hc_bf16_view` + `kernel_hcdown` takes `129 ms` across 120 half-layers at `T = 4096` (`-19 ms` vs `148 ms` hipBLASLt), because the `6.55 MB` BF16 buffer stays resident in the R9700's 64 MB Infinity Cache across all 32 M-tiles. Dequantizing `Wd_q8` on the fly inside `kernel_hcdown` repeats the 34-byte-strided `Q8_0` address calculation and 8× FP32→BF16 RNE rounding across every M-tile and measured `140 ms` at `T = 4096` (`+11 ms` slower than P3a's `129 ms`), so P3b was excluded.)*

---

## What this does NOT fix

- **Does not change default prefill dispatch when opt-in switches are unset:** `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1`, `STRATA_PF_HCDOWN=1`, `STRATA_PF_GEMM=1`, and `STRATA_HCD_EXACT=1` remain behind their existing opt-in environment variables because their accumulation order / FP16 state rounding differs from default hipBLASLt and FP32 serial GDN recurrence.
- **`STRATA_HCD_EXACT=1` hipBLASLt solution IDs (`1176` / `1177` in `src/prefill/gemm_hip.cpp:623`):** `kernel_hcd_exact` is ported to `gfx12` and verified via `strata_pf_hcdown_exact_bf16`, but `gemm_hip.cpp` only dispatches `STRATA_HCD_EXACT=1` when the loaded tuning table selects `gfx1151` solution IDs `1176` or `1177`.
- **Target-device runtime on `gfx1100` / `gfx1151`:** Multi-arch device compilation was verified across `gfx1100,gfx1151,gfx1200,gfx1201`; runtime execution and benchmarks were performed on `gfx1201`, while `gfx11` hardware runtime remains unrun on this host.

---

## Test plan

- [x] `hip_prefill_wmma_gemm_parity` passes `3,529` cases (`max_abs = 0`) and `26` declined-shape checks on `gfx1201`
- [x] `hip_gdn_chunked` passes all `45` p

pulls.title: docs: the 0.1.44.1 changes no page told (start-crash #2324, setup re-run keeps size)
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves # (documents #2324)

## Summary

Docs only - no code changed. Two 0.1.44.1 behaviours that no page told:

1. **Start-time crashes (#2324)**: an engine the OS ends at start (illegal instruction, access violation, the OOM killer, a missing DLL) is now treated as a crash, not a retryable GPU-runtime start. `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` and the `DETAILS.md` troubleshooting table had nothing about it.
2. **Setup run again over an installed model keeps its size**: `--setup` opens the size list with the installed size pre-selected, so Enter / `--yes` keep it; a re-run never silently moves a working install to the recommended (slower, larger) size.

## What changed

- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` - new section for the start crash (#2324): the exit words per OS, the AVX/AVX2/FMA/F16C flags, the `STRATA_ISA_FLOOR` pointer to "Older CPUs".
- `docs/DETAILS.md` - the matching row in the troubleshooting table.
- `docs/INSTALL.md` - the "Running setup again over an installed model?" bullet under "Setup's questions".
- `docs/AI_SETUP.md` - the same re-run rule for an assistant running setup non-interactively.

## Extra Notes

**Verified against the code on `main` (no GPU, no model):**
- #2324 "not retried": `serve/server.py` `engine_crashed` (L475) and the transient-start rule `... and not engine_crashed(rc)` (L562); `serve/test_server.py::StartCrashReported` runs 5/5 OK on Windows (3 skipped, Linux-only signals).
- re-run keeps size: `setup.py` `installed_size` (L2324); `tools/test_setup_rerun_size.py` 8/8 OK.

**Two accuracy fixes vs. the original branch commit, measured against `main`:**
- The AVX/AVX2/FMA/F16C flags are printed only on Linux - `cpu_isa_words()` reads `/proc/cpuinfo` alone, so on Windows/macOS the line names the illegal instruction by itself. The docs say that.
- No reference to the eval harness: `evals/` is not in `main`, so a pointer to it would be a dead link.

Docs only; the default path is untouched.

pulls.title: metal: stub wait_handoff / handoff_publish so the Metal engine links on 0.1.45
pulls.author: bsvinay
pulls.body:
Fixes the Mac link failure qiuzan2001 reported on #1120.

`Verifier::record_window` (src/core/verify.cpp, compiled into the Mac engine via metal/CMakeLists.txt) calls `strata::kernels::wait_handoff` and `strata::kernels::handoff_publish` since the overlapped hand-off landed. Both are defined only in src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu, and the generated metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp stubs the neighbouring `wait_flag_ge` / `wait_flag_ge_or` but not these two, so ld64 reports them undefined.

This adds `metal/src/engine/stubs_145.cpp` (a separate file, like stubs_144.cpp, so the generated stubs.cpp stays untouched), defining both with the header's exact signatures; each calls `strata::metal_engine::missing(...)` like the other stubs. The overlap is opt-in and needs two CUDA/HIP devices, so these are not reached on Metal.

Not built on a Mac (I don't have one); the signatures were checked against include/strata/kernels/verify_kernels.hpp on main. A Metal build to confirm the link would be appreciated.

Note: a static scan of 0.1.45 finds seven more entry points called from Metal-compiled sources (verify.cpp, mtp.cpp) with no Metal definition or stub: `wait_flag_ge_stamped`, `wait_copy_i32_from_mapped`, `gdn_conv_ab_multi`, `gdn_step_norm_groups`, `gather_rows`, `argmax_rows_scratch_bytes`, `row_top_prob_scratch_bytes`. @qiuzan2001, could you paste the full ld64 output? If those are undefined too, the right fix is regenerating stubs.cpp with metal/tools/gen_stubs.py from that log, and I can fold it into this PR.

pulls.title: perf(prefill): use single LDS-only barrier per stage in native_w11_kernel
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Optimizes `native_w11_kernel` (`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`), the default `gfx12` (`RDNA4`) and opt-in `gfx11` (`STRATA_PF_FUSED=1`) int8-WMMA fused MoE prefill kernel:

1. **Removes the duplicate per-stage barrier (`src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu:913, 964`):**
   - Stage `0`'s decoded weights (`wt[0]`, `ws[0]`) are written by `put(raw, 0)` before the prologue barrier (`line 882`), and each subsequent stage `s + 1`'s decoded weights (`wt[(s + 1) & 1]`, `ws[(s + 1) & 1]`) are written by `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` before the end-of-stage barrier added in `#1180` (`line 964`).
   - Because `wt` and `ws` are double-buffered (`wt[2][NW_ROWS][WLD]`, `ws[2][NW_ROWS][4]`), buffer `(s + 1) & 1` is only read in stage `s - 1` (before the barrier at the end of stage `s - 1`). Keeping both the top-of-loop barrier (`line 913`) and the end-of-stage barrier (`line 964`) executed two workgroup barriers per stage (`80` barriers in `GU` across `NS = 40`, `20` in `down` across `NS = 10`) with only `load_unit(s + 2)` and register moves between them.
2. **Replaces full-memory `__syncthreads()` with an LDS-only barrier (`nw_sync_lds()`):**
   - Every barrier in `native_w11_kernel` only synchronizes LDS (`wt`, `ws`, `srow`, `hs`).
   - On HIP, `__syncthreads()` lowers to a workgroup acquire/release fence over all memory (`s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, and `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0) lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `gfx11`).
   - Waiting on `loadcnt(0)` / `vmcnt(0)` at every barrier forced `load_unit(s + 2)` and `fetch_b(s + 1)` global loads to complete at the barrier instead of overlapping the next stage's 16 `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8` instructions, and `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` on `gfx12` flushed the L0 vector cache on every stage even though 4 consecutive `GU` stages (`s >> 2`) read sub-blocks from the same 256-value weight superblock.
   - `nw_sync_lds()` uses `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0); s_barrier` on `STRATA_NAT_W11` (matching `gw_lds_barrier()` in `src/prefill/kernels.cu:1572`) and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1` on `STRATA_NAT_W12`.

---

## Root cause

In `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu:880–976`:
- Commit `3b499f17` (`#1180`) added `__syncthreads()` after `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` at line 964 while leaving the original `__syncthreads()` at the top of `for (int s = 0; s < NS; ++s)` (`line 913`).
- In the `gfx1201` disassembly of `native_w11_kernel<T_IQ3_S, true, true, 8>`:
  - At the end of stage `s`, `put(raw, (s + 1) & 1)` stored to LDS and executed `s_wait_loadcnt_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait 0xffff; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` (`line 964`).
  - Immediately after, `load_unit(s + 2)` issued 5 `global_load` instructions for stage `s + 2`'s compressed weights, and the loop backedge immediately hit the second `__syncthreads()` (`line 913`), emitting `s_wait_loadcnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait 0xffff; global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` — stalling on `load_unit(s + 2)` and invalidating the L0 vector cache before stage `s + 1`'s WMMAs began.

---

## The change

- `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`:
  - Define `nw_sync_lds()` (`s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)\n\ts_barrier` on `STRATA_NAT_W11`, `s_wait_dscnt 0x0\n\ts_barrier_signal -1\n\ts_barrier_wait -1` on `STRATA_NAT_W12`, `__syncthreads()` fallback).
  - Remove the redundant top-of-loop barrier at the start of `for (int s = 0; s < NS; ++s)` and replace the remaining `__syncthreads()` calls in `native_w11_kernel` with `nw_sync_lds()`.

---

## Evidence

### 1. `gfx1201` Disassembly Verification (`llvm-objdump -d`)

- Eliminates all `global_inv scope:SCOPE_SE` instructions from `native_w11_kernel` (previously `82` L0 cache invalidations per 64-row tile in `GU` and `22` in `down`).
- Halves per-stage barrier count (`80 → 39` in `GU`, `20 → 9` in `down`).
- In the steady-state stage loop (`s = 1..NS-2`), `fetch_b(s + 1)`'s 10 `global_load_b64` instructions execute concurrently with all 16 `v_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8` instructions of stage `s` with zero `s_wait_loadcnt` instructions inside the WMMA loop body.

### 2. Bitwise Parity & Single-Layer Prefill Benchmark (`hip_prefill_fused_iq`, `S20_NOMMQ=1`, 3 alternating rounds × 8 back-to-back runs per round on `gfx1201`)

All 21 FNV-1a 64-bit output hashes (`7` format pairs × `3` chunk sizes) are **100% bit-for-bit identical** between `origin/main` (`477ac13c`) and this PR:

pulls.title: perf(hip): enable fused_gr tsum on gfx12, fix q8_inject guard, and use LDS-only barriers

pulls.title: serve: "report_dropped_tool_calls": true names the cut tool calls a whole OpenAI answer leaves out (#211, opt-in)
pulls.author: LostDakota
pulls.body:
## What it changes

A whole (non-streamed) OpenAI answer that ends in the middle of a tool call leaves that call out (#211, fixed in 0.1.31 by #231), because many SDKs run any call that is present. That is right, but the client then can't tell an answer that lost a call apart from one that finished.

`"report_dropped_tool_calls": true` in `strata-<model>.json` adds `strata_dropped_tool_calls` to the message: the name and the argument length (in characters) of each call left out.

```json
"strata_dropped_tool_calls": [{"name": "write_file", "arguments_chars": 4113}]
```

## What it leaves alone

- It is off by default. `openai_collect` builds the same message as before unless the switch is on, so the default answer is byte-identical.
- Which calls are dropped doesn't change, and neither does `finish_reason`.
- Streaming and the Anthropic API don't change.
- The engine (CUDA, HIP, SYCL) isn't touched.

## How I checked

- `serve/test_server.py`: the existing `test_collect_keeps_calls_whose_arguments_parse` now also checks that the field is absent by default. The new `test_collect_names_the_dropped_calls_when_asked` checks the field for `stop` and `length`, and checks it is absent for `tool_calls` and when nothing was cut.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server`: 338 tests, OK (Linux, the project's `.venv`).
- Not tested: a live server with the switch on.

pulls.title: prefill: per-expert NVFP4 scales on the peer-prefill route (opt-in)
pulls.author: florian862-art
pulls.body:
## What

The peer GPU in a `--peer-device` setup computes its experts' MoE rows for every prompt chunk, but on NVFP4 packs its MMQ products ran **without any per-expert scales** (`grp_tail` null, no `s_gate/s_up`, no `s_down`, no `y_scale`) - so its rows were numerically wrong and `set_peer` refused the combination. This PR wires the scales through and keeps the whole route behind `STRATA_PF_PEER_NVFP4=1`.

**Commit 1 (`70d6f941`) - the core patch, `prefill.cpp` + the `generate.cpp` gate only:**
- `gather_native` carries the expert's scale tail into `P.grp_tail` (peer group gather)
- `swiglu_scaled` applies `s_gate/s_up` on the native path (peer loops + primary loop)
- `scale_down_rows` applies `s_down` **in place** on both GPUs' `Dm` rows right after the down-proj - instead of the `row_sd` table the combine reads
- `y_scale` feeds the w4a4 dequant on the gu/dn products
- `moe_combine` gets `row_sd = nullptr` when the peer is active

Two existing bugs fall out of the in-place design: the sums mode never applied `s_down` to GPU 0's own rows (`moe_combine_peer[16]` has no `row_sd` param), and with the peer active `moe_combine` read `m.row_sd[rows_local..T*K)`, which is never written (the 31 non-finite logits behind every cold >=20k prompt on the peer route). `kernels.cu`/`kernels.hpp` are untouched - no kernel ABI change.

**Commit 2 (`0b69db53`) - separate, droppable:** sums mode on the **P2P** route (`STRATA_PF_PEER_SUMS_P2P=1`): forward keeps P2P, the return carries one weighted FP16 sum per token through mapped host memory instead of FP32 rows. Correct but slower than the host route on this box (P2P link here runs at 5.5 GB/s, below PCIe-to-RAM); it should pay off on boxes where P2P beats PCIe (NVLink etc.), hence opt-in + documented.

## Measured (2x RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, NVFP4 pack, 4k cold prompt, median of 3)

| route | prompt tok/s | correctness |
|---|---|---|
| P2P route, FP32 rows back | 1383 | (pre-existing, scales n/a on this route) |
| host route + sums, **no scales** (old C reference) | 2683 | refused for NVFP4 before this PR |
| host route + sums, **with scales (this PR)** | **2718** (2717/2718/2729; 84k prompt: 2638) | recall gate: both needles exact at 24,933 prompt tokens, **0 non-finite logits** (was: every cold >=20k prompt died) |
| P2P forward + sums back (commit 2) | 2259 | recall gate passes, 0 non-finite |

The scale math (two tiny row-scale kernels + `swiglu_scaled` per group, all on `ps`) costs nothing measurable - the patched route is slightly *above* the unscaled reference.

## How to test

```
STRATA_PF_PEER_NVFP4=1 STRATA_PEER_NO_P2P=1   # config C (host route, this PR's core)
STRATA_PF_PEER_NVFP4=1 STRATA_PF_PEER_SUMS_P2P=1   # + commit 2, only interesting with fast P2P
```
The route banner in the log names the live route. Without the env flags nothing changes: `set_peer` keeps refusing NVFP4 experts and `generate.cpp` keeps the `rows == 0` skip.

Design notes, the review history and the full measurement log: `src/prefill/README-nvfp4-peer.md`.

pulls.title: bench: the start-its-own-server path names its port again
pulls.author: victorgabr
pulls.body:
69fe4055 (#2330) inlined the port into `server_base(...)` and dropped the `port = a.port or int(cfg.get("port", 8080))` assignment, but three uses of `port` below it stayed: the port-in-use line, the "Starting the server on port" line, and the `start_server(cfg_path, port, ...)` call itself. Running `tools/strata_bench.py` with no server already up now dies before launching one:

```
NameError: name 'port' is not defined. Did you mean: 'props'?
```

`test_bench_host.py` only exercised `server_base` in isolation, so the path stayed unpinned.

**Changes:** one line in `main()` — `port` is assigned again and passed to `server_base`. Nothing else moves. **Adds:** `StartServerPort` in `tools/test_bench_host.py`, which drives `main()` down the start-its-own-server branch with `start_server`/`wait_ready` stubbed — no GPU, no server, no network — and asserts the config's port and the `--port` override reach `start_server`.

**How I checked:** the new tests raise the NameError on the file before the fix and pass after (`python -m unittest tools.test_bench_host`: 7/7). End to end on a TITAN RTX: with the fix, the bench started its own server and wrote three full community reports today (runs with and without STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP); without it every such run crashed at the line above.

pulls.title: [Engine] batch-groups: a prompt with pictures is read beside the decoding slots too, stall 5.7 -> 0.4 s (opt-in)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
With `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1` a text prompt is read on a thread of its own while the other slots keep decoding, but a prompt with pictures is still read the usual way, so every slot stops for it (docs/BATCHING.md: "A prompt with pictures is read the usual way"). Coding agents send screenshots, and 0.2.0 turns pictures on by default. With this change a prompt with pictures is read the same way as a text prompt. On 0.2.0-beta, 2x RTX 5090, while a 50K-token prompt with a picture is read beside four decoding streams, the streams keep 20.8-23.7 tok/s instead of 6.0-7.1 tok/s and their longest pause goes from 5.7 s to 0.14-0.43 s. Without `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1` nothing changes.

## Related discussion
#2326 (the concurrent read; in main since 0.1.45). #1242 (the per-device image-position table; not touched here). Rebased onto 0.2.0-beta (no conflicts) after the tracker reset; the earlier description's 0.1.45 numbers are kept under Validation.

## Approach
Pictures were kept out because a picture's rows go up through the prompt path's pinned ring (`core::PinnedRing`, #1996), whose size was taken to be known only at the upload; the read's thread could then grow a slot, and a pinned allocation takes the driver's lock (#31). That size is bounded: the gather sends a picture's rows in runs of at most 4 MiB.
- `include/strata/prefill/prompt_uploads.hpp` (new, header-only arithmetic): `picture_run_rows()` is the gather's run (the same expression as before), `prompt_upload_bytes()` the largest upload a chunk can send, pictures included.
- Before a concurrent read, `Prefill::reserve_uploads(T, pictures)` grows the ring to that, as the concurrent read already does for a text chunk. Only the first stage takes picture rows.
- A prompt with pictures does not give way to a shorter request (as before), and the engine ignores a `BYIELD` during its read (with a log line) instead of stopping a run that would not be resumed.
- `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT_PICTURES=0` keeps the usual way, for an A/B.

The embeddings, the conversation cache's picture keys and the vision encoder are untouched. The default path differs in one line only: the gather's run size, which `batch_read_test` checks equals the old expression for every row width up to 8 MiB.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- Build, 0.2.0-beta (main e88ee39d) + this commit (b3e7d696), Windows 11, MSVC 2022, CUDA 13.0, sm_120: `cmake --build <dir> --target batch_read_test strata` and `batch_read_test.exe` -> `batch_read_test: ok`. The same for main e88ee39d (control engine).
- 2x RTX 5090 (Windows 11), Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, `--layer-split 25 --trim-stage-weights --batch 6 --batch-groups 2 --resident-experts --kv-resident 32768`, the vision encoder on GPU 0 (the same encoder binary in every arm), a fresh engine per arm, temperature 0. A cold prompt of about 49,800 tokens with one picture, read alone, then beside four decoding streams (D arms once, P arms twice). Order D0, D1, P0, P1, P1b:

| | main, default (D0) | this, default (D1) | `CONCURRENT=1`, `PICTURES=0` (P0) | `CONCURRENT=1`, this (P1, P1b) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| each stream during the read | 6.1-6.4 tok/s | 5.9-6.0 tok/s | 6.0-7.1 tok/s | 20.8-23.7 tok/s |
| longest pause of a stream | 5.74-5.75 s | 6.00 s | 5.66-5.67 s | 0.14-0.43 s |
| picture prompt beside the streams, first token | 6.21 s | 6.46 s | 6.13, 6.16 s | 6.60, 6.65, 6.70, 6.65 s |
| picture prompt alone, first token | 6.34 s | 6.33 s | 8.90 s | 10.29, 6.44 s |

The engine logged each concurrent picture read as about 49,890 tokens in 6.13-6.21 s with the slots decoding 71-77 rows/s meanwhile; P1b then read six more picture prompts beside the four streams (6.70-6.90 s to the first token). No stall or error lines in any arm.
- Exactness: the picture answer was the same in every arm in each position (alone: all five; beside, round 1: all five; round 2: P0, P1 and P1b).
- Before the rebase, on 0.1.45 (477ac13c), same rig: streams 33.9-36.8 against 4.5-6.1 tok/s, pause 0.07-0.16 s against 5.9-6.0 s; HIP on Windows (gfx1100): the engine and `batch_read_test` built and passed; Linux (gcc 13.3, CUDA 13.0 headers): `prefill.cpp` and `generate.cpp` compiled.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** HIP, Linux and SYCL builds on 0.2.0 (done on 0.1.45 only; SYCL never: no oneAPI here); AMD or Linux on a GPU; Mac (no concurrent read there); `--mtp` with pictures; `--batch-groups 1`.

## Limits
- The prompt with pictures waits about 0.5 s longer for its first token when slots decode beside it (6.6-6.7 s against 6.1-6.2 s for 50K tokens beside four streams): its read shares the GPUs with them. The solo first token was 8.9 s in P0 (without this change) and 10.3 s in P1, against 6.3-6.4 s in D0, D1 and P1b: the first prompt after the engine start, not reproduced in P1b with the same settings.
- About 16 MiB more pinned RAM on the first device, once, the first time a prompt with pictures is read this way.
- A prompt with pictures still never gives way to a shorter request. The image-position table stays one per device (#1242).

pulls.title: perf(hip): vectorize HC_Q8 prefill dequant and enable gfx12 Q8_0 gr_upmix
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
## Summary

Optimizes the `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` hyper-connection (`hc_down` / `hc_up`) prefill read path on RDNA4 (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) and CUDA/HIP in two complementary steps:

1. **Default path (`STRATA_HC_Q8=1`, bitwise-identical):**
   - Vectorizes `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`) from 1 `int8` element per lane (`global_load_u8/i8` + `global_store_b16`) to 8 `int8` elements per lane (`dequant_q8_0_vec8_item` + `bf16x2_from_f32_finite` with `uint4` 16-byte stores, 64 `Q8_0` blocks per 256-thread CTA), and adds pair-fused `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair`) plus `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view_pair` / `hc_bf16_release_pair` (`src/core/native_dense.cpp`).
   - Tracks the last recording stream per scratch slot (`g_hc_ev_stream[dev][slot]`) so same-stream `cudaStreamWaitEvent` calls are elided during single-stream prefill chunks.
   - Moves `hc_bf16_view(*wd)` after `gr_norm_rs` (immediately before `bf16_proj(wd)`) and `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` after `gr_silu` (immediately before `bf16_proj(wu)`) in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` so `gr_norm_rs` (`125.8 MB` at `T=2048`, `251.7 MB` at `T=4096`) and `wu` do not evict `wd` (`6.55 MB`) from the 8 MB L2 / 64 MB Infinity Cache before `bf16_proj(wd)` reads it.

2. **Opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` path on `gfx12` (`gfx1200` / `gfx1201`) + fused `Q8_0` `w_up` dequantization:**
   - Extends `gr_upmix_kernel` and `gr_upmix()` (`src/prefill/kernels.cu`) to `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32_gfx12`, 8-element `um_b16` fragments per lane, `t = t0 + 8 * hi + i` wave32 output row mapping, and `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1`).
   - Adds an optional `const uint8_t* w_up_q8 = nullptr` parameter to `gr_upmix` so that when `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` and `STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` are active (`wu->data == nullptr && wu->hc_q8 != nullptr`), `gr_upmix_kernel` dequantizes each CTA's 64 `w_up` rows (`64 × 320` = 640 `Q8_0` blocks) directly into shared memory `sB` once per CTA. `prefill.cpp` skips `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` entirely, eliminating all 96 `wu` full-matrix dequantizations (`1.26 GB` of BF16 scratch write+read per chunk) in addition to eliminating the `m.gated` (`T × 10,240` FP32 = `16.1 GB` at `T=2048`, `32.2 GB` at `T=4096`) global memory round-trip across all 96 halves.
   - Enables `gr_upmix_parity` (`src/prefill/gr_upmix_parity.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`) on HIP (`gfx11` / `gfx12`) and adds a bitwise parity check verifying `gr_upmix(..., d_wu_q8)` matches `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0 + gr_upmix(..., d_wu_deq)` bit-for-bit across all 21 token counts (`T = 1 .. 32768`).

---

## Root cause

1. **`STRATA_HC_Q8=1` prefill dequantization overhead and cache eviction (`src/core/native_dense.cpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`):**
   - When `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` is set (`NativeDense::add_hc_skip`), the BF16 hyper-connection matrices (`blk.*.attn_hc_down/up.weight`, `blk.*.ffn_hc_down/up.weight`) are skipped at load (`w.data == nullptr`), leaving only `w.hc_q8` (`Q8_0`, `320 × 10,240` = `3,276,800` elements / `102,400` blocks per matrix).
   - On every prefill chunk (`prefill.cpp:2943`), each of the 96 halves called `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view` twice (`192` launches of `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel`), where each thread loaded a single `int8` quant (`global_load_u8`, `global_load_u8`, `global_load_i8`) and issued a 2-byte `global_store_b16` (`601.5 GB/s` on `gfx1201`).
   - Worse, `prefill.cpp` dequantized both `wd` (`6.55 MB` BF16) and `wu` (`6.55 MB` BF16) before `gr_norm_rs`. Running `gr_norm_rs` (`251.7 MB` of `m.R` read + `m.xn16` write at `T=4096`) between dequantization and `bf16_proj(wd)` evicted the freshly dequantized BF16 scratch from the 8 MB L2 / 64 MB Infinity Cache before `bf16_proj` read it.

2. **`STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1` gated off on `gfx12` (`src/prefill/kernels.cu:2112, 2398`):**
   - `gr_upmix()` checked only `gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma(p.gcnArchName)`, returning `false` on `gfx1200` / `gfx1201`. Furthermore, `prefill.cpp:2972` required `wu->data != nullptr` before calling `hc_bf16_view`, or else required dequantizing `wu` (`6.55 MB` per half) into global BF16 scratch first.
   - As a result, `gfx1201` always fell back to `hc_bf16_view(wu)` + `hipBLASLt` (`wu` GEMM) + `gr_mix_r`, writing and re-reading `T × 10,240` FP32 `m.gated` (`80 MB` per half = `7.68 GB` read + `7.68 GB` write at `T=2048`; `30.7 GB` total at `T=4096`).

---

## The change

- `include/strata/kernels/fused_gr.hpp`, `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`:
  - Add `bf16x2_from_f32_finite` and `dequant_q8_0_vec8_item` (8 elements per thread, handling both 2-byte aligned and arbitrary unaligned pointers, using round-to-nearest-even finite packing when `(d_u16 & 0x7C00u) != 0x7C00u` and falling back to `bf16_from_f32` for `±Inf`/`NaN` scales).
  - Update `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`64` `Q8_0` blocks per 256-thread CTA, `uint4` 16B stores) and add `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair`).
- `include/strata/core/native_dense.hpp`, `src/core/native_dense.cpp`, `src/core/layer.cpp`:
  - Add `NativeDense::hc_bf16_view_pair` and `NativeDense::hc_bf16_release_pair`, plus `g_hc_ev_stream[64][2]` tracking to elide redundant same-stream `cudaStreamWaitEvent` calls.
- `include/strata/prefill/kernels.hpp`, `src/prefill/kernels.cu`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`:
  - Port `gr_upmix_kernel` and `gr_upmix` to `gfx1200` / `gfx1201` (`__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32_gfx12`, wave32 `gfx12` fragment/row layout, `s_wait_dscnt 0x0; s_barrier_signal -1; s_barrier_wait -1`).
  - Add `const uint8_t* w_up_q8 = nullptr` to `gr_upmix` so `gr_upmix_kernel` dequantizes `w_up_q8` (`Q8_0`) directly into shared memory `sB`, and wire `prefill.cpp` to skip `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` when `gr_upmix` runs.
  - Move `hc_bf16_view(*wd)` after `gr_norm_rs` and `hc_bf16_view(*wu)` after `gr_silu` in `prefill.cpp`.
- `src/kernels/gr_parity.cpp`, `src/prefill/gr_upmix_parity.cu`, `CMakeLists.txt`:
  - Add bitwise parity self-test for `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0` and `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0_pair` across finite, subnormal, `±0`, `±Inf`, `qNaN`, `sNaN` scales and aligned/unaligned pointers in `gr_parity --selftest`.
  - Enable `gr_upmix_parity` on HIP (`gfx11` / `gfx12`) and verify that `gr_upmix(..., d_wu_q8)` is bitwise identical to `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0 + gr_upmix(..., d_wu_deq)` across all 21 token counts (`T = 1 .. 32768`).

---

## Evidence

### 1. Standalone Kernel Microbenchmarks & Parity (`gfx1201`)

#### A. `gr_dequant_q8_0` (`192` matrices per chunk, `1.93 GB` total read+write traffic on Radeon AI PRO R9700 `gfx1201`)
- Exhaustive bitwise check across all `65,536 × 256 = 16,777,216` `(fp16 d, int8 q)` pairs (`±0`, subnormals, normals, `±Inf`, `qNaN`, `sNaN`): **0 bitwise mismatches** vs scalar `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel`.

| Kernel variant | Launches / chunk | Median GPU time (192 matrices) | Effective bandwidth | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (scalar 1B loads, 2B store) | 192 | `3.204 ms` | `601.5 GB/s` | `1.00×` |
| Vectorized `gr_dequant_q8_0_kernel` (`vec8`, 16B `uint4` store) | 192 | `1.701 ms` | `1,132.7 GB/s` | `1.88×` |
| Pair-fused `gr_dequant_q8_0_pair_kernel` (`pair_vec8`) | 96 | **`1.646 ms`** | **`1,170.7 GB/s`** | **`1.95×` (`-1.56 ms`)** |

#### B. `gr_upmix_parity --bench` on `gfx1201` (`STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING=tools/hip/gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`)
- All 21 token counts (`T = 1, 7, 16, 31, 32, 33, 48, 63, 64, 65, 96, 126, 127, 128, 129, 600, 1000, 2048, 4099, 8192, 32768`) pass (`gr_upmix_parity: 0 failures`):
  - `mixed max |diff| / max |value|`: `7.10e-08 .. 1.86e-07` vs `hipBLASLt + gr_mix_r`; sampled FP64 relative error `5.60e-08 .. 1.92e-07` (matching `hipBLASLt + gr_mix_r`).
  - Direct `Q8_0` (`gr_upmix(..., d_wu_q8)`) vs `fused_gr_dequant_q8_0 + gr_upmix(..., d_wu_deq)`: **0 bitwise diffs across all 21 token counts** (`mixed` FP32, `mixed16` BF16, and `mixed_h` FP16 images).

pulls.title: metal: prompt chain without MetalPerformancePrimitives (macOS 15 SDK)
pulls.author: nullspeech
pulls.body:
### Why

On macOS 15.8 (Apple M2 Max, 96 GB) the engine cannot start the prompt chain at all: every `matmul2d` kernel in `metal/kernels/` is reached through an **unguarded** `#include <MetalPerformancePrimitives/MetalPerformancePrimitives.h>`, and that header only ships with a Metal 4 SDK. `Context::compile()` of `dense_mm.metal` / `moe_mm.metal` / `prompt.metal` / `qsa_prompt.metal` fails, the failure is fatal at init (`exit 3`), and the config has to carry `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window` — which caps prefill at ~58 tok/s on this box.

The GPU was never the limit. `simdgroup_matrix<half,8,8>` + `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` is Apple7+ and has always worked here; the repo's own probe with the guards applied does **7.22 TFLOP/s** at 4096³ (rel L2 2.75e-07 against the fp32 reference) and prints `device Apple M2 Max, metal4 0`. So this is a toolchain question, not an instruction-set question — and it is the same root cause as #2860, one level down.

### What changed

11 files under `metal/`, +399/−28, no kernel semantics touched.

- `#if __has_include(<MetalPerformancePrimitives/...>)` around the MPP include, the `using namespace mpp::tensor_ops;`, and each `matmul2d` kernel body. Four sites get an `#else` twin — `gemm_f16` (dense_mm), `gemm_hc_up` (prompt), `mm_gu2` / `mm_down2` (moe_mm) — each a `simdgroup_matrix<half,8,8>` kernel with the **same signature and the same `[[host_name]]`**, so no host call site changes. The twins reuse the existing threadgroup staging (`stage_w<F, TN, TK>`) and the existing quant tables.
- QSA's three MPP kernels needed no twin: your chain already falls back to `qsa.metal`'s scalar `qsa_score`/`qsa_attn` when `coop_k4` is false, so 17 lines of bare `#if` are enough there.
- `mtl::Context::msl_has_mpp()` asks the **compiler** (one 5-line source that `#error`s when the header is missing) instead of `supports_metal4()`. The GPU family answers "Metal 4" on an M2 running a macOS 26 beta, but the toolchain is the question the kernel's own `#if` answers — keying host and MSL off the same oracle is what keeps variant selection and the compiled library from ever disagreeing.
- `STRATA_METAL_LEGACY=1` forces `#define STRATA_MSL_MPP 0`, so a machine that has both can be measured arm against arm.
- `coop_k4()` (the M5 right-input layout probe, which compiles an MPP-only kernel) returns false without the header instead of aborting on a missing function.
- `MTLGPUFamilyMetal4` is guarded for toolchains that predate the enum.
- Tiles for the twins are measured, not guessed: `mm_gu2_*_16_32_32_2` for gate/up, TN 32 for the dense `gemm_f16` (see below).

### Correctness (all under `STRATA_METAL_LEGACY=1`, M2 Max / macOS 15.8)

| harness | result |
|---|---|
| `dense_mm_parity` | 67 PASS / 0 FAIL, worst rel L2 1.5e-06 vs fp16 operands |
| `prompt_parity` | ALL PASS (mixed 2.35e-04, inject 2.22e-04, swiglu_h 4.77e-04) |
| `gdn_parity` | ALL PASS, ntok 1–8 |
| `moe_mm_parity --v2` | PASS for every format this pack routes: IQ3_XXS 3.18e-05, IQ2_S 2.51e-05, IQ4_XS 2.61e-05, IQ3_S 2.28e-05, Q2_0 4.42e-06, Q8_0 2.55e-05 |
| same, upstream tile vs legacy tile | **identical error numbers** ⇒ the tile choice is speed-only |
| K-quant `16_16_128_2` under legacy | Q4_K 1.71e-05, Q5_K 9.57e-06, Q6_K 2.65e-05 PASS (speed unmeasurable here: this pack's routed experts carry no K-quant) |

### Numbers — one binary, one environment variable apart

1023-token prompts, five alternating runs each:

| arm | prefill tok/s | decode tok/s (64 tokens) | TTFT for 1023 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window` | 58.58 / 57.90 / 57.42 / 58.86 / 59.10 | 26.81, 26.38 | 20.6 – 26.4 s |
| prompt chain on the simdgroup_matrix twins | 182.34 / 177.02 / 173.42 / 179.41 / 173.61 | 28.98, 27.27 | 8.8 – 14.4 s |

**3.02× on prefill** (medians 177.0 vs 58.6), decode unchanged to slightly better. Server-level over HTTP (`/v1/chat/completions`), a 4252-token prompt: 55.3 → 159.4 tok/s median. Short prompts (27–34 tokens) are unchanged because they stay under `_PROMPT_GEMM_MIN` = 64 and never reach the chain. The first prompt after boot is slower on both arms — one pass over the pack is cold storage: 84.3 tok/s cold, 177 once the file cache holds it.

Attribution on one 1024-token chunk (`prompt_chain --breakdown`), same session: upstream dense tile `64_64` = 58 tok/s (gdn proj alone 8.73 s) → dense twin at TN 32 = 140 (gdn proj 1.18 s, qsa proj 2.44 → 0.24, hc gemm 0.80 → 0.36) → expert gate/up `16_32_32_2` = 169 (gu 4.15 → 2.93). So the dense projections carry 2.4× and the expert tile 1.2× of the total 2.9×.

### What this does not claim

It does not overtake llama.cpp on the same weights. Same machine, same prompt texts, the **identical** GGUF file, `llama-server` b11408 (`-ngl 999`, `--parallel 1`, `-c 65536`, MTP draft):

| engine on the identical pack | 4220-token prompt | 1609 | 875 |
|---|---|---|---|
| window path | 58 | – | – |
| this branch | 160–172 | 167–172 | 153–162 |
| llama.cpp b11408 | 285.6 / 254.9 | 267.6 | 267.6 |

The branch recovers ~3× of this engine's own 4.9× deficit on the old SDK and still leaves ~1.6× on the table. The deficit is spread rather than concentrated — llama.cpp's whole 1024-token chunk costs ~3.6 s at that rate, while gate/up (2.93 s) plus gdn proj (1.21 s) here are already 4.14 s — so it points at how the chain schedules these kernels, not at raw `simdgroup_matrix` throughput (the dense twin runs at 6.89 of the 7.22 TFLOP/s the probe measures). Decode is a wash: llama.cpp's 1596 completed production requests median at 30.1 tok/s, this at 27–31.

### Merge state / what I would want reviewed

- **This branch is based on `296b59d2` (v0.1.44.1) and will conflict with `main`.** main is 264 commits ahead, 13 of them under `metal/`; `prompt_chain.inc:302` is the hunk that moved, and the `maxBufferLength` wrap (8b3ec44b, which bounds the MoE kernels per layer) touches `moe_mm.metal` where the twins live. I can rebase and re-run the gates — flagging it as a draft rather than pretending it merges clean. It is also worth noting that main currently does not build on a Mac at all (#2860, compile at `477ac13` / link at `a2de744`; #2895 looks like the fix), so the rebase would need that too.
- The `msl_has_mpp()` oracle + the `__has_include` guards are the part I think is worth merging even if the tile choices stay a follow-up; happy to split it that way if you prefer two reviews.
- The twins are ~350 lines of MSL that only exist for SDKs older than Metal 4 and are dead code on a 26 toolchain. If you would rather not carry them, the alternative is documenting that old-SDK Macs get the window path — but on this machine that is a 3× prefill cliff, and we would rather they lived upstream than in a local patch.
- Open question for you: should `mm_gu2_*_16_32_32_2` also become the MPP default? It is faster for the twins here, and the guard is only about which tile the legacy branch asks for.

Environment: macOS 15.8, Xcode Command Line Tools' macOS 15 SDK, Apple M2 Max (96 GB), engine 0.1.44.1-metal.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: 2x RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, Threadripper 3970X, Flash-Next IQ3_S (0.1.44)
pulls.author: dWacing
pulls.body:
Adds a community benchmark report to `bench/results/` and an index line to `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

**Setup:** 2x RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB on PCIe gen4 x8/x8 (ASRock Rack TRX40D8-2N2T), Threadripper 3970X (AVX2 only, no AVX-512), 128 GB quad-channel DDR4-2666, Ubuntu Server 24.04 headless. Flash-Next **IQ3_S** at 262K context with KV streaming, layer split 25, `--pcie-frac 0.20`.

**Why this report:** the only existing 2x5060 Ti IQ3_S report (2026-10-02) ran 0.1.34 on PCIe gen3 with an 8-core desktop CPU and reached 56-63 tok/s decode; the newer rerun reports reach ~85 but with the lighter IQ3_XXS. This box shows IQ3_S on two 5060 Ti reaching that decode level when the cards get gen4 and a strong AVX2 CPU pool.

**Numbers (suite 1, 3 runs each):** decode 93.6 tok/s short chat, prompt 1185 / 2002 tok/s at 4K / 16K fresh, agent session 90.4 tok/s with 68.8 % conversation-cache hit.

**Extras that may be useful beyond the numbers:**
- A/B: `--prefill auto:32768` is **worse** on a two-card layer split (16K fresh 1531 vs 1895 tok/s; the big chunk borrows the second card's expert-cache slots) — the +21-35 % community reports find for it apply to single-GPU setups.
- A/B: layer split 25 slightly ahead of 20 on this box.
- Measured cost of `"parallel": 2` on 16 GB cards: 0.51 GiB of VRAM per slot per card, expert caches 5106/4393 -> 4528/3883 slots (-11 % per card).
- ESP (experimental speed projection) is ON in all runs, flagged in the report (community reports do not use it).

Speed suite only — no needle/recall check was run.

pulls.title: batch-groups: MTP drafts in the pipelined slot groups (STRATA_PIPED_MTP, opt-in)
pulls.author: JacobSussan
pulls.body:
Closes #2973.

## Summary

With a layer split, `--batch` pipelines the slots in groups (one group per stage), but the pipelined path runs no MTP drafts, and `--batch-mtp` with serial windows leaves all but one card waiting (on four stages it lost 30-40% of the four streams' total against the pipelined default).

`STRATA_PIPED_MTP=N` (with `--batch-mtp`) keeps the pipeline and drafts in it: each group's window carries its slot's token and up to N MTP proposals (at most `--spec` - 1; the first always, each further one while the draft layer was at least `--spec-min-p` sure of the one before, the solo path's rule). It needs one slot per group (as many slots as stages, which `--batch-groups auto` gives for that count) and is left off, with a line at start, otherwise. Default off: nothing changes without the variable.

## How it works

How many rows to keep is known only when the last stage has picked, and by then the earlier stages already run other groups' windows, which reuse the scratch the commit replays from.

- `Verifier::batch_launch_rows`: the group's window, then a small save graph that copies the rows the commit replays (each GDN layer's conv and recurrence inputs, each QSA layer's raw indexer keys, the PLE history snapshot) to the group's own hand-off rows of a per-stage buffer (`init_deferred_commit`). No commit.
- `Verifier::batch_commit_rows`: after the verdict, every stage queues the commit of the kept rows on its own stream (no host wait). It runs before that group's next window on the stage, and the GDN state and indexer tail are untouched until then, as for a solo window. The accepted prefixes come from a per-slot mapped area that is written again only at that slot's next verdict, after its next window has passed the stage.
- The slot's drafter (the `--batch-mtp` slot drafters) catches up on the window's final rows and drafts the next proposals as an asynchronous chain (`chain_launch`, so the pipeline goes on meanwhile). The rows are copied on the last stage's stream, ahead of its next window, and the chain waits on an event after the copy. A group whose chain has not landed lets another group start first.
- A drain (and the moment every slot is done) waits for the queued commits and chains, so an admission, a parked conversation or the solo path taking a slot back sees the final state.
- With it on, the stages keep the window size they have without `--batch-mtp`. `--batch-mtp` alone sizes them for 8-row serial windows, which also lets a lone request's windows grow; here a lone file edit then measured 160 against 178 tok/s.
- `batch_groups::resolve` gains `mtp_piped` (with unit tests), and docs/BATCHING.md a section.

## Exactness

`tools/batch_test.py` (4 slots on a 4-GPU split, 200 and 300 tokens, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0`): every slot decodes exactly the tokens it decodes alone, for `STRATA_PIPED_MTP` = 1, 2 and 3, and for the default path with the same binary. Windows per slot for 1131 tokens: 1131 (default), 652 (N = 1), 506 (N = 2), 455 (N = 3).

## Measured

4x RTX 3090 (PCIe 3.0 x8, no P2P), 2x Xeon Gold 6126, Linux, CUDA 13.2, UD-Q4_K_XL, split 11,24,36, `--trim-stage-weights`, `"parallel": 4` (4 groups of 1), `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.70`, FP16 K/V, `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1`. Four concurrent 900-token answers through the HTTP server, reasoning off, total output tok/s:

| | default | `=1` | `=2` | `=3` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| code (median of 3) | 203 | 244-269 (2 runs) | 270 | 259 (1 run) |
| prose (median of 3) | 209 | 230-240 (2 runs) | 216 | 215 (1 run) |
| a file returned with one rename (1 run; mostly its 3K-token prompts) | 129 | 140-142 | 144 | 153 |
| one request alone: code / edit / prose | 134 / 175 / 96 | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

Proposals kept at N = 1: code 88%, the edit 97%, prose 62%. On this rig a two-row window costs about 1.5x a one-row window (`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE`: the routed experts of two tokens, 0.44 -> 0.74 ms, and the host's plan on the stages that miss experts), which is why prose gains little. Cost: the saved rows (25 MiB per stage at N = 1 with 4 slots, 51 MiB at N = 3), the slot drafters as `--batch-mtp` has them, and the extra graphs per row count.

## Not run

AMD (HIP), the draft layer on the first stage (`mtp_first`: the row copy and its event would then cross devices), helper expert caches, more than one slot per group.

pulls.title: fix(Mac): 0.1.45 does not compile on Metal (three CUDA-only calls in shared host files)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body:
## Summary

0.1.45's Mac build should stop in two shared host files: three changes in this release call CUDA names that `metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h` does not provide. This adds the Metal side of each, the way the code already does it elsewhere. CUDA and HIP are unchanged.

## What changed

| where | came with | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/core/verify.cpp`, `make_stream` | #2326 (its last commit, fcf93bde, was not ported; @qiuzan2001 found it) | `&& !defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)`, as `mtp.cpp` guards the same two calls (default priority) |
| `src/core/verify.cpp`, `device_is_sm75` | #2222 | Metal answers false, as HIP does (no Turing card, no compute capability) |
| `metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h` | #2666's peer-copy probe (`peer_experts.cpp`) | `cudaMemcpyPeer` (the peer async copy and a sync; one GPU) and `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess` (unsupported, as enabling is), as e6ad6c81 added them to the HIP shim |

## How I checked

There is no Mac here, so I compiled the Mac build's shared host sources the way `metal/CMakeLists.txt` does (`metal/include/metal_compat` and `metal/include` first, `STRATA_GPU_METAL=1`, `STRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS=1`, C++20), syntax only, with g++ 13 on Linux:

- **0.1.45:** 32 of the 34 files are clean; two fail with these 7 errors:
  ```
  src/core/verify.cpp:285: 'cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/verify.cpp:286: 'cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/verify.cpp:859: 'cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/verify.cpp:860: 'cudaStreamCreateWithPriority' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/peer_experts.cpp:72: 'cudaMemcpyPeer' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/peer_experts.cpp:157: 'cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess' was not declared in this scope
  src/core/peer_experts.cpp:158: 'cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess' was not declared in this scope
  ```
- **This branch:** all 34 files are clean.
- **CUDA:** the preprocessed `verify.cpp` and `peer_experts.cpp` are identical before and after (CUDA 13.0 headers).
- **HIP:** both changed lines in `verify.cpp` take the branch they took before, and the shim is only on the Metal include path.

Not checked: a real Mac build and link (Apple clang, the metal-cpp side, the Metal kernels in `metal/src/engine`, which this does not touch), and running it.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL, engine 0.1.45 (official suite, --long, MTP 2)
pulls.author: qni-live
pulls.body:
One folder under `bench/results/`, produced by `tools/strata_bench.py --long` on v0.1.45 (three runs per test, medians).

Machine: one RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 GB, 200 W, GPU memory 14,000 MHz; the second card of the box was idle), Threadripper 7960X, 61 GiB RAM, Linux, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.2.
Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (Unsloth, with the MTP block), own `qwen35` path, every main-layer expert resident in VRAM, 65,536 context, `--mtp 2`, vision on.

| Test | Result (median) |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | 259.5 tok/s |
| 4K prompt | 6,968 tok/s, first token 0.58 s |
| 16K prompt | 6,123 tok/s, first token 2.63 s |
| 32K prompt | 4,855 tok/s, first token 6.62 s |
| agent session, follow-up turns | decode 161.7 tok/s, first token 1.50 s, cache hit 0 % |
| `--clients 4` (separate run, 32K context, 4 slots) | 403.9 tok/s total |

Things worth knowing, all measured on this machine:
- **MTP drafts only run with explicit zero penalties.** `Sampling::needs_logits()` sends any request with a repetition, frequency or presence penalty to the one-token path, and a request next to others also gets no drafts. With the server's default sampling the first run of this suite had `drafts accepted 0 of 0` everywhere (short chat 183.6 tok/s, agent 137.3 tok/s). This entry has `temperature 0, presence_penalty 0, repetition_penalty 1.0, frequency_penalty 0` in the config's `sampling` block, and the suite shows `drafts accepted 1207 of 1786` (68 %). Decode over context (3 runs, medians): `--mtp 0` / `2` / `4` = 166.5 / 246.9 / 240.2 tok/s at 1K and 113.1 / 125.0 / 109.9 tok/s at 16K. Prompt speed is unchanged by drafts.
- **`--batch-mtp` with 4 sessions aborts** (`--max-context 32768`, `--mtp 2`, `--batch-mtp`, parallel 4; the MTP block had 163 of 256 experts in VRAM, the rest in the CPU pool): the first multi-session step ends with `strata-q36: cudaMemcpyAsync(ecpu, cpu_out, ...) failed: operation failed due to a previous error during capture (src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:2284)`, then `terminate called ... native MMVQ launch: operation failed due to a previous error during capture`. With `STRATA_Q36_NO_MTP_CPU=1` it runs (65 % of drafts accepted), but that switches every layer to the hybrid mode (prompt speed halves: 4K 3,173 instead of 5,487 tok/s) and `--clients 4` gave 364.9 tok/s against 403.9 without `--batch-mtp`, so I cannot tell whether `--batch-mtp` itself helps. I did not look further into the cause.
- For comparison, the same suite without drafts on a RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF (24 GB, 70 W; 96 of 256 experts per layer in VRAM, the rest in host memory): short chat 82.3 tok/s, 4K prompt 1,770 tok/s, 32K first token 22.1 s.
- Speed only; no correctness check. The agent cache hit is 0 % (each turn re-reads the earlier turns).

*Written with AI assistance (Claude); numbers reviewed by me.*

pulls.title: [Engine] Durable opt-in lifetime token counters in Monitor
pulls.author: Zcg2021
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Monitor's existing session counters reset when the server restarts. This opt-in feature retains request/token totals across restarts, saves each settled request, and adds an all-time locally generated token count in a Usage card **at the bottom of Monitor**. Speed, hardware and cache remain first. When disabled, no usage ledger or lock file is created and no usage field or card appears.

## Related discussion

This builds on @wokhouse's #2370, retaining its six original commits and authorship. It addresses the persistence and disabled-UI concerns raised there, adds writer ownership and Windows validation, and keeps an all-time output headline. Related usage proposals: #2400 and #2204. #2370 was still closed and unmerged when checked.

This updates the existing consolidated proposal after the tracker reset. **Draft pending maintainer agreement on scope and how to consolidate overlapping proposals.** If #2370 is preferred, the reliability changes can be split out after that discussion; this is not a claim that the scope has been approved.

## Approach

Save at request settlement, not per token: unique temporary snapshot, flush/fsync, atomic replacement. Separate cross-process writer lock (`msvcrt` on Windows, `flock` on POSIX) prevents simultaneous servers overwriting a store. Sequential model profiles may share an explicitly configured path. Failed saves remain visible and retry without double counting; corrupt JSON is preserved. Time buckets are bounded. Optional undated imports are labelled and excluded from date windows and speed averages.

Only counters and timestamps are persisted: no prompts, answers, tool arguments or credentials. New settings default off; no native source, model, tokenizer, scheduler or cache-format changes. The UI here is the Python server's `serve/web` Monitor, not the separate new desktop/TUI interface.

During beta adaptation, a real lifecycle gap was reproduced: an embedded `server.main()` could return while retaining the ledger lock until process exit. The patch now closes ownership on normal stop, ready-file failure and HTTP bind failure, and unregisters its exit hook. Regression coverage exercises all three paths.

Enable with `"usage_stats": true` or `serve/server.py --usage-stats`. Optional `usage_stats_path` / `STRATA_USAGE_STATS` selects the file; the parent directory must exist. Simultaneous servers need separate stores. Keep the ledger when upgrading.

## Validation

Tested server revision `c7df4b95b8a30ce3bde61c3972c1ff0cc545a95d`, on upstream `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` / **0.2.0-beta**, October 19–20, 2026 (Europe/Berlin). Later commit adds documentation/evidence only. Windows 11, Python 3.13.1, Ryzen 9 5900X, 128 GB RAM, RTX 3090; macOS 27.0.1, Python 3.13.0, Apple M5 Pro. Mock engines only: no GPU inference or production service interruption.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_server serve.test_usage serve.test_usage_durability serve.test_monitor serve.test_prometheus serve.test_runconfig -q`: Windows **394 run, OK, 3 Unix-signal skips**, 133.889 s. Includes abrupt exit, concurrent recording, competing owners, write failure/retry, corrupt files, disconnect/tool accounting and beta lifecycle cleanup.
- `python docs/usage-v020/check_http.py` on Mac and Windows: eight requests per host, streaming/non-streaming Chat Completions and Responses, enabled/disabled statistics. Each arm produced 72 mock tokens; persisted counters matched API/session totals, reload preserved them, custom window matched. Disabled mode created no ledger/lock/metrics field. Payloads matched after excluding IDs and timestamps; no claim of byte-identical independent streams.
- Three lifecycle regression subcases pass after the fix.
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`, `git diff --check`.
- 1280×720 browser check: original Monitor order, Usage at bottom, permanent all-time total, Lifetime/7-day/Custom selections. Synthetic usage values are labelled in the report; screenshots are not model performance measurements.

**Failed:**

- Initial Mac system-Python attempt lacked `regex`: 296 tests, 146 errors. Switched to the prepared isolated venv; retained the setup failure log.
- Mac venv: **394 tests, one error**, 131.287 s. `VisionArgs.test_min_tokens_is_passed_only_when_set` uses a mock process without `pid`. The exact error reproduced on an unmodified upstream archive. The whole Mac suite is not reported as green.
- Before the lifecycle fix, all three new ownership subcases failed; before/after logs are retained.

**Not run:**

- Native builds/inference on CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal (their sources unchanged), physical power loss, a fresh inference/persistence benchmark, phone layout or separate desktop/TUI UI checks.
- October 17 native integration and persistence timing results remain historical evidence, not beta measurements.

[Full beta report, reproducible probe, screenshots and sanitized raw logs](https://github.com/Zcg2021/Strata/blob/e4ff9b2bc810331473971d2e954b695ff6afe372/docs/usage-v020/README.md).

## Limits

Active requests killed before settlement are excluded. Disk failures are visible and counts remain in memory until a successful save. Undated imports do not recover missing dates/history and must not duplicate already-counted work. The feature tracks the server's token accounting, including reasoning and tools, excluding reused input and rejected speculative drafts. This is not a performance improvement claim or a production deployment.

![Beta Monitor: Usage remains at the bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zcg2021/Strata/e4ff9b2bc810331473971d2e954b695ff6afe372/docs/usage-v020/usage-bottom.png)

pulls.title: [Engine] logit_bias: accept it with --batch (one bias table per slot)
pulls.author: qni-live
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`logit_bias` is refused whenever the engine runs with `--batch`. That makes the Han/Kana/Hangul ban (docs/LOGIT_BIAS.md) unusable on a 4-slot server, which is the setup for several parallel agents.

Result: each batch slot can carry its own bias table, and a bias reaches only its own request. A slot that is reused by a request without a bias carries nothing over. `--batch-mtp` still refuses it.

This PR is rebased on `main` for 0.2.0-beta (`e88ee39d`, tag `v0.2.0-beta`); it applies without conflicts. #1891 is already in `main`, so nothing of it is repeated here.

## Related discussion

none. There is no open issue; `--batch` answers `logit_bias` with HTTP 400 today. It is a focused change that lifts one refusal and adds no new request field.

## Approach

- `include/strata/core/verify.hpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`: `Verifier::set_slot_logit_bias(slot, bias, err)` and `slot_has_bias(slot)`. Only the final stage allocates a table (one float per vocabulary entry, about 1 MB for 248,320 tokens) and copies it, and only when it changed. `set_slot_sampling` keeps the slot's table pointer. `init_slots` frees and clears the tables.
- `sample_rows`: a greedy row whose slot has a table is drawn on the last stage like a sampled row, because the graph's argmax does not know the bias. Rows without a table take the same path as before.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the bias is set at admission, before `set_slot_sampling`; an empty one clears the slot. `--batch-mtp` still answers `ERR logit_bias: --batch-mtp does not take it yet`. `INFO` advertises `logit_bias_batch=1`.
- `serve/logit_bias.py`: the server refuses `--batch` only when the engine does not advertise `logit_bias_batch=1`, so older engines keep the clear 400.
- Tests: `tools/batch_test.py --bias-han` (every second prompt carries the ban and asks for Chinese) and the new `tools/batch_bias_reuse_test.py` (3 waves, banned and free prompts swap slots every wave; a slot's tokens must equal its solo tokens). `docs/LOGIT_BIAS.md` and `serve/test_logit_bias.py` updated.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (32 GB each), Linux 7.0.0-38, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.4 source build (sm_120) of `main` e88ee39d plus this commit (a7026916), Swift IQ3_XXS, `--batch 4 --trim-stage-weights --pipeline-windows 2`, layer split 25, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000`, 64 new tokens, 65,842 banned tokens (all Han/Kana/Hangul). Each test compares a slot's tokens with the same request run alone. Run on 2026-10-19; log `pr2977-tests-lauf.log`.

**Passed:**
- `python3 tools/batch_test.py ... --batch 4 --n 4 --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000 --batch-groups 1"`, no bias anywhere: 4 of 4 slots identical to solo.
- same with `--bias-han`, ban on 2 of 4 slots, greedy, `--batch-groups 1`: 4 of 4 identical, 0 Han/Kana/Hangul characters in the banned slots.
- same, `--batch-groups` auto: 4 of 4 identical, 0 CJK characters in the banned slots.
- `python3 tools/batch_bias_reuse_test.py ... --waves 3`, greedy: 12 of 12 slot rows identical to solo, RESULT: PASS.
- same, sampled (`temperature=0.7 top_k=20 seed=7`): 12 of 12 identical, RESULT: PASS.
- `python3 -m pytest serve/test_logit_bias.py`: 12 passed, 19 subtests passed.
- `cmake --build build -j 40`: builds (CUDA).

**Failed:**
none observed on this revision. My first run of the series used a relative `--exe` that resolved to an older build and answered `continuous batching is not supported`; I discarded it and reran with an absolute path. The results above are from the rerun only.

**Not run:**
- HIP and SYCL builds: the change touches `src/core/verify.cpp` and `src/program/generate.cpp`; only CUDA was built and run.
- Throughput cost and the CJK rate over 150 prompt pairs in batch: measured on the 0.1.45 base for the earlier version of this PR (10 of 150 answers in Chinese script without the ban, 0 of 150 with it; -1 to -3 % batch throughput; +21 ms fixed cost per request), not repeated on 0.2.0-beta.
- A byte comparison of the default path (no bias, `--batch`) against the packaged 0.2.0-beta engine 0.1.45.3. The no-bias slots equal their solo run on the changed build; I did not diff them against the release binary.
- `--batch-mtp` with a bias after the rebase (it is unchanged by this PR), the Qwen3.6 engine path, layer splits over three or more GPUs, and a start with the Windows or Mac engine.

## Limits

- `--batch-mtp` still refuses `logit_bias`.
- Tested on two GPUs, CUDA only, four slots, 64-token requests.
- Written with Claude Code (AI-assisted); I ran and checked every test above on my hardware.
