pulls.title: serve: an opt-in strict_model that refuses a request naming another model
pulls.author: BoogeAI
pulls.body:
## Title

serve: an opt-in `strict_model` that refuses a request naming another model

Issue: Refs #2717

## Summary

The three client routes answer **any** model name with whatever is loaded, and the reply's own `model` is the
server's, so a client pointed at another local model (a fine-tune vs the base, two configs on one port) cannot
tell it is being answered by the wrong weights. `/props` has always refused an unknown name; this makes that
opt-in for the routes a client actually talks to, so a mismatch fails loudly instead of silently.

`"strict_model": true` in `strata-<model>.json`: a request whose `"model"` is neither the served name nor an
alias is refused with the 404 `/props` already uses. Absent or `false` keeps today's path exactly as it is; a
request with no `model`, an empty one or a non-string is still accepted, because every route has always read
that as "this server's model" (`Service.model_for`).

## What changed

- **`serve/server.py`** (+27)
  - `Service.strict_model` (default `False`) and `Service.model_is_served(req)`: `False` only when the request
    names a non-empty string that is not in `model_names()`.
  - The check sits where the three routes are dispatched, next to `begin_request`: `404` with
    `{"error": {"type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "model_not_found", "message": "model not found"}}`
    (`responses_error_body(...)` on `/v1/responses`, as that route already shapes its errors), and one line in
    the log naming the asked and the served models.
  - `main()` reads `strict_model` (a non-boolean stops the start, like `reasoning_close_retry`) and prints one
    line when it is on.
- **`serve/test_server.py`** (+60): a `StrictModel` case over all three routes - the default still answers any
  name, the opt-in refuses another name, and the served name / no model / an empty model are accepted.

## Extra Notes

**How I checked.** Measured against a real server (0.1.45 prebuilt CUDA 13.0, RTX 5080 16 GB, Windows 11
26200, a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next fine-tune loaded):

| request `model` | `strict_model` off (before) | on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the served name | 200 | 200 |
| another model's name (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`) | 200, answered by the loaded model | **404** on all three |
| a deliberate nonsense name | 200 | **404** |
| no `model` field / `"model": ""` | 200 | 200 |

The 404 body on the chat and Anthropic routes is the one above; on `/v1/responses` it is
`{"error": {"message": "model not found", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": null, "code": "model_not_found"}}`.

**What it leaves alone.** The engine, the kernels, setup, `/props` and `/v1/load|unload` (which already
checked), and the behaviour of every request when the config does not set the key - no name is looked at then.
`/v1/messages/count_tokens` is deliberately not gated: it does not answer with weights.

**In the field.** A front-end that declares both local models on one route and a picker that says "the
fine-tune" while the base model is loaded: with the key on, that pick now returns 404 instead of an answer from
the wrong weights (this is what prompted the issue).

**Not tested.** AMD HIP and SYCL (CUDA only here); an aliased model (the configs I have carry no `aliases`, so
`model_is_served` only ever sees the name) - the alias case is covered by using `model_names()` unchanged.

pulls.title: bench: 2x Arc Pro B50 SYCL IQ3_XXS at 256K context
pulls.author: pankleks
pulls.body:
## Results-only community report

Two Intel Arc Pro B50 (Battlemage G21, `xe`, 16.2 GB each) with `--layer-split 25`, native SYCL Release JIT build, Strata 0.1.45 at `477ac13c`, original Flash-Next GSQ-RCO **IQ3_XXS** at the full **262,144-token** configured context.

- Official `strata_bench.py`, three runs per case, warm-up and loading excluded, fresh-prompt cache reuse 0.
- Prompt medians: **607.0 / 678.1 / 662.0 tok/s** at actual 4,019 / 16,058 / 32,049 tokens. Pooled short-chat decode **30.8 tok/s** (28.9-40.2, nine capped requests), median TTFT 0.89 s.
- Three six-turn agent/tool sessions: follow-up decode median **33.3 tok/s**, conversation-cache hit median **68.75 %**.
- Needle recall **6/6** at nominal 32K and 128K (depths 10/50/90 %). The tool's 262k rows are refused with HTTP 400 because its 2 %-under sizing collides with a full window; separately, a fresh **258,039-token** prompt completed at **379.5 tok/s** and returned all three anchors, so long prompts are served.
- Documents that prompt throughput falls off with length on this path (662 at 32K, 379 at 258K) while decode does not, and why: KV stays in pinned RAM via `--kv-resident`, so raising the context cost 103 host-served experts and 1 MiB of VRAM.

Bare-metal office host (Ryzen 9 5950X, 60.7 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04.1, oneAPI 2026.1.1), GPU firmware `21.1182`, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0` required by the layer split. README separates the two-GPU split, the shared n-gram shard and the memory plan from what the automatic collector cannot see. Peak VRAM, power and thermals were not captured for this run.

Includes per-request JSON, recall results, hand-collected host/configuration/version/hash facts and reproduction instructions. Credentials, hostnames, office-LAN details and private workload content are excluded. Five new report files only; no engine or headline-performance changes.

pulls.title: bench: 4x V100-SXM2 + NVLink platform dossier - P2P measured end to end, #2525's data-path question closed, a validated A/B stand (no engine changes)
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
A follow-up to #2525 on the same machine (Minisforum MS-01 + Spring V100-SXM2-NVLINK_D carrier, 4x Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB, NVLink 2.0, engine 0.1.44.1 = `296b59d2`, IQ3_S, 262144). #2525 left one question its own counters could not answer - which flow the 62-78 GB per card during a long prefill actually is - and measured P2P at two sizes only. This folder is the rest of that measurement: the full P2P size ladder, the engine's own counters read against them, the SM70 kernel inventory, and an A/B stand whose noise floor has itself been measured. **No engine changes - measurements, probes and scripts only.**

To be explicit about intent, because I would not want this read as a request: this is not a push for V100 support. The support matrix starting at sm_75 and Volta being a community-tested target in [docs/NVIDIA_V100.md](../main/docs/NVIDIA_V100.md) is the right arrangement for an architecture CUDA 13 no longer builds, and this machine runs a community build and will keep doing so. Everything below is the data half of a question I got curious about, written so that anyone can use a piece of it or ignore all of it.

Three reasons it may still be worth a minute:

1. The *Limits* section of `NVIDIA_V100.md` says a layer split over V100s was not measured. This is such a measurement - four cards, `--layer-split auto`, 262144 context, out to 125 011 prompt tokens, with the engine's counters in the frame.
2. Two of the findings are not about Volta at all, and would show up on any layer-split machine: the `auto` split search is degenerate on this build, and a different split is worth +4.5 % / +7.3 % prompt. Neither involves an sm_70 code path.
3. One transport fact is not about Strata either: on this board a kernel reading a peer's VRAM directly reaches 0.94 of a `cudaMemcpyPeer` copy, which changes what a P2P route would have to allocate - or lets it not allocate at all.

## Status labels used throughout

Every claim in the folder is marked **measured** (this machine), **calculated** (arithmetic on measured numbers), **hypothesis** (not tested) or **not measured**. Nothing is presented as a fact on the strength of the code alone. Where a claim rests on the code plus a match of volumes rather than on a counter, it says so.

## The interconnect, measured end to end

`p2p-results.md`, `p2p-matrix.csv`, `p2p-benchmark.csv` (211 rows: 17 sizes 4 KiB..256 MiB x 6 pairs x 2 directions, no gaps), probes in `probes/`.

- NVLink is fully up and healthy: 24 links, 2 per pair at 25.781 GB/s, P2P and native atomics on all 6 pairs, `CudaArrayAccessSupported = 1`, and enabling peer access costs **0 MiB** of VRAM.
- Peer copy: a **38.77 GB/s plateau**, identical on all six pairs in both directions (256 MiB), reproduced from #2525's 38.8 with a 0.08 % difference. Fixed cost **6.7 us**: `T = 6.7 us + size / 38.8 GB/s`; 50 % of the plateau at 256 KiB, 80 % at 1 MiB, >= 99 % at >= 32 MiB.
- **The 38.8 GB/s ceiling is per device, not per pair or per link**: six pairs running at once give 77.50 GB/s total, 12.92 GB/s per pair (a 3.00x fall). What sets the limit is still a hypothesis.
- **Direct kernel access to a peer's VRAM is a usable transport**: reading a peer's memory from a kernel 32.13 -> 36.25 GB/s at 32 -> 256 MiB = **0.838 -> 0.936 of a peer copy**; copy done inside a kernel 36.63; writing into a peer 36.64; two kernels reading at each other on one pair **65.1 GB/s**. 576 rows, 0 correctness errors, all 12 ordered pairs. This is the new result, and it is what decides the shape of the transport note below.

## The open question from #2525 (its §9.1): answered

#2525 asked which flow moves 62-78 GB into each card during a long prefill - expert streaming or activation staging. It is expert streaming, and three independent sources agree:

- the engine's own counter for a 125 011-token request: `for 269454.7 MB of expert reads`, with `the OS read 1.3 MB from storage (0 major faults)` - i.e. 269 GB taken from the page cache and pushed to the devices; a second session logs 269 472 MB;
- #2525's own PCIe counters for the same shape of request: 270.5 GB into the four cards;
- the slot arithmetic: the prompt path borrows 1954/1841/1706/1631 cache slots for its buffers while all four expert caches are filled exactly (5632/5632, 6656/6656, 6144/6144, 5469/6144), so ~1954 experts x ~2.05 MB x 16 chunks is ~64 GB per card, against 61.9-78.4 GB measured.

Activation staging between stages - the flow a P2P route would carry - is 32.2 GB per request by calculation from the code, which matches #2525's measured 35.2 GB TX within 9 %. So the dominant flow is host->card and the inter-card flow is ~10 % of the bytes.

**And on this machine the dominant flow cannot be moved to NVLink at all**, not as a limitation of the patch but of the geometry: for NVLink to carry an expert, another card has to be holding it, and with a layer split each stage holds only its own layers, all four caches are filled exactly, and 4 x 16 GB of VRAM cannot duplicate 50.3 GB of experts. That is a calculation on measured geometry, and it is the reason the notes below do not propose "put expert streaming on NVLink".

## Two findings that are not about this hardware

**(a) The `--layer-split auto` search is degenerate on this build, and the choice is worth several percent.** Thirty search lines in the working log give four different splits, all scored `predicted 28.4 ms` (`K=12,25,37` x20, `11,24,36` x5, `11,24,37` x4, `11,25,37` x1); the choice moves between runs of the same binary and the same config. Pinning `12,25,37` instead of `auto` measures **+4.48 % prompt tok/s at 31 307 and +6.66..+7.33 % at 122-125k, TTFT -4.2..-6.8 %**, in two independent pairs of cells. The mechanism is visible in the counters: +512 cache slots on CUDA0 (5632 -> 6144), coverage on the narrow CUDA3 89.0 % -> 96.6 %, residency 97 % -> 99 %, -13.1 GB of expert stream per request. The search criterion does not see the cost of the LM head on the last stage, the prefill pipeline, per-card residency, or the cost of streaming.

This is also why this machine's profile sits 1.5-5.7 % below #2525's at the **same binary (sha256 `bdfec9f5..`) and byte-identical config**: the cause was found by pinning the split, and it is the `auto` choice (`11,24,36` vs `12,25,37`) - not the version, not the hardware, not background load, not warm-up. Anyone comparing two reports from one machine should know that the split search can be the variable.

**(b) A structural identity between VRAM and host bytes.** Each cache slot given to something else becomes a non-resident expert that is re-read on every 8192-token chunk, so for a prompt of length T: **1 MiB taken from the expert cache = (T / 8192) MiB of extra host traffic per request**. Two consequences that are arithmetic rather than opinion: moving the hand-off buffers into VRAM saves exactly the bytes it costs (net 0 on a machine with a full cache), while reading the peer's VRAM from a kernel, with no receiving buffer, is net -16.1 GB per request. Freeing VRAM the other way - not trimming CUDA0 at `auto` - is where the bytes actually are.

The calibrated price of a host byte here is about 3.9 GB/s (one pair of configurations: -13 967 MB of host traffic against -3.59 s of TTFT), i.e. 1 GiB of traffic ~ 0.27 s of TTFT ~ 0.5 % at 125k. That is one pair of points in a narrow neighbourhood and it overstates larger reductions; it is quoted so that any idea can be priced before it is built, not as a prediction.

## What is not proven, and said so in the folder

- **No NVLink byte counters exist on this machine** (DCGM 4.7.0 without the profiling module; NVML Sampling & Reporting absent in both 580.178.04 and 595.91.07). Every routing statement is indirect: code + the match between the engine's counters and `rxpci`/`txpci`. No tool ever showed a byte on a link.
- In 0.1.44.1 a layer-split machine issues **no GPU->GPU copy at all**: `--peer-device` with `--layer-split` is refused by the parser, and the stage-helper route is hard-wired `p2p = false` (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1591`). Whether a P2P route would be faster here is **not measured** - only that the transport is capable and what the byte budget is.
- `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP` / `..._FRAC` change nothing measurable on this machine (two sessions each), and `--peer-device` cannot be turned on for lack of free VRAM: both are 0 % here, and the folder does not pretend otherwise.
- **Decode is not a usable measure on this machine**: up to 7.8 % session-to-session spread with an unchanged config, because draft acceptance itself moves 3-7 percentage points. The folder reports decode only as a "must not get worse" control.
- Changing `--layer-split` changes the output on a long prompt: at 10 012 tokens the `auto` and `12,25,37` answers share a 32-character prefix out of 647; at 1259 tokens they are identical. Reported as an observation (F-8); the mechanism is not established, and it is why a placement change cannot be accepted by bit-identity alone.
- GPU3 is not reachable from an external CUDA context while the service runs (`cudaSetDevice(3)` -> out of memory, ~328 MiB free); with the service stopped it behaves exactly like the other three (<= 0.06 GB/s difference).
- Everything is one concurrent request. Concurrent serving was not studied.

## Volta compatibility, checked rather than assumed

`sm70-compatibility.md`, `correctness-report.md`, `correctness-matrix.csv` (41 rows: 27 PASS, 4 LIMITATION, 3 FINDING, 7 GAP). **2084 kernels from 62 cubin/PTX objects load with no error and no JIT**, resource limits are not exceeded (max 255 registers, 41 104 B shared), the SM70 paths are on by default, and the `>= sm_75` requirements are covered by fallback paths - a 20-row "component -> requirement -> check" table. The SM70 numeric primitives (HMMA, fp32/fp16 GEMM) match a CPU reference within `1e-4 * K`; P2P copy and cross-card synchronisation are correct 37/37. Greedy generation is bit-reproducible within one placement configuration and across service restarts; the **first request after any change to engine state returns different text**, and the expert-cache hit rate warms 98.8 -> 99.8 % over 2-3 requests - which is why the stand repeats a request until two `text_sha` match before timing anything.

## A stand that is already validated, in case a branch ever needs a run

`ab-stand.md` and `test-plan.md`, implementation in `scripts/`. It runs a 2x2 matrix plus a repeat of the base (`auto:base -> auto:patched -> split12:base -> split12:patched -> auto:base`), so the repeat sets the noise threshold for that run; it takes a manifest of sha256 for binary, config and scripts plus `build_info` from `/props`; it waits for three readiness signals rather than a sleep; it requires bit-identical output before benchmarking (and says why that check cannot apply to a placement change); it fixes output length with `logit_bias` on the EOS ids and checks `finish_reason`; and it extracts the counters that matter - `MB of expert reads`, `the OS read ... (major faults)`, cache slot counts, `the prompt path borrows ...`, `layer split auto:`, per-card `rxpci`/`txpci`.

Measured noise, so that a difference can be called a difference: **prompt tok/s 0.06 % at 122k, 0.14 % at 32k, 0.42 % at 4k between sessions**; the reproduction of the pinned-split gain in a second independent pair of cells was +4.48 % and +6.66 %. Significance thresholds used: |delta| > 1 % at >= 32k, > 2 % at 4k.

The machine is available and cheap to use: any branch builds here with a private CUDA 12.8 / gcc-14 in about 20 minutes, rolls back in two, and a full A/B run needs one ~40 minute service window. Happy to run anything you point at - and equally happy to run nothing. Nothing in this folder asks for a decision.

## Contents

`bench/results/2026-10-17-community-4x-v100-nvlink-platform/`

- `README.md` - index and the short engineering report: what is confirmed, what is not, the bottleneck, what is proven vs not proven, the order in which the notes sug

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) via OCuLink x4 eGPU dock on a UGREEN iDX6011 Pro NAS — Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 262K, depth sweep to 248K
pulls.author: faf-net
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

This report answers one question for a hardware combination no existing report covers: can a 24 GB gfx1100 card in an **eGPU dock behind an OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x4 link**, hosted by a **NAS with a hybrid laptop-class CPU and LPDDR5X**, serve Flash-Next **IQ3_XXS at the full 262,144-token context**, how does speed hold up with context depth, and does Strata cost quality against mainline llama.cpp on the same file?

Results only: the PR adds one folder, `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rx-7900-xtx-oculink-nas/`, and changes nothing else.

Hardware: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB in a UGREEN LinkStation dock (own PSU), OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x4 · UGREEN iDX6011 Pro, Core Ultra 7 255H (6 P + 8 E + 2 LP-E, no AVX-512), 64 GB LPDDR5X · UGOS Pro 1.19 (Debian 12 base), kernel 6.18.15.

Results (medians, engine timings):

- `strata_bench.py --long`: chat decode 63.7 tok/s; prompt 741 / 1,195 / 1,224 tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K; agent session cache hit 68.6 %, decode 74.0 tok/s
- Context-depth sweep, fresh prompts 1K → 248K: decode **62.0 → 56.1 tok/s** with MTP, 48.9 → 44.9 without the MTP head; prefill 1,080–1,270 tok/s from 16K to 248K over the x4 link; MTP acceptance 48–57 %
- `needle_bench.py`: **9/9** at 32K, 128K and 250K (depths 10/50/90 %)
- **Quality vs mainline llama.cpp on the same GGUF** (`quant_quality.py` text set, 4,995 positions, teacher-forced): **95.7 % same top token, KL 0.020, perplexity 4.009 vs 4.017**, the same gap as between Strata's own CPU and GPU expert paths (95.7 %, KL 0.018)
- `--pool-workers` on the hybrid CPU (IQ2_XS): automatic 56.1 tok/s, 9 workers 76.8 tok/s, so the automatic count was 27 % slower. `--pool-affinity measure` (0.1.45) detected the CPU as "8 P-cores / 8 threads, 8 E-cores" (the 255H has 6 P + 8 E + 2 LP-E). This is a data point for the new physical-core worker default in 0.2.0, which I have not measured
- `--pcie-frac 0` over x4: 76.9 against 76.8 tok/s with the automatic fraction, no loss
- 0.1.44.1 vs 0.1.45 on gfx1100: no measurable speed difference; greedy output differed in 2 of 3 short prompts that 0.1.44.1 answered identically twice
- Card power: 286 W decode, 318 W prefill, 58 W idle with the model loaded

What it adds next to the existing gfx1100 reports (`2026-10-06-community-rx-7900-xtx`, `2026-10-04-community-rx7900xtx-hipblaslt-100500`, `2026-10-03-community-rx7900xtx-rocm102-nightly`) and the one eGPU report (`2026-10-06-community-rtx3090-egpu-64gb`): an x4 OCuLink link instead of a full slot, a NAS host with LPDDR5X and a hybrid CPU, the full 262K context with a depth sweep, and an engine-vs-engine quality comparison.

## Related discussion

none (results-only report; no default, engine or documentation change is proposed)

## Approach

The folder follows `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`: `README.md` in the report template, `results.json` and `bench-output.md` (unedited `strata_bench.py` output), `depth-sweep.jsonl` with `depth_sweep.py` and `charts.py`, `needles-*.json`, and in `quality-vs-llamacpp/` the per-position logprob files of both engines plus the two small scripts that produced and compared them. Field names in `depth-sweep.jsonl` are German; each is explained in the README. Host names, addresses and keys are removed. No model files or packs.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `.venv/bin/python tools/strata_bench.py --url <server> --long` · Strata `296b59d` source build (engine 0.1.44.1), HIP, ROCm 7.10.0a20251120 (TheRock wheels), Ubuntu 24.04 container · 2026-10-17 · results above, `results.json`, `bench-output.md`
- `.venv/bin/python tools/needle_bench.py --url <server> --lengths 32k,128k --depths 10,50,90`, then `--lengths 250k` · same build · 9/9 found · `needles-*.json`
- `quant_quality.py run --config <server config>`, once with the default yardstick settings and once with `--gpu-experts auto`; llama.cpp mainline build 11610 (`091b6a7fc`, Vulkan) fed the same token ids via `llamacpp_logpos.py`; compared with `compare_engines.py` · 95.68 % top-1, KL 0.0198 (GPU experts) / 0.020 (CPU experts)
- `python3 depth_sweep.py --url <server> --model <name> --label mit-mtp`, then without `--mtp` · 2–3 runs per depth · `depth-sweep.jsonl`
- 0.1.45 comparison: source build at tag `v0.1.45`, same settings, our own script (`messen/bench.py` in the linked repo), medians of 3
- 2026-10-19: GitHub reports this branch as mergeable against `main` (`e88ee39`); the PR only adds files, so no rebase was needed

**Failed:**
none observed (`results.json` and `bench-output.md` record no failed or cancelled requests)

**Not run:**
- 0.2.0-beta. The measurements describe `296b59d` / 0.1.44.1 (and 0.1.45 where marked). The 0.2.0 release notes list RX 7000 as compiled but not run; the machine is in daily use, so I have not tried it yet. If a gfx1100 run of 0.2.0-beta with the same scripts would help, I can add it to this folder in a follow-up commit.
- A coding or task-level suite. Quality is covered by the llama.cpp comparison (FP16 K/V, so `--kv int8` is not covered) and by the needles.
- `rocm-smi` inside the server container: GPU name, driver and model label in `bench-output.md` were not read by the tool and are filled in by hand in the README.
- Windows, other quants than IQ3_XXS / IQ2_XS, and the draft `BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md` (the tools do not implement it yet).

## Limits

- One machine, one day, with the NAS's other services running in the background (about 5 GiB RAM). 2 runs per depth at 128K and 248K.
- The baseline is the `296b59d` branch build between 0.1.44 and 0.1.44.1, not the 0.1.44.1 release.
- Depth-sweep prompts are word lists with a short story as output; MTP acceptance depends on the text.
- eGPU note for dock users (not a Strata issue): a dock link drop with a loaded ROCm model oopses kernel 6.18 in the KFD queue teardown, and with `panic_on_oops=1` the host reboots. Fixed upstream in Linux `6cca686dfce7` and `81665e35f143`.

Full write-up of the hardware setup: https://github.com/faf-net/ugreen-idx6011-egpu-llm

pulls.title: [Engine] metal: the gate/up grid follows the tile, so a K-quant layer covers its whole ffn width
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
The prompt chain's gate/up GEMM is dispatched over the wrong grid on a Mac without the M5 right-input layout, for
any pack whose routed gate/up is a K-quant.  It computes 160 of each expert's 640 gate/up rows and leaves the rest as
the previous layer left them, and the down GEMM reads that: wrong tokens, no error, no warning.

### What happens

The prompt GEMMs are dispatched indirectly, and `mm_scan` publishes the grids one MoE layer at a time.  Every one of
those fields is per layer — `meta[3]` is this layer's tile count — except the gate/up grid x, which the host wrote
**once per chunk** as the constant `NFF / 64` (`window.cpp:2132`, `prompt_chain.inc:96`).

The tile is not a constant.  It is chosen from the layer's quant type, and `gu2_tile()` hands Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K a
**TN-16** tile (`_16_16_128_2`).  `mm_gu2` writes TN output columns of `HS` per threadgroup (`moe_mm.metal:302`,
`f0 = tg.x * TN`), so the launch has to cover `NFF / TN` threadgroups.  With `NFF` 640 the constant gave 10 and the
K-quant tile needs 40: rows 0..159 written, 160..639 stale.

The kernel's own header said so — `moe_mm.metal:47`, *"gx_gu in meta[2] ... written by the host once"* — and the
dispatch picks the tile the grid has to match:

```cpp
} else {
    const std::string fn = "mm_gu2_" + std::to_string(eg.type) + gu2_tile(eg.type);   // TN 16 for the K-quants
    gu.tg[0] = 64;
}
```

### Reachability

No flag needed.  `docs/MAC.md:61` offers `--model ...|UD-Q6_K_XL` on any Apple Silicon Mac, and
`docs/UNSLOTH_Q6.md:35-38` records that pack's `ffn_gate_exps`/`ffn_up_exps` as Q6_K in 47 of 48 layers, with
`ffn_down_exps` Q8_0 (whose `mm_down2` instance exists, so the whole prompt path runs).  On an M1–M4 every prompt
chunk of 64 rows or more then multiplies garbage into the hidden states.  The non-M5 configurations the docs
measured use TN-64 tiles, which is why it had not been seen.

### What I changed

- **`metal/src/moe_tiles.h` (new)** — the v2 tiles and the TN each one writes, returned together so they cannot
  drift apart, plus the v3 tiles' TN/SG and the grid rule.
- **`metal/kernels/moe_mm.metal`** — `MmPlanArgs` carries `gu_gx`/`dn_gx` and `mm_scan` writes `meta[2]`/`meta[5]`
  from it.  It already writes the sibling fields per layer; one host value for the whole chunk cannot serve a tile
  that varies by layer.
- **`window.cpp` / `prompt_chain.inc`** — the plan carries the grid of *this layer's* tile, the v3 arm derives it
  from the tile it names, and the host writes are gone.
- The decode window needed nothing: it already derives its grid from the tile it picks
  (`window.cpp:834`, `NFF / (gs * (32 / gl) * gr)`).

### Why no test caught it

Both harnesses picked their v2 tile from a rule of their own instead of the engine's, so the engine's TN-16 dispatch
was never in front of a parity run:

```cpp
// prompt_chain.cpp, v2: TN 64 for every type
(fmt_unit32(eg.type) ? "_16_64_32_2" : "_16_64_16_2")
```

Both now use `gu2_tile`/`dn2_tile`, and `moe_mm_parity`'s v2 default parses the tile's own name back and refuses to
run if the name and its TN disagree.

### Tests

- **`metal/tests/moe_tile_grid_test.cpp` (new)** — a host test: no Metal device, no model, links nothing, registered
  with ctest, so it runs on a configured tree whether or not there is a card.  It checks the tile table, that every
  tile's name parses back to the TN it declares, that the TN divides the output width (an extra threadgroup writes
  past `HS`, a missing one leaves the tail unwritten), and that a K-quant layer's grid is 40 where the constant gave
  10.
  Compiled and run with MSVC 19.51 `/std:c++20`: **39 checks, all pass.**  With the header's K-quant TN put back to
  64 as a counter-proof, **four fail and it exits 1**.
- **`moe_mm_parity.cpp` / `prompt_chain.cpp`** — updated for the plan struct and to run the engine's own tiles.

### What I could not check

**Nothing here was built or run on macOS.** This review was done on Windows with no GPU and no Metal toolchain, so
the two harness changes are *not* run: they are the runs that would confirm the fix end to end, and they are the kind
of thing `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` asks for.  What I have is the host test above and the reading in this description.

### What I left alone

- The v3 (M5) arms already derived their grids from the tile they dispatch, in both files.
- `dn2_tile` returns TN 64 for every type, so the down grid was never wrong.  It is derived the same way now for
  symmetry, not because it was broken.
- The default path stays byte-identical: the v3 arm and every TN-64 tile compute the same grids as before.  The only
  layers whose dispatch changes are the v2 K-quant ones, which were wrong.

There is no issue for this — it came out of a static audit of the tree rather than a report.  Happy to file one if
you would rather triage it there first.

pulls.title: STRATA_LOOP_BREAK=1 (opt-in): a --serve reply that repeats one span three times is pushed out of the copy
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
﻿
## The problem

`repeat_stop_tokens` (#606) ends a reply stuck on one token. It never sees a model that writes the same sentence or
paragraph again and again, and that is the loop we meet in agent use: across 4.06M tokens of one user's opencode
sessions (Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS on a 12 GB laptop), 11% of the sessions longer than 3K tokens had a hard loop and 5.7% of
all tokens were repetition. One regex task ran a 29K-token loop of the same paragraph. Once a span has been written
three times the model's own probabilities keep it in the copy; sampling rarely leaves it.

## What it changes

With `STRATA_LOOP_BREAK=1`, the serve decode path watches the reply (not the prompt):

- For every period p = 1..512 it keeps `run[p]`, the number of tokens in a row equal to the one p before them (one
  compare per period per token). When `run[p] >= 2p` (three copies) and `run[p] >= STRATA_LOOP_BREAK_MIN` (default
  256 tokens), the reply enters break mode for `STRATA_LOOP_BREAK_SPAN` tokens (default 1024). A `<think>`,
  `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>` or ``` token ends break mode early, so it stays inside the span it began in.
- In break mode, before each window, it looks up where the reply's last 8 tokens occurred before (a hash of every
  8-gram -> where it last ended) and takes the token that followed them there: the token that would continue the copy.
  That one id gets `STRATA_LOOP_BREAK_BIAS` (default -100) in the window's FIRST row only. Rows past the first follow
  drafts the target has not taken yet.
- The sampler applies it in `sample_tokens` and in `sample_tokens_spec` (after its early returns, so a fallback never
  adds it twice), on the target's full-vocabulary rows only. The id and bias live in mapped host memory and are read
  by a one-thread kernel, so captured windows pick up each new value.
- One `strata serve: loop break: N loops broken, M windows with a banned copy token` line per request that needed it.

## What it leaves alone

- Unset (the default): `set_loop_ban` is never called and no kernel is launched, so the default path is unchanged.
- Set, but a reply never repeats a span three times: the kernel is launched with bias 0 and returns at once; the
  picks are the same as unset.
- `--pipeline-windows` decode (its next window is built before this one's tokens are known), batch slots and the
  multi-card drive are not covered.
- The edge token ids are Qwen3.8's (the tokenizer every supported Flash-Next build uses).

## Measured / checked

- Offline replay of the trigger over the 4.06M tokens above: it fired 96 times, each on a real loop; no false alarm.
- In daily use on our fork since 2026-10-14 (Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, RTX 5070 Ti Laptop, opencode).
- This branch: CUDA build (sm_120, CUDA 13, MSVC) clean. HIP and SYCL not built (the change is in
  `src/kernels/cuda/sampler.cu`, a plain kernel launch, and `generate.cpp`).
- SMOKE (2026-10-17, RTX 5070 Ti Laptop, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, this branch's engine `--serve` rebased on the current
  `main`, the branch's own server; the model ran in the RAM-budget file tier, so the run's tok/s are not comparable and
  are not a speed claim): with `STRATA_LOOP_BREAK=1` the repetition prompt ("write this sentence exactly 60 times,
  nothing else") ended after 9 lines / 2 unique (305 tokens) and the log carried
  `strata serve: loop break: 1 loops broken, 2 windows with a banned copy token`; with the variable unset the same
  prompt produced 50 identical lines / 1 unique (1750 tokens, 5.7x). A normal prompt (a median function) answered
  correctly in both arms; the two answers are equivalent but not byte-identical (temperature 1.0, and GPU/CPU expert
  rounding differs run to run in this configuration). The engine line above is the one the change promises.

pulls.title: Community Strix Halo bench: UD-Q4_K_XL vs UD-IQ4_XS on 121 GiB UMA (gfx1151)
pulls.author: ianmin2
pulls.body:
### What

Community Strix Halo (gfx1151) results comparing the two Unsloth quants on 121 GiB of unified memory: **UD-Q4_K_XL versus UD-IQ4_XS**, speed *and* correctness, on a machine running as a desktop with a live interactive workload rather than an isolated benchmark host.

`docs/STRIX_HALO.md` §"Measured" already gives the fast-settings A/B for these same two packs; this is the user-facing **"which one should I actually run"** question, where the answer is not the same on both axes.

### Machine

EVO-X2, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (**gfx1151**), 128 GB installed UMA (`MemTotal` 121.2 GiB), Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel `7.0.0-38-generic`, in-tree `amdgpu` (no DKMS), power mode `performance`. ROCm **7.14.1** (`/opt/rocm/core-7.14`, HSA/ROCr 1.21.0, `libamdhip64.so.7.14.60850`), bundled gfx1151/100401 tuning table, **no swap**, no `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`, no BIOS or kernel changes.

### Results

| | UD-IQ4_XS (v0.1.43, budget 55) | UD-Q4_K_XL (v0.1.44.1, budget 71) |
|---|---|---|
| ctxbench standard / hard | 95.6 % / 98.4 % | **96.7 % / 99.5 %** |
| decode: code / prose / 128 K | **69.3 / 50.8 / 38.1** t/s | 67.0 / 41.3 / 35.8 t/s |
| prefill 4 K / 16 K / 128 K | 932 / 1,187 / **1,212** | **1,067 / 1,225** / 1,172 |
| `MemAvailable` during the run | 37–38 GiB | 14 GiB |
| GGUF on disk | 93,682,584,224 B (87.25 GiB) | 111,334,654,784 B (103.69 GiB) |

**The larger quant is more correct and slower at decode.** On 121 GiB you keep either the headroom or the accuracy, not both: Q4_K_XL leaves about 14 GiB for the OS and everything else, and with no swap an over-claim OOMs rather than degrades. `--resident-budget-gib` stays explicit for the reason already documented in `STRIX_HALO.md` (#1715).

### Please read the correctness number with its failure table

I checked the claim behind "96.7 % vs 95.6 %" and it does not mean broad reasoning superiority. Both arms fail the **same two tasks**; B fails them less often:

| Battery | Arm | failed rows | concentrated in |
|---|---|---|---|
| standard | UD-IQ4_XS | 8 | `reasoning/optimisation` ×7, `game_trace/three_files` ×1 |
| standard | UD-Q4_K_XL | 6 | `reasoning/optimisation` ×6 |
| hard | UD-IQ4_XS | 3 | `science_ctx/kinetic_energy` ×2, `synthesis/count_limits` ×1 |
| hard | UD-Q4_K_XL | 1 | `science_ctx/kinetic_energy` ×1 |

`reasoning/optimisation` accounts for 7 of A's 8 and all 6 of B's standard failures, every one with the identical signature `got='None' want='102'` + `RULES BROKEN: answer_line` — output-format compliance on a flaky task, repeated across context levels, carrying most of the 1.1-point gap. The one clean signal is at **level 0** (no reference context at all), where A failed that task and B answered it in 50.3 s, which cannot be a retrieval effect — but it is one task on a task both arms flake on, so the report calls it a hint worth a re-run rather than proof.

### Caveats, stated in the report rather than smoothed over

- The arms differ in **engine version** (0.1.43 vs 0.1.44.1, five weeks) and in spec settings, so speed deltas are quant-**plus**-config.
- The smaller-quant arm was served directly with nothing else resident; the larger-quant arm ran behind a proxy **with live interactive traffic** that could not be detached. `pp`/`tg` are engine-reported so the proxy should not distort them, but the uncontrolled load is real.
- **Single run per long row** (short rows 3×). Not an isolated OS.
- `pp245k` fails in **both** arms at ~267.3 K prompt tokens against a 262,144 window — a context ceiling refused before inference, explicitly **not** an OOM. Nothing here characterises above 128 K.
- **Not measured:** needle recall, parallel/QFUSE, thermal telemetry, build-manifest provenance. `TRIMMED.md` names these so the scope is not mistaken for the fuller gfx1151 reports in this directory.
- **Reproducibility limit:** the load driver and the correctness harness are submitter-local scripts that are *not* published with this report (and are not part of Strata), so these exact numbers cannot be re-derived from the repository alone. Happy to supply them on request. The raw outputs are **SHA-256 pinned in `REPRODUCE.md`** — a checksum against private artefacts, not committed evidence — and are not in the commit.

### Files

4 files, docs and data only — no engine changes. New `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-gfx1151-ud-q4kxl-vs-iq4xs-0.1.44/{README.md,REPRODUCE.md,TRIMMED.md}` plus one index row in `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`.

pulls.title: STRATA_SLOT_COPY_DIRECT: the slot drafters K/V device to device too (--batch-mtp)
pulls.author: andyhrc
pulls.body:
With `STRATA_SLOT_COPY_DIRECT=1` (dd544364) an admission and a slot's resume copy the running state and the QSA K/V device to device. With `--batch-mtp` the slot drafters' K/V still went through a host image (`conversation_kv_save` + `conversation_kv_restore`) in `copy_to_slot` and `copy_from_slot`. This makes that copy go through `conversation_kv_copy` too when the switch is on; `conversation_kv_copy` already restores the draft ring's residency (`kv_mode == 2`) the way a restore does. Without the switch nothing changes.

This is the one part of #2728 that upstream's `STRATA_SLOT_COPY_DIRECT` does not have; it replaces that PR, which I am closing.

### Measured

2x RTX A4000 (layer split on GPUs 1 and 2), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 4 --batch-mtp`, `STRATA_BATCH_MTP_SERIAL=1`, `STRATA_SLOT_COPY_DIRECT=1`. The same requests (a conversation of 8.7K, 36K and 112K tokens, three turns each, while another client decodes), upstream/main 477ac13c against this branch:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 112K tokens: admission slot copy | 89.1 / 89.4 ms | 10.9 / 11.6 ms |
| 112K tokens: whole admission (`slot N takes`) | 158.3 / 158.4 ms | 79.6 / 80.6 ms |
| 112K tokens: give-back on the next turn | 96.4 / 96.4 ms | 17.6 / 17.5 ms |
| 112K tokens: the next turn's prompt (19 tokens read) | 484 / 490 ms | 406 / 410 ms |
| 36K tokens: admission slot copy | 13.9 / 13.8 ms | 5.1 / 6.1 ms |
| 36K tokens: give-back | 36.6 / 20.9 ms | 21.0 / 12.3 ms |
| 8.7K tokens: admission slot copy | 10.2 / 10.2 ms | 8.0 / 8.1 ms |
| 8.7K tokens: give-back | 15.2 / 11.6 ms | 9.4 / 2.2 ms |

The slots' MTP acceptance is the same over the same answers (66.2-71.4 % before, 61.5-67.9 % after; the drafts depend on the copied K/V, so a wrong copy would show here first). The rest of the admission (about 60 ms) is the turn checkpoint's host copy, which `STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1` / `STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1` address.

For context, on this box `--batch-mtp` with one serial group stays behind the pipelined groups without slot drafts at every concurrency (2 GPUs, 1/2/4/6 clients: 43.0/52.3/54.6/53.3 against 46.4/60.1/75.8/73.0 tok/s; 3 GPUs: 62.1/83.4/89.9/88.6 against 62.7/94.8/136.4/170.9), so the change matters where `--batch-mtp` is the batch path (one GPU, no layer split) or chosen anyway.

### Tests

Built natively (CUDA 86); the 2-GPU server runs above.

Issue: Resolves #2860

The Metal engine does not build at 0.1.45 (477ac13): six CUDA calls are missing from metal_compat, and the link
misses 21 kernel entry points. This adds them, the way stubs_144.cpp did for 0.1.44. Only files under metal/
change, so the CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds are untouched.

## What changed
- `metal/include/metal_compat/cuda_runtime.h`: the compute-capability attributes, the stream-priority calls,
  `cudaMemcpyPeer` and `cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess` answer "unsupported". verify.cpp's sm_75 test says no, the
  opt-in high-priority stream falls back to the default stream, and the peer-copy probe (#2666) keeps peer access off.
- `metal/src/engine/stubs_145.cpp` (new): 21 entry points.
  - Five answer "not available" through the caller's documented fallback: `fused_gr_persist_init` (no-op; the
    Verifier calls it on every start, so a stopping stub would stop every start), `fused_gr_read_persist` (false:

- `metal/src/engine/stubs.cpp`: `Gemm::bf16`'s stub takes 0.1.45's `x_f16` argument (one line; the generated file

pulls.title: serve: the Monitor shows the control-line wait a batch request is in
pulls.author: dsj027-collab
pulls.body:
## What this changes

With `--batch`, the server's fifo is no longer where requests queue: each one is registered as running the moment it arrives, and the queue it really waits in is the engine's control lines - one prompt read at a time, behind whatever read is in progress (`_take_control`). The Monitor could not show that anywhere:

- the api-monitor's request list went `queued` -> `generating` in the same second and `queue_s` stayed `0.000`, so a request that waited 55 s for the next read looked identical to one that started reading at once;
- the Monitor's pill only showed `N queued`, which with `--batch` is always 0 while a real queue is standing on the lines.

`_take_control` now marks the request's own monitor record `waiting` while it is in the queue and `reading` when it takes the lines, and adds the seconds it spent waiting to that record's `queue_s` - the field the server's fifo wait already writes, so on `--batch 1` and `--batch N` alike the row shows the whole time before work started. The request list and the pill render the two new states (`N waiting to read` beside `N queued`); `/metrics` has carried `live.waiting`/`live.admitting` for a while now, this only draws them.

## What it leaves alone

No scheduling change and no output change: the default path is byte-identical. Nothing is marked when `api_monitor` is off (the default) - there is no record to mark - and the `waiting` counter, `wait_lens` and `STRATA_ADMIT_SHORT_FIRST` admission order are untouched (a test asserts they still balance).

## How I checked

- `serve/test_monitor_waiting.py` (new, 5 tests): the stubbed-engine pattern of `serve/test_admit_order.py` - no process, no GPU. Covers: free lines land on `reading` with a sub-second `queue_s`; held lines show `waiting` with nothing counted, then `reading` with the wait added; a cancelled wait never claims `reading`, keeps `queue_s` at 0, and leaves `waiting`/`wait_lens` balanced; no record on the thread is inert; the fifo's wait and the lines' wait add up in one field.
- `serve.test_admit_order` + `serve.test_slot_alloc` (11 tests) and `serve.test_server` (337 tests) pass unchanged.
- Live on an RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (Linux, CUDA sm_120, NVFP4 pack, `--batch 2`, engine 0.1.45): 2 x 120K-token requests plus 8 short ones at once - the list showed `waiting` rows with `queue_s` 54-58 s for the slot-bound requests and 0.9 s for the one `STRATA_ADMIT_SHORT_FIRST` let through, matching `/metrics` `live.waiting` (peak 8) sampled at 0.5 s. Not tested: Windows (the change is OS-independent Python + the web app), HIP/SYCL (no engine code touched).

Follow-up to #2109 (its scheduling half shipped as `STRATA_ADMIT_SHORT_FIRST` in 0.1.45; this is the visibility half), and adjacent to #2857/#2858 (per-slot widgets).

pulls.title: q36: parallelise the expert copy at load
pulls.author: ggeorgovassilis
pulls.body:
## What

Parallelise the routed-expert copy in `place_experts()` (`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`).

The load's hot loop copies the routed experts from the GGUF mapping into the host arena, one
expert at a time, on a single thread:

```cpp
for (int64_t e = 0; e < ne; ++e) expert_blob(L, e, L.hblobs + (size_t) e * L.stride);
```

This PR splits that loop into disjoint per-expert chunks across threads, with a new
`STRATA_Q36_PARALLEL_PLACE` switch (`0` = serial, `N` = `N` threads, unset = one thread per
logical core). Each expert's source and destination ranges are disjoint, so the placed bytes
are identical at any thread count — byte-identical by construction.

## Why

On an RTX 4060 Laptop (8 GB) / Ryzen 7 7735HS, loading `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf`
(22.85 GB) was dominated by this single-threaded copy (~300 MB/s, where the machine's memory
bandwidth is ~36–44 GB/s). Measured: the copy drops **~64 s → ~16 s at 8 threads, ~13 s at 16
threads** (~4×), and the total load drops from ~104 s to ~58 s. Greedy-decode output is
byte-identical (parallel vs serial).

## What it leaves alone

- The dense-weight load (`load()`), the `cudaHostAlloc` pin of the arena, and the
  all-in-VRAM placement path are untouched.
- The full-arena `std::memset` before the copy is unchanged (it is not part of this loop).

## Testing

- **Build:** compiles cleanly with CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 (`strata` target).
- **Tests:** `tools/test_setup_*.py` 38/40 pass (2 pre-existing network/config failures in
  `test_setup_engine_hash.py` / `test_setup_golden.py`, unrelated to this change);
  `serve/test_*.py` 784/785 pass (1 flaky `test_keepawake` timing test), 11 skipped.
- **Byte-identity:** `--tokens "1,2,3" --n 24` prints identical `gen:` tokens with
  `STRATA_Q36_PARALLEL_PLACE` unset vs `=0`.
- **Smoke:** the model loads and answers a trivial prompt (`"hi"`).
- Note: this branch is based on `upstream/main`, whose q36 driver does not yet carry the
  `STRATA_Q36_SINGLE_STAGE` staging-buffer fix, so on an 8 GB card it needs a reduced context /
  `--expert-vram 0` to fit; the smoke test was run on the fork's build that includes that fix.

pulls.title: bench: RTX 3090 + RTX 4080 SUPER layer split, with and without other work on the second card
pulls.author: kristoffern
pulls.body:
A results-only submission: `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rtx3090-rtx4080s-split/`. No engine changes.

**Hardware:** RTX 3090 (24 GiB) + RTX 4080 SUPER (16 GiB), both on PCIe 4.0 x8; i9-14900KF (no AVX-512), 123.4 GiB RAM, Linux, driver 595.84. The 4080 SUPER also drives the display (~2.3 GiB), which cannot be removed without ending the desktop session, so it is present in every arm.

**Model:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0, 131072 context, KV int8 with KV streaming, `--spec 4` with the MTP draft layer, otherwise setup's own choices. Engine 0.1.45 (477ac13c), compiled from source.

**Configurations:** four arms on the one machine — each card alone, and the pair as a layer split (`"gpu": [0, 1]`, `"layer_split": "auto"`) in two states. The split arms differ only in whether another CUDA process (a local embedding server, ~3.2 GiB) held memory on the second card, and the `--vram-reserve-later-mib` that left it room (3072 busy, 1536 free).

**Result:** the same pair is **6% slower** at decode than the 3090 alone when the second card is busy, and **17-38% faster** when it is free (chat decode 132.9 vs 113.2 tok/s; 32K prompt 3347 vs 2424 tok/s). The engine log gives the mechanism directly: the second card's expert cache goes from 959 of its 8192 profiled pairs to "82% of the experts resident", and the decode expert-cache hit rate from a 93.0% median to 99.7%. `auto` also moves the boundary from K=32 to K=29.

So the published +18-20% prompt gain for a split reproduces here in direction and size, but only once the second card has room; with a few GiB of someone else's memory on it the same split is a regression. That seemed worth a report, since a second card that does nothing else is not the common case.

**Limitations**, also stated in the README: speed only, no correctness check. One suite run of 3 repetitions per test per arm, so the ranges are run-to-run, not restart-to-restart. The 4080-alone arm carries a 3 GiB reserve for the display, so it is not like-for-like with the 3090's 700 MiB. 4K prompts are slower on the pair in both split arms (the hand-off is overhead before the pipeline fills); the crossover between 4K and 16K was not measured. Long prefill at 16K/32K is near-identical on the two cards alone despite a 34% decode gap, which I did not isolate.

The attached `results-split-*.json` name only the 3090 and 24576 MiB of VRAM: that is #2887, where the bench tool drops the second card on a layer split. The hardware in the README is what actually ran, and `engine-log-excerpt.txt` carries the split lines. `--url` was used throughout because of #2872.

pulls.title: [Engine] keep replica pipes and DONE statistics request-owned
pulls.author: dynaxbill
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Unbatched replicas can release their native pipe before an early-closed child drains DONE, so a successor can receive the previous reply's DONE or tokens. Even after a correct drain, shared native last statistics can be overwritten after unlock. Release 0.2.0-beta still reproduces both failures. Keep the existing per-replica lock through child cleanup, snapshot the caller's new DONE before unlock, and retain its pre-DONE identity when no new result arrived.

## Related discussion

Fixes #2892. Updated in the original thread after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. This is the same focused serving fix, not a new proposal or default change.

## Approach

Scheme A: explicit child close/drain plus a caller-local DONE snapshot, preserving independent replicas, cleanup-error propagation, router/nonfinite bookkeeping, embeddings and batched paths. The refreshed code retains upstream's `_strata_replica_selected` callback and the official callback/telemetry tests pass. No server.py/native kernel, protocol, routing-cost, sampling/default or CUDA Graph changes; no new queue, worker, sleep or retry.

The feature branch integrates main `f57c0adcb31c00f3f216550c004dac4e713a9f70` while preserving the earlier PR history. The replayer defaults to the fixed 0.2.0-beta revision. Its close-only negative control now requires the two forced statistics failures, allows only the additional multi-caller statistics failure, rejects errors, and keeps all 18 fixed contracts mandatory. This records15/18 versus16/18 variability without retrying to pick a count or weakening the fix gate.

## Validation

**Passed:** Windows CPython 3.12.14, pinned Jinja2/regex/MarkupSafe, main `f57c0adcb31c00f3f216550c004dac4e713a9f70` + A; unchanged server.py. `python -m unittest -v` run separately for `serve.test_replica_lifetime`(18), `serve.test_replicas`(19), `serve.test_parallel`(42), `serve.test_request_accounting`(10), `serve.test_request_hardening`(10), `serve.test_queue_keepalive`(3): **102/102**. `python tools/replay_replica_lifetime.py --output <new-dir> --baseline-file <captured-release-replicas.py>`: official 9/18, close-only 16/18, A 18/18; control statusPASS. Baseline release is `3d1fb48090e8f2cefc22d7b5845fb7f5b71f33fa`; a Git checkout can omit baseline-file because that is now the default revision.

**Failed:** official/close-only controls deliberately reproduce ownership bugs. Earlier close-only15/18 raw is preserved. Initial local setup omitted strata_cli, then regex; the unmodified runtime module and pinned dependency resolved imports, without product/test assertion changes. Logs included.

**Not run:** GPU/model execution of 0.2.0-beta / engine 0.1.45.3, native CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds, new performance or full-model KL/perplexity/long-soak qualification. No native source changed. Published engine 0.1.44.1 GPU runs remain historical and are not relabelled as this revision.

Evidence: [new release replay, commands and selected tests](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/tests/data/replica_lifetime/v020-beta/README.md), [historical roots/three repair alternatives/GPU evidence](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/docs/replica_request_lifetime.md), [per-file manifest](https://github.com/dynaxbill/Strata/blob/da681b7b263d319952b98927858c07b934e19ac6/tests/data/replica_lifetime/manifest.json).

## Limits

New runs use the actual Python reader/pump with synthetic native producers (two contracts use real OS pipes), plus HTTP fake engines. They establish the forced ownership failures and the bounded repair, not GPU hardware correctness, universal output quality, empty-reply probability or performance. The two roots chiefly concern unbatched replica handoff; this is not a claim that every batched C4 call fails. Historical GPU data, synthetic request/SSE bytes and their original versions remain unchanged.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] tools: a --compare path that is not a bench report is a message, not a traceback
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
`--compare` and `--compare-only` are documented in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` and named in the `BENCH.bat` /
`bench.sh` headers, and the two flags are easy to swap.  Both went through `load_results()`, which read the path
and let whatever came out of the read escape.  Three ways it went wrong, every one of them ending the run as a
traceback:

**A path that is not there** - a typo:

```
$ python tools/strata_bench.py --compare bench/results/typo --compare-only bench/results/also-typo
  File "tools/strata_bench.py", line 896, in load_results
    return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'bench/results/typo'
```

**A folder that is not a results folder, or a file that is not JSON** - `IsADirectoryError` / `JSONDecodeError`,
the same way.

**A `results.json` that is not a bench report.**  This one needs no typo at all:

```
$ python tools/strata_bench.py --compare bench/results/2026-10-01-community-2x-titan-rtx \
                               --compare-only bench/results/2026-10-04-community-2x-rtx3060
  File "tools/strata_bench.py", line 878, in compare_table
    a, b = summary_metrics(old["results"]), summary_metrics(new["results"])
TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str
```

`bench/results/` holds `results.json` files from the other tools in `tools/` as well - `ab_engine.py` and the
`conversation_cache_*` ones write a top-level list or a dict of `summary`/`runs`.  Of the 27 `results.json` in
`bench/results/` today, none is a `strata_bench.py` report, so `--compare` between two of the folders the repo
itself ships reaches `compare_table()` and dies there.

### Where I changed it

`load_results()` raises `ValueError` carrying the path and what is wrong with it, and the two callers print that
instead of letting it out:

```
ValueError: bench/results/typo has no results.json in it
ValueError: bench/results/typo cannot be read (No such file or directory)
ValueError: bench/results/x/results.json is not valid JSON (...)
ValueError: bench/results/2026-10-01-community-2x-titan-rtx/results.json is not a report tools/strata_bench.py wrote
```

- `--compare-only` reads both folders before it starts anything, so it reports and exits 2, the way the bench
  reports its other bad input.
- `--compare` is read *after* the report is written, so it notes that only the comparison was lost rather than
  undoing a finished run.

The report check is structural - a dict with a dict `machine` and a dict `results` holding `chat`/`prompts`/
`agent`/`clients`, which is what the tables read - rather than a schema number, so it does not turn a future
schema into a new failure.  `test_compare` loads a report the writer really produced, so the check cannot quietly
become too strict without a test going red.

This is the second half of the note at the end of #2792.  The first half of that note - a started server left
behind - no longer applies on `main`: `main()` sets `started` immediately after `start_server()` and its `finally`
stops the server on any exception.  I checked that rather than assumed it, so I did not touch it.

### What I left alone

`project_version()` still catches only `OSError`, so a `CMakeLists.txt` that cannot be read for any other reason
still reaches the top of `main()` as a traceback.  Its neighbour `find_configs()` catches `(OSError, ValueError)`,
so that guard looks like an oversight - but #2879 already fixes the one case that actually bit anyone, and widening
it is a separate change.

### How I checked

Six tests in `tools/test_strata_bench.py`, no GPU or server needed: each way a path is wrong (including a
`results.json` shaped like the other tools'), that a real results folder still loads, both call sites, and that the
comparison of a finished run is only noted rather than fatal.

Five of the six fail on `main` today - four with the raw `FileNotFoundError`, one with `ValueError not raised` for
the other tools' reports.  With this, the 23 tests in the file pass (`python -m unittest tools.test_strata_bench`).

pulls.author: monscoro
pulls.body:
## Title

hip: hipBLASLt tuning table for gfx1200 (RX 9060 XT, hipBLASLt 1.5.0 / 100500)

Issue: none (a data table, no tracking issue).

## Summary

Adds `tools/hip/gfx1200-hipblaslt-100500.txt`, a 57-row hipBLASLt tuning table for the RX 9060 XT (gfx1200) on the hipBLASLt 1.5.0 (version number 100500) that the prebuilt Windows engine packages. setup picks the table by its header, so there is no code or default change: an install that does not report gfx1200 with hipBLASLt 1.5.0 keeps the path it has today, and the existing `gfx1200-hipblaslt-100202.txt` stays in place for ROCm 7.2.4's hipBLASLt 1.2.2.

Measured on one Windows machine, fresh prompts read 5.8 % (4K) and 5.9 % (16K) faster than plain hipBLAS, decode unchanged.

## What changed

- **`tools/hip/gfx1200-hipblaslt-100500.txt`** (new): 57 rows over 22 GEMM geometries at T = 37 .. 6144, calibrated against AMD's TheRock hipBLASLt 1.5.0 for gfx1200 (`STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING_V1 gfx1200 100500`). The solution IDs are scoped to that hipBLASLt version and architecture. The prebuilt Windows engine carries ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 with that hipBLASLt, so on Windows gfx1200 this is the table that fits the shipped library; without one the engine warns that the prompt's dense matrix products go through plain hipBLAS.
- **`docs/AMD_HIP.md`**: the entry in "Shipped tables" and a community-validated-card bullet with the measurement.
- **`bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`**: two rows, one per new folder.
- **`bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rx-9060-xt-swift-1-5-iq2-xs-hipblaslt-100500/`** (new): the tuned arm, with `README.md`, `results.json` and `engine-log-excerpt.txt`.
- **`bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rx-9060-xt-swift-1-5-iq2-xs-hipblas/`** (new): the plain-hipBLAS arm of the same A/B, same three files.

### Measurement

RX 9060 XT 16 GB (gfx1200), Windows 11, Ryzen 9 3900X, 64 GiB RAM, engine 0.1.44.1 (prebuilt Windows HIP), Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS (GSQ-RCO abliterated) at 65536 ctx with `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`. `tools/strata_bench.py`, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges; the two runs differ only in `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`. `--expert-cache auto` even sized the tuned arm's expert cache 1.8 % smaller (5,282 vs 5,377 experts), so the gain is not from a larger cache.

| test | plain hipBLAS | with the table | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4,019-token fresh prompt | 478.5 tok/s (472.0-479.6) | 506.2 (502.3-507.5) | +5.8 % |
| 16,058-token fresh prompt | 548.3 (545.5-552.8) | 580.6 (579.6-581.1) | +5.9 % |
| first token, 4K | 8.43 s (8.41-8.55) | 7.99 s (7.95-8.03) | -5.2 % |
| first token, 16K | 29.33 s (29.09-29.49) | 27.70 s (27.68-27.75) | -5.6 % |
| decode (short chat) | 42.4 tok/s (36.6-47.8) | 42.5 (37.2-47.4) | unchanged |

The prompt ranges of the two arms do not overlap; the decode ranges do. The engine logged `prefill gemm: hipBLASLt tuning enabled (57 rows, gfx1200, version 100500)` and no fallbacks.

## Extra Notes

- The suite's prompt tests are 4K and 16K tokens; a longer prompt (the suite's `--long` 32K, and the 65K / 130K prompts of the gfx1200 report in `docs/AMD_HIP.md`) was not measured here, so the gain at those sizes is unmeasured.
- `tools/strata_bench.py` named the adapter from Windows' display-class registry, which still lists the owner's retired Radeon RX 470, so the first version of both reports said "RX 470, 8 GiB, driver 31.0.21923.11000". The GPU and driver lines in the two READMEs and `results.json` are corrected by hand to what the engine's own log shows (`strata generate: GPU 0: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (gfx1200)`, driver 32.0.31041.1004). That detection is worth its own issue.
- `python tools/test_setup_amd.py` (40 tests) and `python tools/test_setup_choices.py` (47 tests) pass. `setup.hipblaslt_table("gfx1200", [], 100500)` returns the new file, 100202 still returns the older one, and an unknown version still gets the "no table" warning.
- Not run here: a rebuild of any backend (this PR touches no code, only a data table, docs and benchmark reports) and `hip_prefill_hipblaslt_gemm` with the table set. The community who can run the calibration tool against another 1.5.0 build is welcome to; the ids are only guaranteed for this one.
- Left alone: `tools/hip/gfx1200-hipblaslt-100100.txt` (a local file, not part of this PR), the engine, setup's selection logic and every other architecture's table.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] tools: read CMakeLists.txt as UTF-8, not through the OS code page (#2792)
pulls.author: ctr-137
pulls.body:
`tools/strata_bench.py:564` read this install's own `CMakeLists.txt` with no `encoding=`, so the decode went
through `locale.getpreferredencoding()`.  That is GBK or cp932 on a Chinese or Japanese Windows, where the
file's UTF-8 BOM is not a valid sequence - the third byte `0xbf` - and `BENCH.bat` died before any
measurement:

```
  File "tools/strata_bench.py", line 564, in project_version
    m = re.search(r"project\(strata VERSION ([\d.]+)", (ROOT / "CMakeLists.txt").read_text())
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbf in position 2: illegal multibyte sequence
```

`setup.py` reads the same file with `encoding="utf-8"`, so this is an omission here rather than an
intentional locale dependency.

A cp1252 machine decodes the BOM to mojibake and says nothing, which is why only those two locales ever saw
it - and why this needs a test rather than a reproducer.

### What I changed

`tools/strata_bench.py`: read it as `utf-8-sig`.  That matches how this file already reads its other repo and
config files (lines 657, 688, 971), and it strips the BOM the file actually has rather than leaving a
`﻿` in front of the string the regex scans.

### What I left alone

- `/proc/meminfo` and `/proc/cpuinfo` are still read without `encoding=`.  They are the Linux-only branch
  and their content is ASCII whatever the locale, so I did not touch them.
- `project_version()` still catches only `OSError`.  A repo file that is unreadable for any other reason
  still reaches the top of `main()` as a traceback and leaves a started server behind, which the report also
  notes.  `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, so widening that except would cover it - but what the
  bench should do with an unreadable install is a separate decision and I did not want to bundle it here.

### How I checked

Three tests in `tools/test_strata_bench.py`, no GPU or server needed:

- the encoding `project_version()` passes is captured and has to be a UTF-8 one, so a future call that
  silently goes back to the code page fails;
- the file really is undecodable as GBK, which pins why the BOM is the thing to survive and documents the
  reported failure;
- the version it returns is the same as a strict `utf-8-sig` read of the file.

With the fix reverted the first of them fails (`encoding=''`), with it all 20 tests in
`tools/test_strata_bench.py` pass (`python -m unittest tools.test_strata_bench`).

The reporter's workaround (`set PYTHONUTF8=1`) still works and is no longer needed.

Fixes #2792.

pulls.title: serve: STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE, park the prefix that fits
pulls.author: TwoAnts
pulls.body:
# serve: STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE, park the prefix that fits

Issue: Addresses #1938, #2431

## Summary

The problem this targets is cache utilization when the conversation cache is small relative to the context window (e.g. a 3.5 GiB cache against a 256k-token context): one long-chain snapshot exceeds the whole budget, so slots evict each other entirely and almost no useful prefix survives. Conversation-cache parking and eviction are all-or-nothing: a chain that doesn't fit the byte budget or the RAM floor loses its entire snapshot, and the next request re-prefills from the root-ck (measured 225 s for a 160k-token chain) — the exact failure both #1938 and #2431 describe. Instead of a fixed per-slot preserve limit (#1938's proposal), this uses the conversation's own checkpoint chain as the depth ruler: park the deepest prefix that fits, and shrink already-parked entries to one of their own checkpoints before dropping them. The preserve depth then adapts per conversation to the live byte pressure, instead of one global N. Off unless `STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE=1` (env-only switch, matching the recent admission-switch convention).

Note: this change was implemented by an AI agent (with the measurements and the repro scenario run live against the engine) — offering it as a reference implementation; rework to fit the codebase's style is welcome.

## What changed

- `include/strata/core/conversation_cache.hpp` (+72/−1)
  - **Park side:** when the outgoing chain fails the byte budget or the `--conversation-cache-min-free-mib` gate, walk its checkpoint chain deepest-first and park the first prefix that passes both gates. The parked copy keeps root + chain + K/V `[0, L)` and mounts live on that checkpoint's running state; the next request mounts the prefix and re-reads only the tail (the reply plus the new turn, which the client re-renders anyway). A truncated copy is parked even below `--conversation-cache-min-tokens` — a root-deep mirror still saves the shared prefix.
  - **Eviction side (`truncate_oldest`):** an already-parked entry asked to make room is shrunk to one of its own checkpoints (K/V pages past the landing, the deeper checkpoints' running states and their ids go; the landing's state moves into live) before it is dropped whole. A landing below `--conversation-cache-min-tokens` is not worth a slot → the entry goes whole. Pinned entries are never truncated; slot-count pressure (`entries_.size() >= slots_`) still evicts whole, since truncation doesn't reduce the count.
  - **Scope:** single-stage only — the layer-split path has no per-checkpoint byte split to walk.
- `src/core/conversation_cache_test.cpp` — 8 new scenarios: truncation keeps the prefix, min-tokens floor evicts whole, switch-off restores old behavior, pinned skip, byte pressure truncates before evicting, slot-count pressure still evicts whole. 4783 checks pass; engine builds clean.

## Extra Notes

Measured on this base (477ac13c). 4-request scenario (grow a 62k chain → two interleaved requests push the byte budget over → return to the first conversation); test config `--conversation-cache-mib 3500`, 2 slots, `min-tokens 4096`, `prompt-cache-every 4096`:

| | patch on | native |
|---|---|---|
| after 3rd request | `parked=2, bytes=3.43G, evictions=0` (first chain truncated to its 32768 landing) | `evictions=1` (first chain dropped whole) |
| return request (62k prompt) | `restored 32768 tokens (live)` → **26.0 s** | full re-prefill → **51.7 s** |
| scenario total | **131.6 s** | **159.3 s** |

Reproduced three times on the previous base with the same delta (~24–26 s on the return leg alone). No flag added on purpose — the env gate keeps the hot path byte-identical when off.

pulls.title: serve: "skills_compact" (opt-in) keeps opencode's skill list to names and first sentences
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
## What it changes

opencode lists every installed skill in its system message, inside `<available_skills>`, with the whole description and
the file location of each. With 58 skills installed that list was ~32K characters, ~43% of the system message. The
skill tool loads a skill by name with its full text, so the list only has to tell the skills apart.

With `"skills_compact": true` in the config, `openai_to_messages` and `anthropic_to_messages` rewrite that block before
the template sees it: each `<description>` keeps its first sentence (at most 160 characters, cut at a word with ` ...`
when there is no sentence end in reach), and each `<location>` line is dropped. Every skill's `<name>` stays. It runs
next to `env_to_user` (same place, same shape), and it is deterministic, so the prefix cache keeps working.

## What it leaves alone

- Off by default: with the key absent or `false`, the messages are untouched (a test checks the text is identical).
- Only the first system message, only between `<available_skills>` and `</available_skills>`; a prompt without that
  block is unchanged.
- No engine change.

## Measured

A captured opencode 1.18.7 request (build agent, 58 skills, 15 tools), counted with the model's tokenizer: system
message 21,651 -> 16,259 tokens (-5,392, -25%). On an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (12 GB) with Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS that is about
3 s less to read for every session whose system prompt the prefix cache does not already hold. Every skill name is
kept. On by default in our fork's config since 2026-10-13.

## How it was checked

- `serve/test_skills_compact.py` (6 tests): off changes nothing; first sentence kept, location dropped, names kept,
  text around the block kept; a long sentence is cut at a word; the same list gives the same text; no block, no
  change; the Anthropic path too.
- `serve.test_skills_compact`, `serve.test_env_to_user`, `serve.test_frontend`: 37 tests OK.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: one entry next to `env_to_user`.

pulls.title: serve: strata_prefix marks a chat whose history has pictures
pulls.author: stevie67
pulls.body:
Issue: none open for this. Related, not resolved by it: #2255 (pinned prefixes filling the conversation cache).

## Summary

`"strata_prefix"` was ignored for any request with an image in it (`strata_prefix ignored: the request has images`), so one photo anywhere in a chat's history turned it off until that message left the context. Pictures before the boundary now count with the tokens they take in the prompt, and the prefix is marked as for a text-only request.

The use case: a chat client sends `{"messages": K}` with K the index of its final user message. That message carries per-turn text (recalled memories, the clock) that the next turn replays without, so the turn checkpoint never matches again and only the system-prompt checkpoint was reused. With the pin, each turn resumes where the replayed history ends. A chat that once contained a photo lost this until now.

## What changed

- `serve/server.py`
  - The loop in `prepare()` that turns each `<|vision_start|><|image_pad|>` into one pad per image token moved, unchanged, into `Service.expand_image_pads(ids, counts)`. `prepare()` calls it with the encoded counts and keeps its "the prompt and its images do not match" check.
  - `resolve_prefix()` takes the request's image token counts (`image_counts`, in prompt order) instead of `has_images`. `head_ids()` expands the rendered head's pictures with the same helper, so the longest common start runs through them. The refusal for images is gone.
  - New guard: a boundary inside a picture's tokens is ignored with `strata_prefix ... ignored: it ends inside a picture` (only `{"tokens": N}` can land there; a message boundary cannot).
- `serve/test_server.py`, class `SharedPrefix`: three tests with a fake encoder whose two pictures take 3 and 5 tokens, so a wrong count or order misses the boundary:
  - `test_messages_resolve_past_a_picture_in_the_history`: a photo in the history; the prefix ends at the final message's `<|im_start|>` and holds all 3 of its tokens.
  - `test_a_picture_after_the_prefix_stays_out_of_it`: pictures on both sides; 3 tokens before the boundary, 5 after.
  - `test_a_token_boundary_inside_a_picture_is_ignored`: `{"tokens": N}` inside the picture is ignored and said in the log.
  The first two failed before the change (ignored / `KeyError: 'tokens'`); the third fails with the guard removed (`{'tokens': 225} != {}`).
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the pinned-prefix paragraph says pictures count now, names the chat-client use, and gives the measurement below.

## What it leaves alone

- A request without `strata_prefix` takes the same path as before: `prepare()` runs the moved loop with the same counts. `test_without_the_field_nothing_changes` and the `ImageMarkers` tests (#150, #2228) pass unchanged.
- A request with `strata_prefix` and no pictures: `image_counts` is `None`, and `head_ids()` returns what it did.
- The engine: no change. `pin=N` is one more cut in the same read loop as the turn and system-prompt checkpoints, which already handle pictures.
- Python only; no CUDA, HIP or SYCL file is touched.

## How it was checked

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` on this branch (`477ac13c` + this change, macOS, Python 3.14): 851 tests, 850 pass, 11 skipped. Against `main` without the change: 848 tests, 847 pass. The one failure is the same in both, `test_keepawake.KeepAwakeTests.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`, and it fails on this Mac without the change too.
- Live, on the DGX Spark port (#2419, engine 0.1.44.1; the same server patch applied there), GB10, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 131,072 context, `--kv int8`, images on, 2026-10-17. A four-turn chat with a 640x400 PNG in its first message, `{"messages": K}` on every turn with history, per-turn text in the final user message:

  | Turn | Prompt | Reused | Read | Time to read |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 5,333 | 0 | 5,333 | 7.9 s |
  | 2 | 5,478 | 5,392 | 86 | 0.96 s |
  | 3 | 5,503 | 5,395 | 108 | 1.20 s |
  | 4 | 5,527 | 5,421 | 106 | 1.18 s |

  No `ignored` line in the server window. Turns 3 and 4 resumed at the pin of the turn before and still answered about the picture correctly (its colours and its text), so the picture's tokens come back intact from the pinned checkpoint.
- The same client in a real chat (23-31k tokens) before the change, with a photo 27 messages back: every turn reused only the system prompt's checkpoint and read 4.8-7.0k tokens (4.7-7.5 s) before answering.

## Not tested

- Other chat templates than the Qwen3.8 one, and `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` requests with pictures (they reach `resolve_prefix` through the same `prepare()`).
- `{"message": I, "chars": N}` with pictures before message I (covered by the same expansion, no test of its own).
- Pictures given by URL.
- Windows, and any GPU other than the GB10.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: put the streamed usage in its own final chunk when include_usage is requested
pulls.author: Eranicus30666
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
`/v1/chat/completions` ignores `stream_options.include_usage`: the streamed `usage` always stays on the `finish_reason` chunk. OpenAI's streaming contract puts it in its own last chunk with `"choices": []` when the option is set, and gateways and clients read it there.

With this change, when `stream_options.include_usage` is true, the chunk that carries `usage` is written as two chunks: the same chunk without `usage`, then a chunk with `"choices": []` and the `usage`. Without the option (absent, `false` or `null`) the original write is used, so nothing changes. Non-streaming replies are untouched.

Re-checked on the current `main` (identical to `v0.2.1.1`, `9ae93f7b`): `serve/server.py` still has no handling of `stream_options`, so the behaviour described in #2865 is still there.

## Related discussion
Resolves #2865 (closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset). No scope agreement needed: a focused fix of one streaming path.

## Approach
In the streaming loop, a `split_usage` flag is read from `stream_options.include_usage`; only a chunk that carries `usage` is split. Default path, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses` and the legacy completions endpoint are not touched. Three tests in `serve/test_server.py` (usage alone in the last `choices: []` chunk with the option; usage unchanged on the `finish_reason` chunk without it, including `false` and `null`; same numbers as the non-streaming reply).

## Validation
Revision tested: `v0.2.1.1` (`main`, `9ae93f7b`) + this one commit. The tests ran on a local copy of the commit (`cc6d4d9`); it has the same tree as the pushed `9b4e7e7` (identical `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`), only the commit date differs. Environment: Debian 13, Python 3.13.5, venv from `requirements.txt`; engine built from the same tag for sm_86 with CUDA 13.4 (2x NVIDIA A2 16 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL).

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server`: 346 tests, OK (129.6 s).
- Stream check against the mock engine (`serve/server.py --engine mock`): with the commit, 3 of 3 checks pass (usage alone in the last `choices: []` chunk; no `usage` on the `finish_reason` chunk; unchanged without the option).
- Same 3 checks against the real engine (`strata 0.1.46.1`, `serve/server.py --engine strata`): 3 of 3 pass, also against the service in production use.
- Control, same checks on `v0.2.1.1` without this commit (mock and real engine): the two `include_usage` checks fail, the default-path check passes.

**Failed:**
none observed with the commit.

**Not run:**
- HIP, SYCL, Metal builds: the change is Python-only (`serve/`), no engine file is touched, and the engine used was built from the unmodified tag.
- Windows and macOS.
- Clients other than the plain HTTP check above. The LiteLLM symptom reported in #2865 was observed on 0.1.45 in my setup; I did not re-run LiteLLM on 0.1.46.1 for this update.
- `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, the legacy completions endpoint: unchanged by the diff, not exercised.
- A byte-for-byte comparison of the default path: I compared the chunk structure.

## Limits
- The other chunks carry no `usage` key. As I read OpenAI's reference, it sends `"usage": null` on them when the option is set; this change does not add that. Clients that read the last chunk work either way, and I can add it here if you prefer it.
- Only `/v1/chat/completions` is covered.

Co-authored with Claude.
