pulls.title: mtp: the draft layer's experts at Q8_0 and BF16, alongside Q2_0
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
The MTP draft layer's 512 routed experts were Q2_0 only: a format picked by measured draft acceptance, carrying a relative RMS error of 0.42 on the first experts.  Higher precision buys better drafts, hence a higher accept rate, hence speed - never a different output, since the verify window decides every emitted token.  This adds Q8_0 (2.49 GiB) and BF16 (4.69 GiB) as opt-in arms and leaves Q2_0 the default.

Which arm a run uses is the runtime directory, not a flag: `--mtp rt-q8_0` or `--mtp rt-bf16`.  The selection is an `experts.fmt` marker that tools/mtp_rt.py writes beside experts.bin, one line `<format> <gu_type> <d_type>`.  No marker means Q2_0, so every `rt/` that exists today keeps taking exactly the path it always did.

Engine:
  * iq_kernels.cu: Fmt<30> (BF16 weights against a q8_1 activation), and 30 in STRATA_GU_FMTS / STRATA_D_FMTS / STRATA_MMVQ_FMTS.  Q8_0's grouped path at this shape is covered here for the first time as well.
  * `native_expert_supported` asks `embed_type_supported` rather than `is_iq`, which is the set dq_dispatch implements; `is_iq` is left alone, so nothing that gates on it moves.
  * mtp.cpp: one branch in load(), taken once.  The per-expert stride is a function of the chosen layout rather than cpu::BLOB, and the activation buffer is carved at q8_1's 36 bytes per 32 values with Q2_0 reading its 34-byte prefix.  A shared drafter now inherits the layout with the buffer it shares: without that a second session would stride a q8_0 buffer by the Q2_0 blob, silently.
  * The size of experts.bin is checked against the layout, because a mismatch does not crash - it drafts from the wrong bytes and is merely accepted less often.

tools/mtp_pack.py gains a lossless bf16 arm (the checkpoint's own 16-bit words, no round trip, so its reconstruction error is exactly zero) and tools/mtp_rt.py writes the per-expert native blob: gate_up[e] then down[e].  Whole-tensor order would hand every expert the head of its neighbour.

Measured on the 4-GPU rig (iq3_s, 256 greedy tokens): BF16 does not fit - the draft layer lands entirely on the last stage's 8 GB card and 4.84 GiB of experts leaves too few cache slots for the prompt path.  Q8_0 runs at 48.9 tok/s against Q2_0's 49.5-49.9, with an accept rate indistinguishable within the engine's ~8-point run-to-run spread, at a 2007 -> 1134 slot cost on that card.  So this is an arm to measure, not a win to claim.

pulls.title: generate: STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB, a VRAM reserve per part
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB="100,100,300,300"` — an opt-in VRAM reserve per part of a layer split, in the split's
order, in MiB. Entry 0 is the first card and replaces `--vram-reserve-mib`; entry *i* is the *i*-th later card and
replaces `--vram-reserve-later-mib` for that card. A shorter list reuses its last number; extra numbers are
ignored. `STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB` is accepted as the same knob.

Today the flags give the first card its own number and every later card one shared number, which cannot express a
rig whose cards are not the same size or do not hold the same kind of layer. `stage_room()` now takes the part's
ordinal and prefers the list's entry for it; the split search, the stage sizing, the drafter reservation and the
LOW free-VRAM warning all go through it. When the list is active, the LOW line's suggested fix names the list entry
to raise instead of the flag the list overrides.

The start prints the reserve each part will use:

strata generate: VRAM reserves per part: CUDA0 700 MiB, CUDA1 700 MiB, ... (STRATA_VRAM_RESERVE_MIB)

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), `Glm5Model::pool_reserve` (`STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB`).

## What it leaves alone

Unset, `vram_reserve_parts_mib` is empty, `stage_room()` takes the old flag path, the print block does not run, and
its stderr line is absent. The two flags decide exactly as before. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Measurements

No speedup is claimed; this is a control knob. On the four-way Q8_0 rig this was written for (CUDA0/CUDA1 12 GB,
CUDA2/CUDA3 8 GB), a run's LOW lines showed CUDA1 with 511 MiB, CUDA2 with 388 MiB and CUDA3 with 1,156 MiB free.
CUDA3's one layer held all 512 profiled pairs of its layer, so its free VRAM cannot buy another expert there and
that is the card whose reserve can rise without losing cache. A per-card A/B (same split, same
`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX`, list against flags) is the test on a given rig; it has not been run.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = byte-identical by construction (empty list; `stage_room()` uses the old flags; no
  print).
- **Build:** CUDA. `generate.cpp` is host-only code and this adds no device code; it compiles clean against this
  branch's headers with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in
  unrelated code). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (nvcc 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so
  both builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the per-part reserve line above; an unset-vs-set A/B of a run's free VRAM and prompt rate is the
  test of whether a given per-card split pays.

pulls.title: serve: the Monitor's Workers card - one widget per batch slot, each with its own tok/s (#465)
pulls.author: street-tripy
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2857

## Summary
With `"parallel": N` the server runs several requests at once, but the Monitor still shows one
request's numbers: the header pill reads the newest request's rate and the Model state card
shows one request's progress. There is no way to see on the page whether the requests are
decoding together or one after the other.

This adds a **Workers** card to the Monitor — one widget per batch slot with its own state, live
tok/s, tokens written and context fill — and makes the header pill name every decoding stream
(`2 decoding · 80.4 + 76.1 tok/s`). It is opt-in by construction: the card is in the markup
hidden and is shown only when `/metrics` reports `live.parallel`, which the server sets only for
a run config with `"parallel": N`.

## What changed
- `serve/web/index.html` (+7): the `workers-card` markup after *Model state*, `hidden` by
  default, with `workers-sum`, `workers` and `workers-note`.
- `serve/web/app.js` (+63 / -1): `workerWidgetsFor()` builds one widget per slot the first time
  and reuses it, so state and progress transitions animate instead of being replaced every
  second; `renderWorkers()` fills it from the existing `live.slots` and is called from
  `renderMonitor()`. The pill line gained a branch: when two or more slots are decoding it lists
  their rates; otherwise it is the old text.
- `serve/web/app.css` (+17): the card's styles, from existing design tokens only (no new
  colors, fonts or selectors outside `.worker*`).
- `serve/test_monitor.py` (+11): `test_the_workers_card_is_on_the_page_and_opt_in` — the same
  page assertion as `test_the_card_is_on_the_page`, plus that the card ships `hidden` and is
  gated on `live.parallel`.

## Extra Notes
- **Nothing outside `serve/web` and this test.** No server, setup or engine file changed, so
  there is nothing to build: no CUDA, HIP or SYCL file is touched.
- **The default path is unchanged.** Checked on this branch with a `/metrics` payload without
  `parallel`: the card stays hidden, no widget is built, and the pill reads
  `Generating · 79.8 tok/s` as before. With `parallel: 2` both slots render with their own rate.
  No console errors in either state.
- **Tests:** `python -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_runconfig` → 20 tests, all pass
  (19 on `main` + the new one). `node --check serve/web/app.js` is clean.
- **No new API.** The widget reads `live.slots` as `slots_view()` in `serve/server.py` already
  publishes it; the server and its tests are untouched.
- The widgets are filled one second at a time from the existing `poll()`, the way the request
  table already is; each widget keeps its own context bar against `engine.max_context`.
- Left alone on purpose: the standalone API Monitor page (`serve/web/monitor.html`), the Chat
  and About tabs, and every hardware card.
- Possibly touching the same markup as #1114 (rearrangeable Monitor layout) and #2317 (one line
  per card on a layer split); no functional overlap — happy to rebase if either lands first.

pulls.author: Echokovo
pulls.body:
Results-only submission of four folders under `bench/results/`, all measured on one machine with `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test) plus an interleaved A/B driver for the tuning part. No engine changes.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, 24 GiB VRAM
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 9 285K (24 cores / 24 threads, no AVX-512), 125.3 GiB RAM
- OS: Linux 6.17.0-1033-oem, driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2
- Strata: project 0.1.44.1, commit 296b59d2, engine 0.1.44.1

## What is in each folder

| Folder | Model | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2026-10-15-...-unsloth-ud-iq4-xs` | UD-IQ4_XS | baseline before the tuning switches: `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, no `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP`, `--prefill auto` |
| `2026-10-16-...-unsloth-ud-iq4-xs` | UD-IQ4_XS | same machine after the switches: tail-skip at its 0.1.42+ CUDA default, `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1`, `--prefill auto:16384` |
| `2026-10-16-tuning-tail-skip-adapt-overlap-rtx-pro-4000` | UD-IQ4_XS | the interleaved A/B that picked the switches (`ab*.py`, `arms/` configs and logs, raw rows), plus the two reports above as its before/after |
| `2026-10-17-...-unsloth-ud-q4-k-xl` | UD-Q4_K_XL | the larger quantization at the same settings |

The two UD-IQ4_XS community reports are not duplicates: the first is the "before", the second the "after", and the tuning folder is what links them.

## Headline numbers (median, ranges in the reports)

UD-IQ4_XS, before -> after the switches (decode tok/s pooled over 4 requests): 77.9 -> 89.1 (**x1.144** from `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` alone), `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` adds x1.015. Full suite after the change: short chat 89.1 tok/s, 4K prompt 2465.8 tok/s, 16K prompt 2874.4 tok/s, agent decode 96.2 tok/s, cache hit 68.8 %.

UD-Q4_K_XL at the same settings: short chat 77.8 tok/s, 4K prompt 2142.1 tok/s, 16K prompt 2916.5 tok/s, agent decode 84.4 tok/s, cache hit 68.4 %. So the bigger quantization costs about 13 % decode and 13 % on a 4K prompt, while 16K prefill is the same within noise.

All runs: 131072 context, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--mtp rt`, `--pool-workers 15`, thinking off, temperature 0, one slot. Configs in the folders are the install's own, unchanged.

## Limitations

Speed only: no correctness check, no KL check, no needle test. One machine, one GPU, two rounds per tuning arm (greedy), background load and power limits not recorded. `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` changes the output slightly by design (teacher-forced KL 0.003-0.006, top-1 agreement 97.7-98.2 % per `docs/DETAILS.md`). Home folder paths in the tuning folder are replaced by `/home/user`; no API keys, host names or IP addresses are included.

pulls.title: --keep-awake N: hold the system awake while the engine serves (#1727)
pulls.author: suprfire
pulls.body:
Closes #1727 (the feature request for a native prevent-sleep option during active inference on Windows).

## What it changes

A new opt-in engine flag, `--keep-awake N` (an argument in the config's `args`):

- `0` (or no flag) - off.
- `1` - hold the system awake for as long as the engine runs (armed at `READY`).
- `2` - hold it only while a request runs (request start to `DONE`/`STOP`/`ERR`), and hold the display too.

It calls `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED [| ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED])` on the serving thread and clears back to `ES_CONTINUOUS` when the arm ends. Windows only; a no-op elsewhere. `--keep-awake` without `--serve` is refused with a message.

## What it leaves alone

No default changes: with the flag absent nothing calls `SetThreadExecutionState`, so the default path is byte-identical. No new dependency (`windows.h` was already included). The `2` arm hooks the existing `BusyScope` (busy from a request's start to the end of its iteration), so `QUIT` and the between-request commands (`SAVE`/`RESTORE`/`VRAM`) do not arm it.

## Why

Windows counts a CPU-bound server as idle. Nothing in the engine asked the system to stay up, so a long prompt read can run into the display and sleep timers, and an S3 sleep kills the running request (the expert arena survives in RAM, so the model does not reload - the request is what is lost).

## How I checked it

RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB + Ryzen 9 5900X + 64 GB DDR4, Windows 11 (10.0.26200), engine built from this commit (CUDA 13.4, sm_86), Swift IQ3_XXS, `--keep-awake 1`:

- The start block shows `--keep-awake: SetThreadExecutionState(0x80000001) -> 0x80000000 (error 0)` - the return is the previous state, so the request was accepted.
- `powercfg /requests` (elevated) lists the engine under SYSTEM while it serves.
- With the AC sleep timer at **60 s** the machine stayed up **4.5+ minutes** with the engine serving and its uptime never reset; the same machine slept inside a minute with the flag off (Kernel-Power 42 and `powercfg /lastwake` confirm the off-case sleeps).
- The flag is refused without `--serve`, and `--help` lists the three values.

## What I did not test

- The `2` arm (only `1` was measured) and its display hold.
- A machine whose sleep state is S0 low-power idle rather than S3 (this box is S3).
- HIP/SYCL: the change is inside `#ifdef _WIN32` and compiles out on those backends.

pulls.title: Slot checkpoints for clients that rewrite the end of their history (3/3, depends on #2527 and #2528): STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS, STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT, BCHECKS
pulls.author: andyhrc
pulls.body:
## Summary

A client that rewrites the end of its history every time never finds a checkpoint to continue from. Claude Code's
safety classifier is one: each query is the agent's transcript with the new tool calls inserted before the closing
text (`... </transcript>` and the instruction), so the next query leaves this one a few dozen tokens before its end.
The turn checkpoint is past that point, the periodic ones are up to 16K tokens before it, and a slot that receives
the conversation (park=, an admission continuing in its slot) keeps only its deepest checkpoint. On our server
(3 x RTX A4000 layer split, --batch 6) every classifier query of 2026-10-16 read its whole 42-74K-token transcript
again: 15.6-27.4 s per call, several per agent step.

**Part 3, depends on #2527 and #2528**: the branch includes their commits (rebased on 0.1.45); this PR's own are the
last five (`batch: STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS=N`, `generate: STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=<margin>`, `batch, serve: BCHECKS`,
`batch: a slot keeps its deepest checkpoint and the branch one; ...`, `batch: STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT and
STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS apart`). The placement side of the same problem - a slot holding an older version of the
conversation is the one to replace (`STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE`) - is in #2528.

## Change (all opt-in)

- `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=<margin>` (serve, batch or not): before reading, the engine measures how far the prompt
  runs along each conversation it holds (the main session's, every idle slot's) before leaving it; when that point
  is `<margin>` tokens or more past where the read starts and before the turn boundary, the read stops there for one
  more checkpoint, like the root and turn cuts. The next query - which leaves this one later - resumes there. With it
  on, a slot keeps the deepest such branch checkpoint of its conversation (alone, whatever N is).
- `STRATA_SLOT_CHECKPOINTS=N` (batch; unset 1, as before): how many checkpoints a slot keeps - the deepest, then the
  deepest others, the branch one counted in N. The two switches are apart:

  | | without `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT` | with it |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | N = 1 | the deepest (the turn checkpoint), as before | the turn and the branch one (one before there is one) |
  | N = 2 | the two deepest (the turn before or a periodic one) | two: the turn and the branch one, or else the next deepest |

  A restore from a slot checkpoint brings the slot's shallower ones back with it, and a slot that gives back all it
  holds gives back its checkpoints of that conversation with it. Log: `slot 2 keeps 2 checkpoints (at 43340 43867;
  227.6 MiB)`. Pure helpers in `include/strata/program/slot_checkpoints.hpp`, unit test `slot_checkpoints_test`.
- With upstream's `STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1` an admission moves all of them into the slot instead of copying (the
  chain's root and a pinned prefix are copied): the main session drops checkpoints of another conversation at its next
  request anyway. A slot that gives back all it holds moves them back, so the next admission keeps them again (without
  that, the moved ones were lost there - also upstream's single moved turn checkpoint - and a next turn sent back
  without its thinking read 19,342 tokens in 8.5 s instead of 154 in 0.63 s).
- `BCHECKS <slot> <tokens> <lengths>` (with N > 1 or `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT`): after `PARKED`, `BADM 1` and
  `BYIELD` the engine says which checkpoints a slot keeps; the server keeps them per slot (forgotten before it sends
  anything that overwrites the slot), shows them in `/metrics` (`checkpoint_tokens`), and `place()` uses the deepest
  one that starts the prompt as the hint where no slot's history continues it (it was 0). Information only: the
  engine still picks what it reuses.

Unset, every path is the one before.

## Results

3 x RTX A4000, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 0.1.45 + #2527 / #2528, --batch 6 in 3 groups, 200K context,
`STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1 STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1`. A 43-45K-token classifier transcript growing by about 250 tokens per
query, an agent conversation taking the main session between the queries (S: alone; B: a client decoding beside it);
seconds per query 1-6:

| | S | B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without either switch (0.1.45) | 13.7, 13.6, 13.8, 13.9, 14.1, 14.2 | 14.1-14.2 |
| `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=1024`, N unset (1) | 13.6, 14.2, 1.21, 1.65, 1.89, 2.03 | 0.56, 1.20, 1.09, 1.55, 1.82, 1.98 |
| the same, N = 2 | 13.6, 7.3, 1.48, 1.40, 1.89, 2.04 | 0.56, 1.21, 1.09, 1.57, 1.80, 1.97 |
| branch checkpoints taken but not kept by the slot (the rule before the switches were apart, N 1) | 13.6-14.9, none reused | 14.2-15.1, none reused |

From query 3 on, queries resume at the branch checkpoint (43,340 reused, 534-1,329 read). N = 2 adds the second
query of a chain: no branch checkpoint exists yet, and it resumes at the periodic checkpoint (32,768) instead of
reading the whole transcript. The last row is why the branch switch keeps its checkpoint in the slot by itself: the
cut is paid (0.6-0.8 s per query over no switch) and the checkpoint is dropped with the main session's chain.

Margin: 256 against 1024 (both with the slot keeping the branch checkpoint): reads stay at about 570 tokens instead
of growing to 1,329 until the next cut, but a cut in almost every query costs about the same (B, queries 2-6: 7.64 s
both), and a query branching further back than the newest branch checkpoint read its whole transcript again (B
query 1: 14.1 s against 0.56 s). With 1024 a query never falls back to a periodic checkpoint once a branch one exists:
it resumes at the last branch checkpoint, at most the margin plus one query's growth behind.

A thinking chat's next turn sent back without its thinking: 0.63 s (19,176 reused + 154 read). Throughput 62.8 /
180.6 tok/s at 1 / 6 clients (60.9 / 179.0 without either switch; `tools/serve_load.py`).

Memory (host RAM, a checkpoint is 113-114 MiB here): the branch checkpoints count in the main session's
`--prompt-cache` (6); a slot keeps one more where its conversation has one (N 1) or wherever it has two checkpoints
(N 2). With 6 slots the bound grows from 12 to 18 checkpoints, +0.67 GiB, at N 1 in practice by about 114 MiB per
slot holding a classifier-like conversation; with the move a moved checkpoint is not also in the main session's chain.

## How it was checked

Exactness (0.1.44.1 base), with docs/BATCHING.md's settings (STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1, --pcie-frac 0, --adapt-every
1000000, --no-prefill-borrow), greedy: the 6 queries' short answers are the same tokens without and with; of 6
160-token answers, 5 are the same and the third differs from its first token. That one depends only on whether the
read had a cut at 43,340: read at once, or resumed from 32,768 without the cut -> answer A; read through the cut in
one request (no restore), resumed from the branch checkpoint in the main session, or from it in a slot -> answer B.
So the saved, copied and restored state is the one the read had there; the cut changes the chunks of the read after
it, as `pin=` or a resume from an earlier turn checkpoint does.

Tests: `slot_checkpoints_test` 31 checks (the picks for N 0-9 with and without the branch switch, shared prefix, the
branch boundary's conditions); `conv_cache_test`, `conversation_cache_test`; `serve/test_slot_alloc.py` 74 (the hint
from reported checkpoints; BCHECKS lines kept per slot and forgotten before an overwrite), `test_parallel` 35,
`test_slots` 30, `test_cache_trace`.

Built natively on CUDA (sm_86, Linux). The engine change is in `src/program/generate.cpp` only (shared by every
backend's serve loop); not built here: HIP, SYCL.

## Extra Notes

Our production profiles on the machine above run `STRATA_BRANCH_CHECKPOINT=1024 STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE=1
STRATA_CKPT_POOL=1` with N unset (1) since 2026-10-17. In a field test on 2026-10-18 (two Claude Code sessions at once, run twice) each conversation kept its own slot after its first two requests, and every later request re-read only its new part (48-7,260 tokens; 20 of 24 requests in the second run). The claim of the classifier's prompt layout comes from our server's logs of Claude Code (a query's
transcript grows inside `<transcript>...</transcript>`; each new query inserts its tool calls before the closing
tag).

pulls.title: Windows: make device_free_bytes() unified-memory aware on APUs (Strix Halo gfx1151)
pulls.author: moweishun
pulls.body:
# Windows: `device_free_bytes()` is not unified-memory aware, so the auto expert cache cannot size on Strix Halo (gfx1151)

## Summary

On Windows, an APU with unified memory (Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, `gfx1151`) reports a tiny
"free VRAM" figure through `cudaMemGetInfo` — essentially the free space of the BIOS's dedicated
carve-out, often well under 2 GiB. `device_free_bytes()` (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp`) only applies
its unified-memory correction (`MemAvailable` minus headroom) under `#if defined(__linux__)`, so on
Windows the auto expert cache sizes from the small figure and refuses to start
("no VRAM is left for the expert cache"), and an explicit `--expert-cache N` is silently shrunk to
0 slots by the sizing pass ("pre-filled 0 of 0 slots from the profile", no "expert cache N slots"
line).

This PR extends the same unified-memory correction to Windows: when the current device reports
integrated graphics, the free figure is raised to `GlobalMemoryStatusEx().ullAvailPhys` minus the
same `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB` headroom (default 6 GiB). The Linux path is unchanged, and discrete
GPUs are unchanged (the integrated check is per device, as before).

## What it changes

- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp`, `device_free_bytes()`: the integrated-GPU detection moves out of the
  `__linux__`-only block (HIP exposes `cudaDevAttrIntegrated`), and a `_WIN32` branch adds the
  `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` path beside the Linux `/proc/meminfo` path. The
  `STRATA_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB` knob, its default of 6, and its semantics are shared.
- `#include <windows.h>` under `_WIN32` for `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`.

## What it leaves alone

- The Linux `/proc/meminfo` path, the gfx906 compat exclusion, the headroom default and env knob.
- Discrete GPUs on every platform (`unified_memory` false → plain `cudaMemGetInfo`).
- The SYCL port's own copy (`sycl/src/core/expert_cache.cpp`) — not touched.

## Measured on

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, `gfx1151`, wave32), Windows 11 (build 26100), Adrenalin driver
32.0.31041.1004, self-built HIP engine from this tree (`tools/hip/build_windows.bat`,
`STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1151`, ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 wheels), IQ3_S, 200K context, MTP on.

Free figure seen by the engine (after the session's allocations), by BIOS carve-out, before the fix:

| carve-out | `device_free_bytes()` | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 GB | ~0 | auto: refuse; forced: shrunk to 0 slots |
| 16 GB | 0.37 GiB | auto: refuse (needs 241 slots / 611 MiB at 32K) |
| 32 GB | ~1.1 GiB | only 32K context fits (438 slots); 200K refuses |
| 64 GB | 6.69 GiB | 200K sizes 19339 slots — but see the caveats below |

After the fix (16 GB carve-out, 200K): auto sizes 19339 slots (36.84 GiB), pre-fills all of them
from the profile (6.5 s), serves at 40-45 tok/s decode (96.9% cache hit rate), where every
configuration refused to start or shrank to 0 slots before.

## Caveats, stated plainly

- On this chip the dedicated carve-out is smaller than the cache either way, so the cache lands in
  the driver's shared pool (WDDM GTT backed by the same LPDDR5X). The server's
  "0 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded - LOW" warning still prints (the reserve check reads
  the same function, which now reports the large figure and never triggers the shrink loop).
  Measured no stalls across benchmark runs; a follow-up that also accounts for the carve-out in the
  shrink loop may be worth it, but it is deliberately not in this PR.
- The cache allocation is charged to the system commit on Windows (issue #60's note), so a big
  cache wants a page file with room. `tools/hip/build_windows.bat`'s engine printed that note
  during a failed open before the fix; with the fix the auto path converged on the first open.

## How it was checked

- Built the HIP engine for gfx1151 with the patch and ran setup + serving end to end (the numbers
  above). Without the patch, the same tree reproduces the refusals in the table.
- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp` is also compiled by the CUDA build; on Windows CUDA there is no
  integrated AMD GPU, and on Linux the CUDA build already took the `__linux__` path (unchanged).
  Not built here (no NVIDIA GPU on this PC) — the CUDA path's behaviour for a discrete GPU is
  unchanged by construction (the new code only runs when `unified_memory` is true).

pulls.title: prefill: the prompt path's MMQ scratch rides in the loan (opt-in, STRATA_MMQ_SLAB)
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` (opt-in; unset is off): the prompt path's MMQ scratch — its stream-k fixup tiles — comes out of
the loan's unused tail instead of free VRAM.

llama.cpp's `mmq.cuh` allocates those tiles lazily through `ggml_cuda_pool`, which this build backs with a `cudaMalloc`
on whatever is free at that moment — a few MB on a card the expert cache has filled, at the one moment a prompt is
running, and a malloc that fails there aborts the engine mid-read instead of failing the request. A layout does not
use the whole loan: the carve is a bump, so everything from its stop to the loan's end is the prompt's own memory,
provably (a loan is whole cache slots and the top one is only partly needed).

The pool takes the tiles from there in **size classes** (a power of two, 128 KiB floor). The classes are load-bearing:
MMQ's J search picks a different J per launch, so a cache keyed on the exact size holds one buffer per J — 32 buffers,
31.5 MiB on a 579-token chunk in the Maya checkout's measurement — where a class bounds the pool to a few MB.

Three guards make it safe, all load-bearing: it is published per layout keyed on the tail's **address** (a request
whose chunk moves `used` moves the tail and the pool drops the old buffers); `Prefill::run` drops it once the prompt is
read, before the caller refills the borrowed slots; and the loan is the participant's own expert cache `cudaMalloc`ed
on this device, so the tail is this card's memory to write. A tail that is empty (the layout used the whole loan, or
spilled into owned buffers) publishes nothing, and the pool allocates as it always did.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `bf844d5`.

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default), the pool stays on free VRAM exactly as before: `lend_mmq_scratch` publishes nothing and
`mmq::pool_slab` is not given a slab. The size classes are part of the slab path only (they bound the slab's pool);
with the knob off there is no slab to bound. Default path unchanged by construction.

## Measurements

- That commit hit the failure at a 16,384-token chunk on a 5060 (3.4 MB free of 7,707.7 MB, 1.2 MB wanted) and measured
  the slab costing 42–47 more lent experts per part and no change to the chunk arithmetic, on its live split
  (5060/5060/3060/3060).
- **No speedup is claimed here.** What the start's check line shows is whether the slab is in use on a given rig.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`v != nullptr && std::atoi(v) != 0`).
- **Build:** `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` compiles clean with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`);
  `src/prefill/ggml_cuda_host.cu` and `src/prefill/moe_moe.cu` compile clean with the build's nvcc flags (CUDA 13.2,
  `compute_86` and `compute_120`). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja.
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). The device files this touches are the CUDA MMQ
  target's; the slab plumbing in `prefill.cpp` has no per-backend branch.
- **On a start:** `strata prefill mmq: CUDA%d the scratch pool takes a new N MiB buffer` prints for a buffer of 4 MiB
  or more; with `STRATA_MMQ_SLAB=1` and a loan that has a tail it should not appear at all, and a prompt should read
  to completion as before.

pulls.title: docs: --prompt-cache-every is not a piece-size dial here (the fork's is)
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body: ## What this changes A docs bullet for `--prompt-cache-every`, in `docs/DETAILS.md`: the knob is **not** a piece-size dial in this engine. In the Maya checkout it is also a wall-time dial because there its marks bound the segments the prompt path reads, and every segment pays a fill and a drain of the part chain. What the bullet records: - The Maya checkout's numbers for its `STRATA_GLM_CKPT_EVERY` (same 16384 default), local commit `3095719` (2026-10-15), on a 100,535-token fresh read (Maya-L split, 8192-token chunks, one 580-token warm prompt before each arm, engine restarted between arms): `16384` cut the read into 5 pieces read in 148.8 s, `32768` into 4 in 134.9 s (-9.3%), `0` into one of 13 chunks in 93.2 s (-37.4%) — that checkout's numbers on its rig, a piece fitting ~14.6 s + 6.5 s a chunk there. - Why they do not carry over here: a periodic mark is saved at a chunk boundary and the run carries on, so no piece ends at it. What cuts this engine's read into runs is the cut list — a re-read (`STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`), the system-prompt root, a message boundary (`STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY`), the start of the last turn and a pinned prefix — and each of those is one fill and drain. - So `--prompt-cache-every 0` here skips the periodic marks and the near-tail one (a `--prompt-cache-tail` mark needs `--prompt-cache-every` above 0), while the root, the last turn, a message boundary and a pin are still saved — the same trade the Maya checkout documents for its `0`: a client that rewrote a turn *before* the last one mounts a farther mark. The lever for a fresh long read here is those cuts, not this cadence. ## What it leaves alone Documentation only: not one line of code or default changes. Every name and flag the bullet cites was checked against the tree it documents (`--prompt-cache-every`, `--prompt-cache-tail`, `STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`, `STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY`). ## Measurements The numbers above are quoted with what they were measured on (the Maya checkout's rig, Maya-L split, the warm prompt, the restarts between arms). No number is claimed for this engine. ## Checks - Docs-only change; no build to run. The rendered Markdown is the only output. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP (128) is the slots a loan leaves the cache
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_KEEP=N` (**128 by default**): the expert-cache slots a loan must leave resident while a prompt chunk
borrows the cache's tail. On a small cache it is this number, not the auto lend's 90% cap, that picks the chunk. On
the Q8_0 four-way's 691- and 937-slot stages it leaves 563 and 809 slots where the cap would leave 621 and 843.
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_KEEP` is accepted as the same knob.

**The clamp is up, not down**: a lend has to leave the elastic K/V a region to grow into (its floor is
`STRATA_KV_GROW_FLOOR`, 128 by default), so a smaller `N` is clamped to that floor and the start says so — lower both
together to lend more of the cache and let the chunk grow at the K/V's expense. A larger `N` keeps more experts
resident for the prompt's own tokens and buys a smaller chunk.

The number is the same one the auto scan, the per-stage lend regions, the serve loan, the smallest cache a start
accepts and the vram-elastic reserve used before; this change routes all of them through one reader of the variable.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `71c1ca7` (2026-10-15).

## What it leaves alone

Unset, every use is 128, exactly as before — this is by construction, not a measurement, and this PR's default run
is byte-identical on that path. With the variable set to 128 (its default) the numbers are also unchanged.

## Measurements

That commit lowered its pool's floor from 13 to 11 slots a layer (`STRATA_GLM_RESERVE_MB=400`) on a four-way split and
measured, on a 99,758-token conversation, the binding part reach an 8192-token chunk: a 49,152-token piece
61,762 → 57,507 ms (-6.9%) and a whole five-piece read 161,291 → 158,938 ms, on the live split (5060/5060/3060/3060)
— where it was not a free win either (a 16,384-token piece that went from three chunks to two lost 3%,
28,716 → 29,651 ms, since the parts run a chunk as a chain and there is less left to overlap). **No number is claimed
for our rig**: the four-way Q8_0 runs so far used 128, which is this default.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = 128 everywhere by construction.
- **Build:** `src/program/generate.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code). The development branch that also
  carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both
  builds compile the same change.

pulls.title: serve: STRATA_WARM_PROMPT (off) reads one synthetic prompt before READY
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=N` (`--serve`, off by default): one synthetic prompt of N tokens (32 if you ask for less) is read
through the whole part chain **before the engine says READY**, so a session's first request does not pay what only a
session's first prompt pays — the first chunk carries every kernel's first launch, the prompt path's own allocations
and the tiers' first reads, and no later prompt pays any of it. `STRATA_GLM_WARM_PROMPT` is accepted as the same
knob.

The synthetic ids are spread over the vocabulary (`100 + (i * 131) % 20000`), so the routes are not one expert's. It
takes the same loan a request takes (the slots the prompt path is laid out in go non-resident and are refilled from
the arena afterwards), and every participant's state is zeroed before and after it, so no conversation can see it. A
prompt path that cannot run prints why and the first prompt pays it; the start never fails because of it.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `cc58309` (2026-10-14).

## What it leaves alone

Unset or `0` (the default), the whole block is skipped and the engine says READY exactly as before. Nothing outside
the block changes; this is by construction.

## Measurements

- **Reported on 4× RTX 5080 16 GB (2026-10-17, blange48; not run by us): it does what it says.** Linux, layer split
  12,24,36, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 8 --batch-groups 4` (v0.1.45 + this PR + #2673), one run per case,
  warm page cache. Time to READY: **102 s unset vs 101 s** at `STRATA_WARM_PROMPT=512`. First request (a ~325-token
  prompt), time to first token: **1.00 s unset vs 0.72 s** at 512. Later requests were unaffected.
- The Maya checkout's issue #8 reported 95–133 ms/token on a first prompt against 23–44 warm — that checkout's number
  on its rig.
- On this engine the knob is how you measure it: the first request's time to first token, or its `PP` line, with the
  variable set and unset is the A/B.
- The report's build also carried #2673, whose different-greedy-answers issue is being looked at there; this PR was
  off in those comparisons, so it does not look involved.
- What the report does not cover: our own hardware (we have not run it), more than one run per case, or a start with
  a cold page cache.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`wn = 0` skips the block).
- **Build:** `src/program/generate.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in unrelated code). The development branch that also
  carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both
  builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the engine prints `strata serve: warming the prompt path with a N-token prompt before READY`.

pulls.title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES (opt-in) prints where a prompt chunk's wall went
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=1` (opt-in; unset is off) turns on the chunk's stage line: **one line a stage a chunk** with
where the chunk's wall went — the chunk's wall, the copy lane's own span split into what ran before it (lead), the
lane itself and what ran behind it (tail), the bytes it moved and the bytes the chunk's consumers waited on (the
difference is the ring's read-ahead), the hand-off a later stage of a layer split paid, the GPU's own phases over the
chunk, and the experts and host time it spent. It also turns the phase timer on.

Without it a prefill change can only be judged by the prompt's ms/token, which mixes the chunk size, the copy lane,
the host and the phases. The line is what separates them.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `a34f57c`, with its fixes `04b8d65` (the line's events are
destroyed with the prompt path) and `63b3690` (the line reads only the events its chunk recorded). Its spelling
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_STAGES` is accepted as the same knob, so a config written for that checkout runs unchanged.

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default), `stages_on()` is false: no line is printed, the phase timer is not read for it, and no extra
sync is taken for it. The syncs the line does add when on wait only on copies the compute stream has already waited
for (the issuer is joined when the chunk ends), so `STRATA_PREFILL_STAGES=0` beside a `--bench` A/B is how you check
it costs nothing. The default path is unchanged by construction.

## Measurements

This is a diagnostic; it makes no claim to speed anything up. Its own cost is what the set-vs-unset A/B under
`--bench` measures, and the design keeps that at zero by waiting only on work already joined.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (`stages_on()` reads the environment once and returns false).
- **Build:** `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` compiles clean against this branch's headers with the build's own flags
  (`-fsyntax-only`). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (CUDA 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). The change adds no backend-specific branch; it uses
  the same stream/event API the file already used, and the events are only created when the knob is on.

pulls.title: STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN — a long prompt takes the MTP drafter's 512 experts (decode-only) as ring
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=TOKENS` (`--serve` with `--mtp`): a request that **reads** at least TOKENS prompt tokens (`0`:
every request) uses the MTP drafter's 512 routed experts as the prompt path's ring while it is read. TOKENS counts the
tokens this request reads, not the whole prompt: a turn that reuses a cached conversation prefix and reads a few
hundred tokens gains nothing from the room. Those experts are 708 MB (675 MiB) that only the **decode** reads —
`record_rest` is their only reader; a prompt's passes run the draft layer's dense tensors and its K/V — so the prompt
path's ring is pointed **at the block itself**: `slot i = experts_base + (i - rule) * MAXBLOB` (135 slots on a Q8_0
pack, whose largest blob is 4.98 MiB). Opening and closing a room moves the ring count alone
(`Prefill::set_ring_room_active`): the block is never freed, never allocated again and never moves, so no prompt path
is laid out again, the decode's captured round/step graphs stay valid (nothing is dropped), and what comes back before
the first window is the decode's own bytes (`MtpDrafter::experts_reclaim`). In the measured shape's successor this is
two 675 MiB DMAs around the read.

The room is opened after the reused prefix is known (`read_from`) and immediately before `lend()`, so a relayout still
re-carves with the room; a request that must be re-read from 0 (`STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`) counts all of its tokens.

Limits, refused with the reason at start: `--serve` only, `--mtp` needed, `--batch` not supported (its slot drafters
share the solo drafter's weights). A layer split is fine (the room goes to the prompt path on the drafter's card),
`--pipeline-windows` is fine (the room closes before the request's first window), and `--prefill-head-alias` is fine.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commits `7df369c` (`STRATA_GLM_ROOM_MIN`), `d4d0792` (the tail's
slots rounded up to the largest blob) and `5ccf9a4` (the in-place shape, for the MTP config's NextN block). Counting
what a request reads is this port's change, made after the report below.

## What it leaves alone

Unset (the default) `mtp_room_min` is `-1` and not one line of the room runs; the prompt path is laid out exactly as
before. The new code is reachable only behind that check. This is by construction, not by a measurement. `=0` keeps
the behaviour that was measured: every request takes the rod, on 7-token continuations).

## Measurements

- **Reported on an 8 GB RTX 2060 SUPER (2026-10-18, merbana branch, not run by us): the
  room works and pays where the ring is the limit.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--serve --mtp` (Q2_0 drafter,
  675 MiB), `--resident-budget-gib 40` (fully page-locked), `--kv k8v4 --kv-resident 20480`, `--prefill auto`; the
  auto chunk was 6,656 tokens with a **96-slot ring**, the in all), chunk unchanged.
  `STRATA_MTP_ROOM_MIN=0` against the same build unset (paired A/B, 3 pairs, prompt tok/s): 4K 448.4 -> 527.2 (+17%),
  16K 558.9 -> 658.1 (+17%), 32K 584.0 -> 719.7 (+23%); dec17 (noise). The lend cost
  107 ms per roomed request. `STRATA_PREFILL_RING` alone showed the ring was the limit (192 slots: +9.8% / +6.2% /
  +2.3%, decode -3.1 to -3.6 tok/s), so this is the case thn logits after a
  15,521-token prompt were **bitwise equal** to the unset run (two runs per arm, all four identical), the 48-token
  greedy replies matched, and the drafter's acceptance after reclaim was normal (27 of 34).
- **The first shape was measured on our Q8_0 4-way rig (202ught no time.** The room
  opened, the 675 MiB really went into the ring, the block came back before the first window and the decode ran
  unchanged — but a deeper ring was not what the prompt waiens. That shape laid the
  prompt path out again around the block and cost **3.4–4.0p of the read.
- **The in-place shape and the read threshold were measured on our Q8_0 4-way rig (2026-10-19): the room is skipped,
  and its ~206 ms goes with it.** Two engines from the sameainst this one), one start
  each, `MIN=1024`: one 5,042-token chat and three continuations that echoed the answer back. The parent lent the
  room for the whole 5,096-token prompt on continuations thend ~102 ms + reclaim
  ~104 ms); this commit lent nothing. Read time 2,054 -> 1,813 ms, 360 -> 153 ms, 344 -> 152 ms; time to first token
  2.110 -> 1.869 s, 0.409 -> 0.203 s, 0.390 -> 0.199 s. A ` still opened the room on the
  7-token continuations (time to first token 0.432 / 0.415 the difference is the room,
  not the binary. The cold request still took the room in bver: more than one run per
  timing, HIP/SYCL, `--prefill-head-alias`.
- `7df369c` records the room as not yet measured, with its 23 tok/s) on its
  byte-identical 100,535-token read.
- **No blanket speedup is claimed.** The knob is how you meh the variable set and unset,
  `PP` line against `PP` line. The ring gain appears where GB card above) and is nil
  where it is not (our Q8_0 rig). The read threshold's gainend on the ring: it removes
  the room's own DMA from turns that reuse a conversation, ~0.2 s per short turn on our rig.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = off by construction (the parsed threshold is `-1` and every room call is behind it).
- **Threshold:** the room opens only when `n - read_from >= TOKENS`, after `read_from` is known and before `lend()`,
  so the prompt path's relayout re-carves with the ring rooes the ring count alone; the
  room's slot pointers are laid out by `carve` whether or nning it after the head-alias
  rebuild still adds the slots.
- **Build:** both the parent commit and this commit built fild strata`, CUDA 13.2,
  sm_86 + sm_120) and ran on the Q8_0 4-way rig; the two binaries differ by this commit.
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so both
  builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the engine prints the read-token threshold, MiB and slots. Per roomed request it prints the tokens
  this request reads (so a reused prefix is visible againstrafter's block ever moved, the
  first shape said so — the in-place shape cannot.

pulls.title: prefill: STRATA_PREFILL_MAX, a per-part prompt-chunk ceiling
pulls.author: gopinath87607
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,4096,8192,8192"` — an opt-in ceiling on the prompt chunk of each prompt-path
participant, in the split's order. Entry 0 is the first card's path (it reads the chunk's embeddings and hands
its rows on), entry *i* the *i*-th stage; `0` or an absent entry is no ceiling, and values are multiples of 256.
`STRATA_GLM_PREFILL_MAX` is accepted as the same knob.

Strata's layer split is one grid: every stage reads prompt chunks of the chain's size, so a card whose expert
cache cannot fund one pulls *every* stage down to its number (the `#448` warning). The ceiling is the other
choice: a capped stage lays out at `min(chain, its cap)` and `Prefill::run_impl`'s `c0 += m.T` loop reads each
larger hand-off in steps of its own, forwarding each sub-step, while the other stages keep the chain's chunk.
A ceiling only lowers a stage and never raises one.

From the Maya checkout (`project-maya`), local commit `ef3b6e7` (2026-10-15).

Every chunk-pricing site prices a part at its own chunk: the auto scan (`fits_one`, `ring_room`, the old
candidate list), the serve loan (`lend`), the resident-RAM lend regions, stage init (at the stage's own maximum —
`relayout` requires `chunk <= T_max`), the init retry, split-small's extra slots, the own-buffers headroom test
and the head-alias candidates. The start prints one line per capped entry:
`strata serve: prompt chunk: CUDA%d reads N tokens a step (STRATA_PREFILL_MAX N)`, with
`, inside a larger chain chunk` when the cap is below the chain's.

## What it leaves alone

Unset, not one number changes: the list is empty, `part_chunk` / `part_ceiling` return the chain chunk,
`max_head` is 0, and the new print loop runs zero times. This is by construction, not by a measurement.

## Measurements

- That local commit measured moving every part as a loss: 94,840 ms for the capped 16k/16k/8k/7k shape against
  91,718.9 ms for 13 equal chunks of 7,744, on its byte-identical 100,535-token read (an earlier nesting took
  98,568.1 ms). That is why a ceiling only lowers a stage and why this is opt-in.
- **No speedup is claimed here.** On the four-way Q8_0 rig this was written for, the start log does show the case
  the knob is for — the chain settles at 4096 because CUDA3's 690 slots cannot fund 6912
  (`WARNING: prompt chunk 4096 tokens, not 6912 ...`, `#448`) — but a binding-cap A/B
  (`STRATA_PREFILL_MAX="8192,8192,8192,2048"`, expecting the chain to rise toward CUDA0's own 6912 while CUDA3
  reads its hand-offs in 2048-token steps) has not been run yet. Numbers to follow.

## Checks

- **Default path:** unset = byte-identical by construction (empty list; every priced site returns the chain
  chunk; no arithmetic changes).
- **Build:** CUDA. `generate.cpp` is host-only code and this adds no device code; it compiles clean against this
  branch's headers with the build's own flags (`-fsyntax-only`; one pre-existing unused-variable warning in
  unrelated code). The development branch that also carries the change built fully with ninja (nvcc 13.2).
- **HIP / SYCL:** not compiled here (no toolchain on the machine). `generate.cpp` carries no per-backend code, so
  both builds compile the same change.
- **On a start:** the new per-participant line above; an unset-vs-set A/B of the prefill rate is the test of
  whether a cap pays on a given rig.
