Adds a community benchmark: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100) in an
AOOSTAR AG03 eGPU dock (Sapphire Pulse) over Oculink, driven by an ASRock
NUC Box K12 mini-PC (Ryzen 7 H 255, 64 GB RAM, Fedora).

## Setup

- **Strata** 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2), engine 0.1.44.1, hip backend
- **Model** swift-1.5, IQ2_XS, 131,072-token context, 1 parallel slot
- **Config** `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp rt --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`,
  thinking off, temperature 0
- **GPU connection:** the 7900 XTX is not socketed in the mini-PC — it's an
  eGPU over Oculink. The engine matches the link at `pcie_frac 0.19`
  (~1/4 of a desktop x16 PCIe 4.0 bandwidth), so prompt/decode transfers
  are Oculink-bound. Noted in the report so reviewers don't discount the
  prompt rates.

## Results (suite 1, 3 runs each, medians with ranges)

| Test | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short chat (~46 → 100 new tokens) | — | 86.1 (67.1–105.3) | 0.35 s |
| 4K fresh | 1098.4 | — | 3.68 s |
| 16K fresh | 1389.7 | — | 11.58 s |
| 32K fresh | 1411.9 | — | 22.74 s |
| Agent follow-up turns | ~800 cached | 85.4 (68.1–122.5) | 3.65 s |

- Agent-session conversation-cache hit: **68.6%**, only ~52 earlier tokens
  re-read per session; ~13,729 new file tokens read once.

## Notes / limitations

- Speed only — no correctness check was run.
- Background load and GPU power limits not recorded.
- Suite total: 206 s. No concurrency test (`--clients`) was run.
- Per-request data: `results.json`. The server was already running, so there
  is no `engine-log-excerpt.txt` in this folder.

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rx-7900-xtx-oculink-swift-1-5-iq2-xs-2/`
(README.md + results.json). No engine or runtime changes.

pulls.title: [GUI] Web search and page reading for the web app's Chat (DuckDuckGo default, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Serper)
pulls.author: c-OOL-io
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The Chat tab of the lean web app (the serve/Terminal frontend, not the App) has no web access at all: answers are limited to the model's weights, and agent-style use on a headless server had no source-backed option. Upstream shipped web search for the App in 0.2.0; the serve web chat route is still without it.

Before: no search in the web app's Chat, no sources. After: a built-in web search, modeled after how Open WebUI and similar chat tools do it: the model can look the question up before answering, and the answer shows its sources. **Web search is completely off by default**: until the user turns it on in Chat Settings, nothing about this feature sends anything out of the PC. Strata's Chat is deliberately lean, and this feature is built the same way: it adds no tokens until a chat turns search on, and results are budget-capped to a small slice of the model's context window (defaults scale with the context window), so the Chat gains recent information without losing what makes it comfortable for long sessions.

## Related discussion

None (no prior scope-issue exists). Note: this PR *is* the original discussion; it was closed 19.10. in the pre-0.2.0-beta tracker reset ("closed here does not mean rejected") and is rebased on current main and re-validated per the reopen steps. Upstream's App search (`apps/host`, DuckDuckGo via MCP) does not overlap with this work: this targets the serve web chat, with self-hostable engines (SearXNG) and server-side page reading.

## Approach

Search runs server-side in the serve backend (`serve/websearch.py`, stdlib-only); the browser frontend only configures and renders it. All providers are fetched through the Strata server (a browser could not call them directly because of CORS). API keys stay browser-only (localStorage), like the existing API-key field; **nothing search-related is stored on the server**.

### What it looks like in the UI
- A globe button in the composer (first icon, before the paperclip) toggles search for the next message.
- **Chat Settings** (gear) has a *Web search* section: enable/disable, engine picker, SearXNG URL, API key field, max results, page reading and a page reader mode (see below). All web-search controls appear only when the search switch is on; switching it on expands the whole section and fires the privacy toast.
- When search is on, the results are injected as context before the model's turn, with an instruction to answer from them and cite by `[n]`.
- Under each answer the sources appear as `Sources (DuckDuckGo): [1] … | [2] …` (clickable, engine named, read pages get a `read` badge), and they are included in the "Save this chat as Markdown" export.
- While a search runs the status pill shows the truth instead of "Idle": a globe (instead of the state dot) with `Framing query` → `Searching web + reading pages · DuckDuckGo · 12.4 s`; a failed search reads `Search failed` for 2.5 s. The same status line appears in the answer bubble exactly where "Thinking…" would sit.
- If the engine is busy with someone else's turn (another tab or agent) while this chat searches, the pill shows it as a hint (`… · 1 queued`) instead of hiding it or hijacking the label: one priority function owns the pill (search phase > engine state > queue count > idle), so the 1 s metrics poll and the 250 ms search timer can no longer overwrite each other.

### Query optimizer
Conversational wording ("can you look up what the newest Qwen release from Alibaba is") makes weak search queries, so there is an **"Optimize search query"** toggle (on by default): one fast call to the user's own local model (temperature 0, reasoning off, max 100 tokens) extracts the core search question before the search runs.
- The query stays **in the language the user wrote in**: English stays English, German stays German etc. Obvious typos are fixed.
- If the call fails, is aborted, or returns something empty or rambling, the **raw message is searched instead** - the optimizer can never break a search.
- **Transparency**: whenever what was searched differs from what was typed, the sources line shows `Sources (DuckDuckGo) · searched: "…"`, and so does the Markdown export. An optimized query is never hidden behind a plain-looking result.

### Reading result pages in full
Snippets alone often miss the details, so search can also fetch the top result pages and inject their extracted text (Open WebUI's "Web Loader" idea, stdlib `html.parser` based, which skips nav/footer/scripts, prefers `main`/`article`):
- **"Read result pages"** toggle + **"Pages to read"** (1-5).
- **"Limit page text"** toggle (on by default) with a **"Max characters per page"** field (default 5000). Turning it off sends whole pages; see the budget below for why that is still safe.

### Page reader: direct fetch, or Jina Reader for JS-heavy pages
Plain `urllib` cannot render JavaScript-heavy pages, so there is a 3-tier **Page reader** setting:
- **Direct only (default)**: only the Strata server fetches pages; nothing goes to any third party.
- **Jina as fallback**: direct first; pages that fail (JS walls, blocks) are retried through [r.jina.ai](https://r.jina.ai) (free hosted headless browser, no key needed, Apache-2.0).
- **Jina for all pages**: every page goes through r.jina.ai.
- The base URL is overridable via `STRATA_JINA_URL` (e.g. a self-hosted instance), and failures of either path degrade to a readable combined reason.
- **Privacy is surfaced, not buried**: the dropdown explains per selection, a warning line appears whenever a third party could see the URLs, and turning search on fires a toast that names the engine *and* the reader mode ("… go through r.jina.ai - a third party sees those URLs").

### Context-aware reading budget
How much search text goes into the prompt scales with the model's own context window (`reported_ctx()`), so small-context instances are never overloaded:
- The reading budget is a slice of the window (~3 chars/token): **10 %** normally, **25 %** when the user explicitly turns the per-page limit off; the per-page cap is then derived from the budget instead of a fixed number.
- First-use defaults scale the same way from `/health`'s `max_context` (e.g. 16K ctx → 4 results / 1 page × 3000 chars; 128K → 6 / 2 × 5000; 262K → 8 / 3 × 5000).
- Unknown context falls back to the plain 5000/page default.

### Distinct, persistent search warnings
A failed search no longer fails silently: the reason stays on the message (in the sources line, warning-colored) and in the Markdown export, with a different message per cause:
- **no API key set** → `Brave Search needs its API key (Chat Settings > Web search)` (same for Tavily/Serper; a *rejected* key gets its own message, incl. Brave's 422)
- **engine unreachable** (e.g. SearXNG not running) → `SearXNG at http://127.0.0.1:8888 is not reachable (…); start it or pick another engine`
- **DuckDuckGo bot check** → DDG's lite endpoint answers Chrome-impersonating UAs with its `anomaly.js` page; the fetcher uses an honest custom UA and, if the bot page still shows up, says so instead of reporting "no results"
- **engine reachable but nothing found** → `no results`
- **unreadable page** → per-result `read_error` (shown as a warning line), never a silent empty string

### Security hardening
- **`/search` sits behind the web app's own-page guard** (`_own_page`): a JSON body is required (415 for form posts) and a foreign `Origin` is rejected (403; `trusted_origins` still allowed), so a random web page cannot make this PC run searches or fetch URLs through it.
- **http(s) only**: the SearXNG base URL and every result URL that gets page-read pass a scheme check (`_http_url`); `file://`, `data:`, `javascript:` and friends are refused with an explicit reason, so page reading can never become a local file reader.
- **Source links render defensively**: only `http(s)` URLs become clickable `<a href>`; anything else shows as plain text, so no `javascript:`/`data:` links from a poisoned result.
- **Prompt-injection hardening**: the injected search context states that titles, snippets and page text are untrusted web data whose embedded instructions must not be followed.
- **LAN-bound warning**: `/health` reports `lan_bound` (server bound beyond loopback, e.g. `0.0.0.0`); turning search on fires an extra toast line warning that queries and engine keys then cross the network in plain HTTP and that devices on it can use the search without an api_key. On the default `127.0.0.1` bind this warning never appears.
- API keys stay browser-only (localStorage); nothing search-related is stored server-side.

### Settings drawer updates
- The drawer was titled **"Sampling"**; since it now also holds web search settings it is renamed to **"Chat Settings"** (gear tooltip: "Chat Settings: Thinking & Web Search"), the close button got a proper "Close" tooltip, and the save toast says "Settings saved".
- The **Reset** button turns web search completely off and restores the first-use defaults: search disabled, engine back to DuckDuckGo, no API key, instead of leaving a stale engine or an active search behind.
- The empty-state privacy note is qualified and split into two fixed lines: "Nothing leaves it. / Web search is off by default - when on, only the search query goes out."
- Reset and Apply now sit fixed under the "Chat Settings" title while the options scroll below; the sampling options are grouped under a restored "Sampling" heading.

### Scroll fix (drive-by)
Auto-follow-to-bottom was broken for turns where content grows past the stick threshold mid-stream (the thinking panel expanding could pin the view at the user's own message). Stickiness is now captured *before* the content grows, so the view keeps following the answer.

### Engines
| engine | needs |
|---|---|
| DuckDuckGo (default, labeled "anonymous - no key needed") | nothing (lite endpoint) |
| SearXNG | a running instance (default `http://127.0.0.1:8888`) |
| Brave Search | API key |
| Tavily | API key |
| Serper (Google) | API key |

### Design notes
- `serve/websearch.py` is **stdlib-only** (`urllib`, `json`, `re`, `html.parser`, `os`); no new dependencies, cross-platform (Windows/Linux/macOS).
- `POST /search` carries its own engine config per request; nothing is stored on the server.
- Page fetches are capped (10 s timeout, 2 MB download); read results use an explicit contract (`content` on success, `read_error` on failure, `read_via` for Jina-read pages) instead of heuristics.
- `/search` has a catch-all so an unexpected error returns a clean 502 with a server-side log line instead of a broken connection.

## Validation

Re-validated today (20.10.) on the rebased branch `web-search` @ `e447e11f`, which contains upstream `main` including `894d1be1` (0.2.1) and `8aaf188a` (user-args/VRAM fix). Environment: Windows 11, RTX 4080 SUPER 16 GB, Ryzen 9 7950X3D, engine 0.1.45 (`MIN_ENGINE` (0,1,45) met), model qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs, 128K ctx.

**Passed:**
- `python -m unittest serve.test_websearch -v` (the suite now committed in this branch): **14 tests, all green** (scheme guard rejects 15 poison URL types `file:// gopher:// javascript: data: ftp:// dict:// ldap:// sftp:// ssh:// mailto: telnet: jar: chrome-extension: vbscript:` and accepts http(s); reader tier matrix direct/fallback/always incl. Jina rescue on a failing direct fetch and the combined both-paths-fail reason; bad reader values degrade to direct; non-HTML content refused; reading-budget clamps at 10 %/25 % of context with per-page caps derived at 4K/16K/128K; `max_results` clamp).
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py serve/websearch.py serve/runconfig.py tools/strata_bench.py` on the merged revision: clean.
- Live serve run on the merged revision: engine starts with the config's user args passed through exactly (`--vram-reserve-mib 700`, `--pcie-frac 0.20`, `--pool-workers 10`; no override), and 3 benchmark arms measured agent decode 104.9 / 110.7 / 110.8 tok/s, chat decode median 94.1 vs 94.6 basel

pulls.title: Q36: release the GGUF mapping and stop zeroing the overwritten arena
pulls.author: ggeorgovassilis
pulls.body:
## Summary
Implements the Q36 memory-compaction plan (`docs/Q36_MEMORY_COMPACTION.md`): the engine reports its own memory/compaction counters, releases the GGUF mapping after load, and stops zeroing the 18.75 GiB expert arena it immediately overwrites. The original goal - quiet the `kcompactd` churn - was already met by host settings; the measured engine win is ~18.5 GiB of RAM returned to the OS at no decode cost.

## What changed
- `include/strata/platform/mem_report.{hpp,cpp}` (new) + `src/platform/mem_report_test.cpp`: read `/proc/meminfo`, `/proc/vmstat` and the THP mode into the engine's own log, behind `STRATA_MEM_REPORT` (off by default). A row the kernel does not export prints `-`, not 0.
- `include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp`: `GgufFile::release_pages()`/`released()` and `GgufModel::release_pages()`/`released()` — `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` then `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` (fadvise cannot drop pages that are still mapped).
- `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`: `release_model_mapping()` after `place_experts()`, on by default; `STRATA_Q36_RELEASE_MAPPING=0` reverts. A guard makes `expert_blob()` fail loudly if it is ever called after the release. The arena memset now zeroes only the stride padding and the `kMmqTail` tail (plus an NVFP4 scale tail) instead of the whole 18.75 GiB.
- `tests/core/expert_blob_padding_test.cpp` (new): the padding-only zeroing is byte-identical to the whole memset.

## Extra Notes
Measured on an RTX 4060 Max-Q 8 GiB, Ryzen 7 7735HS, 62 GB, 32K, `--kv int8 --mtp 2`:

| | Cached | MemFree | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 47.27 GiB | 3.47 GiB | ~10 |
| after | 28.75 GiB | 22.03 GiB | ~10 |

`Mlocked` stayed 104 KiB throughout - `cudaHostAlloc` on this driver (580.178.04) is memfd/shm-backed, not mlocked, so the plan's "un-pin the arena" phase and its dependent were dropped.

Built: CPU suite 44/44, CUDA build, and the native-expert parity suite on the card (14/14). HIP and SYCL builds were not run here (no ROCm/SYCL on this box).

pulls.title: [Engine] Opt-in single-engine preemption for short requests
pulls.author: Zcg2021
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On unmodified 0.2.0-beta, an interactive request on a single native engine waits for a long response to finish. This was reproduced in all three native CUDA trials: short TTFT 20.784 / 20.542 / 21.129 s when submitted 7 s into the long request.

This opt-in Python scheduler allows cooperative yielding and continuation through the existing STOP/DONE protocol and RAM conversation cache. In three matching flag-off/on pairs, median short TTFT fell from 20.523 to 0.610 s; aggregate output throughput changed from 111.29 to 107.88 tok/s (-3.1%). All nine fact audits and short exact-JSON responses passed. These are small same-machine samples, not a universal performance claim.

## Related discussion

#2821; batch admission priority in #2109 is related but does not interrupt an already-running single-engine response. This updates the original PR after the tracker reset, rather than opening a competing submission. Maintainer agreement on feature scope is still requested in #2821. Keeping this PR **draft** pending that discussion and targeted validation on other backends.

## Approach

The option defaults off. One native GEN runs at a time. STOP is drained through DONE, including trailing accepted tokens, before ownership changes. Continuation uses original token IDs; the original stream parser and tool-call identity stay alive. Minimum run time and queue aging keep long requests moving. Parked cancellation does not stop another owner; engine death explicitly fails affected streams.

The policy is isolated in `serve/solo_priority.py`; no native code, model, tokenizer or cache-format change. The beta port preserves queue timeouts and cancellation accounting and reports admitted solo requests in terminal telemetry. Default-off runtime behavior was compared with an unmodified server; throughput was close, but token-identical native generated code across separate runs is not claimed.

## Validation

Tested server code: `4e510b36845019042e48e715f82b829485c9c69e`, based on upstream main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`. Relevant upstream server/native/tokenizer trees match `v0.2.0-beta`. Windows 11 build 26100, Python 3.13.1, RTX 3090 24 GiB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 128 GiB RAM. Original non-abliterated Qwen3.8 Flash Next ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, 256K context, 32 GiB conversation cache / 8 slots, spec 4, int8 KV. Official beta CUDA13 engine asset version 0.1.45.3 (binary prints 0.1.45); asset digest and exact settings are in the report. No SC117 results are pooled into this revalidation.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'`: Windows **897 tests, OK, 20 skipped**, 474.820 s.
- `python tools/bench_solo_priority.py --base http://127.0.0.1:18082 --fixture fixtures/fixture-128000-803.json --rounds 3 --out <arm>.json`: separate unmodified, patch-off and patch-on servers, same native binary/settings; 9 correct pairs. Type-aware post-check also verified all 20 audit fields in each pair.
- `python tools/check_solo_priority_lifecycle.py --base http://127.0.0.1:18082 --out lifecycle`: queued/active/parked cancellation, surviving 450-item tool arguments, interrupted Responses tool call and correct tool-result acknowledgement. 9 successful responses plus 3 intentional cancellations; no unexpected errors.

- `python tools/soak_solo_priority.py --base http://127.0.0.1:18082 --fixtures fixtures/fixture-64000-117.json fixtures/fixture-96000-291.json fixtures/fixture-128000-803.json --seconds 3600 --out soak`: 424 requests, 410 completions and 14 intentional cancellations; 100 tool round trips and 30 exact audits; zero validation failures or unexpected transport errors. 290 preemptions, zero paused-prefix misses. Short TTFT p50/p95/max 0.923/6.545/46.663 s. The one-hour load plus drain/final audits took 3707.709 s.

- Post-soak lifecycle repetition plus targeted native process termination: queued/active/parked cancellation and the 450-item Responses round trip passed again. The active and parked streams explicitly failed within 1.355 s after the isolated engine was killed; a fresh request automatically reloaded it and returned correct JSON in 24.690 s. Raw results retain the two expected fault-injection errors.

**Failed:**

- Initial port preflight: 9 of 20 focused checks failed due to a missed single-engine lock-acquisition branch during merge resolution. Fixed before the tested revision; the corrected 20 checks and 15 beta lifecycle checks passed. Both failed and corrected logs are retained.

- Mac full suite on preceding code commit `482a0c86`: 896 tests, 3 failures, 1 error, 15 skipped. The exact four failing tests reproduced on unmodified upstream: three `test_lifeline.Lifeline` child-watcher cases and `test_server.VisionArgs.test_min_tokens_is_passed_only_when_set` (mock process has no `pid`). Raw output and upstream controls are retained. The subsequent code change only fixes opt-in terminal state and adds its test; Windows full-suite validation includes it.

**Not run:**

- Native HIP, SYCL or Metal execution/build; no native source was changed or compiled. Windows used the official CUDA release binary. Those hardware combinations remain unverified for this feature.
- Overnight soak, broad model/quantization coverage, vision preemption, or an open-ended coding-quality benchmark. Synthetic tool calls and generated code were not executed.

## Limits

Cold/partial-cache-hit prefill and cache restoration can still delay a short request. The soak observed a 46.663 s short TTFT while another request read 116036 new tokens after restoring a 16384-token prefix. The scheduler deliberately lets restored partial prefill reach its first generated token before yielding. Zero `resume_prefix_missed` is about paused continuations; it does not mean every new request gets a full cache hit. This is not a real-time latency guarantee. Image-bearing requests and checkpoint opt-outs remain non-preemptible; batch/replica execution cannot be combined with the option.

## Reproducible report

[Full beta revalidation report, settings and raw results](https://github.com/Zcg2021/Strata/blob/4312dd7aa7cc87b6a84e2b3a7363dbdff9afc372/bench/results/2026-10-19-solo-priority-v020-beta/README.md).

pulls.title: metal: --rope-scaling, --rope-scale, --rope-freq-base, --rope-freq-scale and --yarn-* reach the decode window's RoPE table
pulls.author: oinani0721
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2767. No other issue or pull request covers RoPE scaling on the Mac engine (search in the first comment).

Every file:line is at 296b59d (v0.1.44.1, the last release) unless marked "branch". Short names are the files under src/, include/ or metal/, not their copies under sycl/; CMakeLists.txt is the root one. On the branch, window.cpp's lines 18-467 move 1 down and its lines after 475 move 4 up, setup_host.cpp's lines after 125 move 6 down, and metal/CMakeLists.txt's lines 106-123 move 9 down and its lines after 123 move 16 down.

## Summary
On a Mac, `--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4` is parsed, resolved and logged as active (`strata generate: rope scaling yarn, factor 4 ...`, generate.cpp:3002-3008), but, by the code, no rotation changes:
- `rope_table_set` does nothing on Metal (metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp:151, "the window keeps its own table");
- every RoPE rotation on Metal is in `qsa_prep`, which reads only the decode window's own cos/sin table (qsa.metal:74);
- `Window::init` builds that table without scaling, from the model file's `rope.freq_base` (window.cpp:468-475).

This PR makes the window build the table with `build_rope_table(64, rope_scaling(), ...)`, the builder the PC's session table uses (layer.cpp:837-840). setup_host.cpp:116-150 keeps rope.cu:48-86: the same 417 tokens once comments, whitespace and braces are ignored. By the code, linear and YaRN scaling, the magnitude factor (YaRN's mscale, or `--yarn-attn-factor`), `--rope-freq-base` and `--rope-freq-scale` then reach every rotation on a Mac without a kernel change (the reading is in the first comment). On an M5 Max (On-model results), yarn x4 changes the decode windows' logits on this branch and changes nothing on main (#2767); for each prompt path (the resident prompt chain, the streaming prompt GEMM) the test compares how close the path stays under yarn x4 to the same prompts read through decode windows, against a threshold derived in the same sitting, and for both paths that threshold did not separate the measured numbers, so they stay a code reading, as the MTP draft layer does.

This is one engine part needed to run past the trained 262,144 tokens on a Mac, not all of them: Mac setup does not write the flags, and nothing checks the memory a long context takes on a resident pack.

## What changed
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`: the table loop in `Window::init` becomes one `window_rope_table(strata::kernels::rope_scaling(), MAXC + 16, cs_.as<float>())` call. The table keeps its size (MAXC + 16 rows) and layout (float2 [pos][32]).
- `metal/src/engine/rope_window.h` (new): `window_rope_table` builds the table with `build_rope_table` into two temporary vectors of (MAXC + 16) x 32 floats each (branch rope_window.h:21), freed when it returns, and interleaves them into the window's rows; nothing it allocates stays. The window and the test run this same code.
- `metal/src/engine/setup_host.cpp`: a declaration of the scaled `build_rope_table` with `__attribute__((flatten))` (branch :126-131), so `RopeScaling::mscale()` is inlined into it under the flag below; the function's body does not change. The file's opening comment now says that `rope_scaling()` and `build_rope_table` fill the window's table.
- `metal/CMakeLists.txt`: `set_source_files_properties(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/engine/setup_host.cpp PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-ffp-contract=off")`, the form CMakeLists.txt:450-453 uses for two HIP files, with a comment that gives the by-hand check for the flatten (below); and the `rope_table_parity` target with `add_test`. The test has its own folder because `tests/*.cpp` are globbed into mtl_rt-only programs (metal/CMakeLists.txt:41-47). Setup builds only `strata` (setup_mac.py:280).
- `metal/tests/engine/rope_table_parity.cpp` (new; CPU only, no GPU or model; 5.7 s and 0.54 GB in ctest on the M5 Max). At the allocation of the 1M probe (bench/results/2026-10-09-rope-yarn-long-context/probe.py, whose default capacity is `--max-context 1048832`, probe.py:32), 1,048,976 rows, it checks:
  1. unscaled: the new table against the replaced loop, byte for byte at every row; and with `--rope-freq-base 5e6`, against that loop given the same base (a copy of the test whose table ignores the base fails here);
  2. yarn x2, x3 and x4, linear x4, yarn x4 with `--yarn-attn-factor 0.9`, linear x4 with `--yarn-attn-factor 1.25` and yarn with `--rope-freq-scale 0.3`: bit for bit against a float64 transcription of ggml's `rope_yarn` (llama.cpp 3cf03257, ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:5958-5973) with every operation rounded on its own. As in src/kernels/rope_parity.cpp:233-236, the correction dims and the ramp come from the shared helpers; an oracle written from ggml's own formulas checks those too (first comment, with its code);
  3. row 0 is (mscale, 0); under YaRN the correction window is pairs [14, 22], and at the last row the first pair extrapolates and the last pair interpolates.

What it leaves alone:
- **The Metal kernels.** No `.metal` file is touched, the spare indexer key included (Extra Notes).
- **Mac setup.** On a Mac, setup.py hands every argument to `metal/setup_mac.py` before its own parser runs (setup.py:5706-5707, 5446), so the `--rope-scaling` and `--rope-scale` it defines (setup.py:5715-5719) never reach that parser; setup_mac.py still drops them with "not used on a Mac" (setup_mac.py:508-510) and writes no rope flags. Setup support is a later PR, which has to count a long context's memory first.
- **Every file outside `metal/`.** The root CMakeLists.txt and sycl/CMakeLists.txt do not reference `metal/`, so no CUDA, HIP or SYCL build compiles a changed file. They were not built.
- **docs/MAC.md.** "Context: measured up to 32K" (MAC.md:176) changes only with measured results.

### How the default path was checked
All on an M5 Max (128 GB), AppleClang 21.0.0, against the Metal build of 296b59d; the commands and their output lines are in the first comment.
1. **The table.** Test check 1: byte-identical at all 1,048,976 rows; a row depends only on its position, so every smaller context's table is a prefix. On the default path `rope_scaling()` is `RopeScaling{}` with `freq_base` from the model file's `qwen4exp.rope.freq_base` (generate.cpp:2940, 2969, 2978-2990), the key the window read before.
2. **The model files.** The GGUF headers (metadata only) of the six models Mac setup offers (setup_mac.py:45-55) and of the abliterated IQ3_S the on-model tests use all carry `qwen4exp.rope.freq_base = 10000000.0` and no `rope.scaling.*` key.
3. **The object code.** Of the 70 objects both builds have, `otool -X -s __TEXT __text <object> | shasum` differs only for `setup_host.cpp.o` (97573d5fa328b5c1 -> fd4ef0c308696cb7) and `window.cpp.o` (afaf2e316677789d -> fc9d170bb55b5ea8). In setup_host.cpp.o 36 of 37 functions are identical; only `build_rope_table(int, const RopeScaling&, int, float*, float*)` changes. In window.cpp.o, with the checkout path normalized, only `Window::init` changes; `window_rope_table` is new and the `std::map` lookup the old loop made is gone.
4. **Build and tests.** ctest passes 2/2 (`runtime_hello`, `rope_table_parity`). `-Wall -Wextra` gives no warning on setup_host.cpp, the test or a file that includes only rope_window.h. `tools.test_setup_mac` and `tools.test_setup_rope` pass (38 tests); no setup file is changed.

### Why `-ffp-contract=off`, and why `flatten`
The project holds this table bit for bit to a float64 reference (rope_scaling.hpp:24-26, 122-123). Without the flag Apple clang 21 fuses YaRN's blend and mscale (4 fused multiply-adds), and at 1M 2 of the 67,134,464 floats of the yarn x2 table differ from the reference (sin at position 589,449 pair 19 and at 910,519 pair 17); at `--max-context` 262,144 and 524,544 none do, which is why ctest runs the 1M allocation. With the flag all seven scaled configurations match.

`generate.cpp.o` keeps an out-of-line `RopeScaling::mscale()` with a fused multiply-add. Compiled with `-fno-inline` as a stand-in for a compiler that stops inlining it, the builder without `flatten` calls `mscale()`, and a strata link binds that call to generate.cpp.o's copy; the flattened builder makes no such call. Today's build inlines it either way, and the flattened build gives the same eight tables (hashes in the first comment). ctest cannot see a lost `flatten`, since the test does not link generate.cpp.o; the CMake comment gives an `nm` check, for the default Release build. With only mscale fused, the 1M yarn table would change at 1 of the 252 factors from 1.25 to 64 in steps of 0.25 (36.25, in 1 float).

Inferred from the build files, not checked on a PC: rope.cu gets no `-march`, `-mfma` or `/arch:` (CMakeLists.txt:354, 1219-1225, 1326-1352), so a PC whose host compiler targets baseline x86-64 rounds it the same way. A host compiler that can fuse by default (an ARM64 Linux host, or `-march=native` in the flags) may not.

## On-model results
Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS 27.0.1), 2026-10-16; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_S (revision eec4e10a, hashes in the first comment), greedy, thinking off; main is 296b59d's Metal build. B0-B2 and B6 ran resident at `--max-context 65536`, except B2's two streaming runs; B3-B5 streamed with `--kv int8`. Desktop programs stayed open (30-42 GB in use beside the engine), so every streaming start ran with its cap lowered by `STRATA_METAL_LEAVE_SHARE` (recorded per run) and with the model's pages dropped from the file cache first; the first comment says why and has every table.
- **B1, the default path (no flag): main against this branch.** One-token decode windows, 86 requests: tokens, DONE fields and draft counts identical, 86 of 86 first-window logit files and 191 of 191 `STRATA_METAL_LOGPOS` rows byte-identical. Setup's default config, 6 requests (decided: the control, this branch run twice, was identical): tokens and DONE fields identical, 6 of 6 logit files byte-identical.
- **B2 on main (#2767):** yarn x4 (`--rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --yarn-orig-ctx 262144`) against no flag gives the same results in every comparison of B1, while the log says `rope scaling yarn, factor 4`.
- **B2 on this branch:** yarn x4 changes all 6 first-window rows of the default config and the logits at all 65 decode-window positions (mean KL 0.0152, top-1 agreement 0.923), and after all 20 prompts in the resident (mean KL 0.0276) and the streaming runs (0.0343). The prompt-path gate is undecided for both paths: the resident prompt chain n 0.0105, e 0.0318, d 0.0084, T 0.0183; the streaming prompt GEMM n 0.0070, e 0.0318, d 0.0101, T 0.0149. d is under T on the means, but T did not separate every prompt's n and e.
- **B6, needles at 8K, 16K and 32K:** 9 of 9 on main, on this branch without a flag (twice: the control was identical) and with yarn x4; main against this branch identical.
- **B3 and B3M, memory (streaming):** the engine holds 18.00, 25.62 and 41.08 GB before its arena at 262,144, 524,544 and 1,048,832 cells, with prompt buffers of 5.19, 6.26 and 8.41 GB; the least a 1M start can hold, computed with the smallest arena the harness accepts, is 58.5 GB, 24.0 GB under the engine's cap of 82.5 GB. `--kv int8` against fp16 at 32K: identical tokens and byte-identical logits, as #2707 reads the code (`qsa_prep` stores K and V as int8 whatever `--kv` says).
- **B4, 512K** (probe.py's three-code prompt, 524,288 tokens, the PC run's input by SHA-256): without scaling 3 of 3, prefill 752 tok/s (697 s), decode 22.1 tok/s; yarn x2 3 of 3, 657 tok/s (799 s), 21.6 tok/s. The cap was lowered to 55.9 GB (a 29.7 GB arena), so prompts read experts again more often than with the engine's own arena.
- **B5, 1M** (probe.py's three-code prompt, 1,048,576 tokens, the PC run's input by SHA-256; `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S=300`, the harness's setting when the arena is smaller than B4's): without scaling 1 of 3 (`CEDAR-482|MARBLE-956|QUARTZ-956`), prefill 589 tok/s (1,781 s), decode 20.0 tok/s; yarn x4 3 of 3, 580 tok/s (1,807 s),

pulls.title: bench: community report — 2x RTX 3060 12 GB, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, 131K context, agent-calibrated (engine 0.1.44.1)
pulls.author: fenix79
pulls.body:
Community speed report from a dedicated 2x RTX 3060 machine: the UD-IQ4_XS pack at the full 131,072-token window, the engine at a `--layer-split auto` split across both cards, with the expert pool tiered in 94 GiB of system RAM.

Adds `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-2x-rtx-3060-ud-iq4-xs-0.1.44.1/` (`README.md` + `results.json`), produced by `tools/strata_bench.py` suite 1 against the running server.

## Machine

- MEG Z490 ACE, i7-11700 (8C/16T), 94.2 GiB RAM; Linux, driver 595.99.02, CUDA 13.2
- 2x RTX 3060 12 GB, both CPU-direct at Gen4 x8 (the CPU's 20 lanes split x8/x8, the NVMe takes the last x4); power limit 170 W per card — decode plateaus near 90 W, only prefill bursts reach the limit
- Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2, release build); `layer split auto`: layers 0-21 on GPU 0, layers 22-47 plus a 2939-slot (6.62 GiB) expert cache on GPU 1

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| short chat decode | 45.2 tok/s (TTFT 0.62 s) |

pulls.title: sycl: setup --vision cpu reads images on the Intel port (the CPU encoder, as on AMD)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Title
sycl: setup --vision cpu reads images on the Intel port (the CPU encoder, as on AMD)

Issue: Resolves #2816

## Summary

Images on the Intel (SYCL) port, the way the AMD (HIP) path has them since #304: the image encoder built for the
CPU by setup, the engine started with `--vision`. docs/INTEL.md's comparison table said "not yet" for images on
the SYCL port, but the engine side has been there since the port (`--vision`, the GENI request with the encoder's
embeddings, the per-cell M-RoPE position table in `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`); what was missing was the setup
wiring. `sycl/setup_intel.py` forced `--vision none`, mapped every `--vision` to "none" and dropped the config's
`"vision"` section. The encoder itself (`tools/vision`, llama.cpp's mtmd + the mmproj file) needs no SYCL: the
CPU build the AMD path uses runs on the PC, outside the container, and `serve/server.py` hands the engine the
embeddings.

With this change `./setup.sh --backend sycl --vision cpu` compiles the encoder for the CPU into `engine-sycl/`
(setup's own `build_vision_cpu`: `tools/vision` against the pinned llama.cpp, `-DSTRATA_VISION_CUDA=OFF
-DSTRATA_PORTABLE=OFF`, once, again when `tools/vision` changes), downloads the mmproj file as setup does, keeps
the config's `"vision"` section (`exe`, `mmproj`, `model`, `threads`: host paths, since the encoder runs on the
host) and `--vision`, and applies the port's own VRAM reserve rule (1,024 MiB up to 32K, ...) instead of the
700 MiB setup writes for the CUDA engine's GPU encoder: the CPU encoder takes no VRAM. A `--vram-reserve-mib`
the user gives is kept. `--vision yes` / `gpu` leave images off with a note saying to use `--vision cpu`, as
`hip_vision` does on AMD (there is no SYCL encoder build). Without `--vision cpu` nothing changes: the
throw-away engine folder and the config are as before.

Measured, 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, oneAPI 2026.1, AOT bmg-g31),
AMD Threadripper 1950X, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp
<BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4`, the encoder from `tools/vision` built with gcc 13 (native,
`-DSTRATA_PORTABLE=OFF`), `mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf`, 8 threads:

- the encoder alone: a 256x256 PNG -> 64 image tokens (an 8x8 grid, 2,560 values each), 1,191 ms on 8 CPU
  threads, no VRAM.
- a 448x448 image of four coloured quadrants, "name the colour of each quadrant", through
  `/v1/chat/completions` on a development tree with the same `serve/` and vision path as `main`: all four
  named correctly ("Top-left: red, top-right: green, bottom-left: blue, bottom-right: yellow"; 280 prompt
  tokens, 4.8 s to the first token including the encode), also while a code request ran on the other slot; a
  512-token text reply decoded at 140.9 and 140.5 tok/s with `--vision` (about the 141 measured without it) on that tree.
- on `main` 296b59d2 (upstream's own engine build, this branch's config: the vision section and `--vision`):
  the four colours right ("Red, Green, Blue, Yellow" to "in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-left,
  bottom-right"), 246 prompt tokens with the picture read in 1.48 s including the encode; a 512-token greedy
  text reply at 81.7 / 79.4 tok/s with `--vision` against 81.8 / 79.4 without (an earlier run of the same binary
  and config), with identical text and draft counts: `--vision` changes nothing for text.
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_sycl`: 24 tests pass (6 new). Every `tools/test_setup_*.py` module run
  with and without this change gives the same result (the same 10 pre-existing failures on `main`: the
  `test_setup_golden` UD-Q4_K_XL cases and two `test_setup_engine_hash` cases; none in the SYCL, AMD, config or
  bench-tip modules).

## What changed

- `sycl/setup_intel.py`:
  - `sycl_vision(asked)` replaces `S.hip_vision` (was `lambda asked: "none"`): `cpu` -> `cpu`; `yes` / `gpu` ->
    `none` with a warning that says `--vision cpu`; anything else `none`.
  - `build_engine_sycl(gpu, llama, vision)` replaces `S.build_engine_hip` (was the stub): with `vision == "none"`
    it returns the same throw-away stub as before (`engine_stub()`, the code moved out of `install()`); with
    `cpu` it stops with the package to install when the PC has no C++ compiler, and otherwise calls setup's
    `build_vision_cpu(eng, stamp, meta, llama, vsrc)` with `eng = engine-sycl/` (new folder next to the
    checkout's `engine/`, which the SYCL setup never used): that compiles `tools/vision` into `build-vision/`,
    copies `strata-vision` beside the stamp and records `vision: cpu` and the `tools/vision` source hash in
    `engine-sycl/BUILD.json`, so a rerun compiles nothing. `build_vision_cpu` is added to the names
    `install()` checks setup.py still has.
  - `to_sycl`: the `"vision"` key is no longer dropped from the config; `--vision` was already passed through.
    The reserve: when `--vision` is in the args and the reserve is setup's vision default (`VISION["cpu"]
    ["reserve_mib"]`, 700) it is treated as not given, which is what setup's own `choices_from_config` does
    with that value (#493), so the port's rule applies.
  - `say_intel` rewrites `build_vision_cpu`'s "engine: engine-sycl/strata, image encoder (CPU): ..." line to
    "image encoder (CPU): ..." (there is no engine in that folder).
  - `install()` still appends `--vision none` when `--vision` is not given: images stay opt-in.
- `tools/test_setup_sycl.py`: `ToSycl.test_the_vision_section_is_kept_and_the_cpu_encoder_takes_no_reserve`
  and a new `Images` class (the vision choice; no images -> the stub and no `cmake_build` call; `cpu` -> one
  `cmake_build` of `tools/vision` with the AMD path's definitions, the copied encoder, the stamp, no second
  build on a rerun, a build again when `tools/vision` changes; no compiler -> a stop naming `build-essential`;
  the source still forces `--vision none` when not asked). No GPU, no network, no compiler: `cmake_build` is
  replaced.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the comparison table's images row, an "Images" bullet in the setup section, the "Images: the
  encoder on the CPU" section with the measurements above, and the "Not done" entry narrowed to the llama.cpp
  configuration.

Not changed: `setup.py` (`git diff main -- setup.py` is empty; the CUDA and HIP paths run the same code), the
engine (`sycl/src`, `src`, `include`: no compiled file is touched, the binary is `main`'s), `serve/`,
`sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`, `tools/vision`. A SYCL build of the encoder (GPU encode) is not part of this: the CPU
encoder is what runs on AMD too.

## Extra Notes

- The encoder runs on the host, not in the `strata-sycl-dev` container, so the PC needs a C++ compiler
  (`build-essential`); setup's pip-installed cmake and ninja do the rest. A PC without one gets a message with
  the package and the `--vision no` way out. The measured encoder above was built with the dev image's gcc 13
  and run inside the same image (our serving setup keeps the server in the container); the setup path builds it
  with the host's compiler - the same CMake definitions.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

pulls.title: strata-q36 on Volta: K-quant prompt experts on a register-fragment tensor-core kernel - prompt +22-25% on a V100, same tokens
pulls.author: merbanan
pulls.body:
On a Volta GPU, strata-q36's prompt-path MoE experts in Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K now use a new FP16 tensor-core kernel (`moe_tc_kq`) instead of MMQ's dp4a path. This covers the gate/up and down products of a prompt chunk.

**How it works**
- A block handles 64 routed rows against 128 weight rows, with 8 warps.
- In each warp, the four `mma.m8n8k4` quad pairs each take a 32-value chunk of a 128-value k step.
- Each lane decodes its row's 32 values straight into A fragments in registers, with the same arithmetic as ggml's `dequantize_row_q*_K`. Weights are never staged in shared memory.
- The q8_1 activations MMQ already produces (DS4 for Q4_K/Q5_K, D4 for Q6_K) are staged as FP16 in shared memory, double-buffered, with the next step's loads in flight under the current step's products.
- The four chunks' partial sums are added with shuffles. Accumulation is FP32.

**Scope**
- Used only when the device is sm_70. Turing and newer already run MMQ on int8 tensor cores.
- `STRATA_PREFILL_TCKQ=0` keeps MMQ.
- The source is compiled only when `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` includes 70 (or `native`/`all`). It is about 140 KB of device code, so default builds (`120`) are unchanged. Outside that build the header's inline no-ops leave the call site free of `#ifdef`s.

**Measured** on one Tesla V100 PCIe 32 GB with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-Q4_K_M. The build is this branch on main 296b59d2 with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70 -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`. Each run is `strata-q36 --bench-pp` (`--max-context 131072`), plus a 16K-token greedy generation compared by md5. Two cooled rounds, alternating the two settings:

| | `STRATA_PREFILL_TCKQ=0` (MMQ) | default (this kernel) |
|---|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 1,685.9 / 1,684.4 | **2,109.0 / 2,109.3** (+25%) |
| pp16384 | 1,518.8 / 1,518.3 | **1,854.6 / 1,854.2** (+22%) |
| MTP2 pp512 | 1,640.5 / 1,640.6 | 2,057.1 / 2,056.4 |
| tg256 | 100.6 / 100.3 | 99.7 / 100.8 |
| 16K greedy, tokens md5 | 75a302c75b7c | 75a302c75b7c (identical) |

The products use FP16 operands with FP32 sums, so they are not bit-identical to MMQ. The 16K greedy tokens came out identical in all four runs. The same kernel design in a Maya-based engine also matched llama.cpp's greedy output for 128 of 128 tokens on this model.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: STRATA_GR_FUSED=1, the two-kernel BF16 hyper-connection read (opt-in)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The SYCL port's default hyper-connection read issues four launches per layer half (norm, sliced down projection, reduce, up projection), each small and latency-bound on an Arc Pro B70. `STRATA_GR_FUSED=1` does the norm, the down projection and its partial reduction in one kernel and the up projection in a second. Same BF16 weights, no extra VRAM, the default read's per-element arithmetic, another summation order. With the flag unset the default read runs unchanged. With `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` set the Q8_0 read runs and this flag changes nothing; this read is for setups that keep BF16 (exact weights wanted, or no VRAM for the Q8_0 copies).

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, one stream: verify window 39.4 / 40.2 -> 37.9 / 38.2 ms (-4%), decode 70.6 / 73.7 -> 81.4 / 81.2 tok/s (most of the tok/s spread is a different draft acceptance of the changed output; the window time is the read's effect). Prompt reading unchanged.

## Related discussion

Feature issue #2811 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). No maintainer agreement on scope yet. **Stacked on #2810** (`STRATA_HC_Q8=1`): this branch is that one plus one commit and reuses its argument struct, scratch and helpers, so #2810 goes first. The diff of this PR alone is the top commit.

## Approach

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`, `namespace gr_fused`: `gr_fused_down_kernel` (a work-group = 32 rows, 2 per lane, x a 1,280-column slab; stages `R' * w_norm` with the slab's sums of squares; the 16 sub-group partials added in a fixed order; the last work-group of a row group to arrive applies rs per stream and resets the counter) and `gr_fused_up_kernel` (16 columns x 4 streams per work-group, K in 4 quarters summed in a fixed order, then the default read's epilogue: pending write, gate, stream mean). The hook in `fused_gr_read_multi`, right after the Q8_0 one. Arguments not at the callers' fixed strides fall back to the default read with one stderr line. `fused_gr_set_fused(int)` for the parity test.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/fused_gr_fused.hpp` (new), `sycl/src/kernels/gr_fused_parity.cpp` (new, in the `--selftest` loop), `docs/INTEL.md`.

Not changed: `src/`, `include/`, the default SYCL read, the Q8_0 read of #2810 (a sibling namespace and one hook line after its hook). `STRATA_GR_*` follows the port's prefix for its read switches.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4 at run time; built with the repository dev image (`sycl/tools/Dockerfile` on the current `llama-sycl-b70:stable`, IGC 2.41.5; an older cached base with IGC 2.36.3 cannot build 0.2.0, see #3219), AOT `bmg-g31`. Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts --expert-cache auto`, one slot, greedy, two fixed coding prompts with 512-token replies, a fresh engine per arm, then fresh 4K and 32K prompts. Coherence check and per-card health after every stop.

**Passed:**

- `gr_fused_parity --selftest` (0.2.0-beta + #2810 + this commit, head a703ff1e, one B70): `gr_fused_parity: pass (0 failing of 33 cases)` (T = 1..8 x pending write on/off x inject rows on/off; both reads against FP64 and each other within 1e-4, R_out bitwise, a captured graph replayed twice bitwise the direct call, the fixed-stride fallback bitwise the default read).
- Engine A/B (decode tok/s, tokens per window, ms per window):

| | prompt 1 | prompt 2 | 4K / 32K read tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main e88ee39d | 70.6, 2.78, 39.4 ms | 73.9, 2.96, 40.0 ms | 1,219 / 2,078 |
| this branch, flag unset | 70.6, 2.78, 39.4 ms | 73.7, 2.96, 40.2 ms | 1,220 / 2,080 |
| `STRATA_GR_FUSED=1` | 81.4, 3.08, 37.9 ms | 81.2, 3.10, 38.2 ms | 1,229 / 2,102 |

- Flag unset: output SHAs and draft counts identical to main. Flag set: coherent, text differs after a near-tie (another summation order). Coherence true and per-card health passed after every stop.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** kernel-level timings on 0.2.0 (unchanged code; on 0.1.x: T = 1 / 4 / 6 reads 38.7 -> 34.8, 50.8 -> 41.5, 62.0 -> 47.1 us), the 40K-context turn, two streams (`--batch-mtp` refused on a layer split), CUDA/HIP (not touched), `ctest` as a whole.

## Limits

- Not bitwise the default read (lo / rs / mixed differ at FP32 rounding level, like the existing opt-in `STRATA_GR_V3`); greedy output changes after a near-tie.
- The `docs/INTEL.md` section quotes the 0.1.x measurement (main 296b59d2); I can swap in the 0.2.0 numbers.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: STRATA_HC_Q8=1 reads the Q8_0 hyper-connection projections (it loaded them and never read them)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On the SYCL (Intel) build `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` did nothing. The loader kept a Q8_0 copy of the hyper-connection projections only when the GGUF stored them as Q8_0 (the ISTA files store BF16, so nothing was copied), and the port's `fused_gr_read_multi` had no Q8_0 read: it ignored `q8_down` / `q8_up` and read the BF16 copies whatever the flag said (`fused_gr.dp.cpp`: "the Q8_0 reads (S23 STRATA_HC_Q8) are not built"). Still the case on 0.2.0-beta.

With this change the flag does on SYCL what it does on CUDA: the hyper-connection down / up projections (the layers' and the final mixer's) are read as Q8_0 in the verify window, from the GGUF's own Q8_0 blocks or from its BF16 values quantized at load. Flag unset: nothing changes.

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, one stream: verify window 39.4 / 40.0 -> 36.8 / 36.9 ms (-7%), decode 70.6 / 73.9 -> 82.4 / 87.8 tok/s (part of it a different draft acceptance of the changed output). Prompt reading unchanged. Costs 0.63 GiB of VRAM (below).

## Related discussion

Bug report #2809 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). #2812 (`STRATA_GR_FUSED=1`) is stacked on this branch.

## Approach

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: prompt attention over 8-query selection unions on XMX (opt-in STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On the SYCL port the QSA prompt attention runs the FP32 decode kernel, 32 positions per launch, and every position gathers its own ~2,051 selected K/V cells. The XMX port (`STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1`) is slower than that, and `docs/INTEL.md` lists a kernel over the union of neighbouring positions' selections as "not built".

This adds that kernel, opt-in (`STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1`). For every 8 neighbouring positions a first kernel builds the sorted union of their selected cells, each cell marked with the positions that chose it. The attention kernel dequantizes the INT8 K/V of 64-cell chunks of that union once to FP16 and runs S^T = K Q^T and O += P V on joint_matrix (8x16x16, FP32 sums) for all 96 rows (8 positions x 12 heads). A cell is -inf in the online softmax for the positions that did not select it, so every position attends to exactly the cells it attends to with the FP32 kernel.

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s: prompt reading 1,220 -> 1,414 tok/s at 4K (+16%) and 2,084 -> 2,387 tok/s at 32K (+15%). Decode is not touched (verify window 39.4 / 40.0 -> 39.4 / 39.2 ms). Unset, outputs and draft counts are identical to main.

## Related discussion

Feature issue #2807 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). No maintainer agreement on scope yet. Opt-in, INT8 KV on Battlemage only; any other KV format or card, or a failed scratch allocation, keeps the existing path (one stderr line says why).

## Approach

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn_union.dp.cpp` (new): the union kernel (one work-group per 8 positions, 16K-cell local bitmaps), the attention kernel (one work-group per 8 positions and KV head, 12 sub-groups of 16, 256 GRF), the launcher and its per-queue scratch.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_union.hpp` (new): the entry point (the contract of `qsa_prompt_attn_batch`) and the switch.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.dp.cpp`: the include and the guarded call before the XMX v2 call (4 lines).
- `sycl/src/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_union_parity.cpp` (new): the parity test (`--selftest` in ctest, skip code 77 off Battlemage).
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`, `docs/INTEL.md`.

Left alone: the selection (block scores, top-k), decode, the FP32 and XMX v2 prompt kernels, other KV formats, every file outside `sycl/` and `docs/`.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4 at run time; built with the repository dev image (`sycl/tools/Dockerfile` on the current `llama-sycl-b70:stable`, IGC 2.41.5; an older cached base with IGC 2.36.3 cannot build 0.2.0, see #3219), AOT `bmg-g31`. Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts --expert-cache auto`, one slot, greedy, two fixed coding prompts with 512-token replies, a fresh engine per arm, then fresh 4K and 32K prompts. Coherence check and per-card health after every stop.

**Passed:**

- `qsa_prompt_attn_union_parity --selftest` (0.2.0-beta + this branch, head 2c97fc0d, one B70): 5 of 5 PASS, `FAILURES: 0` (random INT8 pools behind a shuffled page table, 1.5K-40K contexts, ragged last groups, 2% non-resident pages, a bitwise rerun). Error against FP64 2.6e-3 - 5.0e-3 at an output scale of 3.3-3.6 (FP32 kernel 1.7e-6 - 2.6e-6); one chunk 0.88x (fresh selections, union 5.3x) to 5.45x (union 1.0x) of the FP32 kernel.
- Engine A/B (decode tok/s and verify window ms per prompt; fresh-prompt read tok/s):

| | prompt 1 | prompt 2 | 4K read | 32K read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main e88ee39d | 70.6 (39.4 ms) | 73.9 (40.0 ms) | 1,219 | 2,078 |
| this branch, switch unset | 70.6 (39.4 ms) | 73.9 (40.0 ms) | 1,220 | 2,084 |
| `STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_UNION=1` | 75.2 (39.4 ms) | 77.3 (39.2 ms) | 1,414 | 2,387 |

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: decode QSA selection and attention in fewer, shorter launches (opt-in, bitwise)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On an Arc Pro B70 the QSA selection (block scores, top-k) and attention of a decode window are small, latency-bound launches, and a batch window (`--batch`) ran them one row at a time. This adds four opt-in switches that do the same arithmetic in fewer launches or with less serial work. Each gives exactly the bits of the path it replaces; all are off by default, and each is a branch in front of the existing code that tests its flag first.

| switch | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN=1` | A batch window ran the scores, top-k and attention one row at a time. Now the scores run once per slot, the top-k once per window, and the attention once per window over every slot's pools. |
| `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN=1` | The wide top-k kernel (capacity above ~135K cells) found each radix pass's digit with one thread walking 256 bins. Now a work-group scan. Integers only: the same ids. |
| `STRATA_QSA_SCORES_TRANSPOSED=1` | The decode block scores reduce a block's (query, head) sums together: 16-31 shuffles per block instead of 20 per query, the same pairs in the same order. |
| `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_ACTIVE=1` | The attention merge of a call of 8 rows or fewer folds only the chunks its selection reaches. The MTP drafter's 32K window is 512 chunks. |

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, all four on, outputs bitwise identical in every arm: two streams in one window +1.9% aggregate (54.7 / 61.4 -> 55.7 / 62.6 tok/s), one stream +0.3%. A small engine gain at these contexts; the kernels themselves are 1.3-2.6x faster (table under Validation), and the gain grows with context.

## Related discussion

Feature issue #2805 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). No maintainer agreement on scope yet. If four switches are too many for the gain, `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN` alone carries most of the two-stream effect and I can split it out.

## Approach

- `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`: `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN`; in `record_window`'s QSA branch, a branch before the per-row batch loop runs the scores per slot, one `qsa_block_topk` and one `qsa_decode_attn_multi` for the window.
- `sycl/include/strata/qsa_decode_attn_multi.hpp` (new) and `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.dp.cpp`: `qsa_decode_attn_multi` (`qsa_decode_attn_batch` over up to four pool sets per launch; mixed KV formats or `STRATA_ATTN_LANECELL=1` fall back per set), `attn_merge_active_kernel`.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.dp.cpp`: `block_topk_wide_kernel<bool SCAN = false>` (only the new launch instantiates the scan; the existing launch compiles the same code), `block_scores_multi_t_kernel<NQ>`.
- `sycl/src/kernels/qsa_verify_batch_parity.cpp` (new), two ctest entries: without switches it checks the batch form against per-row calls (2x1, 2x2, 4x2, 6x1, 1x4 windows at 1K / 16K / 64K), selections against `qsa_block_topk_ref`, attention against `qsa_decode_attn_step`, 1-8-query scores against one call per query, the MTP drafter call, and writes a hash of each of 45 outputs; the second entry repeats with the three kernel switches and requires the same hashes. No tolerance anywhere.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a short section.

Left alone: the default path, the prompt path, `qsa_decode_attn_step` (decode without MTP), K/V and indexer appends, streamed-K/V batch windows, CUDA and HIP.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4 at run time; built with the repository dev image (`sycl/tools/Dockerfile` on the current `llama-sycl-b70:stable`, IGC 2.41.5; an older cached base with IGC 2.36.3 cannot build 0.2.0, see #3219), AOT `bmg-g31`. Model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30 --prefill 8192 --max-context 65536 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4 --spec-min-p 0 --stream-experts --expert-cache auto`, one slot, greedy, two fixed coding prompts with 512-token replies, a fresh engine per arm, then fresh 4K and 32K prompts. Coherence check and per-card health after every stop.

**Passed:**

- `qsa_verify_batch_parity --selftest --write-ref` (0.2.0-beta + this branch, head 1c501b02, one B70), then with `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN=1 STRATA_QSA_SCORES_TRANSPOSED=1 STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_ACTIVE=1 --selftest --ref`: both `qsa_verify_batch_parity: PASS (0 failures)`, the second against the first run's hashes.
- One stream (tok/s per prompt; output SHAs and draft counts in all three rows identical):

| | prompt 1 | prompt 2 | 4K / 32K read tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main e88ee39d | 70.6 | 73.9 | 1,219 / 2,078 |
| this branch, switches unset | 70.7 | 73.8 | 1,219 / 2,085 |
| all four switches | 70.8 | 74.1 | 1,220 / 2,080 |

- Two streams in one window (`"parallel": 2`, `--batch-groups 1`, `--max-context 16384 --vram-reserve-mib 512`; a layer split runs no MTP drafts in the slots), aggregate tok/s, 2 runs: unset 54.68 / 61.44, switches 55.73 / 62.55 (+1.9% / +1.8%); per-stream output SHAs identical between the arms. The engine log shows `STRATA_BATCH_QSA_ATTN=1` and `batch windows of up to 2 sequences` on both stages.
- Coherence true and per-card health passed after every stop.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** the kernel bench on 0.2.0 (unchanged code; on 0.1.x, us at 1K / 16K / 64K: batch 2x1 selection + attention 102.8 / 184.0 / 252.6 -> 62.3 / 107.9 / 156.2, 2x2 183.6 / 365.0 / 498.2 -> 78.3 / 138.2 / 205.0, top-k scan 16K / 64K 36.3 / 57.9 -> 19.5 / 42.1, transposed scores 5.5 / 18.7 / 63.1 -> 4.6 / 14.1 / 43.2, MTP merge 86.9 / 223.7 / 460.9 -> 41.0 / 157.2 / 335.9); `STRATA_QSA_TOPK_SCAN` in the engine (the wide top-k is only used above ~135K cells, and `--max-context 200000` does not fit every expert on a plain two-card layer split), `--batch-mtp` windows of 2 rows per slot (refused on a layer split), CUDA/HIP (not touched).

## Limits

- The end-to-end gain at 16K-65K contexts is small (0.3-2%); the switches matter more at long context and in MTP batch windows, which this setup cannot exercise on main.

pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On the Arc Pro B70 the SYCL port's decode GEMVs for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS (`native_mmvq`, 1-8 columns) are bound by instruction issue, not memory: the wide kernels re-read every column's activations for every row. This adds an opt-in kernel family, KREG: one work-group covers a row's whole K, each lane loads its slice of every column's activations once into registers, and the group streams tiles of 2-8 rows against them. `STRATA_MMVQ_KREG=1` turns it on. Unset, the default path is unchanged (output identical to main, measured below).

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, one stream: the verify window 39.4 / 40.0 -> 35.4 / 35.4 ms (-10% / -12%), decode 70.6 / 73.9 -> 83.2 / 91.0 tok/s. Part of the tok/s gain is the changed output drafting better on these prompts; the window time is the fair comparison. Prompt reading unchanged.

## Related discussion

Feature issue #2803 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). No maintainer agreement on scope yet. Independently tested by @deriknel on two B70s with `--pipeline-windows 2` and a 26-layer split (comment below, before the reset): the bench windows 8% shorter, +7% mean over five greedy prompts, flag unset matching the build without the PR, a 148K prompt, image input and a 5-minute soak with no failed request or xe reset. Thank you.

## Approach

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.dp.cpp`: `native_mmvq_kreg_kernel` with traits `KregQ4K`, `KregQ5K`, `KregQ6K`, `KregIQ4XS` (the wide kernels' lane split and dot expressions; K-quant scales decoded branch-free; IQ4_XS's codebook from a 256-entry local table), a transposed sub-group butterfly and a double-buffered local sum across sub-groups. Rows per tile and the 256-register mode per format and column count come from a sweep on the B70.
- `try_kreg<F>()` reads the latched flag first and declines n_in above 32,768 and misaligned matrices; the existing kernels then run as before. One guarded hook per entry point; the output head goes through `native_mmvq`, so it is covered.
- Rebase on 0.2.0: `native_q6_k_mmvq` now has `q6_planar_mmvq` where this PR adds its hook. Order kept as `STRATA_Q6_PACKED`, then planar, then KREG (the same resolution @deriknel used), so a planar copy is never bypassed.
- `sycl/src/kernels/mmvq_kreg_parity.cpp` (new, in the parity loop, `--selftest`): KREG and the default kernels against a float64 reference over the same bytes for each format, 5 shapes and 1-8 columns; T-column KREG bitwise equal to T one-column calls; a power check. `--bench` times both on random weights.
- `sycl/include/strata/kernels/native_mmvq.hpp` and `docs/INTEL.md`.

Left alone: other formats (Q8_0, IQ4_NL, IQ3_S, Q2_0, ...), the multi/small/wave kernels, tensors packed by `STRATA_Q6_PACKED`, `include/`, `src/`, CUDA/HIP.

## Validation

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: cheaper IQ decodes in the grouped expert kernels (STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1, opt-in, bitwise)
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The SYCL lane kernels that read the routed experts (`native_gu_kernel` / `native_down_kernel`, 8 lanes a row) are ALU-bound on an Arc Pro B70, not memory-bound: 280-480 instructions per 32-weight part for its 8 dp4a, reading the experts at 19-44% of DRAM bandwidth. Most of it is the dpct per-byte emulation of `byte_level_permute` in the Q2_0 dot, the compare/select chain of the IQ4_NL codebook lookup, the popcount/multiply ksigns unpacking, and 64-bit `kbx * sizeof(block)` products every iteration.

`STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST=1` switches the seven IQ expert formats (IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ2_S gate/up; IQ4_NL, Q2_0 down) to kernels that produce the same bits with fewer instructions. Off by default; without the flag the engine runs exactly the code it ran before.

Result on 0.2.0-beta, two B70s, one stream: decode 70.5 / 73.7 -> 76.7 / 80.1 tok/s (+8.7%), with output tokens and draft counts identical, so the gain is kernel time alone (verify window 39.5 / 40.2 -> 36.3 / 36.9 ms). Prompt reading unchanged.

## Related discussion

Feature issue #2801 (closed in the 0.2.0 tracker reset). No maintainer agreement on scope yet; opt-in and SYCL-only so the default path stays byte-identical. Happy to change the switch name or drop formats.

## Approach

- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`: `IqFast<TY>` decode traits whose `prep` yields the same integers as `Multi<TY>::prep` / the `vec_dot_*_q8_1` dot and reuses the same `acts` and `finish`; ksigns masks from a 2 KB table, the IQ4_NL codebook through four 256-entry position tables, Q2_0 fields spread with shifts and masks, aligned 8-byte loads. `rows_dot_fast` keeps the k order, per-entry float sum order and `lanes_sum` of the current dots, so the bits cannot move. Two rows per lane in 16-lane sub-groups. One hook line at the top of `launch_gu_port` / `launch_down_port` that returns at once when the latched flag is off. `STRATA_IQ_DECODE_FAST_FMTS=<ggml ids>` restricts it for an A/B.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_decode_tables.inc` (new): the two tables with the formulas that generate them.

Left alone: `include/`, `src/`, CUDA and HIP, every kernel the default path runs, the K-quant / Q5_1 / Q8_0 expert formats, the prompt path.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4 at run time; built with the repository dev image (`sycl/tools/Dockerfile` on the current `llama-sycl-b70:stable`, IGC 2.41.5; an older cached base with IGC 2.36.3 cannot build 0.2.0, see #3219), AOT `bmg-g31`. Coherence check and per-card health after every stop.

**Passed:**

pulls.title: HIP: verify-window routing for non-native routers (256 experts) on every HIP card
pulls.author: pugolini
pulls.body:
## Summary

The native router is 512 × 10 only. A 256-expert model (the Coder) therefore takes the per-token `moe_route` loop inside the verify window on every card except gfx906: one projection + top-k launch pair per token and layer, about 360 small launches per `--spec 4` step. `moe_route_window` (one multi-column BF16 projection + one top-k per layer, bitwise equal to the per-token calls per `route_window_parity`) was compiled for gfx906 only.

This PR runs it on every HIP card by default. `STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=0` restores the per-token loop. On CUDA it is opt-in (`STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=1`), because I have not measured it there.

**Relation to #238:** this does not touch the native router or its 512-only guard. The Coder keeps the generic router's arithmetic; only the number of launches changes, and the output stays byte-identical (below).

## Commits

1. **Verify profile + parity test:** a profile-only stamp after the routing splits slot 17 into `router (proj+topk)` and `plan+bell`, so a slow router shows on its own line (it writes nothing unless `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` or the #649 trace is on). `route_window_parity` now also checks T = 1 and 5 (the `--spec 4` verifier runs every T from 1 to 5).
2. **HIP:** the `STRATA_HIP_GFX906` guard around the `moe_route_window` branch becomes `route_window_on()`.

## Measurements

Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201, ROCm SDK 7.10 wheels), i7-14700, 32 GB RAM, Linux. Coder IQ1_M, `--spec 4`, MTP, resident experts (100 % VRAM hit rate). Engine built from this branch on main `296b59d2`, default gfx12 settings (so `STRATA_HC_Q8` was on in both arms). A = `STRATA_ROUTE_WIN=0` (current main behaviour), B = default.

- `route_window_parity`: **OK**, T = 1..6, 256 experts top-10 and the 1-row gate, bit-identical.
- Routing (projection + top-k) per verify window, `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1`:
  - GDN layers: 3.74 → 1.06 ms
  - QSA layers: 1.24 → 0.34 ms

| Benchmark (temp 0) | A tok/s | B tok/s | ms/step A → B | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 short code/text prompts, 600 max tokens | 98.5 | **108.1 (+9.7 %)** | 29.5 → 26.8 | same text, 5/5 |
| 3 prompts at 45K context, 500 max tokens | 87.1 | **95.1 (+9.2 %)** | 30.8 → 28.3 | same text, 3/3 |

Prefill is unchanged. Acceptance is unchanged (74.9 % / 74.8 %).

## Compatibility with open PRs

This branch merges cleanly with #2492 (gfx12 grid padding) and #2476 (no file lookahead when experts are resident). I run all three together on the same R9700: 13/13 served answers byte-identical to main (5 short, 5 Spanish, 3 at 45K context), with the measurements posted on those PRs.

## Not tested

- CUDA: the branch is guarded as opt-in there.
- gfx906: unchanged by default (it already took this path).
- Other RDNA cards: the path is architecture-independent and parity-checked, but I have only measured gfx1201.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 3060 12 GB on an AVX-only Xeon E5-2630 v2 (no AVX2/FMA): 0.2.0-beta re-run against 0.1.45, PCIe Gen3 x8
pulls.author: Norhiro
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
This reports `STRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx` ("Older CPUs (experimental)") running on a real AVX-only CPU: 2 × Xeon E5-2630 v2 with an RTX 3060 12 GB. The 2026-10-16 report on 0.1.45 (this PR before the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset) is re-run on 0.2.0-beta, as the reopen note asks. 0.1.45 was also measured again on the same hardware.

- 0.2.0-beta (`3d1fb480`, engine 0.1.45.3) builds and runs on this CPU. There is no SIGILL, and all AVX1/AVX2 kernel parity tests pass.
- On the same slot, 0.2.0 decodes 6-12% faster than 0.1.45: short chat 23.6 → 25.1 tok/s, agent turns 27.5 → 30.9 tok/s, cold. This is close to the release notes' +10.2% for an RTX 3060. Prompt reading is within 0-5%.
- Needles 9/9 to 32K. HumanEval 0-39 39/40 base and 37/40 plus. Japanese 11/12. Tools 8/8.
- **Note on the hardware:** the GPU is now in a different slot, PCIe Gen3 x8 instead of Gen2 x4 (engine probe 1.6 → 6.0 GB/s). With the same 0.1.45 engine, prompts read 2.7-3.6 times faster, and an agent turn's first token comes after about 6 s instead of about 22 s. The 2026-10-16 numbers therefore describe the Gen2 x4 slot. The README has a separate section that keeps the slot effect apart from the version effect.

## Related discussion
- This PR (#2793) was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; this update is the re-run on 0.2.0-beta.
- #3235: `tools/strata_bench.py` `NameError: port` on the self-start path. The 0.2.0 speed runs used a one-line local fix, included as `local-patch/strata_bench.py.diff`.
- #3358, #3407, #3409, #3412: the unit-test failures listed under Failed.

## Approach
Results only; no engine or tool changes. This adds `bench/results/2026-10-20-community-rtx-3060-avx-only-e5-2630v2-v020/`: README.md, the raw bench output and logs, the test logs and the scripts. Local paths, the user name, the GPU UUID and network addresses are removed.

## Validation
Revision: 0.2.0-beta `3d1fb480`, source build (CUDA 13.3 pip wheels, g++-14, sm_86, `-DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`). Comparison: 0.1.45 `296b59d2`. Fedora 44, driver 610.57.04, IQ2_XS `ed59f92`, context 40,960, NUMA node 1.

**Passed:**
- `tools/strata_bench.py --long`, cold and warm, 3 runs per test: 0.2.0 at 15:23-15:37 and 0.1.45 at 15:38-15:53 on 2026-10-20. Tables are in the README.
- `tools/needle_bench.py --lengths 4k,16k,32k --depths 10,50,90`: 9/9.
- HumanEval 0-39 (EvalPlus 0.3.1) 39/40 base and 37/40 plus; Japanese 11/12; tools 8/8. Same checks as the 2026-10-09 RTX 3060 report.
- Python tests: 123/130 modules. CTest (`-E 'bench|stress'`, 120 s per test): 137/144. These include `router_dot_parity_avx`, `iq_avx1_parity`, `iq_avx2_parity` and `q8k_quant_parity_avx`.

**Failed:**
- Known on 0.1.45 here: `test_setup_choices`, `test_setup_engine_hash`, `test_setup_golden`, `test_keepawake`; CTest `ple_parity` (no Q2_0 file), `platform_memory_test` (`ulimit -l` 8 MB).
- Environment: `test_iq_pack` (no gguf-py; passes with `STRATA_GGUF_PY`) and `test_nvfp4_local_pack` (no pytest; passes with it).
- Built with upstream llama.cpp (the default): `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2`, `native_hadamard_test` ("no trellis types", as in #3358).
- Upstream, reported separately: `serve.test_lifeline` portable watcher (#3407), `isa_guard_check` on `tq_rows_avx512` (#3409), `ggml_tq_overlay` under CMake 3.31 (#3412).

**Not run:**
- 0.2.0's setup.py, app, Terminal and update feed: only the engine and server from source were tested.
- The NUMA both-sockets A/B, the 65-minute soak and the quant yardstick were not repeated on 0.2.0.
- Pictures (no mmproj installed), UD-IQ4_XS, contexts above 40,960, concurrent clients.
- 0.1.45's needles and T5 checks on the new slot.

## Limits
- One machine. Speed was measured with one run per version, one after the other (not interleaved), so differences of a few percent are within one run's spread.
- The network was connected during these tests.
- The HumanEval +2 against 2026-10-16 is not attributed to 0.2.0: the slot change also changes the engine's PCIe share.

pulls.title: bench/results: RTX 5070 Ti (16 GiB) with 31.6 GiB of RAM — IQ2_XS at 128K in low-RAM mode
pulls.author: Lithivm
pulls.body:
Adds a results-only report for an **RTX 5070 Ti (16 GiB) with 31.6 GiB of system RAM** — the same GPU as `2026-10-04-community-rtx-5070ti-windows` and `2026-10-06-community-rtx5070ti-5900x`, but at half their RAM, which in `bench/results/` is a combination that is not covered yet.

Only three files under `bench/results/2026-10-17-community-rtx-5070-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq2-xs/` (`README.md`, `results.json`, `engine-log-excerpt.txt`). No engine or code changes, as the guide asks for a results-only submission.

## Hardware

- RTX 5070 Ti, 16,303 MiB VRAM, power limit 300 W (not reduced), PCIe Gen5 x16
- Ryzen 7 9700X (8C/16T, AVX-512), **31.6 GiB RAM**
- WD_BLACK SN770 1 TB NVMe (model files and OS on the same drive)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, driver 616.64, CUDA 13.0
- Not an isolated machine (proxy, Steam, ComfyUI MCP bridge, antivirus; the GPU also drives the display)

## Model and configuration

- `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF` @ `ed59f92`, IQ2_XS, both shards with their SHA-256
- Context **131,072**, KV `q4_0`, KV streaming off, **low-RAM mode (`--mmap-experts`)**, expert cache `auto` (~5,000 slots / ~6.8 GiB VRAM), `--prefill auto`, MTP `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1600`
- Strata 0.1.44.1 / engine 0.1.44.1, release binary, zip install (not a git checkout)
- Thinking off for the suite; the suite's requests set `temperature 0`

## Results (medians, ranges over 3 runs)

| Configuration | Actual prompt tokens | Runs | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat (100 tok cap) | 46 | 9 | not measured | 57.2 (36.8-87.0) | 0.54 (0.42-1.06) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4019 | 3 | 270.0 (226.5-270.2) | not measured | 14.94 (14.94-17.80) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16058 | 3 | 447.8 (446.7-518.1) | not measured | 35.94 (31.07-36.03) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14572 | 3 | see report | 45.2 (32.3-51.4) | 12.79 (10.82-17.17) |

Total suite time 420 s.

## What the report is about — and its limitation

This install cannot keep the 36 GB expert arena in 31.6 GiB of RAM, so unlike the two 64 GiB 5070 Ti reports it runs the low-RAM mode and serves the experts through the OS file cache. The measured boundary:

- **decode** lands at ~85-87 tok/s once the cache is warm, roughly half the 64 GiB figures (102 tok/s)
- **prompt processing** is 270-448 tok/s against 1,992-3,523 tok/s at 64 GiB — **4-8x slower**, because the prompt path re-reads lent experts from the SSD

So on a 32 GiB machine the prompt/TTFT side, not decode, is what decides whether the setup is usable (a 16K prompt is 36 s before the first token). The chat row's 36.8-87.0 range is the low-RAM cache warming across the nine back-to-back requests, not run-to-run noise; the report says so in the Results section.

Also recorded because the guide asks for them: storage, PCIe link, power limit and the background load are filled in, and two things the tool got wrong are corrected — it reports the OS as "Windows 10 (10.0.26100)" (actually Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200) and its own README template asks for facts it cannot read (CUDA version, commit on a zip install).

## One tool bug found while preparing this

`tools/strata_bench.py:564` reads `CMakeLists.txt` with `read_text()` and no encoding, so on a Chinese/Japanese Windows (GBK code page) it raises `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xbf in position 2` on the file's UTF-8 BOM and exits **before any measurement**. `setup.py:4649` reads the same file with `encoding="utf-8"`. `PYTHONUTF8=1` works around it. Happy to file it as an issue with the traceback if that is more useful than fixing it in this PR — I left it out of this PR to keep it results-only.

## Summary

Adds optional aria2c support for model downloads.

If aria2c is installed, setup uses it with multiple connections and resume support. If aria2c is not installed, setup falls back to the existing downloader unchanged.

## What changed

- Detect aria2c with `shutil.which("aria2c")`
- Use aria2c for HTTP(S) model downloads when available

- aria2c absent -> built-in downloader works
- interrupted built-in download resumes correctly
- aria2c restored -> resumes the same `.part` file
