pulls.title: [Engine] --peer-device: the adaptive tier's copies land while the next window runs (opt-in STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1)
pulls.author: bulhenvaster
pulls.body:
**Problem and result:** in peer mode (`--peer-device`) `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` is refused ("not with --peer-device"), so every decode window first waits for the previous adapt round's copies. On 0.2.0-beta (`main` e88ee39d) that wait is 5.0-5.2 ms of a 45 ms window. With this change the peer tier joins the overlap and the wait is 0.20-0.23 ms. Decode of 900-token greedy answers on a 161K-token conversation (3 questions x 3 rounds, decode only, medians), two runs each, alternating:

| | `main`, `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` (refused) | this branch, same | this branch + `STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL=1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| adaptive wait per window | 5.21 / 4.98 ms | **0.23 / 0.22 ms** | 0.22 / 0.20 ms |
| window | 45.4 / 45.0 ms | 38.1 / 42.0 ms | 41.6 / 38.0 ms |
| ms per token, all 9 | 11.85 / 11.79 | 11.90 / 10.45 | 10.94 / 11.59 |

The wait is gone in every run; tokens per window move with the text the drafts find, so ms per token is noisier than the window (mean of the two runs: 11.82 -> 11.18, -5%). `STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL` measured no gain over the overlap alone on this build (it gave +1.7% on 0.1.43); I can drop it from this PR if you prefer.

**Approach:** with `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` `PeerExperts::adapt` issues its copies in layer order and signals each layer's landing with the primary's kind of signal (a stream-ordered D2H copy of the layer number into a pinned int, or host functions where the primary uses them), its table takes the swaps at the window's start (`flip_pending`), and a layer waits for a tier's copies only when that tier swapped in it. Without a peer the per-layer wait is the one it was; without the variable nothing changes. Separately, `STRATA_PEER_LAUNCH_IN_POOL=1` (opt-in) runs the peer's launch on the host thread right after the CPU pool's first phase is published instead of before the pool starts (with the cold-read path of 0.2.0 it starts before the CPU's batches, as before). `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` gains a line with the peer's launch and wait. `docs/DETAILS.md`: a paragraph under `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP`.

**Validation** (RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, PCIe 3.0 x8, primary + RTX 3060 12 GB, x16, `--peer-device 1`; Xeon E5-2683 v4, 64 GB DDR4 in two channels; Ubuntu, CUDA 13.3, driver 595.91; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS pack, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --spec 4 --mtp --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --prompt-cache 14 --pcie-frac 0`, `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`; one engine start per run):
- Passed: `cmake --build build --target strata` (CUDA, sm_86 + sm_120) on this branch's tree, no errors.
- Passed: the default path. `main` and this branch, deterministic decode (`--spec-min-p 1.01 --suffix-draft 0 --lookup-chain 0 --adapt-swaps 0`, so no copies), `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1`, no launch switch, a chain of 12 prompt reads with 64-token answers on a 161K conversation: 14 of 14 answers identical.
- Passed: the A/B above (runs `main`, overlap, overlap + launch, then again).
- Failed: none observed.
- Not run: HIP, SYCL and Metal builds; Windows (the host-function signal path); a layer split; tokens compared bit for bit with the adaptive tier on (two runs of `main` already differ: the tier makes the output depend on timing).

**Limits:** one rig measured.

pulls.title: --prompt-cache-spread (opt-in): the first checkpoint in every --prompt-cache-every tokens of the conversation stays, so a request that departs far back reads at most that much again
pulls.author: bulhenvaster
pulls.body:
An agent session grows by short turns and every request saves a checkpoint at its new turn, so least recent use keeps the root and the last few turns - all at the conversation's end.  A request that departs further back (the client's summarization call over the older part, an old tool result rewritten) then falls to the root and reads everything after it again.  With the option, eviction_victim_spread (conv_cache.hpp) keeps the first checkpoint in every --prompt-cache-every tokens as a milestone; the rest rotate by least recent use, the two most recently used always stay, and when only milestones are left the one whose neighbours are closest goes.  Without the option, with fewer than 4 checkpoints or --prompt-cache-every 0 the policy is the plain one.  conv_cache_test covers the new policy.

RTX 5060 Ti (PCIe 3.0 x8) + RTX 3060, --peer-device, IQ3_XXS, --prompt-cache 14: a conversation of 80 turns to 121K tokens, then a request with its first 55 turns and a new instruction (86,182 tokens): without the option 5,023 reused + 81,159 read in 60.3 s, with it 83,387 reused + 2,795 read in 4.1 s.  A day of real agent use (31 automatic compactions): the summarization call read a median 8,062 tokens in 7.2 s instead of ~72K in ~55 s.  The answers can differ in wording (a restored checkpoint and a batched re-read round differently).  Not measured: the RAM of 14 checkpoints at its peak; HIP, SYCL and Metal (the change is host code shared by all of them).

**How it was checked.** Built on its own on top of `main` (296b59d2): CUDA 13.3, sm_86 + sm_120, Linux (Ubuntu), the `strata` target. `conv_cache_test` (header-only) compiled with g++ and passes, including the two new spread cases. The option has run in daily agent use on the rig above since 2026-10-13. HIP, SYCL and Metal were not built: I have only the NVIDIA rig.

One change per PR; nothing else from my fork is in it.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: 4x RTX 3090 24 GiB (250 W each) - Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS at 262,144-token context
pulls.author: filmo
pulls.body:
## Summary

Community benchmark report for **4x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GiB** running **Unsloth Dynamic UD-IQ4_XS** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) at the **262,144-token native context**, measured with `tools/strata_bench.py --clients 1 --long` (3 runs per test, thinking off, medians with ranges; suite total 131 s).

| Test | Prompt tok/s (median, range) | Decode tok/s (median, range) | TTFT s (median, range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat (n=9) | not measured | 113.3 (88.8-153.1) | 0.24 (0.22-0.26) |
| 4K fresh prompt (4,019 tok) | 1313.3 (1249.7-1313.8) | not measured | 3.08 (3.08-3.23) |
| 16K fresh prompt (16,058 tok) | 2393.8 (2359.3-2398.1) | not measured | 6.73 (6.72-6.83) |
| 32K fresh prompt (32,049 tok) | 3240.1 (3234.1-3248.9) | not measured | 9.92 (9.89-9.94) |
| agent session follow-ups | ~1000 mid-session | 127.1 (81.5-139.5) | 2.76 (2.05-3.19) |
| concurrency, 1 client | 75.5 total (69.9-79.4) | - | p95 0.335 |

## Hardware / software

- 4x RTX 3090 24 GiB, **each power-limited to 250 W** on the host (factory 350 W / 420 W for GPU1); GPU0 PCIe x16, GPU1-3 x4, no NVLink; layer split auto (0-11 / 12-26 / 27-35 / 36-47)
- i7-13700K, 44 GiB RAM, Debian 12 LXC on Proxmox VE, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2, Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d)

## Model / configuration

- Unsloth Dynamic UD-IQ4_XS (~94 GB, 3-shard GGUF), BF16 mmproj vision encoder, native-experts pack, MTP draft enabled (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`)
- 262,144-token context, `--kv int8`, `--batch 2` (2 parallel slots), `--expert-cache auto`, `--resident-budget-gib 20` pinned RAM tier: **89% of experts resident at load**, remaining ~35.4 GiB read from a CIFS network share through the file cache (decode expert hit rate 99.7-99.8% during the suite, <=0.1% cross-GPU PCIe reads)

## Limitations

- Speed suite only; no needle/recall check was run
- The `--clients 1` arm is effectively solo: a single request occupies one slot alone and keeps MTP; with shared batch windows MTP is disabled
- 250 W per-GPU power cap lowers sustained boost clocks (~1.73-1.80 GHz observed); expect somewhat better prompt throughput on machines at stock power
- Chat decode range is wide (88.8-153.1) due to MTP draft-acceptance variance on short chats; the agent-session median (127.1) is the more stable solo-decode figure

Per-run data: `results.json`. This PR adds only `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rtx-3090-qwen3-8-flash-next/` (README.md + results.json).

pulls.title: log unauthorized API-key attempts with the client IP (issue #1847)
pulls.author: wszhoho
pulls.body:
## What this does

Adds a log line on API-key authentication failure that includes the client source IP, so fail2ban (or any log-based rate limiter) can match it and ban brute-force attempts. Closes #1847.

Before this change, `_authorized()` in `serve/server.py` replied with a silent 401 JSON body — nothing landed in the journal, so there was nothing for a filter to match on.

```python
print(f"unauthorized: Invalid API Key from {self.client_address[0]}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
```

The wording deliberately mirrors llama.cpp's `unauthorized: Invalid API Key from <ip>` verbatim (as requested in #1847), so an existing fail2ban filter written for llama.cpp works against Strata's logs unchanged.

Notes:
- Goes to `stderr`, consistent with other warnings in this file (e.g. the AMD line at L2845); `flush=True` keeps journald real-time so fail2ban doesn't miss events.
- No `[strata]` prefix on purpose, to keep the line byte-compatible with the stock llama.cpp filter regex.
- `sys` is already imported at module level; no new dependencies.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile serve/server.py` passes.
- Smoke-tested the patched failure branch in isolation: emits exactly `unauthorized: Invalid API Key from 203.0.113.7` on stderr.
- Not end-to-end tested against a running server (needs GPU/model engine); the change is one print statement on the existing 401 path.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RX 7900 XT 20 GB, UD-Q5_K_XL: v0.1.44.1 vs v0.2.0-beta
pulls.author: loeeeee
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Results-only benchmark report from an RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100) on Linux with Unsloth UD-Q5_K_XL at 262K, all experts in RAM. This PR was closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; I rebased it on current `main` and re-ran the measurements on v0.2.0-beta as the reset message asked. It now carries two reports:

- `2026-10-15-community-rx-7900-xt-ud-q5-k-xl` (v0.1.44.1): setup's default configuration vs the same plus `--vram-reserve-mib 1024 --prefill auto:32768`, same day. Unchanged from the original submission.
- `2026-10-20-community-rx-7900-xt-ud-q5-k-xl-0.2.0-beta` (new): the tuned configuration measured the same day on v0.1.44.1 and then on v0.2.0-beta (engine 0.1.45.3), `tools/strata_bench.py --runs 3 --long`, medians:

| | v0.1.44.1 | v0.2.0-beta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4K / 16K / 32K prompt, tok/s | 226 / 833 / 902 | 828 / 1,153 / 1,050 |
| short-chat decode, tok/s | 16.2 | 18.6 |
| agent follow-up first token, s | 5.79 | 5.67 |

Prompt throughput at 16K and 32K is higher and steadier on v0.2.0-beta (+38 % / +16 % in the medians); decode and agent turns are not different beyond the run ranges. The v0.1.44.1 4K run was noisy (172-311 tok/s) and well below the 2026-10-15 result on the same build (577), so the 4K difference is not a speedup claim.

## Related discussion
Previously #2705 (closed by the maintainer in the 0.2.0-beta reset, "closed here does not mean rejected"). Results-only, as `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` describes; no engine changes.

## Approach
New report folder with a comparison README, the tool's own README and `results.json` for each build, one `COMMUNITY.md` row and one `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` entry. The tool's output was edited in two places only: the GPU name (it printed "AMD Radeon") and the service user name that its sanitizer replaced in the Strata version line.

## Validation
**Passed:**
- `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --runs 3 --long` against the running server, once on v0.1.44.1 and once on v0.2.0-beta, same machine and configuration, 2026-10-20. No failed requests in either. Per-request data in each folder's `results.json`.
- Update to v0.2.0-beta via `setup.sh --backend hip` (source build, ROCm 7.2.4): server loaded, engine log "session is up (engine 0.1.45.3)".

**Failed:**
- First v0.2.0-beta setup link failed (`undefined reference: sqrtf@GLIBC_2.43` from librocblas) because the CMake cache in `build-hip` still pointed at the previous ROCm (7.2.3) and glibc. Moving `build-hip` aside and rerunning fixed it. Noted in the report; I did not investigate whether setup should detect a changed ROCm root.
- A second setup run failed copying into `engine/strata` ("Text file busy") while the server was running; stopping the server first fixed it.

**Not run:**
- Needle recall on v0.2.0-beta, long (128K+) prompts, concurrency, memory/clock capture, other backends. No engine change is proposed, so no builds beyond the HIP one above.

## Limits
One session per build, not a controlled A/B. The OS update moved nixpkgs ROCm 7.2.3 -> 7.2.4 between the two runs, so the Strata tag and ROCm are changed together. The machine is shared with coding agents, background load was not controlled, and the cause of the baseline's noise is unknown.

pulls.title: Feature/windows amd vision telemetry
pulls.author: D4ve0s
pulls.body:
## Title

Windows AMD: ADL2 telemetry, one Monitor tile per GPU, images on Windows, and a setup that keeps a two-card split

Issue: Refs #2614, #1380, #112, #2442

## Summary

A Windows AMD card had no telemetry: the Monitor's GPU tiles were empty and a PC with two cards had no way to
see them apart. This reads every AMD card through ADL2 PMLog (`atiadlxx.dll` over ctypes — the same interface
HWInfo and LibreHardwareMonitor use, no new dependency), gives the Monitor one tile per card, and carries the
same numbers into `/metrics`.

Alongside it, three things that stopped a Windows AMD install working: SETUP renumbered or dropped cards when
`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` was already in the environment, re-running SETUP collapsed a two-card split back to one
card (the engine then died at start, reported as "the embedding buffer failed"), and Windows had no image
encoder at all.

One commit, `d0dcf489` plus the review fixes listed under Telemetry and Tests: 35 files, +1501/−145 against
`main` (v0.1.44.1). Everything is opt-in — the CUDA path is untouched, `--yes` never asks the new questions,
AMD images stay off by default, and the default install path writes the same config as v0.1.44.1. No engine
(C++/CUDA/HIP kernel) changes.

## What changed

### Telemetry (`serve/telemetry.py`, +366)

- `_Adl` — ctypes bindings for ADL2 PMLog: adapter enumeration, `PmLogStart` with the sensor set (edge/mem
  temp, board power, gfx/mem activity, bus lanes, power limit), and the malloc callback through
  `ucrtbase.dll` (the heap `atiadlxx.dll` frees on).
- `_AmdWin` — util = max(gfx, mem activity), temp = edge else mem, power = `BOARD_POWER` (already watts, no
  scaling), VRAM used = `DedicatedVRAMUsage`, total = `MemoryInfoX4`. Enumerates present discrete cards,
  deduped by the UDID's `DEV_xxxx` code (each card repeats once per display), integrated GPU skipped.
- Every discrete card is sampled (`amd_card_count()`), not just the display-driving one — `Adapter_Get` hid a
  second idle card. HIP indices and ADL indices are different namespaces and are never mixed.
- PCIe per card — PMLog `BUS_SPEED` is the GPU's internal bus and power-saves to Gen4 at idle, so the slot's
  generation comes from Device Manager (`DEVPKEY_PciDevice_MaxLinkSpeed`, one cached PowerShell query keyed by
  DEV code) and the negotiated width from PMLog `BUS_LANES`. Matches HWInfo on this PC: 9070 XT Gen5 x8,
  R9700 Gen5 x4.
- A reader gives back what the driver lent it: `close()` releases the PMLog device handle and the ADL context,
  a finaliser covers readers that go away with the server, and the one-off call sites (`free_vram_mib()`,
  `server.gpu_vram_mib()`) release theirs. Numbers under Measured.
- `sample()` always emits `gpus[]` with name, `pcie_gen_max` and `pcie_width` per card, even for one card.
- Small NVML fix: `power_limit` returns `float(lim)` instead of a raw value that could be 0.

### SETUP behaviour (`setup.py`, +200/−33)

- **AMD asks "Do you want images?" everywhere, Windows included** (default off; `--yes` never asks; the
  Unsloth Linux default-on is unchanged). `hip_vision()` is now platform-neutral: `yes`/`gpu` → gpu,
  `cpu` → cpu, else none.
- **`previous_amd_split()`** — a re-run with no `--gpu`/`--gpus` keeps the installed config's split (accepts
  `"gpu"` as a list or a `"0,2"` string, newest config wins, keeps the split only while every card is still
  present and usable).
- **`hip_devices()` clears `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` for the probe.** A user-set value hid cards and renumbered
  the rest, so a saved split "0,2" named a card that was no longer at 2.
- **Windows `--gpus` works** — the old "multi-GPU is Linux only" refusal is gone. `engine_step()` renumbers
  the split's cards to HIP numbers after the probe (an integrated Radeon takes HIP 0) and prints what it
  settled on.
- **`hip_vision_windows()`** — for the ready-made zip: run the zip's encoder when `BUILD.json` says
  `vision`/`vision_src`/`vision_archs` match; `gpu` asked without an encoder built for this arch warns and
  falls back to cpu; a stale or missing encoder is recompiled as CPU with MSVC; no compiler offers the winget
  Build Tools (~2 GB), and declining leaves images off.
- **`install_msvc_build_tools()`** — winget `Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools` with the VCTools workload,
  asked first. `cmake_build()` pip-installs cmake and ninja when they are missing (old installs predate
  `requirements.txt`).
- **VRAM reserve rule** — Windows AMD with the CPU encoder writes no `--vram-reserve-mib` at all, so the engine
  keeps its 2560 MiB WDDM floor (#1376, #1709); a written 700 would have defeated it. With a GPU encoder the
  reserve is `max(reserve, 3260)` = the 2560 floor + the encoder's 700. The 12 GB tip only shows where it
  applies.

### Multi-GPU enumeration and JSON config

- The config is re-read and `gpu` normalised whether it is a list or a `"0,2"` string, so an old config survives.
- `tools/hip/package_windows.py` records `vision: "cpu"`, `vision_src` (source hash) and `vision_archs` in
  `BUILD.json`, so SETUP can tell a matching encoder from a stale one.
- `.gitignore` adds `/strata-*.bak` (SETUP's config backups) and `build-vision-cpu.bat`.

### Vision build and packaging

- `tools/hip/build_windows.bat` builds a portable CPU `strata-vision.exe` (AVX2, static CRT, llama.cpp pinned
  by `setup.get_llama_cpp()`) into the zip; `package_windows.py --vision` ships it.
- `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt` gains `STRATA_VISION_HIP` (GGML_HIP) for the Linux HIP encoder path in
  `setup.build_vision_hip()` — **not yet run on hardware**, flagged in TEST_REQUESTS.
- `tools/vision/strata_vision.cpp` also sets `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` in CPU mode — the AMD runtime ignores
  `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.
- `tools/strata_mcp.py` drops the "hip on Windows" and vision refusals; the MCP `strata_install` accepts the
  same vision answers as SETUP (gpu is downgraded to cpu by setup itself when the arch has no encoder).

### Monitor UI (`serve/web/`)

- **Image encoder card**: encoder cache bar, encode-time sparkline, facts (device + threads, last picture with
  tokens/grid/cache-hit, since-start totals, mmproj, picture cap), and a "Reading N pictures" pill and status
  line while an encode runs.
- **Per-GPU tiles** (`renderGpuCards`) when the PC has ≥2 cards; summary Power and PCIe tiles get a `GPU:0 …` /
  `GPU:1 …` line each; the PCIe tile shows each card's own link ("Gen5 x8", "Gen5 x4").
- `app.css`/`app.js` are cache-busted (`?v=3`) so an open tab can't keep a stale script.

### Metrics (`serve/server.py`, `serve/prometheus.py`)

- `Vision` records starts/stops, per-encode times, cache hits, failures and image tokens; `/metrics` gains a
  `vision` block, `encoding_images`, and per-request history rows (images / image tokens / encode ms).
- Prometheus gains 7 series: `strata:vision_images_total`, `image_tokens_total`, `encode_seconds_total`,
  `encode_failures_total`, `cache_images`, `encoder_up`, `encode_ms_last` (absent on a cache hit). Nothing is
  emitted when the model has no vision.
- `engine_args()` adds `--vram-reserve-mib 3260` for hip on Windows with a GPU encoder (2560 WDDM floor + 700
  for the encoder). `gpu_vram_mib()` releases the reader it builds per card.

### Docs

- `AMD_HIP.md`: the ADL2 telemetry paragraph with the B650E measurements, the two-cards-one-model Windows
  section, and the Images-on-Windows section (zip encoder, 2.7–2.9 s per 512×512 picture on a 7800X3D, Build
  Tools ~2 GB, the 3260 reserve).
- `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`: new entry "SETUP.bat forgets a two-card split" with the `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` root
  cause, how to check it, and the measured before/after probe results.
- `DETAILS.md`: Monitor sources (ADL2/NVML/sysfs, per-slot PCIe), the `strata:vision_*` series, the AMD
  image-encoder table row, and the Image encoder card paragraph.
- `MULTI_GPU.md`: Windows AMD `--gpus` line. `AI_SETUP.md`: the AMD images question. `TEST_REQUESTS.md`: two
  rows — Windows AMD `--vision cpu` reports wanted, `--vision gpu` never run on hardware.
- README ×7: "AMD cards read pictures through the processor, on Linux and on Windows alike."

### Tests

- New `serve/test_telemetry_adl.py` (+118): the ADL reader never raises when ADL is missing, readings are sane
  (temp 0–120 °C, watts), every card index below `card_count` reads, per-card PCIe present, and
  `AdlReaderCleanup` — `close()` is safe and idempotent, and 40 one-off `free_vram_mib()` reads do not grow
  the process handle count (Windows only, skipped where there is no `atiadlxx.dll`).
- `tools/test_setup_amd.py`: probe ignores a set `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the vision question is
  platform-neutral.
- `tools/test_setup_choices.py`: 5 new `hip_vision_windows` cases — zip encoder used, gpu from zip, gpu falls
  back to cpu when the arch is missing, stale `vision_src` recompiles, no compiler asks then declines.
- `tools/test_setup_unsloth.py`: `HipImages` (Windows asks, yes → cpu encoder with no `--vram-reserve-mib` in
  the config args, default off, `--yes` never asks, Linux Unsloth default stays on) and `HipSplit` (Windows
  `--gpus 0,2` renumbers to [1,2] when the iGPU takes 0, setup-again keeps a list or a "0,2" string, a fresh
  PC stays one card, Linux keeps its split).
- `serve/test_server.py`: the vision instrumentation, and the three `AmdTelemetry` tests pinned to the Linux
  sysfs reader — they fake an amdgpu tree, so building a real ADL reader here made them depend on the machine
  (#1380). `WebApp.test_page_and_files` now matches `web/app.js` with its `?v=3` cache-bust.
- `serve/test_monitor.py`, `test_prometheus.py`, `test_vision_elastic.py`: the Monitor card's DOM and the
  Prometheus series. `tools/test_strata_mcp.py`: hip vision cpu/yes/gpu/no accepted on both platforms.

## Extra Notes

### Test machine

- Windows 11, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, B650E motherboard, Adrenalin 26.9.2
- AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB — HIP 0, gfx1201, Gen5 x4 (Device Manager and HWInfo agree: "PCIe v5.0 x16 @ x4")
- AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB — HIP 2, gfx1201, Gen5 x8
- 7800X3D integrated graphics (2 CU RDNA2, gfx1036; rocminfo's marketing name is "AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core
  Processor") — HIP 1, skipped by the split and by the ADL2 enumeration
- Model split across the two cards: R9700 layers 0–30, 9070 XT layers 31–47 + head, 131K context
- CPU image encoder running on the 7800X3D; a hand-built HIP encoder also ran on the R9700 (below)

### Measured on that machine

- **Handle growth (the finding reported on #1434).** 40 one-off `free_vram_mib(0, amd=True)` calls hold the
  process handle count at 197 → 197 now that the reader is released. Keeping the readers gave 197 → 278, about
  +2 per call — the same signature crkva measured on a 7900 XTX in #1434 (267 → 347). The server's sampler
  keeps one reader per card, so the growth showed up on the one-off calls: `free_vram_mib()` in the startup
  retry loop and `gpu_vram_mib()` once per card.
- **PCIe per card:** 9070 XT Gen5 x8, R9700 Gen5 x4 — Device Manager and HWInfo agree, and the B650E board
  really does bifurcate, so one aggregate link number would be wrong.
- **Images:** 2.7–2.9 s per 512×512 picture (256 tokens) with the CPU encoder; the screenshot run measured
  3,647 ms for a 23×12 (276-token) picture, cache hit on repeat.
- **Prometheus scrape after 4 image requests:** `strata:vision_images_total 4`, `vision_image_tokens_total
  1073`, `vision_encode_seconds_total 12.767`, `vision_encode_failures_total 0`, `vision_cache_images 4`,

pulls.title: qwen35/q36: --kv - int8 K/V caches (codes + a FP16 scale per 64 values)
pulls.author: TorBere
pulls.body:
Implements the int8 K/V cache for the q36 (qwen35moe) engine's own attention path as `--kv` (strata's name
for the stores: `fp32` default, `int8` for both stores, `k8v32` / `k32v8` for one of the two).  The q36 caches
were FP32 (2 KiB per cell per store), so a 128K context ran out of VRAM for expert slots: 0/256 experts in
VRAM, 34 tok/s.  This is the same effect issue #2464 reports for the V100 (the q36 decode falling from 154 to
56 tok/s as the context fills; llama.cpp quantizes the cache, this engine does not).

## What it does

- `--kv int8`: K and V stored as int8 codes with one FP16 scale per 64 values (group absmax / 127), ~3.9x
  smaller cache (528 B/cell vs 2048 B at head_dim 256); `k8v8` is an alias; `k8v32` / `k32v8` quantize one
  store only; `fp32` (the default) runs bit for bit the old kernels.
- `STRATA_Q36_KV=int8` stays as the environment fallback (`--kv` wins).
- Decode (`k_attn_part`), prompt chunk (`k_kv_f16` -> cuBLAS) and the MTP block dequantize on the fly; the
  verify windows go through the same kernels, the commit/rollback of the cache is unchanged.
- `k_attn_prep` / `k_attn_part` / `k_kv_f16` are `template <bool KI8, bool VI8>`; a small `kv4()` dispatcher
  in `Engine` launches the right specialization, so `kc/vc` stay FP32 pointers and the int8 codes + scales
  live in `kc8/vc8/ks8/vs8`.  `kKVG = 64`; `head_dim` must be a multiple of it (the host says so and stays
  FP32 otherwise).

## Measurements

RTX 3060 12 GB, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (experts 18.75 GiB, streaming), `--mtp 2`, same machine, two
runs each, 120 tokens per run:

| variant | 64K | 128K | experts in VRAM (64K / 128K) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| installed engine (CUDA 13), FP32 | 50.3 tok/s | 35.8 tok/s | 18 / 0 of 256 |
| this source, FP32 (default) | 50.1 tok/s | 33.9 tok/s | 18 / 0 of 256 |
| this source, `--kv int8` | **59.7 tok/s** | **54.8 tok/s** | **46 / 31 of 256** |

At 128K the freed VRAM (~4 GiB) brings 31 experts back into the VRAM, which is where the +53% comes from.
The FP32 build reproduces the installed engine (50.1 vs 50.3 / 33.9 vs 35.8), so the difference is the patch,
not the toolchain.

Needle-in-the-haystack, 52.8K-token prompt, 128K mode, max_tokens 250, temperature 0: both FP32 and int8
find the hidden number; the int8 run took 91 s vs 159 s end to end (1.75x).  A chat answer at the same
context is qualitatively equal between the two.

`--kv k8v32` / `k32v8` smoke tested at 64K: each quantizes one store, so they land between FP32 and int8 â€”
32 experts in VRAM (FP32: 18, int8: 46) and 54.8 / 53.8 tok/s (FP32: 50.1, int8: 59.7).

## Not in this PR

`--kv q4_0` and `k8v4` (PR #21's Hadamard rotation over head_dim 256) are not wired into the q36 kernels
yet; `--kv` refuses them with a note.  The FWHT-256/Q4_0 pieces already exist in the repo
(`src/kernels/cuda/kv_q4.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/kv_q4.hpp`), so a follow-up can add them the same way
(rotate K after RoPE and V, rotate the queries, rotate the output back).

## How it was tested

- Built from this tree with the setup toolchain (CUDA 12.9, sm_86) into a separate build folder; the
  installed engine was not touched.
- A/B runs against the installed engine and the same source without the patch (fp32 path), same prompts.
- `--kv int8` end to end through `serve/server.py` (the config's args carry `--kv int8`).
- The `q36ref` fp32 path is untouched (the FP32 template instantiation is the previous kernel code).

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: opt-in OTLP traces of every /v1 request, and the docs pages 0.1.41 left uncovered
pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
### Problem and result

The opt-in OTLP tracing of every `/v1` request (0.1.41) has no docs page, and the pages that touch it say things the code does not do. The branch carries the tracing feature code (`serve/tracing.py`, `serve/test_tracing.py`, the server wiring) plus the docs that match it, and the eval/bench harness hooks that link a run to the server's own trace.

After: `--trace-otlp` is opt-in (off by default, the default path is byte-identical), traced requests carry no prompt text (the promise and its exception for errored requests are documented), the anchor floor and the half-second quiet drain are documented, and the docs pages match the code.

### Related discussion

Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset; merged with current main and re-verified per the reset note. Supersedes #2003 and #1816 (closed as subsets). The CMP0169 pin and the test_winjob fix were dropped from this PR — they are #3015's and #3017's dedicated changes (AGENTS.md one change per PR).

### Approach

Feature code: `serve/tracing.py` (OTLP exporter, span builder), server wiring behind `--trace-otlp`, `serve/telemetry.py` and `serve/runconfig.py` plumbing. Docs: DETAILS, BATCHING, MULTI_GPU, SECOND_GPU, TROUBLESHOOTING, SECURITY. Harness: `evals/` opt-in `--trace`, `bench/bench_vs_llama.py` trace linking.

### Validation

Passed, merged with 0.2.0-beta main (`e88ee39d`, merge commit `8f066336`), Windows 11, Python 3.15, RTX 4090:

- `python -m unittest serve.test_tracing` → 14/14 OK.
- `python -m unittest evals.test_eval` → 15/15 OK.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server` → 341 OK (3 skipped).

Not run: a real OTLP collector end-to-end; CUDA/HIP/SYCL engine builds (no engine code touched).

### Limits

Opt-in only: with `--trace-otlp` unset the server path is unchanged. Traces carry no prompt text; the documented exception is errored requests. SYCL scripts in this branch are packaging scripts, not engine code.

pulls.title: bench: community report - GTX 1080 Ti (sm_61), STRATA_DENSE_F32 A/B: gemm_f32_parity bitwise on cuBLAS 12.8.4.1
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
A results-only PR: an A/B of the opt-in `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1` (#2178) on a second sm_61 card, on a cuBLAS the route had not been checked against, following [COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md](docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md).

## What it adds

- `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-gtx-1080-ti-dense-f32-ab/`: the `gemm_f32_parity --bench` output, four per-arm transcripts, the A/B runner script, and a README in the report format.
- One list entry in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`, one sentence in `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md` (the parity check now also passed on cuBLAS 12.9 and 12.8.4.1).

## What it leaves alone

Everything else: no engine, setup or tool change, and no default is flipped — `STRATA_DENSE_F32` stays opt-in exactly as #2178 shipped it.

## Hardware and headline numbers

GTX 1080 Ti 11 GB (sm_61, GPU on NUMA node 1, bound per #2684), 2x Xeon E5-2696 v4, driver 580.178.04, CUDA 12.8 toolkit (cuBLAS 12.8.4.1), engine 0.1.44.1 source build, Flash-Next IQ3_S, 262,144-token context, prompt chunk auto = 4,608. Same binary in both arms, arms alternated A B A B, one instance at a time, each arm started at 57-58 C.

| | `STRATA_DENSE_F32=0` | `=1` | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ~565-token prompt, tok/s | 240.4 (232-244) | 257.0 (249-260) | +6.9% |
| ~7,047-token prompt, tok/s | 341.4 (331-356) | 375.2 (359-404) | +9.9% |
| decode, tok/s | 27-34 | 28-34 | unchanged (noise) |

`gemm_f32_parity` on this cuBLAS: **5,201 sizes bitwise equal** — same count as the P40's cuBLAS 12.4.5.8 and the P100/cuBLAS 12.9 run in #2178. The 7,040/7,041 cuBLAS kernel cliff is present on this card too (qsa query 121.7 -> 60.7 ms).

## Limitations

Speed only: no answer-identity or quality suite was run (bitwise parity is the correctness argument here). Short and 7K prompts only; one card; one cuBLAS; Linux. The gain is smaller than the P40's because this card's chunk is 4,608 tokens and cuBLAS 12.8's FP16-operand kernels sit on the fast side at several of those sizes.

Related: #2178 (the route), #2642 (the same machine's suite report), #2684 (the NUMA binding both arms ran under).

pulls.title: web: one long-lived stream instead of a poll per second, and a language pack (#2686, #2687)
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2687, resolves #2686

## Summary

The web app stopped asking the server once a second and now keeps one long-lived response open instead, and it
speaks more than one language: a UTF-8 pack per language under `serve/web/i18n`, Simplified Chinese first.

Two issues, one change each:

- **#2687 (bug):** the page rewrote its own text on every poll, which fought Chrome's page translation and flipped
  the UI back to English - once a second on the Monitor. A stream writes only when something actually changed, and
  nothing at all while nothing does. The page also sets `translate="no"`, so the browser stops offering to translate
  a page that now translates itself.
- **#2686 (feature):** one JSON pack per language, chosen from the browser's own language or from a new switch
  under About > Settings. **UTF-8 everywhere, never GBK/cp936.**

## What changed

- `serve/server.py`: `GET /metrics/stream` and `GET /api/requests/stream` - one `text/event-stream` response each,
  written to only when what the page draws from changed. `?every=N` (1..60, default 1) sets the server's tick;
  `?requests=all` keeps the "Show all" behaviour. Both end when the tab closes (the next tick notices the socket) or
  when the server stops, and both use the existing API-key check. `GET /i18n` lists the packs; `/web/i18n/<lang>.json`
  serves them as `application/json; charset=utf-8`. No path may leave the folder.
- `serve/web/app.js`, `serve/web/monitor.js`: open that stream with `EventSource`. A server without the routes never
  delivers an event, so the page falls back to its old timer - an older server behaves exactly as it did before.
- `serve/web/i18n/en.json`, `serve/web/i18n/zh-CN.json`: 305 keys each, one UTF-8 file per language, with a `meta`
  (`name`, `dir`). `index.html` carries `data-i18n` keys and `app.js` builds its runtime strings through `t()`.
- `serve/web/index.html`, `serve/web/monitor.html`: `translate="no"`.
- `serve/test_web_stream.py`: 17 tests - the streams (the event and its payload, the API key, the client hanging up,
  the server stopping), the packs (valid UTF-8, no BOM, the same key set, served as UTF-8 JSON, no path out of the
  folder), and the pack logic itself run in node with the DOM stubbed out.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: what the streams and the packs are, and how to add a language.

## What it leaves alone

The engine, the OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, the model's answers, the installer and the default path. An English browser
on a current server sees the same page it saw before, and a page on a server without `/metrics/stream` keeps polling
as it always did.

## Extra Notes

**How I checked**

- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_web_stream`: 17 passed.
- `serve.test_monitor`, `serve.test_runconfig`, `serve.test_security`, `serve.test_server`: 356 tests, the 3 errors
  are the pre-existing `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'regex'` from `tools/strata_tokenizer.py` - they fail
  on a clean checkout here too, before this change.
- `node --check` on `app.js` and `monitor.js`; every touched file decoded as UTF-8 with no BOM.

**On the translation itself**

The wording is translated, the terms are not, and a test asserts it: **token** stays "token(s)" - never 代币 or
令牌 - and VRAM, PCIe, Prefill, Decode, MTP, KV cache, Top-p, Top-k, seed, GPU, CPU and API key are left as they
are, because they are what the user reads in the logs, in the docs and in their own client.

**Adding a language later**

Drop a `<lang>.json` next to `en.json` with the same keys and a `meta`: `GET /i18n` picks it up and the Settings
switch lists it. A key a pack lacks shows as the key, never as a blank, so a pack can lag behind the page.

**How the stream was measured**

I did not measure bytes on the wire. What I can say from the code: the old path was one `GET /metrics` per second
per open tab, each answered with the full payload (~7 KB of JSON with a minute of history per series). The new path
is one request per tab, then an event only when the fingerprint of `live`, `hardware`, `totals`, `engine`,
`conversation_cache` and the newest request changes - so an idle Monitor, which is most of the time, gets nothing
after the first event.

pulls.title: tools tests: the golden compare takes either platform's engine names, on both sides
pulls.author: clothespin
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none. No open issue or pull request covers this (searched `test_setup_golden`, `strata-vision.exe` and `golden`).
It is a test-only bug, separate from #2041, which is where I hit it.

## Summary
`tools/test_setup_golden.py` cannot match the committed baseline on Linux. The baseline was recorded on Windows, so its
five unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL configs hold `"<T>/engine/strata-vision.exe"`, while on Linux setup writes `strata-vision`
(`setup.py:498`, `VEXE = "strata-vision.exe" if WIN else "strata-vision"`). `normalize()` replaced only `setup.EXE`, and
only in the config it had just written - the baseline read back in `setUpClass` was compared as it was. Every
UD-Q4_K_XL case therefore differs on Linux: 8 failures, on a clean checkout of `origin/main` (`296b59d2`) as much as on a
branch. One commit, `tools/test_setup_golden.py` only; `tools/test_setup_golden.json` is untouched.

Re-recording with `--write` is not the fix. On Linux it changes exactly those five lines and nothing else, which makes
the baseline Linux-spelled and moves all five onto Windows.

## What changed
`canonical()` maps either platform's spelling of an engine name to one placeholder (`<EXE>`, `<VEXE>`), and
`canonical_all()` runs it through the baseline in `setUpClass`, so a file recorded on either platform compares on both.
Both names come from `setup.EXE` and `setup.VEXE` with the extension stripped, so they cannot drift away from setup.
`normalize()` now calls `canonical()`.

`#973`'s rule is kept: only the whole name matches, so `strata-device.exe`, `strata-x.log` and `strata-vision-bench` are
left alone. `tools/test_setup_golden.json` is untouched, so nothing about what the baseline asserts changes - only how
the two sides are compared.

Left alone: `setup.py`, the baseline JSON, every other test.

### How I checked
Linux, no GPU used, `python tools/test_setup_golden.py`:
- before, on a clean checkout of `origin/main` (`296b59d2`): `FAILED (failures=8)` - 5 in `test_yes`, 3 in
  `test_enter_for_every_question` (the other two UD-Q4_K_XL profiles are skipped by the existing `ram < 48` guard);
- after: `OK`, 4 tests;
- the mapping is symmetric: `"<T>/engine/strata-vision.exe"` and `"<T>/engine/strata-vision"` both reduce to
  `"<T>/engine/<VEXE>"`, as do `strata.exe` and `strata` to `<EXE>`, so Windows - where both sides already agree -
  behaves as it did;
- the negatives hold: `strata-device.exe`, `strata-x.log`, `strata-vision-bench` and an already-replaced `<EXE>` come
  back unchanged.
- every other `tools/test_setup_*.py` and `tools/test_strata_mcp.py` passes as it did before the change.

### Not tested
- Windows. There is no Windows machine here. On Windows `canonical()` maps `strata-vision.exe` to `<VEXE>` on both
  sides of the compare, which is what `normalize()` already did to the live side, so the change should be a no-op there
  - but that is reasoning, not a run.
- A baseline recorded on Linux. `--write` would produce one; I reverted it rather than commit a platform-specific
  baseline.

## Extra Notes
- `tools/test_setup_engine_hash.py` fails 2 tests on `main`, unrelated to this and left as it is:
  `AssertionError: SystemExit not raised` in `test_a_first_install_stops_because_there_is_nothing_to_fall_back_to`, and
  `AssertionError: 'keeping the engine that is installed' not found in ''` in
  `test_updating_keeps_the_installed_engine_instead_of_stopping`. Both are `get_prebuilt()`'s SHA-256 refusal. Worth its
  own issue.
- Until this lands, `python tools/test_setup_golden.py` reports those 8 failures on #2041's branch too, which makes that
  PR's "tests pass" line need a caveat it would rather not have.

pulls.title: [Engine] verify: STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1, a layer's light CPU expert rows join at the next layer's FFN half (heavy rows on time, 0.1 by default; opt-in)
pulls.author: lask3802
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

On one GPU with experts in RAM, every decode layer waits for the CPU pool's expert rows before its combine, and the
GPU idles while the CPU computes. This PR adds an opt-in setting, `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1`, that lets a layer go on
without the CPU's light expert rows and add them one step later, so the CPU computes them while the GPU runs the next
layer's mixer.

- Before, and after with `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU` unset or `0`: unchanged. No allocation, no graph node, no kernel
  choice and no host step changes. (With `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` or the #649 trace on, the profile has one more stamp
  at the end of the mixer's out-projection: "late rows", near 0 then.)
- After, with `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1`: the CPU rows of routing weight below 0.1 (`STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_BELOW`)
  join layer l at layer l+1's FFN half; the heavier ones are waited for in their own layer. **This changes the
  output.** On 0.2.0-beta, on an RTX 2080 Ti alone, it is +15.4% decode tok/s at low context at a teacher-forced KL of
  0.098 against the default (Validation). On the earlier base of this PR (v0.1.44.1, an RTX 3080) it was +15.8% at a
  KL of 0.088, about the KL of the shipped route tail skip (0.083).

This PR is now rebased on `main` (0.2.0-beta) after the tracker reset; the earlier description was for v0.1.44.1.

## Related discussion

- #2689 (deferring every CPU row) was folded into this PR and closed before the tracker reset.
- No scope issue. The change is opt-in and changes no default.

## Approach

With `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1`:

- post(l) combines without the CPU's light rows (routing weight below `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_BELOW`, 0.1 by default)
  and does not wait for them. It waits only for the heavy rows: the pool computes the experts of the CPU entries whose
  weight is >= w first, raises a new mapped flag (`h_pflag_`, to the layer's ring), then computes the rest. The rows
  come out as in one pass: the pool cuts its phases by output rows, so only the order of the jobs changes. post(l)
  combines the heavy rows with a new kernel `copy_rows_by_weight` (the plan's GPU rows zeroed as
  `copy_rows_from_mapped` does).
- pre(l+1) runs its mixer (attention or GDN), then waits for layer l's flag, copies the light rows and adds them to the
  residual with layer l's own routing weights and pending-write coefficient, `2*sigmoid(inject/hc)` (new kernel
  `defer_add_rows`), then does its FFN-side read as usual.
- In a window that defers, the doorbell publishes the routing weights too (`doorbell_publish`, the variant
  `--remote-expert-opt` uses), and `run` / `service` hand the pool the weights and a partial hook for the deferred
  layers.

Nothing the late addition reads is overwritten before it: pre(l+1)'s attention-side read writes `inj_` (not layer l's
`inj2_`), and its router (`w_`), the next plan (`plan_`, `skip_`) and its doorbell come after the addition. So the
host's next expert step never rewrites the doorbell payload or `h_ymiss_` earlier than without deferral, and no buffer
is doubled.

Not deferred: the stage's last layer, and layer 0 when layer 1 runs the PLE block. Windows that run without deferral
(one line at the first capture says which and why): batch windows, `--spec-split` token groups, `--remote-expert-opt`,
`STRATA_PCIE_BALANCE`, the all-resident graph (no CPU rows), a stage with no layer to defer, a control vector on the
stage.

The split is turned off, and every CPU row joins late, when the verifier takes the device plan
(`STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`) and with `--peer-device` or a helper cache (`--expert-cache-device1..3`), whose rows
land after the CPU's (one start-up line). `run` and `service` raise the partial flag after every pool call, so a layer
the pool did not split never leaves a GPU wait behind. The new flag is released with the others before the engine
ends (#267) and shows in the stall diagnostics.

`STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=check` runs the same steps but adds the rows back right after layer l's own combine: no
deferral, the default's sums in another order.

What changed in the rebase on 0.2.0-beta (two places where 0.2's code meets the deferral):

- `STRATA_PCIE_BALANCE=1` times each layer's wait for the CPU rows in its GPU fit, and a deferred layer does not make
  that wait. With both set, `init` turns the deferral off with one line, and `defer_ok` refuses a window with balance
  stamps.
- The 149-cold batches (`STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP=1`, `2` or `3`) compute a layer's CPU experts in batches, inside the job
  loop, when some of their reads are still pending. Such a layer is not split: it waits for all its CPU rows (one
  line, said once). With mode 0 or 4 (4 is the Linux default for the GGUF read in place, which reads everything before
  the pool runs) nothing changes for the split.

Compatibility: SYCL (`sycl/`) has its own copies of every touched source and header except `verify_kernels.hpp`,
which only gains declarations, so nothing it compiles changes. On Metal the calls of the new entry points are
compiled out (`#if !defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)`); the Metal window returns from `init` before the env is read. HIP
compiles the same CUDA sources.

Docs: a DETAILS.md section next to the route tail skip and the PCIe share.

## Validation

Revision: this branch, built and tested at `57cc1beb` on `main` `e88ee39d` (v0.2.0-beta + 12 commits); the tip
`58c72607` differs from it only in three lines of `docs/DETAILS.md`. Baseline for the tests: `e88ee39d` itself, built
and run the same way.

**Passed:**

- Linux CUDA build, all targets: Ubuntu 24.04 (a Proxmox container), GCC 13.3, CUDA 13.0.88, sm_75;86, Release,
  native experts, `ninja -C build all` (368 steps) rc=0, both for this branch and the baseline. The touched sources
  recompiled with their warnings shown: the three warnings (an unused variable in `raise_flag`, a `#pragma clang`
  and an unreferenced kernel in `verify_kernels.cu`) are all in code this change does not touch.

pulls.title: verify: STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1, a layer's CPU expert rows join at the next layer's FFN half (opt-in)
pulls.author: lask3802
pulls.body:
## What it changes

On one GPU with experts in RAM, every decode layer waits for the CPU pool's expert rows before its combine, and the GPU
idles while the CPU computes. With `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1`:

- post(l) combines without the CPU's rows (shared expert, VRAM hits and the PCIe share only) and does not wait. The CPU
  rows are zeroed by a small kernel (`fill_zero`, not a memset node, so the window graph stays kernel-to-kernel).
- pre(l+1) runs its mixer (attention or GDN), then waits for layer l's flag, copies the rows and adds them to the
  residual with layer l's own routing weights and pending-write coefficient, `2*sigmoid(inject/hc)` (new kernel
  `defer_add_rows`), then does its FFN-side read as usual.

So the CPU computes layer l while the GPU runs layer l+1's mixer. That mixer is the only part that runs without layer
l's CPU rows; its router, experts and everything after see them. **This changes the output** (see Quality).

Not deferred: the stage's last layer, and layer 0 when layer 1 runs the PLE block (pre(1) copies the PLE rows, which
the host writes just before flag 1, and relies on post(0)'s wait). Windows that run without deferral (one line at the
first capture says which and why): batch windows, `--spec-split` token groups, `--remote-expert-opt`, the
all-resident graph (no CPU rows), a stage with no layer to defer, a control vector on the stage.

`STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=check` runs the same steps but adds the rows back right after layer l's own combine: no
deferral, the default's sums in another order.

The profile (`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE`) and the #649 trace get one more stamp (slot 15) at the end of the mixer's
out-projection: "out-proj" now ends there and the next interval is "late rows" (the late wait and add). Without
deferral "late rows" is the cost of one stamp; the stamp is a graph node only when the profile or the trace is on.

Docs: a DETAILS.md section next to the route tail skip and the PCIe share.

Where it came from: we run a two-machine setup on top of the remote stage (#1748), where the main machine's GPU waits
for its CPU pool in every layer and was the bottleneck. Deferring the CPU rows by one mixer helped there, and the same
wait exists on a single PC with one GPU, which is what this PR is about and what the numbers below are from.

## What it leaves alone

- Unset (or `0`): no allocation, no graph node, no kernel choice and no host step changes. The env is read once in
  `Verifier::init`; the extra device buffer (`T * k * n_embd` floats) is carved after every other buffer, only when on.
- The host loop (`run`, `service`) is unchanged. Nothing the late addition reads is overwritten before it: pre(l+1)'s
  attention-side read writes `inj_` (not layer l's `inj2_`), and its router (`w_`), the next plan (`plan_`, `skip_`)
  and its doorbell come after the addition. So the host's next expert step never rewrites the doorbell payload or
  `h_ymiss_` earlier than without deferral, and no buffer is doubled.
- SYCL (`sycl/`) and Metal (`metal/`) are not touched. SYCL builds its own, hand-merged `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`;
  the shared `verify_kernels.hpp` only gains two declarations. Bringing the deferral to SYCL would mean merging
  `late_add` into that file and porting `defer_add_rows` and `fill_zero` to `verify_kernels.dp.cpp`. On Metal the
  two calls of the new entry points are compiled out (`#if !defined(STRATA_GPU_METAL)`), so no link stub is needed;
  the Metal window returns from `init` before the env is read.

## Measured

GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (ISTA-DASLab), RTX 3080 10 GB alone (PCIe 4.0 x8, 13.0 GB/s) + Ryzen 9 5900XT, DDR4-3000, Linux;
`--serve` with the setup's config as it is (expert cache auto: 1,404 slots in every arm, the PCIe share automatic), one
fresh engine per arm, order unset, `=1`, two arms of the follow-up PR, unset again. Low context: 12
prompts x 200 tokens, three rounds, mean decode tok/s per round, the median of the three. High context: 3 prompts of
~29-30K tokens read from 0, 200 tokens each, the median of the three. The arms ran on an earlier build of the
follow-up PR #2690 (this branch + its row split, which that build left off unless asked: its `=1` matches this branch's
within two runs of one binary, below).

| arm | low context decode, tok/s | vs unset | high context decode, tok/s | vs unset |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| unset (two runs: 58.88, 58.49) | 58.69 | - | 52.10 | - |
| `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1` | 67.74 | +15.4% | 61.00 | +17.1% |

The prompt read does not change (deferral is decode only): 956-962 tok/s at ~30K in both arms. The high-context
numbers are noisier: the first of the three prompts was the slowest in every arm (44.8-56.3), so take +17% as +15-20%.

## Quality

The output changes. Teacher-forced log-probabilities (`STRATA_LOGPOS`, top 20) on the same machine and model, 4 slices
of plain text, 5,257 positions, read through the verify windows (`--short-read 100000`) so every position takes the
decode path, `--pcie-frac 0`; mean top-20 KL(unset || run) and top-1 agreement with unset, by position in the prompt.
The row `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` is the scale: it is how far the shipped default (route tail skip on, since 0.1.42)
is from the engine without it, on the same text.

| run against unset | KL 0-7 | KL 8-63 | KL 64-639 | KL 640+ | KL all | top-1 agreement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| unset again (the floor) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0004 | 0.0006 | 0.0005 | 99.81% |
| `=check` | 0.0012 | 0.0099 | 0.0123 | 0.0209 | 0.0165 | 96.77% |
| `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` (scale) | 0.0042 | 0.1030 | 0.0641 | 0.0740 | 0.0705 | 93.93% |
| `=1` | 0.0120 | 0.2732 | 0.2113 | 0.8799 | 0.5557 | 81.42% |

`=check` is the same sums in another order: above the floor, as rounding differences grow along the prompt, and a
quarter of the scale. `=1` is the cost of the feature: about 8 times the scale over the whole text, most of it late in
the long prompts (640+). That is why it is opt-in, and why the follow-up keeps the heavy rows on time.

For scale, DETAILS.md's own numbers (a different protocol: greedy answers):

| reference (DETAILS.md, "Missed experts in a verify window") | mean KL |
|---|---|
| route tail skip (default since 0.1.42), RTX 3060 IQ3_XXS / RTX A4000 Q2_0, greedy | 0.0058 / 0.0032 |
| Q2_0 against IQ3_XXS, the same text | 0.1006 |
| the same engine run twice (the floor) | 0.0006-0.0007 |

#2690 (`STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_BELOW`, stacked on this one) keeps the heavy CPU rows on time and cuts most of this deviation for a
small part of the speed.

## Two GPUs in one PC

Checked by reading the code and building it; not run, as we have no PC with two GPUs.

| setup | deferral | why |
|---|---|---|
| layer split over two cards (`--layer-split`, `--split-device`), serial windows | works | each stage is its own `Verifier` with its own layer range, flags, plan, rows and `def_parts_` (`generate.cpp` `stage_ver`, `set_stage`, per-stage `init` under its device); a stage defers its own layers but its last, so the hand-off between cards always follows a combine that waited for its rows; stage 0's `run` syncs its stream before `next_->run`; the pool routes each layer to its stage's plan (`drive_pool_split`) |
| layer split with `--pipeline-windows` | works | two verifiers per stage and parity, each with its own flags; `service` serves one layer at a time on the host thread and the pool call for a layer is synchronous, as in `run` |
| `--layer-split K --split-device 0` (both stages on one card) | works, serial | the same as above on one device (`ver_same`); upstream refuses it with `--pipeline-windows` |
| `--peer-device` | works | the peer's rows are written into the same mapped rows inside the pool call, before the layer's flag; the late addition waits for that flag. Upstream refuses `--peer-device` with a layer split |
| `--expert-cache-device1..3` (helper caches) | works | as the peer: the helper's rows land before the flag |
| `--remote-expert-opt` | not deferred | refused by `defer_ok` (its rows come back reduced through `remote_opt_->copy_rows`); one line says so |

Not verified: anything on real hardware with two GPUs (timing, a second card's driver), AMD multi-GPU.

## How it was checked

| check | how | result |
|---|---|---|
| default path byte-identical | upstream/main 296b59d2 and this branch, both built here, env unset, the teacher-forced run above | within the floor: this branch against upstream differs from position 5,033 of 5,257 on (KL 0.0001, top-1 99.92%), while the same binary run twice differs from position 1,494 on (KL 0.0005), so this run's floor is not zero; upstream against the follow-up branch, which contains this one, was byte-identical. An earlier run of this commit (2026-10-14): byte-identical to upstream, and to itself |
| `=check` within rounding of the default | `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=check` vs unset, the same run | KL 0.0165, top-1 96.77% (table above): a quarter of the scale row |
| the rename (`STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER` to `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU`) changes no step | this branch's binary before and after it, `=1`, the same run | within the floor: KL 0.0002, top-1 99.81% |
| `=1` runs and its lines appear | `strata verify: STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1 (changes the output) ...`, `capturing the N-token window (...), deferred` | both lines; the 1-, 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-token windows deferred (earlier run of this commit) |
| CUDA build | Linux, CUDA 13.0, sm_75;86, Release, native experts | built |
| CPU tests | `conv_cache_test spec_prob_test batch_rows_test conversation_validation_test conversation_transfer_test`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` | all pass |

What `=check` does not check: it adds the rows back in post(l), so it exercises the copy and the arithmetic of the late
addition but not where the wait sits in pre(l+1). Moving the late addition after the FFN-side read, or dropping its
wait, would still pass `=check`. That part rests on reading the code: a missing wait shows only when the CPU is slow
enough for the GPU to reach it first, and I have no test that forces it.

Not built: HIP (no ROCm toolchain here; the new kernels use only `fmaf`, `__expf`, `float4` and plain launches, as
other kernels in this file that already build on HIP), SYCL (none of its sources change), Metal (no Mac).
Not tested: `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1` together with deferral, two GPUs (above), AMD.

## How to try it

```
STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1      # defer (changes the output)
STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=check  # the same steps, the rows added back in the same layer (should match the default within rounding)
STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1        # optional: "late rows" is the late wait and add
```

Set it in the engine's environment (for `serve/server.py`, in the environment the server starts the engine with). The
start-up log says `STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1 (changes the output)` and, at the first capture of each window size,
`capturing the N-token window (...), deferred` or why not.

Pre-existing, not changed here: with `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`, the PLE block and a stage starting at layer 0,
pre(1) copies the PLE rows without waiting for flag 1 when post(0) skipped its wait through the device plan
(`if (ar_on()) wait_flag_ge(m_flag_, 1, cs)` in pre). This change never defers layer 0 under PLE, so it does not
touch that path. A separate issue/PR is the right place for it.

pulls.title: serve: the Profile tab in the web app (opt-in "profile": true): last request, the last 50, a measured run, the tuning with its before and after, the speed settings
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
## What it changes

With `"profile": true` (or `--profile`) the web app gets a fifth tab, **Profile**, next to About. It replaces the
standalone `/profile` page of #2661 with a tab, so the page and the tab do not show the same data twice. Its five cards:

1. **Last request**: the prompt read by phase, the decode window in ms, the hit rate, the PCIe share, KV streaming. A
   line says when a request is running.
2. **Recent requests**: the last 50 requests' timings as three bar sparklines and a table.
3. **Measured run**: `tools/strata_profile.py` with one click: progress, then its three tables and the findings, each
   finding with a chip per setting it names (loaded now / next load).
4. **Tune this PC**: setup's calibration with one click (after a confirm): the elapsed time, then a before/after table
   of the calibrated flags, the calibration's tok/s and the server's note.
5. **Settings that matter for speed**: for 14 settings, the value the running engine reports, the value the next load
   will use, the value the run config file has, one plain sentence and what the last run said about it.

Server side:
- `GET /profile/history` (new): the last 50 requests, read from the engine log (`ProfileHistory`, in memory, timings
  only, no prompts or answers; driven by the `/metrics` poll).
- `GET /profile/settings` (new): the three columns above. It never shows `api_key`, another env value or a path
  (`expert_profile_save` is only `"set"` or null).
- `/profile/status`: `report.findings` (each with the settings it names) and `tune.report` (summary, tok/s, before/after
  rows).
- `GET /profile` is now a 302 to `./#profile` (`../#profile` for `/profile/`), relative, so it works behind a prefix.
- `/health` gains `"profile": true` only when the tab is on.
- `serve/web/profile.html` and `serve/web/profile.js` are deleted. No new file, no new dependency, no CDN.

Server data reaches the page through `textContent` only (a test checks the Profile section of `app.js` has no
`innerHTML`). Both POSTs keep the own-page check (JSON only, no foreign `Origin`, the key when one is set).

## What it leaves alone

The engine, `tools/strata_profile.py`, `tools/calibrate.py` and setup's calibration. No new run-config keys; speed flags
are not edited from the tab. Replicas and HIP are not supported for tuning, as in #2661 (`tune_unavailable` says so).
`/api-monitor` is unchanged.

## Stacked on #2660 and #2661

This branch is `8cd43878` (#2660's `tools/strata_profile.py` + #2661's page) plus one commit. It replaces #2661's
standalone page with the tab. The maintainer can take #2661 alone (the page) or both (the tab instead of the page);
the code is the same either way.

## The default stays as it was

- No line of the engine start path (`StrataEngine.start`, `child_env`) changes. `test_child_env_sets_them_only_with_the_key`
  stays green.
- With no `profile` key: `/health` has no `profile` key. On the mock engine (`--engine mock`) `/health` is
  byte-identical to `8cd43878` (same md5, `fa87eb45...`), and `/profile`, `/profile/history`, `/profile/settings` answer
  404.
- The tab button is `hidden` in `index.html`; only `health.profile === true` shows it. No profile request is made when
  it is off (checked in a browser: 0 fetches).
- `/metrics` never reads the history when it is off. `test_off_by_default` pins this and the `/health` key set. I
  checked the test by mutation: removing the `if self.profile is not None` guard in `metrics()` fails it, and so does
  making `/health` always send a `profile` key.
- Two changes on the default path, both named in the design: the help text of the `profile` key in `/config`
  ("... show the Profile tab ..."), and a `data-key` attribute on the About tab's Model settings inputs. One more:
  typing `#profile` with the tab off now shows a card that says how to turn it on, instead of falling back to Chat.
- Words in two profile-only strings changed from "page" to "tab" (the 503 while tuning, `--profile` help).

## Tests

All without a GPU, from the repository root with `python3 -m unittest`:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `serve.test_profile` | 50 tests, OK (19 before this change) |
| `serve.test_runconfig` | 9, OK |
| `serve.test_monitor` | 10, OK |
| `serve.test_lifecycle` | 9, OK |
| `serve.test_security` | 23, OK |
| `tools.test_strata_profile` | 28, OK |
| `serve.test_server` | 314, 3 errors, the same 3 on `8cd43878` (`No module named 'regex'` in this environment) |
| `node --check serve/web/app.js` | OK |

New tests cover: the history (order, open entry, ring of 50, engine starts, whole lines and 1 MiB, a log that was
emptied or replaced, a long tail without a newline, a batch that cannot be parsed, lines written during a tuning),
`finding_settings` (and that every setting `strata_profile.findings` names is mapped, so a change of its wording fails),
the settings rows, the tune before/after (numbers compared as numbers, the table without the summary line), the
redirects, the key guards, and that the tab's ids are in `index.html` and `app.js`.

## Measured, on a named PC

RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB + Ryzen 7 5800X3D, Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, one run each:
- The timing switches (on while `profile` is on) cost 3.9-4.7% on an 8K-token prompt read, decode within its noise:
  `bench/results/2026-10-15-timing-switches-rtx-5070-ti`.
- A profile run from the tab took 47 s with the model loaded.
- The tuning took 681 s and wrote `--pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.70 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160
  --adapt-decay 0.97` (96.6 tok/s by the calibration's own measurement). One run, no `bench/results` folder for it.

## Checked end to end on that PC

Headless Chromium against the running server with `"profile": true`: no console error, page error or failed request.
- `/health` has the key; the tab shows; `#profile` lands on it; the off card is hidden.
- A chat request: Last request shows its decode tok/s, hit rate and window split; while it runs the in-flight line shows
  "A request is running (Generating · ...)"; the history row appears.
- Run the profile: "Running · 2 s" with the tool's step line; with the tab switched away for 13 s the page sent 2
  `/profile/status` requests (the 10 s away poll); back on the tab: "Done in 47 s", the three tables, 9 findings with 9
  setting chips, the report path.
- Tune: the confirm text appears and Cancel changes nothing.
- "Model settings" in the settings card opens About with the `vram_reserve_mib` input focused.
- `GET /profile` -> 302 `./#profile`, `/profile/` -> `../#profile`. Light and dark themes both render.

A sub-agent reviewer read the diff and ran the checks above on a second mock server and a headless browser; it gave 12
findings (the history filling with the calibration's requests during a tune, a wrong "no setting changed" after a
re-tune, parts of the page rebuilt every 2 s while a run goes, a misleading note for flags the server adds itself, and
smaller ones). All 12 are fixed in this commit, each with a test where the code can be tested. For the fourth I chose
the plain wording: the row says "the run config file has X; the server reads it when Strata starts", because the next
start's flags (`engine_args`, the shell's environment) are not the file's.

One thing in the design is wrong and is not followed: "If the summary says the defaults were already the fastest, the
table has no bold row". A second tuning puts earlier tuned values back to the defaults, so rows do change; the tab
says that in words.

The standalone companion, [Strata Profile Studio](https://github.com/qiuzan2001/strata-profile-studio) (Python standard library only), reads this tool's reports and compares runs against the noise floor of the PC, with a sign test over the agent turns.

pulls.title: tests: cuda_spill_guard fails the CUDA test build when a Strata kernel spills or keeps a per-thread array in local memory
pulls.author: Avicennasis
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2682 (re-filed from #1758)

## Summary
A test-build gate that fails when a release CUDA kernel spills registers or keeps a per-thread array in local memory, per `sm_`. Spills are compiler-output facts, like #1522 and #1469: they show up in the resource report and nowhere in the source, they vary by toolkit and architecture, and they cost decode throughput silently. The compiler writes that report into every object, so the gate reads the kernel libraries that were built anyway with `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` — no build-flag change, no GPU at test time — and mirrors `tools/check_isa_guard.py` in shape. Its table carries the measured state of `296b59d2` on sm_86 and sm_120, so it is green today and documents what is there; from here it holds the line.

## What changed
- `tools/check_cuda_spills.py` (new, 282 lines). Per library, per entry function, per SASS arch: REG, STACK, LOCAL, SHARED from `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` (demangled with `cu++filt` beside it, or binutils `c++filt`). A kernel must have STACK 0 and LOCAL 0 on every `sm_` unless `ALLOWED` carries its allowance for that `sm_`: 37 entries, 53 (kernel, `sm_`) allowances, each the measured maximum with one line above it saying what the array is, or what spilled (stores / loads at the register count ptxas settled on, and the launch bounds). Keyed by the demangled name without template arguments and parameters, so every instantiation of a template kernel shares one entry. The vendored llama.cpp ggml kernels (`mul_mat_q`, `mul_mat_q_stream_k_fixup`, `quantize_mmq_*`, `quantize_q8_1`; instantiated into `strata_mmq`, `strata_mmq_w4a4`, `strata_kq`) are skipped by the one property that singles them out — no namespace at all; every Strata kernel sits in `strata::` or an anonymous namespace — and the report line counts them. `--list` prints every kernel on every `sm_` as CSV, judging nothing; that is how the table's numbers were produced. Exit 0 clean / 1 a violation naming kernel, `sm_`, STACK and LOCAL / 77 when `cuobjdump` or a library is missing, or a library yields no SASS entry function (a pass with nothing counted is not a pass).
- `CMakeLists.txt` (+22): registers `cuda_spill_guard` under `STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA AND STRATA_BUILD_TESTS AND NOT STRATA_ENABLE_HIP AND NOT STRATA_HIP_GFX906` over `$<TARGET_FILE:…>` of `strata_kernels`, `strata_core`, `strata_engine`, `strata_prefill`, `strata_qwen35`, `strata_mmq`, `strata_mmq_w4a4`, `strata_kq` (each guarded by `if(TARGET)`), passing `${CUDAToolkit_BIN_DIR}/cuobjdump`; `find_package(Python3 QUIET)` guarded — no Python, no test, with a status line saying so. `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77`, `TIMEOUT 600`.

### Measured on `296b59d2` (CUDA 13.1, nvcc/cuobjdump V13.1.80, cmake 3.28.3 + ninja, Release, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;120"`, Ubuntu 24.04 container, no GPU)

| | kernels | collapsed names | (kernel, sm) entries | with a stack frame | spilling | spill-free arrays |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gated (Strata) | 1351 | 359 | 2702 | 150 | 61 | 89 |
| skipped (vendored ggml) | 909 | 6 | 1972 | 538 | — | — |

LOCAL is 0 everywhere on this toolkit: spills and per-thread arrays both land in STACK. `cuobjdump`'s STACK/REG agree with `ptxas -v`'s stack frame / registers on every one of the 4720 joined rows (one TU rebuilt with `-Xptxas -v`: identical SASS, only the `ptxasOptions` metadata differs).

The 21 Strata kernels that actually spill (template arguments collapsed; maxima over their instantiations):

| kernel | library | sm | instantiations spilling | stack frame B | spill stores B | spill loads B | registers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `strata::kernels::native_down_amd_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::native_gu_amd_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 3 | 16 | 12 | 12 | 80 |
| `strata::kernels::native_gu_fused_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::native_gu_fused_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 12 | 24 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::native_gu_lds_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 2 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 80 |
| `strata::kernels::native_gu_lds_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 4 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::block_topk_reg_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 112 | 196 | 284 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::block_topk_reg_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 88 | 88 | 276 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 128 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_down_q8_fast_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 8 | 128 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_down_q8_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 2 | 16 | 12 | 24 | 128 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_down_staged_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 4 | 16 | 16 | 16 | 80 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_down_staged_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 2 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 80 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_down_v3_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 12 | 8 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_up_q8_fast_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 8 | 16 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::gr_up_v3_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 2 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 40 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_down_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_down_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 2 | 24 | 12 | 12 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_down_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 4 | 64 | 16 | 16 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_gu_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_gu_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 3 | 8 | 4 | 4 | 80 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_gu_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 7 | 112 | 52 | 64 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_gu_multi_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 2 | 96 | 56 | 64 | 48 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::native_mmvq_il_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 3 | 24 | 60 | 60 | 56 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::prompt_attn_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 2 | 8 | 4 | 12 | 72 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::s27_down_kernel` | kernels | sm_86 | 1 | 16 | 12 | 12 | 64 |
| `strata::kernels::{anonymous}::s27_gu_kernel` | kernels | sm_120 | 1 | 16 | 20 | 20 | 64 |
| `strata::prefill::fused::{anonymous}::native_kernel` | mmq | sm_120 | 2 | 32 | 32 | 32 | 128 |
| `strata::prefill::fused::{anonymous}::native_kernel` | mmq | sm_86 | 6 | 32 | 36 | 52 | 128 |

The other 89 framed entries are spill-free per-thread arrays: `route*`'s `values[16]`, `attn_chunk_kernel`'s `float a[3][32]` (384 B, sm_86 only — sm_120 keeps it in 142 registers), `copy_kernel`'s `Runs` parameter copied to the stack to index it, `s26`/`s27`'s `wr[]`/`s[][]`, `gr_write_*`'s `x`/`v[10]`, the prefill `route_kernel`'s `v[16]`, Q3_K's `uint32_t aux[4]`, `gdn_step_commit_kernel<true>`'s `printf` argument buffer, `gr_down_kernel`'s `gw`/`ss`, and 32 bytes each in `rope_kernel` and `k_attn_prep` whose array I did not locate in the source (their entries say so). The spills are findings, not changed here; the table is the current state, so the gate passes on `296b59d2` and any growth from here is a red test.

### The gate, run
`ctest -R cuda_spill_guard` on the branch, both arches in one build:
```
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_kernels.a: 1234 kernels on sm_120, sm_86 (2468 entries; 0 vendored ggml entries skipped), 132 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_prefill.a: 49 kernels on sm_120, sm_86 (98 entries; 0 vendored ggml entries skipped), 8 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_qwen35.a: 31 kernels on sm_120, sm_86 (62 entries; 0 vendored ggml entries skipped), 2 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_mmq.a: 33 kernels on sm_120, sm_86 (66 entries; 1306 vendored ggml entries skipped), 8 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_mmq_w4a4.a: 1 kernels on sm_120a, sm_86 (2 entries; 154 vendored ggml entries skipped), 0 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
check_cuda_spills: libstrata_kq.so: 0 kernels on sm_120, sm_86 (0 entries; 512 vendored ggml entries skipped), 0 use stack / local memory, 0 not allowed
1/1 Test #120: cuda_spill_guard .................   Passed    1.28 sec
```
(`strata_core` 1 kernel and `strata_engine` 2 kernels, 0 framed, 0 not allowed.)

Red, both ways, against the committed script: one allowance lowered by a byte (`attn_chunk_kernel` sm_86 384 → 383) fails with `VIOLATION void strata::kernels::<unnamed>::attn_chunk_kernel<(int)0, (bool)1, (bool)0, (bool)0>(…) sm_86: STACK 384 LOCAL 0 (over its allowance STACK 383 LOCAL 0) [qsa_decode_attn.cu.o]`, one line per instantiation, and is green again on `git checkout`; a scratch kernel with a dynamically indexed `float buf[1024]` built into `strata_kernels` fails with `VIOLATION strata::kernels::<unnamed>::spill_scratch_kernel(const float *, float *, const int *, int) sm_86: STACK 4096 LOCAL 0 (not in ALLOWED) [spill_scratch.cu.o]` (and sm_120), and is green again once removed and rebuilt. A missing library or a missing `cuobjdump` exits 77 (ctest reports the test skipped).

## Extra Notes
- Entries exist only for sm_86 and sm_120 (and `strata_mmq_w4a4`'s sm_120a, which has none): a build for sm_75 or sm_89 will report the kernels that hold a frame there as `not in ALLOWED` on its first run — the numbers for those two arches come from the first box that builds them, and go in the same way.
- Not measured: HIP and Windows paths (the test is not registered under HIP), any timing or GPU behaviour, and why ptxas settles on different register counts per arch (`gr_down_q8_kernel<7>`: 128 registers and a spill on sm_86, 206 registers and clean on sm_120 — there is no register cap in the tree that explains it).
- If you would rather have the capture live elsewhere (a CMake option next to `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS`, a CI step over the build log), say so and I will move it; the table and the numbers stay the same.

pulls.title: serve: PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files in the chat page's attach button (POST /convert, MarkItDown, optional)
pulls.author: page1
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #2676

## Summary
The chat page's attach button (or a drop) also takes .pdf, .docx, .xlsx and .pptx. The server turns each into Markdown with MarkItDown, and the page attaches it like a text file. MarkItDown is optional and not installed by setup: without it nothing changes, and the button says how to install it.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: `convert_document()` and `POST /convert` (`{"name", "data": base64}` -> `{"text"}`). It answers only Strata's own page, like `/settings`, and reads only what it is sent. Limits: 50 MB per file, 1 MB of text. Errors: 400 for another file type or bad data, 501 when MarkItDown is missing (with the pip command for the running Python), 422 for a damaged or protected file.
- `serve/web/app.js`, `index.html`: the attach button accepts the four types and sends them to `/convert`.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: a short section, with the install line for Windows and Linux. No OCR: a scanned PDF is refused with "No text found".
- `serve/test_server.py`: `ConvertDocuments` (other types refused, own page only, a PDF, a damaged file); the two that need MarkItDown skip without it.

## Extra Notes
Tests: all 43 `serve/test_*.py` suites pass without MarkItDown; the 4 `ConvertDocuments` tests pass with markitdown 0.1.8 (Windows 11, Python 3.13), where a 342 KB PDF became 26K characters in 0.9 s. Not tested on Linux.

pulls.title: serve: log a reply that ended after its thinking with no text and no call (which end: inside the thinking or after </think>)
pulls.author: page1
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: related to #1053

## Summary
Agents sometimes get a turn that thinks and then stops with nothing to show: no text and no tool call. There are two ways to get there: the model ends while the parser is still in the reasoning (#1053's case, which `"reasoning_close_retry"` continues), or it closes `</think>` and stops. The server said nothing either way. Now it prints one line saying which it was.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: when a reply that had thinking finishes with `stop`, no answer and no cancel, one line is printed with the parser state, the text it held and the last 12 tokens:

```
[strata] empty answer: the reply ended after its thinking with no text or call (parser=reasoning, held='', tail='...')
```

What it leaves alone: every reply. It only prints.

## Extra Notes
Seen in use: 15 such lines while replaying real opencode sessions on IQ3_S (RTX 3090, Windows 11), all of the first kind (`parser=reasoning`, nothing held).

Tests: all 43 `serve/test_*.py` suites pass. `serve.test_responses` failed 2 times in 21 runs on this branch, both in `NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler`, a thread-count test. The same test failed 1 time in 24 runs on v0.1.44.1 under the same load (and 0 times in 24 runs on this branch), so it looks timing-sensitive rather than caused by this change.
