pulls.title: Jev System One decision endpoint (/v1/systemone): calibrated typed decisions via an opt-in BROW logits wire
pulls.author: justindressler
pulls.body:
# Jev systemone — System One decision endpoint for Strata

## Introduction

**What a System One decision model is.** Most uses of a language model are
"System Two": the model writes text and the caller reads, parses and trusts it. A
**System One** decision model does the opposite. It receives a **state** (text, JSON, or an
image) and a set of **typed questions**, and returns **typed answers with calibrated
probabilities**: a yes/no (`noul`), a pick-one (`choice`), or an ordinal rating (`score`).
It never generates prose to decide. Nothing has to be parsed, and the confidence is a number
the caller can threshold, route on, or log, rather than a sentence the model chose to write.
That makes it suited to fast, repeatable, auditable decisions inside a loop: routing,
guardrails, triage, scoring, and game or agent control.

**Jev.** "Jev" is TypeSafe's commercial System One decision API: `POST /v1/systemone` with
`{state, questions}`, answers read from token probabilities rather than generated text. Its
request/response shape is the wire this work follows. Open implementations of the same idea
already exist (see References); the goals here are correctness, speed and honest
probabilities, not novelty.

**Laya.** Laya (`convaiinnovations/laya`, Apache-2.0) approaches the same contract with a
different mechanism: a small purpose-trained encoder (ModernBERT-large, 421M parameters;
non-autoregressive) that answers all questions in one forward pass (~33 ms reported),
trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD) so that
honest probabilities are what maximises reward. Two things in its documentation shaped this PR: its probabilities ship
over-confident until a temperature is refit **per question type and option count**
(reported mean ECE 0.466 → 0.081, with the instruction to do this on your own data before
trusting them), and its comparison against Jev uses third-party published Jev figures
that it did not measure itself. We kept the first idea (per-tuple calibration, refit on
local data) and measured our own numbers on our own harness. The mechanism differs: a
general LLM read at its label logits, with no task-specific training.

**jevcpp.** The reference implementation this port follows: a llama.cpp-based server that
serves the Jev wire from a generative model by reading the label logits at the final
prompt position (Qwen3.8-27B, with a shipped calibration file and a metamorphic/golden test
set). Its plan and amendments define the request contract, the frozen prompt template, the
readout math and the test strategy that this PR ports.

**What this PR does.** It brings that System One surface to **Strata**. Strata's engine could
already dump logprobs for verification, but had no per-request way to read the logits of
arbitrary label tokens. This PR adds an opt-in `--jev-brow` engine wire (`BROW`) that returns
the final-row logits for exactly the label tokens asked, and a serve-layer
`/v1/systemone` endpoint that applies the Jev readout math and **per-tuple post-hoc
calibration** (Platt scaling for yes/no, temperature scaling for choice/score) on top. The
same model keeps chat, and can answer decisions inside a chat call, from an image directly,
or decide-then-narrate. It is opt-in per process (`STRATA_JEV_MODES`).

Donor reference: jevcpp on Qwen3.8-27B (q4_k_xl), shipped calibration tuple
`p-jevcpp-qwen38-27b|q4_k_xl|timber|v1|V|all` (T_choice 1.5861). This port runs on
QFN = Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS MoE (RTX 3090, Strata engine v0.1.43-lineage, 32k ctx).

## 1. Features (the full jevcpp surface)

| Feature | Request | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Core decision endpoint | `POST /v1/systemone` `{state, questions}` — noul (yes/no), choice (letters), score (0-10 levels) | ✅ live |
| Frozen D3 prompt | byte-frozen question block (donor render, `enable_thinking=false`, verbatim string states) | ✅ golden-tested |
| BROW readout | `--jev-brow` engine flag; final-row logits, fail-closed | ✅ engine commit |
| Calibration (M3.2) | post-hoc, argmax-preserving: Platt (a,c) for noul, temperature for choice/score; per-tuple (L/V/D/S) files `calib-<mode>.json`; `POST /admin/calib` hot-swap; donor-schema log rows for `fit.py` | ✅ live |
| V-mode (M3.1) | header `X-Jev-Mode: V` — per-option yes/no branches, `p = softmax(s_yes − s_no)`, name-keyed | ✅ live |
| Image → decision (M3.8) | `image_b64` + `image_mode`: `summary` (vision → 160-tok summary → decide) or **`direct`** (raw image embeddings + question, ONE readout) | ✅ live |
| Decide-then-generate (M3.9) | `"then": {"generate": {...}}` — answers folded into the last user turn, one wire request | ✅ live |
| Chat surface (M3.3) | `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"jev": {state|messages, questions}` | ✅ live |
| Concurrency | FIFO-serialized engine turns; 7 clients × 3 questions, zero cross-talk (tested) | ✅ tested |

Error contract: donor's `422` + `{"error": {"field": ...}}`. Streaming refused with the
jev extension, `state` XOR `messages`, `image_mode` validated, D+V refused with 422.

## 2. Usage

```bash
# text decision (one decode step)
curl -s $URL/v1/systemone -d '{
  "state": {"engine": "hot", "load": 0.9},
  "questions": {"q1": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Throttle?"}}}'

# image → decision, direct mode (raw image tokens decide)
curl -s $URL/v1/systemone -d '{
  "image_b64": "'"$(<screen.b64)"'", "image_mode": "direct",
  "questions": {"threat": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Enemy visible?"}}}'

# decide, then narrate
curl -s $URL/v1/systemone -d '{
  "state": {"hp": 12}, "questions": {...},
  "then": {"generate": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Narrate."}],
                        "max_tokens": 128}}}'

# MULTIPLE questions, mixed types, ONE state (each question = its own readout;
# cost scales ~linearly until prefix reuse lands)
curl -s $URL/v1/systemone -d '{
  "state": "Reactor at 84%. Coolant loop A nominal, loop B pressure rising slowly.",
  "questions": {
    "threat":  {"type": "noul",   "instructions": "Is loop B a current threat?"},
    "action":  {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which action first?",
                "criteria": {"inspect": null, "throttle": null, "shutdown": null}},
    "urgency": {"type": "score",  "instructions": "How urgent is intervention?",
                "criteria": ["none", "low", "medium", "high", "critical"]}}}'
# -> {"answers": {"threat":  {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.5429, "calib": "platt_v1"},
#                 {"action":  {"type": "choice", "choice": 0,
#                              "probabilities": [0.830, 0.160, 0.010],
#                              "confidence": 0.7453, "calib": "T_choice_v1"},
#                 {"urgency": {"type": "score", "score": 1.5928,
#                              "probabilities": [0.103, 0.374, 0.376, 0.121, 0.026],
#                              "confidence": 0.2201, "calib": "T_score_v1"}},
#      "margin": top1−top2 present on every answer (cascade-routing number)}
#     "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 303, "readout_tokens": 3}}
# (live response, QFN; note each answer carries its OWN calibrator id)

# INLINE jev on the chat surface — decisions inside an OpenAI chat call; the
# conversation itself is the state (v1-chat template), no "state" field needed
curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -d '{
  "model": "jev",
  "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are the plant supervisor."},
               {"role": "user", "content": "Loop B pressure is rising. Inspect now?"}],
  "jev": {"questions": {"inspect":
      {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Should loop B be inspected now?"}}}}'
# -> {"id": "jev-1792055290765", "object": "jev.response",
#     "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs-jevport",
#     "jev": {"answers": {"inspect": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.9230,
#                                      "calib": "platt_v1"}},
#             "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 82, "readout_tokens": 1}}}
# (live response; jev answers ride alongside the normal chat fields, so any
#  OpenAI client gets decisions without a second endpoint)

# MODE GATING — decisions are OPT-IN (donor --modes; the default differs, see section 4d)
# STRATA_JEV_MODES unset            -> "chat" ONLY: a process that never mentions
#                                      jev behaves exactly like stock Strata
# STRATA_JEV_MODES="chat,decision"  -> both (what the jevport presets run)
# STRATA_JEV_MODES="decision"       -> decision-only: no generation path at all
# Unknown tokens fail closed at load (serve refuses to start).
# "decision" gates /v1/systemone + the chat jev extension;
# "chat"     gates plain generation + then.generate narration.
# Gated surfaces return 404 not_found_error (probing learns nothing).
```

Full surface + examples: `docs/JEV-SYSTEMONE.md`. Refit calibration:
`calib/README.md` (the suite IS the procedure). Mode gating:
`STRATA_JEV_MODES` env (`"decision"` = decision-only — no generation path
exists on the instance at all; outputs are probabilities over the caller's own
labels. Unset = `"chat"` only: decisions are opt-in, and the jevport presets set
`"chat,decision"` explicitly. Fail-closed on unknown tokens and on gated
routes).

Why logit readout instead of asking the model for confidence: models asked to state their
own confidence are mostly overconfident with high calibration error (Groot &
Valdenegro-Toro, TrustNLP 2024, see References). Reading label probabilities from the
logits and calibrating them post-hoc on held-out data (Platt / temperature scaling) is the
standard alternative, and it is what this PR does; its measured effect is in section 4a.
Laya reaches the same conclusion from the training side: its probabilities also need a
temperature refit on local data before they can be trusted.

## 3. Test strategy

**Unit (mock engine) — 73/73 green (jev modules; full serve/ discovery 858 run, 0 fail, 11 skipped):** readout math invariants, prompt rendering
(byte-pinned noul/choice blocks — the Yes/No-swap regression is now a golden test),
per-tuple calibration isolation, V-mode softmax, image two-call/direct shapes,
decide-then-generate, chat-surface validation arms, 7×3 concurrency + FIFO
serialization.

**Live suites** (`calib/bench_suite.py`): dev-split fit → held-out test eval,
standard top-label ECE15 + mean NLL, per-item JSONL logs. Guards: Platt slope
a≤0 refused (label/prompt inversion detector — it caught a real bug), temperature
at search boundaries flagged.

**Adversarial audit protocol** (Justin's rule, 2026-10-15): 1-in-10 of all test
items re-verified by hand — text golds re-read from source passages, image items
regenerated from committed seeds with sha256 match against the logged hash, sampled
error images independently re-counted with vision. Result across text+image+real
suites: 0 scoring hallucinations, 0 gold errors, 1 documented CV-Bench ambiguity.
Artifacts: `audit-*.json`, `audit-imgs/`, `*-item-log.jsonl` (920 rows).

**Real-benchmark converters** (`calib/convert_benchmarks.py`): POPE adversarial,
CV-Bench, CountBenchQA via HF datasets-server; banned-field self-test (answer-bearing
fields never enter requests), sha256 image manifest, dev/test image-disjoint, POPE
sampled by image at exactly 50/50.

**Vision strategy** (externally reviewed before implementation):
6-arm design (D/S/S-QC/S-V/blind/shuffled — the last two are contamination
detectors), circular rotation for choice position bias, phased screen→full→frozen
PR gate.

## 4. Benchmarking results (all live, QFN IQ3_XXS, RTX 3090)

### 4a. Pre/post calibration (held-out test, offline replay of identical items)

| tuple (mode\|qtype\|set) | n | acc pre→post | NLL pre→post | ECE15 pre→post |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L\|noul\|BoolQ | 100 | .890 → **.910** | .298 → **.262** | .084 → **.033** |
| L\|choice\|ARC | 100 | 1.000 → 1.000 | .005 → .007 | .005 → .006 |
| L\|score\|SST-5 | 100 | .520 → .520 | 1.471 → **1.049** | .301 → .154 |
| D\|noul\|POPE-adv | 60 | .867 → **.883** | .204 → **.195** | .122 → **.081** |
| D\|choice\|CV-Bench | 20 | .650 → .650

pulls.title: cpu: decline IQ4_NL down rows for the AVX1 kernels; two cleanups
pulls.author: nashcap
pulls.body:
On CPUs that have AVX but not AVX2, IQ4_NL down rows should be computed by ggml's own dot, not by our 128-bit kernel. ggml is faster there, and always has been. That is the point of this PR: one line in the dispatch. Two small cleanups follow.

## Why these commits exist

#1697 and #1701 landed in v0.1.42 (you ported them with my authorship). I kept working on the same files after that and pushed three more commits to the #1697 thread, and they were never ported. This PR is those three, rebased onto v0.1.44.1. The diff touches only `iq_avx1.cpp`, `q2_avx1.cpp` and `iq_avx1_parity.cpp`.

## 1. IQ4_NL down rows: decline them (the fix)

The other formats this file serves have no hand-written x86 dot in ggml-cpu, which is why the 128-bit kernel wins them. IQ4_NL is the exception: ggml-cpu has a hand-written `__AVX__` dot for it (`ggml_vec_dot_iq4_nl_q8_0`, two blocks per iteration, 256-bit float accumulation). That one beats our kernel on this CPU, and I could not close the gap - I matched its two-block shape and shared the decode across tokens, and it still came out behind.

So the dispatch stops choosing our kernel for that format:

```c
-bool iq128_down_supported(int type) noexcept { return type == 20 || type == 42; }
+bool iq128_down_supported(int type) noexcept { return type == 42; }
```

The kernel stays built and parity-tested; only the dispatch declines it.

Why it is worth a PR: on the IQ3_S pack, 24 of the 33 down layers are IQ4_NL. Today an AVX1 CPU runs the slower of the two kernels for all 24 of them.

Measured as `ms/expert` with `./iq_avx1_parity --bench --mb 96 --nt 1,4 --cpu 12`, two runs of one binary:

| down rows | who wins | margin |
|---|---|---|
| IQ4_NL (type 20) | **ggml** | 0.78-0.93x, every run, never above 1.0 |
| Q2_0 (type 42) | ours | 3.5-5.4x - ggml-cpu has no x86 dot for this type at all |

The bench now prints gate/up and down separately because of this finding. The combined line had been hiding a 0.78x down path inside a 2.1x result.

## 2. Micro-optimizations, all bit-exact

- fp16 to fp32 without F16C: for normal exponents the conversion is one integer shift and add, so that path is taken branchlessly. Zero, subnormal, inf and NaN still go through the full converter.
- Q2_0 down rows: the activation's per-lane `sum(q)` does not depend on the row, so it is computed once per call instead of once per row.
- one `cvtepi32` instead of two for the int32 pair sums.
- two rows through the block loop at a time. At NT=1 the decode chain (index byte, codebook lookup, `madd`) is about 20 cycles of pure latency with nothing to overlap, so the kernel runs latency-bound at roughly a quarter of its issue rate. A second row gives the scheduler something independent to do in the meantime.

(NT is the number of tokens in one verify window that route to the same expert, set by the router. Live decode is almost entirely NT=1.)

Net effect: gate/up rows measure 1.18-1.41x against ggml at NT=1, and 2.0-2.8x at NT=4.

## 3. The two-row form only at NT=1

That pairing pays only at NT=1. At NT >= 2 the row pair plus two token accumulators does not fit in 16 XMM registers and spills: neutral-to-noisy at NT=2, and going further is actively bad - R=3 measured a wash, R=4 measured -42.6% at NT=1 on IQ3_S. So the policy is R=2 at NT=1 and R=1 otherwise. `dot_rows` had no callers left once that path existed, so it is removed.

## Answers do not change

Every change here is either bit-exact by construction (the fp16 identity, the shared `sum(q)`, the fused conversion) or a dispatch decline. Nothing touches the pack format or the converter.

## Verification

Xeon E5-2470 v2 (AVX, no AVX2 / FMA / F16C / AVX-512), RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, v0.1.44.1 source build with `-DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`:

```
iq_avx1_parity: all rows match        (8 format pairs: gu 18/21/22/23 x down 20/42)
q8k_quant_parity: AVX1 copy identical
pool tasks: 168 bitwise comparisons passed
q2_bitplane_parity: PASS
check_isa_guard: 421 functions, 69 hold wide-ISA instructions, 0 not allowed
```

A live profile of the running engine shows the dispatch doing what the code says: `row_dot_r<18,1,2>` and friends at NT=1, `row_dot_r<18,2,1>` at NT>=2, and `ggml_vec_dot_iq4_nl_q8_0` carrying the IQ4_NL down rows at 7.2% of samples while `iq128_down_rows` sits at 2.6% - which is the 24/9 split.

One honest caveat about the numbers: single-format gate/up ratios at NT=1 are noisy (iq3_xxs measured 1.19x on one run and 0.90x on the next). The down-row numbers, which are the argument of this PR, were stable across runs.

pulls.title: bench: RTX 5070 Ti + RTX 3060 vs single 5070 Ti, UD-Q4_K_XL (0.1.44.1)
pulls.author: holgin
pulls.body:
## Title

Related: #2393. Context: #2385; this report measures pinned main, **not** the unmerged planner PR.

## Summary

Same-day community measurements of **Strata 0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`)** with pinned Unsloth Flash Next **UD-Q4_K_XL**, comparing **RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB** against the **5070 Ti alone**. Intel i9-9900K at **4.7 GHz** (AVX2), **128 GiB DDR4-2800 (2800 MT/s)**, Linux, PCIe 3.0 x8 on both cards, NVMe. CPU/RAM operating settings were confirmed by the owner after measurement on 2026-10-15; they were not independently sampled by the original telemetry. Both cards remain physically installed; the 3060 drives the desktop in every arm.

Two reversed blocks contain **eight fresh services and 360 measured requests**: baseline and saved calibration settings for both GPU selections, 64K context, INT8 KV, 32K resident KV and a fixed 72 GiB resident expert budget. Each service runs the official three-repeat suite including fresh 4K/16K/32K prompts, then nine public calibration-prompt probes.

- Baseline dual improves median short-chat / simulated-agent follow-up decode by **13.57% / 15.32%**.
- Single-GPU baseline improves fresh **16K / 32K prefill by 13.34% / 5.40%**; 4K differs by less than 1%.
- Saved dual calibration does not give a general improvement: chat/probe medians fall; agent median improves 3.07%, but token-weighted decode improves only 0.61% with different generated lengths. Transferred single-GPU tuning regresses the tested decode workloads. No profile/default is promoted.

## What changed

One results-only folder under `bench/results/2026-10-14-community-rtx-5070ti-3060-ud-q4-k-xl/` contains the finished report, all individual request timings/tokens/TTFT/reuse/draft counts, engine logs, losslessly compressed numeric telemetry, exact build/model/asset provenance, calibration source, portable configuration templates, reproduction helpers and an offline verifier. `DATA.md` documents fields and units. Original upstream host GPU inventory is retained and its single-GPU labeling caveat (#2062) is explained.

No engine, server, installer, operational default, model weight or generated pack binary is changed or included. The complete submission is approximately 2 MB; telemetry is gzip-compressed to avoid a large generated-text diff.

## Validation

```text
python3 bench/results/2026-10-14-community-rtx-5070ti-3060-ud-q4-k-xl/verify.py
PASS: 360 requests / 8 services; pooled and weighted rates; comparisons; token/reuse counts; probe answer hashes; safety/OC receipts; relative links; privacy patterns; package checksums.
git diff --cached --check
```

Portable helper compilation/CLI checks, rendering all four configurations with spaced absolute paths and overwrite refusal, and mocked smoke/suite/probe ordering passed offline. No additional GPU run is implied. Backend builds are not applicable to this results-only change.

## Extra Notes

Existing OC is held constant: power limits 330 W / 187 W and unchanged LACT/device-limit receipts. No stock-versus-OC gain is claimed. All services had zero service swap/OOM, but **MemoryHigh reclaim occurred in all runs and global swap peaked at 313 MiB**; these are disclosed alongside temperatures and storage reads.

Two independent service restarts per arm, three within-service repeats, normal graphical background activity and answer-dependent agent continuations limit generalization. No coding correctness, both explicit GPU orders, manual splits, independently calibrated single-GPU optimum, 128K/native context, concurrency or uninterrupted one-hour soak was measured. This is partial unequal-GPU evidence for TEST_REQUESTS.md, not a claim that those outstanding requests are fully satisfied.

pulls.title: fix(setup) v2: don't require tensor-data alignment for GGUF shards without
pulls.author: OriginalMadman
pulls.body:
`check_shards()` and `whole_shard()` calculated the minimum GGUF shard size as
`data_start + max(tensor end offsets)`. For a shard containing no tensors, this
incorrectly required the file to extend through the aligned tensor-data start,
even though no tensor payload exists.

This caused valid metadata-only GGUF shards to be rejected as truncated. For
example, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf` was reported as
six bytes short:

- Actual file size: 10,946,618 bytes
- Parsed tensor count: 0
- Aligned data start: 10,946,624 bytes

The downloaded file matched the size and SHA-256 declared in `setup.py`.

## Change

Skip the tensor-payload extent check when a successfully parsed GGUF shard has
no tensors. GGUF parsing, the existing checks for tensor-bearing shards, and
the separate pinned size/SHA-256 verification remain unchanged.

Issue: Resolves https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2470 and https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2346
#2491

pulls.title: kv: --kv-evict clock|lrfu, the streamed page pool's victim pick (#2415)
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

The measurement half of #2415 asked whether the streamed page pool should evict by something other than the resolve kernel's clock sweep. This is the other half: the option itself.

When the pool is full the kernel evicts one block per miss. `--kv-evict clock` (the default, the engine's own) sweeps slots from a hand and takes the first that is unreferenced. `--kv-evict lrfu` keeps a per-block score that **survives eviction**, decays a little every call (the policy bench's lambda = 0.5 per 64 calls), gains on a hit, and evicts the lowest-scoring block - with ties going to the least recently used slot. That tie rule matters: a just-loaded block scores 0 and would otherwise be the first victim, where the clock sweep's reference bit gives it the same second chance.

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

The pool is a cache over an authoritative RAM copy, so **the output cannot change** - the flag only decides which blocks are re-read from RAM. Without `--kv-evict` nothing is allocated, no score is kept and the kernel takes the clock sweep exactly as before.

## How it was checked

- **`kv_stream_parity` PASS** in both modes, all four KV formats - the invariant (streamed == resident, bitwise) holds, and the two modes show the different miss counts the two picks produce on the same selections (int8: 69,581 clock vs 101,744 lrfu over 306 batches).
- **Live counters on this box's GTX 1080 Ti** (IQ3_S, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, 64K-token prompt + 128 decode tokens, ABBA):

| arm | hit rate | MiB read from RAM | tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| clock | 87.89 / 87.23 % | 489.9 / 472.5 | 27.86 / 31.63 |
| lrfu | **88.14 / 88.68 %** | 476.8 / 485.9 | 24.62 / 19.52 |

LRFU reads no more from RAM and its hit rate is a little higher, which is the direction the offline bench predicts: on real selection traces (a 4K-token prompt and a 64K-token one) `tools/replay_kv_stream_policy.py` has LRFU re-reading **2.6-6.0% fewer blocks** than clock at pool sizes between one call's width and the working set, while on the `kv_stream_parity` synthetic pattern (a sliding recent window mixed with uniform draws) clock wins and lrfu matches its own offline model.

## What it does not claim

**No speed claim.** The wall clock did not separate (27.86/31.63 vs 24.62/19.52 tok/s) and could not here: the runs' work differs (918K-1.07M lookups, drafts 74-90 accepted) and this box's run-to-run spread is ±40%. The default stays `clock` per the repo's rule that a default changes only where it was measured faster - the flag is opt-in so the two can be compared on a quieter machine and on the workloads that matter.

## Not tested

HIP (no toolchain here) and SYCL (a separate engine tree with its own `kv_stream` sources); `--batch` and the layer-split paths; long multi-request sessions where the scores accumulate across requests.

⚠️ One build note for reviewers: this branch needs a **normal** `cmake --build`. The `make <target>/fast` shortcuts skip header-dependency checks, so after `kv_stream.hpp`'s `KvStreamMap` grew they left stale objects with the old layout and the engine faulted with an illegal memory access at prefill. Nothing in the PR depends on that; it cost an evening to bisect.

pulls.title: gfx12 layer split: opt-in STRATA_GFX12_SPLIT_DECODE=1 for nine decode switches (2x R9700: +5.8% greedy, +4.9% sampled)
pulls.author: justincinmd
pulls.body:
Issue: follows #1478

## Summary

#1478 left the decode half of the gfx1151 table out of the gfx12 table, because it measured slower on one R9700. On a two-R9700 layer split, with every expert resident, the same switches are faster. This PR adds an opt-in flag for that case: `STRATA_GFX12_SPLIT_DECODE=1`. The default does not change.

Measured on 2x R9700 32 GB, Linux, ROCm 7.2.4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--layer-split 26`, all 24,576 experts resident, spec 4 + MTP:

| | Greedy tok/s | Temp 1.0 tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| v0.1.43, before | 108.9 | 101.5 |
| v0.1.43 + the nine switches | 115.0 | 106.2 |
| v0.1.43, after | 108.5 | 101.0 |

That is +5.8% greedy and +4.9% sampled against the mean of the two stock runs. Decode is the geometric mean of four prompts, 3 runs each. Cold prompt reads at 4.6K / 19K / 69K tokens are +11% / +12% / +12% (one request per size). Per-run data and output hashes: [bench report](https://github.com/justincinmd/Strata/tree/pr/bench-2x-r9700/bench/results/2026-10-12-community-2x-r9700-iq3_s-0.1.43) (also offered as a PR).

## What changed

- `STRATA_GFX12_SPLIT_DECODE=1` (exactly `1`) sets nine switches of the gfx1151 table, unless the user set them: `Q6_PACKED`, `MMVF_ROWS`, `ATTN_LANECELL`, `EXPERT_V2`, `TSUM`, `LFUSE`, `GDN_SPLIT`, `QFUSE`, `PLE_BATCH`.
- They apply only when the resolved split runs on two or more GPUs, every one gfx12, on Linux. Otherwise one start-up line says why they stay off. The engine decides after the split is resolved and before any of them is read.
- Without the flag, a qualifying split prints one hint line. `STRATA_GFX12_DEFAULTS=0` still turns off the whole gfx12 table.
- `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp` / `.hpp`: a pure decision function, `gfx12_split_decode()`. `arch_default_env` and `apply_arch_defaults` keep their 0.1.43 signatures and output.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: one call, HIP only, after the existing check that every used GPU has code in the binary.
- docs/AMD_HIP.md: what each switch does, the measurements and the limits. Short notes in DETAILS.md and MULTI_GPU.md.

Not in the set: `Q8_PACKED` (the measured pack has no Q8_0 matrix it packs) and `SH_STREAM` (not measured on a split). `Q6_PACKED` costs VRAM: +497 MiB for the main head and +81 MiB for the MTP head on this pack.

## Testing

- Without the flag the output equals stock v0.1.43 on every greedy and seeded request, and the start-up log adds only the hint line. With the flag the nine switches turn on, and expert residency does not change. With `--split-device 0` or one visible GPU they stay off.
- Output with the flag: greedy reasoning text, answer text and token counts match stock on 4 prompts in 3 runs. 11 of 12 seeded sampled runs match. Stock v0.1.43 itself varies on some seeded requests from run to run, so this does not show whether the switches are bitwise on gfx12. The new start-up line calls them speed switches, not exact.
- `arch_defaults_test` covers the default, the flag, one GPU, mixed architectures, Windows, malformed values and user-set values.
- CUDA 13.0.2 (sm_120) and oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1 (SYCL) build with no new diagnostics. Compile only. Windows not built.

## Extra Notes

The evidence covers one setup: 2x R9700, one IQ3_S pack, every expert resident. If more gfx12 split runs agree, the set could become a default later.

pulls.title: native dense: count the STRATA_Q8_PACKED copies and allocate them after the required weights
pulls.author: justincinmd
pulls.body:
## Summary

`STRATA_Q8_PACKED=1` (on by default on gfx1151) keeps a second, packed copy of each eligible Q8_0 dense matrix in VRAM. The layer split search did not count that copy. A copy that did not fit also aborted the load. This PR counts the copies and makes them optional.

## What changed

- `NativeDense::weight_bytes_for` prices each packed copy with the same test that `load` uses. The split search no longer under-prices a stage with such matrices.
- `NativeDense::load` makes every required allocation first (the matrices, the `STRATA_HC_Q8` copies, the q8_1 scratch) and the packed copies after them. Before, it made each copy right after its matrix.
- The first copy that does not fit is dropped with one stderr line. The copies after it are not tried. A matrix without a copy uses the GGUF layout, as with the switch off. Any other failure is still an error.
- `include/strata/core/optional_alloc.hpp` (new, header-only): the required-then-optional sequencer that `load` uses.
- `tests/core/optional_alloc_test.cpp` (new, CPU only).

Runs with Q8 packing off keep the same allocations in the same order. On gfx1151 the default path changes: a stage with eligible Q8_0 matrices is priced higher, so an automatic split can place layers differently, and a copy that does not fit no longer stops the load.

## Testing

- `optional_alloc_test` drives the sequencer in `load`'s call order against a fake VRAM budget. Cases: 13 MiB free with three 4 MiB matrices (fails in the old order, loads now), room for some or all copies, a required allocation out of memory, a copy upload failure, and a required allocation after `finish()`.
- HIP (ROCm 7.2.4, gfx1201) builds. CUDA 13.0.2 (sm_120) and oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1 (SYCL) build with no new diagnostics. Compile only.

## Extra Notes

Not run on a GPU with an eligible matrix: no pack I have contains a Q8_0 dense matrix wide enough to pack. I found the problem while testing the gfx1151 decode switches on gfx12 (a separate PR). A gfx1151 run with a Q8_0 pack would confirm it.

pulls.title: HIP build: honor -DGPU_TARGETS / -DAMDGPU_TARGETS when CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES is not given
pulls.author: justincinmd
pulls.body:
## Summary

A manual HIP build with `-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1201` builds a gfx1100 engine. Configure and link give no warning. At start-up the engine refuses the card. This PR makes `-DGPU_TARGETS` and `-DAMDGPU_TARGETS` choose the architecture when `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` is not given.

Cause: `cmake/hip_backend.cmake` defaults `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` to gfx1100 and reads nothing else. ROCm applies `GPU_TARGETS` only to `hip::device`, and Strata links `hip::host`.

```sh
# v0.1.43, ROCm 7.2.4
cmake -S . -B build-hip -G Ninja -DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/rocm -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1201
# -- Strata: HIP enabled, arch gfx1100
```

## What changed

- `cmake/hip_arch_select.cmake` (new): the order is `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES`, `GPU_TARGETS`, `AMDGPU_TARGETS`, then gfx1100. The default does not change. ggml-hip uses the same order.
- The configure line names the source, e.g. `arch gfx1201 (from GPU_TARGETS)`. If `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` and a target variable disagree, `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` wins and configure warns.
- Only values the user gave count. `find_package(hip)` caches its own `GPU_TARGETS` (amdgpu-arch's list), and ROCm 5.7 / 6.2 retype the user's entry. The selector tells them apart by CMake's `-D` marks and a record of what `find_package(hip)` left. A toolchain or parent-project variable wins over the cache, as usual in CMake.
- Strata no longer writes `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` to the cache. The same flags give the same result in a new or a used build folder. A 0.1.43 folder's cached default (gfx1100) is dropped; a value the user edited there is kept.
- `cmake/hip_backend.cmake` calls the selector before and after `find_package(hip)`.
- docs/AMD_HIP.md: three sentences in the Build section.

Not changed: setup.py and `tools/hip/build_windows.bat` pass `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES`, so they build as before. The gfx906 path does not use this file.

## Testing

- `cmake/tests/hip_arch_select_test.cmake`, in ctest as `hip_arch_select_test` under `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS`. It runs 234 configures of a small project that replays ROCm 5.7, 6.2 and 7.2's cache declarations. It needs no HIP toolchain. It covers new and used folders, `-U`, `-C`, toolchain values (also equal to the cache), 0.1.43 folders and the conflict warning. It passes on CMake 3.24, 3.28, 4.1 and 4.4.
- ROCm 7.2.4: `-DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1201` builds gfx1201 code only (57 code objects). v0.1.43 builds gfx1100.
- CUDA 13.0.2 (sm_120) and oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1 (SYCL) build with no new diagnostics. Compile only.

## Extra Notes

One case stays as in 0.1.43: in a 0.1.43 folder where ROCm 5.7 / 6.2 retyped the user's `GPU_TARGETS`, that value cannot be told from ROCm's own entry. Give `-DGPU_TARGETS` again to use it.

pulls.title: PLE: reuse prefetched row vectors across reordered and duplicate gathers
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
DRAFT - NOT READY FOR REVIEW. CUDA/HIP backend builds have not been performed; no reviewers are requested.

Bug report: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2622

Prefetching six PLE token row-vectors in one order and gathering those same vectors in another order currently falls through to a second reader ticket. `prefetch_rows` also deduplicates identical vectors, so `n_prefetch >= n_tokens` excludes a gather containing repeated requests even when every requested vector is available.

This changes only `PleTable::gather_batch` in `src/kernels/ngram.cpp`:

- Match each requested 16-row key against any of the at most 16 prefetch slots, preserving requested output order. Duplicate requests can reuse an immutable slot.
- Collect every outstanding prefetch ticket before clearing the slots, including after a collection failure; retain the first error and return before decoding on failure.

The existing 16-token limit, missing-key/oversize fallback, mapped path, public API and logical byte accounting stay unchanged. The lookup performs at most 256 fixed-size key comparisons. This does not wire batch-session PLE metadata or change kernels.

Reproduction on upstream `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78`: open a finite tiny IQ4_NL GGUF in Direct mode; prefetch six distinct row-vectors A,B,C,D,E,F; record the requested-row count from `io_report`; call `gather_batch` with D,E,F,A,B,C. The baseline requests another 96 rows; the patch requests zero. With only A prefetched, gathering A,A,A changes 48 additional requested rows to zero. Results remain byte-identical to an independently opened Mmap reference.

Validation already executed: a CPU-only harness compiles the actual shared PleTable and the SYCL tree's host PleReader/DirectFile, using g++ 13.3.0, C++17/O2/pthreads. Eleven cases at cache sizes 0/256 and worker thread off/on, both baseline and candidate: **88 cases pass**. This includes ordered/permuted/subset/duplicate/extra/missing keys, duplicate-prefetch suppression, zero/over-limit gathers, prefetch overflow and the pending-token guard. Output guards, finite references, logical bytes and requested-row counts pass. Error injection and out-of-range rows were not tested; drain-all failure handling was reviewed, not fault-injected. Requested-row counts include row-cache hits and do not measure physical disk traffic or latency.

[Evidence and exact identities](https://github.com/hotschmoe/b70_ai_things/blob/fff2c71b0a1d806db428b8489b42fd248d50bebd/docs/20261015_strata_ple_prefetch_readiness.md), [executed fixture](https://github.com/hotschmoe/b70_ai_things/blob/fff2c71b0a1d806db428b8489b42fd248d50bebd/strata/flash-next/lowlevel_probe/ple_prefetch_cpu.cpp). The fixture retains its original local include path; reproduction on another checkout needs that path adjusted. The submitted production patch is byte-for-byte the CPU-tested patch (SHA256 `217550f5994f9159c9a443a81bc71429f481fd823493b44f189f11fc241199b5`).

No end-to-end throughput gain is claimed. A later local two-B70 C2 serving comparison included this same helper in both arms, so it cannot isolate its benefit. Full CUDA/HIP backend builds remain unperformed for this contribution; this draft must not be presented as fully validated across backends.

Related source overlap: #1516 changes the large-prompt reader path and needs a context rebase if merged first; its small-gather fast path still matches positionally. #2073 changes PLE diagnostics; #2326 adds table serialization. Neither implements this key matching. Existing #2511 covers unrelated draft/restore accounting.

pulls.title: serve: /v1/models meta carries llama-server's model facts (n_params, …
pulls.author: Pix13
pulls.body:
## Title

serve: /v1/models meta carries llama-server's model facts (n_params, size, ftype, ...) from the GGUF headers

Issue: none found (searched 2026-10-15: n_params, ftype, /v1/models meta). Related: #1882 (other context keys, same
dict; the two merge without overlap).

## Summary

llama-server's `/v1/models` gives each model a `meta` with `n_params`, `size`, `ftype`, `n_vocab`, `n_ctx_train`
and `n_embd`. Strata gives only `n_ctx`. Proxies and dashboards that read llama-server's model list (for example
Olla's Models panel) show the parameter count, the quantisation and the size on disk from these keys, and leave
them blank for a Strata endpoint.

This change reads them from the `--native` GGUF's headers (`tools/gguf_reader.py`, no tensor data), over every
shard of a split model, the first time `/v1/models` is asked for, and keeps them:

- `n_params`: the elements of every tensor in every shard
- `size`: the shards' bytes on disk
- `ftype`: llama.cpp's `llama_model_ftype_name()` label of `general.file_type` (`"Q8_0"`, `"IQ3_S - 3.4375 bpw"`)
- `n_vocab`, `n_ctx_train`, `n_embd`: `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`, `<arch>.context_length`, `<arch>.embedding_length`

Only the facts found are given. A missing shard gives no `n_params`/`size` (rather than a wrong one); an engine
without a GGUF (pack only, the mock engine) or a GGUF that cannot be read gives the old `meta`, and an unreadable
file is said once on stderr. `meta.n_ctx` is unchanged and stays the engine's.

What it leaves alone: the engine, every other endpoint, requests. On opt-in: the change only adds keys to a dict
whose existing keys keep their values; llama-server always sends them, so I did not put them behind a setting.
Happy to add one if you prefer.

## Measured

Header read, on Rocky 9.8 (files in the page cache):

| model | shards | read | n_params | size | ftype |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| huihui Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0 | 6 (188 GB) | 0.23 s | 176943899520 | 188225033440 | `Q8_0` |
| ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S | 2 (84 GB) | 0.74 s | 176943899520 | 83617662656 | `IQ3_S - 3.4375 bpw` |

Both run with this change since 2026-10-15 (2x RTX 3090 and a V100); Olla shows `177B` / `Q8_0` / `175.30 GB`.

## Test

- `serve/test_server.py`, new `ModelMeta`: a two-shard GGUF written by the test (named by either shard), a missing
  shard, no GGUF, an unreadable GGUF (said once), and `/v1/models` with an alias.
- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py' -t .`: 789 tests, 2 failures that fail on `main` too
  without this change (`test_keepawake ... early_close`, `test_responses.NoLeakedSampler`, timing-dependent here).
- Not tested: Windows, macOS/Metal, a non-split single-file GGUF on a real engine (covered only by the unit test).

pulls.title: [GUI] add opt-in web chat editing, retry and history rewind
pulls.author: uppet
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When an answer loops or takes a wrong turn, Stop ends generation but the Python server's web chat cannot repair the conversation already sent to the model. Users have to start again or carry the bad answer into subsequent requests.

This adds an opt-in **Edit chat history** setting under a visible **Chat settings** button. Users can edit a question and regenerate, correct an assistant answer without generating, regenerate an existing answer, or remove a message and everything after it. A one-step Undo restores the previous history. Editing an earlier turn removes its descendants so the next request uses the corrected conversation.

## Related discussion

- [#271](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/271): related message-level chat controls.
- [#1787](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1787): broader chat-history management; this change does not add a multi-chat sidebar.
- This updates the existing PR following the [0.2.0-beta tracker-reset notice](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2615#issuecomment-6273860120). Maintainer agreement on this feature's scope has not been recorded. Keeping the PR as a draft for that discussion; the reset notice is not treated as scope approval.

## Approach

The feature stays in the existing `serve/web` client and is **off by default**. Its preference is saved only in this browser. It does not change the server API, engine, or desktop app.

History changes wait until generation, including Stop finalization, has finished. User edits preserve available attachments; assistant edits remove stale reasoning, tools, errors and timing metadata. Tool results are removed with their parent turn. Missing attachment content after a reload blocks regeneration and asks for reattachment. The composer is locked during an edit, with Save/Cancel and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter/Escape controls.

The rebase preserves main's model-card sampling defaults and explicit overrides. Regression coverage includes edit/retry requests and a fix for New chat leaving an old Undo available after removing the entire conversation.

## Validation

Tested source: `a768457c8dc71a672bc4a24ffa7ef7de494aa578`, rebased onto main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (0.2.0-beta). Environment: Ubuntu under WSL2/Linux x86_64, Python 3.10.12, Node v24.4.0, Chrome/153.0.8010.12. The runtime checks used a fresh virtual environment with only the repository's pinned `requirements.txt`; `rich` and `textual` were absent.

**Passed:**

- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_web_history serve.test_web_sampling -v`: **22 tests passed**, with Node present and no skips. Covers editing/truncation, attachment handling, stale tool cleanup, Undo, Stop/failure boundaries, keyboard controls, and default/legacy/explicit/greedy sampling through real edit/retry request construction.
- `/tmp/strata-pr2615-runtime-20261020/bin/python tools/minimal_server_smoke.py --report ../runtime-smoke-20261020.json`: **passed**. The embedded terminal-runtime suite reported `Ran 39 tests in 91.002s; OK (skipped=3)`: 36 executed, three Windows-only skips. This uses a fake engine, not GPU inference.
- `WEBCHAT_BASELINE_REF=e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211 node serve/test_web_history_browser.cjs`: **7 browser workflows passed**. `CHROME_BIN` pointed to Chromium and `puppeteer-core` was available as a development tool; neither is a new runtime dependency. The harness serves mock SSE on loopback and blocks external requests. It compares the default-off message DOM and outgoing API payload with unmodified main, then checks settings persistence, user/assistant edits, attachments and unsent drafts, regeneration, truncation, Undo, Stop finalization, and 320/390px layouts. Observed: 7 mock requests, one aborted stream, zero real-model requests, zero page errors.
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`, `node --check serve/test_web_history.js`, `node --check serve/test_web_history_browser.cjs`, and `git diff --check`: all passed.

**Failed:**

- `/tmp/strata-pr2615-runtime-20261020/bin/python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py' -v`: **884 passed, one failure, 14 skips** (`Ran 899 tests in 331.706s; FAILED (failures=1, skipped=14)`). The failure is `test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed`: `AssertionError: False is not true : the child outlived a killed server (watcher)`. All 22 web-history/sampling tests passed within this run. Skips concern optional SDK/tokenizer/schema fixtures and Windows-only checks.
- Isolated comparison: `/tmp/strata-pr2615-runtime-20261020/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed -v` failed with the same assertion on both this PR (15.075s) and a clean detached checkout of main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211` (15.078s), using the same environment. The lifeline code and test are unchanged in this PR. This establishes a baseline failure in this environment; its root cause is not established here, and this PR does not claim a fully green server suite.
- Resolved during the rebase: the first focused run failed one old assertion expecting the previous hardcoded sampling defaults (`temperature: 0.6`, `top_p: 0.95`, `top_k: 20`). The assertion was updated to main's current behavior: omit untouched defaults and let the server select the model-card values. Added edit/retry regression coverage; the final 22-test run passed.

**Not run:**

- GitHub Actions for this head: [Minimal serving runtime](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/actions/runs/39377581889) and [Title area](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/actions/runs/39377581990) currently report `action_required`, with no test jobs started. Maintainer approval is needed for the fork workflows; the local results above do not claim a CI pass.
- Real-model/GPU inference, performance measurements, and native Windows browser/server execution. The browser checks use mock SSE, so they do not establish model quality or hardware performance.
- CUDA, HIP, SYCL and Metal builds: no backend source or build files changed.
- Desktop `apps/host` tests: this PR changes the Python server's existing web page, not the desktop app.

## Limits

Undo is one in-memory snapshot, cleared by a new ordinary question, New chat, or reload. Attachment contents are not persisted by the existing chat storage, so reloaded attachments need reattachment before replay. Editing or regenerating can run tools again; the editor warns about this.

The default-off comparison covers message DOM and API payload against the stated main revision, not the entire page: the visible Chat settings label and layout are intentional changes even when history editing is off. No performance improvement is claimed. Feature scope still needs maintainer agreement, and the server-suite baseline failure above remains unresolved.

pulls.title: sycl: strata-sycl.sh passes EnableRecoverablePageFaults on to the container, 0 included (#2157)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
**What it changes.** `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` (the Docker launcher `setup.py --backend sycl` installs, via `sycl/setup_intel.py`) forwards a fixed set of variables into the container and drops any value of `0` (for the engine's switches, 0 means "not set"). #2157's fix for a lost Arc card is `NEOReadDebugKeys=1` with `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=0` in the engine's environment (2 of 3 runs lost the card without, 0 of 4 with, on the reporter's 2x Arc Pro B70); the second key never reached a setup install: its name was not on the list, and its value is 0. Now `EnableRecoverablePageFaults` is forwarded with any non-empty value, 0 included. The docs side is #2602.

**What it leaves alone.** Every other variable is forwarded or dropped exactly as before (the old zero rule is unchanged in the `else` branch), and setup does not write the key into the config; a user adds it to `"env"` by hand.

**How it was checked.** Not run on Intel hardware (there is none here). `bash -n` and `shellcheck` (clean, as before). A dry run of the old and the new script with a stub `docker` on `PATH` that prints the `-e` arguments:

| `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=0 NEOReadDebugKeys=1` | `NEOReadDebugKeys=1` + the port defaults | the same + `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=0` |
| `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=1 NEOReadDebugKeys=1` | `NEOReadDebugKeys=1` + defaults | the same + `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=1` |
| `EnableRecoverablePageFaults=` `IGC_X=0` `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=0` `UR_Y=a=0` `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0` | `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0 STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=12 STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1 UR_Y=a=0` | identical |

pulls.title: Metal: faster decode GEMVs on M1 / M2 (wider K-quant and IQ4_XS loads, tuned tiles), bitwise the same output
pulls.author: PiMatyja
pulls.body:
## Summary
Wider loads for the Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and IQ4_XS decoders and a tuned tile choice for the dense decode GEMVs, on M1 and M2 only (Apple GPU family 7 and 8). On an M2 Max with IQ3_XXS, decode is about 11% faster and the output is bitwise the same. M3 and newer build exactly what they build today.

## What changed
- `metal/kernels/gemv_wide.metal` (new): the wide decoders, reusing `gemv.metal`'s templates under new kernel names.
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`: on M1 / M2, adds that file and picks a tuned tile for 1-3 token windows. The tile never changes the summation order. If a tuned kernel is missing, too big for threadgroup memory, or the tensor isn't 16-byte aligned, it falls back to today's tile.
- `metal/src/mtl_rt.h` / `.mm`: `max_threadgroup_memory()` and `has_function()`.
- `metal/tests/gemv_parity.cpp`: checks every new kernel bitwise against its stock twin; new `--sweep`.

`STRATA_METAL_GEMV=0` turns it off. `units.metal`, `quant.metal` and `gemv.metal` are untouched, so no other kernel changes on any GPU.

## Extra Notes
M2 Max (30-core GPU), 64 GB, macOS 26.4.1, IQ3_XXS resident (with #2338), greedy, 3 rounds, decode tok/s:

| | GEMV=0 | default |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 400 tokens, code | 35.3 | 39.1 (+10.8%) |
| 400 tokens, story | 35.2 | 38.7 (+10.0%) |
| 256 tokens after ~1K | 35.0 | 39.0 (+11.5%) |
| 256 tokens after ~4K | 34.6 | 38.5 (+11.2%) |

Same text in both arms on all four prompts. Prompt speed unchanged. `gemv_parity` and `gemv_parity --sweep` pass bitwise on the M2 and on an M4 Max, and the other parity tests match main. Not tested on an M1.

pulls.title: serve: the card-order line says how to try the engine's suggested split point in the same order (#2085)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
On #2085 (found while reading that report's `--layer-split` planner notes).

**What it changes.** With `"layer_split": "auto"`, `serve/server.py` `ordered_gpus()` puts the faster card last
(#1352), so the engine gets the cards as, say, `2,0`, and its NEAR TIE line (`src/program/generate.cpp` ~4320,
"To try the other: --layer-split K") counts K in that order. A manual `layer_split` keeps the order the config lists
(`0,2`), so a user who copied K got its layers on the other cards, with the slower card running the head. The
server's `layer split: card order 2,0 (...)` line now ends with `to try the engine's --layer-split K in this order,
list "gpu": [2, 0] with it, #2085`, and docs/MULTI_GPU.md ("Card order with auto") says the same.

**Which fix and why.** The fix is the hint only, not reordering or translating K:
- Reordering a manual split as well would move the layers of every hand-tuned split that exists today.
- Translating K for two cards (K' = layers - K in the listed order) gives the same layer counts, but the head,
  draft and verify then run on the slower card, so it is not the placement the engine priced.
- A manual split keeps the listed order (it returns before the reorder, the #1576 check included), so
  `"gpu": [2, 0]` with `"layer_split": "K"` gives the engine the same device order and K.

**What it leaves alone.** Every card order and every split (no placement changes). The line is printed only when
the order changes, as before.

**How it was checked.** `serve/test_server.py` `GpuChoice.test_card_order`: the reorder line names `"gpu": [2, 0]`
and the engine's suggestion, and a config listing `[2, 0]` with a manual K gets `[2, 0]` (fails on `main`, passes).
With the venv's Python, `serve.test_server`: OK. Python 3.14, Ubuntu (Linux 7.0); no GPU, no engine run.

- The standard suite, 3 runs per test, quiet runs, from 4K to 64K prompts plus the agent session: 114.8 tok/s short-chat decode, 1704.6 / 1945.1 / 1949.5 / 1982.0 tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K / 64K.

**One thing I think is a bug, reported separately:** on the split the engine's per-request counter is `KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM` at every context size and with every KV format, while the same machine, build and `--kv-resident 32768` on the 3090 alone reports `89.58% of 246456 block reads hit VRAM, 103.5 MiB read from RAM` for the same residency line (`32768 of 131072 cells per QSA layer in VRAM`). pulls.title: [Engine] Preserve target probabilities in gated MTP
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1`, the confidence gate selects drafts using the probability of the token it just drew. The original verifier still uses the unfiltered q, and a failed gate becomes a plain target sample. This biases the output toward the draft head's preferred tokens.

This patch keeps the confidence gate and accounts for the missing proposal mass explicitly. It also keeps CPU expert arithmetic independent of how many tokens share a speculative window, so the verifier samples the singleton target distribution.

For `p=(0.5,0.5)`, `q=(0.875,0.125)` and threshold `0.5`, the original gate emits `(0.5625,0.4375)`; the repaired gate emits `(0.5,0.5)`.

## Related discussion

Refs #2028. Thanks to KarlGrier for the report and derivation. This updates the existing #2591 implementation to v0.2.1 (`90767252`, engine 0.1.46) following the tracker reset.

## Approach

The proposal packet retains q on admitted tokens without renormalizing it; call this measure μ. A failed draw becomes an explicit NULL row. Offered tokens use `min(1,p(D)/μ(D))`; rejection and NULL sample the normalized positive part of `p−μ`. A row with no attempted proposal remains an ordinary bonus sample.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q[Draft distribution q] --> G[Confidence gate + eligible suffix root]
    G --> M[Retained measure μ + NULL mass]
    M --> O[Offered token]
    M --> N[NULL]
    O --> A[Accept with min 1, p / μ]
    O --> R[On rejection: sample positive p − μ]
    N --> R
```

CLI and serial serve share the packet builder. Attempt counts and context limits are decided at the producer boundary. Suffix eligibility uses committed context and request-fixed policy statistics. CPU dispatch preserves singleton arithmetic while retaining shared weight decoding where it gives the same result.

The 0.2 port preserves Trellis/Hadamard handling, per-job expert layouts and cold-read batching. Both ready and cold-read job submissions carry the arithmetic mode. ARM builds retain their native singleton arithmetic rather than referencing x86 kernels. Default exact-match drafting remains the default; explicit `top` gating remains available.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `gated_proposal_test`: 266 checks, including macOS ASAN/UBSAN.
- `spec_admission_test` and `STRATA_SPEC_PROB_GATE=top spec_admission_test top`: 900 Top cases and 2,700 μ-packet cases per configuration, with the original biased rule as a negative control.
- `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 STRATA_OLD_SAMPLER=0 STRATA_SAMPLER_ONE_BLOCK=0 spec_proposal_parity`: 432 rows, zero mismatches against an independent CPU oracle on RX 7900 XTX.
- `native_arithmetic_parity`: 4,866,048 finite bitwise comparisons in each of eight Windows configurations, including Trellis formats and Hadamard-folded inputs.
- Full CUDA, HIP, SYCL and Metal engine builds pass. CUDA/GCC and SYCL/oneAPI each pass 13 CPU tests; Metal also passes `strata --version` (`0.1.46-metal`).
- Incremental 12-position comparison against the genuine 0.2.1 release: patched MTP matches both no-MTP singleton references at all 12 raw-logit rows. Original MTP matches 1/12; its token-12 distribution has TV **0.0361348** from the singleton reference. All 24 sampled decisions reconstruct from captured p, q and counters. Trace builds reproduce production outputs.
- The default-mode original/patched 12-token outputs match. After the ARM compile fix, the rebuilt HIP candidate repeats the MTP/singleton check: all 24 logit rows and all outputs match the earlier candidate; the final default-mode check and sampler/CPU suites pass again.

![Target probability agreement on the fixed-prefix fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyanHu-git/Strata/470d558be39f1a8c8edda4d6058b8b5b8331035b/bench/results/2026-10-20-gated-mtp-v021/target-agreement.png)

[Prompt, seeds, binary/library hashes, per-position distributions and figure source](https://github.com/KeyanHu-git/Strata/tree/470d558be39f1a8c8edda4d6058b8b5b8331035b/bench/results/2026-10-20-gated-mtp-v021). The six-run numerical probe generated 72 tokens in 115.47 seconds. Singleton controls advance one token at a time; they do not re-prefill the whole prefix.

**Failed:** No remaining failure in the checks listed above. During preparation, the Metal link exposed two x86-only references; architecture-specific dispatch fixes them. An initial GPU test selected the integrated GPU; the reported run explicitly selects the RX 7900 XTX. These failed setup attempts are retained in the local experiment record.

**Not run:** CUDA, SYCL and Metal model execution; a new full GSM8K evaluation; a 0.2.1 throughput benchmark.

## Limits

The repaired proposal path supports serial generation on one CUDA/HIP device, with lookup-chain, adaptive swaps and PCIe sharing off. Unsupported combinations report an error. SYCL and Metal compile but do not execute this proposal path.

The numerical fixture resolves the earlier token-12 target-probability discrepancy. It does not establish an aggregate model-quality score or explain the later long reasoning trajectory. The previous 100-pair speed measurements remain results for the older engine, not 0.2.1 performance claims.

pulls.title: [Engine] session: support multi-GPU layer-split save/restore (format v3)
pulls.author: LuckyKo
pulls.body:
## Problem

When running Strata with `--layer-split auto` across multiple GPUs, the engine divides model layers into stages (one per GPU). The existing session save/restore (`--slot-save-path`) only handled a single-stage (single-GPU) layout: it saved/restored one set of running state and K/V. On a multi-GPU split, the save was either refused or produced an incomplete file that couldn't be restored.

This made `--slot-save-path` unusable for the most common multi-GPU configuration, which is exactly where long-context session persistence matters most (the RAM cost of re-reading a 30K+ token prompt).

## Solution

Introduce **format v3** for session files that carries per-stage data. Version 2 is reserved for PR #2247's BF16 state codec; this build rejects it explicitly at the version gate.

- **Write:** `put_payload` serializes stage 0 (as before), then — only when `stage_images` is non-empty — a count followed by one block per later stage. Each block holds that stage's running state, K/V parts, and checkpoint. The file header version is set to `kVersionStages = 3`.
- **Read:** `get_payload` reads stage 0 identically to v1, then checks the version. For v3 files it reads the stage count (bounded by `limits.max_stages`) and each subsequent stage block, validating geometry and layer range per stage. A v1 file has no stage section; a v2 file is refused at the version gate (not silently misparsed as v1).
- **Save guard:** if `conversation_checkpoints_split` routes any checkpoint to `cs.rest` (incomplete for the split), the save is refused rather than silently dropping it.
- **Backward compatible:** v1 files read unchanged. A v3 file opened by old code is refused at the version check.

## Read-limit hardening

`SessionReadLimits` gains `max_stages` and a per-stage `stage_limits` vector. The serve loop populates these from the live engine's stage carves before calling `session_file_read`, so a file from a different split (wrong stage count, wrong layer range, oversized K/V) is refused before any allocation — not after a partial read.

## Changes by file

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `include/strata/core/conversation_file.hpp` | `kVersionStages = 3`, `SessionReadLimits::max_stages`, `stage_limits`, `SessionStageLimits` struct |
| `include/strata/core/conversation_snapshot.hpp` | `conversation_stage_read_limits()` declaration |
| `src/core/conversation_file.cpp` | v3 write (`put_payload`), v3 read (`get_payload`), per-stage validation, explicit v2 rejection |
| `src/core/conversation_state.cpp` | `conversation_stage_read_limits()` implementation, `conversation_session_read_limits` updated to carry stage bounds |
| `src/program/generate.cpp` | Serve loop: build `stage_limits` from live stages, set `max_stages`, pass through to read; save path collects per-stage K/V sources; `cs.rest` guard; `draft_stage_kv` helper |
| `src/core/conversation_file_test.cpp` | Round-trip tests for v1 (no stages) and v3 (multi-stage), v2 rejection, v4 rejection, version-mismatch refusal, oversized-stage refusal |
| `src/core/conversation_snapshot_test.cpp` | `conversation_stage_read_limits` unit tests |

## Environment

Strata built from source, CUDA 13.4, Windows 11 / Debian 13
2× NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB) or 2× NVIDIA A2 (16 GB), 64 GB system RAM
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ3_XXS / UD-Q4_K_XL, up to 128K context

## Validation

**Revision:** `94f55cd6` (rebased onto main `e88ee39d`, 0.2.0-beta)
**Environment:** CUDA 13.4, Windows 11, 2× NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120), 64 GB RAM

**Commands:**
```
build-win-cuda13.bat
build-win-cuda13\conversation_file_test.exe
build-win-cuda13\conversation_snapshot_test.exe
build-win-cuda13\conversation_cache_test.exe
build-win-cuda13\conversation_memory_test.exe
build-win-cuda13\conversation_split_failure_test.exe
build-win-cuda13\session_save_reclaim_test.exe
```

**Passed:**
- conversation_file_test: 208 checks
- conversation_snapshot_test: 4027 checks
- conversation_cache_test: 4219 checks
- conversation_memory_test: 25 checks
- conversation_split_failure_test: 36 allocation-failure cases (stages 1–3)
- session_save_reclaim_test: 119 checks
- Smoke test: engine starts on dual-GPU layer-split, chat completion responds, session save/restore round-trip works

**Failed:** none

**Not run:**
- `--batch` / parallel slots
- Restore with a different GPU split than the save
- Full-disk / near-full-VRAM restore (#2409)
- Linux (previously validated on 2× A2 sm_86 by @Eranicus30666, 23K and 94K tokens)

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: opt-in STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRE_S keeps a long conversation's batch slot from a short side request (next turn 12.8 -> 0.3 s)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body: ## Problem and result I run coding agents on Strata with `--batch`. Next to their long conversations, clients send short side requests (a title, a summary, a one-line check). When every free slot holds a conversation, `pick_slot` takes the least recently used one, so a side request can take the slot of a 40K-token conversation that is still going, and that conversation's next turn reads its whole history again: 12.8 s to the first token on 0.2.0-beta (one RTX 5090, below). With the new opt-in `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRE_S=600` the side request takes an expired slot or the one holding the shortest history, and the long conversation's next turn takes 0.34 s. Unset or 0, nothing changes. ## Related discussion #1906 and #1930 (agent sessions reading whole prompts again), #1920, #1938. Next to #2527 / #2528 (andyhrc): their placement policy covers pipelined groups; this is the small counterpart for `--batch` without pipelined groups (one GPU, or `--batch-groups 1`). qiuzan2001 noted here that the config's `"env"` block was ignored: the value is now read from the engine's environment (the server's plus the config's `"env"`). Rebased onto 0.2.0-beta after the tracker reset (one textual conflict: two functions added at the same place). ## Approach `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRE_S` (seconds; off unless set). Set, a new conversation that finds no empty slot takes an expired one first (idle that long or longer: its client has likely moved on), the least recently used among them; else the one holding the shortest history. Unset or 0: the least recently used one, as before (a test checks it picks main's slot on 3,000 random slot tables). A request still goes to the slot holding its own prefix first, and pipelined groups return before this rule. Changes: `pick_slot`'s last `min()` key, `slot_expire_s(env)`, `serve/test_slot_alloc.py`, and the sentence on slot choice in `docs/BATCHING.md`. ## Validation **Passed:** - 0.2.0-beta (main e88ee39d) + this branch (ca7d91a5), Windows 11, Python 3.12: `python -m unittest serve.test_slot_alloc` 25 OK; the whole serve suite (`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"`) 899 OK, 21 skipped, against 881 OK, 21 skipped on main. - One RTX 5090 (Windows 11), engine built from 0.2.0-beta (e88ee39d), Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, `--batch 3`, no pipelined groups, no conversation cache, a fresh engine per arm, `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRE_S=600` in the config's `"env"` block (main ignores it). A third stream decodes all along, so every request goes through a slot. Conversation A (a 40,250-token prompt) and B (about 1,770 tokens) finish and stay in their slots; then a one-line side request; then A's and B's next turns: | | main | this, `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRE_S=600` | this, unset | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | slot the side request took | A's (40,250 tokens held) | B's (1,781 held) | A's (40,250 held) | | A's next turn: first token | 12.78 s | 0.34 s | 12.70 s | | B's next turn: first token | 1.20 s | 1.18 s | 1.17 s | - Before the rebase, on 0.1.45 (477ac13c), same bench: 14.79 / 14.84 s on main against 0.32 / 0.32 s with 600, and 14.72 s unset. A 21-hour replay of my own agent traffic through the slots (ids, times and token counts only): 17.8 / 20.6 / 21.1% fewer prompt tokens read at 4 / 6 / 8 slots with 600. **Failed:** none observed. **Not run:** a split with `--batch-groups 1` on GPUs; the RAM conversation cache on (replay only: smaller gain); AMD, Linux, Mac (Python-only change, nothing to build). ## Limits Opt-in, because it changes whose conversation loses its slot and is measured on one user's traffic. A long conversation whose client has gone keeps its slot until it expires; a client whose prompts never match its slot leaves histories that stay until they expire.

pulls.title: prompt attention (HIP): gate_attn in the WMMA kernel's epilogue (opt-in STRATA_ATTN_GATE=1, the same bits)
pulls.author: libratechw
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none

## Summary
On the full-attention layers' prompt path, the attention writes `attn` and `gate_attn` then reads it back, multiplies each
value by the sigmoid of its gate and writes the o-projection's FP16 input. With `STRATA_ATTN_GATE=1` the HIP
`STRATA_PA_FAST` WMMA kernel does that in its epilogue, with `gate_attn`'s expression, so `attn` is not written and read
back. The bits are the same. The gain is small (+0.6% on a 32K prompt), so it is opt-in. Say if you would rather not
carry it. (It was first part of #2019, which now carries only the q-preparation fusion.)

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn.hpp`: `prompt_attn_wmma_kernel<SPLIT,
  GATED>` and `qsa_prompt_attn_batch_gated`, which returns false (nothing launched) wherever `qsa_prompt_attn_batch` would not
  run the `STRATA_PA_FAST` kernel.
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: with `STRATA_ATTN_GATE=1` (and unrotated K/V) it takes the gated launch; otherwise the
  attention and `gate_attn` run as before.
- `src/kernels/qsa_prompt_attn_parity.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt`: a gated check (the FP16 bits against the attention followed
  by `gate_attn`), and an argument `gated` that makes the exit status that check's alone; ctest
  `hip_prompt_attn_wmma_gated` runs it with `STRATA_PA_FAST=1`: 0 values differ on gfx1151.

Without the switch, the WMMA attention's output hash (`hip_prompt_attn_wmma`, three cases, `STRATA_PA_FAST=0` and `=1`) is
296b59d2's in every run (two rounds; measured on the build that also carried the q-preparation fusion, whose attention
files are this branch's).

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, ROCm 7.14.1, Linux), on 296b59d2, the branch's binary without and with `STRATA_ATTN_GATE=1`,
UD-Q4_K_XL, `--serve --prefill 16384 --spec 4`, the section-5 switches of `docs/STRIX_HALO.md` with
`STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=2048` and `STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1`, a 32K chat request, fresh servers alternating, 7 pairs: 1,243 -> 1,253 tok/s (median), the median of the pair ratios +0.6%, 7 of 7
pairs faster.
The records and scripts are in [libratechw/Strata@686de2e9, `2019g/`](https://github.com/libratechw/Strata/tree/686de2e9eedd6e34c18e7d5fab7a2fd2fe3e4241/2019g).

A check outside ctest (a local copy of the parity test, in the records): with an output row stride of 6,152 instead of
6,144, the gated epilogue matches attention + `gate_attn` and leaves the padding untouched in the tool's three cases.

Builds and tests on this branch:
- HIP gfx1151: ctest, 113 tests: 105 pass (`hip_prompt_attn_wmma_gated` among them), 5 skip, and the same three fail as on
  296b59d2 (`ple_parity`, `expert_parity`, `pool_test`).
- HIP: `strata_kernels`, `strata_prefill` and `strata_mmq` compile for gfx1012, gfx1030, gfx1100, gfx1103, gfx1150, gfx1151,
  gfx1200 and gfx1201.
- CUDA 13.0, RTX 3060 (Windows): builds; ctest, 117 tests: 114 pass, 2 skip, and `ple_parity` fails as on 296b59d2.
- SYCL: not affected (the SYCL port has its own prompt attention and `prefill.cpp`).

Not run: other gfx11 / gfx12 cards, UD-IQ4_XS.

pulls.title: sycl/A770: decode GDN recurrence in large GRF, and the split recurrence by default on Alchemist (bitwise; recurrence 2.6x faster)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
sycl/A770: decode GDN recurrence in large GRF, and the split recurrence by default on Alchemist (bitwise; recurrence 2.6x faster)

## Summary
On an Arc A770 the decode window's GDN recurrence kernels spilled registers: the step kernel used ~7.6 KB of scratch per SIMD32 thread at the default 128 registers, according to unitrace's compile table. Its 32 state rows per thread alone fill the default register file.

On Alchemist this PR does two things:
- launches these kernels in large-GRF mode (256 registers per thread);
- makes upstream's split recurrence (S25/S26, `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT`, already bitwise) the default.

The arithmetic is unchanged, so the output is bit-identical. Every other device launches the same kernels as before.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.dp.cpp`:
  - `gdn_large_grf()`: Alchemist by default; `STRATA_GDN_LARGE_GRF=0/1` overrides.
  - `gdn_launch<Name>()`, which picks the large-GRF or default launch for every kernel `gdn_step_norm_multi` launches.
  - `STRATA_GDN_SPLIT` now defaults to on for Alchemist (`=0` / `=1` still choose).
- `sycl/src/kernels/gdn_bench.cpp` (new, plus a `CMakeLists.txt` target): `gdn_step_norm_multi` at the Coder's shape (h_k 16, h_v 48, S 128) for 1-6 tokens, with 48 layers' own states so they stream from VRAM, host-timed, with an output checksum.

## Extra Notes
Arc A770 16 GB, xe, compute runtime 26.05, oneAPI 2026.1.

`gdn_bench` timings:

| tokens | before (no split) | split | split + large GRF |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 68.8 us | 79.2 | 42.0 |
| 4 | 95.0 | 103.1 | **39.5** |
| 6 | 115.8 | 114.2 | **44.9** |

- **Correctness:** `gdn_parity` reports 0 failures, including `gdn_step_norm_multi T=1..8 == single-token`, bitwise in all 47 cases.
- **Engine:** Coder IQ1_M, 8K prompt, `--resident-experts`, stepped window, same-day pairs. The verify window's GPU wait per round went 39.5 / 38.8 -> 37.6 / 37.9 ms with the split, then 35.9-36.3 -> 33.8-34.0 ms with large GRF on top (3 pairs). The output ids follow the usual run-to-run CPU/GPU placement variation.

Not tested: A750 / A580, i915, Windows.
