pulls.title: [Engine] [SYCL] pair FP16 experts and generalize bounded IQ2 decoding on Battlemage
pulls.author: xiangyuT
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Small FP16 expert groups launch gate/up and down separately for each expert. This patch pairs eligible experts, bounds IQ2_XXS/IQ2_S gate/up decoding and reuses IQ2_XXS metadata.

2026-10-20 retest on a single Arc Pro B70, **32 GiB container RAM limit**, upstream **0.2.0-beta**:
upstream/common frontend `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`; independent candidate `7dc7f483231f31e7ff038ca78e99d9c6b8d5cbce`.
All three lengths are complete.
These are standalone-PR results; no other preview optimizations are enabled.

| Input / output | TTFT upstream → enabled (s) | Improvement | TPOT upstream → enabled (ms/token) | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4096 / 128 | 3.148649 → 2.992501 | +4.959% | 14.734885 → 14.737805 | -0.020% |
| 8192 / 256 | 6.375705 → 6.117914 | +4.043% | 13.859144 → 13.859321 | -0.002% |
| 32768 / 256 | 27.290849 → 26.043838 | +4.569% | 14.393814 → 14.387954 | +0.041% |

Positive improvement means lower latency: mean of three request-wise `100 × (1 − candidate / mean(upstream-before, upstream-after))` values.
The displayed upstream time averages both bracketing blocks. TTFT is request-to-first nonempty SSE text;
TPOT is first-to-last nonempty SSE text arrival divided by engine-generated tokens minus one.
Tiny changes near baseline variation do not establish a meaningful improvement.

## Related discussion

**Source status (2026-10-20):** source branch `feat/sycl-prefill-experts` now points to the tested candidate `7dc7f483231f31e7ff038ca78e99d9c6b8d5cbce`. This PR remains closed; GitHub still reports PR head `faab685c2c0c57c24448754873e5ed0b5d931c4c`. All new measurements and validation in this description apply to the tested candidate. Reopening remains for maintainer review.

This updates the existing PR after the 0.2.0-beta reset and current contribution requirements; it is not a competing submission.
Scope and reopening remain for maintainer review in this thread. Historical pre-beta evidence is folded below.

Related prefill proposal: [#1215](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1215) groups 16 padded experts into oneMKL strided batches. This PR pairs two eligible experts and changes bounded decoding; the implementations and memory requirements differ.

## Approach

Battlemage; positive dimensions, input channels divisible by 256 and combined gate/up FP16 extent below 4 GiB. Bounded decoding has no fixed matrix-shape whitelist. Pairing separately retains IQ2_XXS/IQ2_S gate/up, Q2_0 down, geometry and 1–16-row guards, and flushes pending work before staging-slot reuse. Unsupported formats/extents retain upstream paths. The current upstream ESIMD auto-prefill selection is preserved in both timing arms; it can bypass FP16 paths on eligible shapes. The targeted operator checks exercise pairing and bounded decoding directly.

**New paths are now opt-in.** Every control below is disabled when unset or `0`.
Set controls before starting the engine and restart after changes because values are cached/read during initialization.
Only the controls for this PR are set to `1` in the measured candidate; pure upstream and the candidate-default check leave them unset.

| Control | With `1` |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_SYCL_F16_EXPERT_PAIR` | Independent pairing of eligible FP16 expert groups. |
| `STRATA_SYCL_DEQUANT_GU_BOUNDED` | Bounded GU decoder and permission for its metadata-sharing child. |
| `STRATA_SYCL_GU16_METADATA_QUARTET` | IQ2_XXS/type-16 metadata reuse; requires bounded decoding. |

For full fallback leave all unset or set both F16_EXPERT_PAIR and DEQUANT_GU_BOUNDED to 0. GU16_METADATA_QUARTET has no effect without bounded decoding. The prior root-group-sync removal is retained; native recording is not revalidated here.

## Validation

### Passed

- Exact-source SYCL Release/AOT `bmg-g31` engine build. No non-SYCL backend files are changed.
- 84 finite/guarded gate/up cases pass; 30 full-output hash rows match upstream/default-off/enabled. All 168 real-weight paired-versus-individual expert cases pass.
- Fresh-process serving: all seven corresponding requests (one short warmup, three full-input warmups, three measured requests) have identical engine token IDs and text across upstream-before / enabled candidate / upstream-after at every length. The extra 4K candidate-default block also matches all seven requests.
- Timing blocks restart after an excluded INT8 calibration process, read the same persisted crossover file, and verify its hash is unchanged. Warmup/calibrating/default-functional blocks are excluded from performance.

Sanitized operator output:

```text
gu-baseline.log: RESULT 84 finite guarded GU cases
gu-default.log: RESULT 84 finite guarded GU cases
gu-enabled.log: RESULT 84 finite guarded GU cases
pair-real-weights.log: {"kind":"all_byte_pass","pair_cases":168,"real_experts":2,"GU_H_Down_guards":true}
```



### Failed

The first real-weight pair fixture stopped with `nonfinite`. Source inspection found an asynchronous activation upload whose host vector was destroyed before completion. The original fixture/logs are preserved; after the one-line wait/lifetime correction, all 168 pair cases pass byte-for-byte with guards. The production source and built engine are unchanged. No endpoint latency block for this PR had started before the stop.

### Not run

Runtime scope for this retest is the single B70/Linux/AOT setup below. Other GPUs, Windows, multi-GPU serving, JIT and whole-engine native recording were not revalidated.
Old cross-target compilation, broad prompt/logit corpora and historical microbenchmarks are not new-head evidence.
CUDA/HIP/Metal were not built: this patch touches only the separate SYCL implementation.

<details>
<summary>Environment, exact build settings and complete launch example</summary>

- Ubuntu 24.04, Linux `6.17.0-1007-intel`, Intel xe; Xeon w5-3435X, host MemTotal 503.36 GiB.
- One Arc Pro B70, 32 GB VRAM, PCI `0000:cc:00.0`; only that card is visible to the test container (logical GPU `0`).
- Image `intel/omix:0.4.0-devel-ubuntu24.04`, image ID `sha256:53f0003fa66044935d69065836ba8ac40fab289b94655667fdeac0bdfa7e75c6`.
- oneAPI DPC++ `2026.1.1`; compute runtime `26.31.39395.13`, device driver `1.17.39395+13`.
- Container: `--memory 34359738368 --memory-swap -1 --cpus 16 --shm-size 1g`; one client, no batching. This is a cgroup limit on a larger host, not validation of a physically 32 GiB machine.
- `llama.cpp` dependency `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d`; TLA disabled.
- [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09/IQ2_XS), original IQ2_XS, both numbered shards. Model revision `ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09`.
- MTP from [Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/tree/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540), revision `de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540`; observed draft vocabulary `106299` (137.9 MiB head).

Build the candidate with the following commands in the oneAPI environment. Build the upstream comparator identically,
substituting `/sources/baseline` and `/task/build-baseline`. Sources are pinned to the full commits above.

```sh
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh
cmake -S /sources/pr2584/sycl -B /task/build-pr2584 -G 'Unix Makefiles' \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON \
  -DSTRATA_SYCL_AOT=bmg-g31 -DSTRATA_SYCL_PARITY=ON \
  -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=/deps/llama.cpp
cmake --build /task/build-pr2584 --target strata -j 6
```

The following is a complete candidate configuration sample, not an unexplained environment-variable name.
Save it as `/task/pr2584-candidate.json`. `/sources/baseline` is the pinned upstream checkout used for the common Python frontend;
`/sources/pr2584` is the candidate checkout; `/task` is the writable test directory. `/opt/strata-venv` is the serving Python environment mounted into the container. The `/models/Strata/...` paths are mounts
for the already-prepared pack/tokenizer, the two original GGUF shards and MTP runtime. Adjust those paths to the local files.


pulls.author: xiangyuT
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Upstream disables adaptation in NoHost streamed-expert serving because eviction could leave an expert in neither VRAM nor the mirror. This patch enables synchronous resident/mirror exchanges and counts expert presence in completed verification windows before updating the logical-to-physical tables.

2026-10-20 retest on a single Arc Pro B70, **32 GiB container RAM limit**, upstream **0.2.0-beta**:
upstream/common frontend `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`; independent candidate `781c02f01a36cd60d05fcc75027e8c63cb4b2ea1`.
All three lengths are complete.
These are standalone-PR results; no other preview optimizations are enabled.

| Input / output | TTFT upstream → enabled (s) | Improvement | TPOT upstream → enabled (ms/token) | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4096 / 128 | 3.149382 → 3.165642 | -0.516% | 14.729789 → 14.407403 | +2.179% |
| 8192 / 256 | 6.377939 → 6.403878 | -0.407% | 13.862769 → 13.060571 | +5.783% |
| 32768 / 256 | 27.297558 → 27.422142 | -0.456% | 14.392036 → 13.827926 | +3.963% |

Positive improvement means lower latency: mean of three request-wise `100 × (1 − candidate / mean(upstream-before, upstream-after))` values.
The displayed upstream time averages both bracketing blocks. TTFT is request-to-first nonempty SSE text;
TPOT is first-to-last nonempty SSE text arrival divided by engine-generated tokens minus one.
Tiny changes near baseline variation do not establish a meaningful improvement.

## Related discussion

**Source status (2026-10-20):** source branch `feat/sycl-mirror-adapt` now points to the tested candidate `781c02f01a36cd60d05fcc75027e8c63cb4b2ea1`. Reopening remains for maintainer review.

This updates the existing PR after the 0.2.0-beta reset and current contribution requirements; it is not a competing submission.
Scope and reopening remain for maintainer review in this thread. Historical pre-beta evidence is folded below.

This remains the original synchronous mirror-adaptation proposal. Packed-resident/raw-host and coalesced-exchange extensions from the combined preview are outside this PR.

## Approach

Battlemage, single-device/single-slot serving, NoHost device planning, streamed native experts and a complete mirror. Requires fixed capacity, positive adaptation interval, 1–96 swaps, no prefill borrowing, no elastic cache and no profile saving. Usage counters are installed after verifier initialization and before graph capture. Unsupported serving configurations, CLI and batching retain upstream behavior. This comparison changes the cache adaptation policy, not only an exchange kernel. Warmups also exercise adaptation; results reflect this warmed, repeated synthetic code-review workload.

**New paths are now opt-in.** Every control below is disabled when unset or `0`.
Set controls before starting the engine and restart after changes because values are cached/read during initialization.
Only the controls for this PR are set to `1` in the measured candidate; pure upstream and the candidate-default check leave them unset.

| `STRATA_SYCL_MIRROR_ADAPT` | Master: synchronous mirror-aware adaptation in the guarded serving configuration. |
| `STRATA_SYCL_ADAPT_WINDOW_PRESENCE` | Count an expert once per completed verify window; requires MIRROR_ADAPT. |

MIRROR_ADAPT unset/0 restores upstream behavior. MIRROR_ADAPT=1 with ADAPT_WINDOW_PRESENCE unset/0 counts every routing occurrence. The measured candidate sets both to 1; STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1 and STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1 are separate prerequisites.

### Passed

- Exact-source SYCL Release/AOT `bmg-g31` engine build. No non-SYCL backend files are changed.
- Real-weight synchronous mirror/expert-identity exchanges, repeated swaps, output guards and invalid-argument checks pass.
- Fresh-process serving: all seven corresponding requests (one short warmup, three full-input warmups, three measured requests) have identical engine token IDs and text across upstream-before / enabled candidate / upstream-after at every length. The extra 4K candidate-default block also matches all seven requests.
- Timing blocks restart after an excluded INT8 calibration process, read the same persisted crossover file, and verify its hash is unchanged. Warmup/calibrating/default-functional blocks are excluded from performance.

```text
SYCL mirror adaptive cache: sync exchange; 17756 slots, 25603865600 cache bytes, 9851110400 mirror bytes
```

None observed in the completed checks listed above.

Runtime scope for this retest is the single B70/Linux/AOT setup below. Other GPUs, Windows, multi-GPU serving, JIT and whole-engine native recording were not revalidated.
Old cross-target compilation, broad prompt/logit corpora and historical microbenchmarks are not new-head evidence.
CUDA/HIP/Metal were not built: this patch touches only the separate SYCL implementation.

pulls.title: setup, serve: a run config that holds an API key is readable by its owner only (0600) (#1919)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
One item of #1919: "the run config holds the API key and is written with the default umask ... Expected: mode 0600
on POSIX."

**What it changes.** On Linux and macOS, `strata-<model>.json` was created with the default umask (0644 with the
usual 022), so every user of the PC could read `"api_key"`, the key that guards a server opened with `--host
0.0.0.0`. Now, when the new or the earlier config has a non-empty `api_key`, these are created 0600 from their first
byte (through `os.open(..., 0o600)` plus `fchmod`, so a `.tmp` or `.bak` left from an earlier run is tightened too):
- `setup.write_config` (every config setup writes, including `repoint_config`'s);
- `write_setup_config`'s `strata-<model>.json.bak` of the earlier config;
- the web page's Model settings save (`serve/runconfig.save`) and its `.bak`.

**What it leaves alone.** A config without a key (`"api_key"` missing or `""`): the same bytes and the same mode
as before. Windows: untouched. What is in the file. `docker-entrypoint.sh`: its `cp -f` after a re-setup keeps the
mode of an existing volume file, so a volume config from a key-less install stays 0644 until setup or the page
writes it again. Two consequences a user may notice: in the container (setup and the server run as root) a host user
needs sudo to read a key-holding config on the volume; and a config shared between accounts, or read by another
service user, is no longer readable by them once it holds a key. Removing the key in a save leaves that save 0600.

**How it was checked.**
- `tools/test_setup_risk.py` `test_a_config_with_an_api_key_is_the_owner_s_only_1919`: with umask 022, a config
  with a key is 0600 (also over a 0644 `.tmp` left behind), one without is 0644, and `write_setup_config`'s `.bak`
  of a key-holding config is 0600 with the earlier content.
- `serve/test_runconfig.py`: a save from the page keeps a key-holding config and its `.bak` 0600; a config without a
  key (the fixture's `"api_key": ""`) is saved 0644 as before.
- On `upstream/main` the two key tests fail and the no-key test passes.
- `serve.test_runconfig`, `serve.test_security`, `tools/test_setup_risk.py`, `test_setup_choices.py`,
  `test_setup_menu.py`, `test_setup_unsloth.py`, `test_setup_qwen36.py`, `test_setup_config.py`,
  `test_setup_configs.py`: OK. Python 3.14, Ubuntu (Linux 7.0); not run on macOS or Windows.

pulls.author: qiuzan2001

Fixes the recoverable part of #2451 (forms 1-3 of the report), based on the patch and tests @mbaaku posted there
(credited as co-author). Form 4 (no value generated at all) and the `<arg_value>` form are left out.

**What it changes.** `parse_tool_call` reads only `<parameter=NAME>`. Coder IQ1_M with a coding agent's 21 tools
wrote `<parameter name="command">`, `<parameter name=command>` or a nameless `<parameter>` holding every argument as

With `"tool_call_recovery": true` and tools declared, a small filter (`ParamForms`) in front of `OutputParser`
rewrites those forms into `<parameter=NAME>` (the JSON one into one parameter per key), so the streamed `tool_args`
and the final call agree. Changes from the posted patch, after two reviews:
- it rewrites only where a parameter opens (after the `<function=NAME>` tag or a `</parameter>`), never inside a

pulls.title: batch: a slot that gives its whole conversation back to the main session hands over its checkpoints too
pulls.author: andyhrc
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open that I found.

## Summary

With `--batch`, a request's conversation moves between a batch slot and the solo path (the main session): a
request left alone in its slot goes back to the solo path, and goes back into a slot when another request arrives.
When a slot gives its **whole** conversation back to the main session, the main session's checkpoints are cleared
and only the slot's tokens come over - the slot's own checkpoints (the turn boundary saved when the request was
admitted) stay behind. When the conversation then goes back into a slot or is parked, there is no checkpoint left
to copy. A next turn that continues the prompt but not the whole reply - a client that rewrites the end of the
answer it sends back - then finds nothing to resume from and is read from token 0.

This PR lets the checkpoints come with the conversation, as they already do for a read that gave way (`BYIELD`),
and as an admission and `park=` already copy the longest one into the slot. Independent of #2527 / #2528.

## Seen in use

3 x RTX A4000 16 GB (layer split), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 6` in 3 groups, two people with Claude Code.
A 121,183-token conversation went slot -> solo -> slot while the other user's requests came and went:

```
strata batch: slot 0 takes 121183 tokens (copied in 1501.8 ms)      <- admission, with its turn checkpoint
strata batch: slot 0 gave back 121479 tokens of this conversation (all it holds)
strata batch: slot 0 takes 121699 tokens (copied in 1240.6 ms)      <- back into a slot: no checkpoint to copy
strata serve: prompt 125512 tokens = 0 reused + 125512 read in 40477 ms
```

The next turn shared 121,483 tokens with the slot but split from it 300 tokens into the previous answer, so it
could only resume from the turn boundary - which was gone. 40 s of prompt reading instead of about 4,300 tokens.

## Measured

Same machine; a 27.5K-token conversation that is admitted into a slot, goes to the solo path when the other request
ends, goes back into a slot when a third arrives, and finishes; its next turn sends the first answer rewritten
after its first 8% (before any mid-reply checkpoint). The same server code, only the engine differs:

| Engine | Next turn: tokens reused | read | time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before | 0 | 27,651 | 10.9 s |
| this PR | 27,499 | 152 | 0.69 s |

## What changed

`src/program/generate.cpp` and its SYCL copy `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, where an idle slot gives back all it
holds (`slot_ck == nullptr`): its checkpoints are appended to the main session's chain (each a prefix of the slot's
tokens, so of `live`), with a fresh LRU stamp. The partial-read case (`BYIELD`), which already did this, is
unchanged and not done twice.

## How it was checked

- The scenario above on CUDA (sm_86, Linux), before and after; built with the regular native build.
- Not built: SYCL (no oneAPI here) and HIP. The SYCL change is the same 11 lines in the same block.

pulls.title: SYCL: Fix concurrent prefix cache
pulls.author: rriggs
pulls.body:
# SYCL: Fix concurrent prefix cache

Issue: Resolves #2518, #1906 for SYCL

## Summary
Concurrent requests stop using the prompt cache: with --batch 2 or more, a client whose prompts share a prefix gets a full re-read on every request after the first, where --concurrency 1 reuses the cache. Three changes fix it: the message-boundary scan now reaches past a long final turn, each batch slot keeps the checkpoints its read takes, and an admission carries every checkpoint that prefixes the conversation instead of only the longest.

Builds on #2384 (the slot → solo → slot checkpoint fix) and ports it to SYCL; that and the two remaining failure shapes it left open are the ones here.


## What changed
`include/strata/program/message_boundary.hpp` (via the sycl/ copy's call site; the header is shared)
- `message_checkpoint_boundary()` scanned back from the new assistant turn-token for the previous turn-token, giving up after max_tail = 1024 tokens. A final user turn longer than that — a 2,048-token question over a shared context: a benchmark's depth cell, or a RAG request — meant the boundary between the shared context and the question was never found, so no checkpoint was taken there and every later request over the context re-read all of it. The call site now passes max_tail = 16384; the scan is token comparisons, so the cost is trivial.

`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`
- Mirror (checkpoint_at): each checkpoint a batch slot's read takes is copied into that slot's own checkpoint list at the moment it is created. The main session's list is cleared by the next admission, and at --batch 4 a concurrent admission clears it before the first read finishes, so anything only in the main list can be lost mid-read. The mirror is set per BGEN admission and cleared when the read ends.
- Carry-all (BGEN admission): the admission kept one checkpoint in the slot — the longest prefix of the incoming prompt, which is the turn boundary (context + old question + reply). The message boundary between the shared context and the question is shorter and is what a later request branching inside the conversation resumes from; with only the turn checkpoint in the slot, that request diverged before the checkpoint's end and re-read the whole context. The admission now carries every checkpoint that prefixes the conversation.
- SYCL port of #2384: #2384's engine-side hunk was applied to src/program/generate.cpp only; the SYCL port builds its own copy (sycl/src/program/generate.cpp). Same hunk, applied there.


## Extra Notes
Measured on an Arc Pro B70 (32 GB), Flash-Next IQ3_S, --batch 4, --max-context 131072, four concurrent conversations of ~20.9K tokens each sharing context with distinct questions:
- all four follow-up requests resume at the message boundary (20,916–20,918 tokens reused, 22 read, ~460 ms each); the round takes 3.4 s against 72.5 s when they re-read
- llama-benchy --depth 8192 --pp 2048 --concurrency 4 with prefix caching: the depth cell went from 193 to 710 tok/s aggregate, and the variance dropped from ±57 to ±24
- at --concurrency 1 nothing changes: the reuse there came from the main session's live state, which was never broken     

The message-boundary checkpoint is behind STRATA_CACHE_MESSAGE_BOUNDARY=1 (opt-in, as before); the two new paths only matter when that is on. Nothing outside the listed files changes.

pulls.title: serve: a number json reads as infinite, or nesting deeper than Python recurses, is a 400 instead of a dropped connection
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
**What it changes.** Python's `json` reads `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `NaN` and `1e400` (as an infinite float) and nests as deep as its recursion limit allows. Some of those requests got no HTTP answer at all: the connection closed and a traceback went to the log.

- `POST /v1/chat/completions` / `/v1/messages` with `"max_tokens"` or `"max_completion_tokens"` of `Infinity`, `-Infinity` or `1e400`: `int()` raised `OverflowError`, which no `except` in `_post` took.
- A body nested past `json`'s limit (100,000 levels), or a tool's `parameters` schema 600 levels deep (the server's own walk of it): `RecursionError`, same result.
- `POST /config` (the Settings view's keys): `reasoning_budget_tokens: Infinity` and a 400-digit whole number for `sampling.temperature` (`float()` overflows) dropped the connection the same way, and `Infinity` for `idle_unload_s`, `engine_silence_s` or `sampling.temperature` was accepted and written into the run config as `Infinity`, which is not JSON that other programs (editors, `jq`) read.

Now `OverflowError` and `RecursionError` join the existing malformed-request 400 (`TypeError`, `KeyError`, ... "the request is malformed (...)", traceback in the log; a `RecursionError` logs its last 8 frames instead of ~1,000, ~240 KB per request before). `runconfig._number` refuses a float that is not finite (a 400 naming the key), and `_config_post` answers an `OverflowError` with 400. A huge *whole* number for `idle_unload_s` is still taken, as before.

**What it leaves alone.** Every request that got an answer before gets the same answer: the new `except` entries only catch what used to escape to the socket server, and an error after the answer began is still re-raised as before. The web app cannot send these values (`JSON.stringify(Infinity)` is `null`). Needs the API key where one is set, like any request.

**How it was checked.** New tests, each failing before the change: `test_request_hardening.Hardening.test_an_infinite_number_is_400` (9 cases), `test_a_too_deeply_nested_body_is_400` (600 and 100,000 levels), `test_runconfig.Apply.test_refused` (non-finite values for 8 keys, and a huge whole number still taken), `test_runconfig.Http.test_a_number_too_big_or_not_finite_is_400`. The whole `serve` suite passes on the final commit (788 tests) except `test_keepawake.test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`, which fails the same way on `main` on this Linux box (Ubuntu, Python 3.14). A sub-agent reviewer fuzzed 1e400 and a 400-digit integer into ~22 numeric fields on 10 routes: no dropped connection after the change. Found in a security read of `serve/server.py` (#544's invitation).

pulls.title: bench: community report, 3x GPU (RTX 5060 Ti + 2080 Ti + 3080 Ti), Qwen 125B MoE IQ3_XXS
pulls.author: wronglebowsk
pulls.body:
### Summary

Community benchmark report measuring **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (125B MoE, IQ3_XXS, 3.4 bpw) running across a heterogeneous 3-GPU desktop setup using Strata v0.1.44 with MTP speculative decoding (`--spec 4`, `--spec-min-p 0.65`).

### Hardware and Software
- **GPUs:** 3 NVIDIA GPUs (39.8 GiB total VRAM)
  - GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GiB, `sm_120`, Blackwell)
  - GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti (11 GiB, `sm_75`, Turing)
  - GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (12 GiB, `sm_86`, Ampere)
- **Host CPU:** Dual Intel Xeon E5-2683 v4 (32 cores / 64 threads)
- **RAM:** 185 GB DDR4
- **OS / Drivers:** Linux 7.2.6-generic, NVIDIA Driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4
- **Engine:** Strata v0.1.44 (commit ed4773eb), native unified kernel build (`sm_75`, `sm_86`, `sm_120`)

### Configuration
- **Model:** `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_XXS`
- **Context:** 262,144 tokens (`--kv k8v4`)
- **Parallel Pipeline:** `--layer-split 17,29` across the 3 GPUs
- **Speculative Decoding:** `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.65 --mtp rt`
- **Vision:** `--vision` sidecar enabled

### Results Summary
- **Short Chat Decode:** **104.0 tok/s** median (89.9 – 117.7 tok/s), TTFT **0.45 s** (450 ms)
- **4K Prompt Prefill:** **1,033.8 tok/s** median, TTFT **3.91 s**
- **16K Prompt Prefill:** **2,046.8 tok/s** median, TTFT **7.88 s**
- **32K Prompt Prefill:** **2,788.0 tok/s** median, TTFT **11.55 s**
- **Agent Session:** **108.9 tok/s** median decode (up to **154.8 tok/s** peak), **68.7%** cache hit rate, **4** tokens re-read per session across 6 turns.

All files are formatted per `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`, with personal paths, hostnames, and IP addresses automatically redacted.

pulls.title: web: the header pill's live region says the state when it changes, not the speed every second
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
**What it changes.** The status pill in the header was `role="status" aria-live="polite"`, and `render()` rewrote its text on every one-second poll of `/metrics`, with a number that changes each time while a request runs ("Generating · 45.3 tok/s", "Reading prompt · 37%"). A screen reader read the pill about once a second for the whole answer. Now:

- the live region is a visually hidden span (`#pill-say`, `role="status" aria-live="polite"`) that gets only the state: the text before " · " ("Generating", "Reading prompt", "Idle", "2 queued", "API key needed", "Server not reachable"), and only when it changes;
- `render()` sets the pill once per poll: it set the state and then "N queued" over it, so with a queue the region changed twice a second;
- a `.st-sr` rule (the usual clip pattern) in `app.css`.

**What it leaves alone.** What the pill shows and its colour states; its text stays in the page and readable on demand. On phones, where `#pill-text` is hidden (`display: none` below 640 px), the old live region announced nothing; the new one announces the state there too.

**How it was checked.**
- Headless Chromium (Playwright) with `/health` and `/metrics` faked in the page (no server load): 3 s idle, 6 s generating with tok/s changing every poll, then idle, with a MutationObserver on every `role="status"` element for 12.5 s:
  - before: 12 changes (one per poll, idle included), 6 different "Generating · N tok/s" texts;

pulls.title: [Engine] [SYCL] accelerate IQ4_XS MMVQ on Battlemage
pulls.author: xiangyuT
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

IQ4_XS × Q8_1 decode repeatedly loads headers, packed weights and adjacent activation blocks. This patch shares those loads across quantization groups/token columns and uses an exact bit-select lookup.

2026-10-20 retest on a single Arc Pro B70, **32 GiB container RAM limit**, upstream **0.2.0-beta**:
upstream/common frontend `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`; independent candidate `635ebb20c13255250a5b9fc79f2592a8256e5268`.
All three lengths are complete.
These are standalone-PR results; no other preview optimizations are enabled.

| Input / output | TTFT upstream → enabled (s) | Improvement | TPOT upstream → enabled (ms/token) | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4096 / 128 | 3.151388 → 3.150641 | +0.024% | 14.730184 → 13.866511 | +5.864% |
| 8192 / 256 | 6.377553 → 6.376644 | +0.014% | 13.858997 → 13.072603 | +5.675% |
| 32768 / 256 | 27.296890 → 27.289905 | +0.026% | 14.392408 → 13.585960 | +5.603% |

Positive improvement means lower latency: mean of three request-wise `100 × (1 − candidate / mean(upstream-before, upstream-after))` values.
The displayed upstream time averages both bracketing blocks. TTFT is request-to-first nonempty SSE text;
TPOT is first-to-last nonempty SSE text arrival divided by engine-generated tokens minus one.
Tiny changes near baseline variation do not establish a meaningful improvement.

## Related discussion

**Source status (2026-10-20):** source branch `feat/sycl-iq4-mmvq` now points to the tested candidate `635ebb20c13255250a5b9fc79f2592a8256e5268`. This PR remains closed; GitHub still reports PR head `e5c0c9c69d38c9469c185ba67c0f7d61e0ecc564`. All new measurements and validation in this description apply to the tested candidate. Reopening remains for maintainer review.

This updates the existing PR after the 0.2.0-beta reset and current contribution requirements; it is not a competing submission.
Scope and reopening remain for maintainer review in this thread. Historical pre-beta evidence is folded below.

Related MMVQ implementation: [#2804](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/2804) / [#2803](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2803) select KREG kernels at the same entry points. Coordinate shared dispatch hooks with this pair-reuse/lookup path.

## Approach

Battlemage only, K=2560/6144 and T=1–6, with alignment/row/shape guards; pair reuse and its Q8-split child require T≤4. The single-column K=2560/N=640 case retains its existing dispatch. Q8 splitting is further limited to selected shapes.

**New paths are now opt-in.** Every control below is disabled when unset or `0`.
Set controls before starting the engine and restart after changes because values are cached/read during initialization.
Only the controls for this PR are set to `1` in the measured candidate; pure upstream and the candidate-default check leave them unset.

| Control | With `1` |
| --- | --- |
| `STRATA_SYCL_IQ4_PAIR_REUSE` | Pair reuse; also permits its Q8-split child. |
| `STRATA_SYCL_IQ4_Q8_SPLIT` | Adjacent Q8 blocks/scales; requires pair reuse. |
| `STRATA_SYCL_IQ4_LOOKUP` | Independent bit-select lookup when pair reuse is not selected. |

To disable the complete change, leave all three unset or set both PAIR_REUSE and LOOKUP to 0. Q8_SPLIT has no effect without PAIR_REUSE.

## Validation

### Passed

- Exact-source SYCL Release/AOT `bmg-g31` engine build. No non-SYCL backend files are changed.
- 78 IQ4 full-output hash rows match upstream, default-off and enabled execution; per-column byte comparisons and output guards pass.
- Fresh-process serving: all seven corresponding requests (one short warmup, three full-input warmups, three measured requests) have identical engine token IDs and text across upstream-before / enabled candidate / upstream-after at every length. The extra 4K candidate-default block also matches all seven requests.
- Timing blocks restart after an excluded INT8 calibration process, read the same persisted crossover file, and verify its hash is unchanged. Warmup/calibrating/default-functional blocks are excluded from performance.

Sanitized operator output:

```text
iq4-baseline.log: RESULT cases_outputs=646482 bit_diffs=0 nonfinite=0 failures=0
iq4-default.log: RESULT cases_outputs=646482 bit_diffs=0 nonfinite=0 failures=0
iq4-enabled.log: RESULT cases_outputs=646482 bit_diffs=0 nonfinite=0 failures=0
```



### Failed

The initial upstream/default 4K warmup comparison stopped on different output between a first-time calibrating upstream process and subsequent cached processes. All three measured requests matched, but the warmup mismatch was preserved. Restarting the same unmodified upstream binary with the persisted cache matched all seven candidate-default requests. The current comparison excludes that attempt and uses restarted, cached processes throughout. The upstream cache stores a rounded crossover; the controlled result establishes the initialization-state difference, without isolating every numerical cause.

### Not run

Runtime scope for this retest is the single B70/Linux/AOT setup below. Other GPUs, Windows, multi-GPU serving, JIT and whole-engine native recording were not revalidated.
Old cross-target compilation, broad prompt/logit corpora and historical microbenchmarks are not new-head evidence.
CUDA/HIP/Metal were not built: this patch touches only the separate SYCL implementation.

pulls.title: setup: cpu_info() reads a /proc/cpuinfo without a flags line as no AVX2, not a traceback (#1935)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
The product half of #1935 (the test half is #2552, separate so each can be taken alone).

**What it changes.** On Linux, `cpu_info()` in `setup.py` took the `flags` line's regex match without checking it.
aarch64's `/proc/cpuinfo` lists `Features` instead, and some emulated x86 containers list neither, so setup stopped
with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'` (a traceback on any Linux ARM host). A missing line
now means no flags (no AVX2, no AVX-512), the same way `cpu_floor()` already reads it (it catches `AttributeError`);
the CPU name is still read from `model name`.

**What it leaves alone.** A `/proc/cpuinfo` with a `flags` line (every x86 host this ran on before): the same flags,
AVX2/AVX-512 answer and name. Windows: untouched. What setup does next on an ARM host is unchanged by this PR: it
prints `CPU: <name> (no AVX2)`, `cpu_floor` says "unsupported", and setup stops with its existing message
("this CPU has neither AVX2 nor SSE4.2 ...") instead of a traceback. That message is about x86; making it name ARM
is left out.

**How it was checked.**
- New `tools/test_setup_oldcpu.py` `FloorTest.test_a_cpuinfo_without_flags_1935`: an aarch64 cpuinfo (`Features`)
  and an emulated one (no flags line) give `(name, False, False)` and floor "unsupported"; a flags line with avx2
  still gives `True`. On `main` it fails with the issue's `AttributeError`.
- `python3 tools/test_setup_oldcpu.py`: OK (1 Windows-only skip). `test_setup_choices.py`, `test_setup_amd.py`,
  `test_setup_stale_stamp.py`, `test_setup_unsloth.py`: OK.
- Python 3.14, Ubuntu (Linux 7.0), x86-64 (Ryzen 7 5800X3D); the ARM cpuinfo is a fixture, not an ARM machine.

pulls.title: docs: SECOND_GPU.md names the engine options that exist, not setup options that never did
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
**What it changes.** `docs/SECOND_GPU.md` told the user to run

```
./setup.sh --setup --gpu1-experts 5000 --gpu2-experts 5000 --gpu3-experts 5000
.\START-HERE.bat --setup --gpu1-experts 5000 ...
```

and to add `--gpu-placement layer|stripe` to that command. Setup has no such options: they came with the original patch (109a209e), which put only the engine's options in the tree (`git log -S gpu1-experts -- setup.py setup.sh START-HERE.bat` is empty). Both commands stop with

```
setup.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --gpu1-experts 5000
```

The page now says what works, from the code:
- put `--expert-cache-device1..3 N|auto` and `--expert-cache-remote-placement stripe|layer` (default `stripe`) in the run config's `"args"` (`src/program/generate.cpp` parses them; `serve/server.py` `engine_args` passes `"args"` on), and start Strata again;
- on a PC with several cards setup writes `"gpu"` as the one card it runs on, and `child_env` then sets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to that card alone: the helper cards go in the config's `"env"` (`"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "0,1,2,3"`, applied after `"gpu"`, as `tools/test_calibrate.py` does). A `"gpu"` list of several cards is a layer split, every card runs a stage, and the engine stops ("--expert-cache-remote with a layer split needs a GPU that runs no stage");
- a `--setup` run leaves hand-added `"args"` out (`carry_over` / `args_dropped`) and keeps `"env"`.

pulls.title: calibrate: an engine that stops while a later step measures it drops that candidate, not the run (#2313)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
Fixes the calibrate side of #2313 (who sent the engine its SIGTERM is not known and not touched here).

**What it changes.** In `tools/calibrate.py` a later step's engine that fails to *start* already costs only that
candidate (#1337, `restart()`). An engine that started and then stopped *while it was measured* (`EngineDied`; in
#2313 exit code -15 during the 4-worker step) still ended the whole calibration: setup printed "the tuning did not
finish" and the PCIe share, draft floor and worker counts measured before were lost. Now, in the worker step and the
expert-tier step, a measurement that raises is said (`measuring 4 workers failed: the engine stopped unexpectedly
(exit code -15) - this candidate is dropped, the earlier results are kept`), noted in `report["failed_runs"]`, and
that candidate is dropped; the step's choice is made from the candidates that finished, and when the default's own
run failed the default stays.

`close()` also closes the pipe to an engine that has gone after the failed `QUIT` write, so Python no longer prints
`Exception ignored while finalizing file ... BrokenPipeError` later (the traceback in the issue).

**What it leaves alone.** Every run where no engine stops: the same measurements, choices and output. An engine that
stops during the first sweep (steps 1-3, one engine start) still ends the run, as before: nothing is measured yet.
`setup.py`'s `calibrate_config` is unchanged (it reads only `settings` and `tok_s`). This PR and #2544 (also
`tools/calibrate.py`, #2465) touch different lines of `measure()`.

**How it was checked.**
- `tools/test_calibrate.py`:
  - `test_an_engine_that_stops_while_measured_only_drops_that_candidate_2313`: a stand-in engine raises `EngineDied`
    in the 4-worker run and in the 80-swap tier run; the PCIe share and the 3-worker win survive, both failures are
    in `failed_runs`. On `main` the run ends with `EngineDied`.
  - `test_close_an_engine_that_has_gone_2313`: `close()` on a real child process that has exited leaves stdin
    closed and nothing for `sys.unraisablehook`. On `main` the pipe stays open.
- `python3 tools/test_calibrate.py`: 19 tests OK.
- Python 3.14, Ubuntu (Linux 7.0); no GPU needed (stand-in engines). Not run on the reporter's HIP eGPU, nor on Windows.

pulls.title: config save follows a symlinked run config and writes its target (#2256)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
Fixes #2256. Based on the patch @adolfotregosa attached to the issue (credited as co-author); the code change is
theirs, the tests are rewritten so the web-page test is its own method.

**What it changes.** In the container the server starts from `/opt/strata/strata-<model>.json`, a symlink into the
data volume (`docker-entrypoint.sh`, #1244). The web page's Model settings save (`serve/runconfig.save`) and setup's
`write_config` wrote a temporary file and `os.replace`d it over the path, which replaced the link with a regular
file inside the image: the page said saved, the volume's file never changed, and a recreated container lost the
edit. Both now follow a symlink and write its target (`runconfig.save` keeps `<name>.bak` next to the target), and
the link stays a link.

**What it leaves alone.**
- A run config that is a plain file (every install outside the container): written exactly as before (the change is
  behind `path.is_symlink()`).
- `setup.write_config` on a link into a folder that no longer exists replaces the link with a file, as before (it
  follows only a link whose target's folder exists), so a setup run never fails where it used to succeed.
- `docker-entrypoint.sh` is unchanged. After `setup.py --setup` it runs `cmp -s link cfg || cp -f link cfg`; with the
  link kept and pointing at `$cfg`, `cmp` finds the same file and `cp` does not run.
- One behaviour that does change on purpose: a link whose target cannot be replaced (a read-only or single-file bind
  mount given as `CONFIG=`) now makes the save fail with the server's existing "the run config cannot be written"
  message, where before the edit silently went into the image layer.

**How it was checked.**
- `serve/test_runconfig.py` `Http.test_the_container_symlink_is_written_through_2256`: the config is a link into a
  "volume" folder; a POST /config from the page writes the target, keeps the link, and leaves the `.bak` beside the
  target. Fails on `main` (the target keeps temperature 0.7).
- `tools/test_setup_risk.py` `BrokenEarlierConfig.test_write_config_follows_the_container_symlink_2256`: the same
  for `write_config`, plus a link into a missing folder (replaced by a file, as before). Fails on `main`.
- `python3 -m unittest serve.test_runconfig serve.test_security`: OK. `python3 tools/test_setup_risk.py`: OK.
- Python 3.14, Ubuntu (Linux 7.0); no GPU needed. Not run inside the Docker image.

pulls.title: calibrate: each step says which value it kept, and why the default stays over a round's best (#2465)
pulls.author: qiuzan2001
pulls.body:
Addresses #2465 (the part that is a bug in what calibrate prints; the choices it makes are unchanged).

**What it changes.** `tools/calibrate.py` keeps a round's best only when the confirm round (the best against the
default, interleaved) or the worker/expert-tier measurements show it more than 3% faster (`pick`, `MIN_GAIN`). That
rule printed nothing, so in #2465 the arrows said PCIe share 1, draft floor 0.7 and the 160-swap tier while the saved
config carried the defaults. Each of the three decisions now ends with one line:

```
    the best against the default, median of 3: the default (PCIe share 0.55 and draft floor 0.5) 125.8, the best (PCIe share 1 and draft floor 0.7) 128.1
    -> PCIe share 1 and draft floor 0.7 measured +1.8% over the default (PCIe share 0.55 and draft floor 0.5), not more than the 3% a setting must win by: the default stays
    ...
    -> every 1, 160 swaps, decay 0.97 measured +2.1% over the default (the engine's expert tier), not more than the 3% a setting must win by: the default stays
```

(numbers here are illustrative, from the issue's medians), or `-> <value>: +N% over the default (...): kept`, or
`-> <default> (the default) is the fastest: kept`. One sentence in docs/DETAILS.md ("Tuning for your PC") says so.

**What it leaves alone.** Which settings are chosen and written: the diff only adds `say()` lines and the `verdict()`
helper, which reads the same medians `pick()` does and returns no line when the default did not start. The 3% rule
itself, the sweep arrows, setup's `calibrate_config()` summary line. Whether the 3% rule is the right one (the issue's
other suggestion, "save exactly what the arrows name") is a maintainer decision, so I did not change it.

**How it was checked.**
- New tests in `tools/test_calibrate.py`: `test_a_round_winner_the_config_does_not_carry_is_explained_2465` (the
  issue's case: PCIe 1 +2%, draft floor 0.7 +0.5%, the 160-swap tier +2%: settings `{}`, and the lines say the
  default stays with the gain; plus a kept worker count and a kept PCIe/draft pair) and `test_verdict` (each branch,
  and a default that measured 0 tok/s is not divided by). Both fail on `main`.
- `python3 tools/test_calibrate.py`: 19 tests OK. `python3 tools/test_setup_choices.py`: OK.
  `tools/test_setup_golden.py` has 8 failures (the unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL rows) on `upstream/main` without this change too,

pulls.title: bench: RTX 3060 + i7-7700K, Coder IQ1_M and IQ2_XS calibration results
pulls.author: fszlin
pulls.body:
Results-only community report (no engine changes).

Hardware: RTX 3060 12 GB (PCIe 3.0 x16), i7-7700K (4C/8T, AVX2, no AVX-512),
46.9 GiB RAM, Samsung 970 EVO Plus NVMe (PCIe 3.0 x4) for the model files,
Debian 13 (Linux 6.12), driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.1 toolkit.
Software: Strata 0.1.44.1 (commit 296b59d2), setup's own configuration with
--context 131072 and --draft-vocab en.
Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder, IQ1_M; all 23.4 GiB of experts in RAM,
2,666 experts (5.11 GiB) in the GPU cache.

`tools/strata_bench.py --long`, 3 runs per test, thinking off, medians:
- chat decode 34.3 tok/s (30.1-41.0), first token 1.10 s
- fresh prompts: 4K 974 tok/s, 16K 1,111 tok/s, 32K 1,110 tok/s (32K first token 28.9 s)
- agent session: cache hit 68.6%, turn first token 3.5 s, decode 36.6 tok/s

A same-machine run at 32K context gave the same results within noise (agent
decode about 15% higher at 32K, partly run-to-run variation).

Not tested: answer quality, recall, a real 128K prompt, thinking mode,
power or clock capture. Other Docker services were running during the run.

## Update: IQ2_XS before and after calibration (2026-10-16)

Adds two same-day IQ2_XS reports on the same RTX 3060 12 GB / i7-7700K / 46.9 GiB RAM Linux PC, still project and engine 0.1.44.1 (measured source 296b59d2). Results and report documentation only; no engine, setup, or runtime-default changes.

- Before calibration: `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rtx-3060-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq2-xs/`
- After calibration: `bench/results/2026-10-16-community-rtx-3060-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq2-xs-2/`

Both run `./bench.sh --long` (the `tools/strata_bench.py` wrapper), three repetitions per test, thinking off, temperature 0, parallel 1, 131072 configured context, INT8 KV with 32768 resident cells, vision enabled, 4096 MiB conversation cache / four slots, and async adaptation enabled. CPU vision configuration is retained in the JSON; the speed suite does not test image understanding.

| Median metric | Coder IQ1_M (Oct 14) | IQ2_XS before calibration | IQ2_XS after calibration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat decode, tok/s | 34.3 | 45.7 | 43.7 |
| Agent follow-up decode, tok/s | 36.6 | 48.0 | 47.8 |
| Fresh 4K prompt, tok/s | 974.3 | 883.7 | 894.7 |
| Fresh 16K prompt, tok/s | 1111.4 | 1045.5 | 1049.2 |
| Fresh 32K prompt, tok/s | 1110.3 | 1042.5 | 1049.9 |
| Chat first token, seconds | 1.10 | 0.97 | 0.85 |
| Agent follow-up first token, seconds | 3.54 | 4.04 | 4.04 |
| Agent follow-up cache hit, percent | 68.6 | 68.6 | 68.7 |

Calibration saved `--pcie-frac 0.34 --spec-min-p 0.70 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97`. Saved engine information reports three CPU workers in both IQ2_XS runs. Expert-cache capacity changed from 4324 slots / 5943 MiB to 4387 slots / 6030 MiB. Before calibration the draft threshold was 0.50; PCIe fraction already reported 0.34.

**Interpretation and limits:**
- No clear overall calibration gain on this suite: 4K prompt throughput +1.2%, 16K +0.4%, 32K +0.7%; chat decode -4.4%, agent decode -0.4%; chat first-token latency about 12% lower and agent first-token latency unchanged. These are sequential suites, not repeated independent A/B pairs; cache state and background load were not controlled between suites.
- The earlier Coder launch does not explicitly set the conversation-cache budget or async adaptation. The Coder comparison spans different days, models, generated replies, and complete configurations; this is not an isolated model or quantization speedup claim.
- Largest fresh prompt tested: 32049 tokens. Configuring 128K is not validation of a full-128K session or its memory stability.
- Speed only: no answer-quality, recall, or broad coding evaluation. Live-session observations and ad hoc coding tests are deliberately excluded.
- The post-calibration benchmark reused an already-running server, so it correctly has no `engine-log-excerpt.txt`; its JSON includes launch settings and engine information.
- Private DNS suffixes in the two new JSON reports were redacted beyond the benchmark's automatic redaction. Numerical measurements are unchanged.

**Checks:** both JSON reports parse, both record no failed benchmark requests, relative report links resolve, the benchmark's offline comparison command runs successfully, and `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit. No backend builds: this PR adds benchmark data and Markdown only.

pulls.title: metal: q4_0 KV cache on the Mac engine (--kv q4_0, opt-in; the non-q4 path byte-identical when off)
pulls.author: afanty2021
pulls.body:
## What it changes

The PC engine's q4_0 K/V format (PR #21's FWHT-256 Hadamard rotation) brought to the Metal backend, opt-in
through the engine's existing `--kv q4_0` flag:

- `metal/kernels/kv_q4.metal` (new): the FWHT-256 rotation, quantize and dequantize kernels, and the pool
  layout (576 B per cell per QSA layer against the non-q4 path's 1,056).
- `metal/kernels/qsa.metal`, `qsa_prompt.metal`: the decode and prompt chains made format-aware — the five
  QSA dispatch sites carry function constant 25 in both the pipeline key and the Constants, so a q4 run gets
  its own specializations instead of silently reusing the cached int8 ones over q4 pools.
- `metal/src/engine/`: `kv_format.h` (new, the single source for pool sizes / keys / the format choice),
  `kv_q4_host.cpp` (new, the host side), `window.cpp` and `prompt_chain.inc` wired: q4 pools at init, the MTP
  drafter swaps pools in the same format, `--kv k8v4` refused at startup.
- Both prompt fast paths (the matrix-unit GEMM chain and the flash chain) run over q4 pools; the M1-era
  fallback that read q4 prompts through decode windows is gone, `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window` still forces it.
- `metal/setup_mac.py`: opt-in `--kv q4_0` that lands in the generated engine config's `args`
  (`tools/test_setup_mac.py` extended).
- `tools/quant_quality.py`: opt-in `--kv` on `run`/`prompt` (replaces the harness's fixed fp16 pin only when
  passed).
- `docs/MAC.md`: the option, the quality/speed numbers, the KV-memory numbers, the not-testeds.
- `bench/results/2026-10-15-mac-kv-q4/` (new): the whole Mac measurement round — scripts, raw TSVs, distilled
  run lines, README.

## What it leaves alone

- No file under `src/` or `include/` is touched, so no CUDA/HIP/SYCL build is affected (the Metal engine's
  host code is the PC's, compiled for macOS as before).
- With q4 off, every pipeline key, Constants set and binding order on the non-q4 path is today's int8 one,
  byte for byte (pinned by tests, below). Defaults everywhere: setup writes no `--kv` unless asked, the
  engine's default is the same non-q4 path as the last release.
- Snapshot/restore and cross-format disk sessions: unchanged shared-side behavior (a cross-format session is
  refused by the shared code, as before).

## Opt-in, and how the default path was checked byte-identical

Three independent gates:

1. **Test gates (fc-off byte identity).** `metal/tests/kv_format_test.cpp` pins the five-key reduction (every
   constant set an engine site now binds is compiled as its own specialization) and a stale-key
   counterfactual; `qsa_q4_parity.cpp` and `qsa_prompt_parity.cpp` assert the fc-off outputs against
   double-precision references — with q4 off every key, Constants set and binding order is the current int8
   one, byte for byte.
2. **Engine-level int8 regression (F4).** On the M4 Pro, an int8 short-prompt run on this branch produced
   output byte-identical to the pre-branch baseline run (bd1f3153), zero stub lines — the engine's int8 path
   does not move.
3. **Harness default-args diff.** `tools/quant_quality.py`'s `engine_args()` output was diffed before vs
   after the opt-in `--kv` change over the three gpu_experts modes: identical without the flag. For setup,
   `metal/setup_mac.py`'s `engine_args()` was compared against HEAD over a 48-cell matrix
   (stream x ram x context x shard shapes; 0 diffs) plus the full generated config on three of those cells:
   identical without `--kv`, and with it the pair `--kv q4_0` is appended at the end and nothing else moves
   (pinned by `tools/test_setup_mac.py`).

## Measured (Apple M4 Pro, 20 cores, 48 GB unified memory, macOS 27.0.1; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0, experts
streamed from the SSD; engine built from this branch; every number same-day 2026-10-15, nothing extrapolated)

The framing fact for the reference column: on Metal, `--kv fp16` and `--kv int8` are **one path** — the
window's pools are the int8 ones either way (`kv_format.h`; the fp16-flagged run's own log prints
`KV int8`), and the two teacher-forced TSVs of the round are byte-identical
(md5 `4e942a7375715ac014956fbdbf6110f6`). So the reference below is that shared non-q4 path, q4_0 is the
only smaller K/V format on Mac, and no fp16-vs-int8 delta exists on this backend.

| Measurement | q4_0 | shared path (int8) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Teacher-forced top-1 (4,995 positions, 5 segments) | 94.45% | 100.00% |
| Teacher-forced mean KL / p99 | 0.03414 / 0.4467 | 0.00000 / 0.0000 |
| Perplexity (reference 4.442) | 4.517 (+1.7%) | 4.442 |
| Worst segment (agent transcript, PPL) | +7.3% | — |
| Prompt fast path, 20 full-vocab prompts: top-1 | 100.00% | reference |
| Prompt fast path KL mean / median (upper-middle) / max | 0.03565 / 0.00434 / 0.19546 | reference |
| Decode tok/s (4-id prompt, 64 new) | 20.84 | 21.09 (−1.2%) |
| Prefill tok/s (2,199 tokens prefilled of a 2,200-id prompt) | 213.15 | 215.54 (−1.1%) |
| KV B per cell per QSA layer (12 layers) | 576 | 1,056 |
| KV bytes at 32K context (32,896 cells, calc) | 227,377,152 | 416,858,112 |
| KV bytes at 64K context (65,664 cells, calc) | 453,869,568 | 832,094,208 |
| Log's before-the-arena delta (32K / 64K) | 0.19 / 0.38 GB less | — |
| Arena resident expert slots (32K / 64K) | 16,081 / 15,657 | 15,840 / 15,163 (+241 / +494) |
| Needles (8K/16K/32K at 10/50/90% depth) | 8/9 | 3/3 (controls at 50%) |

- The speed deltas (−1.2% decode, −1.1% prefill) sit at the edge of run-to-run noise: the same-code
  fp16-vs-int8 pair (one path on Metal) measured −1.3% decode, bounding noise near 1%. Single runs per cell.
- The needle miss is 32K at 90% depth: the model took the needle sentence for a prompt injection and declined
  to repeat it (a behavior miss, not a garbled retrieval; all 8 retrievals were the exact codeword).
  Disclosures, as recorded in the bench README: the question ends with "The access code is" — a completion cue
  all arms share, so the comparison is internally fair but the 8/9 is under an easier phrasing than a neutral
  QA form; the miss has no int8 control at 90% depth (controls ran at 50%), so a shared-path refusal there
  cannot be excluded; and its reply was cut mid-sentence at the 64-token budget — the injection-suspicion
  reasoning is explicit, a final refusal sentence is not.

## Disclosures (from the final segment review)

- **Arena stand-by slots:** under q4_0 the prompt fast path is on in every format, and the streaming arena
  plans 576 stand-by slots for the prompt-GEMM chain (64 without it). Escape hatches:
  `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT_GEMM=0` (prompts off the matrix-unit GEMM chain; the arena is then planned without the
  stand-by slots) and `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window` (prompts through decode windows — the slow, exact
  fallback).
- **What the measured fast path is on this host:** the M4 Pro is !k4 (`coop_k4=false`), so the prompt fast path behind
  every prompt-path and prefill number above is the matrix-unit GEMM chain over the v1 layout — the flash chain is off
  by default on !k4 hardware and never dispatched here (same hardware fact as the k4 arm below).
- **Prompt-path numeric divergence class:** the prompt GEMM chain dequantizes its operands to fp16 once per
  chunk (the matrix units), so its numerics are a different floating-point order from the decode window's
  (fp32 fused) — outputs can differ on near-ties, the same class as any reordering. Measured under q4_0 on
  the 20-prompt set: argmax never flipped (top-1 100%), full-vocab KL as in the table.
- **M5 k4-layout q4 numerics:** the fc-7 right-input layouts are compiled as real pipelines in the tests, but
  this M4 Pro is !k4 hardware and never dispatches them (see Not tested).
- `--kv k8v4`: the only statement is the explicit startup refusal — "metal window: --kv k8v4 is not
  implemented on Metal (use fp16, int8 or q4_0)". No partial implementation exists.
- `STRATA_KV_ROT=1` (the PC's rotated int8 K/V env): refused at startup next to `--kv int8`, like k8v4 — there
  the PC rotates the pools and the shared conversation-snapshot tag adds +16 for the rotation, so a Metal session
  would save a tag claiming a rotation its pools do not have (the env is parsed in kv_format_check as
  generate.cpp does; the int8 flag comes through the existing qsa_kv_int8 getter). Next to fp16 (and no `--kv`)
  the env is a no-op on both engines — the rotation is gated on the int8 flag (layer.cpp: `kv_rot = kv_q4 ||
  (kv_int8 && env)`, and generate.cpp sets kv_int8 only for `--kv int8`), so nothing rotates and the tag adds
  nothing; allowed, matching the PC's silent no-op. Next to `--kv q4_0` the rotation is intrinsic and the tag
  never adds it, so the env there is a harmless no-op too.
## Not tested

- The M5 k4-layout q4 numeric arm (fc-7 right-input layouts): compiled but never dispatched on this !k4 host.
- MTP + q4_0 end to end: every measured run used the template's `--spec 2 --suffix-draft 0`; the drafter's
  same-format pool swap is structurally validated by tests, not exercised end to end.
- PC consistency: no PC run this round; the 2026-09-27 PC table (`bench/results/2026-09-27-kv-q4/`) is a
  different backend and a `--kv-resident` streaming configuration, so its numbers are not comparable and are
  not cited.
- Speed repeats (one run per cell; the same-code pair bounds noise near 1%) and needle breadth (one codeword,
  one filler corpus, one run per case, no distractors, int8 controls at 50% depth only).
- Other Macs: every number above is from one M4 Pro, 48 GB.

- Long-context quality: every quality segment is 1,000 tokens. The PC round measured the q4_0 perplexity
  cost growing with context (+8% at 1K to +12% at 8K on a document), so the +1.7% here is a short-context
  number and must not be read as the format's cost at 32K.

Known follow-ups, none in this PR: the flash q4 epilogue is barrier-dense (a perf item only k4 hardware would
feel, and this !k4 host never dispatched it), the flash `vs` dead array is still to be removed,
prompt_chain's pre-existing argv bounds pattern and kv_format_test's pre-existing non-q4 flash constant sets
predate the branch and stay as found, and the Task-1-era nits stand (the `pipe()` per-call cache lookup, the
identity-page gather case, the offsetof asserts).

## Reproducing

`bench/results/2026-10-15-mac-kv-q4/README.md` is the entry point: the exact commands for the
teacher-forced round (`tools/quant_quality.py run/compare`), the prompt-path round (`prompt`/`pcompare`), the
speed pairs (`speed.sh`), the KV/arena numbers (`kvmem.sh`) and the needle matrix (`needle.py`), all with the
committed raw TSVs and distilled run lines beside them (`data/speed-runs.txt`, `data/kvmem-runs.txt`,
`needle-results.tsv`, the stderr summaries); the full engine logs stay out per the repo's `logs/` ignore and
regenerate from the committed scripts. The in-tree test gates: `ninja -C build-metal` then the binaries in
`metal/tests/` (`kv_q4_parity`, `kv_q4_engine`, `kv_format_test`, `qsa_q4_parity`, `qsa_prompt_parity`).
Setup's default-identity is `python3 -m unittest tools.test_setup_mac` (no GPU, no downloads).

note: `data/prompt-path/pcompare.txt`'s reference line was edited by hand to point at the committed
per-prompt.tsv (the regeneration commands are in the README); the aggregates were never hand-touched.

## Prior art searched (issues and PRs)

Re-checked read-only at packaging time (`gh search issues`/`gh pr view` against the upstream repo, terms: metal kv,
kv q4, k8v4, mac backend, apple silicon, metal PRs): **no issue or PR covers KV quantization on the Mac/Metal
backend** — this PR opens that ground, and the PC lineage below is the prior art.

- PR #21 (merged): the PC q4_0 KV mode this branch ports to Metal. PR #120 (k8v4, closed) and #293 (int8
  rotation, closed) are the format's siblings; PR #452/#904 are the PC prompt/append follow-ups.
- Issue #2403 (open): `--kv q4_0` faults on a PC (HIP) when the KV itself streams (`--kv-resident`) with MTP
  drafts. Different code path — the Metal engine has no `--k

pulls.title: feat(setup): add --engine-args to pass extra engine flags to the run config
pulls.author: hlo-world
pulls.body:
## Motivation

setup.sh already exposes some of the engine's flags as its own options (--context, --kv, --vram-reserve-mib, --parallel, ...), but the engine has far more levers than setup has options: the MTP verify depth (--spec) and the prefill chunk size (--prefill), for example, have no setup-side switch. A user who wants them has to hand-edit the generated run config - and a later setup run can rewrite that edit out from under them.

This PR adds one generic switch instead of one option per engine flag: `--engine-args`, a shell-quoted string of extra engine arguments appended to the model's engine arguments, in both install paths (own-path families and ready-made packs).

## How it works

- `--engine-args` takes a shell-quoted string, e.g. `--engine-args '--prefill 1024 --spec 3'`. Parsed with shlex, so quotes around individual values work.
- Replace-not-duplicate: a same-named flag setup already wrote as a flag value pair is dropped before the extras are appended, so `--engine-args --prefill 1024` overrides setup's `--prefill` instead of leaving two occurrences. The engine takes the last occurrence of a flag either way. A two-value flag (such as `--control-vector-layer-range`) is matched by its value count, so it is replaced whole.
- The pre-v0.1.13 config migration (a `--prefill 2048` becomes `auto`) skips a `--prefill` named in the extras: that value is the user's own, not a legacy default.
- After a calibration runs, the saved extras are re-merged on top of it: calibration resets every flag in tools/calibrate.py DEFAULTS, and a user-chosen value would otherwise be moved or dropped.
- Persistence: the raw string is saved in the run config as `engine_args_extra` (added to SETUP_KEYS), so re-running setup keeps the extras without re-passing them; passing the flag again overrides the saved value. `--engine-args ''` clears them.
- Verification: unit tests for the merge (append, replace, two-value arity, boolean flags) and the calibration re-apply, plus an end-to-end `--engine-args` run through `install_own_path` in tools/test_setup_qwen36.py.

## Usage

```
./setup.sh --setup --family qwen36 --model UD-Q4_K_XL --engine-args '--prefill 1024 --spec 3 --ple-io ram'
```

The generated run config's `args` ends with the extras, and a later `./setup.sh` run for the same model keeps them.

---

**Review response** (second revision): the three reported issues are fixed - the test Namespace gains `engine_args` (plus end-to-end and unit coverage for the option), the merge matches same-named flags by their value count so a two-value flag is replaced whole instead of leaving a stray token, and the saved extras are re-merged right after each `CAL.apply` so a user-chosen value stays on top of the calibration. tools/test_setup_qwen36.py passes (21 tests), as does the rest of the setup/calibrate suites.
