pulls.title: spec: STRATA_MTP_ADAPTIVE=1, the MTP window's own size from the draft policy's learned expected-commits-per-ms
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

The draft policy already measures every window size it sees (the round's time, and how many tokens that size committed) to decide MTP-vs-lookup. This makes it also pick **the MTP window's own size** (`STRATA_MTP_ADAPTIVE=1`, opt-in): among the sizes up to the drafter's own, the best expected-commits-per-ms, taking a smaller one only when it beats the full window by the policy's margin (3%).

The rule that matters is the probe order: **every size is measured before a guess can price one out** - the full window first (the incumbent), then the smaller ones largest-first. My first cut measured only the smaller sizes, and the pinned-text bench below caught it locking T4 out forever on a machine whose window rows are cheaper than the prior cost shape assumes (T2:89 windows, 21.12 tok/s).

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

`DraftPolicy::choose_mtp` (new), called from the one-shot and single-GPU serve decode loops only when the flag is set. **Without the flag nothing asks the policy and every window is the drafter's own.** The window only decides how many drafts one round checks - verification keeps the output whatever the window is.

## How it was checked

- `src/spec/draft_policy_test.cpp` (7 new checks): the probe order (full 4→3→2→1), the margin rule picking the best expected-commits-per-ms size, and both extremes (a paying full window stays; a window whose drafts never land shrinks to 1).
- **Pinned-text A/B on this box's GTX 1080 Ti** (IQ3_S, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, 192 tokens, `--spec-follow` pins the text to the model's own greedy continuation of a 42x128 prompt - the repo's own mechanism for comparing speculation settings on the same text - ABBA interleaved):

| stream | fixed | adaptive |
|---|---|---|
| steady (draftable continuation) | 25.12 / 24.62 tok/s, T4:52/54 of 68 rounds | **26.43 / 26.26**, T4:48/50 of 69 |
| shifting (same vocabulary, second half shuffled) | 22.57 / 22.74, T1:89 T4:29 of 132 | 23.05 / 22.03, T1:94/95 |

Same acceptance counts in every pair (123-124 of ~168 steady; 58-60 shifting). On the steady stream both adaptive runs beat both fixed runs (about 5%); on the shifting one the min-p gate already shrinks the windows and the policy stays level with it. The first cut's failure (never measuring the full window) is in the commit message as the counter-example the probe rule is for.

## Not tested

Free-running (unpinned) runs cannot resolve this comparison: issue #152's text variance moved acceptance between 31% and 81% on the same synthetic prompts and tok/s by ±20% - noted so nobody quotes those. Also untested: HIP (no toolchain here), SYCL (separate engine tree), `--batch` windows, the layer-split pipeline's windows (the policy learns there but the hook is not added), and non-greedy draws (the window rule does not touch the draws; `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` remains the recipe for byte-stable greedy text). Two early flagged runs died at the expert-arena setup before any window - environmental (a 46 GiB arena on a memory-pressured box), the site precedes the flag's first use, not reproduced in a dozen later runs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: Slot placement policy for STRATA_SLOT_CACHE_AFFINITY (2/2, depends on #2527): protection by history length, retention scores, value decay, no wait
pulls.author: andyhrc
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open that I found; part 2 of #2527.


## How this PR relates to #2527 (please read first)

This is **part 2 of 3** and **depends on #2527**.

- **#2527 (part 1)**: the engine changes and the server side, with `serve/slot_policy.py` as an interface only.
- **This PR**: our implementation of that interface, including expired-history parking and quadratic idle-value decay.
  Small supporting server changes preserve the last actual use across parking and skip low-value main histories.
  The branch includes the mechanism commits; review the policy changes after #2527.
- **#2843 (part 3)**: slot checkpoints for clients that rewrite the end of their history (Claude Code's
  safety classifier); depends on this one. Its placement side, `STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE`, is in this PR.
- **#2589** (SuperDistance) is the small counterpart for the path this PR does not change: `--batch` without
  pipelined groups (one GPU, or `--batch-groups 1`).
- **Merge order**: #2527 first, then this one. The policy is also applied to our production checkout;
  the time-decay change awaits the next server restart.
- **If you prefer other rules than ours**: keep #2527 and replace `serve/slot_policy.py`; the thresholds below are
  parameters, so many variations need no code at all.

**Rebased on 0.1.45 (2026-10-18)**: the same changes, placed where upstream moved the code; the measurements below were taken on 0.1.44.1. Tests after the rebase: `serve/test_slot_alloc.py` 72, `test_parallel` 35, `test_slots` 30, `test_cache_trace` 4; the engine builds natively on CUDA (sm_86).

## Summary

The policy behind `serve/slot_policy.py`'s interface: which idle slot a request runs in, which history to give up,
how long one is protected, where the solo path's conversation is parked. The policy is kept identical in this PR and our production checkout on the machine described in #2527.
This revision has run in production since 2026-10-15 (GPU checks below).

Plain rules cannot tell which history to give up when a new conversation needs a slot and none is free of value: the
one used longest ago may be a 90K-token conversation whose user is reading the answer, the newest a side request's 300
tokens. This policy weighs length and age, and every threshold is a parameter in the server config's `"env"`, so most
other behaviour is a matter of setting them:

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STRATA_SLOT_TTL_MAX_S` | 120 | protection at 262144 tokens; the whole curve scales with it |
| `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRED_KEEP_SCORE` | 0.01 | an expired history whose current decayed value is at least this goes last |
| `STRATA_SLOT_IDLE_VALUE_ZERO_S` | 1800 | total idle age, including protection, when value reaches zero; 0 disables decay |
| `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_VALUE_RATIO` | 2 | a park takes an expired history worth keeping only when the main session's is worth this many times more; 0: never |
| `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_MIN_VALUE` | 0.01 | a solo conversation whose value at its idle age is below this is not parked |
| `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_KEPT_SHARE` | 0.98 | a slot holding this share of the solo conversation already keeps it (no park) |
| `STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE` | 0.98 | an idle history sharing this share of its own length with the prompt, but not its start, is an older version of the same conversation: replaced in place, protected or not; 0: off |

## The rules

- **Protection by length**: 0.1 s at 500 tokens, 2 s at 2K, 10 s at 8K, 45 s at 32K, 65 s at 50K, 90 s at 100K, 120 s
  at 262144 (piecewise linear).
- **Retention** = (n / 50000)^0.7 x (n / (n + 2000))^2 x (0.25 + 0.75 x freshness), freshness = 1 - age / TTL, 0 once
  expired; overwrite score = 1 / (1 + retention). A fresh 50K history is worth about 1, a 500-token one 0.002.
- **Value after expiry** = (n / 50000)^0.7 x (n / (n + 2000))^2 x 0.25 x (1 - x^2),
  where x = clamp((age - TTL) / (idle_value_zero_s - TTL), 0, 1). Age is measured from the end of the last actual
  use, including the protection period. Loss per second increases throughout the decay window. With the default
  1800 s total idle limit, value is zero at 30 minutes for every supported length. Protection takes precedence
  if a configured limit is shorter than the TTL; 0 disables decay. Allocation and parking use the same value.
  This replaces the earlier exponential half-life parameter. The curve is the requested retention rule;
  no new GPU workload measurement establishes an optimal lifetime.
- **Main-session parking** first checks this value against `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRED_KEEP_SCORE`; a zero or below-threshold
  main history is not parked even if a blank slot exists. A park preserves the main history's last actual use,
  so copying cannot renew its protection or idle lifetime. Continued use refreshes the timestamp on completion.
  A zero-value history is still eligible for prefix reuse until it is overwritten; the score controls replacement
  and parking, never cache validity or matching. No timer deletes history at 30 minutes.
- **Blank slots** (empty, invalid, or a superseded copy) count as expired and worthless; **an expired history is not
  deleted** - it still matches until it is overwritten.
- **A continued conversation** runs in its slot or in a blank slot of a less loaded group, **never in a slot that
  holds another conversation**; near matches (2% of the best, one second of the prompt rate, 4096 tokens) are sources.
  An earlier version that put group balance first moved two idle Claude Code conversations into each other's slot on
  every turn, and each turn read 60-100K tokens from token 0.
- **An older version of the same conversation** (2026-10-17): an idle history that shares at least
  `STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE` of its own length with the prompt but is not its start - the client rewrote its end -
  is replaced in place, protected or not: the new prompt is the newer version of it. Claude Code's safety classifier
  sends such prompts (each query inserts its tool calls before the closing text of the transcript); under the rules
  above the previous query's slot is still protected (65 s at 50K) when the next query comes, so each query would
  take another slot and the older versions would fill the slots.
- **A new conversation** takes what is not worth keeping first (blank, or an expired history below
  `STRATA_SLOT_EXPIRED_KEEP_SCORE`), then by group load, then the lowest value (a blank slot first at an equal
  value). A park uses the same order (`reclaim_slot`).
- **No wait**: every history protected - overwrite the least loss at once (losses within 10% by group load). An
  earlier version waited up to 5 s first, once per request; with more requests than slots each wait ran its full 5 s
  with a slot idle and ended in the same overwrite (7 of 7 in a 15-minute test with 8 clients on 6 slots).
- **Park**: not when its value at its idle age is below `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_MIN_VALUE` (no separate length cut-off; a
  copy of 10K-170K tokens took 0.17-2.56 s in production, every slot paused), not when a slot holds a valid copy of
  `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_KEPT_SHARE` of it already (the copy breaks even with re-reading a 1-4% tail at 1,000-3,000 tok/s);
  the conversation's own older copy; else an older version of it (`STRATA_SLOT_SIBLING_SHARE`, protected or
  not; the most shared first); else the new-conversation order above, where a history worth keeping counts only
  when the main session's conversation is worth `STRATA_SLOT_PARK_VALUE_RATIO` times as much. Never another
  protected slot; nowhere suitable: no park.
- On an engine without `slot_padding_safe=1`, starting a row above a protected idle history costs its retention too.

## Results

The first table and the park line predate this revision. No throughput or cache-hit measurement over a working day
is claimed for the 30-minute default; the scenario checks of this revision follow them.

3 x RTX A4000 16 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, 0.1.44.1, `--batch 6` in 3 groups, `STRATA_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ROWS=1`.
Conversation A (37K tokens) parked, two clients generating 1,500-token answers in a loop (batch mode stays on),
conversations B (9K) and C (7.9K) taking turns about every 30 s - past their protection of about 11 and 10 s. Tokens
reused on turns 1-3:

| Ordering of expired histories | B | C |
| --- | --- | --- |
| by group load first (an earlier version) | 0 every turn | 0 every turn |
| + one still worth keeping goes last (this PR) | all but the ~20 new | 0 every turn |
| + wait for a cheaper slot about to leave its protection (removed) | all but the ~20 new | all but the ~20 new |

In the first row a new turn took the other conversation's expired slot for group balance, so B and C overwrote each
other; in the second, C went to a side request that arrived a second after another one finished, while that one's
1.5K-token history was about to leave its protection. The third row waited for that protection to end, under the same
once-per-request wait; it went with that wait. This PR accepts the case: a protected history is not overwritten while
an expired one can be.

Park: a 37,359-token conversation's next turn after a side request reused 37,352 tokens and took about 1 s (0 and
14 s without), with the same greedy output.

This revision, same machine and settings, `STRATA_SLOT_IDLE_VALUE_ZERO_S=150` so that decay shows within minutes:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| a park keeps the last use | A (11.9K) parked 27.0 s after its turn ended: the slot's age is 27.0 s, not 0 |
| a main history past the zero age | idle 160 s: the next solo request records `park_skip` (main_low_value), no slot taken |
| every slot worth keeping, main worth less than twice as much | six slots of 10,062 tokens (value 0.056), main 12.9K: no park |
| main worth more than twice as much | main 42.1K (0.202): parked into the slot with the lowest value (the oldest); its next turn reused 42,092 of 42,119 tokens, 0.7 s |

Older versions (2026-10-17, same machine, production settings): a 43-45K-token classifier transcript queried six
times beside an agent conversation and a request kept decoding: each query from the second on was placed in the
previous query's slot (`sibling`, 5 of 5), the agent's turns in their own (`reuse`); single user 63.7 tok/s, 6
concurrent x 2048 tokens 178.7 tok/s, as before.

## How it was checked

`serve/test_slot_alloc.py` (the policy's own cases, including the production ones above), `serve/test_parallel.py`
(the trace fields),
`serve/test_cache_trace.py`. New cases cover accelerating loss, expiry continuity and the total idle cutoff,
threshold crossing for 8K through 262K, refreshing age on use, zero-value prefix matching, main-session timestamp
recording, pre-park threshold checks, age inheritance during parking, busy/excluded targets and custom/disabled/
invalid settings. Protected histories retain their protection if a configured total idle limit is shorter.

`python -m unittest serve.test_slot_alloc serve.test_cache_trace serve.test_parallel -q`: 104 tests pass (56.1 s).
`place()` before and after the shared reclaim order chose the same slot in 200,000 random slot tables.
Historical full-suite check before the decay change: `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t .` passes except
`serve.test_responses.NoLeakedSampler`, which fails on upstream main on this machine too.

## Extra Notes

Only the thresholds have names; if you want a different trade-off (for example a fixed protection time, or plain
least-recently-used), `place()` is the one function to change, and the server side does not need to.

pulls.title: Keep conversations in pipelined batch slots (1/2, policy in #2528): active-row windows, park=, cache-aware placement behind a policy interface
pulls.author: andyhrc
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open that I found; happy to open one first if you prefer.

## How this PR relates to #2528 (please read first)

This is **part 1 of 2**.

- **This PR**: the engine changes (active-row windows, `park=`) and the server side of cache-aware placement, with
  `serve/slot_policy.py` as an **interface only** - its policy functions raise `NotImplementedError`.
- **Part 2 (#2528)**: our placement policy - the real `serve/slot_policy.py` and the tests that need it. Its branch
  contains this PR's commits with its own on top.
- **Merge order**: this PR first, then part 2. With both merged, the code is byte for byte what we run in production.
- **If you prefer other rules than ours**: merge this PR and write your own `serve/slot_policy.py` against the
  interface instead of part 2; the server side does not change.
- **This PR alone**: nothing changes until `STRATA_SLOT_CACHE_AFFINITY=1` or `STRATA_CACHE_TRACE=1` is set, and
  those then need a policy.

**Rebased on 0.1.45 (2026-10-18)**: the same changes, placed where upstream moved the code; the measurements below were taken on 0.1.44.1. Tests after the rebase: `serve/test_slot_alloc.py` 15, `test_parallel` 32, `test_slots` 30, `test_cache_trace` 2; the engine builds natively on CUDA (sm_86).

## Summary

On a layer split with `--batch`, conversations are lost between turns in two ways: a pipelined group's window runs
every slot up to its last active one, so an idle slot below an active one is a pad row and loses its state; and a long
conversation on the solo path is overwritten by the next, unrelated request. With agent clients (Claude Code, Codex) -
long conversations in many short turns, short side requests in between - that meant re-reading tens of thousands of
tokens on a large share of turns.

This PR adds the mechanism, all opt-in: the engine keeps idle slots and can park the solo path's conversation, and
the server places requests by what the slots hold. **Which history to give up is left to a placement policy behind an
interface** (`serve/slot_policy.py`): this PR ships the interface only, so you can plug in the rules you prefer. Ours
is #2528; the two together are exactly what we run in production.

## The problem, measured

3 x RTX A4000 16 GB (PCIe 4.0 x16, layer split), AMD EPYC 7543, 62 GB RAM, Ubuntu; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S
(GSQ-RCO), 200K context, int8 KV, `--kv-resident 32768`, `--batch` 3-6 in 3 groups; two people working with Claude Code
and Codex. The engine log of 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-14: of 3,027 prompts of 8K tokens or more, 538 reused less than half
of their previous turn and 40.7M prompt tokens were read again. Classified by prompt lengths (the log has no content,
so this is a heuristic):

| Why the previous turn was gone | Prompts | Tokens read again |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| it was in a batch slot that another conversation took | 170 | 16.4M |
| it ran on the solo path, and the next request (often a short side request) replaced the main session | 244 | 15.0M |
| the client changed the history (not addressed here) | 63 | 6.1M |
| no earlier turn (a first turn, or a restart) | 66 | 3.1M |

At ~2,900 tok/s for long prompts on this machine, the first two rows are about three hours of prompt reading.

## What changed

1. **engine: `STRATA_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ROWS=1`** - a pipelined group's window lists only its active slots
   (`include/strata/program/pipeline_rows.hpp`, `Verifier::batch_launch_rows` for CUDA and SYCL): no pad row, an idle
   slot keeps its conversation, `INFO slot_padding_safe=1`; after a prompt's restore, `CACHE_SOURCE <slot or -1>
   <tokens>`. `tests/core/pipeline_rows_test.cpp`, registered in CMake.
2. **engine: `park=B`** (`INFO slot_park=1 turn_token=<id>`, with the variable above) - when a prompt is another
   conversation (it does not share what the main session holds up to its last turn, the last `<|im_start|>`: two chats
   of one client share a long system prompt, a next turn without the reply's thinking shares the history), the engine
   first copies the main session's conversation into idle slot B and says `PARKED B <tokens>`. The server's claim uses
   the same test.
3. **server: `STRATA_SLOT_CACHE_AFFINITY=1`** - with pipelined groups `pick_slot` asks `slot_policy.place()`, which
   always answers a free slot (a request waits only when every slot is busy, as before); the server tracks the main
   session and asks `slot_policy.park_destination()` before sending `park=`; without `slot_padding_safe=1` it tracks
   from `BADM`/`BT`/`BDONE` which idle slot a later window has padded over. `/metrics` gains `live.cache_events` (the
   last 96 placement events), request keys and client addresses (the socket's, not `X-Forwarded-For`), `live.solo_*`
   and per-slot cache fields; `STRATA_CACHE_TRACE=1` adds a per-request snapshot of what each slot shared with the
   prompt (`serve/cache_trace.py`, lengths only).

The interface (`serve/slot_policy.py`): `place`, `park_destination`, `cache_state`, `superseded_slots`,
`reliable_flags`, `configure` / `settings` - their docstrings state the
contract. Without a policy, `STRATA_SLOT_CACHE_AFFINITY=1` and `STRATA_CACHE_TRACE=1` raise `NotImplementedError`.

With every variable unset the engine's output and the generation path are unchanged. The new `/metrics` fields are
present with the variables unset too (additive only); if you prefer them behind a variable, say so.

## Results (same machine, with our policy from #2528)

| | Without | With |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 37,359-token conversation, next turn after a side request: tokens reused | 0 | 37,352 |
| ... time of that turn | 14 s | about 1 s |
| parking 36-37K tokens (five runs) | - | 414-451 ms |

The greedy output (temperature 0) after the restore was the same as before the side request. Alternating
conversations under load: see #2528.

Throughput of commit 1 (the same binary with `STRATA_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ROWS` off / on, `tools/serve_load.py`, 6 clients
x 2048 tokens, temperature 0, one run each): 177.4 / 173.5 tok/s total, first token p50 2.4 / 3.7 s; one client 67.3 /
66.7 tok/s. With all six slots busy the windows hold the same rows; other runs of this configuration with other builds
measured 173.9-178.2 tok/s, so this is close to the run-to-run spread, but it was not repeated.

## How it was checked

- Each commit: `generate.cpp` and `verify.cpp` compile with the CUDA build's flags (sm_86, Linux);
  `tests/core/pipeline_rows_test` passes; `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t .` passes except
  `serve.test_responses.NoLeakedSampler`, which fails on upstream main on this machine too (5 of 6 runs).
- Not built: SYCL (no oneAPI here) and HIP; the SYCL change mirrors the CUDA one.
- This code runs in production on the machine above since 2026-10-15 (with part 2 on top).

## Extra Notes

A client that rewrites history (for example one that drops the reasoning of earlier turns) cannot match a cached
prefix whatever the placement does; not addressed.

pulls.title: [Engine] Preserve decoded batch-slot conversations before slot reuse
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `--parallel`/`--batch` slots, an admission (or a prompt read that gives way, BYIELD) copies a new conversation over an idle slot while the conversation cache holds only that slot conversation's prompt as it was read before admission. When the user returns to that chat, the engine reads the decoded reply again, or the whole prefix if the cache evicted the older copies meanwhile. Still the case on 0.2.0-beta (measured below: a returning 10,329-token conversation replayed all 10,329 tokens).

With this change an idle text slot is parked into the conversation cache before it is overwritten, so the returning turn reuses everything the engine held: on the same test, 0 tokens replayed for both returning conversations.

## Related discussion

none (a correctness fix to existing conversation-cache behaviour; no new flag or default).

## Approach

- `park_slot` parks an idle text slot's sessions, checkpoints and per-slot draft K/V through the same budget, RAM admission and snapshot path as `park_current` (renamed `park_source`), unless the main session or a parked conversation already holds that state (`ConversationCache::holds`, new).
- A slot that gives its conversation back to the main session gives its checkpoints with it, so newer versions supersede the older parked copies (#342); with `STRATA_SLOT_CKPT_MOVE` they move as the one continued from did.
- Image slots, and MTP without a per-slot batch drafter, are not parked (logged), as before.
- Files: `include/strata/core/conversation_cache.hpp`, `src/core/conversation_cache_test.cpp` (new cases), `src/program/generate.cpp` (CUDA) and `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` (SYCL) with the same logic.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it (head 4972d47c). 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, SYCL AOT `bmg-g31` built with the repository dev image. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30`, `"parallel": 2`, `--max-context 16384 --vram-reserve-mib 512 --kv int8 --spec 4` (no MTP: a SYCL layer split turns batch MTP off, and MTP slots without a per-slot drafter are not parked), `--conversation-cache-mib 32768 --conversation-cache-slots 4`.

Test (the same script for both builds): conversations A and B (10,074-token prompts, each with three code words spread through it) decode 256-token replies in the two slots; C and D are then admitted into those slots; A and B return one at a time with their replies kept verbatim and ask for the code words. Expected: the returning turn reuses prompt + reply - 1 = 10,329 tokens.

**Passed:**

- This branch: A returned with `cache_n` 10,329, `prompt_n` 28, replayed 0; B with `cache_n` 10,329, `prompt_n` 28, replayed 0. The engine logged one `conversation cache: parked 10329 tokens from slot 0 in 212.5 ms` (main logs none). Both replies repeat their three code words.
- `main` e88ee39d, same test: A replayed 0 (its slot was not overwritten), B returned with `cache_n` 0 and replayed all 10,329 tokens (the failure this fixes). Code words correct in both builds.
- CPU tests of this branch in the oneAPI build image (`g++ -std=c++20`): `conversation_cache_test: 4824 checks passed`; `conversation_split_failure_test` rc=0 (allocation-failure cases preserved at 1, 2 and 3 stages).
- The SYCL engine of this branch builds (`strata`, AOT bmg-g31). Per-card health passed after both runs.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** CUDA build and GPU run (`src/program/generate.cpp` was edited to mirror the SYCL change and reviewed, not compiled: no NVIDIA card here); MTP slots with a per-slot batch drafter (`--batch-mtp`, refused on a SYCL layer split); image slots (not parked by design); long contexts (on 0.1.x a 199,501-token four-chat RAM-return test on an expert-parallel development stack reused 199,839 held tokens and replayed 0 reply tokens; not re-run on 0.2.0).

## Limits

- Latest text continuations are covered; returning to an arbitrary shorter branch point of a conversation is outside this guarantee.
- No latency claim: parking costs a snapshot copy into the cache budget at admission time.
- Independent of #2511.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

pulls.title: bench: community reports - RTX 4090 and Minisforum MS-01 + 4x Tesla V100 SXM2 (NVLink), Flash-Next at 204800 / 262144, engine 0.1.44.1
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
Two reports of the same release on two different machines, measured 2026-10-14/15 with **one method, one prompt generator and one case set**, so they can be read side by side. Each is self-contained: the previous version was re-measured in the same session, and a same-binary control gives the noise band that decides what is a change.

- `bench/results/2026-10-14-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-code/` - RTX 4090, IQ3_XXS, context 204800, code-explanation prompts; the follow-up of the [2026-10-08 report](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/tree/main/bench/results/2026-10-08-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-code) (same PC, same model, same config), so it covers 0.1.41, 0.1.42, 0.1.43/0.1.43.1 and 0.1.44/0.1.44.1 at once
- `bench/results/2026-10-14-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-ru/` - the same sweep with Russian prose
- `bench/results/2026-10-14-community-4x-tesla-v100-iq3-s-262k-code/` - a **Minisforum MS-01 mini PC driving a 4-slot SXM2 NVLink carrier board** (4x Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB) with `--layer-split auto`, IQ3_S, context 262144, measured out to **260331 prompt tokens (99.3% of the window)**; first report from this machine in this format

The reason for publishing them together is that they are the positive and the negative half of one claim: **the two defaults that turned on in 0.1.41 and 0.1.42 are adaptive.** On the single-card RTX 4090, which streams experts from NVMe, they give +31% short-prompt reading and +13.8% decode, and both effects were isolated to their own feature by turning each one off. On the four-card V100 machine, where 98% of the experts are resident, the engine's own start log turns `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` off by itself and never arms the CPU prefill share - and neither gain appears. That is the designed behaviour, and now it is measured on both sides.

## Hardware, model, configuration

**Machine 1 - RTX 4090.** RTX 4090 24 GB (23028 MiB), Ryzen 9 7950X, 46464 MiB RAM, NVMe (ADATA LEGEND 960), Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-38, driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.4. Model `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs`, context 204800, INT8 KV, `--mmap-experts`, expert cache auto (6986 slots / 11.24 GiB), MTP draft pack, `--spec 4`, `draft_vocab=cyrillic`, experimental speed projection (control vector, layers 4-44), `--vram-reserve-mib 989`, `--pool-workers 10`, and `env: {"STRATA_PF_FUSED": "1"}` in the server config. Engine **compiled from source** for `sm_89` with CUDA 13.4 - the release publishes Windows archives only, so this is the only path on Linux; 0.1.38 … 0.1.40.3 and 0.1.44.1 in these reports were all built the same way on this machine.

Unchanged from the previous reports: the launch command (compared line by line in the server log), the server config files, the learned expert profile, and the engine's auto prompt chunk - `8192 tokens, a 96-slot ring` in 0.1.38 through 0.1.44.1 - so the numbers are comparable with the earlier reports from this PC.

**Machine 2 - a Minisforum MS-01 mini PC plus a four-slot SXM2 carrier board.** Host: MS-01 (DMI: "Micro Computer (HK) Tech Limited" / "Venus Series", board AHWSA, BIOS AHWSA.1.22 of 2024-03-12), i9-13900H (14 cores / 20 threads, Raptor Lake-P), 96 GB DDR5, 2 TB NVMe (SOLIDIGM P44 Pro), 2x 10GbE SFP+ + 2x 2.5GbE, Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-38, driver 580.178.04. **RAM is not a constraint: ~16.7 GiB in use with the model loaded, peak 17.5 GiB of the 96 GB installed (under 19%).**

The GPUs are not PCIe cards in a server: they are four SXM2 modules on a **Spring V100 SXM2 4-GPU carrier board (model V100-SXM2-NVLINK_D V2.10)** - NVLink 2.0 in NVIDIA's Hybrid Cube Mesh, host side behind a Broadcom **PEX8748** Gen3 switch with two external SFF-8654 channels (single x16 or 8+8 bifurcation), the modules liquid-cooled on a 360 mm AIO loop as the board's manual requires. The board ships with a `PCIe x16 -> 2 x SFF-8654` transition board; **only one cable is used here, and the link runs as x8, because the MS-01's full-length slot is wired electrically as x8** - measured, not assumed: `/sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:00:01.0` reports `max_link_width = 8`, the negotiated link is 8.0 GT/s x8, the board's x16-capable upstream port negotiates x8 Gen3, and each of the four GPUs behind the switch also negotiates x8 Gen3. So four x8 GPU downlinks share one x8 host uplink (4:1 oversubscription, ~7.9 GB/s shared), while **NVLink is fully up: 6 links per card at 25.781 GB/s, `nvidia-smi topo -m` reports NV2 between every pair** - ~155 GB/s per direction per card. Whether Strata's inter-layer traffic goes over NVLink or the PCIe switch was probed - see below.

Model `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s`, context 262144, INT8 KV, `--mmap-experts`, `--vram-reserve-mib 512`, `--pool-workers 12`, `--spec 4`, `draft_vocab=cyrillic`, the same kind of control vector and online-learned expert profile. Engine **built on the machine with a private CUDA 12.8 toolkit and a private gcc-14** for `sm_70` (`STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`, `engine-cuda12/BUILD.json` records `"source": "local"`); 0.1.43 and 0.1.44.1 were both built with that same toolchain, and the two trees' server configs were compared before the swap and are **byte-identical**. Sizing from the start log: `layer split: CUDA3 runs layers 37-47, expert cache 5442 slots (11.37 GiB)`, `token graph hit path: 24088 resident experts`, `layer split: 98% of the experts resident, the prompt path's streamed ring 96 slots`, and the prompt path borrows cache slots from the other three cards. **The prompt chunk is the same `8192 tokens, a 96-slot ring`** as on machine 1, which is what makes the two reports method-comparable.

**An interconnect probe was run on machine 2** (`nvlink-probe.py`, raw data `nvlink-probe-phases.json`). DCGM's NVLink byte counters are not obtainable there — DCGM 4.7.0 has no profiling module on that host, and that does not change with a root host engine — so the probe measures the other side of the same question: any byte not going over NVLink has to cross the card's PCIe link, and those counters work unprivileged. Result: idle is exactly 0 on all four cards; a generation request moves ≤ 0.7 GB per card (matching `docs/MULTI_GPU.md`: a few hundred KB per verify window); **a 125 351-token prompt moves 62–78 GB into and 7–12 GB out of every card, sustained 1.2–1.6 GB/s with peaks of 5–6 GB/s against the ~7.9 GB/s ceiling of the Gen3 x8 link the machine has**. The engine's P2P prompt routes are not enabled in this configuration (`STRATA_PREFILL_HELP` unset, no `--peer-device`, and `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1591` takes the mapped-host route `whether or not the cards could reach each other (measured there)`). So on this machine the prompt path is PCIe-bound, and that is a plausible mechanism for the small long-prompt regression — stated as a hypothesis, not separated by these runs.

**P2P itself was then measured directly** (`p2p-probe.cu`, results in `p2p-probe-results.json`), because the code comment behind `pp->p2p = false` records that the host route was chosen from measurements on **2x RTX 3090, PCIe 4.0 x16 each, no P2P** (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1560-1570`) — i.e. on hardware where the P2P branch could not be turned on at all. On this board it can be: `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer` is 1/1 on all six pairs with `AccessSupported=1`, `NativeAtomicSupported=1`, `PerformanceRank=0`, NVML reports `NVLINK=OK` for every pair, and **peer copies run at 38.4 GB/s idle and 29.4–29.9 GB/s while the server is doing a 31375-token prefill** — a bandwidth this PCIe fabric cannot produce (7.9 GB/s per card behind one shared x8 uplink), which is also indirect evidence that an enabled P2P route really would use NVLink here. Enabling peer access costs **0 MiB** of device memory, so it is not blocked by the 256–1350 MiB of VRAM free with the model loaded. What the prompt path actually moves is 62–78 GB *into* each card against 7–12 GB *between* cards, so the first thing a P2P route would change is the smaller flow; whether the dominant flow could also be served from a peer's resident copy is the question I cannot answer from the counters. A platform dossier — capability matrix, measured peer bandwidth under load, the byte budget per phase, the code map, and a validation protocol that works without DCGM counters — is in `nvlink-platform-dossier.md`, together with the probes. A branch is enough to test any of this here: the machine builds from source with a private CUDA 12.8 / gcc-14 in ~20 minutes and rolls back in 2.

**A follow-up run (2026-10-15) measured both fabrics and the two prompt-path knobs** — dossier §8, data in `interconnect-experiments/`. With the model unloaded, so that all six pairs can be measured: card↔card **38.8 GB/s on every pair in either direction**, host→card 6.29 GB/s one card at a time and **1.56 GB/s per card when all four stream at once** (6.29 / 4 = 1.57 — the 4:1 oversubscription measured rather than inferred). Summing the four cards per second during one 125351-token prefill: 5.25 GB/s in a median second, 7.67 GB/s at p95, 9.33 GB/s in the worst second, 33 of 75 seconds at or above 6 GB/s — against a nominal Gen3 x8 ceiling of 7.88 GB/s per direction, so a long prefill here runs at about two thirds of its host link. `--peer-device` is refused together with `--layer-split` by the argument parser itself (`strata generate: --peer-device cannot be combined with --layer-split (use one or the other)`), which closes the configuration question: in 0.1.44.1 no flag or environment variable makes a layer-split machine issue a GPU→GPU copy. `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP` and `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_FRAC` were then run in two sessions each against a control at 120 / 2048 / 3072 / 4096 / 32768 / 131072 tokens: **no change in reading speed anywhere** (every difference inside the control band); the helper raised card→host traffic by 15–20 GB per request in one session and not in the next, and where it engaged it cost no measurable time. The one anomaly seen alongside it — two 14–21 s stalls at 131072 tokens with the reading rate unchanged — did not reproduce.

## Method (identical in both reports)

Full warm-up sweep run first and discarded (on machine 1 its first 4K read ran at 1522.7 tok/s with a 2.62 s TTFT against 2155.7-2166.5 tok/s and 1.85 s in the measured pass - the cold expert cache, not the version), then 4K / 16K / 32K / 64K / 128K and the top of the configured context, plus a generation-only case; 3 runs per configuration, medians reported; a random marker in every prompt so the prefix cache is never reused (the reused column reports 0 in every run of both machines); throughput from the engine's timing fields; TTFT over streaming; `tools/needle_bench.py` at 32K and 128K, depths 10/50/90; peak VRAM sampled every 2 s (per card on the four-card machine). The whole session on each machine - warm-up, measurement, control, previous version, opt-outs - ran as one detached process, so nothing was interleaved by the driver.

## What each folder contains

`runs.json` (0.1.44.1) plus reference runs, so each comparison is self-contained:

- `runs-0.1.40.3-previous.json` (machine 1) / `runs-0.1.43-previous.json` (machine 2) - the previous version, **re-measured in the same session**: its binary / whole tree was swapped in, the server restarted, the warm-up sweep run and discarded, then the same sweep measured, then swapped back;
- `runs-0.1.44.1-control.json` - a full repeat of the sweep on **the identical 0.1.44.1 binary**: the noise band of this method (machine 1: prompt -5.8…+2.1%, decode -6.7…+8.9% depending on the case; machine 2: prompt within ±0.3%, decode -4.4…+1.8%);
- machine 1 only: `runs-0.1.44.1-no-tail-skip.json` and `runs-0.1.44.1-no-cpu-share.json` - the same build with one new default turned off each, which is what turns "consistent with X" into "caused by X";
- machine 1 only: `runs-long-context.json`, `runs-long-context-control.json`, `runs-long-context-0.1.40.3.json` and the matching `needles-long-context*.json` - the same sweep extended to 156291 / 185531 / 200015 actual prompt tokens out of the confi

pulls.title: engine, server: #533 elastic VRAM per GPU of a layer split (VRAM <reserve_mib> [device])
pulls.author: GonzMartinez
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`#533` on a layer split: the VRAM reserve becomes per card.

- engine: `--vram-elastic` no longer refuses a layer split; every card's expert cache is segmented (512 MiB), and `VRAM <reserve_mib> [device]` moves one card's cache (device = the engine's number, 0 = the main card, the `--split-device` numbering) or every card of the run. Shrink/grow run on that card against its own free VRAM, the eviction scan is scoped to that stage's layers (slot numbers are per cache), and the prompt loan is re-lent at the largest chunk every card can still lend. One report line per card, then `VRAM-DONE`.
- verify: `refresh_residency` re-decides the 100%-resident fast path from the residency as it is now, and throws away the captured window graphs when it flips — the zero-doorbell capture holds no per-layer plan waits, so a shrink that takes a resident expert has to leave it, or the CPU pool is never told about the misses.
- server: `POST /v1/vram` takes `gpu` (validated against the run's cards), answers with one entry per card in `gpus` plus the totals over them, and still works with an engine that answers one line and no `VRAM-DONE`. `min_free_vram_mib` reads every card the run will use and names the busy ones.
- a lone dash names the start's reserve so a device can follow it (`VRAM - 1`): a number in the first slot IS the reserve, so `reserve_mib: null` with a `gpu` used to send `VRAM 1` — a 1 MiB reserve on EVERY card, not the start's reserve on GPU 1. `VRAM -1` is still refused.
- `shrink` keeps whole segments and rounds its keep UP, so a reserve asked for arrived up to one segment short and a need under one segment freed nothing at all; `segment_floor` rounds the keep DOWN to a segment boundary (12000 asked from 8292 free lands 12384, not 11872).
- SYCL port: the same command syntax and report lines; the segmented cache stays CUDA-only, so it refuses.
- `vram_elastic` and `vram_segment_mib` are editable keys (from the next start), and `tools/comfy_vram_handoff.py` drives the whole handoff: reserve, queue, wait, /free, restore.
- docs: the #533 paragraphs in DETAILS.md and MULTI_GPU.md.

## What it leaves alone

The default path is byte-identical to the last release: `vram_elastic` is opt-in, and with it off a split runs as before. Single-card runs, the helper caches, `--peer-device` and the resident low-RAM mode are untouched. The split itself never moves: a card keeps its dense weights, its session and its KV, and nothing is reloaded.

## Measured (2x RTX 3090, driver 595.71.05, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, layers 0-23 / 24-47, `"parallel": 2`, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`, 512-token greedy decode)

- With ComfyUI's Qwen-Image 2.1 on the second card: GPU 1 went from 16380 to 1024 MiB of cache (559 of 8833 experts, the prompt chunk 8192 -> 512) and left 15200 MiB free, where the image model's measured peak at 1024x1024 with DynamicVRAM is 15240 MiB. With ComfyUI holding 15240 MiB on GPU 1 and that card's cache at 3072 MiB, the engine answered a request in 1.1 s.
- With the cache whole on both cards, `"vram_elastic": true` and `false` give the same cache (20 091 slots, 33 037 MiB) and 106.6 vs 106.4 tok/s — the segments cost nothing while nothing is handed away.
- A second CUDA client costs 305 MiB before it allocates anything (`torch.cuda.init()` and its first tensor took the card from 23505 to 23810 MiB used); it fails in `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain` with CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at 80 MiB free and attaches at 613.

## How I checked

- `serve/test_vram.py` on this branch: 14 tests, OK — the line with a device, per-card aggregation, the old engine, refusals, the route, a reserve kept for an unloaded engine.
- `serve/test_server.py` on this branch: 311 tests, OK — its free-VRAM guard takes the per-card reading and checks a two-card run.
- Built and measured on CUDA (the 2x 3090 above). The SYCL port carries the same syntax and refuses; it was not compiled here, and no HIP build was run.

pulls.title: setup: Build on ROCm 10 (TheRock Packaging)
pulls.author: brookpatten
pulls.body:
## Summary
Updates compilation to handle the changes in rocm 10

## What changed
setup.py: detect ROCm toolchain layout instead of hardcoding ROCm 9 paths

ROCm 10 (TheRock packaging) moved the LLVM toolchain under core/: the compiler is now bin/amdclang++ (no more llvm/bin/clang++), headers live in core/include, and device bitcode is in core/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode. Two hardcoded assumptions broke on that layout:

-DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER pointed at the nonexistent llvm/bin/clang++. CMake treats a changed, missing compiler as a cache reset and silently reconfigures CPU-only — which drops the strata target from build.ninja, so the build dies with ninja: error: unknown target 'strata'.
--rocm-path / HIP_PATH pointed at the ROCm top level. With ROCm 10's clang, that skips injecting the HIP device runtime wrapper, so device-context math (fmaxf, fabsf, logf, __expf, …) resolves to host-only glibc declarations and every kernel .cu fails with "no matching function" (~44 errors across sampler, router_top10, quantize_act, …).
The fix detects which layout is present and picks the first path that exists, in both build_engine_hip and build_image_engine:

hip_compiler: bin/amdclang++ → llvm/bin/clang++ → core/lib/llvm/bin/clang++
rocm_inc (for HIP_PATH and --rocm-path): core when core/include exists, else the top level
bitcode path list gains core/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode
Older ROCm layouts keep working — the previous paths remain in each fallback chain. 

Verified on ROCm 10.1.0 / gfx1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700): full clean build, engine launches, on cachyos with rocm-bin 10 installed from paru.

pulls.title: setup: pin -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON and -DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON in the CUDA and HIP engine builds (stale CMake cache silently drops the K-quant kernels)
pulls.author: p3lusa
pulls.body:
## Summary

`setup.py` compiles the CUDA engine without ever passing `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS`, relying on the CMake `option()` default. That default was `OFF` when the option was introduced (`ac7db2e5`, 2026-10-05) and flipped to `ON` in `465cd61d` (2026-10-12). **CMake does not rewrite an option that is already in `CMakeCache.txt`**, so a `build/` folder first configured while the default was `OFF` keeps `STRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS:BOOL=OFF` forever — even after `git pull` brings the new `CMakeLists.txt` with the `ON` default.

`source_hash(ENGINE_SOURCES)` fingerprints the source files (so setup *does* recompile after the pull), but it does **not** cover CMake option values. The result: setup recompiles the engine, silently, with the Q6_K gate/up grouped expert kernels still disabled.

This PR pins `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON` explicitly in the CUDA engine build (`setup.py`) and in the Dockerfile build, so a stale cache entry can no longer override the default the build promises.

## The failure (exact startup error)

Starting the model `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, whose routed experts are Q4_K gate/up + Q6_K down) through `./setup.sh --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6001 --setup` (choice 6 → 1), the engine started and immediately refused to load the model:

```
[strata] engine started: .../engine/strata --serve --native .../Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --max-context 8192 --prefill auto --mtp 2
strata-q36: blk.34.experts are Q4_K/Q6_K, which the native expert kernels do not take (build with -DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON for Q6_K)
```

The engine binary in `engine/` had been built with `STRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=OFF`, so `K::native_expert_supported()` (`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:973`) rejected the Q6_K expert layout and the model never loaded. Retrying with smaller `--max-context` (131072 → 65536 → 32768 → 8192) did not help — it is not a memory issue, the kernels were simply absent from the binary.

## Root cause

1. `build/CMakeCache.txt` on the affected machine had `STRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS:BOOL=OFF`.
2. The repo checkout (`296b59d2`, 2026-10-14) **does** contain the `ON`-default commit `465cd61d`, and its `CMakeLists.txt:83` reads `option(STRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS ... ON)`.
3. But the `build/` folder predates that flip: it was configured when the default was still `OFF`. CMake keeps the cached value and ignores the new default on re-configure.
4. `setup.py`'s recompile trigger (`source_hash`) saw the changed sources and recompiled — but recompiled with the cached `OFF`, so the Q6_K kernels were never compiled in.

Verified with a minimal CMake reproduction:
- configure with `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=OFF` → cache `OFF`
- change the default in `CMakeLists.txt` to `ON`, re-configure **without** the flag → cache stays `OFF` (the bug)
- re-configure **with** `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON` → cache becomes `ON` (the fix)

## Is it hardware-specific?

**No.** It is a CMake cache-staleness issue, independent of GPU, architecture, or OS. The only requirements to hit it are:
- a `build/` folder configured before the default flipped to `ON` (i.e. before `465cd61d`), and
- a model whose routed experts use Q6_K (Unsloth UD-Q6_K_XL, and UD-Q4_K_XL files that put Q6_K on the down-projections, e.g. `blk.34` here).

The affected machine was an **RTX 3080 Ti (sm_86, 12 GB VRAM), 26 GB RAM, Linux (Ubuntu)**, running the model in Strata's hybrid-experts mode (51/256 experts per layer in VRAM, the rest in pinned host RAM). The hardware only determines *how* the model runs (hybrid experts on a 12 GB card); it does not cause the failure. Any platform with a stale `build/` cache and a Q6_K-expert model hits the same error.

## The patch

- `setup.py` (`build_engine`, CUDA path): add `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON` and `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON` to the engine `cmake_build` definitions. An explicit `-D` on the configure command line overrides the stale cache entry, so the engine always has the Q6_K gate/up kernels and the `strata_kq` K-quant MMQ library its default build promises. (`465cd61d` flipped both options OFF→ON the same way and CMake caches both the same way — qiuzan2001's review; pinning only one leaves the other stale.)
- `setup.py` (`build_engine_hip`): both pins on the HIP configure too. `build-hip` has the same stale-cache case — the `ON` default never reaches an existing cache. Safe for the gfx906/#1396 concern: `setup.py` never builds gfx906 (its AMD path is gfx1100/gfx1101/gfx1102/gfx1200/gfx1201), and both flags match the `main` defaults, so a clean HIP configure is byte-identical — the `-D` only overrides a stale entry.
- `Dockerfile`: same pins, for consistency (the Docker build starts from a clean cache, so it already gets `ON` from the default; the explicit flags document intent and are robust if the default ever changes).
- `tools/test_setup_choices.py` / `tools/test_setup_amd.py`: assert both flags reach the CUDA and HIP engine def lists, so a future edit that drops a pin fails a test.

## Verification

On the affected machine, after reconfiguring with `-DSTRATA_Q6K_EXPERTS=ON` and rebuilding, the engine binary gained the Q6_K grouped-kernel instances (`native_gu_kernel<14>` / `native_down_kernel<14>`; template instantiations went from 102 → 143), and the same startup line that previously failed now reaches:

```
strata-q36: prompt experts on the native grouped kernels
strata-q36: context 8192 cells, prompt chunk 2048, MTP block loaded, ...
strata-q36: warmed up in 15.5 s ...
READY 8192 stop
```

The `blk.34.experts ... do not take` error is gone.

pulls.title: HIP: decode QSA top-k on the register kernel at 262K capacity
pulls.author: rindi-ismail
pulls.body:
## Title
HIP: decode QSA top-k on the register kernel at 262K capacity

## Summary
On HIP with `--max-context 262144`, every decode window runs the QSA top-k on the one-workgroup reference kernel. The `TK_PER_MAX` register kernel exists on AMD for exactly this capacity (its comment says so), but only the prompt path reached it. This sends decode there too.

Measured with the repo's own tests (`qsa_topk_parity`):
- **Same ids:** identical selections on gfx1201 and gfx1100.
- **Kernel time:** 2.1-2.4x faster at 98K-262K on the R9700 and 1.7-1.8x on the 7900 XTX.

End to end, on an R9700 + 7900 XTX split, decode at 157K context goes from 66.8 / 64.7 to 69.8 / 68.6 tok/s (two pairs), and short context is unchanged.

## What changed
`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, `qsa_block_topk`, HIP only (9 lines):
- **Old behaviour:** a call without a block count (decode; its graphs are captured) kept `fit = TK_T * TK_PER` = 33,792 blocks. With a 262,144 capacity (`max_blocks` = 65,538), every decode call went to `qsa_block_topk_ref`. That kernel is one 256-thread workgroup per query, rereading the keys on each of its four radix passes, so a decode window with 2-6 queries ran its selection on 2-6 compute units.
- **New behaviour:** on HIP, such a call uses `TK_T * TK_PER_MAX` (66 per thread, 67,584 blocks), so decode runs `block_topk_reg_kernel<TK_PER_MAX>`. That kernel reads only the live `n_bid + 1` blocks and returns the same ids.
- **Escape hatch:** `STRATA_TOPK_DECODE_REG=0` restores the old dispatch. It is read once, like the other switches here.

Left alone:
- the CUDA dispatch (the change is inside `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`; the `#else` branch is the original line)
- the prompt path's `counted` rule and `kRegMinBlocks`
- both kernels and the cluster path

## How I checked
**Ids.** `src/kernels/qsa_topk_parity.cpp` was built against this change and run on each card with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`:
- `--selftest`: PASS on both.
- Decode-shaped calls (4 queries, `COUNT=0`, capacity 262,144) at 2,500 / 4,096 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 24,576 / 32,768 / 98,304 / 160,965 / 262,144: PASS, with identical ids for continuous, 64-level and all-equal scores.

**Kernel time** (the parity test's `dispatched` time, 4 queries, before -> after; 30-50 reps):

| Context | R9700 (gfx1201) | RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) |
|---|---|---|
| 2,500 | 0.038 -> 0.042 ms | 0.036 -> 0.039 ms |
| 8,192 | 0.041 -> 0.040 ms | 0.038 -> 0.038 ms |
| 24,576 | 0.059 -> 0.042 ms | 0.050 -> 0.039 ms |
| 32,768 | 0.063 -> 0.040 ms | 0.051 -> 0.037 ms |
| 98,304 | 0.171 -> 0.078 ms | 0.125 -> 0.073 ms |
| 160,965 | 0.218 -> 0.102 ms | 0.162 -> 0.096 ms |
| 262,144 | 0.383 -> 0.158 ms | 0.275 -> 0.154 ms |

Below about 4K cells the register kernel's fixed cost is 3-4 µs more per call. Over 12 QSA layers that is under 0.2% of a ~26 ms window, and short-context decode measured the same.

**Where it showed up.** A decode profile (`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1 STRATA_SPLIT_TIMING=1`) at 1K / 64K / 157K showed the same ~2 tokens per window at every length. The QSA `scores+topk` per window grew as follows:

| Stage | 1K | 64K | 157K | 157K with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R9700 | 0.10 ms | 1.31 ms | 2.05 ms | 1.30 ms |
| XTX | 0.08 ms | 0.98 ms | 1.47 ms | 1.11 ms |

**End to end.**
- **Machine:** Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB + RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, layer split 26 (R9700 first), `--pipeline-windows 2` (the default), Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 125 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04.1, ROCm 7.2.4.
- **Model and settings:** Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --mtp`.
- **Method:** one restart per arm, run in the order off, on, off, on. Four fixed questions with no prefix, then a 156,996-token prefix read once and the same four questions on it from the prompt cache. 300 tokens each, greedy. ms/window comes from the engine's `decode timing` line.

| Arm | Short tok/s | Short ms/window | 157K tok/s | 157K ms/window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `STRATA_TOPK_DECODE_REG=0` (before) | 79.5 / 82.1 | 27.53 / 26.98 | 66.8 / 64.7 | 32.91 / 32.25 |
| this PR | 82.4 / 82.6 | 27.53 / 27.52 | 69.8 / 68.6 | 31.10 / 31.87 |

Tokens per window were 2.17-2.38 in every arm.

**Builds:**
- HIP built (`gfx1100;gfx1201`).
- CUDA was not built, but its preprocessed source is unchanged.
- SYCL has its own file.

## Extra Notes
- Related: #669 found the same cost of the reference top-k above 135K cells on CUDA.
- A further change I measured but left out of this PR: a parallel digit search inside `block_topk_reg_kernel`. It is another 10-25% on the kernel and showed no visible end-to-end change. It is on my fork's [`xtx-r9700-tuning`](https://github.com/rindi-ismail/Strata/tree/xtx-r9700-tuning) branch with the raw logs and scripts ([docs/XTX_R9700_SPLIT.md](https://github.com/rindi-ismail/Strata/blob/xtx-r9700-tuning/docs/XTX_R9700_SPLIT.md)).

pulls.title: prefill: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING may list one table per architecture
pulls.author: rindi-ismail
pulls.body:
## Title
prefill: STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING may list one table per architecture

## Summary
On a layer split over two AMD architectures, the second card rejects the one tuning table and runs its prompt GEMMs on untuned hipBLASEx, although `tools/hip` ships its table. This lets the variable list one table per architecture. Measured on an R9700 (gfx1201) + RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100): a fresh 32K prompt reads at 1,870 tok/s instead of 1,277 (+46%), a 157K prompt at 3,006 instead of 1,846-1,866 (+62%). Decode is unchanged.

## What changed
`src/prefill/gemm.cu`, `create_hipblaslt_state` only (inside `#if defined(__HIPCC__) && defined(STRATA_HIPBLASLT_AVAILABLE)`):
- `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING` may hold several paths, separated by `:` (`;` on Windows). Each card loads the first table whose architecture family and hipBLASLt version match it.
- If none matches, the per-file errors are printed joined with `; ` and the card falls back to hipBLASEx, as before.
- **A single path behaves exactly as before**, apart from the error text when that one file is rejected, which is the same message.

Left alone:
- the table format and `hipblaslt_tuning.hpp`
- the per-solution checks and the GEMM path
- setup (it still writes one table; a split with two architectures can now be given both by hand)
- the SYCL copy of the loader (`sycl/src/prefill/gemm.dp.cpp`)

Before, on this split, the log said `prefill gemm: tuning architecture mismatch: file=gfx1201 runtime=gfx1100; using hipBLASEx`. Now it loads both: `hipBLASLt tuning enabled (26 rows, gfx1100, version 100202)` and `(24 rows, gfx1201, version 100202)`.

## How I checked
- **Machine:** Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB + RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, layer split 26 (R9700 first), Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 125 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04.1, ROCm 7.2.4, hipBLASLt 1.2.2 (100202). Engine 0.1.44.1 at `296b59d` built with setup's HIP build for `gfx1100;gfx1201`.
- **Model and settings:** Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--prefill auto:32768`.
- **Method:** one engine restart per arm, and a fresh prompt with a random nonce first so nothing is reused.

| Arm | 32K prompt tok/s (per restart) | 157K prompt tok/s | Short decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx1201 table only (the XTX falls back) | 1,277 / 1,278 / 1,276 | 1,846 / 1,866 | 94.4 / 95.8 |
| both tables | 1,874 / 1,873 / 1,868 | 3,006 | 95.3 / 94.3 / 95.2 |

- **Default path:** with one path the loop runs once with the same `load()` call, so the result is the same as before.
- **Builds:** HIP was built. CUDA and SYCL were not. The changed function sits inside the HIP + hipBLASLt block, so the CUDA build compiles the same source as before, and SYCL has its own file.
- **Answer quality:** the XTX's prompt GEMMs now use the tuned hipBLASLt solutions from the shipped gfx1100 table, which round differently from hipBLASEx. Answer quality was not measured separately.

## Extra Notes
- Raw logs, scripts and the full write-up of this machine's tuning are on my fork: [docs/XTX_R9700_SPLIT.md](https://github.com/rindi-ismail/Strata/blob/xtx-r9700-tuning/docs/XTX_R9700_SPLIT.md) and [bench/results/2026-10-14-community-r9700-7900xtx-split](https://github.com/rindi-ismail/Strata/tree/xtx-r9700-tuning/bench/results/2026-10-14-community-r9700-7900xtx-split).
- A possible follow-up: setup could write both tables when it finds two architectures. It is not in this PR.
