pulls.title: [Engine] Report batch MTP draft counts across slot handoffs
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When a request's decode moves between the solo path and a batch slot (it is promoted into a slot when a second request arrives, and goes back to solo when that one ends, #1869), the API's `timings.draft_n` / `draft_n_accepted` and the `/metrics` totals reported only the last leg's drafts. `BDONE` carried no draft counts at all. Still the case on 0.2.0-beta: a 512-token request reported 220 accepted / 312 offered while the engine's own DONE lines for it summed to 300 / 435.

With this change every leg is counted: the same test reports 300 / 438, equal to the engine's per-DONE sums and to the `/metrics` delta.

## Related discussion

none (a reporting fix; no change to decoding or defaults).

## Approach

- `BDONE` appends the slot leg's accepted / offered draft counts (CUDA `src/program/generate.cpp` and SYCL `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`; `0 0` without `--batch-mtp`).
- `serve/server.py`: `_apply_bdone` adds them to the admission's counts; `carry_leg` / `add_carry` keep them when a slot request goes back to the solo path, so a final solo DONE adds to the earlier counts instead of replacing them. An older engine's four-field `BDONE` leaves the admission's counts as they were; a missing count stays unreported, an explicit zero stays known.
- `docs/BATCHING.md`: the optional protocol fields. `serve/test_slot_drafts.py` (new) and `serve/test_parallel.py`: the mixed-leg and handoff cases.

## Validation

Setup: 0.2.0-beta `main` e88ee39d against this branch rebased on it (head 9e736891). 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, SYCL AOT `bmg-g31` built with the repository dev image. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ISTA GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split 30`, `"parallel": 2`, `--max-context 16384 --vram-reserve-mib 512 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp <BF16 draft layer> --mtp-max-t 4`.

Test (the same script for both builds): (1) a 512-token request decodes alone, a 64-token request arrives 4 s later (the first is promoted into a slot, then handed back to solo when the short one ends); (2) two 256-token requests together. The API's draft counts are compared with the sum of the engine's per-request DONE / BDONE draft lines in the same log window and with the `/metrics` totals delta.

**Passed:**

- This branch, case 1: API 300 accepted / 438 offered = engine sum 300 / 438 (legs 80/123 solo, 0/0 and 0/0 in the slot, 220/315 solo) = `/metrics` delta. Case 2: 0 / 0 everywhere (a layer split runs no MTP in the slots).
- `main` e88ee39d, case 1: API 220 / 312 against an engine sum of 300 / 435 (the first solo leg's 80 / 123 dropped); `/metrics` matches the API, so both under-report. Case 2: 0 / 0.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_slot_drafts serve.test_parallel` in the runtime image: `Ran 47 tests ... OK`.
- The SYCL engine of this branch builds (`strata`, AOT bmg-g31). Per-card health passed after both runs.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** CUDA build (the CUDA `BDONE` emitter was edited and reviewed, not compiled: no NVIDIA card here); non-zero slot-leg counts on SYCL (needs `--batch-mtp`, refused on a layer split; on 0.1.x an expert-parallel development stack gave BDONE 40 / 46 plus final DONE 304 / 371 = API 344 / 417, not re-run on 0.2.0).

## Limits

- Telemetry only; no throughput or quality effect.
- "Accepted" means accepted by verification, including a draft not emitted because the request then stops.
- Independent of #2526.
- Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code): the code, the measurements and this text were produced by Claude on the submitter's two Arc Pro B70s, at the submitter's request.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: serve: a durable on-disk conversation tier with a warm→cold cascade that degrades instead of deleting, per-stage segments, a prefix restore ladder, Windows chunked large pages, and a parking target (ram|disk|auto) that spills a rejected park
pulls.author: shahrokhzargarpour
pulls.body:
## Title
serve: a durable on-disk conversation tier with a warm→cold cascade that degrades instead of deleting, per-stage segments, a prefix restore ladder, Windows chunked large pages, and a parking target (ram|disk|auto) that spills a rejected park

Issue: Resolves #2597

## Summary

**This series is built, and it is what runs.** The engine binary produced from this tree is the one serving on the machine that took every measurement in this body; the numbers below are that binary's. Where this document says **"applies, not verified"**, it refers to the **cherry-pick-alone** case in *The commits each capability needs*: a commit applied on its own to `main` was checked for conflicts, and nothing was compiled in that scratch tree. It is **not** a statement that the code was never built.

**Fourteen capabilities in one series; all of it opt-in and off by default.** With every flag absent the tree is byte-for-byte upstream, and the series applies clean in order on the base. The map, one line each:

- **A. Durable on-disk conversation tier** (`07613f4b`) — the conversation cache gets a disk copy (spill, archive, system-prompt cache).
- **B. Two-pass streaming session restore** (`c514173e`) — restore a parked image without holding its K/V in RAM.
- **C. Per-stage content-addressed segments** (`26d29b52`, `7cd80013`) — the shared prefix as addressable pieces, with the frontier anchored at the `<|im_start|>` opener.
- **D. Prefix restore ladder** (`1cc359d4`, `STRATA_RESTORE_LADDER`) — a parked image that fails validation no longer loses the prefix.
- **E. Windows chunked large pages + expert-arena-first** (`3e14ba41`) — the CUDA side.
- **F. Continuous batch-read agenda** (`0269a3c2`, `STRATA_BATCH_AGENDA`, opt-in).
- **G. Parking target + spill-instead-of-discard + transient floor** (`acc09864`, `571f1203`) — the transistor `ram|disk|auto`.
- **H. Default spill / system-prompt-cache directories** (`2f8d3cad`, `b0c177f1`) — the folder resolves without a flag.
- **I. Disk-tier & cache observability** (`20e5760b`, `b9b83c86`, `16b67c46`, `1f572df4`) — engine `INFO`, `/metrics`, Monitor rows.
- **J. The cascade** (`ac5a1746`, `33d41214`, `686d0b57`, `bb31e4e4`) — a warm level; a level at budget degrades instead of deleting; only the cold deletes.
- **K. Cold-level eviction fix** (`ba89b7fc`) — the cold evicts by its MiB budget, not by a hidden cap of 256 entries.
- **L. Monitor** (`de0f1f3a`, `8f6bfa10`, `5320268c`, `1895e7ed`, `256d76b3`) — per-slot clocks, a tachometer, the solo speed, the RAM row.
- **M. Installer** (`528be20f`, `6a93aadf`) — several requests at once, and the conversations kept on disk.
- **N. Documentation** (`940eb9bf`, `d40cb783`, `957d27b0`) — the tier, the ladder, the frontier, the pages, the parking, the identity.

Three of the fourteen **apply alone on `296b59d2`** — **A, B and E** ("apply alone" means the cherry-pick is conflict-free, not that the capability runs on its own). The rest are a chain, and each says in its own section which commits it needs. Every capability below is a self-sufficient unit: its problem, its flags and defaults, its numbers with their source, what it does **not** claim, and the minimal set of commits to take it.

Two framings hold for the whole series. **The parking work** adds a parking target and the rule that closes the hole the disk tier was built for: when the physical-RAM gate rejects a park, the capture is no longer discarded — it spills to disk under a transient floor, and a discard is now *counted* and printed (`discards=N`). **The cascade** gives the disk tier a level above it: the conversation cache runs **RAM → warm M.2 → cold disk**, and a level that runs out of budget **demotes** its oldest entry instead of deleting it; only the cold level deletes, and each level is switched off by its own budget.

**The installer's always-path does not change, and that is measured rather than asserted:** `setup.py` before and after the change, across 5 machines × 5 sizes × (`--yes` or Enter), gives **50 cases and 50 identical results**, with `--yes` asking nothing at all.

## What changed

### A. Durable on-disk conversation tier (spill, archive, system-prompt cache)

**The problem.** With four parallel slots, long contexts and a bounded `--kv-resident`, host RAM runs out while a conversation is being parked, and the disk tier sits *after* the physical-RAM admission gate. When the gate failed, the engine **dropped the capture instead of spilling it**, so the next turn **re-prefilled the whole prompt from token 0**. There was no durable on-disk copy of a parked conversation to fall back on at all.

**What it does.** The conversation cache keeps a durable on-disk copy.
- `--conversation-cache-spill-dir` + `--conversation-cache-spill-on park` — the spill folder and the moment it is written; the folder survives a restart and the `SCSM` sidecar is rescanned on open.
- The spill tier owns its **writer thread** (only the write is asynchronous). The `SCSM` sidecar carries tokens and images, not K/V; `best()`/`load()` restore on re-entry.
- **Identity and validity** — `SessionFileIdentity` (model fingerprint + config fingerprint, `engine = STRATA_VERSION`). `kMetaVersion = 2`; **v1 is still read**.
- **Budget and GC** — `--conversation-cache-disk-mib` (**default `8192`**), `--conversation-cache-spill-when-full evict-oldest|reject`, `--conversation-cache-spill-max-age-days`.
- **Free-space preflight** — `--session-min-free-mib` (**default `4096`**).
- **Shared root** — `--system-prompt-cache` (dir/budget/slots/max-age/key) and the shared-`Sys` dedup of the segment tier.
- **Match knobs** — `--conversation-cache-similarity` and `--conversation-cache-n-min`, both at their defaults (**`0`**), so a disk hit is accepted with no minimum overlap. (These two are **not** in upstream `main`.)
- With every flag absent the tree is byte-for-byte upstream.

**What was measured.**
- Restore from disk against a cold prefill: **171,516 tokens in 657 ms** read back from disk — the whole reload **6.6 s** — against **158,649 ms (158.6 s)** to prefill the same prompt cold — **≈24×** (the ratio is against the 6.6 s reload, not the 657 ms read). Source: the tier note of 2026-10-14 and the published body's demo table; the 657 ms line is in the engine log.
- The disk tier on disk (2026-10-15): **268.0 GiB of images** + **53.9 GiB of segments** across **256 conversations**, against a 450 GiB budget. Source: a directory listing of the spill folder.
- System-prompt cache (the whole engine log, read 2026-10-15 11:27): **8 hits / 106 misses**.
- **Changing the system prompt invalidates all reuse today** (live engine, 2026-10-15): the control (identical system prompt) reuses **3943/3948**; a change **at the end** reuses **0/4226**; a change **in the middle** reuses **0/3958**; and the control that proves it — the same changed prompt sent a second time — reuses **4221/4226**. Counts identical across 3 repetitions. **The cause is located:** the hash of each segment **chains the frontier** (`prev_frontier`), and the system prompt is the **first** segment — the **root** of the chain; the matcher cuts at the first divergence (`a segment after a hole can never be a valid reuse`). Source: `src/core/conversation_segments.cpp` and `09-implementacion/2026-10-15-system-prompt-recalculable-v1.0.0.md`.

**Updates we plan** (design, not implementation, no date promised): stop the segment identity from chaining the frontier; store the K **de-rotated** and re-anchor them; and recompute the recurrent state (**GDN**) **bounded to the changed span**.

**What this does not claim.** The C++ of this commit was **not compiled**: the state is **applies, not verified**, never a tilde. The ≈24× is against the 6.6 s reload, not the 657 ms read. One machine, one model, one pass per cell — not a benchmark and no throughput promise.

**Upstream issues.** Related — **#47** and **#661** (both closed/completed) are the origin requests for a conversation tier on disk; **#2596** (ours, open) *reports and documents* that a different `K` invalidates the whole on-disk tier.

**The commits it needs.**

| commits (in order) | take it alone? | needs first | verified? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `07613f4b` | **yes** | — | applies alone on `296b59d2`; `serve/runconfig.py`, `serve/server.py`, `serve/test_monitor.py`, `serve/test_runconfig.py`, `setup.py` → `py_compile` OK; **the C++ not compiled → applies, not verified** |

### B. Two-pass streaming session restore

**The problem.** Restoring a parked image materialised the K/V in host RAM; a large image held its whole K/V in RAM during the restore.

**What it does.** The session restore runs **two passes**: the read pass validates the image, the apply pass copies it in **16 MiB blocks** — so the K/V is not held in RAM as one whole.

**What was measured.** No separate figure of its own — **no measurable before/after**: the mechanism is measured through A's restore pair (171,516 tokens / 657 ms read / 6.6 s reload / 158.6 s cold), where the two-pass restore is the path that reads it back. Source: the tier note of 2026-10-14.

**What this does not claim.** Only C++/`.cu`/docs — **the C++ was not compiled: applies, not verified**. There is no isolated measurement of the streaming pass itself.

**Upstream issues.** Related — **#1269** (open PR) carries a nearly identical streaming-restore title; **#747** (closed/completed) is the multi-GPU parking terrain the streamed restore reads back.

**The commits it needs.**

| commits (in order) | take it alone? | needs first | verified? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c514173e` | **yes** | — | applies alone on `296b59d2`; only C++/`.cu`/docs → **applies, not verified** |

### C. Per-stage content-addressed segments (and the anchored frontier)

**The problem.** A park rewrites the whole image at once, and the shared root of a prompt (`Sys`) is written far more often than it is read back: the engine had no way to address the reusable pieces of a prompt separately.

**What it does.**
- `--conversation-cache-segments` + `--conversation-cache-segment-budget-mib` — a **content-addressed per-stage** segment tier; `conversation_segments.{hpp,cpp}`.
- `7cd80013` — the **frontier** of the segment store is anchored at the `<|im_start|>` opener, not at the role token.

**What was measured.** Nothing live for this commit on its own — **no measurable before/after**: the note declares host checks **174 → 188** — **declared, not reproduced**. The shared-`Sys` dedup is **not conclusively measured** (one pass, concurrent traffic).

**What this does not claim.** Not verified (the measurement does not run a parse per commit, and the C++ is not compiled here). The segment plan currently cuts **three** pieces (`Sys`, `Other`, `Answer`); `Think`/`Read`/`Write`/`ToolCall`/`ToolResult` exist in the enum but are **not materialised** (the cutter is missing). The `Sys` dedup is not conclusively measured.

**Upstream issues.** Related — **#2508** (ours, open) proposes compacting the stationary KV components, the same territory as the segment dedup; **#1962** (open) proposes sharing prefix KV blocks. No upstream issue covers the cutter itself.

**The commits it needs.**

| commits (in order) | take it alone? | needs first | verified? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `26d29b52`, `7cd80013` | no | A, B | applies in order; not verified. The note declares host checks 174→188 — declared, not reproduced |

### D. Prefix restore ladder (`STRATA_RESTORE_LADDER`)

**The problem.** A parked image that fails validation — e.g. `discard snapshot (stage count: saved=0 current=1)` — loses the prefix, and the turn re-prefills. (#2595 is 40 of these in one boot, one of 165,543 tokens.)

**What it does.** `STRATA_RESTORE_LADDER` — when a parked image fails validation, the ladder rescues the prefix from the bad image so the turn does not lose it; `conversation_restore_ladder.hpp`.

**What was measured.** The ladder's `image rejected` branch **did not fire in the live matrix

pulls.title: [Needs Testing on Multi-GPU, Nvidia, AMD, Intel, MacOS] Web Engine tab: GPU switches for the user's vendor + in-page restart/save
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
**Needs Testing on Multi-GPU and AMD, Intel, MacOS** — the detection, catalog, and restart paths are designed to work on Linux, Windows, and macOS, and are unit-tested for all of them, but the only real hardware exercised here is a single AMD card (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201, Linux). NVIDIA, Intel, Apple Metal, and multi-GPU layer splits are proven by mocks/tests only.

## What this adds

A web **Engine** tab that shows only the speed/feature switches relevant to the GPU(s) the user actually runs, lets them edit and save those switches into the run config, and **restarts the engine from the page** so the new env/args take effect. Plus a human/AI-readable reference of every switch grouped by GPU manufacturer.

- `docs/GPU_OPTIONS.md` — every env var, engine CLI flag, and setup/CLI option grouped by manufacturer (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Metal, cross-vendor, CPU-only), each with what it changes, its gate, and recommended use.
- `docs/ALL_OPTIONS.md` — the master inventory the catalog is generated from (engine flags, server CLI, installer CLI tables).
- `serve/engine_options.py` — the Engine tab's catalog: 351 env switches + 30 engine CLI args (tunable + experimental tiers; debug/internal stay reference-only), plus vendor/arch detection.
- `serve/runconfig.py` — new catalog-allowlisted config keys: `env.NAME`, `arg.--flag` (int/float, bounds-checked), `argflag.--flag`, `argstr.--flag`, `argenum.--flag`.
- `serve/server.py` — `GET /engine-options`, `POST /restart`, and `Service._spawn_from(cfg)` which rebuilds the engine spawn (exe, args, env, cwd, log) from the saved config, so a restart picks up what the page saved.
- `serve/web/` — the Engine tab: scope header (`amd · gfx1201 · strata-<model>.json`), search, experimental toggle, grouped rows with description/gate, save, and a restart banner that appears only when a restart would change the spawn.

## How GPU detection works (cross-platform by construction)

No OS-specific hardware APIs — deliberately. The tab needs the GPU the **engine uses**, not the GPUs the OS enumerates:

1. The run config's `backend` key is the primary signal: `cuda`→nvidia, `hip`→amd, `sycl`→intel, `metal`→apple.
2. The engine's own startup lines in its log (which the server writes on every OS) refine it: `gfx\d{3,4}`, `sm_\d{2,3}`, `compute capability X.Y` (two-digit majors included, e.g. `12.0`→`sm_120`), `Arc …`, `Apple M… Pro/Max/Ultra`.
3. **Multi-GPU layer splits**: every architecture line in the log tail is collected, so a mixed NVIDIA+AMD split lists both vendors' switches (union, deduped). A mixed split shows `nvidia + amd` in the scope header.

This works identically on Linux, Windows, and macOS because it reads the config and the engine's log — no WMI/`system_profiler`/`/sys` branches, no driver-dependent libraries, no extra permissions.

## Safety

- The catalog is the allowlist: only listed keys are accepted by `runconfig.check()`; unlisted names, control characters, oversized values, out-of-bounds numbers, and bad enum choices are refused.
- `/restart`, `/unload`, `/load`, `/config` accept JSON only from Strata's own page (Origin/CSRF check) — a cross-site form POST gets 403.
- Restart is busy-safe: while a request or a load holds the turn, `/restart` returns 409 (`{"status": "busy"}`) at once and changes nothing; it does not wait for the turn. `restart_supported()` is false for mock/replica setups, which get an honest 400.
- A `None` value means "engine default": the key is removed from the config (including setup-written flags like `--kv`).
- Config writes are atomic (temp file + backup + `os.replace`).

## Tests

Full serve suite on top of current `main`: **451/451 OK** (`serve.test_runconfig serve.test_server serve.test_lifecycle serve.test_security serve.test_frontend serve.test_monitor serve.test_slots serve.test_replicas`).

New coverage: catalog sanity; vendor mapping for all four backends; arch regexes (gfx, sm_ incl. `sm_120`, compute capability, Arc, Apple M); multi-GPU union (`detect_archs`, `detect_vendors`, mixed `nvidia + amd` scope over HTTP, no duplicate keys); Apple Metal options + config save round-trip; env/arg round-trips incl. float args (`--spec-min-p 0.65`); refusals (bounds, enums, types); restart guarded (evil Origin 403, mock 400, busy 409 with config untouched); Metal-config restart rebuilds the spawn with the saved env.

## Verified / not verified

- Verified on real hardware: Linux + AMD gfx1201, single GPU — tab scope, vendor filtering, save, live service health.
- Verified by mocks (Linux): Apple Metal config (`backend: metal` + `Apple M4 Pro` startup line → `apple` scope, Metal switches shown, AMD/NVIDIA hidden, save round-trip), mixed NVIDIA+AMD split, mock restart paths.
- **Not verified on real hardware: NVIDIA, Intel, macOS, and any multi-GPU machine.** The in-page restart button is fake-engine-tested, not clicked against a production GPU. Windows process-group handling on restart (`creationflags`) is not exercised.

## Reproduce

```
python -m serve.server --config strata-<model>.json   # open the web page, Engine tab
python -m unittest serve.test_runconfig serve.test_server serve.test_lifecycle \
    serve.test_security serve.test_frontend serve.test_monitor serve.test_slots serve.test_replicas
```

## Known limitations

- Detection reads the last 4 MiB of the engine log; a banner older than that (log rotated away) falls back to the `backend` key alone.
- The Metal setup flags (`metal/setup_mac.py`) are documented in `docs/GPU_OPTIONS.md` but are bootstrap choices, not live engine env/args, so they are not Engine-tab-editable.
- `serve/engine_options.py` is generated from the inventory in `docs/ALL_OPTIONS.md`; regenerate after upgrades (the generator lives in the contributor's tooling, not in this repo).

pulls.title: setup: a shard with no tensors is not "short" (UD-Q5_K_XL 00001-of-00006 stopped setup on a correct download)
pulls.author: joesinvestments
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open; found while setting up UD-Q5_K_XL on a Mac (`./setup.sh --setup --family unsloth --model UD-Q5_K_XL`).

## Summary
All six UD-Q5_K_XL shards download, then setup stops:
`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf is short: 10,946,618 of 10,946,624 bytes (6 missing)`.
The file is right: the Hub lists it at 10,946,618 bytes and its SHA-256 equals the pin (`610922cd...`). That shard
holds only metadata, and `check_shards()` takes `g.data_start` (the header rounded up to the alignment) as its least
length, which a tensor-less file never reaches. A shard with no tensors has no tensor data to be short of.

## What changed
- `setup.py`, `check_shards()`: `if have < need:` becomes `if have < need and g.tensors:`.
- `tools/test_shards.py`: `test_tensorless_shard_needs_no_alignment_padding` (a 24-byte GGUF with no tensors passes).
- Left alone: shards with tensors are checked as before (the short-shard and #657 tests are unchanged and pass); the
  pinned SHA-256 checks still cover the tensor-less shard.

## How it was checked
- `python -m unittest tools.test_shards`: the new test fails on `main` 296b59d2 with the "is short" message and passes
  with the change; 14 of 14 pass.
- `tools/test_setup_*.py`, all 40, on `main` and on this branch: every test ends with the same result on both (run on
  macOS, where 15 of them fail on `main` too for PC-only reasons such as the ROCm wheels).
- End to end on a Mac Studio M5 Max 64 GB (macOS 27.0.1): with this change setup finished for UD-Q5_K_XL, and the
  engine serves it (Metal, experts streamed from the SSD).
- Not built: no engine code is touched.

pulls.title: macOS: read available memory for the conversation memory guard
pulls.author: joesinvestments
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: part of #2502 (cause 1 of 2; the Metal snapshot check is the other and is not touched here)

## Summary
On every Mac the engine logs `memory guard: the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore are
refused`, because `sample_host_memory()` has readings for `_WIN32` and `__linux__` only. This adds a macOS reading:
free + inactive + purgeable pages, the rule `src/core/expert_source.cpp` already uses for macOS, and `hw.memsize` for
the total.

## What changed
- `src/core/conversation_memory.cpp` only (+16 lines): an `#elif defined(__APPLE__)` include of `<mach/mach.h>` and
  `<sys/sysctl.h>`, and an `#elif defined(__APPLE__)` branch in `sample_host_memory()` that feeds `combine()` as the
  other platforms do. The source label stays `meminfo`, to keep the change small.
- Left alone: Windows, Linux (cgroups included), the guard's rules, defaults, setup, docs.

## How it was checked
- Built and run on a Mac Studio M5 Max 64 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (Metal engine; this file is byte-identical in v0.1.44 and
  `main` 296b59d2). The start-up line changes from `the available RAM cannot be read; parking and session save/restore
  are refused` to `memory guard: limit 64.0 GiB (source: meminfo), current 5.1 GiB, reclaimable cache credited 0.0 GiB;
  available 58.9 GiB (MemAvailable 58.9 GiB), floor 2560 MiB`.
- Default path: answers byte-identical to the release engine. Greedy, 3 prompts x 5 runs, 256 tokens, on IQ3_XXS and
  UD-Q4_K_XL (both streaming from the SSD), same speed (UD-Q4_K_XL 56.7 / 51.9 / 52.5 tok/s before and after).
- Not built: CUDA, HIP, SYCL (no such hardware here). With `__APPLE__` undefined the file reduces to exactly the
  current source: `unifdef -U__APPLE__ -D__linux__ -U_WIN32` gives the same 284 lines before and after, and
  `unifdef -U__APPLE__ -D_WIN32 -U__linux__` the same 292 lines.

## Extra Notes
With this change and `--conversation-cache-mib 4096 --conversation-cache-slots 4`, parking on Metal is attempted but
then refused by the snapshot check (`invalid checkpoint running-state payload`), described in #2502. So this PR alone
does not make a side request keep the main conversation on a Mac; it removes the first of the two blocks.

pulls.title: resident: fix budget clamp double-counting the pre-claimed arena
pulls.author: G0-0000
pulls.body:
## Bug

With the NUMA pre-claim path (`--numa-hot-node`), `reserve_resident_arena()` faults the whole `--resident-budget-gib` arena into the cgroup's `current` **before** `pin_cache_complement()` reads available memory. The clamp (`clamp_resident_budget`) then charges the budget for its own arena — the same RAM counted once as "used" and again as "to allocate".

Measured on a Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB (UD-Q4_K_XL, 71.73 GiB of experts, 48.22 GiB RAM complement, cgroup MemoryMax 100 GiB, 125.76 GiB host):

```
--resident-budget-gib 49.00 exceeds available RAM
(47.40 GiB minus 4 GiB headroom and a 0.25 GiB margin): 42.75 GiB
```

42.75 < 48.22, so 5.08 GiB of experts stayed file-backed although the host had ~50 GiB free.

## Fix

Add the not-yet-used claim back to the available-memory reading — the reading the clamp would have taken had it run before the claim. The credit is zero when no arena was claimed, so the non-arena path is byte-identical. A new log line prints the accounting (`reading + claim = available − headroom − margin → granted`).

## Measured, after the fix

- 49.00 GiB requested → 49.00 GiB granted; the 48.22 GiB complement is fully resident (0 experts file-backed)
- from_files == 0 now holds, so `--drop-file-cache` fires at last (see #2243 — it was gated off in every partial-residency run)
- post-load: file cache 4.75 GiB (was 43.2), cgroup current 59.1 GiB (was 88.9), load 52 s
- no claim → zero credit → arithmetic unchanged (default path untouched)

## Discussion (not in this PR)

Once the budget covers the whole complement, the file tier is never read at runtime, so its page cache is dead weight. We load with `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1` (O_DIRECT), which removed the remaining ~43 GiB of load-time cache pollution for us. Arguably, unbuffered load should be the default when `--resident-budget-gib` covers the full complement — happy to follow up with a measured PR if you agree.

## Dependency and validation

Depends on #2242: arena_preclaim_ is introduced there, so this PR cannot build standalone against main until #2242 merges. Please do not merge this PR first. The fix plus credit regression tests were integrated LOCALLY on #2242 head f2ab2310; CUDA sm_70 strata and file_expert_source_test built, and CPU-only test passed with active NUMA credit assertions. These tests are NOT YET in this PR branch; I will update it once #2242 merges. HIP/SYCL and GPU runtime not tested.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: an engine program that cannot be started is a 503, not a dropped connection
pulls.author: devYRPauli
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

When the server cannot start the engine program, the request that starts the engine gets no HTTP answer. The client sees a closed connection with no status line. Any `OSError` from `subprocess.Popen` takes this path: a missing program, a file that is not executable, or a program that Windows blocks (#735). Each failed start also leaves one start narrator thread running, and the last failed start keeps its engine log open.

With this PR, the request gets a 503 with the reason, for example `the engine could not be started: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/strata'`. No narrator thread stays alive, and the log handle is closed.

## Related discussion

Resolves #2496. I re-tested the issue on 0.2.0-beta, and it is reopened.

## Approach

- `StrataEngine.__init__`: when `popen()` raises an `OSError`, the start sets the `loading` event and closes its handle on the engine log. Then it re-raises the same `OSError`, so the startup path keeps its exception type.
- `Service.ensure_loaded`: an `OSError` from `engine.restart()` becomes `EngineDied("the engine could not be started: ...")`. The request path already answers `EngineDied` with a 503, as it does for an engine that exits before READY (#1527). The vision encoder unload on failure is unchanged.
- `serve/test_ready_timeout.py`: new class `SpawnFailure`. A lazy engine with a missing program gets a 503 on chat, messages, responses and a streamed chat. The test also checks that the log handle is closed and that no narrator thread stays alive. The class runs on Windows too, because a missing program fails the same way there.

The diff is 2 files, +49/-3. It merges cleanly with main f57c0adc.

## Validation

All runs: macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Pro, Python 3.12.14, no GPU, serve/ only. The PR head is e7680b9d7, which contains 0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480).

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_ready_timeout.SpawnFailure` on the PR head: OK.
- The same test file on 0.2.0-beta without the fix: 4 errors (the 4 requests drop) and 1 failure (a narrator thread stays alive). So the test catches the bug.
- A script sends 6 requests for each of 3 causes. The requests are chat, messages and responses, streamed and not. The causes are a missing program, a file that is not executable, and a simulated WinError 4551 (an `OSError` raised at the `subprocess.Popen` boundary). On 0.2.0-beta all 18 requests end with `RemoteDisconnected`, 6 narrator threads stay alive per cause, and the log handle stays open. On the PR head all 18 get a 503 with the reason, no narrator thread stays alive, and the log handle is closed.
- Earlier, on main 296b59d2, I reverted each half of the fix on its own. Without the `ensure_loaded` change, the 4 requests drop. Without the `__init__` change, the log handle stays open and the narrator threads stay alive.

**Failed:**

`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p 'test_*.py'`: 882 tests on the PR head and 881 on 0.2.0-beta. Both runs have the same 3 failures and 1 error, so this PR adds no failure:

- `test_lifeline.Lifeline`: 3 tests, for example `the child outlived a killed server (watcher)`.
- `test_server.VisionArgs.test_min_tokens_is_passed_only_when_set`: `AttributeError: 'Proc' object has no attribute 'pid'`.

**Not run:**

- A real Windows machine. The WinError 4551 case is simulated, so the Windows error path is not verified on Windows.
- Engine builds and GPU runs. The change is in serve/ only, and no engine starts in these tests.

## Limits

- The `/load` route catches only `GpuBusy`, so `EngineDied` and `EngineStuck` still drop its connection. That is a separate change.
- A failed load on `/v1/responses` answers 503 without the "the next request restarts it" suffix. That text comes from the Responses handler, and this PR does not change it.
- #2435 makes the same change for the elastic image encoder. #1563 edits the same `popen()` call, so one of the two PRs needs a rebase after the other merges.

pulls.title: sycl: images on the SYCL port (CPU encoder, --vision cpu)
pulls.author: skipzx-lab
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none. docs/INTEL.md listed images as "Not done" on the SYCL port.

## Summary
This turns on images for the Intel SYCL port. The engine already had `--vision` / `GENI` / M-RoPE from the port, and that code works unchanged. This PR adds what was missing around it: a way to build the CPU encoder, setup support, and getting the embeddings file into the engine's container. Images stay opt-in (`--vision cpu`). Without the flag the config is byte-identical to before.

## What changed
- `sycl/tools/build-vision.sh` (new): builds `strata-vision` (tools/vision, CPU, the same cmake flags as setup's `build_vision_cpu`) in the `strata-sycl-dev` image.
  - It copies the image's `libgomp.so.1` next to the binary and writes a launcher, `build-vision/strata-vision.sh`, so a host without an OpenMP runtime can run it.
  - It prints the image's glibc version. Without `third_party/llama.cpp` it ends with `BUILD EXIT 1` and says what to run.
- `sycl/setup_intel.py`:
  - `--vision cpu` turns images on. `yes` and `gpu` also select the CPU encoder and print a warning, because the port has no GPU encoder. Images stay off by default.
  - It stops early, with the three steps in order, when images are asked for and the encoder is not built.
  - `to_sycl()` keeps the `vision` section with host paths (the encoder runs on the host) and the launcher as `exe`, and adds `--vision` exactly once.
  - Setup's 700 MiB GPU-encoder reserve is dropped unless the user typed it, because the CPU encoder takes no VRAM.
  - Side fix: the `--vram-reserve-mib` / `--vision` checks in `install()` now see the `--flag=value` form too. Before, `--vision=cpu` or `--vram-reserve-mib=N` got a second copy of the flag added.
- `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`: `install_vision_paths()` runs only with a `vision` section. It puts the embeddings file under `/dev/shm/strata-sycl-vision`, or `<data root>/vision-tmp` when `/dev/shm` is short, both mode 0700, and exports `STRATA_SYCL_VISION_DIRS`.
- `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`: with `--vision` in the args, it mounts those directories read-only at the same paths. Without `--vision` nothing changes.
- `tools/test_setup_sycl_vision.py` (new, 33 tests, no GPU or network) covers:
  - the mapping and the early stop;
  - `to_sycl` with and without images, the latter checked against the output of the code before this change;
  - the reserve rule;
  - the path redirection, run in temp directories;
  - the wrapper's mounts, using a fake `docker`;
  - `bash -n`, and `build-vision.sh` without llama.cpp.
- `docs/INTEL.md`:
  - the feature table entry;
  - a new "Images (SYCL port)" section covering the build order, how it works, RAM, the image-token cap and measurements;
  - "Not done" now covers only the llama.cpp path.

## Extra Notes
- Measured on an Arc Pro B60 24 GB (xe, PCIe Gen3 x8) with a Xeon W-2155, Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts`, and the encoder on 4 threads.
  - A 1920x1080 dashboard screenshot read correctly in 4.0 s with the cap at 1024 (1,071 tokens). Uncapped it was 2,103 tokens and 5.2 s.
  - Several images in one message, follow-up turns, PNG/JPEG/WebP, OpenAI and Anthropic image blocks, streaming, and a broken image (400, then the next request reads) all work.
  - Text-only decode is unchanged.
- The IQ1_M model misreads some repeated-digit strings in pictures, for example "2222" read as "22". The pinned llama.cpp's `llama-mtmd-cli` (SYCL, the same GGUF and mmproj) gives exactly the same four wrong answers, so this comes from the model at this quant, not from the port.
- Not tested:
  - an Alchemist card;
  - a layer split, although the mrope table upload already covers every stage;
  - setup's default cap of 300 image tokens. I measured at 1024 and uncapped; the docs say so.
- Builds: the SYCL engine itself is unchanged, and the encoder was built with `build-vision.sh` in the dev image. No CUDA or HIP files are touched.
- Tests: `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_sycl_vision tools.test_setup_sycl tools.test_setup_small_card` gives 67 OK.

pulls.author: Nilabh-code

## Summary

Results-only community benchmark submission: adds `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rtx-5060-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-coder-iq1-m/` per `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`. No engine or source changes.

Produced by the repository's own `tools/strata_bench.py` (suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges) against the HTTP API of a Strata server started from the install configuration. Model loading is not timed; a warm-up chat and a 1K prompt are discarded first. Speed only — **no correctness check was run.**

## What changed

- `bench/results/2026-10-15-community-rtx-5060-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-coder-iq1-m/README.md` — the report (machine-generated header, format of the docs template).
- `.../results.json` — per-request data: prompt/generated tokens, engine timings, cache reuse, errors, plus the machine facts and the launch command.
- `.../engine-log-excerpt.txt` — the engine's start-up lines from the run.

Nothing else is touched; no model files or packs are included.

## Hardware, model, settings

- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GiB VRAM (16,311 MiB reported), driver 616.92, CUDA version not read.
- **CPU / RAM:** 13th Gen Intel Core i5-13400F (10 cores / 16 threads), 31.8 GiB installed RAM. Windows 11 (10.0.26300).
- **Strata / engine:** 0.1.44.1 (project downloaded as a release, not a git checkout, so no commit hash: `strata_commit: null`).
- **Model:** `qwen3.8-flash-next-coder-iq1_m` (Coder IQ1_M, GSQ/RCO, two GGUF shards) with `--vision` and the vision encoder loaded.
- **Context:** 204,800 tokens, parallel slots 1, KV `q4_0`, `--resident-experts`, `--expert-cache auto`, `--prefill auto`, `--spec 4`, `--mtp rt`, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`, `--pool-workers 5`, adaptive tier 160/0.97.
- Launch command verbatim (credentials removed, none present):

```text
strata.exe --pack coder-iq1_m --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile expert-profile-coder.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp rt --max-context 204800 --kv q4_0 --resident-experts --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700 --control-vector-scaled Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-experimental-speed-projection.gguf:1.0 --control-vector-layer-range 4 44 --cvec-mode project --cvec-dir per-layer --spec-min-p 0.5 --pool-workers 5 --adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --adapt-decay 0.97
```

Note for readers: this run has the **experimental speed projection** control vector enabled and `--resident-experts` — it is not a stock configuration, so it should not be read as the model's default numbers.

## Results (medians, range in parentheses)

| Configuration | Prompt tokens | Reused | Generated | Runs | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| short chat | 46 | 0 | 100 | 9 | not measured | 34.5 (32.8–47.8) | 0.73 (0.65–0.88) |
| 4K prompt, fresh | 4,019 | 0 | 24 cap | 3 | 1,261.1 (1,125.7–1,281.2) | not measured | 3.23 (3.16–3.62) |
| 16K prompt, fresh | 16,058 | 0 | 24 cap | 3 | 1,466.7 (1,441.1–1,515.9) | not measured | 10.98 (10.64–11.19) |
| agent session, follow-up turns | 14,533 at the last turn | 68.7 % hit | up to 64 | 3 | see README | 39.6 (29.1–59.1) | 2.70 (2.00–3.15) |

Agent-session conversation cache: 68.7 % of follow-up prompt tokens reused; the 13,728 new tokens of the appended files are read once; the first turn (nothing cached) has a 1.59 s first token. Per-turn table is in the README. Total suite time 153 s.

## Limitations (also stated in the report)

- **Speed suite only.** No needle/recall test, no HumanEval, no tool-call check — quality is entirely untested here.
- Background workloads and power limits were **not recorded**; the GPU was not isolated from the desktop.
- Storage type and PCIe link width/speed not measured; CUDA version not read.
- The tool reports `strata_commit: null` because this install is a downloaded release rather than a git checkout.
- Single machine, Windows-only; short-chat decode spread (32.8–47.8 tok/s) shows this box is on the noisy side for 100-token answers.

## Extra Notes

Report was read before sharing; paths in `results.json` are already placeholdered by the benchmark (`C:\Users\<user>\...`), and no user, host or network identifiers are present. Happy to re-run anything specific (e.g. `--long` at 32K, or needle checks) if you want it alongside this.

pulls.title: gfx12: empty workgroups past the full-die fill stall in the decode matvecs (grid_pad)
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
## Title
gfx12: empty workgroups past the full-die fill stall in the decode matvecs (`grid_pad`)

Issue: none open on this (searched issues and PRs for the stall, 2048-wave grids and R9700 decode). The cause is
ROCm/TheRock#9300.

## Summary
On RDNA4 with the full die (R9700 / 9070 XT: 32 WGPs = 2,048 wave slots), a dispatch whose waves land at, or just
below, a whole multiple of the slots runs ~8–14 µs longer than one a few waves bigger. Reproduced on an R9700 with
ROCm 7.14.1 and 7.2.4 alike: 512-thread blocks with a pointer argument and LDS, 118–124 and 129–133 blocks 2.24 µs
per launch, 125–128 blocks 16.4 µs. Several of Strata's decode matvecs hit it. This PR launches them with a few extra
workgroups that return at once.

Measured on one R9700 (gfx1201), Linux, ROCm 7.14.1, against main 296b59d2 (after v0.1.44.1). One launch in a
hipGraph, weights rotated past the 64 MB Infinity Cache:

| launch | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `native_small_mmvq` 6144→2560 (ssm_out / attn_output), 1 column, 2560 blocks | 41.3 µs | 30.2 µs |
| `native_small_mmvq` 2560→512 (attn_k / attn_v / indexer q), 1 column, 512 blocks | 16.5 µs | 5.0 µs |
| `bf16_f32_mmvf_kernel` 2560→512 (router), 512 blocks of 256 threads | 19.7 µs | 7.2 µs |
| `bf16_f32_mmvf_kernel` 2560→1024 | 24.5 µs | 11.7 µs |

Server: UD-IQ4_XS, `--spec 4` with MTP, kv int8, `--max-context 32768`, the gfx12 decode switches and
`STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT=1`. Main, this PR with `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0`, and this PR; 3 starts each, alternating, 3 prompts
× 512 tokens, greedy. Prompts 1 and 2 are shown: prompt 3's text varied between starts, see Extra Notes; one start's
prompt 2 also differed and is left out.

| | verify ms/window (p1 / p2) | GPU wait (p1 / p2) | tok/s (p1 / p2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 21.84–22.18 / 20.97–21.28 | 17.68–17.73 / 17.15–17.23 | 59.0–60.4 / 71.1–72.6 |
| this PR, `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0` | 21.75–22.19 / 20.88–20.93 | 17.67–17.69 / 17.17 | 58.7–59.4 / 69.9–72.6 |
| this PR | 21.28–21.64 / 20.33–20.36 | 17.14–17.18 / 16.55–16.57 | 60.5–61.4 / 73.9–74.8 |

## What changed
- `include/strata/kernels/grid_pad.hpp` (new): `grid_pad(blocks, threads)` returns the grid to launch — `blocks`
  plus a few empty blocks when the launch's waves fall within the last max(16, 4·waves-per-block) slots below a
  multiple of the slots, or within 16·k waves past the k-th multiple (at most 256), fitted to the measurements.
  gfx12 only (`gcnArchName` gfx1200 / gfx1201); other HIP cards and CUDA get the grid unchanged. `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0`
  turns it off, `=1` applies it on any HIP card.
- `src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.cu`: `native_small_mmvq_kernel` and `native_mmvq_multi_kernel` (with the LFUSE pair)
  return at once in a block past their real rows; their launchers go through `grid_pad`. The math is untouched.
- `src/kernels/cuda/native_bf16.cu`: `bf16_f32_mmvf_kernel` takes `n_out` and returns in a block past it; its
  launcher goes through `grid_pad`.
- `src/kernels/grid_pad_test.cpp` + `CMakeLists.txt`: `grid_pad_test`, the rule on the measured cases (no GPU).
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: an entry under RDNA4's speed switches.

Left alone: every other kernel and launch, the default on every non-gfx12 card, CUDA, and the SYCL port (it builds its
own migrated `.dp.cpp` copies of these kernels, so none of the changed files reach it).

**The default output stays byte-identical.** Every padded launcher on random inputs (`native_mmvq` at 1–8 columns on
the model's dense shapes, the LFUSE pair, `bf16_f32_mmvf`; 12.5 M values in 153 segments), `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0` vs on
in separate processes, with `STRATA_TSUM` 0 and 1: the outputs are byte-identical, and nothing past them is written.

**Builds:** HIP (gfx1201, system ROCm 7.14.1): ctest 112/113 — `ple_parity` fails as on main (needs the Q2_0
fixture) — and the matvec parity tests also with `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0` (52/52). CUDA (nvcc 13.4, sm_120): compiles and
links, `grid_pad_test` passes (no NVIDIA GPU here to run it). SYCL: not built — none of the changed files are in its
build.

## Extra Notes
- The early return also changes `native_mmvq_multi_kernel`'s code: the Q6_K head (2560→248320) at 2–8 columns gets
  3–11% faster (T=4: 1158 → 1037 µs), attn_gate / qkv / attn_q at 4–6 columns 1.0–1.8 µs (2–3%) slower; on the
  server the two cancel (the `STRATA_GRID_PAD=0` row above matches main).
- Served answers, `STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT` off, the same request first after start: 4 starts of main and 8 of this PR
  (4 with the padding off, 4 on): 11 of 12 the same text, and the one that differs is a main start. That matches the
  "Known" line in docs/AMD_HIP.md (a HIP run's greedy output sometimes differs from another start's); the
  kernel-level check above is what shows that this PR does not change the output.
- On a 0.1.43.1-based build with `--kv-grow --vram-elastic` (the open HIP VMM PRs) the same server A/B gave
  verify −1.0 ms/window (−4.5%) and +3.4…4.7% tok/s, 27 of 27 answers byte-identical. There the early return alone
  also took away a stall of the multi kernel (attn_gate at 2–4 columns 41–44 → 31 µs) that main avoids through
  `q8_0_rows1`.
- Not tested: running it on CUDA; other RDNA4 dies (the 56-CU RX 9070 did not show the stall in the ROCm report; the
  padding there costs a few empty blocks); Windows.

pulls.title: fix(setup): don't require tensor-data alignment for GGUF shards without …
pulls.author: OriginalMadman
pulls.body:
## Change

Skip the tensor-payload extent check when a successfully parsed GGUF shard has no tensors. GGUF parsing, the existing checks for tensor-bearing shards, and the separate pinned size/SHA-256 verification remain unchanged.

`check_shards()` and `whole_shard()` calculated the minimum GGUF shard size as `data_start + max(tensor end offsets)`. For a shard containing no tensors, this incorrectly required the file to extend through the aligned tensor-data start, even though no tensor payload exists.

This caused valid metadata-only GGUF shards to be rejected as truncated. For example, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q5_K_XL-00001-of-00006.gguf` was reported as six bytes short:

- Actual file size: 10,946,618 bytes
- Parsed tensor count: 0
- Aligned data start: 10,946,624 bytes

The downloaded file matched the size and SHA-256 declared in `setup.py`.

## Title
setup: Alchemist on xe also gets the Level Zero v2 adapter (UR_LOADER_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=1; A770 decode +7%, prompt +3%)

## Summary
On an Arc A770 under xe, each of the stepped verify window's ~97 graph segments per round took 53-200 µs to submit with the default Level Zero adapter. With the v2 adapter it takes about 25 µs (timed in the window's serve).

Setup now writes `UR_LOADER_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=1` for an Alchemist card on xe, next to `UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS`. **This builds on #2394**, which adds that block.

- `sycl/setup_intel.py`: the env entry, for Alchemist on xe only.
- `tools/test_setup_sycl.py`: the existing Alchemist/xe test also asserts the variable, and that a B-series card and i915 do not get it.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: one paragraph.

## Extra Notes
Arc A770 16 GB, xe, compute runtime 26.05, oneAPI 2026.1. Same day, same binary, with and without the variable:

| | v2 | default |
|---|---|---|
| 8K decode (3 pairs) | 35.49 / 36.38 / 34.29 | 33.90 / 32.39 / 32.56 tok/s |
| 8K prefill | 791-795 | 768-775 tok/s |
| 32K | 795.9 prefill, 29.97 decode | 782.4 prefill, 28.21 decode |
| GPU wait per round | 39.4-39.7 | 43-48 ms |

**Stability.** With the default adapter, about 1 in 10 runs had a decode about 3× slower (serves stalled under memory pressure); none did with v2.

pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
sycl/A770: faster hyper-connection read on Arc A-series (gr_bench 88 / 123 / 151 -> 62 / 83 / 100 us at 1 / 4 / 6 tokens)

## Summary
`fused_gr_read_multi` on Alchemist, the `gr_more_groups` path. This is the decode window's per-layer hc read, run twice per layer, and it sits on the stepped window's critical path. There are five changes, each with an env switch and each the default on Alchemist only. Every other device runs the same kernels as before.

Three are **bit-identical** (`gr_bench` checksums unchanged):
1. The down reduce is folded into the sliced down kernel: each row block's last slice to finish sums the 80 slice partials, in the same order (`STRATA_GR_FUSED_REDUCE`). That is one launch fewer.
2. The up kernel runs at 4 columns per block (640 blocks), up from 8 (`STRATA_GR_UP_MORE_COLS`).
3. The up kernel reads the `lo` values the fused reduce computed once, instead of every block recomputing them (`STRATA_GR_LO_READY`).

Two change the **fp32 summation order**. The output sums agree to about 1e-7 relative, and the output was quality-checked:

4. The norm is folded into the down kernel (`STRATA_GR_NORM_FOLD`). The slices stage the pending-updated residual × `w_norm` unscaled, together with its sums of squares. The reduce then applies each stream's `rs` to that stream's partial dots. This removes the norm launch and the `xn` write and re-read.
5. The up projection runs one row per lane (`STRATA_GR_UP_V5`). The old kernel re-read all of `lo` from local memory for every row and every token, about 160 KB per block, and was local-memory bound on the A770. Now all lanes read the same `lo` value at once, as a broadcast.

`STRATA_GR_NORM_FOLD=0 STRATA_GR_UP_V5=0` gives back the old bits exactly.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`:
  - `gr_down_sliced_kernel` gains the `FUSED` / `NF` epilogues.
  - New `gr_up_v5_kernel`.
  - `launch_gr_down_more` / `launch_gr_up_more` choose between them.
  - New switches: `gr_fused_reduce`, `gr_norm_fold`, `gr_up_more_cols`, `gr_lo_ready`, `gr_up_v5`.
  - New scratch: slice counters and slice sums of squares.

## Extra Notes
Arc A770 16 GB, xe, compute runtime 26.05, oneAPI 2026.1. `gr_bench`, in µs:

| tokens | before | 1-3 (bitwise) | + 4 | + 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 88.4 | 74.6 | 62.2 | 63.8 |
| 4 | 123.1 | 104.9 | 90.3 | 83.3 |
| 6 | 150.8 | 133.2 | 115.4 | 100.5 |

**Decode** (Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts`, spec 4):
- **1-3:** 33.64 / 33.41 → 34.80 / 34.84 tok/s with the expert large-GRF PR, ids identical.
- **4-5:** GPU wait per round 39.2-39.9 → 38.1-39.2 ms at 8K / 32K / 2K. Decode is within run-to-run noise (about +1%). The generated text is equivalent, and the 2K ids are identical.
- **Rejected along the way:** 8 lanes per row for the up kernel (slower), an all-80-in-flight reduce (spills), and 2 / 16 / 32 columns.

Not tested: A750 / A580, i915, Windows.

pulls.title: sycl: Alchemist expert cache in segments, so borrowed prompt GEMM operands are not staged (A770 prompt +8-12%, output identical)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
sycl: Alchemist expert cache in segments, so borrowed prompt GEMM operands are not staged (A770 prompt +8-12%, output identical)

## Summary
The prompt path borrows the top expert-cache slots, 5.4-7.6 GiB into the ~8.6 GiB arena. oneMKL misreads a GEMM operand that lies more than 4 GiB into **one** allocation, so `staged_gemm` copied nearly every expert GEMM operand first. In an 8K prompt that is 24,576 staged GEMMs and about 200 GB of device copies.

On Alchemist, the arena is now allocated as equal physical segments behind one reserved address range (`sycl_ext_oneapi_virtual_mem`). The rest of the engine still sees one contiguous range. The arena is not registered for staging, because the same GEMMs read right in a segmented range at any offset.

## What changed
- `sycl/include/strata/sycl_queue.hpp`: `malloc_device_segmented` / `free_device_segmented` and `arena_segmented_wanted`. Segments are 512 MiB (whole 2 MiB pages, all equal: Level Zero refused a smaller last segment).
- `sycl/src/core/expert_cache.cpp`: `ExpertCache::open` takes that path on Alchemist, and `close()` frees it.
- `sycl/src/prefill/gemm.dp.cpp`: a comment.
- `sycl/probe/a770/gemm_far_probe.cpp`: the probe that places the misread.
- Switches: `STRATA_ARENA_SEGMENTED=0` gives one allocation as before; `=1` opts in other devices. `STRATA_ARENA_SEGMENT_MIB` sets the segment size.
- No virtual-memory support or any failure falls back to the previous allocation.

## Extra Notes
**Probe** (`gemm_far_probe`, A770, xe, compute runtime 26.05, oneAPI 2026.1):
- One 8 GiB `malloc_device`, T = 7987: X past 4 GiB gives a wrong last partial tile; W and X past 4 GiB gives nearly every element wrong.
- Physical segments behind one range: every case reads right. This held for 0.25, 0.5 and 2 GiB segments, fp16 and bf16, with W, X or Y anywhere, and across segment boundaries.

**Engine** (Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts`, learned24, `--prefill-borrow`, spec 4, greedy, `STRATA_PF_XMX=2`), same-day A/B against itself with `STRATA_ARENA_SEGMENTED=0`:

| prompt | segmented | one allocation | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 678.8 tok/s prefill, 27.17 decode | 627.4, 27.31 | identical ids |
| 32K | 720.7 tok/s prefill, 22.90 decode | 649.1, 22.98 | identical ids |

**Default path elsewhere.** Battlemage and every other device are byte-identical. The gate is `intel_gpu_gen(dev) == IntelGpuGen::Alchemist`.

Not tested: A750 / A580 (i915), Windows, `--vram-elastic`, a layer split, prompts without borrowing.

pulls.title: sycl: pin the RAM-resident expert copy in 2 GiB chunks when one pinned allocation is refused (Arc A770; prompt DMA for every expert, host staging 3.3 s -> 0.16 s)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545, #1606 (Arc A770)

## Summary
With `--resident-experts`, the RAM copy of the experts the VRAM cache does not hold is requested as **one** pinned host allocation. On an Arc A770 (DG2, `xe`) every single pinned allocation of 4 GiB or more is refused, even with `UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1`, while 2 GiB pieces are not. So the 11-18 GiB copy fell back to `malloc` + `mlock`. The CUDA engine registers that fallback (`cudaHostRegister`); the SYCL port could not (DPCT1027), so the GPU's copies from it ran at the pageable rate and the prompt path streamed every expert through the host stager instead of DMA.

This pins the copy in 2 GiB chunks when the single allocation is refused, as `GgufExpertSource::mirror` already does for the `--stream-experts` mirror: the blobs are laid out so none crosses a 2 GiB boundary and `complement_at()` maps an offset to its chunk. Cards whose single pinned allocation succeeds take exactly today's path.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/core/expert_source.cpp` (`FileExpertSource::pin_cache_complement`): after the single `malloc_host` is refused, re-lay the offsets and allocate `ceil(bytes / 2 GiB)` pinned chunks; on any refusal, free them and keep the pageable fallback. `resident_blob`, `device_alias`, the copy-in loop and the adaptive tier's writes go through `complement_at()`. The exchange-buffer rotation (one contiguous arena) is not offered with chunks. `close()` frees the chunks.
- `sycl/include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `complement_chunks_`, `complement_at()`.
- `STRATA_RESIDENT_CHUNKED=0` keeps the pageable fallback.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM. Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts --expert-cache auto --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --spec 4 --mtp`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1`, `UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1`, an 18 GiB resident copy, same day, with vs without (`STRATA_RESIDENT_CHUNKED=0`):

| | pageable (today) | chunked pinned |
|---|---|---|
| resident copy | 18.03 GiB, pinned 0 | 18.04 GiB, pinned 18.04 GiB in 10 chunks |
| experts the prompt streams by DMA (8K) | 0 of 9,352 | 9,352 of 9,352 |
| host staging during the prompt, 8K / 32K | 3,307 / 13,466 ms | 163 / 626 ms |
| lent slots refilled after the prompt | 583-640 ms | 266 ms |
| adaptive tier swaps (decode) | 3.8-4.0 ms/round | 0.86-0.90 ms/round |
| prompt 8K / 32K | 669.8 / 668.2 tok/s | 680.4 / 677.5 tok/s |
| decode 8K / 32K (with #2207) | 30.88 / 26.87 tok/s | 31.04 / 27.22 tok/s |

Output ids identical in every pair (8K `72b762d5b2a3`, 32K `eb3432fea981`). The end-to-end gain is small because on this card the prompt is GPU-bound (the expert GEMMs), but the stager's ~3 s of host copying per 8K prompt and most of the tier's copy time are gone. This branch alone (`a0116b27`-era `main` = v0.1.44.1): 678.2 tok/s at 8K, all 9,352 by DMA, same ids.

The probe for the allocation limit: `pinned_probe` in the A770 report (#2216) / our fork's `sycl/probe/a770/` (one `malloc_host` of 4.00 GiB fails, 7 x 2 GiB succeed, 17.3 GB/s from pinned against 4.2 GB/s from pageable).

Not tested: i915 (the A750's arena path does not use this function's pinned branch the same way), Battlemage (its single allocation succeeds, so this path does not run), Windows. CUDA/HIP: SYCL-only files.

pulls.title: sycl: images on the Intel port, and the setup wiring for it
pulls.author: beyondcr
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none; this adds the image encoder to the Intel port (related to #1545, #1606, the Arc A770 setup work
this was measured on, and #2229, which covers the CPU half of the same wiring).

## Summary
On `main`, images are the one feature the CUDA engine has that the Intel port does not. The engine's half of the
path is already ported (`--vision`, the `GENI` request, the per-cell M-RoPE table, the `SVE1` file); what is
missing is the program that turns a picture into those rows.

That program is `strata-vision`, the encoder in `tools/vision`. It is a thin front end over llama.cpp's `mtmd`
and the model's `mmproj` GGUF, with no kernel of Strata's own, and `tools/mtmd/clip.cpp` selects its backend by
device *type*, so llama.cpp's SYCL backend runs the CLIP graph on the Arc with **no source change to the tool**.
What was missing was a build option and a wiring step.

This change adds both, demonstrated end to end on an Arc A770 on `xe`: `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt` gains
`STRATA_VISION_SYCL`, the encoder gets the launcher a oneAPI binary needs, `sycl/tools/build.sh` builds it
beside the engine, and `sycl/setup_intel.py` stops answering `--vision` with `none`. `docs/INTEL.md`'s
comparison table and its "Not done" section said images were missing on the port; the port's row is now `yes`.

## What changed
Six files, +374/-7, all under `tools/`, `sycl/` and `docs/`. Nothing else is touched.

- `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt` (+25/-1): `option(STRATA_VISION_SYCL ...)` for the Intel GPU, the matching
  `set(GGML_SYCL ... FORCE)` beside the existing `GGML_CUDA` line, and one `if(STRATA_VISION_SYCL)` block that
  requires `MKL_DIR` (ggml-sycl's CMake does `find_package(MKL REQUIRED)` for the INTEL target) and prints one
  `STATUS` line. The GPU backends are one list (`STRATA_VISION_GPU`), refused when more than one is set. The
  option defaults OFF, so a build that does not pass it configures exactly as before.
- `sycl/serve/strata-vision-sycl.sh` (new, 58 lines): the encoder's launcher, in the shape of `strata-sycl.sh`,
  the engine's own. A header names its two variables (`STRATA_VISION_BIN`, `STRATA_ONEAPI_ROOT`); the
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is composed from the oneAPI install it finds, with no hard-coded paths; an `ldd` preflight
  makes a missing runtime fail with a named fix instead of the loader's message; and `exec "$bin" "$@"` passes
  every argument the server sends through unchanged.
- `sycl/setup_intel.py` (+83/-3): `sycl_vision_encoder()` (discovers the built encoder the way `sycl_engine()`
  discovers the engine), `vision_intel()` (`yes`/`gpu` place the CLIP graph on the Arc, `cpu` runs the same
  binary without `--gpu`; anything else, or no encoder, leaves images off with a message), `build_engine_sycl()`
  (stages the encoder where the config can name it), and `to_sycl()`, which keeps the config's `vision` section,
  names the launcher, and raises `--vram-reserve-mib` to the encoder's own need.
- `sycl/tools/build.sh` (+46): no targets builds the encoder beside the engine, `strata-vision` builds it alone,
  `strata` still builds the engine alone. Missing a llama.cpp checkout or oneMKL it says so and the engine still
  builds.
- `docs/INTEL.md` (+21/-3): the `images` row of the comparison table, a short "Images on the SYCL port" section
  (what the encoder is, what to build, the `--vision` wiring, what the first image costs), and the "Not done"
  entry rewritten so it no longer claims images are missing on the port. The section carries no measurement of
  this work (no card, no encode times, no comparison against the CPU producer, no end-to-end claim); the numbers
  are below, where a reviewer looks for them.
- `tools/test_setup_intel_vision.py` (new, 11 tests): off stays off; `yes`/`gpu` need a built encoder; `cpu` is
  the same binary without `--gpu`; the config's `vision` section survives `to_sycl()` and names the launcher;
  and the launcher exists, is executable, keeps the encoder's arguments, and finds the oneAPI install from the
  `icpx` on `PATH` or from `STRATA_ONEAPI_ROOT`, with the real launcher run against a tree laid out like an
  install.

## How it was checked (Arc A770 16 GB, Alchemist, compute capability 12.55, xe, Linux 7.2.6, oneAPI 2026.1 JIT, Ryzen 9 3950X, 64 GB RAM)
Model `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-IQ3_XXS` with its own `mmproj` (F16, `projection_dim` 2560). Encoder built
against llama.cpp `207bdab`. Every number below was measured on this branch's own binary, on this card.

**The build.** `cmake -S tools/vision -B build-vision-sycl -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
-DLLAMA_DIR=<checkout> -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx -DSTRATA_VISION_SYCL=ON
-DMKL_DIR=<oneMKL cmake dir>` then `--target strata-vision`: **239 targets, 0 errors**. The same configure run
four ways:

| configure | result |
| --- | --- |
| `-DSTRATA_VISION_SYCL=ON -DMKL_DIR=…` | `GGML_SYCL=ON`, `GGML_SYCL_F16=OFF`, `GGML_SYCL_DNN=ON` (oneDNN is not installed, so it is inert), `GGML_CUDA=OFF` |
| `-DSTRATA_VISION_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_VISION_SYCL=ON` | configure refused: `STRATA_VISION_CUDA;STRATA_VISION_SYCL are exclusive; a build has one GPU backend` |
| `-DSTRATA_VISION_SYCL=ON` with no `MKL_DIR` | configure refused with the message above, before ggml sees it |
| no GPU option | `GGML_SYCL=OFF`, unchanged from today |

**What it encodes.** Against this model's `mmproj`:

```
READY 2560
OK 720 40 18 1063
OK 256 16 16 214
```

720 rows on a 40x18 raster grid, `n_embd=2560`, one `SVE1` record, for a real 1862x1094 screenshot. 256 rows on
16x16 for a 512x512 picture. `nx*ny == n` and the width the engine insists on.

**Two producers, one binary.** The encoder is both producers (with `--gpu` the CLIP graph is on the Arc,
without it on the CPU), which removes the usual confound in a CPU-versus-GPU comparison. Compared record by
record with a local comparator (it reads two `SVE1` files and reports the per-row cosine and the max and mean
absolute difference; it is a measuring instrument, so it is not in the tree):

| picture | grid | header / width | mean abs diff | max abs diff | per-row cosine, mean | min | rows below 0.99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 512x512 | 16x16 | identical | 4.028e-04 | 1.522e-02 | **0.999685** | 0.971744 (row 229) | 1 of 256 |
| 1862x1094 (a real screenshot) | 40x18 | identical | 4.010e-04 | 3.088e-02 | **0.999711** | 0.970711 (row 100) | 4 of 720 |

**Numerically close, not bit-exact.** Two controls: the Intel producer is byte-deterministic (two runs,
identical files), and turning flash attention off on the CPU backend alone moves the same rows by 1.0e-02 (max
abs), about two thirds of the 1.5e-02 that the same picture's CPU-and-GPU pair differs by, so the residual is
arithmetic ordering rather than preprocessing. A wrong resize, patch raster order or merge order gives rows that
are unrelated (cosine near zero), not rows that agree to three decimal places.

**Encode time, on the Arc** (this branch's binary, same A770):

| what | time |
| --- | --- |
| process start (device, CLIP graph, projector) | ~1 s |
| the warm-up before `READY` (one 2048x2048 image at the 1024-token cap) | **18.6 s**, once per server start |
| a real 1862x1094 screenshot (720 rows, 40x18) | **1.06 s** (the CPU backend: 5.02 s) |
| a 512x512 picture (256 rows, 16x16) | **0.21 s** (the CPU backend: 1.39 s) |

The warm-up is almost all one-time JIT compilation of the CLIP graph, not the picture. No performance claim is
made: the encoder is not on the critical path (one encode per picture, cached by the image's hash for later
turns), and nothing about the text model's speed changes.

**End to end.** `--vision` reaches the engine, the encoder starts before it (so its device buffers are allocated
before the engine sizes its expert cache), and a fresh OpenAI image request about the real screenshot returns
the right two facts about it:

```
$ python3 ask_image.py 8096 wiki-intel-arc.png "Transcribe the page title at the top of this screenshot, and
    name the company the sidebar box says designed the product."
Page title: **Intel Arc**
Designed by (per the sidebar infobox): **Intel**
usage: prompt 798 tokens (78 text + the encoder's 720 image rows), completion 139
```

The request ran against a server whose `vision.exe` is this branch's launcher and whose encoder is this branch's
own build.

**The launcher's preflight, four ways.** With no oneAPI install reachable (no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, no `icpx` on
`PATH`, no `/opt/intel/oneapi`) it exits 1 with the one fix to apply. The capture is
`evidence/fresh/launcher-preflight-four-ways-runtime-root.txt`, run on this commit; the three
`launcher-preflight-both-ways*` files beside it are the earlier revisions, kept as they were taken and labelled
(the revision before the last review pass, the three-commit tip, the run before the launcher was renamed):

```
strata-vision: the image encoder cannot start: missing runtime libraries: libsycl.so.9
strata-vision: install Intel oneAPI (the DPC++ compiler and oneMKL components), then either
strata-vision:   source <oneapi>/setvars.sh        # before starting the server, or
strata-vision:   export STRATA_ONEAPI_ROOT=<oneapi-install-root>
```

It preflights clean and execs the encoder in the other three cases: with `STRATA_ONEAPI_ROOT` set to the oneAPI
tree; with nothing set but an install at Intel's own default `/opt/intel/oneapi`; and with the `icpx` on `PATH`
and the loader path otherwise empty, the route that takes the root from the compiler's own location. An unknown
argument reaches the encoder's own parser (`unknown argument --bogus`, exit 2, device untouched), which proves
resolution without using the card. On the card the encoder runs to `READY 2560` and `OK` records.

## Extra Notes
- **Scope.** An Arc A770 on `xe` only: not Battlemage or a B-series, not an A750 on `i915`, not a two-card box.
  `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` is the device switch, moot on one Intel card.
- **The installer on a host with a system oneAPI install.** The build behind this change takes the encoder's
  toolchain from the port's container overlay; at run time the launcher finds oneAPI from `icpx` on `PATH`, from
  `STRATA_ONEAPI_ROOT`, or from Intel's own default `/opt/intel/oneapi`.
- **Not bit-exact** (see the table). A row can differ in the last places. Use is unaffected: the engine reads the
  rows as the picture and answers about it correctly, and a token that diverges against llama.cpp is not excluded.
- **Why the encoder has a launcher of its own.** `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` is the engine's launcher and runs

pulls.title: serve: keep console writes outside shared state locks
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Title

serve: keep console writes outside shared state locks

Issue: Resolves #2432

## Summary

The request-finish path prints its completion line while holding `status_lock`. When Windows QuickEdit pauses the console, that write waits with the lock held, blocking status queries and progress updates.

Build the completion messages while updating state, then print them after releasing both `status_lock` and the serial engine turn (`fifo`). A completed request no longer retains either lock while waiting for its console write. Apply the same state-lock ordering to batch-slot admission, MCP startup and restart, and the optional schema dependency message.

## What changed

Each operation collects its log lines under the state lock and writes them after release. Request completion first settles its statistics and status, exits the engine turn, then writes the saved lines. The request-finish, batch-slot and MCP paths use an outer `finally`, so prepared messages are still written if the operation raises. Messages retain their order within each operation.

The orphan-slot reaper returns the slots it freed to its caller, which reports them outside the condition lock. Locks that serialize engine-pipe writes and configuration updates continue to cover those operations.

## Extra Notes

Four regression tests cover blocked console output, output under state locks and exception paths. The blocked-output test checks that both `status_lock` and `fifo` are available while the completion writer waits. It fails against the earlier revision, which still held `fifo`, and passes with this change on macOS and Windows. The full service suite passes on macOS: 778 tests and 5638 subtests, with 11 skips.

An HTTP check on both platforms pauses the completion-line writer while a request is finishing. `/v1/status` returns HTTP 200 while that writer is blocked, and the chat request completes after the writer is released. These checks use a mock engine and a blocking stdout replacement to reproduce console backpressure. The printing thread waits for the console; shared state and the serial engine turn are available to other handlers. Other synchronous log writes can still wait on a paused console.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: send the role chunk with the first response data
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Fixes #2391. On a streamed OpenAI chat completion, `openai_chunks` sends the `{"role": "assistant", "content": ""}` chunk before the engine has read the prompt. A client that times the first data chunk (llama-benchy's TTFR / est_ppt) therefore measures a prefill of about 0 ms.

Before: the role chunk is the first SSE data, sent before the prompt read. After: the role chunk goes out once, together with the first real data (content, reasoning, a tool call, MCP data, requested `prompt_progress`, or the final chunk of an empty answer). Keep-alive pings during the prompt read stay SSE comments. Non-streamed responses (`openai_collect`) are unchanged.

## Related discussion
https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2391

## Approach
`openai_chunks` opens the stream lazily: a small `first()` helper yields the role chunk exactly once, right before the first chunk that carries data. vLLM and llama.cpp also send the role with the first output. This changes only when the role chunk is sent, not what any chunk contains. `serve/test_first_chunk.py` covers content, reasoning, streamed and whole tool calls, empty answers, errors before the first token, pings, requested and unavailable progress, and MCP rounds.

## Validation
Rebased on main e88ee39d. The v0.2.0-beta tag (3d1fb480) is an ancestor of it, and no commit between them touches `serve/server.py`. Environment: Debian 13 x86_64, Python 3.13.5, `pip install -r requirements.txt` in a venv, CPU only, no engine (the tests use a fake service).

**Passed:**
- `git am` of the two rebased commits onto a fresh checkout of main e88ee39d: applied cleanly.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_first_chunk`, patched on main e88ee39d: 12 tests, OK.
- The same test file on unpatched main e88ee39d: 10 of 12 fail (`a data chunk went out before the prompt was read`, and the role chunk sent while progress was unavailable). This confirms that #2391 still exists on v0.2.0-beta.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server`, patched on main e88ee39d: 341 tests, OK. The result is the same on unpatched main.

**Failed:**
none observed

**Not run:**
- A live server with a real model and llama-benchy TTFR. No GPU on this machine, so the client-side timing is not measured.
- The Anthropic and Responses stream dialects: this change touches only the OpenAI chat-completions stream.

## Limits
The change affects only when the role chunk is sent. A client that expects the role chunk before any keep-alive comment now sees the comments first. Those are SSE comments, not data.
