pulls.title: [Engine] serve: skip file lookahead when experts remain resident
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Fixes #1922. When every expert is already covered by the GPU cache or the RAM complement, the routing-aware file lookahead keeps computing next-layer routes even though there is nothing left for it to fetch. That work runs on the same CPU as the expert workers.

Before: the lookahead submits predictions on every decode layer, even with complete GPU/RAM coverage. After: in fixed-capacity serial serving with complete coverage, the engine stops submitting those predictions and logs `routing-aware prefetch off (complete GPU/RAM coverage during serial decode)`. Every other configuration keeps the current behavior.

## Related discussion
https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1922
Benchmark report for the earlier measurement: #2520.

## Approach
The decision is made once, immediately before `READY`, after prompt-buffer reservations, KV planning and the prediction consumers are set up. Some startup reservations remove GPU-only experts after the RAM complement is built, so the check reads the final residency table, not an earlier snapshot.

Coverage stays complete afterwards: adaptive exchanges save the outgoing expert before its GPU slot is reused, and serial prompts return borrowed slots before decode. Batch serving, elastic KV, Foresight, lookahead statistics and an explicit `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD` setting all keep the lookahead running. The rule lives in a small header (`include/strata/core/resident_decode_prefetch.hpp`) used by both the CUDA/HIP and the SYCL serve paths. The predictor's startup allocations and its idle thread remain.

`tests/core/resident_decode_prefetch_test.cpp` covers eligibility, every exclusion, duplicate GPU/RAM copies, 20,000 modeled exchanges, prompt loans and permanent slot removal.

On main the PR is unchanged in substance. The only conflict was textual: main now calls `pin_sim_report("at READY")` and `pin_reserve_release_hard()` at the same spot, and the coverage check is placed right after them, still immediately before `READY`. The 0.2 additions that can rewrite residency during decode (`STRATA_RAM_ADAPT` / `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT2`) only promote experts that are in neither tier, so under complete coverage they have nothing to promote.

## Validation
Rebased on main c093ac26. The two commits were first validated on main e88ee39d (contains v0.2.0-beta, 3d1fb480), then applied without conflicts to c093ac26, where the CPU build and tests were rerun. The GPU checks below were run on e88ee39d and have not been repeated on c093ac26. Two environments:
- CPU: Debian 13 x86_64, g++ 14.2.0, CMake 3.31.6. `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`, Ninja.
- GPU: Windows, Ryzen 5 7600X, 32 GB RAM, RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 (the version pinned by `tools/hip/build_windows.bat`). HIP build with `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1100`, Release.

**Passed:**
- `git am` of the two commits onto fresh checkouts of main e88ee39d and of main c093ac26: applied cleanly on both.
- `resident_decode_prefetch_test` on main e88ee39d + this PR: `PASS: 81552 checks; 20000 modeled exchange cycles`, both with g++ on Linux and with the ROCm toolchain on Windows. Same result on main c093ac26 + this PR with g++ on Linux.
- `ctest` on main e88ee39d + this PR (CPU): 43 of 49 pass. Unpatched main e88ee39d: 42 of 48 pass. The same 6 tests fail on both trees for environment reasons: stock ggml without the trellis types (`native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2`), no model pack (`expert_parity`, `pool_test`), and `isa_guard_check` on `tq_avx512.cpp`. On main c093ac26 + this PR: 44 of 50 pass, unpatched c093ac26 43 of 49, with the same 6 failures.
- HIP build (gfx1100) of unpatched main e88ee39d and of main e88ee39d + this PR: both build with 0 errors.
- Serial `--serve` on main e88ee39d + this PR, on the RX 7900 XTX with Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts`, `--expert-cache 4416` (5759 GPU slots), 128K context, int8 KV, MTP, lookahead in automatic mode (`STRATA_LOOKAHEAD` unset). Request: 61-token English prompt, 128 tokens, temperature 0, seed 1922, each run a fresh start.
  - With complete GPU/RAM coverage (12.60 and 12.63 GiB of experts in RAM), both patched runs printed `routing-aware prefetch off (complete GPU/RAM coverage during serial decode)` and read 0 experts from the file during decode.
  - Their 128 generated tokens are byte-identical to unpatched main under complete coverage (same token IDs in all fully resident runs of either build).
  - In earlier runs where startup could not keep every expert resident, the patched build did not print that line and kept the lookahead on, as intended.
- Unpatched main e88ee39d and c093ac26 have no coverage-based skip in either `generate.cpp`, so #1922 still applies.

**Failed:**
none observed

**Not run:**
- HIP build and GPU `--serve` on main c093ac26 (c093ac26 also changes `src/program/generate.cpp`; the patch applies there without conflicts).
- CUDA and SYCL builds on main e88ee39d or c093ac26. The SYCL path uses the same header and the same inserted check as the HIP/CUDA path.
- A/B throughput measurement on 0.2. Two reasons:
  - On the test machine, 0.2 could not keep the full expert set resident reliably: in an attempted 600-token A/B, 5 of 7 fresh-start arms fell short of the Windows commit limit and read experts from the file, which left no valid pair.
  - Run-to-run variance is too large. Two identical fresh-start runs with full residency (same build, lookahead forced on in both, same 600-token requests) decoded English at 57.2 and 44.8 tok/s, about 25% apart, far more than the expected 1–2% effect.
- The throughput figures for this PR were measured on 0.1 (base 296b59d2), not on 0.2: RX 7900 XTX with IQ1_M, 11 matched English pairs, +1.67% decode throughput (40.40 → 41.08 tok/s) and 6.10% less request CPU time (report in #2520). An independent check by pugolini (in this PR's comments) on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 with Coder IQ1_M, also on 0.1: about +1.1%, served text byte-identical on 13 prompts, and the coverage check fired.

## Limits
The decision is made once at startup. It applies only to serial serving with fixed capacity; batched serving and elastic KV keep the lookahead because they can create file-backed decode work. The gain is small (about 1–2% decode on the setups measured so far, all on 0.1), and it only appears when the whole model fits in GPU + RAM.

pulls.title: Metal: the GGUF reader refuses malformed headers with a message instead of crashing or exiting (#1919)
pulls.author: PiMatyja
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Refs #1919 (malformed GGUF headers). #2288 does the same for setup's Python reader (tools/gguf_reader.py); this PR is the Metal engine's C++ reader only.

## Summary

`metal/src/gguf_lite.cpp` reads the header of every GGUF the Metal engine opens (the model shard and the MTP file, `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`). On a malformed or crafted header it could read outside the mapping, abort, exit the process (`ref::block_bytes` calls `std::exit(2)` on an unknown tensor type), allocate without bound, or accept tensors that lie outside the file, which the engine then reads. Now every such header is refused with a message from `File::open`, and every valid file loads as before: same tensors, types, shapes, offsets, sizes and metadata.

## What changed

- `metal/src/gguf_lite.cpp`
  - `Reader::get` / `Reader::str`: the bounds checks compare lengths, not pointers (`p + n` could wrap). After the first failed read every read returns 0, so no garbage count is used after a short read.
  - `fstat` is checked; an empty file is refused.
  - Arrays: an array of arrays or of an unknown type is refused (llama.cpp's `gguf.cpp` refuses them too). A numeric array whose length runs past the end is refused before the read pointer moves.
  - An unknown metadata value type is refused with its number.
  - `n_dims` above 4 (GGML_MAX_DIMS) is refused before the shape is read.
  - `general.alignment` must be a power of two in the uint32 range (the spec's type; llama.cpp also requires a power of two). No other upper bound.
  - Per tensor: the element count and the byte size are checked for overflow; an unknown type is refused before `block_elems` / `block_bytes` are called; offset + size must lie inside the file (the same rule as llama.cpp's loader, "data is not within the file bounds").
- `metal/src/ref_quant.h` / `.cpp`: `ref::known_type(t)`, true for exactly the types `block_bytes` knows. `block_elems` falls back to 256 for any type, so it cannot be used for this.
- `metal/tests/gguf_lite_test.cpp` (new, picked up by the `tests/*.cpp` glob, no GPU): builds crafted files byte by byte and checks each is refused with the expected message, plus valid tiny files that must load with the right offsets and sizes.

Left alone: GGUF v2 is still refused; duplicate tensor names (the last wins, as before); tensor offsets that are not a multiple of the alignment (not a bounds problem); rows that are not whole blocks (the size rounds down, as before); the engine's own use of a tensor's shape (`window.cpp`, `stream.cpp`); the CUDA / HIP / SYCL reader (`include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp`). Only `metal/` files change.

## Extra Notes

### How it was checked

macOS on Apple Silicon (arm64), Apple clang, `cmake -S metal -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && make -C build gguf_lite_test` (metal-cpp not needed for it). Base: 296b59d (v0.1.44.1).

```
ok   loads:   a valid file, alignment 64
ok   loads:   a valid file, alignment 16384
ok   loads:   a valid file, alignment 131072
ok   loads:   no tensors, ends before the data start
ok   refused: every truncation of the valid file           290 prefixes
ok   refused: not GGUF magic                               not a GGUF file
ok   refused: version 2                                    GGUF version is not 3
ok   refused: key length past the end                      truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: string length past the end                   truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: u32 array past the end                       truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: string array past the end                    truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: u8 array count that wraps the read pointer   truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: nested array                                 GGUF array of type 9: k
ok   refused: array of unknown type 77                     GGUF array of type 77: k
ok   refused: unknown value type 77                        unknown GGUF value type 77: k
ok   refused: 5 dimensions                                 tensor has 5 dimensions: a
ok   refused: huge tensor count                            truncated GGUF header
ok   refused: general.alignment 0                          general.alignment is not a power of two
ok   refused: general.alignment 48                         general.alignment is not a power of two
ok   refused: general.alignment 2147483649                 general.alignment is not a power of two
ok   refused: general.alignment 2^32 (u64)                 general.alignment is not a power of two
ok   refused: general.alignment -64 (i32)                  general.alignment is not a power of two
ok   refused: offset past the file end                     tensor lies outside the file: a
ok   refused: offset + size past the file end              tensor lies outside the file: a
ok   refused: offset wraps around                          tensor lies outside the file: a
ok   refused: shape product overflows                      tensor shape overflows: a
ok   refused: byte size overflows                          tensor size overflows: a
ok   refused: unknown tensor type 99                       unknown tensor type 99: a
ok   refused: unknown tensor type 3 (Q4_1)                 unknown tensor type 3: a
ok   refused: negative tensor type                         unknown tensor type -2147483648: a
ALL PASS
```

The same test also passes built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined`. `-Wall -Wextra`: no warnings in the changed files.

### Before and after

The same cases against the unchanged `gguf_lite.cpp`, each in its own child process so that a crash or exit does not stop the run (a child asking for more than 1 GB was stopped):

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String length 2^64-1 | aborts (`std::length_error`: `p + n` wraps, the check passes) | refused |
| u8 array count that moves the read pointer back | SIGSEGV (reads before the mapping) | refused |
| u32 array past the end | loads (read pointer left past the end) | refused |
| Nested array, array of unknown type | loads (skips 0 bytes, the inner array is read as the next key) | refused |
| Unknown value type | refused as "truncated GGUF header" | refused, names the type |
| 5 dimensions | loads | refused |
| Huge tensor count | allocates over 1 GB (a dimension count read from the bytes after a failed name) | refused |
| `general.alignment` 0 | loads: the division by zero gives 0 on arm64, so the data starts at byte 0 and tensors point into the header | refused |
| `general.alignment` 48, 2^31+1, 2^32 (u64), -64 (i32) | loads | refused |
| Tensor offset or offset + size past the end, offset that wraps | loads (the engine then reads outside the file) | refused |
| Shape product or byte size overflows | loads with a wrapped size | refused |
| Unknown tensor type (99, Q4_1, 0x80000000) | process exits with code 2 (`ref: unknown type`) | refused |
| Truncations of a valid file | 159 of 290 prefixes load (every cut after the tensor table) | all 290 refused |

### Valid files load the same

- Files written with llama.cpp's gguf-py (0.19.0): 55 tensors covering every type `known_type` accepts (F32, F16, BF16, Q4_0, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, each as 1-D, 2-D and 3-D, plus one more Q4_0), with string, int and float arrays in the metadata, at the default alignment and at 16384 (the alignment `metal/tools/metal_repack.py` writes), and a copy of the second with that extra tensor's type set to Q2_0 (42). Before and after print the same table for all three (name, type, shape, offset, bytes, every number and string key). For the first two the tensor table also matches gguf-py's own `GGUFReader` (data offset and byte count).
- llama.cpp's 18 v3 vocab files (`models/ggml-vocab-*.gguf`: no tensors, large token string arrays): the same metadata before and after. The one v2 file (aquila) is refused before and after.

Not checked: a full model shard and the MTP file on a Mac. The reader only reads headers, so the gguf-py files above cover the same code; a load of a real pack with this change is the remaining check.

pulls.title: MCP: opt-in cached image previews and authenticated downloads
pulls.author: cuijinkuo
pulls.body:
## Summary

Related: #2130 and #2343.

## Setup tutorial

[Enable web search and image generation, preview and downloads](https://github.com/cuijinkuo/Strata/blob/codex/mcp-image-results/docs/MCP_TOOLS_GUIDE.md)

The guide includes configuration fragments, a search provider, a ComfyUI bridge, a runnable image-preview adapter, verification steps and small-GPU handoff precautions. Enable `mcp.image_results` and configure the providers separately; this switch does not install a generation model. The automatic GPU lifecycle controller is not included in this PR.

An MCP image result currently becomes text describing an unseen picture. This opt-in implementation passes supported raster results through existing vision preparation and gives the web chat a preview and authenticated download link. SHA-256 cache references survive refreshes and subsequent turns without storing base64 in localStorage.

**Overlap with #2343:** that PR already implements image-to-model delivery and client-side base64 lifting. This is an alternative cache-based transport, with persistent references and download support. The changes touch the same code and must be reconciled before merging. Client-side base64 lifting is not included here.

## What changed

- Enable with `"mcp": {"image_results": true}`; disabled by default. Default text results and stream result fields remain unchanged.
- Cache PNG/JPEG/WebP only, by SHA-256 beside the run configuration. Reject invalid base64, unsupported media and arbitrary file references. Four images per result, each capped at 24 million base64 characters (about 18 MB decoded).
- Downloads use existing API authentication, basename checks, raster MIME types, nosniff and same-origin resource policy. The browser fetches using authorization headers and downloads through Blob URLs.
- Show previews outside collapsed tool details. Reclaim ready/pending Blob URLs on New chat and pagehide; rehydrate on BFCache restoration.
- Forward images through the existing vision path when configured, otherwise preserve the text fallback and user-visible preview. Cache write failure preserves the tool text result. Text remains subject to max_result_chars.

## Validation

- Rebased by merging main at 477ac13c. Related regression suite: 426 tests, OK (3 skipped), without loading GPU models. Media and web-sampling checks: 24 tests passed.
- Tutorial JSON examples and Python adapter were validated, including stdio initialization/tool listing, byte-preserving image delivery and outside-directory, invalid-extension and missing-file rejection. Third-party provider installations were not benchmarked.
- Tests cover cache deduplication and byte preservation, invalid content and caps, authenticated delivery and traversal refusal, cached-history resolution, stream metadata/vision dispatch, text truncation, cache write failure, and unchanged default text/event fields.
- `node --check serve/web/app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Against this branch’s mock server, a saved 1024px PNG preview rendered within a 390px viewport, and its actual download matched the source SHA-256. This is desktop browser viewport testing, not physical iPhone/Safari testing or a new generation benchmark.

## Extra notes

No C++/CUDA/HIP/SYCL files changed. ComfyUI installation, GPU coordination and search providers remain external integrations. Narrow-viewport fixes keep tool summaries, images and composer controls within the screen; checked at 320, 390, 640, 768 and 1280 pixels. Cache retention is manual; deleting cached files invalidates old references. See docs/MCP_IMAGES.md.

pulls.title: fix(sycl): permit Level Zero IPC in expert-parallel containers
pulls.author: hotschmoe
pulls.body:
Expert parallelism in #1798/#2205 fails during Level Zero IPC handle import in a container using Docker's default seccomp profile. Both cards report peer access available, but cross-card and self-import return `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`0x78000004`).

Add `--cap-add SYS_PTRACE` only when `--expert-parallel-device` is present. This permits the relevant syscalls under Docker's existing capability-dependent seccomp rules. The default profile remains enabled, and ordinary layer-split launches receive no extra capability. Document the option for custom launchers. This is a launcher prerequisite for the open EP PRs, with no engine feature copied into this branch.

Validation on two Intel Arc Pro B70s, kernel 7.1, Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.4, Level Zero 1.28.2, oneAPI 2026.1:

- Default container: all eight imports fail (cross-card and self, cold and warm allocations, both directions).
- SYS_PTRACE only, default seccomp retained: all eight imports succeed.
- Seccomp-unconfined only: all eight imports succeed; this broader option is not used in the patch.
- Full EP model with the capability: all 24,576 experts resident, 768 generated diagnostic tokens, zero peer-row mismatches; deterministic concurrent arithmetic, reasoning, and a tool round trip pass.
- Normal teardown, per-card health, and ten compiled two-rank all-reduces pass.
- `bash -n` and mocked Docker argv checks pass for layer-split and EP paths, including a model path containing spaces.

The exact blocked syscall was not traced. Local launcher measurements use the same conditional capability; the upstream wrapper's argument construction was checked with a mock Docker executable.

pulls.title: engine+serve: the confidence monitor (STRATA_CONFIDENCE=1, measurement only)
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

An online number for "is the model confident right now" - ActKV's confidence signal (arXiv:2609.31395, section 6), which its evaluation used to detect an insufficient KV budget from the model's own behaviour:

- **Per kept decode row**: ActKV's token confidence `T` = the negative mean log-probability of the top 20 predicted tokens (a higher `T` is a sharper distribution).
- **Per request**: the mean of `T` and ActKV's trend slope `alpha` (sliding min-pool w=64 s=8, bottom 10% kept, first-order fit; negative means confidence is falling). The engine emits `CONF <tokens> <mean> <slope>` just before the request's `DONE`; the server attaches it to the request row and `GET /metrics` carries a `"confidence"` summary (count, mean, last mean, last slope).

Why it belongs in the engine: it is the signal for comparing lossy settings the numbers cannot - `--kv q4_0` against `int8`, a tight `--kv-resident` - and later for budget feedback. The constants are ActKV's evaluation values; nothing here claims they are right for Strata, and no default changes.

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

`STRATA_CONFIDENCE=1` in the environment turns it on. **Without the flag nothing runs**: no copies, no line changes, every answer unchanged. The flag copies the head's logits from the GPU once per window (the `STRATA_LOGPOS` pattern), so it slows the decode - like `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING`, for comparing, not timing. No Metal path (it says so and turns itself off there).

## How it was checked

- `src/core/confidence_test.cpp` (CPU): the math on hand-worked rows (a flat row gives `T = log V`, a peaked row the exact value), the pooling, and the time ordering the trend fit needs - that last one caught a bug in my first cut (sorting the bottom set destroyed the trend).
- `serve/test_server.py` (`ConfidenceMonitor`): the `CONF`-before-`DONE` pairing, a bad `CONF` line refusing to poison `DONE`, the row fields and the summary through `GET /metrics`. **The full serve suite passes: 787 tests, 11 skipped.**
- **Live on this box's GTX 1080 Ti** (IQ3_S, `--serve`, two `GEN`s in one session, `STRATA_CONFIDENCE=1`): a 128-token repeating prompt reports `CONF 7 5.7530 0.000000`, a scattered-id prompt `CONF 1 4.7600 0.000000` - the metric moves the way ActKV's signal should. `slope` is 0 for requests shorter than one pool window (pinned by the test too).

## Not tested

HIP (no toolchain here) and SYCL (separate engine tree). Multi-window trend behaviour on a long request (the live run's requests are short - the slope path is exercised in the unit test, not on hardware). Any threshold for "confidence is too low" - this PR is the measurement, not the alarm.

pulls.title: gfx906/HIP build broken on v0.1.44.1: two compile blockers (platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h missing three cublas maps, and the new strata_mmq_w4a4 target missing GGML_USE_HIP)
pulls.author: kietq8684-design
pulls.body:
Fixes the build regression reported in #2459.

### Summary
`-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON` no longer builds on the latest tag. v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`) builds clean; v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`)
fails with two independent blockers, both introduced after 0.1.42. `docs/AMD_HIP.md:472` says the gfx906 engine
"is checked to compile for gfx906", so this is a regression rather than a missing feature. A 9-line patch makes
`ninja -C build-906 strata` finish with 149/149 linked, exit 0.

### Environment
- GPU: Radeon VII 16 GB (`0x66af`) + Radeon Pro VII / Instinct MI50 16 GB (`0x66a1`), both gfx906
- ROCm: HIP 7.14 (hipcc 7.14.60850) from `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
- Kernel: 6.8.0-146-p2p, Ubuntu 24.04, `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=9.0.6`
- Build: `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 -DSTRATA_GGML_DIR=/llama
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++`, Ninja
- llama.cpp at the pinned commit (`3cf03257f`)
- `git describe` on the tree: v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`) builds; worktree at v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d`) fails

### Blocker 1 — `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h` is missing three mappings

`include/strata/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h` gained `cublasSgemm`, `cublasSgemmStridedBatched` and
`cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx` between 0.1.42 and 0.1.44.1, and `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` (new in 0.1.44.1) uses
them. But that file is **not on the gfx906 include path**: `CMakeLists.txt:60` says the cuBLAS names are mapped by
`include/strata/platform/hip_compat/`, lines 138/141/142 attach it `BEFORE INTERFACE`, and the only strata-side
`-I` in `compile_commands.json` is `-I/src/include/strata/platform/hip_compat`. That second file still maps
`cublasGemmEx` only, so the three names are undeclared.

Fix — add to `include/strata/platform/hip_compat/cublas_v2.h`:

```diff
 #define cublasGemmEx hipblasGemmEx
+#define cublasSgemm hipblasSgemm
+#define cublasSgemmStridedBatched hipblasSgemmStridedBatched
+#define cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx hipblasGemmStridedBatchedEx
```

### Blocker 2 — the new `strata_mmq_w4a4` target has no `GGML_USE_HIP`

```
FAILED: CMakeFiles/strata_mmq_w4a4.dir/src/prefill/mmq_nvfp4_w4a4.cu.o
/llama/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/cuda.h:4:10: error: 'cuda.h' file not found with <angled> include
/llama/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vendors/cuda.h:6:10: fatal error: 'cuda_bf16.h' file not found
```

`mmq_nvfp4_w4a4.cu` includes llama.cpp's `common.cuh`, which selects `vendors/hip.h` only under
`#if defined(GGML_USE_HIP)` and otherwise pulls `vendors/cuda.h` (`<cuda.h>`, `<cuda_bf16.h>` — absent in a HIP
environment; `platform/hip_compat/` provides only `cuda_fp16.h`, `cuda_runtime.h`, `math_constants.h`).
`CMakeLists.txt:1791` sets `GGML_USE_HIP` on `strata_mmq` for the gfx906 branch and `:1576` has the `=1` form for
gfx11, but the `strata_mmq_w4a4` target added at `:1449-1457` was missed. Its sibling `mmq_nvfp4_w4a8.cu` has the
define and compiles (877 KB `.o`), which is what identifies this as an omission rather than a design choice.
CUDA builds are unaffected — they want `vendors/cuda.h`.

Fix — in `CMakeLists.txt`, after `target_link_libraries(strata_mmq PRIVATE strata_mmq_w4a4)`:

```diff
     target_link_libraries(strata_mmq PRIVATE strata_mmq_w4a4)
+    # gfx906 / HIP: this unit includes ggml-cuda's common.cuh, which only takes vendors/hip.h when
+    # GGML_USE_HIP is defined (strata_mmq gets it in the HIP branches below).  Without it the CUDA
+    # vendor headers (<cuda.h>, <cuda_bf16.h>) are pulled in and the HIP build fails.
+    if(STRATA_HIP_GFX906 OR STRATA_ENABLE_HIP)
+      target_compile_definitions(strata_mmq_w4a4 PRIVATE GGML_USE_HIP)
+    endif()
```

### Result with the patch
`ninja -C build-906 strata` → **149/149 linked, exit 0**, `build-906/strata` = 26,224,152 B (v0.1.42 is 21 MB).
Patch total: 9 lines (`cublas_v2.h` +3, `CMakeLists.txt` +6). The 0.1.42 tree is untouched.

### Note (not a blocker, just a build-time observation)
`strata_mmq_w4a4` is a unit that the gfx906/HIP path does not use at all, so an alternative to the define above
is to skip the target on this branch entirely — either way the HIP build should not be pulling CUDA vendor headers
for it.

pulls.title: engine: --dump-kv-select, the decode windows' KV block selections as a policy-bench trace (#2415)
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

The engine-side half of #2415 (the bench is #2434): `--dump-kv-select PATH` records what the KV streaming page pool is actually asked for - **one record per resolve call** of the decode windows, `int32 layer, int32 k, k int32 block ids, k float32 weights`, the shape `tools/replay_kv_stream_policy.py` reads.

- The resolve wrapper copies each selection into per-QSA-layer **pinned staging at fixed addresses**, so the captured graphs bake the copies in as memcpy nodes; a flush after the window's `cudaStreamSynchronize` appends the records. Weights are 1.0 (the indexer's scores are not copied).
- The staging is allocated at `kv_select_dump_open`, **before any window is captured** - the first build died on exactly that (an allocation inside a capture poisons its stream).

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

The resolve wrapper gains a `dump_slot` argument (the two verify call sites pass the QSA ordinal; the prompt path passes nothing), a small dump block in layer.cpp, a flush in verify.cpp after the window sync, and `--dump-kv-select` plumbing in generate.cpp. **Without the flag nothing runs and every answer is unchanged** - the copies are the only new work, and they exist only when the flag is given.

## How it was checked

- `kv_stream_parity` **PASS** (q4_0 and k8v4: 0 failures, ring restore identical) on a GTX 1080 Ti (sm_61, `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`), CUDA build with g++-14.
- **Live captures** from this box's IQ3_S pack (the deployment's own args + `--dump-kv-select`): a 127-token prompt → a 115 KB trace (348 calls), a 4095-token prompt → a 3.5 MB trace (684 calls, 441,848 block lookups, 12,586 distinct blocks). The engine ran unchanged otherwise (prefill 276 tok/s, decode 20.7 tok/s on this card).
- Both traces replay through #2434's bench. On the 4K trace, at a per-layer pool between one call's width (646 blocks) and the working set (~1,050 blocks) the **real selections rank the policies**:

| pool/layer | compulsory | clock (today) | lrfu | lru | oracle |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 768 | 12,586 | 41,878 | **40,046** | 69,929 | 31,552 |
| 896 | 12,586 | 21,741 | **21,014** | 23,646 | 16,114 |

(misses; lower is better). So on real QSA selections LRFU beats the kernel's CLOCK by 3-4% of misses, LRU is worse than both, and Belady says more is on the table - the numbers #2415 asked for before anyone changes the default.

## Not tested

HIP (no toolchain on this box; the .cu sources are shared with the HIP build) and SYCL (a separate engine tree with no dump). The `--batch` window path keeps each layer's last call per window (documented in DETAILS.md). No wall-time claim from the miss counts - that is the live A/B #2415's next step, using the engine's own `KV streaming:` line.

pulls.title: [Other] serve: an all-cached image turn never wakes the elastic encoder
pulls.author: jerry78424
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
An elastic image encoder is woken (seconds of start, VRAM the expert cache gives up) on every turn that re-sends pictures it has already encoded - which is what most clients do on every turn. A turn whose images are all in the hash cache needs no encoder process at all.

Measured on RTX 5090 32 GB, Windows 11 (26200), engine 0.1.44.1, nvfp4, `elastic_idle_s: 10` (table and verbatim log lines in #2454): before - a text-only turn with a re-sent picture cost a 2.3 s start + 2085 MiB taken from the expert cache; after - 722 ms with no start line. A re-sent-picture turn: 1277 ms, no start. New pictures unchanged (3979-4213 ms, still start).

## Related discussion
Resolves #2454. Independent of #2641 (the tool-picture wake lands in this same method - textual overlap only; the two PRs conflict in neither order, verified by cherry-pick).

## Approach
- `serve/server.py`: `Vision.key_of()` / `Vision.cached()` - a hash-cache lookup that answers with the process down (the cache and its .sve files survive an unload, as before) and marks a hit most recently used, as `encode()` does on its hit path. `prepare()` maps the turn's images through the cache first, for an elastic encoder only: when every one is a hit the turn skips the encode FIFO, `_vision_up()` and the encode. A miss - alone or alongside hits - keeps today's path byte-for-byte: FIFO, make-room, start, encode.
- `serve/test_vision_cache_wake.py` (new, CPU-only, no engine): a re-sent picture does not wake a stopped encoder; a new picture alongside cached ones still wakes it; the lookup answers with the process down and keeps the re-sent picture from aging out of the 64-entry cache; a non-elastic turn keeps today's path even when every picture is cached.
- `docs/VRAM_ELASTIC.md`, `docs/DETAILS.md`: both halves of the elastic rule - a picture's turn starts the encoder, a turn of pictures the cache knows takes neither the turn nor a start.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Every new behavior fails on a tree without the code that provides it.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_vision_elastic serve.test_vision_busy serve.test_vision_cache_wake serve.test_images`: the vision four 36 OK - at `e88ee39d` (v0.2.0-beta-12), rebased 2026-10-20, Windows 11 26200, Python 3.12 venv, CPU-only tests.
- Full serve suite: 791 OK (15 skipped).
- With #2641 cherry-picked on top: the files stay 19 + 19 OK.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** AMD/HIP and layer-split machines (a layer split refuses elastic anyway; its start failure is #2435). No native files are touched, so no native builds are required.

## Limits
- What it leaves alone: non-elastic vision, the start/stop/idle lifecycle itself, the encode path, and every native file (no CUDA/HIP/SYCL build needed).
- The measured numbers are one machine (RTX 5090, nvfp4); the mechanism - no process start for an all-cached turn - is hardware-independent, but the saved seconds are not claimed for other machines.

pulls.title: setup: no KV streaming on one card that holds every expert and the whole KV cache (#2261)
pulls.author: ischencheng
pulls.body:
Fixes #2261.

From 64K up setup writes `--kv-resident 32768` whenever the RAM holds the K/V copy. On a card that already holds every expert and the whole K/V in VRAM, the VRAM this frees has nothing left to hold, and the cells past 32K are read from RAM.

With `--kv-streaming auto`, setup now keeps the K/V in VRAM on one card (no layer split, not a shared-memory GPU) when its VRAM covers the experts (`arena_gb`), the whole K/V of each session (1 + the `parallel` slots, from `--parallel` or the installed config) and 8.5 GB beside them. The 8.5 GB is what the engine used beside the experts and the K/V on an L40S (6.9 GB), its 700 MiB reserve, and about 1 GB for a desktop. Only the native packs' sizes: Unsloth's and the NVFP4 files keep the RAM test alone, since their dense side was not measured. `--kv-streaming on|off` work as before, and `kv_streaming_wanted` gives the same answer as Step 7. At 262K this turns streaming off for Q2_0 / IQ2_XS / IQ1_M on 48 GB cards and for every native size on 80 and 96 GB cards.

A/B on one L40S (46068 MiB, sm_89, Linux), engine 0.1.44.1 (296b59d), IQ2_XS, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8`: `--kv-resident 32768` (S) against no `--kv-resident` (R). Every expert is in VRAM in both arms (24576 of 24576; 5.4 vs 2.4 GiB free). One warm-up start, then S R / R S / S R on two Modal hosts. Engine timings from the replies, medians of 3:

| host | request | S | R |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| A | 48K-token prompt, read | 4327 tok/s | 4580 tok/s |
| A | 120K-token prompt, read | 4385 | 4738 |
| B | 48K / 120K prompt, read | 4616 / 4789 | 4616 / 4837 |
| B | 3 short chats, decode | 231.7 / 150.5 / 166.0 | 237.0 / 153.9 / 168.9 |
| B | decode after the 48K / 120K prompt | 140.4 / 134.8 | 147.0 / 141.1 |

On host B both arms of a round read the same prompts, so decode compares too (R was faster in 15 of 15 pairs). On host A the long prompts were new at each start, so only their read speed compares (R faster in 6 of 6). Host A's short chat and host B's 48K read were within 1% either way. The gains are smaller than beastrobin's on the RTX PRO 6000, in the same direction. R also pins 3.09 GiB less RAM.

Left as it is: IQ3_XXS on the L40S, where not every expert fits, still streams. There streaming gets 22991 expert slots against 21163, but the long prompts still read about 7% faster without it on host A; decode was too noisy to tell.

Tests: two new tests in `tools/test_setup_risk.py` (KvStreaming). The RTX PRO 6000 with IQ3_S and the L40S with IQ2_XS keep the K/V in VRAM; `--kv-streaming on`, IQ3_XXS on the L40S, `--parallel 2`, two L40S in a split, UD-Q4_K_XL and NVFP4 still stream. The first fails on main. All `tools/test_setup_*.py` on Linux (Python 3.12): the same 10 failures on main and on this branch (the UD-Q4_K_XL goldens, and two engine_hash tests that look for a release download), and the 2 new tests pass.

Not tested: Windows, AMD, the RTX PRO 6000 itself, `--parallel` or the GPU image encoder on a big card, `--kv k8v4` and `q4_0`.

pulls.title: native_kernels: sm_86 dense Q8_0 GEMVs keep two rows per block (#2441)
pulls.author: yannickloth
pulls.body:
Fixes the ~20-25% decode regression reported in #2441 on an RTX A3000 Laptop 12 GB (sm_86).

## What this changes

0.1.44 made the dense Q8_0 GEMV (`src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.cu`) take one row per block on **every** sm_86 card with `n_out >= 2048`. It was measured on an RTX A4000 (+1-4% at 2-4 columns; 6144 -> 2560 at 6 columns 70% -> 76%). This reverts the sm_86 default to two rows per block. gfx1201 (RDNA4) is unchanged: it keeps one row where it was measured.

`STRATA_NO_MMVQ_ROWS2=1` still forces one row everywhere, sm_86 included, so the rule can be re-measured per card.

## Why

#2441, RTX A3000 Laptop 12 GB (GA104, sm_86, 32 SMs) + i7-12850HX, IQ3_XXS GSQ-RCO pack, `--spec 4`, same request on both engines:

| engine | decode (tok/s) | drafts accepted |
|---|---:|---|
| 0.1.43.1 | 38.1, 38.5, 40.2, 42.1 | 78.9 - 85.7% |
| 0.1.44.1 | 28.7, 32.0, 35.0, 39.7 | 73.9 - 83.6% |
| 0.1.44.1, `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` | 23.7 - 25.8 | 79.1 - 83.1% |

On CUDA/Linux the only decode-path default that changed in 0.1.44 besides the commit batching is this sm_86 rule, and sm_86 is exactly the reporter's card. The dense Q8_0 GDN and attention GEMVs of a verify window are a large share of that window's GPU time, so a per-SKU row choice that is +1-4% on a 48-SM A4000 can be a large loss on a 32-SM A3000.

## Verification

- **Still to run (draft):** the RTX A3000 A/B. Expected: `STRATA_NO_MMVQ_ROWS2=0` (two rows) restores ~0.1.43.1, and `STRATA_NO_MMVQ_ROWS2=1` on 0.1.44.1 reproduces the regression. Please ask the reporter in #2441 to post it before this lands.
- **Answers do not change:** the one-row and two-row kernels keep their own partial sums and reduction, so output is bit-identical.
- **Not built here:** no engine was compiled for this PR; the removed code is the non-HIP branch only, so HIP and SYCL paths are untouched.
- If the A/B instead points at `STRATA_COMMIT_BATCH`, this PR is the wrong fix and will be closed - that is the other default-on 0.1.44 decode change.

Reported and diagnosed on hardware the maintainers do not have (per docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md).

Refs #2441.

pulls.title: [Engine] conversation cache: evict redundant holders without losing pinned prefixes
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Fixes #2255. When every parked conversation holds a pinned prefix (`pin=N`), `evict_oldest()` refuses every entry. A client that pins its system prompt on every request fills all slots with branches of that one prefix, and every later park is refused even when the byte budget has room.

Before: with only pinned entries left, nothing can be evicted and parking is skipped. After: the oldest unpinned entry still goes first; when none is left, the oldest pinned entry goes if every pin it holds has another pinned holder with the same token IDs, image identity and steering mode. Each pinned prefix keeps at least one holder, and parking is still refused when every remaining entry is the last holder of some pin.

## Related discussion
https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2255 (reported and diagnosed by @bennizone).

## Approach
The rule stays inside `conversation_cache.hpp`; there are no new options or budget changes. An older entry is kept when it is the only holder of a different pin, so keeping "any one pinned entry" is not enough. A non-mutating `evictable_bytes()` uses the same rule: simulated removals keep the last holder of each pin and exclude retained K/V. Removing an entry can only take a holder away, so one pass in age order marks the same entries as repeated `evict_oldest()` calls.

Main has since added borrowing (#1164): while a borrowed donor is being restored, it is guarded (identified by its serial) and must not be evicted, and `make_room()` checks up front whether the outgoing image fits beside the entries that stay, so it refuses without evicting anything. This rebase works with that mechanism instead of around it:
- The guarded donor is never evicted, but it still counts as a holder of its pins, because it stays parked.
- The guard precheck no longer treats every pinned entry as staying. It uses the same simulated eviction, so it does not refuse a borrow that redundant holders can make room for, and it still refuses before evicting anything when only the donor and the last holders would remain.
- Eviction goes through main's `erase()`, so entries and serials stay in step, and `evictable_bytes()` leaves out the guarded donor.

The pinned-prefix note in `docs/DETAILS.md` now says the cache keeps at least one holder of each prefix.

`src/core/conversation_cache_test.cpp` covers repeated holders, independent pins, multi-pin entries, image and steering identity, slot and byte pressure, and accounting. It runs all 4,096 assignments of three pins to four conversations and compares the predicted reclaimable bytes with actual repeated eviction. New cases cover a guarded donor next to redundant holders: the precheck lets the park through, the donor stays and keeps its pin held, a newer holder goes when the oldest redundant holder is the donor, and the preview matches a guarded drain.

## Validation
Rebased on main c093ac26 (v0.2.0-beta plus 110 later commits, part of the 0.2.1 work). Environment: Debian 13 x86_64, g++ 14.2.0, CMake 4.4.4, Ninja, CPU only. `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_CONVERSATION_TESTS=ON`.

**Passed:**
- `git am` of the three rebased commits onto a fresh checkout of main c093ac26: applied cleanly, and the tree is identical to the rebased branch.
- `conversation_cache_test` on main c093ac26 + this PR: `45153 checks passed`. It also passes when built standalone with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined`.
- `ctest` on main c093ac26 + this PR: 48 of 54 pass, including all four `conversation_*` tests and `session_save_reclaim_test`. Unpatched main c093ac26: also 48 of 54 pass. The same 6 tests fail on both trees for environment reasons: stock ggml without the trellis types (`native_hadamard_test`, `tq_cpu_parity`, `tq_cpu_parity_avx2`), no model pack (`expert_parity`, `pool_test`), and `isa_guard_check` on `tq_avx512.cpp`.
- The bug still reproduces on main c093ac26. I built the eviction tests against unpatched main c093ac26, with failures counted instead of stopping at the first one: 15 of 4,808 checks fail. The first is "a fourth holder is parked: the oldest holder goes (#2255)", and 6 of the 15 are the new borrow cases. Main's own `conversation_cache_test` passes (4,772 checks).
- If the eviction change is kept but main's old precheck is left in (every pinned entry counted as staying), the 6 borrow cases fail: the borrow is refused although a redundant holder could go.

**Failed:**
none observed

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and SYCL builds on main c093ac26: there is no GPU toolchain on this machine. The callers (`generate.cpp` and `session_save_reclaim.hpp`) use only `make_room()`, `evict_oldest()`, `guard()` and `unguard()`, and none of their signatures changed.
- Model execution on main c093ac26.
- Earlier results, all on the 0.1-era base 296b59d2, not on 0.2: Ryzen 5 7600X / RX 7900 XTX, Windows, Coder IQ1_M with MTP. 15 fixed multi-turn requests per arm: parking refusals went from 8 to 0, branch snapshot restores from 0 to 6, and tokens prefilled across six revisits from 1,778 to 90. All 15 paired outputs were token-identical. On that base there were full HIP (gfx1100), CUDA (sm_120) and SYCL engine builds.

## Limits
The extra scan runs only after the search for an unpinned entry fails. Its cost grows with entry count, checkpoint count and prefix length, and its effect on production latency has not been measured. #2253 and #2082 add RAM admission on top of `evictable_bytes()`. If they land, they should keep this definition, not an unpinned-only count, and keep both sets of tests.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: the IQ4_XS expert dot reads its codebook from registers
pulls.author: deriknel
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
`vec_dot_iq4_xs_q8_1`, the dot the expert gate/up lane kernels use for IQ4_XS, looks each 4-bit value up with `get_int_from_table_16`, which reads `kvalues_iq4nl` from global memory on every lookup. `vec_dot_iq4_nl_q8_1` and IQ4_XS's split kernel already get the same ints from `iq4nl_pair`, which keeps the codebook in registers. With this change the IQ4_XS dot does the same, with the same output. The gain scales with how many expert layers are IQ4_XS.

## Related discussion
Haxi52 measured it on Swift 1.5 IQ4_XS, where every routed expert's gate/up rows are IQ4_XS, on three Arc Pro B70s with 0.1.44 (comment below): decode 51.1 -> 66.0 tok/s chat, 49.5 -> 65.0 agent (+29% / +31%), prompt reading unchanged, parity suites passing. No scope agreement needed: a focused fix.

## Approach
`sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`, `vec_dot_iq4_xs_q8_1`: `iq4nl_pair(aux_q4)` in place of `get_int_from_table_16(aux_q4, kvalues_iq4nl)`, under the existing compile-time `STRATA_IQ4NL_FAST` switch (on by default; `-DSTRATA_IQ4NL_FAST=0` keeps the old lookup). Both return the same ints. The branch still merges cleanly into `main`.

## Validation
Setup for every run: `main` e88ee39d built for SYCL (AOT `bmg-g31`, oneAPI 2026.1, Compute Runtime 26.35.39758.10, IGC 2.41.5) in a container; host CachyOS, kernel 7.2.11, `xe`. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, layer split 26, Swift 1.5 Flash-Next IQ3_S with every expert in VRAM, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.6`, `--prefill 4096`. Each build has only this PR's commit on top of `main`. Greedy check: 5 fixed prompts (prose, code, maths, an edit, a story), temperature 0, 400 tokens, thinking off, compared character by character. Swift IQ3_S has IQ4_XS on one expert layer of 48, so the gain here is small. Pipeline windows off; `main` and this PR alternated on fresh engines, two runs each.

**Passed:**
- Decode, bench medians: `main` 83.2 / 82.8 (prose), 106.6 / 106.6 (code); this PR 83.9 / 84.0 and 107.4 / 107.7 (+1.1% / +0.9%).
- Greedy text on the 5 prompts identical to `main`'s, both runs.
- `ctest` on both cards: the same 3 failures as on `main`; `iq_parity` with fixtures, 0 failures.
- Kernel time on 0.1.44.1 (unitrace, IQ4_XS gate/up kernel, 633 launches): 378.0 -> 171.4 us per launch; not re-traced on 0.2.0.

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and Metal builds: the change is in `sycl/` only.
- An IQ4_XS-heavy model on our cards (Haxi52's run above covers it on 0.1.44).

## Limits
The grouped gate/up path (`native_gu_multi_kernel`) is not changed; Haxi52 found its cost is elsewhere (lane layout and loads).

We investigated (myself and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code) and I reviewed the findings and ran every test on my two Arc Pro B70s on my CachyOS machine.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: defer pipelined one-token commits to the host verdict (port of c81f9984)
pulls.author: deriknel
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
With `--pipeline-windows 2` on SYCL, greedy text forks from the serial loop's within the first few hundred characters. A pipelined verifier (`set_always_publish`) captures its one-token window with the in-graph state advance, and `pl_commit_async` then runs the commit graph on top of it, so every one-token window advances the first stage's recurrent (GDN) state twice. c81f9984 fixed this in the CUDA verifier on 2026-10-09; the SYCL verifier still has the old condition. With this change the pipelined text matches the serial loop's.

## Related discussion
Needs #2433, without which `--pipeline-windows` does not run on SYCL at all. Ports c81f9984. No scope agreement needed: a focused fix.

## Approach
`sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`, the two conditions c81f9984 changed in `src/core/verify.cpp`:
- `Verifier::record_window`: `self_commit` is off when `always_publish_` is set.
- `Verifier::commit`: the branch that skips the commit graph for a one-token window is not taken when `always_publish_` is set.

Only `--pipeline-windows` calls `set_always_publish(true)`, so the serial loop does not change. The branch still merges cleanly into `main`.

## Validation
Setup for every run: `main` e88ee39d built for SYCL (AOT `bmg-g31`, oneAPI 2026.1, Compute Runtime 26.35.39758.10, IGC 2.41.5) in a container; host CachyOS, kernel 7.2.11, `xe`. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, layer split 26, Swift 1.5 Flash-Next IQ3_S with every expert in VRAM, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.6`, `--prefill 4096`. Each build has only this PR's commit on top of `main`. Greedy check: 5 fixed prompts (prose, code, maths, an edit, a story), temperature 0, 400 tokens, thinking off, compared character by character. The serial reference is `main` with pipeline windows off.

**Passed:**
- `main` + #2433 + this PR, `--pipeline-windows 2`: all 5 greedy texts identical to the serial loop's, in two rounds.
- Same build: decode 88.8 / 126.4 tok/s (prose / code) pipelined, against 83.0 / 106.6 serial on `main` (+7% / +19%).
- Same build: a ~148K-token prompt (answer found) and 10 prompts of ~13K tokens (all found), no `verify: error`, no lost device, no `xe` reset.
- `ctest` on both cards: the same 3 failures as on `main`; `iq_parity` with fixtures, 0 failures.

**Failed:**
- `main` + #2433 only, `--pipeline-windows 2` (the bug): pipelined text differs from the serial loop's at character 72 (prose), 146 (code) and 50 (story); maths and the edit are the same.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and Metal builds: the change is in `sycl/` only.

## Limits
None known. On 0.1.43.1 we also confirmed the cause with `STRATA_ONE_TOKEN_COMMIT=0` (identical text and state hashes), not repeated on 0.2.0.

We investigated (myself and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code) and I reviewed the findings and ran every test on my two Arc Pro B70s on my CachyOS machine.

pulls.title: tools: the KV streaming page-pool policy bench - CLOCK against LRFU, LRU and Belady (#2415)
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

The measurement-first half of #2415: `tools/replay_kv_stream_policy.py` replays KV block selections through the streaming page pool's policies **offline** and reports misses, hit rate and the bytes re-read over the compulsory load - the same split #1089 reports for the expert cache.

- **Trace**: `int32 layer, int32 k, k block ids, k float32 weights` per resolve call - the `--dump-routing` record layout, so an engine-side `--dump-kv-select` (the follow-up this PR does not add) can write the same shape.
- **CLOCK** is modeled as kv_stream.cu's `resolve_kernel` at slot granularity: reference on use and load, a second-chance sweep from a hand, a slot this call uses never taken, and the kernel's `3*n` scan limit on overflow (`OVERFLOW (too few resident cells)`).
- **LRFU** is ActKV's keep score (`KS = lambda*KS + gain`): the hit range is the top `--top-frac` weight mass of a call with ties at the cut included, decayed every `--decay-every` calls (ActKV decays per compression step, kvmem per request - the cadence is a knob because the right one here is what the sweep finds). **LRU** and **Belady** are the recency baseline and the offline ceiling.
- Five synthetic patterns (scan, loop, agent, intermittent, spotty) stand in until real traces exist.

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

Two `tools/` files and one docs line in DETAILS.md. **The engine and every answer are untouched** - no flag, no kernel, no default.

## How it was checked

`python -m unittest tools.test_replay_kv_stream_policy` - **9 tests**, no GPU, no model pack:

- two hand-worked traces that pin the policies exactly (CLOCK's sweep clearing a resting hot block's reference: 7 misses where LRFU/LRU/Belady make 5; LRFU's keep score keeping a historically hot block LRU ages out: 3 against 4);
- the overflow path (a call that fills the pool terminates like the kernel instead of looping);
- invariants (no policy under the compulsory load; Belady never worse; a scan is all compulsory for everyone);
- a trace round trip and a bad-file refusal.

What the patterns say so far (seed 42, one layer; the parameters are in each line):

| pattern | what it shows |
|---|---|
| `scan` (400 calls, width 100, 1024 slots) | every policy at the 40,000 floor - a scan is all compulsory |
| `spotty` (2000 calls, hot 32 every other call, 8 one-offs, 48 slots) | **CLOCK 8,038 vs the 8,016 floor** - its sweep clears the resting hot set's references between its uses; LRFU/LRU/Belady at the floor |
| `loop` (1000 calls, window 64 over 400 blocks, 128 slots) | all three at 32,032; Belady 25,696 - the churn is structural, only the ceiling does better |
| `intermittent` (1000 calls, hot 32 every call, cold 48 every 8th, 64 slots) | CLOCK = LRFU = Belady at the 2,071 structural floor; **LRU 8,771** - recency ages the hot set out |
| `agent` (2000 calls, tail 96 + task 96 + 16 one-offs, 128 slots) | CLOCK = LRFU = Belady at 216,874; **LRU 414,459** - recency ages the task set out |

So: LRFU is never worse than CLOCK in these patterns and closes its one gap (spotty); the case for making it the default needs real selection traces - which is #2415's engine-side dump follow-up.

## Not tested

Real selection traces (no engine dump exists yet), multi-layer interleavings beyond the `--layers` round-robin, weight-driven hit ranges as the indexer produces them (the synthetic patterns use equal weights), and any link between these miss counts and wall time on a card.

pulls.title: [Engine] sycl: a pipelined window still on the GPU is polled again, not failed
pulls.author: deriknel
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
On the SYCL build, `--pipeline-windows 2` fails the first request: `Verifier::done()` still has dpct's placeholder for CUDA's error check and treats a window that is still running as an error. The request ends with `verify: error`, and tearing the window down while the GPU still runs it can abort the engine with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED`. With this change a window still on the GPU is polled again, as the CUDA verifier does, and pipelined requests complete.

## Related discussion
#2800 (hotschmoe) reports the same failure on two B70s and is fixed by this change; hotschmoe also re-tested it on 0.2.0-beta (`main` e88ee39d) in the comment below. No scope agreement needed: a focused fix.

## Approach
`sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`, `Verifier::done()` only:
- A query of 1 (still running) returns false without setting `err`, as the `cudaErrorNotReady` branch does in `src/core/verify.cpp`.
- While it waits, the queue is flushed every 2 ms (`ext_oneapi_empty()` in place of `cudaStreamQuery`); the 20 s timeout from #267 stays.
- The DPCT placeholder comments go. A SYCL error arrives as an exception, which the existing `catch` handles.

Every caller of `done()` polls a window started with `pl_launch`, so the serial loop does not change. The branch still merges cleanly into `main`.

## Validation
Setup for every run: `main` e88ee39d built for SYCL (AOT `bmg-g31`, oneAPI 2026.1, Compute Runtime 26.35.39758.10, IGC 2.41.5) in a container; host CachyOS, kernel 7.2.11, `xe`. 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, layer split 26, Swift 1.5 Flash-Next IQ3_S with every expert in VRAM, `--max-context 262144`, int8 KV, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.6`, `--prefill 4096`. Each build has only this PR's commit on top of `main`. Greedy check: 5 fixed prompts (prose, code, maths, an edit, a story), temperature 0, 400 tokens, thinking off, compared character by character.

**Passed:**
- `main` + this PR, `--pipeline-windows 2`: bench and greedy requests complete, 0 `verify: error` lines in the engine log; decode 87.3 / 126.8 tok/s (prose / code).
- With #2436 as well: a ~148K-token prompt (answer found) and 10 prompts of ~13K tokens (all found), no `verify: error`, no lost device, no `xe` reset.
- `ctest` on both cards: the same 3 failures as on `main` (`gr_parity`, `ple_parity`, `s2_expert_grouped_parity`); `iq_parity` with fixtures, 0 failures.

**Failed:**
- `main` alone with `--pipeline-windows 2` (the bug): the first request returns HTTP 400 `verify: error`; the engine log shows `strata serve: verify: error`.

**Not run:**
- CUDA, HIP and Metal builds: the change is in `sycl/` only.
- Single-card `--pipeline-windows`.

## Limits
With this change alone the pipelined text can fork from the serial loop's; #2436 fixes that and needs this PR to run at all.

We investigated (myself and Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code) and I reviewed the findings and ran every test on my two Arc Pro B70s on my CachyOS machine.

pulls.title: Add Intel GPU monitoring on Windows via IGCL
pulls.author: marcelloc
pulls.body:
# Add Intel GPU monitoring on Windows via IGCL

## Summary

**Compatible with Strata 0.1.44.1**, the upstream version used when preparing
this contribution (commit `296b59d2`). The IGCL monitor was validated with the
native Windows SYCL server after integrating that release.

Populate the SYCL monitor's missing Intel GPU readings on Windows using an
optional native IGCL helper. The user explicitly builds/installs the helper;
inference continues without it when it is unavailable.

Related: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1940 and
https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1390. This contribution can complement
their native Windows work; it does not include engine portability changes.

## What changed

- Read supported activity, memory, temperatures, chip energy and PCIe link data.
- Derive rates safely; discard invalid, reset or stale readings.
- Clean up the helper on server/parent exit and launch it without a console.
- Label chip power and PCIe link capability accurately in the Windows monitor.
- Add collector and UI label tests, a manual build script and setup documentation.

The helper uses the driver-installed ControlLib.dll. No vendor binaries or
headers are bundled. Shared CUDA/HIP server files are unchanged.

## Validation

Windows 10 / Intel Arc Pro B70: helper build, actual API readings during
inference, parent-exit cleanup, collector and monitor unit tests, and JavaScript
label tests were exercised in the local implementation. The source files in
this contribution match that implementation. See docs/WINDOWS_INTEL_MONITOR.md.

Additional user-reported usage: code review with IQ3_XXS, MTP and a context
configured to 128K, with the server remaining up since the previous day.
This is practical usage evidence, not an instrumented soak test; it does not
establish that the conversation filled the entire 128K context window.

## Extra Notes

Ready for review based on the Windows 10 / B70 validation above. Windows 11
and multi-GPU mapping remain untested; results can be added when available.

The IGCL collector is Windows-specific, but the integration also touches
`sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, which is shared with Linux. Linux regression
validation has not been performed. Maintainer or community help checking that
path is welcome; no Linux compatibility validation is claimed here.

Power is GPU chip power, not total board power. PCIe throughput is
unavailable and is not inferred from generation/width. A failed helper requires
server restart after the underlying issue is resolved.

pulls.title: [Engine] HC_Q8: skip the layers' bf16 hyper-connection copies on a layer split too
pulls.author: paltian
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
`STRATA_HC_Q8=1` reads the hyper-connection down/up projections from Q8_0 copies. On a single GPU it also leaves their bf16 copies out of the arena (`add_hc_skip`). On a layer split that skip was gated off (`!multi_gpu` in `generate.cpp`), so each card kept the bf16 copies **and** got the 0.63 GiB of Q8_0 copies on top. HC_Q8 cost VRAM on a split instead of saving it.

With this change a split skips the bf16 copies the same way, and each card gives the freed VRAM to its expert cache. Measured on 0.2.1 (`c093ac26`), UD-Q4_K_XL, 2x RTX 5060 Ti, `--layer-split auto`:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| canonical tensors skipped | 303 | 495 (+192 = the 4x48 `hc_*_down/up` rows) |
| dense weights loaded from the pack | 1416 MiB | 216 MiB |
| expert cache, both cards | 2967 slots (9.15 GiB) | 3370 slots (10.29 GiB) |
| auto split | K=6 (CUDA1 2341 slots) | K=7 (CUDA1 2735 slots) |
| prompt 32k / 120k | 1128 / 1334 tok/s | 1160 / 1380 tok/s (+2.8% / +3.4%) |
| decode 4k / 32k (10 pairs) | 28.2 / 33.1 tok/s | 30.5 / 35.5 tok/s (+7.8% / +7.4%) |

## Related discussion
This is #2427, closed by the 2026-10-19 tracker reset, rebased on 0.2.1 and re-validated. It answers the review there: the default reach via setup (below), a same-config A/B on the split (Validation), and the `native_dense.cpp` comment (fixed). It extends the single-GPU HC_Q8 path (b60aab1b) to a layer split. #704 was a requantization approach and was closed as "not with a layer split".

**Default reach, needs the owner's call:** `setup.py:3190` writes `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` for CUDA UD-* installs. So this change is active by default on every CUDA UD-* layer split, not only for users who set the variable. There the prompt path and the per-token read switch from the bf16 copy to the Q8_0 dequantized into scratch (the read one GPU has used since b60aab1b). The freed VRAM also moves the auto placement (split point, prompt chunk, cache slots). Greedy output on such a split is therefore no longer bit-identical to 0.2.1 (KL below). `STRATA_HC_Q8=0` keeps the full bf16 read as before.

## Approach
One gate in `src/program/generate.cpp`: drop `!multi_gpu` from the `add_hc_skip` condition. Plus a comment fix in `native_dense.cpp`.

The prompt path and the token read already take these rows through `hc_bf16_view`, which dequantizes the Q8_0 into per-device scratch. So a split can drop the bf16 copies exactly as one GPU does. `add_hc_skip` names all `hc_*_down/up` rows. Each stage's loader still limits itself to its own layers through `in_range`, and a skipped row is quantized on the host from the pack file. Kernels are untouched.

What changes on a split: the verify windows already read the Q8_0 copies with and without the patch (`STRATA_HC_Q8=1: 0.63 GiB of Q8_0 hyper-connection projections` in both logs). The prompt path and the per-token read move from the bf16 copy to the Q8_0 through `hc_bf16_view`, as on one GPU.

## Validation
Environment: AMD Ryzen 7 5700X3D (8C/16T), 94 GB RAM, 2x RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120, driver 610.57.04; CUDA0 on a x4 link, probed 3.1 GB/s, CUDA1 x8, 14.3 GB/s), Debian kernel 6.12.107, CUDA build `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;120"`. Patched `3908d716` (= this branch) against stock `c093ac26`, both built with identical options. The server config is my production config (UD-Q4_K_XL, `--spec 4 --mtp`, `--kv int8`, `--prefill auto`, `--layer-split auto`, `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`).

**Passed:**
- `ctest -j 4` on `3908d716`: 66/68 passed. `ple_parity` and `platform_memory_test` (mlock, `ulimit -l`) fail identically on stock.
- A/B speed, docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md protocol: a fresh server per arm and round, alternating order, one discarded warm-up, unique prompt prefix (0 tokens reused), thinking off, temperature 0. Engine timings come from the engine log, TTFT from the client stream. All requests `finish: stop`, no errors.
  - Run 1: 5 rounds, ~4k/32k/120k prompts, 256 tokens. Prompt 4k +1.0% (4/5 pairs faster), 32k +2.8% (5/5, +2.1..+3.2%), 120k +3.4% (5/5, +3.0..+6.2%), TTFT 120k 93.0 → 90.1 s.
  - Run 2: 10 rounds, ~4k/32k prompts, 512 tokens. Prompt 32k +3.3% (10/10, +2.2..+4.1%). Decode 4k +7.8% (10/10, +1.0..+10.4%), 32k +7.4% (10/10, +2.7..+13.1%).
  - The same A/B on 0.2.0 (`e88ee39d`, 5 rounds) gave prompt 32k +2.9%, 120k +3.1%, 5/5 pairs each.
  - The single-pair A/B posted in #2427 (one 91,712-token prompt, a different reserve config) saw prompt and decode unchanged. The runs here have 5-10 pairs per size and see the gain consistently.
- `--batch 2` on the split, two concurrent requests (45k + 49k and 4k + 4k tokens), patched, stock and stock again. Run in the 0.2.1 default (one serial group) and with `--batch-groups 2` (pipelined, 2 groups of 1). All answers complete, correct and coherent, no errors in the engine logs.
- Output check, same prompts on both arms: 1 of 4 cases bit-identical, the others diverge after 85-504 characters with equivalent content. With the split pinned (`layer_split "7"`, `--prefill 4096`) the divergence moves later. Changing only the placement on stock (auto vs pinned) diverges about as early as the patch does, so placement is a large part of the difference, beside the bf16 → Q8_0 read.
- KL on the split (on #2427's branch, 2026-10-15, the same one-line change; not repeated on 0.2.1): `tools/quant_quality.py`, `--layer-split auto`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`, reserve raised so the MTP head fits, the same on both arms. Prompt path (`prompt`/`pcompare`, 20 prompts of 256-1000 tokens, full vocabulary): top-1 100% (20/20), KL mean / median / max 0.00134 / 0.00042 / 0.00781. Decode (`run`/`compare`, teacher-forced, 4,995 positions): top-1 95.10%, KL mean / p99 0.02858 / 0.4818, perplexity 4.062 vs 4.020. The decode figure includes the cache-size effect (1539 → 1932 slots): changing only the cache size moves it about as much (#704: top-1 94.1%, KL 3.4e-2). Draft acceptance unchanged (53.7% vs 54.0%, 3 runs each).

<details><summary>Per-run results</summary>

Run 2, decode tok/s (rounds 0-9):
- 4k stock 28.1 28.5 28.6 28.4 27.8 27.8 30.3 28.0 28.0 29.2
- 4k patched 31.0 29.7 29.7 30.6 30.7 30.2 30.6 30.3 29.6 30.8
- 32k stock 30.0 31.4 32.1 33.7 33.1 32.4 33.6 33.6 33.8 33.1
- 32k patched 32.6 35.5 36.3 36.5 36.6 35.2 36.2 35.6 34.7 34.5

Run 2, prompt 32k tok/s:
- stock 1119.7 1122.8 1124.5 1134.4 1127.3 1135.2 1127.1 1138.7 1125.3 1128.4
- patched 1164.4 1157.8 1159.6 1161.6 1167.0 1160.3 1165.3 1170.9 1171.1 1170.4

Run 1, prompt tok/s (rounds 0-4):
- 4k stock 496.8 490.9 497.2 493.1 498.3 / patched 495.1 507.9 506.2 502.0 501.1
- 32k stock 1126.7 1137.6 1135.3 1124.5 1128.3 / patched 1150.4 1161.6 1171.2 1157.6 1160.2
- 120k stock 1336.4 1317.0 1301.8 1334.3 1338.5 / patched 1379.8 1380.4 1382.3 1378.3 1378.6

Run 1, decode tok/s:
- 4k stock 28.3 29.2 28.9 28.5 28.8 / patched 19.1 30.3 30.4 31.6 29.4
- 32k stock 32.9 31.2 33.3 32.0 31.8 / patched 27.2 35.1 36.1 35.2 35.9
- 120k stock 33.2 34.5 32.3 32.9 33.1 / patched 32.9 38.2 36.7 35.6 37.0
</details>

**Failed:**
None observed. One observation in the decode numbers: 3 of 20 patched servers across the 0.2.0 and 0.2.1 five-round runs decoded 10-35% slower for their whole lifetime (0 of 20 stock). They showed the same cache layout, cache hit rate, draft acceptance and graph captures as the fast ones. The 10-round decode run (10 patched servers) had none, and the cause is not found.

**Not run:**
- The KL check on 0.2.1 itself (the numbers above are from the pre-reset branch, same change). The single-GPU KL of the Q8_0 read is in docs/QUANTS.md (UD-Q4_K_XL: mean 0.0562 → 0.0526, p99 0.925 → 0.716).
- HIP / SYCL / Metal builds (the gate is shared code. gfx12 defaults HC_Q8 on, so a HIP split would be affected the same way).
- A split with `--keep-canonical` (the gate sits inside `!keep_canonical`, unchanged).
- More than two GPUs, and `--batch-mtp`.
- No test in ctest covers this path. I did not add one: the change is a gate on an existing, tested path, and a unit test would only restate it.

## Limits
- The gain comes from the freed VRAM, so it depends on how far the experts already fit: on cards that hold all experts it is smaller.
- Part of the measured gain is the auto split moving (K=6 → 7). That is a consequence of the freed VRAM, not separate from it, but a manual `layer_split` sees only the cache part.
- In batch mode stock itself is not reproducible run to run for one of the four cases (both group modes), so batch output comparisons are only content checks.

pulls.title: serve: GET /metrics gives each request's PCIe expert bytes and its own KV streaming share, and a bandwidth summary
pulls.author: MrKop-git
pulls.body:
## Summary

Observability for the bandwidth view (the link-tier work in #2099), server side only:

- **Per request** — `offloaded` (the DONE line's count of routed experts the GPU read over PCIe) as `pcie_experts_mib` and `pcie_experts_gib_s` over the request's decode time. The blob size is the **mean the engine reports for its own expert cache** (its INFO line's `expert_cache_mib` over `expert_slots`) - a pack's blobs differ in size (a native pack has one size per layer: the default is 1,382,400 B, NVFP4 2.76 MB, IQ2_XS 1.51 MB), so no constant is assumed and the fields are `null` when the engine did not report enough.
- **Per request** (KV streaming on) — `kv_block_reads`, `kv_hit_pct`, `kv_ram_mib`: one request's own share of the engine's per-request `KV streaming:` summary. That summary's counters are **cumulative over the process** (generate.cpp's own comment), so the server reports each line's difference from the previous one and matches it to the request that owns it - the line's own numbers are not a request's share. A request whose engine died before writing its summary keeps `null`; the fields are absent while KV streaming is off.
- **`GET /metrics`** — a `"bandwidth"` object: mean and peak of the 1 s hardware series since the start (`gpu_pcie_rx_mb`, `gpu_pcie_tx_mb`, `disk_read_mb`, `disk_write_mb`; `null` without hardware telemetry).

## What it changes and what it leaves alone

Additive fields in the JSON of `GET /metrics` (the same way `conversation_cache` was added), plus the fields' description in docs/DETAILS.md. **The engine, its DONE line and every answer are untouched** - no flag, no default change.

## How it was checked

- `serve/test_server.py` (`PcieExpertsBytes`): the bytes and GiB/s from the engine's own cache size, and `null` for zero offloaded / no INFO / an older engine's DONE line.
- `serve/test_monitor.py` (`KvStreamingLines`): two cumulative summaries become their differences (1000 then 2000 reads, 0.8 then 1.0 MiB, 80.0% then 87.5% per request), taken once each and attached to the right request rows through `GET /metrics`.
- The full serve suite passes: **789 tests, 11 skipped**.
- Not tested: a live capture against a real engine's `KV streaming:` line (the exact float formatting is pinned by the tests' strings against generate.cpp's `%.2f%% of %llu block reads` / `%.1f MiB`), and multi-slot (`--batch`) attribution - with several slots finishing at once the lines still arrive in finish order and the rows match that order.

Display-only. Observed against `nvidia-smi`'s current link on the box in #2099 (Gen1 / Gen3 x8 / Gen3 x16 tiers): the card reports a Gen3 capability while the link runs below it under the power cap, and the old wording presented the capability as the link.

pulls.title: arm64: build + run Strata on NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121) - rebased onto v0.1.41, IQ3_S validated
pulls.author: ccatzin-zumwalt
pulls.body:
## What this adds

    Builds and runs Strata on the NVIDIA DGX Spark: an aarch64 host (10 Cortex-X925 +
    10 Cortex-A725) with a Blackwell GPU (GB10, sm_121) sharing 128 GB of unified
    memory. Up to now the Spark could only use the community aarch64 port; this branch
    rebases that port onto v0.1.41 (after the upstream history cleanup), fixes the
    drift the new base introduced, and validates it end-to-end with IQ3_S.

    ## Attribution

    This is a rebase of the community aarch64 port — PRs #409 (eelgaev), #901
    (githubhjs) and #1077 (johnlockejrr) — onto v0.1.41 (`fb58e0d`), plus the drift
    fixes the new base required. All original authorship is preserved in the
    history; our own changes are the rebase fixes, marked "DGX Spark GB10 (aarch64)"
    in the affected blocks.

    ## Changes

    - `include/strata/platform/cpu_relax.hpp`: portable `_mm_pause` / `_mm_sfence`
      (yield / `dmb oshst` on aarch64).
    - `src/kernels/cpu/portable.cpp`: scalar + NEON activation quantizer and the BF16
      router dot. The AVX-only kernels are refused on ARM; native packs (IQ3_S
      included) fall through to ggml-cpu's NEON dot products.
    - `CMakeLists.txt`: `STRATA_CPU_X86` guard drops the AVX kernel files on aarch64
      and sets `-ffp-contract=off`; passes `GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH` to ggml-cpu.
    - `setup.py` / `Dockerfile`: aarch64 detection, ggml CPU features read from
      `/proc/cpuinfo` (gcc's `-mcpu=native` finds none on GB10's big.LITTLE part),
      sm_121 auto-selection, and GB10 unified-memory handling (the GPU reports no
      memory of its own; setup counts system RAM).
    - x86-intrinsic guards in graph/session/verify/mtp/pool/expert_layout/generate,
      including the `expert_layout.cpp` / `native_expert.cpp` blocks this base had
      moved.
    - `docs/DGX_SPARK.md`: documents the rebase, the install path, and the IQ3_S
      validation numbers.

    x86 builds are untouched: every change is behind an aarch64 guard or in
    aarch64-only files.

    ## Validation (one DGX Spark, 2026-10-08)

    IQ3_S (GSQ-RCO), 256K context, `--parallel 4`, `--kv int8`, `--mmap-experts`,
    all 24,576 experts in the cache:

    - decode 58.8–66.0 tok/s; prompt 103–111 tok/s on short requests;
    - 127K-token long prompt prefilled at 1512 tok/s, with a needle-in-haystack
      marker retrieved correctly from that depth;
    - MTP accepting 13/14 and 60/79 proposals;
    - above the community reference on Spark (47 tok/s, UD-IQ4_XS).

    ## Testing notes / known gaps

    - Validated on aarch64 only; we could not re-run the x86 build matrix on an
      x86_64 host, though the diff is guard-only for x86.
    - Needle-in-haystack was verified at 127K depth, not the full 256K.
    - A 1h+ soak (docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md) has not been run on this rebase yet.

    Happy to run any of these if you want them before merge.

pulls.title: fix: avoid CUDA OOM during conversation-cache restore
pulls.author: MarsLuay
pulls.body:
Fixes #2408

## Summary

- Add a small, unit-tested `restore_has_headroom` predicate for multi-device cache restores.
- Before restoring an incoming conversation snapshot, sample free VRAM on the primary CUDA device and every layer-split stage.
- If any sampled device is below `--vram-reserve-mib`, return the snapshot to the conversation cache and reread the prompt instead of risking a process-fatal CUDA allocation.
- Preserve the existing behavior when no device sample is available or a CUDA memory query fails; this is a conservative fallback, not a new hard failure path.
- Limit the VRAM headroom admission check to layer-split restores; a single-GPU restore keeps the existing path even when free VRAM is below the sizing reserve.

## Evidence from #2408

A Strata 0.1.40 run on an RTX 3080 Ti + Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB used a two-GPU layer split with a 700 MiB VRAM reserve and a 4096 MiB conversation cache. The log recorded:

```text
strata serve: conversation cache: parked 148167 tokens in 1573.2 ms; parked=2 bytes=3335695744 evictions=8 snapshot_bytes=3097849640
strata serve: conversation cache: restored 148167 tokens (live) in 524.1 ms; parked=2 bytes=2737274704
strata serve: prompt 148295 tokens = 148167 reused + 128 read in 3229 ms (39.6 tok/s), 88 generated in 11781 ms (7.5 tok/s), drafts accepted 54 of 61, 6 checkpoints
CUDA error: out of memory
  current device: 1, in function ggml_cuda_set_device
```

The restore path is an optimization; when the later split stage is already below the configured reserve, rereading the prompt is safer than admitting the snapshot and failing during device residency reconstruction.

## Validation

Passed with the local CPU-only test configuration (the tests cover the shared restore-admission helper):

- `cmake -S C:/tmp/strata-pr-repo -B C:/tmp/strata-pr-repo/build-cpu -G Ninja -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`
- `cmake --build C:/tmp/strata-pr-repo/build-cpu --target split_rules_test conv_cache_test --parallel 4`
- `ctest --test-dir C:/tmp/strata-pr-repo/build-cpu -C Debug --output-on-failure -R "^(split_rules_test|conv_cache_test)$"` — 2/2 passed
- `git diff --check`
- Follow-up regression case: `conv_cache_test` now covers a below-reserve single-GPU restore, which remains eligible.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RX 9070 XT 16 GB on Windows, IQ3_XXS, engine 0.1.44.1
pulls.author: winky1717
pulls.body:
Results-only submission: a community benchmark of Strata 0.1.44.1 on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201) under Windows 11, measured with the built-in benchmark (suite 1, 3 runs per test). No engine code, default or documentation is changed.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201), Windows driver 32.0.31036.15, stock settings (power limit and clocks not recorded)
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 8 cores / 16 threads (AVX-512 present)
- RAM: 46.8 GiB; Windows commit limit about 124 GiB (a 77 GiB page file)
- Storage: the model shards and the prepared pack on an SK hynix PVC10 HFS001TEM9X173N NVMe SSD
- PCIe: Gen5 x16; the engine's own start-up probe measured 54.9 GB/s host->device
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Engine: 0.1.44.1, the prebuilt Windows HIP zip (ROCm 10.2.0a20260930)

## Model and configuration

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, 262144-token context, the install's own settings:

`--kv k8v4 --kv-resident 32768 --resident-experts --vram-reserve-mib 256 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ... --max-context 262144`

Runtime state of the run: 5293 experts in the GPU cache (8.58 GiB of VRAM), 32.32 GiB of experts resident in RAM (pageable).

## Results (medians over 3 runs, the engine's own timings)

| Test | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | First token |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| short chat, 100 tokens out | - | 65.7 (60.5-79.3) | 0.39 s |
| 4K fresh prompt | 800.5 (799.4-808.5) | - | 5.04 s |
| 16K fresh prompt | 921.1 (920.6-926.5) | - | 17.46 s |
| agent session, follow-up turns | - | 68.8 (40.0-87.3) | 4.67 s |

Conversation-cache hit over the agent session's follow-up turns: 68.7%.

## Second folder: a `--kv-resident` A/B on the same machine

`2026-10-14-community-rx-9070-xt-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs-2/` is the same machine, day and configuration with `--kv-resident 32768` removed. Prompt throughput 1.9-2.5% lower and first-token time 2.0-2.5% higher (both with non-overlapping run-to-run ranges); the decode medians are lower too (chat -4.4%, agent -6.8%) but with overlapping ranges, so those are directional only. With streaming the engine also skipped 22% fewer expert contributions (`route tail skip`), so it is the better of the two on both counts. The two folders are submitted together because they differ in exactly one flag.

## Limitations

- Speed only: no correctness, recall or needle check was run.
- One machine, one engine session, the desktop in normal use; no clock or power capture, and nothing was isolated or pinned.
- The reported commit is a local branch: upstream `main` at `296b59d2` plus two local patches (a Simplified Chinese UI translation and the Windows AMD telemetry of PRs #1434/#1152). Neither touches the engine or the model path, so the numbers are the engine's own.
