pulls.title: Add opt-in usage, output history and authenticated remote dashboard
pulls.author: QuickkApps
pulls.body:
## Summary
Updates the existing contribution with persistent output History, source labels, app-bar Average TPS, authenticated remote-dashboard sharing, startup/recovery improvements, and an illustrated setup guide. The features are opt-in; the ordinary model, sampling, thinking budget and client output limits are not changed.

**[Complete setup and operation guide](https://github.com/QuickkApps/Strata/blob/7883e5668cb668542b23abd8798b325688cb211c/docs/LOCAL_FEATURES.md)**

The guide covers installation prerequisites, configuration, OpenAI/Anthropic editor URLs, Claude Code, authentication, Tailscale activation, automatic startup, recovery, shutdown, credential rotation, accounting definitions, storage/privacy, troubleshooting, and reproducible examples.

## What changed
- Persistent Usage ledger and daily/all-time views: prompt/output/cached/total tokens, cached hit percentage, weighted average and live/last decode rate, active time, process CPU time, GPU energy, average GPU power, configurable API-equivalent value, electricity cost and estimated savings.
- Shared header Average TPS immediately after Cached tokens; responsive header sizing prevents the figures from overlapping content on mobile.
- Opt-in SQLite output History across Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses, streaming or not. Output, Thinking, Tools and Details panes; search, status filtering, pagination, copy and full-text download.
- History source labels use explicit app headers or recognized product User-Agents, otherwise Unknown. Labels are self-reported, not authentication. History displays the actual serving model, while Details preserves client aliases as requested_model; API responses remain unchanged.
- Authenticated loopback Node gateway with optional administrative dashboard sharing over Tailscale Funnel. API and dashboard have separate connection pools; Basic-auth browser POSTs require the same origin.
- Per-request credential loading, stale owned-gateway revision checks, serialized startup and a supervised parent-bound watchdog. Existing fail-closed ownership checks for the whole HTTPS port and process/config paths are retained.
- Optional Claude Code profile/launcher without modifying global settings automatically. Claude-named compatibility aliases still run the loaded Strata model; the example requests 132,000 combined output tokens, with no separate thinking budget. Clients may clamp this value.
- Existing experimental unlimited_output continuation remains a separate opt-in in this branch. It is not enabled by the guide or default configuration and is not infinite model memory.

No native engine/kernel or frontend parser source is changed. New changes were ported selectively rather than replacing newer upstream image, vision, model-family or recovery behavior with an older installed copy.

## Enable Explicitly
Merge only the desired keys into an existing model configuration, preserving engine paths and arguments, then restart:
```json
{
  "usage_tracker": true,
  "output_history": true,
  "remote_access": true
}
```

Remote startup currently requires Windows, Node.js, signed-in Tailscale with Funnel enabled, and a Strata-engine server on loopback port 8080. Cloning alone does not publish anything. The gateway generates credentials in the current user's protected local application-data directory.

Dashboard sharing is separately disabled by default. To enable it, merge exposeDashboard: true into the private gateway configuration and rerun the helper. Browser login is username strata, password the generated gateway key. The contribution requires API authentication and does not include a public no-key mode.

OpenAI editor base URLs end in /v1; Anthropic/Claude Code base URLs use the root, without /v1. See the guide for exact steps and private credential handling.

## Example Screens
Actual dashboard components rendered with synthetic data, fixed January sample dates and neutral UTC example metadata. These are UI examples, not benchmarks. No real conversations, device hostname, credentials or runtime databases are included.

### Monitor Dashboard
![Monitor dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuickkApps/Strata/7883e5668cb668542b23abd8798b325688cb211c/docs/media/dashboard-example.jpg)

### Usage
![Usage statistics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuickkApps/Strata/7883e5668cb668542b23abd8798b325688cb211c/docs/media/usage-example.jpg)

### History
![History with app source and actual model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuickkApps/Strata/7883e5668cb668542b23abd8798b325688cb211c/docs/media/history-example.jpg)

The guide includes an additional Usage overview. Reproduce the images locally with:
```shell
python tools/preview_dashboard.py --port 8096 --seconds 300
```
The preview binds loopback only, uses no GPU/Tailscale/user files and cleans its temporary data on exit.

## Accounting And Privacy Limits
- Cached tokens are part of prompt tokens, not additional total tokens. Average decode is recorded decoded tokens / recorded decode seconds, excluding prefill, idle, inserted control tokens and untimed historical work.
- GPU energy uses cumulative board-energy deltas where available and sampled-power integration otherwise, only during active intervals. Missing measurements retain coverage gaps. This is whole-board energy, not exact per-model or whole-PC electricity; other GPU programs can contribute.
- Prices, tariffs and exchange rates are manual benchmarks. Editing them revalues history; this is not a bill or earnings ledger.
- History is plaintext with no automatic retention limit. It saves emitted output/thinking/tool arguments and whitelisted metadata, not complete input prompts or raw request headers. Generated content can still contain sensitive information. Bounded background writes can report incomplete recording without failing inference.
- Dashboard credentials grant trusted administrative access, including History/config/model controls and configured MCP capabilities. API keys also retain upstream trusted-client capabilities. The watchdog cannot fix power/network outages, forced sleep, expired credentials or editor incompatibility.
- No personal model configuration, keys, public hostname, usage/history data, audit artifacts, models, native binaries or virtual environment is included. The separate running installation was left unchanged.

## Verification
- Full server suite: **846 tests, OK (15 environment-dependent skips)**.
- Focused history/usage/remote checks: 53 tests passed. The final gateway and deferred-fetch History UI rerun passed 7 tests, covering auth, key rotation, fail-closed config, dashboard gating, source-header forwarding and cross-site Basic-auth rejection.
- Synthetic preview checks passed for fixed dates/UTC metadata, daily totals, weighted TPS and saved examples. Desktop and 390-pixel mobile browser checks passed after the header-overlap correction.
- Ruff correctness checks pass on touched Python modules; B023/F401 checks pass on helper/history/test modules. Six existing server B023 closure warnings remain unchanged from the previous commit.
- JavaScript syntax and focused ESLint pass; CSS syntax/property/color checks pass. All PowerShell helpers parse under Windows PowerShell. PSScriptAnalyzer was unavailable for this update, so no new analyzer claim is made.
- Read-only publication/security review found no outstanding blocker after addressing browser-origin checks and screenshot time-zone privacy.
- No CUDA/HIP/SYCL build, full PC reboot, real Funnel reconfiguration, performance/quality benchmark or actual other-device editor workflow was performed for this PR update. Tests do not modify the running model or public tunnel.

Related discussions: #1876, #1925, #2204, #2370. Their unmerged implementations are not silently combined with this ledger.

pulls.title: `--vram-elastic` with `--kv-grow`: VRAM takes its chunks where the K/V grows into (resubmits #2201)
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
## Title
`--vram-elastic` with `--kv-grow`: VRAM takes its chunks where the K/V grows into (resubmits #2201)

Issue: follows up #2201 (held for #2189; "send it together with the new #2189"). Builds on #2398 for HIP.

## Summary

Today the two switches exclude each other. With `--vram-elastic` the engine says `--kv-grow is off` and puts the whole
K/V in VRAM, because #533's cache is cut into segments while `--kv-grow` needs one VMM range of chunks. On an R9700
with a 262K context that costs ~1,400 cache slots, more VRAM than a game or an image encoder would borrow. This PR lets
both switches run together.

This branch is #2398 plus one commit; only the last commit is this change. It does not depend on #2398 on CUDA, and
once #2398 is in, it rebases onto main with no conflict in the code.

## What changed

`src/program/generate.cpp`:
- With both switches, the cache keeps `--kv-grow`'s arena (one range of 2 MiB chunks). `VRAM` works on the region the
  K/V grows into: slots `[lo, top)`, just below the prompt path's loan.
- **Shrink:** the same eviction the K/V's growth uses (hotter experts there move into the coldest slots of the loan
  region first). It is now `kvg_take`, split out of `kvg_ensure` unchanged; the chunks go to the driver instead of to
  the K/V.
- **Grow:** new chunks are mapped there, and those slots are refilled with the profile's hottest experts that the GPU
  does not hold. This is now `kvg_give_back`, split out of `kvg_trim` unchanged. So after a grow the cache holds what a
  K/V trim would leave, not necessarily the experts the shrink took (the segments put the same ones back). The docs say
  so.
- The prompt path's loan and chunk are not touched. While the cache is shrunk, the K/V keeps growing from the cache's
  slots, not from the reserve.
- A small counter keeps track of the chunks given to the driver. It is settled against the arena's empty places,
  because the K/V's first cells are new VRAM, and a trim below them maps those chunks into the arena too. Without that,
  the count drifted by ~100 MiB and a grow reported "no VRAM" for chunks that had no place.

`docs/DETAILS.md`, `docs/VRAM_ELASTIC.md`: the new "With `--kv-grow`" section. The image-encoder section (#2196) no
longer says that `--vram-elastic` turns `--kv-grow` off.

What it leaves alone: either switch alone (`kvg_ensure` and `kvg_trim` do the same steps through the two helpers;
without `--kv-grow`, `VRAM` keeps the segments). The default path does not reach any of it.

## Extra Notes

**How it was checked**

On v0.1.44 (this branch: #2398 + this commit; R9700 32 GB, ROCm 7.14.1, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, every expert in RAM, 262K
context, `--kv-grow --vram-elastic` through `serve.server`):
- Full HIP ctest: 111 of 112. The failure is `ple_parity`, which needs the Q2_0 fixture.
- Live:
  - The cache was 10,940 slots (24.68 GiB), with `elastic K/V: 16384 of 262144 cells in VRAM`.
  - `VRAM 4000` left 4,000 MiB free (9,427 slots holding experts).
  - A 30.6K-token prompt with a needle was answered right while the cache was shrunk; the K/V grew from the cache's
    slots.
  - `VRAM 0` brought back 10,848 slots; the K/V keeps the rest for its cells.
- With setup's ROCm 7.10 wheels, #2398's check turns both switches off, the line says why, and the engine served
  normally.
- CUDA: builds and links with nvcc 13.4.92, sm_120, 0 errors. Not run on an NVIDIA GPU.
- SYCL: `sycl/` builds with oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1, 0 errors (the port has its own `generate.cpp`; this change does not
  reach it).

Measured before the rebase (0.1.43.1 + #2189, the same box), with a needle at 3/5 of each prompt and a 320-token answer:

| step | VRAM call | slots holding experts (of 10,865) | free | needle / decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 78K prompt, whole cache | - | 10,492 (the K/V took 373) | - | ok / 96.6 tok/s |
| `reserve 4000` | 106 ms | 8,872 | 4,000 MiB | - |
| 78K prompt (the K/V grows again while shrunk) | - | - | - | ok / 92.0 |
| `reserve 8000` | 113 ms | 7,094 | 8,000 MiB | - |
| 156K prompt (the K/V to 2.13 GiB) | - | - | - | ok / 87.8 |
| `reserve 0` | 418 ms | 10,865 | 453 MiB | - |
| 78K prompt, then a short one (the K/V trims) | - | - | - | ok / 96.1 |
| `reserve 4000`, `reserve 0` | 101 ms, 199 ms | 9,281, 10,865 | 4,001, 453 MiB | - |

- The driver's own counter followed: 31.5 GiB, then 30.5 at `reserve 4000`, 28.0 after the 78K prompt, 24.1 at
  `reserve 8000` with the 156K K/V, and back to 31.4.
- `--kv-grow` alone: every needle was found, and the K/V grew and trimmed as before.
- With the elastic image encoder (#2196, now in 0.1.44) on the same card:
  - the first picture made `VRAM` keep 2 GiB free (52 ms), and the encoder started in 3.1 s;
  - a 156K prompt grew the K/V to 163,840 cells while the encoder held its share (needle found);
  - after 60 s without a picture the encoder stopped, and the cache was whole again.

**Not tested:** NVIDIA at run time, Windows, more than one shrink-grow cycle while the K/V holds a parked conversation.

pulls.title: HIP: virtual memory for `--kv-grow` and `--vram-elastic`, on only where a start-up check passes (resubmits #2189)
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
## Title
HIP: virtual memory for `--kv-grow` and `--vram-elastic`, on only where a start-up check passes (resubmits #2189)

Issue: follows up #2189 (closed: "a check at start that turns HIP's virtual memory on only where it works"); #533;
#1475's setup now skips for the right reason.

## Summary

#2189 rebased on v0.1.44, plus a check at the first use on each GPU. HIP's virtual memory stays on only where the
runtime shows that it works. Everywhere else, `--kv-grow` and `--vram-elastic` stay off, the log says why, and the
engine runs on with the cache in one allocation. With setup's ROCm 7.10.0a20251120 wheels on an R9700 the check fails
(granularity 4 KiB). With ROCm 7.14.1 it passes.

The check also fixes a bug #2189 had on every ROCm: on Linux, ROCm keeps one open file per physical allocation. A 24 GiB
`--kv-grow` arena of 2 MiB chunks needs ~12,500 open files, so under the usual soft limit of 1,024 the cache could not
be mapped at any size.

#2399 (`--vram-elastic` with `--kv-grow`, the resubmitted #2201) is opened at the same time and builds on this one.

## What changed

Commit 1: #2189 rebased, unchanged.
- `src/core/vmm.cpp` is the one place that talks to the driver's virtual memory, for both backends (CUDA's driver API,
  HIP's `hipMem*`).
- `expert_cache.cpp`'s segments go through it.
- The only conflict was the new `STRATA_GPU_METAL` guard: Metal now sits next to gfx906 (no backend).

Commit 2: the check.
- `src/core/vmm.cpp`: a per-device verdict, decided once, at the first use. On HIP it requires:
  - a recommended allocation granularity of 2 MiB or more;
  - 32 MiB mapped in chunks of that size to move `hipMemGetInfo`'s free memory down by about that much, and back up once
    they are unmapped and released (the addresses stay reserved). One retry, in case another program moves the counter
    at the same moment;
  - on Linux, enough open files for every chunk of the card. The soft limit is raised as far as the hard limit allows,
    and the log says so. The engine uses no `select()`, the one thing a higher limit could break.

  CUDA decides as before (entry points and the device attribute), without the measurement.
- `include/strata/core/vmm.hpp`: `vmm_off_reason()`, which says what the check saw and names the HIP runtime.
  `vmm_available()` / `vmm_device_supported()` answer with the verdict.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the reason goes into `--kv-grow is off (...; no GPU virtual memory: <reason>)` and
  `--vram-elastic is off: <reason>`.
- `src/core/expert_cache.cpp`: the segmented cache's open error carries the reason.

  Before, `--vram-elastic` on a driver without virtual memory failed the start. Now it falls back like the other cases,
  on CUDA too.
- `tests/core/vmm_test.cpp`:
  - when the GPU is "off", there is always a reason (printed with the skip);
  - on HIP/Linux: the soft limit covers the card, and a range of 1,100 chunks maps whole.
- `docs/VRAM_ELASTIC.md`, `docs/DETAILS.md`: the check, the open files, and what the two ROCm versions do.

What it leaves alone:
- The default path. Without `--kv-grow` / `--vram-elastic`, nothing calls the new code (both callers short-circuit on
  the switch).
- The CUDA behaviour of both switches.
- The gfx906 and Metal builds (no virtual memory).
- SYCL: the port keeps its own `vmm.cpp`, `expert_cache.cpp` and `generate.cpp`. From this change it compiles only the
  two headers: `vmm.hpp` gains declarations that nothing in `sycl/` calls, and `expert_cache.hpp` changes only a
  comment.
- Setup and the server.

## Extra Notes

**How it was checked.** Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201), Linux 6.8, amdgpu 6.19.14. Both ROCm versions ran on the
same machine with the same build flags (`-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1201 -DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON
-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`). Setup's wheels were installed from the gfx120X-all index into a venv and built with setup's
`--rocm-path` / `--rocm-device-lib-path` flags. Live runs used Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, every expert in RAM, a 262K context,
`--kv-grow` and `"vram_elastic": true` through `serve.server`, started from a shell with the default open-file limit
(soft 1,024).

*ROCm 7.10.0a20251120 (HIP runtime 7.2.53210):*
- `vmm_test`: `no GPU virtual memory here (the recommended allocation granularity is 4 KiB, not 2 MiB or more (HIP
  runtime 7.2.53210)) - skipped`. `expert_cache_segmented_test` skips (77) with the same reason. Before, both failed.
  This is #1475's setup.
- Full ctest: 111 of 112. The failure is `ple_parity` (it needs the Q2_0 fixture, as on 7.14.1). In one of two runs,
  `hip_prefill_native_batch` also segfaulted once; it links only the kernels, not `vmm.cpp`, and it passed in the other
  run.
- Live: `--kv-grow is off (...; no GPU virtual memory: the recommended allocation granularity is 4 KiB, not 2 MiB or
  more (HIP runtime 7.2.53210))` and `--vram-elastic is off: <the same>`. The cache was 9,578 slots (21.58 GiB) in one
  allocation. Answers were normal, and `POST /v1/vram` got the usual 400.
- Because the granularity check fails first, the release part never ran on 7.10. The "freed 0 bytes" you saw was not
  measured here.

*ROCm 7.14.1 (HIP runtime 7.14.60850):*
- Full ctest: 111 of 112 (`ple_parity`, as above). `vmm_test` and `expert_cache_segmented_test` pass.
- Live, with this PR's segments (`--kv-grow` is off next to `--vram-elastic` here, as on v0.1.44): `VRAM 4000` left
  3,662 MiB free. A 30.6K-token prompt with a needle was answered right while the cache was shrunk. `VRAM 0` brought
  back all 9,578 slots.
- The open-file limit: the log says `open-file limit 1024 -> 17336`. Without that raise, a fresh process mapped 1,017
  chunks and then `hipMemCreate` failed; the free VRAM came back whole after each failed attempt. Under
  `ulimit -Hn 4096` (with PR B's build, the same check): `--vram-elastic is off: ROCm keeps an open file per 2 MiB chunk: 17336 needed, and the open-file
  limit is 4096 (hard 4096; ...)`, and the engine served with one allocation.
- Mutation: with the check leaving its chunks unreleased, the GPU is turned off with `the free VRAM fell by 32 MiB for
  32 MiB mapped and rose by 0 MiB after its release`, and both tests skip.
- The default path, against v0.1.44 on the same box: both engines built the same way, run with the default flags (no
  `--kv-grow`, no `--vram-elastic`), greedy, 256 tokens, two prompts, in the order v0.1.44, this, v0.1.44, this. The
  answers were byte-identical: one output hash per prompt across all four runs, with decode 60.1 / 60.1 / 60.1 / 59.9
  and 70.8 / 70.7 / 70.8 / 70.7 tok/s. No line about virtual memory or open files appeared.

*Other backends:*
- CUDA: builds and links with nvcc 13.4.92, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`, 0 errors, and no warnings in the changed
  files. Not run on an NVIDIA GPU (there is none here).
- SYCL: the whole `sycl/` project (engine and parity tests, 217 targets) builds with oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1 on both
  branches, 0 errors, and no warnings from the two headers. Not run: there is no Intel GPU here.
- `serve.test_vram` and `serve.test_vision_elastic` pass (14 tests).

**Not tested:** NVIDIA at run time; Windows (HIP keeps `--vram-elastic` off there, and `--kv-grow` goes through the same
check, without the open-file part); the gfx906 build; other RDNA cards; ROCm versions between 7.10 and 7.14.1.

pulls.title: serve: allow JSON response_format with tools on /v1/chat/completions
pulls.author: Xantier
pulls.body:
Issue: none. Follows #782, and picks up the structured-output part of #763, which closed when main was force-pushed.

## Summary

POST /v1/chat/completions returned 400 structured response_format with tools/MCP is not supported for any request that sent both tools and a JSON response_format. #782 made /v1/responses accept this combination. This PR applies the same approach to the chat route: a turn that calls a tool passes through unchanged, and the turn that ends in text is validated against the schema as before.

Measured with tool-eval-bench 2.8.1.dev1 (69 scenarios, seed 42, 3 trials each) on an RX 9070 16 GB, Ryzen 5 3600 and 64GB of DDR4-2400, running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S on engine 0.1.43.1 with reasoning_effort: low:

| Build | Mean points (3 trials) | TC-65, TC-66, TC-67, TC-69 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 128.3 / 138 | partial in every trial (400 on the turn after the tool result) |
| this PR | 131.3 / 138 | pass in every trial, no 400s |

## What changed

- serve/server.py, _openai: prepare_format gets with_tools=bool(tools), so the system directive says the schema is for the final answer only. This is the directive #782 added. The 400 now applies only to strata_mcp.
- serve/server.py, structured_chunks: the first chunk with tool_calls releases what was held and streams the rest unchecked. A turn without a tool call is buffered and validated exactly as before.
- serve/test_structured.py: the assertion that expected 400 for tools now covers MCP only. New tests cover a tool call passing through (streamed and non-streamed), a valid final answer with tools, and a final answer that breaks the schema (502 structured_output_failed).
- docs/DETAILS.md: describes the tools behaviour in place of "refused explicitly".

Left alone: requests without response_format, and JSON formats without tools, take the same path as before, and the existing tests pass unchanged. MCP with a JSON format is still refused, because run_with_mcp runs tool rounds inside one request, so there is no single final turn to validate.

## Extra Notes

- Tests on this branch (v0.1.44.1 base, Python 3.12, jsonschema 4.26.0): serve.test_structured 13, serve.test_responses 40 and serve.test_server 314, all OK.
- This does not conflict with #1328, which leaves the chat route's 400 unchanged. If there is a reason to keep the chat route stricter than /v1/responses, I'd like to hear it.

pulls.title: setup: Alchemist on xe gets UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 (A770 expert cache 1,906 -> 4,540 slots, decode +45%)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545, #1606 (Arc A770)

## Summary
On an Arc A770 16 GB under `xe`, Level Zero refuses a single device allocation above DG2's `max_mem_alloc_size` (~4 GiB) unless `UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1`. `--expert-cache auto` then falls back to what fits under it: **1,906 slots (3.64 GiB) instead of 4,540 (8.64 GiB)**, and decode drops by a third. Nothing in setup, `strata-sycl.sh` or the docs sets the variable today. This makes setup write it into an Alchemist card's config on `xe` (next to the FP64-emulation variables). The JIT build's `-ze-opt-greater-than-4GB-buffer-required` already keeps the kernels correct past 4 GiB, which is what makes the bigger arena safe.

## What changed
- `sycl/setup_intel.py` (`to_sycl`): `env["UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS"] = "1"` for an Alchemist card on `xe`. i915 (the A750) and the B-series are unchanged.
- `tools/test_setup_sycl.py`: Alchemist on `xe` gets it; a B-series card and an A750 on i915 do not. `python tools/test_setup_sycl.py`: 19 tests OK.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: one sentence in the ">4 GiB" bullet.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM, 2026-10-14. Same binary (`v0.1.44.1` + #2207 + #2215), Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts --expert-cache auto --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --vram-reserve-mib 1200 --prefill-borrow --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1 STRATA_PF_XMX=2`, without and with the variable:

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| expert cache | 1,906 slots, 3.64 GiB | 4,540 slots, 8.64 GiB |
| 8K prompt | 237.9, 363.9 tok/s (2 chunks) | 509.2, 547.1, 559.8 tok/s (1 chunk) |
| 8K decode | 16.51, 17.46 tok/s (hits 0.52) | 23.97, 26.75, 27.62 tok/s (hits 0.76) |
| 2K decode | 14.67, 14.71 tok/s (hits 0.37) | 23.20, 25.95 tok/s (hits 0.61) |

The generated text is a correct answer in both (decoded and read). The token ids differ between the two because the cache holds different experts (the CPU-vs-GPU rounding). For contrast, our 2026-10-08 fork build, from before #1602 landed, answered `!!!!` (token 0) with the variable set: the bigger arena needs the 64-bit-address build.

With setup's own `--stream-experts` config this card hit the same limit on Monday (`ExpertCache: cudaMalloc(4.86 GiB) failed ... trying a smaller expert cache: 1891 slots`).

Not tested: an A770 on i915 (#1606), which likely has the same limit but is left alone here; a Docker (`strata-sycl.sh`) run (the wrapper passes `UR_*` through).

pulls.title: metal: build supports_metal4() without the macOS 26 SDK
pulls.author: nullspeech
pulls.body:
## What breaks

`mtl_rt.mm`'s `supports_metal4()` names `MTLGPUFamilyMetal4`, which is declared only in the macOS 26 SDK headers. On a Mac still on macOS 15 the only SDK you can get is 15.x, so the Metal engine does not compile at all — and there is no prebuilt Mac engine in the release assets, so this is the first wall a macOS 15 user hits, before anything runtime-related.

## Fix

Declare the same numeric family and cast it at the single call site. `5002` is what the repo's own vendored metal-cpp already uses (`third_party/metal-cpp/Metal/MTLDevice.hpp:193`: `GPUFamilyMetal4 = 5002`), and the `@available(macOS 26.0, *)` gate is untouched, so a 26-SDK build emits the identical call and cannot change behaviour there.

```
metal/src/mtl_rt.mm | 5 ++++-
```

## Measured (this machine)

M2 Max, 96 GB, macOS 15.8, engine at `main` (296b59d2, 0.1.44.1), IQ3_S:

- engine compiles and starts, serves 131072-context requests;
- prompt read 58-59 tok/s, decode 31-40 tok/s, MTP drafts ~85% accepted;
- `gdn_parity` prints `max 512 threads per threadgroup` and passes for `GDN_NTOK 1..8` (that's the #2323 fix, verified here).

## Scope, so nobody reads too much into it

This only unblocks the **C++ build**. It does not make MPP runtime available on macOS 15: `dense_mm.metal`, `moe_mm.metal`, `qsa_prompt.metal`, `prompt.metal` and `mm_bench.metal` include `<MetalPerformancePrimitives/...>` unguarded, and `Context::compile()` answers a failed shader compile with `std::exit(3)`. A macOS 15 Mac therefore still has to run `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT=window` with `COOP_K4=0`. The natural follow-up is `__has_include` on that header plus a GPU-family probe, so window mode becomes the engine's own choice rather than something the user has to know about — happy to write that up if you want it here rather than in #2323.

Context: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2323#issuecomment-6158924728

pulls.title: planner: rank auto layer splits for prompt pipelines
pulls.author: MarsLuay
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Add `--layer-split-objective interactive|prompt|decode` for `--layer-split auto`.
- Make the default `interactive` objective first select the legacy serial-decode optimum, then optimize the slowest prompt-pipeline stage only among placements whose predicted serial decode cost does not regress.
- Keep `prompt` as an explicit unconstrained prompt-throughput priority and `decode` as the serial stage-sum ranking.
- Preserve explicit layer splits unchanged and apply the same objective to four-stage candidate scoring.

This addresses the heterogeneous-GPU planner mismatch where maximizing cache coverage or prompt throughput can select a decode-slow split. The planner remains model-based and does not benchmark at startup. The decode guard is a prediction constraint, not a universal hardware guarantee.

Tracking issue: #2393

Related: #2052, #509, #2085

## Measured evidence

These are actual same-host measurements from 2026-10-14 using Strata **0.1.40** (version-scoped evidence, not a claim about current 0.1.44 throughput): RTX 3080 Ti + Tesla V100, SC117 IQ3_S, 262,144 context, 259,841-token prompt, `int8`, 32K KV resident, speculative decoding 4, and no prompt reuse.

| planner/config | prompt time | prompt rate | decode | cache hit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Before:** `--layer-split auto` | 228.6 s | 1,136.7 tok/s | 31.4 tok/s | 90.9% |
| **Reference:** explicit balanced `--layer-split 24` | **169.2 s** | **1,535.4 tok/s** | **28.7 tok/s** | 78.1% |

The balanced split reduced prompt time by 26.0% and improved prompt throughput by 35.1%, despite its lower cache-hit percentage. These measurements motivate the prompt objective; they are not post-PR binary results.

A fresh 128K request was also run against the already-running **0.1.40** runtime with explicit balanced `--layer-split 24`: 124,631 prompt tokens, 76.91 s prompt time, 1,620.5 prompt tok/s, 7.86 s decode, 32.6 decode tok/s, 74.5% cache hit, no prompt reuse. This is version-scoped runtime remeasurement only; it does not validate this unbuilt PR head.

## Validation

- `cmake --build build-pr --config Debug --target split_rules_test`
- `ctest --test-dir build-pr -C Debug --output-on-failure -R '^(split_rules_test|share_rules_test|host_limits_test|arch_defaults_test|batch_read_test|batch_groups_test|split_ring_test|draft_kv_plan_test|coupled_draft_test|controller_test|message_boundary_test|conv_cache_test)$'` — 12/12 passed
- `git diff --check`

pulls.title: Batch slots keep a conversation's turn checkpoints across slot -> solo -> slot moves (#1906)
pulls.author: davidbhoward
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #1906

## Summary
With `"parallel": 2` on a layer split (pipelined groups of one slot) and thinking on, most turns of a two-agent session read their whole history again. Two causes, both small:

1. A request that leaves its slot for the solo path and comes back (the hand-back to the solo path when a slot is left alone) loses the slot's turn checkpoints. The client's next turn comes back without the reply's thinking, so it only matches up to that turn boundary, finds no checkpoint, and reads from token 0.
2. `pick_slot` skips the held-prefix choice whenever groups are pipelined (`if gs:`), so the returning request can be admitted over the other conversation's slot. Groups of one slot have no pad rows and keep their conversation, so this now only applies to `gs > 1`, and a slot that matches up to its last turn boundary counts as holding the conversation.

## What changed
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: when a slot gives back all it holds, its checkpoints move into the main session's chain with the conversation (they stay valid, the main session holds the same tokens).
- `serve/server.py`: `if gs:` -> `if gs > 1:`, and `held_prefix` also counts a common start that covers at least half of what the slot holds.

Nothing else. Output is unchanged: this only decides which cached state a turn continues from.

## Extra Notes
This PR was written and posted by Claude (an AI assistant), at the request of the fork's owner, @davidbhoward.

Measured on 2x RTX 3090, layer split 25, IQ3_S, 262144, `"parallel": 2`, on `296b59d2` with and without this change. Two clients with `reasoning_effort: low`, 6 turns each on a ~31K history, history sent back without the thinking, two runs each:

| | turns that read the whole history (2 expected) | time reading |
|---|---|---|
| main | 10, 10 | 95 s, 95 s |
| this change | 2, 2 | 27 s, 28 s |

At 235-245K histories the same miss costs about 57 s per turn. Built and tested on CUDA only; the change is host code, but I did not build HIP or SYCL. The reproduction script is small and I can attach it if useful.

pulls.title: setup: put the CUDA runtime DLLs (bin\x64) on the image job's search path on Windows
pulls.author: hogtinbao
pulls.body:
Fixes #2381.

## The bug

`setup.py`'s `build_image_engine` recorded `lib_dirs` for a Windows CUDA build as `<CUDA_ROOT>\bin`:

```python
lib_dirs = [str(root / "bin")] if WIN else [str(d) for d in (root / "lib64", root / "lib") if d.is_dir()]
```

CUDA 12 moved the runtime libraries to `<CUDA_ROOT>\bin\x64`; `bin` keeps only the tools (`nvcc.exe`, `ptxas.exe`, `nvlink.exe`, ...). On a CUDA 13.0.2 install:

```
<CUDA_ROOT>\bin\*.dll        0 files
<CUDA_ROOT>\bin\x64\*.dll   27 files   (cublas64_13.dll, cublasLt64_13.dll, cudart64_13.dll, ...)
```

`tools/image/install.py` stores that list in the run config (`images.lib_dirs`), and `serve/images.py` / `serve/server.py` prepend it to the child's `PATH`. So `sd-cli.exe` cannot resolve `cublas64_13.dll`, exits with `3221225781` (`0xC0000135`, `STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND`), and the API answers:

```
HTTP 500 {"error": {"type": "server_error", "code": "image_generation_failed",
                    "message": "sd-cli exited with code 3221225781; the end of its log:\n"}}
```

Anyone who installs CUDA on Windows and enables image generation hits this; nothing else in the build or the three model files is at fault.

## The fix

```python
lib_dirs = ([str(d) for d in (root / "bin" / "x64", root / "bin") if d.is_dir()] if WIN
            else [str(d) for d in (root / "lib64", root / "lib") if d.is_dir()])
```

`bin\x64` first, `bin` second, so CUDA 11 (DLLs in `bin`), CUDA 12/13 (`bin\x64`), and any layout that has both are covered. The Linux branch is untouched.

## Verification

- On a real CUDA 13.0.2 root the new expression returns `[<CUDA>\bin\x64, <CUDA>\bin]` with `cublas64_13.dll` present in the first entry, where the old expression returned only `<CUDA>\bin` (0 DLLs in it).
- `python -m unittest tools.test_qimage` → 14 tests OK; `python -m unittest serve.test_images` → 19 tests OK.
- End to end on Windows 11 / RTX 5070 Ti 12 GB / CUDA 13.0.2 / `Q6_K`, with `images.lib_dirs` hand-patched the same way: `POST /v1/images/generations` renders 512×512 in ~21 s and 1024×1024 in ~26 s.

pulls.title: setup: calibrate a dual config whose gpu is the string 0,1
pulls.author: MEsfits
pulls.body:
Fixes #2378.

`hardware_key()` passed the config's raw `"gpu"` value to `gpu_info()`, which matches a single card by number — so `./setup.sh --calibrate` on a dual config with `"gpu": "0,1"` ran every measurement round, then died with `there is no GPU 0,1` at the save step (and left tier-measurement flags half-written into the user's file).

- New `gpu_sel()` normalizes `0`, `[0, 2]` and `"0,2"` (the string form `serve` already splits); `hardware_key()` uses it for the string case, keeping `None` flowing to `hip_config_cards` where it means "default card".
- `recommend_remote_expert_opt()` uses it too instead of silently skipping string-form duals with a helper cache.
- Regression test `test_nvidia_string_dual_keys_like_the_list` in `CalibrationKey`.

Verified: string `"0,1"` yields the identical key as `[0, 1]`; single-int, single-string, and missing-key forms unchanged; all 36 `test_setup_amd.py` tests pass; full `test_setup_*.py` (583 tests) shows only the same 10 pre-existing environment failures as unmodified code (stash A/B).

Tested live on 2x RTX 3090 (24GB): the previously crashing save path now completes.

pulls.title: setup: give the --families probe the engine's ROCm DLLs on PATH (#2372)
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
Closes #2372.

A ready-made Windows HIP engine keeps `hipblas.dll` and `libhipblaslt.dll` in `rocm/bin` beside it, and its loader asks for them **before `main`**. `engine_families()` launched `strata.exe --families` with no environment, so on Windows both DLLs were reported missing, `--families` printed nothing, and setup read that as "this engine does not run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B yet" — while the engine was already current. The report's diagnosis, and the shape of the fix.

`hip_devices()` already builds that PATH for the device probe (`hip_lib_dirs(eng)` prepended to the inherited `PATH`); the families probe now gets the same one.

## Testing

New `tools/test_setup_engine_families.py` — hermetic (a temporary engine directory with a `BUILD.json`, `subprocess.run` captured; no engine, no GPU, no network):

- the probe is launched with `env["PATH"]` starting at the engine's `rocm/bin`, and the inherited environment kept;
- the command is still `<engine>/<EXE> --families`;
- an engine whose `BUILD.json` lists no `lib_dirs` keeps the inherited `PATH` unchanged;
- empty output still yields the Flash-Next default (`{"qwen4exp"}`).

Removing the `env=` argument fails two of the three (`failures=1, errors=1`) — `the probe ran without an environment` — so the guard is the reported bug rather than a restatement.

The rest of `tools/test_setup_*.py` is unchanged (37 pass; `test_setup_engine_hash` and `test_setup_golden` fail identically without this change).

pulls.title: fix(serve): coerce XML tool arguments consistently by schema
pulls.author: anstaendig
pulls.body:
## Summary
XML tool calls can contain Python-style literals such as `<parameter=unlock>False</parameter>`. JSON decoding fails and currently passes `"False"` to clients as a truthy string, which can reverse the intended action. Convert supported scalar literals using the declared type in both completed and streamed tool calls.

Related to #1955, which covers boolean conversion in the completed-call parser. This change also applies conversion to streamed argument fragments and covers nullable and numeric parameters.

## What changed
- Add one shared conversion helper for `parse_tool_call()` and `OutputParser._scan()`. Accept case-insensitive booleans, nullable `None`, and decimal numeric fallbacks when the declared type permits them.
- Pass the full property schema through both paths. Implicit Python literals are accepted only for absent or empty property schemas; nonempty schemas without a top-level type (`enum`, `anyOf`, `$ref`, etc.) retain the previous JSON-or-raw fallback.
- Preserve string-only parameters verbatim, including `["string"]`. Preserve existing JSON-first decoding, including quoted JSON strings, objects and arrays. Unknown or incompatible values stay raw; new numeric fallbacks reject non-finite values.
- Add parser regressions in `serve/test_tool_argument_types.py`, including whole output, character-wise streaming, every two-chunk split, multiple calls, literal tags inside strings and incomplete parameters. Add a localhost mock-engine test for streamed and non-streamed OpenAI and Anthropic responses.

## Extra Notes
Validation on upstream `296b59d2` plus this change, macOS / Python 3.12, using cached Jinja2, regex and jsonschema dependencies:

```sh
python -m unittest serve.test_tool_argument_types serve.test_frontend serve.test_server serve.test_responses serve.test_mcp -q
```

413 tests passed. An additional 3,325 differential checks against upstream `296b59d2` passed for legacy JSON/string/raw values, reasoning/content events, literal tags, truncation and chunking, including 1,330 checks for properties with constraints or metadata but no usable top-level type. `git diff --check` passed.

The tag delimiters and existing parser state transitions are unchanged. No C++/CUDA/HIP/SYCL backend files are touched. No deployment, GPU inference or BFCL rerun was performed; benchmark recovery is unmeasured.

pulls.title: add lifetime useage statistics to monitoring
pulls.author: wokhouse
pulls.body: Branch `pr/usage-stats` from `v0.1.43`. Commits: `1c612cec`, `df2aaf7a`, `f721c2ae`, and `64f426dc` (code), `66f4ab46` and `35557294` (docs). Issue #2241 asks for this feature. The report there says: > My Strata generated 150 million tokens… Strata doesn't have a total token count history that could be reset via, the session history also doesn't really add up things either? Issue #35 (monitor totals only since boot) and PR #1707 (token analytics) are closed. #1707 added no persistent storage. No open pull request covers this. ## What it changes The monitor's request history covers the current run only. The token analytics from #1707 keep no data across restarts. This pull request adds an opt-in counter store in `serve/usage.py`. It counts requests, prompt tokens read, prompt tokens reused, output tokens, prompt milliseconds, decode milliseconds, and MTP drafts offered and accepted. The store writes to a small JSON file next to the run config. The counters stay in that file after a restart. The store holds counters only. It holds no prompts, no answers, and no request bodies. - The feature is off by default. Set `"usage_stats": true` in `strata-.json`, or add `--usage-stats` to `serve/server.py`. - `GET /metrics` returns a `usage` object with lifetime totals and the `1d`, `7d`, and `30d` views. - A custom range uses `?from_ts=&to_ts=`. - The Usage panel in the monitor tab shows these views. - The panel opens on the 7-day view. The view you pick is kept in the browser and restored on the next load. A Custom range comes back with its dates filled in. A stored value that is not a known view falls back to 7 days. - The store keeps hourly buckets for 31 days. A custom range inside that window answers at hour resolution. A range that starts earlier is clamped to the oldest kept bucket. The panel reports the window it summed. - The range buttons wrap on a narrow screen. A row that cannot wrap is 410px wide at its narrowest, and the monitor pane scrolls sideways instead of the buttons. ## What it leaves alone This change touches no engine file. It changes Python and the web app only, so no CUDA, HIP, or SYCL rebuild is needed. No default changes. With the flag off, the usage code does nothing, no file is written, and `/metrics` reports `{"enabled": false}`. The Prometheus text output does not change. ## How I checked - `serve/test_usage.py` is new and has 14 tests. - The tests cover the off no-op, the counters, and persistence when the store reopens. - They also cover recovery from a corrupt file, the four time views, and the custom range. - The custom range tests cover the sum, the clamp, and an empty window. - A second battery of 30 checks runs the store directly. It feeds wrongly typed counters, a clock that steps backwards, two writers at one time, an unwritable path, and odd ranges. - I checked the HTTP layer against a live server. Empty, missing, and non-numeric range parameters return 200 and are ignored. A range outside the kept window is clamped to it. - `serve.test_server` passes 296 of 296. `test_monitor` passes 10 of 10, `test_prometheus` 6 of 6, and `test_runconfig` 9 of 9. - I checked the panel in a real browser. A fresh browser opens on 7 days. A pick survives a reload. A stored value that is not a view falls back to 7 days. A remembered Custom view comes back with its dates filled in. - The browser checks cover the date picker too. A range that crosses a DST change sums the right window. An empty window reads differently from dates that were never set. Storage that throws, which private mode does, does not break the page. - I checked the panel at phone widths: 320, 360, 390, 430, 540, and 768 px. The pane does not scroll sideways at any of them. The buttons wrap to three or four lines, and a press still works. - The edge tests found four faults, and this branch fixes them. A hand-edited counters file stopped the server at boot. A clock that stepped backwards dropped a bucket from a view. The date prefill used the UTC day, so a user east of UTC saw the wrong window. A window with no data told the user to pick dates again. - I checked the route against the mock engine. A request with no `from_ts` gets no custom view. A request with a valid range gets a window. Junk in the parameters is ignored. The range works with `?requests=all`. - I put this build into production on my own box on 2026-10-13. The box runs Linux, an RTX 4090 with 24 GB, 60 GB RAM, and batch-1. It serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S on engine 0.1.43. I read the counters file afterwards. It holds counters only. ## Not tested Windows and the HIP path are untested here. This box runs Linux only. I did not test `--batch` or concurrency above 1. This box serves batch-1. This change adds no cost-per-token conversion. The counters are raw numbers, and no price table is added. ---

pulls.title: setup: honour --source on a Mac, whose hand-over skips setup.py's parser (#2363)
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
Closes #2363.

On a Mac `setup.py` hands over to `metal/setup_mac.py` before its own parser runs, so the `--source` flag that sets `STRATA_SOURCE` is never seen; `setup_mac.py`'s parser did not define it either, so it landed in `parse_known_args`' leftovers and was dropped — right after the failed download had recommended it:

```
  [!]  not used on a Mac: --source modelscope
```

`--source` is now defined in the Mac parser and sets `STRATA_SOURCE`, exactly as `setup.py` does (`choices=SOURCES`, same help). The environment variable already worked on a Mac; the documented flag does now too.

## Testing

`python -m unittest tools.test_setup_mac` — the new case drives `main(["--source","modelscope","--yes","--check","--data-dir",<tmp>])` with the Mac checks mocked the way the rest of that file does (sysctl/sw_vers/xcode-select; no GPU, no network), and requires `STRATA_SOURCE` to be set **and** no `not used on a Mac` warning for `--source`.

- With the change: 20 tests, `OK`.
- With the flag definition and the `os.environ` line removed: `AssertionError: None != 'modelscope'`.

The other `tools/test_setup_*.py` modules behave as before (`test_setup_engine_hash` and `test_setup_golden` fail identically in this checkout without this change).

The hand-over itself is untouched: the Mac parser still owns the Mac argv, it just knows this one flag now.

**Hardware:** 4x RTX 3090 24 GB at a 380 W limit each. PCIe: two cards at Gen3 x16, two at Gen4 x8. The rest of

| Workload | stock 0.1.44 | modified 0.1.43 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 user, ~147-token prompt, 512 out | 111.7 | 116.2 |

pulls.title: tools: poll the server address the config binds, not loopback (#2330)
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
Closes #2330.

`strata_bench.py` starts the server on the config's `host` and then polls readiness at a hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (`tools/strata_bench.py:967`), so a host bound to a specific interface never answers the poll — the report saw the log confirm readiness at `192.168.1.10` while BENCH kept printing "still loading" for 11 minutes.

The change is @Swallowtail23's patch from the report, with the mapping lifted into `server_base` so the test can reach it and nothing else altered: use the configured host, default to loopback when there is none, map the wildcard binds (`0.0.0.0` → `127.0.0.1`, `::` → `::1`) to something connectable, and bracket IPv6 literals. An explicit `--url` still takes precedence.

## Testing

`python -m unittest tools.test_bench_host` — five cases: a configured LAN host, an absent host, both wildcards, a bare and an already-bracketed IPv6 literal, and a hostname. Replacing the mapping with the old hardcoded `127.0.0.1` fails four of them, so they are guards rather than restatements.

pulls.title: telemetry: the Mac's Monitor cards - GPU load and VRAM from IOKit, th…
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
…e rest said out loud

On a Mac the Monitor tab's GPU cards were empty: telemetry had NVML (NVIDIA) and the amdgpu sysfs files (#301) and nothing else, so the Metal backend read nothing.  The Apple GPU's load and memory are in the IOKit registry's IOAccelerator nodes (ioreg -l -w0 -r -c IOAccelerator, 22 ms), and the device's memory budget is the same Metal property the engine reads (metal/src/mtl_rt.mm's recommended_working_set, the engine's "GPU working set" log line
- 26,800,603,136 bytes here, which is 25.0 GiB).

_Metal (a new reader beside _Nvml and _Amd): the index'th accelerator node's PerformanceStatistics give Device Utilization % (older chips: the renderer or the tiler) and the in-use system memory; the total is the working set, read through the Metal framework and objc_msgSend (no PyObjC).  The temperature and power sensors are not readable without root (powermetrics), and an Apple Silicon GPU sits on the die, so there is no PCIe link: the cards show a dash and static gpu_note says why, the same way #1380's note does for a Windows AMD card.  gpu_reader takes `amd` first, so the AMD trees still read on a Mac for the tests, and a missing selector is asked for before it is sent (an unanswered one raises an Objective-C exception no ctypes call can catch).

Service.free_vram_mib now goes through gpu_reader instead of _Nvml directly, so the Mac gets that reading too (it used to return None there).

Measured on an M1 Max (macOS 26.6.2): through the server, GET /metrics during a request - gpu_name "Apple M1 Max", gpu_vram_total_mib 25559, gpu_util 74-77 % while decoding (9 % once idle), gpu_mem_used 10.5 GiB in use of 24.96 GiB, cpu 12.6 %; the plain-text /prometheus-format metrics carry the same series.  serve/test_server.py: MacTelemetry (fixture registry: two accelerators, index selection, renderer/tiler fallback, a raising runner, the note and the samples) plus AmdTelemetry, TelemetryNoDisks, Monitor and the full serve/test_server.py (318 tests) pass on the same box.

What it leaves alone: the NVIDIA and AMD paths (a test-only gpu_reader order change on macOS), and the web app - the cards read the series it already had.

pulls.title: serve: average the throughput gauges over the window between scrapes (#2341)
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
Closes #2341.

`/metrics/prometheus` exposed `llamacpp:prompt_tokens_seconds` and `llamacpp:predicted_tokens_seconds` as `total_tokens / total_seconds` over the server's lifetime, so a server idle for hours still advertised e.g. 58 tok/s, with nothing in the text format to say how old the number was.

llama.cpp does not do that under those names. Both rates come from `server_metrics::bucket` (`tools/server/server-common.h`), which a scrape resets — *"the gauges are averaged over the window between two scrapes"* (`tools/server/server-context.cpp`) — and `bucket::n_per_second()` returns `0.0` when the window is empty. So the same dashboard that decays to `0` against llama.cpp froze at the last request's speed against Strata.

The `*_total` counters stay cumulative; only the two gauges now come from a bucket held across scrapes, exposed as the delta. The HELP text says which window they cover.

## Testing

`python -m unittest serve.test_server.PrometheusMetrics`

The new case sends one request, scrapes, then scrapes again with no traffic in between and requires `(0, 0)` for the two gauges while `llamacpp:tokens_predicted_total` stays put. Against the old code that second scrape returns the frozen `(602.5, 50.0)` (the failure is in the report), so the case is a real guard rather than a restatement.

`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p 'test_*.py'` — 770 tests, `OK (skipped=8)`, with this checkout's `requirements.txt` installed (a bare system Python was missing `regex`, which is unrelated to the change).

pulls.title: fused_gr: STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST=1 on CUDA too (opt-in): decode +0.5-0.6% on a V100 + PG500 layer split
pulls.author: Warabii1248
pulls.body:
## Title

fused_gr: STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST=1 on CUDA too (opt-in): decode +0.5-0.6% on a V100 + PG500 layer split

Issue: none (on `main`, independent of other PRs; three lines in the CUDA side of `norm_fast_on()` and one comment)

## Summary

`norm_fast_on()` reads `STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST` under HIP only (on by default for gfx12); on CUDA it always returns false.
`gr_norm_split_fast_kernel` is built for CUDA too and is documented as bitwise equal to `gr_norm_split_kernel` (the same elements, operations and order).
It is used only when the hyper-connection read runs split or staged (`variant >= kHcSplit`); on this machine the engine reports
`the hyper-connection read runs as staged` on both cards.

This lets CUDA opt in with the same variable, on every CUDA architecture; we measured sm_70 only. Without the variable nothing changes.
It is separate from `gr_fast()` (on with `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`), which swaps the plain read's norm kernel and the up kernel; it does not choose
the split / staged norm that this variable switches. The numbers below are with `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1` and this variable on top.

## What changed

- `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`: on the CUDA side of `norm_fast_on()` (`#else`), read `STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST` once and return true when it is set and not 0.
  The HIP side is unchanged. The comment above it, "gfx12 only until another arch is measured", now says CUDA opts in (second commit, comment only).
- Other backends: both HIP builds (`STRATA_ENABLE_HIP` and `STRATA_HIP_GFX906`) compile the `.cu` files as HIP and take the unchanged `__HIPCC__` side.
  The SYCL build uses its own copy (`sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`), which this does not touch.
  HIP builds, without a GPU in ROCm 7.14 containers: `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906` (the `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
  image docs/AMD_HIP.md uses; `strata`) and `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1100;gfx1201"` (`rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.14.1-full`;
  `strata`) both compile with 0 errors. Not run (no AMD card here). SYCL not built: it does not compile the changed file.

## Checks (Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB + Tesla PG500-216 (sm_70, 32 GB), layer split K=24, Linux, CUDA 12.9, `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`)

How we checked: a build of this branch's first commit (`main` `a0116b2` + `16da736`; the second commit changes a comment only), the parity test and the
micro benchmark on each card with and without the variable, then the engine with and without it in ABBA order at two power limits.

- `gr_parity --selftest` (`STRATA_HC_SPLIT=2`) on the V100 and the PG500, `STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST` unset and `=1` (4 runs): every line passes.
  `fused_gr_bench 100 1 5 48` (48 weight sets in turn, read cold): the norm stage V100 9.1-9.2 -> 8.2 us, PG500 8.1-8.2 -> 7.2-7.3 us (T 1-5), `0 differing`.
- Engine: the GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS model and pack that `setup.py --model IQ3_XXS` installs (`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`), with setup's
  launch settings (`--mmap-experts`, image input on, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`), 256K context, int8 KV, layer split K=24, `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`,
  `STRATA_PLE_PROBE=0` (skips the start-up PLE read check and keeps direct reads). Every expert resident on both cards.
  Temperature 0, no thinking, three short questions (English, Japanese, code; generated to their caps of 400 / 600 / 400 tokens).
  A fresh engine start per run, one warm-up pass, then two passes (9 requests per start). On, off, off, on (ABBA) at 170 W and at 250 W.
  Decode tok/s (measured on the client from the stream; mean of two starts):

  | | English | Japanese | code |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | 170 W off | 99.90 | 111.00 | 122.15 |
  | 170 W `STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST=1` | 100.50 (+0.6%) | 111.70 (+0.6%) | 122.80 (+0.5%) |
  | 250 W off | 99.95 | 111.10 | 122.20 |
  | 250 W `STRATA_GR_NORM_FAST=1` | 100.45 (+0.5%) | 111.65 (+0.5%) | 122.85 (+0.5%) |

  Per start (English / Japanese / code): 170 W on 100.5 / 111.7 / 122.8 twice, off 99.9 / 111.0 / 122.1 and 99.9 / 111.0 / 122.2;
  250 W on 100.5 / 111.7 / 122.9 and 100.4 / 111.6 / 122.8, off 100.0 / 111.2 / 122.3 and 99.9 / 111.0 / 122.1.
  The two starts of a setting are within 0.2 tok/s, and every start with the variable is above every start without it.
- Replies: identical bit for bit per question in all 72 requests (8 starts x 9), on and off alike.
  MTP drafts accepted / drafted (the 9 requests of one start): 2,712 / 3,448 in all 8 starts.

sm_70: the multi-block greedy pick (argmax_rows) as an opt-in, STRATA_ARGMAX_ROWS_SM70=1: decode +0.7-0.8% on a V100 + PG500 layer split

## Summary

`argmax_rows_wanted()` turns on `argmax_rows`, the greedy pick that spreads a row over several blocks (one per 4,096 vocabulary entries, at most 128),
for compute capability 8.x only. On 7.x the verify's and the drafter's greedy pick is `sampler_greedy_kernel` (one block of 1,024 threads a row).
`argmax_rows` returns the same token as the one-block pick bit for bit; `verify_parity` checks that.

`STRATA_ARGMAX_ROWS_SM70=1` lets a compute capability 7.x card take that path. Without the variable nothing changes (the 7.x branch reads the variable
and returns false). The check is `major == 7`, so sm_72 and sm_75 (Turing) could opt in too; we measured sm_70 only.

pulls.title: pf_wmma: a second Volta prompt-expert kernel for IQ2_S gate/up and IQ4_NL down (STRATA_PF_WMMA2=1, opt-in): prompt +2.5-4.3% on a V100 + PG500 layer split
pulls.author: Warabii1248
pulls.body:
## Title

pf_wmma: a second Volta prompt-expert kernel for IQ2_S gate/up and IQ4_NL down (STRATA_PF_WMMA2=1, opt-in): prompt +2.5-4.3% on a V100 + PG500 layer split

Issue: stacked on #2355 (`v100-pf-wmma-layer-split`, which carries #1771 and the layer-split fix). This PR's changes are its last two commits, `6a7425d` and `dc6cd5f` (a comment). Like #2355, it carries #1771's conflict with main at `ed4773e` in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`.
Opt-in, so nothing changes without the variable.

## Summary

`gemm_iq_f16_grouped_kernel` (#1771's FP16 tensor-core prompt experts) dequantizes each K chunk of 128 weight rows into shared memory before the
tensor-core math: an IQ super-block (chunk 256) through `dq_dispatch`, one warp a row; IQ4_NL and Q2_0 (chunk 128) with their own loops
(IQ4_NL: one thread per row and 64-value half). The grid tables and the weight bytes are read from global memory as each chunk needs them.
We think that on a V100 this step does not fully hide behind the tensor-core math. The kernel below spreads it over the whole block; it also differs in
tile shape, static shared memory and launch bounds, and we did not isolate which part gives the gain.

The GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS model that `setup.py --model IQ3_XXS` installs mixes expert types per layer: gate/up is IQ2_S in 10 of 48 layers and down is
IQ4_NL in 18 of 48. The new kernel takes those two types; the other layers keep the existing kernel, so the gain below comes from those layers only.

Behind the same entry point it adds a second kernel for these two types:
- A block = 128 weight rows of one expert x 64 sorted rows, K stages of 64. 8 warps = 4 x 2; each warp holds a 32 x 32 piece of the output in 2 x 2 `wmma` 16x16x16 fragments (FP32 sums).
- Each thread dequantizes exactly one 32-value sub-block per stage (row `t % 128`, sub-block `t / 128`) from a "raw stage" in shared memory
  (one IQ2_S super-block or four IQ4_NL blocks a row) that the whole block reads as contiguous 4-byte words.
  While the tensor cores work on a stage, the next raw stage and the next activations are already in registers (one barrier pair a stage).
- The IQ2_S grid and sign masks, or a byte -> two `kvalues_iq4nl` table for IQ4_NL, live in shared memory.
- Static shared memory <= 48 KiB (no per-device attribute to set). Full 16-row output tiles go straight to `Y`; an expert's last partial tile goes through a per-warp scratch.

By design the dequantized values are the ones `dq_iq2_s` / `dq_iq4_nl` give, in natural order, so the tensor cores get the same FP16 weights in the
same k order as in the existing kernel. Every other type, shape and alignment keeps the existing kernel.

The layout (a raw stage in shared memory, one sub-block per thread per stage) follows a Volta MoE kernel we wrote for our own llama.cpp build
(local patches, not published; the comment in the code says so). The code here is new, written with `nvcuda::wmma` and Strata's own group layout (no ggml dependency).

## What changed

- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: the second kernel, and with `STRATA_PF_WMMA2=1` a branch that sends IQ2_S (K a multiple of 512) and IQ4_NL (K a multiple of 128) to it.
  The variable is read like `STRATA_PF_WMMA` (on when its first character is `1`); unset or anything else: the existing kernel.
- Other backends: all of it is inside the `#if !defined(__HIPCC__)` block of `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` (both HIP builds compile the stub that returns false,
  unchanged), and the SYCL build has no `gemm_iq_f16_grouped`.
  HIP builds, without a GPU in ROCm 7.14 containers: `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906` (the `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
  image docs/AMD_HIP.md uses; `strata` and `pf_wmma_parity`) and `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1100;gfx1201"` (`rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.14.1-full`;
  `strata`) both compile with 0 errors. Not run (no AMD card here). SYCL not built: it does not compile the changed file.

## Checks (Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB + Tesla PG500-216 (sm_70, 32 GB), layer split K=24, CUDA 12.9, Linux, `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`)

How we checked: a build of #2355's branch + `6a7425d` (`dc6cd5f` changes a comment only), the parity test on both cards, then the engine with and without the variable in ABBA order at two power limits.

- `pf_wmma_parity` (unset and `STRATA_PF_WMMA2=1`): 0 failures on 2 devices both times. It compares the result against a double-precision reference;
  in the three cases the new kernel takes, its max |err| equals the existing kernel's (IQ2_S 1280x2560 0.000444 of 106, IQ4_NL 1280x2560 0.000393 of 97.5,
  IQ4_NL 2560x640 0.000162 of 65.4), which fits the same weights summed in the same order.
  (The first version rounded the IQ2_S sub-scale to FP16 before multiplying and gave 0.0435: within tolerance but not the same values, so we changed it.)
- Engine: the GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS model and pack that `setup.py --model IQ3_XXS` installs (`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`), with setup's
  launch settings (`--mmap-experts`, image input on, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`), 256K context, int8 KV, layer split K=24, `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`,
  `STRATA_PLE_PROBE=0` (skips the start-up PLE read check and keeps direct reads). Every expert resident on both cards.
  A fresh engine start per run, on, off, off, on (ABBA), at 170 W and at 250 W.
  Prompt tok/s (prompt tokens / time to the first content token, measured on the client). Fresh 26.7K, 52K and 104K prompts, then another 26.7K and 52K (nothing reused):

  | prompt | 170 W off (2 runs) | 170 W on (2 runs) | ratio of means | 250 W off (2 runs) | 250 W on (2 runs) | ratio of means |
  |---|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|
  | 52,019 | 2,191.7 / 2,195.8 | 2,276.6 / 2,277.3 | +3.8% | 2,360.8 / 2,361.9 | 2,439.7 / 2,449.2 | +3.5% |
  | 103,869 | 2,267.2 / 2,267.5 | 2,332.5 / 2,325.4 | +2.7% | 2,457.1 / 2,457.0 | 2,511.4 / 2,525.4 | +2.5% |
  | 26,692 (second) | 1,905.5 / 1,907.0 | 1,986.4 / 1,985.0 | +4.2% | 2,038.4 / 2,040.7 | 2,127.5 / 2,126.0 | +4.3% |
  | 52,020 (second) | 2,191.4 / 2,193.6 | 2,261.0 / 2,273.9 | +3.4% | 2,362.7 / 2,356.0 | 2,453.0 / 2,446.4 | +3.8% |

  Every run with the variable is above every run without it; the two runs of a setting are within 0.6%. The first 26.7K after start (26,693 tokens)
  is left out of the table because one run (170 W off, 1,517.1) was far below its pair; all eight values: 170 W off 1,517.1 / 1,764.4, on 1,827.4 / 1,826.1;
  250 W off 1,864.3 / 1,869.8, on 1,939.3 / 1,938.6.
  The kernel runs on the prompt path only; decode is not part of this comparison.
- The long-prompt recall check (answer a passphrase placed in the middle) passed in all 40 requests (8 starts x 5).

## Extra Notes

- Only some layers of this model take the kernel (see Summary). Extending the same layout to other types (IQ3_S, IQ2_XS, IQ2_XXS, IQ3_XXS, Q2_0) might gain more; not done here.
- Disclosure: the change and this text were prepared with an AI assistant (Claude); the numbers are from runs on the machine above.

pulls.title: pf_wmma: set the tiles' shared-memory attribute on each card, so the second card of a layer split can launch them
pulls.author: Warabii1248
pulls.body:
## Title

pf_wmma: set the tiles' shared-memory attribute on each card, so the second card of a layer split can launch them

Issue: stacked on #1771 (which carries #1401's FP16 prompt commits). This PR's changes are the last two commits, `d5fdec0` and `2cec5c3`. #1771 no longer merges cleanly into main at `ed4773e` (a conflict in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`); this branch carries that conflict, and its own two commits touch only `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu` and `src/kernels/pf_wmma_parity.cpp`.

## Summary

`gemm_iq_f16_grouped` sets the over-48 KiB dynamic shared-memory attribute of its three tile kernels once per process (`static bool attr`).
`cudaFuncSetAttribute` applies to the current device only, so on a layer split only the card that launched the tiles first has it.
The next card's launch fails, `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` returns false, and the prompt stops with `prefill: the WMMA expert tiles could not launch`
(the engine exits with code 1 and serve restarts it). The measurements in #1401 / #1771 that we found are on one card, where this path is not reached.

The fix keeps the flag per device (the same per-device `[64]` shape as `exp_mode()` in the same file).
`pf_wmma_parity` now runs its cases on every sm_70+ card in turn within one process, as a layer split does; before the fix every case fails on the second card.

## What changed

- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: set the attribute once per device instead of once per process (`static bool attr[64]`, `cudaGetDevice`).
- `src/kernels/pf_wmma_parity.cpp`: run the cases on each sm_70+ device in turn (`cudaSetDevice`); the summary line gives the device count.
- Other backends: the `iq_kernels.cu` change is inside the `#if !defined(__HIPCC__)` block of `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` (both HIP builds compile the stub
  that returns false, unchanged), and the SYCL build has no `gemm_iq_f16_grouped`.
  HIP builds, without a GPU in ROCm 7.14 containers: `-DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906` (the `mixa3607/rocm-gfx906:7.14-complete`
  image docs/AMD_HIP.md uses; `strata` and `pf_wmma_parity`) and `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_HIP=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES="gfx1100;gfx1201"` (`rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.14.1-full`;
  `strata`) both compile with 0 errors. Not run (no AMD card here). SYCL not built: it does not compile the changed files (it has its own `iq_kernels` copy and no `pf_wmma_parity`).

The branch is v0.1.43 (`7695859`) with #1771's five commits cherry-picked onto it (#1771 itself is on v0.1.41, `fb58e0d`; the patches are
unchanged, authors kept, `cherry picked from` trailers) and the two commits above on top. No commit in `7695859..a0116b2` (`main` when this branch was made) touches `iq_kernels.cu` or `pf_wmma_parity.cpp`; since `a0116b2`, main has changed `iq_kernels.cu` (at `ed4773e` that file merges without a text conflict; we have not built the branch on `ed4773e`).

Effect on default behavior: with one card, that card's attribute is set at the same point as before. On a layer split of two or more cards, the prompt that stopped now runs.

## Checks (Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB + Tesla PG500-216 (sm_70, 32 GB), layer split K=24, CUDA 12.9, Linux, `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`)

How we checked: the parity test before and after the fix, then the engine on the layer split before the fix and, after it, with and without the tiles.

- `pf_wmma_parity` before the fix: device 0 8 / 8 ok, device 1 8 / 8 "not launched" (`8 failures on 2 devices`, exit code 1).
  After: `0 failures on 2 devices`, exit code 0. The second card's errors equal the first card's (e.g. IQ4_NL 2560x640 max |err| 0.000162 of 65.4).
- Engine: the GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS model and pack that `setup.py --model IQ3_XXS` installs (`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`, nothing else changed),
  `--mmap-experts`, 256K context, int8 KV, `STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`, every expert in VRAM, 170 W power limit.
  - Before the fix, default (`STRATA_PF_WMMA` on): the first prompt stops with `prefill: the WMMA expert tiles could not launch` (0 tokens read; the engine exits with code 1 and serve restarts it).
  - After the fix: `STRATA_PF_WMMA=0` against the default, alternating, a fresh engine start per run. After each start, fresh prompts of 26.7K
    (the first request), 52K (the second) and 104K tokens (the third), nothing reused. Prompt tok/s = prompt tokens / time to the first content token, measured on the client:

    | prompt tokens | `STRATA_PF_WMMA=0` (3 runs) | default (3 runs) | ratio of medians |
    |---|---|---|---:|
    | 26,689-26,690 | 1,670.6 / 1,667.9 / 1,669.8 | 1,765.8 / 1,766.8 / 1,765.3 | +5.7% |
    | 52,015-52,016 | 2,064.9 / 2,063.1 / 2,065.2 | 2,201.4 / 2,200.1 / 2,204.3 | +6.6% |
    | 103,865-103,866 | 2,138.8 / 2,136.2 / 2,137.5 | 2,275.3 / 2,273.3 / 2,271.5 | +6.4% |

    Every default run is above every `=0` run. The third default run is a re-run: in the first attempt the start-up PLE read check measured 9,325 rows/s
    (the other five starts 33,428-37,238), and 0.1.43's automatic switch moved that run to `--ple-io mmap` (385 / 1,115 / 1,075 tok/s; we did not find the cause).
    That is the PLE read mode, not the tiles, so we re-ran it with `STRATA_PLE_PROBE=0` (`--ple-io direct`, what the check chose on every other start).
    (In 0.1.43.1 the switch only warns, #2040.)

pulls.author: Tsury

When a config or shared setting supplies a reasoning default, `Service.with_shared()` replaces an explicit `reasoning_effort: false` because its absence check uses truthiness. On 0.1.44.1 with config LOW, the existing HTTP/render fixture produces LOW instead of thinking off for that request. The release already documents `false` as off.

Treat only missing, null or empty effort as absent. Add the explicit-false case to the existing request-over-config HTTP regression. Requests that omit effort still use the configured/shared default; ordinary string levels and template kwargs keep their existing precedence. No kernel, sampling, model policy or default change.

Validation: the added assertion fails on exact tag `296b59d2f73c8f04a805df29c2fa97655adace78` with `low != none`, then all 11 `serve.test_effort_paths` methods pass after the one-line fix. Python/Jinja fixture only; no GPU inference. Neither touched Python file builds a CUDA/HIP/SYCL backend.

pulls.title: Suffix-reuse: conversation KV prefix mount, quant-safe splices, state checkpoint ladder
pulls.author: justindressler
pulls.body:
## Summary

Suffix-reuse for the conversation KV cache: reuse verified conversation prefixes across
requests, splices, and mid-history edits — built on v0.1.45 (rebased from v0.1.43; rebase verified live) as a stack of three independent,
default-off flags. **All flags off = byte-identical engine behavior** (verified empirically
per commit).

**Three orthogonal features:**

1. **`--cache-suffix-reuse <N>`** — mount a parked previous conversation whose token prefix
   matches the incoming prompt (LCP-verified), narrowing the read window. Works across all
   five KV formats (fp16, int8, int8+KV_ROT, k8v4, q4_0) — splicing int8/k8v4/q4_0 through
   their exact quant/dequant paths so reused blocks stay byte-identical.
2. **`--prompt-cache-dense-tail <N>`** (FW-1) — dense checkpointing of the tail region so
   late-turn conversations restore cheaply.
3. **`--prompt-cache-state-every <N>`** (FW-2b) — state checkpoint ladder at a token cadence,
   capping the re-read gap after mid-history edits and compaction-style rewrites.

Full design, invariants, and measurement methodology: `docs/SUFFIX_REUSE.md` (in this PR).

## Results (RTX 3090 24 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next abliterated GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, 131k ctx, MTP spec-4, temp 0)

| Suite | Base | This PR | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Needle-retention (3 seeds × 96) | 0.750 | 0.792 ± 0.042 | reward-neutral across seeds; seed-42 margin alone was an artifact — honestly documented |
| Mean prompt reuse (needle harness) | 0% | 15.5% | compaction-phase concentration documented |
| kv-store 4-family re-cert | — | kv 24/24, sudoku 15/15, log 15/24 | correctness ≥ base on all four families |
| KV-format sweep | — | 5/5 GREEN | fp16/int8/kvrot/k8v4/q4_0, identical reuse across formats (81.0% best) |
| Steady-state 3-turn | — | 160→161→162 correct, 89.3% token reuse, 3.4s vs 45.2s cold prefill |
| Needle A/B (state-every on/off) | 0.750 / 0.0% reuse | 0.833 / 25.2% reuse | same binary+seed+config, single-flag delta |

| v0.1.45 rebase: 4-turn live probe (3090) | — | all pass | cold 26.9s; append 98.4% reuse (1.3s); mid-edit splice @ token 66; identical replay 99.8% (0.7s) |
| v0.1.45 rebase: NIAH needle, 21.9k-token haystack | — | **5/5 depths** (10–90%) | exact passphrase recall, no cache shortcuts (unique filler per depth) |
| Measured line coverage (gcov, host-test scope) | — | **95%** (2195/2291) | 269/269 cases green; residual lines are CUDA-only branches (verified live instead) |

End-to-end behavior verified on a real interactive chat workload (mid-history edits,
regenerations, appends; thinking model, streaming): double-digit-to-near-full prompt reuse on
edit-shaped requests, prefill dropping from ~11.5s to 1–4s on cache hits, generation quality
and output length unaffected (prefill-only mechanism).

## Correctness invariants

- Off-flags → byte-identical outputs (A/B verified per layer, cross-binary diff = self-noise)
- Mounts only from **LCP-verified** prefixes; recurrence-state restore refuses any rung above
  the divergence point (fail-closed; stale-state probe from v3 development never reaches main)
- Splice paths for quantized formats round-trip through the format's own quant/dequant ops —
  reused K/V blocks are bit-equal to a full read's

## Review & verification

- Each layer independently code-reviewed (APPROVE, 0 blocking on the final layer; 3
  informational MINORs, all docs-adjacent)
- Fresh clean builds + CPU test suites green per layer (52/52 base, 82/0 group)
- 3-seed validation on the headline claim before shipping

pulls.title: moe_mm_parity: the default tile that did not exist, and --v3's v1 arg…
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
…ument list

Two stale defaults, both of which kept the test from covering what the engine ships.

The default tile was TM 16 TN 64 TK 16, but the v1 kernel set only instantiates TK 64: the default run died at pipeline creation on any GPU (measured on an M1 Max: "mtl: no function mm_gu_42_16_64_16_2"). TK is now 64, which both the v1 and the v2 sets instantiate, so the default run and --v2 both work; the engine's v2 tile for Q2_0 (16,64,16,2) stays reachable with --tile.

--v3 bound the v1 kernels' argument list ({W, x, H, stok, tiles, ma}) to the v3 kernels: tiles was read as the sorted-token buffer and MmArgs as raw int2 pairs, so every stride, n_embd and expert id was garbage. On the M1 Max that is a deterministic GPU command-buffer error in the GEMM pass; with the right arguments the v3 kernels run, and a separate M1 limit shows (≥40 threadgroups of mm_gu3 fault, 35 pass, data-independent) that the engine does not hit: gu_v3 = dn_v3 = coop_k4, which is false on the M1. v3 now binds {W, XS, HS, tiles, ma} as the engine does, fills XS for v3 too (v3 is v2's gather plus the register-operand GEMMs), and binds HS - not H - to down3 with DSG simdgroups.

Measured on an M1 Max (macOS 26.6.2, Q2_0, T 256, 64 experts): default (v1) PASS, rel L2 2.53e-06 vs the fp16-operand reference and 2.37e-04 vs exact; --v2 PASS, 4.42e-06 and 2.37e-04, also with the engine's tile (16,64,16,2).

Leaves alone: no kernel, engine or other test change.

pulls.title: metal: the M1 Max prompt kernels - a select with a device load in the…
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
… arm loses the threadgroup

The two prompt kernels (qsa_attn_mm, qsa_flash) fill their single-simdgroup matmul2d right inputs with

    rk[i] = id >= 0 ? half(float(kq[row * QD + k]) * float(ksc[...])) : half(0.0f);

and that shape - a select with the device load in the arm - loses the threadgroup on an M1 Max: every dispatch of the two kernels fails with
kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim, deterministically, and they run only under MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1. The engine builds this library at start, so nothing is served.

The row is now clamped with max(id, 0), the load is unconditional, and the select is on the value. For an id >= 0 the value is what it was; for an id < 0 it was discarded either way, so the results do not change.

Measured on an M1 Max (macOS 26.6.2, Metal compiler 32023): qsa_prompt_parity ALL PASS - qsa_attn_mm vs qsa_attn rel L2 3.09e-04 (pos0 0) and 3.56e-04 (pos0 30000), qsa_flash 3.72e-04 and 4.22e-04, qsa_score_mm worst rel 2.66e-06 (T 96, within budget and with 2051 selected cells a token); before the change the test faulted on its first dispatch. Through the server, on the reporter's streaming config (Q2_0, --expert-cache 64, prefill auto, spec 2): a 9,940 -token prompt prefilled in 53.4 s (186 tok/s), 24 tokens decoded in 3.0 s (7.9 tok/s), no GPU error.

The compile failure that hid this - qsa_flash's cooperative_tensor copy, "cannot initialize a parameter of type 'void *' with an rvalue of type 'const void *'" - is already fixed in main (#2323); this change is the runtime half of the same two kernels' M1 Max bring-up.

What it leaves alone: the COOP_K4 path (a function constant: compiled out of the M1/M4 pipelines), qsa.metal, and every host file; no CUDA, HIP or SYCL backend builds these kernels. docs/MAC.md records the M1 Max with the measured tok/s.
