pulls.title: fix(metal): prompt buffer fallback when arena chunks are too small (#2323)
pulls.author: kingdonb
pulls.body:
Completes #2323 for small-memory Macs. #2323's reporter ran a 96 GB M2 Max, where the arena's chunks are several GB and the prompt's 1.60 GB of buffers always fit. On a 24 GB M2 the arena shrinks at start (here: chunks of 0.8–1.0 GB), every chunk is skipped by the bytes + (64 MB) check in ExpertStream::region, and every prompt stops with metal prompt: no arena region for the prompt buffers.

The standalone-mmap fallback ("the arena is small: the prompt's … buffers are their own allocation", from the small-arena work) sat inside the chunk loop behind the slot-class check, so it was only reached when a chunk was big enough. This moves it into one function both call sites use: a fitting chunk whose slots a class cannot spare (behavior unchanged), and no fitting chunk at all (was a hard stop, now the same standalone allocation).

Changes: metal/src/engine/stream.cpp (+ one private helper, declared in stream.h), one sentence in docs/MAC.md. Leaves alone: the fitting-chunk carve, the slot-class rule, arena sizing, decode paths; only metal/ is touched (Metal-only files; built on the M2 with Apple clang 21 / metal-cpp_26).

No arena that could host the prompt region before behaves differently — the new path only runs where region() returned nullptr and the first prompt failed. Verified on a 24 GB M2 (macOS 26.6.2, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO-Q2_0, 31.64 GiB .experts): the fallback line replaces the error, prompts run end-to-end (3.7–4.1 tok/s steady in web chat, multi-turn, no crashes).

Not tested here: the M4/M5 (not on hand — the fitting-chunk and tight-slot paths are statement-identical to 0.1.44.1, so their numbers should stand); prompt tok/s before/after (the fallback replaces a hard stop, so there is no "before" to compare); and the memory-pressure story of the extra ~1.6 GB beside a shrunken arena (nothing swapped in our runs; a proper measurement is wanted).

pulls.title: [Engine] MCP: a picture a tool returns reaches the model as a picture (#2130)
pulls.author: dsvi
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Closes #2130.

This allows model to request images through MCP and analyze them with its visual part.

An MCP tool result that carries an `image` block reached the model as a sentence about a picture:

```
[image (image/png, 2,337,795 bytes): not shown to the model]
```

`serve/mcp.py`'s `result_text()` joined the content blocks into one string, so a server that reads image files, takes screenshots or renders charts could hand a picture back and the model never saw it. The model can already ask for the picture with an MCP call - that is what #2130 asks for - only the way back was missing. Now the picture goes to the vision encoder and into the prompt where the server put it, and the model sees the pixels.

The same gap is worse for a client that runs the MCP server on its own side. Chatbox (and the rest built on the AI SDK) never touches Strata's MCP path, and for `/v1/chat/completions` the SDK JSON-stringifies a tool's `content` output, so the base64 of the picture lands inside the tool message. From a real Chatbox conversation against a 262144-token context:

```
request exceeds the context window: prompt (1491022 tokens) leaves no room to answer in the context (262144); requests are never truncated
```

Before: a 400, and the conversation dies on the turn after the picture. After: the picture is taken out of the text and given to the encoder, and the turn answers.

## Related discussion

[#2130](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2130) - the request itself, no scope discussion needed beyond it.

@qiuzan2001's review on this PR found a false positive in the text lifting (a 2-byte `BM` read as a bitmap). It is reproduced, fixed and covered by a test in the second commit, `fee135c1`; see Limits.

## Approach

**1. Strata's own MCP path - `serve/mcp.py`.** `result_text()` became `result_parts()`: the same text as before, plus - only when the result carried pictures - that same content in the prompt's own part shape (`{"type": "image", "source": "data:…"}`, which `serve/frontend.py`'s `_parts_of` and `chat_template.jinja` already consume). `McpHub.call` also returns `parts` and `images`, and `run_with_mcp` appends `r["parts"] or r["text"]`. Block order and the newlines between blocks survive, so the picture sits where the server put it. A result with no pictures produces byte-identical prompt text: `parts` is `None` and the tool message stays the plain string it was.

- Caps per result: 8 pictures of 32 MiB each (`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` is `serve/server.py`'s `IMAGE_URL_MAX`, the chat's own image limit). Past a cap the picture is named in the text, as it always was. `max_result_chars` caps **text** only.
- A `resource` block whose `blob` has an `image/*` mime counts as a picture (the same base64, another wrapper). `audio`, `resource_link` and error results stay text, and Strata still never opens a path an MCP server names.
- Without a vision encoder, or for a picture it cannot decode: `[image omitted: …]` in its place and the chat goes on - the existing `_note_unreadable_tool_images` path, not a new one.
- The web app shows the picture in the tool block and resends it as an image part on the next turn; the base64 is dropped from `localStorage` (it is megabytes).

**2. A picture a client hands back as text - `serve/server.py`.** `Service._lift_pictures_from_tool_text`, at the top of `prepare()`: a base64 run of 1024 characters or more in a **tool's** string content that decodes to a PNG or JPEG magic (or a RIFF/WEBP header) is taken out of the text and given to the encoder as an image part, with `[image (image/png, 1,528,438 bytes)]` left in the text where it was. Same caps as one MCP result. Only `role: "tool"` string content is read - a user who pastes base64 means the characters - and a client that sends the picture as a real image part (an Anthropic `tool_result`, an OpenAI `image_url`) never needed this and is untouched.

Compatibility: no C++ is touched, so no CUDA / HIP / SYCL / Metal rebuild. `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` do not run MCP, so nothing there changes; `GET /mcp` is unchanged.

## Validation

All of it on `fee135c1` (this branch, rebased on `main` at `f57c0adc`), Linux, Python 3.14.8, the IQ3_S pack tokenizer (`tools/strata_tokenizer.py` reading `packs/iq3_s/tokenizer`). The repository's CI does not run the Python suite, so these are local runs.

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest serve.test_tool_text_images serve.test_mcp` -> `Ran 37 tests in 13.973s / OK` (29 + 8; 36 of them are this PR's, one is the new BMP/GIF check).
- `python -m unittest discover -s . -p "test_*.py"` -> `Ran 893 tests in 375.149s`, `FAILED (failures=1, skipped=18)`. The one failure is `serve.test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed`; the same test fails on plain `origin/main` (`f57c0adc`) in a separate worktree with `AssertionError: False is not true : the child outlived a killed server (watcher)`, so it is not from this change.
- The false positive @qiuzan2001 reported, run against both magic tables. With the 5 magics this PR started with: `lifted=1`, and the tool text becomes `result: [image (image/bmp, 3,016 bytes)]` plus an image part. With the 2 it now has: `lifted=0`, kind `None`, and the text is byte for byte what the client sent.
- The Chatbox payload again, IQ3_S pack tokenizer: the tool message is 2,038,158 characters = **1,486,521 tokens** as text; after the lift, **120 tokens of text + 1 picture**, the base64 replaced by `[image (image/png, 1,528,438 bytes)]`.
- Cost of the scan, best of 5: **13.2 ms** for that 2,038,158-character tool message (8.2 ms in a separate single run), **6.9 ms** for a 2,256,008-character tool message with no picture in it, under 0.1 ms for a 2,408-character one.

**Failed:**

- Nothing apart from the `serve.test_lifeline` failure above, which reproduces on plain `main`.

**Not run:**

- The live end to end (real model, the `img` MCP server, the web app) on this revision. It was run on the previous revision of this branch (`ca1c1f7`, on `main` at `296b59d`) on an RTX 3090, 24 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S + mmproj: the `img` server's `read_image` on a 4320x2432 JPEG (resized by that server to a 640x360 PNG, 455 KB) arrived through the hub as one picture with parts in the order `['text', 'text', 'image']`, and a red 160x120 PNG sent as an Anthropic `tool_result` image block was answered "Red" at 142 input tokens. That evidence is for `ca1c1f7`, not `fee135c1`; the second commit changes only which magic bytes are read out of a tool's text.
- CUDA / HIP / SYCL / Metal builds: there is no C++ in the diff.
- Windows and macOS: everything above was run on Linux.

## Limits

- The text lifting reads only a PNG's or a JPEG's magic bytes (plus a RIFF/WEBP header). A BMP or GIF whose bytes arrive as base64 inside a tool's text stays text. Why: @qiuzan2001's case - `base64(b"BMW service log " + b"x" * 3000)` begins with a bitmap's 2-byte `BM`, and the log line was taken away from the model and handed to the encoder as a 3,016-byte "bitmap". Checking the BMP header would not make a 2-byte magic safe to guess at in ordinary text, and a GIF's 6 bytes are not worth extra rules either, so BMP and GIF are out of the sniffing table. A BMP or GIF a client sends as a real image part still reaches the encoder: `Vision.normalize` passes both through to stb_image, as it always did.
- The scan runs on every request that carries tool messages, with no switch. I left it without a flag deliberately: a client that hands pictures back as text has no way to say so, and with the flag off the conversation dies at 1.49M tokens. It is one regex pass over the tool text, and the cost is above.
- `MAX_RESULT_IMAGES` (8) and `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` (32 MiB) are constants, not config settings.
- The lift reads string content only. A client that puts the base64 in a nested JSON field of a tool message is still read as one string, but a client that splits it across two messages is not.

pulls.title: sycl mmvq: Q6_K decode kernels no longer ALU-bound; Q6_K output heads as aligned planes; int4 activation loads
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
**What it changes (SYCL port only, `sycl/`):**
- **Q6_K six-bit offset as SWAR.** The Q6_K wide kernel (and the planar one below) computed `v - 32` with dpct's per-byte saturating `char4` subtract (`dpct::vectorized_binary(sub_sat)`), which compiles to a per-byte loop on Xe. No byte can saturate there, so a 4-operation SWAR form gives the same bits. Q6_K dense matvec: 59.5 -> 30.8 us (1 row), 77.4 -> 45.5 us (4 rows).
- **`STRATA_Q6_PLANAR` (on by default, `=0` turns it off).** The Q6_K LM head and the MTP draft head are converted at load into ql / qh / scales / d planes (the same bytes; the GGUF-layout allocation is freed, so VRAM does not change), so each lane's loads are single aligned 16-byte loads. The draft head's subset is gathered from the planar head. `native_q6_k_mmvq` serves every registered matrix at any column count.
- **`ld_i4_a4`:** the Q8_1 activation quants (4-byte aligned) are read as one dword-vector load in the Q4_K / Q5_K / IQ4_XS wide kernels (Q5_K, 4 rows: 81 -> 68 us).

These are three parts of one kernel pass and are sent together. Each gives bitwise-equal outputs; I can split them if you prefer.

**What it leaves alone:** CUDA and HIP (`src/`), the prompt path, every other quant type's math. Greedy output is byte-identical to the build without the change (below).

**How it was checked**, on one Arc Pro B65 32 GB (Xe2, AOT `bmg-g31`, xe driver, oneAPI 2026.1 `strata-sycl-dev` image), Swift 1.5 GSQ-RCO IQ3_S with `--stream-experts` (about 13,000 of 24,576 expert slots in VRAM, the rest in the pinned host mirror), `--spec 4` + MTP, single slot, v0.1.44 (`ed4773eb`) with and without this commit, same config, 3 interleaved pairs, 3 greedy 256-token prompts + one ~9.4K-token prompt per arm:

| | v0.1.44 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| decode tok/s (per pair) | 37.0 / 36.8 / 36.8 | 39.3 / 39.5 / 39.0 |
| decode, mean | 36.9 | 39.3 (+6.6%) |
| prompt reading tok/s | 818 | 817 |
| greedy replies byte-identical | | 12 / 12 |

The kernel timings above were measured on 0.1.41 with the same kernels. The same change has been in our daily server since 0.1.41.

**Not tested:** Arc A-series (i915) and Arc B580/B570 (`bmg-g21`); models whose expert tensors are Q6_K (the Unsloth UD files); the SYCL kernel parity tests (not registered in our build image: no numpy). Windows (no SYCL launcher there).

pulls.title: metal: keep IQ3_XXS resident on 64 GB Macs (wrap a model bigger than maxBufferLength as overlapping buffers)
pulls.author: hokar3361
pulls.body:
## What this changes

On a 64 GB Mac, the IQ3_XXS pack cannot stay resident in v0.1.44: `Context::wrap` makes one no-copy `MTLBuffer` of the whole model file (47.0 GB), which is larger than the device's `maxBufferLength` (41.75 GB on an M4 Max 64 GB), so it fails with `mtl: wrap 47039873024 failed` (with `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`), and the automatic choice streams the experts from the SSD.

This PR lets such a file be wrapped and used in place:

- `metal/src/mtl_rt.{h,mm}`: a new `wrap(ptr, bytes, max_span)`. When `bytes > maxBufferLength`, the file is wrapped as several no-copy buffers that overlap by `max_span` (the largest range ever bound at one offset). When a dispatch binds the buffer at offset `off`, `encode()` / `run_icb()` pick chunk `min(off / stride, n - 1)` and bind it at `off - k * stride`, so every bound range lies whole inside its chunk.
- `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`, `prompt_chain.inc`: the routed-expert kernels (decode `moe_gu_*`/`moe_down_*`, the prompt GEMMs and the prompt chain) bound the model at offset 0 and passed the experts' absolute file offsets in their argument structs. They are now bound at the layer's first expert tensor with offsets relative to it (`moe_rebase`). `max_span` = the largest tensor or the largest layer's gate+up+down range (1.20 GB here).

## What it leaves alone

- A model that fits one buffer (every pack on a 128 GB Mac) takes the old `wrap(ptr, bytes)` path, and `moe_rebase` returns 0 there, so the default path is unchanged.
- The automatic resident/stream decision (`ExpertStream::wanted`, setup) is unchanged: a 64 GB Mac still streams unless `STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0` is set. I did not change the default because I have not checked the memory headroom with other programs running beside it.
- No CUDA / HIP / SYCL file is touched. `STRATA_METAL_WRAP_SPLIT=0` keeps the old single-buffer wrap.

## How I checked

Mac Studio M4 Max 64 GB (macOS 15), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, same build otherwise:

- `strata generate` with a 12-token and a 360-token prompt: resident (`STRATA_METAL_STREAM=0`) and streamed give the same tokens, and the traced top logits are equal.
- Through the server (greedy, `reasoning_effort: none`): the 400-token code and story answers are identical resident vs streamed, and resident+MTP vs resident.

## Measured (same Mac, same day, decode tok/s)

`bench-strata.py --lengths 1024,4096 --max-tokens 256 --repeat 3` (1K / 4K), plus 400 greedy tokens of "Write a Python function that parses an ISO-8601 date string and returns the weekday name. Include error handling." (code) and "Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper who finds a message in a bottle." (story):

| | 1K | 4K | code | story |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1.44, setup's config for 64 GB (experts streamed, no MTP) | 52.6 | 52.0 | 29.1 | 37.1 |
| this PR, resident, no MTP | 59.7 | 59.0 | 58.1 | 58.3 |
| this PR, resident, MTP draft layer, `--spec 2` | 73.5 | 72.3 | 69.5 | 59.3 |

(`--spec 3`: 67.0 / 70.7 / 67.1 / 48.7; `--spec 4`: 73.9 / 72.9 / 67.3 / 41.5; suffix drafter on: 73.7 / 71.9 / 69.8 / 59.1.)

## Not tested

Other Macs (M1-M3, M5, 96 GB), Q2_0 / IQ3_S packs, memory pressure with other large programs open, and contexts beyond 32K.

pulls.title: sycl serve: STRATA_SYCL_MEMLOCK=0 leaves out --ulimit memlock=-1 (unprivileged LXC, rootless Docker)
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
**What it changes:** `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` keeps `--ulimit memlock=-1` by default; `STRATA_SYCL_MEMLOCK=0` leaves it out. One header line documents it.

**Why:** since 0.1.42 (e02bd99) the launcher always passes `--ulimit memlock=-1`. Docker inside an unprivileged LXC container (and, as far as we know, rootless Docker) may not raise that limit, and `docker run` then fails before the engine starts:

    error setting rlimit type 8: operation not permitted

The server only sees the engine exit at start, and there is no setting to avoid it short of editing the launcher. On our host the engine ran without the flag up to 0.1.41 and runs on 0.1.44 with this setting (below).

**What it leaves alone:** the default (`--ulimit memlock=-1` is still passed; the `docker run` arguments are identical to main, checked with a `docker` stub that prints them), and everything else in the launcher. CUDA/HIP untouched.

**How it was checked:**
- The `docker` stub: default identical to main; with `STRATA_SYCL_MEMLOCK=0` the argument list has no `--ulimit`.
- On one Arc Pro B65 in an unprivileged LXC container (xe driver), with upstream's launcher every engine start failed with the rlimit error above. With `STRATA_SYCL_MEMLOCK=0` a v0.1.44 engine started (`docker inspect`: no ulimits) and ran Swift 1.5 IQ3_S: pinned host mirror, KV streaming and a 61,052-token prompt worked, 36.8 tok/s decode.

**Not tested:** rootless Docker and Podman themselves (the LXC case is the one we hit), and whether pinned-memory speed differs with the flag on a host that accepts it.

pulls.title: sycl serve: opt-in non-root engine container and read-only data mount
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
**What it changes:** two opt-in settings in `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`, documented in its header:
- `STRATA_SYCL_USER=uid:gid` runs the engine container as that user (`--user`, `HOME=/tmp`) and adds the groups that own `/dev/dri/*` (`--group-add`), so the engine can still open the GPU.
- `STRATA_SYCL_RO=1` mounts the data root at `/work` read-only.

**Why:** the container runs as root with the whole data root (models, packs, the checkout) mounted read-write, though the engine only reads it while serving. With these set, a fault or a bad input in the engine cannot write to the model files or the checkout. docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md also notes the root container stops `gputop` from attributing the engine; a user-owned engine fixes that.

**What it leaves alone:** with neither variable set, the `docker run` arguments are identical to main (checked with a `docker` stub that prints them, sorted, `env -i`). Builds still need a writable mount; this is for serving only. CUDA/HIP untouched.

**How it was checked:**
- The `docker` stub: default identical to main; with `STRATA_SYCL_USER=65534:65534 STRATA_SYCL_RO=1` the arguments gain `--user 65534:65534`, `-e HOME=/tmp`, one `--group-add` per `/dev/dri` group and `<root>:/work:ro`.
- On one Arc Pro B65 (xe driver, render group access through `--group-add`), a v0.1.44 engine built for `bmg-g31` ran Swift 1.5 IQ3_S with `STRATA_SYCL_USER=65534:65534 STRATA_SYCL_RO=1` (`docker inspect`: user `65534:65534`, `/work` with `RW=false`) through every arm of our benchmark runs (36.8 tok/s decode), a 61,052-token prompt (finish `stop`) and a `"parallel": 2` run with four concurrent requests. The same two settings have run in our daily server since 0.1.41; when we turned them on there, decode stayed within run-to-run noise on the same build. We did not repeat that root vs non-root comparison on 0.1.44.

**Not tested:** rootless Docker, Podman, two-card setups.

pulls.title: sycl serve: keep STRATA_API_KEY out of the engine container
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
**What it changes:** one line in `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`: the loop that forwards `STRATA_*` variables into the engine container now skips `STRATA_API_KEY`, the same way it already skips the script's own `STRATA_SYCL_*` settings. The header comment says so.

**Why:** the server takes its key from `STRATA_API_KEY` (#1344, the environment form of `--api-key`). Started that way with the SYCL engine, the server's environment reaches `strata-sycl.sh`, which passes every `STRATA_*` variable on as `docker run -e`. The key then sits in the container's config, readable by anyone who can run `docker inspect strata-sycl-serve` or read the docker command line in `ps`. The engine never reads it; only the Python server checks keys.

**What it leaves alone:** every other forwarded variable, the defaults, the server, and the CUDA/HIP paths. A config's `"api_key"` field never reached the launcher, so nothing changes for it.

**How it was checked:**
- `docker` replaced by a stub that prints its arguments, `env -i` with `STRATA_API_KEY=k` set: on main the argument list holds `-e STRATA_API_KEY=k`; with this change it does not, and every other argument is identical (same sorted list).
- On one Arc Pro B65 (xe driver), the same one-line exclusion has been in our launcher since 0.1.41: the server is started with `STRATA_API_KEY` exported, and `docker inspect` of the engine container shows neither the variable nor the key in its env or command, while the server still answers 401 without the key and 200 with it.

**Not tested:** Windows (the SYCL launcher is Linux-only), two-card setups.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: Tesla P40 (Windows Server 2022 VM), four models at 256K context
pulls.author: vitecopeter
pulls.body:
Community benchmark: one Tesla P40 (sm_61, experimental CUDA 12 engine) in a Windows Server 2022 VM, four models at a 262,144-token context, measured on 2026-10-13 with `BENCH.bat` (`tools/strata_bench.py`, suite 1, 3 runs per test).

Results only: four folders under `bench/results/` and their four rows in `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`, no code changes.

## Machine

- GPU: 1x Tesla P40 24 GB (22 GiB usable), passed through to the VM, TCC mode, driver 582.78; power limit raised to 250 W (`nvidia-smi -pl 250`) for all four runs
- CPU: Xeon E5-2630 v3 @ 2.40 GHz (8 cores / 16 threads, AVX2, no AVX-512, DDR4-1866); the VM has 16 vCPUs on 1 socket and 98 GB RAM
- Hypervisor and OS: Hyper-V; the guest is Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348)
- Storage: model files on a VHDX attached to the VM as an extra drive, on a Samsung 990 PRO 2 TB NVMe in a PCIe-to-M.2 adapter card (host-side Samsung Magician: 3,408 MB/s sequential read, 469K random-read IOPS). The VM had a checkpoint, so the VHDX was a differencing disk (reads go through the checkpoint chain)
- Strata 0.1.43 from the main zip (not a git checkout), ready-made CUDA 12 engine
- Background on the VM during the runs: Task Manager, a PowerShell window with `nvidia-smi`, and a browser with Strata's Monitor page open; the Ollama service on the VM was stopped

## Configuration

Every model was set up with `--context 262144 --vision yes`, 8-bit KV with KV streaming, then tuned with `START-HERE.bat --calibrate` at 250 W before its benchmark. The calibrated values differ per model and are in each report's launch line (all chose `--pcie-frac 1.00` and `--adapt-every 1`; `--spec-min-p` 0.50-0.70, `--adapt-swaps` 80-160).

## Results (medians; ranges and per-request data in each folder)

| Model | Chat decode tok/s | Agent decode tok/s | 4K prompt tok/s | 16K prompt tok/s | Agent turn TTFT (s) | Suite time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Coder IQ1_M | 26.8 | 31.3 | 358.7 | 405.5 | 8.91 | 373 s |
| IQ3_S (ISTA-DASLab) | 21.5 | 26.2 | 344.7 | 396.4 | 9.91 | 420 s |
| UD-IQ4_XS (Unsloth) | 11.9 | 15.8 | 274.2 | 355.8 | 12.83 | 838 s |
| UD-Q4_K_XL (Unsloth) | 9.4 | 11.4 | 244.5 | 333.1 | 14.44 | 949 s |

## Observations

- The two native packs (Coder, IQ3_S) hold all their experts in RAM; the two Unsloth GGUF-in-place packs run with the RAM budget (55 / 70 GiB) and are about half as fast at decode on this CPU.
- Unsloth packs, agent session: the follow-up turns read their new tokens at only 38-73 tok/s (run 1 of each), against 274-356 tok/s for fresh 4K/16K prompts in the same run; the native packs read the same agent turns at 226-335 tok/s. Their first fresh 4K/16K prompt was also slow (UD-IQ4_XS 86.5 / 224.3, UD-Q4_K_XL 84.2 / 195.9 tok/s) before the later runs reached full speed. Not investigated further.
- The UD-IQ4_XS config carries `STRATA_WATCHDOG_S=600` (shown in its report) from an earlier 512K attempt; it only changes the stall watchdog's limit, and no stall happened in these runs.

## Edits to the generated files

`results.json` kept the absolute paths of the model files and the image encoder under the data folder next to the checkout (`<drive>\...\Strata-data\models\...`): the redactor replaces the checkout (`<strata>`), home, temp, user and host, but not that folder. I replaced those five paths with `<strata>\..\Strata-data\...` by hand; nothing else was changed.

## Not tested

Correctness (speed suite only), `--long`, `--clients`, thinking on, contexts above 256K (a 512K start with YaRN stalled at the first prompt chunk on this card; that goes into a separate issue).

pulls.title: qwen35: widen F16 by hand so upload_f32 builds on CUDA 12.1
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
Fixes Niko1221/Strata#2322.

`upload_f32` runs on the host and widens F16 with `__half2float(__ushort_as_half(...))`. `__ushort_as_half` is a `__device__` intrinsic, so on CUDA toolkits that do not have a host form (12.1 and 12.4 per the report) `nvcc` refuses it:

```
src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu:809: calling a __device__ function "__ushort_as_half(unsigned short)" from a __host__ function "upload_f32" is not allowed
```

This widens the bits the way the neighbouring `bf16_to_f32` already does for BF16, so the host path stops naming a device intrinsic and the file compiles on every toolkit.

## Testing

- `scripts/syntax_check.sh src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu` (HIP compat shim) passes; it passed before too, so it is a regression guard here, not a reproduction of the CUDA-only error.
- The conversion itself was checked against a reference for every 16-bit input: `f16_to_f32` matches NumPy's `float16` -> `float32` bit-for-bit across all 65536 values (0 mismatches; NaN treated as a class). That covers the subnormal branch.
- Not run: a real CUDA build (no NVIDIA toolchain here), which is the build the report is about. AGENTS.md asks for builds of touched backends; this is the boundary.

pulls.title: batch-groups: read a cold prompt beside the decoding slots, stall 11.9 -> 0.8 s, same work 6.4% sooner (opt-in)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Related: #2275, #1906 and #1603 (on the pipelined groups every decoding stream stops for a whole prompt read),
and #2050 (the other approach, reads in pieces; this PR does not depend on it).

## Motivation
I run Strata as the backend for coding agents on 2x RTX 5090. Every new agent starts with a long cold prompt, and with
`--batch-groups` > 1 every agent that is already decoding stops until that prompt is read.

vLLM and SGLang avoid this with chunked prefill: a new prompt's chunks share batches with the running requests' decode
steps. #2050 brought the time-sliced form of that here (the read in pieces, taking turns with decode windows), but
every turn drains the pipeline, so the new prompt waits longer, and with a coarse chunk one piece is still about 21 s
of reading (superniker on #2050). Strata's prompt path and its decode windows use different kernels and buffers, so
they cannot share one forward pass, but they can run at the same time on the same GPUs. That is this PR.

## Summary
With `STRATA_PIPED_CONCURRENT=1` (opt-in, experimental) a cold prompt is read on a thread of its own while the slot
groups keep decoding. With the variable unset nothing changes: main's tokens (SHA-256 equal) at main's speed.

On 2x RTX 5090, four streams decoding while a 64K and a 32K cold prompt join:

| | main | this mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| longest pause of a stream | 11.9 s | **0.8 s** |
| the streams' rate while the prompts are read | 2-3 tok/s | **85-92 tok/s** |
| both GPUs busy while the prompts are read | 80% | **88%** |
| **the same work done in** | 26.1-27.1 s | **24.6-25.3 s, 6.4% sooner** |
| the joining prompts' first token | 6.8 / 5.8-5.9 s | 8.1-8.2 / 8.2-8.3 s |
| a one-line question 1 s into a cold 45K read: its first token | 5.7-5.9 s | **1.9 s** |

The whole workload finishes sooner because the GPUs stay busier during a read; on main they sit partly idle while every
stream waits. The price is the joining prompt's own first token, which comes 20-47% later.

![Four decoding streams while two cold prompts join: when each stream was paused, for main, #2050 and this mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuperDistance/Strata/25454236c30540a13b64667604655c6e83b6bf42/cold-joins-main.png)

![The same work, done 6.4% sooner: where the time goes for main and this mode, and how busy the GPUs were while the prompts were read](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuperDistance/Strata/25454236c30540a13b64667604655c6e83b6bf42/same-work-sooner.png)

## How it works
- The read runs on a worker thread. The main thread keeps the groups decoding through the pipeline (`pump`) and takes
  `BSTOP` and `BYIELD` meanwhile.
- Two rules keep it from hanging: the slots' doorbells are served by a thread that never calls CUDA, and nothing is
  allocated or freed on the read's threads (everything is sized before the read starts).
- The windows' streams get the device's highest priority on CUDA.
- A `BYIELD` ends the read at its next chunk, and the part read waits in a slot, as #656's give-way does.
- The stall watchdog stays on for the whole read.
- On Linux the read's threads run off the host thread's core and the pool workers' CPUs (a new thread there inherits
  the host thread's one-core mask; Windows' CPU Sets are not inherited).

<details><summary>Where the two rules come from, and what an independent review found</summary>

Two hangs turned up while building this, both read from the engine's stall dumps against its PDB. Both had #31's
shape: the main thread waited for the CUDA driver's lock in `cudaSetDevice` while the lock's holder waited for the GPU
(a `cudaFree` in the drafter's prompt pass, then cuBLASLt's lazy load of a GEMM module), and a window on that GPU
waited for its doorbell. A doorbell served by a thread that never calls CUDA cannot be held up that way. An independent
review then found five more things, fixed in the third commit: configurations where serving a doorbell does call CUDA
(the mode is now off there), #1996's pinned upload rings growing mid-read (now reserved first), a window that would
never finish going unnoticed, the watchdog switching itself off when the last slot finished mid-read, and a rare race
that could serve a new window with the previous one's row count.

</details>

## How to review
1. `src/program/generate.cpp`, `read_part`: the block under `if (piped && pr_conc && req_imgs.empty())`, then `pump`'s
   two changes (the watchdog during a read, the launch that wakes the doorbell thread).
2. `src/core/verify.cpp`: `batch_serve` is `batch_poll`'s per-layer service moved out unchanged.
3. Everything else enforces the two rules above. `concurrent_read_off` (`batch_read.hpp`, tested in `batch_read_test`)
   lists the configurations where the mode stays off.

## Results
Measured on 2x RTX 5090 (Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, split 25, `--batch 6 --batch-groups 2`), engines built from main `a0116b27`.

- **Against #2050's 32K pieces:** longest pause 0.97 s against 4.6 s (main 12.7 s), and 1,377 stream tokens during the
  reads against 509 (main 293).
- **The same work, sooner:** 6.4% over four runs each, counted only on runs that did the same work; the ranges do not
  overlap.
- **Host RAM and VRAM** (ylzbj1-stack's question on #1906): the read and the decoding now compete. The read gives up
  about a sixth of its speed, the streams keep 22-29% of their rate instead of almost none, and the engine uses 16.6
  cores against 6.3. VRAM stays flat.
- **Exactness:** with the determinism settings, two runs gave byte-identical answers while a 136K prompt was read beside
  a 105K conversation.
- **An hour of randomised load:** 1,723 requests, 1,125 reads beside decoding slots and 558 give-ways, with no stall and
  no error; memory stayed flat.
- **16 GB cards and a weaker host:** the same shape, but the joining prompt pays more (67-109% later on 16 GB cards).
- **Linux** (WSL2 on the same machine, main `ed4773eb`, #2050's bench): a cold 32K join stops the streams 0.7 s against
  6.1-6.5 s on main and 2.9-3.1 s with #2050's 16K pieces, and they emit 925-1,065 tokens during it against 222-229
  and 814-860. The first version kept the read's threads on the host thread's core there (6.1 rows/s on blange48's
  4x RTX 5080); the sixth commit fixes that.
- **In my local testing** (coding agents, first 18 hours): 8,503 requests and 5,052 reads beside decoding slots, with no
  stall and no hang.

<details><summary>Tables and method</summary>

**Against #2050** (a cold 59.6K prompt at 6 s and a 33.7K one at 12 s, the same prompts in every arm):

| | main | #2050, 32K pieces, 400 ms | this mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| longest pause of a stream | 12.7 s | 4.6 s | **0.97 s** |
| the streams' tokens while the prompts are read | 293 | 509 | **1,377** |
| the prompts' first token | 7.3 / 6.6 s | 8.5 / 8.9 s | 9.0 / 9.7 s |

With a second prompt under half the first one's length (72.4K and 28.1K), the long read gives way at its next chunk by
#656's rule, here at 57,344 of 72,368 tokens: the short prompt gained little (7.4 against main's 7.1 s) and the long
one waited for it (17.2 against 8.3 s). A rule that compares what is left to read, as @blange48 carries on #2170, would
skip a give-way that late; that belongs in its own PR.

**The same work, sooner.** The four streams send the same prompts in every run, greedy, and their answers came out the
same length (3,828-3,899 tokens on main, 3,831-3,865 here). Finishing time is the last stream's last token. Order main,
this mode, this mode, main. Both arms decode at about 330 tok/s before the joins; main then stops the streams for about
12.8 s, while this mode keeps them near 90 tok/s through a 15.7 s read, which puts it 1.5-2 s ahead. GPU busy is
`nvidia-smi`'s utilization every 100 ms during the read period. The gain depends on how much of the time is spent
reading; with no reads there is none.

**Host contention** (the cold 64K prompt read alone, then beside the decoding streams; read speeds from the engine's
line for the whole request):

| full config, four streams of 40K | main | #2050, 32K pieces | this mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| the read alone | 8,581 tok/s | 7,442 tok/s | 8,731 tok/s |
| the read beside the streams | 8,606 tok/s (they stop) | 7,418 tok/s (they wait) | 7,331 tok/s (-16%) |
| the streams before / during the read | 345 / 4 tok/s | 348 / 18 tok/s | 303 / 67 tok/s |
| longest pause of a stream | 7.7 s | 4.7 s | **0.48 s** |
| the engine's CPU during the read | 6.3 cores | 4.7 cores | 16.6 cores |

| CPU-bound host (20 GB of each card reserved, experts not resident, AVX2, 6 pool workers), one stream | main | this mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| the read alone | 5,226 tok/s | 5,307 tok/s |
| the read beside the stream | 5,180 tok/s (it stops) | 4,508 tok/s (-15%) |
| the stream before / during the read | 92 / 1.3 tok/s | 93 / 27 tok/s |
| the stream's longest pause | 12.6 s | **0.31 s** |

**16 GB cards** (`--vram-reserve-mib 16600 --kv-resident 16384`): the streams' rate during the reads 0.9 -> 52.9 tok/s,
all four done 70.6 -> 63.8 s, GPUs busy 80% -> 92%, the joining prompts' first token 9.5 / 10.1 -> 15.8 / 21.1 s.
**A weaker host** (16 GB cards, experts from the mapped file, AVX2, 6 pool workers, `--batch 2`): a stream's longest
stop 11.1 -> 0.41 s beside a 64K read and 20.3 -> 0.64 s beside a 127K one, the prompt's first token +4-7%.

**Linux** (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, the same machine and engine, all builds on main `ed4773eb` with #2050's commits applied
for its arm; `piped_read_join_bench.py`'s cold32k, followup and two_joiners; the n-gram table in RAM in every arm, since
WSL's disk reads it about 7x slower; 2-3 runs each):

| | main | #2050, 16K pieces | this mode, first version | this mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| cold32k: longest stream stop | 6.1-6.5 s | 2.9-3.1 s | 0.8-0.9 s | **0.7 s** |
| cold32k: the joining prompt's first token | 5.8-6.1 s | 9.6-10.0 s | 8.2-8.6 s | 7.0-7.3 s |
| cold32k: stream tokens during the join | 222-229 | 814-860 | 454-484 | **925-1,065** |
| followup: a short prompt 1 s into a cold 45K read, its first token | 6.4-6.6 s | 2.7 s | 1.7-1.8 s | **1.6-2.0 s** |
| two_joiners: longest stream stop | 15.6-15.9 s | 5.9-6.0 s | 1.7-2.0 s | **1.2-1.6 s** |
| two_joiners: stream tokens during the joins | 303-313 | 1,460-1,559 | 664-718 | **1,796-2,046** |

The slots decoded 24-37 rows/s during a 30K+ read with the first version and 95-127 with the fix.

**Exactness.** With the usual settings near-tie tokens flip a little more often than on main (the prompt path borrows
some of the decode's GPU expert slots, and those experts run on the CPU kernels, which round differently). With
`--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --prompt-cache 0 --no-prefill-borrow` this mode's two runs were byte-identical for all
three answers; release's two runs with the same settings still differed. In `batch_interleave_test.py --long 40000`
every request equaled its solo tokens in two runs of three; the third had a near tie that flips on main as well. With
the variable unset, six greedy answers' SHA-256 equal main's in two engine starts each.

**Load.** The hour: four streams, cold joins of 4-128K every 4-15 s, short questions, follow-ups, clients leaving
mid-read; GPU0's VRAM grew 82 MiB over 80 minutes (in my local testing an engine grew 44 MiB in its first hours and
then held). My local testing ran v0.1.43 with #2050 and this ported; against the 20 hours before it on #2050's pieces,
the slowest tenth of long reads fell from 15.8 to 7.5 s, but the workload differed, so that is not a controlled A/B.

</details>

## Costs and limits
- The joining prompt's first token comes 20-47% later (67-109% on 16 GB cards).
- The read is about 15% slower beside decoding streams, and the engine uses more of the host (16.6 cores against 6.3).

pulls.title: --batch: keep system-prompt roots apart from the conversations (--prompt-cache-roots, opt-in)
pulls.author: brocktice
pulls.body:
## Why

We serve an agent client whose every chat opens with the same ~79K-token system prompt and tool list, on `parallel: 4` with `--batch-mtp` and `--conversation-cache-mib 8192`. Its chats overlap with other traffic all day, and every new chat read the whole opening again (20-35 s) although the engine had read the same tokens minutes before.

The cause is in `--batch`. The root checkpoint (the end of the system prompt, PR #65) lives in the main session's chain, but:

- a slot keeps only its turn checkpoint (the deepest one) at admission;
- a request that continues from a slot clears the main chain and takes over that one checkpoint;
- the next park then drops the older parked copies that still held the root (#342's `drop_superseded`).

After a few turns of any chat nothing holds the root any more. Solo traffic does not show it: a request that runs alone stays on the main session and its chain stays whole.

## What it does

`--prompt-cache-roots N` (default 0 = off, every path unchanged) keeps a copy of the last N roots the engine made, apart from any conversation (one per distinct system prompt, ~118 MB of RAM each; least recently made or used leaves first). A root's state depends on its tokens alone, so:

- **main session:** at a request's start, and after a slot or a parked conversation was restored, a kept root goes back into the chain (at its front, where retention pins it) when the session's cells hold its tokens and the prompt starts with them;
- **idle slot:** a kept root whose tokens an idle slot holds is a source like the slot's own checkpoints: the slot's K/V up to the root is copied back and the root's state restored;
- **#879** (non-finite logits) drops the kept roots with everything else.

Because the main chain keeps its root again, parked conversations keep it too, so a new chat also mounts through a parked one.

## Tests

`conv_cache_test` covers the store (kept, refreshed, the least recently used one leaves, other images or control-vector mode do not match, clear).

**Real engine:** v0.1.43 on one RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `parallel: 4`, `--batch-mtp`, `--conversation-cache-mib 8192`. A 42K-token system prompt; chat A three turns, a request with another system prompt, chat B two turns, chat C. Greedy, the same requests with the flag off and on:

| | flag off | flag on |
|---|---|---|
| sequential (no overlap) | new chats reuse 42,146 tokens | the same |
| two other requests always decoding: new chat B (`--prompt-cache-roots 2`) | **0 reused, 11.6 s** | **42,146 reused, 0.8 s** |
| parking off (`--conversation-cache-mib 0`), the root only in an idle slot: new chat B (`--prompt-cache-roots 8`) | **0 reused, 7.9 s** | **42,146 reused, 0.8 s** |

Answers were identical between the arms except one 600-token answer decoded beside another request; that one also differs between two runs with the flag off (batched greedy decode is not run-to-run identical).

N matters: in the last scenario with N = 2, a third system prompt pushed the 42K root out before chat B came, so we run 8.

**In use:** v0.1.43 plus this change has run with `--prompt-cache-roots 8` on two RTX PRO 6000s for about 8 hours of mixed agent, chat and tool traffic (about 2,800 requests, no errors); new chats of that client now reuse their shared opening.

**Builds:** the measurements above are from this change on v0.1.43. Rebased on current `main`, it builds for CUDA (sm_120) and CTest passes (`conv_cache_test` included) except `ple_parity`, which needs a Q2_0 model file I do not have. I could not build HIP or SYCL (no toolchain here). The change is host-only C++ in `src/program/generate.cpp` and `conv_cache.hpp`; the SYCL `generate.cpp` includes the header but does not use the new class (the header also compiles alone with g++ `-Wall -Wextra`).

**Default path:** with the flag at 0 the store is empty and every new branch is skipped: `seed_root`, the slot lookup and `keep` all test `enabled()` or `prompt_cache_roots` first, so no checkpoint, copy or log line differs.

Related: #1529 keeps the root in the disk tier's spilled files. This change is the RAM side under `--batch` and does not touch the disk tier.

Happy to change the shape (a default other than 0, or keeping the roots inside the conversation cache's budget).

pulls.title: route-resident: support 256-expert top-8 models (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
pulls.author: atomicmilkshake
pulls.body:
### Summary

Generalizes the opt-in \STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT\ kernel and verifier guard from 512/10 models to also support 256-expert top-8 models (\qwen35moe\ / Qwen3.6-35B-A3B).

Follows Ethan's warp-reduction rewrite (#1737) and separates out the 256/8 portion previously included in #1820 into a clean, standalone change on top of upstream \main\.

### Details

1. **Kernel parameterization (\src/kernels/cuda/native_router.cu\)**:
   - Templates \oute_resident_impl<NE, K>\ across warp-multiple expert counts. Both 512 and 256 are multiples of 32, so the \__shfl_down_sync\ reduction tree stays convergent across lanes.
   - Retains the original \oute_resident_k\ (512/10) CUDA symbol and entry point, and instantiates \oute_resident_geometry_k<256, 8>\ for Qwen geometries.
   - Restricts buffer writes (\weights\, \id\, \stats\) to lane 0, eliminating redundant warp writes.
   - Maintains a backward-compatible 10-argument \
ative_route_resident\ overload so existing 512/10 call sites (\src/core/mtp.cpp\, metal stubs) continue without change.

2. **Verifier & Configuration (\src/core/verify.cpp\)**:
   - Zero-based tail ranks default to \5-7\ for 256/8 and \6-9\ for 512/10 unless overridden by \STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT_RANKS=lo-hi\.
   - Widens the launch guard to \(NE == 512 && K == 10) || (NE == 256 && K == 8)\.

3. **Parity Test (\src/kernels/route_resident_parity.cu\)**:
   - Generalizes the test against scalar reference implementations for both \512/10\ and \256/8\ geometries.
   - Passes with 0 mismatches across 240 synthetic cases for each geometry (480 total cases), verifying bit-for-bit ID and counter parity, and weights within 0 ulp.

### Context

Extracted from #1820 per maintainer single-change guideline. Validated on 0.1.42 (+9.7% decode / -13.1% window on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B).

pulls.title: bench: Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL two-host RTX 5090/3090 rerun and quality checks
pulls.author: petria
pulls.body:
## Summary

New 2026-10-13 results for Unsloth Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **UD-Q4_K_XL** on an RTX 5090 coordinator and RTX 3090 prefix worker in **two separate Linux hosts**. This is a rerun of the model reported in #2166, not a different model or an update to that PR.

The deployment uses Strata 0.1.43 plus our retained custom stage-RPC changes; this PR **does not add RPC support to upstream**.

## Configuration and method

- 196,608 context, INT8 GPU-resident KV, 24/24 layers, fixed 2048 prefill, resident experts, MTP4/minimum probability .5 and retained suffix lookup.
- Worker/coordinator VRAM reserves 4096/1000 MiB; CPU pools 11/31; one active sequence. Vision enabled but not exercised.
- Frozen, unchanged upstream tools and public corpus at `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`; 517 consumed source inputs and all 14 coding-fixture files verified against that commit.
- Both-node telemetry begins before the first request; optional disabled request monitoring no longer causes a sampling gap.

## Results

- Built-in speed suite: **36/36 measured requests**, three repeats, four excluded warm-up/calibration requests. Chat decode median **66.4 tok/s**; fresh 4K/16K/32K prefill **1177.2 / 1362.8 / 1399.1 tok/s**; agent-cache follow-up decode **81.1 tok/s**.
- Unchanged repository recall test: **6/6**, 32K/128K targets at depths 10/50/90, fixed seed 7, reasoning off.
- Three existing RX 9060 XT community TypeScript fixtures through nine fresh ephemeral Codex sessions with medium reasoning: **9/9 attempts passed**. Independent read-only, network-disabled acceptance checks: **243/243**, representing **81 distinct cases repeated three times**.
- **65 completed tool calls**; no failed agent turns, timeouts or scope violations. One nonzero shell exit was `git status` in a non-Git fixture, not a backend or acceptance failure.
- Quality collection: **76 native requests**, **3,315,714 prompt tokens**, **2,138,255 reused**, **22,678 generated** including reasoning/tool serialization; weighted fresh prefill **1313.8 tok/s**, decode **76.4 tok/s**, draft acceptance **73.03%**. These are separate from the reasoning-off speed summaries.
- **100 speed + 601 quality telemetry samples**, no collector errors. Worker inference-process sampled VRAM peak **15.91 GiB**, below the 20-GiB guard; desktop allocations are reported separately.

## Comparison and limitations

The worker automatic expert cache is now **3522 slots / 10526 MiB**, versus **4110 / 12292 MiB** in #2166; desktop load and generated answers also differ. The report includes the original Unsloth speed comparison and retained GSQ IQ3_S shared-workload raw data, with the 128K/16+32 versus 192K/24+24 differences explicit. This is not an isolated model-quality, hardware A/B or RPC-overhead claim.

Only repository-provided speed/recall/coding fixtures were run: no gistfile1/fable or custom challenge. Visible acceptance tests, three small coding fixtures, adaptive/warm cache, no vision/concurrency/cold-cache/full-192K quality assessment. NIC counters include other interface traffic. Peaks are sampled lower bounds.

The custom engine source/binaries are not distributed, so upstream base alone cannot reproduce network RPC. Replay scripts assume a compatible existing deployment. An initial missing remote workload-directory preflight issued zero inference requests; corrected/verified staging preceded the published run and its failed preflight archive remains private.

## Validation and contents

Only `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-rtx5090-rtx3090-stage-rpc-unsloth-udq4-rerun/` is added: report, per-request results, both-node telemetry, configs/provenance, generated source, acceptance/tool logs and replay scripts.

- All native request/token/timing/draft records reconcile with boundary counters.
- Engine configurations, binaries, source/diff identities and service invocations stayed unchanged throughout the tests.
- Instructions/tests preserved; source-only scope and helper usage reviewed; generated bytes/CRLF and hashes preserved.
- Offline collector/redaction/accounting regressions pass; public JSON/JSONL, relative links, Python/shell syntax, privacy and results-only diff checked. Git whitespace checks use `cr-at-eol` for preserved Windows-origin CRLF.
- No models, packs, executables, TLS keys, credentials, private addresses, request bodies or personal sessions included. Existing #2166 is unchanged.

pulls.title: SYCL verify: batch windows keep the doorbell nodes under the lean window ("parallel" crashed on a B70)
pulls.author: aangelinsf
pulls.body:
## Title

Issue: none filed. I searched open and closed issues and PRs (about 20 queries, including the control query "Arc Pro B70") and found no report of this crash. Nearest: #1762 (`--batch 2` on a B65: non-finite residuals and a stall, not a segfault), #1721, #776 / #845 (the all-resident counterpart in the batch path), #1118.

## Summary

On the SYCL port, `"parallel": 2` crashes the engine the first time two requests share a decode window, on v0.1.43.1 (`a0116b27`) and on main / v0.1.44 (`ed4773eb`). The 0.1.43 "lean verify window" (`46a77907`) drops the doorbell nodes from batch windows, and the host batch path still waits for them. The fix is one condition in `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`: batch windows keep their doorbells, solo windows stay lean.

## What changed

`sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`: add `&& !batch_rec_` to the `lean` condition in `record_window()`, plus a comment saying why. That is the whole diff.

I kept it conservative: batch windows keep their doorbells even on an all-resident stage, where lean would be harmless, because a captured batch graph is reused across windows. A narrower condition is your call.

## Extra Notes

**The crash.** One Arc Pro B70, `"parallel": 2`, first time two requests share a window:

    strata verify: captured the batch window over slots 0,1
    terminate called after throwing an instance of 'sycl::_V1::exception'
      what():  level_zero backend failed with error: 37 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED)
    [strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 139) ... verify batch: layer 0 never rang (graph finished)

It reproduced 6 times out of 6, with `--spec 4`, `--spec 2` and `--batch-mtp`. A single slot was fine, and so was `"parallel": 2` with requests sent one after another.

**Cause.** The lean window drops the doorbell publish, the flag waits and the plan copy, because no host answers them. `capture_batch()` records batch windows through the same `record_window()` with `batch_rec_` set, so batch graphs were recorded lean too. The host batch path (`run_slot_rows` / `batch_poll`) still waits for each layer's doorbell unless the stage is all-resident. On a stage with mirrored experts the graph finishes with the ring silent. `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN=00` on the stock build makes the crash go away, which confirms this.

**Setup.** Arc Pro B70 32 GB (8086:e223), xe driver, Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0. `strata-sycl-dev` image: oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.0, compute-runtime 26.35.39758.10, Level Zero 1.32.0, AOT `bmg-g31`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS native pack on one GPU, 17,234 of 24,576 expert slots in VRAM and the rest mirrored. Engine args: `--stream-experts --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ... --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 110000 --prefill 4096 --vram-reserve-mib 2048`. Launcher defaults `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1 STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`.

**Control and soak (new).** A long run of two real coding agents did not help here: their requests rarely decode at the same time, so the batch-window path went unexercised. So I wrote a small harness (stdlib Python, about 250 lines) that forces the overlap: two streaming requests started together, 5 scenarios cycled (two overlapping 400-token decodes; two concurrent ~13k-token prompts; staggered starts; one client hanging up mid-stream; a long prompt against a short one). It fails a run if the engine dies, restarts or logs a crash line, and also if the two-sequence path never ran, which it detects as interleaved `BT <slot> <token>` lines from both slots (the one-time "captured the batch window" line rotates out of the log).

| Build | Run | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Stock v0.1.43.1 (`a0116b27`), same flags | first overlapped pair | engine died within 2 s: `layer 0 never rang (graph finished)`, exit 139 |
| This patch | 10 rounds | 10/10, 1,909 slot-interleave transitions, 0 crash lines |
| This patch | 20-minute soak | 72/72, 13,954 slot-interleave transitions, 0 crash lines, no restart |
| This patch, after swapping back from the stock build | 10 rounds | 10/10, 1,934 interleave transitions, 0 crash lines |

Two concurrent 400-token decodes finish in about 13 s; two concurrent ~13k-token prompts in 20 s and 34 s. I can attach the harness if it is useful.

**Equivalence.** On main (v0.1.44): stock still crashes with `"parallel": 2`; with this patch there is no crash, and `tools/batch_test.py --batch 2 --n 2 --max-new 64 --extra "--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000" --dump` is **byte-identical** to the stock build with `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN=00`, with and without `--batch-mtp`. `--batch-mtp` runs: two slot drafters load, and two streams decode at 63–65 tok/s there.

**Solo vs batch parity (pre-existing, not changed by this PR).** On this card batch tokens still differ from solo at the same positions: slot 0 at token 6 and slot 1 at token 38, and they differ in exactly the same way on the stock build with `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN=00`, like the B65 report in #1721. The text stays coherent. In my own overlap harness, batched text was also about 10% shorter than solo for three prompts (first differing character at 64, 88 and 165). I did **not** measure those prompts on stock with lean off, so I can't say whether that length difference is the same pre-existing behavior.

**Speed (v0.1.43.1 with the same one-line change).** One stream decodes ~73 tok/s; two batched streams decode 66 tok/s from the first batch token, or 82 tok/s with `--batch-mtp`. Two real coding agents at once, wall time per run: single slot 52–57 s (4 runs); `parallel: 2` 26–57 s, mean 38 s (5 runs); `parallel: 2` + `--batch-mtp` 33–55 s, mean 38 s (5 runs). Most of the gain comes from each slot keeping its own conversation cache instead of re-reading ~12k tokens on every switch. Single-slot behavior is unchanged: solo windows are still lean, and ran ~4% faster than with `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN=00`.

**Side note: the launcher drops `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN=0`.** `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` treats a value of exactly `0` as "not set" and doesn't pass it into the container. `STRATA_VERIFY_LEAN` is on by default and turned off by a leading `0`, so `0` never reaches the engine; I had to use `00` to A/B. It's not needed after this fix, but it's worth documenting or special-casing for switches that default on.

pulls.title: KV cache: FP16 sliding window + attention sinks, and an optional 2-bit K / 4-bit V cache scheme (--kv q2k) [EXPERIMENTAL]
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
# KV cache: FP16 sliding window + attention sinks, and an optional 2-bit K / 4-bit V cache scheme (`--kv q2k`) [EXPERIMENTAL]

> **Status: experimental.** Opt-in only (`--kv q2k`, `--kv-window N`, `--kv-k-gain B`); default behavior is unchanged when the flags are off. It needs more testing before it can be considered production-ready: the behavioral and long-context runs below are single-model, single-document measurements, and the window-1024 anomaly is unexplained.

## Summary

Two composable KV-cache features behind opt-in flags, plus a correction that makes them work together:

1. **`--kv-window N` (`--kv-sink S`)** — an FP16 overlay over the first `S` cells (attention sinks) and the most recent `N` cells of the quantized KV bulk. Those cells read exact; the rest stays quantized. Costs 304 KiB per layer at N=128, S=8 including 16 slack slots (3.56 MiB for 12 layers).
2. **`--kv q2k`** — a cache format storing **K at 2 bits with per-channel scales and V at 4 bits per token (q4_0)**: 448 B/cell vs q4_0's 576 B (−22%), 4.6× smaller than FP16 (2048 B).
3. **`--kv-k-gain B`** (q2/q2k) — a K reconstruction gain: the stored K scale is `B` × the rule's, the codes are unchanged. It undoes the 2-bit codebook's score shrink, which is what made the window *hurt* q2k. Zero extra bytes.

**Recommended with q2k: `--kv-window 256 --kv-sink 8 --kv-k-gain 1.10`** — decode-path KL −36.8% vs plain q2k (8 of 9 texts) for +6.6 MiB.

> **Correction to the previous revision (run-to-run variance).** The last revision said greedy decode is not run-to-run reproducible "under QSA top-k tie-breaks and atomic partial-group KV writes" and reported decode-path numbers as 5-run means. That diagnosis was wrong, and the cause was our measurement setup: **we did not have the prefill CPU share turned off.** For prompt chunks under 1024 tokens the prefill hands part of the MoE expert work to the CPU, and that split changes from run to run — a 730-token prompt's logits differed by up to 6.8 between two identical runs. With `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` two runs are bit-identical (129 teacher-forced decode rows, max |diff| 0; a second forced FP16 run scores KL 0.0000 against the first on all nine texts below). Every number in this revision was measured that way, and the 512-token logits table was re-measured (it moved by up to 2.5 points of top-1). The earlier decode-path comparison also used a greedy reference, which speculatively drafts multi-token windows and so does not produce rows comparable to the arms'; the decode numbers below use a teacher-forced FP16 reference instead.

Every directional claim below carries the number that pins it; the gate (`kv_q2_parity`) reproduces the attention-error tables from a real KV dump.

## Why this shape

### The bit-allocation rule came from the real cache, not the synthetic one

Measured with the gate's attention-output probe (relative RMS of attention output vs an FP16 cache) on a real stored KV cache dumped from a live serve (`--dump-kv`; 864 cells, 2 KV heads × 256 dims, rotated as stored), layer 3 unless stated:

| arm | B/cell/head | attention error |
|---|---:|---:|
| q4_0 (reference) | 288 | 0.888% |
| **K 2-bit per-channel + V 4-bit (`q2k`)** | **224** | **1.911%** |
| K 4-bit + V 2-bit per-channel | 224 | 3.171% |
| K 2-bit + V 2-bit per-channel (symmetric q2) | 160 | 3.508% |
| K per-channel + V per-token, both 2-bit (KIVI's placement) | 160 | 5.188% |

At equal bytes (224 B), **the bits belong on V**: K2c+V4 beats K4+V2c on every real layer measured (table below). On the synthetic gate cache the ranking is the reverse (K looks more sensitive) — synthetic data has no channel structure, which is why no ranking here is taken from it.

The mechanism: V's quantization error enters the output directly through `softmax(qKᵀ)·V`, while much of K's error is common-mode across cells and cancels in the softmax normalization (`docs/kv-q2.md`). Both published intuitions survive, scoped:

- **K's outliers are channel-aligned** (KIVI's premise) — true on real layers (K channel RMS max/median 5.8× on L3 up to 74.9× on L47), and honored by the per-channel K scale, not by more bits.
- **V is the tensor the output feels** — so V gets 4 bits while K takes 2.

### Why per-channel K and per-token V

Per-channel K scales (`block_q2c_0`: one fp16 scale per dimension per 32-cell group, a 4-level Lloyd-Max codebook) absorb K's channel outliers. V reuses the existing q4_0 path (per-token blocks), so the format adds no new V quantizer. KIVI's 2-bit per-token V loses on this cache: the Hadamard rotation leaves V's channel structure in place (V channel RMS max/median 7.9–14.5×), so 2-bit V would want per-channel scales too — at 4 bits per token, V carries q4_0's own error.

### Why the FP16 window — and why q2k needs the gain to use it

The window is a separate, format-agnostic device. It only acts at decode: prompt-mode (prefill) logits never read the overlay, which is why the previous revision measured "no logit precision" — that was a blind spot of the measurement, not a property of the window.

- At decode it helps q4_0: **−19.6%** KL (7 of 9 texts).
- With q2k alone it **hurts: +10.3%** (4 of 9 better). The 4-level Lloyd-Max K codebook is MSE-optimal, so its reconstruction is shrunk: on real queries q2k's attention scores come out at **0.92–0.97×** the exact ones (q4_0: 0.997–0.998). Next to exact window cells that is a bias — the exact cells out-score the shrunk bulk, and the softmax over-weights the window by **+1.7..+5.9%** of its mass on 11 of 12 layers.
- **`--kv-k-gain`** stores the K scale `B` × larger while choosing the codes against the un-gained scale, so no value moves to another level and only the reconstruction grows. With B = 1.10 the window turns into a gain: **−29.3%** at 128 cells, **−36.8%** at 256 (vs plain q2k).
- Behaviorally the window recovers **symmetric q2's** short-answer loss (q2 2/3 → q2 + window 3/3); q2k matches the q4_0 reference on the recall probe without it (3/3).

## Measurements

### Gate (device kernels vs host reference)

- `kv_q2_parity`: synthetic cache 40/40 checks (incl. the K-gain pin: stored scale = B × the rule, bit for bit, codes chosen against the un-gained scale); real cache layers 3/11/23/47 36/36 each. The q2k device arm (real append + gather kernels) lands on the host row: L3 1.910% device vs 1.911% host.
- `kv_window_parity`: 10/10 — sink and window cells read bit-exactly equal to an FP16 pool; cells outside read the bulk pool bit-for-bit; `kv_window_restore` reproduces the bulk dequantization.
- `kv_q4_parity`, `kv_q8_parity`, `kv_stream_parity`, `kv_hybrid_parity`: pass (existing formats untouched).

### Attention error by layer (real cache)

| layer | K channel spread | q4_0 | **q2k (K2c+V4)** | K4+V2c | q2 (K2c+V2c) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| L3 | 5.8× | 0.888% | **1.911%** | 3.171% | 3.508% |
| L11 | 5.9× | 0.740% | **2.002%** | 2.589% | 3.471% |
| L23 | 14.2× | 0.941% | **2.211%** | 2.768% | 3.655% |
| L47 | 74.9× | 1.040% | **1.645%** | 2.663% | 2.948% |

The outlier layer (L47) is where q2k comes closest to q4_0.

### Attention error under the engine's append patterns (real cache)

The row above appends every cell in one call — whole 32-cell groups — so it never runs the partial-group scale rule. The engine does, every request: speculative verify appends 2–5-cell windows that cross group boundaries, decode appends into the group the prompt ended in, and after a reused conversation prefix the 2048-cell prefill chunks fall mid-group. `kv_q2_parity` now replays those patterns on the same K/V and readers (attention output vs FP16). Three scale rules for a group first written by a partial batch: **old** = the pre-review kernel (sum / 32), **/n** = RMS of the n cells, **shrink** = shipped (full-group RMS, the previous group's mean square standing in for the cells not yet written):

| layer | q4_0 | q2k one-shot | spec verify (3-cell windows) old / /n / shrink | chunked prefill (100-cell chunks, stress) old / /n / shrink | prompt + decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| L3 | 0.888% | 1.910% | 1.978% / 1.912% / **1.892%** | 3.631% / 2.076% / 2.186% | 1.910% |
| L11 | 0.740% | 2.002% | 2.030% / 2.011% / 2.012% | 3.617% / 2.727% / **2.626%** | 2.002% |
| L23 | 0.941% | 2.211% | 2.895% / 2.667% / **2.245%** | 3.767% / 2.509% / **2.161%** | 2.211% |
| L47 | 1.040% | 1.648% | 1.457% / 1.799% / **1.720%** | 1.438% / 1.346% / 1.803% | 1.648% |

- Speculative verify (what every decode does at each group boundary): the excess over one-shot, summed over the four layers, is +8.0% with `/n` and **+1.3% with shrink**.
- Chunked prefill is a stress case (real chunks are 2048 cells, aligned from position 0): shrink is mixed by layer there (1.4% worse summed than `/n`) and 30% better than the pre-review kernel.
- Prompt + decode lands exactly on the one-shot row (pinned). On the extreme-outlier layer 47 an undersized scale acts as clipping, which is why the pre-review kernel measures better there.

### Logits (512-token prompts, prompt mode, vs FP16: top-1 agreement / mean KL) — re-measured with the CPU share off

| text | q4_0 | q2 | **q2k** |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | 90.4% / 0.060 | 74.6% / 0.329 | **77.1% / 0.226** |
| document | 91.6% / 0.030 | 81.2% / 0.203 | **83.8% / 0.133** |
| chat | 92.4% / 0.027 | 81.2% / 0.177 | **83.4% / 0.144** |

q2k's KL is 3.8–5.3× q4_0's at the prompt level: it is a cheaper format, not a lossless one. (The previous revision's table, measured with the CPU share on, read 2.5–5×.)

### Decode path (teacher-forced decode, 9 texts, vs FP16)

Every arm is fed the same 128-token continuation, one token per window, and each row is compared with a forced FP16 run's row at the same position. Nine texts: three built-in prompts (chat, document, code agent) and six repo files up to 6144 tokens. A second FP16 run scores KL 0.0000 against the reference on all nine. Change = geometric mean over the texts vs plain q2k, with the texts that improved.

| arm | mean KL | top-1 | vs q2k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| q4_0 | 0.0198 | 96.6% | −89.9% (9/9) |
| q4_0 + window 128 | 0.0174 | 96.9% | −91.9% (9/9) |
| q2k | 0.1825 | 88.5% | |
| q2k + window 128 | 0.2060 | 87.3% | +10.3% (4/9) |
| q2k + window 128 + gain 1.10 | 0.1338 | 89.8% | −29.3% (7/9) |
| **q2k + window 256 + gain 1.10** | **0.1203** | **90.3%** | **−36.8% (8/9)** |

Gain sweep at window 128 (same texts, development build): 1.03 −9%, 1.05 −15%, 1.08 −26%, 1.10 −30%, 1.13 −29%; the gain alone, with no exact cells, −1%. Even the best q2k setting keeps ~6× q4_0's decode KL.

These rows were measured on this PR's build with a temporary copy of our teacher-forced decode tooling (`--force-tokens` + a per-window logits dump; not part of this PR). The PR build's prompt logits are byte-identical to our development build's under the same flags (`--kv q2k`, and `--kv q2k --kv-window 256 --kv-sink 8 --kv-k-gain 1.10`). The two builds sit on different upstream bases, and their decode rows differ slightly for every quantized format — plain q4_0 included — but never for FP16, so the development build's numbers are not quoted as this PR's.

### Behavioral A/B (~5K-token buried-fact probe, `tools/kv_recall_report.py`)

Eight vault codes buried in a document: **mid** = the body; **late** = the last few paragraphs (~180–350 tokens before generation: outside a 128-cell window, inside a 512/1024 one). Scored by the instructed (vault, code) pair. Release q4_0 is the shipped binary; every other arm is this branch.

| arm | mid | late | short answers | decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| release q4_0 (reference) | 4/4 | 4/4 | 3/3 | 158.3 t/s |
| q4_0 (this branch) | 4/4 | 4/4 | 3/3 | 159.0 t/s |
| q2 (symmetric) | 4/4 | 4/4 | **2/3** | 134.6 t/s |
| **q2k (no window)** | 4/4 | 4/4 | **3/3** | 137.5 t/s |

q2k matches the q4_0 reference on every measure at 22% less

pulls.title: Monitor: one line per card on a layer split (load, VRAM, temperature, power, PCIe)
pulls.author: kennuardo
pulls.body: Issue: none (related: #2001 is about the Intel reader picking the wrong card; this is about the charts on a layer split) ## Summary On a two-card layer split the Monitor tab's sparklines show one series per tile (mean load, total VRAM and power, the hottest temperature, the first card's PCIe traffic), so the charts cannot say which card is working. With this change the GPU load, VRAM, GPU temp, Power and PCIe tiles draw GPU 0 as today and GPU 1 as a dashed second line on the same scale, and the tiles' subtext names the cards ("RTX 5070 Ti 72% · RTX 5060 Ti 26%"). One card: nothing changes, on the server or on the page. ## What changed - `serve/telemetry.py`: with more than one card, `_loop` also records each card's own `gpu_util`, `gpu_mem_used`, `gpu_temp`, `gpu_power`, `gpu_pcie_rx_mb` in the same 60-sample history, and the `gpus` entries carry `pcie_rx_mb` / `pcie_tx_mb` (the reader already read them; they were only summed). Single card: no new keys. - `serve/web/app.js`: `sparkPair()` draws GPU 0 (solid line + area) and GPU 1 (dashed) on one scale when the per-card series exist, else falls back to `spark()` exactly as before. The per-card subtext uses short card names split from `hardware_static.gpu_name` (vendor prefix dropped, falls back to `GPU ` when the names and the card count disagree), one card per side of the tile with the value in bold; the Power and PCIe tiles get the per-card subtext the other tiles already had. - `serve/web/app.css`: the second line in `--st-info`; the per-card subtext as a flex row. ## Extra Notes - Measured on an RTX 5070 Ti + RTX 5060 Ti layer split, Linux, engine 0.1.43.1: `/metrics` grows by five 60-sample series per card (about 3 KB); the sampler does no new reads. - Default path: with one card the history keys, the `gpus` entries and the rendered tiles are the same as before (`sparkPair` returns to `spark()` when `gpu1_*` is absent). - Touches the same PCIe tile as #2272; both apply, the conflict is a few lines in `render()`. - Checked: the serve test suite, `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p "test_*.py" -t .` on this branch and on `main` at a0116b2: `Ran 725 tests ... OK (skipped=11)` on both (Linux, Python 3.14). The page was checked by hand on the two-card split (screenshot) and reads the same as before with one card (the per-card series are absent, `sparkPair` falls back to `spark`).
