pulls.title: docker: complete deployment bundle with a management console
pulls.author: jazzlee008
pulls.body:
## Summary

Adds `docker/` — a self-contained deployment bundle for Strata: the engine
image, an nginx TLS + authorization entry point, and a FastAPI manager serving
a monitoring console and recording inference metrics.

The upstream repo already ships a root-level `Dockerfile` and
`docker-entrypoint.sh` for a single inference container. This adds the pieces
around it that a shared or long-running deployment needs: a gateway that
terminates TLS and checks credentials, a manager that exposes metrics and
lets you manage keys, and a Compose file that wires the three together.

## What's included

```
docker/
├── docker-compose.yml     three services: nginx / manager / strata
├── Dockerfile             engine image (compiled from the Strata sources)
├── Dockerfile.nginx       gateway image
├── nginx.conf             TLS + auth_request + SSE/WebSocket forwarding
├── manager/               FastAPI console (app.py, Dockerfile, static/)
├── scripts/               cert generation, key bootstrap, build-context prep
└── tests/                 i18n coverage check
```

Only `nginx` publishes a host port. `manager` and `strata` are reachable on the
internal network only, so the engine never depends on its own authorization.

## The stack

| Service | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `nginx` | The only external entry point. TLS termination, `auth_request` authorization, SSE and WebSocket forwarding |
| `manager` | System metrics (SQLite), inference metrics, API key store, user sessions, container lifecycle, web shell, console UI |
| `strata` | The CUDA inference engine. GPU-exclusive, internal network only |

## Design notes worth reviewing

**The build context is assembled by a script.** The engine Dockerfile contains
`COPY . .`, so a build needs the full source tree. Pointing the build context at
the repository root would also send sibling secrets (TLS private keys, API key
files) to the Docker daemon, even though they are never copied into the image.
`scripts/prepare-build.sh` copies the sources plus this directory's Dockerfile
into a clean `.build-context/`, so the context never contains credentials.

**The console is bilingual.** English by default; Chinese when the browser asks
for it; a header button overrides the choice. Runtime-generated strings go
through `t()`, the rest are translated by walking the DOM on load.
`node tests/i18n-coverage.js` builds a DOM from the real `index.html`, runs
`applyLang()`, and fails if any Chinese text survives — it currently reports 0.

**WebSockets authorize themselves.** `/ws/` deliberately bypasses nginx
`auth_request`: the subrequest does not inherit the original query string, so
`?api_key=` (the only way a browser can carry a credential on a WebSocket)
cannot be verified at that layer. The manager's WebSocket endpoints check the
session cookie or the query parameter instead.

**Shell access is opt-in.** The terminal tab does not connect on load; it
requires an explicit click on *Connect*, shows a status indicator, and
disconnecting terminates the shell session.

**This Dockerfile tracks the upstream one.** Same build logic, with two local
adjustments: China-friendly apt/PyPI mirrors, and removal of the `# syntax`
directive (it makes BuildKit fetch a frontend image from docker.io). Both are
easy to drop; CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to re-sync from upstream.

## Verification

Built and run on an RTX 4090 (24 GB) with `IQ3_S`, 256K context, vision
enabled:

- `docker compose config` — clean
- `docker compose up -d --build` — all three containers reach `healthy`
- Unauthenticated `/api/*` and `/v1/*` → 401; UI shell, `/health` open
- `node tests/i18n-coverage.js` → 0 untranslated strings
- Inference: 125B MoE, ~100 tok/s steady state, 256K context loaded

## Known limitations

Happy to take feedback on any of these:

1. **The web shell runs as root.** It requires an explicit connect click, but
   command auditing, session timeouts and a non-root user are not implemented.
2. **The engine is single-slot**, so concurrent requests queue. This is the
   engine's design, not something the bundle introduces.
3. **System metrics are sampled every 10 seconds** (`SAMPLE_INTERVAL`).
4. **Self-signed TLS.** Clients must trust the certificate manually. ACME or
   mounting an externally issued certificate would be a natural next step.
5. **`prepare-build.sh` is a shell script.** It could be a `make` target or a
   Compose-native mechanism if the project prefers.

## Files

- `README.md` — user-facing documentation
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — checklist, conventions, known limitations, upstream sync

pulls.title: setup: write the gfx1103 exact speed switches for the opt-in install
pulls.author: AlexisCarbonell
pulls.body:
Issue: Refs #1423 (same pattern as the gfx1150 opt-in in #2147)

## Summary

The engine turns 18 exact (bit-identical) switches on by default on gfx1151 (`src/core/arch_defaults.cpp`) but keeps
gfx1103 out of its arch defaults (`src/core/arch_defaults_test.cpp` asserts `arch_default_env("gfx1103")` stays
empty). A gfx1103 install gets the 17 that apply here - the gfx1151 set less `STRATA_HCD_EXACT`, which copies the
gfx1151 hipBLASLt table's solutions 1176 / 1177 and so does not fit beside a gfx1103 table - written into the
config's `env` beside `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`.

## What changed

- `setup.py`
    - `GFX1103_SWITCHES`: the 17 exact switches, with what was measured on the 780M.
    - `SETUP_ENV` carries them, so a re-run refreshes them and turning the opt-in off takes them out again.
    - The opt-in install writes them into the config's `env`; the `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1103=1` comment and the
      gfx1103 note now name the dot4 / WMMA kernels, the table and `docs/RADEON_780M.md`.
- `tools/test_setup_strix_halo.py`: `Gfx1103Switches` keeps `GFX1103_SWITCHES` equal to the gfx1151 arch-default
  table minus `STRATA_HCD_EXACT` and checks the `SETUP_ENV` wiring; the gfx1103 note test requires the new doc link.
- `docs/RADEON_780M.md` (new): the opt-in build, the toolchain, the table, the switches, the measured numbers.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: the integrated-Radeon detection line points at the new doc.

## Extra Notes

- One 780M (Ryzen 7 8745HS, 60 GB, GTT 50 GiB, ROCm 10.1, Q2_0, 4K prompt) measured the same greedy token ids with
  the 17 switches on and with them off, **+13% to +15% prompt** (183-186 -> 211-212 tok/s) and **decode +3.2%**
  (16.63 -> 17.17 tok/s, 640 greedy tokens, 3 of 3 pairs).
- Default path unchanged when the variable is unset; `tools/test_setup_strix_halo.py` (40), `test_setup_rocm_pins`
  (17), `test_setup_amd` (36) and `test_setup_choices` (50) pass.
- The engine's arch defaults are deliberately left alone (gfx1103 stays out of `arch_defaults.cpp`); the switches
  are written by setup, exactly as the gfx1150 opt-in does.
- The TheRock wheel route for gfx1103 was not exercised here (the hand build produced the numbers); setup's pin is
  unchanged.

pulls.title: hip: a hipBLASLt tuning table for gfx1103 (Radeon 780M)
pulls.author: AlexisCarbonell
pulls.body:
Issue: Follow-up to #1423

## Summary

The Radeon 780M (gfx1103, RDNA3, 12 CUs) builds and runs (issue #1423), but there was no hipBLASLt table for it, so
the prompt's dense GEMMs ran on plain hipBLAS. This adds `tools/hip/gfx1103-hipblaslt-100401.txt`, calibrated on one
780M with ROCm 10.1's hipBLASLt 1.4.1 (version number `100401`; the same version number as the shipped gfx1150
table, which was calibrated on 7.14.1).

## What changed

- `tools/hip/gfx1103-hipblaslt-100401.txt` (new, 143 rows): the 16 dense GEMM geometries a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
  prompt logs at T = 64, 128, ..., 16384, calibrated with `tools/hip/tune_hipblaslt --workspace-mib 32`. Two passes
  back to back; each row keeps the solution with the lowest median of all six repetitions, and a row is left out
  when no candidate beats plain hipBLAS, so 143 of the 144 cases are in: 1.05-23.30x per GEMM, geometric mean 4.95x.
  The one left out (`bf16 N=1 K=2560 T=64`) falls back to hipBLASEx.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: a "Shipped tables" entry.
- `bench/results/2026-10-12-community-gfx1103/`: the rig, the method, the runs (`runs.csv`), the server config and
  the raw logs.
- `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md` and `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`: one entry each.

## Extra Notes

- Prompt speed on the 780M (Q2_0): **90 tok/s on plain hipBLAS -> 187 with the table** at a 4K prompt, medians of an
  interleaved A/B; with the gfx1103 exact switches and the WMMA opt-ins, 277 at 4K and 272 at 32K (the earlier
  bench configuration; the shipping one adds `--spec 2 --lookup-chain 4`, which measures 276.7 at 4K).
- Context ladder to 131K on the shipping configuration (fresh prompts from this repository's own docs): prefill
  holds ~310 tok/s to 32K, then 258.2 at 64K, 215.5 at 96K and 198.5-221.4 at 128K across two runs (that is the
  full-read average; the last ~14K tokens at 128K depth read at ~206 tok/s with the prefix cached). Decode 16 ->
  ~10 tok/s with depth; GTT stays at 38.1 of 50 GiB.
- `hip_prefill_hipblaslt_gemm` passes with it (`launches=4 fallbacks=0`); `hip_prefill_hcd_exact_parity` skips,
  because the table picks no 1176 / 1177 for the HC down GEMM - the gfx1150 table gets the same skip, which is why
  `STRATA_HCD_EXACT` is not in the gfx1103 switch set.
- setup installs for gfx1103 only with `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1103=1`, and then picks the table up when the
  installed hipBLASLt reports 1.4.1.
- Not tested: another hipBLASLt build (the engine refuses other version numbers), other models, contexts above 131K.

pulls.title: hip: gfx1103 gets the native dot4 and the gfx11 WMMA kernels
pulls.author: AlexisCarbonell
pulls.body:
Issue: Refs #1423

## Summary

The Radeon 780M / 760M / 740M (Phoenix / Hawk Point, gfx1103) was outside the `dp4a` guard in
`hip_compat/intrinsics.hpp` and outside the `__gfx11xx__` list of the WMMA kernels: every quantized dot product ran
the four-step byte loop, and the prompt attention, block scorer, prompt GEMMs and prompt experts took the hipBLAS /
portable-kernel paths. This puts gfx1103 in both lists, like gfx1102 and gfx1150 (the same `v_dot4_i32_iu8`; the
gfx1150 port runs the same WMMA files).

## What changed

- `include/strata/hip_compat/intrinsics.hpp`: `__gfx1103__` in the sudot4 guard (native signed dot4).
- `include/strata/kernels/gfx_arch.hpp`: gfx1103 in `gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma()` (the runtime gates of every WMMA
  path), and the header comment.
- `src/prefill/wmma_gemm.cu` (6 guards), `src/prefill/kernels.cu`, `src/prefill/moe_fused.cu`,
  `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu`, `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`:
  `__gfx1103__` in the `#if` guards.
- `cmake/hip_backend.cmake` and `docs/STRIX_HALO.md`: the comments that named gfx1103 as excluded.
- `src/core/arch_defaults_test.cpp`: `arch_default_env("gfx1103")` stays empty (the switches are setup's; see the
  companion setup PR), and `tools/test_setup_strix_halo.py` now expects gfx1103 in the engine's WMMA list.

## Extra Notes

Measured on one 780M (Ryzen 7 8745HS, 60 GB, GTT 50 GiB, ROCm 10.1, Q2_0 + MTP, 32K context):

- decode **8.70 -> 13.44 tok/s** at a 32K prompt with default flags (dot4 is the default change);
- the WMMA parity tests now **run and pass** on gfx1103 instead of skipping (`hip_intrinsics`,
  `hip_prefill_wmma_gemm_parity`, `hip_prompt_attn_wmma`, `qsa_*`, `hip_prefill_fused_moe`, `hip_prefill_fused_iq`,
  `hip_gemm_f16_io_parity`, `hip_prefill_mmq_parity`); `ctest`: 57 passed, 2 skipped (the two hipBLASLt tests, which
  run and pass with the table), 2 environmental failures (`ple_parity` needs the `bench/micro` fixtures,
  `platform_memory_test` needs a memlock limit above 8 MiB);
- the greedy token ids are unchanged against the pre-port build at 4K and 32K (dot4 is exact integer arithmetic);
- HIP builds for gfx1103 and for `gfx1100;gfx1103;gfx1201` compile. CUDA and SYCL were not built here (no toolchains
  on the test box); the added macros are undefined for them, as for the other gfx11 targets.

Raw runs and the numbers: `bench/results/2026-10-12-community-gfx1103`.

## Title

Add community Codex quality baseline for the #1850 battery

## Summary

Adds a measured external quality baseline for the seven suites in the RTX 5070 Ti quantization study (#1850), using Codex CLI 0.162.1 configured as `gpt-6.1-sol` with `ultra` reasoning. Five Bugs finished with **25/25 visible and 25/25 hidden checks (100% each)** after corrections identified during the debugging and validation workflow. HumanEval+ passed 156/164 first attempts and 160/164 after one allowed repair per failure; Tool Eval Bench scored 90.2% mean with 0.4 percentage-point sample SD over five 92-case trials.

## What changed

- Adds `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-codex-quality-baseline/README.md` with all seven raw quality scores, harness pins, coverage and protocol limits.
- Adds `benchmark-scores.json` with exact score counts, the five-trial tool grade matrix, needle grid, safe artifact hashes and separately recorded original/recovered tool results.
- Adds `five-bugs-final-validation.json` with all 25 visible and 25 hidden outcomes after corrections, the five corrected solution hashes and the t4 checker qualification.

## Extra Notes

This is a results-only submission. The hosted model used an adapted CLI transport; it does not measure Strata inference, GPU performance or a normalized OVERALL score. MMLU covers only 100 abstract algebra questions. The five largest needle inputs used a separate transport after a frontend limit, with exact logical prompts and about 222K actual input tokens. One tool transport timeout was recovered using two preserved replies and one previously unanswered reply; the original report remains separately recorded.

Five Bugs initially scored 25/25 visible and 20/25 hidden across independent candidates. The final 25/25 in each suite comes from grading each of five fixed corrected solutions five times, after using repository documentation and checker feedback. The report describes the corrections and the t4 quoted-attribute checker expectation; no checker was changed. The original independent-run score is preserved separately.

Validation: all 172 HumanEval+ candidate pass/fail results agreed with independent stock EvalPlus 0.3.1 Linux grading; all 460 tool cells and 25 needle cells were audited; the original score JSON is byte-identical to the frozen public export. The final Five Bugs record contains 25 unique task/trial pairs, each passing both checkers, with hashes matching the five corrected files. The report uses a distinct quality schema and filenames, outside `tools/strata_bench.py`'s directory-based `results.json` reader. No engine or server code changes.

pulls.title: prefill: STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1 on gfx11 WMMA (opt-in; gfx1151: recurrence 1.6x, a warm 4K-128K prompt 1.1-2.5%)
pulls.author: libratechw
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (follows #1372, which added `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` for CUDA; related: #1296, the gfx1100 WY arm)

## Summary

`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=1` exists for CUDA (#1372) and is compiled out on HIP. On gfx1151 the prompt's recurrence is
`gdn_rec_quad2c_kernel` plus a norm kernel: token by token, FP32, on the vector ALUs. This PR makes the same switch take a gfx11
path: the WY form of the gated delta rule in chunks of 16 tokens, every product one 16x16x16 WMMA (FP16 operands, FP32
accumulation, the state in the waves' accumulators), with the output norm and the z gate fused into the scan.

It is off by default; the default path is unchanged. It rounds differently from the FP32 recurrence (FP16 operands), which is why
it is opt-in; the KL numbers are below.

## What changed

- `src/prefill/kernels.cu`, HIP only, behind the `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED` switch in `gdn_recurrence_variant` (variants 0 and 1, the
  ones `gdn_recurrence` uses; `STRATA_GDN_REC_HEADS` is read once at the top of the function now, one declaration moved up):
  - `gdn_wmma_prep_kernel`: T = (I + A)^-1 and P of every chunk at once (they do not depend on the state); a block per
    (key head, chunk), a wave per value head.
  - `gdn_wmma_scan_kernel`: a block per value head, a wave per 16 value columns; walks the chunks and loads the next chunk's k/q/v
    while this one computes. Its barriers wait for LDS only (`__syncthreads()` also waits for every global load in flight, which
    would put the prefetch in front of every barrier), and the prefetched rows are `ext_vector_type` values (HIP's `float4` copies
    go through a stack object, which also waits for the load); both are in the code comments.
  - `gdn_rec_wmma`: the launch. It returns false, and the existing kernels run, for a part outside `gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma` (gfx1100-1103, gfx1150, gfx1151), fewer
    than 64 tokens and an output row stride not divisible by 8; the caller skips it under `STRATA_GDN_REC_HEADS`. The part is
    judged per call from the current device of the calling thread. The gfx11-only instructions sit inside the gfx11 device passes.
- `tests/hip/gdn_chunked.cpp` and CMake: `hip_gdn_chunked`, `hip_gdn_chunked_off`, `hip_gdn_chunked_default`, and
  `hip_gdn_chunked --bench` / `--bench-default` (one layer's time on this path / on gfx1151's default kernels). `tests/hip/gdn_rec_head.cpp` unsets `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED` (its variants 0 and 1 are the references there).
- `include/strata/prefill/kernels.hpp` (the variant comment), `docs/AMD_HIP.md` (conditions, numbers, how to run the checks),
  `docs/DETAILS.md` (the CUDA entry now says what HIP does).

Not touched: the CUDA kernels (the `#if !defined(__HIPCC__)` block), the SYCL port, any default. On HIP `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED=2` is
the same as 1 (the docs say so).

## Checks

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), ROCm 7.14.1, Linux 7.0, UD-IQ4_XS unless stated, all on this commit. "Section 5" is the nine variables of
`docs/STRIX_HALO.md` section 5 (with `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=2048` where the doc has 4096); "defaults" is the engine without them
(section 4's gfx1151 defaults stay).

**The default path is unchanged.** With the switch unset or 0, for a chunk of fewer than 64 tokens and for a row stride the path
does not take, the output and the carried state are bit-identical to the existing recurrence (`hip_gdn_chunked_off`,
`hip_gdn_chunked_default`; both set `STRATA_GDN_HEAD=1` and `STRATA_GDN_PP=2`, gfx1151's defaults).

**Numerics (`hip_gdn_chunked`).** 0-16,385 tokens, the 64-token edge, 16-token remainders, row strides 6144 / 6152 / 6145, weak
decay, beta = 0, and a request split at 129 + 128 tokens with the state carried. Bounds: relative RMS of the FP16 output and of the
final state <= 0.003; max |diff| <= 2% of the reference's max + 1e-5; all finite; guard values around the output unchanged. Two
short cases are also compared with a double-precision CPU recurrence of three value heads.

**First-token KL against the same run without the switch** (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`; 12 natural-text prompts of 1.5K-24K tokens,
nats, full vocabulary):

| | UD-IQ4_XS mean / max | UD-Q4_K_XL mean / max | top-1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| defaults, with vs without the switch | 0.0066 / 0.016 | 0.0059 / 0.043 | 12 of 12 |
| section 5, with vs without the switch | 0.0043 / 0.013 | 0.0095 / 0.054 | 12 of 12 |

Section 5's own switches against the defaults are 0.0076 (IQ4_XS) and 0.0065 (Q4_K_XL); that is a different change, given for scale
and not as a limit for this one. #1372 reports 0.002-0.009 for the CUDA path. The mean is carried by a few prompts (one at 0.054;
the medians are 0.001-0.004). Only the first generated token is compared, and across the 12 prompts it takes only two distinct values,
so top-1 agreement is a weak check: a long generation, coding / agent use and perplexity have **not** been measured, which is the
reason for opt-in.

**Speed, one layer** (`hip_gdn_chunked --bench` against `--bench-default`, which runs gfx1151's default kernels with
`STRATA_GDN_PP=2` and `STRATA_GDN_NOY=1`; the switch is read once per process, so the two are separate runs, alternated three
times; each run reports the GPU-event median of 7 runs after 2 warmups with the same nonzero start state; recurrence + norm;
medians of the three):

| tokens | default kernels | this PR | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 0.090 ms | 0.050 ms | 1.8x |
| 256 | 0.280 ms | 0.192 ms | 1.46x |
| 2,048 | 2.603 ms | 1.779 ms | 1.46x |
| 16,384 | 20.830 ms | 13.203 ms | 1.58x |
| 32,768 | 42.229 ms | 26.429 ms | 1.60x |

**Speed, whole prompt.** The same binary on both sides, only `STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED` differing, a fresh engine per side, resident
budget 55 GiB, int8 KV, 11 pairs in alternating order after a discarded one, 256-token answers, the engine's `prompt_ms`. Every
prompt has its own nonce at the front and was read in full (0 reused tokens in every request). Each engine reads a discarded 4K
prompt first: on those first prompts the same pairs gave 95% intervals of [1.015, 1.021] (section 5) and [0.991, 1.210]
(defaults). Before each prompt the client waits until the page-migration and direct-reclaim counters of `/proc/vmstat` have
stood still for 3 s; a pair in which either prompt still met page migration (over 50,000 pages) or direct reclaim was dropped
and measured again (2 of 68 pairs, both on the defaults: a 32K prompt with the switch on and a 128K one with it off, which
met 365,000 and 161,000 migrated pages and were 0.51 s and 1.15 s slower than the median of their side; with them kept, 32K
and 128K give 1.011 (10 of 12 and 12 of 12 faster)). Times are
medians; off / on is the geometric mean of the 11 per-pair ratios with a 95% bootstrap interval:

| tokens | arm | off -> on | off / on | faster | sign test p |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4,096 | section 5 | 3.701 -> 3.630 s | 1.019 [1.017, 1.021] | 11 of 11 | 0.001 |
| 4,096 | defaults | 5.947 -> 5.876 s | 1.012 [1.008, 1.016] | 10 of 11 | 0.012 |
| 32,768 | section 5 | 26.024 -> 25.401 s | 1.024 [1.023, 1.026] | 11 of 11 | 0.001 |
| 32,768 | defaults | 44.684 -> 44.122 s | 1.012 [1.009, 1.016] | 10 of 11 | 0.012 |
| 128,000 | section 5 | 107.468 -> 104.858 s | 1.025 [1.023, 1.026] | 11 of 11 | 0.001 |
| 128,000 | defaults | 195.498 -> 193.445 s | 1.011 [1.008, 1.013] | 11 of 11 | 0.001 |

So about 2.4% on top of section 5 and about 1.1% on the defaults, for a prompt that is not the first one after a start. With 36
gated-DeltaNet layers the layer figures predict about 0.55 s saved on a 32K prompt; 0.62 s (section 5) and 0.56 s (defaults) were
measured.

**Builds.** HIP: `kernels.cu` compiles for gfx1030, gfx1100, gfx1103, gfx1151, gfx1152 and gfx1201 (the scan kernel holds 26 WMMA
instructions for gfx1100 / gfx1103 / gfx1151 and only a trap for gfx1152 / gfx1201, which the runtime gate never launches it on); the four HIP tests above (the three
`hip_gdn_chunked*` and `hip_gdn_rec_head`) pass on gfx1151. Run on gfx1151 only: nothing here has been run on another gfx11 card (gfx1103 joined `gfx_arch_is_gfx11_wmma` upstream after this
was first written, and this path follows that list) or

pulls.title: [Engine] Anthropic API: cache_creation_input_tokens, the prompt tokens read now and kept for the next request
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`/v1/messages` never reports `cache_creation_input_tokens`. Every token a request reads stays in the session (and in the conversation cache) for the next request, which is what Anthropic calls a cache write. Clients that show cache writes, such as Claude Code, always see none: their status line and cost estimate count every newly read token as uncached input.

| field | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cache_read_input_tokens` | the reused prefix | the same |
| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | absent | the tokens read now, but the last |
| `input_tokens` | the tokens read now | 1, the last prompt token |

The three fields still add up to the prompt, so a client's context fill does not change.

## Related discussion

Fixes #2289 (re-tested on 0.2.0-beta there: still present).

## Approach

Only `anthropic_events`' `message_delta` usage changes; the OpenAI and Responses paths are untouched. `input_tokens` stays at least 1: Claude Code takes 0 as "not given" and keeps `message_start`'s whole prompt beside the cache counts, which counts the prompt twice (#1013). The usage assertions in the tests now check the three-way split and `input_tokens >= 1`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Rebased onto 0.2.1 (upstream main `90767252`) as `be7e591c`; 0.2.1 split `serve/test_parallel.py`, so the changed assertion is now in `serve/test_parallel_yield.py`. `python -m pytest -q serve/test_server.py serve/test_parallel.py serve/test_parallel_yield.py serve/test_request_accounting.py`: 392 passed, 3 skipped, 444 subtests passed (Windows 11, Python 3.14).
- The changed tests against 0.2.1's own `serve/server.py` (this change taken out): 4 fail, among them `UsageAndStatus.test_anthropic` and the two `RequestAccounting.test_anthropic_*_classifies_only_original_input_as_cached`. With the change they pass.
- In daily use with Claude Code on my box (2x CMP 50HX, Ubuntu 24.04.4) since 2026-10-13, in my fork, which is now on 0.2.0-beta (`342185bd`) with this change. Claude Code shows the cache writes.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** this exact branch against a GPU engine (the change is in the usage fields; the tests use the server's stub engine).

## Limits

Display only: the totals were already right.

pulls.title: [Other] tools: validate GGUF headers and tensor extents
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Problem and result
Fixes #1919. `tools/gguf_reader.py` reads the GGUF header without bounding its reads by the file size. `setup.check_shards` / `whole_shard` compute a shard's required size with `expected_bytes() or 0`. As a result, a truncated or malformed shard can pass as whole: a cut-off header, counts past the end of the file, an invalid alignment, or a last tensor of a type whose size is unknown. The engine then fails much later.

Before: these files either raise low-level errors (`struct.error`, `MemoryError` on huge counts) or are accepted as whole. After: the reader rejects a malformed header with a clear `ValueError`. `GGUFFile.data_end()` returns the extent the file must have, from every tensor whose size is known. A shard whose extent cannot be proven (an unknown or repacked tensor type) is reported as unverifiable and kept, not called corrupt. A metadata-only shard (0 tensors) ends at its parsed header, not at the aligned data start. This was the review point on an 84-byte file, and it is the same shape as #2346.

## Related discussion
https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1919
#2346 landed on main as 6ca7e929: `check_shards` special-cases a shard with no tensors. This PR keeps that guard. It adds the reader-side bounds and the `data_end()` extent that `check_shards` and `whole_shard` now share.

## Approach
Bounded reads in `GGUFFile` (every length or count is checked against the bytes left), alignment must be a positive power of two, and `data_end()` checks all known tensor extents, including unsorted offsets. `UnsupportedTensorSize` separates "cannot verify" from "truncated". `setup.check_shards` asks the user to keep an unverifiable file instead of deleting it. No change to how valid files are read.

## Validation
Rebased on main e88ee39d. The v0.2.0-beta tag (3d1fb480) is an ancestor of it, and no commit between them touches `tools/gguf_reader.py` or `setup.py`. Environment: Debian 13 x86_64, Python 3.13.5, `pip install -r requirements.txt` in a venv, CPU only, synthetic GGUF files written by the tests.

**Passed:**
- `git am` of the two rebased commits onto a fresh checkout of main e88ee39d: applied cleanly.
- `python -m unittest tools.test_gguf_reader_malformed`, patched on main e88ee39d: 18 tests, OK. On unpatched main e88ee39d it fails (16 failures, 19 errors, counted per subtest; mostly no `data_end()`, raw read errors, and short shards accepted), which confirms that #1919 still exists on v0.2.0-beta.
- Patched on main e88ee39d, also OK, with the same results as unpatched main: `tools.test_setup_shard_check` (2, including the #2346 case), `tools.test_shards` (13), `tools.test_setup_unsloth` (57), `tools.test_setup_choices` (53), `tools.test_setup_mac` (24), `tools.test_strata_tokenizer` (11, 3 skipped).

**Failed:**
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_golden`: 48 subtest failures (golden config mismatch). This is not caused by this change: unpatched main e88ee39d fails the same 48 subtests in this environment.

**Not run:**
- A real multi-GB model shard (for example Unsloth's UD-Q5_K_XL 00001). Only synthetic files were tested.
- An engine load of a malformed shard end to end.

## Limits
A tensor type with no known block geometry still cannot be size-checked. Such a shard is reported as unverifiable rather than whole or corrupt.

pulls.title: setup: resume downloads when HEAD omits Content-Length
pulls.author: KeyanHu-git
pulls.body:
## Title

setup: resume downloads when HEAD omits Content-Length

Issue: Fixes #1915.

## Summary

A clean early EOF can leave a partial model file under its final name when HEAD omits `Content-Length`. In #1915, setup renamed a 5.47 GB fragment of a 29.61 GB shard before the later size check rejected it.

This change establishes the expected length before accepting completion. Short responses remain in `.part` and resume with Range; a transfer whose completeness cannot be established stays partial and reports why.

## What changed

- **Expected length:** use ModelScope's published size when HEAD has none, and obtain the total from GET `Content-Range` or `Content-Length`. Fetch ModelScope metadata once and reuse it for the final SHA-256 check.
- **Resume validation:** check the returned range and length before appending or clearing existing bytes. A valid full response to a Range request restarts from zero; a conflicting response preserves the partial file.
- **Completion handling:** retain `IncompleteRead.partial`, resume interrupted chunked responses, and accept HTTP 416 as completion only when the reported total matches the local file and any known length. Complete chunked responses and explicit empty files remain supported.
- **Regression tests:** add `tools/test_setup_download_length.py` with local HTTP fixtures for early EOF, ModelScope metadata reuse, Range handling, HTTP 416 and completion boundaries.

## Extra Notes

### Validation

Windows 11, Python 3.12.0; base: `a0116b2`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Two root-cause regressions on unmodified upstream | One assertion failure and one error |
| Same regressions with this patch | Both pass |
| Download-length and ModelScope suites | **23 tests pass**, including 14 new tests |
| Full setup suite on upstream | 474 tests; one existing SYCL assertion failure |
| Full setup suite with this patch | 488 tests; the same SYCL assertion failure |

```bash
python -m unittest tools.test_setup_download_length tools.test_setup_modelscope
python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_setup_*.py'
```

The root-cause fixtures check resumed offsets, final bytes and hash verification. The unchanged full-suite failure is `test_setup_sycl.ToSycl.test_xe_ranks_the_experts_with_the_sycl_profile_and_i915_keeps_the_shipped_one`.

A separate bounded probe of the real ModelScope URL on this host found no length in HEAD. GET advertised 65,536 bytes and a total of 29,608,446,496 bytes, but returned EOF after 47,824 bytes. This checks the real transport condition; the complete model was not downloaded again.

### Compatibility and related work

The download interface is unchanged. Close-delimited responses without a known length now stop with their `.part` retained; a completion mark without a published hash still records transfer completion rather than cryptographic integrity.

#1405 also refactors `download()` and local-file reuse. Its transfer loop still obtains the length from HEAD. If it lands first, this patch will need to be integrated with that refactor.

pulls.title: fix(vision): retain image ownership through request preparation
pulls.author: Tsury
pulls.body:
The current image cache keeps records during encode_all, but releases the service FIFO before preparing the combined embedding file. Another request can evict those files between encoding and stat/copy. A refused request with more than 64 cached images can also leave the cache above its bound.

Keep the FIFO and a reentrant image batch lock through encoding, validation and combined-file copying. Defer eviction to the outermost batch's finally block. Preserve combined-file ownership and trim back to 64 afterward. Close encoder pipes during teardown and clean failed startup. On the specific native decoder refusal, retry once through the existing Pillow normalization path; conversion failures retain temporary-file cleanup.

Based on main `a0116b2782a5b82622358c04a06496485d12b2d6`. #1072/#1207 addressed retention during encoding; the stock source still exposes the interval through combined-copy. This PR covers that remaining ownership interval instead of duplicating the shipped encode_all change.

Validation: 20 focused model-free vision tests pass. The nine cache-lifetime methods fail on stock for eviction/copy ordering or failure-path bounds. Scheduled two-request races check the real cache and copy boundary, with no GPU/model. Existing image marker, temporary-file and shutdown checks pass. The normalization retry tests isolate protocol behavior; they do not qualify a new image decoder.

Command: `python3 -m unittest serve.test_vision_cache serve.test_server.VisionDecode serve.test_server.ImageMarkers serve.test_server.VisionTempFiles serve.test_server.VisionShutdown`.

No new device build, GPU campaign or deployment. The longer FIFO hold protects request ownership; its throughput cost is unmeasured.

pulls.title: fix(serve): preserve late instruction roles across adapters
pulls.author: Tsury
pulls.body:
Late system/developer messages currently become user messages on the Chat, Messages and Responses paths. Their position survives, but their instruction role does not.

Preserve the role through adapters and render late system/developer content as system messages in the bundled template. Keep leading instruction merging and the existing rejection of images in system content. Remove the conversion helper and its imports.

Based on main `a0116b2782a5b82622358c04a06496485d12b2d6`. Related #56 fixed template refusal by changing late roles to user; this change retains the accepted messages' instruction role instead. Custom templates remain responsible for their own accepted roles.

Validation: 52 focused model-free client/Responses tests pass. The strengthened existing HTTP tests fail on stock for the missing system-role markers and pass after this change. They verify order and one occurrence of each late instruction. No new GPU workload or deployment, and no model-quality or throughput claim.

Command: `python3 -m unittest serve.test_server.ClientShapes serve.test_responses`.

pulls.title: fix(serve): preserve declared tool schemas through streamed aliases
pulls.author: Tsury
pulls.body:
A declared namespaced tool written as a flat alias or with whitespace can lose its parameter schema during streaming. For example, a declared string `path` of `123` becomes the number `123`, and an ambiguous alias can route to the first namespace.

Canonicalize only unambiguous aliases at the parser boundary, with exact declared names taking precedence. Apply the same name to streaming events and completed calls. Keep padded unknown names as text. Preserve literal call markers, and end an unclosed wrapper before the next call instead of merging arguments. Remove the redundant Responses-only alias map.

Based on main `a0116b2782a5b82622358c04a06496485d12b2d6`. This completes parser/schema handling beyond the namespace routing shipped for #812.

Validation: 63 focused model-free tests pass, covering streaming/chunk boundaries, alias collisions, string parameters, recovery, literal markers and Responses round trips. Eight regression methods fail on the unmodified source for the expected parsing/schema differences. No new GPU build, inference campaign or deployment. Existing maintained deployment evidence is reused; no throughput claim.

Command: `python3 -m unittest serve.test_native_tool_parser serve.test_tool_call_unclosed serve.test_server.ToolCallRecovery serve.test_server.ToolCallRecoveryOff serve.test_responses`.

pulls.title: [Other] add legacy /v1/completions for raw-prompt clients (#2277)
pulls.author: kossum
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Clients that apply their own chat template need to send a raw prompt to `/v1/completions`. Strata currently has no endpoint for that.

This adds the legacy OpenAI endpoint with streaming and non-streaming responses, `text_completion` objects, and token usage. The server doesn't apply the chat template again.

## Related discussion

#2277

## Approach

The handler uses the existing generation path and accepts one string prompt. `max_tokens: 0` or a negative value uses the remaining context.

Explicit thinking-disable flags append the template's no-thinking tail. Without those flags, the prompt passes through unchanged.

Streaming sends each piece of text once. With `echo: true`, it sends the prompt once at the start; the finish chunk has empty text.

This also keeps the structured-output error handler in the chat endpoint, so a failed streamed response sends an SSE error and `[DONE]`, not another HTTP response inside the stream. Engine errors after streaming starts are handled as SSE errors too.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta). These local checks ran on `7e08755f`.

**Passed:**

Windows, Python 3.13.2, with jsonschema installed:

```sh
uv run --no-project --with regex --with jinja2 --with jsonschema python -m unittest serve.test_server serve.test_structured serve.test_monitor
```

368 tests, OK, 3 skipped.

Linux, Python 3.11 in Docker, using a dedicated venv with only the pinned `requirements.txt` packages:

```sh
python tools/minimal_server_smoke.py --report /tmp/minimal-server-smoke.json
```

Reported `"passed": true`.

`git diff --check upstream/main` also passed.

**Failed:**

The full suite in the same Linux venv:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'
```

888 tests, 2 failures, 18 skipped:

- `test_lifeline.Lifeline.test_the_portable_watcher_ends_the_child_when_the_server_is_killed`
- `test_server.VisionTempFiles.test_work_dir_has_no_space_when_temp_has_one`

I reran both tests on clean main `e88ee39d` with the same container and dependencies. Both fail there with the same assertions. I haven't changed either behavior in this PR.

**Not run:**

- Live-model testing on this rebased revision. The earlier live checks were on an older revision.
- CUDA, HIP, SYCL or Metal builds. This PR changes Python serving code, not native backend code.
- A byte-for-byte comparison of all existing endpoints against the release.

## Limits

Only a string prompt and `n=1` / `best_of=1` are supported. Suffix and logprobs are rejected.

`stream_options` accepts only `include_usage`, and only with streaming. Usage still comes on the finish chunk, not a separate `choices: []` chunk, so this doesn't yet implement the full OpenAI streaming-usage format.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RX 9060 XT (gfx1200) with 16 GB of RAM and a SATA SSD, Coder IQ1_M at 128K on 0.1.43.1, stock vs tuned
pulls.author: mandoof1
pulls.body:
Issue: none (results-only report)

## Summary
The Coder IQ1_M runs on a Linux PC with 15.5 GiB of usable RAM, half of the 32 GB the README lists for it, with the experts read from a SATA SSD (`--mmap-experts`). This report gives a same-day comparison, on 0.1.43.1 (`a0116b2`), between stock with setup's own configuration and the configuration I use every day, and lists what made the difference.

| Same day, same PC | Stock, setup's config (16K) | Tuned (128K) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| short chat decode | 2.6 tok/s, 2 of 9 requests ended the engine | 8.9 tok/s, no failures |
| 4K prompt | 43.6 tok/s, first token 92 s | 178.4 tok/s, first token 23 s |
| 16K / 32K prompt | do not fit | 323 / 373 tok/s |
| agent session (6 turns x 3) | first turn: no output for 312 s, engine ended; stopped | 18/18 turns, 68.7% cache hit |

The 8.9 tok/s is the bench's short chat (100-token replies, thinking off). In everyday agent use with thinking on, decode runs at 12-17 tok/s with peaks of 25 (earlier measurements in the report).

The stock run shows `verify: timed out at layer 19` (#267) and 3.4 M major faults in one request: the experts arrive about 4 KB at a time from the SATA drive.

The settings that mattered most here:
- `GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576` (the ROCclr USERPTR mechanism from TROUBLESHOOTING.md / #1705; upstream sets it only with `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP=1`, not on the `--mmap-experts` path)
- the server in a `MemorySwapMax=0` systemd scope (zram is on by default on CachyOS)
- static residency with `--adapt-every 100000`
- longer stall limits
- an expert profile learned from agent prompts (included, 98 KB)

## What changed
Only a new folder, `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-rx-9060-xt-16gb-ram/`:
- `README.md`: hardware, configuration, method, results, earlier tuning measurements, and the settings that were measured slower here
- `tuned-128k/`, `stock-16k/`: the `strata_bench.py` output of each run (`README.md`, `results.json`, `engine-log-excerpt.txt`) and a 2 s RAM/VRAM/disk sample file (`mem-samples.txt`)
- `strata-coder-iq1_m-128k.json`: the tuned configuration, paths replaced
- `expert-profile-agent.bin`: the agent-learned expert profile for the Coder IQ1_M pack
- `local-patches.diff`: three small local engine patches used in the tuned run, for reproduction only

No source, docs or defaults are changed.

## Extra Notes
- The local patches are a `STRATA_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_S` env, `MADV_WILLNEED` hints before prefill staging and the post-prompt slot refill, and `STRATA_PROFILE_ROUTING_ONLY=1` for `--expert-profile-save` under static residency. They are built and tested with HIP only. If any of them is wanted as an engine change, I can open it as its own PR with the measurements and builds it needs.
- Not tested: CUDA and SYCL builds of the patches, Windows, NVMe, thinking-on speed through the suite, correctness checks, more than one slot. Each configuration was run once, tuned first.

pulls.title: serve: an AMD card's load, VRAM, temperature and power on Windows
pulls.author: unimo-chan
pulls.body:
## What this changes

On Windows an AMD card has no NVML and no amdgpu sysfs, so `serve/telemetry.py` had nothing to read and the
dashboard said *"no GPU load or VRAM readings for AMD cards on Windows yet"* (the `gpu_note` below, from #1380).
This adds a reader built from what the machine does have — all of it through `ctypes`, no package:

- **DXGI** (`CreateDXGIFactory1` → `EnumAdapters1` → `GetDesc1`): the card's name, its dedicated memory total,
  and its LUID. The card is the one whose vendor ID is 0x1002, so an NVIDIA display card in the same PC is not
  mistaken for the card the engine runs on.
- **Performance counters** (`PdhAddEnglishCounterW`, English counter names, instances picked by that LUID) — the
  same counters Task Manager's GPU column reads: `\GPU Adapter Memory(luid_…)\Dedicated Usage` for the VRAM in
  use, `\GPU Engine(*luid_…*)\Utilization Percentage` for load (the busiest engine, which is what Task Manager
  shows; measured on this machine: 93% on the compute engine where the `Running Time` counter beside it computed
  94% over the same window). DXGI's own `QueryVideoMemoryInfo` is per-process and reported 0 while the engine
  held 19 GiB, so it is not used.
- **ADLX** (`amdadlx64.dll`, installed with the Adrenalin driver) for temperature and power: the ADLX services
  reached through their vtable slots (ADLX interfaces are plain C++ vtables, not COM), the GPU found through the
  ADL mapping and matched to the name DXGI reported. On this driver plain `ADLXInitialize` answers an empty GPU
  list, so `ADLXInitializeWithIncompatibleDriver2` is the entry that works; `GPUPower` answers NOT_SUPPORTED, so
  power falls back to `GPUTotalBoardPower`. Initialization is once per process (a second
  `GetPerformanceMonitoringServices` hangs, measured).
- `gpu_reader(amd=True)` returns this on Windows when there is no amdgpu sysfs; the Linux path and the NVIDIA
  path are untouched, and a card none of the three reaches still gets a word why instead of empty tiles.

Enumeration, counters and property reads only — no device, no context: it takes no VRAM from the engine and
cannot stall it.

## What it leaves alone

- **No PCIe readings at all** — neither the link nor the traffic. The card's own PCI devnode describes the switch
  inside an RX 7000 (measured: Gen4 x16 reported by the endpoint while the card sits in a Gen3 x8 slot on a
  B450), and the three devices above it report nothing, so the host-facing link is one Windows cannot name; the
  tile stays blank there rather than showing the card's own capability (#1734, #2137). For the traffic: PDH has
  no PCIe counter set and ADLX 1.5's headers name no bus metric — that half is the engine's own byte counter, in #2272.
- **No new dependency.** `adlxpybind` ships cp310–cp313 `win_amd64` wheels and no sdist, so a `pip install` fails
  on any other Python; `ctypes` needs nothing and the file already uses it for NVML.
- Linux, NVIDIA, the engine, and every other file.

## Where this overlaps

#1871 (dashboard readings for AMD cards), #1152 (Windows AMD telemetry, with an Arabic UI), #1224 (ADLX through
`adlxpybind`) and #1434 are all open in this area, and I read them before writing this. This one is the
ctypes-only route: no install step, and it is the ADLX *fallback chain* (`GPUPower` → `GPUTotalBoardPower`) and
the LUID-picked performance counters that make the numbers appear on a driver where the direct calls answer
NOT_SUPPORTED. If any of those PRs lands first, this should be rebased on it rather than shipped beside it.

## How I checked

RX 7900 XT, driver 32.0.23033.1002, ADLX 1.5.0.124, Windows 11, Python 3.12.10, with the engine holding the
model:

- idle: 42–43 °C, 67–82 W, util 0, 19248 MiB of 20418 MiB in use (the engine's own allocation).
- during one chat request (400 completion tokens in 9.1 s): util 90–95 %, power up to 292 W, 47 °C.
- the ADLX path is the only one that answers temperature and power here: ADL (`atiadlxx`) enumerates the card but
  answers −1/−5 for every sensor call, and no performance counter or WMI class reports them.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_server.AmdTelemetry serve.test_server.TelemetryNoDisks
  serve.test_server.SharingTheGpu serve.test_server.DesktopVramNote serve.test_server.WebApp
  serve.test_server.PrometheusMetrics serve.test_server.LiveRate`: **42 tests, OK** (Python 3.12.10, on main at
  `a0116b2`). Full `serve.test_server` on this branch: **308 tests, OK** in 101 s (Windows 11, Python 3.12.10), nothing skipped.
- Cross-checked against AMD's own client for the same library — the `adlxpybind` 1.4.6 wheel, unpacked rather than
  installed: it answers the same 43.0 °C and the same 19248 MiB, and the same `GPUPower` 0.0 with
  `GPUTotalBoardPower` 64.0. The temperature and VRAM figures are not an artifact of reading the vtable by hand.

One existing test changed: the sysfs link test built its reader with `gpu_reader(0, amd=True)`, which on Windows
is now the DXGI reader; it constructs `telemetry._Amd(0)` directly instead. Its assertions are unchanged.

Not tested: an RX 6000 or an older driver, a machine without `amdadlx64.dll` (the reader returns nothing and the
existing note is shown), and a second card.

pulls.title: Monitor: the PCIe traffic from the bytes the engine moved, not from a driver counter
pulls.author: unimo-chan
pulls.body:
## What this changes

The Monitor's PCIe tile shows a traffic rate only when the driver reports one. `_Nvml.read()` fills `pcie_rx_mb`
from `nvmlDeviceGetPcieThroughput`; nothing else does. An AMD card has no such counter to read: on Windows there
is no NVML, the performance-counter set has no PCIe entry (only the five GPU sets and RDMA Activity) and neither
`amdadlx64.dll` nor `atiadlxx.dll` exports a bus metric; on Linux amdgpu's `pcie_bw` counts messages, not bytes
(#1734). The one component that does know the traffic is the engine: it staged those expert blobs itself.

So the engine counts the bytes and the server turns them into a rate:

- `ExpertDispatch::pcie_bytes` (`include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`) — one blob per staged expert, in every
  `--pcie-mode`: the copy engine writes them into staging, kernel and direct modes read the host's blob where it
  lies. `offload_entries` already counted routed *entries*, not bytes. Counted in
  `expert_pool_dispatch_multi`, the same place `pcie_experts` is.
- The engine prints the running total on `PCIE <bytes>` lines at the points where it already flushes a token line
  (both decode loops and both batch loops), and adds one field to `DONE`: the request's own MB.
- `serve/server.py` keeps `(time, bytes)` samples and takes the slope over the same window the token rate uses
  (`RATE_WINDOW_S`), and reads the request's figure from the `DONE` line. It fills `gpu_pcie_rx_mb` **only when
  the reader says it has no traffic counter of its own** — a `has_pcie_throughput` flag, True on NVML, False on
  the AMD paths — so an NVIDIA card keeps showing NVML's own numbers.
- The tile puts the traffic next to the bandwidth the engine measured at its own start (`PCIe probe: N GB/s
  host->device`, already on stderr, which the server owns as the log): `412 MB/s · 12.1% of 3.4 GB/s measured`.
  The request list's `+X% PCIe` badge gains the MB behind it.

## What it leaves alone

- The generation half of the tile: no `pcie_gen`/`pcie_width` is added anywhere, and nothing turns a measured
  GB/s into a generation (Gen4 x8 and Gen3 x16 measure the same). #2137's point about the Gen headline is a
  separate change.
- NVML's readings, and amdgpu's `pcie_bw` — #1734's question about the three sysfs integers is untouched here;
  this answers the rate half from the engine instead, which works on Windows too.
- No new option and no default change: the engine's output gains lines, and the server only reads them. An engine
  older than this prints no `PCIE` lines and the tile stays as it is.

## How I checked

- `python -m unittest serve.test_server.DraftCounts serve.test_server.PrometheusMetrics serve.test_server.PcieShare
  serve.test_server.CancelledRead serve.test_server.LiveRate serve.test_server.WebApp serve.test_server.AmdTelemetry
  serve.test_server.TelemetryNoDisks` on this branch (main at `a0116b2`, Python 3.12.10): **27 tests, OK** — the
  classes that parse the engine's `DONE` line, serve `/metrics`, and run the sampler, with the stock tests
  unchanged. The `DONE` parser still accepts the shorter lines of an older engine: those tests pass as they are.
  So the `PCIE` lines and the new `DONE` field are exercised against the mock engine, not a real one. Full `serve.test_server` on this branch: **308 tests, OK** in 101 s (Windows 11, Python 3.12.10), nothing skipped.
- **Not built.** This machine has no CMake, MSVC, CUDA or SYCL toolchain, so the C++ side is not compiled here —
  the CUDA and SYCL trees get the same lines, and both are unverified by a compiler. A build of `src/` (CUDA/HIP)
  and `sycl/` before review is what AGENTS.md asks for; I could not do it, and I am saying so rather than
  implying it.

pulls.title: --shared-expert-arena: one engine loads the file, the others wait and attach
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
**`--shared-expert-arena`: one engine loads the file, the others wait and attach**

#129 added the shared arena as a primitive and left two things to the caller: who loads the file ("no
leader/follower population protocol yet") and its lifetime. Today every engine that names the file reads the whole
pack into it again at start - 55 GiB for UD-IQ4_XS, written into pages another engine may be reading - and nothing
keeps two loads apart. This adds that part, inside the engine, so two engines of one pack (one per GPU, each with its
own expert cache and K/V; #1461's pair is one such setup) keep one RAM copy and load it once.

**What it changes** (`src/core/pinned.cu`, `pinned.hpp`, `expert_source.cpp/.hpp`, `generate.cpp`; the selftest;
`DETAILS.md`; measurements in `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-r9700-shared-expert-arena/`)

- **Who loads:** two one-byte OFD locks on the file (Linux 3.15; they belong to the open file, so the kernel drops them
  when an engine exits or dies). FILL is held by the engine that loads the file until the load passed its checks; an
  engine started meanwhile waits on it (`shared arena ...: engine N is loading it, waiting`) and then attaches - no
  read of the pack, `attached 55.43 GiB another engine loaded, nothing read`. USER is held shared while an engine maps
  the file.
- **Lifetime:** the file stays when the last engine exits, so a restart attaches too; deleting it frees the RAM. An
  engine that dies while loading leaves the file to the next one, which loads it again. A file of another pack, size or
  format is replaced when no engine maps it (USER taken exclusively, then unlinked - never truncated under a mapping)
  and refused while one does.
- **Format V2:** the header is one 2 MiB page, so the arena starts 2 MiB-aligned in the file and in memory and
  hugetlbfs can hold it (the V1 comment said it could not). V1 files are replaced like any other format when unused.
- **Pages:** the file is allocated up front (`posix_fallocate`: a tmpfs smaller than the arena is an error naming the
  size, not a SIGBUS part-way through the load), mapped before the GPU registration (`MADV_POPULATE_*`, Linux 5.14),
  and the loading engine makes its 2 MiB pages whole with `MADV_COLLAPSE` (Linux 6.1) while they are still empty. The
  start reports `N of M GiB on 2 MiB pages`; on AMD, when part of it is on 4 KB pages, it says why that matters.
- **Why 2 MiB pages matter on AMD:** `hipHostRegister` does not pin host memory on ROCm 7.14.1 (`VmPin` 0); the
  kernel's compaction moves 4 KB pages, and every move stops the process's GPU queues while the driver maps the range
  again. With 16 GiB registered, one forced compaction: 194-295 ms of stopped queues on 4 KB pages, 0-18 ms on a tmpfs
  `huge=always`; CPU reads and host->device copies were the same on both (table in `DETAILS.md`, method and the other
  backings - hugetlbfs, `hipHostMalloc`, `hipMemCreate` on the host - in the bench folder).

**What it leaves alone:** without `--shared-expert-arena` nothing changes - `PinnedArena` without a file takes the old
path, `shared_publish()` is a no-op, and `ArenaExpertSource`'s load is the same code one level deeper. The SYCL tree
keeps its own V1 copy of the option: a V1 engine refuses a V2 file (size and header do not match) rather than
misreading it, and since it takes no locks its V1 file counts as unused here - unlinked, not truncated, so it keeps
its mapping. Linux only: the code is under `__linux__`; on Windows (as before) and on other platforms, macOS
included, a shared file is refused with "implemented on Linux only".

**Checked**

- HIP build (gfx1201, ROCm 7.14.1): ctest 108/109, the one failure `ple_parity` as before (needs the Q2_0 model).
  `pinned_shared_test`, rewritten for the protocol, runs the other engines as child processes: the second waits while
  the first loads and attaches once it publishes; an attach in the same process; another pack and another size
  refused while mapped; a restart attaches; a file of another pack held by another process refused, replaced once
  that process is gone; a loader killed before publishing leaves the file to the next one. Run on `/dev/shm` and on a
  hugetlbfs mount (`STRATA_TEST_ARENA_DIR`): both report the file whole on 2 MiB pages. CUDA: builds and links with
  nvcc 13.4.92, sm_120, 0 errors; not run on an NVIDIA GPU.
- End to end, R9700 32 GB, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS (55.4 GiB of experts), `--spec 4 --mtp`, 48 greedy tokens, tmpfs
  `size=58G,huge=always,noswap`:

| run | arena checksum (`STRATA_VERIFY_ARENA=1`) | tokens | start to exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| default arena (no flag) | 92a4fc0d243d7402 | reference | 105 s |
| shared file, fresh: loads it | 92a4fc0d243d7402 | same | 108 s |
| shared file again: attaches | 92a4fc0d243d7402 | same | 68 s |
| two engines 3 s apart on a fresh file (2,000-slot caches): one loads, one waits and attaches | 92a4fc0d243d7402 both | same as each other | 111 s, 109 s |

  The load itself is about 32 s here (1.7-1.8 GiB/s from the file cache); the rest of a start is the same either way.
  With the smaller caches the tokens differ from the reference from the 6th on, both engines alike - which experts a
  card holds changes the rounding, as the docs say for other cache sizes. The fresh file of the second run was on 2 MiB
  pages for 50.6 of 55.4 GiB (the machine had just freed a 55 GiB arena; `MADV_COLLAPSE` could not make the rest
  whole), the fourth for all of it after `MADV_COLLAPSE`.
- Two engines generating at the same time, one per GPU (the R9700 x16 and a second R9700 on PCIe 3.0 x4), one copy of
  the experts in RAM (69 GB of 125 GB still available with both running), 512 greedy tokens each:

| arena file | x16 alone | x4 alone | both at once, two runs: x16 / x4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tmpfs `huge=always` | 63.3 tok/s | 42.2 tok/s | 63.9 / 41.3, 66.9 / 42.1 |
| hugetlbfs (`vm.nr_overcommit_hugepages`) | 67.2 tok/s | - | 66.8 / 37.4, 66.9 / 41.9 |

  Same checksum everywhere; each engine's tokens the same alone and in the pair. A forced compaction during the pair's
  decode stopped the x16 engine's queues 0 ms in three of four runs and the x4 engine's 0.6-0.7 s in each, on tmpfs and
  hugetlbfs alike - memory other than the arena, not traced here. The hugetlbfs pages (28,384) went back to the system
  when the file was deleted. The engine runs on hugetlbfs were made before a fix of the start line's count (hugetlb
  pages are in `Shared_Hugetlb`, not `Rss`: it said 0 of 55.44 GiB); the selftest on a hugetlbfs mount
  (`STRATA_TEST_ARENA_DIR`) now shows the file whole on 2 MiB pages.

**Not tested:** NVIDIA at run time (`cudaHostRegister` pins the file's pages there); the server (`serve/`) running two
engines (#1461's desk is one); kernels older than 6.1 (`MADV_COLLAPSE` then reports itself unavailable in the start
line).

pulls.title: Conversation cache: --conversation-cache-park-gain N (opt-in, default 0): a turn that grew a few hundred tokens no longer rewrites a whole 3 GB snapshot
pulls.author: Krypto-Whitehat
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #2264

## Summary

`--conversation-cache-park-gain N` makes parking rate-limited by growth, opt-in and **default 0 = park every turn, byte-identical to today**. A conversation that advanced fewer than N tokens since the copy it would supersede keeps that copy: it still holds this conversation's prefix (a conversation only appends), and re-parking writes the whole snapshot only for the next turn to drop it again.

The report behind this measured 1,418 successful parks for one long single conversation, 2,251.9 GB of host copy written and 105.8 GB (4.7 %) ever read back, with 425 superseded copies dropped and 1,548 s of copy time on the request path. With the gate on it measured 3 park events and 3.26 GB (-66.7 %), the remaining copy being the conversation's first park.

The default stays off because the measurement is from one rig. Deciding whether it should be on by default is the maintainer's call, and nothing here forecloses it.

## What changed

- `include/strata/core/conversation_cache.hpp`: one new const accessor, `parked_prefix_tokens(ids, images, checkpoints, cvec)`. It reports, in tokens, the longest parked entry the outgoing state supersedes - exactly the entries `drop_superseded()` would remove, found the same way `drop_superseded()` finds them (deepest checkpoint the outgoing chain still holds), so the gate can never name a different entry than the one a park would drop.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`, the park decision (line 10445 at `a0116b27`): the existing condition gains one term, `park_worth`. With the default 0 that term is constantly true and the line behaves as before.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the option, the `--conversation-cache-park-gain N` parse (alongside the other `--conversation-cache-*` flags, same `INT32_MAX` bound as `--conversation-cache-slots`), and the help text.
- `src/core/conversation_cache_test.cpp`: seven checks for the accessor - an empty cache, parking a conversation, the entry the chain supersedes, another conversation sharing only the root, the other steering mode, an appended tail, and an entry without checkpoints.

Left alone on purpose: the default (`0`, so no behaviour change without the flag), the copy path itself, `drop_superseded()` and the K/V retention, the physical-RAM admission gate, and every log line. This is one flag, one accessor and one term in one condition.

## Extra Notes

- Checked by build: `cmake -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89` with nvcc 13.4.92 and MSVC 14.44. The `strata` target compiles and links with 0 errors (Windows CUDA, sm_89, so the Linux-only paths of this file are not what that compiles). `conversation_cache_test` builds and passes: 4,226 checks, exit 0.
- The unit test earned its keep: it failed the first assertion because I had expected the entry's live length (6) where the accessor reports the deepest checkpoint (5). `drop_superseded()` keys on the checkpoint, so 5 is the right answer and the expectation was wrong.
- Not tested here: HIP and SYCL (no toolchain on this machine), and **no decode run on this box** - there is no model and no matching rig. Every tok/s number in the issue comes from the reporter's own A/B on an RTX 5090 Laptop, not from a run of this patch. What is verified here is that the change compiles and that the accessor names exactly what a park would supersede.
- The gate is a policy decision with a real trade-off the maintainer should weigh: a conversation that rewrites (edits an earlier turn) is not a prefix of its parked copy, so with the gate on, such a conversation keeps an entry it cannot reuse until it grows past the threshold. That is the same loss the cache already accepts for `drop_superseded`, and it is why this ships opt-in.

pulls.title: Add opt-in browser model downloads and switching through official setup
pulls.author: kw39
pulls.body:
Users currently run setup and separate start scripts to download or change models. This adds an opt-in Models table with download review, progress, start/stop and switching that stays available while setup or a model loads.

Launch with `MODELS.bat` or `sh models.sh`. The Models page listens on `127.0.0.1:8090`; chat and the API use port 8080.

- Read regular model choices from `setup.py` and run `setup.py --setup --yes --no-start`. Official setup chooses GPU, backend, context, KV, low-RAM mode and cache settings. Downloads require a reviewed plan with its data folder pinned.
- Keep a compatible shared Qwen lookup-table location after checking shard metadata. Preserve official setup's `.json.bak` of the user's earlier settings and save the generated config separately to `.json.lookup.bak` before changing paths. Swift and Unsloth keep their own tables; OrcaRouter and experimental models link to manual workflows.
- Check files before switching, refuse busy or externally started servers, and attempt to restore the previous model if a new load fails. Keep Open Chat available for healthy lazy-loading and idle-unloaded servers, which load on the next request.
- Keep management local with Host/Origin checks, same-origin JSON requests and a per-launch token. Recover pending setup after reopening and allow one Models launcher per checkout.

Lifecycle fixes cover the reported Linux TIME_WAIT port reuse and setup cancellation races. Windows retains exclusive port checks and ends the verified owned process tree after unloading, including virtual-environment launcher children.

The normal installer, default web app, server and engine backends remain unchanged from the feature's v0.1.43.1 merge base. The shared management helper receives the port-probe and Windows-stop fixes. No inference tuning or OrcaRouter conversion is added.

Validation:
- All six Windows/Ubuntu CI jobs pass with Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14. Each runs 59 Python tests (one expected platform-specific skip) and five page behavior tests. [Latest CI results](https://github.com/kw39/Strata/actions/runs/38693510176).
- Local Windows 10 / Python 3.14.4 and Ubuntu/WSL2 / Python 3.12.3 runs passed the 59-test suite. Python/JavaScript syntax, Linux launcher syntax and diff checks passed.
- Regression coverage includes official setup backup preservation, repeated lookup recovery, lazy loading, idle-unloaded chat access, real TIME_WAIT sockets, repeated switching, rollback, early/concurrent cancellation, Windows child shutdown and local request protection.
- Headless Edge checks confirmed chat access for lazy/idle-unloaded servers and hidden chat during switching. Earlier desktop/mobile layout checks also passed.
- Tests use fake setup/server processes and status responses: actual model downloads and GPU inference were not run. No C++/CUDA/HIP/SYCL sources changed.

Related to #925. Usage and limitations are documented in `docs/MODEL_MANAGER.md`.

pulls.title: [Engine] OpenAI logprobs / top_logprobs / allowed_token_ids for the CUDA/HIP engine
pulls.author: xiezhipeng-git
pulls.body:
Problem and result. `/v1/chat/completions` on the CUDA/HIP engine accepted `logprobs` / `top_logprobs` and returned HTTP 200, but `choices[0].logprobs.content` was always `[]`. A client that ranks candidate tokens from the model's own distribution — constrained decoding, candidate scoring, tool-choice re-ranking — silently got nothing: the request succeeds, the content is correct, only the field is missing, so the failure is invisible unless the caller asserts on the field. After this change, `logprobs: true` with `top_logprobs` 0..20 (the legacy completions form `logprobs: N` is also accepted) returns one entry per token with its top alternatives, and `allowed_token_ids` returns a distribution renormalised over exactly the ids the caller named.

Related discussion. #1916 proposed the same feature for CUDA/HIP and is closed. This implementation follows the protocol the SYCL port already speaks (835d30b1) and the Metal port (31f26683), so one server-side reader serves all three backends.

Approach.

- Engine half, `src/program/generate.cpp`: `logprobs=K` and `allowed=a,b,c` are two extra keys on the `--serve` GEN line (an engine that predates them skips them as unknown), and one `LP <logprob> [id:logprob ...]` line is written after each `T <id>` in the same flush. The value comes from the verify window's head logits **before** sampling, penalties and temperature, so it is the model's distribution rather than the sampler's. Off by default: a request without `logprobs` produces the previous output byte for byte, and the per-token cost is one integer compare.
- Server half, `serve/server.py`: `sampling_keys` appends the two keys only when asked; `generate` reads each token's `LP` line before yielding the token (a held line is consumed before the next read, so an engine without LP lines loses no lines, and a `DONE` read while looking for one still ends the request); `LogprobEntries` decodes token bytes incrementally so the entries joined spell the reply; `allowed_token_ids` keeps the named ids and renormalises over them; `structured_chunks` re-aligns the entries when `response_format: json_schema` rewrites the content and returns **no** logprobs rather than a set that does not match.
- Compatibility: additive and opt-in. A request that does not ask for logprobs gets the same bytes as before, and no default changes.

Validation.

Rebased onto `upstream/main` `e88ee39d` (which contains `v0.2.0-beta` `b73dbce3`); head `104becfd`. The diff is 3 files, +570/−8, unchanged by the rebase.

Passed:

- Full CUDA build and link, revision `104becfd`: `cmake --build build-lp --target strata` — Release, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89`, CUDA 13.3 (V13.3.73), MSVC 14.41, Windows 11, RTX 4090. `[154/154] Linking CXX executable strata.exe`, exit 0.
- `python -m unittest serve.test_logprobs` — 17 tests, OK, on `104becfd`.
- Hardware run, same revision and engine (`strata.exe` built from it, model Swift-1.5 IQ3_XXS, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`), `max_tokens: 1`, `temperature: 0`, `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false`:
  - non-streamed, `top_logprobs: 20` → `logprobs.content` length 1, `top_logprobs` width 20; entry token `A` at -0.1028 with `B -3.121`, `C -3.201`, `D -5.1109`.
  - the same request with `tools` and `tool_choice: "auto"` → entries present, width 20, labels `A/D/C/B`.
  - `stream: true` → the delta carries `logprobs.content` (1 entry, token `A`, -0.0801, top width 20).
- An external client (a separate project) that scores 5 candidate labels from this endpoint: 7 scoring requests in a 30k-token session, 0 errors, 0 disabled calls. Run against the same commit before the rebase (`80494788`); the endpoint behaviour it depends on is the same code path exercised above.

Failed: none observed.

Not run:

- HIP backend build. `src/program/generate.cpp` is shared by the CUDA and HIP builds; only the CUDA configuration was built here (no AMD GPU or toolchain on this machine).
- SYCL backend build. It carries its own implementation (`install_logprobs` in `sycl/serve/server_intel.py`) and this change does not touch it; no Intel GPU or toolchain here.
- `--batch` mode: see Limits.

Limits.

- `--batch` does not return logprobs. `generate_batched` never reads `LP` lines; only the solo/serial path (`generate`) does, so a server started with `--batch` answers `logprobs.content: []`. Giving the batched path the same read-before-yield step is the remaining work if that combination is wanted.
- The reported logprob describes the model's distribution before penalties and temperature, not the post-sampling one.
- With `response_format: json_schema` the returned content may not be spelled by the tokens; in that case no logprobs are returned, by design.
- CUDA/HIP only; the SYCL and Metal implementations are untouched.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: the RAM gate releases the heap and stops evicting when it cannot help (rebased #1394)
pulls.author: alanthinker
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The physical-RAM gate of the parking path assumes an evicted parked conversation is visible to `/proc/meminfo` before the next check reads it. That assumption is wrong for the allocations this cache actually makes: `ConversationBuffer` is a list of 16 MiB segments, and glibc's mmap threshold is dynamic - the first generation of segments is mmap'd, freeing one raises the threshold past 16 MiB (capped at 32 MiB), and every later segment comes from the main heap. Freeing one of those only moves the bytes onto the allocator's free list: RSS, and with it `MemAvailable`, does not move.

On today's `main` (0.2.0-beta) the gate added for #1347 evicts parked conversations one at a time and re-reads the figure after each. In steady state the figure never moves, so the loop can empty the whole cache and still refuse the snapshot - worse than the refusal it was meant to remove: every parked conversation is lost and every later request re-reads its whole prompt (measured in #1347: 270k tokens, 96 s, 32 times in one session).

After this change a release (`malloc_trim(0)`) runs before the first re-read and after every eviction, so a dropped conversation shows up in the next reading; and where the missing bytes exceed what the parked conversations could give back, the gate gives up before evicting anything.

## Related discussion

#1347 (the issue, reproduced on an RTX 4080 SUPER with 91 GB RAM), #1394 (the original PR by @Arthur031221, unmergeable after #879 / #1601 / #1573 landed), and this thread:

- @qiuzan2001's point about the two contradicting comments is fixed in the second commit.
- @alfre2v reproduced the bug independently on an RTX 3090 / 64 GB box (glibc 2.35, sm_86) and tested this branch there: unpatched v0.1.44.1 failed in every run (8 refusals in one, the engine heap reaching 6.9 GiB, a 214K-token snapshot re-read in 90 s), and this PR admitted the snapshot in all three of its runs with no cost on fresh 4K-32K prompts. Their numbers also answer the trim-timing question raised above: on a heap holding up to 5.5 GiB of freed segments a trim took 37-482 ms (median about 111 ms, roughly 80-90 ms per GiB returned), 12-14 trims per 19-minute run, about 2.4 s in total - against a 90 s re-read. They also measured two side effects (the heap stays large between trims; long prompts read about 2% slower right after a trim) and one residual case outside this PR, the post-capture floor check dropping a freshly captured snapshot in 1 of 3 runs.

## Approach

- `conversation_release_freed_memory()` (`malloc_trim(0)` under `__GLIBC__`, a no-op elsewhere) is called before the first re-read and after every eviction.
- `ConversationCache::admit_ram()` gives up **before** evicting anything when the missing bytes exceed `evictable_bytes()` - what `evict_oldest()` may actually take, i.e. entries **not** holding a pinned shared prefix - and re-checks the figure after each reading, so losing telemetry ends the loop.
- The reading stays the memory guard's (`sample_host_memory()`: `MemAvailable`, the cgroup limits above the engine, `--memory-limit-mib`) and the refusal line keeps `ram_note()`.

## Validation

Rebased on `main` at `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3); branch tip `3dbc9aca`. Built and tested by me on the serving box from #1347: Linux, RTX 4080 SUPER (32 GB), 94 GB RAM, CUDA 13.2, sm_89.

Passed:
- `cmake -B build -DSTRATA_BUILD_CONVERSATION_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89 && cmake --build build --target conversation_cache_test conversation_memory_test`
- `conversation_cache_test`: 4829 checks passed
- `conversation_memory_test`: 24 checks passed
- the cache tests main added since: `session_save_reclaim_test` 119 checks, `conversation_file_test` 201 checks, `conversation_split_failure_test` passed
- the full engine target `strata` compiles (CUDA 13.2, sm_89)

Failed: none.

Not run: running the rebuilt 0.2.0-beta engine on the GPU (this box still serves on the deployed 0.1.x build; the binary compiled, it was not started); HIP, SYCL and Metal builds.

Separate from my checks: @alfre2v ran this branch (at `ab963c96` + `f09887f6`) end-to-end on an RTX 3090 / 64 GB box, results in Related discussion; their soak numbers are theirs, not mine.

## Limits

- The -0.3 MB / 127.7 MB figures in the first comment were measured on the v0.1.43.1-era serving heap; I have not reproduced that heap shape on 0.2.0-beta, so I quote no new trim numbers of my own - @alfre2v's trim timings above are the measured answer.
- `malloc_trim(0)` returns what has coalesced to an arena's top; a mid-heap segment that cannot coalesce stays invisible even after the release. The loop still converges: further evictions eventually coalesce, and `evictable_bytes()` bounds the case where even emptying the cache could not help.
- The trim runs only when a reading comes out short, so between parks the freed segments stay in the heap (@alfre2v: up to 8.9 GiB on their box); other programs on the machine see less free RAM in between, and long prompts read about 2% slower right after a trim (fresh pages fault in).
- The post-capture floor check keeps its own "freed heap is visible at once" assumption and can still drop a freshly captured snapshot (@alfre2v saw it in 1 of 3 runs); this PR does not touch it.
- `--session-save-reclaim` (#1573) keeps the same assumption between its steps; left alone here to keep this PR to the parking gate.
