pulls.title: --session-state-codec bf16: a saved/parked conversation's running state at half the bytes
pulls.author: sumomomomomo
pulls.body:
Closes #2377

## Overview

Adds opt-in `--session-state-codec bf16` to reduce the RAM and disk needed for conversation checkpoints. For the tested model, checkpoint state is approximately **50% smaller** and session files are **5.6–39.3% smaller**, providing headroom for more cached conversations or denser resume points.

In the 32K workload, **BF16 at 8K checkpoint spacing delivered comparable complete-turn latency to FP32 at the default 16K spacing**. Parking was faster across the tested context sizes, while continuing resumes added approximately **2–6 ms**.

The [benchmark harness, raw results and engine logs](https://github.com/sumomomomomo/strata-bf16-bench-artifacts) are now public.

## Architecture

- **Encode at capture:** retained checkpoints use the configured codec immediately, including layer-split checkpoint parts.
- **Keep computation FP32:** live GPU state and temporary working-state transfers remain FP32.
- **Restore lazily:** only the selected checkpoint is decoded; other retained snapshots remain compressed.
- **Copy directly when parking:** existing BF16 checkpoints are copied without widening and re-encoding.
- **Preserve per-checkpoint identity:** each snapshot records its codec, supporting mixed chains and cross-codec reads.

The codec covers GDN recurrence/convolution history, PLE history, and QSA indexer tails/dead keys. Integer positions and K/V storage are unchanged. Encoding uses round-to-nearest-even and is lossy; widening is exact.

## Validation

Benchmarks used Linux, CUDA 12.8, a Tesla V100 32 GB as the single model GPU, a 24-core/32-thread Intel CPU, 93 GB reported RAM, IQ3_S, INT8 K/V, and a Samsung 990 EVO Plus SSD.

Latency comparisons used the same `strata.head` binary, with runs recorded at `e79abfc0`: two rounds with reversed arm order, two warm-ups and ten measured repetitions per round. Figures below are medians of round medians. RSS measurements were re-run at `79955461`.

### Checkpoint spacing and turn latency

A fresh 31,813-token document followed by short turns:

| Configuration | Fresh prefill | Turn prompt phase | Complete turn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP32 / 16K spacing | 21.717 s | 736.5 ms | 1.074 s |
| BF16 / 16K spacing | 21.703 s | 687.5 ms | 1.027 s |
| FP32 / 8K spacing | 21.796 s | 806.0 ms | 1.135 s |
| BF16 / 8K spacing | 21.868 s | 721.0 ms | 1.054 s |

Complete-turn timings include parking, resumption and generation; they are not TTFT or isolated capture timings. This sweep measures latency; recall is assessed separately below.

### Parked conversation performance

At 16K checkpoint spacing, FP32 → BF16:

| Context | Continuing resume | Parking on rewind | Complete rewind request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K | 49.25 → 51.48 ms | 142.13 → 90.78 ms | 0.329 → 0.283 s |
| 63K | 71.15 → 77.05 ms | 163.98 → 104.90 ms | 0.344 → 0.295 s |
| 121K | 121.98 → 127.53 ms | 198.33 → 101.25 ms | 0.432 → 0.333 s |

In a separate 32K run with four parked images, cache-accounted allocation fell from **3.73 GB to 3.08 GB (17.4%)**. These figures include allocator capacity; they are not serialized payload sizes or a guarantee of proportionally more conversations per cache budget.

### SAVE / RESTORE memory

Observed RSS growth, FP32 → BF16:

| Context | First SAVE after prefill | Disk RESTORE |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 32K | 353.2 → 180.5 MiB | 350.3 → 406.5 MiB |
| 63K | 354.0 → 181.2 MiB | 805.1 → 861.3 MiB |

First SAVE was measured separately from later saves, which reuse allocations. RESTORE figures are medians of nine repetitions. BF16 RESTORE grew RSS by approximately **56.2 MiB more** at both sizes.

RSS was sampled every 20 ms on fresh processes; these are observed increments, not guaranteed peak-memory bounds.

### Functional and failure-path checks

- Explicit rewind needle questions: **20/20 per tested cell for both codecs** at 32K, 63K and approximately 121K, including freshly captured BF16 checkpoints.
- Earlier disk/park recall: **9/9 at 32K**; disk recall **3/3 at approximately 121K**. Repeated park/resume/generate cycles: **12/12**, both codecs.
- Unit coverage includes rounding and special values, file versions, mixed chains, stage split/merge, validation, memory accounting and SAVE admission.
- Allocation-failure and reporting coverage: **43 capture checks and 25 reporting checks**, including sanitizer runs.
- CUDA suite: **125/126 passing**; `ple_parity` requires a missing artifact and also fails before this change.

## Compatibility and limitations

- Opt-in; FP32, checkpoint spacing and retention defaults remain unchanged. Default FP32 serialization was checked against the parent build.
- All-FP32 files remain version 1; BF16 files use version 2. Codec-aware engines read either; older builds reject version 2.
- HIP and SYCL remain unbuilt; Windows remains untested. The SYCL port does not implement the BF16 option.
- Stage splitting has unit coverage; real multi-GPU park/restore remains untested.
- Isolated capture latency, retained RAM before the first park, equivalent-history memory at 8K/16K, and memory-tight admission improvements remain unmeasured.
- Logits/KL comparisons and broader long-continuation quality evaluation remain outstanding. Needle results establish behavior on the tested workloads.

Implementation and detailed results: `docs/STATE_SNAPSHOT_BF16.md`.

Public evidence: [artifact manifest](https://github.com/sumomomomomo/strata-bf16-bench-artifacts/blob/main/MANIFEST.md), [harness and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/sumomomomomo/strata-bf16-bench-artifacts/tree/main/harness), and [raw results](https://github.com/sumomomomomo/strata-bf16-bench-artifacts/tree/main/results). The manifest identifies historical runs, superseded measurements and provenance gaps; earlier session-file timings are not presented as current-build performance.

## AI Disclosure

Created with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3 3.05bpw.

pulls.title: drop-file-cache: --drop-file-cache returns the model files' page cache after the startup reads (opt-in)
pulls.author: G0-0000
pulls.body:
## What it changes

New opt-in engine flag `--drop-file-cache` (Linux): after the startup reads complete, and only when a
self-check confirms that no expert is read from the files, the engine issues madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)
followed by posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED) over the model files' mapping, which returns the page
cache to the kernel (both calls are needed; either alone does not release the pages).

## What it leaves alone

With the flag absent, no syscall is issued and nothing changes byte for byte.  The self-check refuses
to run the drop whenever any expert is read from the files (mapped-only layouts, partial complements).

## Why

The engine maps the model GGUFs MAP_SHARED and reads the experts through them once; the kernel keeps
those pages for the life of the process, so a 24/7 server holds a full extra copy of the expert data in
the page cache (measured 55.4 GiB on the host below) even though every expert is already in VRAM or in
the page-locked RAM copy - the reads that actually need the cache are only the lend-region refills
(~4 GiB).  Related discussions: #1194, #1682, #1571 (the Windows working-set analogue).

## How it was measured

Same host as the NUMA placement (Supermicro X10DRC, V100-SXM2-32GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS,
125 GB RAM):

- Cached dropped by 50-57 GiB (varies with the baseline page-cache state), in 6.7-8.2 s, once per start;
- node1 free memory +~20 GiB;
- decode: interleaved A/B, 46.6 -> 46.7 tok/s (no regression); the first large prompt re-reads the lent
  region (~1.2-4 GiB) from the drive once (+5-8% on that request), and the pages return through the
  file cache afterwards.

## How it was tested

GPU-free: a synthetic two-shard unit test (mapped pages 3452 -> 0, the advised byte count, and a
byte-identical re-read after the drop) plus the full non-CUDA ctest subset; on-GPU: two controlled
stop-the-service windows (reclaim amount, refill placement, interleave A/B) and a production run.

## Note

A local extension binds the refill reads to the cold NUMA node (so the pages that come back land away
from the GPU's node); it depends on the --numa-hot-node feature and can be sent as a follow-up if this
is of interest.

pulls.title: numa-placement: --numa-hot-node N - keep the GPU-side host pools on the GPU's NUMA node (Linux, dual-socket, opt-in)
pulls.author: G0-0000
pulls.body:
## What it changes

New opt-in engine flag `--numa-hot-node <n|off>` (Linux, dual-socket hosts):

- **The resident complement** (the page-locked RAM copy of the experts the GPU cache does not hold) is
  claimed on node N **before** the expert cache's startup fill reads tens of GiB through the page cache
  (mmap -> mbind(MPOL_BIND) -> pre-touch -> the existing register+lock path consumes it).
- **The five pinned host pools** the per-token path touches - the K/V streaming host copy, the doorbell,
  the host embedding, the session loop scratch and the weight staging buffers - allocate with the calling
  thread bound to node N.
- **A conversation cache's parked segments** (16 MiB glibc segments, bulk snapshot data) are faulted in on
  the **cold** node - derived as the first node that is not the hot one - leaving the GPU's node to the
  pools above.
- The NUMA primitives (mbind/set_mempolicy wrappers) moved from expert_source.cpp's anonymous namespace
  into a shared `numa_policy.hpp`, and `docs/AI_SETUP.md` / `docs/DETAILS.md` document how to find the
  GPU's node at install time.

## What it leaves alone

With the flag absent or `off`, **no syscall is issued** and every allocation, output and log line is
byte-identical to before.  `0` is a valid node number (bind to node 0); only `off` - or the flag's
absence - turns the feature off.  A single-node host has no cold node and the S3 part does nothing there.

## Why

#1900 sketched this.  On a two-socket host the GPU hangs off one node; the engine's hot host pools want
to be on that node, but the startup fill's page cache and the complement used to race for it, and under
memory pressure the complement ended up on the other socket (measured 80.6% before, 100% after, stable
across restarts).

## How it was measured

Supermicro X10DRC (dual Xeon Broadwell-EP), Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS:

- complement: 31.42 GiB, 100% on the GPU's node (`bind:1`), claimed in 18-37 s before the fill;
- the five pinned pools: 100% on the GPU's node (unchanged steady state - the win is determinism under
  pressure);
- parked conversation snapshots: 89-100% on the cold node;
- decode/prompt speeds unchanged (the placement moves pages, not the token path), verified with
  interleaved A/B.

## How it was tested

GPU-free: complement-claim unit tests (per-page node check via get_mempolicy, duplicate-claim and
out-of-range rejection) and the full non-CUDA ctest subset.  On-GPU: startup runs, parity runs, and
three controlled stop-the-service windows comparing numa_maps aggregates.

## Open question

The node is read once at install time (`cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/<GPU-BDF>/numa_node`) and written into
the configuration - we did **not** add runtime auto-detection, on purpose.  If you would rather have
setup's check print a suggestion (or anything else around this), we are happy to do it.

pulls.title: Remote stage: a worker for the SYCL build (Intel Arc), stacked on #1748 / #1887 (protocol 7); STRATA_LOGPOS_IDS for cross-engine KL
pulls.author: YukihiroHemmi
pulls.body:
Stacked on lask3802's `remote-stage-rowfmt` (618d8f99: #1748 with 5c454ed6 and `--pipeline-windows 2` on a remote main, #1887's conversation checkpoints, the `row_formats` hello, protocol 7), unchanged. Rebased onto it on 2026-10-14; the branch before that is tagged `remote-stage-v5-cc7af052` in this fork (its own bf16 opt-in, `STRATA_STAGE_ROWS_BF16`, is dropped in favour of `STRATA_REMOTE_ROWS`). This adds a **worker for the SYCL build** (Intel Arc) and two measurement-only environment variables. Nothing changes unless `--stage-worker` is given to the SYCL build, or `STRATA_LOGPOS_IDS` / `STRATA_LOGPOS_SPLIT_AT` are set.

## What it changes

- **`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`**: the SYCL engine can run as the last stage worker (`--serve --stage-worker PORT --stage-begin K --stream-experts`): layers [K, 48) with all their experts in VRAM (read from the GGUF; it stops at start with the count if they do not fit), its own dense weights and session, no head, MTP, PLE table or embedding table. The main process (and any relay) is the CUDA or HIP build. On protocol 7 it keeps its layers' part of the conversation checkpoints (`reset(keep)`, `CkptSave` / `CkptRestore`, `kStageCkptMax`, `stage_ckpt_ram_ok`) as the CUDA/HIP last worker does, and reads and sends whatever row format the main process asks for (`serve_stage` lists every format; `stage_link.cpp` converts). A relay worker, `--remote-stage`, `--vision`, `--mtp` and `--pipeline-windows` are refused at start on the SYCL build. The SYCL `Verifier` gets `set_no_head`, `GgufExpertSource` gets `set_layer_range`, `sycl/src/core/conversation_state.cpp` gets the explicit-length checkpoint save/restore that #1887 added to `src/core`.
- **`include/strata/core/logpos_ids.hpp`** (new, shared): `STRATA_LOGPOS_IDS=<baseline dump>` makes `STRATA_LOGPOS` also write the log-probabilities of the baseline's top-k ids at each position, so two engines' distributions can be compared by KL without the ids drifting out of the top-k; `STRATA_LOGPOS_SPLIT_AT=N` reads [0, N) of a prompt as chunks and the rest as windows (both trees). Off by default; `src/core/logpos_ids_test.cpp` covers the header.
- **Docs**: `docs/REMOTE_STAGE.md` (an "Intel Arc as a worker" section and the measurements below), `docs/INTEL.md` (a note).

## What it leaves alone

Every CUDA/HIP source of the base except the one-line `logpos::write_ids` call in `src/core/verify.cpp` and the `STRATA_LOGPOS_SPLIT_AT` branch in `src/program/generate.cpp`; both are inert without the variable. No defaults change.

## Checks

- `stage_link_test`, `stage_ckpt_store_test` and `logpos_ids_test` pass on the CUDA (sm_89, sm_120), HIP (gfx1100, ROCm 7.10) and SYCL (bmg-g31) builds of this branch.
- Before the rebase: builds of 4bbcb16e and of this branch, started without the new options, wrote byte-identical `STRATA_LOGPOS` dumps for both the CUDA engine (4070) and the SYCL engine (B70).

## Measured

2026-10-14, this branch, four GPUs on three PCs over 2.5 GbE (main RTX 5070 Ti layers 0-10 → HIP relay RX 7900 XT 11-22 → CUDA relay RTX 4070 23-29 → SYCL last worker Arc Pro B70 30-47), OrcaRouter Q4_K_S, served settings (`--max-context 262144 --kv-resident 32768 --prefill 2048`):

| build and flags | decode tok/s | 1K prompt | 4K prompt |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| before the rebase (protocol 5, our bf16 opt-in) | 58.9-78.8 | 437 | 849 |
| this branch, `STRATA_REMOTE_ROWS=bf16` | 59.4-80.4 | 439 | 850 |
| this branch, bf16, `--pipeline-windows 2` | 53.6-74.1 | 441 | 851 |

- KL against the 5070 Ti alone (5 texts, 1,363 positions): 0.0169, argmax 93.0% (0.0170 with our earlier bf16, 0.0179 with fp32).
- Checkpoints through the SYCL last stage (`--prompt-cache 6`): two 4-turn chats on a 30,783-token shared system prompt, sent twice: time to first token 27.4-30.5 s for every request without checkpoints, 0.25-2.6 s with them (after the first); 15 restores on both sides, 0 errors; at exact flags 8 of 8 repeats byte-identical.

Earlier (2026-10-13, before the rebase): one PC, loopback (4070 main, B70 worker, IQ2_XS, K=12): decode 73-109 tok/s vs 44-74 on the B70 alone, KL 0.135 against the B70 alone with a backend floor of 0.152. Two PCs (5070 Ti main, B70 worker, IQ3_XXS, K=23): decode 78-108 vs 81-104 on the 5070 Ti alone, KL 0.015.

Not run: HIP as the main process, a relay through a SYCL worker, images, Windows builds of this branch. Raw data and the measurement scripts (`kl_run.py`, `kl_check.py`, `speed_bench.py`) are available on request.


YukihiroHemmi@🐜

pulls.title: test: exercise uncached BPE paths in tokenizer parity checks
pulls.author: mustafaerdinc
pulls.body:
## Summary

Tokenizer parity checks can reuse cached piece IDs from a previous algorithm and pass without executing the requested scan, heap, or default path. Clear the cache between comparisons and add regressions that prove deliberately incorrect output is detected.

Related to the investigation in #1385. This test coverage change does not establish the cause or resolution of that intermittent crash.

## What changed

- Clear the piece cache before forced scan, forced heap, and default parity comparisons.
- Add three negative regressions covering incorrect scan, heap, and default output after cache population.
- Use an independent serial reference for shared-tokenizer workers. Exercise warmed-cache and uncached runs, verifying all eight uncached workers reach BPE.
- Remove the speculative interpreter-fault attribution from the test docstring. Production tokenizer code and runtime defaults are unchanged.

## Validation

- The three negative regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward; independent review found no blocking issue in this test-only change.
- After rebasing onto main at a0116b2, ran the following on macOS arm64 with CPython 3.14.8 and the model tokenizer files available: **24 tests passed, zero skips**, in 18.825 seconds.

```sh
STRATA_TOKENIZER=/path/to/tokenizer PYTHON_JIT=0 python -B -m unittest -v \
  serve.test_detok tools.test_strata_tokenizer tools.test_tokenizer_plain_spans
```

- No CUDA, HIP, or SYCL source is changed; no backend build is claimed.

## Extra Notes

The threaded wrapper proves test coverage, not the cause or resolution of #1385. The original-workload and minimal-reproducer investigation remains separate; this PR should not close that issue.

  reports' script, unchanged), `table.py`, and per arm `config.json` (local paths rewritten), `summary.json`,
  `results.json`, `BUILD.txt`. No engine or docs change.

## Extra Notes

- Both cards ran with a 245 W board power cap (default 255 W); the earlier reports from this machine did not state it.
- The prs arms bundle several open pull requests and switches; only the bundle was measured.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, PCIe 4.0 x8 each) / Ryzen 5 5600X, ROCm 10.0.

pulls.title: Batch decode: one launch for all rows in QSA attention and GDN recurrence (opt-in)
pulls.author: yi-sudo
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change)

## Summary
With `--batch N`, the verify window ran QSA block scoring, top-k and decode attention as one launch per row, and the
GDN recurrence (in the window and in the 1-row commit) as one launch per slot. With 4-8 live slots, these serial
launches are most of what a window costs beyond the expert reads. Two opt-in switches run each of them as one launch
for all rows:

- `STRATA_BATCH_ATTN_ROWS=1`: block scores, top-k and decode attention for all of the window's rows (up to 8), one
  launch each. Every row still reads its own slot's indexer keys and K/V pools. These are passed by value as kernel
  params, so the graph captured per row layout stays valid. A slot that streams KV (`kv_mode` 1) keeps the per-row
  path.
- `STRATA_BATCH_GDN_GROUPS=1`: the GDN recurrence in the window, and the commit of 1-row groups, for all slots in one
  launch (`grid.y` = slot group). The conv commits stay per slot.

**Default path:** with both switches unset, the engine runs the same launches as before. Only kernel params with a
`{}` default were added, and they are unused when `n = 0`.

**Exactness with the switches on:** the arithmetic per row is the same. I sent 4 concurrent temperature-0 prompts
(`parity.py`) and the patched build produced byte-identical output to upstream `a0116b2`, with both `--batch 4` and
`--batch 8`.

**Measured** 2026-10-13, same day for both arms, on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (96 GB, driver
610.57.04, CUDA 13.0, Linux). Settings: IQ3_S with all 24,576 experts in VRAM, `--kv int8`, 262144 context,
`--mtp --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--vision`. The load went through the HTTP server: C different story prompts sent
at once, 1024 tokens each, temperature 0.7, mean of 2 rounds. Total tok/s:

| Concurrent | `--batch 4` | + both switches | `--batch 8` (reserve 6144 MiB) | + both switches |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 179.2 | 179.4 | 186.6 | 179.7 |
| 2 | 204.1 | 218.7 | | |
| 3 | 243.2 | 276.6 | | |
| 4 | 268.4 | 311.7 | 267.7 | 311.6 |
| 6 | | | 297.7 | 354.8 |
| 8 | | | 308.4 | 374.8 |

The window time, from `strata batch:` in the engine log:
- 4 rows: 14.3 ms → 12.2 ms
- 8 rows: 24.6 ms → 19.9 ms

That is about 1.7-1.9 ms per added row instead of 2.4 ms. The same patch on 0.1.43 (`7695859`) gave 268.5 → 312.9
(`--batch 4`, 4 clients) and 308.5 → 377.8 (`--batch 8`, 8 clients).

Scripts, raw JSON and engine logs: https://github.com/yi-sudo/strata-batch-boost (`lab/`, `lab/results/latest-a0116b2`).

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/qsa_decode_attn.hpp`:
  - `attn_chunk_kernel` takes an optional `QsaAttnPoolsRows`; query `blockIdx.z` uses its own pools.
  - New `qsa_decode_attn_batch_rows`.
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp`:
  - `block_scores_multi_kernel` takes an optional `QsaScoreRows` (per-query pooled/dead keys).
  - New `qsa_block_scores_rows`.
- `src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/verify_kernels.hpp`:
  - `gdn_step_norm_multi_kernel` takes an optional `GdnGroups` (per-group state, keep, first row, token count).
  - New `gdn_step_norm_groups`, for the window and for the commit.
- `src/core/verify.cpp`:
  - `record_window` uses the row launches in the `batch_rec_` QSA and GDN branches when the switches are set.
  - `capture_commit_batch` collects 1-row groups into one GDN commit launch.
- `docs/BATCHING.md`: a short section with the switches and the table above.

What this leaves alone: the solo path, `--batch-mtp`, layer splits (not tested), KV streaming (falls back), the conv
commits, the indexer appends, and every default.

## Extra Notes
- **Backends:** built and run with CUDA (sm_120) only. The `.cu` files are also part of the HIP build, which I could
  not build here (no ROCm). The SYCL port has its own copies of these files and is untouched.
- **Not tested:** a layer split / multi-GPU, experts on PCIe or the CPU, and AMD.
- **Related PRs:** #1524 also targets concurrent throughput, but by a different route (wider speculative batches,
  shared experts). #1888 changes the QSA decode attention kernel for the single-query case. This PR is independent of
  both and only merges launches.
- **Also tried, not included:** more MTP drafts per slot with `--batch-mtp`. Drafts are accepted 50-57% of the time
  in batch windows, but a row only pays above ~67%, so it was slower (raw data in the repo above).

pulls.title: docs(bench): RTX 3060 12GB / 32GB RAM Coder IQ1_M with Budget12 64K profile
pulls.author: wookie4lif3
pulls.body:
# docs(bench): RTX 3060 12GB / 32GB RAM Coder IQ1_M with Budget12 64K profile

## Summary

Adds a community results-only report from one Windows 11 / RTX 3060 12GB / i5-11400F / 31.8 GiB RAM machine running **unmodified upstream Strata v0.1.43** (`7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`) with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Coder IQ1_M**.

The contribution has three **separately labeled** evidence groups: the original upstream 32K speed suite, non-stock near-32K extensions, and a distinct 65,536-token Budget12 configuration and one-shot reasoning investigation. It does **not** change any Strata source or model weights.

## Stock and custom 32K measurements

- Stock `tools/strata_bench.py` (3 repeats): **33/33** completed requests; short-chat decode median **26.0 tok/s** (9 requests); fresh 4K prefill **717.0 tok/s**; fresh 16K prefill **904.5 tok/s**. Original `results.json` included.
- Custom near-32K extension: **31,294** actual fresh input tokens, **908.4 tok/s** median prefill and **34.56 s** median first-token latency (n=3). This is **not** an exact 32,768-token input.
- Built-in near-30.5K needle check: **3/3 found**, one attempt each at 10%, 50%, and 90% positions. A predictable 256-token sequence achieved **57.2 tok/s** median decode (n=3); **not** a general chat-speed claim.

## Separate experimental Budget12 64K profile

- **Actual, SHA-256-verified local JSON exported as a sanitized, non-runnable path-placeholder config**, with the original source and sanitized-output hashes recorded in `budget12-export-receipt.json`. New files `budget12-sanitized-config.json` and `budget12-REPRODUCE.md` document the exact observed flags and how to adapt paths on a different installation.
- Config: `--max-context 65536`, `--kv int8` (non-streaming), `--expert-cache auto`, `--prefill auto`, `--spec 4`, `--spec-min-p 0.5`, and `--resident-budget-gib 12`. The verified original configuration was **not modified**, and the upstream engine was **not forked**. Budget12 run reported **2,152 expert cache slots**.
- Full-resident 64A finished with ~451 MiB free host RAM; 64B stopped at the safety preflight. Budget12 enabled completed ~54K-input runs with much more sampled host RAM available, with different throughput and task results.
- Exact-answer diagnostics (single-shot cases): 64F **10/10** manual repository evaluation, 64G **12/13**, 64H **accuracy not evaluable** (no final answer; `length`), 64I **12/18**, 64J **24/24** (including six canonical/replay record-provenance fields). The per-request `reasoning_budget_tokens: 6144` and `max_tokens: 8192` produced valid completions for 64I/J.

## Evidence and limitations

- Stock `results.json`, custom `extended-results.json`, needle results, the exact custom benchmark script and separate 64K summary CSV are included. The synthetic 64K grades are self-contained research tests summarized in the report; private case packets and full reasoning transcripts are **not** included.
- All tests are from **one host**. 64I and 64J differ in randomized input and prompting, so their score difference **does not demonstrate a controlled causal improvement** or general 100% reliability. The 64J prefill rate slowed to **349.2 tok/s** from 64I's **833.5 tok/s**, with the cause unknown.
- The sanitized JSON intentionally contains invalid local-path placeholders. It is a verified configuration **template for manual adaptation, not a drop-in one-click installation**. RAM/VRAM safety thresholds were enforced by an external benchmark runner, not Strata itself. No hardware-independent or production-grade correctness claim is made.

Please review as a **documentation-and-community-benchmark contribution** following `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`. No runtime changes, binaries, copyrighted model weights, private machine paths or raw user test transcripts are proposed.

pulls.title: HIP gfx1100: bit-exact decode and prompt-path speedups (+12% decode, KL 0)
pulls.author: android-imdad
pulls.body:
Bit-exact speedups for HIP on gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX), measured with `tools/strata_bench.py --long` against same-day upstream main `a0116b27`. Every change keeps the output identical: teacher-forced KL against upstream main at the same expert slot count is **0.0000, 100.0% same top-1, PPL 4.442 / 4.442** over 2,557 positions (16K / 16K / 64K prompts, verify-window decode). Changes that alter numerics (the Q8_0 hyper-connection read from BF16 packs, dropping the BF16 hc copies) are left out of this PR.

## Results (RX 7900 XTX, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 62.4 GiB, Linux, ROCm 10.2, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S)

Alternating rounds; each cell is the median of 3 runs. Full reports, `results.json` and engine log excerpts are in `bench/results/2026-10-13-community-rx-7900-xtx-gfx1100-exact-speedups/`.

| test | upstream r1 | upstream r2 | PR r1 | PR r2 | PR defaults-only | PR vs upstream |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| chat decode tok/s | 84.8 | 88.7 | 96.5 | 97.3 | 92.3 | **+11.7%** |
| 4K prompt tok/s | 1049.0 | 1088.8 | 1118.0 | 1117.0 | 1116.6 | +4.5% |
| 16K prompt tok/s | 1360.5 | 1401.1 | 1427.1 | 1425.3 | 1426.3 | +3.3% |
| 32K prompt tok/s | 1421.7 | 1420.6 | 1445.6 | 1442.5 | 1444.8 | +1.6% |
| agent turn first token (s) | 3.97 | 3.82 | 3.75 | 3.75 | 3.73 | -3.7% |
| agent decode tok/s | 94.1 | 99.1 | 105.2 | 115.7 | 107.7 | **+14.3%** |

Every PR round beats every upstream round in each row. "PR defaults-only" = the PR build without the seven opt-in env switches below, i.e. what a user gets without changing their config. Both engines were built with the same CMake options (`gfx1100`, `-DSTRATA_HIP_EXP_LAYOUTS -DSTRATA_HIP_MMVQ_IL`) and run with the same config, no control vector.

## What changes

**On by default** (each is bitwise the old path; `=0` turns it off):
- `STRATA_ROUTE_FAST`: router lane exchanges as DPP moves; the MoE input copied to the host by the router GEMV's blocks
- `STRATA_GDN_NORM128`: GDN output norm with its one working row group and DPP exchanges (9.3 → 2.0 µs a layer)
- `STRATA_GRUP_WIDE`: the hyper-connection read's up kernel with 512 threads for 1-6 tokens
- `STRATA_TOPK_REGKEYS`, `STRATA_TOPK_SCAN`: QSA top-k keys in registers; serial scans as block scans
- `STRATA_MTP_SELECT_WIDE`: the drafter's row select over 40 blocks (12 → 2.2 µs)
- `STRATA_WAIT_COPY256`: the expert plan read over PCIe by 256 threads
- `STRATA_MULTI_BLOCK_ARGMAX` on HIP (was CUDA-only): 12.0 → 6.0 µs a call
- `STRATA_ADAPT_COPY2`: adaptive-tier swap copies over two DMA streams
- `STRATA_DMA_FLAG_WRITE` (HIP): the PCIe share's landed flag written by the copy stream (`hipStreamWriteValue32`, 6.7 µs) instead of a host function (15 µs)
- `STRATA_DQ_FAST` (Q6_K / IQ4_XS dequant by warps), `STRATA_SCAN_UNROLL` (argmax / top-probability scans), `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_BOUND` (the drafter's attention merge stops at the last filled chunk)

**Opt-in** (env `=1`): `STRATA_WAIT_FUSE`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_PLAIN` (needs `-DSTRATA_HIP_MMVQ_IL`), `STRATA_COMBINE_HITS`, `STRATA_ROUTE_PUB`, `STRATA_WAIT_COMBINE`, `STRATA_PF_LEAN_ISSUE`, `STRATA_PF_COPY2`. Also opt-in and neutral here: `STRATA_GR_FUSE`, `STRATA_DOWN_SWIGLU`, `STRATA_PCIE_FORK`, `STRATA_ADAPT_LAYERWAIT`, `STRATA_GRUP_PF`. Test knobs: `STRATA_EXPERT_SLOTS_MAX`, `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75_NC`.

**Fix:** with `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_PLAIN`, the 32-column hc up kernel (which does not write the interleaved `q8_il` copy) is skipped. Otherwise the attention projections read a stale copy and replies stop after one token. Without the interleaved copy the kernel choice is unchanged.

## How it was checked
- KL: `--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0`, the same arguments for both engines, 7,229 expert slots on both; upstream against itself also gives 0.0000 (`kl-teacher-forced.txt` in the results folder).
- Each change was also checked individually during development with a deterministic serve harness (same drafts and text hashes) and kernel-level random-input harnesses for the selection kernels.

## Not tested
- **CUDA and SYCL builds** (no NVIDIA or Intel GPU here). The new HIP-only code (DPP / `permlanex16`, `hipStreamWriteValue32`) is guarded by `__HIPCC__` / `STRATA_USE_HIP`, but the shared `.cu` files were not compiled for CUDA. A CUDA build check before merge would be appreciated.
- Other AMD architectures (gfx906, gfx12, RDNA2).
- The single-request suite only; `--clients N` was not run.

pulls.title: [HIP] Keep mixed-gfx prefill GEMM modes per device (#690, #703)
pulls.author: PJGV333
pulls.body:
## Summary

A correctness-oriented, opt-in HIP prompt-precision policy for mixed gfx103x/non-gfx103x multi-GPU prefill, rebuilt on Strata v0.1.45. No performance improvement is claimed.

## Changes

- Preserve `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1` as the historical all-device FP16 mode. Add `=all` as a new explicit all-device alias; it was not a historical v0.1.45 option.
- Add `=gfx103x` to select FP16-in/FP16-out only on gfx103x, while other HIP devices retain BF16-in/FP32-out. Reuse the existing per-device cache and preserve the upstream first-character `1` compatibility behavior (for example, `10`).
- Preserve the existing RDNA2 GEMM and SGEMM implementations.
- Add heterogeneous dispatch and numerical regression coverage, including deterministic nonzero inputs and CPU GEMM/GR SiLU references in the large stress shape, both device orders, and a return-to-first-device check.

## Validation

- RX 9070 XT (`gfx1201`) + RX 6750 XT (`gfx1031`), ROCm 7.2.53211, HIP clang 22.0.0.
- HIP build targeting both architectures succeeded; focused serial CTest passed 9/9.
- A controlled, serial, same-source A/B matrix comprised 29 executions: 13 returned success and 16 exited nonzero across tested control/candidate configurations. The selective `=gfx103x` candidate mode passed three repeated forward-order runs, the reversed order, and the tested `STRATA_RDNA2_SGEMM=1` and `=all` configurations.

## Scope and limitations

Validated only on gfx1201 + gfx1031. Some nonselective configurations emitted `no kernel image is available for execution on the device` in both the v0.1.45 control and candidate, while other device-order/SGEMM combinations passed. The underlying ROCm kernel-image error has not been isolated; this is not a universal fix claim. The FP16 and BF16 paths are not claimed to be bit-identical, and no performance improvement is claimed.

CUDA and SYCL were not compiled because `nvcc` and `icpx` were unavailable on the test system. The functional change is HIP-specific, but cross-backend build verification remains outstanding.

An earlier local snapshot completed a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S prompt of 81,886 tokens with MTP, PLE, and Q4_0 KV; that result was not run on final HEAD. A roughly 130K-token request exceeded the 300-second limit and did not complete. Conventional-only and multimodal inference were not validated.

## Extra Notes

pulls.title: STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1 (opt-in, HIP): the verifier's hyper-connection read as one persistent kernel (gfx1030: read 1.35-2.10x, per window -4.2 % / -2.8 %)
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none of its own. `STRATA_GR_V3=1` is another opt-in for the same read; on gfx1030 it needs the two-half split, which fails its check (#375), so it falls back to the default read.

## Summary
At 1-8 tokens the verifier's hyper-connection read (twice per layer) is three small launches with two global
dependencies, and on gfx1030 the down projection runs 41 blocks on 40 WGPs. Opt-in `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1` (HIP) runs it
as **one kernel of 80 blocks with two grid barriers**: the down projection split by column slices over all 80 blocks,
a distributed reduction, then the up projection and the same epilogue as `gr_up_kernel`.

2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030), ROCm 10.0, layer split:

- the read alone, 1-8 tokens: **1.35-2.10x** (38.9 us against 55.1 us at 2 tokens);
- ms per verify window, this branch, one binary with the variable unset / set, 6 alternating rounds:
  **4K 25.81 -> 24.73 (-4.2 %), 32K 24.40 -> 23.72 (-2.8 %)**, every round the same way; tokens per window and
  prompt speed unchanged.

Not bit-identical (another summation order). Against a double-accumulation reference (`STRATA_HC_PERSIST=3`) on the
106K-token chat of a 3-chat `STRATA_LOGPOS` run on this branch: KL 0.0131 / argmax 96.3 % against the default read's
0.0136 / 95.0 %.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`: the persistent kernel, its start-up check and `fused_gr_read_persist`, all inside
  `#if defined(__HIPCC__)`; CUDA and SYCL get two empty stubs.
- `src/core/verify.cpp`: `Verifier::init` calls `fused_gr_persist_init()`; the multi read tries
  `fused_gr_read_persist` first and falls through to `fused_gr_read_multi` when it returns false (off, more tokens
  than were checked, a Q8 / QFUSE read).
- `include/strata/kernels/fused_gr.hpp`: the two declarations.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md` (RDNA2 section): one bullet.
- `bench/results/2026-10-12-hc-persist-gfx1030/`: the measurements, smaller cards simulated with `HSA_CU_MASK`, what
  was tried and dropped, and `hc_persist_bench.cpp` to time the read alone.

How it stays safe on cards it was not written for:
- wave64 is refused;
- every token count is **run** once at start-up with a 50 ms barrier timeout and compared with the default read; a
  timeout keeps the default read for that count and larger ones (checked: 1 and 5 WGPs via `HSA_CU_MASK` time out and
  fall back, no hang). No occupancy API in front of it: it promised too many blocks on 30 WGPs and too few with
  Ubuntu's HIP 7.1 runtime, which turned the read off although it runs resident there;
- one `strata hc:` line per card says what was decided.

What it leaves alone: the default path (with the variable unset both entry points return in their first line), the
drafter's reads (their own stream), the prompt path, CUDA, SYCL.

Default path byte-identical: main (a0116b27) built without and with this change, same options, variable unset: the
106K chat's 481 scored positions are bitwise identical (the two shorter chats differ between two runs of the same
binary on this machine, so they cannot show it).

## Extra Notes
- Built: HIP (gfx1030) only. **CUDA and SYCL were not built** (no toolkit here); the new code is HIP-only and the
  other backends see two stubs and two declarations.
- Only one card model was measured. Simulated 30 / 20 WGPs keep Navi 21's bus and Infinity Cache, so a real 6700 XT /
  6600, RDNA 3, RDNA 4 are open. **Help wanted**: from any RDNA card, the `strata hc:` line and a
  `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1` run with and without `STRATA_HC_PERSIST=1`.
- 0 stalls in every engine run with it (more than 30); in daily use on this machine since 2026-10-12.
- Unrelated, seen once while checking: main's default path failed one 106K checkpoint save with "conversation
  snapshot running-state copy: an illegal memory access was encountered" (the variable unset, so this code did not
  run); a rerun passed. The same message as #1932; noted there would be the place if it comes back.

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, PCIe 4.0 x8 each) / Ryzen 5 5600X, ROCm 10.0.

pulls.title: pcie: the measured PCIe share default (PcieAuto) on gfx1100 too — gate-measured on a native pack
pulls.author: xyzzing
pulls.body:
0.1.43 made PcieAuto the default under the gfx12 decode defaults on HIP (`decode_defaults_arch_ok` → gfx1200/gfx1201, measured on 2×R9700) and for the canonical pack on CUDA (ab97f174). Every other AMD part keeps its earlier behaviour.

This extends the default to **gfx1100 (RX 7900 XT/XTX/GRE)** — the one other arch where the in-run refinement has been gate-measured, on a native (IQ) pack:

**No-regression gate** (4 alternating engine starts @64K, same args/env, paired medians): prefill 2189 (base) vs 2180 (with the arm), decode 65.4 vs 65.4 — inside noise. The gate's rule was no-regression, so the arm stays.

**Engagement** (under `--serve`, real ~95K-token request): the in-run refinement fires and prints `pool 42-45 us/missed expert (45-48 GB/s of expert bytes), the link 28.4-28.5 GB/s -> pcie_frac 0.25 (was 0.55)`, self-limited to 3 updates — the engine's own `f = L/(L + 1.85 r)`. It has run as our daily-driver production config since 2026-10-12 and was re-verified after the 0.1.43.1 refresh.

Scope, deliberately narrow:
- **gfx1100 only** — `pcie_auto_fork_arch_ok()` pins the arch string exactly. gfx1200/1201 keep 0.1.43's default; every other AMD part keeps the gate's earlier behaviour. Nothing is claimed for unmeasured archs.
- **Native packs only** — the canonical pack keeps its CUDA-only refinement, including the Windows opt-in (STRATA_PCIE_AUTO_CANON).
- Opt-outs unchanged: `STRATA_PCIE_FRAC_DEFAULT=old`, `--pcie-frac N`, the layer-split rules (incl. the `STRATA_PCIE_AUTO_SPLIT` opt-in).

Build: HIP gfx1100, 373/373 targets on the nightly ROCm 10.2 toolchain. The arm is host-side policy (no kernel change); the CUDA path is untouched — `pcie_auto_fork_arch_ok()` returns false there and `decode_defaults_arch_ok()` is always true.

pulls.title: verify: STRATA_NO_PCIE_GROUP=1 drops the empty PCIe-share stage with --pcie-frac 0
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
With `--pcie-frac 0` the pool never plans PCIe experts, yet every layer of a verify window still runs the PCIe-share stage over zero groups: the flag B wait, `fetch_blobs` + `rebase_ptrs` (staging mode 2) and the grouped gate/up, SwiGLU and down launches with `kPcieGroupRows` rows that find nothing to do. Six dependent kernels, ~18 µs a layer on an RTX 2080 Ti (kernel-node nsys), ~0.86 ms of a ~25 ms window.

`STRATA_NO_PCIE_GROUP=1` records the window graph without that stage. It is opt-in and only valid with `--pcie-frac 0` (the graphs are captured once, and the share can otherwise be refined at run time): if the pool ever publishes a plan with PCIe experts, the host loop stops the engine with a message (`STRATA_NO_PCIE_GROUP=1 needs --pcie-frac 0 (layer L planned N PCIe experts)`) after releasing the GPU's waits, instead of letting the GPU skip experts. I checked that path by starting the engine without `--pcie-frac 0`: it stops at the first window that plans a PCIe expert.

On this card, with the expert cache warm (~96-97 % VRAM hits in decode), the CPU takes the few misses the PCIe share would have taken without a measurable loss: `--pcie-frac 0` alone was neutral (Spanish 86.9 vs 87.8 t/s, code 106.3 vs 106.1, 32K 78.2 vs 78.4 - within the run-to-run spread).

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700 (4 cores), 56 GB DDR4-2133, PCIe 3.0 x16, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W. Flash-Next, canonical Q2_0 pack, `--resident-experts`, `--max-context 524288`, `--serve`, with the other open Turing decode PRs applied.

## Engine (512 new tokens, two runs each)

| | `--pcie-frac` auto | `--pcie-frac 0` + `STRATA_NO_PCIE_GROUP=1` | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Spanish chat (57-token prompt) | 87.8 t/s | 89.8 t/s | +2.3 % |
| code | 106.1 | 108.4 | +2.2 % |
| English, 32K | 78.4 | 80.1 | +2.2 % |
| English, 128K | 75.0 | 76.8 | +2.4 % |
| English, 389,560 tokens | 74.7 | 75.1 | +0.6 % |

The prompt reads are unchanged (32K 17.6 s, 390K 223.6 s).

A follow-up could make this automatic when `--pcie-frac 0` is given (no env), if you prefer that.

pulls.title: sm_75: fewer launches per decode layer: plan wait folded, fused quantize + interleave (bitwise)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
A verify window launches ~35 dependent kernels per layer on its main stream, and on Turing each dependent graph node costs ~0.8 µs of gap (kernel-node nsys). This folds two pairs that always run back to back into one launch each, writing the same bytes:

- **The plan's host-flag wait folded into its copy**: 143-amdk's `wait_copy_i32_from_mapped`, gfx12-only until now. On CUDA `STRATA_FUSE_WAIT` selects it: `2` = the plan only (the Turing default), `1` = also the CPU rows' `copy_rows_from_mapped_after`, `0` = neither. The rows' version makes every row block of the copy poll the flag over PCIe and was −1.5 % on an RTX 2080 Ti, so it stays opt-in. `STRATA_FUSE_HITS` is unchanged (off on CUDA; measured neutral here).
- **`native_quantize_q8_1_il`**: a projection input's q8_1 blocks and their interleaved copy (`native_q8_1_interleave`) in one kernel. The quantization is `native_quantize_q8_1_kernel`'s; an int of the interleaved copy is four codes gathered from lanes `4p..4p+3` with two shuffles, and the copy's scale is the block's `__low2float(ds)`. Used for the GDN qkv and out-projection inputs and the QSA input and out-projection (`quant_in` in `record_window`); the head keeps its two launches. `STRATA_QIL=0` / `1` forces it off / on; the default is on for sm_75.

Both bitwise: the fused quantize was compared byte for byte with quantize + interleave (both buffers) at 2,560 / 6,144 / 10,240 inputs and 2-4 columns, all-zero blocks included.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W. Flash-Next, canonical Q2_0 pack, `--max-context 524288`, `--serve`, with the other open Turing decode PRs applied.

## Engine (512 new tokens, two runs each, two separate A/Bs)

| A/B 1 | Spanish chat | code | English 32K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| neither | 90.1 t/s | 107.8 t/s | 80.6 t/s |
| plan wait folded (`STRATA_FUSE_WAIT=2`) | 90.9 | 108.5 | 81.7 |

| A/B 2 | Spanish chat | code | English 32K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| plan wait folded | 88.3\* | 108.0 | 80.8 |
| + fused quantize | 90.7 | 109.1 | 80.7 |

\* one of the two runs had low draft acceptance (240/337 against ~258/338); the other was 91.4. Small gains (~+1 % and ~+0.5-1 %), but up to three fewer launches per layer in every window, for the same bytes.

pulls.title: sm_75: Q2_0 matvec with one warp per four rows (bitwise)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
On Turing the Q2_0 matvec of the decode windows is far from the card's bandwidth: the QSA layers' `attn_q` (2560 → 12288, Q2_0 in the canonical pack) takes 80 µs at three columns, ~110 GB/s on an RTX 2080 Ti. The exact layout gives each row four warps and half a 64-value block per thread, then a cross-warp reduction; at the engine's 2,560 inputs a row has 40 blocks, so 48 of the 128 threads have no chunk and the reduction is most of the kernel.

`q2_0_warp_rows_kernel` gives a warp four rows. Lane `l` runs the chunks of the exact kernel's threads `l`, `32 + l`, `64 + l` and `96 + l`, in their loop order, adds the four sums the way warp 0 adds the other warps' partials, then the same `warp_sum`. Every output is bit for bit `native_q2_0_mmvq_kernel`'s (one column) and `launch_multi`'s exact layout (two to four columns); the upstream (non-exact) layout keeps its kernel.

Default on sm_75 only (the only card I can measure); `STRATA_Q2_WARP=0` keeps the old kernels, `=1` takes this one on any CUDA card.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W. Flash-Next, canonical Q2_0 pack, `--max-context 524288`, `--serve`.

## Kernel (2560 × 12288, cold weights: six copies in rotation, 300 calls)

| columns | exact layout | warp rows | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 36.6 µs | 24.8 µs | 1.48× |
| 2 | 59.8 µs | 31.4 µs | 1.90× |
| 3 | 68.3 µs | 31.3 µs | 2.18× |
| 4 | 88.4 µs | 36.6 µs | 2.42× |

The outputs are compared with `memcmp` against the engine's own launch for every column count: identical. One and two rows per warp, and eight warps per block, were measured too; four rows and four warps was best.

## Engine

Together with the QSA attention change of #2220 (both bitwise, measured as one step), 512 new tokens, two runs each: Spanish chat 86.0 → 87.8 t/s, code 103.1 → 106.1, English at 32K 75.3 → 78.4. The same kernel also serves the shared expert's Q2_0 gate/up on its side stream.

pulls.title: sm_75: QSA decode attention for INT8 KV off the shared-memory pipe (bitwise)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
The decode attention over the QSA selection (`attn_chunk_kernel<1>`, INT8 pools) saturates the SM's shared-memory pipe on Turing. Its time grew linearly with the queries while the SMs were half empty: per cell, every warp reads two 16-byte slices of each of the 12 query heads from shared memory (a two-way bank conflict at `lane * 8`) and runs 12 `warp_sum`s, 60 shuffles; the value loop then reads the 12 probabilities of a cell as 12 scalar loads. Loading the K/V codes earlier (software prefetch) changed nothing, so it is not memory latency.

`attn_chunk_q8_v3_kernel` does the same operations in the same order:

- the lane's slice of the 12 heads (8 dimensions each) is read from shared memory once, into registers;
- the 12 lane sums are reduced with `reduce12_gfx906` (16 shuffles; every sum is `warp_sum`'s pairs, as its comment says);
- the probabilities are stored cell-major, so the value loop reads a cell's 12 as three 16-byte broadcasts.

The chunk partials and the merged output are bit for bit the default kernel's. It is used by both entry points (`qsa_decode_attn_batch`, `qsa_decode_attn_step`), so the MTP drafter's attention gets it too. Default on sm_75 only; `STRATA_ATTN_V3=0` keeps the default kernel, `=1` takes this one on any CUDA card. Lane-cell scoring (`STRATA_ATTN_LANECELL=1`) keeps its path.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W. Flash-Next, canonical Q2_0 pack, `--kv int8`, `--max-context 524288`, `--serve`.

## Kernel (chunk kernel + merge, synthetic INT8 pools, permuted page table, 200 calls)

| selected cells | queries | default | v3 | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,051 | 1 | 51.6 µs | 34.5 µs | 1.50× |
| 2,051 | 2 | 78.5 µs | 41.0 µs | 1.91× |
| 2,051 | 3 | 110.0 µs | 73.0 µs | 1.51× |
| 2,051 | 4 | 145.6 µs | 84.9 µs | 1.71× |
| 600 | 1 | 45.9 µs | 28.6 µs | 1.60× |
| 600 | 2 | 74.6 µs | 32.8 µs | 2.27× |
| 600 | 3 | 105.5 µs | 33.5 µs | 3.15× |
| 600 | 4 | 136.9 µs | 33.3 µs | 4.11× |

Partials and outputs compared with `memcmp` against the default kernel in every case: identical. With the swizzle and `reduce12` alone (the gfx906 variants, also bitwise on CUDA) the 2,051-cell / 3-query case is 78 µs; the register copy of the query is what takes it to 73 µs, and further at fewer cells. At 2,051 cells and 3-4 queries the registers allow two blocks per SM (198-264 blocks: two waves); forcing three spills.

`qsa_prompt_attn_parity` reports the same errors with `STRATA_ATTN_V3=0` and `1` (its reference is this decode kernel: int8 32K / 2,048 queries 71.5 → 36.0 ms per chunk).

## Engine

Together with the Q2_0 matvec change of #2221 (both bitwise, measured as one step), 512 new tokens, two runs each: Spanish chat 86.0 → 87.8 t/s, code 103.1 → 106.1, English at 32K 75.3 → 78.4.

pulls.title: Fix the cgroup RAM grant ignoring clean active file cache
pulls.author: kuhlsnu
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none filed, the numbers are below.

## Summary
Bug: in a container, the resident RAM budget swings with the page cache's history instead of the box. It changes how much RAM a start is granted, not decode or prefill speed. `cgroup_available_bytes` credits only `inactive_file`, but the model files Strata reads while loading land on the active list, so the same box with the same 50 GiB container cap granted 0.00, 20.29, 17.53, 29.66 and 26.99 GiB across five starts (2x RTX 3090, 2026-10-09). The container held 21.59 GiB of `active_file` and 0.75 GiB of `inactive_file` at the time.

This counts clean active file pages as reclaimable too, still bounded to `memory.current` and less dirty and writeback pages, so the grant stops depending on which cgroup paid for the cache first.

## What changed
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: `cgroup_available_bytes` sums `inactive_file + active_file` (saturating), and `read_cgroup_memory_stat` reads and requires `active_file` like the other counters.
- `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `CgroupMemoryStat` gains `active_file`.
- `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: a loaded-model case (the 3090 numbers), a sum bounded to `current`, and an overflow case.

Left alone on purpose:
- **HIP keeps the inactive-only rule.** `pin_blobs` in `generate.cpp` registers mapped file ranges, and those pinned pages sit on the active list without being reclaimable, so crediting them could overstate the room. I have no AMD box to measure it on.
- **The SYCL mirror** (`sycl/src/core/expert_source.cpp`) and `conversation_memory.cpp`'s own credit rule are unchanged.

On the comment in `conversation_memory.cpp` that active_file "holds mlocked pages": as far as I can tell the kernel moves mlocked pages to the unevictable list (`Documentation/mm/unevictable-lru.rst`), so that is not a reason to leave active_file out. Pinned (registered) file pages are, which is why HIP is excluded here.

## Extra Notes
What ran (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, g++ 13.3, CUDA 12.0 for the `.cu` objects the test links):
- `file_expert_source_test` passes on this commit. Against the parent it fails to compile (the struct gained a field), and with the old inactive-only sum it fails with `clean active file cache was not credited against the cgroup cap`.
- CPU-only `ctest`: 39/39 before and after.

Not run yet: the after-fix grant on the GPU box. The patched build has served on that box since 2026-10-09 with no budget refusal in its 127 start and stop logs, but those starts did not log the grant. I'll add five instrumented cold starts as a comment after 2026-10-15.

Not built: HIP and SYCL. The HIP branch is a preprocessor switch back to the current rule; with `-DSTRATA_USE_HIP=1` both changed files compile and the test passes on the CPU build, which checks the branch logic but not ROCm. SYCL's files are not touched.

Default behaviour changes inside a cgroup with active file cache, so this is a fix to the default path rather than an opt-in feature; without a cgroup memory limit (`memory.max` of `max`) nothing changes.

pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (CPU decode speed on AVX2 machines without AVX-512)

## Summary
On an AVX-2 CPU without AVX-512, a CPU expert that serves one token runs ggml-cpu's single-token `vec_dot` (#152). This adds a gate/up kernel for IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S / IQ2_S that uses the AVX-2 rows' decode but keeps **ggml's float order exactly** (the same per-lane integer sums, `d = x.d * y.d` and one fmadd per block, the format constant after `hsum_float_8`'s tree), so the output does not change, only the time: one-token gate/up -27% (IQ3_S) and -6% (IQ3_XXS) per expert on a Ryzen 7 3800X. `STRATA_CPU_SINGLE_EXACT=0` keeps ggml's dot.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp`, `include/strata/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.hpp`: `iq256_gu_single_exact` (+ `row_dot_single`, `gu_single`, `hsum8_ggml`). Upstream's multi-token kernels are untouched.
- `src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp`: `native_gu_rows` takes it for `nt == 1`, types 18/21/22, only where it would have reached ggml's dot (after the multi-token checks, so `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN` / `STRATA_IQ3S_MT1` behave as before), the CPU has AVX2 and no AVX-512, **and** ggml-cpu itself was built for AVX2 and not AVX-512 (`ggml_cpu_has_*`: a `STRATA_ISA_FLOOR` build's ggml dots round differently). `STRATA_NO_IQ256` still means ggml's dot. Down rows are unchanged.
- `src/kernels/cpu/iq_single_parity.cpp` (new): the kernel and `native_gu_rows` at one token against ggml's `vec_dot` bit for bit; exit 77 where the reference is not ggml's AVX2 build. Registered in the top-level build (also as `iq_single_parity_off` with `STRATA_CPU_SINGLE_EXACT=0`) and in `sycl/`.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: a paragraph with the switch and the numbers below.

## How it was checked
Ryzen 7 3800X (Zen 2, AVX2, no AVX-512), Ubuntu 26.04.1, g++ 15.2 (top-level CPU build) and icpx 2026.1 (SYCL build).
- `iq_single_parity`: 0 bitwise mismatches (default and `STRATA_CPU_SINGLE_EXACT=0`); `iq_avx2_parity`: 0 failures.
- `iq_avx2_parity --bench --dispatch`, 1 token, one thread, engine path, ms per expert (gate/up): IQ3_S 0.497 -> 0.365, IQ3_XXS 0.343 -> 0.322; down unchanged (0.095).
- In the SYCL engine on an Arc A770 (Coder IQ1_M, 8K prompt, 256 tokens, the engine's `pool multi` stats): gate/up 15.2-15.4 -> 14.0-14.2 ms/round, CPU pool call about -3%, output ids identical in every run. End-to-end decode did not change measurably there (the pool is ~30 ms of a ~110 ms round).

**Not built: CUDA and HIP** (no toolchains on this machine). The files are shared CPU code; nothing CUDA/HIP-specific is touched, but please build those before merging. Measured on Zen 2 only.

## Extra Notes
An earlier version also had an exact IQ4_NL down kernel; it measured ~2% slower in the engine, so it is not in this PR.

pulls.title: CUDA: keep CPU expert servicing active during instrumented graph launches
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Compute Sanitizer can block `cudaGraphLaunch` while the verifier graph waits for CPU expert doorbells supplied by the calling thread. This is the launch/service cycle diagnosed in #1383 and #1341; #1383 added a warning.

Add opt-in `STRATA_VERIFY_ASYNC_LAUNCH=1`: a separate host thread launches the CUDA graph while the caller serves its CPU requests. Join and propagate the real launch error before returning a frontier; release mapped GPU waits on an early service failure.

Before/after diagnostic on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB, Qwen3.8 Flash Next Q8_0 / FP16 KV:

- The original parent/two-sibling full-memcheck probe remained locked for **14+ hours**, with no completed forward operation.
- The same probe completed in **43.6 seconds** after this scheduling fix: three exact fresh-oracle comparisons, unchanged parent bytes, four instrumented native processes and **zero sanitizer errors**.
- The elapsed-time reduction comes from breaking the wait cycle.

Current-main validation (`a0116b27`, RTX 4090, Linux, CUDA 13.3):

- CUDA signal/cleanup/error-propagation regression passed; synchronous negative control failed after its eight-second watchdog; regression memcheck reported zero errors.
- A two-token Q8_0 fixture produced byte-identical full 248,320-logit dumps on upstream main, patched default, threaded mode and memcheck. The CLI memcheck uses `--report-api-errors explicit`; default extended reporting also logged internal cuBLAS fatbinary-loading diagnostics.

Minimal change: launch helper, `Verifier::run` integration, CUDA regression/CMake registration and usage documentation. The option defaults off. Scope is the CUDA single-request verifier; direct batch/pipelined entry points retain their scheduling. HIP active verifier source matches upstream; SYCL source is unchanged. G1 certification runs separately from this branch.

pulls.title: sycl/A770: wide MMVQ kernels at 2-8 columns in large-GRF mode on Arc A-series (bit-identical; 1.3-7.4x kernel, decode +10-17%)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545, #1606 (Arc A-series decode)

## Summary
The wide MMVQ kernels (Q6_K `a2` and the generic `native_mmvq_wide`) spill registers at 2-8 columns with the default 128 GRFs on an Arc A770, and their bandwidth collapses as the column count grows (Q6_K 2560x10240: 248 GB/s at 1 column, 74 GB/s at 4, 8 GB/s at 8). On Alchemist they now launch in large-GRF mode (256) at 2-8 columns: **1.3-7.4x faster at 2-8 columns, bit-identical**, decode +10-17% on an A770 (the verify window runs these at 2-6 columns every round).

Large GRF halves the threads resident per Xe core, so it is the default on Alchemist only (`strata::intel_gpu_gen`). Battlemage and every other device, and 1 column everywhere, launch the same kernels as today. `STRATA_MMVQ_LARGE_GRF=1` forces it on, `=0` off.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.dp.cpp`: `mmvq_large_grf(queue)` (once per process, Alchemist by default, env override); in `launch_q6k_wide` (a2 path) and `launch_wide`, `if constexpr (NCOLS > 1)` + the runtime switch launch a `grf_size<256>` copy of the same kernel, else the existing launch, unchanged.
- `sycl/src/kernels/mmvq_bench.cpp`: prints a checksum of the output (FNV-1a over the float bits), so the modes can be compared bit for bit.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM, same day.

`mmvq_bench <n_in> <n_out> <cols>`, Q6_K, `main` vs this PR (us; checksums identical with `STRATA_MMVQ_LARGE_GRF=0` and `=1` in all 15 cases):

| shape | 1 col | 2 cols | 4 cols | 6 cols | 8 cols |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2560 x 2560 | 33.5 -> 33.4 | 55.2 -> 30.0 | 97.0 -> 36.0 | 150.7 -> 44.5 | 631.1 -> 153.1 |
| 2560 x 10240 | 86.6 -> 86.1 | 157.4 -> 79.4 | 289.3 -> 92.9 | 552.8 -> 110.2 | 2726.5 -> 370.5 |
| 10240 x 2560 | 83.7 -> 83.9 | 119.4 -> 88.9 | 237.4 -> 103.1 | 393.9 -> 129.8 | 1704.4 -> 465.2 |

End to end, `a0116b27` + #2190 + #2193 + #2203 with and without this PR, Coder IQ1_M, 8K-token prompt, 256 tokens, greedy, `--resident-experts --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --spec 4 --mtp`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1`:

pulls.title: sycl: with --expert-parallel-device, card N computes its own experts of each prompt chunk
pulls.author: recutita
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
With `--expert-parallel-device N` (#1798), card N now computes its own experts of each prompt chunk. Until now the prompt path ran every expert on card 0 and read card N's experts from the GGUF for every chunk, so a prompt's speed hung on the file cache holding them (a 7200 rpm disk read an 807-token prompt at 12.3 tok/s, reported in #1798). It is on whenever `--expert-parallel-device` is set; `STRATA_EP_PREFILL=0` turns it off and keeps the GGUF reads. Without `--expert-parallel-device` nothing changes.

Built on #1798: this branch holds its two commits and this one (c7bb8dd5); only the last is this PR.

### Measured
2x Arc Pro B70 (32 GB each, xe, Linux), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 60 GB RAM, NVMe, through the server (`sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, 131,072 context, INT8 KV with `--kv-resident 32768`, `--vram-reserve-mib 2048`, `--prefill 4096`), greedy, thinking off. Each value is the median of three fresh documents (256 tokens generated each), two runs per arm, the arms alternated. Hot: one document read first, so the GGUF pages are in the page cache (28-32 GiB of the two files before each document of the old path). Cold: the files' page cache dropped (`posix_fadvise` `DONTNEED`, 0 GiB left) before each document.

| prompt | page cache | `STRATA_EP_PREFILL=0` | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 627 tokens | hot | 509, 507 tok/s | 761, 761 tok/s | +50% |
| 2,441 tokens | hot | 1,091, 1,091 tok/s | 1,218, 1,219 tok/s | +12% |
| 627 tokens | cold | 226, 223 tok/s | 757, 762 tok/s | 3.4x |
| 2,441 tokens | cold | 590, 584 tok/s | 1,221, 1,225 tok/s | 2.1x |

Decode after the prompts (99-107 tok/s) and short chats (75.7-76.2 tok/s) are the same in both arms.

Where the time goes (`STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1`, one chunk, hot), 2,427 tokens: card 0's expert phases (dequantize, gate/up, down) take 517 ms instead of 1,252 and card N computes its share in 430 ms meanwhile; the combine, which now waits for card N and copies its rows, grows from 56 to 413 ms; the GPU timeline goes from 2,547 to 2,147 ms and the host's GGUF staging from 2,190 ms to none. 612 tokens: card 0's expert phases 924 -> 367 ms, card N 244 ms, combine 15 -> 105 ms, timeline 1,452 -> 955 ms. With the page cache dropped the old path's timeline is 4,311 ms (2,427 tokens) and 2,888 ms (612); this PR's does not change.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`: `Prefill::set_ep_peer`. It reuses the `--peer-device` prompt share (`PeerPrefill`) with card N's `ExpertCache` as the source of its experts. Per MoE layer, card 0 writes the chunk's FP16 activations into a region on card N; card N gathers its rows and runs card 0's FP16 expert path on them (dequantize, oneMKL gate/up, SwiGLU, oneMKL down; this build has no MMQ, which the `--peer-device` share uses), writing the rows into a second region; card 0 waits for card N on the host and copies the rows into its combine input past its caches. Both regions are card N's memory opened on card 0 through Level Zero IPC (`ep_mem.hpp`, as the decode windows' inbox), since dpct gives each card its own context.
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: the call in `--serve`, unless `STRATA_EP_PREFILL=0`. If card N's buffers do not fit (420 MiB of regions at `--prefill 4096`, plus the FP16 path's buffers) the log says so and the GGUF reads stay.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the prompt path line of the expert-parallel section.

## How it was checked
- Output: the same four prompts (documents of about 1,000 and 4,000 tokens, two short chats, 256 tokens greedy each) through the server with this PR and with `STRATA_EP_PREFILL=0`, two starts of each: all four outputs byte-identical across the four starts.
- The arm with `STRATA_EP_PREFILL=0` logged no expert-parallel prompt line; the other logged `card 1 computes its experts' rows of each prompt chunk (420 MiB of exchange regions)`.
- SYCL build (AOT `bmg-g31`), `strata`.

## Extra Notes
- `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` passes no variable whose value is `0` to the engine, so `"STRATA_EP_PREFILL": "0"` in a config's `"env"` does not reach it through that launcher (the measurements above used `"00"`, which the engine reads as 0). This is the launcher's rule for every switch and is left alone here.
- Card N stays idle for most of a chunk (1,682 of 2,147 ms above) and card 0 waits for it in the combine; overlapping them further is not part of this PR.
- Tested only on 2x B70 under xe on Linux with NVMe storage; not on a slower disk, on Arc A-series cards (i915), on Windows, or with cards of two different kinds.

pulls.title: Monitor: token usage and cost per day, priced, with the folder's models merged or shown one by one
pulls.author: pipti
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #900

## Summary

The Monitor gains a **Token usage and cost** card. It keeps, per day, what each request used (prompt, reused, written tokens) and what the machine actually drew for it (watt-hours, folded in from the Power card's own sampler), so the figures survive a restart and describe real days rather than one sitting. Everything is priced at your own rates, set in About > Token pricing.

A run folder normally holds the usage file of every model one has run. The card adds them all up by default; the one choice **Merged / By model** — on the card's own title bar and in About > Settings — shows them one by one instead, both as a line per model and as one row per model and day in the per-day list.

Three commits, one feature. Nothing in the engine, the request path or any default changes.

## What changed

- **serve/usage.py** (new, 294 lines) — `UsageStore` keeps the per-day counts in `strata-<model>.usage.json` beside the run config (tokens, watt-hours, seconds sampled) and prices them: `DEFAULT_PRICING` is CNY 2 / 0.4 / 8 per million tokens (input / cached input / output), 0.55 per kWh, 100 W for the rest of the box — all settable, kept in `strata-<model>.pricing.json`. `read_days()` is the one reader of a usage file, `days_view()` the one builder of the card's rows (today, the last 14 days newest first, the all-time sum, each priced), and `summed()` adds several models' days up. `ModelsUsage` names each model after the `model_name` of the run config beside its file (the file's stem when there is none; two configs of one model are one model), and reads the other files at most once per poll, keyed by mtime and size. A file that is missing or half written reads as the days it holds.
- **serve/server.py** — `Service.usage_view()` is what GET /usage, POST /pricing and the usage block of GET /metrics answer: the folder merged, plus `models` for the per-model view, every model priced with this server's prices. The running model's counts come from the live store rather than its file, so the seconds the sampler holds in memory are not lost; the other models come from disk, which their own server saves every `SAVE_EVERY_S`. `start_telemetry()` points the sampler's new `on_sample(sample, dt)` at `Service._sample_power`, which folds `gpu_power` into the store and splits the busy share at `GPU_BUSY_PCT` (the same line `gpu_busy()` draws). A server started without a run config keeps the numbers in memory only, as before.
- **serve/telemetry.py** — the power sampler gained `on_sample(sample, dt)`, called with the time the reading actually covers; a hook that raises can never end the sampler thread.
- **serve/web/** — the Monitor card (tokens, electricity and total; a line per model with its today and all-time figures when the per-model view is on), its per-day list (a kWh column; a Model column and a row per model and day in the per-model view), the Token pricing card in About, and the one choice in its two places, kept in this browser. `app.css` grew `.seg--2` (two choices) and `.seg--sm` (the card's small one). A server that sends no per-model view keeps the merged card, as before.
- **serve/test_usage.py** (new, 368 lines) — 18 tests: the store's days and prices, a hand-edited file with nonsense in it, the folder's names, sums and whose counts win, POST /pricing, and the /usage + /metrics payload in both views against the mock engine.
- **docs/DETAILS.md** — what the card keeps, where the two files live, and where the choice is.

## Extra Notes

- **Overlap:** #1876 and #1925 put GPU energy and its price on the Power card. This bills the whole box on the usage card instead — the card's measured watt-hours plus `other_watts` over the seconds sampled. Happy to drop that commit or fold it into theirs if you would rather keep the two apart; the token card stands on its own without it.
- **Verified:** the full suite on this branch rebased onto a0116b27 (`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"`) runs 743 tests, 12 skipped, and reports one error — `serve.test_server.HipEnvGuard.test_only_for_hip`, which does `Path(r"Z:\definitely\not\here").exists()` in `hip_env_guard` and hits a disconnected network drive here (`OSError: [WinError 1331]`). A clean a0116b27 checkout on this same machine fails the same test the same way (`Ran 4 tests ... FAILED (errors=1)`), so it is this PC's `Z:` drive, not the change; `serve.test_usage` is 18 tests, all passing. On the machine here (RTX 5090 32 GB, Ultra 9 285K, 95 GB) a folder of three models came out as 1,937 requests / 157,142,730 prompt / 10.53 kWh / ¥142.25 merged, and 857 + 469 + 611 requests with ¥68.83 + ¥40.53 + ¥32.89 split per model, which is what the per-day files hold. Both views and both switches were clicked through in a headless browser against a mock engine, with no console errors.
- **Leaves alone:** no new dependencies, no change to the engine, the flags, the request path or any default; the two JSON files are plain and can be read, edited or deleted by hand, and a server without a run config keeps its counts in memory only. The card hides itself when the payload carries no usage block, so an unmodified older server shows exactly the page it did before — if you would rather the card be opt-in on this build too (hidden until a flag or a file turns it on), that is a small change and I will make it.

pulls.title: sycl/A770: fused GR read with more, smaller work-groups on Arc A-series (same sums; decode +3-5%; on top of #2193)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Depends on #2193 (this branch contains its commit; review only the second commit, `sycl/A770: fused GR read with more, smaller work-groups on Arc A-series`).

## Summary
After #2193 the fused GR read on an Arc A770 still launches too few work-groups to fill the card (80 for the sliced down kernel, 160 for the multi-token up kernel). On Alchemist this splits them further: **the same values, summed in the same order**, by more groups. `gr_bench` 1.2-1.3x faster, decode +3-5% on an A770, identical outputs. Default on Alchemist only; every other device launches today's kernels. `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS=1` forces it on, `=0` off.

## What changed
`sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp` (and one header comment in `sycl/src/kernels/gr_bench.cpp`):
- sliced down kernel: one work-group per (slice, row block), 80 x 6 = 480 groups; each row's partial is computed exactly as before, by a different group.
- `gr_down_reduce`: 8 slice loads in flight per step, then added one at a time, so the sum accumulates slices 0, 1, ..., 79 in the same sequence of float adds as the old loop (`static_assert(GRS_SLICES % 8 == 0)`; `-fp-model=precise`).
- up kernel: templated on the column count, 8 columns per group (320 groups instead of 160) on this path; `UPM_COLS` stays 16 for every other user. Only group 0 writes the per-token `lo` values, which every group computes identically.
- `gr_more_groups(queue)`: once per process, `strata::intel_gpu_gen == Alchemist` by default, env override; independent of `STRATA_GR_LARGE_GRF`.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM; `a0116b27` + #2190 + #2193 with and without this commit, same day.

- `gr_bench`, 1-6 tokens, checksums identical for every token count:

  | build | us (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 tokens) |
  |---|---|
  | #2193 | 132.2 / 118.9 / 133.6 / 150.5 / 168.3 / 183.5 |
  | this PR | 116.1 / 94.6 / 105.8 / 122.9 / 136.4 / 148.4 |

- `gr_multi_parity`: 32 cases, 0 failures, with `STRATA_GR_MORE_GROUPS=0` and `=1`. `gr_parity`: only the pre-existing `QFUSE ... not written` failure that `main` has on this card.
- Decode, Coder IQ1_M, 8K-token prompt, 256 tokens, greedy, `--resident-experts --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --spec 4 --mtp`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1`: #2193 22.12 / 22.35 / 22.55 / 22.65 tok/s -> this PR 23.24 / 23.61 / 23.62 tok/s; output ids identical (`72b762d5b2a3`) in all seven runs.

Not built or run on Battlemage or i915. SYCL-only file.

## Extra Notes

pulls.title: --vram-elastic with --kv-grow: VRAM takes its chunks where the K/V grows into
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
**`--vram-elastic` with `--kv-grow`: VRAM takes its chunks where the K/V grows into**

Today the two switches exclude each other: with `--vram-elastic` the engine says `--kv-grow is off` and puts the whole
K/V in VRAM, because #533's cache is cut into segments and `--kv-grow` needs one VMM range of chunks. On our R9700 that
cost 1,413 cache slots for a 262K context (9,405 instead of 10,818) - more than the VRAM a game or an image encoder would
borrow. This lets both run.

**What it changes** (`src/program/generate.cpp`; docs in `DETAILS.md` and `VRAM_ELASTIC.md`)

- With both switches the cache keeps `--kv-grow`'s arena (one range of 2 MiB chunks), and `VRAM` works on the region
  the K/V grows into: slots `[lo, top)`, just below the prompt path's loan.
- **Shrink:** the same eviction the K/V's growth uses (hotter experts there move into the coldest loan-region slots
  first), now `kvg_take`, split out of `kvg_ensure` unchanged; the chunks go to the driver instead of to the K/V.
- **Grow:** new chunks mapped there and those slots refilled with the profile's hottest experts the GPU does not hold,
  now `kvg_give_back`, split out of `kvg_trim` unchanged. So after a grow the cache holds what a K/V trim would leave,
  not necessarily the experts the shrink took (the segments put the same ones back); the docs say so.
- The prompt path's loan and chunk are not touched. The K/V keeps growing while the cache is shrunk, from the cache's
  slots, not from the reserve. A small counter keeps the chunks given to the driver; it is settled against the arena's
  empty places, because the K/V's first cells are new VRAM and a trim below them maps those chunks into the arena too
  (without that the count drifted by ~100 MiB and a grow reported "no VRAM" for chunks that had no place).

**What it leaves alone:** either switch alone. `kvg_ensure` and `kvg_trim` do the same steps through the two helpers;
without `--kv-grow`, `VRAM` keeps the segments. The default path does not reach any of it.

**Checked** (on top of #2189 for HIP; the change itself does not depend on it)

- HIP build (gfx1201, ROCm 7.14.1) of this plus #2189: ctest 108/109, the one failure `ple_parity` as before; CUDA:
  this branch alone builds and links with nvcc 13.4.92, sm_120, 0 errors. Not run on an NVIDIA GPU.
- Live, R9700 32 GB, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, every expert in RAM, `--kv-grow --vram-elastic`, 262K context, a needle at 3/5
  of each prompt and a 320-token answer:

| step | VRAM call | slots holding experts (of 10,865) | free | needle / decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 78K prompt, whole cache | - | 10,492 (the K/V took 373) | - | ok / 96.6 tok/s |
| `reserve 4000` | 106 ms | 8,872 | 4,000 MiB | - |
| 78K prompt (the K/V grows again while shrunk) | - | - | - | ok / 92.0 |
| `reserve 8000` | 113 ms | 7,094 | 8,000 MiB | - |
| 156K prompt (the K/V to 2.13 GiB) | - | - | - | ok / 87.8 |
| `reserve 0` | 418 ms | 10,865 | 453 MiB | - |
| 78K prompt, then a short one (the K/V trims) | - | - | - | ok / 96.1 |
| `reserve 4000`, `reserve 0` | 101 ms, 199 ms | 9,281, 10,865 | 4,001, 453 MiB | - |

  The driver's own counter followed (31.5 -> 30.5 -> 28.0 GiB at 4000, 24.1 GiB at 8000 with the 156K K/V, back to
  31.4); the engine's "MiB with the driver" went back to 0 at each full grow.
- `--kv-grow` alone with this build: 78K, a short request (trim), 156K, a short one, 78K - every needle found, the K/V
  grew and trimmed as before.
- Together with the elastic image encoder (#2196) on the same card: the first picture made `VRAM` keep 2 GiB free
  (52 ms) and the encoder started in 3.1 s; a 156K prompt then grew the K/V to 163,840 cells while the encoder held its
  share (needle found); after 60 s without a picture the encoder stopped and the cache was whole again (10,888 of
  10,888 slots, 0 MiB with the driver); a second cycle the same.

**Not tested:** NVIDIA at run time, Windows, more than one shrink-grow cycle with a parked conversation held by the K/V.
