pulls.title: sycl: prompt GDN recurrence with one barrier per token on Alchemist (bit-identical; A770 kernel 2.1x, prompt +3-7%)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545, #1606 (Arc A-series prompt speed)

## Summary
The prompt path's GDN recurrence on Alchemist: the column kernel needs five work-group barriers per token; this variant keeps its four row groups and FMA chains **in the same order**, but puts four columns x four row groups in one 16-lane sub-group, so the two cross-row-group sums become sub-group shuffles and a token needs one barrier. Bit-identical output; ~2.1x faster kernel, +3-7% prompt speed on an Arc A770.

On by default on Alchemist only (`strata::intel_gpu_gen`); every other card keeps the column kernels, unchanged. `STRATA_GDN_XE=0` turns it off, `STRATA_GDN_XE=1` turns it on for any Intel GPU with 16-lane sub-groups (a reviewer with a B-series can check bits and time with it).

## What changed
- `sycl/include/strata/prefill/gdn_xe.hpp` (new): the kernel (variant 6 of `gdn_recurrence_variant`, 256 GRFs).
- `sycl/src/prefill/kernels.dp.cpp`: the gate (`gdn_xe_on`, once per process) and the dispatch; `STRATA_GDN_HEAD` / `STRATA_GDN_REC_HEADS` still win.
- `include/strata/prefill/kernels.hpp`: the variant's comment.
- `sycl/src/kernels/gdn_parity.cpp`: a prefill section comparing variant 6 with variant 0 bit for bit (state, FP32 and FP16 outputs; T = 1, 7, 256, 1000, two seeds, the production entry point and T = 0); skips on anything that is not an Intel GPU with 16- and 32-lane sub-groups. `--prefill-tokens N --prefill-repeat R` times both kernels.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: links `gdn_parity` to `strata_prefill`; `ctest -R prefill_gdn_parity`.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: one bullet in the Alchemist section.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM. Same day, `a0116b27` + #2190 + #2193 (without #2190 this card cannot start; #2193 removes a decode stall that otherwise dominates every run) with and without this commit.

- `gdn_parity --selftest --prefill-only`: 0 failures. Timing, 48 heads, 0 mismatches, max_abs 0:

  | tokens | column kernels | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8,192 | 51.0 ms | 24.4-24.6 ms |
  | 32,768 | 203.6-235.9 ms | 110.0-112.6 ms |

- End to end, Coder IQ1_M, `--resident-experts --expert-cache auto --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --vram-reserve-mib 1200 --prefill-borrow --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp`, greedy:

  | prompt | without | with this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8K tokens | 386.4 tok/s | 396.3, 406.7 tok/s |
  | 32K tokens | 477.9, 480.0 tok/s | 511.1, 517.5 tok/s |

  Output ids identical to the baseline in every run (8K `72b762d5b2a3`, 32K `eb3432fea981`).

Not run on Battlemage or i915. CUDA/HIP: SYCL-only files (plus a comment in a shared header).

## Extra Notes
Tried and not taken: the same kernel with its state in SLM (no register spills, same bits, ~4x slower: 13.7 vs 3.1-3.3 ms at T=1000).

pulls.title: serve: the image encoder only while there are pictures ("elastic": true in the vision section)
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
**serve: the image encoder only while there are pictures (`"elastic": true` in the `"vision"` section, opt-in)**

A GPU image encoder holds its VRAM (~1.3-1.5 GB here) for as long as the server runs, so the expert cache is smaller
for every request, with or without pictures. With `"vram_elastic": true` (#533) the engine can give VRAM back between
requests, so the server can lend the encoder its VRAM only while pictures come.

**What it changes** (`serve/server.py`, opt-in; docs in `docs/VRAM_ELASTIC.md` and the images part of `docs/DETAILS.md`)

- `"elastic": true` in the `"vision"` section, with the config's `"vram_elastic": true`: the encoder does not start with
  the server or with a load. `"elastic_mib"` (default 2048) and `"elastic_idle_s"` (default 120) set its share and how
  long it stays without a picture. Without `"vram_elastic"` the server says so and starts the encoder as before.
- **A picture's turn** (the FIFO turn an encode already takes, so nothing runs on the GPU beside it): if the encoder is not
  running, the engine's `VRAM` first keeps `elastic_mib` free on top of the reserve (the last `POST /v1/vram`, or 0),
  then the encoder starts. If the cache cannot shrink (the resident low-RAM mode, no `--vram-elastic`) the encoder
  starts anyway and the log says why.
- **Idle:** a thread stops the encoder between requests after `elastic_idle_s` without a picture and sends `VRAM` with
  the reserve again; 0 when none was asked, because `null` (the start's reserve) left the cache a segment or more below
  the size it had (measured: 10446 of 10736 slots with `null`, 10736 with 0).
- `POST /v1/vram` while the encoder runs keeps the asked reserve on top of its share; an unload stops it too.
  `Service._vision_down()` no longer counts a stopped elastic encoder as down, so a load never starts it.

**What it leaves alone:** everything without the key (the encoder starts as before; the 725 server tests that were
there pass unchanged), the engine, setup, the CPU encoder.

**Checked**

- `serve/test_vision_elastic.py` (7 tests, fake engine and encoder): the first picture shrinks then starts, later ones
  reuse it, idle stops and grows back to the full size (and not while a request holds the turn or a picture came
  recently), the reserve stacks, an engine that cannot shrink still gets its encoder, an unload lets go, the load never
  starts it, the config keys. Four mutations, each caught: no start in the image turn, growing back to the start's
  reserve (`null`), the load restarting an elastic encoder, the reserve not stacking.
- The whole server suite: 732 tests OK (11 skipped; 725 before plus these 7), on this branch (base `a0116b2`).
- Live on an R9700 32 GB (gfx1201, ROCm 7.14.1, Linux; HIP's virtual memory from #2189), UD-IQ4_XS with every expert in
  RAM, the BF16 encoder at up to 1,024 tokens: the first picture made the cache keep 2 GiB free and the encoder started
  in 4.7 s taking 1,339 MiB; a request with one picture took 8.6 s including that start (5.0 s on a later cold start,
  the encoder starting in 2.7 s); 2 / 5 / 10 pictures with the encoder running took 3.8 / 5.6 / 9.0 s (~0.45 s to encode
  each, the same as the encoder on a second card); after 60 s idle it stopped and the cache grew back to its full
  size (21,704 of 21,702 MiB).

**Not tested:** NVIDIA live (the server path is the same; the engine's `VRAM` there is the existing #533), Windows,
several requests with pictures at once with `--parallel` (the turn is the same FIFO turn an encode takes today).

A note found on the way: `--vram-elastic` turns `--kv-grow` off (the engine says so), so a config with both runs with the
whole K/V in VRAM; on this box that was 9,405 cache slots instead of 10,818. Making the two work together is a separate
change.

pulls.title: setup --update: an MTP folder shared by several configs keeps the draft subset of the most recently used one (the oldest config's default subset replaced cyrillic: Russian decode 68 -> 54 tok/s)
pulls.author: bulhenvaster
pulls.body:
## Title
setup --update: an MTP folder shared by several configs keeps the draft subset of the most recently used one

Issue: none open that I could find (searched issues and pull requests for "draft vocab update cyrillic" and "draft subset shared mtp").

## Summary
`setup.py --update` (`update.sh` / `UPDATE.bat`) refreshes the draft subset once per installed config, most recently
used first. When two configs name the same MTP folder, the folder ends with the subset of the config used **longest
ago**. A config without `"draft_vocab"` counts as `cjk`, so it puts the default subset over the `cyrillic` (or `fr`,
`en`) one of the config that is actually in use.

Seen on one install after the update to 0.1.43: `strata-iq3_xxs.json` has `"draft_vocab": "cyrillic"`, an older
`strata-iq3_xxs-helper.json` (same model, another GPU mode, same `--mtp` folder) has no key. After `update.sh` the
folder's `draft_vocab.bin` was byte-identical to `data/draft_vocab.bin`, and the engine started with
`draft head over 106299 tokens` instead of `58963`.

Measured on that install (RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB with `--peer-device`, Xeon E5-2683 v4, IQ3_XXS, engine
0.1.43, Linux), a greedy 600-token Russian story, two alternating runs per subset:

| Subset in the MTP folder | Decode tok/s | Tokens per window |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default (what the update left) | 54.0 / 54.0 | 1.39 |
| cyrillic (what the config asks for) | 68.7 / 68.6 | 1.90 |

English prose and code were within the run-to-run spread between the two.

## What changed
- `setup.py`: `update_install` calls a new `refresh_shared_draft_vocab(cfg, done)`, which refreshes an MTP folder once,
  for the first (most recently used) config that names it, and skips the folder for the later ones.
  `refresh_draft_vocab` itself is unchanged.
- `tools/test_setup_draft_vocab.py`: three tests - the most recently used config decides for a shared folder, separate
  folders each keep their own subset, a config without `--mtp` is skipped.

What it leaves alone: an install where every config has its own MTP folder, or where all configs choose the same
subset, gets exactly the files it got before. Starting a model still installs that config's own subset (so starting
the older config switches a shared folder, as before); only the update path is changed. No engine code is touched.

How I checked: `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_draft_vocab` (10 pass, 3 new),
`tools.test_setup_config` and `tools.test_setup_configs` (18 pass). No GPU or download is involved in the change.

## Extra Notes
Not tested on Windows or with the AMD engine; the changed code is pure file work and has no platform branch.

pulls.title: sycl: fused GR read without the private GrMulti copy (GR_PICK); large GRF on Arc A-series only - A770 decode 5.4 -> 22 tok/s
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545, #1606 (Arc A770 decode)

## Summary
On an Arc A770 (Alchemist, `xe`) the fused GR read kernels index the by-value kernel argument `GrMulti` with a runtime token index (`m.a[k]`). IGC then copies the whole ~1.2 KB struct into every work-item's private scratch (unitrace: ~40 KB private per SIMD32 thread in `gr_up_multi` / `gr_down_reduce` / `gr_norm_split`). `GR_PICK` selects one field with compile-time indices only, so nothing is copied. Addressing only: the same values, read and summed in the same order, so outputs are bit-identical.

On current `main` this copy is what makes A770 decode crawl with `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1`: each window segment ends with the fused GR read, and the host waits ~3.5 ms longer per segment. With this PR, 8K decode goes from **5.9 to 22.1-22.6 tok/s with the same output tokens**.

The same commit runs the sliced down kernel and the multi-token up kernel in large-GRF mode (256 registers) on Alchemist only (`strata::intel_gpu_gen`), because at 128 the up kernel still spills ~3.4 KB/thread there. Large GRF halves the threads per Xe core, so Battlemage and every other device launch exactly the kernels they launch today. `STRATA_GR_LARGE_GRF=1` forces it on anywhere, `=0` off.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`: `GR_PICK` (a fold over `std::index_sequence` of selects on the uniform argument) replaces `m.a[k].field` in the multi-token GR kernels; `gr_large_grf(queue)` (once per process, Alchemist by default, env override) picks between the existing launch and a `grf_size<256>` copy of the same kernel for the sliced down and multi-token up launches. On a non-Alchemist device, only the GR_PICK addressing change applies.

## How it was checked
Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1 (JIT), Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM; builds of `a0116b27` (+ #2190, without which this card cannot size its expert cache) with and without this commit, same day.

**Bit-identity.** `gr_bench` (1-6 tokens, real Coder dims) prints the same checksum for every token count on `main`, with this commit, and with `STRATA_GR_LARGE_GRF=0`. `gr_multi_parity`: 32 cases, 0 failures. `gr_parity`: the same single failure as on `main` (`QFUSE: T=1 rep 0: not written` in the fused GR read + q8_1 case) — pre-existing on this card, unrelated to this change.

**Kernel time, `gr_bench`, 1-6 tokens:**

| build | us (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 tokens) |
|---|---|
| `main` | 218.0 / 205.5 / 219.4 / 227.7 / 244.9 / 258.4 |
| this PR, `STRATA_GR_LARGE_GRF=0` (GR_PICK only) | 199.6 / 185.5 / 197.4 / 205.3 / 225.0 / 238.8 |
| this PR (Alchemist default: GR_PICK + large GRF) | 132.2 / 118.9 / 133.6 / 150.5 / 168.3 / 183.5 |

**Decode, Coder IQ1_M, 8K-token code prompt, 256 new tokens, greedy**, `--resident-experts --expert-cache auto --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --vram-reserve-mib 1200 --prefill-borrow --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp --adapt-every 8`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1`:

| build | decode tok/s | verify window: wait for rings / pool ms per round |
|---|---|---|
| `main` + #2190 | 5.37; 5.88 and 5.93 with `STRATA_DOORBELL_CHECK=1` / `STRATA_LEND_MIRROR=0` (5 other default runs hung, see the note below) | 69-71 / 183-208 |
| this PR, `STRATA_GR_LARGE_GRF=0` | 20.61, 20.93 | 66.5-67.5 / 35.6-41.2 |
| this PR | 22.12, 22.55, 15.60 (*) | 58.1-59.1 / 33.7-35.2 |

(*) the 15.60 run followed an OOM-killed run (cold page cache; its pool phase was 56.9 ms/round). Output ids are identical to `main` in every run where the expert placement matched (`72b762d5b2a3`); one large-GRF-off run had a different cache placement (hits 0.7605 vs 0.7468) and different ids, which the CPU-vs-GPU expert rounding explains (seen on `main` too).

Not built or run on Battlemage, i915 or Windows; on those the change is the GR_PICK addressing only (and the large-GRF switch if forced). CUDA/HIP: file is SYCL-only.

## Extra Notes
- Follow-ups from the same A770 work, as separate PRs: more work-groups in the GR read (stacked on this one), large GRF for the wide MMVQ kernels, the GDN Xe recurrence, and spill removal in the routers / QSA select / grouped gate-up.
- Separately (issue to follow): on `main` + #2190 this card intermittently hangs at the start of a decode window (main thread in `Verifier::run` -> `queue::wait`, no xe reset logged, RSS grows until the OOM killer); 3 of 5 baseline runs here hit it, 1 of ~15 runs with this PR.

pulls.title: --prefill-head-alias (opt-in, --serve, one GPU): the output head's VRAM holds the prompt buffers while a prompt is read
pulls.author: Maxim-Mazurok
pulls.body:
NOTE: This is human-designed, AI-coded, we optimised memory allocation per phase, and achieved substantial measured boost in decode and prefill speed. Please check the draft, hope it helps at least as an inspiration, I might not have time to polish it up, will try to answer questions. Thanks for considering! Max.

## Title

`--prefill-head-alias` (opt-in, `--serve`, one GPU): the output head's VRAM holds the prompt buffers while a prompt is read

Issue: none. I searched open issues and PRs for head/prefill-workspace/phase-VRAM work and found nothing related.

## Summary

On an 8 GB card the prompt chunk is as large as the free VRAM allows, and prefill speed follows the chunk closely: 185 tok/s at 256 tokens, 292 at 512, 443 at 1,024 and 631 at 1,792, all on the same 29,854-token prompt. Without this change, every chunk above 768 tokens needed a lower `--vram-reserve-mib`, and that left 0 MiB free, which is where WDDM starts paging.

The idea is to treat VRAM as phase-dependent storage. Two large users never work at the same time:

- the **native output head** (417 MiB, Q5_K on IQ3_XXS) is needed only while generating;
- the **batched prompt path's buffers** are needed only while a prompt is read.

With `--prefill-head-alias`, the head is unloaded while a prompt is read, its VRAM is used for prompt buffers, and it is read back in before the first decode window. The auto cache is also sized with the head out, so the prompt path can borrow almost the whole cache (slots 1..N) for a 2,048-token chunk. After the prompt, the cache is refilled as usual.

**Results.** All numbers are from an RTX PRO 2000 Blackwell Laptop (8 GB, Windows 11, WDDM), IQ3_XXS, 590 MiB reserve, on a local 0.1.41 build with this change. The full tables and settings are in `docs/PREFILL_HEAD_ALIAS.md`.

| | Default (auto chunk 512) | `--prefill-head-alias` (chunk 2,048) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prefill, 29,854-token prompt, fresh engine per trial | 292.5 tok/s (12 trials) | 667.1 tok/s (6 trials) |
| Expert-cache slots | 508 | 749 |
| Free VRAM after start / while decoding | 287 / 207-287 MiB | 289 / **0 MiB** |
| Agent loop, prefill (context-matched) | 256 tok/s | 583 tok/s (+125%, 95% CI +123 to +129) |
| Agent loop, decode (context-matched) | 24.8 tok/s | 29.2 tok/s (+19%, 95% CI +17 to +23) |
| Agent loop, expert-cache hits | 20.8% | 25.9% |

The agent-loop rows come from 1,200 requests over 8 cycles (default) and 2,649 requests over 20 cycles (head alias) of OpenCode agents. A large part of the decode difference comes from the default runs' long slow stretches near 19.5 tok/s, which the head-alias run did not have. Against the default's fast stretches only, decode was about 6% faster. We do not know what caused the slow stretches.

A controlled replay held the prompt and a 3,072-token forced output fixed, with a fresh engine per trial:

| Setting | Prefill | Decode |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1-slot cache | 441 tok/s | 22.3 tok/s |
| 1-slot + head alias | 666 tok/s | 24.5 tok/s |
| auto cache + head alias | 668 tok/s | 26.2 tok/s |

The default (auto cache without the alias) was not run in that forced mode.

**Cost.** Short reads get slower. Every request reloads the head (median 255 ms) and lends and refills almost the whole cache. The engine's prompt time (production medians, default -> head alias) by fresh tokens read:

| Fresh tokens | Default | Head alias |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1-64 | 671 ms | 1,311 ms |
| 65-512 | 1,703 ms | 2,453 ms |
| 513-2,048 | 4,062 ms | 3,331 ms |
| 2,049-8,192 | 15,206 ms | 6,876 ms |

It pays off from somewhere between 513 and 2,048 fresh tokens.

**How this was made.** The direction and the idea are mine: use VRAM as phase-dependent storage, and chase bigger prompt chunks because our benchmarks showed a clear trend. I understand Strata's memory layout only in part. The code was written with an AI coding assistant ("vibe-coded"), then measured and run in production on my machine for about 26 hours (2,717 requests) with no errors or restarts. Please review it with that in mind. The areas I am least sure about are listed under Extra Notes.

## What changed

- `src/program/generate.cpp`
  - `--prefill-head-alias` option, usage text, and refusal reasons: needs `--serve`, one GPU and no layer split, no `--batch`, no `--pipeline-windows`, `--short-read 0`, `--expert-cache 1|auto`, `--mtp`, and a native head.
  - At start: MTP binds its draft head from the output head; then the head is unloaded before the auto cache is sized. The loan starts at slot 1, and the chunk is the largest of 2,048/1,536/1,024/512 that fits the borrowed slots plus free VRAM with 512 MiB to spare. A `cudaGetLastError()` retry covers a 0-byte free reading right after the unload.
  - Per request: unload the head and rebuild the prompt path before reading; free the prompt buffers and reload the head after refilling the lent slots.
  - The per-request loan keeps the start-up layout in alias mode. The upstream #2090 sizing is unchanged when the flag is off; it only moved inside `if (!o.prefill_head_alias)`.
  - The verifier is given the (temporarily unloaded) head, and MTP is not bound a second time.
  - Guard: the verify graphs captured in the first decode hold the head's address. If a later reload lands elsewhere, the engine stops with `ERR` (and the server restarts it) instead of running stale graphs.
- `include/strata/core/native_head.hpp`, `src/core/native_head.cpp`: `NativeHead::unload()`, which the destructor now uses.
- `include/strata/core/mtp.hpp`: `MtpDrafter::set_window_R()`, so the verify rows can be attached after an early bind.
- `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: `Prefill::init(..., bool borrow_spill = false)`. When the borrowed region is full, `Alloc::take` continues with owned `cudaMalloc` buffers (the "hybrid" layout). `relayout` refuses a hybrid layout. With `borrow_spill` false, `take` behaves exactly as before.
- `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: the matching `init` signature. It refuses `borrow_spill`, because the SYCL engine has no flag for it.
- `docs/PREFILL_HEAD_ALIAS.md` (new) and a bullet in `docs/DETAILS.md`.

What it leaves alone: the default path. Every new branch is behind the flag or behind `borrow_spill`. No defaults changed, and there are no server, setup or API changes. To use it, add `--prefill-head-alias` and `--short-read 0` to the model config's `args`.

## Extra Notes

**How I checked:**
- Built this branch (rebased on `main` @ a0116b27, v0.1.43.1) for CUDA 13.0, sm_120, MSVC 14.44 on Windows. It compiles.
- Smoke-tested this branch on the same PC, flag off and on, with the same build and a fresh engine each. Both runs used `STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB=auto`; without it, the full sliced arena pin left 0 GiB free for the cache on this 64 GB PC (#243), with the flag off as well. The requests were a 29,842-token prompt cold, a 31-token follow-up on its prefix, two 45-token prompts, and the long prompt again. All completed with coherent answers. The cold prompt read at 276.5/277.1 tok/s with the flag off and 643.1/649.7 tok/s with it on; decode was 35.7/34.7 and 34.1/31.6 tok/s (free generation, 768 tokens). The head came back at the same address on every reload.
- The longer measurements (tables above) come from my 0.1.41 build with the same change. The upstream #2090 loan sizing was the one real merge conflict.
- Default path: by construction (see What changed). I have not run window-hash parity of flag-off against `main`.

**Not tested:** HIP (same sources; I have no AMD card), SYCL (signature only), Linux, other cards and models, multi-GPU (refused).

**Open questions for review:**
1. **Head address.** `cudaMalloc` does not promise the same address on reload. The guard turns a moved head into a restart, but a cleaner fix would keep the address: a CUDA VMM range whose backing is swapped, or prompt buffers placed inside the head's own allocation instead of freeing it. Which do you prefer?
2. **0 MiB free while decoding.** The cache is sized with the head out, so after the reload the verify windows were captured with 0 MiB free on this card (the default had 207-287 MiB), and 0.1.43.1's new start-of-request warning fires at 0 MiB. We saw no paging over 2,717 requests, but it may be wrong for other cards. Should the sizing reserve the head's bytes for decode and spend only the prompt path's own share?
3. **Short reads.** A threshold on fresh tokens could keep the head and read through the decode windows, as `--short-read` does, removing the cost above for small reads: 614 of 2,717 requests read 64 or fewer.

pulls.title: sycl: size the expert cache from the DRM fdinfo when xe reports 0 free card memory (Arc A770, #1545)
pulls.author: aslater3
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1545 (Arc A770 on `xe`); related to #1606

## Summary
On an Arc A770 16 GB on the `xe` driver, Level Zero has no `ext_intel_free_memory`, so `get_memory_info` returns 0 free bytes (with the right total). `device_free_bytes()` kept the 0 — the #1440 fdinfo path only lowers a figure that is too high — so `--expert-cache auto` sized the cache from 0 bytes and a config with `--spec` could not start. This reads "0 free with a known total" as unknown and, on Linux, uses the card's total less this process's DRM fdinfo figure (the same source the A750/i915 path already uses). Any driver that reports a non-zero free figure is unaffected; off Linux the 0 stands.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/core/expert_cache.cpp` (`device_free_bytes`): when the driver reports 0 free and a non-zero total, on Linux, `free = total - own_drm_local_bytes()`, with a one-time message. Nothing else.

## How it was checked (Arc A770 16 GB, `xe`, Linux 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1, Ryzen 7 3800X, 30 GB RAM; JIT build of `a0116b27` with and without this commit; same day)
Coder IQ1_M, `--expert-cache auto --resident-experts --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --kv-resident 20480 --vram-reserve-mib 1200 --prefill-borrow --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp ...`, an 8K-token prompt:

- `main` (`a0116b27`):
  ```
  get_memory_info: ext_intel_free_memory is not supported.
  strata generate: expert cache auto: 0.00 GiB free, 1200 MiB reserved (+5 MiB for the draft head) -> 0 slots
  strata generate: no VRAM is left for the expert cache: it needs at least 286 slots (726 MiB), about 1932 MiB more than this card has free. ...
  strata generate: --spec needs the device residency table (--expert-profile, --expert-cache and the token graph)
  ```
  exit code 2.
- With this commit:
  ```
  strata: the driver reports no free card memory (xe without ext_intel_free_memory); sizing from the DRM fdinfo (this process holds 5.29 GiB)
  strata generate: expert cache auto: 9.82 GiB free, 1200 MiB reserved (+5 MiB for the draft head) -> 3486 slots
  ```
  the 8K prompt is read (542-555 tok/s) and decoding runs.

Not built for CUDA/HIP (the file is SYCL-only). Not tested on Windows (unchanged there by construction) or with two cards on `xe`.

## Extra Notes
- @flare04 reported carrying a "device_free_bytes() host-mirror sizing fix" for the same A770/xe case in #1545; this may overlap with it.
- Upstream's own `--stream-experts` config (setup_intel) does not fit this 30 GB machine for Coder IQ1_M at 128K (the mirror needs ~23.5 GB pinned; 15.7 GB fit, then `REFUSED: 2137 experts are neither in VRAM nor mirrored`), which is why the A770 here runs `--resident-experts`. Separate from this PR; it will be in the A770 benchmark report.

pulls.title: HIP: virtual memory for --kv-grow and --vram-elastic (#533) through vmm.hpp
pulls.author: i-Vladimir-i
pulls.body:
**HIP: virtual memory for `--kv-grow` and `--vram-elastic` (#533) through `vmm.hpp`**

Both switches were NVIDIA-only: `vmm.cpp` had a stub for HIP, and `expert_cache.cpp` carried a second copy of the CUDA
driver table for #533's segments and refused at open on HIP. ROCm has the same functions (`hipMemAddressReserve`,
`hipMemCreate`, `hipMemMap`, `hipMemSetAccess`, `hipMemUnmap`, `hipMemRelease`), so this ports them.

**What it changes**

- `src/core/vmm.cpp` is the one place that talks to the driver's virtual memory, for both backends: a small set of
  driver operations per backend (CUDA: the driver API through the runtime's entry points, as before; HIP: the
  runtime's `hipMem*`), and the chunks, `VmmRange` and #533's segments written once on top of it.
- HIP's chunk is the **recommended** granularity (2 MiB). The minimum one is 4 KiB on gfx1201 / ROCm 7.14.1, and
  `hipMemGetInfo` counts each 4 KiB chunk as 2 MiB, so the elastic K/V would have needed 512 times as many chunks.
  CUDA keeps its minimum (2 MiB).
- `expert_cache.cpp`'s segmented arena calls `vmm_segment_*` / `vmm_reserve` / `vmm_address_free` instead of its own
  driver table. On CUDA these are the same driver calls with the same sizes in the same order (`cuMemCreate`,
  `cuMemMap`, `cuMemSetAccess`, `cuMemUnmap`, `cuMemRelease`, `cuMemAddressFree`, the recommended granularity for the
  segments as before).
- `generate.cpp`: `--vram-elastic` is no longer refused on HIP; it stays off on **HIP on Windows** (AMD's virtual
  memory was measured on Linux only). The help line and the `VRAM` refusal no longer say NVIDIA. Docs follow.
- Tests: `vmm_test` checks the HIP chunk size; `expert_cache_segmented_test` runs on HIP instead of skipping.

**What it leaves alone:** the default path (without `--kv-grow` / `--vram-elastic` nothing calls the new code except
`vmm_available()`, which only queries); the CUDA behaviour of both switches; the gfx906 compat build (no virtual
memory, as before: never measured there); every setup and server path.

**Measured before writing it** (a standalone probe on gfx1201, ROCm 7.14.1, amdgpu 6.19, Linux), because vLLM's ROCm
sleep mode needed workarounds (vllm-project/vllm#37533, #43022, #60367):

- The VRAM of a released handle is back for other programs within 10 ms by the driver's own counter
  (`mem_info_vram_used`) **while its address range stays reserved**, and `hipMemGetInfo` shows it at once. So the
  VA free-and-re-reserve cycle vLLM needed on MI300 / ROCm 7.2 is not needed here, and `VRAM`'s free-memory check reads
  the right number.
- A reservation cannot be freed in part (`hipMemAddressFree` of its tail: an error that also breaks the later full
  free), and one `hipMemSetAccess` or `hipMemcpy` cannot span two reservations (a kernel can). So, as on CUDA, one
  reservation per range.
- Small device-to-host copies (4 B to 1 MiB) from a device-only mapping work on this large-BAR card, so no host access
  is mapped (vLLM #60367 needed it on MI300 / ROCm 7.2).
- AMD's HIP docs warn that RDNA may read wrong data through two virtual aliases of one physical allocation. Neither
  user maps a chunk twice at once (the K/V maps a chunk the cache has unmapped), and `vmm_test` moves chunks that way.

**How it was checked**

- HIP (gfx1201, ROCm 7.14.1): full ctest 108/109, the one failure is `ple_parity` (needs the Q2_0 fixture, as on the
  base commit); one skip fewer than the base (`expert_cache_segmented_test` now passes). `vmm_test` and
  `expert_cache_segmented_test` pass on both cards of the box.
- Mutations, each caught: the HIP chunk at the minimum granularity (`vmm_test`), a segment unmapped but not released
  (`expert_cache_segmented_test`: "VRAM not given back"), no access set (`vmm_test` fails, the segmented test hangs).
- CUDA: the whole tree builds and links with nvcc 13.4.92, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`, 0 errors and no warnings in
  the changed files. **Not run on an NVIDIA GPU** (there is none here).
- `serve.test_vram`: 7 tests OK.
- Live, R9700 32 GB, Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS, every expert in RAM (both switches need it), `--serve`:
  - `--vram-elastic`: reserves of 4000 / 8000 / 16000 MiB took 35 / 44 / 80 ms and gave the driver 3.2 / 7.2 /
    14.7 GiB; decode 120.7 -> 119 / 114 / 98 tok/s (256-token greedy answers); `{"reserve_mib": null}` grew it back in
    0.56 s, `{"reserve_mib": 0}` to the full 10736 slots. With `--adapt-every 0 STRATA_ROUTE_RESIDENT=0` the answer
    after growing back was token for token the one before the shrink (with the adaptive tier or route-resident on, two
    identical requests already differ without any shrink, so that is the only clean comparison).
  - `--kv-grow` against the K/V window (`--kv-resident 32768`), 320-token answers, two runs each: decode at 36K
    tokens 115/115 vs 93/100 tok/s, at 78K 94/94 vs 94/94, at 156K 96/94 vs 81/88; prompt the same except one window
    run at 156K (1600 vs 2400 tok/s, the earlier window run there read at 2393); every needle found.

**Not tested:** NVIDIA at run time, Windows (HIP stays off there for `--vram-elastic`), the gfx906 build, other RDNA
cards, `--kv-grow` together with batch slots (it refuses them, unchanged).

pulls.title: tools/windows: enable_large_pages.ps1 helper to grant SeLockMemoryPrivilege
pulls.author: dvasdekis
pulls.body:
### Summary

Adds 	ools/windows/enable_large_pages.ps1 to configure the 'Lock pages in memory' privilege (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) on Windows:
- Uses secedit to safely grant SeLockMemoryPrivilege to the current user (or specified account).
- Enables 2 MB large pages (MEM_LARGE_PAGES) for Strata's host expert arena (24-30 GiB), reducing TLB overhead from ~6.5M 4KB entries down to ~12.8K 2MB entries.
- Verifies administrative permissions and includes GUI fallback instructions for secpol.msc.

### What it leaves alone
- Zero runtime code touched; standalone administrative helper script only.

Adds  ench/quality_suite.py, a checkable evaluation suite designed for head-to-head model and quantization comparisons on the same box:
- 15 objective questions with verifiable right answers across arithmetic, factual recall, Python synthesis, bug diagnosis, and strict instruction following.

pulls.title: Windows HIP: dynamically resolve hipKernelNameRefByPtr and map auto PCIe mode to DMA
pulls.author: dvasdekis
pulls.body:
### Summary

Fixes two Windows HIP runtime issues:

1. **Loader crash STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xC0000139)**:
   - src/core/verify.cpp uses hipKernelNameRefByPtr for node inspection under STRATA_VERIFY_NODES.
   - On Windows, amdhip64_7.dll (from AMD TheRock wheels / ROCm 10.2 / 7.2.4 nightly) does not export hipKernelNameRefByPtr, although the symbol exists in the import library amdhip64_7.lib.
   - As a result, strata.exe linked cleanly but terminated immediately upon execution before entering main().
   - Resolved by dynamically resolving hipKernelNameRefByPtr via GetProcAddress under _WIN32, gracefully returning nullptr if unexported.

2. **PCIe offload auto mode on Windows HIP**:
   - On Windows HIP, device kernels cannot dereference host virtual memory directly (hipHostGetDevicePointer does not provide an alias).
   - --pcie-mode auto previously selected kernel mode (mode 2).
   - Added resolve_pcie_mode(), routing --pcie-mode auto to host-to-device DMA streaming (mode 0) on Windows HIP.

### What it leaves alone
- Linux HIP, CUDA, and SYCL paths are unchanged.
- Output logits and token generation remain bit-identical.

### Verification
- Tested on Windows 11 with AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), ROCm 10.2.
- strata.exe launches normally without DLL entry point errors.
- Verified on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M with 15/15 passed on bench/quality_suite.py.

pulls.title: core: read the model's geometry from its GGUF metadata and refuse a shape the kernels are not compiled for
pulls.author: gt50
pulls.body:
## Title
Read the model's geometry from its GGUF metadata and refuse a shape the kernels are not compiled for

## Summary
The engine took its dimensions from `ModelGeometry`'s defaults and read only the expert count, the experts per token and the rope keys from the model file; `check_architecture` compared six keys with numbers written into the guard. Any other key was never looked at: a file that declares, say, an indexer budget of 1024 ran with the kernels' 2048 and said nothing. Now the whole geometry comes from the file's `qwen4exp.*` keys, and a file of a shape the kernels are not compiled for is refused at load, naming the key. For every file the guard accepts nothing changes: the same numbers reach the same kernels, and the output is the same (measured below).

This does not make another architecture run (the forward pass and kernels are still qwen4exp's); it is the step a second model would start from: one place that says what the file declares, one that says what the kernels are compiled for, and the check between them.

## What changed
- **`include/strata/core/geometry.hpp` (new):** `ModelGeometry`, moved out of `layout.hpp` and dependency-free so kernels can include it, with the GGUF key of each field and new fields `n_vocab`, `rms_eps`, `n_rot`, `idx_block`, `idx_top_k`, `n_expert_used`. `kCompiledGeometry` is the shape the kernels are compiled for.
- **`include/strata/artifact/gguf_reader.hpp`:**
  - `read_geometry(f, g)` fills the geometry from the metadata shard (llama.cpp's key names). Another architecture is refused by name first. The six keys the guard always required stay required; any other absent key keeps the compiled value. Keys that state one thing twice must agree: `full_attention_interval` and `compress_ratios` (whose non-zero entry is the pooling block), key and value head widths, routed and shared expert widths, `ssm.inner_size` and `state_size x time_step_rank`. Experts per token 1..64 and at most the expert count.
  - `geometry_unsupported(g)` names the first key whose value the kernels are not compiled for, e.g. `qwen4exp.attention.indexer.top_k = 1024, the kernels are compiled for 2048`. Only the expert count (the GSQ-RCO Coder's 256), the experts per token and the vocabulary may differ.
  - `check_architecture` is the two together; `Qwen4ExpGuard` is gone.
- **Kernels:** the files that fix a dimension at compile time `static_assert` it against `kCompiledGeometry` (fused_gr, qsa_decode_attn, qsa_prompt_attn, qsa_select, native_qsa_indexer, native_qsa_score, fused_gdn, native_gdn, verify_kernels, s2_expert_grouped, native_ple_postops, cpu/expert.hpp; in `sycl/` the same plus qsa_prompt_attn_xmx), so a kernel and the struct cannot drift apart without the build failing.
- **`src/program/generate.cpp`:** the geometry and K come from `read_geometry` and are checked before any weight moves; the native embedding takes `n_embd` / `n_vocab` from it instead of `g0` and a literal 248320.
- **`qsa_shapes(g)` (`layout.hpp`):** one function builds the QSA kernel shapes from the geometry, used by layer, mtp, session, verify, prefill, generate's prompt-chunk sizing and the state fingerprint (each built them by hand before; n_rot, idx_block and idx_top_k came from constants).
- **`sycl/`:** the same changes in its copies of generate, layer, mtp, session, verify and prefill.
- **Tests:** `tests/core/gguf_geometry_test.cpp` (synthetic GGUFs: the full key set, the six required keys, a pruned expert count, every disagreement case, unsupported shapes, a dense `qwen35` file, another architecture; `--real SHARD1` prints a real file's geometry and the verdict). `gguf_fixture.hpp` writes f32 and array keys.

## Extra Notes
- **Measured** on a Radeon 8060S (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Windows 11), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS with `--spec 4 --mtp` and the server's other flags, greedy, 256 tokens; this branch and `main` a0116b27 both built here with `tools/hip/build_windows.bat` (gfx1151, engine 0.1.43.1):
  - Prompts of 39 (prose), 48 (code) and 5,568 tokens (a document): the same tokens from both builds, and the same as 0.1.40.2 (before the rebase, the branch matched 0.1.40.2 too).
  - Decode 33 / 47-49 / 39-40 tok/s on both. Reading the 5,568-token prompt: this branch 298, 491, 550 tok/s, `main` 421, 428, 554 tok/s; that spread is run to run on both (on the 0.1.40.2 base, two local builds read it at 404 and 411 tok/s, mean of 3).
  - The same file with `attention.indexer.top_k` patched to 1024 (only the metadata shard changed): `main` loads and answers with 2048; this branch refuses in 0.5 s with the message above.
  - Qwen3.8-27B (UD-Q6_K_XL, Q8_0, a Q4_K_P fine-tune) through `--native`: `architecture is 'qwen35', this engine requires 'qwen4exp'` in 0.5 s, as `main` says.
- **Tests:** ctest 104 of 108 on that build. The four failures need what this PC does not have: `hip_handoff` (the Windows HIP failure in docs/AMD_HIP.md), `ple_parity`, `expert_parity` and `pool_test` (the Q2_0 model and pack fixtures). The GGUF tests also pass built with MSVC `/W4 /WX`.
- **Not tested:** the SYCL tree (no oneAPI compiler here); its changes are line for line the CUDA/HIP tree's. CUDA was not built either; the kernel asserts are host-side `static_assert`s.

pulls.title: sm_61 (Tesla P40): a wide dequant kernel, expert mode 8 and its matvec table by default (bitwise), the dense GEMMs as cublasSgemm opt-in (7K prompt 360-432 -> 464-474 tok/s)
pulls.author: Techannel
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open for this. The P40 path is #395's; #1639's Pascal Q6_K kernel is the P100's decode GEMV, a different kernel from the prompt-path dequantization here.

## Summary
One Tesla P40 (sm_61) with IQ3_S on `a0116b2` (0.1.43.1). On this card the GPU is the bottleneck of the prompt and of the decode (the prompt's GPU timeline equals its wall time, a decode window is 49 ms of GPU stages with 1-3 ms of CPU experts), so I read the profile first and changed four things where it pointed. Each gives exactly the bits of what it replaces; three become sm_61's defaults, the fourth is opt-in.

Through the server, medians of 3 requests, two runs per build alternated, every run started with the card at 65 C:

| | `a0116b2` | this PR (defaults) | this PR + `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 565-token prompt, tok/s | 203 / 205 | 256 / 255 | 254 / 252 |
| 7,047-token prompt, tok/s | 360-365 or 430-432, by the token count | 369-374 or 437-443 | 464-474 at every count |
| decode after the short prompt, tok/s | 35.0 / 34.2 | 38.2 / 37.2 | 37.7 / 37.9 |

The decode gain is small and inside the spread of single requests; the GPU stage profile shows the same size (49.1 -> 45.6 ms per window). Everything, with every request, is in `bench/results/2026-10-12-p40-sm61-kernels/`.

## What changed
Four commits, one per change:

1. **`dequant_bf16.cu`: a thread per 8 values for Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K / IQ4_XS** (16-bit loads, one 16-byte store, the same expression per value). The per-group kernel runs at 10 GB/s for Q6_K on a P40 and costs every prompt chunk of the IQ3_S pack ~0.5 s, whatever its length. Q6_K 10240 x 2560: 7.25 -> 0.33 ms; Q4_K 5.2x, Q5_K 3.8x, IQ4_XS 3.6x. New `dequant_wide_parity`: 360 cases bitwise (FP16 / BF16 / FP32 out, a padded stride, row slices, sane and raw random blocks). Default on compute capability 6.1 only; `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE=0` / `=1` for any card.
2. **`gemm.cu`: opt-in `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1` on Pascal - the qkv / query / gate / output projections' FP16-operand GEMMs as `cublasSgemm` on FP32 copies.** cuBLAS 12.4 picks its slow FP16-operand kernel for most chunk sizes on this card: qkv runs at 7.6 TFLOPS for T 7,030-7,040 and at 4.3 from T 7,041 (49 -> 85 ms), so the same 7K prompt reads in 16.3 or 19.5 s depending on its token count. `cublasSgemm` runs at 8.4-9.8 TFLOPS from T 512. For the five shapes and the sizes the route takes the result is bitwise the FP16 call's: new `gemm_f32_parity`, 5,201 chunk sizes through `Gemm::f16`. **That equality is a property of the cuBLAS build (12.4.5.8 measured), not of the code, which is why it is opt-in** and why the tool is not registered as a ctest.
3. **`iq_kernels.cu`, `native_mmvq.cu`: expert mode 8 and `kIlRows_61` / `kIl1Rows_61` for sm_61**, as sm_60 has them (`STRATA_SM61_TABLE=0`). `native_expert_bench` on the pack's layers, bitwise: IQ3_S 390 -> 255 us for an 18-expert call at 2 tokens. The tables are from three runs of `mmvq_il_parity --bench --emit-table`, identical but for two Q3_K cells.
4. **docs + bench**: the sm_61 section of `docs/OLDER_GPUS.md`, the results folder, one line in `COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

What it leaves alone: every other card runs what it ran (the three defaults are picked only on compute capability 6.1, sm_60 keeps its own; the GEMM route needs the variable and a 6.x card). No change to the server, setup or any HIP / SYCL path.

## Extra Notes
- **How I checked the bits.** Kernel level: the parity tools above plus `mmvq_il_parity` (the table) and `native_expert_parity` on the model's layers. End to end: seven fixed greedy prompts, two runs of each build with `--prompt-cache 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --pcie-frac 0 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0 STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`: byte-identical answers in 4 of 4 runs on 7 of 7 prompts. Without `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` the comparison cannot be made on this AVX2 CPU - the *same* build gave two answers to one prompt in two runs (`native_gu_mt_min`'s lone-token rounding and timing-dependent draft windows); the docs section says so.
- **One PR, three code changes.** AGENTS.md asks for one change per pull request. The three are independent (they share only `CMakeLists.txt` and the docs section) but come from one measurement session, so I kept them as separate commits here. If you would rather have three PRs, say so and I will split them.
- **Built:** the sm_61 CUDA 12.4 engine and tests (`-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`), and `strata_kernels` / `strata_prefill` / the two new tools for sm_75 without that flag. **Not built:** the CUDA 13 engine, HIP, SYCL - I have no toolkit for them here.
- **Not tested:** any other sm_61 card (P4, GTX 10), Windows, cuBLAS other than 12.4.5.8, two cards or a layer split, `--batch`, prompts above 7K tokens, a quality suite.
- **Two things that distort a P40 measurement**, both in the README: the card's thermal slowdown at 89 C (clock 1,531 -> ~1,300 MHz within minutes; I cooled to 65 C before every run), and the token-count dependence above, which looks like 20% of run-to-run noise on the old build.
- Measured and not taken: `STRATA_GR_FAST=1` is slower on the P40 below 5 tokens (82 -> 88 us at one).
- The engine A/B was run on two builds of this code that differ from these commits only in the GEMM route's default; on the commits as pushed I ran the parity tools and one engine pass each with and without `STRATA_DENSE_F32=1` (default: 261 tok/s short, 439-446 long at 7,045-7,047 tokens; with the variable: 250 short, 465-473 long).

The server here runs with all four.

pulls.title: STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR_MAP: the route prior per layer (opt-in); off in layers 0-11 keeps the speed with KL 0.141 -> 0.108
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
## What

`STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR_MAP=<one digit per layer>` (opt-in, with `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR` > 0, changes the output like the prior
itself): the route prior's bonus per layer is digit / 10; `0` turns the prior off for that layer, layers past the end of
the map keep `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR`. Unset: the code path is the same as today.

## Why

`docs/DETAILS.md` lists `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR` as "adds speed, doubles the KL". Most of that KL comes from the early layers:
a swapped expert there changes everything after it. Measured with the prior (0.5) on in one band of 12 layers at a time
(KL against the same build with no prior, 47 prompts, Turkish / English / code, teacher-forced):

| prior 0.5 only in layers | KL |
| --- | --- |
| 0-11 | 0.111 |
| 12-23 | 0.072 |
| 24-35 | 0.069 |
| 36-47 | 0.057 |
| all (no map) | 0.141 |

## Measured

RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB, Core Ultra 7 255HX, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS (GSQ-RCO), `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0.5`, decode speed from
agent turns in mirrored order (engine generation tok/s):

| map | KL all / code | decode tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none (every layer 0.5) | 0.141 / 0.198 | 113.9 |
| `000000000000` + 36 x `5` (off in layers 0-11) | **0.108 / 0.147** | 113.0 (-0.7%, run-to-run spread is ~3%) |
| layers 12-23 and 36-47 only | 0.095 / 0.128 | 108.1 (-5.0%) |

KL is against the same build and config with no prior (every change here has a floor of ~0.04-0.05 from the other
opt-in switches of the config, so the bands do not add up).

So the first map keeps the prior's speed with about a quarter less KL (a third less in code). In daily use since 12 October
(`STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0.5`, `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR_MAP=000000000000555555555555555555555555555555555555`). Built and
smoke-tested on today's `main` (a0116b27). `docs/DETAILS.md` gets the table.

pulls.title: serve: "env_to_user" (opt-in) moves opencode's <env> block into the first user message (new session's first request 11.9 -> 1.1 s)
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
## What

`"env_to_user": true` in `strata-<model>.json` (opt-in): opencode's `<env>` block (with its "Here is some useful
information about the environment you are running in:" line) is taken out of the system message and put at the front of
the first user message, for OpenAI and Anthropic requests (string content, or a leading text part before content parts).
Without the key nothing changes.

## Why

opencode writes the block (working directory, today's date) near the start of its system message, about 3,000 characters
in, before ~41,000 characters of instructions and tool definitions that are the same in every session. The prefix cache
(and `--prefix-cache-dir` on disk) only reuses a prompt's start, so every new folder and every new day read the whole
system turn again: ~14K tokens, 8-12 s on a 12 GB laptop, before the first token of every new session. I captured two
first requests from two folders with a fake server: the block was the only difference in the system message.

With the block in the user turn the system turn (and the tools the template writes into it) is the same for every
session, and the cache restores it. The model still reads the same lines, one turn later.

## Measured

RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, `--prefix-cache-dir` on, opencode, a new session in a second folder:

| | first request | from cache | read | time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `env_to_user` off | 14,753 tokens | 0 | 14,753 | 11.9 s |
| `env_to_user` on | 14,073 tokens | 13,693 | 380 | **1.1 s** |

Quality check: a task that asks for the working directory and the date answered both correctly 3/3 with the switch on.
On my machine's history, 34 such cold reads averaged 10.3 s each.

## Tests

`serve/test_env_to_user.py` (6): the block moves, two folders give the same system turn, content parts get a leading text
part, Anthropic requests too, and off / no block changes nothing. `serve/test_frontend.py` passes. `docs/DETAILS.md` has a
paragraph next to `tool_call_recovery`.

pulls.title: pool: STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT - parked workers sleep with UMONITOR/UMWAIT instead of spinning (opt-in, -3.1% ms/window on a 12 GB laptop, bitwise)
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
## What

`STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT=<TSC cycles>` (opt-in, x86 with WAITPKG, MSVC x64 builds): a parked CPU pool worker no longer spins on
`_mm_pause`. It arms `UMONITOR` on the epoch's cache line and sleeps in `UMWAIT` (C0.1) until the host publishes the next
phase (the write to that line wakes it in hardware) or the cycles run out; then it checks the clock and the sleep rule as
before.

- `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT_C02=1`: the deeper C0.2 state instead of C0.1.
- `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT_ESC=<cycles>`: C0.1 for the first cycles of a park, C0.2 after (a long park is a GPU phase).
- Unset, `0`, a CPU without WAITPKG (CPUID.7.0:ECX[5], one line says so) or a non-MSVC build: the spin, unchanged.

## Why

On a laptop the CPU and the GPU share one power and thermal budget. During the GPU's part of a decode window the parked
workers spin, and that power is taken from the GPU (here `sw_power_cap` was active in ~100% of the samples). Sleeping in
UMWAIT gives it back; the wake on the publish is a hardware monitor, so a worker still starts the next phase at once.

## Measured

RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB, Core Ultra 7 255HX (16 P+E cores, WAITPKG), 64 GB DDR5-5600, Windows 11, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS
(GSQ-RCO), the same config in every arm, mirrored order, engine ms per decode window, GPU power from `nvidia-smi` every 500 ms:

| arm | ms/window (two runs) | mean | vs spin | GPU power | SM clock |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 13 workers, spin (before) | 29.42 / 29.79 | 29.61 | - | 122.0 / 122.7 W | 2400 / 2361 MHz |
| 13 workers, `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT=100000` | 29.02 / 29.04 | 29.03 | -2.0% | 128.2 / 125.3 W | 2416 / 2400 MHz |
| 16 workers, `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT=100000` | 28.96 / 28.44 | 28.70 | **-3.1%** | 128.4 / 128.0 W | 2444 / 2422 MHz |
| 19 workers, `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT=100000` | 31.31 / 31.15 | 31.23 | +5.5% | 126.6 / 124.9 W | 2365 / 2391 MHz |

The sleep hands the GPU ~6 W, and it also lets more workers pay off (16 spinning workers had been slower than 13). C0.2
and the escalating wait were within the noise of C0.1 (28.57 / 28.68 vs 28.90 ms, inconsistent across mirrored pairs), so
C0.1 is the default state. Output is bitwise the same: only how a parked thread waits changes.

Running daily on this laptop since 10 October with `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT=100000 --pool-workers 16`. Built and smoke-tested
on today's `main` (a0116b27): the engine prints `STRATA_POOL_UMWAIT: parked workers wait with UMWAIT (100000 cycles)`,
chat and tool calls answer as before.

## Not done

GCC/Clang builds (they need `-mwaitpkg` or a target attribute on the worker), and `TPAUSE` for parks without a monitored
line. AMD CPUs have `MONITORX/MWAITX` instead; not tried.

pulls.title: serve: fix a race that makes a long prompt read give way to a short request one chunk late, or never; its TTFT -64% where it hit (#656)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Related: #656 (a long prompt read gives way to a much shorter request; closed when the idea shipped as `BYIELD`
in 0.1.39, the code this fixes) and #2050, where @blange48 found that with `STRATA_PIPED_READ_PIECE=8192` a 42.7K
read gave way only at 16,384 tokens. That was this race in the server, and it is on main too: on one GPU, a short
request misses the boundary it should get in most cases. Overlaps #1288 (which waiting requests count as shorter) and
#2109 (request priority): they change *what* the two give-way checks test, this changes *when* they run. Both already
need a rebase on main; after this one, their new condition goes into `give_way()` / `ask()`. Searched 2026-10-12 for
`BYIELD`, "gives way", `_shorter_waiting` and "heartbeat PP".

## Summary
**In short:** the server asks a long read to give way only when the engine prints a progress line (`PP`). On a
`--batch` server with one GPU, every chunk of a read is a boundary whose only `PP` line comes at its end. The `BYIELD`
answers that line, and it reaches the engine after the engine has looked. So a short request waits one chunk more, or
for the whole read when that was the last boundary the read could give way at. The server now also asks on the
half-second poll it already runs while the engine is quiet. On one RTX 5090 this cut late give-ways from 28 of 40 runs
to 4. **Where the race hit, the short request's TTFT fell 64%: from 4.52 s to 1.62 s, the median of 24 paired runs.**
Server only, +70/-17 lines with tests.

**Why it matters:** the engine looks for a `BYIELD` at each boundary, right after the chunk's `PP` line:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as short request
    participant S as server
    participant E as engine
    Note over E: reads chunk k (its only PP line comes at its end)
    C->>S: arrives, waits (its prompt is under half as long)
    alt main
        E->>S: PP (chunk k done)
        E->>E: boundary k: no BYIELD yet, reads chunk k+1
        S->>E: BYIELD (the answer to that PP)
        Note over E: gives way at boundary k+1, or never if k was the last it could
    else with this change
        S->>E: BYIELD (quiet poll, within 0.5 s)
        E->>S: PP (chunk k done)
        E->>E: boundary k: gives way (YIELDED)
    end
```

On main the `BYIELD` was in time only at 16,384. There the engine saves a periodic checkpoint after printing the
`PP` line (`--prompt-cache-every`, default 16,384), which keeps it busy until the `BYIELD` is in. The same race hits
#2050's pipelined pieces of one chunk.

**How:** `_control()` already waits for the engine's lines with a 0.5 s timeout. On a timeout it now calls
`on_quiet()`, and the solo read and the admission read pass the same check they run at a `PP` line. Nothing else
changes: the rule for who counts as shorter, `YIELDS_MAX`, one `BYIELD` per read, and what happens when the read ends
before the engine sees it. The engine drops it (`generate.cpp` main loop), and a solo read's reserved slot is freed at
its `DONE`, as before.

**Measured on one RTX 5090** (Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, `--batch 4`, resident experts, 8K chunks of about 1.9 s; the engine
built from main `a0116b27`), main's server and this one. Each server got two engine starts, in the order main, this,
this, main. A one-line request was sent d s into a cold ~33K read, at 12 delays, twice each. The runs were done with
nothing else decoding (the read is a solo `GEN`, `give_way()`) and with one stream decoding beside it (an admission,
`ask()`). Each run's times came from a log of the server's control events, described below. These are the numbers of
a second window (2026-10-13); the first (2026-10-12) gave the same counts, and this table's TTFTs within 0.05 s.

| | main | with this change |
|---|---:|---:|
| late: a boundary passed after the short request started waiting | 28 of 40 | **4 of 40** |
| of those, never gave way (it waited for the whole read) | 12 | **0** |
| `BYIELD` sent after the request started waiting, median (max) | 1.04-1.52 s (2.72) | **0.23-0.24 s (0.45)** |
| short request's TTFT where main was late (nothing decoding / one stream) | 3.59 / 4.39 s | **1.70 / 1.56 s** |
| short request's TTFT where main never gave way | 4.62 / 7.59 s | **1.55 / 2.34 s** |
| both requests' TTFT where both gave way at the same boundary | | the same (medians within 0.02 s) |

The 4 late runs with this change were requests that started waiting 0.01-0.12 s before that boundary's `PP` line,
too close for any poll. Every request that came 0.35 s or more before a boundary got it.

<details><summary>Per delay: where the read gave way and the short request's TTFT (mean of the 2 runs)</summary>

Nothing else decoding:

| sent after | main: gave way at | main: its TTFT | with: gave way at | with: its TTFT |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 0.20 s | 16,384 (late) | 4.34 s | **8,192** | **2.52 s** |
| 0.75 s | 16,384 (late) | 3.59 s | **8,192** | **1.70 s** |
| 1.30 s | 16,384 (late) | 3.02 s | **8,192** | **1.15 s** |
| 1.85 s | 16,384 (late) | 2.42 s | 16,384 (late) | 2.41 s |
| 2.40 s | 16,384 | 2.01 s | 16,384 | 1.98 s |
| 2.95 s | 16,384 | 1.41 s | 16,384 | 1.42 s |
| 3.50 s | 16,384 | 0.85 s | 16,384 | 0.86 s |
| 4.05 s | never (late) | 5.55 s | **24,576** | **2.09 s** |
| 4.60 s | never (late) | 4.62 s | **24,576** | **1.55 s** |
| 5.15 s | never (late) | 3.98 s | **24,576** | **1.00 s** |
| 5.70 s | no boundary left | 3.09 s | no boundary left | 3.19 s |
| 6.25 s | no boundary left | 3.58 s | no boundary left | 3.56 s |

One stream decoding beside the read:

| sent after | main: gave way at | main: its TTFT | with: gave way at | with: its TTFT |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 0.30 s | 16,384 (late) | 4.89 s | **8,192** | **2.09 s** |
| 1.05 s | 16,384 (late) | 4.08 s | **8,192** | **1.30 s** |
| 1.80 s | 16,384 (late) | 3.30 s | 16,384 (late) | 3.30 s |
| 2.55 s | 16,384 | 2.72 s | 16,384 | 2.69 s |
| 3.30 s | 16,384 | 1.85 s | 16,384 | 1.90 s |
| 4.05 s | 16,384 | 1.12 s | 16,384 | 1.11 s |
| 4.80 s | never (late) | 8.13 s | **24,576** | **3.13 s** |
| 5.55 s | never (late) | 7.59 s | **24,576** | **2.34 s** |
| 6.30 s | 32,768 (late) | 4.39 s | **24,576** | **1.56 s** |
| 7.05 s | never (late) | 6.31 s | **24,576** | **0.84 s** |
| 7.80 s | no boundary left | 5.70 s | no boundary left | 5.67 s |
| 8.55 s | no boundary left | 4.80 s | no boundary left | 4.82 s |

The two runs at each delay were within 0.16 s of each other.

</details>

**On 2x RTX 5090 with #2050** (`--batch 6 --batch-groups 2`, `STRATA_PIPED_READ_PIECE=8192`, the engine built from
main with #2050's two commits; main's server and this one, two engine starts each, measured the same way): a one-line
request 0.5-3 s into a cold ~45K read, whose one-chunk pieces take about 1.5 s. Main gave way a piece late in 10 of 12
runs, this change in 4. Those 4 started waiting 0.10-0.12 s before the piece's `PP` line, as above. Where the race hit
(7 paired runs), the short request's TTFT went from 2.59-5.08 s to 1.08-1.84 s (median 3.19 -> 1.56 s).

**Try it without a GPU** (the fake engine in `serve/test_parallel.py`, one boundary in the read):

```
python -m unittest serve.test_parallel -k far_apart
```

On main, the solo and admission tests fail in every run, 10 of 10 each, with `[] != [2560]`: the read finished
without giving way. With this change all three passed 25 of 25 runs, about 3.4 s per test.

**Where main is better:** in one pair of the 2x RTX 5090 runs (1.5 s, the second engine start), main gave way at
8,192 and this change at 16,384. That request came 0.11-0.14 s before the `PP` line, inside one poll, so both servers
sent the `BYIELD` with that line, and main's won the race in that start. At a `PP` line this change runs the same
check as main, so its `BYIELD` is never later than main's. Otherwise, where both gave way at the same boundary, or no
boundary was left, both requests' TTFTs were the same. Where main never gave way, the long prompt's own first token
came 0.72 s later with nothing decoding (0.40 s sooner with a stream decoding). That is #656's trade, which main makes
too when the ask is in time: the short request goes first. The poll's cost is one look at the waiting list (a lock and
a scan) per half second of engine silence during a read.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: `_control(..., on_quiet=None)` calls `on_quiet()` on its quiet poll. The solo and admission
  reads' give-way checks move, unchanged, into two small functions (`give_way()`, `ask()`). They run at a `PP` line, as
  before, and on that poll.
- `serve/test_parallel.py`: the fake engine takes `--pp-every K` (a `PP` line and a boundary every K chunks). Three
  tests: a solo read and an admission give way at their first boundary, and a request about as long gets no `BYIELD`
  on the poll either.

## Extra Notes
**Tests:** every `serve/test_*.py` module passes on main (`a0116b27`, 725 tests) and with this commit (728: the
three new ones). `serve.test_parallel` passed 3 of 3 full runs.

**How the runs were timed:** a measurement-only patch (not in this PR) made both servers log each control
event: its time and token counts, no text. From that log, each run records when the short request started waiting,
when each boundary's `PP` line came, when the `BYIELD` went out and where the read gave way. The prompts were this
repository's own files, so every read was cold. I can share the scripts.

**Base:** rebased onto main `a0116b27`. The only change near it on main is #1994's `try`/`except` around the
admission loop, which now wraps the new `for` line. The #2050 runs used its two commits rebased onto `a0116b27`
(the same patches as its head, `63335d4e`), with this commit's `server.py`.

**Not measured:** AMD and Intel GPUs. This is server only, with no engine or backend file changes, so there is no
CUDA, HIP or SYCL build to check. The gain grows with the chunk time: a late give-way costs one chunk, or the rest of
the read.

pulls.title: serve: refuse a port another program holds on 127.0.0.1, and say which program
pulls.author: ByteJuggler
pulls.body:
On Windows, Strata on `0.0.0.0:8080` could start beside another program holding `127.0.0.1:8080` (Steam's `steamwebhelper.exe` on some PCs). The server said `ready`, but every client on the PC (web app, chat.py, coding tools, BENCH) reached the other program. The bench then waited "still loading" for 10 minutes. Without `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`, Windows allows a wildcard bind next to another process's specific bind; `SO_REUSEADDR` was already off (#769).

**Changes**
- `Server.server_bind`: `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` on Windows. The existing early test bind in `main()` now fails before the model loads (checked against a live Steam listener: `WinError 10048`).
- The "port in use" message names the program and PID, says when it is probably Strata itself, offers a port that is free now, and gives the commands for this start (`--port`) and for good (`SETUP.bat --port` / `./setup.sh --setup --port`). It is printed without argparse's usage line in front.
- `strata_bench.py`: the pre-check counts any listener on the port, not only one that answers `/health` with JSON (Steam answers 404), and names it.

**Before**
```
server.py: error: port 8080 is already in use - ...      (only when the bind failed; in the Steam case it did not)
```
**After** (`--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080`, Steam running)
```
[strata] cannot start: port 8080 is already in use by steamwebhelper.exe (PID 36952) on 127.0.0.1.
It listens only on this PC's own address, but programs on this PC (the web app, chat.py, your coding tools) use http://127.0.0.1:8080 and would reach it instead of Strata.
Close that program, or give Strata another port (8081 is free now):
  - this start only: add --port 8081
  - from now on: run setup again with --port 8081 (Windows: SETUP.bat --port 8081; Linux: ./setup.sh --setup --port 8081)
  then point your clients at http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1
```
Bench:
```
Port 8080 on this PC already answers, but not as Strata: it is steamwebhelper.exe (PID 36952) on 127.0.0.1.
Close that program, or run the benchmark on another port: BENCH.bat --port 8081 (or python tools/strata_bench.py --port 8081).
```

**Tests**
- A real-socket test that `0.0.0.0:P` cannot be bound beside a `127.0.0.1:P` listener (fails before this change on Windows), message tests, and bench port-check tests.
- `serve.test_server` passes (310). `tools/` has 3 failures in `test_setup_engine_hash.WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller`, which fail the same way on `main`.

pulls.title: bench: RTX 5090 + RTX 3090 two-host stage-RPC UD-Q4_K_XL results
pulls.author: petria
pulls.body:
## Summary

Community speed and repository-only correctness results for original Unsloth
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, running on an RTX 5090 coordinator and RTX 3090
prefix worker in **two separate Linux hosts**. The engine is Strata 0.1.43 plus
local, uncommitted stage-RPC changes, not stock Strata network RPC support.

## Results

The original speed measurements remain unchanged: three repetitions per test,
36 measured requests plus 4 warm-up/calibration requests, no failures or skips.
Short-chat decode median **71.3 tokens/s**; fresh 4K/16K/32K prefill
**1226.4 / 1420.4 / 1446.1 tokens/s**. Agent follow-up decode median
**88.7 tokens/s**, conversation-prefix reuse **68.781%**.

The separate quality follow-up used only tests/fixtures already in this repository:

- Unchanged `tools/needle_bench.py`: **6/6 recall cases passed**, at 32k/128k and
  depths 10/50/90; actual inputs 32,804–32,805 and 124,961–124,963 tokens.
- The three existing RX 9060 XT community TypeScript fixtures, through fresh
  Codex CLI sessions with medium reasoning: **9/9 attempts passed** (three per
  fixture). Independently reran the original acceptance tests in read-only,
  network-disabled Bubblewrap copies: **243/243 checks**, representing **81
  distinct acceptance cases repeated three times**, not 243 distinct problems.
- **64 completed tool calls**, no failed agent turns or timeouts. Two nonzero
  shell exits were `git status` in a non-Git workspace and `grep -c` finding zero
  failed tests; neither was a backend or acceptance-test failure.
- **77 native requests**, 3,364,168 cumulative prompt tokens, 2,189,767 reused,
  and 26,866 generated (including reasoning). Weighted throughput across the
  quality collection: **1427.8 fresh-prompt tokens/s**, **81.2 decode tokens/s**;
  MTP acceptance **72.02%**. These are separate from the original speed suite.
- Both-node follow-up telemetry: **515 samples**; observed Strata worker-process
  VRAM **17.63 GiB**, distinguished from whole-card desktop allocations.

## What changed

Only the results folder
`bench/results/2026-10-12-community-rtx5090-rtx3090-stage-rpc-udq4/` changes:
the original README/reproduction notes link to a new `quality/` directory.
It contains method/scoring limitations, raw recall results, per-attempt coding
results, unchanged generated source, independent acceptance logs, sanitized tool
events, native per-request measurements, both-node telemetry, provenance and
portable reproduction scripts. No gistfile1/fable task or custom coding challenge.

## Validation

- All 77 native request records reconcile exactly with start/end counters.
- Fixture tests/instructions unchanged, allowed source-file scope checked,
  generated solution hashes preserved, required refactoring helpers reviewed.
- Both engines' configurations, binary hashes, base revision, tracked-source
  diff, service PID and invocation identities stayed unchanged. Existing stack
  was not restarted, rebuilt or reconfigured and remains running.
- Original speed data validated unchanged; JSON/JSONL, local links, Python/shell
  syntax, privacy and results-only diff checked. Generated sources preserve
  original bytes/CRLF line endings; Git whitespace checks use `cr-at-eol`.
- Published collector has an offline-tested fallback for disabled optional
  request-body monitoring; HTTP 404 still yields native metrics, while genuine
  HTTP errors remain visible. This collection-only correction does not change
  any measured inference request; measured/published controller hashes differ
  explicitly in provenance.

## Limitations and collection incident

This PR **does not add RPC code to upstream**. Custom engine source changes and
binaries are not distributed, so the upstream base commit alone cannot recreate
the experimental network deployment. That limitation remains explicit.

The quality follow-up's first collector required optional `/api/requests`, which
was disabled (HTTP 404). A metrics-only collector recovered sampling without
engine changes or replaying tests. Hardware sampling begins **138.5 seconds**
after collection started: early memory peaks are unmeasured. All completed
request timings were recovered from retained native history. Native request-body
monitor TTFT/separate reasoning-token counts are unavailable; Codex usage is
kept separately where exposed.

Warm expert cache and an active desktop; no stock/single-GPU or same-day A/B
comparison, cold-cache, vision/concurrency, full 192K coding, or broad coding
leaderboard assessment. Coding acceptance tests were visible to the agent.
No universal quality/speedup claim. No models, generated packs, executable
binaries, credentials, private addresses, raw request bodies, personal session
history or TLS keys are included.

pulls.title: web: runtime i18n layer (English + Chinese), zero markup changes
pulls.author: sdjger-xiaoniu
pulls.body:
## What

The web UI is English-only. This adds a **runtime translation layer** so the interface
follows the browser language, with **no changes to the existing markup or logic** —
`index.html` and `monitor.html` each gain a single `<script>` line.

## Why runtime translation instead of editing the strings

1. **Zero intrusion.** The existing HTML and `app.js` are untouched, so this cannot
   change behaviour, layout or the English text (English is the identity locale:
   no entry means "show the source string as written").
2. **It also covers runtime strings.** `app.js` builds a lot of the interface at
   runtime (statuses, metric labels, toasts, request rows). Those strings never
   appear in the static HTML, so a markup-level approach would miss them.
   A `MutationObserver` keeps translating as the page re-renders.
3. **Adding a language is one object.** `LOCALES` in `serve/web/i18n.js` — copy `zh`
   and translate the values. Nothing else changes.

## How it picks a language

`navigator.language` (`zh*` → Chinese, otherwise English), with a manual override
kept in `localStorage`:

```js
StrataI18N.getLang()        // "en" | "zh"
StrataI18N.listLangs()      // ["en", "zh"]
StrataI18N.setLang('zh')    // remembers and reloads
StrataI18N.t('Chat')        // translate a string on demand
```

## Matching order

1. exact match against the locale table
2. regex patterns for strings that carry numbers
   (`Generating · 42.1 tok/s` → `生成中 · 42.1 tok/s`)
3. a guarded partial pass, with word boundaries, for labels `app.js` assembles
   from fragments (`Done`, `Speed`, `Power`, `6 cores · 12 threads`)

Technical terms stay in English on purpose: `GPU`, `VRAM`, `PCIe`, `Gen3`,
`tok/s`, `MB/s`, `W`, `°C`, and the product name `Strata`.

## Scope

- Chinese covers the whole chat view, the monitor view, the About/settings view,
  the sampling drawer and the API Monitor page (~300 entries).
- English output is **byte-identical** to today's UI.

## Testing

Loaded against a local 0.1.43.1 install: chat, monitor, sampling drawer and
`/api-monitor` all render in Chinese; switching back to English restores the
original strings.

pulls.title: bench: 2x RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB community results (Flash-Next Q4_K_M abliterated, 196K ctx, layer split)
pulls.author: tokyorave
pulls.body:
Community benchmark: **2x RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB**, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Q4_K_M abliterated** (community quant, 36-shard GGUF + native pack), **196,608-token context**, CUDA layer split. Run with the stock `tools/strata_bench.py` suite (`--runs 3 --long`) against the daily-driver server as recommended in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB (24 GiB total), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.2. Second card sits on a PCIe x4 link (probed 3.3 GB/s host→device vs 21.1 GB/s on the first) |
| CPU / RAM | i5-13600K (14c/20t, AVX2, no AVX-512), `performance` governor, 76.1 GiB RAM |
| OS | Linux 7.0.0-38-generic |
| Strata | engine 0.1.43 (source build `3ef5e6c5`), Linux CUDA sm_86 |
| Model | `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Abliterated-Uncensored-AD-4.25bpw-Q4_K_M`, PLE table 320M rows, expert blobs up to 2.66 MB, 52.59 GiB total |

Non-default serving flags (each A/B-measured on this box, kept only if it won and stayed stable):
- `--trim-stage-weights --layer-split 27` — the big one: each card loads only its layers' dense weights. Resident experts **4694 → 6714** (+43%), prompt chunk 7424 → 13312, decode +24%. `auto` picks K=41 here (7 layers on the slow x4 card) and decodes far worse, so a manual 27.
- `--adapt-swaps 96 --adapt-every 4` — small steady gain over 48/8.
- `--kv-resident 24576` tested faster but **reverted**: breaks MTP prefill on 16K prompts (`input records do not fit`) and crashed the engine once; 32768 stays.
- `STRATA_SPLIT_MTP_BATCH=1` — +1–3% prompt reads on the split, kept.
- `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1` — +5% on 16K prompts, ~0 on 4K, kept. Caveat: K-quant fused prompt kernels are unmeasured upstream, so prompt numerics may differ slightly from MMQ (same class of divergence the expert cache already introduces).
- `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=5`, `--vram-reserve-mib 450` (274 MiB free at load; 300 OOMs verify, 688 costs ~300 slots).

## Results (medians, ranges in files)

| Test | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| short chat (46 tok) | — | 104.5 (98.7–122.2) |
| 4K fresh | 458.6 (458.5–458.8) | — |
| 16K fresh | 1198.2 (1194.0–1198.6) | — |
| 32K fresh (`--long`) | 1456.4 (1448.9–1459.9) | — |
| agent follow-ups (14.5K ctx) | cache reuse 68.6% | 104.1 (68.7–131.9) |

No failed requests in the suite (9 chat + 3×4K/16K/32K + 3 agent sessions, one engine session). Speed only, no correctness check — same scope as the stock suite. Rejected during tuning and **not** in this config: helper-GPU mode (`--expert-cache-device1`, decode −27% and a verify OOM on this card pair), `--expert-cache-per-layer` (hit 76–89% vs ~91%), `spec 6` (same 69% draft accept as 4), `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=0` (neutral — overlap is refused on a layer split anyway), `tail-skip 7` (slower), `pipeline-windows 0` (slower despite +214 slots).

## Files

- `bench/results/2026-10-12-community-2x-rtx-3080-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-abliterated-q4km/README.md` — stock tool report
- `results.json` — per-request data (timings, TTFT, draft acceptance)
- `engine-log-excerpt.txt` — startup block (cache sizes, split, resident count). Note: the suite ran with `--url` against the already-running server, so the excerpt is the matching startup block from the live server log rather than tool-captured; local paths redacted, numbers untouched.

pulls.title: setup: an interrupted engine update is tried again instead of skipped for good (#2159)
pulls.author: ByteJuggler
pulls.body:
Fixes #2159.

`get_prebuilt` moves `BUILD.json` to `BUILD.json.prev` before downloading, and `update_installed_engine` only puts it back if the process survives to its `new is None` branch. After a crash, reboot or closed window mid-update, every later update returned early on the missing `BUILD.json`, so the install stayed on its old engine without saying so.

Now, when `BUILD.json` is missing but `BUILD.json.prev` and the exe are there, the stamp is restored (with a warning) and the update runs again.

- New test `test_an_interrupted_update_is_tried_again` (fails before the change, passes after).
- `tools/` suite: 3 failures in `test_setup_engine_hash.WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller`, which fail the same way on `main` without this change.
