   Chat decode 32.4, 4K 752.8, 16K 1470.0, agent decode 48.4, cache hit 68.8%.
3. `2026-10-12-community-rtx-4090-swift-1-5-iq3-s`
   — **Swift 1.5 IQ3_S** (with `--vision`, `--ple-gguf`, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`),
   131,072-token context. Chat decode 88.9, 4K 1231.7, 16K 2409.2,
   agent decode 115.8, cache hit 68.7%.

**Method:** `python tools/strata_bench.py`, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges;
thinking off, temperature 0; model loading not timed.

**Limitations:** speed-only suite — no correctness/recall check was run. Background
load and power limits not recorded. CUDA version not read. Each folder contains
`README.md`, per-request `results.json`, and an `engine-log-excerpt.txt`.

pulls.title: serve: answer GET /models/sse (llama.cpp's model status feed)
pulls.author: Daniel-Aaron-Bloom
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #2154

## Summary

Answer `GET /models/sse` (llama.cpp's model status feed) so front-ends that watch model status get load and unload events instead of a 404 and endless reconnects. The connection stays open; quiet stretches get the usual SSE-comment keep-alive.

## What changed

- `serve/server.py`: the new route (API key as on the other metadata endpoints), a per-watcher queue on `Service` (`sse_lock` / `sse_clients`) and `sse_notify()`, and `status_change` emissions on the transitions the server already has: `loading` and `loaded` around a load, `unloaded` (exit code 0) on unload, `unloaded` with the exit code when the engine had died and is started again. `/models` now builds its entry through a new `Service.model_entry()`, which the SSE `info` reuses; the `/models` answer itself is unchanged.
- `serve/test_lifecycle.py`: three tests - the feed end to end over real HTTP (subscribe, load -> `loading`/`loaded` with `info`, unload -> `unloaded`), the quiet heartbeat, the API-key gate.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the endpoint in the API table and a short paragraph.

## Extra Notes

- Purely additive: no existing endpoint changes its answer (the `/models` refactor produces the same JSON) and no default changes, so the default path stays byte-identical.
- No C++ files are touched, so there is nothing to build for CUDA, HIP or SYCL.
- How I checked: the three new tests run the endpoint over real HTTP; `serve/test_lifecycle.py` 12 pass (9 existing + 3 new), the full `serve/` suite 717 pass / 11 skipped (the skips are pre-existing). Not yet watched live against a client session.

pulls.title: [Docs] the xe expert tier has no SSD fallback, and --spec 0 is refused on native packs (#1796)
pulls.author: nekomario28
pulls.body:
## Problem

The Intel SYCL pages describe an SSD expert tier that the wrapper's default (`STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1`, set by `strata-sycl.sh`) does not have: every expert must be in VRAM or in the pinned RAM mirror, and the engine refuses to start when the two do not cover the model. The same pages recommend `--spec 0` to avoid the verify window without saying that a native (IQ) pack refuses it.

## Result

- `docs/INTEL_ARC.md`: under the wrapper default the xe expert tier has no SSD fallback, and the two places an expert can be are named.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the same limit for `--stream-experts`, and that a native pack takes `--spec 2` at the smallest.
- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`: the `--spec 0` advice now says it does not apply to native packs.

## Validation

Passed:
- Documentation-only change: no build and no GPU run were required, so none were run for this branch (not run: engine build, hardware execution).
- Claim re-checked against `main` at `e88ee39d`: `src/program/generate.cpp:3572` refuses a native (IQ) pack unless `--spec >= 2`, and `setup.py` exports `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1` in the `strata-sycl.sh` wrapper.
- Relative links and anchors in the three edited files scanned locally: no broken targets.

pulls.title: hip(RDNA4): fused-GR register-half down kernel for gfx1200/gfx1201 decode
pulls.author: bsorensen110
pulls.body:
### Summary

Adds one extra selection for the hyper-connection fused-GR read on AMD RDNA4: the down-projection kernel
`gr_down_register_half_kernel` ("P4"), which carries the next activation tile in a compile-time register tuple
before scattering it into the existing shared-memory buffer. It is gated to runtime `gfx1200`/`gfx1201` only, and
it is selected **only when asked for** — `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=7` — and only after a per-device self-test proves it is
**bitwise identical** to the existing staged kernel. If any gate fails, the established staged / split / plain
path is selected unchanged.

This is not a replacement of the gfx12 kernel set and not a new arithmetic path. The accumulation order, tile
order, grid, block size and dynamic shared-memory layout are the staged kernel's; only the way the `h+2` tile
reaches shared memory differs.

Opt-in surface: `STRATA_HC_SPLIT` (new selector value `7`, existing `0`/`1`/`2`). **Unset stays on the staged
upstream path on every architecture: it never runs the P4 self-test and never selects P4.** `=2` requests staged,
`=1` split, `=0` plain. Only `=7` requests P4, and only on `gfx1200`/`gfx1201`, still subject to both parity
gates. Every other architecture keeps upstream's staged selection.

Files: `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`, `include/strata/kernels/fused_gr.hpp`,
`include/strata/kernels/fused_gr_policy.hpp` (new), `tests/kernels/fused_gr_p4_policy_test.cpp` (new),
`CMakeLists.txt`, `docs/AMD_HIP.md`.

### Motivation

The fused-GR read is part of the per-token decode path and stages activation tiles for each hidden-state tile.
P4 tests whether an explicit per-thread register prefetch can hide some of that data-movement cost without
changing the dot products. The existing staged implementation fills a shared-memory double buffer through
`stage_htile`; P4 preserves that shared layout and the staged arithmetic order.

P4 splits the next tile into two compile-time halves: half A is already in registers before the tile is needed,
and half B is fetched in the middle of the dot-product loop. The compile-time `HcChain` avoids a runtime-indexed
per-thread array that the source comment says could lower to private scratch on gfx1201. Fetching half B at `q==2`
is intended to expose load/compute overlap with the remaining dot products; **that overlap has not been confirmed
by an ISA dump or profiler**. The arithmetic and q/k order are unchanged, so bitwise parity with staged is required.

Related prior work, distinct from this change: #2070 (CUDA sm_75 hyper-connection up kernel and token-pair
staged down kernel), #1370 (CUDA sm_80+ opt-in `STRATA_HC_UPMIX`), and closed #329 (gfx12 WMMA for QSA prompt
attention). None of them touch the RDNA4 fused-GR decode down path.

### Implementation

`src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`:

- `HcChain<I>` — a recursive struct of `float4` slots indexed only at compile time. The source comment states
  this is to keep the per-slot activations from lowering to private scratch on gfx1201; no ISA dump or profile
  is included with this PR.
- `gr_down_register_half_kernel<MAX_T, EXACT_T>` follows `gr_down_staged_kernel` exactly for tiles 0 and 1
  (`stage_htile` + `cp_async_commit`), then handles tile `h+2` in two halves per thread:
  - `NS = ceil(MAX_T * (H_TILE/4) / THREADS)` slots per thread, split at `H0 = (NS+1)/2`. For the generic
    instantiation (`MAX_T = 8`, `H_TILE = 1280`, `THREADS = 256`) that is 10 slots, 5 per half, i.e. 40 floats
    per thread in registers.
  - half A (`t0`) of tile `h+2` is loaded one iteration ahead — at the end of iteration `h` the kernel issues
    `hc_load_all` for tile `h+3`, which is iteration `h+1`'s half A (tile 2's half A is loaded before the loop);
  - half B (`t1`) of tile `h+2` is fetched inside the dot loop at `q == 2`, so that its global loads are issued
    while the remaining dot products of tile `h` are still executing. **This is the intended schedule, not a
    measured overlap** — no codegen or profiling evidence is attached.
  - both halves are then scattered into the shared buffer. `hc_scatter_all` uses the same index swizzle as
    `stage_htile` (`k*(H_TILE/4) + (s4&1)*(H_TILE/8) + (s4>>1)`), so the dot products read the same shared
    layout, and the same bits.
  - Inactive lanes (the inject block's non-participating warps) skip the mid-dot prefetch and perform their own
    single fetch of half B, because they still take part in the shared-buffer scatter.
- Launch shares staged's grid (`DOWN_BLOCKS + 1`, 256 threads) and dynamic shared-memory size, and the kernel
  instantiations get the same `cudaFuncSetAttribute` treatment as the staged ones (max dynamic shared memory,
  100% shared-memory carveout).
- `fused_gr_read_multi` dispatches `kHcRegisterHalf` (=7) to this kernel; plain/split/staged dispatch is
  unchanged.
- `fused_gr_check()` and `fused_gr_variant()` ask the policy header what the environment asks for, so the
  selector rules live in one place and are unit-tested. `fused_gr_variant()` reports the requested path capped at
  staged until the check has run, so an untested `=7` request never reaches the candidate kernel.

`include/strata/kernels/fused_gr_policy.hpp` (new, header-only, no GPU) holds the selection and error rules as
`constexpr` functions so they are unit-testable:

```cpp
constexpr int fused_gr_env_variant(bool env_present, char first) noexcept;     // unset -> staged
constexpr bool fused_gr_p4_selftest_requested(int want, bool gfx12) noexcept;  // only =7, only on gfx12
constexpr int fused_gr_select(int want, bool split_ok, bool staged_ok, bool p4_gate_ok) noexcept;
constexpr bool fused_gr_p4_parity_gate(bool gfx12, bool staged_ok, bool p4_ok) noexcept;
constexpr bool fused_gr_p4_q32_parity_marker_ok(bool selftest_ok, bool qfuse_hc, bool staged_ok, bool p4_ok) noexcept;
enum class GrBackend : unsigned char { Cuda, Hip };
constexpr bool fused_gr_context_fatal(int err, GrBackend backend) noexcept;
```

`fused_gr.cu` `static_assert`s every code the classifier uses against its own backend's header name
(`cudaError*` in `driver_types.h`, `hipError*` in `hip_runtime_api.h`) in the backend being compiled, so a header
that renames or renumbers one breaks the build instead of the classification. The CUDA-only codes (226, 714–718,
721, 810, 911, 912) are asserted in the CUDA branch and the HIP-only HSA runtime codes (1052, 1053) in the HIP
branch; HIP's different meanings for 911 (`hipErrorInvalidChannelDescriptor`) and 912 (`hipErrorInvalidTexture`)
are asserted where they differ, together with the classification those numbers get in that backend.

### Correctness and fallback

Architecture gate. `p4_gfx12_device()` reads `cudaDeviceProp::gcnArchName` at runtime and accepts only
`gfx1200` or `gfx1201` (`gfx_arch_is_gfx12`). Under a non-HIP compile it returns false. An explicit
`STRATA_HC_SPLIT=7` on any other part logs that P4 is restricted to gfx1200/gfx1201 and keeps staged.

Opt-in gate. The P4 self-test runs only for an explicit `=7` on gfx1200/gfx1201. Unset, `=2`, `=1` and `=0` never
run it, and the selector never promotes P4 on their behalf: unset with every gate passing stays staged. On
gfx1200/gfx1201 with anything but `=7` the check logs that P4 is opt-in through `=7`.

Promotion gate. P4 is selected only when `gfx12 && staged_ok && p4_ok` — that is, the staged kernel must itself
match the plain reference bitwise, **and** P4 must match staged bitwise. A P4 candidate that passes while the
staged reference is failing cannot be promoted.

Self-test coverage (`fused_gr_selftest`, run once per card and latched in `fused_gr_check`): T = 1..8, apply
off/on, injection weights present/null, and with and without the q8_1 path (the q8 arm also exercises the
`QFUSE_HC` q32 up kernel). Compared bitwise: `lo`, `rs`, `inject`, `mixed`, `R_out` floats **and** the `q8_1`
output bytes.

Failure isolation, split by what the error leaves usable. The candidate runs on its own non-blocking stream,
which isolates **recoverable candidate-only** errors: a refused P4 launch, a bad configuration/handle, P4 stream
creation, final synchronization, or stream-destruction failure disables P4 without invalidating staged/split checks.
Shared scratch-allocation, reference-stream setup/sync/destruction, or shared cleanup failures fail the self-test, so
P4 cannot be selected. A separate stream does **not** isolate an asynchronous device fault — an illegal address or
device exception from the candidate poisons the shared context for the whole process, so fallback kernels would only
return the same error. Context-fatal errors returned by device/property/attribute queries, H2D copies or memsets,
shared-memory setup, launch/sync, read-back, allocation, stream creation/destruction, final sync or cleanup are
classified before clearing an error or making another GPU call; they log the code, flush output and call
`std::_Exit(1)` immediately. This matches #224's handling in `src/program/generate.cpp` and avoids unwinding/
destructors on a poisoned context. The fatal set includes illegal address (700), timeout (702), destroyed context
(709), device assert (710), launch failure (719), and uncorrectable ECC (214) in both backends, plus CUDA's 226,
714–718, 721, 810 and 911. HIP's 911/912 are known recoverable API errors; HIP's 1052/1053 are documented HSA-call
failures. Unknown (`cudaErrorUnknown`/`hipErrorUnknown`) and all other unclassified runtime values fail closed; only
explicitly listed ordinary API/resource errors (invalid value/configuration, allocation/launch-resource refusal,
invalid device function/image, bad handle, not-ready, unsupported limit/capture, etc.) are allowed to fall back.

Selector semantics (`STRATA_HC_SPLIT`): **unset = staged, the upstream path** — no P4 self-test, no P4 selection;
`=2` requests staged; `=1` selects split; `=0` selects plain; `=7` is the only value that requests the P4
self-test, on gfx1200/gfx1201 only, and selects P4 only if both gates pass, falling back staged → split → plain
otherwise.

Diagnostic marker. The `P4 + QFUSE_HC q32 outputs passed bitwise parity` line is emitted only when the whole
self-test succeeded, `QFUSE_HC` is enabled, and both parity flags passed — it cannot print after an unrelated
self-test failure.

### Measurements

These are previous same-host results, not a new run on the rebased branch. The host was a Radeon AI PRO R9700
(native gfx1201), ROCm 10.2.0 nightly / HIP 7.17.26391 / hipBLASLt 100500, running Swift / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
IQ3_XXS. Each arm used a 439-token warmup and three fresh 80-line / 1,111-token outputs at `temperature=0` and
`cache_n=0`. The staged and P4 arms used the same v0.1.43 serve module and **same integration binary**, serially,
differing only by selector. That binary also carried independent local MMQ/hipBLASLt overlays, held constant across
both arms; these numbers are an integration-build A/B, not a clean-upstream benchmark.

| Arm | Median decode | Range (3 trials) |
|---|---:|---:|
| v0.1.43 staged upstream path (`STRATA_HC_SPLIT=2`) | 153.2 tok/s | 152.2 – 154.3 |
| v0.1.43 P4, that build's promoted default (unset) | 156.1 tok/s | 153.3 – 156.8 |

P4's observed median is **+1.89% vs the staged upstream path**. The ranges overlap (153.3–154.3), so this is not a
statistically established gain: three trials on one host/workload. **The 156.1 tok/s P4 timing comes from the
earlier integration build, where an unset selector promoted P4 once both gates passed.** The explicit `=7`
selector that this update makes the only P4 request was exercised for correctness in those runs, not for timing,
and no P4 or clean-upstream decode run was performed on the rebased v0.1.43.1 tree because the live service was
kept online.

Correctness observed in the existing runs: P4 and staged replies were byte-identical in all three paired trials.
The four tested selector configurations — `=2` staged, `=1` split, `=7` P4 opt-in, and that build's unset P4
default — all returned the same arithmetic answer `391`

pulls.title: SYCL: preserve the borrowed default queue during teardown
pulls.author: alex4o
pulls.body:
## Summary

Do not initialize uncreated, owned SYCL queue handles with DPCT's borrowed default queue. Otherwise teardown can delete that queue and leave DPCT's default-queue pointer dangling.

Related: #1555 (the same null-sentinel migration trap; this patch targets Prefill/MtpDrafter rather than Verifier).

## What changed

- Initialize Prefill::Impl::copy and kv_copy to nullptr until their creation paths run.
- Initialize MtpDrafter::side_ to nullptr until load() creates its owned queue.
- Keep borrowed Prefill::Impl::cs pointing to the default queue; do not change its ownership.
- Add sycl_teardown_queue_test under STRATA_SYCL_PARITY, with a 30-second timeout.

The existing guarded cleanup still destroys genuinely owned queues. This does not skip cleanup, change inference arithmetic, or use _Exit to hide errors.

## Failure and regression

A non-serve A770 run completed a long generation, then exited with SIGSEGV. A core inspected with matching oneAPI libraries showed:

    sycl::detail::usm::free
    sycl::free
    strata::core::MtpDrafter::~MtpDrafter
    main

Prefill had already destroyed kv_copy even with KV prefetch disabled, because its initializer made it alias the default queue. MTP's later weight free then used that dangling queue. An unloaded/failed-load MTP object had the analogous side_ ownership problem.

The model-free GPU regression retains a live USM allocation across unloaded MTP, rejected MTP load, uninitialized prefill, repeated reset, and rejected prefill initialization. It checks default-queue identity/context/device, allocation contents, and a subsequent free. Five scenarios × eight repetitions = 40 lifecycles.

## Validation

On PR base a0116b2, A770/i915, oneAPI 2026.1:

    cmake --build <build> --target strata sycl_teardown_queue_test
    ctest --test-dir <build> -R '^sycl_teardown_queue_test$' --output-on-failure

Both full engine build and regression passed. The same regression compiled against unfixed headers/libraries fails at unloaded MTP with UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED; with this patch all 40 lifecycles pass.

Earlier isolated experiments on base 61b3fb5 applied these same ownership fixes and completed four full-context CLI runs with normal exit 0, after the original teardown crash. These runs also included separate diagnostic/GRF changes, so they supplement—not replace—the focused regression. [Validation notes](https://gist.github.com/alex4o/6f5912c82d67393fe5ca3aac26ff5b63).

## Limits

With STRATA_KV_PREFETCH=1, nullptr now allows the intended dedicated queue to be created where the old nonnull initializer suppressed creation. That opt-in asynchronous path was reviewed but not runtime-tested. Peer/multi-GPU teardown and other similar migrated sentinels are outside this focused patch. Only SYCL files are touched; CUDA/HIP were not changed.

pulls.title: SYCL: opt in to 256 GRFs for fused hyperconnection up
pulls.author: alex4o
pulls.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in 256-GRF launch for the default fused hyperconnection up kernel. On an Intel Arc A770 16 GB / i915 with oneAPI 2026.1, this removed the measured register-spill allocation and improved matched warmed decode by about 13%.

Related: #1606 (decode optimization only; this does not claim to fix that report's prefill bottleneck).

## What changed

Only sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp changes:

- STRATA_GR_UP_LARGE_GRF=1 selects grf_size<256> and a distinct kernel identity.
- Unset, 0, or any value other than 1 retains the original kernel name and launch properties.
- Body, arithmetic, indexing, range, subgroup size 32, and root-sync property are shared/unchanged. Other GR paths are untouched.
- The flag is sampled once: restart the engine to change it.

The option remains off by default. The experimental Intel GRF header is an unconditional compile dependency; validation is on oneAPI 2026.1, the toolchain documented for this port. Older compilers and other GPUs were not tested.

## Validation

**This PR on base a0116b2:** full SYCL strata and gr_bench builds passed in strata-sycl-dev with icpx 2026.1. Separate gr_bench runs printed effective flag values unset / 0 / 1; all six output checksums (T=1..6) matched each other and the earlier OFF checksums. CUDA/HIP source is unchanged.

**Earlier full-model experiments on base 61b3fb5, with this exact kernel patch:**

| Matched OFF decode | Matched ON decode |
|---:|---:|
| 18.7 tokens/s | 21.2 tokens/s |
| 18.6 tokens/s | 21.1 tokens/s |
| 19.3 tokens/s | 21.4 tokens/s |

Ryzen 5800X, 48 GB-class RAM, IQ3_XXS, INT8 KV, 131072 capacity, 4096 prefill, spec4, CPU cache misses. Two warm-ups per arm; three 384-token timing samples without prefix reuse. Median gain 13.4%. These capped samples are not complete-answer correctness tests.

- Compiler metadata: 3520-byte spill allocation -> zero; 256 GRFs. Private-memory size remains 40192 bytes.
- A direct fused-kernel fixture covered 432 cases / 77,575,968 output floats, including T=1..8, injection/apply/in-place variants. OFF/ON and repeated OFF were bit-identical; finite/guard checks passed.
- A 129,845-token prompt and complete 549-token OFF reference vs exact-token ON replay produced 136,327,680 bit-identical float32 logits. Both arms used the same isolated diagnostic capture/teardown fix and controlled T1/adaptation-off execution; neither diagnostic is part of this PR.
- An independent unforced ON run with production speculation/adaptation emitted the same complete answer. OFF and ON recovered 5/5 codes and passed 384 LRU checks each.
- A later OFF/OFF repeat showed numerical variation. The matched equality is evidence for this tested pair, not a claim of deterministic repetition or universal numerical equivalence.

[Detailed protocol, limitations and reproducible direct fixture](https://gist.github.com/alex4o/6f5912c82d67393fe5ca3aac26ff5b63). Full-model speed/128K tests were not rerun on current upstream a0116b2; the changed GRF source was unchanged upstream between the two bases. No universal 20+ tokens/s claim.

pulls.title: hip: add a gfx1150 hipBLASLt 100500 tuning table (Radeon 890M / Ryzen AI 9 HX 370)
pulls.author: onionbutties
pulls.body:
Issue: #1217 (the gfx1150 build/run report) - the table it did not have

## Summary
A hipBLASLt tuning table for gfx1150 (Radeon 890M on a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, Strix Point), for engines built with
hipBLASLt 1.5.0 (version 100500). Setup picks it up by itself when the installed hipBLASLt reports 100500.

## What changed
- `tools/hip/gfx1150-hipblaslt-100500.txt` (new): 141 rows over the 16 dense GEMM geometries of
  `gfx1150-hipblaslt-100401.txt` at T = 64, 128, ..., 16384.
  - Two `tune_hipblaslt --workspace-mib 32` passes; each row keeps the solution with the lowest mean of the six
    repetitions (a repetition stalls now and then on this chip, so the tool's mean-of-three pick can differ between
    passes).
  - The three rows slower than plain hipBLAS (the tiny bf16 N=1 K=2560 shape at T = 64 / 128 / 256; about 13-39 us and
    noise-dominated) are left out, so those buckets route to the nearest good row.
  - Every remaining row beats plain hipBLAS: 1.07x to 16.7x per GEMM, geometric mean 5.0x.
- No source change: the engine already loads a table for the running card's arch and version
  (`src/prefill/hipblaslt_tuning.hpp`).

## Extra Notes
- Calibrated on one machine: Radeon 890M (gfx1150), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 96 GB DDR5-5600, Windows 11, engine 0.1.43,
  ROCm 10.2.0a20260930, hipBLASLt 1.5.0. A table's solution IDs are scoped to one hipBLASLt version and architecture,
  so a different 1.5.0 build should recalibrate before using it (the engine refuses any other header version).
- The prompt-speed gain of the whole model is not measured separately here (the per-GEMM numbers above are); per the
  maintainers' convention a shipped table should show the end-to-end prompt speed too.
- The installer opt-in that wires this table in for a gfx1150 install is #2147.

pulls.title: setup: opt-in gfx1150 (Radeon 890M / 880M, Strix Point) as a unified-memory AMD card
pulls.author: onionbutties
pulls.body:
Issue: #1217 (the gfx1150 build/run report) - setup does not install for gfx1150 yet

## Summary
An opt-in, `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX1150=1`, that lets setup install for the Radeon 890M / 880M iGPU (Ryzen AI 300,
Strix Point, gfx1150) as a unified-memory AMD card like Strix Halo. The engine already builds and runs for gfx1150
(0.1.40.2, #1217); only the installer did not know it.

## What changed
- `setup.py`
  - `GFX1150_OPT_IN` and gfx1150 in `AMD_ARCHS` / `ROCM_INDEXES` (TheRock `gfx1150` index), gated so the default path
    is byte-identical when the variable is unset.
  - `is_uma_apu(g)`: the shared unified-memory handling now covers Strix Halo (gfx1151), gfx1150 and the gfx1103
    opt-in (was Strix Halo plus gfx1103 inline). `amd_apply_uma`, `igpu_notes` and `amd_gpus_win` use it.
  - `gfx1150_notes`: the unified-memory notes for this chip (never the Strix Halo text).
  - The install writes the chip's exact speed switches into the config's `env`, beside `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`
    (`GFX1150_SWITCHES`): the gfx1151 arch-default set (`src/core/arch_defaults.cpp`) less `STRATA_HCD_EXACT`, which
    copies the gfx1151 table's solutions 1176 / 1177 and does not fit a gfx1150 table. The Radeon 890M report measured
    the same greedy answers with all 17 on and with all 17 off, decode +2% and prompts +3-6%. The set is in
    `SETUP_ENV`, so a re-run refreshes it and it does not linger when the opt-in is turned off.
- `tools/test_setup_strix_halo.py`: `Gfx1150Switches` keeps `GFX1150_SWITCHES` equal to the gfx1151 table minus
  `STRATA_HCD_EXACT`, asserts the engine's own default path for gfx1150 stays empty
  (`arch_default_env("gfx1150").empty()`), and checks the `SETUP_ENV` wiring.

## Extra Notes
- No release ships a ready-made Windows engine for gfx1150, so the note tells the user to build one with
  `STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1150 tools\hip\build_windows.bat` and start setup with `--prebuilt dist\`.
- Default path is byte-identical when the variable is unset; `tools/test_setup_strix_halo.py` (40),
  `tools/test_setup_amd.py` (36) and `tools/test_setup_choices.py` (47) pass.
- Verified end to end on a Radeon 890M (Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 96 GB, Windows 11): the engine builds for gfx1150, setup
  accepts the card, and the model runs with all 24,576 experts in the GPU pool at about 11 tokens/s decode.
- The engine's arch defaults are deliberately left alone (gfx1150 stays out of `arch_defaults.cpp`); the switches are
  written by setup instead.
- The gfx1150 hipBLASLt tuning table is #2148.

pulls.title: sm_75: the v2 prompt attention in one stage, three blocks per SM (bitwise, attention 1.66x; stacked on #2092)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
Stacked on #2092 (the Turing v2 prompt attention, `STRATA_PA_V2T=1`): its first commit is #2092's.

With register staging, #2092's v2 keeps the next chunk's K/V pieces in registers until the current chunk's p·v is done, so its second shared-memory stage buys nothing on Turing - but `Smem2` is 45.6 KB and a Turing SM has 64 KB: one 4-warp block per SM, one warp per scheduler, every latency exposed. ncu on a 130K chunk: 12.5 % warps active, the tensor pipe at 8 %.

Below sm_80 the kernel now takes `Smem2T`: one K/V stage, and no separate q·k partials (`part`, 8.4 KB). The partials of cell group `nt` (8 cells, 16 rows) are exactly 512 bytes, and the cells they come from occupy bytes `[512 nt, 512 nt + 512)` of the warp's own K slice (the swizzle stays inside a cell's 64 bytes), read by then - so after a `__syncwarp` each group's partials overwrite its own cells. The softmax reads them across warps after the same `__syncthreads` as before, and the next chunk's `store_stage` comes after the second one, as before. 19.7 KB a block: three per SM (168 registers fit three). Same arithmetic, same order: the same bits.

The second commit adds `tests/cuda/pa_bench.cpp`, which replays a recorded selection (`STRATA_QSA_DUMP` gets `STRATA_QSA_DUMP_LAYER=i` and `STRATA_QSA_DUMP_STEPS=1`), random q and int8 K/V, and prints the median time and an output hash.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W; `v0.1.43` + #2092. Q2_0, `--prefill auto:16384`, `STRATA_PA_V2T=1`.

## `pa_bench` (QSA layer 5, last chunk of a 130,559-token prompt: 15,871 queries × 2,051 cells)

| | ms | output hash |
|---|---:|---|
| #2092 | 113.8 | `2541296d11c7be6f` |
| this | 68.5 | `2541296d11c7be6f` |

## Engine

| prompt | before | after | first logits |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 98K (6 chunks) | 53.3 s | 49.9 s | bitwise identical |
| 4K | 3.54 s | 3.42 s | bitwise identical |

(with the fused experts of #2145 on; the generated text is the same.) Deep, served (`--serve`, 512K context): 389,560 tokens from scratch 255.0 → 223.6 s and +16K at 406K 12.82 → 11.42 s together with the fused experts; needle 2/2 at 352,660 tokens.

pulls.title: prefill: the fused int8 prompt experts on Turing (sm_75), opt-in (+9 % prefill on RTX 2080 Ti)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
On Turing the prompt path's experts always go through llama.cpp's MMQ: the fused int8 kernels (`moe_fused.cu` for the Strata Q2_0 pack, `moe_fused_iq.cu`'s `native_kernel` for the native packs, #136) need sm_80. On an RTX 2080 Ti MMQ's Q2_0 kernel runs at ~20-30 TOPS (255 registers with spills, one CTA per SM) and is the largest single cost of a long prompt read.

This ports both to sm_75, opt-in on top of `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` with `STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75=1`:

- `cp.async` → plain 16-byte copies (the barriers around them stay), `prefetch.global.L2` kept;
- `mma` m16n8k32 / m16n8k16 with s8 operands → four / two `m8n8k16` (rows g / g + 8 by k 0-15 / 16-31). The int32 sums are exact in any order, so `d` is what the sm_80 instruction gives; MAGIC is passed as the C operand of each pair's first `m8n8k16`;
- two activation stages below sm_80 (64 KB of shared memory per SM), `smem_bytes` / the launch / the occupancy query take the device's depth (`host_astages()`);
- `native_kernel` takes **Q2_0 gate/up** (64-value blocks: a block per stage, as the down rows already read theirs), so the canonical Q2_0 pack (Q2_0 / Q2_0 in every layer) runs fused. `gu_covered()` lists Q2_0 on CUDA;
- on Turing only that pair is set up (`DevInfo::t75`: `native_supported` answers false for the others, which keep MMQ);
- Turing, Q2_0 only (`T75_DEV`): a stage's two 32-value halves share the block's `d`, so a row's dot is `d (dx_0 dot_0 + dx_1 dot_1)` - 11 % fewer instructions (the kernel is bound by its FP32 epilogue on Turing, not the tensor pipe). sm_80+ keeps its code and bits.

`prefill_fused_iq_test` gets the Q2_0 / Q2_0 pair, and skips the pairs a Turing card does not set up instead of failing.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W; `v0.1.43`. Canonical Q2_0 pack, `--prefill auto:16384`, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2`.

## Kernels (`prefill_fused_iq_test --only="Q2_0 / Q2_0"`, one layer, 512 experts, top 10)

| tokens | MMQ path | fused | |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2,048 | 12.99 ms | 6.61 ms | 1.96× |
| 8,192 | 30.75 ms | 21.18 ms\* | 1.45× |
| 16,384 | 55.02 ms | 37.15 ms | 1.48× |

\* before the Q2_0 epilogue change. Fused vs MMQ rel RMS 1.6e-5 - 2.7e-5; both 1.09e-2 against the FP32 reference (the int8 activations' own error). `prefill_fused_moe_test` (Strata pack) passes too: 5.29 ms fused vs MMQ 3.67×, rel RMS 6.7e-5.

## Engine

98K prompt (16K chunks, two runs each, deterministic run to run): 58.3 → 53.3 s (+9.4 %). 4K: 3.63 → 3.54 s.

Accuracy in the engine: layer 0 of a 32K prompt (identical input on both paths), every one of the 163,840 (token, expert) rows of the expert output against MMQ's: median rel 1.6e-7, p99.9 2.6e-3, max 7.6e-3 (the rows where H's int8 rounding falls the other way); against the FP16 expert path (`STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0`) MMQ and fused have the same error (median 1.08e-2).

Teacher-forced, as in #655 / #2071 (the first P tokens through the prompt path, the next 2,048 through the verify windows, `STRATA_LOGPOS_TOPK=20`):

| P | KL (MMQ ‖ fused) | KL (FP16 ‖ MMQ) | perplexity FP16 / MMQ / fused |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 16,384 | 0.0101 | 0.0090 | 7.308 / 7.255 / 7.501 |
| 32,768 | 0.0226 | 0.0110 | 4.561 / 4.557 / 4.354 |
| 65,536 | 0.0186 | 0.0262 | 4.110 / 4.096 / 4.122 |

The perplexity moves either way (+3.4 %, −4.5 %, +0.6 %) - trajectory noise: the QSA selection is discrete, so any change of the prompt path's rounding gives KLs of this size (enabling only one layer's fused experts already moves the first logit by KL ~1e-3, as much as the FP16 path in every layer). The verify phase's time over the same 2,048 tokens: MMQ 42.36 s, fused 42.28 s.

The server here will run with `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 STRATA_PF_FUSED_SM75=1`.

pulls.title: [Engine] serve: honour llama-server's thinking_budget_tokens (a llama.cpp client's thinking budget was silently ignored)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A client written for llama-server sends its thinking budget as `thinking_budget_tokens`. Strata's server reads only `reasoning_budget_tokens`, so it ignores that field: **the request runs with no thinking budget at all**, and nothing is logged or reported. llama-server reads both names (`tools/server/server-common.cpp` takes `reasoning_budget_tokens` and falls back to `thinking_budget_tokens`), and its Anthropic adapter (`server-chat.cpp`) writes the second one, so any client built against llama-server can hit this.

How it showed up: the pi coding agent's llama.cpp provider ([pi-llama-cpp](https://github.com/gsanhueza/pi-llama-cpp)) sends `thinking_budget_tokens` (8,192 at pi's default level). During an automatic compaction (a 109,013-token history, answer capped at 26,214 tokens) the model thought until the cap and never wrote the summary. pi sent the same request again five times, about 250 s each (21 minutes), without compacting.

- **Before:** `thinking_budget_tokens: N` is ignored, and the thinking runs until `max_tokens` or the end of the context.
- **After:** it is the same budget as `reasoning_budget_tokens: N`. The thinking is wrapped up at N tokens, and `reasoning_budget_tokens` wins when both are set.

## Related discussion

Fixes #2141 (re-tested on 0.2.0-beta there: still present).

## Approach

`Service.reasoning_budget()` reads `reasoning_budget_tokens` and, when it is absent, `thinking_budget_tokens`, as llama-server does. The validation is unchanged (a whole number; 0 means no budget), and the config default still applies when neither field is given.

- `serve/server.py`: 4 lines in `reasoning_budget()`.
- `serve/test_server.py`: `test_llama_cpp_thinking_budget_tokens_is_the_same_budget`. The alias wraps the thinking up at the same point, and `reasoning_budget_tokens` takes precedence when both are set.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the alias is named in the thinking-budget paragraph.

The engine is not touched; there are no compatibility effects for clients that send `reasoning_budget_tokens`.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Rebased onto 0.2.0-beta (`f57c0adc`) as `b394c6fc`. `python -m pytest -q serve/test_server.py`: 339 passed, 3 skipped, 444 subtests passed (Windows 11, Python 3.14).
- The new test against 0.2.0-beta's own `serve/server.py` (this change taken out) fails: the thought comes back whole instead of cut at 20 tokens. With the change it passes.
- In daily use on my box (2x CMP 50HX, Ubuntu 24.04.4) since 2026-10-12, in my fork, which is now on 0.2.0-beta (`342185bd`) with this change.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** this exact branch against a GPU engine (the change is in request parsing; the test uses the server's stub engine).

## Limits

Only the name is added; the budget's behaviour is the existing one.

pulls.title: serve: the prompt path's loan has room for a short request that keeps 0.1.39's ring (#2090)
pulls.author: ischencheng
pulls.body:
Fixes #2090.

With `--prefill auto` the serve scan sizes the prompt path's loan for the chunk it picked, with the byte-budget ring. A request whose chunk is at most 0.1.39's pick (`small` in `set_ring_budget(..., small)`) reads with 0.1.39's ring instead. On a pack with bigger blobs than Q2_0's that ring has more slots (384 against 227 on IQ3_XXS), so the short request can need more of the cache than the loan holds. `lend` clamps it to the loan's first slot, `relayout` runs out of room, and the engine exits with "lending the prompt path its slots failed". That is why it only showed with `--prefill auto` and only at some cache sizes in the report.

The loan now has room for both: `max(part_slots(chunk), part_slots(small))`. The same helper is used where the loan is sized again (the step-down after a failed init, and `relend` under `--vram-elastic`). `lend` is unchanged, so each request still lends only the slots its own chunk needs. A request that fitted before lends the same slots. Where 0.1.39's chunk needs no more slots than the chosen one, the loan does not change at all.

Measured on Modal, one L4 24 GB (sm_89, Linux), the official IQ3_XXS pack, upstream main 7695859, `--prefill auto --max-context 131072 --kv int8`. I set `--expert-cache N` by hand to land on the cache sizes where this happens. Each start gets four fresh prompts whose first part rounds up to a 2048 / 3072 / 4096 / 6144-token chunk.

| `--expert-cache` | auto chunk, ring | the short chunk needs | loan main -> this PR | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 905, 910, 915 | 2816, 227 slots | 2048: 1059-1060 slots | 1023-1024 -> 1059-1060 | engine exits, 3 of 3 starts | 0 of 3 |
| 1088, 1094, 1100 | 3840, 227 | 3072: 1288-1289 | 1252-1254 -> 1288-1289 | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| 1284, 1290 | 4864, 227 | 4096: 1517 | 1481-1482 -> 1517 | 2 of 2 | 0 of 2 |
| 900, 1130, 1296 | 2816 / 4096 / 5120, 227 | fits | 1024 / 1309 / 1539, unchanged | 0 | 0 |

Two more runs of some of the failing rows gave the same result (main 5 of 5 starts, this PR 0 of 5). Main's error is the one in the report, with 13 GB of VRAM free:

```
lending the prompt path its slots failed: prefill: device buffers for a chunk of 2048 tokens do not fit (13033 of 22563 MiB free at the failure; 1719 MiB taken, the failing buffer wanted 20 MiB)
```

Replies (temperature 0, thinking off, 64 tokens) to the 2048 / 3072 / 4096 prompts are the same on main and this PR at every cache size where main answered them. The 6144 one changes between starts of main itself on this setup (3 different replies in 4 starts at `--expert-cache 900`); this PR's reply was one of main's.

`src/program/generate.cpp` also builds for HIP: compiled it in a ROCm 7.0 build for gfx1201 (that one file, no GPU), with the same 98 warnings as main.

Not tested: Windows, the reporter's IQ3_S pack and 4070 Ti, a HIP run, layer splits, `--vram-elastic`. `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` has the same scan and is not changed here. The resident RAM mode sizes its RAM copy's lend region from `plan_lend`, which still counts the chosen chunk only, so there a short request's extra slots are read from the model file during that prompt.

pulls.title: Add disk-backed conversation cache parking (--conversation-cache-storage disk)
pulls.author: dsovsyannikov
pulls.body:
## Relation to parallel work

Two parallel efforts in the queue address disk parking; keeping this PR open as the minimal third option, with the differences called out:

- **#1937** (older, Oct 11): disk as an **overflow tier under the RAM cache** — an evicted RAM entry is written to disk instead of dropped, via the same session-file primitives this PR uses. Hot conversations stay in RAM; a background writer keeps switches from waiting on the disk; `--conversation-disk-persist` survives restarts. Best when a RAM budget exists and only its overflow is the problem.
- **#2098**: a **page-granular disk tier** with version-tagged snapshot directories, a shared blob, GC and 467 checks, field-tested at 62–68 GB. The fullest design if cross-version persistence and page sharing matter.
- **This PR**: disk as **the parking backend itself** (`ram|disk`), not a spill target — a parked conversation holds zero resident RAM (measured −26 MiB vs +308 MiB held). Targets hosts where even the RAM parking budget does not fit beside the expert arena (admission there skips every conversation), or wherever you simply do not want parked state in RAM. Single +964/−15 commit; a parked conversation's bytes are identical to what `POST /slots/0?action=save` already writes.

Related: #2082 (admission fail-safety — the Windows commit-limit cases this PR's floor handling also dances around) and #2077 (`--prompt-cache-file`, a complementary restart-persistence angle).

## Motivation

The conversation cache parks a switched-out conversation as a snapshot in host RAM, which keeps alternating chats (an agent controller plus subagents, for example) from re-reading their history. But on a machine whose RAM cannot hold the resident expert arena beside a parking budget, the admission check (`available_host_bytes()` vs the snapshot estimate + `--conversation-cache-min-free-mib`) skips every conversation, so the feature is effectively unavailable there. This PR adds an opt-in disk backend: parked snapshots live on SSD and cost no resident RAM.

## What it adds

- Engine flags: `--conversation-cache-storage ram|disk` (default `ram` — current behaviour unchanged) and `--conversation-cache-dir DIR`. In disk mode `--conversation-cache-mib` is the disk budget.
- `ConversationDiskCache` reuses the session-file snapshot format with its validation and atomic publish (temp file + rename + flush), so a parked conversation is the same bytes a `SAVE` writes. LRU eviction deletes the oldest file when the budget is exceeded.
- The RAM side keeps only a small index (conversation ids/images): after `park()` the snapshot costs no resident memory.
- `/metrics` `conversation_cache` gains a `storage` field; the Monitor tab reflects the mode.
- Known limits: disk mode refuses `--layer-split` (the session format has no stage images); retained-K/V reuse stays a ram-mode feature; restore speed depends on the page cache (42.5 ms hot in the measurement below, closer to the session-restore second when cold); a snapshot is tied to the engine version that wrote it (no tag gating — see #2098 for that machinery).

## Tests

- New `conversation_disk_test` (55 checks): park/restore byte-exact, LRU eviction, budget accounting, preflight refusal.
- `tools/parking_test.py` and `tools/conversation_cache_parity.py` accept `--storage disk`; new `tools/conversation_cache_disk_measure.py` reproduces the numbers below.
- Parity gate A/B/A: **byte-exact main-model state** in both backends.
- Built and run on Windows 11 (MSVC 19.44 + CUDA 13.3, RTX 5090 Laptop) and WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (CUDA 13.3), engine 0.1.43, base 7695859a.

## Measured (RTX 5090 Laptop 24 GB, IQ3_XXS pack, 14.4K-token conversation, 435 MiB snapshot)

| metric | ram | disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| park | 105 ms | 411 ms (456 MB NVMe write) |
| restore | 32 ms | 42.5 ms (page-cache hot) |
| Δ engine RSS on park | **+308 MiB held** | **−26 MiB** |
| reused tokens on resume | 14087 / 14188 | 14087 / 14188 |
| decode after restore | 30.3 tok/s | 27.7 tok/s |

Restoring the same conversation from disk after a full engine restart took 152 ms and the continuation was served from the restored state.

On the RAM-tight host this targets (resident arena leaves ~1.4–2.7 GiB free), ram mode skips parking entirely while disk mode keeps alternating conversations at ~2–4 s per switch instead of a full re-read of the history.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 5090 D v2 (24 GB), IQ3_S (abliterated), engine 0.1.43
pulls.author: sobhechristl361

First community report on an **RTX 5090 D v2** (the 24 GB China-market variant).

- **Hardware:** RTX 5090 D v2 24 GB (power limit 546.25 W, PCIe Gen4 x16, engine probe 28.4 GB/s host-to-device), Ryzen 5 5600X (no AVX-512, AVX-2 expert kernels), 128 GB DDR4-3600, KINGSTON SNV3S2000G 2 TB NVMe, Windows 11 26200, driver 616.56, CUDA 13, Strata / engine 0.1.43 (official Windows release).
- **Model:** ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO **abliterated** IQ3_S, context 262144, KV int8, expert cache auto = 5104 slots / 9.71 GiB VRAM (profile-prefilled, no eviction), MTP --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5, prefill auto 8192, vision on.
- **Results (medians):** chat decode 70.3 tok/s (60.7-91.1, n=9); agent-session decode 102.2 tok/s (76.6-152.8); fresh-prompt 2327 / 4572 / 4679 tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K; TTFT 0.49 s chat, 6.89 s at 32K; agent cache hit 68.7 %.
- **Correctness:** needle_bench at 32k, depths 10/50/90: 3/3 found.
- **Limitations:** the server was live-serving the agent session that launched this benchmark (one request at a time): two short-chat TTFT outliers (19.4 s, 23.9 s) are queueing behind live requests, not engine speed; the decode and prompt throughputs are the engine's own timings and are unaffected. No VRAM/RAM peak sampling, no concurrency or sustained-thermal runs.

Measured with the built-in suite (`tools/strata_bench.py --long --url`) against the already-running server. Files: README.md + results.json + needles.json + engine-log-excerpt.txt under `bench/results/2026-10-12-community-rtx-5090-d-v2-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-s/`.

pulls.title: sycl: run on an integrated Arc (Arc 140T, xe): free memory from /proc/meminfo, no prompt-slot borrowing, a native launcher
pulls.author: andersson82
pulls.body:
## Title
sycl: run on an integrated Arc (Arc 140T, xe): free memory from /proc/meminfo, no prompt-slot borrowing, a native launcher

Issue: none; the "integrated Arc GPUs ... not tested" line of docs/INTEL_ARC.md (and #515 for the B390 on Windows, not covered here)

## Summary
The SYCL port did not start on an integrated Arc: the Arc 140T has no free-memory query, so the expert cache was sized
from 0. With the three changes below it runs the Coder IQ1_M on the 140T with 62 GiB of RAM, through the normal server,
at 12.0-17.4 tok/s decode, and reads a 72,648-token prompt at 156.5 tok/s.

## What changed
- `sycl/include/dpct/device.hpp`, `get_memory_info`: on a device with `host_unified_memory` and no `ext_intel_free_memory`,
  free memory is `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` (Linux only); `STRATA_SYCL_FREE_MIB` sets it by hand (the `xe` driver
  keeps freed GPU memory in a pool that `MemAvailable` does not count until a reboot). Other devices: the code path is the
  one before.
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: no prompt-slot borrowing on a `host_unified_memory` device. With borrowing, the answer
  after a borrowing prompt was token 0 (every expert activation NaN from the second prompt chunk; measured on the 0.1.40
  port, any context). Discrete cards keep the old rule.
- `sycl/serve/strata-sycl-native.sh` (new): the config's `exe` for the engine on the PC's own oneAPI, no Docker. Sets the
  same port defaults as `strata-sycl.sh` (each overridable from the config's `"env"`) plus `STRATA_NO_MULTI_GR=1`
  (15.1 vs 18.3 tok/s on the 140T with the multi-token GR kernels, 0.1.40, same output) and an OOM score of 1000 for the
  engine.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a new section "Integrated Arc: the Arc 140T" (build, what is different from a card, a config to run it by
  hand, the numbers). `docs/INTEL_ARC.md`: the 140T is no longer in "not tested".

Left alone: discrete cards (every change is behind `host_unified_memory`, which a card with its own VRAM should not
report; I have no discrete card to check), CUDA and HIP (no file of theirs is touched), setup (its own PR, which builds
on this one).

## Measurements
Arc 140T (8086:7d51, Xe-LPG+), Core Ultra 9 285H, 62 GiB RAM, Fedora 44 (kernel 7.2.9, `xe`), oneAPI 2026.0, JIT build.
Coder IQ1_M, `--spec 4 --mtp`, `--max-context 98304`, `--kv int8`, `--stream-experts`, through
`sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, greedy, thinking off. Engine 0.1.43 with these changes and #2110 (without #2110 every request
stalls on the 140T).

| | |
|---|---|
| decode, 100-token answers, 10 requests | 12.0-17.4 tok/s, all 12,288 experts cached (first start after a boot) |
| the same, later start (the `xe` pool) | 11.5-17.2 tok/s, 10,496 cached, 1,792 mirrored |
| a 72,648-token prompt | read at 156.5 tok/s, the fact on its first line recalled |
| first start / later starts | 79 s / 7 s with `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=1` (0.1.40) |

## Extra Notes
How I checked:
- Built this branch alone on `origin/main` with `sycl/tools/build.sh` on the PC's oneAPI: 0 errors. Rebased onto
  current main (296b59d2) for this update; the engine files are unchanged (only a `docs/INTEL.md` hunk's context moved).
- `bash -n` on the launcher.

Not tested:
- Any discrete Intel card (I have none); the code paths there should be unchanged.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] strata_bench: read CUDA UMD version, storage and GPU power/PCIe detail
pulls.author: JoShMiQueL
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The community report came out with fields missing or wrong:

- Current drivers print `CUDA UMD Version: 13.4` in `nvidia-smi`, not `CUDA Version:`, so `machine.cuda` came out null and the README said `CUDA: not read`.
- Where it was read, it was the newest CUDA the **driver** supports, labelled as if the engine had been built with it (raised by autemetry-james in this thread).
- Storage always said `not measured`, the GPU line carried no power limit, PCIe link, state or temperature, and Windows 11 reported as `Windows 10` because `platform.release()` is still `10`.

After the change a report reads `CUDA (driver supports up to): 13.4; engine built for CUDA 13.0`, names the storage device, adds a `GPU detail (after the run, near idle)` line with power limit and draw, PCIe gen x width, pstate and temperature, and says `Windows 11`. The measurement path (HTTP suite, statistics, `results.json`) is untouched: this changes what a report prints, not what it measures.

## Related discussion

none

## Approach

- Accept both header forms from nvidia-smi and label the value as the driver's ceiling.
- Read `machine.engine_build` from the engine's `BUILD.json` next to the exe, so driver ceiling and build toolkit are both in the report; no engine change.
- Take the extra nvidia-smi fields from the GPUs the server uses (the selection of #1985), and label the line `(after the run, near idle)`: `collect_machine` runs a second time after the suite, so they are end-of-run, near-idle figures (qiuzan2001).
- Storage: `Get-PhysicalDisk` on Windows, `system_profiler` on macOS, `lsblk -e 7` on Linux (`-e 7` drops the snap loop devices that flooded the line on a stock Ubuntu, qiuzan2001).

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python tools/test_strata_bench.py` on `8f7fd37d`, rebased on `main` `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta): 20 tests, OK. The new checks cover the rendered report line with both CUDA numbers, the storage line, the GPU detail line, both nvidia-smi CUDA header forms, and the power/PCIe/pstate/temperature parsing.
- `python tools/test_windows_amd_gpu.py` and `python tools/test_bench_host.py`, same revision: 5 and 5 tests, OK.
- Live read on this PC (RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, driver 616.92, Windows 11 build 26200): `gpu_info_local()` returned `power_limit_w=165.00`, `power_draw_w=20.25`, `pcie=gen4 x8`, `pstate=P3`, `temp_c=45`, `cuda=13.4`; `storage_info()` returned `Samsung SSD 990 EVO Plus 2TB SSD/NVMe`; the OS label resolves to `Windows 11`.
- `ruff check tools/strata_bench.py tools/test_strata_bench.py`: the same 4 findings as on `main`, no new ones (3 of them are the `port` NameError below).
- A report generated with this change, all fields filled, is in #2112.

**Failed:**

- `python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-coder-iq1_m.json --port 9 --runs 1 --quiet` on `main` `e88ee39d` ends in `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` (`tools/strata_bench.py:1040`), from #2330. It is a separate problem and is not touched here; it blocks a default run that starts its own server on 0.2.0-beta.

**Not run:**

- The macOS (`system_profiler`) and Linux (`lsblk -e 7`) storage branches: no such machine here, they are read, not executed.
- A full bench suite on 0.2.0-beta: blocked by the `port` NameError above. The tests drive the `--url` path against a fake server, not a real engine.

## Limits

- The GPU detail line is sampled after the suite, near idle; it is not a load figure and the label says so.
- `engine_build` needs a `BUILD.json` next to the exe; without one the field is left out rather than guessed.
- This changes what a report prints. The measurements in #2112 were taken on engine 0.1.43 and are not re-measured here.

pulls.title: --batch: request priority (a free slot and the next prompt read go to the highest priority waiting)
pulls.author: brocktice
pulls.body:
## Why

We serve Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S on two RTX PRO 6000 (one engine per card, `parallel: 4`, `--batch-mtp`, all experts in VRAM) to several clients at once: an interactive coding agent, a log-alert summarizer that must answer within seconds, and an evaluation battery that sends thousands of requests a day.

With first-come-first-served waiting, a burst of battery requests filled all 8 slots and the alert summarizer queued behind it, so its calls timed out and our monitoring paged us. More slots don't fix it, because a burst can always fill them. Under SGLang we used `--enable-priority-scheduling` (a per-request `priority`), and we lost that when we moved to Strata.

We've been running the same idea in a router in front of Strata for several days. The alert summarizer's slowest call over a full day was 4.6 s (1,210 calls) while the battery kept 8 requests in flight. This PR moves it into the server, where it can see the slots and the #656 give-way path.

## What it does

`"priority"` in the request body is an integer, higher goes first. It's the same field SGLang and vLLM read, so gateways like LiteLLM already pass it through. If the field is absent or not an integer, it counts as 0.

With `--batch`:

- **A free slot** goes to the highest-priority request waiting for one.
- **The control lines** (the next prompt read or admission) go to the highest-priority request waiting for them.
- **#656 give-way:** a long read gives way to a waiting request of a *higher* priority, whatever its length. It never gives way to a much shorter request of a *lower* priority. Within one priority level, the old rule applies (a prompt under half as long). `YIELDS_MAX` still caps how often a read gives way.
- **No preemption:** a running request is never paused.

With every request at 0, all checks reduce to the existing code paths.

**Deadlock note:** requests waiting for a *slot* never hold back the *control lines*. A read that gave way holds a slot and needs the lines to continue and free that slot, whatever its priority; otherwise long/long/short with mixed priorities would deadlock (the ENGINE_REVIEW finding 1 shape). A request that gave way and is letting others go first (`after_epoch`) also doesn't outrank anyone until its epoch passes.

**Not covered:** the single-request path without `--batch` (the server's `fifo` lock). That lock is shared with the vision encoder and settings changes, so changing it seemed like a separate discussion.

## Tests

New tests in `serve/test_parallel.py`, using the existing fake engine:

- `test_a_free_slot_goes_to_the_highest_priority_waiting`: both slots busy, a priority-0 request waits, then a priority-5 one arrives; the first free slot goes to the priority-5 request.
- `test_a_long_read_gives_way_to_a_higher_priority`: two prompts of the same length; the later, higher-priority one makes the first read give way.
- `test_no_way_given_to_a_lower_priority`: a short priority-0 prompt does not make a priority-5 read give way.
- `Priority.test_request_priority` and `test_outranked_skips_a_request_letting_others_go_first` (unit).

All three service tests fail on `main` (checked three times each) and pass with the change. `serve/test_parallel.py` passed 5 runs in a row. The full `serve/` suite passes except `test_responses.NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler`, which also fails on unmodified `main` in 2 of 3 runs here (a sampler thread from an earlier test is still shutting down).

**Real engine:** v0.1.43 on one RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `parallel: 4`, `--batch-mtp`. The same request mix was run with and without the field:

| Scenario | Without priority | With priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 slots decoding 700-token stories, 8 more waiting (priority 10); a short request arrives 2 s in. First token: | 45.3 s / 39.1 s (10 and 8 of the waiting requests went first) | 12.2 s / 12.0 s (the first slot to free, nobody ahead of it) |
| A ~84K-token read under way (priority 10); an equally long request arrives 3 s in. Its first token: | 29.5 s (waited for the whole first read) | 16.0 s (the first read gave way at 16,384 tokens, parked in slot 2, and finished at 33.3 s) |

No errors; every request finished.

`docs/BATCHING.md` has a short paragraph describing the behavior.

Happy to change the shape: a config default per API key, `/metrics` waiting counts per priority, or the non-batch path.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: sycl verify: complete STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER for the commit path
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
Completes the `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER` path for the verify window's commit.

## The gap

The eager path is already half-built for the window: `capture()` returns early under `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER`, `run()` replays the body through `record_window`, the stage table branches on the flag, and the stepped-mode check excludes it. `prepare_chain()` in `mtp.cpp` documents the state of the rest out loud:

```
err = "mtp: chains need command graphs (STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1 has none)";
```

The commit is the missing half: `capture_commit()` records a command graph and `commit()` launches it, so a backend with no graph extension cannot get through a window's commit at all. That is not a hypothetical - the OpenCL UR adapter has no command-graph backend, which is why `run()` already carries the window replay.

## The change

`capture_commit`'s body is now `Verifier::record_commit`, and the two callers are:

```cpp
capture_commit()   records it between begin_recording/end_recording and finalizes commit_exec_,
                   or answers "captured" under eager
commit()           STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER ? record_commit() : ext_oneapi_graph(*commit_exec_)
```

The body refreshes everything it reads - the mapped `commit_` upload first, then the layer snapshots - so a replay sees the same inputs the graph would have, and it is safe to run once per window. `h_commit_` is written by `commit()` before the launch, exactly as before.

## What it leaves alone

The graph path records the same kernels in the same order and finalizes them the same way - only the body moved into a function the eager path can call. `record_window`, the MTP drafter's replays and the one-token self-commit are untouched.

## On "is this a bug?"

On `main` today the same state is refused, not broken: `run()` calls `if (!capture(T, err) || !capture_commit(err)) return false;`, so `capture_commit()` fails at `begin_recording()` and `run()` bails with "verify: begin commit capture failed". I hit the null-`commit_exec_` case only after a Windows/OpenCL port of mine had started answering "captured" without building a graph. So this is a **completion, not a fix for a crash reachable on main** - and I would rather say that plainly than dress it up as a crash report.

## Measurements

Arc Pro B70, 32 GB, Windows 11 24H2, engine 0.1.43, coder-IQ1_M, 2047-token prompt, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--max-context 131072`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--stream-experts --vram-reserve-mib 2048`, greedy, with `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1 STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1 STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1 STRATA_MIRROR_MIB=4096`:

```
with the commit replay:  exit 0, prefill 2047 tokens in 25252 ms -> 81.1 tok/s
                         decode 128 tokens in 1921 ms -> 66.6 tok/s
                         speculation 3.91 tokens per round (33 rounds of 6, 96/96 drafts)
through serve:          220 tokens in 3679 ms -> 59.8 tok/s, 166/168 drafts accepted
```

## What I could not verify

- **Built and run on SYCL/Windows only.** I have no CUDA, HIP or Linux toolchain here, so I cannot show the graph path is untouched on those, although the change sits inside a branch that is false unless `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER` is set.
- **This tree's SYCL port does not compile on Windows as it stands.** A clean checkout of the release I based this on fails twice on Windows (`pinned.dp.cpp` uses the CUDA runtime API under an unguarded `#ifdef _WIN32`; `verify_kernels.dp.cpp` hits the `OUT` macro). My numbers come from a tree that also carries those repairs. If you want a patch that builds standalone here, that is a separate change.

## Suggested review order

1. `capture_commit()` - is answering "captured" under eager the right contract, and does it belong here rather than in the caller?
2. `record_commit()` - the body refresh is unchanged, but it is now called per-window instead of once at capture.
3. `commit()` - the `else` I added around the existing graph launch.

pulls.title: feat(mtp): support native Q4_0 and Q8_0 experts
pulls.author: xszwow
pulls.body:
## Summary

Teach the Flash-Next MTP drafter to load routed experts in native GGUF Q4_0 or Q8_0 row layout, in addition to the existing Q2_0 S2 runtime.

This is opt-in through a runtime generated by `tools/mtp_rt.py`. Existing runtimes without `experts.txt` keep the legacy Q2_0 S2 path and default behavior.

## What changed

- `tools/mtp_rt.py` now:
  - detects the routed experts' GGML type;
  - preserves Q4_0 and Q8_0 rows in native `[gate | up | down]` order;
  - keeps Q2_0 in the existing S2 relayout;
  - writes `experts.txt` with a version, layout, types, and bytes per expert.
- `MtpDrafter` reads and validates that metadata, checks the exact `experts.bin` size, allocates the correct expert blob size, and dispatches native runtimes through the existing grouped native-expert kernels.
- `tools/mtp_fetch.py` accepts opt-in `STRATA_MTP_REPO` and `STRATA_MTP_REVISION` values for a compatible fine-tune's MTP tensors. With neither variable set, the original Qwen URL, pinned revision, and SHA-256 verification path are unchanged.
- Shared slot drafters inherit the selected layout and types from their owner.

The model geometry, server defaults, CLI defaults, legacy Q2_0 runtime, and non-MTP paths are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased cleanly onto `main` at `7695859a`; the four touched files had no intervening upstream changes since the tested 0.1.42 base (`61b3fb5d`).

Static/tool checks:

- `python -m py_compile tools/mtp_fetch.py tools/mtp_rt.py`
- `python -m unittest tools.test_mtp_fetch`: 8 passed
- `git diff --check`

Conversion check:

- Converted a 1,596,806,016-byte Q4_0 MTP GGUF with this branch.
- The generated `experts.bin` (1,415,577,600 bytes), `experts.txt`, `dense.bin`, and `dense.txt` were byte-identical to the runtime used for the HIP tests.
- `experts.bin` SHA-256: `cb101ab35f946698ef09dddc942c41620ac03de40483a661ea07052b59ff16c5`
- `experts.txt` SHA-256: `c6fed393954caefd784ba689f7cc23f045f82051631406333c3b37c34e4ba44f`
- A Q8_0 runtime was also converted successfully; it was not used for the end-to-end run below.

End-to-end run:

- Windows 11, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), 128 GB unified RAM, Windows HIP Release build from the tested 0.1.42 source.
- The engine reported `native types 2/2`, loaded 1,350 MiB of Q4_0 MTP experts, reached `session is up`, and served repeated text, long-context, tool-use, and vision-integrated requests.
- The deployed Q4_0 runtime has been used with `--spec 6..8`, an 8,192-token MTP window, INT8 KV, and up to 262,144 total context capacity.

## Compatibility and limits

- A missing `experts.txt` means the legacy Q2_0 S2 layout, preserving old runtimes.
- Metadata rejects unknown versions, keys, layouts, types, shapes, blob sizes, and truncated/oversized expert files before inference.
- Q4_0 was built and run on Windows HIP. Q8_0 conversion was checked, but Q8_0 inference was not run.
- CUDA build/runtime validation is still outstanding, so this is a draft under the repository's backend-validation rule.
- SYCL has its separate engine path and was not changed.

Related performance/configuration evidence is kept separate from this code change in #1947.

pulls.title: docs/TEST_REQUESTS: an Arc on Windows with and without the Level Zero platform (#1549)
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
One row for `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md`: an Arc on Windows with and without the Level Zero platform.

## Why

The OpenCL adapter is the one place where the SYCL Graph extension, oneMKL SYCL BLAS and the free-VRAM query are **all** missing at the same time. I found that on an Arc Pro B70 where the Level Zero loader does not load, so the UR adapters fall back to OpenCL. What I cannot tell from one machine is whether that fallback is a rare driver state or a common one - i.e. whether the OpenCL path is worth maintaining and testing at all.

One report from a Windows Arc that lists `level_zero:gpu`, and one from a Windows Arc that does not, answers it. If Level Zero is normally present, the OpenCL path is an emergency fallback and I would rather know that than keep polishing it. If it is sometimes absent, that is worth a test in CI or at least a documented known-state.

## What I measured, so the row is grounded

Arc Pro B70, 32 GB, Windows 11 24H2, driver 32.0.101.8976, where the Level Zero loader does not load (a V2 loader against a V1-only ICD) and the UR adapters fall back to OpenCL. On that backend:

- oneMKL SYCL BLAS reports that it is not usable on this backend, so the prompt path's expert GEMM fails with a status-999 error unless something else provides it
- `begin_recording` fails with `opencl backend is not supported by SYCL Graph extension`
- `ext_intel_free_memory` answers "not supported", so `get_memory_info` returns 0 - which sizes the expert cache to *nothing*, not to a wrong number

That last one is the reason I am asking rather than just fixing it: an engine that computes 0 free VRAM and then refuses with a message about experts being "neither in VRAM nor mirrored" is pointing at the mirror, not at the figure that answered zero.

## What I did not test

No Level Zero, no CUDA, no HIP, no second Windows Arc, and no Linux. Everything above is one card, one driver, one backend. I am not claiming this state is common - that is the question.

## Note on scope

This touches only `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` and adds one row. It is deliberately the smallest possible thing so it can be reviewed or rejected in seconds, independently of any code change I might bring later for the OpenCL path.

pulls.title: disk park: the profile tag carries the engine version, and the blob carries the tag
pulls.author: leocoic
pulls.body:
## Title
disk park: the profile tag carries the engine version, and the blob carries the tag

## Summary
The parked tier had no idea which engine wrote it. `DiskParkProfile::tag()` hashed model / kv format / context / rope only, so 62 GB of pages stored by 0.1.41 are read back verbatim by 0.1.43 — after any version that changes numerics, that is recurrent state computed by the previous routing. The blob layer was worse: `checkpoints.bin` carries no tag at all and is one file shared by every tag directory.

Both layers now carry the version. This branch also lands the disk park tier itself (a disk tier under the parked-conversation cache) and the fixes found while building it.

## What changed
- `disk_park_digest.hpp/.cpp/_test.cpp` — `describe()` now includes `STRATA_VERSION` (and `STRATA_DISK_PARK_KEY` for a manual key); the field table goes `v1` → `v2`, so a version bump opens a new `tag-XXXXXXXX/` directory instead of reusing the old one.
- `disk_park_blob.hpp/.cpp/_test.cpp` — magic `SKB1` → `SKB2`. The profile tag is written into the file header at `@8` (those 4 bytes were reserved padding, so the 16-byte header and 32-byte entry header keep their exact layout — no record moves) and into every entry header at `@+4` (which used to hold a `version` field nothing read back). On a tag mismatch the layer is neither read nor appended to, the old file is moved with a single rename to `checkpoints.bin.tag-XXXXXXXX.stale` (bytes untouched, not deleted) and a fresh file for the current tag is opened; `STRATA_BLOB_STALE=off` disables it instead. The scan skips entries whose tag does not match, which is safe because each entry carries its own length.
- `p13_blob_compact.hpp` + `tools/park-gc.cpp` — `p13_session_dirs` used to sweep `root/tag-*/*/`, mixing live keys from every tag into one blob. `park-gc` now reads the tag from the blob header (`--tag` overrides) and compacts only that tag's session dirs.
- `generate.cpp` — both the snapshot layer and the blob layer get `disk_park.profile().tag()`.
- `conversation_cache.hpp` + serve — an evicted entry is handed to the caller instead of dropped; a failed checkpoint restore no longer exits the engine; after non-finite logits a request does not read K/V back from the disk tier.
- `tools/p13-park-sweep.sh` — the default park root comes from `$HOME` instead of one machine's home path; systemd units should set `Environment=STRATA_PARK_STREAM=…` explicitly.

Version-gate commit alone: 9 files, +175 / −32. Whole branch: 11 commits, 35 files.

## Extra Notes
Tested on the 3090 with `strata 0.1.43`: snapshot dir renamed `tag-A812110E` → `tag-AA00AEC7` — the tag algorithm changed, the numerics did not, so 68 GB was not re-stored. After restart the first requests show `hit_rate 0.90–0.92` with `prompt_read` of only 686–1326. The old `checkpoints.bin` was archived rather than relabelled (its records were written by 0.1.41 before 13:27 and by 0.1.43 after, so relabelling it would be a lie); the new file has header `SKB2` with tag `AA00AEC7`.

Tests: blob 68 (new version-gate section) / digest 28 / spool 64 / logs 98 / session 136 / bridge 54 / image 19 = **467 checks, 0 failures**.

For anyone with existing caches: the new engine will not read an old `tag-XXXXXXXX/` directory. If the numerics did not change across the upgrade, rename the directory to the new tag (no re-store). If they did, let it cold start — that is exactly what this gate is for. `checkpoints.bin` in the old `SKB1` format is unreadable by design: archive it or delete it.

pulls.title: sm_75: the prompt path's top-k with one full read of the scores (identical ids)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
**Builds on #2072** (it sits next to that PR's split top-k in `qsa_select.cu`); the first commit here is #2072's, the second is this one.

Past ~115K cells the prompt path's top-k is DRAM traffic on Turing: `block_topk_wide_kernel` reads a query's scores six times (four radix passes, a count, the emit), 400 KB a query at 400K, 256 queries a call.

`block_topk_sample_kernel` reads them once:
1. a bound LB: the KS-th largest key among every 32nd block (KS = 2 × the selection's blocks / 32 + 16);
2. one read of all blocks, keeping those with key ≥ LB in shared memory;
3. when those hold at least `width` cells, the width-th largest cell key (block_topk_kernel's threshold) is ≥ LB, so every block at or above the threshold is a candidate: the threshold, `above` and the tie budget computed over the candidates with block_topk_kernel's rule are the reference's, and the candidates sorted by block (bitonic) emit the reference's cells in its order;
4. otherwise (too few cells above LB, or more than 4,096 candidates) the query is flagged and `block_topk_wide_kernel<true>` runs it - the all-equal-scores case of the parity test takes that path.

Used for prompt calls above 28,672 active blocks (below, the wide kernel is as fast); `STRATA_TOPK_SAMPLE=0` keeps the wide kernel.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W; `v0.1.43` + #2072, `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. Model Q2_0, `--max-context 524288`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2` (#2071).

## `qsa_topk_parity CTX 256 20 524288 1` (a prompt call), dispatched time

| context | wide | sample |
|---|---:|---:|
| 98K | 0.397 ms | 0.396 (wide: below the bound) |
| 131K | 0.513 | 0.452 |
| 262K | 0.952 | 0.589 |
| 400K | 1.476 | 0.706 |
| 520K | 1.840 | 0.787 |

`qsa_topk_parity --selftest`: PASS (continuous, 64-level and equal scores; identical ids). `qsa_topk_active_parity` (`STRATA_TOPK_ACTIVE_ANY=1`): 20 cases, identical.

## Engine

First logits after a 196K prompt: bitwise identical to the run without it (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`). The gain sits at depth: with this, #2071 and #2091 and #2092, appending 16K tokens to a 390K conversation (`--serve`) went 15.9 → 12.9 s here.

pulls.title: sm_75: the v2 int8 prompt attention with register staging instead of cp.async (STRATA_PA_V2T=1)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
On Turing the int8-KV prompt attention runs v1, because v2 (`prompt_attn_i8_kernel`) stages each warp's K/V slices with `cp.async`, which does not exist before sm_80. v1 keeps one 4-warp CTA per SM (37 KB of shared memory) and gathers a chunk, waits, computes; the attention is ~18 % of a 130K prompt read on an RTX 2080 Ti.

Here, below sm_80, v2's `issue()` loads the warp's next pieces into registers (4 + 4 `uint4` a lane) and `store_stage()` writes them into the warp's other stage after the current chunk's p·v, where v2 already stores the next chunk's scales - the same bytes in the same places as the cp.async pipeline; each warp only touches its own stages, so `__syncwarp` suffices as before. The MMAs are the m16n8k8 pairs v1 already uses on Turing. Opt-in (`STRATA_PA_V2T=1`): another summation order than v1, like v2 against v1 on sm_80.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W; `v0.1.43`. Model Q2_0, `--resident-experts`, `--max-context 524288`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`, `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2`.

## `qsa_prompt_attn_parity` (int8 KV), ms per chunk and error against FP64

| context × queries | v1 | v2 (register staged) | error vs FP64, v1 / v2 (output scale) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 32K × 1024 | 12.98 | 7.63 | 4.3e-6 / 3.7e-6 (3.7) |
| 64K × 512 | 6.73 | 4.79 | 3.7e-6 / 4.9e-6 (3.5) |
| 1.5K × 1500 | 6.20 | 5.03 | 4.5e-6 / 4.5e-6 (3.6) |
| 2.1K × 256 | 3.16 | 2.31 | 3.3e-6 / 3.8e-6 (3.6) |

## Engine

98K prompt read (one-shot, two runs each): 1473 → 1550 tok/s (+5.2 %), deterministic run to run.

Quality, teacher-forced as in #655 / #2071 (`--serve`, the first P tokens through the prompt path, the next 2,048 resumed through the verify windows, `STRATA_LOGPOS_TOPK=20`, raw Spanish text):

| prefix | argmax agreement | KL (v1 ‖ v2) | perplexity v1 / v2 | argmax where v1's top-2 gap ≥ 0.5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 97.0 % | 0.0169 | 4.623 / 4.538 | 1937 / 1963 |
| 98,304 | 94.3 % | 0.0137 | 5.426 / 5.421 | 1661 / 1675 |

Noise floor: at 32K two v1 runs are identical; at 98K two v1 runs already differ by KL 0.0103 (argmax 95.5 %), so most of the 98K difference is the engine's own run-to-run variation there. Perplexity moves by −1.8 % and −0.1 %.

The server here runs with `STRATA_PA_V2T=1` since 2026-10-12.

pulls.title: sm_75: the hyper-connection's xn16 written as the FP16 its tensor-core GEMMs read (bitwise, prompt +3 %)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
The follow-up I mentioned in #655. With `STRATA_BF16_TC=1` the prompt path converts `xn16` (T × 10240) from BF16 to FP16 before each of its two GEMMs (the down and inject projections), in 16M-element slices: on a 130K prompt read that was ~2.8 s of `bf16_to_f16_kernel` (nsys), 3.2 % of the read.

Now the four `xn16` writers (`gr_norm`, `gr_norm_rs`, `gr_write_norm_rs`, `gr_write_cvec_norm_rs`) can store `gemm.cu`'s conversion of the BF16 value directly (`bf_to_hf_conv`: the same clamp of finite values beyond ±65504 and the same rounding as `bf16_to_f16_kernel`), and `Gemm::bf16(..., x_f16)` skips the conversion on the tensor-core path - the same slices, so the same GEMMs. Any other path (one output row, no room for the buffers) converts the image back to BF16 a slice at a time (exact: every value is a BF16 that fits FP16, or was clamped as the tensor-core path clamps it).

It is on only where it changes nothing: the stage runs BF16 on FP16 tensor cores (`Gemm::bf16_converts_x()`), without the BF16X2 low parts and with the unpadded `xn16` stride; the MTP draft's own read keeps BF16. `STRATA_XN_F16=0` turns it off.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75), i7-6700, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM 1650 MHz, 240 W; `v0.1.43`. Model Q2_0, `--resident-experts`, `--max-context 524288`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `STRATA_BF16_TC=1`.

## Results

| | `STRATA_XN_F16=0` | `=1` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 98K prompt read, run 1 | 1431.6 tok/s | 1473.4 |
| 98K prompt read, run 2 | 1430.4 | 1474.0 |

First logits after the 98K prompt (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`): bitwise identical. A 4K one-shot run writes the same tokens.
