pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 3090 | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL | Strata 0.1.43
pulls.author: faazzol
pulls.body:
This PR adds a community benchmark for **Strata 0.1.43**, measured on October 12, 2026.

**Hardware**
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 — 24 GiB VRAM
- AMD Ryzen 9 5950X — 16 cores / 32 threads
- 64 GB RAM
- Linux / CUDA 13.0

**Model**
- Qwen3.8 Flash Next
- Quantization: Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL
- Context: 65,536 tokens

**Benchmark results (median)**
- Short-chat decode: **33.1 tokens/s**
- 4K prompt prefill: **180.5 tokens/s**
- 16K prompt prefill: **382.9 tokens/s**
- Agent conversation cache reuse: **68.8%**

The contribution includes the three generated benchmark files:
- `README.md`
- `results.json`
- `engine-log-excerpt.txt`

The benchmark measures performance only; model accuracy and answer correctness were not evaluated.

No changes to Strata's source code.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 3090 + RTX 5070 + RTX 5070 Ti layer split (Q2_0)
pulls.author: HerkulesTerminator
pulls.body:
Results-only submission. No engine changes.

**Hardware:** RTX 3090 (24 GB) + RTX 5070 (12 GB) + RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB), i7-8700K, 64 GB RAM, model shards on a spinning HDD. No 32 GB card in the machine.

**Model:** ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF, Q2_0, custom pack via tools/iq_pack.py. Engine 0.1.42 local source build.

**Config:** gpu [0,1,2], layer_split 28,40, --pipeline-windows 2, --trim-stage-weights, --kv int8, --kv-resident 16384, --max-context 260000, STRATA_SPLIT_OWN=1, STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1. Engine reports 99% of profiled expert pairs resident.

**Headline numbers** (3 runs each, greedy, 256-token cap, salted prompts so nothing was prefix-cached):

| Config | Prompt tok/s median (range) | Decode tok/s median (range) | TTFT median (range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| short (756 tok) | 1,175 (1,058-1,176) | 129.2 (117.1-133.8) | 0.66 s (0.66-0.73) |
| long (44,736 tok) | 3,275 (3,274-3,276) | 109.2 (108.0-114.0) | 13.71 s (13.70-13.72) |

Needle recall: 6/6 at 32k and 128k, depths 10/50/90.

**Main limitation:** the 12 GB RTX 5070 stage holds 5,922 of its 6,144 profiled expert pairs; the 222 non-resident pairs stream from RAM on every prompt chunk. Split position also matters a lot - the 5070 Ti has the slowest PCIe link of the three (3.0 GB/s engine probe), and moving layers onto it degrades prefill sharply.

Two values are marked `not measured` in the README: the PCIe link width (lspci -vv returns no LnkCap/LnkSta on this host) and the Hugging Face revision of the Q2_0 shards (not recorded at download time; byte sizes are given instead).

Files: README.md, runs.json (per-run engine timings + TTFT + total latency + VRAM/RAM snapshots), needles.json, community_bench.py.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB unequal layer split (PCIe gen5 x8 + gen3 x4), IQ3_S, engine 0.1.43
pulls.author: mmbeanz
pulls.body:
## What this is

A community benchmark report from an unequal two-card rig, answering `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` row 1 (two NVIDIA cards of different sizes, `--layer-split auto`) and A/B-ing the two live 0.1.43 default debates (#2010/#1975 overlap, route tail-skip) on a **split**. Note: the overlap turned out to be disabled on layer splits, so only the tail-skip A/B tests a live feature here; the overlap arm is a null control (see finding 4 in #2085). Those threads measured single-GPU only.

Results-only: one new folder, `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx-5060ti-3060-split/`, no engine changes. The branch is from tag `v0.1.43` (`7695859a`), the exact commit the engine was built from (plus one local `setup.py`-only pip->uv commit; no engine code touched).

## Hardware

"bertha" - Ryzen 9 7900X, 64 GB DDR5-6400, Linux (CachyOS, engine in systemd-nspawn), driver 615.71.09, CUDA 13.4.

- **RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB** on PCIe **5.0 x8** - measured H2D 28.2-28.7 GB/s
- **RTX 3060 12 GB** on PCIe **3.0 x4** behind the chipset - measured H2D 3.15-3.2 GB/s

Links and H2D measured under load with `tools/h2d_bench`. The auto-generated `machine` block is unusable on this host (#2062) and was hand-corrected; the original values and every other edit are listed in `NOTES.md`.

## Model

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **IQ3_S** (ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO pack, sha256 in `sha256sums.txt`), 512K context (yarn 2.0), pinned expert profile - no `--expert-profile-save` anywhere.

## Configurations tested

All `tools/strata_bench.py --long --runs 3`, one continuous evening session, 0 failures, `/metrics?requests=all` per-request histories included.

| run | config |
| --- | --- |
| A | baseline `--layer-split 40` |
| B1 | `--layer-split auto` (planner chose K=3) |
| B1c | explicit `--layer-split 6` (the engine's printed suggestion, followed literally) |
| B1d | explicit `--layer-split 42` (the as-given-frame equivalent) |
| C | baseline + `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=0` (null control: overlap is already off on a split) |
| D | baseline + `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` |
| needles | `needle_bench.py` 32K/128K/256K x depths 10/50/90: **9/9 found** |

## Headline numbers

- Baseline: 32K prompt **1,721 tok/s**, short-chat decode **74.4 tok/s**.
- `auto` costs **-25.0%** of 32K prompt throughput (chunk clamp, #1616).
- The literal printed suggestion costs **-76%**: explicit splits do not inherit the #1352 card reorder - a question for maintainers is in the report.
- Tail-skip measures **+5.2%** here, not +10-20%, and decays with context; `ADAPT_OVERLAP` is **inert on layer splits** - the engine disables it before reading the flag (corrected after review in #2010; see commit 79cc236).
- Hit rate tracks **per-layer coverage**, not held-expert count (8,842 vs 5,935 held, statistically identical hit rate).

## Not tested

Long soak, batching/concurrency, vision latency, mmap file tier, Windows/HIP, single-card configs on this box. `hit_rate` is the decode-phase metric only.

## Discussion

The announcement issue with the full findings: #2085. The C and D rows were also posted as comments on #2010 and #2007; the #2010 comment's overlap conclusion was corrected afterwards (see the correction comment in #2010 and finding 4 in #2085).

*Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed every line and ran the measurements myself.*

pulls.title: fix: make conversation parking admission fail safely
pulls.author: ivanov84
pulls.body:
## Summary

This hardens conversation-cache admission and retained K/V reuse under memory pressure. On Windows the engine
runs out of the *system commit* limit rather than physical RAM, and the park path had no way to tell that it had
already given up, no way to see why an allocation failed, and it silently dropped the retained K/V whenever
admission said no.

The eviction round now lives in `ConversationCache::evict_for_admission()`, which makes the loop's decisions
testable for the first time; the tests assert the old and new loops against one cache state.

## Changes

- **Stop eviction when it cannot make admission progress.** The inline loop was bounded by `slots()` and called
  `evict_oldest()` unconditionally, so a request larger than the total freeable capacity evicted every parked
  conversation and still refused. `evict_for_admission()` checks the request against `evictable_bytes()` first
  and stops at the first round that stops making progress, reporting why (`stalled`, `hopeless`, `freeable`).
- **Avoid unnecessary eviction when no additional capacity is required.** The retained K/V is already held, so it
  is subtracted before the admission need is computed; a park that needs no new capacity evicts nothing.
- **Preserve retained K/V reuse state when admission is declined.** `take_reuse()` used to leave the buffers with
  the caller, so a declined park lost them and the next turn rebuilt them. They go back through `put_reuse()` on
  every early-return path.
- **Improve diagnostics.** Allocation failures now name where they happened (`at the capture`, `after the
  checkpoint split`, `after the full-model load`) and the probe reports whether the machine is out of commit or
  out of address space. Refusal lines print both resources and the process' own commit rather than one number.
- **Regression coverage** for admission and eviction edge cases, including a twelve-case table asserting the old
  and new loops agree everywhere they should and differ only in the hopeless case.

## Validation

Built and run on Windows, MSVC + CUDA 12.8, sm_120:

```
cmake -G Ninja + fresh build dir         exit 0, 1 warning (upstream dequant.cpp C4456)
conversation_cache_test                  4286 checks passed
conversation_memory_test                 32 checks passed
conversation_split_failure_test          stages 1/2/3 allocation-failure cases preserved: 8/12/16
ctest                                    43/43 passed, 2 skipped (CPU-only build: expert_multi, isa_guard)
cl /Zs over the CUDA park path           exit 0
CUDA engine build                        exit 0, strata 0.1.43
git diff --check                         clean
```

String audit of the built engine: the textless `allocation failed; skip parking` is gone, and the named-cause and
admission lines are present.

End-to-end, against a real model on this machine — the user's production server running a build of this tree,
2026-10-11 23:42 to 2026-10-12 02:46, two RTX 5060 Ti with `--layer-split auto`, `--max-context 262144`,
`--conversation-cache-mib 16384 --conversation-cache-slots 4 --conversation-cache-min-free-mib 4096`. Counted
over that session's log:

```
park attempts: 216 (176 at >= 50k tokens, largest 232826 tokens)
refusals:      1 of 216
"allocation failed; skip parking": 0
restores: 130; 129 of the 216 parks reused retained K/V (up to 3.29 GiB in one park)
evict-to-admit rounds: 12 (11 evicted one conversation, one evicted two; largest admitted request 4006 MiB)
budget (make_room) refusals: 0; refusal arms seen: hopeless 1, stalled 0, short_by 0
```

The single refusal is the `hopeless` arm: the request was 3966 MiB against 2152 MiB freeable in total, and it
names both numbers instead of evicting a conversation that could not have paid for it. Parking continued normally
afterwards. The same workload on the unpatched 0.1.40.1 engine logged 293 `skip parking` lines — 203 of them the
bare textless `allocation failed; skip parking` and 90 the budget refusal ending in a static
`or telemetry unavailable` — out of 2772 attempts (291 refused, 10.5%). That build never ran an evict-to-admit
round at all: the loop that would have run does not exist in 0.1.40.

That run was built from the 0.1.42 base of this series; the rebase onto 0.1.43 changed no source of the patch, so
the runtime evidence is the same code. The binary was string-audited first: the textless failure line absent, the
named-cause and admission lines present.

## Limitations

- The stalled arm of `evict_for_admission()`, the `bad_alloc` probe, and the budget-refusal K/V hand-back are
  asserted only by the native tests. The run above produced no stalled round (evicting did return memory on this
  machine), no failed allocation, and no budget refusal, so those three paths are runtime-untested.
- Windows-only validation. The SYCL copy of the park path was edited by hand and reviewed, but no oneAPI toolchain
  is installed here, so it is not compiled. The header changes do reach the SYCL build through the shared include
  path.
- Multi-GPU runtime behavior beyond this one two-GPU WDDM data point is not covered.
- The change does not reduce the system-commit cost of the resident expert arena, which is the underlying pressure
  on this machine; it makes admission stop early, keep what it already holds, and say why it declined.
- Not every previously observed parking failure has a known cause. What is measured here is that these refusals
  now explain themselves.

## Review focus

- Retained K/V ownership on every early-return and exception path in the park body: it is taken with
  `take_reuse()` and must be handed back with `put_reuse()` on all of them.
- The resource accounting used by admission: `evictable_bytes()` deliberately excludes the retained K/V and pinned
  entries, because `evict_oldest()` cannot free either. `bytes()` still charges both, which is correct for the
  cache budget and wrong for "what can I free right now".
- The safety of the allocation diagnostic probe: it reserves, tries to commit, and must release the reservation on
  every path, including failure.
- `ConversationCache::clear()` from #879 is upstream's, and it is consistent with this: it zeroes `reuse_`, and
  `evictable_bytes()` never counted it.

<sub>This PR was prepared by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the author. The agent's work was reviewed by two
independent review passes before the branch was pushed; the review notes and the answers to them are recorded in
`LOCAL-PARKING-PATCH-0.1.43.md`, which is included in the branch along with the repo-local `AGENTS.md` notes.
Happy to drop either file from the change if you would rather keep them out of the repository.</sub>

pulls.title: dequant: the prompt projections' BF16 dequant with 16-byte stores on sm_75 (bit-exact; STRATA_TC_SM75=0 keeps the per-group kernel)
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (bit-exact speed change on sm_75).

## Summary
On compute capability 7.5 the prompt path's BF16 projections are dequantized by a kernel that writes 16 bytes per
thread instead of 2 bytes every 64. A conversion with no arithmetic: the output is **bit for bit** the per-group
kernel's. `STRATA_TC_SM75=0` keeps the old kernel; other cards are untouched. 0.1.43's #1720 coalesced the Q8_0 path
the same way; this covers the BF16 projections on Turing.

## What changed
`src/kernels/cuda/dequant_bf16.cu` (the sm_75 kernel and its dispatch), `include/strata/core/tc_sm75.hpp` (the
`STRATA_TC_SM75` switch, shared with the hc16 PR).

## Measurements
Part of the 100 s -> 75 s of a 131K prompt on the RTX 2080 Ti stage (with SIMT by default and hc16). Values identical
(memcmp of the dequantized images in the fork's test build).

Built and started on v0.1.43 (RTX 2080 Ti + RTX 3060 layer split, Windows): the engine serves as before, same answer; the dequantized images were compared byte for byte in the fork's test build when the change was made.

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti), see #2073.

pulls.title: qsa_select: the FP32 tiled block scores below sm_80 (PR #1091) on by default; STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=0 keeps the warp kernel
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (a default change below sm_80, with the numbers).

## Summary
#1091 (konijiwa110) added the FP32 tiled QSA block-scores kernel for the prompt path below sm_80 and it was merged
**opt-in** (`STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1`). This turns it **on by default** on compute capability < 8.0; `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=0`
keeps the warp kernel. sm_80 and newer keep their TF32 tensor-core kernel; HIP is untouched.

## Why
On Turing the warp kernel runs at ~1 TFLOPS against ~6.9 for the tiled one, and the QSA block scores are a visible
share of a long prompt. #1091 measured +22% at 128K and +44% at 248K prompt speed on an RTX 2080 Ti; here, with the
two sm_75 changes of the same series, a 131K prompt on the 2080 Ti stage went from 100 s to 75 s. The ready-made
engine is what most Turing users run, and they do not read the environment table.

## What changed
`src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu` (`qsa_block_scores_tc`: the `simt` default), `include/strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp`
(the comment), `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` (the log line says which kernel ran).

## Bit for bit
No: the tiled kernel sums in another order than the warp kernel, as the opt-in already did. The prompt's selection
can differ at the rounding level.

## Measurements
RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split (the 2080 Ti holds layers 16-47), Qwen3.8
IQ3_XXS: 131K prompt 100 s -> 75 s together with the 16-byte dequant and hc16 (separate PRs). TITAN RTX, #1981: the
community report ran with the switch on.

Built and started on v0.1.43 (RTX 2080 Ti + RTX 3060 layer split, Windows): the engine serves as before, same answer. The prompt-time figures come from this fork's daily build, where the three Turing prefill changes have run together since 0.1.40.

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti), see #2073.

pulls.title: [Engine] add native Windows support for Intel SYCL GPUs
pulls.author: lm902
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The upstream SYCL source installer rejects Windows, and the engine has build and file interfaces that prevent a native Windows build. This PR enables the existing source installer and SYCL engine on Windows, including device detection, build, model loading and generation. No container is required. Release packaging and desktop-app/Terminal engine distribution are outside this change.

Updated on 2026-10-19 for **0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3**. Tested head **6edb90627e1150758f841897f3c76c57fa1231af** merges upstream **e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211** without rewriting the published branch.

## Related discussion

This updates the existing #2079 and its Windows Level Zero/runtime investigation. The scope remains native Windows support, not a new optimization or a replacement PR.

## Approach

- Reuse the existing installer and engine; add Windows oneAPI build/runtime paths, GPU selection and early Level Zero capability checks.
- Use overlapped positioned reads, pointer-width file handles and the Windows RAM budget. Do not label an ordinary VirtualAlloc arena as registered GPU host memory.
- Keep compatibility fixes conditional on Windows. Upstream ESIMD/INT8 kernels, MMQ defaults and the 8192-token prefill recommendation are unchanged. The prefill source delta is seven Windows-conditional lines for calibration-cache directory creation (`_mkdir`).
- Add focused setup/compiler regression tests and Windows instructions in `docs/INTEL_ARC.md`. No user configs, model files, benchmark artifacts or separate GPU image-encoder feature are included.

## Validation

Tested on Windows 11 Pro for Workstations Insider build 26220, Core i9-13900KF, 64 GB RAM, Arc Pro B70 32 GB (31.159 GiB), graphics driver 32.0.101.9034 / Level Zero driver 1.17.39500+2. Tools: VS 2022 17.14.40, MSVC 14.44, Windows SDK 10.0.26100, DPC++ 2026.1.1, oneMKL 2026.1.0, Python 3.11.9; Release/Ninja, SPIR-V JIT.

Tested tree: `d7b1e6c3853440637f57eb35d6d09587e9e4ca02`. Engine SHA-256: `c989b1466cdb14f08a7d1a354c01143d1fa69c6a0801f2f4dbe8b0f709adc988`.

**Passed:**

- `cmd /d /c sycl\tools\build_windows.bat`: all native SYCL targets built, including ESIMD; rebuilt after the final cache-directory fix.
- `python -m unittest tools.test_setup_sycl tools.test_setup_golden`: **46/46 passed**, including prefill recommendation and MMQ-default regression checks.
- `strata.exe --list-devices` with `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu`: B70, PCI ID `e223`, correct VRAM, Level Zero backend, free-memory and command-graph support.
- `ctest --test-dir build-sycl-win --output-on-failure -R "^(esimd_moe_parity|esimd_moe_mode_test|prefill_gdn_parity)$"`: **3/3 passed** after the final compile fix.
- IQ3_S: six independent engine starts and all 12 measured requests below completed normally. Each read 4096 input tokens and generated 64 (`finish=length`, zero cache reuse). Same tested tree, binary, configuration and input hashes across all arms. Device-plan/no-host protections remained enabled; no RAM guard fired.

**Failed:**

- Full installer discovery (`tools/test_setup*.py`): **701 passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped / 706**. One parallel-download test observed a duplicate first range; two `test_setup_engine_hash.WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller` tests failed on release lookup/refusal behavior. All three reproduced with unmodified upstream `setup.py` in the same environment.
- `ctest --test-dir build-sycl-win --output-on-failure --timeout 60`: **33 passed, 3 failed / 36**. Failures: `gr_parity` (unsupported QFUSE), `ple_parity` (missing external fixture), `s2_expert_grouped_parity` (bitwise differences). No kernel, tolerance or exclusion was changed to hide them.
- A preliminary IQ2_XS capture failed in external-harness shutdown bookkeeping after generation. Its record was retained and excluded; after fixing the harness, the complete four-start sequence was rerun. No IQ3_S session failed or was excluded.

**Not run:**

- Image input and desktop-app/Terminal packaging on this revision. The direct-engine tests do not validate those workflows.
- Controlled quality evaluation, fixed-clock/power characterization or a prefill chunk-size sweep. These measurements do not compare engine versions.

### IQ3_S: INT8 prefill on Windows

Same IQ3_S GGUF/pack and binary; `--max-context 32768 --kv int8 --prefill 4096 --expert-cache 11500 --stream-experts --vram-reserve-mib 1024 --pool-workers 15 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0 --conversation-cache-mib 0`, MTP enabled, 12 stager threads. Speed projection and persistent SYCL caching were off. All arms shared one test-local INT8 calibration cache.

Start order: **A0, B0, C0, C1, B1, A1**. A leaves `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ` and its alias unset; B sets it to `0`; C sets it to `auto`. This switch was the only intentional arm difference. Each start excluded one full 4096-token/64-output warmup, then measured two full 4096-token requests, temperature 0, 64-output cap. Distinct leading markers prevented prefix reuse; corresponding inputs were identical across arms. Generation/timings used the existing `serve.server.StrataEngine` and `request_timings` APIs.

| Start | MMQ setting | Prefill sample 1 (tok/s) | Prefill sample 2 (tok/s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A0 | unset/default | 459.7 | 457.4 |
| B0 | `0` | 338.2 | 336.8 |
| C0 | `auto` | 453.5 | 454.0 |
| C1 | `auto` | 453.4 | 452.3 |
| B1 | `0` | 340.3 | 344.5 |
| A1 | unset/default | 452.2 | 451.4 |

Median of four measured samples per arm: **default 454.80**, **off 339.25**, **auto 453.45 tok/s**. Default vs off: **+34.06%**; explicit auto vs off: **+33.66%**. Ranges: default 451.4-459.7, off 336.8-344.5, auto 452.3-454.0 tok/s. Logs confirm automatic INT8/fused DPAS in A/C and no enabled INT8 prompt-expert path in B. This is a repeated prefill gain for this Windows workload, not a new optimization introduced by this PR.

For each measured input, default and explicit auto produced identical 64-token outputs in both rounds. **Off differed from them starting at output token 4.** These runs do not establish quality equivalence or a decode speedup. Expert-cache arguments were fixed, but actual mixed-format residency varied by two slots (12825-12827; 24936-24941 MiB). Minimum available system RAM was 14.65 GiB; the safety threshold was 2 GiB. Clocks and desktop activity were not locked. Startup/warmup times were excluded, including B0's longer startup.

The earlier IQ2_XS 32K-prompt/8192-chunk experiment remains negative: default median 1427.10 vs off 1426.35 tok/s (+0.053%, overlapping ranges). Individual samples in A0/B0/B1/A1 order: default 1433.3/1427.9, off 1430.2/1425.1, off 1424.2/1427.6, default 1421.2/1426.3. It also used 256K capacity and speed projection, unlike this IQ3_S setup. The experiments therefore do not isolate model size as the reason for the different gains.

Raw session JSON, input hashes, output token IDs and logs are retained locally outside the repository. All measured samples are reported above; these are focused Windows validation runs, not a standard/approved benchmark submission.

## Limits

The native Windows path requires working Level Zero, GPU free-memory queries and command graphs; OpenCL-only inference is refused before loading the model. The failed checks above remain disclosed. Existing user model/config files and network/authentication settings are unchanged. Upstream performance kernels and defaults are preserved.

pulls.title: prefill: refill the lent expert slots from the GGUF mapping's pieces (STRATA_REFILL_PARTS=1, gfx1151's table: 4K +3.1%, 32K +1.0%)
pulls.author: libratechw
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none

## Summary
After a prompt, the expert-cache slots it borrowed are refilled from the experts' files. With the GGUF read in place an expert
is three tensor slices (gate, up, down, possibly in two shards), so `blob_stable` first assembled each 4 MB blob in a staging
buffer (a copy on the calling thread) and the refill then copied that to the slot. Each slice is contiguous in its mapped
tensor, so it can go straight to its offset in the slot. The bytes in the slot are the same.

## What changed
- `ExpertSource::blob_parts` (default: none), `FileExpertSource::blob_parts` (the GGUF in place only; the RAM copy, an
  override, unbuffered reads, a closed mapping and `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1` keep `blob_stable`), and the pass-through in
  `RemotePrefillSource` (none for an expert the helper holds, the fallback's pieces otherwise). `blob_parts` counts the read
  as `blob` does a read out of the mapping (`count_mapped_read`, now shared by both).
- `ExpertCache::fill_slot_queued_parts`: the pieces on the same queue as `fill_slot_queued`; `sync_queued` waits as before.
- `generate.cpp`: the `--serve` refill (`refill_issue`) uses them when `STRATA_REFILL_PARTS=1`. The single-run refill is
  unchanged.
- `src/core/arch_defaults.cpp`: gfx1151 sets `STRATA_REFILL_PARTS=1` (`STRATA_REFILL_PARTS=0` or `STRATA_GFX1151_DEFAULTS=0`
  turns it off); `docs/STRIX_HALO.md`: its row.
- `tests/core/expert_layout_test.cpp`: the pieces, each at its offset, equal the assembled blob byte for byte (the fixture's
  second layer spans two shards).

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, ROCm 7.14.1, Linux), on 296b59d2, UD-Q4_K_XL, `--serve --prefill 16384 --spec 4`, the section-5
switches of `docs/STRIX_HALO.md` with `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=2048` and `STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1`, a chat request of 4K / 32K
tokens (a fresh nonce each, reasoning off, 256 tokens out), fresh servers alternating, 7 pairs (32K: of 8, dropping one
with page migration or reclaim during a prompt). Every one of the 7 pairs is faster:

| | 4K | 32K |
|---|---:|---:|
| 296b59d2, prompt tok/s (median) | 1,130 | 1,242 |
| this branch | 1,164 | 1,255 |
| median of the pair ratios | +3.1% | +1.0% |

The records (each request's engine timing, the requests, the servers' arguments and variables) and the scripts are in
[libratechw/Strata@9b1a9fd5, `2078/`](https://github.com/libratechw/Strata/tree/9b1a9fd5d0a4850320a9211eb727de283d1e90a7/2078);
its README says how the runs were made.

Builds and tests on this branch:
- HIP gfx1151: ctest, 112 tests: 104 pass (`expert_layout_test` among them), 5 skip, and the same three fail as on 296b59d2
  (`ple_parity`, `expert_parity`, `pool_test`).
- HIP: `strata_kernels`, `strata_prefill` and `strata_mmq` compile for gfx1012, gfx1030, gfx1100, gfx1103, gfx1150, gfx1151,
  gfx1200 and gfx1201.
- CUDA 13.0, RTX 3060 (Windows): builds; ctest, 117 tests: 114 pass (`expert_layout_test` among them), 2 skip, and `ple_parity`
  fails as on 296b59d2.
- SYCL (oneAPI 2026.1 icpx): builds. The SYCL port has its own `expert_source.hpp/.cpp`, `expert_cache.cpp` and `generate.cpp`,
  not changed; it shares `expert_cache.hpp` and `arch_defaults.cpp`.

Not run: UD-IQ4_XS, the single-run refill, gfx1151 under Windows, and `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=1`.

pulls.title: serve: --prompt-cache-file <path>, the long prompt prefix saved to disk and restored across restarts (opt-in)
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in feature: the prompt prefix survives a restart).

## Summary
`--prompt-cache-file <path>` (opt-in) writes the root checkpoint of the shared prompt prefix to a file and reads it
back at the next start, so the first turn after a restart resumes from the saved prefix instead of reading it again.
Format v2 holds one image per `--layer-split` block (so it works with two cards) and the MTP drafter's root cells.
Without the option nothing changes.

## Why
The in-RAM prompt cache (`--prompt-cache-tail` / `--prompt-cache-every`) dies with the engine. An agent session
(Claude Code through a local gateway here) starts with a 40-130K prefix that is the same across restarts; every
restart of the server re-read it. Measured on this box the first 40K prompt after a restart went from **~42 s** to
**16-20 s** with the file.

## What changed
- `src/core/prefix_cache_file.cpp`, `include/strata/core/prefix_cache_file.hpp` (new, library `strata_prefix_cache`):
  the file format (header with the engine's identity, one image per block, the drafter's root), write and read,
  BCrypt SHA-256 on Windows / the C++ fallback elsewhere.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the option; the save after the root checkpoint is taken, the restore at start-up
  before the first request; host memory checked with `available_host_bytes()` before the restore; the file's
  **identity** covers the executable, the arguments and the `STRATA_*` / `CUDA_*` environment, so a file written by
  another configuration is replaced, never misread.
- `src/core/mtp.cpp`, `include/strata/core/mtp.hpp`: the drafter uses `first_needed()` so every cell of the saved root
  is computed, not only the ones the current window asks for.
- `src/core/prefix_cache_file_test.cpp`: the format, round trip and identity checks.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: the library and the test.

## Relation to open work
#1937 (parked conversations on the disk, `--conversation-disk-dir`) and #1810 (conversation checkpoints with disk
restore) persist **conversations** of the conversation cache; this persists the **shared prompt prefix root** (the
`--prompt-cache` checkpoint every conversation of a session starts from, including the drafter's state) and is
independent of the conversation cache. They can coexist; none of them is merged at the time of writing.

## Measurements
RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB, Windows 11, `--layer-split 16 --pipeline-windows 2`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS.
Reading a 40K-token first prompt takes ~42 s on this box; with the file the first turn after a restart resumes from
the saved root instead (one image per block read from an NVMe). Decode and later turns are unchanged; the output tokens
are the same with and without the file (the same checkpoint, read from RAM or from the file). The save/restore path has
run in this fork's daily build since 0.1.40 with 40-130K prefixes. On v0.1.43 the branch was built and started twice
with the option (`prefix disk cache: enabled`, identity computed in 17-23 ms), same answers.

## Risks / limits
Opt-in. The file is rewritten when the identity changes (a new engine build, a changed option): one re-read, as
without the option. A file of a different format version is ignored and replaced.

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti).

pulls.title: QSA decode attention: PR #540's two-cells-per-step chunk kernel on every CUDA card and a bounded merge (STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1, opt-in, bit-exact)
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change, bit-exact).

## Summary
`STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1` (opt-in, off by default) runs the QSA layers' decode attention - the verify window's and the MTP
drafter's, single query and batch - through PR #540's chunk kernel (`attn_chunk_kernel_pre75`: two cells per step
with a 12-shuffle reduction, cell-major probabilities, V loaded four at a time) on **every** CUDA card, and merges the
chunks with `attn_merge_v2_kernel`, a merge that skips the chunks the chunk kernel marked empty. Upstream compiles the
pre75 kernel only with `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60` and picks it below sm_75; here it is compiled in every CUDA build
and selected by the variable. The output is **bit for bit** the default kernels' (see below). HIP is untouched.

## Why
The default `attn_chunk_kernel` reduces each cell with 5 `warp_sum` shuffles per head (60 per cell pair); the pre75
body does two cells per step with `reduce12` (16 shuffles) and reads the V rows four at a time. nsys on an RTX 3060
(stage 0 of a layer split, 131K context): `attn_chunk_kernel` **99.8 us** a call against **46.4 us** with the pre75
body; the same ratio on an RTX 2080 Ti. The decode attention is ~8% of the per-row cost of a window at 131K on these
cards, so the end-to-end gain is small but free.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_decode_attn.cu`: `attn_chunk_kernel_pre75<M, NC, ...>` compiled in every CUDA build;
  `daily_attn()` reads `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY`; the kernel choice `STRATA_ATTN_CHUNK_SEL(M, PRE)` takes it on any card
  when set (below sm_75 in an experimental build as before). `attn_merge_v2_kernel` with the chunk-empty marks;
  `STRATA_ATTN_MERGE_V2=0|1` forces the merge alone, `STRATA_ATTN_PRE75=0` turns the chunk kernel off (A/B).
  `spt` shares `sq`'s shared memory, so the kernel uses 15,872 B like the default one (68-78 registers against 37-41,
  256 threads a block).
- `include/strata/kernels/qsa_decode_attn.hpp`: the selection helpers.
- `src/kernels/qsa_merge_daily_parity.cpp` (tests): memcmp of the chunk kernel and the merge against upstream's on
  four KV formats, widths at the chunk borders and non-resident pages; `--bench` times the two chunk kernels back to
  back. Registered as ctest `qsa_merge_daily_parity_default` and `_daily`.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: the harness.

## Bit for bit
`reduce12` adds at every level the same two pairs as `warp_sum`'s butterfly (xor 16, 8, 4, 2, 1; float addition
commutes), the V cells fold in the same cell order with the same `fmaf`, the masked cells stay excluded; the merge v2
does the same `fmaf` in the same order and skips exactly the chunks the chunk kernel marks empty. `qsa_merge_daily_parity` on an RTX 2080 Ti (v0.1.43 build, tests on): **1,168 cases, 0 differ** (fp16 290, int8 291, q4_0 294, k8v4 293; 21,190,308 nonzero output values), with `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY` unset and `=1`. In the engine the greedy text and the drafter's acceptance are unchanged (deterministic
131K bench, forced tokens and windows).

## Measurements
RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) + RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS,
131K context, `--kv int8`.

`qsa_merge_daily_parity --bench` on the RTX 2080 Ti (CUDA events, 200 calls per arm, B-A-B: Daily kernel, upstream
kernel, Daily kernel again; int8 KV, 32,768-cell capacity, window of n_q queries):

| n_q | width (cells) | chunk kernel: upstream | PR #540 body | ratio | merge: upstream | merge v2 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32,768 | 448.9 us | **264.3 us** | 0.59 | 182.6 us | **45.6 us** | 0.25 |
| 2 | 32,768 | 849.8 | **483.9** | 0.57 | 186.6 | **60.9** | 0.33 |
| 3 | 32,768 | 1,259.8 | **727.3** | 0.58 | 202.3 | **85.1** | 0.42 |
| 4 | 32,768 | 1,692.3 | **969.0** | 0.57 | 208.4 | **106.5** | 0.51 |
| 4 | 2,051 | 132.7 | **86.6** | 0.65 | 41.3 | **9.9** | 0.24 |

fp16, q4_0 and k8v4 KV show the same ratios (0.57-0.63 for the chunk kernel, 0.24-0.51 for the merge). In the engine
(nsys, RTX 3060, 131K context) `attn_chunk_kernel` went from 99.8 us to 46.4 us a call.

End to end it is part of a stack that matches its reference within noise; the attention alone is ~8% of the per-row
cost, so no separate end-to-end claim is made here.

Built and started on v0.1.43 with `STRATA_ATTN_DAILY=1` (RTX 2080 Ti + RTX 3060 layer split, Windows): the engine serves as before, same answer.

## Risks / limits
Opt-in: nothing changes with the variable unset. The kernel body is PR #540's (sskver) and the merge is Hardin22's
`attn_merge_v2_kernel`, both carried in this fork since 0.1.40 and credited in the source. #1888 (split attention on
the int8 mma path, sm_80+) is a different kernel and not bit-exact; the two do not overlap (this one serves Turing).

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti).

pulls.title: PLE: --ple-io direct stays direct when the start-up probe measures the disk slow (STRATA_PLE_AUTO_MMAP=1 opts into the mmap switch); PLE read diagnostics
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (a start-up default that misfired on a slow SSD, and read diagnostics).

## Summary
Since 0.1.42 the engine probes the PLE table at start-up and, under 15,000 rows/s, switches `--ple-io direct` to
`mmap` on its own. The probe reads 64 rows a batch from a cold table, a far lower queue depth than a prompt chunk's
batched read, so a healthy SATA SSD can measure "slow" and the switch costs a long prompt more than three times its
time. This change keeps the probe and its warning but makes the switch **opt-in** (`STRATA_PLE_AUTO_MMAP=1`); an
explicit `--ple-io` is untouched. It also adds a few PLE read diagnostics.

## Why
Measured on one PC (PLE table on a SATA SSD, 131K-token prompt, two-card layer split): the probe read **1,259 rows/s**,
switched to mmap, and the prompt took **260 s**; the same engine with direct I/O took **75 s** and decode was 3.9%
faster (the mmap mode also drops the row cache and the in-flight reads). mmap faults the rows in one 4 KiB page at a
time; direct I/O keeps `--ple-inflight` reads in flight and the chunk read-ahead hides them. The probe's figure is a
cold, low-depth read and does not predict the prompt path's throughput.

## What changed
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the probe still runs and prints `PLE direct read probe: N rows/s`; under the threshold it
  warns and **keeps direct** unless `STRATA_PLE_AUTO_MMAP=1` (then it switches as before). With
  `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` the decode summary adds the primary verifier's PLE gather time per window and the reader's
  cumulative counters before and after the request (`strata decode PLE primary/before/after`).
- `src/ngram/ple_reader.cpp`, `include/strata/ngram/ple_reader.hpp`: `ple io:` adds the read mean, the maximum and the
  count of reads over 100 ms (all reads, where p50/p99 cover the last 65,536).
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: a chunk that waited more than 1 s for its PLE rows logs one line
  (`strata prefill: the chunk at token N waited X ms for its PLE rows`).
- `src/kernels/ngram.cpp`, `include/strata/core/verify.hpp`: the gather time counter.

No kernel changes; the output tokens are the same in both I/O modes.

## Measurements
RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, `--layer-split 16 --pipeline-windows 2`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
IQ3_XXS, 131K-token prompt, PLE table on a SATA SSD (cold):

| | prompt 131K | decode (131K, 1024 tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1.42 default (probe -> mmap) | 260 s | reference |
| direct kept (this change) | **75 s** | **+3.9%** |

With the table on an NVMe the probe says `fine` (91,220 rows/s here) and nothing changes.

Built and started on v0.1.43 (`7695859a`, RTX 2080 Ti + RTX 3060 layer split, Windows): the probe reports `43,290 rows/s (fine)` on the NVMe, the engine serves as before; the same code has run in this fork's daily build since 0.1.42.

## Risks / limits
A disk that really is too slow for direct I/O keeps direct unless `STRATA_PLE_AUTO_MMAP=1` is set; the warning says
so and names the variable. `--ple-io ram` and an explicit `--ple-io mmap` behave as before.

Part of a series from a public patch registry (`stack/` in the fork imanu86/Strata-2080Ti): one lever per PR, each
opt-in or bit-exact, measured on the same two-card box.

pulls.title: sm_75: the decode QSA selection at long context, a halving scorer and a split top-k (bitwise, decode +6-12 % at 410K)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
At long context a verify window's QSA selection is a fixed cost per layer that the rest of the window does not hide: at ~420K cells on an RTX 2080 Ti the 12 layers' scores and top-k took ~6 ms of a ~52 ms window (nsys, `--serve`, 256 tokens after a 422K conversation). Both kernels here produce the same bits as today's, and both have a switch.

1. **`block_scores_halve_kernel`** (decode scorer, `block_scores_multi_kernel`'s replacement on sm_75). Its time grew with the window's queries: 117 / 265 / 510 µs for 1 / 3 / 6 queries at 420K. The keys are read once, so the cost was the 5 xor shuffles per (query, head) value - 20 per block and query - and, once those were gone, the per-block shared-memory reads of the queries (ncu: `mio_throttle`). Here the 4 × queries values (padded to a power of 2) are reduced together by recursive halving: at offset o each lane keeps half its values and adds its partner's copy of them. That is the pair (lane l, lane l ^ o) the butterfly adds for that value at that offset, with the same offsets in the same order, so every value's additions are the butterfly's operand for operand (float addition commutes). The lane's query values live in registers; 5-8 queries run as two calls of up to 4. `STRATA_SCORES_HALVE=0` keeps the old kernel.
2. **`qsa_block_topk_split`** (decode top-k without clusters). Sm_90+ has `block_topk_cluster_kernel`; elsewhere a window's 1-8 queries ran `block_topk_wide_kernel` on 1-8 SMs. Here a query's blocks are cut into chunks of 2,048, and six short launches do four radix passes (each chunk adds its histogram to the query's global one), a count of each chunk's cells above / at the threshold, and the emit. Each pass's CTAs take the previous digit from the complete histogram with `block_topk_kernel`'s rule (a pure function of integer counts), so the threshold, `above`, the tie budget and the emitted cells are the same: identical ids by construction. `STRATA_TOPK_SPLIT=0` keeps the wide kernel; `=1` turns it on for any card (tests).

Both default on sm_75 only (measured there); nothing changes for other cards.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75, PCIe 3.0 x16), i7-6700, 56 GB DDR4-2133, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM clock locked at 1650 MHz, 240 W. `v0.1.43` built from source with `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. Model Q2_0, `--resident-experts`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.7`, `--max-context 524288` (YaRN ×2), `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`.

## Scorer: `QSA_BENCH_DECODE=1 qsa_select_bench CTX Q 50 524288` (new mode: a decode call, hash of the scores)

| context | queries | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32K | 1 / 3 / 4 / 8 | 12.1 / 24.8 / 31.7 / 59.2 µs | 7.7 / 14.5 / 15.0 / 36.0 |
| 131K | 1 / 3 / 4 / 8 | 41.1 / 86.8 / 113.6 / 217.0 | 34.2 / 66.2 / 67.1 / 93.3 |
| 420K | 1 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 | 116.7 / 264.9 / 346.6 / 509.7 / 773.9 | 100.5 / 117.9 / 124.5 / 238.0 / 255.1 |

The same hash before and after in every case (1-8 queries, 32K-524K). At 3-4 queries and 420K it now reads the keys at ~390 GB/s.

## Top-k: `qsa_topk_parity CTX Q 50 524288 0` (a decode call), dispatched time

| context | 1 query | 3 | 6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 9K | 0.034 → 0.032 ms | 0.034 → 0.035 | 0.033 → 0.042 |

## Engine: decode after a long conversation

`--serve`: one 390K request, then two appends of 16K tokens, 256 tokens generated after each (resumed from the conversation, so the decode sits at ~406K and ~422K):

A one-shot 4K run writes the same tokens before and after (same MD5) at the same speed. The server here runs it since 2026-10-12.

pulls.title: sm_75: a faster tiled FP32 block scorer (STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2), and the case for SIMT on RTX 20 by default
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
On Turing the prompt path's QSA block scores run the warp kernel (no TF32 tensor cores, so `qsa_block_scores_tc` falls back), and at long context they dominate the prompt. `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` on an RTX 2080 Ti, appending 16K tokens to a 390K conversation (`--serve`, conversation cache reused):

| phase | default | `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1` |
|---|---:|---:|
| qsa select | 19.0 s (61.5 %) | 3.5 s (23.0 %) |
| whole 16K read | 31.5 s (521 tok/s) | 15.9 s (1031 tok/s) |

This PR adds `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2`: `block_scores_simt_kernel` with 32 queries × 128 blocks per CTA (8 × 8 products per thread instead of 8 × 4) and the next K chunk's loads in registers while the current one is used. Every (row, block) dot is the same `fmaf` chain over k = 0..127 and the same relu sum over the heads, so its scores are **bitwise those of `=1`**. `qsa_select_bench` gets an optional hash of the fast scorer's bytes (`QSA_BENCH_HASH=1`) to show it: the same hash for `=1` and `=2` at 131K, 262K, 400K and 510K.

`=2` stays opt-in like `=1`. The second half of this description is the data I'd offer for turning SIMT on by default on sm_75 (your call, as with `STRATA_BF16_TC`).

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75, PCIe 3.0 x16), i7-6700, 56 GB DDR4-2133, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM clock locked at 1650 MHz, 240 W. `v0.1.43` built from source with `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. Model Q2_0, `--resident-experts`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.7`, `--max-context 524288` (YaRN ×2), `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`.

## Scorer: `qsa_select_bench CTX 256 5 524288`

| context | warp kernel | SIMT=1 | SIMT=2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 131K | 7.66 ms | 1.21 ms | 0.95 ms |
| 262K | 15.25 ms | 2.01 ms | 1.87 ms |
| 400K | 23.24 ms | 2.96 ms | 2.82 ms |
| 510K | 29.60 ms | 3.77 ms | 3.57 ms |

Selections against the warp kernel: 256/256 identical at 262K, 400K and 510K, 255/256 at 131K (0.0002 % of cells). Accuracy against FP64: max error 5.8e-5 vs the warp kernel's 2.1e-5 (2.3e-7 of the score scale).

## Engine, one-shot, `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT` 0 vs 2

Prompt read, same binary, real text (the 256K token file of the benches):

| prompt | default | SIMT=2 | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 49K | 1349 tok/s | 1451 | +7.6 % |
| 98K | 1230 | 1434 | +16.6 % |
| 147K | 1129 | 1407 | +24.6 % |
| 197K | 1042 | 1380 | +32.4 % |

Decode does not change: it scores with `block_scores_multi_kernel`, which this does not touch.

## Quality: teacher-forced, the two paths against each other

The method from #655 (docs/UNSLOTH_Q4.md): a `--serve` engine with `--adapt-every 100000`, the first P tokens read by the prompt path (the path this changes) as one request, then the next 2,048 tokens resumed at P through the verify windows with `--short-read`, `STRATA_LOGPOS` with `STRATA_LOGPOS_TOPK=20` writing every position. Raw text (Don Quixote, Spanish).

| prefix read batched | positions | argmax agreement | KL (off ‖ on) | perplexity off / on | argmax where off's top-2 gap ≥ 0.5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 2,047 | 97.9 % | 0.0099 | 4.552 / 4.620 | 1954 / 1970 |
| 98,304 | 2,047 | 95.3 % | 0.0136 | 5.409 / 5.416 | 1672 / 1686 |

- **Noise floor:** two runs with SIMT off write identical files (KL 0, every position the same), so every difference above is the scorer's summation order.
- **Near-ties:** where the off run's two most likely tokens are at least 0.5 nats apart, the argmax agrees at 1954 of 1970 positions (32K) and 1672 of 1686 (98K). Perplexity moves by +1.5 % and +0.1 %.
- **For scale:** the KL is that of `STRATA_BF16_TC` in #655 (0.0085-0.011) and below the 0.02-0.05 that DETAILS.md lists for other prompt-path changes.
- **First-token logits** after prompts of 48K / 98K / 147K / 197K tokens (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`, full vocabulary): KL 7.5e-4 / 9.6e-3 / 7.3e-6 / 2.9e-4; the same argmax in 3 of 4 (at 98K the two candidates were a near-tie, and SIMT gave the real next token the higher probability).
- **Needles:** 2 of 2 at 352K tokens through the server (`/v1/chat/completions`, thinking off).

The server here runs 0.1.43 with this patch and `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=2` since 2026-10-12.

## Tests

`qsa_parity`: 0 failures. `qsa_select_bench` with `QSA_BENCH_HASH=1`: the same hash for `=1` and `=2` at every context above.

pulls.title: sm_75: a hyper-connection up kernel for 3+ tokens and the staged down kernel in token pairs (bitwise)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
The hyper-connection read is ~19 % of an RTX 2080 Ti's decode GPU time (96 reads per window, 13 MB of BF16 weights each). Two Turing-only changes, both bitwise equal to the kernels they replace (`gr_parity`, `gr_multi_parity`, and the same `fused_gr_bench` hashes):

1. **`gr_up75_kernel`** for 3+ tokens: two batches of 4 rows of `w_up` loaded before the dots (was: one row's load after the previous row's epilogue; ncu showed ~9k of a warp's ~22k cycles waiting on memory), each token's activations read from shared memory once per batch, the 4 xor reductions interleaved, and the rows' last 8 chunks held 4 rows to a `uint4` and shuffled to their lane. Every row's lane sums, xor tree and epilogue are `gr_up_multi_kernel`'s. At 1-2 tokens `gr_up_multi_kernel` is as fast or faster, so it stays there. `STRATA_GR_UP75=0` turns it off.
2. **The staged down kernel takes a token group from `blockIdx.y`**: on sm_75 a launch of 4 or 6 tokens runs as pairs, more blocks for the 41-block grid; every (row, token) is still summed by one warp exactly as before. `STRATA_GR_DOWN_TG=n` forces groups of n (0 = off). One token per group is slower at every T (the weights are read from L2 once per group), so only pairs.

## `fused_gr_bench 300 1 6 8` (cold: 8 weight sets rotated), `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=2`, RTX 2080 Ti at 1650 MHz

Whole read (norm + down + up), µs:

| tokens | before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 37.1 | 37.1 |
| 2 | 43.6 | 43.7 |
| 3 | 53.2 | 50.2 |
| 4 | 64.1 | 57.6 |
| 5 | 76.2 | 69.3 |
| 6 | 86.1 | 70.9 |

## Engine: same binary, switches off / on

One-shot, 256 new tokens, greedy, runs interleaved off / on / on / off (off = `STRATA_GR_UP75=0 STRATA_GR_DOWN_TG=0`; measured with the Turing tables of #2069 on, both arms), decode tok/s:

| prompt | off | on | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4K | 55.79 / 55.74 | 56.09 / 56.07 | +0.6 % |
| 32K | 53.52 / 53.16 | 53.98 / 55.15 | +2.3 % |

At 4K all four runs wrote the same tokens. A verify window here averages ~2.2 tokens, where the kernels change little; the gain grows with the window (T 4-6 above), so it is larger with `--spec` above 4 or a layer split's larger windows.

## Tests

`gr_parity --selftest`: OK. `gr_multi_parity`: 32 cases, 0 failures. `fused_gr_bench`: bitwise equal, the same hashes with the switches on and off.

pulls.title: sm_75: Turing tables for the decode matvecs and the grouped experts (bitwise, decode +6 %)
pulls.author: rafatxf
pulls.body:
Two Turing-only defaults, both bitwise equal to what RTX 20 runs today, both with a switch to turn them off. Measured on an RTX 2080 Ti; I have no other sm_75 card to check them on.

1. **`kIlRows_75`** (`native_mmvq.cu`): the interleaved small-batch matvec kernels with their own table, as Volta and Pascal have. The 2-6 column dense projections of a verify window ran the plain multi-column kernels, which on Turing are bound by `dp4a` throughput from 2 columns on. `STRATA_SM75_IL=0` keeps the plain kernels. No one-column table: the engine's dedicated single-column kernels sum in another order, for a 0.5 % gain.
2. **Expert layout mode 4 on sm_75** (`iq_kernels.cu`, `exp_mode()`): the AMD layouts already build for CUDA; mode 4 is bitwise equal to mode 0 and faster for the window's usual 1-2 entries per expert. Its down projection loses once groups hold 3+ entries, so windows of 4+ tokens (`cap_groups > 30`) keep mode 0 for the down projection. `STRATA_SM75_EXP=0` keeps mode 0; `STRATA_EXP_MODE` still overrides.

## Setup

RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75, PCIe 3.0 x16), i7-6700, 56 GB DDR4-2133, CUDA 13.0, driver 595, SM clock locked at 1650 MHz, 240 W. `v0.1.43` built from source with `-DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`. ## Summary

Adds a results-only community report for a dual Quadro RTX 6000 24 GiB / dual
Xeon Gold 6138 ThinkStation P720 running Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL.

  fresh 4K/16K/32K prefill 840.8/1542.0/1796.7 tok/s.

  tok/s (+11.7%) from 0.1.40.3 to 0.1.43; prefill essentially unchanged.

  interleave outperformed node-0-only memory placement on the tested corpus.

The standard suite and custom comparisons are reported separately. Two launches
per custom configuration/version; three repeats in the standard suite. Configured
context is 262144, largest tested input is 43440 tokens. No long-context recall or
quality evaluation. The version comparison uses release defaults, including
STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7, which can change answers. No claim of byte-identical
output or causal attribution of speedups. CPU vision helper was retained.

The official report's auto-detected CUDA 13.2 field is explicitly identified as
driver capability; the engine was built with CUDA toolkit 12.4 for sm_75.

No engine changes or model files are included. Adds a report link to
docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

Related measurement context: #1900 (opt-in NUMA placement proposal). This report
provides workload-specific measurements; it does not implement that proposal or
claim that GPU-local placement always helps.

pulls.title: Linux AMD: images on the GPU through Vulkan, on a chosen card or the integrated GPU (vision.device)
pulls.author: ChangXiang-SCU
pulls.body:
## Title
Linux AMD: images on the GPU through Vulkan, on a chosen card or the integrated GPU (`vision.device`)

Issue: none. Related: #1768 (Windows AMD, Vulkan encoder in setup), #1521.

## Summary
On Linux with an AMD card, setup builds the image encoder for the CPU only. Built with ggml's Vulkan backend, the same encoder runs on a Radeon through Mesa's RADV driver, 20-30x faster. What was missing is a way to say **which GPU** it runs on. With two cards, mtmd takes the first discrete GPU in Vulkan's order, which can be the engine's own card. On a Ryzen APU it never picks the integrated GPU while a discrete one is present.

This PR adds that choice, plus the build option and the Linux docs:

- `strata-vision --device <GPU>` (with `--gpu`) takes a PCI address (`0000:03:00.0`, or `03:00.0`) or ggml's name for the device (`Vulkan1`, `CUDA0`), and hands it to mtmd as `mtmd_context_params.device`.
- `strata-vision --list-devices` prints the GPUs the build sees and exits.
- `"device"` in the config's `"vision"` section is passed as `--device`. It is a hand-edited key, and a setup run again keeps it.
- `STRATA_VISION_VULKAN` in `tools/vision`: the same two lines as #1768, so the two PRs merge in either order. I checked this with `git merge-tree` against #1768's head.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: how to build and set it up on Linux by hand, with measurements. `docs/DETAILS.md`: the `"device"` key.

Without `"device"` / `--device` nothing changes. On the test PC the default picked the same card as before, and its embeddings were bit-identical to `--device 0000:03:00.0` and `--device Vulkan1`. The new stderr line naming the GPU is printed only with `--device`.

### Measured
**Setup**
- Ryzen 7 7840U (Radeon 780M), 64 GB RAM, 2x RX 6950 XT (gfx1030, 16 GB) on OCuLink.
- Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, Mesa 26.0.8 RADV.
- Engine: 0.1.42, IQ3_XXS, on the 6950 XT at `0000:06:00.0`.
- BF16 mmproj, one 1024x768 picture.
- Times are the encoder's own (`OK ... ms`), 3 runs after the warm-up.

`--list-devices` output on this PC:
```
Vulkan0    0000:6a:00.0  integrated   33054 MiB  AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX)
Vulkan1    0000:03:00.0  discrete     16368 MiB  AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT (RADV NAVI21)
Vulkan2    0000:06:00.0  discrete     16368 MiB  AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT (RADV NAVI21)
```

| Encoder | 300 image tokens | 768 image tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU, 8 threads (AVX-512 build) | 3.0-3.8 s | 11.0-11.2 s |
| RX 6950 XT, the other card (`"device": "0000:03:00.0"`) | 0.15 s | 0.36-0.37 s |
| Radeon 780M, integrated (`"device": "0000:6a:00.0"`) | 0.79-0.80 s | 2.11-2.12 s |
| RX 6950 XT, the engine's card, `--vram-reserve-mib 700` | 0.51-0.52 s | 3.0-3.5 s |
| RX 6950 XT, the engine's card, `--vram-reserve-mib 1300` | 0.15 s | 0.36 s |

- **Sharing the engine's card:** the encoder needs about 1 GB at 1,024 image tokens. With the default 700 MiB reserve it still runs, with no error, but 3-10x slower. With 1300 it runs at full speed, and the expert cache has 3,593 slots instead of 3,954 (5.86 instead of 6.45 GiB).
- **Accuracy vs the CPU encoder:** the per-token cosine is 0.9997 on average on both GPUs. The lowest single token is 0.953 (6950 XT) and 0.892 (780M). The two 6950 XT give bit-identical embeddings.
- **End to end through the server**, with `"device"` set in the config: the same correct answer (three shapes, their colours, the text `ZX-4096`), in 8.8 s on the 6950 XT, 10.7 s on the 780M, and 19.7 s on the CPU.

## What changed
- `tools/vision/strata_vision.cpp`:
  - `--device` and `--list-devices`.
  - An `ERR` line on stdout, as for the other start errors, when the GPU is not found or `--device` is given without `--gpu`.
  - One stderr line naming the chosen GPU (only with `--device`).

- `serve/server.py`: `Vision` passes `vision.device` as `--device`, only when it is set.
- `serve/test_server.py`: `--device` is passed only when set.
- `tools/test_setup_config.py`: a setup run again keeps `"device"`.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: "Images on the GPU through Vulkan (Linux, by hand)", and the two lines that said images are CPU-only now link to it.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the `"device"` key, next to `"cuda_device"`.

`setup.py` is untouched; #1768 already adds `--vision gpu` for AMD there.

## How I checked
**Builds of `tools/vision`**
- CPU and Vulkan (Linux, GCC): on the PC above.
- CUDA 12.8, `sm_120`: on a 4x RTX 5090 Linux box.

**Runtime**
- Vulkan, `--device` by address and by name: on the 6950 XTs and the 780M, as measured above.
- CUDA:
  - `--list-devices` gives `CUDA0..3` with `0000:01:00.0`, `0000:02:00.0`, `0000:41:00.0` and `0000:85:00.0`.
  - `--device 01:00.0` and `--device CUDA3` select those cards.
  - With `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2`, the card at `0000:41:00.0` becomes `CUDA0`. That renumbering is why the address is the stable name.
  - That box has no model files, so the CUDA run stopped at loading the model, after the device was chosen.
- CPU build: `--list-devices` says there is no GPU, and `--device` without `--gpu` ends with an `ERR` line. An unknown address ends with `ERR no GPU ... here`.

**Tests**
- On `main` + this PR: `python -m unittest serve.test_server` (297), `tools/test_setup_config.py` (15) and `tools/test_setup_amd.py` (36) pass.
- The same changes on the 0.1.42 install pass `serve.test_server` (292).

## Extra Notes
- **Not tested:**
  - Windows. #1768 covers the Windows build. `--device` uses the same ggml calls there, but I have not run it.
  - Other Radeon generations.
  - A Vulkan encoder beside a multi-GPU layer split.
- **Possible follow-up**, not in this PR: setup could write `"device"` itself, choosing a card the engine does not use or the integrated GPU, and raise the reserve when it has to share.

pulls.title: QSA decode: the window's block scores with the queries in registers and six shuffles per block (STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1, opt-in, bit-exact)
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change).

## Summary
`STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` (opt-in, off by default) computes the verify window's QSA **block scores** (decode, up to 4 queries)
with a kernel that keeps the queries' slices in registers and reduces the four heads with six shuffles per block instead
of twenty. Scores and top-k ids are **bit for bit** the multi kernel's (`qsa_rows_bench --rows`, `memcmp`, 16 cases per
card). CUDA only; the prompt path (#1825's territory) and HIP are not touched.

## Why
In a 131k decode the QSA kernel that grows most with the window's rows is `block_scores_multi_kernel`: ~20 us more per
call for every row of the window on both an RTX 2080 Ti and an RTX 3060 (nsys, 8 QSA layers on the second card of a
layer split). The keys are already read once for all the queries; the cost per row is in the shared-memory and
shuffle pipes - per (key block, query) 4 x `LDS.128` of the query slices and 5 shuffles per head (20 per block and
query), at 32,769 blocks ~15-20 us of issue per query.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu`: `block_scores_rows_kernel<NQ>` (NQ = 1..4): the NQ queries' slices (4 heads x 4
  floats per lane) in registers for the whole kernel (44 / 63 / 78 / 94 registers, no stack); the four heads' lane
  products reduced with a scatter that keeps `warp_sum`'s pairings (xor 16 and 8 leave one head per lane, then 4, 2, 1)
  and gathered on lane 0 in head order. Tail block and the `+1e9` as before. `qsa_block_scores` takes it for the
  calls without `active_blocks` with up to 4 queries when `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1`; otherwise, or beyond 4 queries, the
  multi kernel runs as before.
- `include/strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp`: the `rows` entry.
- `src/kernels/qsa_rows_bench.cpp` (`EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`): what the T rows of a verification window cost in a QSA layer's
  decode kernels at a long context (block scores, top-k, attention over each row's selection, indexer append;
  synthetic data at the real geometry, int8 pools, no model); `--rows` runs the new kernel against the multi kernel,
  scores and top-k ids bit for bit at T = 1..4 at 131k and at a short context with a full tail block, and prints both
  kernels' microseconds.
- `docs/QSAROWS.md`.

## Bit for bit
Every addition in the new reduction adds the same two operands of the same `warp_sum` level (float addition commutes),
the product expression is the same text in the same file, the relus are summed in head order. `qsa_rows_bench --rows`:
8 cases per card (T 1-4 x two contexts), 0 differ, on sm_75 and sm_86. In the engine the greedy text and the drafter's
acceptance are unchanged.

## Measurements
Hardware: RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) + RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
IQ3_XXS pack, 131k context, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8`.

`qsa_block_scores`, us per call at 131k (both kernels read the same pooled keys):

| | T=1 | T=2 | T=3 | T=4 | per row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 2080 Ti, multi (reference) | 47.2 | 56.9 | 78.2 | 101.2 | +18.0 |
| RTX 2080 Ti, `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` | **36.2** | **38.0** | **49.2** | **54.6** | **+6.1** |
| RTX 3060, multi | 73.4 | 109.4 | 151.9 | 193.5 | +40.0 |
| RTX 3060, `STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1` | **63.3** | **75.5** | **98.0** | **130.2** | **+22.3** |

In the engine (nsys): per window the second card saves 0.09 ms at T=1 and 0.37 ms at T=4 (8 QSA layers), the first
0.04 / 0.25 ms (4 layers). End to end, deterministic 131k bench (forced tokens and window sizes, 1024 decode tokens,
three interleaved runs lever on / off / on): **+3.2% and +0.1%** decode tokens/s in the two B arms, text identical.
Together with the companion experts lever (`STRATA_EXPDEC=1`, separate PR): +2.9%.

Ported and validated on v0.1.43 (micro-bench bit-exact on both cards; our full stack on 0.1.43 matches our 0.1.42
daily on the forced 131k bench).

## Risks / limits
- Off by default; `STRATA_QSA_ROWS` must be exactly `1`. Only the decode calls with <= 4 queries and no `active_blocks`
  change; everything else runs the kernels it ran before.
- On the RTX 3060 at T=4 the kernel is at 94 registers (2 CTAs per SM); a two-pass version of 2 queries would stay at 63
  if that card matters more.
- Not measured on sm_80/89/120 or HIP.



**Scope.** The gain comes from VRAM-resident routed experts / decode QSA scores on Turing/Ampere setups where these kernels are a large share of the verify window. On rigs where most routed experts are off-GPU (e.g. 4x RTX 5080 16 GB, see the test in #2058) the window is dominated by stage hand-offs and host experts, and the levers measure neutral.

pulls.title: Verify window: the routed experts' gate/up with the group's q8_1 rows in shared memory (STRATA_EXPDEC=1, opt-in, bit-exact)
pulls.author: imanu86
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change).

## Summary
`STRATA_EXPDEC=1` (opt-in, off by default) runs the verify window's VRAM-resident routed experts' **gate/up** through a
kernel that keeps the group's q8_1 activation rows in shared memory and computes several rows per lane. Same kernels
otherwise, same launch order, and the output is **bit for bit** the default kernels' (`expdec_bench` checks it with
`memcmp` on every cell). CUDA only; HIP and the prompt path are not touched.

## Why
`native_gu_multi_kernel` already decodes each weight part once per block and applies it to the group's 1-4 entries,
but the apply re-reads each entry's q8_1 block from global memory with 9 scattered 4-byte loads (36-byte blocks: a
warp's load touches 16-32 sectors). Measured with nsys on a 131k decode (RTX 2080 Ti, stage 1 of a layer split), an
extra row of the window costs about 60% of a whole expert - ~1.6 us against ~2.6 us per expert and layer - although it
reads nothing from DRAM. That is most of the gate/up kernel's slope with the window's rows (+0.86 ms per row).

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: `expdec_gu_kernel<TG, R, MINB>` (gate/up IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ2_S at
  n_embd 2560) and `expdec_down_kernel<TD, R>` (down Q2_0 at n_ff 640; IQ4_NL with `STRATA_EXPDEC_D20=1`). The group's
  entries are staged 4 at a time in a layout where a call's 8 words are two conflict-free 16-byte loads (IQ4_NL: two
  8-byte loads) and the fp16 block scale is already a float; R rows per lane share the activation words; a block takes
  `rb` rows (auto from the launch's groups) instead of 16; the IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S codebooks are staged in shared memory like
  the IQ2 ones. `Split<TG>::apply_u` is `apply` on the block's words; `Split<18>/<21>::load<true>` read the staged grid.
  `native_expert_grouped` takes the new kernels when the lever is on and the layout matches, else the default ones.
- `include/strata/kernels/iq_kernels.hpp`: `native_expert_set_expdec`, `native_expert_set_expdec_params` /
  `native_expert_expdec_params` (`NativeExpertExpdecParams`), `native_expert_expdec_takes`.
- `src/kernels/expdec_bench.cpp` (`EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`): the default kernels against EXPDEC at T 1-4 on 10 format pairs,
  synthetic blobs read cold from a >= 96 MB pool, `memcmp` of the output, median of 5 x `reps` calls, per phase.
- `docs/EXPERTDEC.md`.

Knobs (environment, read at startup): `STRATA_EXPDEC_R` (gate/up rows per lane, 1 | 2, default 1), `STRATA_EXPDEC_DR`
(down, 1 | 2 | 4, default 4), `STRATA_EXPDEC_MINB` (gate/up `__launch_bounds__` min blocks per SM, 4 | 2, default 4),
`STRATA_EXPDEC_RB` / `_DRB` (rows per block, 0 = auto), `STRATA_EXPDEC_MINBLK` (the auto rule's minimum blocks, 800),
`STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN` (the down too, default 0), `STRATA_EXPDEC_D20` (IQ4_NL down too, default 0). The first launch of
each (role, format) logs one line (`strata expdec: CUDA1 gate/up type 21: expdec_gu_kernel R 1 MINB 4, ... captured
into a graph`).

**The down stays separate on purpose.** In the micro-bench the Q2_0 down with EXPDEC is 0.65-0.85x of the default, but
in the engine (nsys, two captures with two block geometries) it was about 10% *slower* than the default kernel, which
already keeps the group's h rows in shared memory; IQ4_NL showed no gain in either. So `STRATA_EXPDEC=1` takes the
gate/up only and `STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=1` is a separate opt-in for whoever wants to measure it on another card.

## Bit for bit
For every (row, entry) the sum is the default kernel's tree (`row_dot_80_sub16`: lane t of a 16-lane sub-warp does
calls t, t+32, t+64 into `s` and t+16, t+48 into `s16`, `s = __fadd_rn(s, s16)`, butterfly xor 8-4-2-1; `row_dot_40_sub8`
/ `row_dot_20_sub16` for the downs). The same lane does the same calls in the same order with the same integer and
float operations on the same words; the entries of a group are independent, so the staging and the rows-per-lane /
rows-per-block choices only change which lane computes what. `expdec_bench`: `identical` on all 1,280 cells (10 pairs x
T 1-4 x 2 window shapes x 8 choices x 2 cards). In the engine the greedy text is unchanged.

## Measurements
Hardware: RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (sm_75) + RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 12.6, layer split (3060: layers 0-15,
2080 Ti: 16-47 + head), `--pipeline-windows 2`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS pack, 131k context.

Micro-bench, gate/up phase, us per call with 20 distinct experts (the shape of a real window), `def` -> ratio with EXPDEC:

| card | format | T=1 | T=2 | T=3 | T=4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 2080 Ti | IQ3_S | 72 / 0.73x | 112 / 0.79x | 124 / 0.75x | 138 / 0.74x |
| RTX 2080 Ti | IQ3_XXS | 61 / 0.79x | 95 / 0.84x | 107 / 0.79x | 119 / 0.77x |
| RTX 2080 Ti | IQ2_XXS / IQ2_XS / IQ2_S | 42-62 / 0.75-0.98x | 74-83 / 0.92x | 86-96 / 0.86-0.87x | 97-109 / 0.84x |
| RTX 3060 | IQ3_S | 74 / 1.09x | 144 / 0.99x | 154 / 0.89x | 174 / 0.87x |
| RTX 3060 | IQ3_XXS | 78 / 0.89x | 132 / 0.92x | 143 / 0.90x | 162 / 0.82x |
| RTX 3060 | IQ2_XXS / IQ2_XS / IQ2_S | 60-68 / 0.90-1.04x | 112-118 / 0.89-1.00x | 119-136 / 0.89-0.95x | 132-149 / 0.87-0.91x |

Per-expert / per-entry cost (us per layer call, RTX 2080 Ti, IQ3_S): 5.20 / 1.26 default -> 3.73 / 0.64.

nsys in the engine (96 verify windows, median kernel time per window at T = 1 / 2 / 3 / 4):
RTX 2080 Ti gate/up 1.60 / 2.58 / 3.51 / 4.16 ms -> **1.42 / 2.07 / 2.75 / 3.20 ms (-11 / -20 / -22 / -23%)**, slope per
row +0.86 -> +0.60 ms; RTX 3060 gate/up 0.77 / 1.43 / 1.97 / 2.23 -> 0.80 / 1.21 / 1.83 / 1.84 ms.

End to end, deterministic 131k bench (forced tokens and window sizes, 1024 decode tokens, three interleaved runs
lever on / off / on): **+1.1%** decode tokens/s (+0.0 and +2.1 in the two B arms, no B arm below A), text identical.
With the companion QSA scores lever (`STRATA_QSA_ROWS=1`, separate PR) on top: +2.9% together. The expert kernels are
~20% of the critical card's window and EXPDEC takes ~20% of that, so the end-to-end number is small by construction.

Ported and validated on v0.1.43 (micro-bench bit-exact on both cards; our full stack on 0.1.43 matches our 0.1.42
daily on the forced 131k bench).

## Risks / limits
- Off by default; a format or geometry outside the list keeps the default kernel for that role; `STRATA_OLD_IQ_MMVQ=1`
  turns it off as it turns the multi kernels off. Captured graphs keep the kernels they captured.
- Shared memory per block: 11.5 KB of activations + 1-8 KB of codebook (IQ2_S: 19.7 KB); registers 64 with the default
  `MINB` 4 (116-128 with `2`). Checked with `cuobjdump -res-usage` on sm_75 and sm_86.
- Not measured on sm_80/89/120 or on HIP (CUDA only). The weight side (the 8-9 two-byte loads per call and row) is
  untouched and is the next step; T=1 gains less (the flat cost is the weight side).



**Scope.** The gain comes from VRAM-resident routed experts / decode QSA scores on Turing/Ampere setups where these kernels are a large share of the verify window. On rigs where most routed experts are off-GPU (e.g. 4x RTX 5080 16 GB, see the test in #2058) the window is dominated by stage hand-offs and host experts, and the levers measure neutral.

pulls.title: serve: an opt-in "stream_all_tool_args" sends a tool call's non-string argument in pieces as the model writes it (#1666)
pulls.author: psqq
pulls.body:
Resolves #1666 (the keep-alive that already covers the idle timeout is in main as 14b9dd2e; this is the
other half: the argument itself stops being silence)

## Summary
A tool-call parameter whose declared type is not a string - an array, an object, a number - is held until
`</parameter>` and goes out as one `tool_args` piece, so an app that shows the arguments as they arrive sits on
`{"edits":` for minutes and then shows the finished call at once. `"stream_all_tool_args": true` in
`strata-<model>.json` sends that text as it is written, the way a string parameter already does. Off by default.

## What changed
- `serve/frontend.py`: `OutputParser` gains `stream_all_args`. In the `raw` state the value's JSON text passes
  through as it arrives, holding back a possible partial `</parameter>` (the same `_hold` the `str` state uses) and a
  candidate end whose follower has not arrived yet, so #210 still holds: a `</parameter>` inside the value stays part
  of the value. When the parameter ends, only what has not gone out yet is sent. `_close_scan` closes a call cut
  inside such a value with the rest of that text, not with a JSON string of it.
- `serve/server.py`: the config key `stream_all_tool_args` (must be true or false) reaches the parser.
- `serve/runconfig.py`: the key is editable from the About tab's Model settings card.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: a bullet with the measurements; the streaming bullet now says a non-string parameter waits for
  its end unless the switch is on.
- `serve/test_tool_args_stream.py`: 8 cases.

What it leaves alone: without the key the stream is byte-identical to before; string parameters are untouched; the
final `tool_call` of a call that was streamed is still not sent again, so the pieces a client joins are the
arguments; the value is still parsed and checked at the end, so a broken argument is still the error it was. With it
on, what the model wrote is what goes out, so the whitespace is no longer normalized.

## Extra Notes
Parser, an `edit` call whose `edits` is an array of two objects (217 characters), fed at a token width of 8: 15
argument pieces with one of 217 without the switch, 44 pieces with none longer than 9 with it. End to end over
`/v1/chat/completions` with `MockEngine` (one token per step): 17 argument deltas, largest 247 characters, without
the switch; 263 deltas, largest 8, with it; `finish_reason: tool_calls` and the joined pieces equal to the reported
arguments in both cases. On a real agent turn (Qwen3.8 Flash-Next IQ3_S, an `edit` call with two edits): 27 argument
deltas, 26 of them carrying 78 characters in all and one carrying 3,145 - 97% of the arguments in a single piece.
Checked with `python -m unittest serve.test_tool_args_stream serve.test_parser_track serve.test_reasoning_tools
serve.test_reasoning_rescue serve.test_frontend serve.test_runconfig serve.test_structured` (87 tests, OK) and
`serve.test_server` (291 tests; the only errors are the three that import the `regex` module, the same on an
unmodified tree). Not tested: Windows and AMD paths beyond their suites.

*🤖 Fully generated by an LLM (qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s)*

pulls.title: hip: gfx103x creates the MTP drafter's side stream again (RX 6800, Windows: 7.9K prompt 584–596 → 798–808 tok/s)
pulls.author: did-technomancer
pulls.body:
Fixes the prompt-read regression on gfx103x since 0.1.40.2 (#2055): on those cards the engine creates the MTP
drafter's `side_` stream again. Other HIP cards stay as they are.

## What changes

`MtpDrafter::load` (`src/core/mtp.cpp`): on HIP the `side_` stream is created when the card's architecture starts with
`gfx103`; `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=1` / `=0` turns it on or off on any HIP card. The two events (`sh_fork_`, `sh_join_`)
are not created on HIP, as after #1240. CUDA is unchanged. Plus a paragraph in `docs/AMD_HIP.md`.

## Why

#1240 (`ac52c2c7`) dropped the stream and the two events on HIP, because nothing uses them and on an R9700 they slowed
prompts. On an RX 6800 under Windows it is the other way round: the stream's existence alone speeds prompts up, the
events change nothing, and all of the difference is in the `wait copy` phase (the bisect, the 0.1.40–0.1.43 table and
the phase breakdown are in #2055).

## Measurements

```text
GPU      AMD Radeon RX 6800 16 GB (gfx1030), two monitors on it
CPU      AMD Ryzen 7 5700X3D, 8 cores / 16 threads, AVX2, no AVX-512
RAM      64 GB DDR4-3200 (4x16)
OS       Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 26H2 (build 26300)
ROCm     10.2.0a20260930 (TheRock), rocBLAS 5.8.0.efafc1c1
Engine   this branch (main 7695859a + this commit), tools\hip\build_windows.bat, STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1030
Model    Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768, 128K context, MTP --spec 4,
         --draft-vocab cyrillic, --prefill 8192; STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1
```

One binary, one server per row, the arms alternating; the prompts are `serve/server.py`'s code, temperature 0:

| | 7.9K prompt, tok/s | 30.4K prompt, tok/s | 3 prompts of ~850 tokens, tok/s | Decode en / uk / code, tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=0` | 584 | 553 | 134–144 | 45.3 / 48.8 / 49.7 |
| unset (the stream exists) | **798** | **863** | 163–168 | 44.3 / 53.8 / 46.0 |
| `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=0` | 596 | 600 | 146–164 | 43.0 / 49.5 / 47.3 |
| unset (the stream exists) | **808** | **855** | 158–180 | 44.6 / 50.0 / 50.2 |

The 7.9K prompt reads 35–37% faster and the 30.4K one 43–56% faster. Decode is within the run-to-run spread.

## Not checked

- gfx103x on Linux and with several cards: this is one card under Windows. 2x RX 6900 XT on Linux in #1272 already
  showed the opposite sign for `STRATA_SH_STREAM`, so a number from there is needed; `STRATA_MTP_SIDE_STREAM=0` gives
  0.1.43's behaviour back.
- R9700 and other HIP cards: nothing changes for them, and I cannot test them.
- The tests (`ctest`) were not run: the build here is `strata` and `strata-device` only.
- Why an unused stream's existence removes `wait copy`: I don't know.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB / 64 GB RAM, v0.1.43 IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS

Adds Sonny's Labs community measurements for **Strata v0.1.43** (`7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`) on one **RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB**, Ryzen 5 5600G, **64 GB installed RAM** (58.8 GiB OS-usable), PCIe Gen3 x16 and NVMe.

All eight original README/results files are byte-identical to the generated outputs, with verification hashes; separate supplements provide source/image/model pins, hardware, settings and cache-state details. Engine compiled before runtime using CUDA 13.0.0 / SM120; LOW_RAM resident mode, int8 KV and requested spec 4.
