Official speed outputs do not establish correctness; separately scored workloads and further limitations are linked in the [technical report](https://report5.firetussin.com/).

Validation: original-output SHA256 agreement, all submission checksum entries verified, sensitive-identifier/credential-pattern review, and results-only diff review. No engine/source changes, model files, packs, container archives or large telemetry. Hardware/software descriptions remain for reproducibility. Generated upstream RAM wording is clarified in the umbrella report without changing original files.

pulls.title: batch-groups: a cold prompt read no longer pauses every stream for its whole length, longest pause 12.2 -> 4.2 s on 2x RTX 5090 (opt-in)
pulls.author: SuperDistance
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Related: #1906 (streams stop for a whole prompt read with `--batch-groups` > 1; its question 3 asks why
`batch_read_piece` returns 0 for pipelined groups; the full re-reads it also reports are a separate matter) and #1603 (a comment there reports the same stop: a 160K read with
`--batch-groups auto` left the other slot at 0.03 tok/s; the hang in its title is a separate matter). #1504 (closed) read
in pieces on `--batch-groups 1` only and left the pipelined path out; its thread asked for the follow-up TTFT during a
45K read, measured below. Nearby: #1441 (`--prefill-pipe` chunk sizes; pieces here are whole chunks of any size).
Searched 2026-10-12 for `batch_read_piece`, `piped`, `pipelined`, `BYIELD`, `batch-groups`, `DECODE_SHARE` and `stall`.

## Motivation
I run Strata on 2x RTX 5090 (`--batch-groups 2`) as the backend for Hermes agents doing development work. Each time a new
agent joins, its first request is a long cold prompt (system prompt, tools, repository context), and every agent that is
already decoding stops until that prompt has been read. With several agents at work this happens often, so the running
streams keep stalling for seconds and their tokens per second swing between full speed and zero.

This change lets a cold prompt join smoothly: the running streams keep getting tokens while it is read, and the new
agent's first token comes a little later in exchange. Like an incremental garbage collector, it turns one long
stop-the-world pause into several short ones; the total time paused stays about the same.

## Summary
**Why it matters:** with a layer split and `--batch-groups` > 1, a prompt is read in one `sp.run`. Every decoding slot
waits for the whole prompt, `STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE` has no effect, and `BYIELD` is never taken. On one GPU the slots
already decode between a prompt's chunks, and a short request can take over a long read.

**How:** `STRATA_PIPED_READ_PIECE=N` reads the prompt in pieces of N tokens (whole chunks, 1 to 32). Each piece is one
pipelined run, so only its end drains the pipeline. At each piece's end:
- a waiting request with a prompt under half as long can take over, with the existing `BYIELD` code (the drained pipeline
  is what a give-way needs);
- the decoding slots run through the pipeline for `STRATA_BATCH_DECODE_SHARE` x the piece's time, capped and floored by
  `STRATA_PIPED_DECODE_MAX_MS` / `STRATA_PIPED_DECODE_MIN_MS`.

A read that starts right after another such read gives the slots one decode budget first. Unset: one run, as before.

**Measured** on 2x RTX 5090 (Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, split 25, `--batch 6 --batch-groups 2 --resident-experts`, k8v4, 262K,
`--kv-resident 32768`): v0.1.43 vs this change, both built here, a fresh engine per run, `STRATA_PIPED_DECODE_MAX_MS=400`.
Release and 32K: median of 5 interleaved pairs (ABBA); 16K: one run.

Four streams decoding while two cold prompts join (64K, then 32K 6 s later):

| | release | 32K pieces | 16K pieces |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| longest pause of a stream | 12.2 s | **4.2 s** | **2.6 s** |
| total time paused per stream | 12.2 s | 13.3 s | 15.7 s |
| tokens the streams got meanwhile | 289 | **527** | **793** |
| the two prompts' TTFT | 6.9 / 6.1 s | 8.1 / 8.5 s | 10.5 / 12.0 s |
| token rate of the run | 173 tok/s | 166 tok/s | 154 tok/s |

Nothing decoding, a cold 45K prompt (#1504's test, median of 3):

| | release | 32K pieces | 16K pieces |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| one-line question sent 1 s in: its TTFT | 5.4 s | **3.6 s** | **1.8 s** |
| the 45K prompt's TTFT | 6.0 s | 7.3 s | 8.0 s |
| the same prompt read alone | 5.7 s | 6.4 s | 7.1 s |

The 32K pause was lower in 5 of 5 pairs. Total time paused counts gaps over 0.5 s (mean of the four streams).

**Where upstream's default is better:** throughput and the long prompt's TTFT. Each piece ends with a drained pipeline:
the joining prompts' TTFT is 27% longer with 32K pieces (73% with 16K), the token rate is 4% lower (within run-to-run
spread), and an idle 45K read takes 12% longer (25% with 16K), since pieces are also taken when nothing decodes. Leave it
off when aggregate tokens or one client's long prompts matter most; turn it on when a multi-second stall is worse than a
later first token. Single-chunk pieces would cost the read the most (#1504's "65% longer read").

**Next to #2326:** #2326 reads the prompt on a thread of its own beside the decoding, instead of in pieces. Where it can
run it does better (longest pause 0.97 s against 4.6 s), but it stays off with the GGUF read in place (setup's mode for
Unsloth's files when RAM is short), the helper caches, `--pcie-mode dma` and prompts with pictures. There, and on hosts
where the CPU is the limit (these pieces used 4.7 cores during a read against 16.6 for #2326), this change is the option.
It pays off least with a coarse prompt chunk: each piece costs one pipeline fill, about 7.5 s with superniker's
26,624-token chunks. The two don't depend on each other; with both in, #2326 reads where it can and the pieces apply
elsewhere.

## What changed
- `include/strata/program/batch_read.hpp` (header-only): `piped_read_piece()`, `piped_decode_budget_ms()`,
  `piped_read_lead_in()`.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`, `read_part`: the piecewise read on the pipelined path; at each piece's end the existing
  `BSTOP` / `BYIELD` handling, then `pump(true)` for the budget and `pipe_drain()`; the lead-in; one stderr line per piece
  and lead-in. Unset: `batch_read_piece()` as before.
- `tests/program/batch_read_test.cpp`: each new function (rounding, the 32-chunk cap, chunk 0, cap and floor, lead-in).
- `docs/BATCHING.md`: the opt-in's section, and how to run `batch_interleave_test.py` on pipelined groups.
- `tools/piped_read_join_bench.py` (new, stdlib only): the scenarios above (`--scenarios two_joiners,followup,read_alone
  --repeat N`) and `--determinism`.

## Extra Notes
**Text equality:** upstream's `tools/batch_interleave_test.py` passes every step with 16K pieces: C's 40K read goes in
three pieces while A and B decode, D gives way at 16,384 tokens (`YIELDED 2 16384`) while E is admitted, and every request
equals its solo tokens. The release fails step 4 (D never gives way). Settings: `--long 40000 --pcie-frac 0
--adapt-every 1000000 --no-prefill-borrow`, plus `--batch 4 --batch-groups 2` (3 slots make one group) and no
conversation cache (it would restore D in step 4). With the variables unset, both builds gave the same SHA-256 for six
greedy answers, twice each, under `--prompt-cache 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --pcie-frac 0` (DETAILS.md), and ran at the same
speed (45K read alone 5.66 vs 5.69 s, median of 3; two-joiner pause 12.2 s on both). Text equality, not bit-exactness, and
greedy only.

**Run-to-run spread:** the longest pause was 12.16-12.23 s for the release in all five runs and 4.19-4.22 s for 32K in
four. In the fifth, the 64K prompt's first piece took 9.3 s instead of 3.95 s before any slot decoded (so not this
change's code), giving a 9.5 s pause and 13.5 / 13.9 s TTFTs; it stays in the medians. Token rate ranged 169-180 tok/s
(release) and 136-174 tok/s (32K).

**Built** on one Windows 11 PC: CUDA 13.0 (VS 2022, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120 -DSTRATA_PORTABLE=ON`) and HIP via
`tools\hip\build_windows.bat tests` (ROCm 10.2.0a20260930, gfx1100). `batch_read_test` passes on both and
`batch_groups_test` on HIP; the only new warnings are the MSVC `getenv` notes the file's other `std::getenv` calls also
print. SYCL is untouched: it builds its own `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp` and never includes `batch_read.hpp`. Three
commits, rebased onto v0.1.44.1 (`296b59d2`); the numbers above are from v0.1.43.

pulls.title: bench: 4× V100-16GB Q4_K_XL (sm_70 MMQ + bandwidth-proportional layer split)
pulls.author: zealotq
pulls.body:
## Hardware
4× Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB (sm_70), 2× Xeon E5-2696 v4, 247 GiB RAM; asymmetric PCIe x8/x16/x8/x16 (H2D 6.15/11.89/5.90/10.29 GB/s).

## Model & config
Unsloth Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL, native-experts pack (--compat-bf16), layer-split 9,25,34 (per-card to PCIe bandwidth), --spec 4, int8 KV, STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1.

## Results
- 2K prefill 458.5 tok/s (median, 5 runs); 81K prefill 2989 tok/s (median, 3 runs)
- Needle recall 6/6 at 32k and 128k (tools/needle_bench.py)

## Main findings
1. `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON` gives ZERO prefill gain on sm_70: the path is confirmed taken (slot borrow 1635 vs 1606), but prefill is unchanged because the bottleneck is PCIe streaming of non-resident experts, not the dequant→FP16 GPU work (the official 4× figure is sm_86 int8-TC only).
2. Bandwidth-proportional layer split (11,25,37 → 9,25,34) = +12.9% prefill and stabilizes repeated 81k requests.
3. **2026-10-13 update — the remaining 81K collapse is root-caused: conversation-cache parking.** The 2026-10-12 report left one quirk open ("81K traffic could leave the host degraded; survived restarts, cleared only on reboot"). It is not the host. `--conversation-cache-mib 16384` parks a **2.558 GiB KV snapshot after every long request** (2.6–3.2 s each) and `reused_kv_bytes` is **0** every time — fresh prompts never read it back. With `--conversation-cache-mib 0 --conversation-cache-slots 0`, 81K prefill is flat at **3092–3098 tok/s across 8 runs (+10.5%)** instead of dropping to ~2801 from run 2 onward (`bench/results/2026-10-13-community-4x-v100-16gb-convcache`). KV-streaming hit rate and expert-cache hit rate are unchanged, so neither is the cause. Scope note: this is about *fresh* long prompts; on continuing multi-turn traffic the cache does pay off (cf. #2181, 68.7% hit over an agent session).

## Limitations
TTFT approximated from engine-log read time; decode single-session; needle covers 32k/128k only. The engine is now a **0.1.43.1** source build (was 0.1.42), still with `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`.

pulls.title: bench: RTX 3070 MTP control-decision latency and break-even
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Adds matched RTX 3070 results for known-length control outputs, with a chart, a reproducible break-even estimate, raw per-token arrivals and a capacity-aware rule of thumb.

![MTP on/off control-decision chart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/a557e683e8682dc287b97bd05106e16cec9c71c8/bench/results/2026-10-12-community-rtx3070-mtp-crossover/control-decisions/control-decisions.png)

For fresh inputs of 48K, 64K, 96K and 128K, MTP off completed the measured 1,000-token request 39.7%–47.5% sooner. The 10- and 100-token comparisons use recorded arrival prefixes from those 1,000-token runs. They also favor off; they are not separate capped requests.

**Rule of thumb for this workload:** use MTP off for 10, 100 and 1,000 output tokens. The measured 1,000-token decode gain repays MTP’s added prefill at an estimated output length near one-sixth of fresh input (about input tokens ÷ 6): approximately 8,163 / 10,976 / 16,011 / 21,939 tokens at 48K / 64K / 96K / 128K. These are constant-rate projections, not measured crossings. At 128K input, only 2,048 output slots remain in the tested context, so the projected crossing does not fit. Check context capacity; consider MTP on only well beyond the projected crossing, then verify on the actual workload.

Ten or 100 separate uncached 1K decisions still favor off because every request pays prefill again. Cached-prefix decisions were not measured. A 10K answer is only a small on candidate at 48K in the projection; 100K examples exceed the tested capacity for every input length.

Evidence: one matched pair at each input length, warm engines, no prompt reuse, exactly 1,000 output tokens per run. The model is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, INT8 KV; this is not a Q4 result. Outputs differ between modes, and no quality claim is made. Longer-answer calculations assume constant decode rates and are explicitly marked as estimates.

- [Follow-up report, methods, estimates and raw data](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/tree/a557e683e8682dc287b97bd05106e16cec9c71c8/bench/results/2026-10-12-community-rtx3070-mtp-crossover/control-decisions)
- [Earlier 4K/16K/64K cohort and chart](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/tree/a557e683e8682dc287b97bd05106e16cec9c71c8/bench/results/2026-10-12-community-rtx3070-mtp-crossover)

Validation: both cohort checkers and the decision-model verifier pass; the PNG was visually inspected; staged git diff --check passed. Documentation and measurements only; no inference defaults changed.

pulls.title: serve: fix potential race in NoLeakedSampler during test runs
pulls.author: clothespin
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none of its own. The flake was noted as pre-existing in the validation notes of #1327, #1563, #1840 and #2023;
#1840 fixed it for its own new test file only.

## Summary
`NoLeakedSampler.test_server_close_ends_the_sampler` in `serve/test_responses.py` fails now and then with
`AssertionError: 1 != 2` (`serve/test_responses.py:284`). The server is not leaking anything; the test was counting
another test's thread. This changes the test only. `serve/` code is unchanged.

## What changed
`serve/test_responses.py` (+7 -8).

The test counted every thread in the process whose name ends in "(_loop)". `Telemetry.close()`
(`serve/telemetry.py:420`) only sets the stop flag, so the sampler of a server an earlier test closed can still be
taking its last reading when this test starts. The count before `serve()` is then 1, that thread ends while the new
server starts, and the count after is 1, not 2.

The test now notes the threads alive before `serve()` and takes the one new "(_loop)" thread as its own server's
sampler. After `server_close()` it waits up to 5 s for that thread to end, the same limit the old loop used.

Checked on Linux (Arch, Python from the repo's `.venv`):
- `python -m unittest serve.test_responses`, 30 runs each: 2 failures before (both this test, `1 != 2`), 0 after.
- With the failing order forced (an earlier server's sampler still alive when the test starts): fails 3 of 3 before,
  passes 3 of 3 after.
- With `Telemetry.close()` made a no-op, so a server really leaks its sampler: the test fails before and after, so it
  still catches the leak it was written for.
- Full discovery (`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"`): 706 tests, 8 skipped, 1 failure. That
  failure is `test_keepawake`'s `test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close`, which also fails on
  unchanged `main` and is the race #1901 fixes.

Not run: Windows, macOS.

pulls.title: STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE: rotation for packs whose layers differ in expert block size (spares kept per size)
pulls.author: Xiaomi2008
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #864 (the opt-in exchange buffer rotation). I searched the open threads: #1340 and #1838 touch the resident RAM exchanges but not this limit.

## What it changes

`STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1` now works on packs whose layers differ in expert block size. Until now rotation required one block size for all layers and fell back to the copy path otherwise ("requires equal-size expert blocks"). Swift 1.5 IQ3_S has seven sizes (1,510,400 to 2,662,400 bytes) and IQ3_XXS nine, so neither could rotate.

- `ExchangeStorage` keeps its spare buffers per block size (`initialize_sized`). A swap exchanges two experts of one layer, so an exchange takes a spare of its layer's size and hands back one of the same size; every size keeps its number of spares. `commit()` refuses a spare of another size and an expert of another layer.
- `exchange_buffer()` takes the layer; `reserve_exchanges()` takes the number of trailing buffers that only stage copies (`--adapt-async`'s second half), kept in the largest size alone.
- With `--adapt-async 1` a rotated round flips in the tick that sees the copies in (nothing for the job to move), one verify window sooner.

## What it leaves alone

Rotation stays opt-in. Unset, nothing new runs: the copy path, the uniform `initialize()` geometry and its checks are as before, and no default or preset changes. Switched on, the exchange allocation is one spare of every size per swap of a round: 1.06 GiB of page-locked RAM on IQ3_S with `--adapt-swaps 80` (1.26 GiB with `--adapt-async 1`) against 0.20 and 0.40 GiB.

## Measured

Core i7-13700K, RTX 5090 32 GB, 64 GB DDR5, Windows 11, driver 617.42. Swift 1.5 IQ3_S, 128K, `--resident-experts` (about 11,000 of 24,576 experts in VRAM), `--adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97`, `--spec 4`, `--pool-affinity p-cores`.

**This branch (main at 7695859a + this commit, engine 0.1.43), same day, one binary, only the variable differs.** One 8K prompt, the same 1,500 forced tokens (`--spec-follow`), blocking tier, runs interleaved:

| | decode tok/s |
|---|---|
| unset | 171.2, 170.3, 173.2 |
| `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE=1` | 195.9, 194.9, 197.2 |

An unset run and two rotated runs that sized the cache alike (11,099 slots) wrote the same `--window-hashes` file for all 434 windows. (The unset run that sized 11,017 slots differs from the others, as any other cache size does.)

**The same commit on 0.1.42** (my fork's main, which also carries #1911 and #1912):

| Run | Rotation off | Rotation on |
|---|---|---|
| The same forced-token run | 161.6-165.1 (five runs) | 184.9-188.7 (four runs) |
| `--serve`, 23 coding-agent turns (`tools/agent_turns_bench.py`'s turns, greedy, up to 400 new tokens), three interleaved rounds, blocking tier (off = the build before) | 147.8 / 159.2 / 158.4 | 175.2 / 184.9 / 172.8 |
| The same turns with `--adapt-async 1`, one binary, two rounds | 166.0 / 170.1 | 185.6 / 182.5 |

The tier swaps about 30 experts per verify window all through a run on this box, so the copy path moved about 50 MiB of RAM per window on the decode thread.

## How it was checked, and what was not

- `tests/core/exchange_storage_test.cpp` gains a three-size case (6,144 exchanges: bytes, aliases, the refusals, overlapping resident blocks) and passes on this branch, built alone with MSVC 14.50. I did not run it under ASan/UBSan, and I did not run `file_expert_source_test --rotation-gpu`.
- Built for CUDA only on this branch (sm_120, CUDA 13.0.88, MSVC 14.50 with nvcc's `--allow-unsupported-compiler`). **HIP and SYCL were not compiled**; `expert_source.cpp` and `generate.cpp` are built by both.
- Not measured: Linux, AMD cards, a layer split, a pack with one block size on this machine, the serve runs on 0.1.43.

Details and the numbers: `docs/EXCHANGE_ROTATION.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: setup: agentionai's Signal 3.8 Flash Next as --family signal (AP-Q4_K_XL, AP-IQ4_XS), images with its own encoder
pulls.author: clothespin
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none. No open issue or pull request covers Signal (searched "Signal", "agentionai" and "AP-Q4_K_XL"). This
builds on #290 (`--embd-gguf`).

## Summary
Adds agentionai's [Signal 3.8 Flash Next](https://huggingface.co/agentionai/Signal-3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF) to setup as
`--family signal`, with its two ~4-bit sizes, AP-Q4_K_XL (101 GB) and AP-IQ4_XS (90 GB), and images through Signal's
own encoder. The engine runs the file unchanged. What was missing: a pack built with `--compat-bf16` (its dense weights
are Q6_K), a BF16 copy of its Q6_K token embedding (the stock engine has no GPU dequantizer for it), and the installer
plumbing. No engine source changes, no default changes, and the other families' configs are byte-identical
(`tools/test_setup_golden` passes).

## What changed
Three commits, one feature. The first two stand on their own if you would rather take them separately.

1. `tools/embd_bf16_pack.py`: `--gguf PATH` (and `--tensor`) dequantizes a GGUF's token embedding to BF16 for
   `--embd-gguf`, rounding to nearest even as `--compat-bf16` does. On Signal AP-Q4_K_XL: 248,320 x 2,560 Q6_K, a
   1,271,398,784-byte file, worst rounding error 0.00036. `--model` (from the checkpoint) writes the same header byte for
   byte as before.
2. `docs/SIGNAL_AP_Q4_K_XL.md` (new) and a pointer in `docs/MODELS.md`: the manual workflow, in the style of
   `docs/ORCA.md`, with a config calibrated on one machine and what was and was not checked.
3. `setup.py`: the `signal` family and the AP-Q4_K_XL and AP-IQ4_XS models, pinned at revision `eba565be` with each
   file's size and SHA-256.
   - setup writes `<pack>/token-embd-bf16.gguf` and adds `--embd-gguf` to the config, for this family only;
   - with images on, it downloads `mmproj-F16.gguf` from the repository and saves it as
     `mmproj-Signal-3.8-Flash-Next-F16.gguf`;
   - `budget_model()` and `--gguf-dir`'s name check now handle a one-file name with the `AP-` prefix (before, they
     took Signal for UD-Q4_K_XL, or for a GGUF Strata cannot run);
   - AP-Q4_K_XL is NVIDIA only, and setup asks on AMD, for the same reason as UD-Q4_K_XL: no HIP prompt kernels for
     Q4_K experts.

   Also: `tools/strata_mcp.py` (its fallback model table), `tools/test_setup_signal.py` (10 tests: the pins, the
   budget, the file and config names, the pack and embedding commands and `--embd-gguf` in a mocked install, the
   encoder's download name), and docs: English README, `MODELS.md`, `AI_SETUP.md`.

Left alone: the engine, every default, the other families' configs, the translated READMEs.

### Measured
Linux, RTX 4090 (24 GB), Ryzen 9 7950X3D, 93 GB RAM, engine 0.1.43 at `7695859a`, 2026-10-11, with the file already
downloaded:
`./setup.sh --family signal --model AP-Q4_K_XL --gguf-dir <folder> --vision gpu --build --yes --no-start`

- It took 5 minutes, including the SHA-256 check of the 101 GB file and compiling `strata-vision`. The pack, tokenizer
  and embedding file it wrote are byte for byte the ones built by hand in the doc.
- The config it wrote (32K context, 8-bit KV, 63 GiB RAM budget, images on) was ready in 86 s. `tools/strata_bench.py`,
  3 runs per test, thinking off, temperature 0:

| test | median | range |
|---|---|---|
| short chat, decode | 59.9 tokens/s | 48.1-70.8 |
| short chat, first token | 0.38 s | 0.33-0.45 |
| 4K prompt | 1400 tokens/s | 960-1402 |
| 16K prompt | 2301 tokens/s | 1834-2317 |
| agent session, decode | 71.2 tokens/s | 44.4-89.8 |
| agent session, prompt reused from the cache | 68.7% | 68.6-68.8% |

- Images: a drawn test picture got "7341 red circle blue square lighthouse" (all four right);
  `docs/media/pagoda-preview.webp` got an accurate two-sentence description.
- The text checks from `docs/ORCA.md`: arithmetic (391), a Python function, a translation, and a cancelled stream
  followed by a correct answer (19). One answer was wrong: asked for the second-largest number in a list, it said 100
  (it is 99).

### Not tested
- AP-IQ4_XS was not downloaded or run. I read only its header: it differs from AP-Q4_K_XL only in the experts'
  gate/up type, IQ3_S, the same pair UD-IQ4_XS uses.
- Setup's own download of the files (the run above used `--gguf-dir`).
- Windows, AMD cards, several GPUs, and the image encoder on the CPU.
- Output quality against the base model, and the draft head's acceptance rate on this fine-tune.
- `embd_bf16_pack.py --gguf` has no unit test of its own; it is covered by the run above. `--model` was not run end to
  end (no safetensors checkpoint on the test machine).

## Extra Notes
- Neither size is marked experimental. Their experts (67.9 and 57.3 GB) fall between UD-IQ4_XS (regular) and
  UD-Q4_K_XL (experimental). Happy to flag either one if you prefer.
- Tests: all `tools/test_setup_*.py` and `tools/test_strata_mcp.py` pass, except the two tests in
  `tools/test_setup_engine_hash.py`, which fail the same way on `main`.

pulls.title: serve: preserve literal </tool_call> in prompts
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
## Title
serve: preserve literal `</tool_call>` in prompts

Issue: Resolves https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/2026

## Summary

Asking the model to print `</tool_call>` verbatim can produce an empty final response. The tokenizer treats this spelling as a user-defined special token even inside ordinary message text. Protecting it as plain text in the prompt makes the reported reproduction return the requested string.

## What changed

- Add `TOOL_LITERAL_TAGS` with one entry, `</tool_call>`, to the existing literal-span protection.
- Protect occurrences in messages, assistant history/reasoning, tool results, definitions, and argument values while preserving template-generated tool-call closers as special tokens.
- Add regressions for prompt token IDs, literal model output, all two-part streaming boundaries, real tool calls, explicit stop sequences, and streaming/non-streaming HTTP responses.

This is a standalone fix against `main`; it does not depend on #1886. No new state machine, retry, configuration option, or engine change is required. Prompts without the target literal retain identical token IDs.

## Extra Notes

### Validation

The issue's exact prompt was run through the service with a real IQ3_XXS model on Linux/CUDA (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). Ten interleaved before/after pairs used seeds 42-51, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, thinking enabled, and no tools. Both arms used the PR code; the baseline restored the original literal registry. Raw input/output token IDs were captured.

| Result | Original registry | With fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exactly `</tool_call>` | 0/10 | 10/10 |
| Empty final response | 9/10 | 0/10 |
| Incorrect `<\|im_start\|>` response | 1/10 | 0/10 |

The `</aaa>` and `</mcp_tool>` controls each passed before and after. The reporter's IQ3_S/Windows/AMD configuration was not tested.

339 tests passed on the standalone PR branch (Windows, Python 3.13.15). Regression command (no model/GPU required):

```sh
python -m unittest serve.test_literal_tool_tags serve.test_frontend serve.test_reasoning_tools serve.test_tool_name_space serve.test_server -q
```

Removing the new registry entry makes 20 prompt-protection subcases fail; restoring it passes them. Existing output parsing already preserves a standalone closer, so the production fix stays in prompt tokenization.

pulls.title: [GUI] Add Optional Windows Tray For Local Model Control
pulls.author: medking82
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Windows users need quick access to their local Strata server without keeping a console or browser open. This opt-in Tray adds a read-only client and a separately configured managed mode for model profiles, context, idle unload and explicit Preload/Unload. It is not installed or started by the default installer.

## Related discussion

#2034. Rebased onto 0.2.0-beta `main` (`e88ee39d`) for the tracker reset. **Scope agreement for the managed feature is still requested; this remains a draft proposal.** The earlier issue proposed a narrower read-only client. No maintainer agreement on the expanded scope is assumed.

## Approach

All files are isolated under `tools/windows-tray/`. Existing engine, server, frontend, setup and default installation files are byte-identical to the base revision. The Tray forwards client authentication unchanged and owns only the processes in its private Windows Job. Lifecycle changes close admission and drain admitted requests before acting; occupied ports are refused. Startup and restart stay lazy.

Managed mode uses the official context choices (8K, 32K, 64K, 128K, 200K, 256K, 384K, 512K), and Never/5/10/30 minute idle unload, preserving the original profiles and saved settings. An optional `desktop_app` path adds Open Strata App and a separate App update metadata check using the official feed. App installation and signature verification stay in the App. Legacy engine staging is retained only for legacy assets; signed 0.2 component releases explicitly defer to the official component updater.

The current official desktop icon replaces the earlier favicon. The old personal Tray screenshot was removed; no personal configuration or screenshot is included. This generic proposal has no Codex dependency or client-capacity synchronization.

## Validation

Commands below omit the local windowless-runner wrapper and use a disposable output/dependency directory.

**Passed:**

- Windows x64, .NET Framework compiler v4, Python 3.12; patch `d2303a53` on base `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta).
- `tools/windows-tray/Build.ps1 -Test -OutputDirectory <temporary directory>` and `TrayTests.exe`: **54 checks passed**, including actual PerMonitorV2, loopback API parsing, auth/redirect boundaries, embedded icon, diagnostic privacy, argument quoting, App version/metadata validation and malformed-feed handling.
- `tools/windows-tray/Build.ps1 -OutputDirectory <temporary directory>`: production WinForms executable built.
- `python -B tools/windows-tray/managed/test_managed.py`: **16 tests passed** against this base's unmodified official MockEngine and disposable streaming fixtures. Covers lazy lifecycle, profile/settings preservation, 30-minute persistence, authentication forwarding, foreign-port refusal, streaming drain, archive/digest/staging checks and deferral of signed component releases.
- `git diff --check`; all changed paths are below `tools/windows-tray/`.

**Failed:**

- Initial mock-server runs lacked the base revision's `jinja2` and `regex` dependencies. The final run passed with those pinned official dependencies installed in an isolated test directory; the production Python environment was not changed.

**Not run:**

- Real GPU cold load, generation, unload/idle timing or upgrades; Windows reboot/autostart; cross-monitor transitions; configured-App launch and App installer interaction in this generic candidate. The official MockEngine always reports loaded and a fixed 32768 context; unloaded behavior is tested separately with fake control responses. No inference or model download was submitted for this update.

## Limits

Draft pending scope agreement and targeted Windows hardware acceptance. Signed component installation belongs to the official updater. This Tray does not provide an upstream plugin API or manage App-owned prepared-model registration. Read-only mode does not accept API keys; protected servers report authentication required.

medians with ranges), measured on the machine's own HTTP API.

- Hardware: 2x RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB (44 GiB VRAM), i5-11500T 6C/12T,
  62.6 GiB DDR4-2933, Ubuntu (kernel 7.0.0-28), driver 610.57.04
- Engine: 0.1.43 source build (commit 7695859a), sm_75
- Model: original Flash-Next IQ3_S at the native 262144-token context,
  layer split 24 across the two cards, `--kv int8`, `--prefill auto`
- Results: chat decode 78.9 tok/s; fresh prompts 873.7 / 1521.9 / 1776.9
  tok/s at 4K / 16K / 32K; agent session 68.8% cache hit

report at 0.1.40.3 on the same model and context.

Two notes from this machine that may interest others:

- `STRATA_BF16_TC=1` and `STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1` were both set. The first
  is a no-op here (7.x cards take the FP16 tensor-core path by default);
  the second measured +18% on short prompts in our own A/B.
- The conversation cache budget only matters if the admission rule can be
  met: with a full expert arena in RAM, MemAvailable after load was about
  2.58 GB, below the "snapshot + 2560 MiB floor" every time, so a large
  `--conversation-cache-mib` produced 166 rejected parks, 21 evictions and
  a first-token spike to 72 s. Lowering the budget to 2048 MiB removed
  both the rejections and the spike and left prompt throughput unchanged.

No correctness check was run; background load and power limits were not
recorded (the cards were on their default policy during the runs).

pulls.author: WCHungBlake
pulls.body:
Adds Strata as a documented backend for **acp-bridge**, a small (~5MB) static Rust adapter that speaks ACP (Agent Client Protocol) — the protocol Zed, JetBrains and other editors use for coding agents.

**What it adds:**
- `docs/DETAILS.md` — a new "ACP-capable editors via acp-bridge" bullet under **Using it**, with a ready-to-paste acp-bridge config pointing at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`
- `README.md` — one bullet in the "Your apps and coding agents" list pointing to the new section

**Why it fits naturally:**
- Strata's OpenAI-compatible surface is exactly the backend type acp-bridge consumes; no changes on either side needed
- acp-bridge's 0.9.2 release handles thinking-mode Qwen output specifically (tool calls embedded in the content channel instead of the structured `tool_calls` field), and an automated compatibility suite for both Qwen shapes runs against a mock Strata `/v1` in the acp-bridge repo (`tests/strata_compat.rs`, currently green CI)
- ACP support complements the OpenCode / Claude Code / Codex CLI items already listed — same API, a different editor protocol

Docs only; no build or runtime behavior touched.

pulls.title: bench: RTX 5090 desktop 1M-agent — 0.1.42 vs 0.1.43 interleaved A/B (overlap default pays +1.2/+2.4% decode; #1712 wash-to-negative on sm_120)
pulls.author: gravitomagnetic
pulls.body:
Follow-up to our merged 5090 reports (#1592 lineage), same box and config, on the v0.1.43 release.

Six legs, A B A B A B, wrapper paired per tag, version gate passed on all six, 30 s settle. Two probe sets per leg: our classic 200K/decode/needle/repetition suite, and strata-bench `gprobe` short prompts (150/300/450 tokens) — the band the #1712 pinned-upload change touches.

Headlines:
- **ADAPT_OVERLAP pays on this regime**: instruct decode +1.2%, greedy +2.4% (engine log tok/s; every 0.1.43 leg beat every 0.1.42 leg). Prefill/needle flat. All gates clean (needle 6/6, zero repetition 6/6), consistent with the release's byte-identical CUDA claim.
- **#1712 is a small consistent cost here**: all 9 gprobe pairs +0.1–0.4%. The staged walk on sm_120 + native IQ3_S + 91–94% hit rate is expert-bytes-bound; the pageable-copy stall it removes is smaller than the memcpy+event-sync it adds. Not an objection to the default — the gfx1100 fix is worth more than 3 ms — but a measured data point for a per-platform gate.
- **Regime contrast with #2010** (5090 laptop x8, overlap −21%): this box streams only 4–5.5% of routed experts in steady state. A residency/PCIe-fraction-aware default could cover both. Cross-posted there.

**Verdict: 0.1.43 is our daily keeper.**

Raw data in `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx5090-1m-agent-0143/data/` (twelve per-leg JSONs + serve-log extracts).

pulls.author: picmax
pulls.body:
## Title

bench: community reports - RTX 2000 Ada 16 GB, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at 262K, engine 0.1.42 and 0.1.43

Issue: none (community benchmark submission, per `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`)

## Summary

Two reports from the same machine, model and configuration: one on 0.1.43, one on 0.1.42 as the baseline. The suite's own numbers say the two versions are level on this box. A same-machine A/B says the file-tier fix does pay here, but **only on real text** - the generated word lists used by the suite and by `tools/ab_engine.py` show nothing at all. That is the part I would value a read on.

## What changed

- added `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx-2000-ada-generation-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs-0143/` - suite 1, 3 runs per test, medians with ranges
- added `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx-2000-ada-generation-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs-0142/` - same, previous engine, as the A/B baseline
- `COMMUNITY.md`: one row per new folder

## Extra Notes

One machine, one engine loaded at a time, engine version confirmed from `BUILD.json` at every swap, 128-token greedy completions at temperature 0 with the prompt cache defeated by a unique prefix per request.

**This PR's reports, 0.1.42 -> 0.1.43, same shapes the suite uses:**

| | 0.1.42 | 0.1.43 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| short chat decode | 42.8 (36.8-51.8) | 41.2 (36.6-49.9) | ranges overlap, no separation |
| agent session decode (~14.5K ctx) | 41.5 (25.5-48.8) | 42.0 (21.8-50.7) | ranges overlap, no separation |
| 4K prompt | 861.3 (856.6-862.8) | 879.7 (879.4-880.0) | +2.1%, ranges do not overlap |
| 16K prompt | 895.5 (893.2-899.3) | 905.0 (899.7-906.7) | +1.1% |

**Prompt-shape test.** Client-side streaming rate, engines alternated in place (0.1.42, 0.1.43, 0.1.42, 0.1.43), two sessions per cell, same token count in both prompts per pair:

| prompt | 0.1.42 | 0.1.43 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| prose, 7,159 tokens | 41.1 (40.5-41.8) | 42.5 (42.2-42.7) | +3.2% |
| word list, 7,159 tokens (`ab_engine.py`'s long prompt, reproduced exactly) | 39.6 (38.0-41.3) | 39.0 (36.0-41.9) | no change |
| prose, 9,975 tokens | 36.7 (34.7-38.7) | 39.5 (39.4-39.7) | +7.8% |

Not a length effect: same harness, same schedule, same token count, prose gains and the word list does not.

**Controls.** With the file-tier fix turned off (`STRATA_KEEP_MAPPING=1`), 0.1.43 lands back on the 0.1.42 figure on the same prose (36.4 tok/s at 10K against 36.4 for 0.1.42), so the gain tracks the fix rather than the day; a rollback control measured after the run agrees with the baseline too. Day-to-day drift on this box is 8-10%, so everything was measured inside one window.

**What I could not explain.** The word list pushes *more* expert traffic to the file tier than the prose does - 5.3% of routed experts read over PCIe against 2.3%, both from the engine's own counters - yet it shows no gain. So "more file-tier traffic, more to win" is measured and wrong here, and I have no mechanism for why real text gains and a word list does not. If the 12-22 GiB Windows cases in the release notes are the intended shape and ours (about 40 GiB resident, streaming under half) is simply outside it, that would fit the numbers too.

**Also checked so the result is not a reporting artifact.** 0.1.43 changed the semantics of `timings` (`prompt_n` now counts what the engine really read, the rest in `cache_n`). The engine's own decode rate and an independent client-side streaming rate agree within 0.8% on both versions, so the suite's decode column is comparable across these two builds.

**Note on the reports.** The settings are this machine's tuned daily configuration (an earlier design-of-experiments study: PCIe share 0.29, KV resident 20480 MiB, prefill 4096, short-read 64, vision with a 700 MiB reserve), not a benchmark-specific setup. The fields the suite leaves blank - storage, background load, power limits - are filled in: D: NVMe holds the shards, nothing else used the GPU during the runs, and the card is at its 70 W board limit (default and maximum for this SKU).

pulls.title: prefill: gfx11 F16 matrix-core routed experts (opt-in STRATA_PF_F16=1): prompt +10-14% on gfx1151
pulls.author: libratechw
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Refs #1258

## Summary
With `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` the routed experts of a prompt run on gfx11's int8 matrix cores, each weight sub-block decoded to int8
with a per-block epilogue. `STRATA_PF_F16=1` runs the covered formats on the F16 matrix cores instead: the codes stay packed in
LDS, each wave turns its own rows into F16, and the F16 WMMA accumulates all of K in FP32. The K-quant kernels adapt gufo's
`RoutedF16GEMMKernel` (97b8645f, MIT; attribution and licence text at the top of both new files). The output differs from the
int8 kernels', so it is off by default; gfx12 keeps the int8 kernels.

## What changed
- `src/prefill/moe_f16_common.cuh` (new): the switch, the work item, the activations staged as F16, the WMMA loop, the two
  epilogues.
- `src/prefill/moe_f16_kq.cu/.hpp` (new): Q4_K / Q5_K gate/up and Q5_1 down (with `STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1`). They read the
  weights 16 / 8 bytes at a time, so each of gate/up and down takes them only when the batch's blobs, offsets and row
  strides are aligned to that (the native blobs are promised 2 bytes); otherwise that half stays on its int8 kernel. gfx906,
  whose build leaves this file out, covers nothing here.
- `src/prefill/moe_fused_iq.cu`: `native_f16_kernel` for IQ2_XXS / IQ2_XS / IQ2_S / IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S / IQ4_XS gate/up and Q2_0 /
  IQ4_NL / Q8_0 down (through the existing 16-bit loads), and the dispatch.
- `tests/cuda/prefill_fused_iq_test.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt`: with `STRATA_PF_F16=1` on a gfx11 device the test allows 5e-3
  against the int8 model and MMQ (measured 2.7e-3) and places the blobs 256-byte aligned, so the F16 kernels are what it
  checks; elsewhere the int8 limits stay. ctest `hip_prefill_fused_iq_f16` runs the default pairs with the switch,
  `hip_prefill_fused_iq_f16_kq` the four K-quant pairs (it sets `STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1` too).
- `docs/STRIX_HALO.md`: what it covers, the layer and prompt times, first-token KL.

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, ROCm 7.14.1, Linux), on 296b59d2. One layer, `hip_prefill_fused_iq`, 16,384 tokens, top 10 over
512 experts, median of 3:

| gate/up / down | int8 kernels, ms | F16, ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| Q4_K / Q5_1 (UD-Q4_K_XL) | 86.4 | 53.7 (-38%) |
| Q4_K / Q8_0 | 85.9 | 53.5 (-38%) |
| IQ3_S / IQ4_NL (UD-IQ4_XS) | 79.8 | 58.2 (-27%) |

Prompt tok/s, the branch's binary without and with `STRATA_PF_F16=1`, `--serve --prefill 16384 --spec 4`, the section-5
switches with `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=2048` (UD-Q4_K_XL also `STRATA_PF_FUSED_KQ=1`), a chat request of 4K / 32K tokens,
fresh servers alternating, 5 pairs after dropping those with page migration or reclaim; median tok/s and the median of the
pair ratios, every pair faster:

| | 4K | 32K |
|---|---:|---:|
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 1,129 -> 1,294 (+14.4%) | 1,249 -> 1,422 (+13.9%) |
| UD-IQ4_XS | 1,114 -> 1,269 (+13.5%) | 1,266 -> 1,389 (+9.9%) |

The UD-Q4_K_XL 32K cell is of this code; the layer times and the other three cells are of an earlier head with the same
kernels (before the alignment check and the test changes). Without the switch, the layer's output hashes (six pairs, 2,048
and 16,384 tokens) are 296b59d2's.

First-token KL against a run with no switches, 12 natural-text chat requests of 1.5K-24K tokens, mean (median); the fast arms
with `STRATA_PF_SWITCH_MIN_T=0`; the top token is the same in 12 of 12 in every arm:

| | section-5 switches + int8 fused experts | + `STRATA_PF_F16=1` |
|---|---:|---:|
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 0.0065 (0.0017) | 0.0114 (0.0048) |
| UD-IQ4_XS | 0.0076 (0.0035) | 0.0104 (0.0057) |

F16 moves further from the default than the int8 path, so this stays opt-in. The records and scripts are in
[libratechw/Strata@e5d05554, `2020/`](https://github.com/libratechw/Strata/tree/e5d0555410983415288228c096fdb1fbabb01df7/2020).

Builds and tests:
- HIP gfx1151, this head: ctest, 114 tests: 106 pass (the three `hip_prefill_fused_iq*` among them), 5 skip, and the same
  three fail as on 296b59d2 (`ple_parity`, `expert_parity`, `pool_test`).
- HIP: `moe_fused_iq.cu` and `moe_f16_kq.cu` compile for gfx1012, gfx1030, gfx1100, gfx1103, gfx1150, gfx1151, gfx1200 and
  gfx1201 (77506be1; the head changes neither file). gfx906: `moe_fused_iq.cu` no longer leaves the `f16kq` functions
  undefined (it did at 77506be1); the whole gfx906 build stops earlier, at `mmq_nvfp4_w4a4.cu` (ggml's `vendors/cuda.h`),
  which this branch does not touch.
- CUDA 13.0, RTX 3060 (Windows), 77506be1 (the head's changes since are in a header CUDA does not include, a HIP ctest, a
  test comment and the doc): builds; ctest, 117 tests: 114 pass, 2 skip, and `ple_parity` fails as on 296b59d2.
- SYCL: not affected (the SYCL experts are their own files).

Not run: other gfx11 cards (gfx1100-1103, gfx1150), and quality beyond the first-token KL.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Builds and tests on this branch:

## Title
Issue: Refs #1180

## Summary
Since 0.1.40.2 the `waves_per_eu(8)` variant of `native_w11_kernel` is uncapped on clang 22 and newer, because clang 22
computes wrong results with it on gfx1100 (#1180). On gfx1151 with clang 23 (ROCm 7.14.1) the capped kernels give the same
bits and take less time. This applies the cap there again, per format, and leaves every other architecture and compiler as
it is.

## Title

## Summary
`prompt_attn_wmma_kernel` interleaved a chunk's global reads with its compute: the V slice was staged first, then each 16-cell
tile loaded its K scale and fragments between the q.k WMMAs, so a wave waited on each read in turn. The chunk's reads now go

`block_topk_reg_kernel`, the QSA block top-k on CUDA and HIP, picked each radix digit with thread 0 walking up to 255 bins

pulls.title: Draft: immutable branching contexts with serialized execution and shared checkpoints
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Branch from a consumed prefix, advance independent futures, and rewind movable branch references without changing canonical history. Optional CUDA and host-RAM checkpoints accelerate replay; complete checkpoint eviction preserves the history needed to rebuild.

This is a foundation for #1938 and #1962, not a claim that either request is complete.

## Current prototype

- One canonical immutable history and controller representation, revision-checked branch moves, and durable consumed-token publication.
- Shared CUDA allocations with copy-on-write, native host-RAM snapshots, exact-history reuse, and direct allocation/ownership/work counters.
- Owner-affine execution leases and a simple FIFO slot queue. Execution is explicitly serialized on one backend workspace; queued cancellation, slot reuse and interrupted publication have regression coverage.
- A separately linked, uncached full-history oracle that accepts no branch checkpoint or retained handle.

## Corrected validation

Linux, RTX 4090, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q8_0 weights, FP16 KV:

- Eight supporting test methods passed, with 34 exact full-vocabulary comparisons; maximum absolute logit error 0.0. No skips or expected failures in these passing runs.
- Four comparisons match ordinary execution for the one-token control. Thirty compare branching operations against fresh full-history forwards, with 296 oracle-computed tokens.
- Coverage includes controller state, ownership, FIFO execution, interrupted publication, slot reuse, RAM restoration and complete checkpoint eviction. RAM hits avoided prefix computation; changed and fully evicted prefixes replayed their nine tokens.
- G0: 51/51. All four reference mutants detected.

Both private drivers previously omitted resident expert contributions because they did not bind the expert dispatch plan. The fix corrects both drivers. Earlier branch/oracle agreement shared that defect and does not establish ordinary-model correctness. The controlled regression failed before the fix (maximum error 1.1226537227630615) and passed exactly afterward. No tolerance or reference equation was relaxed. Actual PCIe expert execution was not exercised by this fixture.

[Executed evidence and fingerprints](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/68c0459894deae0b6641914e5efdba9a479fecf3/experimental/branching_context/evidence/dispatch-correction-validation.json)

## Help wanted: batched-prefill equivalence

The immediate priority is a reliable one-request-at-a-time prototype. Batched execution is not required for that milestone, but ordinary batched-prefill equivalence must be resolved before claiming general serving-path parity.

Help tracing differences between ordinary prefill chunks and the pinned token-level operator is welcome, especially expert dispatch, placement and accumulation order. Full diagnostic vectors and work counts were preserved; the historical maximum 1.5612177848815918 is an absolute logit difference, not a percentage or an accepted tolerance. The dispatch fix establishes the one-token control, not multi-token equivalence.

[Preserved prefill diagnosis](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/68c0459894deae0b6641914e5efdba9a479fecf3/experimental/branching_context/evidence/normal-prefill-validation.json)

## Remaining scope

Draft validation only. The current numerical profile is unqualified and no cumulative G1-G5 PASS is claimed. Full current-build suites, crash/OOM campaigns, evaluation/adoption workflow, release hardening, performance qualification and conversation-server integration remain. The unchanged native conversation snapshot test still fails its same-address growth expectation. HIP/SYCL builds, native Windows persistence and image inputs are unvalidated or unsupported.

The feature remains experimental and opt-in. Default serving-path parity has not been fully established. The Python store currently requires POSIX fcntl.

[Build, usage and limitations](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/68c0459894deae0b6641914e5efdba9a479fecf3/experimental/branching_context/README.md)

pulls.title: STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP: opt-in on every backend (RTX 5090 Laptop, Linux CUDA: 84.6 vs 106.6 tok/s decode median with it); log the state in both directions
pulls.author: Krypto-Whitehat
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #2010

## Summary

`STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP` is opt-in on every backend now, and the startup log names its state (with the reason when it cannot run).

On CUDA on Linux it was on by default since 0.1.43, measured on an RTX A4000 (+5.5..8.3% decode) and a Tesla P100 (+4.4%). On three other boxes it costs 19..26% decode, and each of those three measured it the same way: one 0.1.43 build, only the flag changed between runs.

- **This report** - RTX 5090 Laptop, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, Core Ultra 9 275HX (8 P + 16 E), native IQ3_XXS pack, `--expert-cache auto --expert-cache-per-layer` (10,320 slots, 16.78 GiB cache), PCIe Gen5 x8 at 28.7 GB/s probe: 106.6 tok/s median with `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=0` against 84.6 at the default, 5 generations of 256 tokens, slowest of the fast run (89.1) above the fastest of the slow one (87.9). Same-day v0.1.42 control on the same config: 98.1 tok/s.
- **`jstrot` in #2010** - RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, i7-14700K, 64 GB, pool limited to 16 threads: ~52 tok/s at the default, and `=0` brings it back to the 0.1.42 level of ~64.
- **`demon851113` in #2010** - RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB desktop, Ryzen 7 7700 (8c/16t, AVX-512), 93 GB DDR5, PCIe 5.0 x16, IQ3_S native pack, `--expert-cache auto` (no per-layer), `--batch 2`: the same build `7695859a` for every run, one variable per run, median of 3 generations of 300 tokens: **68.4 at the default, 86.4 with `=0` (+26%)**. Control in the same session: 0.1.40.1 = 81.1 / 82.0 at `--batch 2` and 90.2 at `--batch 1`, against 79.1 for the 0.1.43 default at `--batch 1`, so with the overlap off 0.1.43 sits about 5% above 0.1.40.1. They also swept six neighbouring switches (`STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL`, `STRATA_PCIE_FRAC_DEFAULT`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE`, `STRATA_NAN_GUARD`) and none of them moves the number.

The one measurement that favours the default is `gravitomagnetic` in #2010: +1.2% instruct / +2.4% greedy on an RTX 5090 desktop (Ryzen 7950X, 32 GB, 122 GB RAM, `--expert-cache 6500` auto-filling to 8,338 slots, about 33% of experts resident, no PCIe pressure in steady state). That is an interleaved A B A B A B run of the 0.1.42 and 0.1.43 tags, both at their own defaults, so the delta carries the overlap change together with everything else 0.1.43 shipped. It is a sound measurement of "is 0.1.43 slower on this box"; it does not isolate the switch on its own.

What separates the two groups is not laptop versus desktop and not hybrid versus AVX-512 CPU - `demon851113` is a desktop with full AVX-512 and still loses 26%. It is how much of the expert set stays resident. The three losses are 16 GB and 24 GB cards with a small resident share; the win is a 32 GB card with about a third of the experts resident.

`=1` turns it on, `=0` turns it off. The copies, the gate and the tokens are untouched, so the answers do not depend on the switch.

## What changed

- `src/program/generate.cpp`, `adapt_overlap()`: the three platform branches (HIP opt-in, Windows CUDA opt-in, Linux CUDA on) become one `=1` turns it on. The per-box numbers move into the comment next to it, so the reason for a default sits where it is read.
- `src/program/generate.cpp` serve startup block: the `why` predicates are read in both states (they are side-effect free) and the off state is logged once, as `strata serve: adaptive overlap: off (STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1 turns it on)` or `... off: not on a layer split` and so on. Until now only the on state was logged, so with `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=0` in a config nothing in the log said that the overlap was off.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the setting entry states the new default and keeps every measured number with what it was measured on (A4000 +5.5..8.3%, 6 interleaved pairs; P100 +4.4%; RTX 5070 on Windows -2.6% on Q2_0; RTX 5090 Laptop -21%).

Left alone on purpose: the copy path itself (`AdaptGate`, `soft_commit_exchanges`), every predicate that turns the overlap off, and the tokens. This is a default and a log line, nothing else.

## Extra Notes

- Checked by build: `cmake -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89` with nvcc 13.4.92 and MSVC 14.44. The `strata` target compiles and links with 0 errors before the patch and after it (Windows CUDA, sm_89, so the Linux branch of the default is not what this compiles).
- Not tested: HIP and SYCL (no toolchain on this machine), and the decode numbers are from the rigs in #2010, not from a run of this patch.
- **The cost of this patch on the boxes that gained from the default:** an A4000 and a P100 now need `STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1` for their +5.5..8.3% / +4.4%. If you would rather not take that away by default, gating on the resident share instead of on the OS is where the measurements above separate: 16 GB and 24 GB cards with a small resident share lose 19..26%, a 32 GB card with about a third of the experts resident gains. I do not have a cheap and reliable runtime signal for "resident share" that I would trust as a default, so I am asking rather than guessing, and I would rather ship the opt-in flip now and add the gate once it is measured than hold this back on it.
- One new line prints on every serve startup, also where the overlap could not run anyway; there it names why.

pulls.title: Add experimental Linux gfx900 setup with wave64 validation
pulls.author: sagentlab
pulls.body:
Vega 10 (`gfx900`) is rejected by ordinary setup. This adds an explicit Linux opt-in that installs gfx900-capable ROCm packages, builds the wave64 engine, and checks the device before downloading the model.

Replaces #839, which GitHub closed after the main-branch history rewrite. This branch starts at current upstream `main` (`7695859a`) and carries only the two original contribution commits plus rebase follow-ups, preserving their author.

- Use `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_GFX900=1 ./setup.sh --yes --backend hip`; the experimental build uses `build-gfx900` and TheRock packages pinned to `7.14.0a20260612`. Existing architectures, ROCm family selection and iGPU handling retain the current main behavior. Windows and mixed gfx900/wave32 builds are refused.
- Check the compiled architecture and wave size before launching kernels, fix the HIP/libstdc++ attribute conflict, and preserve modulo-2^32 signed software dp4a accumulation.
- Provide a gfx900-only FP32-product/FP16-conversion fallback for the new main's optional prefill `STRATA_GDN_NOY` path, whose inline instruction cannot compile for gfx900. Its optional-path numerical parity is not claimed.
- Put the wave64 intrinsic, BF16/FP16 GEMM and device tests under `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS`. Keep the installer device probe available when tests are off. Retain main's existing `cudaFuncSetAttribute` template and carve-out define without duplicating them.
- Document installation, longer-context guidance and a retained 0.1.39 MI25 log measurement: 38 uncached prompt tokens at 39.9 tokens/s and 256 generated tokens at 31.6 tokens/s. This is one historical request, not a measurement of the rebased engine.

Validation on the rebased branch:

- 211 setup tests pass across gfx900, AMD, choices, config, older GPUs, dependency pins, update, ROCm pins, Strix Halo, AMD startup and GPU-update suites.
- CMake configures with tests on and off; with tests off, wave64 test targets are absent and `strata-device` remains available.
- Full Release gfx900 `strata` engine build succeeds against current main (0.1.43).
- Rebuilt wave64 intrinsic, BF16/FP16 GEMM and device self-tests: 3/3 pass on the MI25 with ROCm `7.14.0a20260612`.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The 2026-10-04 full installer and inference checks in `docs/AMD_GFX900.md` are historical evidence from #839. A gfx906 owner run requested in the previous review is still outstanding; this PC has gfx900, so no gfx906 runtime validation is claimed. The gfx906 signed dp4a instruction path remains unchanged. Images and multiple-card inference remain unvalidated.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB in a KVM guest with Docker: 0.2.0-beta against 0.1.43
pulls.author: moneymikeMD
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A results-only benchmark report for a card with no other report here: one RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB (sm_86) in a KVM guest with
GPU passthrough, served from Docker. Re-run on 0.2.0-beta as asked when the tracker was reset; it replaces the 0.1.42
report this PR carried before.

The 0.2.0-beta image (engine package 0.1.45.3) and the 0.1.43 image were run in alternation on the same model files at
context 262,144, a fresh container per sweep, three runs per cell:

- IQ3_S decode 76.4 / 77.1 / 68.4 tok/s on 0.1.43 against 97.0 / 92.2 / 81.8 on 0.2.0 at 4K / 32K / 128K (two sweeps
  each; every 0.2.0 sweep beat every 0.1.43 sweep). Prompt speed within 4%. With `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0` 0.2.0 gives
  83.5 / 79.6 / 73.8, so the new sm_86 table is worth 14 / 14 / 10% here. `TUNE=quick`: "already fastest".
- Swift 1.5 IQ3_S: 77.2 / 77.4 / 63.2 against 96.0 / 97.1 / 85.6.
- UD-IQ4_XS: with 0.2.0's own settings the engine was killed for lack of RAM on this 94 GiB guest in 4 of 4 starts
  (kernel lines and engine log included). Reading `setup.py`, `unsloth_budget()` keeps every expert in RAM when the RAM is
  at least the experts plus 16 GiB, which does not count the PLE table locked in RAM or the KV streamed to RAM at this
  context; 0.1.43's setup wrote `--resident-budget-gib 55` for the same file. With that budget given by hand, 0.2.0 reads
  prompts 46 / 31 / 13% slower than 0.1.43 and decodes 21 / 7 / 11% slower; `STRATA_PREFILL_HOST_PLAN=0` changed nothing.
- Needles 9 of 9 at 32K, 128K and 262K on 0.2.0 IQ3_S.

## Related discussion

Reopening #2005 after the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset. No scope agreement needed (benchmark report).

## Approach

New folder `bench/results/2026-10-19-community-rtx-3080-ti-kvm-docker-0.2.0/` (README, every run as JSON lines, the run
configs with the key removed, the 0.2.0 engine logs, the scripts as run) and one entry in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md`.
No code changes.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `docker/build.sh --flavor cuda --engine <package> --tag strata:0.2.0-beta-cuda13 --base public.ecr.aws/docker/library/ubuntu:24.04`
  at v0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480) with the released `strata-engine-0.1.45.3-linux-x86_64-cuda-cuda13.tar.gz` (SHA-256 matches
  `SHA256SUMS.txt`), after adding `docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md` to the script's `paths=` list (below); the build's own checks passed.
- `sweep.py` (in the folder) and `tools/needle_bench.py` against both images on 2026-10-19, Ubuntu 26.04.1 guest, driver
  615.71.09, Docker 29.9.0; the numbers above are from those runs (`sweep-*.jsonl`, `needles-iq3_s-0.2.0.json`).
- The `STRATA_SET` values of each arm show up in that arm's engine log.

**Failed:**

- `docker/build.sh` unchanged at v0.2.0-beta: `missing payload item: docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md` (its build-context list has
  `docs/MANAGEMENT_PROTOCOL.md` but not `docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md`, which `packaging/package_terminal.py` requires; the
  line is the same on `main` at f57c0adc). Not fixed in this PR.
- 0.2.0 UD-IQ4_XS with its own settings: OOM-killed, 4 of 4 starts, as above.

**Not run:**

- A bare-metal run of the same machine (VM and Docker cost not measured).
- The 0.1.42 comparison is one sweep, after the others, not interleaved.
- Generated tokens were not compared between versions; no quality check beyond the needles.
- Vision, concurrent requests, a soak, agent sessions.

## Limits

Three runs per cell and two sweeps per interleaved arm. The 0.1.43 and 0.1.42 images are sm_86-only source builds; the
0.2.0 image uses the released engine package. The cause of the slower UD-IQ4_XS prompt read with the budget was not found.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RTX 3060 + RTX 4060 Ti (Windows, layer split), IQ3_XXS on 0.1.43
pulls.author: oh-codes
pulls.body:
Community benchmark, suite 1 (`--long`), 3 runs per test, medians of the runs, produced on the install's own configuration.

**Results.** Fresh prompts: 4K **508.3**, 16K **910.7**, 32K **1087.2** tok/s prefill; first token 7.95 / 17.69 / 29.56 s. Short chat **46.8** tok/s decode. Agent session, 6 turns with four tools: **56.8** tok/s decode, **68.8%** cache hit.

**Why this pair is worth a row.** It is a deliberately mismatched two-card split on Windows:

- RTX 3060 12 GB in an **x4 Gen3** slot (link max width 4 against the card's 16) — the second slot of a B550 board — against an **x8 Gen4** RTX 4060 Ti. The engine's own probe reads **2.9 GB/s** for the 3060 against **13.0 GB/s** for the 4060 Ti, and drops the 3060's expert share to `pcie_frac 0.08` (default 0.55).
- AM4 Ryzen 7 3700X (Zen 2, no AVX-512), 64 GiB DDR4-3000 dual-channel.
- The layer split (0-20 on the 3060, 21-47 and the head on the 4060 Ti) is **written by hand**, not chosen by the placement search: `layer_split auto` picks an extreme on this pair — a two-layer first stage on 0.1.40.2 and 0.1.41, which collapsed decode to about 25 tok/s.

**Leaves alone:** no engine change, no docs, no tooling.

**Two notes on `tools/strata_bench.py`**, both seen while producing this and neither fixed here:

1. The results folder is named from the first GPU only, so this 3060 + 4060 Ti pair was written as `2026-10-11-community-2x-rtx-3060-...`. The README title inside was already correct; the folder here is renamed to `2026-10-11-community-rtx-3060-4060ti-swift-iq3-xxs`.
2. The Settings block prints the config's `args` array only, so it omitted `--layer-split 21`. `layer_split` and `gpu` are siblings of `args` in the config JSON, and the server is what appends the flag to the engine command line — so anyone reproducing from that block would build a single-GPU setup and get different numbers. The README here carries the corrected line, with a note saying why it is there.

Both are reported here rather than as a separate issue because neither is the subject of an open thread; #1985 is about the opposite case, a report listing GPUs that are not in use.

**Comparability note.** This run carries 0.1.42's new `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7` default, which changes the answers slightly (KL 0.0058 on an RTX 3060 with IQ3_XXS, top-1 agreement 97.7%), so it is not directly comparable with a 0.1.41 report of the same hardware with the switch off.

pulls.title: calibrate: measure the shared-expert stream fork on AMD (STRATA_SH_STREAM) and keep it per PC (#1272)
pulls.author: Vop3p
pulls.body:
## Summary

`tools/calibrate.py` gets a sixth step on AMD: it measures the shared-expert stream fork (`STRATA_SH_STREAM`) off against on, a restart each, and writes `STRATA_SH_STREAM=1` into the config's `"env"` only when it wins by more than `MIN_GAIN`. This is the per-card choice left open in #1272.

The HIP default stays off (#816, #826): an RX 6800 on Windows and 4x R9700 decode 12-45% faster without the fork. The same card family on another PC goes the other way (#1272: 2x RX 6900 XT on Linux), and the output is identical either way, so a measurement on the user's PC is the right place to decide it.

## What changed

- `tools/calibrate.py`: step 6, HIP only (`cfg["backend"] == "hip"`), after the adaptive-tier step and with everything chosen before. Both values are set explicitly (`0` and `1`), so a value the config already carried does not decide the baseline; two rates each; the existing `pick()` / `MIN_GAIN` rule and the #1337 failed-start handling. `measure()` returns the choice as `"env"`; `start_engine` takes an optional env; `apply_env()` sets the chosen variables and removes the other `ENV_KEYS`, so an older calibration's choice does not linger.
- `setup.py`: `--calibrate` writes `"env"` into the config and the settings file; a reinstall applies a saved calibration's `"env"` the same way (one saved before this step leaves `"env"` alone). Where setup offers calibration is unchanged (NVIDIA only; on AMD it is still `./setup.sh --calibrate` by hand, #566).
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: the `STRATA_SH_STREAM` note says calibrate measures it.
- `tools/test_calibrate.py`: four tests (the step runs on HIP only and keeps the fork only on a win; a failed start keeps the default; `apply_env`; setup writes and later removes the variable) and the `run()` test now checks that `hip` is passed. 21 of 21 pass.

## Measured

Real engine (the 0.1.42 tag, built with setup's HIP flags), 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, PCIe 4.0 x8 each), Ryzen 5 5600X, Ubuntu 26.04, ROCm 10.0, GSQ-RCO IQ3_S on a layer split, a setup-style config (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, empty `"env"`). The whole calibration ran in 982 s with no failed start and no stall:

| step | chosen | measured |
|---|---|---|
| PCIe share | 0.00 | 62.0 against 59.2 tok/s at the probed 0.39 |
| draft floor | 0.70 | 62.3 against 61.3 at 0.5 |
| pool workers | 5 (the engine's) | 3: 60.3, 2: 56.5 |
| expert tier | every 1, 80 swaps, decay 0.97 | 63.8 against 61.6 |
| **shared-expert fork (new)** | **`STRATA_SH_STREAM=1`** | **off 62.2 / 61.3, on 67.2 / 66.6 tok/s (+8.3%)** |

Identity, separately, with a fixed protocol (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5`, 4K and 32K prompts, two each, fresh starts; the baseline reproduces its text and draft counts across starts): fork on against off gives the same text on 4 of 4 requests on the split and on one card, decode +8.7 / +9.9% (split) and +5.8 / +6.0% (one card).

Not tested: Windows HIP, other AMD cards (the step's purpose is that they decide for themselves), a CUDA build (the step does not run there).

Developed with an AI coding assistant; every number above was measured on 2x RX 6900 XT (gfx1030, PCIe 4.0 x8 each) / Ryzen 5 5600X, ROCm 10.0.

pulls.title: Add opt-in external llama.cpp token engine
pulls.author: rajpaulsingh6-stack
pulls.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `--engine llama-http` seam that lets Strata retain ownership of chat templating, tokenization, tool/API loops, request accounting, and OpenAI compatibility while an already-running llama.cpp-compatible server owns platform-specific device setup. The adapter validates `/health`, sends token IDs rather than rendered text, streams raw token IDs back, forwards a bounded set of sampling fields, and records prompt/decode/speculative-draft metrics. It deliberately does not start, stop, or unload the external runtime.

This is intended as an experimental provider seam, not a claim of general native macOS or Metal support. Relates to #1968.

## Verified vertical slice

Hardware: Mac Studio M2 Max (32 GB) with RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB in a Razer Core X V2 over USB-C/PCIe.

Runtime: Strata `llama-http` -> Macuda/llama.cpp b11433 -> TinyGPU -> RTX target, with M2 Max Metal running Qwen3.8 Flash-Next MTP Q8_0 drafts (`draft-mtp`, max 3). Target model was Swift-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated Q2_0 (66.5 GB).

- Exact-response smoke: `MADARA STRATA MACUDA MTP MAX3 LIVE`; 5.1 decode tok/s; 9/9 offered draft tokens accepted.
- Workbook benchmark: the fused node selected the correct preserve-and-validate action for an 88-row, 14-team October 2026 NYC sports schedule; GenOffice reported 0 errors and 0 warnings; model QC ran at 3.3 tok/s with 81/120 drafts accepted.
- Browser-grounded Knicks narrative: 243 words from NBA.com and ESPN facts; 4.1 tok/s with 263/420 drafts accepted.
- `python -m py_compile serve/server.py` and `git diff --check` passed.

## Performance boundary

In a controlled 128-token prompt, direct RTX target decode was 6.40 tok/s. Metal MTP drafting reached 5.61 tok/s with 84/126 draft tokens accepted (66.7%); CPU/RAM MTP drafting reached 4.85 tok/s with 83/129 accepted (64.3%). The host draft lanes are correct but slower on this USB4 topology, so this PR exposes the seam without making speculative decoding the default.

## Limits

- No external process lifecycle management.
- No Strata vision embeddings through this engine.
- Tested on one macOS/Macuda/TinyGPU configuration at 1024-token context.
- This draft PR contains the adapter only; benchmark artifacts and device-specific configuration are intentionally not committed.

pulls.title: STRATA_HC_HOST=1: hyper-connection down/up pairs in pinned host memory (opt-in, CUDA)
pulls.author: zsariboga
pulls.body:
## What

`STRATA_HC_HOST=1` (opt-in, CUDA): the 192 hyper-connection down/up projections (1.17 GiB BF16 on Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS)
leave VRAM and live in pinned, mapped host memory. The freed VRAM goes to the expert cache.

- They are loaded through the normal loader into a temporary device arena (so they take the engine form), copied once
  into pinned mapped host memory, and the arena is freed.
- The verify windows read the Q8_0 copy, so this needs `STRATA_HC_Q8=1`. A native GGUF whose hc down/up rows are BF16
  (the GSQ-RCO quants) now also gets a load-time Q8_0 copy, so the Q8 read is taken there too.
- The prompt path stages a layer's pair to the device on its own stream with two slots: the next half's pair is copied
  while this half computes. Without staging it read the pair over PCIe and prompt reads fell from ~1,900 to ~220 tok/s.

Without the variable nothing changes: the default path is the same code as before.

## Why

On a 12 GB card the expert cache is what decides decode speed, and the hyper-connection pair is the largest dense
block left in VRAM. With `STRATA_HC_Q8=1` the decode windows already read the Q8_0 copy, so the BF16 pair is only
needed by the prompt path, which can stage it.

## Measured

RTX 5070 Ti Laptop 12 GB (PCIe 5.0 x8), Core Ultra 7 255HX, 64 GB DDR5-5600, Windows 11, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS (GSQ-RCO),
this branch (main 7695859a + this commit), the same config in both arms except `STRATA_HC_HOST`:

| | `STRATA_HC_HOST` unset | `STRATA_HC_HOST=1` |
|---|---|---|
| expert cache | 2,494 slots (4.04 GiB) | 3,221 slots (5.22 GiB), +29% |
| agent decode, ms/token | 11.376 / 11.778 (mean 11.58) | 11.602 / 11.346 (mean 11.47), -0.9% |
| CPU expert time per verify window | 13.4 / 15.4 ms | 11.5 / 12.8 ms, -15% |

Agent decode: 32 real opencode turns from held-out sessions, 256 tokens each, temperature 1.0, engine ms/token,
order off, on, on, off. On this branch the bigger cache takes ~15% of the CPU experts' time away, but the decode
window barely moves (-0.9%, inside the run-to-run noise): with the stock routing the GPU side is the longer path here.

On my daily fork, which also runs cache-aware routing (PR #1017) and so turns cache slots into speed much more
directly, the same change (2,968 -> 3,221 slots there) measured -8.4% ms/token, and the two-slot prompt staging another -1.3%; warm prompt reads were unchanged (1,923 vs
1,868-1,909 tok/s).

## Checked

- CUDA build (sm_120, MSVC + CUDA 13) and both arms above start, answer and call tools.
- Not built for HIP or SYCL: I have no such card. The host-staging code is in the CUDA prompt path and the loader;
  `STRATA_HC_HOST` is read only there.

## About me

I run Strata every day on a gaming laptop (the hardware above) as the backend of opencode, and keep a fork with the
measurements, the config and the rejected experiments in
[docs/LAPTOP_12GB_TUNING.md](https://github.com/zsariboga/Strata/blob/laptop-12gb/docs/LAPTOP_12GB_TUNING.md)
(55 -> ~140 tok/s engine decode on this laptop since 0.1.38). My earlier PRs: #1536, #1537.
