pulls.author: aspineux
pulls.body:
# Community benchmark: Quadro RTX 8000 48 GB, Xeon E5-2687W 0, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 131K context (v0.1.42)

Results only — one new folder under `bench/results/`, no engine, server or default changes.

**Measured on 2026-10-11 by [aspineux](https://github.com/aspineux).**

## Hardware

- **GPU** Quadro RTX 8000, 49,152 MiB (Turing, sm_75) — **power-limited to 200 W against a
  260 W default**, observed peak 205-224 W, 87-98% utilisation
- **PCIe** gen3 x16 at max; engine's startup probe reports 11.5 GB/s host-to-device
- **CPU** Intel Xeon E5-2687W 0 @ 3.10 GHz, 8c/16t — **no AVX2 and no AVX-512**
  (`-march=native` resolves to `sandybridge`; engine `BUILD.json` says `isa_floor: "avx"`), so
  the CPU expert pool runs the AVX1 path
- **RAM** 125.72 GiB, no hugepages · **OS** Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8.0-146-generic
- **Driver** 580.178.04, engine built against CUDA 12.2
- **Strata** tag `v0.1.42`, commit `61b3fb5d`, source build (`source: local`, `archs: [75]`)

## Model and configuration tested

Unsloth **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL** (4 GGUF shards, ~111 GB), native-experts pack,
`--expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin`, MTP draft head, `--max-context 131072`, `--kv int8`,
`--kv-resident 32768`, `--resident-budget-gib 71`, `--expert-cache auto`, `--prefill auto`,
`--spec 4`, `--spec-min-p 0.70`, `--pcie-frac 0.32`, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`, `--vision`.
One slot (no `--batch`). Server on `127.0.0.1:8080`, no API key.

Engine at startup: `expert cache 13099 slots, 38.26 GiB of VRAM`, `R4 hit path ON`,
`resident 33.47 GiB, pinned 33.47 GiB in 37 s`, `335 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded`.

## What was tested
# Community benchmark: Quadro RTX 8000 48 GB, Xeon E5-2687W 0, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 131K context (v0.1.42)

Results only — one new folder under `bench/results/`, no engine, server or default changes.

**Measured on 2026-10-11 by [aspineux](https://github.com/aspineux).**

## Hardware

- **GPU** Quadro RTX 8000, 49,152 MiB (Turing, sm_75) — **power-limited to 200 W against a
  260 W default**, observed peak 205-224 W, 87-98% utilisation
- **PCIe** gen3 x16 at max; engine's startup probe reports 11.5 GB/s host-to-device
- **CPU** Intel Xeon E5-2687W 0 @ 3.10 GHz, 8c/16t — **no AVX2 and no AVX-512**
  (`-march=native` resolves to `sandybridge`; engine `BUILD.json` says `isa_floor: "avx"`), so
  the CPU expert pool runs the AVX1 path
- **RAM** 125.72 GiB, no hugepages · **OS** Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8.0-146-generic
- **Driver** 580.178.04, engine built against CUDA 12.2
- **Strata** tag `v0.1.42`, commit `61b3fb5d`, source build (`source: local`, `archs: [75]`)

## Model and configuration tested

Unsloth **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL** (4 GGUF shards, ~111 GB), native-experts pack,
`--expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin`, MTP draft head, `--max-context 131072`, `--kv int8`,
`--kv-resident 32768`, `--resident-budget-gib 71`, `--expert-cache auto`, `--prefill auto`,
`--spec 4`, `--spec-min-p 0.70`, `--pcie-frac 0.32`, `--vram-reserve-mib 700`, `--vision`.
One slot (no `--batch`). Server on `127.0.0.1:8080`, no API key.

Engine at startup: `expert cache 13099 slots, 38.26 GiB of VRAM`, `R4 hit path ON`,
`resident 33.47 GiB, pinned 33.47 GiB in 37 s`, `335 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded`.

## What was tested

All prompt and decode throughput comes from the engine's own `timings`, never from dividing
generated tokens by request time. Every prompt is byte-fresh with a nonce; **`reused 0` on all
twelve sweep runs**.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh prompt / decode, 3 runs each | 4K: **728.4** / **61.5** tok/s · 32K: **1,012.8** / **53.1** · 128K: **896.5** / **53.2** |
| Needle recall (`needle_bench`) | **6 of 6 found** — 32K (32,804 tok) and 128K (125,536 tok), depths 10/50/90 |
| Concurrency (`serve_load`, 1/2/4 clients) | 45.0 / 52.7 / 50.8 total tok/s, TTFT p50 0.72 / 3.08 / 7.99 s, 0 errors — flat throughput, one slot queues |
| **Soak, 74.9 min, 708 requests** | **708 ok, 0 failures, 0 timeouts.** Decode 73.95 → 75.0 tok/s (first → last decile), quarters 73.9 / 74.3 / 74.4 / 74.2. RAM +0.06 GiB. VRAM free **335 MiB at all 142 samples**. Peak 69 °C |
| **Cold engine restart** | `POST /unload` 6.79 s (GPU back to 1 MiB used), `POST /load` **65.7 s**. First touch: 32K 1,019.0 prompt / 59.6 decode tok/s, 128K 899.1 / 59.5 |

This answers the open row in `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` for a long soak on a resident setup.

## Limitations, stated plainly

1. **The measurement agent shared the engine.** This box serves the agent that ran the scripts
   (`PI_PROVIDER=strata`, `PI_MODEL=qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-q4_k_xl`), so client and
   subject are the same server. Controls: every measurement in a blocking foreground call, one
   at a time, plus a per-run check that the engine was idle before the request and that the
   newest `/metrics` record matches it. **0 of 9 warm sweep runs flagged contaminated.** The
   soak ran with no other traffic. Please weigh this accordingly.
2. **Warm expert cache for the main sweep.** All nine sweep runs share one long-lived session.
   Run 1 of each length is clearly slower (32K: 37.7 tok/s at 92.6% hit) than runs 2-3 (55.6
   median at ~98% hit); both are reported separately in the README.
3. **The cold arm is a cold *engine*, not a cold boot.** `POST /unload` + `POST /load` restarts
   the engine process (PID 27516 → 106524, GPU 48,180 → 1 MiB) but the shards stay in the OS
   page cache, so file reads are warm. 37 s of the 65.7 s is re-creating the page-locked,
   mapped complement. A reboot number is **not** measured.
4. **200 W power cap** — compare against uncapped Turing cards with that in mind.
5. **Not tested:** cold boot, `--batch` slots and true parallel decode, multi-GPU /
   `--layer-split`, `--calibrate`, vision requests (encoder configured, no image sent), low-RAM
   mode, contexts beyond 131,072, quality benchmarks, and any A/B against another build.

## Two observations, as questions rather than findings

- **`335 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded`** with `--expert-cache auto` and
  `--vram-reserve-mib 700`. `docs/DETAILS.md` names this line as the tell for a cache that leaves
  no free VRAM and cost 7x decode elsewhere. Here decode is healthy (53-61 tok/s on the sweep,
  74.2 tok/s steady across the soak) and the free figure **never moved in 75 minutes**, so I am
  **not** reporting a degradation — but it sits inside the margin the docs warn about. Would a
  `--vram-reserve-mib` sweep say the auto sizer is leaving too little on a 48 GB card?
- **A freshly restarted engine beat the first run inside the long session.** First touch after
  the cold restart: 59.6 / 59.5 decode tok/s at 32K / 128K with 98.9% / 99.3% expert hit. First
  run of each length in the long session: 37.7 / 44.8 tok/s at 92.6% / 96.2% hit. Both are
  first-touch-for-that-prompt. **n = 1 per cell and prompt lengths differ slightly**, so this is
  a question: does the resident complement settle differently after ~1,400 mixed requests than
  after a clean profile-driven start?

## Reproducing

`README.md` in the folder lists every command, the exact engine arguments, and the field names
and units of each JSON file. Folder is 448 KB — no model files, no packs, no API keys, and the
logs contain token counts and timings only, no prompt or answer text.

pulls.title: Linux CUDA: warm adaptive-overlap callbacks before host pinning (opt-in)
pulls.author: oal
pulls.body:
Related to #1975.

## Change

Add a Linux/CUDA-only opt-in, `STRATA_ADAPT_CALLBACK_WARMUP=1`: submit and synchronize one no-op CUDA host callback **before constructing ExpertPool**, while the calling thread still has its original allowed CPU set. This prevents the lazily created callback worker from inheriting the decoding thread's single-core affinity.

The engine change is 12 lines. Swap selection, per-layer callbacks/waits, residency updates and GPU math are unchanged. No callback or synchronization is added when the flag is unset or adaptive overlap is disabled; no global default changes. Also includes a standalone reproducer, benchmark report and flag documentation.

## Why

On this RTX 5090 / Ryzen 9 9950X system, the decoding host is pinned to CPU 0. CUDA's callback worker created after that inherits CPU 0, competing with the host spinning for its completion. Subsequent copies on that stream cannot proceed until the callback runs.

Standalone CUDA/Linux reproduction, 200 unprofiled callback/spin handshakes:

| First callback submitted | Callback affinity | Median latency |
|---|---|---:|
| After caller pinning | CPU 0 | 984.51 us |
| Before caller pinning | CPUs 0–31 | 4.01 us |

## Inference results

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, existing `--adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 160 --adapt-decay 0.97` calibration. NVIDIA 610.57.04, CUDA 13.3.33/sm_120, Fedora Silverblue / Ubuntu 26.04 NVIDIA distrobox.

Normal/warm-up/warm-up/normal starts, fixed `--pcie-frac 0.4`, temperature 0, 512-token caps, no competing inference workload; warm-up rounds excluded:

| Case | Normal callbacks, mean | Early warm-up, mean | Requests/setting |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4K, three prompts | 142.82 TPS | 207.75 TPS | 12 |
| 100K, warmed code prompt | 232.96 TPS | 252.19 TPS | 4 |

Adaptive-gate waiting, including warm-up, fell from **4.357 ms/window to 0.000343 ms/window**. These are a new paired suite, not replacements for #1975's original 126/170 TPS figures.

Full methodology and reproducer commands: `bench/results/2026-10-11-rtx-5090-callback-affinity/README.md`.

## Validation / draft status

- Linux CUDA Release/sm_120 compile and link passed: changed C++ objects linked against existing same-version CUDA libraries. Standalone reproducer compiled and its original equivalent exercised on this machine.
- The inference A/B used an experimental build with its GPU-signal alternative **disabled in every arm**; only callback warm-up changed. This PR's minimal warm-up-only engine patch compiled separately.
- Some token arrays matched; full-suite bit-exactness is **not claimed**, since auto-sized cache capacities and existing-path outputs also varied between starts.
- Keeping this a draft pending clean minimal-PR inference validation, other GPU/driver checks and the upstream-requested HIP/SYCL build checks. The new code is guarded out on HIP/Windows; SYCL's separate program source is unchanged.
- Production remains on the existing overlap-off workaround; the installed engine and calibration were not changed.

Single-card TITAN RTX community report, supersedes #1531 (engine 0.1.40.2 → 0.1.43, produced by the shipped `tools/strata_bench.py` this time). One NVIDIA TITAN RTX 24 GB, Xeon E5-2660 v3, 126 GiB RAM, NVMe, Linux 6.1.183, driver 580.178.04.

## Suite 1 medians (IQ3_S, 262K context, one slot)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Decode, short chat | 65.3 t/s (59.2-69.6) |
| Decode, agent turns | 67.5 t/s (55.2-87.9) |
| Prompt, 4K fresh | 1,140 tok/s, TTFT 3.55 s |
| Prompt, 16K fresh | 1,615 tok/s, TTFT 9.98 s |
| Agent conversation-cache hit | 68.6% |
| Expert cache | 7,946 slots resident; 94.6-98.1% decode hit during the run |

## Opt-in Turing switches

The run's config carries `STRATA_BF16_TC=1` + `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1`. A clean A/B was run on this machine the same day with the same engine and the same suite, one restart per arm (switches off vs on):

- 16K prompt: 1,319 -> 1,615 tok/s (+22%), TTFT 12.2 -> 10.0 s

- agent-turn first token: 4.09 -> 3.96 s

## Limitations

- Speed suite only: no needle/recall run this time (#1531 had 9/9 to 250K on the same card).
- One session with a warm expert cache; cold-box rows would sit lower.
- Desktop compositor on the same GPU; power limit 280 W (default), 251-272 W observed under decode at 1965 MHz, memory utilization 30-52%.
- The tested tree is `d7953d8f`, a working merge of `upstream/main`; its diff to `main` touches setup/serve/tests only, no engine sources.

**Hardware and model.** AMD Instinct MI50 32 GB + Radeon VII 16 GB (gfx906), Core i5-12400F, 61.6 GiB RAM.
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored IQ3_XXS (pack `orca-iq3_xxs`, profile `expert-profile.bin`), context 131,072,

**How it was run.** `tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8085 --runs 3 --clients 1`, against a server
that was already running — hence no engine-log excerpt in the folders.

**What the one flag is worth on a model that fits in RAM** (medians over 3 runs):

| | resident | `--mmap-experts` | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 4K prompt tok/s | 546.9 (546.5-549.5) | 473.6 (375.1-477.0) | −13.4% |
| 16K prompt tok/s | 621.8 (619.7-622.0) | 543.9 (543.2-546.1) | −12.5% |
| 4K / 16K first token | 7.38 / 25.87 s | 8.52 / 29.56 s | +14-15% |
| chat decode | 44.0 (41.9-62.1) | 41.2 (34.8-53.0) | ranges overlap |
| agent decode | 41.7 (34.9-62.0) | 44.7 (33.7-53.2) | ranges overlap |
| 1 concurrent client | 31.7 tok/s | 32.5 tok/s | same |

On this model the page-cache mode costs the prompt path about 12-13% and the first token 14-15%; decode is
not attributable at n=3. The wide range in the mmap arm's 4K row is one run paying for a cold page cache
(375.1). Not measured: the case low-RAM exists for — an arena larger than RAM, where the resident mode cannot
run at all.

**Provenance — these are not stock 0.1.43 numbers.** They come from the gfx906 image we maintain
(`xxdoman/strata-mi50`, engine built from tag v0.1.43). That build carries three HIP build gates (without
them the 0.1.40+ tree does not compile on gfx906) and the rocBLAS solution-table reader — the idea is in
#981, which is gated behind a path gfx906 never compiles, so we widened the gate. The image enables that
table together with the FP16 prompt path it needs (`STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1`, which the engine calls "not
bit-identical to the default"). The table is a prefill lever, not a decode one: measured by environment
switch on the same engine, +9.5% / +10.8% prompt at 16K / 32K, decode unchanged. Model files, packs and the
harness are the stock ones.

If it is more useful as a single folder, say which one and I will drop the other.

pulls.title: tools/strata_bench.py: keep the ROCm driver read on the ROCm path
pulls.author: xxDoman
pulls.body:
On a machine with ROCm only (no NVIDIA tooling) `gpu_info_local()` fills `gpus` from
`rocm-smi --showproductname`'s Card Series lines. The list is therefore not empty, but the
`driver` field in it is `None`, so the `gpu_driver` field of the report picks that `None` and the
`rocm_driver` read a few lines above - in the same function - is thrown away. The header then
prints:

```
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: not read; CUDA: not read
```

With the value used when it is present, it falls back to `rocm_driver`:

```
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic; GPU driver: 7.0.0-38-generic; CUDA: not read
```

Verified on a ROCm machine: `rocm-smi --showdriverversion` returns the version, the report said
"not read" before the change and shows the version after it. The affected field is header
metadata only; nothing in the measurement path changes, and `CUDA: not read` stays, which is
correct on an AMD-only box.

pulls.title: serve: continue a final assistant message instead of restating it (#1950)
pulls.author: MistyMoonR
pulls.body:
Fixes #1950.

A request whose last message is an assistant one (the Anthropic API's prefill, and OpenAI clients that do the same) used to get a prompt that closed that turn and opened a fresh one, so the model wrote a new reply that restated the prefill from the top. A stop string then matched the prefill's own text inside that restatement and ended the reply with finish=stop after ~35 characters. Reproduced with the reporter's exact request on Linux as well (the issue is Windows 0.1.42; our box is 2x RTX 4090, v0.1.42 and v0.1.43): the 35-character stub with `stop: ["\ndef"]`, the full body without the stop list.

The template is unchanged and is the same in 0.1.39 (where the reporter says it did not truncate); the prompt shape is the bug, and whether the restatement reaches a stop string varies with the build's numerics. A client that prefills the assistant turn is asking for a continuation, so the prompt should end inside that turn.

**The fix (serve layer only):**
- `Service.continues_final()`: true when the last message is an assistant one with plain, non-empty text and no tool calls; `"effort_position": "end"` configs keep their own prompt shape.
- For such a request `encode_prompt` renders the template without its generation prompt and leaves the turn's closing `<|im_end|>` off, so the prompt ends with the text to continue, inside the assistant's turn.
- The reply's thinking flag is off for these requests (the closed thinking block is already in the prompt), so the parser starts in content state.

**What does not change** (tested): a request whose last message is a user turn, a final assistant message with tool calls, or whitespace-only text gets the exact old prompt; a stop string still cuts the model's own text the moment the model writes it; `StopMatcher` is untouched (a stop string still never runs across a tool call or thinking).

**Verified:**
- 6 new tests (`FinalAssistantContinuation`, byte tokenizer, so the stop strings are split across tokens): the prompt ends with the prefill inside the turn; a stop string in the prefill never ends the reply; a stop string in the continuation still cuts it; the old shapes are unchanged; the Anthropic route continues too. Full serve suite: 712 OK (11 skipped) on 0.1.43 with this patch; the tree without it runs 706.
- End to end on the engine (2x RTX 4090 sm_89, driver 580.95.05, CUDA 13, layer split 25, --pipeline-windows 2, --spec 4, Swift-1.5 Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, KV int8, 262K context, v0.1.43 + this patch): the reporter's request returns the same full body with and without the stop list; a probe that asks for a second function is cut exactly at the model's own `\ndef`; promptfoo suite 6/6; no reasoning recoveries.
- Not tested: 0.1.39 itself (why it usually did not reach the stop string is not investigated); HIP and SYCL builds (the change is Python-only).

pulls.title: fix(bench): prevent UnicodeDecodeError on Windows
pulls.author: saruiwa
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fix a `UnicodeDecodeError` in `BENCH.bat` on Windows systems using non-UTF-8 default encodings, such as CP932 (Japanese Windows).

## Problem

On Japanese Windows with Python 3.11, running `BENCH.bat` fails during machine information collection because `project_version()` reads `CMakeLists.txt` without specifying an encoding.

Python defaults to CP932, which cannot decode the UTF-8 BOM at the beginning of the file.

```text
UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0xef in position 0: illegal multibyte sequence
```

## Fix

Explicitly use `encoding="utf-8-sig"` when reading `CMakeLists.txt`.

This handles UTF-8 files with or without a BOM, regardless of the system's default encoding.

## Testing

- Reproduced the issue on Japanese Windows with Python 3.11.
- Confirmed that setting `PYTHONUTF8=1` works around the issue.
- [x] Verify that `BENCH.bat` completes without `PYTHONUTF8` after applying the fix.

pulls.title: setup: --draft-vocab latin ships a draft subset for accented Latin-script answers
pulls.author: ANBAL534
pulls.body:
The draft layer proposes tokens from a subset (rt/draft_vocab.bin), so a token outside that subset can never be drafted. The shipped English/code subset (--draft-vocab en, 40,525 ids) holds 37,803 of the vocabulary's 138,517 Latin tokens, and 27 Han / 71 kana / 36 hangul / 34 cjk_punct / 142 Cyrillic ones - the shape #137 fixed for CJK and #597 for French. A Latin-script answer that leans on accents and diacritics (Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Czech, Romanian, Turkish, Vietnamese) has its words in the subset and most of its accented pieces outside it.

--draft-vocab latin ships a subset for those languages: the English/code base with its dedicated non-Latin tokens removed and every non-ASCII Latin token of the vocabulary added - 54,262 ids. It is built with tools/draft_vocab.py --add latin, the same selector the Cyrillic subset uses, so anyone can rebuild it from the GGUF.

**TL;DR**

- a fifth shipped draft subset: --draft-vocab latin, English/code plus the vocabulary's non-ASCII Latin tokens
- 54,262 ids: 51,905 of the 138,517 Latin tokens, and 0 Han, 0 kana, 0 hangul, 0 cjk_punct, 0 Cyrillic
- 178 MiB of draft-head VRAM on IQ3_S, between fr (151) and cyrillic (193), and 170 MiB under the cjk default (348)
- opt-in, one value of an existing flag: no engine change, no new flag, no new dependency

## What changes

- data/draft_vocab_latin.bin (54,262 ids) joins the shipped subsets, and setup.py lists it in DRAFT_VOCABS, in DRAFT_VOCAB_MIB (178 MiB, the same size proportion the other subsets are measured by) and in the --draft-vocab help.
- tools/draft_vocab.py --add latin: the base's ids keep their order and its UTF-8 byte fragments stay (the fallback path keeps working), tokens belonging to another script are dropped, and every token carrying a non-ASCII Latin letter, or a combining mark on one, is added in id order. Unicode script properties do the work: Unicode's Latin script is not one block, so SCRIPTS["latin"] is an empty entry and the regexes decide.
- --add latin refuses to mix with another --add or with --corpus, and needs --base data/draft_vocab_en.bin: it is a whole-script selection over the English/code base, not a corpus selection.
- docs/DETAILS.md documents the subset next to the Cyrillic and French paragraphs.

## Why it helps

- **Accented words get drafted.** The subset carries 51,905 Latin tokens against the base's 37,803, and gives up the 310 dedicated non-Latin tokens the base held (27 Han, 71 kana, 36 hangul, 34 cjk_punct, 142 Cyrillic). A cafÃ©, a StraÃe, a żółć answer has its own tokens in the draft head instead of being spelled out of byte fragments.
- **Cheaper than the default it replaces.** 178 MiB of draft-head VRAM on IQ3_S against the cjk default's 348, for a PC that answers in a Latin-script language and does not need Han at all.
- **Rebuildable, not a blob.** The file comes out of one command, so a user with a language the subset misses can rebuild it, and the shipped one can be checked against the GGUF:

    python tools/draft_vocab.py --gguf <model>-00001-of-0000N.gguf --base data/draft_vocab_en.bin --add latin --out data/draft_vocab_latin.bin

## The subsets today

| --draft-vocab | ids | draft head on IQ3_S | what it adds over English/code |
|---|---|---|---|
| cjk (default) | 106,299 | 348 MiB | Han, kana, hangul, CJK punctuation |
| cyrillic | 58,963 | 193 MiB | the whole Cyrillic script |
| **latin** | **54,262** | **178 MiB** | **every non-ASCII Latin token; the base's 310 non-Latin tokens dropped** |
| fr | 46,211 | 151 MiB | French corpus tokens (#597) |
| en | 40,525 | 133 MiB | - |

The ids column is each shipped file's size in int32 ids; the MiB column is setup.py's DRAFT_VOCAB_MIB, measured on IQ3_S, the largest.

## Testing

- tools/test_draft_vocab_latin.py (3 tests): the selector on a fixed token list - accents kept (café, Straße, façade, żółć, niño, e+U+0301), Han, kana, Cyrillic, Greek, ideographic comma and emoji dropped, byte fragments and punctuation kept; latin as a shared SCRIPTS entry through select_ids; and the two refusals (no --base, mixed with another --add or --corpus).
- tools/test_setup_draft_vocab.py: --draft-vocab latin replaces a shipped subset in the MTP folder and does nothing when run again; the small-card note accepts latin; DRAFT_VOCAB_MIB["latin"] is checked against the shipped file's size the way the other subsets are.
- Setup's own tests, which need no GPU and no download: test_setup_draft_vocab, test_draft_vocab, test_setup_choices, test_setup_golden, test_setup_pins and test_iq_pack all pass on this branch (merged with today's main).
- The subset's numbers above come from tools/draft_vocab.py --stats on the shipped file, read against the Swift 1.5 IQ3_S shard 1 vocabulary.
- Not measured: the acceptance rate and tokens/s per language. The subset is shipped and wired; the comparative run (the same prompts with en, latin and the language's own subset, on one card) is pending, and I will add the numbers here.

## Scope

Only the draft head reads this file. The main model answers in any language: a token outside the subset is written normally, it is simply never drafted. A later --draft-vocab cjk|en|cyrillic|fr replaces the file as it does for the other shipped subsets, and a subset made by hand is kept. Cyrillic, CJK, Greek and Arabic answers draft less than with their own subset, with the base's byte fragments as the fallback - the same trade --draft-vocab en already makes, in exchange for the accented Latin tokens.

pulls.title: [Engine] support the official Flash-Next DFlash2 checkpoint
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The official `incoai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-DFlash2` checkpoint requires five attention layers with 128-wide heads, raw HC-mean target features, dynamic convolution and a predecessor-conditioned selector. This change implements that checkpoint contract and supports original BF16 weights plus Q8_0, Q5_0 and Q4_0 backbone quantizations, using the full shared target output head.

Setup offers MTP (default), experimental DFlash2, or no model drafter. DFlash2 selection enables the local CUDA build, pinned download/conversion and artifact-specific calibration. Weights, private KV pools and attention scratch are accounted for before auto-sizing the expert cache, including the configured context length and elastic growth. MTP and DFlash2 cannot be selected together.

## Related discussion

Explicit maintainer confirmation of the expanded official-checkpoint/setup scope remains pending. This remains a draft while that scope and missing backend validation are resolved.

## Approach

DFlash2 is opt-in behind `STRATA_ENABLE_DFLASH2=ON`. The converter validates the checkpoint geometry and preserves all 45 norm, convolution and selector tensors in BF16; the 36 backbone matrices can be quantized. Setup offers BF16, Q8_0 and Q4_0; Q5_0 is also supported by the converter/runtime and included in the measurements below.

Prompt and conversation snapshots retain the draft context. Cache controls enforce matching actual expert placement before checking output. The shared runtime includes the infrastructure required for proposal verification, a fix for state publication on the opt-in QFUSE path and a fix for the CPU-only loader-test build dependency. The existing default drafter stays MTP.

## Performance: MTP versus DFlash2

Fresh same-source runs on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GiB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 125.7 GiB RAM, Linux, CUDA 13.4 / SM89. Target: local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 pack, BF16 embeddings, FP8 PLE, shared Q5_K output head, INT8 KV. Context 8192, prefill 256, auto expert cache, allocation reserve 512 MiB. All arms fill available VRAM; smaller draft allocations permit more target experts.

Greedy seed 1234, 96 new tokens, four fixed prompts (27/54/33/2425 input tokens), one warmup per prompt and three measured repeats per speculative arm. MTP at floor 0 is run before and after all four DFlash2 variants. An additional MTP run at setup's floor 0.5 follows those series and is the table reference; this sensitivity check was added after the initial series to avoid comparing only against an untuned zero-floor baseline. Both MTP settings remain in the raw evidence.

DFlash2 uses three proposals (verifier capacity 8, fixed block 3); MTP uses up to three proposals (verifier capacity 4), probability floor 0 in the fixed-budget series, plus the separate MTP setup-floor 0.5 control. The DFlash2 block length is fixed; the study does not independently tune each drafter.

CPU prompt sharing, PCIe sharing, adaptive swaps, suffix/lookup drafting and prompt/conversation snapshots are off. Engines run sequentially, with no build or other benchmark during measurements. Values are medians of native decode throughput; prefill/startup are excluded. Geomean weights all four task medians equally.

| Drafter | Code tok/s | Math tok/s | Prose tok/s | Long tok/s | Geomean tok/s (vs MTP) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP (setup floor 0.5) | 38.05 | 44.84 | 39.94 | 55.19 | 44.04 (reference) |
| MTP (floor 0, pooled) | 36.81 | 43.68 | 36.26 | 48.61 | 41.03 (-6.8%) |
| DFlash2 BF16 | **43.25 (+13.7%)** | 43.16 (-3.7%) | 36.40 (-8.9%) | 41.77 (-24.3%) | 41.05 (-6.8%) |
| DFlash2 Q8_0 | **45.08 (+18.5%)** | 44.45 (-0.9%) | 37.05 (-7.2%) | 44.58 (-19.2%) | 42.65 (-3.1%) |
| DFlash2 Q5_0 | **45.19 (+18.8%)** | 44.87 (+0.1%) | 33.71 (-15.6%) | 43.89 (-20.5%) | 41.62 (-5.5%) |
| DFlash2 Q4_0 | **47.11 (+23.8%)** | **45.36 (+1.2%)** | **40.66 (+1.8%)** | 43.52 (-21.1%) | 44.10 (+0.1%) — tie |

Q4_0 has the best observed DFlash2 aggregate, 44.10 versus MTP's 44.04 tok/s (+0.1%). Their per-repeat geometric-mean ranges overlap: treat this as an overall tie. Its clear code advantage is +23.8%; math/prose improve by 1.2%/1.8% in this sample, while the long prompt regresses by 21.1%. Q8_0, Q5_0 and BF16 are slower in aggregate.

Per-repeat geometric means span 43.00–44.10 tok/s for MTP floor 0.5 and 44.07–44.20 tok/s for DFlash2 Q4_0. Bold task cells mean every measured DFlash2 sample exceeded every MTP floor-0.5 sample for that task; percentages are relative to MTP for that column. The bracketing zero-floor MTP's end/start geomean changed by -0.49%. Three samples per DFlash2/default-floor MTP task and six pooled zero-floor MTP samples are too few to establish a general speedup. Non-overlapping observed throughput ranges: bf16/code, Q8_0/code, Q5_0/code, Q4_0/code, Q4_0/math, Q4_0/prose. These are descriptive ranges, not confidence intervals.

| Drafter | Initial runtime MiB | Extra draft-head MiB | GPU expert slots | Minimum GPU free MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP floor 0, start | 801.0 | 275.7 | 3140 | 182 |
| DFlash2 BF16 | 1354.6 | 0.0 | 3038 | 130 |
| DFlash2 Q8_0 | 945.0 | 0.0 | 3193 | 132 |
| DFlash2 Q5_0 | 780.9 | 0.0 | 3256 | 133 |
| DFlash2 Q4_0 | 726.2 | 0.0 | 3277 | 129 |
| MTP floor 0, end | 801.0 | 275.7 | 3141 | 181 |
| MTP floor 0.5 | 801.0 | 275.7 | 3143 | 166 |

The initial runtime column is the engine's load counter, not total process VRAM. MTP subsequently allocates another 275.7 MiB of selected output-head rows, plus index/sampling buffers. DFlash2's counter includes its weights, private KV pools and scratch, and it shares the full target output head without another head-weight copy. Expert slots and GPU-free snapshots show the practical final placement.

[Raw runs, ranges, memory and output controls](https://github.com/j-luwierski/Strata/blob/86af7286254d1efb148cf0aa8c9a96868d4e9f09/bench/results/2026-10-19-dflash2-pr-performance/README.md).

## Validation

Engine source tested at `af85f5ce3b4411833b5529361ae18ffdadbdce3f`, based on main `e88ee39d1d6be6e3364183af3b39b62a7ed6f211`. Performance evidence commit: `86af7286254d1efb148cf0aa8c9a96868d4e9f09`; it adds scripts/results without changing engine code. Linux, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 16 GiB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 125.7 GiB RAM, CUDA 13.4, GCC 14.2, SM89.

**Passed:**

- CUDA extension ON/OFF builds; 12 selected CUDA CTests, plus extension-OFF loader rejection.
- 203 setup/conversion/cache/tool tests and 342 server tests.
- CPU-only full build after fixing the loader test's CUDA-header dependency.
- Main/OFF/ON regression comparison: 768 candidate IDs match main across AR/MTP, greedy/sampled requests and three prompts. Final rebuild executable hashes are unchanged.
- Official Q8 DFlash2 cache test: eight cases, 256/256 IDs equal both fresh DFlash2 and target-only controls at matching 2000 expert slots. Checks live continuation, parked conversation restoration, prompt snapshots, rewind and sampled-to-greedy transition.
- Full 128K draft-memory allocation with BF16/Q8/Q4 and short generation; one actual 8192→16384-cell growth with an 8448-token prompt.

Commands, source/executable hashes, raw IDs and logs are in [validation evidence](https://github.com/j-luwierski/Strata/blob/86af7286254d1efb148cf0aa8c9a96868d4e9f09/bench/results/2026-10-19-dflash2-pr/README.md).

**Failed:**

- Four CPU CTests fail with the available dependency/tooling: three require missing Trellis types and one reports an AVX512 allowlist violation. All four reproduce on unmodified main. The full candidate CPU run has 44 passed, one skipped and four failed tests.
- Initial CPU-only build and setup golden-fixture failures were corrected and rerun successfully; original failures are retained.
- The initial default-path harness rejected a valid early EOS from a truncated prompt. The corrected harness uses the full prompt and compares actual IDs; its failed attempt is retained.
- An earlier 256 MiB VRAM-reserve startup failed to fit verifier allocations. That failed attempt and an interrupted fixed-cache experiment are retained in the earlier quantization evidence and excluded from measured medians.

- A preliminary performance restart overlapped teardown of the preceding engine and failed the host memory guard. The previous process tree was fully stopped before the final complete series. That failure and the interrupted prefill-512 attempt are retained and excluded from medians.

**Not run:**

HIP/SYCL compilation and execution (ROCm/`icpx` unavailable), Metal, Windows, multi-GPU, concurrent requests and a full 128K-token prompt. The CUDA extension is explicitly restricted to one GPU and serial requests. Shared backend changes still require the missing builds; keep this draft pending targeted validation.

## Limits

Sampled DFlash2 requests use target-only fallback. Exact cache output checks cover one-proposal split windows and fixed placement; they do not prove byte equality for every arithmetic path. Disk session restoration is unsupported.

Maximum VRAM residency means each drafter can fit a different number of target experts. This measures the practical combined effect of smaller draft weights and a larger expert cache, rather than isolated kernels. Different placements can also change target rounding; matching-placement output controls and raw results are retained. Performance conclusions apply to this hardware and these prompts only.

pulls.title: serve: --prompt-cache-spread, checkpoints kept spread back from the conversation's end (opt-in)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

Opt-in `--prompt-cache-spread`: when the conversation checkpoints are over `--prompt-cache`, the one that leaves is
chosen so that the kept ones stay spread back from the conversation's end, instead of the least recently used. Without
the flag nothing changes.

## Why

The engine keeps 6 checkpoints and rotates them by least recent use. Every turn adds one at its start, so after a few
short turns all of them sit within the last 1-2K tokens (plus the pinned system-prompt root). That is fine while a
client only appends. Agent clients do not always: they trim an old tool output, drop a step, or rewrite an earlier turn
a few thousand tokens back. The new prompt then matches none of the recent checkpoints, the resume falls back to the
system prompt, and the whole conversation is read again.

Found with the pi coding agent (and the pi-blackhole extensions) on a long agent session, from the engine log:

| conversation held | new prompt | same as held for | resumed at | read again |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 210,952 | 210,528 | 204,349 (6K before the end) | 9,525 | 201,003 tokens, 100 s |
| 206,572 | 205,253 | 163,508 (42K before the end) | 0 | 205,253 tokens, 101 s |

In both, a checkpoint a few thousand tokens before the edit would have saved most of the read; least recent use had
rotated those out.

## How

- `conv_cache::spread_victim` (`include/strata/program/conv_cache.hpp`): over the chain (ascending), the victim is the
  checkpoint whose removal leaves the smallest gap for its distance from the newest one,
  `(len[i+1] - len[i-1]) / (len[newest] - len[i-1])`. Dense recent points go first, so the kept ones thin out
  geometrically towards the root. Never the root, the newest or a pinned (`strata_prefix`) one; the
  `--prompt-cache-tail` checkpoint first, as in the existing policy; with no candidate, the existing policy.
- `generate.cpp`: the flag, and the choice between the two policies at the one place a checkpoint is dropped.
- The resume is unchanged: a checkpoint is used only when the prompt starts with exactly its tokens and pictures.
- Same number of checkpoints, no more RAM.

In a simulation of 200 turns of 1,000 tokens after a 9,525-token system prompt (`conv_cache_test`):

| 6 checkpoints, kept (tokens before the end) | edit 6K back | edit 42K back |
|---|---:|---:|
| least recent use: 0, 1K, 2K, 3K, 4K and the root | reads 200K | reads 200K |
| spread: 0, 1K, 3K, 8K, 43K, 200K | reads **8K** | reads **43K** |

## Measured

2x CMP 50HX (Turing sm_75, `--layer-split auto`), 2x Xeon E5-2670 v2, 64 GB RAM, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, CUDA 13.3,
GCC 14. An 82,593-token conversation (a 65K-token document, then 20 short turns sent 2 at a time, each request
continuing the previous one), then the same conversation with a turn ~6 steps back rewritten and a question; greedy,
thinking off:

| | resumed at | time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `--prompt-cache-spread` | 73,610 | **10.2 s** |
| `--prompt-cache 0` (read in full) | 0 | 40.0 s |

With the expert placement fixed (`--adapt-swaps 0 --pcie-frac 0.17`) the answer after the resume was the same text as
the full read. Without fixing it, two full reads already differ in wording (the placement moves with timing), so that
comparison needs the fixed placement.

Tests: `conv_cache_test` passes, with the new cases (the simulation above against least recent use; every candidate
pinned and one slot fall back to the existing policy). Not run on Windows or HIP.

## Relation to #1937

Found while measuring the disk tier of #1937 on the same agent sessions, with a diagnostic that logs how many tokens a
request read again although a held conversation had them. It is independent of #1937: any long conversation whose
client edits its history benefits, with or without parked conversations.

## How to try

Add `"--prompt-cache-spread"` to the config's `args`.

pulls.title: Tool calls: a boolean parameter written as True/False is a boolean
pulls.author: ChrizzzXX
pulls.body:
## Title
Tool calls: a boolean parameter written as `True`/`False` reaches the client as a boolean

## Summary
With `huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated-GGUF` (`swift-IQ2_XS`, engine 0.1.42, RTX 5090 Laptop) the model writes boolean
tool parameters the Python way:

```
<function=licht_schalten>
<parameter=an>
True
</parameter>
...
```

`parse_tool_call` JSON-decodes non-string parameters, `json.loads("True")` fails, and the value is passed on as the string `"True"`.
A client that checks the schema (or does `if args["an"] is True`) then gets a string instead of a boolean. It happened in 4 of 4
calls of the same request in our test; integer and string parameters of the same call were fine.

## What changed
- `serve/frontend.py` (`parse_tool_call`): when the tool's schema declares the parameter `"type": "boolean"` and the value is
  `true`/`false` in any case (surrounding spaces ignored), it becomes a boolean. Everything else is unchanged: string parameters stay
  strings (`"True"` in a string field is kept as written), other values are still JSON-decoded, and an unparseable boolean value
  (`maybe`) is still passed through as before.
- `serve/test_frontend.py`: `BooleanToolArguments` covers `True`/`False`/`true`/`false`/` TRUE `, a string parameter holding `True`,
  an integer next to it, and the pass-through of an invalid value.

`python -m unittest serve.test_frontend serve.test_server` passes (306 tests on our machine). After the change the same request
returns `{"raum": "Wohnzimmer", "an": true, "helligkeit": 40}`.

## Extra Notes
Only the XML-style `<parameter=...>` path is touched; the JSON tool-call path (`json_tool_call`) already gets real JSON booleans.
