pulls.title: --pool-affinity measure: on a hybrid CPU, time the all and p-cores pool layouts at start and take the faster (opt-in)
pulls.author: Xiaomi2008
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (searched the open issues and pull requests; nothing covers this)

## Summary
`--pool-affinity measure` (opt-in; hybrid CPUs, native packs): at start the `all` and `p-cores` pool layouts are timed on the pack's own experts, and the faster one is taken.

The default layout puts a worker on every physical core, and a layer's experts are done when the slowest worker is. On a Core i7-13700K (8 P + 8 E cores) the E-cores make the verify window wait, by an amount that changes from run to run, so a fixed rule did not seem right.

What is timed is the decode's own call (`run_split_multi_native`): two experts of four tokens per layer, every layer in turn, the host spinning ~150 us between two layers as it does on the GPU's flags, three interleaved blocks per layout, about a second in all. `p-cores` is taken unless `all` is more than 10% faster. One line prints both readings and the choice.

## What changed
- src/program/generate.cpp: the `measure` value of `--pool-affinity`, its usage text, `measure_pool_affinity()` and the call before the pool is built.
- docs/DETAILS.md: one entry with the measurements and the limit.

## Extra Notes
### Measured

This branch (0.1.42 + this change), Core i7-13700K, RTX 5090, 64 GB, Windows 11, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 128K context, one 8K prompt and the same 1,500 forced tokens (`--spec-follow`), three interleaved rounds:

| | decode tok/s | CPU pool per verify window |
|---|---|---|
| default (`all`, 15 workers) | 146.6 / 151.8 / 158.0 | 6.3 - 7.6 ms |
| `--pool-affinity measure` (read `all` at 16.4 - 17.6 ms, took `p-cores`) | 200.0 / 201.5 / 204.8 | 2.1 - 2.2 ms |
| `--pool-affinity p-cores` (7 workers) | 200.3 / 203.9 / 204.9 | 2.1 ms |

### Its limit

It is one reading at start and is not repeated. Over four server starts of one day on 0.1.41 it read `all` at 14.8, 21.9 and 25.3 ms against 6.1 to 6.2 ms for `p-cores` and took `p-cores`; once it read `all` at 6.6 ms against 8.6 ms and took `all`. The same day `all` ran the pool at 2.4 ms per window in one run and 6.7 to 13.2 ms in others. Where the E-cores' speed changes while the engine runs, `--pool-affinity p-cores` is the steady choice, and the docs entry says so. If a fixed `p-cores` default on hybrid CPUs is preferred to this switch, these numbers may still be of use for that.

### What it leaves alone

- Without the value nothing new runs: the option parses as before and the function is not called. I did not run the byte-identity tests; this is from the code path.
- The layout changes no result, only where threads run.
- On a CPU that is not hybrid, or without a native pack with its experts in RAM, it says so and keeps `all`.
- `--pool-affinity auto | p-cores | all` are unchanged.

### Not tested

- Built for CUDA only: sm_120, CUDA 13.0.88, MSVC 14.50 with nvcc's `--allow-unsupported-compiler`. **HIP and SYCL were not compiled**; the change is in `generate.cpp`, which both build (the SYCL tree has its own copy, which this PR does not touch).
- One hybrid CPU. No Linux run, no other Intel hybrid part, no AMD card.
- No unit test: the function needs a loaded pack and a pool.

Docs: one entry in `docs/DETAILS.md`.

### The whole tuned config on this PC, through the server (context, not this change alone)

0.1.42 built from source, the same engine binary in both columns, the Python server, the same requests, two interleaved rounds (each: a start, three 9K prompts, a 54K and an 85K prompt). Core i7-13700K, RTX 5090, 64 GB, Windows 11, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 128K, image encoder on the GPU.

| request | setup's arguments | tuned config |
|---|---|---|
| decode, 9K prompt, first request after the start | 118 / 144 tok/s | 184 / 177 tok/s |
| decode, 9K prompt, 2nd and 3rd | 173 - 194 tok/s | 195 - 212 tok/s |
| decode, 54K prompt | 153 / 156 tok/s | 217 / 198 tok/s |
| decode, 85K prompt | 149 / 131 tok/s | 179 / 192 tok/s |
| prefill, 9K prompt, 2nd and 3rd | 4,180 - 4,760 tok/s | 6,410 - 6,520 tok/s |
| prefill, 54K and 85K prompts | 5,700 - 5,980 tok/s | 6,880 - 6,900 tok/s |
| VRAM free with everything loaded | 458 / 561 MiB | 1,039 / 1,083 MiB |

The tuned config differs from setup's arguments in more than this PR, so the table does not isolate it:
- `--pool-affinity p-cores` (what this PR's `measure` picked in three of four starts): the largest part of the decode difference. The isolated measurement is the table above (146.6 - 158.0 against 200.0 - 204.9 tok/s).
- `STRATA_GR_V3=1` and `--adapt-every 1 --adapt-swaps 80 --adapt-decay 0.97`, existing switches: on the same forced text, P-cores in both arms, 220 - 223 tok/s without and 236 - 239 with both (two interleaved rounds).
- `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1` and `--prefill auto:16384`, existing switches: the prefill rows. On 0.1.41, a 30K prompt: 5,644 - 5,676 tok/s without, 6,533 - 6,575 with both (two rounds). Quality of the fused kernel here, teacher-forced over 2,000 tokens after an 8K prompt: 17 - 19 tokens differ from the text the default prompt path generated, against 9 for the default path itself.
- `--pcie-frac 0.25`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1500` and `STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device` (#1911): the VRAM row.

Not the released 0.1.42 binary: both columns are this source build.

pulls.title: Expert cache: STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device reads the whole card's free VRAM through NVML (opt-in, Windows + NVIDIA)
pulls.author: Xiaomi2008
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none (searched the open issues and pull requests; nothing covers this)

## Summary
`STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device` (opt-in, Windows + NVIDIA): `--expert-cache auto` reads the free VRAM of the whole card through NVML, and takes the smaller of that and CUDA's own figure.

Under WDDM `cudaMemGetInfo` answers for the calling process only. Measured on an RTX 5090, driver 610.88: with 6 GiB written by another process, `cudaMemGetInfo` in a second process still read 30,994 MiB free where NVML read 24,348. So with the image encoder loaded (1,547 MiB here) the cache is sized from a figure that much too high, the check after the slots are written reads less than the reserve, and the cache is shrunk by guesses.

Six starts of one config on 0.1.40.3 and 0.1.41 (Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 128K, the default 700 MiB reserve, image encoder on the GPU) ended with 9,002 to 14,454 slots and 93 MiB to 10 GiB of VRAM free.

The switch is used in three places: the sizing, the check after the slots are written, and the serve check's "VRAM free with everything loaded" figure. `nvml.dll` is loaded from the system directory at first use and the device is found by its PCI bus id. One line at first use prints both figures.

## What changed
- src/core/expert_cache.cpp: `device_free_bytes()` takes the smaller of CUDA's figure and NVML's when the variable is set (a new `nvml_device_free`, Windows CUDA builds only).
- include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp: the comment on `device_free_bytes()`.
- src/program/generate.cpp: the serve check's free figure goes through the same function (one line).
- docs/DETAILS.md: one entry with the measurements.

## Extra Notes
### Measured

This branch (0.1.42 + this change), RTX 5090, Core i7-13700K, 64 GB, Windows 11, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, 128K, image encoder on the GPU, three interleaved server starts each:

| | slots | shrink steps | VRAM free with everything loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (700 MiB reserve) | 13,543 | 2 | 336 / 602 / 602 MiB |
| `STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1500` | 13,102 - 13,130 | 1 | 1,107 / 1,225 / 1,288 MiB |

At the sizing NVML read 23,695 MiB free where CUDA read 25,458. On 0.1.41 with the switch: one pass, 13,007 to 13,188 slots and 973 to 1,392 MiB free over seven starts.

Why the headroom matters here: a run that filled the card to 0 MiB free decoded 80-115 tok/s where the same forced text ran at 205-230 tok/s with 900 MiB or more free.

### What it leaves alone

- Unset, `device_free_bytes()` returns what it did, and the serve check's figure is the same value (`min` of the same number). I did not run the byte-identity tests; this is from the code path: the new branch is behind the environment variable.
- The cache size changes no output bit.
- Linux, HIP and SYCL: the new code is compiled for Windows CUDA builds only (`STRATA_EC_NVML_FREE`).
- The shrink loop itself is unchanged.

### Not tested

- Built for CUDA only: sm_120, CUDA 13.0.88, MSVC 14.50 with nvcc's `--allow-unsupported-compiler` (this PC has no Visual Studio 2022). **HIP and SYCL were not compiled.** `expert_cache.cpp` and `generate.cpp` are built by both; the HIP build compiles none of the new branch (it sits under `!STRATA_EC_NO_VMM`), SYCL I did not look at.
- One machine, one card, one driver. No multi-GPU run (the device is matched by PCI bus id, which I could only exercise with one card).
- Cards where another process holds no VRAM show no difference, by construction.

Docs: one entry in `docs/DETAILS.md`.

### In use, with the rest of a tuned config (context)

0.1.42 built from source, through the server, two interleaved rounds of the same requests on this PC: setup's arguments ended with 458 / 561 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded, a config with `STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device` and `--vram-reserve-mib 1500` with 1,039 / 1,083 MiB. That config also changes the CPU pool layout and other switches, and its speed table is in #1912; none of the speed difference there is this change, which only decides how much VRAM the cache takes.

pulls.title: arena: pin by need (STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED=1) and a PCIe share floor (STRATA_PCIE_MIN1=1), +5-7 % prompt read on Windows
pulls.author: RubenTorney
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1903

## Summary

On Windows `cudaHostRegister` of the whole arena fails (WDDM shared budget, about half the RAM) and the sliced fallback
registers the first ~30 GiB, layers 0-31 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S: layers 32-47 never get a PCIe share, while ~10 GiB of the
registered prefix hold GPU-resident experts that DMA never reads. With `STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED=1` the arena gives every blob a
page-aligned stride (+0.15 % RAM) and registers the expert profile's non-GPU-resident experts by rank, up to
`STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB` (29 GiB by default on Windows, to leave the shared segment some room). `STRATA_PCIE_MIN1=1` sends one
miss over PCIe as soon as a layer has two (the share `(nmiss * pcie_num) >> 8` rounds to 0 at 1-2 misses). Both opt-in.

RTX 3090 + Ryzen 5 5600X: 28.96 GiB registered = 92 % of the non-resident experts, all 48 layers get a PCIe share.
**Prompt read +5-7 %** at 56K-117K tokens (2,172 → 2,313 and 2,091 → 2,208 tok/s). Decode: level on the blocking tier
(x0.999 cold, 6/12), **x1.02-1.03 (10 of 12 prompts faster)** on top of `--adapt-async 1` (the other PR) with `--pcie-frac 0.6`.

## What changed

- `src/core/pinned.cu`, `include/strata/core/pinned.hpp`: a `PinnedArena` constructor that registers a list of byte ranges
  in order before any page is touched, stops at the cap or the first refusal, and unregisters them in the destructor;
  `PadMap`, the per-blob placement used by the loaders (`load_experts_ranges`, `load_experts_gguf`) when the layout is padded.
  `STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB=auto` applies to this path too.
- `src/platform/memory.cpp`, `.hpp`: `lock_resident_ranges` keeps the holes between the ranges resident (one working-set raise).
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`, `.hpp` (`ArenaExpertSource`): `arena_off()` (one offset function for `blob`, `blob_at`,
  `pinned`, `device_alias`, the ranges); `set_pin_priority`; `pinned()` / `device_alias()` / `pcie_layer()` by ranges (a blob is
  pinned only if it lies wholly inside one registered range); `STRATA_PCIE_MIN1` in the PCIe share.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: before the arena is loaded, the profile's pairs past the estimated GPU-resident count (from
  `--expert-cache` or the free VRAM, as the cache's `auto` computes it) are ranked into ranges; one log line
  `pin by need: N ranges, X GiB pinned, Y % of the non-resident experts`.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`, `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx3090-5600x-arena-pin-by-need/`.

## How the default path was checked

- Without `STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED` the layout, the loaders and the sliced pin are untouched. Bit-exact mode
  (`STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0`), greedy, 6 prompts: on the 5 prompts that v0.1.42 reproduces between
  two of its own fresh engines, this branch without the variables gives the same answers byte for byte (sha256). The 6th
  prompt differs between two runs of v0.1.42 itself in that mode on this machine.
- Built: CUDA only (Windows, VS 2022 17.14, CUDA 12.8, sm_86). **Not built: HIP, SYCL**; `pinned.cu` and `expert_source.cpp`
  are shared with those builds (the new code is host code behind the variable).

## Extra Notes

- The padded layout reads `experts.bin` through the buffered loader (a contiguous unbuffered read cannot land strided); load
  speed was unchanged here (6.7 GiB/s).
- `STRATA_VERIFY_ARENA`'s checksum is over the padded layout when the variable is on (not comparable with the packed one).
- The resident count is estimated before the cache exists; an error costs DMA-registered bytes on resident experts or skips a
  few hot ones, never correctness (`STRATA_PIN_BY_NEED_SKIP=N` sets it).
- Independent of the other PR (no shared code); the decode gain shows only with it.

pulls.title: adaptive tier: --adapt-async 1 in the arena mode (one GPU, copy-in only), x1.07-1.11 cold decode on an RTX 3090 + Ryzen 5 5600X
pulls.author: RubenTorney
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: #1903

## Summary

In the arena mode the blocking adaptive tier creates and joins a thread every verify window and the next window waits for its
copies: ~3.2 of 25.9 ms per window on this machine (the interval #1863 found outside the timing breakdown). This lets
`--adapt-async 1` run in the arena too. The arena holds every expert in RAM, so a round is a copy-in only: no copy back, no RAM
move, no exchange buffers. Opt-in; without `--adapt-async 1` (and in the resident RAM mode, and on several GPUs) nothing changes.

Cold A/B against the v0.1.42 tag (12 distinct prompts x 2 rounds, fresh server per arm and round, paired): **x1.07, faster on
12 of 12 prompts** (97.2 → 107.7 tok/s; x1.11 in an earlier run the same day, when the learned profile was younger and the tier
swapped more). One cold window: 25.9 → 21.6 ms, adapt wait 0.41 ms, join 0.

## What changed

- `src/program/generate.cpp`
  - The `--adapt-async` gates accept the arena (`srcp == &arena_src`) on one GPU; a layer split stays on the blocking tier.
  - The asynchronous tier's state machine, arena case: `exchange = false`, the source blob is `ArenaExpertSource::blob_at()`,
    the RAM-move steps are skipped. The evicted slot is marked non-resident and `res_upload` runs before the round's copies are
    posted; an expert becomes resident only once its copy's event has completed.
  - `STRATA_ADAPT_ASYNC_WAIT=1` (default in the arena): the tick after a round waits for that round, so the window in which an
    expert turns GPU-resident does not depend on timing. `STRATA_ADAPT_PICK_INLINE=1` (default in the arena): the pick runs on
    the host thread, one round per window. `STRATA_ADAPT_ASYNC_BATCH=N` caps the copies posted per tick (default 0 = all;
    16 measured 16 % slower here). Arena rounds are as large as the blocking tier's (`--adapt-swaps`, not capped at 96).
  - Fences: every K/V grow (`kvg_ensure`'s quiesce lambdas), `kv_quiesce` and the `VRAM` command now land the round in flight
    (`adapt_quiesce`) — they only called `apply_pending(true)`, so a swap still copying could write a slot just lent to the K/V.
    This also applies to the resident mode's asynchronous tier. A failed round still drains its copies before slots move.
  - `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1`: the serial `--serve` line adds `adapt wait X join Y, Z swaps/window` (part of #1863).
  - `--adapt-async` help text.
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`, `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`: `ArenaExpertSource::blob_at()`, `blob()` without the
  read counter (it runs on the job thread).
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the arena paragraph next to `--adapt-async 1`.
- `bench/results/2026-10-11-community-rtx3090-5600x-arena-async/`: method, numbers, raw data (sha256 of every answer), harness.

## How the default path was checked

- Bit-exact mode (`STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0`), greedy, 6 prompts, two fresh v0.1.42 engines and one of this branch:
  on the 5 prompts that v0.1.42 reproduces between two of its own fresh engines, v0.1.42 and this branch without
  `--adapt-async` give the same answers byte for byte (sha256), with `--expert-cache auto` and with a fixed size. The 6th
  prompt differs between two runs of v0.1.42 itself in that mode on this machine.
- Built: CUDA only (Windows, VS 2022 17.14, CUDA 12.8, sm_86). **Not built: HIP, SYCL** (no such hardware here); the change is
  host code in `generate.cpp` / `expert_source.cpp`, no backend-specific path.

## Extra Notes

- Like the resident mode's asynchronous tier, answers are not bit-exact from run to run with the option on (which window first
  computes a swapped-in expert on the GPU). On this machine greedy answers already differ between two fresh engines of the
  unpatched build (the CPU/GPU split of the misses depends on timing).
- After a long prompt the gain shrinks: the prompt itself has moved its experts into VRAM (hit rate 97-99 %), the tier has
  little left to swap: level with v0.1.42 at 56K and 117K tokens (95.3 / 97.3 and 97.0 / 96.1 tok/s).
- Robustness (full test branch: this change plus other opt-in switches): 63K-token prompt then 4 follow-up turns, K/V grown
  to 65,536 cells during the conversation, no `ERR`.
- Reviewed for fence correctness before the A/B (VRAM command after STOP, K/V grow, request start drain, error path).

pulls.author: midhatn

The synchronous mock request can finish before the asynchronous keepawake worker runs. The service test then waits for an ON/OFF pair that the worker never needed to emit, causing an intermittent assertion failure.

Keep the mock request generator open until the fake Windows call records ON, then finish it and check OFF. Register cleanup for both request generators and the worker so failed assertions also release them. This changes only the test fixture; the runtime's keepawake behavior is unchanged.

Validation on upstream main `61b3fb5d`: the original test fails deterministically when an event barrier delays the worker until after the mock request ends. The corrected fixture passes five runs with that controlled ordering, and all six keepawake tests pass. The real Windows power API was forbidden throughout; no model was loaded and no actual suspend/resume behavior is claimed.

pulls.title: serve: the thinking budget's continuation keeps the tokens emitted after the STOP, so it is not read again
pulls.author: Vokturz
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open for this (searched); the closest are #1620 (fixed in 0.1.42: a cancel before the restored conversation is read past) and #615 (why the Monitor's prefill column looks low for such requests). This one is a cancel after the generation: the thinking budget's STOP.

## Summary
When the thinking reaches `reasoning_budget_tokens`, the server stops the engine and continues with the prompt + the generated tokens + the wrap-up. The engine emits a verify window's tokens at once and finishes the window in flight after the STOP, so it can emit a few tokens past the server's cut. Those were drained and dropped, but the engine's session holds them (every emitted token but the last). With two or more past the cut, the session was no longer a prefix of the continuation: the engine fell back to the prompt's checkpoint and read all of the thinking again.

Now the tokens read while draining to DONE are kept and join the thinking before the wrap-up, so the continuation holds the whole session and reuses it.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`
  - `StrataEngine.generate` keeps the `T` lines it reads while draining to DONE after a STOP in `self.after_stop` (reset at every request, before the batch branch, which does not fill it).
  - `Service._run`, at the budget's wrap-up: the `after_stop` tokens are fed like the rest of the thinking (emitted to the client, counted, appended to `seg`) before `REASONING_WRAP_UP`, when there is room and they are plain thinking.
  - `after_stop_continues(tok, ids, stop_ids)`: no end-of-turn token among them, no `<` (it may start `</think>` or a call, which the parser treats on its own), no character split at their end. Otherwise the continuation is built as before.
- `serve/test_server.py`: `ThinkingBudgetAfterStop` - a mock engine that emits 3 tokens past the stop (they join the thinking and the second prompt is the first + all of them + the wrap-up), a tag past the stop is left out as before, and the helper.

## Extra Notes
**Answers can differ:** where the engine had run past the cut, the thinking now keeps those few tokens (at most what one verify window emits) before the wrap-up, where it used to drop them, and the answer is written after them. A request without a budget, or whose budget is not reached, is unchanged.

**Measured** on engine 0.1.42 (local CUDA 13.3 build), RTX 3090, WSL2, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, `--spec 4 --max-context 204800 --kv-resident 32768`, the same ~720-token coding prompt with a random nonce, one request at a time:

| `reasoning_budget_tokens` 300, 20 requests | continuations that reused the session | read the thinking again |
|---|---|---|
| before | 12 | 8 (40%), 4.9 s in all |
| after | 20 | 0 |

After, the thinking kept 0-5 tokens past the budget (`thinking budget reached (300..305 tokens)`: 7 x 300, 8 x 301, 2 x 302, 2 x 304, 1 x 305). With a 12,000-token budget the same race costs a re-read of the whole thinking, here 12,023 tokens in 4.4 s:

```
prompt 710 tokens = 0 reused + 710 read in 1629 ms (435.8 tok/s), 12004 generated in 92457 ms ...
prompt 12728 tokens = 705 reused + 12023 read in 4418 ms (2721.5 tok/s), 5780 generated ...
```

After the change, 3 of 3 such continuations reused 12,710-12,711 tokens and read 19.

**Tests:** `python -m unittest serve.test_server serve.test_request_accounting`: 301 tests pass.

**Not changed here:** the batch slots' path; the forced tool call that opens after the thinking (`tool_choice`), the other STOP-and-continue path, which has the same pattern; `reasoning_close_retry`; the engine. **Not tested:** native Linux or Windows, other models.

pulls.title: setup: build the HIP engine with the K-quant MMQ prompt kernels (UD-Q4_K_XL's experts on RDNA2, 633 -> 1,036 tok/s)
pulls.author: elightcap
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: relates to #429 and #1278 (no issue of its own)

## Summary
`build_engine_hip` in `setup.py` passed `-DSTRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=ON` but not `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON`, so a setup-built AMD engine has no MMQ kernels for UD-Q4_K_XL's Q4_K / Q5_K / Q5_1 experts and the prompt path dequantizes every expert to FP16 and multiplies it with hipBLAS. On an RX 6900 XT that was 65-77% of a prompt's GPU time (`STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1`: dequant + the two GEMMs), about 5 TFLOPS on the gate/up product of an 8K chunk. The HIP CMake branch already lists the K-quant instances under the option (#1278 registers their test and measured the model on an R9700 built by hand with the flag); this makes setup turn it on, so ggml's RDNA2 MMQ tiles take those formats. The option is compile-time only: packs without K-quant experts run exactly as before.

## What changed
- `setup.py`: `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON` in the HIP cmake flags, with a comment. The AMD confirmation for UD-Q4_K_XL (#429) now says the model has run on one AMD card (this one) and is untested on the user's, instead of calling the prompt kernels NVIDIA-only; the `nvidia_only` flag and the question itself are unchanged.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`, RDNA2 section: a bullet with the measurement below, the decode-window profile of the same machine and a per-request `pcie_frac` sweep (0.55 / 0.35 / 0.2 / 0.1 -> 57.2 / 56.2 / 54.2 / 53.3 ms per window, so the smallest share was about 7% faster per window here; the 0.1.42 CUDA rule would pick 0.35).

What it leaves alone: CUDA builds, the engine's own MMQ plan (`mmq_plan`, `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` still gives the FP16 path), `STRATA_DENSE_MMQ` (still opt-in), the gfx11 fused experts.

## Measured
RX 6900 XT 16 GB (gfx1030, PCIe 4.0 x16), Ryzen 9 5950X, 128 GB DDR4, Arch Linux, ROCm 7.2.4, engine 0.1.42 built with and without `-DSTRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS=ON` (both with #1683's lend-region fix, which does not touch the kernels), `--resident-budget-gib 71 --prefill auto --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072`, `STRATA_HIP_PROMPT_F16=1 STRATA_SH_STREAM=1 STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7`, one run per cell, greedy, the same prompts:

| prompt | without | with K-quant MMQ |
|---|---|---|
| fresh 7.8K tokens | 633 tok/s (dequant 0.85 s, gate/up 4.5 s, down 1.2 s of 11.3 s) | **1,036 tok/s** (0.39 / 1.15 / 0.52 of 7.0 s) |
| fresh 15.8K tokens | 677 tok/s (1.7 / 9.1 / 2.4 of 22.4 s) | **1,104 tok/s** (0.77 / 2.33 / 1.06 of 13.8 s) |
| fresh 887 tokens | 4.6 s of GPU time | 3.5 s |
| 250-token follow-up chunk on an 8K chat | 2.8 s (dequant 0.44, gate/up 1.24, down 0.59) | 1.8 s (0.24 / 0.16 / 0.08); `wait copy` is then 53% of it |

Hidden code words placed mid-document at 8K and 16K were found (one prompt each). Decode is unchanged: 58-68 ms per verify window before and after, 32-38 tok/s. The output is not bit-identical to the FP16 path (int8 MMQ activations), as on CUDA, where this is the path setup builds for the model. After this change the short chunks of an agent's turns are bound by the experts streamed over PCIe; `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto` (opt-in on HIP) took the 887-token prompt from 3.75 to 2.65 s and the 250-token chunk from 2.23 to 1.50 s here, but one card is not enough to change that default, so it is only noted.

Not tested: another AMD card, Windows HIP, the greedy comparison against llama.cpp, `hip_prefill_mmq_kquant` (tests are off in setup's build; #1278 ran it on an R9700).

pulls.title: resident RAM mode: a budget keeps the prompt path's lend region when it has room (#1683)
pulls.author: elightcap
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1683

## Summary
With `--resident-budget-gib`, the RAM copy kept no lend region: `pin_cache_complement` set `lend_from_slot = -1` in its budget branch, so the experts of the cache slots the prompt path borrows were in neither VRAM nor RAM during a prompt and were read from the model files on every chunk (and again when the slots were refilled), even when the budget had room for them. This is the first of the two options in #1683, the one the maintainer reply preferred: the budget branch now appends the lend region after the ranked experts, from the last slot down (the order the borrowing takes them), as far as the budget reaches. The budget stays a hard cap; experts past it keep the file fallback and the warning says so.

Only where experts are placed changes, not the maths: the lent experts are copied from RAM instead of the files.

## What changed
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: in the budget branch of `pin_cache_complement`, the lend region's pairs (slot >= `lend_from_slot`, highest slot first) are added to the ranked plan while they fit in `budget_bytes`; a new start-up line reports `the prompt path's lend region: N of its M slots keep their experts in RAM too (X GiB of the budget's remaining Y GiB)`. `complement_lent_slots_` and the existing `N of the prompt path's M lendable slots` line and #1389 warning cover the budget case too; the warning's advice names the budget when one is set.
- `src/program/generate.cpp`: the #669 start warning (lent slots without a RAM copy) also fires with a budget and then says a larger `--resident-budget-gib` is the remedy, not a smaller chunk (with a budget the count used to be 0 whatever the chunk, as #1683 notes).
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: the RAM budget paragraph says the lend region is kept when the budget has room, with the measurement below.

What it leaves alone: `--resident-experts` (the unbudgeted path and `choose_resident_keep_from`), the layer split's stage lend regions, the soft what-fits mode's ranking (the lend region comes after the ranked experts there as well), every expert tier's behaviour once the copy is built.

## Measured
RX 6900 XT 16 GB (HIP, gfx1030), Ryzen 9 5950X, 125 GB RAM, Arch Linux, ROCm 7.2.4, engine 0.1.42, Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, `--resident-budget-gib 71 --prefill auto --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072`. The copy held all 63.47 GiB of experts outside the GPU cache and 7.5 GiB of the budget stayed unused; the prompt path borrows 1,231 slots (3.60 GiB). Before the change the start log had no lendable-slots line at all; after it: `1231 of its 1231 slots keep their experts in RAM too (3.60 GiB of the budget's remaining 7.53 GiB)`. One run per case, greedy, the same prompts, the server's own log lines:

| request | before: expert reads from the files / SSD reads / host staging | after |
|---|---|---|
| 256-token follow-up on a 1K chat | 680 MB / 203 MB (684 major faults) / 1.0 s | 0 / 15 MB (3) / 0.13 s |
| fresh 7.8K prompt | 7.5 GB / 2.8 GB (10,735) / 1.27 s | 0 / 0.3 GB (0) / 0.23 s |
| 561-token follow-up on an 8K chat | 1.2 GB / 244 MB (925) / 1.5 s | 0 / 10 MB (0) / 0.30 s |
| fresh 15.8K prompt | 11.6 GB / 1.9 GB (6,219) / 1.85 s | 0 / 0.3 GB (0) / 0.50 s |

Prompt speed on those fresh prompts: 887 tokens 180 -> 194 tok/s, 7.8K 633 -> 676, 15.8K 677 -> 698 (the staging mostly overlapped the GPU here; the gain is in the SSD traffic and on machines where it does not). Decode unchanged (58-68 ms per verify window in both runs). The 0.1.42 production log of the same machine showed 0.5-2.6 GB of file reads per agent turn and 24 GB for one fresh 17K prompt, all gone after this.

Not tested: a layer split, a helper GPU, Windows, a budget too small for the whole lend region (the code path takes the contiguous tail that fits and warns), CUDA (host code only, no backend-specific lines).

pulls.title: [TUI] highlight fenced code blocks in streamed chat output
pulls.author: MegaRushX
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`chat.py` printed streamed assistant content raw, so any fenced code block (HTML, Python, JSON, ...) landed as flat gray plain text in the terminal. After this change, lines inside a fenced code block are colored in the terminal (tags, strings, comments, keywords, numbers; one regex family per language: HTML/XML, Python, C/C++, JS/TS, shell, JSON, CSS, SQL, diff), prose passes through untouched, and a fence whose ``` marker is split across streamed chunks still opens. Only a partial last line is held back until its newline arrives; the stream stays incremental.

## Related discussion

none — not attached to an open issue. AI-agent contribution, unsolicited: this came from running the chat UI and reading the code. Closed in the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset (Oct 19); reopening per the process. Say the word and I stop or take it down.

## Approach

New `highlight.py`, standard library only, wired into `chat.py`'s stream loop (`hl.feed()` per chunk, `hl.flush()` at the end). No dependency, no engine files touched, pure host Python, no build needed. Assistant history keeps the raw text; only the terminal display is painted. Output when stdout is not a tty stays byte-identical to the last release.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- `python3 test_highlight.py` — 8/8 (prose unchanged with/without color, python + html blocks highlighted, fence split across chunks, partial-line hold-back, unknown-language passthrough, all bytes preserved). Environment: Linux host Python 3.12, run on 0.2.0-beta main `e88ee39d` with this patch rebased locally (rebase clean, no conflicts), and on the PR head `fa862640` earlier.

**Failed:**
- none observed

**Not run:**
- GUI (WASM), CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Metal builds — host Python change only, no engine code touched, nothing to build.

## Limits

Languages are covered by regex families, not full grammars; nested markup inside a fenced block (markdown inside a code fence, etc.) passes through unpainted. Note on this reopen: the rebased branch could not be pushed — my token lacks the `workflow` scope and the new upstream `.github/workflows/intake.yml` sits in the push path, so the PR head remains `fa862640`, which applies cleanly on `e88ee39d` (verified by local rebase above).

pulls.title: Non-finite logits (#879): a guard with self-healing
pulls.author: lask3802
pulls.body:
Refs #879, #606.

## What it changes

Rarely a window's logits become NaN and the reply degenerates into token 0 (`!`) repeated. The poison sits in the
conversation's K/V and recurrent state, so with the prompt cache every later turn of that conversation stays poisoned
until it is read again from token 0. The q8_1 clamps of 0.1.39 and later removed the overflows found so far; reports
on 0.1.41 (#879) show that some cause is left. This PR does not look for that cause. It stops serving the poison:

- Every verify window of `--serve` checks its head logits on the GPU beside the greedy pick: one small kernel writes a
  flag per slice of each row into mapped memory, and the host reads the flags after the sync the window already does.
  No extra sync.
- A flagged window emits none of its tokens; the engine prints one `non-finite logits (#879)` line with the position
  and ends the request with `DONE ... nonfinite` (a batch slot: `BDONE <slot> <n> nonfinite`).
- The next request first drops the live session, every checkpoint, every parked conversation and every idle batch
  slot, and reads its prompt from token 0. A slot still running finishes its reply and is not kept after it.
- The server retries a request that had sent nothing yet once, transparently; a reply that had started ends as
  `"length"` (as `repeat_stop_tokens` does); a second fire on the retry is an error (503 before an answer, an error
  event in a stream). With replicas, the router forgets what that replica held.
- `STRATA_NAN_INJECT=<n>[,<n>...]` (debug) reports the n-th checked window as non-finite, to exercise the path.

On by default, as a fix; `STRATA_NAN_GUARD=0` turns it off (no kernel is recorded).

Covered: the serial decode loop (one GPU or a layer split), the `--pipeline-windows` decode loop of a layer split, the
prompt's short tail (`read_windows`, `read_windows_pl`), and both batch-slot loops.

## What it leaves alone

- Answers without a NaN (checked below, byte for byte).
- The one-shot command line (`strata` without `--serve`) and the SYCL port in `sycl/` (it has its own verify path)
  do not check.
- `repeat_stop_tokens` stays as the backstop.

## Measured

RTX 3080 (PCIe 4.0 x8), Linux, RVN IQ3_S with the usual one-GPU config (`--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4
--mtp ... --conversation-cache-mib 8192`), this branch's build.

- **Answers**, guard on vs `STRATA_NAN_GUARD=0`, at fixed expert sets (`--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0 --adapt-swaps 0
  --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`), a chat replay of 2 x 4 turns on a
  16K-token system prompt: byte-identical in 3 pairs (one with `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, one with
  `STRATA_SH_STREAM=0`); two guard-on runs 8 of 8. One more guard-off run differed from every other run from its first
  answer on, and a second guard-off run matched the guard-on runs, so that was a difference between runs of this
  config, not the guard. (Also 8 of 8 on an older base, fb58e0d plus the remote-stage PRs.)
- **Cost**, Nsight Systems, 6 requests x 200 tokens: `logits_nonfinite_kernel` 424 launches, 4.77 us on average
  (7.78 us at most), 2.0 ms against 21.6 s of decode: **0.009%**. A decode rate A/B (40 prompts x 200 tokens,
  on/off/off/on: 40.78 / 40.94 / 40.86 / 40.45 tok/s, on the older base) cannot resolve a difference that small.
- **`STRATA_NAN_INJECT=1,60`**: a new chat's first window flagged -> the server sent the request again from token 0
  and the client saw one normal answer; the 60th window, mid-reply in the next turn -> that reply ended as `"length"`
  after 58 tokens; the turn after it reused 0 cached tokens and answered normally. The engine logged exactly the two
  injected windows.

A real fire was not seen in these runs. On a two-PC remote-stage build (#1748 + #1887) the guard stayed silent through
163 requests of the load that had poisoned about 4 in 10 before that build's own fix, so the guard is the backstop,
not the fix, there.

## Builds and tests

- CUDA 13.0 on Linux (GCC, sm_75 + sm_86); serve tests 697 OK, 11 skipped (`NonFiniteLogits`,
  `test_nonfinite_in_batch_mode`, `test_nonfinite_forgets_the_replica` are new); ctest without a GPU: 24 pass
  (`conversation_cache_test` with the new `clear()` among them), the GPU parity tests not run.
- MSVC 2022 + CUDA 13.0: the touched files compile; `conversation_cache_test` and `conv_cache_test` pass.
- HIP (ROCm 7.0, gfx1100): compiles. SYCL (oneAPI 2026.1.1): compiles.

pulls.title: logit_bias: normalize a long list once per request (65,929 entries: +175 ms -> +24 ms)
pulls.author: qni-live
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #1646 (and #1627). One file changed (`serve/logit_bias.py`) plus tests. No engine change, no new option, the default path returns and raises exactly what it did.

**Result:** with a 65,929-entry list a request now costs **+24 ms instead of +175 ms** on a live 0.1.42 engine; the normalization alone drops from **204 ms to 8 ms** (five calls on a freshly parsed list). Same results, same errors, 12 tests (5 existing, 7 new).

## Why

A standing ban of a whole script is a long list: all Han, Kana and Hangul tokens of the vocabulary are 65,929 IDs (1.05 MB of JSON), sent with every request. On v0.1.42 it is normalized **five times per request**: `bias_api.normalize` in `_openai` (line 5217), `validate_request` at 5228 and again in `generate` (1569), and `engine_key` twice (`sampling_keys` runs for the cache key at 1253 and for the GEN line at 1577; each `engine_key` normalizes, sorts and joins a ~790 KB string). In isolation that is about 200 ms of Python per request, whatever the answer length.

Measured on a live 0.1.42 engine (2x RTX PRO 4500 layer split, Linux, 7,091-token prompt with prefix-cache hit, temperature 0, 9 runs per cell, medians): the list cost **+175 ms** at `max_tokens` 1, +173 ms at 50 and +180 ms at 400 (+10 to +18 % on a one-second agent turn). The engine's own decode rate is not affected (-1 %).

## What changed

`normalize()` and `engine_key()` keep their signatures and results. The module remembers the last normalized lists:

- the same object again in one request is answered from `_last`;
- an equal list in a later request is found by its compact JSON text (`vocab_size` is part of the key, so validation against the vocabulary is unchanged);
- only a list that normalized without an error is stored, so a bad list still raises on every call; lists under 64 entries skip the cache; at most 4 lists are kept.

The key is the JSON text, not the list: Python compares `[[7, False]]` and `[[7, 0]]` as equal, and a `==` key would turn a ban into "no bias". `normalize()` hands out a copy, so a caller cannot change a cached entry. `engine_key()` builds its string once per cached list.

## How it was checked

- `python -m unittest serve.test_logit_bias`: the 5 existing tests and 7 new ones pass (same answers as the uncached function for dict and pair-list forms and both vocabulary sizes; `False` is not `0` in either order; bad lists are never stored, including `True == 1`, a duplicate ID and NaN; vocabulary size is part of the key; the result is a copy; an equal list in a later request is a hit; the cache is bounded).
- The five calls of one request with a freshly parsed 65,929-entry list, Threadripper 7960X, CPython: **204 ms -> 8 ms**, same `engine_key` string (786,687 characters). A cold first request is 99 ms.
- On the live engine, the same measurement as above with this file in place: **+175 ms -> +24 ms** per request (65,929 IDs; 30,000 IDs +10 ms, 12,000 IDs +5 ms); the Han ban still works (a request for a Chinese translation returned 0 Han characters with the list, 6 without).

## What it leaves alone

- The wire format, the error messages and the HTTP 400 paths.
- The remaining ~24 ms are the JSON parse of the body and the compact JSON text used as the key. A standing ban in the config or a file read at start (so the list need not travel with each request at all) would remove them; that is a separate decision and this change does not preempt it.
- It assumes the parsed request body is not modified in place between the calls of one request, which nothing in `serve/` does.

Not tested: HIP and SYCL engines (Python only, no backend file touched), `--batch` (rejected before this code, unchanged).

Written with AI assistance (Claude); numbers reviewed by me.

pulls.title: sycl: Windows/OpenCL support for the merged port, and a live free-VRAM figure for the expert cache (#1549)
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
## What this is

`main` now carries the SYCL port, built and measured on Linux with Level Zero, where oneMKL and command graphs both work. This is the **Windows half** — the pieces Windows needs that a Linux build never exercises, plus the expert-cache sizing fix that came out of building it.

**Rebased onto `7695859a`** (the 0.1.43 release); the first version of this PR was against `a1c47bc9`. All measurements below are from the rebased tree.

Single card, all measurements: **Arc Pro B70, 32 GB, Windows 11 24H2, driver 32.0.101.8976 (Arc Pro line) / 32.0.101.9034 (generic), OpenCL + eager replay, engine 0.1.43**.

## The eight commits

| | |
|---|---|
| `223ee707` | serve: make the expert-cache VRAM headroom a knob, opt-in on CUDA and HIP |
| `fe7aaa44` | probe+port: a live free-VRAM figure for the OpenCL backend |
| `9f1b6a57` | Windows/OpenCL bring-up for the merged SYCL port |
| `9188d551` | sycl: the serve-side VRAM check asks the same source as the cache sizing |
| `99664a1d` | sycl: the per-layer sizing path asks the same source as the auto branch |
| `6cdf81f5` | sycl verify: the eager path replays the commit instead of dereferencing a null graph |
| `d2a7ddac` | sycl: the free-VRAM comment names the fallback that exists (comment only) |
| `1baf4c95` | sycl: opt-in Level Zero on Windows, and the diagnosis behind it |

## What it changes

**1. The Windows build layer** — `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`, `sycl/tools/build.bat`, `sycl/tools/onemath_config.hpp`, `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.bat`. Compiler-ID gating (`/fp:precise` and `/W3` for MSVC, `-fp-model=precise` elsewhere — the precise model is load-bearing: `quantize_act_parity` goes from byte-exact to 303k mismatches without it), `STRATA_SYCL_JIT_STATELESS` (the IGC >4 GiB surface-offset bug), the oneMKL stub for an installer-free conda install, and the DLLs beside `strata.exe`.

**2. Portability fixes in the migrated copies** — the `STRATA_USE_CUDA` guard in `pinned.dp.cpp`, `OUT`→`WRITE_OUT` in `verify_kernels.dp.cpp`, Windows file I/O in `gguf_expert_source.cpp`, the `small`/`memmem` fixes in `generate.cpp`, and the plain-SYCL fallback GEMM in `gemm.dp.cpp` gated on `onemkl_usable()`.

**3. The live free-VRAM figure** — on OpenCL there is no free-VRAM query at all (`ext_intel_free_memory` needs Level Zero sysman), so `get_memory_info` answers **0**, which sizes the cache to *nothing*. `own_gpu_local()` asks DXGI. Same binary, free card, 2047-token prompt: **0 slots / refused** → **12,288 slots / 23.42 GiB, prompt 81.1 tok/s, decode 66.6 tok/s**.

**4. `6cdf81f5`, submitted separately as #2106** — completes `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER` for the commit path. `main`'s eager support covers the window (`record_window`, `run()`'s guard) but not the commit; `mtp.cpp`'s `prepare_chain` documents the gap out loud.

**5. `1baf4c95`, the Level Zero diagnosis** — opt-in `STRATA_SYCL_LEVEL_ZERO=1` in the launcher, off by default, plus `LEVEL_ZERO_FINDINGS.md` recording how it was established. Off by default because the serve request path stalls intermittently; when it runs it is **108.8 tok/s decode and 81.1 prefill against OpenCL's 66.6 / 81.1**, with the v1 Level Zero adapter beating v2 by +24% decode and 34x faster graph capture.

## The one thing I would most want reviewed

`ur_adapter_level_zero.dll` imports `UMF.dll` and the `VCRUNTIME140*` set, and `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` stages neither beside `strata.exe`. The adapter fails to load, the UR loader reports only OpenCL, and `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0` kills the process with `0xC0000409` before `main` prints anything. **The silence is the expensive part**: every Level Zero adapter failure looks like "there is no Level Zero here", which is what sent me down the OpenCL path in the first place and cost days. The workaround in this PR is `Library\bin` first on `PATH`; the proper fix is to extend the copy list.

Second, and related: the **v1 Level Zero adapter beats v2** decisively on this card (+24% decode, graph capture 276 ms vs 9,495 ms). #1940 pins v2 on for graph replay (intel/llvm#23073); on a B70 with this workload that trade is the wrong one.

## What this leaves alone

Every new feature is opt-in and the default path is byte-identical unless a variable is set: `STRATA_EXPERT_CACHE_HEADROOM` defaults to 0 everywhere, `STRATA_SYCL_LEVEL_ZERO` is unset by default, and `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER` is only read where it already was. Every launcher variable is only written when not already defined, so an explicit `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` for a two-card split still wins. No engine source changed in `1baf4c95`.

## What I could not verify — please read before reviewing

- **Built and run on SYCL/Windows only.** I have no CUDA, HIP or Linux toolchain on this machine. Files here are shared across backends and I could not build them.
- **A clean checkout of the SYCL port does not compile on Windows** without commit `9f1b6a57` (`pinned.dp.cpp`'s unguarded CUDA calls, the `OUT` macro in `verify_kernels.dp.cpp`). So it cannot be built standalone here.
- **oneMKL still refuses** — *"does not support this API"* — against both the PyPI runtime and the standalone oneAPI 2026.0 runtime, with identical timings. The engine's expert GEMMs are BF16 (`gemm.dp.cpp:1031`), the likely unsupported type; that is a hypothesis, not a measurement. So the prompt path is on the plain-SYCL fallback and the prefill figures are not oneMKL-backed.
- **The Level Zero path is not reliable as a default.** The stall message, what it is not, and where to instrument next are in `LEVEL_ZERO_FINDINGS.md`.

## Suggested review order

1. `gemm.dp.cpp` — the plain-SYCL fallback is what makes prompts run at all here, and it is the biggest piece.
2. `verify.cpp` — the `capture_commit` eager guard (#2106 is the same change standalone).
3. `expert_cache.cpp` — the DXGI figure, since it changes sizing behaviour on every SYCL backend.
4. `CMakeLists.txt` — the copy list above, and the compiler-ID gating.

I would rather split this: `223ee707` + `d2a7ddac` are one coherent knob, `6cdf81f5` is #2106, and `1baf4c95` is really a bug report about the copy list with an opt-in switch attached.

pulls.author: KarlGrier

## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change)

## Summary
`STRATA_SIDE_MIXER=1` or `=2` (opt-in, off by default) records the mixer's work that reads only the layer's input on
branches of the verify window's CUDA graph, beside the projections that the recurrence and the attention wait for:

- `=1`: the GDN gates (a/b) on one branch, joined before the recurrence; the QSA indexer's chain (key projection, tail
  snapshot, key append, query projection with norm and RoPE, block scores, top-k) on it, joined before the attention.
- `=2`: also the GDN gate projection (z) and the QSA queries' chain (projection, q/gate split, norm, RoPE, rotation) on a
  second branch. A branch that projects reads F4's interleaved q8_1 copy, written on the main stream before the fork, and
  qkv is recorded before the branch so that its grid is dispatched first.

Each step is the in-line code with its stream as a parameter, so the outputs are bitwise the same (exact7 with the switch
on, below). `STRATA_DF_BRANCH` is the same idea for fewer of these steps; it is off whenever this switch is set. The idea
is from Eddoursul's fork (34a35db, b063c13).

## Title
Issue: none (an opt-in speed change)

## Summary
`STRATA_QSA_SPLIT_ATTN=1` (opt-in, off by default) runs the QSA layers' decode attention - the verify window's and the draft
layer's - through the prompt path's int8 tensor-core kernel, with each query's cells split among up to 20 blocks (about two

(fd23d91); the kernel here is written against this tree's `qsa_prompt_attn.cu` and its helpers.

pulls.title: [Engine] Remote stage: conversation checkpoints across the link (--prompt-cache), stacked on #1748
pulls.author: lask3802
pulls.body:
**Stacked on #1748.** The first nineteen commits are #1748's; this PR adds the last six: the feature, its docs, what
#1748's recovery (the main process connecting again) needs from them, the `--pipeline-windows 2` case, and the notes
of the rebase. Both PRs are on `main` e88ee39d (0.2.0-beta, engine 0.1.45.3).

## Problem and result

With `--remote-stage`, every prompt was read from token 0. A conversation checkpoint holds only the running state of
the process's own layers, so the main process could not restore the worker's. A chat client sends the whole
conversation every turn, so every turn of a long chat waited for the whole prompt again: about 15 s at 16K tokens on
the test pair below.

With `--prompt-cache N` given **explicitly** on the main process, the worker keeps its layers' part of each checkpoint
under an id the main process hands it, and the chain works as on one GPU at the prompt's synchronous cut points. On
this head (0.2.0-beta), an RTX 2080 Ti main + RTX 3080 worker, the later turns' median time to the first token is
0.38 s with `--prompt-cache 6` against 12.83 s without (Validation). On an RTX 3080 + RTX 2080 Ti pair (engine 0.1.43,
earlier heads), time to the first token at the served flags, thinking on, 400 tokens:

| | #1748 (every prompt from 0) | This PR, `--prompt-cache 6` |
|---|---|---|
| First turn, 16,079 tokens | 15.00 s | 14.50 s |
| The 7 later turns | 14.19-15.06 s | **0.32-0.44 s** |

A turn read from 0 was 0.7-1.3 s slower with checkpoints on 0.1.41 and 0.1.42, and not slower in this run. The prompt
is read in parts that end at its cut points, and a checkpoint is saved at each. With `--prompt-cache`, answers need not
be byte-identical to a run without it, because the read order differs; the repeated-turn check is the exactness test.

### Measured on earlier heads

An RTX 3080 main (layers 0-25, the head, the drafter) and an RTX 2080 Ti worker (layers 26-47) over 10 GbE, RVN
IQ3_S, Linux, engine 0.1.43; #1748's build is the base. The replay is two chats of four turns on one shared system
prompt of about 16,000 tokens, greedy. Exact flags: `--pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 0 --adapt-swaps 0` on both PCs,
`--mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0` on the main, and `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` on both.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Default path (no `--prompt-cache`, exact flags) vs #1748, one run of each | 8 of 8 byte-identical |
| Every request sent twice, the next turn resuming through a checkpoint (exact flags) | 8 of 8 repeats byte-identical; with thinking on, 8 of 8; with each request first cancelled mid-decode, 8 of 8, and equal to the run without cancels. 53 restores on both PCs, 0 errors |
| Worker store emptied before each restore | the request reads from token 0 and finishes |
| Picture chats (`--vision` on both PCs): two turns, the second sent twice | the second turn resumed through a checkpoint or continued the live session; the re-sent turn byte-identical; all 6 answers equal those of a run without `--prompt-cache` |
| Live continuations with the worker's adaptive tier on, 15 min, 100-2,500 new tokens a turn | 165 requests, 158 live continuations (97 reading 1,000+ tokens): 0 replies of `!`. Without the settle, on an earlier build with the same load: about 4 in 10 |

In these runs the worker's adaptive overlap was on (#1748's build then followed upstream's default on the worker
too). #1748 has since made it opt-in on a worker (`STRATA_ADAPT_OVERLAP=1`), since it measured no faster there; a
worker without it takes the path of the 0.1.42 runs, where the same live-continuation check gave 161 requests and
0 replies of `!`. The same checks on 0.1.41 and 0.1.42 gave the same results: 8 of 8 on each repeated-turn line, 53
restores, no `!` reply, and later turns in 0.28-0.54 s. On 0.1.42 the default path against #1748 did not repeat from
run to run (8 of 8 in 2 of 6 pairs), as 0.1.42 did not on one GPU either; on 0.1.43 it did.

With `--pipeline-windows 2` on the main process (same PCs and model, exact flags, `--expert-cache 1951`,
`STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` on the main process): repeated turns 8 of 8 byte-identical with 15 restores on both sides
and 0 errors, the same with thinking on and with cancellation; a forced restore miss (`STRATA_REMOTE_CKPT_DROP=1`)
read from 0 and finished. The numbers are in `docs/remote-stage/CHECKPOINTS.md`.

**Faults between two turns.** On the same pair with this branch's build, #1748's agent and server, `--prompt-cache 6`
and pictures allowed (served flags). Each conversation's second turn asks for something only its first turn holds (a
code word, or the first word of the previous answer), greedy. The worker was killed with SIGKILL between the turns,
and its agent started it again. "Before" is the docs commit; "after" is the reconnect commit ("checkpoints and the
live session after a reconnect") before its worker-error texts and take-over check, which none of these runs reach.

| Between the turns | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing (text; picture) | both right | both right |
| The worker killed (text, the live session continued) | 503 "remote stage: the peer closed the connection"; the engine restarted | right, after 45.0 s (the worker's restart and load); the engine kept |
| The worker killed (picture, a checkpoint mounted) | 400 "restoring a conversation checkpoint failed: remote stage: send failed: Broken pipe"; the engine restarted | right, after 53.3 s (the word, then more text than the one word asked for) |
| Chat X, then chat Y, the worker killed, X's second turn (the checkpoint of their shared start) | 503; the engine restarted | right, after 61.0 s |
| The main engine killed (text) | right, after 11.8 s | right, after 12.6 s |

The same session on 0.1.43.1 gave every second turn right (worker killed: 45.2 s text, 52.2 s picture, 61.1 s another
chat's checkpoint; main engine killed: 38.1 s), and again on top of #1748's open-points commit (45.1 / 52.1 / 61.0 s;
11.8 s).

## Related discussion

- This PR was open before the 0.2.0-beta reset (closed with every open PR on 2026-10-19); this is the same branch
  rebased onto `main` e88ee39d on top of #1748's rebase. No maintainer agreement on scope yet.
- #1748 (the remote stage) is its base; this PR changes nothing for a remote stage without `--prompt-cache`.

## Approach

- **Protocol 5 -> 6.** New messages `CkptSave` / `CkptRestore` carry an id, a position and the list of ids to keep,
  and `Reset` carries that list too.
- **Retention.** Only the main process decides what is kept; the worker prunes when an operation succeeds. The main
  process works out the chain a new checkpoint leaves before the worker stores its part, with the same eviction it
  applies after (`--prompt-cache-spread` included), so both PCs drop the same checkpoint.
- **Limits at the hello.** The worker refuses more than 64 parts, or more parts than fit in half of its available RAM,
  or any part when it cannot read its RAM (as the engine's own RAM guard refuses parking then). A main process that
  takes a worker over (#1748) is held to the same limits as one that connects to a free worker. Checkpoint lists are
  bounded (at most `kStageCkptMax` ids, checked before the read).
- **Disconnect.** The worker clears its store.
- **Errors.** A checkpoint the worker does not hold makes the request read from token 0; a lost link at a request's
  start is made again (below); any other error ends the engine as before. When the error is the link's or the
  worker's, the `ERR` line starts with it, so the server answers 503 with Retry-After, not 400. A failed image
  position table (#1748's `Positions`) outlives a `CkptRestore` as it outlives a `Reset`, because it belongs to the
  request being started.
- **After a reconnect.** The worker the main process reaches after connecting again (a restarted worker, or a
  take-over) holds no session and no checkpoint. So at each request's start the main process checks the idle link
  with nothing sent (`StageClient::alive`: a 0 ms poll, then a 1-byte peek; the worker never sends unasked) and
  connects again there if it is lost. Whenever the link is made again in a request (that check, its positions, its
  Reset, its `CkptRestore`), the main process drops its live session and every checkpoint, and the request reads from
  token 0 with a Reset that keeps nothing. A reconnect cancelled at these request-start paths ends that request, and
  the engine stays.
- **A live continuation settles the worker first.** A request that continues the live session waits for the worker's
  last Commit and for the adaptive tier's swaps in flight before it lends cache slots to the prompt (`hs.prefill`), as
  a Reset and a restore do. Without that, a loan could hand the prompt path slots that a swap was still writing, and
  the reply degenerated into `!`.
- **`--pipeline-windows 2`.** No checkpoint is saved, and the live session is not continued, after a pipelined drain
  that failed.

**Following upstream.** The rebase onto 0.2.0-beta met upstream's checkpoint chain changes: `--prompt-cache-spread`
(its eviction now goes through the same function on both of the main process's paths, above), and
`STRATA_CKPT_POOL` / `STRATA_CKPT_THREADS`, which act on the main process's own part only (a remote main has no
in-process stage; the worker keeps its part by id). 0.1.44's Metal backend hands the checkpoint save and restore to
its decode window; the range-taking overloads this branch adds stay on the session's buffers, and a remote stage is
refused on Metal (#1748). Upstream's `copy_checkpoint_beating` (the parked conversation's copies, #2049) copies a
checkpoint's `remote_id` too. Details: `docs/remote-stage/CHECKPOINTS.md`, "After the rebase onto 0.2.0-beta".

**What it leaves alone.**
- **The default path.** Without `--prompt-cache`, a remote main keeps `prompt_cache` at 0: no new message is sent,
  the prompt is not split, and a Reset is the same header-only message. One-GPU and in-process splits see two
  mechanical refactors only (the eviction loop and the zero-and-reset at request start moved into lambdas, the same
  calls in the same order). On one GPU with the conversation cache, upstream `main`'s, #1748's and this branch's
  builds gave byte-identical answers on 0.1.42; that was not run again since.
- Mid-prompt checkpoints (`--prompt-cache-every`, `--prompt-cache-tail`) and parking (`--conversation-cache-mib`) stay
  off with a remote stage; session files are refused. A config with `--conversation-cache-mib` starts, and the main
  process says in its log that parking is off.
- A worker's `CkptSave` and `CkptRestore` are watched by the engine's stall watchdog as its other messages are.
- The hello says protocol 6, so a main and a worker must both run this version, with or without checkpoints.
- The check at a request's start sends nothing, so the default path's messages do not change.
- A relay (three PCs) forwards the new messages, and it links its next worker again after each main process's hello,
  so the next worker checks the real ckpt_max (read from the code and unit-tested, not run on GPUs).

Files: `include/strata/net/stage_ckpt_store.hpp` and `src/net/stage_ckpt_store_test.cpp` (new: the worker's store),
`include/strata/net/stage_link.hpp` and `src/net/stage_link.cpp` (the messages), `src/net/stage_link_test.cpp`,
`src/program/generate.cpp` (the main process's chain and the worker's side), `include/strata/core/verify.hpp` (a
comment), `src/core/conversation_state.cpp`, `conversation_copy.hpp`, `conversation_cache.hpp`, `conversation_snapshot.hpp`
(a checkpoint for a layer range and its `remote_id`), `src/core/conversation_validation_test.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt`,
and the docs (`docs/remote-stage/CHECKPOINTS.md`, new; `docs/REMOTE_STAGE.md`, `docs/remote-stage/ENGINEERING.md`).

## Validation

Revision: this head, 8ee568ff (#1748's a3e15682 plus six commits, on `main` e88ee39d) (the builds and tests below ran on it before a last wording fix in ENGINE

pulls.title: serve: preserve literal </think> across reasoning parsing
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
## Summary

Builds on the end-of-thinking recovery and captured real-world specimens from #1840, then makes parser transitions depend on the actual special-token identity. This keeps an ordinary `</think>` string in reasoning when it is quoted or appears mid-line, including when the model continues reasoning afterward.

## Reproduction and fix

With #1840's end-of-turn recovery alone, a deterministic token-stream test puts a literal `</think>` in ordinary prose and then continues reasoning. The parser switches to answer mode at the string; the remaining reasoning and quoted tag are routed to the answer. A second test emits the special close token inside an unclosed inline-code span and stops. The recovery continuation preserves the backtick boundary, but the close token is exposed as a structural close instead of quoted reasoning text.

This branch adds token-aware parser signaling and bounded continuation handling. In the same streams, the full prose and quoted tag stay in reasoning, and the answer remains `42`. The original #1840 empty-reasoning / no-answer recovery and its real-turn specimens remain included.

## Validation

- Focused literal-thinking, parser, and #1840 recovery suites: 45 tests passed.
- Full serving suite on latest `main`: 735 tests passed, 12 skipped.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: clean.

These are deterministic service/parser tests; no live Qwen3.8 / dual-3090 rerun is claimed. The recovery/continuation guard remains opt-in, while token-identity parsing is always used.

Supersedes the standalone draft in #1839 and combines its parser-ambiguity fix with #1840's reproduction and recovery.

pulls.title: serve: on Windows the engine and the image encoder start without a console window of their own
pulls.author: LeGeRyChEeSe
pulls.body:
## Title

Issue: none found (searched 2026-10-10: console window, CREATE_NO_WINDOW).

## Summary
When the server has no console - started with `pythonw`, as a service, or by a launcher that hides it - Windows gives
each console program it starts a **new, visible** console window: one for `strata.exe`, one for the image encoder,
again at every engine restart. Their output already goes through pipes and the log, so the window is empty, and
closing it by mistake ends the engine.

`popen()` (the #735 wrapper both use) now passes `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows, as
`serve/mcp.py` already does for MCP servers. A caller's own `creationflags` wins. Nothing changes elsewhere, and
nothing changes for a server started from a console (the child's console was the parent's, and its I/O is redirected).
The job object of `serve/winjob.py` still ties the children to the server's lifetime.

## Test
- `serve/test_server.py`, `test_no_console_window_on_windows`: the flag on Windows, absent elsewhere, a caller's own
  flags kept.
- Live check on Windows 11: a `pythonw` parent starts a console child that prints `GetConsoleWindow()`. With
  `subprocess.Popen` it gets a window (non-zero handle); through `popen()` it gets none (0).

pulls.title: serve: a tool call whose `</tool_call>` is missing ends at its own `</function>` (two calls were merged into one, or the arguments lost)
pulls.author: LeGeRyChEeSe
pulls.body:
## Title

Issue: none found (searched 2026-10-10: "missing </tool_call>", "tool_call not closed", "two tool calls merged").
Related: #210 (call_end), #211 (a call cut before its closer), #1172 (recover's batch in one wrapper, opt-in).

## Summary
**Why it matters:** when the model leaves out a call's `</tool_call>`, `call_end` falls back to the *next*
`</tool_call>` anywhere in the output. Two cases go wrong, with or without `tool_call_recovery`, streamed or not:

| model output | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `<tool_call>` read(a.py) *(no closer)* `<tool_call>` write(b.py, "x = 1") `</tool_call>` | **one** call: `read` with `{"path": "b.py", "content": "x = 1"}` | `read(a.py)`, then `write(b.py, "x = 1")` |
| `<tool_call>` read(a.py) *(no closer)* `Done.` | `read` with `{}` (streamed) or no call | `read(a.py)`, then the content `Done.` |

The first is the worse one: an agent runs the first tool with the second tool's arguments.

**The change** (`OutputParser.feed`, the wrapped-call branch, a few lines): after the call's own `</function>` - found by
`function_end`, which walks the parameters with `param_end`, so a value that holds `</function>` or `<tool_call>` does
not count - the next non-blank text decides:
- `</tool_call>` (or the start of it, still arriving): closes the call, as before;
- `<function=` or `<parameter=` (or the start of one, still arriving): left to recover's batch (opt-in), unchanged;
- anything else (another `<tool_call>`, text): the call ends at its `</function>`, and what follows is read as usual.

Nothing changes for a call that has its closer.

## Test
- `serve/test_tool_call_unclosed.py` (new): the two cases above, closed calls unchanged, and a parameter value that
  holds `</function>` and `<tool_call>`; each with `stream_tools` and `recover` on and off, fed 1, 3 and 7 characters
  at a time (48 sub-tests; 24 fail without the change).
- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"`: 695 tests, OK (11 skipped), the three branches together; `ToolCallRecovery` (the opt-in batch, fed 1 and 7 characters at a time) included.

pulls.title: setup: the images question now asks where the encoder runs (GPU / CPU)
pulls.author: xtremexp
pulls.body:
## Description
--vision cpu (the image encoder on the CPU, no VRAM) has existed since 0.1.32 (#304), and setup uses it itself when a ready-made encoder has no code for the card (#331). Only the interactive prompt never offered it: Do you want images? [y/n], and yes always meant the GPU. So the people who would want it most — a card full of experts — cannot find it without knowing the flag.

The GPU encoder keeps ~1.4 GB of VRAM free, which leaves ~1,000 fewer experts cached and costs 2-8% on prompt and output speed (docs/DETAILS.md, "Speed with images on", 4K context, Q2_0 / IQ2_XS / IQ3_XXS). The CPU encoder costs nothing on the GPU and reads a picture in about 3 s at 300 image tokens on 8 cores.

## What changed
Saying yes to "Do you want images?" now asks a second question: Image encoder? [1]: 1) GPU (recommended) 2) CPU (no VRAM). The intro line names both costs. --help for --vision mentions cpu. Docs: the four questions in DETAILS.md, the Images section, the question list in INSTALL.md.

## What it leaves alone
GPU stays the default, so Enter and --yes behave exactly as before (--yes leaves images off, as documented). The --vision flags, their parsing, the build, the config format and the server are untouched — the CPU answer writes the same config --vision cpu writes. The AMD path is untouched: it has no GPU encoder, so it never reaches this prompt (hip_vision).

pulls.author: taxah92
pulls.body:
A community report for `bench/results/`: a same-day A/B of **0.1.41** (`fb58e0d`) against **0.1.42** (`61b3fb5`) on one Tesla V100-SXM2 16 GB (sm_70, Linux in a Proxmox guest, PCIe Gen3 x16, the engine's start-up probe measures 13.1 GB/s host→device).

- **Hardware:** Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB, EPYC 7532 (32 vCPU), 94 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 26.04, CUDA 12.4.131; source builds for sm_70 (`-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`), no local patches in either tree.
- **Model and config:** Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, 1M YaRN, k8v4 KV, `--spec 3` with MTP, `--pcie-frac` unset in both arms; `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=7` pinned in the 0.1.42 arm only (its new default).
- **Results:** decode **+34…+62%** (medians of three runs, ranges do not overlap), prompt throughput unchanged, `tools/needle_bench.py` 32k+128k **6/6 on both versions**, and the same answers on an own 128K Russian needle at depths 10/50/90.
- **What the log shows:** the measured PCIe share moved `pcie_frac` from the start-up rule's 0.36 to **0.10–0.15, at or on the floor of the 0.10–0.60 search range** (it re-measures up to three times per start and follows the CPU-pool timing: 45–52 GB/s against the 13.1 GB/s link); the tail-skip counter skipped 151,008 of 158,991 missed-expert entries. Expert-cache slot counts are identical on both versions, so the gain is not a different number of resident experts. One aside: `/metrics` keeps reporting the start-up `pcie_frac` (0.36) and does not follow the adaptive value.
- **Question for the maintainers:** the share search ends at its floor on this host — is 0.10 the right floor for machines whose CPU pool is 3.5–4× their PCIe link?
- **Limits:** one machine; the two new defaults were not separated (no `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0` or `STRATA_PCIE_FRAC_DEFAULT=old` arm); the long-context arms are single runs; TTFT was not measured (non-streaming requests); no KL/perplexity.

Raw JSONs of both phases and the measurement stand (`ab.py`) are in the folder. This PR adds the folder, one row in `bench/results/COMMUNITY.md` and one entry in `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` — **no engine changes**.

pulls.title: Add opt-in cumulative GPU energy monitoring to the Power card
pulls.author: hash13
pulls.body: Extended version with electricity pricing: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1925 ## Summary This PR adds opt-in cumulative GPU energy monitoring to the existing Power card, based on Strata v0.1.42. The implementation reuses Strata's existing GPU telemetry, multi-GPU support, and Monitor refresh infrastructure. No additional services, dependencies, or persistent storage are required. This is intentionally a small first step, without request-level energy attribution or token cost calculations. ## Screenshot ## Configuration Enable energy monitoring by adding an `electricity` block at the top level of the existing Strata JSON configuration: ```json "electricity": {} ``` An empty object is sufficient to enable the feature. Without this block, the existing Power card remains unchanged. Electricity prices and currency settings are not used in this initial version. ## Power Card The existing Power card continues to display: - Current GPU power consumption (W) - NVIDIA power limit (W) - Power history sparkline When enabled, it additionally displays cumulative GPU energy consumption since telemetry started. Example: ```text Power 70 W of 440 W limit · 26.0 Wh ``` Energy values are formatted using the browser's locale: | Energy consumption | Display | |---|---| | Below 1 kWh | Wh, one decimal place | | From 1 kWh | kWh, three decimal places | The accumulated value updates automatically through the existing Monitor refresh cycle. ## Energy Measurement The implementation prefers NVIDIA's cumulative NVML hardware energy counter (`nvmlDeviceGetTotalEnergyConsumption`). Unlike integrating periodically sampled power readings, the hardware counter directly reports accumulated energy. This provides more reliable measurements, particularly when GPU power changes between samples. If the hardware counter is unavailable, energy consumption is estimated by integrating the existing GPU power readings over time. For multi-GPU configurations, the energy consumption of monitored GPUs is aggregated. The accumulated energy is kept in memory and resets when Strata restarts. ## Scope The cumulative energy value is exposed through the existing `/metrics` hardware data. Measurement covers GPU energy only. CPU, RAM, motherboard, storage, fans, and PSU losses are not included. Request-level energy attribution is deferred to a later PR, initially limited to serial requests to avoid double counting energy during overlapping requests. ## Changed Files | File | Changes | |---|---| | `serve/telemetry.py` | Cumulative GPU energy measurement using NVML with sampled-power fallback | | `serve/server.py` | Optional `electricity` configuration passed to telemetry | | `serve/web/app.js` | Wh/kWh display in the existing Power card |

pulls.title: Dashboard: GPU load, VRAM, temperature, power and PCIe for AMD cards …
pulls.author: WeisTekEng
pulls.body: ## Title Dashboard: GPU load, VRAM, temperature, power and PCIe for AMD cards on Windows Issue: Resolves #1380 ## Summary On Windows with an AMD card the Monitor dashboard showed nothing for GPU load, VRAM, temperature, power or PCIe, because `serve/telemetry.py` could only read the amdgpu sysfs files, which exist only on Linux. This adds a Windows reader that gets the same readings from DXGI, the performance counters, AMD's ADL library and the PCI device properties. Each source is optional: whatever fails to start leaves its readings empty and the others still show. Tested on an RX 9070 XT Nitro+ (gfx1201), Windows, Ryzen 9 5900X. `python -m serve.telemetry 0 amd` on that PC: ``` GPU 0: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT sources: {'pdh': True, 'adl': True, 'pci': True} ADL supported sensors (id: value): {1: 261, 2: 2786, 8: 25, 9: 28, 14: 3656, 15: 100, 19: 0, 20: 0, 21: 794, 27: 27, 38: 0, 39: 0, 40: 3, 41: 16, 46: 0, 47: 0, 48: 0, 49: 0, 58: 4, 73: 49} {'util': 7.0, 'mem_used': 15658614784.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 54.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 7.0, 'mem_used': 15660449792.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 52.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 2.0, 'mem_used': 15660449792.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 45.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 3.0, 'mem_used': 15657566208.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 45.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 5.0, 'mem_used': 15647342592.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 46.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 5.0, 'mem_used': 15657566208.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 47.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 4.0, 'mem_used': 15657566208.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 44.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} {'util': 5.0, 'mem_used': 15657566208.0, 'mem_total': 16977723392, 'temp': 25.0, 'power': 45.0, 'pcie_gen': 5, 'pcie_gen_max': 5, 'pcie_width': 16} ``` ## What changed - `serve/telemetry.py` - New `_AmdWin` reader, chosen by `gpu_reader()` for the AMD backend on Windows. Linux and NVIDIA paths are unchanged. - DXGI: the card's name, device id, LUID and total VRAM. Adapters are ordered like HIP numbers them (an integrated Radeon first, then discrete cards), so `--gpu` selects the same card. - Performance counters (`GPU Engine`, `GPU Adapter Memory`) matched by the card's LUID: load (the busiest engine, as Task Manager shows) and VRAM in use. The query is reopened every 15 reads, and the last good value is kept for up to 3 empty reads. - ADL (`atiadlxx.dll`, installed with the Adrenalin driver), PMLog sensors: temperature, power and load. ADL reports AMD's vendor id as the decimal 1002, not 0x1002, so both are accepted. - SetupAPI PCI link properties: current and maximum PCIe generation, and width. - A source that does not start records why (`errors`), and `python -m serve.telemetry [index] [amd]` prints it with eight seconds of readings, so a problem on someone's PC can be diagnosed without starting the server. - The `gpu_note` text no longer says "Windows" or "Linux" and names what was tried. - `serve/web/app.js`: the VRAM tile's fallback text is now "not available" instead of "not available on Windows AMD yet". - `serve/test_telemetry_amd_windows.py` (new, 17 tests): parsing, sensor choice, adapter ordering, ctypes struct sizes, and the fallbacks, with the Windows APIs faked so they run anywhere. - `serve/test_server.py`: `AmdTelemetry` is pinned to the Linux reader (`@mock.patch("serve.telemetry.IS_WIN", False)`). Those tests fake a sysfs tree and call `gpu_reader(…, amd=True)`, so on a Windows machine they were getting the new reader and failing. ## Extra Notes - No new dependencies: everything is ctypes against DLLs Windows or the AMD driver already provide. No admin rights needed. - PCIe throughput can't be read on Windows, so that tile shows the link (for example Gen5 x16) but no MB/s. The Windows reader also doesn't fill the `pcie_path` / `pcie_own_gen` keys from #1733, which are specific to the Linux sysfs walk. - Two behaviours change on Windows AMD because they read the same values: `gpu_busy` (which uses the load reading) can now see a busy GPU, and `free_vram_mib` now returns a value instead of None. As far as I can tell both are only used when configured or by the watchdog, but please double-check. - Only tested on one machine. Not tested: other Radeon cards, a PC with an integrated GPU plus a discrete one (the ordering follows #325 but is unverified), or two identical cards (ADL is matched by PCI device id, so it could pick the wrong one). - ADL's units (temperature in °C, power in W) come from AMD's sensor definitions. The probe above shows 25 °C and 44-54 W at idle, which matches the board power sensor (49 W) in the supported-sensors line. - Needs the Adrenalin driver for ADL. Without it, load, VRAM and PCIe still show.
