pulls.title: serve: Ctrl+C prints "Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper ...>" from the vision encoder's buffered QUIT
pulls.author: weituotian
pulls.body:
Stopping the server with Ctrl+C, with an image encoder configured (`"vision"` in the config), prints two lines of Python noise between `[strata] stopping` and `[strata] stopped`:

```
[strata] stopping (Ctrl+C again to end the engine at once) ...
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name=4 encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "D:\projects\ai\Strata\serve\server.py", line 2076, in shutdown
    self.close()
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
[strata] stopped
```

The model stops correctly and the shell prompt comes back - the shutdown itself is fine, it is only the report. But it names a line of our own code at every stop, which reads like a crash.

### Why it happens

`Vision.close()` writes `QUIT` into the encoder's stdin and then drops the process:

```python
try:
    proc.stdin.write("QUIT\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()
    proc.wait(timeout=10)
except Exception:
    ...
self.stopped = True          # proc, and its pipes, are left to the GC
```

The pipes are made with `text=True, bufsize=1`, so the newline flushes inside `write()`. Ctrl+C reaches every process attached to the console, so the encoder can already be gone by then, and that flush raises `OSError [Errno 22]` - the existing `except Exception` catches it, so the shutdown carries on. But `QUIT` is then still in the `TextIOWrapper`'s buffer. When `proc` goes out of scope at the end of `close()`, the wrapper's finalizer flushes it again, raises the same `OSError`, and CPython prints it as `Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name=4 ...>`, with the caller's frame (`shutdown`, the `self.close()` line) - exactly the two lines above.

`StrataEngine.close()` has never shown this, because it already closes its stdin and ignores the error, with a comment that names this very case:

```python
self.proc.stdin.close()             # buffered data may flush again after the engine has exited
```

(serve/server.py:1863). The encoder's `close()` never got the same guard. That is the whole of this PR.

### Minimal reproduction, no model and no GPU needed

Windows 11 26100, CPython 3.13.14:

```python
import gc, subprocess, sys

def arm(explicit_close):
    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "pass"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         text=True, encoding="utf-8", bufsize=1)
    p.wait(timeout=10)                       # the child (the "encoder") is gone, its read end is closed
    try:
        p.stdin.write("QUIT\n")
        p.stdin.flush()
    except OSError as e:
        print("   the flush raised:", e)
    if explicit_close:                       # what this PR does
        for pipe in (p.stdin, p.stdout):
            try:
                pipe.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
    del p
    gc.collect()
```

Arm A, as the code is today:

```
   the flush raised: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name=3 encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "pipe_gc_test.py", line 30, in arm
    del p
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
```

Arm B, with the pipes closed here and the error ignored: the `close()` raises the same `[Errno 22]`, it is swallowed, the wrapper is marked closed, and the GC prints nothing at all.

### On a real server

1. Start it with an image encoder in the config (any model), wait for `ready:`.
2. Press Ctrl+C once.
3. The two lines appear between `[strata] stopping` and `[strata] stopped`; the fix removes them.

Without a `"vision"` section the lines never appear in the first place - only `vision.shutdown` is in the closer list, which is why this went unnoticed for so long.

### The change

Nine lines at the end of `Vision.close()` (serve/server.py:2164-2172): close the encoder's stdin there, ignoring `OSError`, the way `StrataEngine.close()` already does.

### What it leaves alone

- The shutdown sequence is untouched: the same `QUIT`, the same `wait(10)`, the same `kill`, the same `wait`.
- No new setting, no new default, no change on a healthy encoder: a successful `QUIT` leaves the buffer empty, so the added `close()` is a no-op there.
- One file, `serve/server.py`.

### How it was checked

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` on this branch rebased onto `61b3fb5d`: **690 tests, OK (11 skipped)**.
- The reproduction above: arm A prints the message, arm B does not.

### Caveats

- Measured on Windows 11 26100, CPython 3.13.14, engine 0.1.41, encoder on the CPU (`"gpu": false`). **No Linux run.** The mechanism is not Windows-specific (SIGINT goes to the whole process group there too, and the second flush would raise `BrokenPipeError` instead), but I have not reproduced it on Linux and this PR does not claim it.
- I searched the issues and pull requests first: `TextIOWrapper` and `Exception ignored` find nothing, so this is a new thread rather than a reply to an existing one (#352 and #1317 are about the encoder's pipe in other ways, #181 about ending the processes with the server).

pulls.title: weights: add an opt-in read-only safetensors source (no engine changes)
pulls.author: spideytznn
pulls.body:
Original NVIDIA ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints cannot currently be consumed as safetensors by Strata's weight-source interface. This first patch provides a read-only source and standalone inspector, ahead of model/layout and runtime integration. It is related to #1858; the complete experimental implementation and its measured limits are linked there.

The source validates the index and all shard headers, retains physical shapes and absolute byte ranges, performs bounded coalesced reads into caller-owned spans, accounts for bytes by family, and can seal expert/MTP reads or close all resident startup handles. It rejects malformed descriptors, duplicate JSON keys, unsafe paths, index mismatches and out-of-bounds reads. nlohmann/json 3.12.0 is vendored with its MIT license and hash; configuration downloads nothing.

This is explicitly opt-in through `cmake -S native_safetensors ...`. All 12 changed paths are additions. The root CMake file, every existing engine/backend/setup file, CLI and runtime default are unchanged byte-for-byte against the tested upstream baseline `fb58e0dbc8399662c0e47c76578c6e878b14f6cf`. No complete inference or speed improvement is claimed by this patch; NVFP4 layout binding, CUDA execution, scheduling and server integration are separate follow-ups.

Validation on Windows, MSVC 19.44.35228 / Python 3.13.15:

- Standalone Release and Debug builds pass with `/W4 /WX`; CTest passes 2/2 in each configuration.
- The C++ fixture verifies scatter/coalescing, family counters, descriptor ownership, validation-before-I/O, sealing and reuse of owned sample bytes.
- Python runs 12 adversarial/container tests: 11 pass and the symlink-escape fixture is skipped because the account lacks Windows symlink privileges. The sparse >4 GiB seek test passes.
- The Release inspector parses the original checkpoint's 11 shards / 299,545 tensors, reading 40,402,984 header bytes with every payload-family counter zero.

No CUDA, HIP or SYCL backend files are touched or built. Linux execution has not been validated. Build commands, behavior and limitations are documented in `docs/SAFETENSORS_SOURCE.md`.

pulls.title: Host memory probe: accept the root cgroup v2 group ("0::/", WSL without systemd)
pulls.author: AkaP88
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none open, found it on my own setup.

## Summary
Ran into this on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04, no systemd): `/proc/self/cgroup` is just `0::/`, so the path ends up as `/sys/fs/cgroup/` with a trailing slash. That never matches the root, and since the root group has no `memory.max` the probe gives up, so the engine doesn't know how much RAM is free.

## What changed
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: use the root directly when the line is `0::/`.
- `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: added a test for it, it fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Extra Notes
- Been running 0.1.31 with this patch on a 3090 + IQ2_XS with `--resident-experts` for a while now without issues.
- Also it's better to copy the model files in your wsl disk rather than accessing it from /mnt/ as WSL-Windows Bridge is super slow (top at ~90 mb / sec instead of 3-4 GB/s)

pulls.title: Loop guard: catch a young sentence loop, splice medium effort on recovery
pulls.author: Yunado
pulls.body:
A production agent session this week looped inside its reasoning: one ~20-word sentence, 15 times in a row, carrying a stale premise from the previous turn. Two small additions to the #728 guard, both behind the existing opt-in `"reasoning_loop_recovery"` key.

**Early detection.** The coverage look measures the last 2,000 words, so a young loop stays under the 25% line while it burns budget (this one measured ~15% at 15 repetitions, ~1,000 tokens spent before the guard could see it). A parallel trigger now fires when the same sentence runs 5 times in a row at the end of the reasoning. Pieces shorter than 8 words and 40 characters are out of the count, so repeated code, short lines and numbered enumerations stay safe; interleaved repetition remains the coverage look's job.

**Medium effort recovery.** `focused_recovery_prompt` now matches the medium sentence as well as the xhigh one and splices it to low, so a medium-effort request gets the same rescue. The coding-agent report in #728 looped at effort medium, the shape this opens up. The xhigh splice is byte-identical; a test pins that.

Checked: `tools/loop_guard_test.py`, 17 assertions (splice parity, medium, the None cases, the production shape, the length gate, CJK, interleaving, a coverage regression), plain python, no GPU or model needed. Not tested: a live looped session end to end.

pulls.title: serve: tokenise the prompt from the last shared prefix, not from the start
pulls.author: gputier
pulls.body:
This reopens #567 on the new main, as Niko1221 suggested after the history rewrite. It supersedes #567 and closes nothing.

Every request re-encoded the whole conversation before the engine saw it. `PromptEncoder` keeps the last prompts with their ids and resume points, and encodes only the text that follows the longest shared prefix. The ids are the ones a full encode gives, token for token.

## Changes against #567

Rebased on v0.1.42 (61b3fb5d). #931's literals (control-token text inside a message stays text) go through the incremental encoder: the shared prefix ends where the two prompts' plain spans first differ. blange48 merged #567 with #931 the same way on port-567, and stays credited as co-author. f346dc6b's piece cache is kept, and the incremental encoder sits on top of it. Upstream's `tools/test_strata_tokenizer.py` tests are all kept, and ours are added.

Two fixes of #567's own behaviour:

- Every rendered prompt starts with the template's header, a special-token boundary, so a prompt from another conversation counted as extending the kept one and replaced it. A subagent's request cost the main conversation its reuse on the next turn (8,276 characters reused, then 236). Now a prompt replaces an entry only when it reuses more than half of that entry's text. Otherwise it is a new entry, and the server keeps one per slot of the engine's conversation cache (`--conversation-cache-slots`, 4 without it). Token counts (`/v1/messages/count_tokens`) read the kept prompts without storing one.
- A prompt refused because it does not fit the context is no longer kept by the encoder. Other refusals keep it, since the client resends the same prompt.

SECURITY.md now says that the server keeps the text and ids of its last few prompts in memory, and that no endpoint shows them.

## Numbers and tests

Measured on v0.1.41 with llama.cpp's qwen35 vocabulary, `Service.encode_prompt` per turn, 12 measured turns per pass, in a 10-CPU Linux container on an Apple M5 Pro:

- 125K-token agent conversation resent with one more ~500-token turn: 42.5 ms per turn on v0.1.41, 11.0 ms with this PR (3 passes, spread between passes 0.5 ms). Final branch, one pass: 11.7 ms.
- 89K-token prompt resent identically: 29.5 ms on v0.1.41, 6.6 ms with this PR. Final branch: 6.6 ms.
- Ids identical to v0.1.41 on all 84 compared turns, and on every turn of the final-branch run.
- On a slower CPU the absolute times are higher: sergqwer measured 221 ms to 5 ms at 125K on #567, before the piece cache.

`python -m pytest serve tools/test_strata_tokenizer.py`: 598 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed (v0.1.41 alone: 584 passed, 11 skipped). The 7 extra skips are the qwen35-vocabulary tests, which need `STRATA_TOKENIZER` or llama.cpp's vocab file. Fuzz: 2,400 random plain/literal-span cases, incremental against full, and 2,400 random message prompts through `Service.encode_prompt` with control-token and think text quoted. All equal.

Five commits on v0.1.41:

- c319b113 serve: the prompt is tokenised from the last shared prefix, not from the start (co-author blange48)
- b98660e9 serve: #567's server tests take their reference from a full encode_prompt
- 854564d5 tools: llama.cpp's qwen35 vectors are checked with the qwen35 vocabulary
- 8941f1f4 serve, tools: #567's tests and ByteTokenizer without repeated code
- 96e6139b serve: #567's kept prompts, one per conversation, none refused for the context

pulls.title: Community report: 10-file quant battery on RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (ISTA vs Swift vs Gyro-S/M)
pulls.author: Zauberio
pulls.body:
### What this is

Updated community quality battery requested via Xavier: **10 local files, 3 quant/finetune labs, 20 local effort arms, 20 local tool arms**, on **RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB / Ryzen 9800X3D / 64 GB RAM / Windows + WSL2**. Eight stock files use **0.1.40.3 (`34CDE150B21148E6`)**; current Gyro-S and Gyro-M scored measurements use separate AgentionAI rc2 setups. Shared evaluators do not isolate model-only stock/fork differences. GPT-6-luna MAX and GPT-6.1-SOL ultra are separately labeled OpenAI-hosted quality references, not recommendations or local RTX runs; both are outside the local counts.

**[Download the full PDF](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/raw/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/strata-community.pdf)** (17 pages) · **[GitHub report](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/blob/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/README.md)** · **[Canonical metrics](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/blob/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/data/ALL-METRICS.json)** · **[Luna reference detail](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/blob/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/data/hosted-api-reference.json)** · **[SOL reference detail](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/blob/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/data/hosted-api-reference-sol.json)** · **[Rebuild/audit scripts](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/tree/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/scripts)**.

### What changed in this revision

- **Comprehensive decision methodology:** replaced the limited four-axis index with a complete all-test capability and deployment matrix, an explicit default recommendation and workload-specific alternatives. No arbitrary master score; no new measurement or production-model swap.

- Gyro-S rc2 and Gyro-M rc2 are integrated into the common coding, tools, knowledge/debugging, economics, speed and final-board views — **no standalone model chapter**. Gyro-S current valid rc2 sampled suites, including a scored algebra run, are imported with hashes. Old rc1 data stays archived.
- GPT-6-luna MAX and GPT-6.1-SOL ultra are each integrated as **separate OpenAI-hosted reference rows/bars, score-ordered where comparable, with no medal decoration**; both stay outside local file/arm counts, recommendations, ranks, composites and local performance claims. SOL uses the first-upload result only; the later feedback-assisted Five Bugs validation is excluded.
- Whole tables stay on one page; section headings/explainers stay with their first result. Every table has an automated PDF-page proof.
- Final scorecard and Pick Your File share one evidence-based registry: **Swift IQ3_S (UkisAI), low, is the recommended daily-driver default**. All test families, a new **Speed (Total Wall)** column (code+debug+5-run tool, lower is faster) and deployment caveats are considered; there is no master score, weighting or numeric overall rank. Swift Q2_0 low is the fastest total wall (55m54s) and best stock tool floor; specialist alternatives and experimental forks remain explicitly qualified.
- Former partial coding denominators (155/163, 157/163) are resolved as documented: Base low 155/164 through offline scoring adjudication; Swift IQ3_S low 157/164 through a complete matched run. All 20 local effort rows are included in the final decision matrix, without numeric overall ranks. Gyro-M decode remains unverified only in speed diagnostics; historical Gyro-S rc1 sampled suites are not mixed into rc2 evidence. Historical rc1 coding 153/162 after two HTTP 502s is superseded by the complete rc2 coding runs.

### Measured headlines, with scope

- GPT-6-luna MAX external reference: HumanEval+ 95.7% final (93.3% first); TEB 90.0 +/- 1.9, Pass@5 92.4%, Pass^5 75.0%, Hard Mode 87.8%; Five Bugs 25/25 visible / 20/25 hidden.
- GPT-6.1-SOL ultra hosted reference, **from first upload only**: HumanEval+ 95.1% first / 97.6% final; TEB 90.2 +/- 0.4, Pass@5 88.0%, Pass^5 83.7%, Hard Mode 85.4%; Five Bugs 25/25 visible / 20/25 hidden. The second upload’s feedback-assisted regrades are excluded; one trial-2 TC-56 timeout was recovered through a validated original-prefix continuation, with original and recovery records preserved in the first-upload source. [First-upload source](https://github.com/Jhacarreiro/Strata/commit/a48292f5766f66efcdb1e23396569b0907c44c04).
- SOL’s supporting samples: GSM8K 98/100 (8-shot; exact question-set identity versus the study is unverified); abstract algebra 96/100 (first 100 only); IFEval 45/50 prompts and 70/76 constraints; Needle 25/25 at a 260,096-token target, with the five largest inputs 221,595–221,877 actual tokens and a transport change.
- KNOWLEDGE & DEBUGGING: the top hidden Five Bugs score is tied at 20/25 among S-IQ3_S (UkisAI), GPT-6-luna MAX (OpenAI-hosted API reference), GPT-6.1-SOL ultra (OpenAI-hosted Codex reference). Local-first tie order lists S-IQ3_S first; it is not a unique win.
- Matched hosted decode performance is unavailable; all hosted speed rates are withheld. SOL has no GPU/throughput/latency measurements. Luna’s provider-reported HE+ 42.0 tok/s includes hidden reasoning and is neither visible-text throughput nor a local decode measurement.
- Gyro-M HE+: 156/164 low (95.1%), 157/164 xhigh (95.7%). Two xhigh length-limited blank finals remain failures.
- Same pinned TEB cohort: mean 86.0 +/- 1.4 low / 87.8 +/- 1.1 xhigh; floor 78.3 / 71.7. Hard Mode improves while empirical reliability falls; no model-only causal conclusion.
- Gyro-S rc2 HE+: 157/164 at both efforts; TEB mean 88.6 / 89.0, Pass^5 79.3 / 76.1. The overall battery status is `aborted_or_invalid` (auxiliary `plugin-mmlu` hit HTTP 429 in the original run); HE+/TEB and valid rc2 math/IFEval/Five Bugs/Needle slices are included individually, and a guarded offline algebra-only rerun on the pinned rc2 model/engine scored 79% (first 100 abstract-algebra, 5-shot), imported with provenance.
- The highest stock floor remains S-Q2_0 (UkisAI) low (78.3); Gyro-M low ties the observed floor on an experimental fork, not a stock-composite rank.
- Minimum 205 MiB free VRAM, peak 78 C. This 16 GB Gyro-M result is experimental, not a supported daily-driver recommendation.

### Validity and engine findings

Campaign **`completed_with_invalid_slices`**: CTest 49 passed / 2 skipped / 1 failed (`ple_parity`, missing fixtures); separate reader selftest passed. Gyro-M raw safety gates failed both efforts: low: failed (6 raw warnings); xhigh: failed (2 raw warnings); this is distinct from stored evaluator ratings. Both HE audits exist, but a step-name merge defect made done.json mark them absent; blank-final validity handling was too permissive. Raw status and failures are preserved.

Historical Gyro-S rc1 has no valid tool-eval baseline; its synthetic speed profiles remain excluded. Current Gyro-S rc2 coding, tool and engine-log-audited speed rows use the pinned rc2 identity; Gyro-M rc2 tool arms are also scored. Gyro-M raw endpoint speed is shown in the performance tables (and excluded from the decode charts) because the client targeted :8090, the recorded launcher used :8080, the available router maps :8081 to :8080, and no route proof or engine-side request log was retained. Separate Swift v2.8.0 / 97-scenario tool data is not blended in. No engine/server/default code is changed by this PR.

### What we did NOT test

Vision quality; multi-GPU; other GPUs/VRAM sizes; multi-day agents; additional seeds; full knowledge datasets; Gyro-M beyond 131K. Valid rc2 GSM8K, algebra, IFEval, Five Bugs and Needle results are included; additional independent repetitions were not performed. Results are same-rig historical observations, not same-day model-only stock/fork controls. For Luna, MAX is explicitly pinned; unsupported/unverified Chat Completions sampling fields (temperature, presence_penalty, seed, top-p/top-k) are not forwarded by the Codex Responses bridge. For SOL, GSM8K used seed 42, but the original study sampling seed was not retained, so exact sample identity is unverified. MMLU is only the first 100 abstract_algebra questions (5-shot); IFEval is only the first 50 prompts. Tool trials used concurrency 4 versus the reference study concurrency 1. Requested temperature, seed and token budgets are not enforced by Codex CLI. The SOL Codex CLI used a JSON-schema bridge; requested temperature/seed/token budgets were not enforced. Neither hosted result supplies comparable GPU performance; all hosted speed rates are withheld.

### We publish our fixes

The independent `scripts/audit_revision.py` checks source identity, denominators, score order, and hosted/local exclusions. This revision publishes **five report corrections**: historical partial coding denominators are resolved by documented offline scoring adjudication and a complete matched replacement run; tool-category values use five-run means; inflated raw prompt-prefill rates are retired; the reliability gap is labeled Pass@5 ceiling minus Pass^5 floor; and the peak-temperature summary is corrected from 64 C to the measured 78 C. These are transparent report/audit corrections, not new model or hardware measurements.

### Reproduce and audit

`data/ALL-METRICS.json -> scripts/build_revision.py -> PDF + README + ten charts + claims.json + FINAL-SCOREBOARD.json`. Task JSONs, all 20 raw local five-trial tool arms, measured local perf profiles, both sanitized hosted-reference details, source manifest and validation scripts are included. The hosted-reference details contain audited scores, protocol and source hashes only — no prompts, model outputs, thoughts or credentials. Coding raw data is gzip-compressed; secrets/rig addresses are redacted. Scope stays one report folder plus the existing community-benchmarks row. See [TRIMMED.md](https://github.com/Zauberio/Strata/blob/study/quant-battery-rtx5070ti/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-quant-study-rtx5070ti/TRIMMED.md) for exclusions.

If committing a PDF is undesirable, I can move it to a release/attachment without changing the measured report.

pulls.title: serve: an opt-in VRAM headroom for --expert-cache auto (#1549)
pulls.author: demetree
pulls.body:
## What this changes

`--expert-cache auto` sizes the VRAM-resident expert tier to every byte the card reports free. On a card
that ends up nearly full that is wrong by a lot: the prompt path then reads tens of times slower while
doing exactly the same work.

It adds one opt-in setting and **changes no default**:

```
STRATA_EXPERT_CACHE_HEADROOM=<fraction>    # "1/6", "0.17", or "0" for the sizing you have today
```

the share of free device memory `auto` keeps for the session's other buffers instead of experts. The
helper is `strata::core::expert_cache_headroom()` in `include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp`, read by
the CUDA/HIP sizing in `src/program/generate.cpp`.

**What it leaves alone.** The default is zero, so every backend keeps the sizing it always had and the
default path is byte-identical to the last release: with the variable unset, the old expression is
evaluated. An explicit `--expert-cache N` is the user's own budget and is never cut. When the headroom
would leave no room at all, the old sizing stands. Nothing in the prompt, decode or expert paths is
touched - the cache is just sized smaller.

## Why, and what it was measured on

An Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, driver 32.0.101.8976), the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS pack, OpenCL backend,
eager, `--prefill 4096`, greedy, 64-token prompt. The same 3,668 gate/up and 3,668 down naive GEMM calls
at every cache size - only the cache size and the memory left over change:

| expert cache | VRAM of experts | prefill | ms per expert GEMM call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17,687 slots (`auto` before) | 28.82 GiB | 426 s | 111 |
| 15,382 slots | 24.95 GiB | 472 s | 122 |
| 14,704 slots | 23.87 GiB | 9.7 s | 2.32 |
| 10,698 slots | 17.36 GiB | 10.3 s | 2.39 |

A cliff, not a slope: every size up to 14,704 slots is stable at ~10 s and every size from 15,382 up
takes minutes. The two expert GEMM phases are 95.8% of the GPU timeline in the slow arm, and the phase
waiting for the host-to-device staging copies is **34 ms of 957,283** - the bytes are not the problem.
Memory during the slow pass peaks at 31.2 GiB of dedicated memory (the card full) and holds ~15 GiB
shared; the fast one peaks at 30.08 GiB dedicated and ~3.4 GiB shared. That is consistent with WDDM
paging an over-subscribed allocation to system memory, which the engine's own comment at the sizing
describes, but it is not proven.

Ruled out, each measured: the host mirror (35% of the same pack mirrored over PCIe costs nothing, 2.05
ms per call against 2.01 with every expert resident); the prompt length (the cost is fixed per expert
call, not per token); subnormals in the dequantized weights or activations (none in either pack);
`--kv-resident` (7,589 ms against 7,587 ms). The kernel calls and their shapes are identical in every
arm. No accuracy cost: the cut and the uncut sizing give identical greedy output tokens - eight tokens,
`271 71093 271 550 18381 198 12 1510`, from a scrambled 48-token prompt.

`docs/EXPERT_CACHE_HEADROOM.md` has the full findings, the A/B protocol for a card this has not been
measured on, and what each outcome would mean; `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` gets a row for it.

## How I checked it

- With the variable unset, `free_room` is the expression the last release evaluates - no code path
  changes.
- With `1/6` set on the B70, the knob reproduces the measurement: 14,688 slots (23.83 GiB) against
  17,687 (28.82 GiB) unset, with identical output tokens.
- The header compiles: the SYCL build includes it and passes.
- **Not compiled:** this machine has no `nvcc` or `hipcc`, so the CUDA/HIP sources in this pull request
  were not built where the change was written. The call site is the same statement the SYCL port makes
  against the same helper.

## What this is not

This is not a claim that the effect is real on NVIDIA or AMD. It is Windows/WDDM evidence from one
Intel card, offered as a knob so it can be measured elsewhere. If it turns out to be a no-op on CUDA
the default stays zero, and if the cliff is real there the numbers from the A/B are what would justify
turning it on.

Closes the sizing half of #1549.

pulls.title: serve: a reply that ends inside its thinking with no answer is continued (#1814)
pulls.author: 47Hunter47
pulls.body:
Fixes #1814. #1178's turn-side case is the same end and is covered by the same flag.

**Update to this description (14 Oct):** the branch is rebased onto `main` (`v0.1.44.1`, `296b59d2`) and is now **7 commits, 6 files (+546/−2)**. The `</tool_response>` half that used to be a commit here is **no longer in this PR**: upstream shipped it in 0.1.44 (`62185aab`, the #2026 follow-up, listed in the 0.1.44 notes as "A literal `<tool_call>`, `<tool_response>` or `</tool_response>` in a message is text (47Hunter47, #2026)"), so the rebase dropped my copy. After the rebase the guard probe on this machine (engine and server 0.1.44.1) is 0 of 4 empty replies, with `ended_inside_thinking: true` on the run that ended inside its thinking. Everything below about the guard is current; the `</tool_response>` section is kept for the record, with where it shipped.

## What I see

The model is about to write its closing thinking tag and the **turn-end token comes instead**:

```
[strata] raw: 'We need to respond to user: "In a markdown code fence, show exactly how the closing
thinking tag looks ... inside prose."\n\nNeed likely show closing thinking tag: <|im_end|>'
```

`finish_reason` is `stop`, the reasoning stops mid-sentence, no answer is produced, and the client gets an empty reply.

**Reproduced on 0.1.44 itself**, from a stock checkout of the tag `v0.1.44` (`ed4773eb`) — the tag's own `serve/`, no local patches (`literal_think_guard` does not exist there), `/props.build_info` = `Strata 0.1.44`, engine 0.1.44, RTX 3090 with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 250K context, `--kv int8`, sampling 1.0/0.95/20, thinking budget 16384:

| prompt | runs | empty replies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the minimal input from #1178 (asking for the turn-end marker, verbatim) | 8 | **8 of 8** (86 to 255 tokens generated) |
| the prompt from #1814 (show the closing thinking tag in a code fence) | 10 | 3 of 10 |

One of those turns, as the engine log prints it:

```
[strata] req openai: msgs=1 tools=0 max_tokens_raw=4000/None max_new=4000 thinking=True stream=False prompt_tokens=76
[strata] thinking capped at 3000 of max_tokens 4000 to leave room for the answer (budget 16384)
[strata] thinking: 76 of budget 3000 (max 4000) tokens, 86.3 tok/s, 1 s
[strata] done: 89 tokens in 1 s (81.9 tok/s) (stop, cancel=False), expert cache 98.1% hit
[strata] raw: '...使用 ChatML 格式：<|im_start|>user\n内容<|im_end|>'
```

89 tokens of a 3000-token thinking budget, ended with `stop`: not a budget cut and not a length cut. `/metrics` on that tree has no `ended_inside_thinking` series, so an empty reply carries no sign of why it is empty.

On 0.1.41 the same trigger prompt behaved the same way but not on every run: 6 of 9, then 3 of 5, then 0 of 6. The prompt has to make the model reach for its closing tag, and the cut lands right where the tag would start, or right after a backtick - which matches what danirebollo describes in the issue.

Five real turns are in `serve/fixtures/literal_think_specimens.json` (`STRATA_DEBUG=1`, dumped on this box on 0.1.41): three `no-answer`, one `answered`, one `length-cut`.

## Why the parser cannot catch it

In this tokenizer the token that ends the turn, `<|im_end|>`, is a type-3 control token (id 248046, matched only with `parse_special`), and the closing thinking tag `</think>` is a type-4 token (id 248069, matched either way). The turn ends on that control token itself - the server's stop set - so no character of the marker is emitted, and nothing in the stream says "I meant that": a turn that ends inside its thinking looks exactly like a turn that ended there on purpose. That is also why #537's mark/unmark work (the input side) does not cover it.

## The fix: the token's text is given back, then the thinking is closed (both behind one opt-in flag)

**1. The end is reported** (with the flag on, like the continuation):

* one log line per reply: `the reply ended inside its thinking with no answer (N tokens generated)` - with the guard on the continuation line follows it, and once its cap is reached the line says so
* `totals.ended_inside_thinking`, exposed as `strata:totals_ended_inside_thinking_total` on both `/metrics/prometheus` (llama.cpp's names) and `/metrics` with `Accept: text/plain` (vLLM's). It counts *ends* inside the thinking, so a reply the guard continues past can count more than once.
* `"ended_inside_thinking": true` beside `choices` in the response, and in the stream's last chunk (the same place `timings` goes)

So a client that turned the guard on and got an empty reply is told why it is empty and can retry, and an operator sees the rate. The field is absent on a normal reply.

**2. The continuation** (`"literal_think_guard": true` in `strata-<model>.json`, or `STRATA_LITERAL_THINK_GUARD=1`), like #1053 - two moves, in this order:

**(a) the token that ended the turn is given back as text** (#1178, reported by TwoAnts). The turn ends on the control token itself, so the reply stops with the sentence unfinished, and closing the thinking there answers with a stub (the table below). So the guard writes the marker's text back where the model was writing it - as ordinary text (the tokenizer's `plain` spans, #931's mechanism) in the reply and in the next pass's prompt - and the thought goes on from there. At the token level, with the real pack tokenizer: `encode("<|im_end|>", parse_special=True)` is the single control token 248046, while `encode("<|im_end|>", parse_special=True, plain=[(0, 10)])` is the same six ordinary text tokens as the unparsed string - which is what makes the next pass carry on instead of stopping at once. Capped per reply (`LITERAL_MARKER_WRITES = 2`, with a `literal_think_writes` counter in the request trace); a thought that repeats whole passages is #728's loop, not a marker it mentions, and goes straight to the close.

**(b) otherwise the thinking is closed** the way #123's wrap-up closes it (`REASONING_CLOSE`), so the next pass's prompt is the one that produced the reply plus what it generated plus that close, and the engine continues from the prefix it already holds. `parser.state == "content"` is the same end from the other side - the model wrote the tag as text, the parser took it as the marker and nothing followed - and there the tag goes back into the reasoning text first (`OutputParser.reopen_reasoning()`). Capped per reply (`LITERAL_THINK_RETRIES = 2`) with a `literal_think_retries` counter in the request trace, so a model that keeps doing it cannot loop.

Both moves are behind the same switch, like #1053: with the flag off a server behaves exactly as it did before #1814 and before #1178 - no log line, no total, no `/metrics` series, no field on the response - so reporting and continuation are one deliberate choice, and the reporting can stay a proof of concept until it is approved on its own. They work together: whichever fires first sets `close_retried`. If you would rather have either on by default, the default is one line (`Service.literal_think_guard`).

## Measured with the flag on

Same two prompts, same box, engine and server 0.1.44, `literal_think_guard: true`: **0 empty of 8**. Every end was reported (`ended_inside_thinking: true` on those responses, the journal line, `totals.ended_inside_thinking` = 15 over the session), and the runs that ended while writing the marker were written back and continued:

```
[strata] the reply ended inside its thinking while writing <|im_end|>: its text is written back as ordinary text and the thinking goes on (1 of 2, literal_think_guard)
[strata] the reply ended inside its thinking while writing <|im_end|>: its text is written back as ordinary text and the thinking goes on (2 of 2, literal_think_guard)
[strata] the reply ended inside its thinking with no answer (269 tokens generated): closing the thinking so the model answers (1 of 2, literal_think_guard)
```

Why the write-back and not the close alone (#1178's prompt, 4 runs each on 0.1.43, both sets 4/4 ended inside the thinking so the guard fired every run):

| reply owed to | empty | answered | what the answer was |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the close alone | 0/4 | 4/4 | `<|im_start|>`, a plan leaked into the answer, `<|im_start|>assistant ...`, `<|im_end|>` |
| the close + the write-back | 0/4 | 4/4 | `<|im_end|>`, `"<|im_end|>"`, `<|im_end|>`, `"<|im_end|>"` |

## `</tool_response>`: the same token arriving from the prompt (shipped upstream in 0.1.44)

This was the second commit here and is not in this PR any more: upstream took it in 0.1.44 (`62185aab`), and the 0.1.44 notes credit it. For the record, what it was and what it measured:

#2026 marked `</tool_call>` - the token that ends a call - as text when it appears in a user, system or tool message. `</tool_response>` closes a tool *result* and is the same kind of token here: id 248067 in this pack's tokenizer, type 4, matched by the tokenizer with or without `parse_special`. A prompt quoting it therefore handed the model the real closer, and the turn ended where the reply should start. Six runs per string on this box (IQ3_XXS, 250K context, `--kv int8`, engine and server 0.1.43.1):

| asked for | replies that came back exactly as asked |
| --- | --- |
| `</aaa>` (not in the vocabulary) | 12 of 12 |
| `</tool_call>` (marked since 0.1.43.1) | 15 of 15 |
| `<tool_call>` | 11 of 12 |
| `<tool_response>` | 6 of 6 |
| `</tool_response>` | **0 of 15** |

The pattern was which literal *closes* a block the template opens - `</tool_call>` closes the answer's call block, `</tool_response>` closes a tool result's block, and the two openers do neither. The one case that must not be marked is a **user** message that starts with `<tool_response>` and ends with `</tool_response>`: the template's `multi_step_tool` scan reads it as a wrapped tool result, and marking happens before the template renders, so `wrapped_tool_result()` gave exactly those messages the set an assistant message keeps. At the token level it came back 4 of 4 after the change, `</aaa>` unchanged, against 0 of 15 before. All of that is upstream's now.

## Tests

`serve/test_literal_think_guard.py` (19 tests) replays the five real turns through a mock engine: every `no-answer` specimen gets the answer with one continuation, the token's text reaches the reply and travels into the next pass as `plain` text (not as the control token, which would stop that pass at once), a looping thought gets the close instead of the write-back, the flag-off case carries nothing (no log, no total, no field) and stays empty, the answer the guard reached is reported too, a reply that hit the cap is reported and still empty, an `answered`/`length-cut` specimen is not touched, a normal reply carries no flag, the flag is off by default, and both caps hold. `serve/test_prometheus.py` checks the `/metrics` series does not exist until the guard counts.

`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` -> **790 tests, 11 skipped, 1 failure**: `test_keepawake`'s `test_service_holds_for_the_whole_request_including_early_close` (its `wait_for(..., t=3.0)` races the keepawake thread's release). `serve.test_keepawake` alone fails the same way on the tag `v0.1.44` in a clean worktree (6 tests, 1 failure in both trees), so it is not from this change.

I have it running on this machine (one 3090, IQ3_XXS, the same config the issue reports) with the flag on.

## Scope

It continues an empty reply and reports it; it does not repair the content. When the model reaches for a stop token's text, the reply that comes back after the continuation can still be that marker, or plan text left over from the thinking (measured on my box: 2 of 3 runs answered the marker question correctly, 1 of 3 came back as a stub), so this is the turn-side half. The trigger itself belongs to two other layers: the prompt side (a quoted literal must not reach the model as the real special token - `</tool_call>` since 0.1.43.1, `</tool_response>` since 0.1.44) and the parser side, which is what #1886 is

pulls.title: fix(serve): preserve literal closing thinking tags
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #537 and related to #1814. When ordinary text tokens spell `</think>` during reasoning, the parser must keep those bytes as reasoning text; only the tokenizer's dedicated end-of-thinking token should close the block. This change makes parser transitions depend on token identity.

The bounded `literal_think_guard` handles dedicated `<think>` / `</think>` tokens in answer text or inside reasoning code spans by rendering the tag with ordinary text-token IDs and resuming from the preserved prefix. If end-of-turn arrives inside an unclosed reasoning code span before any answer or tool call, it similarly inserts literal `</think>` text and resumes. The guard is enabled by default to match #1814 and can be disabled with `"literal_think_guard": false`. It is capped at 64 repairs per reply, respects client stops, and accounts for inserted tokens against the output budget.

### Evidence

- Controlled ordinary-text tag case: the original parser misrouted the tag in 12/12 requests; token-identity parsing handled all 12 with the same generated token IDs.
- A live RTX PRO 6000 run naturally emitted dedicated closing-tag IDs inside reasoning code. The guard replaced them and continued from the verified prefix, but those replies reached their output cap while still reasoning; this verifies repair mechanics, not complete answers.
- A Linux stress test with 4,106- and 8,370-token parser/tool histories produced one baseline stop after an opening backtick in 8 requests. No dedicated closing-tag ID appeared in any of 16 baseline/guard requests. Its synthetic history included the expected symptom, so it is not an independent reproduction of the reporter's agent session.
- We could not test the reported two RTX 3090 GPUs, and the exact dedicated-token-then-stop sequence remains unobserved.

### Validation

- Focused parser/service/HTTP tests: 30 passed on Windows and Linux.
- Full Windows serving suite: 623 passed, 10 skipped (438.513s).
- Full Linux serving suite from a native WSL filesystem with `regex` and `jsonschema` available: 623 passed, 12 skipped (339.043s).

Related but separate work: [#1818](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1818) covers CPU IQ expert dispatch and draft-grouping independence; [#1813](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1813) covers speculative/TCP parity; [#1773](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1773) covers Q8 TCP parity/timings.

pulls.title: Resident RAM mode: the RAM copy follows the conversation (`STRATA_RAM_ADAPT`, opt-in)
pulls.author: SanghunYun
pulls.body:
## Title Issue: Resolves #1837 ## Summary In the resident RAM mode the RAM copy is chosen once, at start. On a PC whose RAM cannot hold every expert the GPU does not, an expert outside the copy is read through the file tier when needed, but is not retained in the resident RAM copy. Read buffers or the OS cache may hold its bytes; the adaptive tier exchanges only the resident copy and VRAM. `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=` (opt-in) lets the resident RAM copy follow the conversation as the VRAM tier does. Rebased onto **v0.1.43 (`7695859a`)** and measured again on RTX 3060 12 GB / 32 GB RAM / IQ2_XS, with `--adapt-async 1 --spec 3` and the release's default tail skip (7). 47 recorded Korean requests from my own use (tools, follow-ups and Open WebUI background tasks) were frozen and replayed in order: release → option on → release, each in a fresh engine starting from the same held learned profile. The prompts are private and are not attached. These are total tokens / total engine time, compared with the **closing release**, not medians of three runs per arm: | actual new-input group | v0.1.43 decode tok/s | `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | gain | |---|---:|---:|---:| | all 47 requests | 43.26 | 50.40 | **+16.5%** | | short (<2,000 new tokens), 39 requests | 43.36 | 50.41 | **+16.3%** | | long (≥2,000 new tokens), 8 requests | 43.09 | 50.39 | **+16.9%** | The two release arms decode at 43.33 and 43.26 tok/s (0.16% apart). Prompt speed differs by 2.5% overall, within run variation; short/long prompt speed differs by +4.0% / +0.6%. Decode demand file-tier blob reads fall from **14.15 → 2.67 per generated token**. The 8,056 RAM promotions read another blob each: **3.16 per token with those added**, a 77.7% reduction. These counts are not physical SSD I/O. **With tail skip.** RAM residency does not exempt an expert from being skipped. This option keeps needed experts' original bytes in RAM instead of reading them through the file tier again; it does not change the routing or the VRAM tier's rule. The gain above is with v0.1.43's default tail skip. Tail skip off was not retested on v0.1.43. The previous v0.1.42 and v0.1.41 measurements remain below, labelled with their releases and workloads. **How it works** 1. **When:** before a decode window, while no adaptive round is in flight (not in a request's first window). 2. **What it reads:** the adaptive tier's own decayed routing counts. Nothing new is counted. 3. **The choice:** per layer, the file-tier expert with the highest count (2 or more, the tier's candidate floor) and the RAM expert with the lowest (below 0.5). The pairs with the largest difference first, at most `n` per window. 4. **The move:** the incoming blob is read from the file beside the copy, then written into the outgoing expert's place. Experts of one layer have one size, so the RAM stays the same size. The outgoing expert is on the file tier again and can come back the same way. The routing, the weights and the VRAM tier's rule are untouched. **Checked** - **Off = main.** With the variable unset: the same 4,489-token prompt, 256 new tokens, greedy, the blocking tier, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`, a fresh engine each time, v0.1.43 / this PR off / v0.1.43 - three answers, one SHA-256. (On v0.1.41: four answers, one SHA-256.) - **Unit test** (`file_expert_source_test --rotation-gpu`, pinned and pageable): the moved-in bytes are the file's, the moved-out expert is read from the file again, a refused call changes nothing, and an exchange with the VRAM tier still works after a move. - **Soak** (on v0.1.41, not repeated): 61 minutes back to back with the option on - 140 requests, none failed, 22,065 experts moved, decode 45.1-46.4 tok/s by ten-minute slice, engine RSS 23.65 -> 23.68 GiB, no error line. - **v0.1.43 replay:** 141 requests across the three speed arms and three off-identity requests, none failed. - **Earlier v0.1.42:** 12 runs, 48 requests, none failed. (The 24 runs on v0.1.41: 96 requests, none failed.) ## What changed - `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`, `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: `FileExpertSource::replace_resident(layer, in, out)`. It refuses when `out` is not in the copy, `in` already is, an exchange is staged, either has an exchange override, or `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE` is active; a failed read leaves the copy as it was. `ram_adapts()` counts the moves. - `src/program/generate.cpp`: the choice above, in the serial `--serve` decode loop before `adapt_tick`, and one line in the per-request stats once an expert has moved. It does nothing with a layer split, a peer GPU, a helper cache or batch slots. - `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: `test_replace_resident`. - `docs/DETAILS.md`: the option, beside `--adapt-async`. Left alone: the routing, the weights, the VRAM tier's rule, the expert profile and `--expert-profile-save`, the prompt path (its routing is not counted; a later prompt reads from the RAM copy as decode left it), every default. ## Extra Notes **Not tested / limits** - Built and run on CUDA/Linux. This head also builds and links on HIP (ROCm 7.10.0a20251120, gfx1100, Ubuntu 26.04); the default host-side `file_expert_source_test` passed with GPU access disabled. AMD model inference and `--rotation-gpu` were not run on HIP. Windows and SYCL were not built. SYCL selects its own copies of the modified engine sources and header, so this change does not add RAM adaptation to the SYCL path. - One machine, one quantization. With every expert in RAM or VRAM there is no file-tier candidate, so nothing moves. - The two thresholds (2 and 0.5) were not tuned; `n` = 8 and 32 measured the same on my own workload (v0.1.41). - On v0.1.43, performance was measured only with `--adapt-async 1 --spec 3`, default tail skip and the private Korean replay above. Tail skip off, the blocking tier, `--spec 2`, the public four-language benchmark and the soak were not repeated on v0.1.43. The #1324 comparison is from earlier releases. The earlier gains are not directly divided by these numbers, since the workloads and starting profiles differ. - Not every individual request improved: the median request-level decode gain is 14.9%; 41 requests improved by more than 3%, five were within ±3%, and the initial 12-token background task was 3.2% slower. No short/long aggregate section worsened in this run. - Each move is a blocking read of one blob (about 0.4 ms in the earlier v0.1.41 measurement) on the decode thread, at most `n` per window. - `--pipeline-windows 2` runs another loop, which this PR does not touch. - Answers were not graded. The moved bytes are the file's.
Machine and settings RTX 3060 12 GB connected over OCuLink (PCIe 4.0 x4, 170 W limit); Ryzen 7 7840HS engineering sample (8 cores / 16 threads, reported as `AMD Eng Sample: 100-000000964-50_Y`, 3.5 GHz maximum); 32 GB LPDDR5-6400; Samsung PM981 512 GB NVMe (MZVLB512HAJQ, PCIe 3.0 x4). Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, on the power-saver profile (`amd-pstate-epp`, `powersave` governor, EPP `power`) for every run of both arms; driver 615.78, CUDA 13.4, source build (`STRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS`, `STRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS`, sm_86). Model: ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS (revision ed59f92), for the earlier v0.1.41/v0.1.42 measurements, the repository's `data/expert-profile.bin`, no learned profile. 20.5 GiB of experts in RAM, 3,968 expert slots in VRAM (3,970 on v0.1.41), about 6,000 experts on the file tier. The earlier v0.1.41/v0.1.42 settings, both arms: `--expert-cache 4200 --resident-budget-gib 20.5 --mmap-experts --kv k8v4 --max-context 131072 --prefill auto:16384 --pool-workers 7 --ple-io direct --greedy --vision --prompt-cache 2 --conversation-cache-mib 1536 --conversation-cache-slots 3`, `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1`, `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=8`, `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, and the adaptive tier and verify window of the table's row (`--spec 3` is `--spec 3 --mtp-max-t 3 --spec-min-p 0.5`; `--spec 2` is `--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 2`). The timing variables `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING`, `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` and `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` were set in both arms. The only difference between the arms is the binary and `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8`. The v0.1.42 runs: `--adapt-async 1`, `--spec 3` only, with `--suffix-draft 0 --vram-reserve-mib 500`; `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` unset (so 7) or `0`, as the row says; `--pcie-frac` unset, and 0.1.42's own measurement settled on 0.15 in every run of every arm.
v0.1.43: workload, cache state and every arm Actual prompt contexts are 281-33,241 tokens. All 47 model-input token-ID hashes match across arms. The closing release and option-on arm read 75,917 tokens and reused 375,160; two requests' read counters differed by one token each, with the same totals. The opening release read 88,847 and reused 362,230 because two requests restored less of their prefix; its aggregate prompt speed is not directly compared with the option-on arm. | arm (execution order) | generated tokens | decode tok/s | read / reused | prompt tok/s | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | release-before | 16,598 | 43.33 | 88,847 / 362,230 | 327.31 | | option-on | 16,293 | 50.40 | 75,917 / 375,160 | 313.09 | | release-after | 17,175 | 43.26 | 75,917 / 375,160 | 305.35 | Output lengths differ, so whole-run elapsed-time ratios are not used as speed gains. Each arm has 47 API requests and 56 engine generation segments including recoveries. The same local OpenAI-compatible server and engine DONE timing fields were used on both sides. No requests were graded. 3,968 actual expert slots, resident budget 20.5 GiB, K8V4, prefill auto:16384, `--spec 3 --mtp-max-t 3 --spec-min-p 0.5`, `--suffix-draft 0 --pool-workers 7 --vram-reserve-mib 500`, CPU prefill share auto, `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1`. `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING` and `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` are on in both arms; the GPU verify profiler is off in both. The same learned starting profile is restored before every arm and restored/released after the experiment; the live profile does not retain learning from the test requests. The release's PCIe auto settles on 0.15. Prompt cache=2, conversation cache=1,536 MiB/3 slots, minimum free=1,280 MiB. Each arm is a fresh process; the OS page cache is not forcibly cleared. Vision is configured on-demand on the separate AMD/Vulkan device, but no images were used. The 131,072 context setting is not a claim that 128K input was tested. The initial storage load is included in the first request, so excluding it the engine process reads 537.7 → 329.1 GB from storage across the remaining requests (decimal GB). This includes prompt, decode, RAM moves and other engine I/O, not decode expert I/O alone. Demand decode reads are 243,086 → 43,422; RAM promotions are 0 → 8,056 and are counted separately. v0.1.43's adaptive overlap does not run with `--adapt-async 1` and is also off by default in resident RAM mode. Overlap-on, Windows, AMD GPU inference, multi-GPU, pipeline/batch and long-running soak were not tested here. The existing memory guard stayed active; no guard limit was violated. Config and learned profile were restored and serving was left stopped after the tests.
v0.1.42: previous headline and language transition `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=` (opt-in) lets the RAM copy follow the conversation as the VRAM tier does. RTX 3060 12 GB, 32 GB of RAM, IQ2_XS, measured again against v0.1.42 (`61b3fb5`), `--adapt-async 1`, `--spec 3`; decode tok/s, median of three fresh-process runs per arm: | route tail skip | v0.1.42 | `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 7 (the 0.1.42 default) | 45.19 | 49.51 | **+9.6%** | | off (`STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`) | 35.36 | 40.40 | **+14.3%** | Prompt speed stays within run variation (466-471 tok/s without, 470-472 with). Blob reads from the file fall from 41.9K to 21.1K per run (68.7K to 33.9K with tail

pulls.title: [GUI] serve: a Chinese / English language switch for the web app (adapted to 0.2.0-beta)
pulls.author: hogtinbao
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The web UI in `serve/web/` is English-only. On a Chinese Windows install the settings page, the sampling drawer, the monitor table and even the server's own validation errors are unreadable to the person running the model, and there is no hook to translate them without editing `app.js` / `monitor.js` — files upstream rewrites regularly.

This PR adds a self-contained translation layer that is opt-in at runtime: one new file `serve/web/i18n-zh.js` plus one `<script>` line in each page. A `Language` control in the header switches between **English**, **简体中文** and **中英文** (Chinese with the English original in small type beneath it). The default stays English, so anyone who never touches the control sees the current UI. Model output is never rewritten — chat bubbles, thinking, code blocks and tool-call payloads are in the skip list.

## Related discussion

#1836 — the earlier revision of this change (adapted to v0.1.45). It was closed by the 0.2.0-beta tracker reset, not on merit. This revision is rebased onto `e88ee39d` and re-verified there.

## Approach

- One new file, no build step, no edits to `app.js`, `monitor.js` or `app.css`; each page gets a single script tag. If the file is absent the pages behave exactly as today.
- A dictionary for static strings plus regex rules for text that carries numbers (`56.9 tok/s`, `3,201 tokens · 12.3 tok/s`, `Saved (…); the earlier file is ….bak`). A `MutationObserver` translates nodes the pages create later, and `title` / `placeholder` / `aria-label` / `<option>` text is translated too.
- Both languages stay in the DOM and CSS picks one, so switching back to English restores the original page (attributes and option labels included).
- Only user-visible chrome is translated; config **values** posted to `/config` remain English (only the option text is translated), so the layer cannot change what the server stores.
- No new dependency, no network access, ~40 KB, MIT, same license header as the rest of the repo.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `python -m unittest discover -s serve -p 'test_*.py'` on this branch — Windows 11, Python 3.12, revision `78e13ae` rebased on `e88ee39d`: `Ran 881 tests in 334.4s ... FAILED (errors=1, skipped=20)`. The one error is `serve/test_winjob.py::test_children_end_with_a_killed_server` (see **Failed**).
- `python -m unittest serve.test_winjob -v` on pristine `e88ee39d` in a clean worktree — the same error, 1 of 3 tests, so it is pre-existing on the base revision, not caused by this change.
- Real server on this branch: `serve/server.py` started with the layer attached; `/health` returned `{"status": "ok", "loaded": true, "images": true, "image_generation": true, ...}`; a `/v1/chat/completions` request with `reasoning_effort: "none"` answered normally (18 tokens, `finish_reason: "stop"`) — the API path is untouched.
- `curl /` and `curl /api-monitor` return the pages with the added script tag; `curl /web/i18n-zh.js` serves the file with HTTP 200.
- `node --check serve/web/i18n-zh.js` — no syntax errors.
- Server error strings round-trip: `POST /config {"set": {"lazy_load": true}}` returns the 400 message `lazy_load: lazy loading is text-only, and this model reads images ("vision")`; that exact string, and the other seven validation messages from `serve/runconfig.py`, are matched by the layer's rules (checked by evaluating the file's own dictionary + rules in node, and by POSTing the failing values).
- Manual use on this PC since v0.1.40: chat, monitor, image page and the settings page, in all three language modes, light and dark; switching back to English restores the original UI.

**Failed:**

- `serve/test_winjob.py::test_children_end_with_a_killed_server` — `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable` at `test_winjob.py:32` (the job-object query returns nothing on this machine). Reproduces on `e88ee39d` without this branch, so it is environmental.

**Not run:**

- No automated browser test. Rendering was checked by eye (Edge and Chrome on Windows, 1366×768 and 1920×1080, light and dark, three language modes). Headless `--dump-dom` hangs against the live page on this machine because it streams `/metrics`, so there is no scripted UI check in this PR.
- No Linux or macOS check of the pages. The file is plain DOM code with no platform branches, but I did not run it there.
- No check of the desktop app (`apps/host`) — it has its own strings and is untouched here.

## Limits

- Covers the web UI only, not the Tauri app.
- The translations live in one file that needs a refresh whenever upstream rewords a string; an unmatched string simply stays English (no runtime error). The file is organised by upstream version, so the diff for such a refresh is small.
- Not a general i18n framework — no locale files, no plural rules. If upstream later wants first-class i18n, this should be replaced by it rather than extended.

pulls.title: Community benchmark: 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, Swift IQ3_XXS, engine 0.1.41 against 0.1.40.1 (single stream to 248k, --batch 8 sweep)
pulls.author: qni-live
pulls.body:
Adds one results folder, `bench/results/2026-10-10-community-2x-rtx-pro-4500-engine-0.1.41/`, and nothing else. No engine changes.

- Hardware: 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB (GB203, sm_120), Threadripper 7960X, 61 GiB RAM, Linux, driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.x. Source builds of v0.1.41 (fb58e0d) and v0.1.40.1.
- Model: Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, layer split 25 over both cards, 262,144 context, `--pipeline-windows 2`, German draft vocabulary, memory clock 14,000 MHz in every sample.
- Single stream at 4k, 32k, 128k and 248k prompt tokens (3 runs each, 0.1.41 against 0.1.40.1, order ABA): prompt reading is the same (128k: 6,148 and 6,146 tok/s against 6,142); the decode difference is inside the run-to-run spread (up to 15 % at 32k).
- `--batch 8` client sweep (`tools/serve_load.py`, 1, 2, 4, 8 clients, 3 rounds, 256 tokens): `--batch-groups auto` gives 115 / 152 / 208 / 256 total tok/s, against 109 / 126 / 159 / 175 for groups 1. That is +46 % at 8 clients, inside the +32 % to +68 % of the release notes. First token at 8 clients 1.6 s, against 7.0 s for the same requests queued on a single stream. Eight slot sessions take 12.1 GiB of VRAM per card (71 % of the experts stay resident) and `--pipeline-windows` is off.
- Needle recall 6 of 6, tool calls 9 of 9 valid. `layer_split: auto` chose layer 24 and did not reorder the two identical cards (#1760 not reproduced here).
- Not tested: `--batch 4` in this folder, long prompts, tool calls or vision in batch mode, Windows, cards of different speed.

pulls.title: Add optional isolated full-TeX chat math rendering
pulls.author: CC-David-CC

Adds optional XeLaTeX → PDF → filtered SVG rendering for assistant equations, with the shared parser, settings, queue and source-preserving chat integration. The shared core does not render. Rendering starts disabled; the compiler container is built and started explicitly, with no dependencies installed by normal Strata startup.

Refreshed to upstream main `61b3fb5d` and shared math core `253ea8cf`. Compilation has no fixed CPU/wall budget, host transport timeout or TeX browser conversion deadline. Browser-only adapters retain their default deadlines. Cancelled compiler RPCs keep their queue slot until completion and discard the cancelled result. Memory, process, filesystem, input/output and SVG limits remain enabled.

Fresh Windows/Docker Desktop validation: 41 endpoint/security tests, seven valid compiler cases, six malformed/restricted compiler cases, and the complete Chromium, Firefox and Playwright WebKit suites passed. The unbounded recursive TeX macro fixture is explicitly skipped and requires operator cancellation by restarting the worker. Source copy/export/history/model requests remain unchanged; the SVG uses source alt text rather than semantic MathML.

[Current refresh evidence and reproduction](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/tree/fba796708ed8f2953eff23eec550e4d094d0e83f/web-math-results/current-main-refresh), including exact image/worker identity, isolation, raw timings and screenshots. Single acceptance-run timings are descriptive; Chromium cold timing includes corpus contention. The archived image is 7.04 GB uncompressed, not an estimated download size.

Addresses [#1769](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1769) and [#1780](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1780). See [setup and adapter contract](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/fba796708ed8f2953eff23eec550e4d094d0e83f/docs/WEB_MATH.md).

pulls.title: Add shared LaTeX/web math core without a rendering engine
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Adds the shared web chat integration for future math renderers. **This PR contains no viewer, typesetting engine, fonts, or TeX compiler.** The placeholder adapter reports unavailable and leaves equations as readable source. Related to #1769 and #1780; rendering support will come in separate follow-up PRs.

- Adds an opt-in **Render math** setting, disabled by default. With it disabled, assistant answers use the existing Markdown path.
- Recognizes inline `\(...\)` and conservative `$...$`, plus display `\[...\]` and `$$...$$`. Protects equation source before Markdown formatting and keeps code and currency literal.
- Preserves source for copying, Markdown export, saved history, and subsequent model requests. Handles streaming and ignores stale asynchronous results.
- Defines the renderer adapter contract, serialized conversion queue, 256-entry cache, 16 KiB UTF-8 input limit, initialization deadline, and asynchronous rendering deadline. Adds restricted same-origin asset serving for later bundled renderers.
- Includes the shared fixture corpus and browser acceptance suite. Separate KaTeX, MathJax, and isolated full TeX branches supply the adapters and dependencies on top of this core.

Core smoke-tested in Chromium for default-off behavior, unavailable-engine source fallback, persistence, API source preservation, and disabling round-trip without engine assets. The shared acceptance suite also passed on the KaTeX implementation in Chromium, Firefox, and Playwright WebKit. Timers cannot interrupt synchronous JavaScript; adapters must bound macro expansion. Macro isolation is an adapter requirement.

See [the interface and branch structure](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/feat/web-math-common/docs/WEB_MATH_INTERFACE.md). The full browser acceptance suite requires a real implementation adapter; this foundation deliberately does not typeset equations.

pulls.title: sycl: register iq_parity and ple_parity like the top-level build
pulls.author: Momoyeyu
pulls.body:
Fixes #1795.

## What

The port's generic parity loop registered every test as `<test> --selftest`. For `iq_parity` that string became its fixture-directory argument (`argv[1]`), and for `ple_parity` the GGUF/capture-bin relative paths resolved against the build tree — so both failed on every checkout for reasons unrelated to the kernels, exactly as the reporter showed.

This takes `iq` and `ple` out of the `foreach` and gives them the same registrations the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` uses:

- `iq_parity`: the `tools/iq_fixture.py` CTest fixture (generated into the build tree), the same python-with-numpy interpreter probe (`IQ_FIXTURE_PYTHON` overrides it), `FIXTURES_SETUP`/`FIXTURES_REQUIRED`, and exit-3 as a skip. The test itself runs as `iq_parity <build>/iq_fixture`.
- `ple_parity`: `WORKING_DIRECTORY` = the engine root so the binary's documented relative defaults (`pack/full`, `bench/micro`, `../../Q2_0/...`) resolve; `--in`/`--out` from a `STRATA_PLE_FIXTURE_DIR` cache path (default `bench/micro`), plus new `STRATA_PLE_GGUF` and `STRATA_PLE_PACK` configure-time inputs for the artifacts the reporter asked to name.

Missing inputs stay a hard error inside the test, as the top-level build intends — this only makes the error satisfiable, and `docs/INTEL.md`'s parity table now names the variables.

## Checked

- `ctest -N` on the exact parity block (stubbed `strata_resolve`/targets): `iq_parity_fixtures` + `iq_parity` and `ple_parity` each register exactly once; with `-DSTRATA_PLE_GGUF`/`STRATA_PLE_PACK` the command line gains `--gguf`/`--pack`, without them it is clean of stray arguments; the fixtures command is `<python> <root>/tools/iq_fixture.py --out <build>/iq_fixture`.
- Not run: a real `ctest` — this machine has no SYCL toolchain; the registration logic is what changed, and it is verified to mirror the top-level contract. A port user can confirm with the issue's repro (`ctest -R '^(iq|ple)_parity$'`).

pulls.title: serve: probe the SYCL launcher's engine binary for --tail-role-token
pulls.author: Momoyeyu
pulls.body:
Fixes #1781.

## What

`effort_end_args()` decides `--tail-role-token` support by grepping `exe`. On the SYCL port `exe` is `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`, a launcher that execs `${STRATA_SYCL_BIN:-build-sycl-aot/strata}` inside a container — the script never names the flag, so `"effort_position": "end"` printed the "needs engine 0.1.39" line and stayed off on every SYCL install, exactly as the reporter measured.

A `#!` exe now gets a second read through `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (the config's `env`, then the process environment) or the default `build-sycl-aot/strata`, relative to the repo two levels above the script — the same layout the launcher computes. A binary exe reads exactly as before; a missing/unreadable binary falls back to the launcher's text, so the probe still answers "unsupported" rather than crashing.

## What it leaves alone

- CUDA/HIP paths: `exe` is the engine there, so the new branch never runs.
- The probe's semantics: still a byte-grep of the engine image, still no version parsing, still a silent `None` when the flag is absent.
- The launcher itself: `strata-sycl.sh` is unchanged; this is server-side resolution of the convention it already documents.

## Tests

`serve/test_effort_position.py` (new, 6 tests): binary exe unchanged behavior; the SYCL layout via the default path and via `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (config `env` and process env); a launcher whose binary lacks the flag; an unreadable/missing binary falling back to the script; `start`/invalid-value handling. 6/6 pass, plus `test_runconfig` and `test_frontend` (17 tests) unchanged.

Not tested: a real SYCL container run — the probe only reads files, and the reporter's environment has the actual image; the layout mirrors the launcher's own `${STRATA_SYCL_BIN:-...}` default and `../..` repo resolution.

pulls.title: qsa_select: prompt-path block scores with a thread per query head (below sm_80, same bits)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

The prompt path's QSA block scores on cards without the TF32 scorer (below sm_80; measured on Turing, sm_75) run on a
new kernel that is 4.6-5.2x faster per call, with bitwise the same scores. sm_80 and newer, HIP, and decode run the
same code as before. `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD=0` turns it off.

Two commits:

1. **A thread per (query, head)** (`block_scores_thread_kernel`). The old kernel scored every (query, key block) with
   a whole warp: 20 shuffles and five 512-byte loads per score. Now each lane keeps one 128-value query head in
   registers, reads each key once from shared memory as a broadcast, and adds its 32 four-value partials in the
   same tree that lane 0 of the old xor-shuffle sum used. Same pairs, same order, so the same bits. The heads are
   summed 0..3 from 0.0f as before, and the tail block keeps `block_scores_tail_kernel`.
2. **Four lanes per query.** Nsight Compute showed the first version bound by the shared-memory pipe
   (`mio_throttle`): one key load per 4 FMAs. The old shuffle tree splits into four quarters that only meet at the
   end, so now four lanes share a query, each holds one quarter of all four heads, one key load feeds 16 FMAs, and
   two xor shuffles finish the same tree. Still the same bits.

New test: `qsa_scores_parity` checks every score of the new kernel against `block_scores_kernel` (normal values, wide
magnitudes with zeros, small integers with ties; up to 262K context), then times both.

## Measured

CMP 50HX (TU102, sm_75, unlocked to RTX 2080 speed), CUDA 13.3, GCC 14.2.

- `qsa_scores_parity`: 141 M scores bitwise identical on both cards.
- Time per call, old warp kernel -> this PR:

  | queries | context | before | after |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1,024 | 140K | 35.9 ms | 6.2 ms |
  | 1,024 | 200K | 52.4 ms | 8.5 ms |

- Why it matters: in an nsys profile of one +4.4K-token prompt at 140K (Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2x CMP 50HX,
  `--layer-split auto`), `block_scores_kernel` was the largest prompt kernel: 1,045 ms per card, 17 % of the time.
- Whole engine, same setup: a coding-agent session from 34K to 190K tokens (36 turns, +~4.4K tokens each, greedy,
  fresh server per run) gave word-for-word the same text as before. Time to first token at 190K went from 10.49 s to
  7.13 s, but that number also includes the tokenizer change in #1823; the scorer's own share was not split out.

Note: measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes; re-measuring on 0.1.41
is still to do. Volta and Pascal (the experimental build) also take this kernel and were not tested.

## How to check

On an sm_75 card: `qsa_scores_parity` (also in ctest). It prints `PASS` when every score matches, and the time of both
kernels.

pulls.title: cpu: Q2_0 rows on AVX-only CPUs (q2_avx1.cpp) instead of ggml-cpu's scalar dot
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

The older-CPU build (`STRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`) on an AVX-only CPU (Sandy / Ivy Bridge, Xeon E5 v1/v2): a native pack's
Q2_0 expert rows run on a new AVX kernel (`src/kernels/cpu/q2_avx1.cpp`) instead of ggml-cpu's Q2_0 `vec_dot`, which
is scalar on x86. Bitwise the same results as the scalar reference. AVX2 / AVX-512 CPUs and CPUs without AVX run the
same code as before.

## Why

In the IQ3_XXS pack, Q2_0 is the down projection of 30 of the 48 layers, so on these CPUs most CPU expert work went
through a scalar loop.

## Change

- `q2_native_kernels()` also accepts an AVX-only CPU (`cpu_avx1_ok()`).
- `q2_rows_any`: AVX-512 -> AVX2 -> **AVX1 (new)** -> scalar. `act_quant_any` uses a scalar Q8_1 quantizer without AVX2.
- `q2_0_gguf_rows_multi_avx1`: compiled with `-mavx` / `/arch:AVX` only (no FMA). The 2-bit codes are unpacked once
  per block for all tokens; SSSE3 `maddubs` / `madd` integer dots (exact: a pair sums to at most 762, no saturation);
  an exact half -> float; the float steps in the scalar order, so the bits equal `q2_0_gguf_rows_multi_scalar`.
- The router lookahead keeps 0.1.41's `kq_avx1.cpp`.
- New test `q2_avx1_parity` (ctest; exit 77 without AVX).

## Measured

2x Xeon E5-2670 v2 (Ivy Bridge-EP), GCC 14.2:

- `q2_avx1_parity`: bitwise equal to the scalar reference for all 65,536 half scales and 216 random cases (1-12
  tokens, partial row ranges, padded and unaligned rows, edge and zero-scale activations).
- One expert's down rows (2560 x 640) on one core:

  | tokens | scalar | AVX1 |
  |---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 3.86 ms | 0.41 ms (9.4x) |
  | 4 | 13.2 ms | 0.78 ms (16.9x) |

Measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. On current `main` (0.1.41) it was checked on a Ryzen 7 5700X with
`STRATA_FORCE_ISA=avx`: `q2_avx1_parity` passes (12.5x over scalar at 1 token), and so do all CPU tests.

pulls.title: tokenizer: a long message's ids remembered whole, on top of the piece cache
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

`tools/strata_tokenizer.py`: on top of 0.1.41's piece cache, a long piece of text between special tokens (one chat
message, 1,024+ characters) keeps its ids too. The ids are the same; only the work is skipped. At most 256 texts are
kept, and the cache is cleared when full.

## Why

An agent sends its whole conversation again every turn. The piece cache skips the BPE merges of repeated pieces, but
the pre-tokenizer regex still runs over the whole conversation each turn. Text between special tokens is already
encoded on its own, so a message seen before can return its ids directly.

## Measured

2.5 GHz Xeon E5-2670 v2, before the piece cache existed (fork based on 0.1.38): at a 190K-token conversation,
encoding took 1.06 s per turn before and 0.042 s with this cache. The ids were identical on all 36 turns of a
coding-agent session (34K -> 190K tokens).

How much this adds on top of the piece cache alone was **not measured yet**: the piece cache already removes the
merges, so the gain is the regex pass over the old messages.

`tools.test_strata_tokenizer` and `serve.test_detok` pass.

pulls.title: prefill: gate/up MMQ reads the experts in place (CUDA; patched copy of llama.cpp mmq.cuh)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

CUDA builds, native i-quant packs, prompt path: the gate/up MMQ product reads each expert's weights where they
already are (expert cache slot or stream ring slot) instead of copying them into a group buffer first. Same bytes into
the same kernel, so the same results. `STRATA_MMQ_INPLACE=0` turns it off. HIP builds keep the old path.

## Why

Before MMQ, the prompt path copied every routed expert's gate/up and down rows into a contiguous group buffer,
resident experts included. An expert blob is already "gate rows then up rows", the exact matrix MMQ wants, so the
gate/up copy is only there because MMQ takes one base pointer and a fixed stride.

## Change

- **llama.cpp is not edited.** CMake writes a copy of the pinned `mmq.cuh` into the build tree with one change in its
  three tile loops: a negative expert stride means `x` is a table of expert pointers. The MMQ instance files (and the
  headers that include `mmq.cuh`) compile against that copy. Configure stops if the patched text is not found exactly
  three times (a different llama.cpp). The changed lines are inside kernel templates, so `quantize.cu`, which sees
  the original header, is unaffected.
- **Prompt path:** a complete group's gate/up MMQ gets a table of expert pointers (`m.grp_ptrs`, written on the
  stream by `group_ptrs`). The group's ring slots are released after the gate/up MMQ instead of after the gather.
- **Down rows keep their copy on purpose:** MMQ reads one tile past a 640-value matrix's last row, and that must be
  the zeroed tail (`MMQ_TAIL`), not the next cache slot.
- A flush forced inside a group (a skipped ring entry) copies both, as before.

## Measured

2x CMP 50HX (sm_75), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split auto`, one +4.4K-token prompt at 140K context (nsys):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `copy16_group_kernel`, GPU 0 | 75.5 ms | 31.9 ms |
| `copy16_group_kernel`, GPU 1 | 77.0 ms | 46.4 ms |
| `mul_mat_q` | 803.6 ms | 804.8 ms |
| engine read time | 6,792 ms | 6,746 ms (-0.7 %) |

A coding-agent session from 34K to 190K tokens (36 turns) gave word-for-word the same text as before.

The gain on this box is small because it is PCIe Gen2 and the second GPU waits on PCIe; a card where the copies are
a bigger part of the prompt should gain more, but that was not measured.

Note: measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes; re-measuring on 0.1.41
is still to do. Only sm_75 was tested.

## How to check

Build (configure must pass the patch check), then compare a prompt's output and read time with
`STRATA_MMQ_INPLACE=0` and without it: the output should be the same.
