pulls.title: qsa_prompt_attn: int8 K/V prefetched in registers and sharing one buffer (Turing / sm_75)
pulls.author: xrip
pulls.body:
## What

Turing (sm_75) only, `--kv int8` only: the prompt attention kernel that Turing runs (v1, `qsa_prompt_attn.cu`) gets
faster with the same output bits. Other GPUs and other KV modes run the same code as before.

## Why

On Turing the v1 kernel used 37.9 KB of shared memory per 128-thread block, so only one block fit on an SM (4 warps,
12.5 % of what an SM can hold). Each 32-cell chunk also loaded its scattered K and V rows only after the previous
chunk had finished. Nsight Compute on a CMP 50HX (TU102, RTX 2080 Ti class) showed `long_scoreboard` (waiting on
global loads) as the top stall.

## Change

1. **The next chunk's int8 K/V rows and scales go into registers while the current chunk computes**, then are stored
   where the old gather stored them. (sm_80+ uses `cp.async` for this; Turing does not have it.)
2. **K and V share one shared-memory buffer.** K is read only by the scores and V only by `p·v`, so V is written over
   K after the scores' barrier; the softmax's barrier keeps it before `p·v`. 37.9 -> 29.2 KB per block: **two blocks
   per SM** instead of one.

The same bytes land in the same places and the arithmetic is unchanged, so the results are bitwise the same.

`qsa_prompt_attn_parity` now also prints a checksum of the new kernel's output, so two builds can be compared bit
for bit.

## Measured

CMP 50HX (sm_75, unlocked to RTX 2080 speed, 20 GB), CUDA 13.3, GCC 14.2.

`qsa_prompt_attn_parity`, int8, 2,048 queries:

| context | before | after | change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 40K | 21.45 ms | 12.91 ms | -40 % |
| 140K | 21.94 ms | 13.31 ms | -39 % |

All output checksums (int8 and fp16, at 4K / 40K / 140K) match the old kernel.

Whole engine: Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2x CMP 50HX with `--layer-split auto`, 2x Xeon E5-2670 v2. A coding-agent session
grew from 34K to 190K tokens over 36 turns (+~4.4K tokens per turn, greedy, fresh server per run). The text of all 36
turns was identical to the old build. Incremental prompt read time went down 3.5 % (median per-turn ratio 0.965), and
decode did not change.

Note: these numbers were measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes;
re-measuring on 0.1.41 is still to do.

## How to check

On an sm_75 card, before and after:

```
qsa_prompt_attn_parity 40000 2048
qsa_prompt_attn_parity 140000 2048
```

The `new output checksum` lines should be equal and the time per chunk lower.

pulls.title: qwen35moe follow-ups: VRAM cap + quality mode, MTP for F16 draft tensors, chunked GDN, 256/8 route-resident
pulls.author: atomicmilkshake
pulls.body:
## What this is

A **stacked PR on top of #1402** (qwen35moe support). It contains the qwen35moe follow-up work we built
and measured while validating that PR on one machine (RTX 3080 10 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 13.2, sm_86):

- MTP for third-party single-file GGUFs whose draft block is stored as **F16**;
- an **opt-in VRAM fraction cap** (`--vram-frac`) and a **quality cap mode** (`--vram-cap-mode quality`)
  that keeps every expert miss on the same GPU kernel as a hit;
- opt-in **chunked DeltaNet prefill** for qwen35moe;
- **route-resident routing generalized to 256-expert / top-8 models** (the #1737 warp-shuffle idea,
  merged with our 256/8 implementation);
- the determinism fixes the auto expert cache needed on Windows/WDDM;
- setup-family and SYCL follow-ups.

Base: #1402 head `48534f3`. The first commits in the diff are #1402's; the 16 commits listed below are
this PR's content. The five upstream PRs we also adopted locally (#1700, #1660, #1659, #1696, #1720) are
**deliberately not included** — they are separate PRs and should land on their own.

The repo's guide is *one change per pull request*. This is a stack of related qwen35moe follow-ups; I am
happy to split it into separate PRs (MTP-F16; cap+quality; chunked GDN; route-resident 256/8) if that is
easier to review. The MTP F16 commit is the smallest and probably the most valuable on its own.

## Commits

**MTP for third-party GGUFs**
- `MTP: accept F16 draft tensors in a single-file GGUF` — the draft-layer loader took F32 for norms and
  BF16/F32 for routers, so a single-file GGUF whose MTP block keeps `ffn_gate_inp.weight` at F16 refused to
  start. F16→F32 is exact; F16→BF16 uses the same round-to-nearest-even as the F32 path. The finite cases
  check out over all 65,536 half bit patterns; NaN needed a later fix (the first checker skipped NaNs, and
  the rounded addition carried them into infinity/signed zero — see the follow-up commit below). Measured on
  the Huihui Q4_K file: **62.5 tok/s vs 26.0** without MTP, 21/25 drafts accepted.
- `Gate Huihui MTP on the F16 draft loader capability` — setup only offers MTP for that family when the
  loader supports it.

**Opt-in VRAM cap + quality mode**
- `Add opt-in total VRAM fraction cap through cache reserves` — `--vram-frac F` sizes the expert cache so
  the engine's own use stays under F of the card; a floor is kept free and the plan is frozen pre-touch
  (post-touch readings only accept or refuse; no resize).
- `Add opt-in uniform-GPU VRAM cap quality mode` — `--vram-cap-mode quality` routes every expert miss
  through the grouped GPU kernel, no CPU fallback. Measured **20/20 token-identical** outputs vs the
  uncapped run, 6,759 vs 9,397 MiB peak.
- `Book late VRAM and refuse serve requests that cross the floor` + `cap booking: keep the named late
  allocations, leave graphs to the slack + refusal` — books the chunked-GDN scratch and MTP prefill records
  in the frozen budget, re-checks the floor on the serve path and after `cudaGraphInstantiate`, and logs
  free memory at READY / first capture / first chunked launch / first checkpoint. Validated: free
  3,511–3,577 MiB against the 2,048 MiB floor, no refusals, prefix reuse intact.

**qwen35moe prefill and routing**
- `Port opt-in chunked DeltaNet recurrence to qwen35moe` — opt-in (`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED`), parity-checked
  against the default recurrence.
- `Use qwen35moe active expert count for router lookahead` — width 8 instead of qwen4exp's 10.
- `Port opt-in route-resident routing to 256-expert top-8 models` — the 256/8 counterpart of #1737.
- `route-resident: one warp per token for the 512/10 and 256/8 swap` — merges #1737's warp-shuffle swap
  with the 256/8 implementation into one templated kernel (`route_resident_impl<NE,K>`). This commit can
  replace #1737 if preferred: it contains its approach for 512/10 and adds 256/8.

**Determinism, setup, SYCL**
- `Make expert-cache auto use one fixed 1 GiB haircut` + `Bucket the qwen35moe auto-cache haircut and check
  the reserve` — fixes the auto-cache non-reproducibility on Windows/WDDM (2,974 vs 3,494 slots between
  identical runs) and refuses cleanly instead of stalling under low headroom.
- `Add Huihui abliterated Qwen3.6 setup family` — the family in `setup.py` with tests.
- `Keep the shared Qwen36 setup test harness offline on Windows`.
- `qsa: mirror the dense-attention validate() fix into the SYCL twin` — the CUDA fix in #1402 did not touch
  the SYCL twin.
- `SYCL generate: explicitly refuse the CUDA-only VRAM cap flags` — fail closed instead of ignoring them.

## Validation (RTX 3080 10 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 13.2, sm_86)

**Measured on this exact branch** (stacked on `48534f3`):
- Build: VS 18 / Ninja / Release / sm_86, exit 0.
- Full `ctest`: 96 passed, 1 skipped (`expert_multi_test`), 1 failed (`ple_parity`, missing Flash-Next
  **Q2_0** fixture, not present on this machine). The two cap tests are `vram_cap_test` (169 CPU checks)
  and `vram_cap_quality_test` (2,529 CPU checks); the other suites are the repo's own.
- Capped quality + MTP smoke on the Huihui Q4_K file: exit 0, output token ids identical to the validated
  line (64/64), `--expert-cache 3200` capped to 1430 slots, free 3,513 MiB after the first capture.

**Measured on the integrated line this work sits in** (`95f205d` + the cap-floor fix, sha `d58e8ded`;
it also contains the five upstream PRs we adopted locally — #1700/#1660/#1659/#1696/#1720 — which this PR
deliberately excludes):
- Cap + quality: 20/20 token-identical vs uncapped, 6,759 vs 9,397 MiB peak.
- MTP: 62.5 vs 26.0 tok/s (2.4×), 21/25 accepted; server path 71.1 tok/s.
- Full stack (cap + quality + MTP + chunked + route-resident): 10/10 arms exit 0, whole-card peaks
  7,269–7,371 MiB under the 8,192 ceiling; server prefix reuse 1,005/1,012 with TTFT 1.89 s → 0.098 s;
  chunked kernel launches confirmed under Nsight Systems; HumanEval 39/40 at 2,048 and **39/40 at 4,096**
  (no truncations; the single miss is HumanEval/132's wrong implementation).
- Determinism: byte-identical outputs across repeated runs **at a fixed cache geometry**; the bucketed
  haircut reduces but cannot eliminate sensitivity when the pre-touch reading crosses a bucket boundary, so
  a run can still open a different slot count. Cache size does not change the output tokens in quality mode
  (20/20 identical), but the slot count is not guaranteed bit-identical run to run. Clean refusal (no stall)
  when the reserve cannot be met.
- Backends: **CUDA built and exercised; HIP and SYCL were not built** (no toolchain on this machine). The
  SYCL changes are verified by inspection only, which does not meet `AGENTS.md`'s build-every-touched-backend
  rule; an Intel/HIP machine should build them before this is merged.

## What this leaves alone

- **Defaults:** cap, quality, chunked and route-resident are all opt-in. Two of the determinism commits do
  change the qwen35moe **fast-mode** auto-cache path: the bucketed haircut activates under WDDM for eligible
  native non-indexed models even without `--vram-frac`, and the router lookahead uses the model's active
  expert count (8 instead of 10). qwen4exp keeps its measured-shortfall loop; no other default path changes.
- **qwen4exp:** the route-resident change keeps the 512/10 behavior; the auto-cache fixes keep the
  measured-shortfall loop for qwen4exp.
- **Not included:** #1700 / #1660 / #1659 / #1696 / #1720 (separate PRs) and #1737 (superseded by the
  templated 512/10 + 256/8 commit here).

## Follow-up fixes from an adversarial review (2026-10-10)

Three review findings were fixed on top of the stack:

- `MTP F16: keep NaN NaN in the F16/BF16 conversion` — the rounded addition carried NaN into infinity or a
  signed zero; NaN now keeps a nonzero BF16 mantissa.
- `SYCL: refuse a malformed STRATA_VRAM_FRAC like the CUDA build does` — 0, NaN, empty, trailing junk and
  underflow-to-zero were silently ignored; they now exit 2 as on CUDA.
- `VRAM cap: check the floor at every chunk, at serve decode admission, before pipelined windows` — the
  floor was checked only before the first prompt chunk; a long prefill, a fully reused prompt, and the
  `--pipeline-windows` decode loop could step past it. Prefill now has a per-chunk guard, serve re-checks
  at decode admission, **all five `pl_launch` sites are guarded** (the initial A, the speculative B, the
  promoted A's stage-1 launch, and both prompt-pipeline launches), and the first-use chunked-GDN scratch
  allocation checks the floor before taking its bytes.

Still open from that review (not fixed here): the stack does not meet the repo's one-change-per-PR rule,
and HIP/SYCL builds are not run.

## Known limits

- One machine: Windows, RTX 3080, CUDA. No AMD/Intel or Linux numbers here.
- The F16 draft conversion is bit-checked and end-to-end on the Huihui GGUF; no other F16-draft model was
  available.
- Quality mode requires a native expert pack; on this machine it cannot run the 46.8 GiB Flash-Next arena
  because the whole arena cannot be pinned (a host limit, unrelated to these paths).
- The determinism fixes target the Windows/WDDM auto-cache path; Linux behavior was not re-measured here.

pulls.title: fix: make CPU IQ dispatch independent of draft occupancy
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Uses the same supported CPU IQ kernel for a token alone and for a group of draft tokens. The previous default switched arithmetic at two tokens, allowing group occupancy to change rounding even when the accepted prefix and rollback were correct. The default now matches `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, including IQ4_NL down rows. `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=2` retains the legacy behavior for comparison; `STRATA_IQ3S_MT1` is redundant.

Refreshed onto current main (`61b3fb5d`). Direct native CPU checks compare each token's gate/up and down rows bit for bit across widths 1 through 8. Default, forced AVX2 and ggml controls pass; the explicit legacy threshold fails the negative control as expected. CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds and CPU checks passed. CUDA/HIP GPU synthetic format comparisons use numerical tolerances and do not prove end-to-end speculative token identity.

This is a correctness tradeoff, not an unconditional speed improvement. Fresh Ryzen 7600X3D one-token CPU expert microbenchmarks measured +68.61% time for IQ2_XS, +17.65% IQ2_XXS, +13.22% IQ3_XXS and +10.03% IQ3_S; IQ2_S and IQ4_XS were approximately unchanged. Three processes per setting alternate default/legacy order; these are per-expert costs, not whole-model decode regressions.

The fresh 14-request mixed CPU/GPU no-draft/single-token/drafted comparison passes exactly when approximate tail skipping is disabled (`STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`). Earlier default-policy divergences are retained and explained: rank-7 skipping uses minimum expert rank across the token window, so adding draft rows can change target contributions. This PR preserves ordinary tail-skip defaults. The controlled main pipeline matrix also passes; suffix-on-pipeline coverage remains incomplete. These finite controls do not claim arbitrary model, CPU/GPU or pipeline parity.

[Fresh results, full token records, diagnostic controls and all cost logs](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/18d3a37f/bench/results/2026-10-11-draft-independent-iq/README.md). [Historical validation on its original source](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/18d3a37f/bench/results/2026-10-10-draft-independent-iq/README.md). No deployed server configuration was changed.

pulls.author: Buddychek
pulls.body:
## Title
Opt-in OTLP traces of every /v1 request (0.1.41), plus the docs pages 0.1.41 left uncovered

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
Adds the opt-in OTLP tracing that 0.1.41 shipped in `serve/` as a tested, documented feature, and covers the 0.1.41 behaviors no page documented: one trace per `/v1` request exported as OTLP/HTTP JSON, the switches no page listed, the watchdog/body-cap/batch-groups behaviors, the AMD/Linux card order, and the markdown hygiene around them. Off by default: with no endpoint set, the request path is byte-identical to the release build.

## What changed
**serve/tracing.py (new)** — one OpenTelemetry trace per request, built from the seconds the Monitor already measures (queue, load, prefill, decode) and exported as OTLP/HTTP JSON on its own thread, so a down collector never blocks a request. A client `traceparent` becomes the root span's parent; every answer carries its own `traceparent`. With tracing on and the monitor off, timings and token counts only — no prompt or answer text reaches a collector. OTLP/HTTP is written as JSON by hand: tracing adds no package to the install. Enable with `--trace-otlp`, `"trace_otlp"` in the run config, or `$STRATA_TRACE_OTLP` ("default" = http://localhost:4318/v1/traces).

**serve/server.py, serve/runconfig.py** — the tracing hooks in the request path (begin/finish, the answer's traceparent header, trace-only records with the monitor off) and the runconfig endpoint validation with the same check the server applies at start.

**serve/test_tracing.py (new, 9 tests)** — collector stand-in, per-request span tree, W3C context both ways, dead-collector survival, endpoint precedence (CLI > config > env), off-by-default. 9/9 pass.

**CMakeLists.txt, sycl/CMakeLists.txt** — pin CMP0169 OLD around the FetchContent of strata_llamacpp (CMake 3.30 deprecates FetchContent_Populate(<name>); CMake 4.4 warns every configure), guarded so CMake < 3.30 still configures.

**docs/** — DETAILS.md: the tracing section and the 0.1.41 switches no page listed, card order on AMD/Linux (KFD topology SIMDs x clock), STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS next to the research hooks, markdown hygiene (spaced table delimiters, fenced code with a language, the tier figure as a markdown image). TROUBLESHOOTING.md: the tracing row, the watchdog/body-cap/batch-groups behaviors, the gcc/glibc row in the table's two-column shape. BATCHING.md, MULTI_GPU.md, SECOND_GPU.md: the batch-groups and card-order rows they were missing.

## Extra Notes
Tested on Python 3.15 (venv), no GPU: serve.test_tracing 9/9; serve.test_server + test_monitor + test_runconfig + test_request_accounting 297/297; all together 306/306 on this branch's base (fb58e0d). Tracing is opt-in and the default path is untouched. Not tested: the CMake pins on a CMake < 3.30 machine (the guard is by reading; the 3.30+ warning path is seen on every configure of this build), and the OTLP collector round-trip against a real Jaeger/Tempo.

pulls.title: Add exact speculative-window token parity and coverage gate
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Adds an opt-in standard-library gate comparing full token IDs and finish reasons across draft floors, serial/pipeline windows, forced rollback and repeated references. It fails on divergence, prompt reuse, incomplete requests, ignored switches or missing required coverage. It changes no engine defaults.

Refreshed to main `61b3fb5d`: all 48 pipeline comparisons and 12 default-dispatch comparisons pass with exact routing controlled by `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`. The separate 24-request matched local/TCP comparison passes on current PR #1748 (`f2673bd2`), which supplies TCP support absent from plain main. Fifteen GPU-free gate tests pass. An explicit `matched-history` mode compares adaptive arms at the same repeat and prompt while rejecting reordered histories; the default still requires stable repeated references.

The eight-request suffix control matches tokens but correctly fails because pipeline suffix coverage is zero. Earlier default rank-7 routing differences reflect an intentional approximation whose expert decisions depend on all rows in a window; they do not establish a rollback defect. The docs now specify tail skipping, CPU arithmetic and placement controls separately.

[Fresh manifests, full outputs, engine logs and limits](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/cd4d0670/bench/results/2026-10-11-spec-window-refresh/README.md). Historical evidence remains separately dated. These finite P4 checks do not certify dynamic adaptation, sampled decoding, arbitrary pipeline depth, other backends or remote overlapped decode.

pulls.title: serve: a queue cap (max_queue) answers 429 + Retry-After instead of queueing without end
pulls.author: streber42
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #1809

## Summary
`"max_queue": N` in `strata-<model>.json` (or `--max-queue N`) lets at most N generation requests wait beyond the running slots. One more gets an immediate **429** with a whole-second `Retry-After` (1-60 s), sent before any byte of the answer, so a streamed request never starts a stream it cannot finish. If it is unset, the queue has no limit, as before; `0` rejects whatever cannot start at once.

The status is 429 and not 503 because litellm and the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs retry a 429 and read it as "busy". litellm cools the deployment down for `Retry-After` and moves to another deployment in the group, or waits and retries when Strata is the only one. A 503 counts as a server failure there.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`
  - **Admission:** `Service.admit()` / `release()` count admitted requests (running and waiting) under `status_lock`. They use a new counter instead of `status["queued"]`, which reads about 0 while `--batch` requests wait on the slots. The counter lives on the Service, so an engine restart (#1012) keeps it.
  - **Where the check runs:** `do_POST` checks right after `begin_request` for `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` only, and releases in its `finally`, so every way out (disconnect, `EngineDied`, a 400) frees the place.
  - **Retry-After:** `Service.retry_after()` is the mean `duration_s` of the last 8 finished requests divided by the slots, rounded up and clamped to 1-60 s, or 10 s before any request has finished. It is a whole number because litellm reads it with `int()`.
  - **429 body:** each dialect gets its own error shape (OpenAI `rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, Anthropic `rate_limit_error`, the Responses error body). `_json` gains an optional `headers` argument for the `Retry-After` header.
  - **Metrics:** `/metrics` gains `totals.rejected`, `live.inflight` and `live.max_queue`, and `/v1/status` `activity` gains `admitted`, `max_queue` and `rejected`. No field was renamed.
  - **Settings:** `--max-queue`; a bad config value stops the start with a message, and the start prints one line when the cap is on.
- `serve/runconfig.py`: `max_queue` is editable from the web page's Model settings (`int>=0`, empty means no limit).
- `serve/test_queue_cap.py`: 25 tests.
  - Unit tests: the capacity, max_queue 0, the release floor, and the Retry-After estimate and clamps.
  - Over HTTP with the fake batch engine: a 429 with an integer `Retry-After` and the right body for all three dialects; a streamed request over the cap gets a JSON 429, not a stream; count_tokens and status are not limited; no limit when unset; the count returns to 0 after a finished, streamed, 400, `EngineDied` and disconnected request.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: a "Limiting the queue" section with measurements and notes for litellm, the `/metrics` field, and the web-editable key.

## Extra Notes
- **Tests:** `python -m unittest serve.test_queue_cap serve.test_runconfig serve.test_parallel` gives 57 OK on this branch, which is current `main` with the commit on top. The full `serve` suite runs 622 tests; its 7 errors are all `No module named 'regex'` in my Python, in `test_detok` and `test_server`, and none come from this change.
- **Measured** on two RTX 3090s (layer split), UD-Q4_K_XL, 0.1.40.1 with this change, one request at a time:
  - With `max_queue` 2: of 5 requests sent at once, 3 were answered in 5.1, 7.7 and 10.1 s, and 2 got the 429 in under 2 ms.
  - Behind litellm with live traffic and `max_queue` 4: the `Retry-After` it sent over 5,379 rejections had a median of 8 s and a maximum of 31 s.
  - Over 10.6 hours it answered 3,885 requests and rejected 3,154 attempts, litellm's retries included.
- **Related:** #1619 / #1673 (a ping while a request waits for the turn) tackles the other side of the same wait. #1673 keeps a waiting client alive, and this PR limits how many can wait. They merge without conflicts, and with both applied, `serve.test_queue_cap`, `serve.test_parallel` and `serve.test_server` (including #1673's `QueuedHeartbeat`) pass; the only errors are the same `regex` ones.
- **Open questions:**
  - Requests from Strata's own web page count toward the cap. The page already shows the server's message ("the queue is full ...; retry after N s").
  - The estimate ignores how long the running requests have already gone. Under load they are often past the mean, so subtracting it would give 1 s and spend a client's retries in seconds.
  - With several slots, prompts are still read one at a time, so the estimate is rough there.

## Title
Config: "forward", POSTs to a path answered by another server (embeddings, reranking)

## Summary
Clients that expect `/v1/embeddings` and `/v1/rerank` beside the chat model, as llama-server or LM Studio provide, can't use them with Strata today (404). `"forward": {"/v1/embeddings": "http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/embeddings"}` passes POSTs to those paths to another server and its answer back as it came, so those clients keep one base URL. Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`serve/server.py`:**
  - `forward_of()`: paths start with `/` and can't be Strata's own (`OWN_API_PATHS`, `/v1/responses*`); URLs are http(s); anything else is a config error at start.
  - The handler's `_forward()` runs after Strata's Host, API-key and web-page checks, and does not send Strata's API key on.
  - A server that doesn't answer gives `502` with `code: forward_failed`. The start log names each forward.
- **Docs:** `docs/DETAILS.md`.

## Extra Notes
- **Checked on Windows:** `llama-server --embedding` with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 127.0.0.1:8081, reached through Strata from the host and from a Docker container. A client's search by meaning found the right document for 8 of 8 test questions.
- **Default path:** without the key nothing is forwarded, and unknown paths still give 404 (tested).

pulls.title: config: user_args - engine options of the user's own that setup keeps
pulls.author: gt50
pulls.body:
## Title
Config: "user_args", engine options of the user's own that setup keeps

## Summary
Setup writes `"args"` on every run, so engine options added there by hand are dropped and named (#629). `"user_args"` is a list of the user's own options, e.g. `["--no-prefill-borrow", "--kv-resident", "0"]`. The server applies it over `"args"` when it starts the engine: an option in both takes the `user_args` value, any other is added. Setup never writes the key, so `carry_over` already keeps it. Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`serve/server.py`:**
  - `user_args_of()`: a list of strings starting with an option, else a config error at start;

## Title
Issue: relates to #606 and #728

## Summary
Two things about replies Strata ends because they repeat:
- **Opt-in:** a guard for a short phrase repeated back to back.
- **Always:** the stop is named.

Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`serve/server.py`, `"repeat_stop_period": N`** (opt-in; default 1 = only #606's one-token rule):
  - a run of `repeat_stop_tokens` tokens that repeats with a period of 2..N tokens ends the reply like #606;
  - O(N) per token;
  - seen on a scanned page: `[unclear] ` written until `max_tokens` ran out (12,000 tokens, 229 s), which the one-token rule never sees;
  - 16 is a good value.
- **`choices[0].stop_cause`:** a reply ended by either guard (or by #728's `reasoning_loop_recovery: "stop"`) keeps `finish_reason: "length"` and adds Strata's own `"stop_cause": "repetition"` / `"reasoning_loop"`. On the OpenAI chat API, streamed and not.
- **`serve/structured.py`:** a structured answer ended that way fails with a message that says the reply repeated itself, instead of "increase the output budget", which a larger `max_tokens` cannot fix. Responses API too.
  - Seen with a one-field `json_schema` on a scanned rent roll: the model wrote the escaped newline 256 times, #606 stopped it, and the client was told to raise the budget.
- **Docs:** `docs/DETAILS.md`.

## Extra Notes
- **Default path:** with the default `repeat_stop_period` 1, the guard code is skipped. Replies that end normally, or at `max_tokens`, are unchanged. `stop_cause` and the new message appear only when #606 or #728 already end a reply, which are replies that were already cut short.
- **Tests:**

pulls.title: bench: RX 9060 XT IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS community results
pulls.author: isoux35
pulls.body:
## Summary
Community measurements on a Windows desktop with an RX 9060 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D and 64 GB RAM, using the packaged Strata 0.1.40.3 HIP engine and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS / IQ3_XXS.

- IQ2_XS prefill sweep: 2,048 / 4,096 / 8,192 / 16,384, with three measured runs per prompt size and configuration.
- Matched 32K-context coding comparison: three synthetic fixtures, three runs each per model; both completed 9/9 tasks and 243/243 acceptance checks.
- One 113,501-token recall request with a 122,880-token context limit, plus conversation-prefix reuse and tool-call smoke checks.

## Tested models and settings

Models: **ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS**, using existing prepared packs and a Q2_0 MTP runtime pack. Engine: **Strata 0.1.40.3, native Windows HIP**, not Vulkan or WSL inference. OpenCode 1.18.34 / OpenChamber 1.24.2 were the clients.

Common settings (portable arguments; model paths omitted):

```text
STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1
--expert-cache auto --prefill 8192
--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5
--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 2048
```

**Context:** 32,768 for both models in the matched coding comparison; 122,880 for the IQ2_XS prefill sweep and near-limit recall. The sweep varied prefill only. One parallel request; vision and speed projection off. Sampling: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0, seed 42, repeat penalty 1.0, presence/frequency penalties 0. Coding used medium reasoning with an 8,192-token output allowance; recall used low reasoning with a 1,024-token cap.

## Measured results

### Matched 32K coding: IQ2_XS versus IQ3_XXS

Three synthetic TypeScript fixtures, three runs each per model:

| Measurement | IQ2_XS | IQ3_XXS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tasks passed | 9/9 | 9/9 |
| Acceptance checks across repetitions | 243/243 | 243/243 |
| Median task time, seconds | 99.988 | 136.321 |
| Task time range, seconds | 55.463–145.326 | 81.012–166.632 |
| Weighted engine decode, tok/s | **49.61** | **42.52** |
| Minimum available host RAM, GiB | 8.92 | 3.11 |
| Peak dedicated adapter counter, GiB | 14.88 | 15.04 |
| Peak shared adapter counter, GiB | 34.16 | 41.12 |

IQ2_XS had about **27% lower median task time** and **17% higher weighted decode throughput** on these tasks. Both passed the limited checks; this does not establish equal general answer quality. The 243 checks are 81 across the three fixtures repeated three times. Weighted decode includes reasoning and can include client helper requests. Shared GPU memory is system RAM, not extra VRAM; adapter peaks must not be added together. IQ2 ran first, then IQ3; order was not randomized.

### IQ2_XS prefill tuning at 122,880 configured context

Median results over three fresh-prompt requests per size and setting (no prefix reuse; loading excluded):

| Prefill | 8,019-token input: prompt / decode tok/s | 8K wall seconds | 28,180-token input: prompt / decode tok/s | 28K wall seconds |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 346.3 / 53.2 | 25.400 | 347.0 / 57.9 | 83.355 |
| 4,096 | 593.3 / 52.7 | 15.703 | 593.1 / 57.0 | 49.558 |
| **8,192** | **879.4 / 56.3** | **11.212** | **807.4 / 57.6** | **37.008** |
| 16,384 | 876.3 / 55.3 | 11.384 | 811.2 / 57.8 | 36.778 |

Prefill 8,192 reduced median wall time by about **56%** versus 2,048 at both lengths; 16,384 gave no meaningful further benefit. Recall content passed 24/24, but strict plain JSON passed 0/24 because responses used Markdown fences. Outputs were only 111–120 tokens, and adaptive expert/OS caches remained within each arm.

### IQ2_XS large-context recall

**One run**, context 122,880, prefill 8,192; **113,501 input / 119 output / 0 reused tokens**:

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Engine prompt processing | **789.9 tok/s** |
| Engine decode | **46.9 tok/s** |
| First streamed token (includes reasoning) | 144.157 s |
| Total wall time | 146.629 s |
| Minimum available host RAM | 9.49 GiB |

All three start/middle/end markers were recovered, with the same Markdown-fenced JSON issue. This is a single simple recall test, **not validated 120K coding or an 8K answer at the limit**.

**Configuration retained on this desktop:** IQ2_XS, prefill 8,192, context 122,880, with normal client compaction retained; IQ3_XXS remains a fallback. This is not a comparison against the previous dense Qwen 27B llama.cpp setup.

Full ranges, per-run data, cache/tool checks and reproduction details: [benchmark report](https://github.com/isoux35/Strata/blob/33b9505360b3921d712e448660df0fd86cf05b7c/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/README.md) and [methods](https://github.com/isoux35/Strata/blob/33b9505360b3921d712e448660df0fd86cf05b7c/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/METHODS.md).

## What changed
Adds only `bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/`: a short report, detailed methods, per-run JSON, synthetic fixtures and generated solutions, and reproduction scripts. No engine, backend, installer or default-setting changes.

## Extra notes
All 18 exported solutions were independently rechecked (486 passing acceptance checks, zero failures), and all 42 solution-file hashes verified. The 70 committed files match the reviewed export byte for byte. Credentials, private configurations, personal paths, conversation logs, model binaries and executable hashes are excluded.

Limitations are explicit: one machine, fixed arm order, adaptive expert caches, short decode outputs in the prefill sweep, fenced JSON failures, and a single large-context recall test rather than complex long-context coding. Memory readings are whole-host/whole-adapter observations; the short stability window is not an overnight guarantee.

pulls.title: fix(setup): discard damaged llama.cpp source archives
pulls.author: hulkbig
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Fixes #1797

## Summary
A damaged cached llama.cpp source ZIP can keep its `.done` mark after `get_llama_cpp()` raises `BadZipFile`. Every later setup run then reuses the same bad archive. Remove that archive and its mark so the next run can download it again.

Kept as a draft: CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds have not been run, so the backend-build requirement in AGENTS.md has not been met. The applicability of that requirement to this installer-only change still needs clarification before requesting review.

## What changed
- Catch `zipfile.BadZipFile` only around opening and extracting the llama.cpp source archive, and reuse `drop_archive()` for that exact ZIP and its `.done` mark.
- Re-raise the original exception. If cleanup raises `OSError`, warn about manual cleanup without replacing the original archive error.
- Add isolated local-file regressions for invalid/truncated archives, extraction-time CRC failure and recovery, cleanup edge cases, successful reuse, and non-corruption errors that must retain their cache.

The download strategy, retries, source pin, archive member filtering, successful extraction path, and engine/backend code are unchanged. This does not add checksums or change archive-security policy.

Related: #1126 changes the same function to use `safe_extract()`, but its current implementation does not remove this damaged source cache. These changes address different behavior; any future integration must preserve that safe-extraction work. #424 covers the analogous engine-archive path.

## Extra Notes
Local validation on Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.18.44), Python 3.12.14, at `cdb17c717260bdb9122099bac055df82ef197f0e`:
- Real production `get_llama_cpp()` / `download(file://...)` reproduction: two calls on unchanged base `fb58e0d` keep reusing the bad ZIP and mark. With the fix, the first call removes them and the second installs a valid local archive. Network calls are prohibited in these regressions.
- `python tools/test_setup_llama_archive.py -v`: 10 tests passed. The same final suite fails on the unchanged base.
- Independent review: 9 additional boundary checks passed.
- `python tools/test_setup_golden.py -v`: 4 passed, including saved-configuration byte consistency.
- 33 selected adjacent archive checks passed through an offline runner with socket calls blocked: `tools.test_setup_pins.Engine`; `tools.test_setup_engine_hash` classes `ArchiveVerification`, `DigestLookup`, `WhereTheHashComesFrom`, `Wiring`; and `WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller.test_the_cuda_and_amd_paths_both_verify`.
- `python tools/test_setup_choices.py -v`: 39 passed, 1 environment error (`RotationalDisk.test_sysfs`: missing `/sys/block`), identical on base and patch.
- `python -m py_compile setup.py tools/test_setup_llama_archive.py`, `git diff --check`, and exact-base patch replay checks passed.

Validation limits: no CUDA/HIP/SYCL build, Windows run, GPU/model execution, or real remote llama.cpp download. Three existing adjacent checks with unmocked HEAD requests were excluded from the final offline selection. An earlier broad engine-hash run made release-asset HEAD requests, received HTTP 404, and was interrupted; the full suite is not reported as passing. No online CI success is assumed.

pulls.title: sycl: --expert-parallel-device N, two Arc cards compute each layer's experts together
pulls.author: recutita
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
An opt-in way for the SYCL port to use two Arc cards for each layer's experts: `--expert-parallel-device N`. Card 0 runs every layer, card N holds the experts card 0 does not, and for each layer of a decode window both cards compute their own experts at the same time. Without the option nothing changes.

Needs #1589 (the Verifier's null-stream sentinel, issue #1555), now in main: without it card N's verifier takes card 0's queue and its first capture fails.

### Measured
2x Arc Pro B70 (32 GB each, xe, Linux), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 60 GB RAM, through the server (`sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, 131,072 context, INT8 KV with `--kv-resident 32768`, `--vram-reserve-mib 2048`, the default drafting), greedy, thinking off, the same request 3 times (the 2nd and 3rd; the 1st reads the prompt):

| | `--layer-split auto` | `--expert-parallel-device 1` |
|---|---|---|
| where the experts live | layers 0-28 on card 0, 29-47 on card 1, every expert in VRAM | card 0: 283 per layer, card 1: the other 229, every expert in VRAM |
| decode, a BST class (600 tokens) | 94.3 tok/s | 107.9 tok/s (+14.4%) |
| decode, a 300-word explanation (384 tokens) | 64.2 tok/s | 72.6 tok/s (+13.1%) |
| output | | byte-identical to the layer split, all 6 requests of each |


### Why not 2x
Only the experts run on both cards. Stage times of a 4-token window (`STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1`): the experts take 11.8 ms with the layer split and 8.2 ms with expert parallelism, the rest 41.0 and 40.7 ms. These run without the graph (the port's in-graph timestamps read 0), every kernel launched and timed from the host, so they are larger than with the graph and their ratio (52.8 / 48.9 = 1.08x) is not the decode's gain; they show which part got shorter. A unitrace of 96 decoded tokens shows what the handshake still costs card 0 per layer: its wait for card N's rows 26 us (card N's inbox copy, plan and row send are on its path), the send 3.5 us. In the same trace each card's expert kernels take 160-170 ms of the trace's 1.1 s.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: the option and its checks (a second card, `--stream-experts`; not with `--layer-split`, `--peer-device` or `--pipeline-windows`). Each card's set of experts is fixed at the start: each layer's experts are dealt to the two cards hottest first, in pairs alternating 0,1 / 1,0, until card 0's per-layer quota is full, so both cards serve about the same share of each layer's routing. Card N gets an `ExpertCache` of its own, filled from the GGUF. Per-layer slots, no prompt loans and no adaptive swaps, since either would leave an expert on neither card mid-request.
- `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`, `sycl/include/strata/core/verify.hpp`: `Verifier::set_ep`. Card N's half of each window is a graph of its own, recorded beside card 0's and launched just before it; the same for the `--batch` graphs. Per layer, card 0 pushes the routed ids and the q8_1 MoE input into card N's inbox; card N plans and computes its entries and writes their rows straight into card 0's `parts_`; card 0 waits for that before its combine, which is the single-card one. After each window, `ep_check` reports a wait that ran to its bound or an expert on neither card.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/ep_kernels.dp.cpp`, `sycl/include/strata/kernels/ep_kernels.hpp` (new): the handshake kernels. The flags hold an epoch each card's graph advances on the device (a host value would freeze at capture), and every spin is bounded. Two orderings mattered, each found by a greedy answer that changed between identical requests: data the other card wrote is read past the caches (an inbound PCIe write does not invalidate the reader's caches), and card N writes its rows and raises its flag in one kernel (`ep_send_rows`); with the flag in a later kernel, 2 of 6 requests read a row that was not all there yet.
- `sycl/include/strata/core/ep_mem.hpp` (new): the regions one card writes and the other reads. dpct gives each device its own `sycl::context`, so each region is a Level Zero allocation of its own on its owner, opened on the other card through an IPC handle in the same process.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.dp.cpp`: `resident_plan_ep`, the device plan for one card of the pair. It reuses `resident_plan_kernel` with two new parameters; with them, entries the other card owns are left out of the groups instead of being a plan error. Their defaults keep the old behaviour, and the existing calls do not pass them, so `resident_plan` is unchanged.
- `sycl/src/kernels/resident_plan_ep_parity.cpp` (new, in the parity tests): both cards' plans against a host replay.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: the new kernel file and the parity test.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section with the table above, how it works, what it needs, the server config and the checks.

## How it was checked
- `resident_plan_ep_parity`: 420 cases, 0 failures; `resident_plan_parity`: 641 cases, 0 failures (GPU, synthetic, no model). It checks that the two plans together cover every entry once, an expert on neither card sets the plan error, and with every expert on card 0 the plan is `resident_plan`'s word for word.
- `STRATA_EP_VERIFY=1` (with `STRATA_EP_MIRROR=1`) has card 0 compute every row itself and compare card N's rows with them word for word: no row differed in the 448 windows the three runs reported. `STRATA_EP_SELF=1` runs the window on card 0's own rows only; its output is byte-identical to the expert-parallel one.
- Output with the option: byte-identical to `--layer-split` for both prompts, all 6 requests of each (table above).
- `--batch 4` with the option (server, 128K context, this branch's build): 4 requests at once (512 tokens each) gave the same output as one request alone.
- Without the option: the same tokens as main's binary, one card with the RAM mirror, `--tokens` with a 40-token prompt, greedy, 32K context: T=1 (`--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`, 256 tokens) and MTP (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp`, 512 tokens), identical output hashes.
- SYCL build (AOT `bmg-g31`): all targets including the parity tests, and `strata` again after the last change (a comment and the docs).

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched; CUDA and HIP are unchanged.
- The prompt path reads card N's experts from the GGUF on card 0 (a 1,996-token prompt: 719 tok/s against 768 on one card with the RAM mirror). `STRATA_EP_MIRROR=1` also mirrors them in pinned RAM (18 GB for IQ3_XXS).
- A run without `--mtp` ends with an error at exit after its output, as on main; #1642 fixes that and is separate.
- Tested only on 2x B70 under xe on Linux; not on Arc A-series cards (i915), on Windows, or with cards of two different kinds.

pulls.author: Mitsuasa513
pulls.body:
One Radeon Pro VII 16 GB (Vega 20, gfx906 - the MI50's ISA) on a Xeon E5-2666 v3, built on the host with the distribution's own ROCm 6.2 instead of the community rocm-gfx906 Docker image, and measured at the 131,072-token context with KV streaming.

**What is new.** The two gfx906 reports in the tree are 2x MI50 16 GB and 1x MI50 32 GB. This is a single 16 GB card - the cheap end of this family - and it also carries the power/temperature readings and the per-request cache behaviour the earlier two do not. (#1596's "16 GB-limit" case limits a 32 GB card in software, which is a different measurement.)

**Results.** On 0.1.40.4: decode 24.2 / 24.0 / 23.7 tok/s, prompt 350 / 339 / 284 tok/s at 4,096 / 32,768 / 128,000 prompt tokens; 9 of 9 speed requests read their whole prompt; needles 6/6 at 32k and 128k. Against the 32 GB MI50 that is about a third less decode at the same prompt speed, and the engine log says why: this card's expert cache holds 7,245 of the model's 12,288 experts (19,304 on the 32 GB card), with a steady-state decode hit rate of 87.7-89.6 % against 97-99.5 %.

**Issue #1691 did not reproduce.** Two 0.1.41 sweeps (9 requests each) and its needle run showed no `verify: timed out at layer N`, no decode collapse and no engine exit; `grep -ci 'timed out'` over the whole 0.1.41 engine log is 0. The conditions differ from that report (ROCm 6.2 against 10.x, IQ2_XS against UD-IQ4_XS, int8 KV against q4_0, 131,072 against 262,144), so this narrows the bug rather than closing it. The README lists what it does not rule out.

**ROCm 6.2 needs four host patches**: the gfx906 branch's CUDA-compat include path, the 24 CUDA->HIP name mappings that 0.1.40.x's split headers lost, a `cudaInitDevice` shim, and `HIPBLAS_V2` plus a `cublasSetWorkspace` no-op. They are in `patches/` with the reasoning in `BUILD.json`. Happy to split them into their own PR if that is easier to review - the report can land on its own.

Two notes. The engine and build logs are committed past `.gitignore` (`*.log`); `TRIMMED.md` describes the folder's trimming, and I will drop the two build logs if you would rather keep a bench folder under a megabyte. And the board is a third-party (HUAQIANGBEI-refurbished) 16 GB Vega 20 sold under the Radeon Pro VII name - the VBIOS is where `rocminfo` gets that name, the ISA is gfx906 either way - so I have kept the raw `lspci`/`rocminfo` output in the folder rather than paraphrase it.

pulls.title: setup: find_vcvars() without CUDA asks vswhere for no version range (#881)
pulls.author: Hugua700
pulls.body:
#881's CPU image encoder cannot be built on a machine whose only C++ tools are Visual Studio 2026, because `find_vcvars()` returns `None` there.

`[16.0,18.0)` is CUDA 13's requirement (#985), and it was applied to every caller. #985 then added `cuda_v` to relax it for CUDA 13.3+ — correct for CUDA callers, but a **non-CUDA** caller still passes no `cuda_v`, so the range still applies and VS 2026 stays invisible. `build_vision_cpu()` calls `find_vcvars()` with no arguments, so on that machine it cannot build the encoder at all.

This is also a prerequisite for #1789's `--vision cpu` on Windows: that accepts a hand-built encoder, but building it still goes through `find_vcvars()`.

**The change** (one function, one file):

- `cuda_v is None` → ask vswhere for no version range. The CPU encoder is built by MSVC, which is happy with any version, and `tools/hip/build_windows.bat` already calls vswhere that way.
- CUDA callers unchanged: `cuda_v=(13, 0)` still refuses VS 18, `cuda_v=(13, 3)` still takes it.
- `STRATA_VCVARS=<vcvars64.bat>` picks an install by hand, for a vswhere that cannot be used (e.g. a range-matched install that is broken).

**Measured** on the machine of #881 (RX 6800M / gfx1031, Windows 11, Chinese locale, the only C++ tools are Visual Studio 2026 Build Tools 18.4.11605):

```
find_vcvars()               -> <VS 18>\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat
find_vcvars(cuda_v=(13, 0)) -> None
find_vcvars(cuda_v=(13, 3)) -> <VS 18>\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat
```

**Not included here**, deliberately:

- the Windows plumbing itself (`hip_vision()`'s gate, placing the encoder beside the engine) — #1789 covers that, and covers it better;
- shipping the encoder inside the ready-made zip, which would remove the toolchain requirement entirely. That is a release-policy decision: `package_windows.py` would carry a `strata-vision.exe` built with `-DSTRATA_PORTABLE=ON` (AVX2 baseline + static CRT, so it runs on other machines), the zip goes 120 → 122 MiB, `BUILD.json` records `"vision": "cpu"`, and a build without an encoder packages exactly as before. Happy to file it if wanted.

pulls.title: sycl mtp: slot drafters copy the shared draft head's type (#1121 on the SYCL port, as #1110 did for CUDA)
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1121 for the SYCL port (the CUDA source was fixed in #1110)

## Summary
`--batch-mtp` still ends the Intel (SYCL) engine on the first batch admission with `strata batch: MTP admission for slot 0 failed: mtp: unsupported native MMVQ GGML type`. The cause is the one #1110 fixed in `src/core/mtp.cpp`: a slot drafter that shares the main drafter's draft-vocab head copies `dhead_`, `dvocab_` and `n_dvocab_` but not `dhead_type_`, which stays `-1`. `sycl/src/core/mtp.cpp` never got that line. This adds it. Nothing else changes; without `--batch-mtp` no drafter shares a head, so that path is untouched.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/core/mtp.cpp`, `MtpDrafter::bind`: `dhead_type_ = shared->dhead_type_;` next to the other three copies (same line and comment as the CUDA source).

## How it was checked
Arc Pro B65 32 GB (xe, PCIe Gen4 x16), engine 0.1.41 built with `sycl/tools/build.sh` (AOT `bmg-g31`), Swift 1.5 IQ3_S GSQ-RCO (all 512 experts; ~12.5k in VRAM, the rest in the pinned host mirror), `--mtp rt --spec 4`, `rt/draft_vocab.bin` present, `"parallel"` 2 and 4. Server with #1721's `_pump` fix (needed for any `"parallel"` on SYCL).

| | result |
|---|---|
| without this line, `--batch-mtp`, parallel 2 | engine exits at the first admission (the error above), both clients get nothing |
| without this line + `STRATA_MTP_FULL_HEAD=1` (the workaround in #1121) | works; single-slot decode 34.4 tok/s vs 38.4 without the variable (the full head costs ~10%) |
| **with this line**, `--batch-mtp`, parallel 2, no env | works: 199 batch windows, avg 2.60 rows, both replies coherent |
| **with this line**, parallel 4 | works: 175 windows, avg 6.83 rows |

Throughput on this card is a separate story and not this PR's claim (4 concurrent 300-token requests: 29.5 tok/s queued on one slot, 31.9 with 2 slots + `--batch-mtp`, 32.4 with 4; the batch windows wait on mirrored experts over PCIe). The time to first token drops from up to 29 s to under 6 s with 4 slots.

Not tested: CUDA/HIP (untouched), greedy token equality of batched vs solo (on SYCL that already differs without `--batch-mtp`; noted on #1721).

## Extra Notes
Only the SYCL port is touched. Assisted-by: Claude Code.

pulls.title: serve: preserve tool prefixes for tool_choice=none
pulls.author: llj098
pulls.body:
## Summary

Keep tool declarations in the Chat Completions prompt when `tool_choice` is `"none"`, while independently disabling structured tool-call output and the MCP tool-execution loop.

A client can keep its conversation and tools unchanged, append a summarization/compaction instruction, and set `tool_choice: "none"`. Currently `_openai()` replaces `tools` with `None`. Because the model's template puts tool declarations near the beginning, this changes the leading prompt tokens and prevents an otherwise matching conversation checkpoint from being reused. A long context is not necessary to reproduce this input-prefix mismatch.

Related: #1222 addressed Codex/Responses compaction. This PR targets `/v1/chat/completions`; it does not change the Responses compaction mechanism or require client/session metadata.

## What changed

- Retain prompt tool declarations for `tool_choice: "none"`.
- Add keyword-only `parse_tools=True` to `OutputParser` and `Service.run`. Chat Completions sets it to false for `none`, including disabling recovery of calls inside reasoning. Preserve the existing `tool_call_recovery` option for other requests.
- Do not enter `run_with_mcp` under `none`; MCP declarations can remain in the prompt without executing model-requested tools.
- Preserve acceptance of `response_format` with tool declarations when `tool_choice` is `none`; the existing structured-output/MCP restriction remains.
- Add regression coverage for equal absent/auto/none prompt tokens, streamed/non-streamed responses, thinking on/off, split and truncated tool markup, recovery on/off, MCP non-execution, and JSON response format.

If the model writes tool-shaped text under `none`, it is returned as ordinary reasoning/content, **not** `tool_calls` or a `tool_calls` finish reason. This is an output-parsing/execution restriction, not a new grammar or sampling constraint.

Normal `auto`/absent/required/named behavior, Responses and Anthropic routing, the native engine, and KV formats/policies are left alone. The branch is based directly on upstream `fb58e0dbc8399662c0e47c76578c6e878b14f6cf` and contains only this change, in four Python files.

## Validation

### CPU/mock regressions

```sh
python -m unittest \
  serve.test_frontend serve.test_server serve.test_reasoning_tools \
  serve.test_structured serve.test_responses serve.test_mcp
```

**372 tests passed** on the PR worktree. No GPU backend files changed.

### Short-context prefix reproduction

Compared unmodified upstream `fb58e0d` with this patch using the real model tokenizer/chat template, actual isolated HTTP handlers, and `MockEngine` generation. The fixture has two tool definitions and 128 short synthetic records, followed by an assistant reply and a summarization request with `tool_choice: "none"`. The context limit is 4096 tokens.

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary request input tokens | 3196 | 3196 |
| Appended compaction request input tokens | 2948 | 3237 |
| Common prefix with ordinary request | 41 | 3196 |
| Native prefix predicate's matching length | 0 | 3191 |

The ordinary request's token sequence is identical before/after. For the final row, a **synthetic checkpoint token sequence** ending before the first assistant turn (3191 tokens) was supplied to the **unmodified upstream C++ `conversation_prefix`** function.

This checks HTTP rendering and native **token matching only**: no actual KV/GDN snapshot was captured or restored, and no GPU inference or cache-hit/performance benchmark was performed. It removes this specific source of prefix invalidation; it does not guarantee hits when other prompt content or checkpoint boundaries change.

pulls.title: [GUI] saved chats in a sidebar, kept in the browser (#676), opt-in
pulls.author: Scotty-Hudson
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #676

## Problem and result

The web page keeps one chat. A reload, a "New chat", or a tab switch leaves the conversation on the screen and nowhere else, so there is nothing to go back to.

With the switch on (off by default), the left sidebar holds the list of chats: open one, rename it, delete it with Undo, search it, grouped by day. They live in the browser — IndexedDB, database `strata`, store `chats`, one record per chat — because a conversation can be several megabytes and `localStorage` is capped at about 5 MB for the whole page. With the switch off the page is the one from the last release: one chat under `strata.chat`, and IndexedDB is never opened.

## Related discussion

#676 is the request (the tracker sweep closed it as stale on 2026-10-13; a comment with the 0.1.44.1 version line asks for it to be reopened). #361 was closed with the note that this `serve/web/app.js` work is welcome. The +1 there said a minimal version — list, open, rename, delete, storage — would cover them; this is that, plus the day groups and the search box.

## Approach

**`serve/web/app.js`**
- The switch (`strata.history`, off by default) and the chat list: entries of `{id, title, time, messages}`, one IndexedDB record per chat — cheaper than re-serialising the whole list for one message. The open chat is the one on the screen, so `apiMessages()` and the request path are as they were.
- The list is by recency with day groups (Today / Yesterday / Previous 7 days / Previous 30 days / Older), a search over titles and message text, rename (Enter saves, Esc cancels, a click inside the field keeps it open), delete with Undo, and a collapse to a rail.
- A browser that only had `strata.chat` gets it as the first record; a browser that will not take IndexedDB (private mode) keeps the list in memory and says so once.
- Pictures and files are stored as their names only — a data URL would fill the storage. A write the browser refuses warns once, and the message fits the reason (`QuotaExceededError` says the storage is full, an abort for another reason does not).

**`serve/web/index.html`** — the `<aside>` (hidden until the switch is on) and the switch row under About > Settings.
**`serve/web/app.css`** — the sidebar, the rows, and the narrow-screen overlay (under 760px the list overlays the chat).
**`serve/web/sprite.svg`** — one symbol, `i-edit`, for rename.
**`serve/test_chat_sidebar.py`**, **`serve/test_chat_sidebar.js`** — new, described under Validation.

What it leaves alone: every engine file and the request path; `store.set` and the other storage keys (the small ones — the switch, which chat is open — stay in `localStorage`); the export button; the sampling drawer, the Monitor, the API; and "New chat" when the switch is off, which still clears the chat with an Undo. No new network calls, nothing about the list goes to the server.

How I checked the default path. `app.js` run against a stub DOM, the same actions on main's `app.js` and on this branch with the switch off:

```
main (last release)              this branch, switch off
at start:      strata.chat       at start:      strata.chat
after saveChat: strata.chat      after saveChat: strata.chat
after New chat: strata.chat      after New chat: strata.chat
```

Same key, same contents after every step. To be exact about "byte-identical": with the switch off the storage key, the contents and the behaviour are the same as the last release; the page does carry the sidebar markup and the switch row, and the chat sits inside one extra wrapper div, so the HTML is not identical — the sidebar is hidden and nothing in it runs. If you would rather have the markup itself behind the switch, say so and I will generate it from JS.

## Validation

**Passed:**

```
python3 -m unittest serve.test_chat_sidebar          15 tests, OK
node serve/test_chat_sidebar.js                      20 scenarios, all ok
node --check serve/web/app.js                        clean
python3 -m unittest serve.test_frontend serve.test_web_sampling     29 tests, OK
```

On `9094446b`, rebased onto `main` at `f57c0adc`. Linux, Python 3.14.4, node v24.21.0.

`serve/test_chat_sidebar.py` checks the page and the served routes, and runs the js file (it skips on a machine without node). `serve/test_chat_sidebar.js` runs `app.js` against a stub DOM and a stub IndexedDB — twenty outcomes: the read, the write, private mode, a full storage, a store that is not there, a blocked open, a fresh database, a read transaction that aborts, an abort for another reason, a reload, the single chat when off, the search, the day groups, rename through the field, a click inside the rename field, delete with Undo, and delete of a chat the list does not hold.

The stub is faithful only where the code depends on it: the result of a read is on the request and not on the store, a refused write fires `abort`, a blocked open never resolves on its own, the `chats` store exists only because the upgrade handler made it, and requests answer on a later tick, so the code cannot pass by answering too early.

Each check was verified by putting the old code back and running it again: eighteen fail, including the two bugs the review found.

**Failed:** none observed.

**Not run:** real quota limits (no browser here fills a quota on demand); the cross-tab case (a chat written in another tab does not show until that page is reloaded, because there is no event for it); a real browser's IndexedDB — headless Chrome here cannot persist storage across invocations, and the server serves an allowlist of `serve/web` files, so the js file is a model of the page, not a browser.

## Limits

The search reads every chat's message text, so the whole store is in memory after the first load — which is the multi-megabyte case raised in the review. The search box stays in the PR; if you would rather have it over titles only, that would let the app keep titles and timestamps apart from the message bodies.

Pictures and files are stored as their names only, so a picture shows while the page lives and becomes its name after a reload. IndexedDB would allow keeping them as blobs; that needs a second store (so the list can load without the images) and an eviction rule, so it is not in this PR.

pulls.title: serve: scope watchdog diagnostics to the current engine run
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Upstream now searches the last 256 KB of the engine log for a watchdog, fixing the usual long-trace case. This follow-up searches the current engine run in reverse, so an older run's watchdog cannot explain a new exit and a trace longer than 256 KB cannot hide the current cause.

Preserves server-stop and current-error handling. Adds regressions for prior-run attribution, trace length, reverse-read boundaries, missing trailing newlines, and diagnostic precedence. Documents the reported HIP runtime workaround without claiming it fixes hangs or reboots. No native engine or inference default changes remain in the diff.

Validation on current main 61b3fb5d: 8 focused EngineDeath tests passed; the full serving suite ran 696 tests successfully, with 15 skips. git diff --check passed.

Related: #1705 and #872. #1931 adds separate opt-in HIP runtime stability controls. A stability-profile run validates its specific runtime configuration; it is not evidence that this diagnostics PR fixes the underlying failure.

## Summary

Adds a results-only Strata 0.1.41 community benchmark submission for a Windows 10 machine with:

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
- Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4, 14 cores / 28 threads
- 64 GB RAM

The compact submission includes results, summaries, initial server status, Strata BUILD metadata, sanitized measured configs, and a README. Bulky raw request/chunk dumps were intentionally omitted and are documented in `TRIMMED.md`.

pulls.title: web: add persistent chats and MCP management
pulls.author: VykosX
pulls.body:
## Summary

Adds a native-feeling persistence and MCP-management layer to Strata's existing Web UI without changing the inference engine or model-specific defaults.

## What changed

- Persist Web UI conversations as JSON under `conversations/`, with a docked conversation list, switching, New Chat creating a new conversation instead of clearing history, and delete confirmation.
- Add a dedicated **MCP** tab between Monitor and About.
- Manage any number of MCP servers using either transport Strata already supports:
  - Streamable HTTP via `url`.
  - stdio via `command`, JSON `args`, optional `cwd`, and JSON `env`.
- Show per-server connection state, transport, and enumerated tools.
- Add exact context usage through Strata's current template/tokenizer path, displayed as a semi-circular used/total gauge.
- Add dependency-free syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks while preserving the existing Markdown renderer and Strata styling.

### MCP configuration safety

The UI is a frontend for Strata's existing MCP backend rather than a parallel protocol implementation.

- HTTP header values and stdio environment values are never returned to the browser.
- Hidden HTTP headers are preserved only while the URL is unchanged.
- Hidden stdio env values are preserved only while command/args/cwd are unchanged; changing the launch identity drops them instead of silently forwarding credentials to a different process.
- Editing/removing one named server leaves the others untouched.
- stdio is explicitly described as starting a local process with the user's rights.
- Changes are persisted to the current run config and take effect after restarting Strata.

### Conversation persistence

- UUID-backed IDs are validated before becoming paths.
- Writes use a unique temporary file followed by atomic replace.
- Conversation files are capped at 64 MiB.
- `/conversations/` is gitignored.
- The existing browser-local chat remains only as a fallback/migration path.

### Context meter

`/context-count` runs the current OpenAI-shaped Web UI history through Strata's own conversion/template/tokenizer path, including MCP tool schemas when enabled. The displayed count is therefore the actual prompt shape Strata will send, not a character estimate.

## Validation

Clean worktree based on current `origin/main`:

- `serve.test_local_ui`: **9/9 passed**
- `serve.test_server`: **271/271 passed**
- `serve.test_mcp`: **25/25 passed**
- `serve.test_runconfig`: **9/9 passed**
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`: passed
- Python compile checks: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

A live acceptance test also added a stdio server beside an existing HTTP server, verified both were listed together, confirmed secret env values were not returned to the browser, verified the preserve/drop rules across edits, removed only the temporary server, and confirmed the original server remained unchanged.

## Screenshots

![Persistent conversations, syntax highlighting, and context gauge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_CHAT.png)

![Multiple MCP servers using HTTP and stdio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_MCP.png)

pulls.title: serve: effort_position "end" reads the SYCL engine binary, not its launcher script (#1781)
pulls.author: leadgtr7
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1781

## Summary
`"effort_position": "end"` (#458) never turned on with the Intel port: the server checked the launcher script `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` for `--tail-role-token` instead of the engine binary it runs, and fell back to the top-of-prompt effort with "needs engine 0.1.39 or newer". This resolves the launcher to its binary before the check. CUDA and HIP are untouched: their `exe` is the engine and is read as before.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: new `engine_binary(exe, cfg)`. For an `exe` named `strata-sycl.sh` it returns the launcher's repo + `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (from the config's `env`, else the environment, else `build-sycl-aot/strata`, the launcher's own default) when that file exists; otherwise `exe` unchanged. `effort_end_args()` reads that file instead of `exe`. Nothing else uses it.
- `tools/test_effort_end_args.py` (new, no GPU, fake files in a temp repo): launcher + binary with the option -> args; binary without it -> None; `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` from the config's `env`; launcher with no binary -> falls back to reading the launcher (old behaviour); a plain engine `exe` with and without the option (unchanged path); `start`/unset stays off.

## How it was checked
- `python -m unittest tools.test_effort_end_args`: 6 pass on `fb58e0d` + this commit. Without the `server.py` change the two launcher tests fail (2 failures), so they test the fix.
- On an Arc Pro B65 (engine 0.1.41 built with `sycl/tools/build.sh`), `engine_binary(".../sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh", {})` resolves to `.../build-sycl-aot/strata`, which contains `--tail-role-token`.
