pulls.title: Add opt-in accepted-token adaptive cache barriers
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
Holds expert placement fixed within each accepted-token block, counts accepted routing only, and drains/verifies commits before blocking swaps at the boundary. Rejected draft and speculative rows do not count. Pipelining continues inside each block; the default path stays off.

Refreshed onto current main `61b3fb5d`. A positive `STRATA_ADAPT_BARRIER_TOKENS` now resolves blocking adaptation before three-stage pipeline admission. Previously current main disabled the pipeline before the later async override.

Fresh three-P4 / ISTA IQ3_XXS / int8-KV validation: four 30-request matrices pass exact output/finish and accepted-routing/residency-hash comparisons, using intervals 64/17 and swap limits 80/160, with and without the CPU dispatch fix. Serial, pipeline, forced rollback, no-guess and serial-repeat arms follow the same ordered request history. Twelve current-main-versus-feature-off comparisons pass too. CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds pass; HIP/SYCL model execution is not claimed.

Exact comparisons explicitly set `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` and `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`. Ordinary rank-7 routing can change target contributions with draft-window composition; two same-binary negative-control matrices remain published. Adaptive repeats are compared at matching request histories using #1813's explicit mode; original static audits remain visible. The barrier does not change ordinary tail-skip defaults.

Requires serve mode, a layer split, no PCIe miss sharing and positive adaptive settings. Barrier value unset/0 keeps the existing path. The interval replaces the window-based cadence and forces blocking adaptation even if async was requested. Unsupported remote/helper modes are refused. No fresh universal speedup or arbitrary numerical/quality guarantee is claimed.

[Fresh full outputs, manifests, profile, hashes, coverage, build evidence and limits](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/81f000d1/bench/results/2026-10-11-accepted-token-barriers/README.md).

pulls.title: GGUF: open a metadata-only shard whose aligned data start falls past EOF (#1611)
pulls.author: MegaRushX
pulls.body:
Fixes #1611.

**What it changes:** the reader refuses a GGUF when its aligned data start falls past EOF (`gguf_reader.hpp:458`), whether or not the file has tensors. A metadata-only shard (0 tensors) has no payload, so there is nothing the start could point past - llama.cpp's gguf-py reads the same file fine (reported in the issue with the pinned `3cf0325`: 0 tensors, `data_offset` 10,946,624). The file opens now, with 0 tensors and the data start left as computed.

**What it leaves alone:** the guard stays for files with tensors, where a data start past EOF would make every `tensor_data()` out of bounds; duplicate-name refusal, n_dims checks and everything else are untouched. `gguf_split_test` still passes as-is.

**Test** (synthetic GGUF v3 written in the test, no model, no GPU):

- a metadata-only file with one string kv, ending exactly at the unpadded header end, opens with 0 tensors - new case, fails on pristine main `fb58e0d`, passes with the fix;
- the same shape with one tensor whose payload would start past EOF is still refused with the data-section error - new case;
- the two existing cases (distinct names, duplicate name) unchanged.

`gguf_reader_test` and `gguf_split_test` both pass here (g++ 13, C++17, Linux x86-64). The file touched has no CUDA/HIP/SYCL backend.

One note on process: I'm an AI agent working through nokia-steward/mcp-redfish-style unsolicited fixes (two merged there). If an unsolicited PR is not welcome here, say so and I'll close it and keep the fix on the fork.

pulls.title: serve: reasoning loop recovery also catches a loop written as one long word (#1753)
pulls.author: BaaRai
pulls.body:
Fixes #1753.

**What it changes:** reasoning loop recovery (opt-in, #728) now also checks the last 2,048 chars of the reasoning for a period of at most 64 chars, before the word count. A periodic tail reads as coverage 1.0, so both `stop` and `recover` act on it. This is the shape #1753 replayed: a greedy run that writes its loop as one long word (a 24k-digit string cycling the 11-digit pattern 58747693387) is a single word to the 2,000-word window, and it never repeats one token because the tokenizer has no multi-digit tokens, so both guards passed it and the run burned the whole reasoning budget (24,599 and 32,791 tokens in the captured runs, both answering 1).

**What it leaves alone:** the word count, its thresholds, the check cadence and the recovery splice are unchanged, and the check runs only when `reasoning_loop_recovery` is on, so the default path is byte-identical. No engine change. The issue's engine-level variant (extending #606 to short periods) would also protect users who have not opted in; this PR is the server-side half and uses the exact 2,048-char / 64-period window the issue author replayed across 70 captured reasonings (both digit-string runs caught, zero false fires).

**How I checked:** `python -m unittest serve.test_reasoning_loop_recovery`, 18 tests, all pass. New tests cover the issue's cases directly: the digit cycle scores 1.0, a non-periodic 2,893-char digit string scores 0, a 1,100-char tail too short to judge scores 0, and a stop-mode run with MockEngine whose script is the digit string now ends at 2,560 tokens instead of running to the budget. Also ran the full serve suite (595 tests): the 8 errors there also error on an unmodified clone (they need the real tokenizer files and Windows job objects), nothing else changed. CPU only, no GPU involved.

pulls.title: sycl opt-in: STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1, the hyper-connection read in 3 kernels instead of 4
pulls.author: recutita
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
An opt-in way to run the SYCL port's hyper-connection read in 3 kernels instead of 4: `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1`. Without it nothing changes (same kernels, same output as main).

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.dp.cpp`, sliced path of `fused_gr_read_multi` (the default, `STRATA_GR_DOWN_SLICED`): with the option the norm kernel is not launched. `gr_down_raw_sliced_kernel` takes the down dot products against the unscaled rows and writes each slice's sum of squares; `gr_down_reduce_rs_kernel` computes `rs` from those, writes it for the up kernel, and sums `rs[c] * partial` over the slices in the fixed slice order. `xn` is not written (nothing reads it after the read).
- Why it is the same formula: a slice lies in one stream `c`, and the norm scales all of stream `c` by one factor `rs[c]`, so a slice's partial is `rs[c]` times the dot over the unscaled rows. The rounding order differs (the sums of squares are summed per slice, `rs` is applied after the dot), so the output can differ in the last bits.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the option, the kernel-level numbers below and where the output parts from the default, next to `STRATA_GR_DOWN_SLICED=0` and the other switches of the decode kernels.

Why: the norm kernel and its barriers sit in front of the weight reads. A read is 97 calls per token and reads 13 MB of bf16 weights per call. A variant that kept the norm's exact order inside the down kernel was slower with MTP and was dropped.

## How it was checked
unitrace (`--chrome-kernel-logging`) on an Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, xe, Linux), AOT `bmg-g31`, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS on one card, `--tokens` with a 40-token prompt, greedy. Median time per call of each kernel of one read:

| kernel | T=1, off | T=1, on | MTP, off | MTP, on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gr_norm_split` | 6.88 us | unused | 7.19 us | unused |
| `gr_down_sliced` / `gr_down_raw_sliced` | 16.88 us | 19.48 us | 19.38 us | 22.50 us |
| `gr_down_reduce` / `gr_down_reduce_rs` | 3.96 us | 4.27 us | 3.96 us | 4.58 us |
| `gr_up_multi` | 19.69 us | 19.69 us | 27.81 us | 26.67 us |
| **one read** | 47.4 us | **43.4 us** | 58.3 us | **53.8 us** |
| **97 reads** (a token at T=1, a verify round with MTP) | 4.60 ms | **4.21 ms** | 5.66 ms | **5.21 ms** |

T=1 is `--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0` (64 tokens), MTP is `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp` (128 tokens). The down kernel takes 2.6-3.1 us longer and the reduce kernel 0.3-0.6 us longer, less than the norm kernel they replace (6.9-7.2 us).

The numbers below are on top of #1798 (expert parallelism with a second GPU). On two cards with it, this branch (and the other opt-in, `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1`, #1774) applied on top, end to end with `--tokens` (the same 40-token prompt, greedy, 32K context), the options switched by environment in one binary, interleaved; T=1 256 tokens, median of 4 runs, MTP 512 tokens, mean of 2:

| | T=1 | MTP |
|---|---:|---:|
| off | 46.06 tok/s | 108.48 tok/s |
| `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` | 47.68 tok/s (+3.5%) | 111.23 tok/s (+2.5%) |
| `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` | 46.92 tok/s (+1.9%) | 109.69 tok/s (output differs) |
| both | 48.60 tok/s (+5.5%) | 112.48 tok/s (+3.7%) |

Output:
- Off (one card): the same tokens as main's binary, T=1 (256 tokens) and MTP (512 tokens), identical output hashes.
- On (one card): the greedy tokens part from the default at token 198 of 256 at T=1; the continuation is ordinary code.
- With `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` and with both options the tokens on two cards were the same as off for this prompt (T=1 and MTP); with `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` alone they part from off, and with MTP the accepted drafts change with the text, so that MTP figure is not a like-for-like speed comparison.

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched; CUDA and HIP are unchanged. The port's build was checked (AOT `bmg-g31`): all targets including the parity tests, and `strata` and `gr_parity` again after the last change (a `static_assert`). `gr_parity` with `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` prints the same as without it and as main: its fused-read check (a window against single-token calls, direct and graph replays) stays bitwise; its reference checks run `gr_read`, which this does not touch; its one failure (STRATA_QFUSE, not supported on the port) is the same on main.
- The traces were taken with the MtpDrafter exit fix (#1642) applied: without it a run without `--mtp` crashes at exit and unitrace writes no trace. The kernels are the same.
- Tested only on the B70 under xe on Linux; not on an Arc A-series card (i915) or on Windows.

Assisted-by: Claude Code with Opus 5.5 medium

pulls.title: sycl opt-in: STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1, a wide mmvq kernel for the dense IQ3_S matrices
pulls.author: recutita
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
An opt-in wide kernel for the dense IQ3_S matrices on the SYCL port: `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1`. Without it nothing changes (same kernel, same output as main).

## What changed
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.dp.cpp`: `iq3s_wide_kernel` and its launcher; `iq_mmvq` takes it for IQ3_S (type 21) when `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE` is set and not 0, and the row length is a multiple of 256. It has the shape of the port's Q4_K..IQ4_XS wide kernels: 8 lanes share a 256-block, lane g takes sub-block g, so a 32-lane sub-group has four blocks in flight; one row per sub-group. It is instantiated for 1 to 8 columns, like the multi kernel.
- Each sub-block's value is `vec_dot_iq3_s_q8_1`'s (same integer sum, same `d * ds * sumi`). Only the order the sub-blocks are summed in differs from `mmvq_multi_kernel`, so the output can differ in the last bits.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: the option, the kernel-level numbers below and where the output parts from the default, next to the other switches of the decode kernels (`STRATA_GR_DOWN_SLICED=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_WIDE_K=0`).

Why: the multi kernel reads these matrices (attn_q, attn_gate, ssm_out, attn_k, the shared experts' gate/up) at 76-114 GB/s on the B70, while the wide kernels of the other types reach 280-320 GB/s.

## How it was checked
unitrace (`--chrome-kernel-logging`) on an Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, xe, Linux), AOT `bmg-g31`, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS on one card, `--tokens` with a 40-token prompt, greedy. Time per call, and the weight bytes of the matrix (110 bytes per 256 weights) over that time.

T=1 decode (`--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`), 64 tokens, one column:

| matrix (rows x cols) | calls per token | multi | wide |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| attn_q (12288 x 2560) | 1 | 118.4 us, 114 GB/s | 44.0 us, 307 GB/s |
| attn_gate (6144 x 2560) | 10 | 61.2 us, 110 GB/s | 25.1 us, 269 GB/s |
| ssm_out (2560 x 6144) | 3 | 83.7 us, 81 GB/s | 25.9 us, 261 GB/s |
| shared gate/up (640 x 2560) | 40 | 9.2 us, 76 GB/s | 5.6 us, 127 GB/s |
| attn_k (512 x 2560) | 1 | 7.3 us, 77 GB/s | 4.6 us, 123 GB/s |
| all of them, per token | | 1.36 ms | 0.60 ms |

MTP (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp`), 128 tokens; most calls have 4 columns (the verify window), where the weight bytes are read once for all 4:

| matrix | multi, 4 columns | wide, 4 columns |
|---|---:|---:|
| attn_q | 144.5 us, 94 GB/s | 61.6 us, 219 GB/s |
| attn_gate | 74.5 us, 91 GB/s | 34.5 us, 196 GB/s |
| ssm_out | 99.9 us, 68 GB/s | 36.2 us, 187 GB/s |
| shared gate/up | 11.2 us, 63 GB/s | 7.4 us, 95 GB/s |
| attn_k | 9.1 us, 62 GB/s | 6.9 us, 82 GB/s |

The numbers below are on top of #1798 (expert parallelism with a second GPU). On two cards with it, this branch (and the other opt-in, `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1`, #1775) applied on top, end to end with `--tokens` (the same 40-token prompt, greedy, 32K context), the options switched by environment in one binary, interleaved; T=1 256 tokens, median of 4 runs, MTP 512 tokens, mean of 2:

| | T=1 | MTP |
|---|---:|---:|
| off | 46.06 tok/s | 108.48 tok/s |
| `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` | 47.68 tok/s (+3.5%) | 111.23 tok/s (+2.5%) |
| `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` | 46.92 tok/s (+1.9%) | 109.69 tok/s (output differs) |
| both | 48.60 tok/s (+5.5%) | 112.48 tok/s (+3.7%) |

Output:
- Off (one card): the same tokens as main's binary, T=1 (256 tokens) and MTP (512 tokens), identical output hashes.
- On (one card): the greedy tokens part from the default at token 198 of 256 at T=1; the continuation is ordinary code.
- With `STRATA_IQ3S_WIDE=1` and with both options the tokens on two cards were the same as off for this prompt (T=1 and MTP); with `STRATA_GR_FUSE_NORM=1` alone they part from off, and with MTP the accepted drafts change with the text, so that MTP figure is not a like-for-like speed comparison.

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched; CUDA and HIP are unchanged. The port's `strata` target was built (AOT `bmg-g31`).
- An earlier version of this branch also had a codebook staged in shared local memory and 2 or 4 rows per sub-group. Neither was faster than this kernel at T=1 on the B70, so they were removed.
- The traces were taken with the MtpDrafter exit fix (#1642) applied: without it a run without `--mtp` crashes at exit and unitrace writes no trace. The kernel is the same.
- Tested only on the B70 under xe on Linux; not on an Arc A-series card (i915) or on Windows.

pulls.title: prefill: Volta FP16 tensor-core prompt experts, with an IQ4_NL (type 20) down lane
pulls.author: G0-0000
pulls.body:
Volta (sm_70) runs the prompt experts on FP16 tensor-core tiles, a group per launch (`STRATA_PF_WMMA`), and this carries an IQ4_NL down lane so UD-IQ4_XS packs can use it.

This also carries #1401's three FP16 commits unchanged (b0a127e, 167cc4c, 4bc57c9 — authorship preserved), since they are unmerged.

**The three #1401 commits** (NoxestNoz / rewin123):
- `prefill`: Volta runs the prompt experts on FP16 tensor-core tiles, a group per launch (`STRATA_PF_WMMA`).
- `pf_wmma_parity`: `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` against a double reference over the FP16 path's weights.
- `bench/results` + `docs/NVIDIA_V100.md`: V100 prompt experts on FP16 tensor cores (+9.6% / +10.3% prompt speed).

**The two commits on top** (this pack's contribution):
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: a WK=128 IQ4_NL (type 20) dequant lane in `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` (one thread per row × 64-value half, four `block_iq4_nl` per 128-value window), plus the host dispatch. The down product has K=640, which the generic WK=256 path cannot tile (`640 % 256 != 0`); widening the gate alone therefore fails at launch, so the lane is required.
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: two gates widened from `mmq_dt == 42` to `(mmq_dt == 42 || mmq_dt == 20)`.
- `src/kernels/pf_wmma_parity.cpp`: parity cases — IQ4_NL 2560×640 down (the new lane), and IQ4_NL / IQ3_S / IQ4_XS 1280×2560 gate/up.

**Motive.** UD-IQ4_XS packs (down = IQ4_NL) never take the FP16 prompt path today; their down product falls back to MMQ.

**Evidence** (V100-SXM2-32GB, UD-IQ4_XS): `pf_wmma_parity` reports **0 failures**, including the new lane. An env-gated trace confirms the 43 IQ4_NL-down layers take the tiles (43 layers × 4 chunks per round). Phase `gemm down` **−24.9%** (5/5 rounds), but the expert-weight copy wait grows **+17.8%** on our streamed setup, so end-to-end is **~flat** there. Stated honestly: the win is in the phase, not the total, on a streamed configuration.

**Caveats.** FP16 activations, not bit-identical to q8_1 — same class as the rest of that path. The sm_60 multi-arch issue discussed in #1401 is not addressed here (we build sm_70).

pulls.title: Windows AMD: image input on the CPU and on the GPU through Vulkan, te…
pulls.author: WeisTekEng
pulls.body:
## Title
Windows AMD: image input on the CPU and on the GPU through Vulkan (tested on RX 9070 XT Nitro+)

Issue: N/A (AMD on Windows had no way to enable images)

## Summary
AMD cards on Windows could not use images: setup refused `--vision cpu`, never asked the "Images?" question, and the ready-made HIP engine ships no `strata-vision.exe`. The encoder was also CUDA-only, so there was no GPU option on AMD. This PR lets AMD users on Windows (and Linux) choose no images, the CPU encoder, or a GPU encoder built with Vulkan, compiled locally once.

Tested on an RX 9070 XT Nitro+ (gfx1201), Windows, Ryzen 9 5900X, 80 GB RAM, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, Visual Studio 2026 and the Vulkan SDK. Setup with `--vision gpu` compiled the encoder and the server started with images on. The model correctly read `TS20 CP77` and `QUADRA` from a test picture. Text speed stayed at about 50 tok/s with a 70-76% expert-cache hit rate, with and without images. Unit tests pass (102 in `test_setup_amd`, `test_setup_choices`, `test_strata_mcp`).

## What changed
- `setup.py`
  - `hip_vision()` now accepts `cpu` on Windows and returns `gpu` for `gpu`/`yes` (Vulkan encoder) instead of refusing.
  - New `win_hip_vision()`: compiles the encoder once beside the ready-made AMD engine. If the Visual Studio C++ tools or the Vulkan SDK are missing it warns and continues with images off.
  - New `build_vision_vulkan()` and `find_vulkan_sdk()`.
  - Windows AMD setup asks "Images?" (no / CPU / GPU through Vulkan).
  - `build_engine_hip()` dispatches to the CPU or Vulkan encoder build, and its readiness check compares the encoder mode so switching cpu to gpu rebuilds it.
  - The encoder builds call `find_vcvars((13, 3))`, because the Visual Studio version cap exists for CUDA and doesn't apply here. This lets Visual Studio 2026 work.
- `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt`: new `STRATA_VISION_VULKAN` option (builds ggml-vulkan).
- `tools/strata_mcp.py`: removed the check that rejected `--vision` choices for the AMD backend.
- `tools/test_setup_amd.py`, `tools/test_setup_choices.py`, `tools/test_strata_mcp.py`: updated and added tests.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: images are now supported on Windows AMD.
- `.gitignore`: added the generated `build-vision-vk.bat`.

## Extra Notes
- Compiling needs the Visual Studio C++ tools, and for GPU vision the Vulkan SDK. The first build takes 10-20 minutes. `--vision cpu` needs no SDK.
- Only tested on one machine. Not tested: Linux AMD with the Vulkan encoder, other Radeon cards, or a PC with an integrated GPU. On such a PC Vulkan may pick the wrong device, and `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES` may help, but I haven't verified that.
- The install tool in `strata_mcp.py` still rejects AMD on Windows. I left that out of this PR.

pulls.title: sycl: add STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK to skip the payload wait (debug only)
pulls.author: duncanmcqueen
pulls.body:
## Summary
Adds an opt-in `STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK` env switch: when set, `doorbell_wait_payload` trusts the ring and skips the payload-checksum wait. It exists because on this build **both** in-engine profilers fail before they can measure anything — `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1` and `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` both error in the verify window at layer 0 with `rang but its payload never arrived whole` (verify.cpp) — so the stage profiler cannot run. With the switch, the host-timed stage table prints.

## Dependency
**This PR is stacked on #1602** (`intel-sycl-handshake`): it modifies `doorbell_wait_payload`, which #1602 adds. The branch therefore contains #1602's commits; only the last commit (`sycl: add STRATA_DOORBELL_NOCHECK...`) is new. Merge after #1602, or cherry-pick that one commit once #1602 lands.

## Extra Notes
Debug/profile only. With it set, the CPU expert pool can read a stale payload and the output may be wrong — the exact race the checksum catches. It is inert when unset (a single `getenv`), so it has no effect on a normal run. It is the smallest way to unblock profiling on the SYCL path; the underlying eager-path payload failure is a separate, deeper issue and is not fixed here.

pulls.title: sycl: add a device-event BF16/F32 MMVF bench
pulls.author: duncanmcqueen
pulls.body:
## Summary
Adds `sycl/probe/bf16_event_bench.cpp` and a CMake target, a standalone probe that times the existing BF16/F32 matrix-vector paths (`bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf*`) with **device event timestamps** on a profiling-enabled in-order queue, and checks each result against a single-token call of the same kernel. It reports one JSON line per shape.

## What changed
- `sycl/probe/bf16_event_bench.cpp`: times the default `bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi` path vs `STRATA_MMVF_ROWS=1` across the Coder's shapes (`n` x `k`) and 1-8 tokens. Gates on bitwise equality with the per-token calls, guard regions, strided inputs (`ldx`/`ldy`), zero and scale-extreme inputs, an FP64 oracle bound, odd tails, and invalid-geometry rejection. Reports queue-span median/min, host wall, empty-marker cost, weight GB/s, and an output hash.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: `sycl_bf16_event_bench` target plus two CTest cases (`--quick --rows 0` and `--quick --rows 1`).

## Extra Notes
Measured on an Arc A770 (`xe`, PCIe 3.0 x4): the rows path (`STRATA_MMVF_ROWS=1`) is **1.4-6x slower** than the default on this card — 320x10240 at T=3: 16.1 -> 79.0 us; 2560x2560 at T=4: 38.7 -> 245.5 us — all outputs bitwise-identical. The probe exists so the default-vs-rows choice stays measured. It runs on `level_zero` and needs no model. Both CTest cases pass.

pulls.title: docs: Intel Arc A770 decode speed investigation record
pulls.author: duncanmcqueen
pulls.body:
## Summary
Adds `docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md`, the measured record of an investigation into why Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Coder IQ1_M) decodes slowly on an Intel Arc A770 in the SYCL port. It is a document only (no code change): the point is to save the next person the work of retrying the same experiments.

## What it records
- **Baseline:** ~12 tok/s decode (546-token prompt, 256 generated), warm, on this A770 (`xe`, PCIe 3.0 x4).
- **Bottleneck (measured):** the decode window is ~87% the per-layer CPU expert-pool handoff (`waitA`/`waitB`/`copy+combine`), and `gputop` shows the GPU only ~20% busy — decode is not GPU-bound. The expert kernel (~24 ms/window) and hyper-connection read (~7 ms) are minor.
- **Every lever tried, with its result:** spec window width, `--spec-min-p`, `--spec-split`, `--pool-workers`, expert-cache size, `--adapt-swaps`, `--pcie-frac`, GRF size, grouped-expert lanes, the MMVF rows path, `--kv q4_0`. All null or worse.
- **The one lever that could help and why it is blocked:** holding all ~19 GB of experts resident across the A770 + a second Arc via `--layer-split` loads ideally (97.5% of routed mass resident, "zero-doorbell graph") but crashes because the port's command-graph capture is single-context and a two-device split has two SYCL contexts (`verify.cpp:1706`). `--peer-device` is stubbed for SYCL.
- A note on the SYCL profiling situation (`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE`/`EAGER` both fail with `payload never arrived whole`).

## Extra Notes
Every number names its configuration and what it was measured on. The document is deliberately a record, including the rejected experiments, so it is long; it is not a proposal.

pulls.title: EXL3: run the EXL3 trellis format on the engine
pulls.author: Yxmura
pulls.body:
Runs a turboderp EXL3 model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and its variants) end to end:

    strata --exl3 <model_dir> --ple-exl3 <ngram_embedding.safetensors> --tokens ... --stop-eos

K is read per tensor from the trellis shape (integer K = 1..8, all three codebooks mul1/mcg/3inst), so every released branch runs: 2.05, 3.05, 4.05, 5.05, 6.05 bpw.

## What

- **docs/EXL3.md, tools/exl3/, tools/test_exl3_*.py.** Format spec, numpy codec (codebook, reconstruct, ngram), safetensors/tokenizer adapters, the engine-form checker.
- **CPU kernel** `src/kernels/cpu/exl3.cpp`. Decode LUT, sliding window, tensor-core perm, H128, folded GEMV, ngram row.
- **GPU kernels** `src/kernels/cuda/exl3.cu`, `exl3_experts.cu`. Reconstruct, fused decode-GEMV, batched MoE expert FFN, `Exl3ExpertStore`, `Exl3ExpertStream` (per-token expert streaming with an LRU VRAM cache, `--expert-cache`), `exl3_moe_rows`, `exl3_embed_gather`, `exl3_shared_expert`.
- **Loader** `src/artifact/exl3_pack.cpp` builds the engine `WeightTable` from the model directory (1079 roles): the EXL3 linears attached as `Exl3Mat`, the norms/router/hyper-connection/GDN parameters/embedding staged in the engine's form. Plus `include/strata/artifact/{safetensors,exl3_model}.hpp`.
- **ngram** `PleTable::open_exl3`.
- **Engine seam** `WeightRef::exl3` + `gemv_quantized` (`src/core/layer.cpp`), `--exl3`/`--ple-exl3` in `generate.cpp`.

## Bitrates

Every released branch is checked on its own weights (`tools/exl3/fetch_branch_tensors.py` pulls one expert and one dense linear from each branch's shards, `strata-exl3-gpu` compares the GPU decode-GEMV against the CPU reference on them):

| branch | experts | attn / head | GPU vs CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.05bpw_h4_ng4 | K=2 | K=4 | rel 2.9e-4 |
| 3.05bpw_h5_ng5 | K=3 | K=5 | rel 2.9e-4 |
| 4.05bpw_h6_ng6 | K=4 | K=6 | rel 2.9e-4 |
| 5.05bpw_h6_ng6 | K=5 | K=6, K=7 | rel 2.9e-4 |
| 6.05bpw_h6_ng6 | K=6 | K=8 | rel 2.9e-4 |

## Measured

Radeon PRO W7800 (gfx1100, 32 GB, ROCm), 8 CPU pool threads, model on a SATA SSD, `--expert-cache 0` (every routed expert streamed from disk), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3 3.05bpw.

| | |
|---|---|
| load | 15.4 s (1079 roles, 2117.4 MiB EXL3 linears, 2679.3 MiB staged); 21.2 s with the dense linears requantized to Q8_0 (3592.6 MiB) |
| prefill | 9.0 tok/s (14 tokens) |
| decode | 11.9 tok/s (40 tokens, steady state); 5.5 tok/s with `--expert-cache 0` |
| expert FFN | 0.36 ms/layer on the GPU (48 layers); 493 ms/layer on one CPU thread |
| layer 0 / 47 vs CPU | rel 1.1e-3 / 1.0e-3 |

Five passes on the decode path, each measured on its own:

| change | decode |
|---|---|
| (before) | 2.3 tok/s |
| routed experts cached in VRAM (`--expert-cache` per layer, `auto`/unset sizes it from the free VRAM; without it the stream reads and uploads 890 MB per token) | 8.9 |
| dense GEMV retuned (window geometry hoisted out of the k loop, 256 threads, 2 output tiles per block, a k split that keeps ~256 blocks in flight) | 10.2 |
| the misses read with `pread` (0.3 GB/s through the mmap against 10.4 GB/s with preadv on the same page-cached tensors) spread over 4 threads into pinned staging | 10.8 |
| the resident experts' FFN enqueued before the staging starts (its own staging stream, then a scatter back into the router's order) | 11.05 |
| `gr_inject` / `gr_down` given four partial sums (one block of four warps walked 10,240 elements in 320 dependent steps) | 11.9 |
| the expert GEMV at four output tiles per block, swept on the real layer with `strata-exl3-moe` (T=2 0.385 -> T=4 0.308 ms/layer, -20%) | 3.7 ms/token |
| the reconstructed fp16 weight freed after its transpose (it leaked ~7 GiB of VRAM across the 301 dense projections, and the expert cache could not have it) | 216 -> 297 slots/layer |
| the expert FFN's accumulator zeroing folded into the prescale before it, and its f32 accumulator written as the f16 output (four kernels fewer) | k=1: 0.108 -> 0.093 ms/layer |
| the native bf16 projections on by default for EXL3 (the SSM gates, router and indexer are bf16 rows in the engine's form either way) | dense token 38.798 -> 35.572 ms |
| the dense linears requantized to Q8_0 at load and served by `native_mmvq` (measured with the experts skipped, so it prices the dense work alone: 47.4 -> 28.9 ms/token) | 21.1 -> 34.5 (dense only) |

The token is now: expert FFN 17 ms (the miss half ~5), dense GEMVs 23 ms, expert reads 13-27 ms (tracking the
70-94% hit rate), hyper-connections ~7 ms, the rest in the smaller kernels.  The per-layer chain is serial by
construction (router, host reads, expert FFN, combine, next layer).

**Where the dense token's time is.**  `--stage-timing --no-capture --no-pool` on the dense path: 35.572 ms per token, of which the attention block is 15.1 (the GDN's sub-stages sum to 9.5), **the hyper-connection reads 8.1** (`gr_read (attn)` 4.1 + `gr_read (ffn)` 4.0), the router 1.3, the writes 0.8, everything else under 1.  The hyper-connections are the biggest fixable block and the reason is concrete: `gr_down_kernel` stages the whole `xn` (D = 10,240 floats, 40 KB) in shared memory, which caps it at one block per compute unit against 121 blocks for 70 units, and the pair measures 8.1 ms against the ~2.6 ms its 1.27 GB/token of bf16 weights costs at bandwidth.  The change is to keep each thread's k-slice in registers and reduce the norm's sums in a small shared buffer; it is in `fused_gr.cu`, which the native pack shares, so it needs that path's selftest too.

**The expert FFN's geometry and kernel count, measured on the real layer.**  `strata-exl3-moe` runs the whole expert FFN on layer 0 with real weights, and both the tiles per block and the kernel count were settled on it.  Tiles: T=1 0.534, T=2 0.385 (what it was), T=3 0.321, T=4 0.308, T=5 0.319, T=6 0.327, T=7 0.342, T=8 0.325 ms/layer, so T=4.  Kernel count: k = 1, 2, 5, 10 measures 0.108, 0.130, 0.214, 0.332, i.e. 0.0249 ms per expert and 0.083 ms/layer of fixed cost; folding the three accumulator memsets into the prescale and the f32 accumulator into the f16 output takes the k=1 case to 0.093.  Three things measured worse and are not in the tree: shared-memory tile staging (0.462-0.487), a higher k-group count (0.330 at x2, 0.543 at x4), and launch bounds (256x4/6/8 within 0.004 ms of each other).

**The leak the VRAM accounting hid.**  `stage_exl3_requantized` allocates the reconstructed fp16 matrix, transposes it, and never freed the untransposed copy.  It is the same size as the matrix, so the 301 dense projections leaked ~7 GiB, and the expert cache was sized from what was left: 18.52 GiB free -> 216 slots/layer before, 25.28 GiB -> 297 after.  The decode's steady state (a 200-token run, the median of the last 30 tokens) went from a 97.4 ms pool to 83.1 ms with the uploads at 76.2 -> 62.0 ms, and a 15-token prompt from 14.0 s to 12.2 s.

**The steady state is the saturated routing, and it takes a while to get there.**  Measured on a 220-token run,
the per-token cache hit rate climbed 82% -> 90% -> 92.5% -> 98.8% -> 99.0% and the uploads fell from 400+ ms to
20-37 ms; a token then measures ~76-100 ms (~10-12 tok/s): dense work 29 ms (Q8_0), routed experts' FFN ~17 ms,
the host's wait on it ~19 ms, hyper-connections ~7 ms, the trickle of first-time experts 20-37 ms, the smaller
kernels ~10 ms.  With the reads priced at zero those parts sum to ~46 ms (~21 tok/s).  The prefill is the same
reads without a warm cache: a 15-token prompt measured 14-22 s (0.6-1.0 tok/s) with 113-2121 ms of uploads per
token against 1.8-3.6 ms of FFN, and a prompt's distinct experts are ~85% of the sum of its tokens' routes, so
batching would save that 15% and no more.  What makes a 64 GB machine's prefill 447-966 tok/s is that its whole
expert set is in RAM; this model's 45 GB of experts do not fit in 24.5 GiB of free VRAM plus ~20 GB of RAM, so
those reads are structural.

## Why a GGUF pack of the same model decodes faster, measured

- A trellis weight costs about **two loads and eleven ALU ops** to decode; a ggml block quant's `vec_dot` costs
  about one load per 4-5 weights.  The dense GEMV was load-instruction-bound: 3.5 G dense weights x 2 loads per
  token, 23 ms.  **The dense linears are now requantized to Q8_0 at load** (`stage_exl3_requantized`) and served
  by the engine's native MMVQ, the path a GGUF pack's dense projections already take.  Measured on the W7800, a
  2560x10240 matrix: the decode-GEMV kernel **106.8 us** against the native Q8_0 MMVQ kernel's **31.8 us**, 3.4x.
  Q5_K was tried first and rejected on the measurement: a 5-bit block quant on top of the trellis decode's own
  10-bit codes measures a **4%** round-trip error and the model answers "surface表面的表面的"; Q8_0's is **0.65%**
  and the model is correct.  Q8_0 is 1.7x the bytes of the trellis it replaces (3592.6 against 2117.4 MiB of
  dense linears, ~31 MiB per layer, about 16 expert slots), and the requantization streams through small
  row-chunk buffers so the model's page cache survives the load.  `STRATA_EXL3_DENSE=exl3` keeps the trellis.

  The bytes are the price, and they show up in the batched prefill, which reads the weights once per batch: the
  dense work of a 14-token prompt measures 20.5 ms against 31.6 ms with Q8_0 (683.8 against 442.5 tok/s), the
  same 1.5x that the byte counts predict.  In the pooled prefill the dense projections are 20-32 ms of a
  1.55 s batch (9.0 tok/s measured), so that is ~1% there, while the decode reads those weights every token and
  gains the 18.4 ms.
- **The v-head reorder is part of the weight, and a requantized copy has to carry it.**  The GDN's v projections
  (`attn_qkv`, `attn_gate`, `ssm_out`) are staged with their v heads permuted and the activations are permuted to
  match, so the requantizer runs `stage_exl3`'s own host-side reorder before it reconstructs.  Without it those
  three roles answer nonsense while the QSA roles (`Vr::None`) are correct, measured.
- The experts cannot go on the CPU pool the way a GGUF pack's do: the CPU's EXL3 folded GEMV is **493 ms/layer**
  against the GPU's **0.36 ms/layer** (`strata-exl3-moe`, 10 experts), so the trellis decode has to stay on the
  GPU and its streaming is on the per-layer critical path.

Both prompts answer correctly: "The capital of France is **Paris**." and a Python hello-world program, with and without PLE.

## Validation

- `ctest -R exl3`: 20/20. CPU numpy fixture + parity per K=1..8; `exl3_gpu_parity` K=1..8; `exl3_gemv_parity` K=1..8 plus the expert (640x2560) and attn (2560x10240) shapes; `ple_exl3_parity`.
- `strata-exl3-pack --run`: 1079 roles, 301 dense EXL3 projections, 0 faults.
- `strata-exl3-pack --dump` + `tools/exl3/check_engine_form.py`: 22/22 roles match llama.cpp's converter on the real weights (the v-head reorder, -exp(A_log), +1 gammas, [out][in] indexer staging), byte-exact for the trellis permutations.
- `python3 tools/test_exl3_{codebook,reconstruct,ngram}.py`: OK.
- Full `strata` target builds.

## Two bugs the parity tests cannot see

The parity tests share the decode with the numpy reference, so only the BF16 base model can catch a decode error. Comparing against it found:

- the trellis window read was a linear LSB bitstream read; ExLlamaV3 packs per 16-value span, MSB-first, then byte-swaps, and reads with a funnel shift (`unpack_trellis`/`dq`). Fixed in the numpy codec, the CPU decoder and both GPU kernels.
- the loader was missing llama.cpp's converter transforms, so every GDN layer paired q/k/v from the wrong heads and the decay was wrong. Fixed, and checked on the real model by `check_engine_form.py`.

pulls.title: [Engine] Add opt-in Galahad session storage
pulls.author: j-luwierski
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

Strata's existing slot API can persist its current conversation to a local file. Users who need encrypted, durable named sessions on supported NVIDIA systems have no integrated storage backend. With this opt-in change, the same API saves and restores complete Strata session images through Galahad; the existing file backend and default inference path stay unchanged.

## Related discussion

Previous submission and maintainer instructions: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1761. The maintainer asked that this PR be rebased on current main, use the required title and template, and then receive `/reopen`.

## Approach

Add a separate Galahad adapter for full session images, configuration and CLI options, size/error handling, and user documentation. Galahad remains an optional import and requires a separately installed licensed package. Session operations remain explicit, limited to slot 0, and unavailable with parallel requests or the ordinary file backend. Rebased on main while preserving the current session-save retry behavior. Galahad shutdown is guarded against duplicate close calls from normal shutdown and `atexit`.

## Validation

**Passed:**

- `.venv/bin/python -m unittest serve.test_galahad serve.test_slots serve.test_security` — 67 tests passed on Linux x86-64, Python 3.13, at revision `7e3494582faecba5934c1d43b692b98ecfe080e1`, based on main `5bda973a`.
- `.venv/bin/python serve/server.py --help` — Galahad options are present.
- `git diff origin/main --check` — no whitespace errors.

**Failed:**

- None observed.

**Not run:**

- Licensed native Galahad save/restart/restore, GPU output parity, and performance checks: this environment has no licensed NVIDIA setup.
- CUDA, HIP, and SYCL builds: no engine or backend kernel files changed.

## Limits

Requires Linux x86-64, a licensed NVIDIA GPU, and `galahad-kv==1.31.5`. Names are immutable, only slot 0 is supported, and the feature does not add automatic prefix caching. Mock tests establish the adapter and HTTP contract, not native persistence, encryption, GPU correctness, or performance.

pulls.title: tools tests: test_amd_is_not_asked mocks the Linux HIP engine build too (it wrote sys.prefix/.strata-rocm.json)
pulls.author: chaog992
pulls.body:
## Title

Issue: no dedicated issue opened. This is the separate Unsloth test failure noted in #1658.

Related precedent: #975, fixed test-only in d1ec32b. This change is independent of #1658.

## Summary

`IQ4XS.test_amd_is_not_asked` mocks `get_prebuilt_hip`, which setup uses on Windows, but not `build_engine_hip`,
which setup uses on Linux. The tested Linux machine has no usable system ROCm, so the test runs setup's real ROCm step.
That step requests AMD's ROCm package index, writes `Path(sys.prefix)/.strata-rocm.json` and tries to launch
`rocm-sdk`. The file's docstring promises "Mocked - no GPU, no downloads, nothing written outside a temp folder".

With the system Python, the stamp write raises `PermissionError`. In a fresh venv the test passes and leaves the
stamp, even though `setup.main()` has stopped with exit code 1: its two string assertions do not check that setup
completed. A stamp with the same version and index can also make a later setup in that environment skip the ROCm
install.

## What changed

`tools/test_setup_unsloth.py` (+2/-1): the test also mocks `build_engine_hip`, returning the same temporary engine
directory as the existing `get_prebuilt_hip` mock.

`setup.py` and the assertions are unchanged. No CUDA, HIP or SYCL engine code is changed.

## Extra Notes

WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04.1. Base fb58e0d, head cfa6197.

- `python3 -m unittest tools.test_setup_unsloth`, three runs per revision with the system Python 3.12.3 and with a
  venv made from it:
  - system Python: one error before; all 38 tests pass after;
  - venv: all 38 pass before and after, but only the base leaves the ROCm stamp.
- Python 3.10.22, 3.13.7 and 3.14.8 venvs: all 38 tests pass on both revisions; only the base leaves the stamp.
- An audit hook on this test's `setup.main()` call in a venv:
  - base: exits 1, requests the ROCm index and tries to launch `rocm-sdk path --root`;
  - head: exits 0, with none of those effects and no stamp.
- A deliberate mutation that turns on the AMD warning for UD-IQ4_XS makes the fixed test fail at its warning
  assertion, so the test still guards what it is for.
- With the system Python, the other 27 setup test files give the same results on both revisions. The existing
  failures remain in `test_setup_risk` (#1658 addresses it) and `test_setup_engine_hash` (#1510 addresses it).
- Other tests in this file still attempt read-only `nvidia-smi` queries.
- With `setup.WIN=True` on Linux, this test stops at the device check on both revisions. So an exit-code assertion
  would also need a `hip_card` mock.
- Not run: actual Windows and native Linux.

pulls.title: HIP: keep the old file-tier cache rule on AMD + build without CUDA toolkit (#1691)
pulls.author: KevinX8
pulls.body:
Bisected the gfx906 prompt stalls and 0.1.41 verify timeouts to 805088d (#1194); full story in #1691. Now rebased onto v0.1.44.1 (two commits).

**Commit 1 - the fix (HIP builds only, 6 lines, one file):** keep the pre-#1194 rule in `file_tier_unbuffered` - read the file tier unbuffered unless the page cache can hold every read byte. The 5%-of-read-bytes rule stays everywhere else.

**Why:** on ROCm the expert arena is HMM-tracked but unpinned (VmPin 0 after hipHostRegister). Cached file-tier reads churn the page cache, reclaim unmaps the arena's pages, and KFD suspends all of the process's GPU queues (measured: up to 45 of 60 s suspended while idle, 7-26 s per prompt). Past 60 s the watchdog kills the engine. On a 60 GB box with a 43 GiB resident budget the new rule picks the cached path (12.4 GiB of experts read from files, ~4-6 GiB of cache room); 0.1.40 read unbuffered there.

**Commit 2 - build fix (CMake only, no engine sources):** stock v0.1.44.x does not compile for gfx906 on a ROCm-only box. Two new unconditional TUs need the CUDA toolkit: `strata_mmq_w4a4` (needs cuda_runtime.h/cublas; RTX-50-only with runtime W4A8 fallback) and `strata_qwen35` (raw cublas calls, runs only for qwen35moe models; generate.cpp already guards `STRATA_HAVE_QWEN35`). Both are now gated on `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER`, so CUDA builds are unaffected and ROCm-only builds work again.

**Measured on 1x MI50 16 GB (gfx906), ROCm 10.1, 60 GB RAM, budget 43 GiB, v0.1.44.1 + these changes, standard 256k config:** file tier reads unbuffered; prompt 1 (cold, 6734 tokens) 61 tok/s, prompt 2 273 tok/s warming to ~300 tok/s on synthetic uniform-random-word prompts (which route across all experts and defeat the profile-ranked RAM copy); coherent real-world prompts (source code) reach 330+ tok/s on the same build. a same-session back-to-back A/B (forced restarts, identical prompts) gives 0.1.43+PR 286/297 tok/s vs 0.1.44.1+PR 276/289 tok/s with identical 25.7 tok/s decode - no version gap, the earlier 356-365 figures were quieter-box runs. 300-token story 260 tok/s prefill / 26.5 tok/s decode; 0 watchdog stalls / 0 verify timeouts. (The 0.1.43-based revision of the rule change gave 356-365 tok/s prompts on the same box; prompt 1 here carries first-request warm-up. Stock 0.1.44.1 on the same box: 18-62 tok/s, engine dead on prompt 2 - see #1691 for the proof run.)

**Not fixed by this change:** while a large RAM hog is actively running with no request in flight, the GPU is still suspended for most of that window (the #1705/#750 pressure case); the next request after it is unaffected.

pulls.title: bench: community report, RTX 5060 Ti / RTX A4000 16 GB (WSL2), GSQ-RCO IQ3_S on engine 0.1.41
pulls.author: kgmkm
pulls.body:
## Summary

Community benchmark for engine 0.1.41 on one RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
(Ryzen 7 3700X, 128 GB RAM, Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04), serving the
official ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S at 131,072 context, single-GPU, with
experimental speed projection enabled. Results only: no engine, build or
test changes.

One run per condition (stated in the README, no median/range), all prompts
unique with 0 reused tokens:

| Configuration | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| decode-story (48 prompt, 1400 gen) | 45.4 | 48.2 |
| decode-explan (47 prompt, 1284 gen) | 41.9 | 47.7 |
| prompt-4k (3820 prompt) | 343.0 | n/a |
| prompt-20k (19196 prompt) | 598.3 | n/a |

Draft acceptance 58.7%/61.7%, decode expert cache hit 86.1% best. The README
also includes an ESP refusal A/B on the same prompt: ESP on generated 500
tokens (finish=length), ESP off stopped at 106 tokens with a refusal text.

## What changed

- Add `bench/results/2026-10-09-community-rtx-5060ti-wsl2-iq3_s-0141/`:
  the README (hardware, settings, method, tables, limitations),
  per-condition medians (`measurements.csv`), one row per request
  (`requests.csv`), a `/metrics` snapshot, the sanitized server config and
  engine start lines, an engine-log excerpt, and the client script.
  Local paths are generalized and no credentials are included.
- Add nothing else: no code, docs, or index changes (index left to
  the maintainers).
- Not attached: the full multi-GB engine log and the model/pack files.
  The README lists what is missing.

## Extra Notes

- WSL2 + virtiofs stack (WSL components 3.0.1.0, distro in WSL2 mode),
  so these numbers describe that stack, not native Linux on the same card.
- Short-prompt reads carry the 0.1.41 CPU-share caveat noted in the README.
- Not tested: needle recall, TTFT, vision, soak, other quants, larger
  contexts, a layer split across the second card, calibration sweeps.

## Update: RTX A4000 companion report

Added `bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rtx-a4000-0141/`: same model,
config, script and method on the second card in the same box (RTX A4000
16 GB, Ampere, PCIe Gen4 x4, `--gpu 0`, port 8084), measured 2026-10-10,
one run per condition.

| Configuration | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| decode-story (48 prompt, 1400 gen) | 42.7 | 41.4 |
| decode-explan (47 prompt, 1337 gen) | 37.5 | 42.1 |
| prompt-4k (3657 prompt) | 261.7 | n/a |
| prompt-20k (18052 prompt) | 486.9 | n/a |

Draft acceptance 56.4%/61.3%, decode cache hit 79.0%/75.1%, ESP A/B same
outcome (500 generated tokens vs a 107-token refusal). About 13% slower
decode and 19-24% slower long-prompt reads than the 5060 Ti sibling,
consistent with the older architecture and the x4 link (6.5 vs 14.1 GB/s
probed).

Also fixed in this push: `benchmark-iq3s.sh` in the 5060 Ti folder now
locates the repo root by walking up to `serve/server.py` instead of
assuming a fixed depth, so it runs correctly from its committed location.

pulls.title: Two HIP fixes for Strix Halo (gfx1151): the wide top-k kernel and the VMM entry points
pulls.author: vlupilin
pulls.body:
# PR: two HIP fixes for Strix Halo (gfx1151) — the wide top-k kernel and the VMM entry points

Both changes are "a CUDA-only path that is dead on AMD for no hardware reason".
No behaviour change on NVIDIA cards; both are measured on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395
(Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 10.1) with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 512K
context (YaRN 2), and reproduce with the repo's own tools (`qsa_select_bench`).

## 1. topk: compile the wide kernel on HIP too

`block_topk_wide_kernel` is plain shared-memory / atomicAdd code (no sm_90
feature), but its definition and dispatch branch sat behind
`#if !defined(__HIPCC__)`. On AMD every context past the register kernel's
reach (~135K cells) fell back to the 4-pass ref radix. The ids are identical
by construction — `qsa_select_bench` states 256/256 at 256 queries x 65537
blocks and 1/1 at nq=1.

Measured (`qsa_select_bench`, gfx1151):
- nq=1, 131073 blocks (a decode window at 512K context): 2.24 -> **0.77 ms** (2.9x)
- nq=256, 65537 blocks (a prompt batch at 262K): 3.16 -> **1.43 ms** (2.2x)

End-to-end on that PC this (with the scorer change of a follow-up) took the
decode of a 512K-token prompt from ~24-26 up and flattened the prefill curve
(515K: 473 -> 634 tok/s). `STRATA_TOPK_STREAM=0` still restores the register
kernel.

## 2. vmm: resolve the driver entry points under their hip- names on HIP

`vmm.cpp` looks up `cuMemAddressReserve` & co. by name; `libamdhip64` exports
the same entry points only as `hipMemAddressReserve`, `hipMemCreate`, ... — so
`vmm_available()` was always false on AMD and `--kv-grow` (and the VMM expert
cache) could never engage; the flag just printed "is off". The signatures
match, so on `__HIPCC__` the resolver now dlsym's the hip- name of the same
entry point.

With this, the APU loads `--kv-grow` with `--expert-cache 24576` (all experts,
49.8 GiB of GTT) and serves requests. Caveat we hit during bring-up: after one
K/V growth transition the first request hung once (watchdog restart); we run
this combination only under supervision, so the elastic paths deserve their
own validation pass on other cards before the default changes.

## Validation on our side

- `native_grouped_parity`, `hip_native_qsa_score`, `hip_prefill_fused_iq`:
  all pass (the top-k ids gate is inside `qsa_select_bench`).
- Needle retrieval 5/5 at 131K and 507K tokens after both changes.
- The engine's own `ExpertCache::verify_slot` byte-check passes.

pulls.title: [Engine] Remote stage: run the later layers of a layer split on other PCs, over TCP (opt-in; Linux and Windows; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
pulls.author: lask3802
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

A layer split hands a token from one stage to the next once per verify window, and each prompt chunk's rows once
per chunk, but both stages had to be cards in one PC. A model that one 10 GB card caches poorly stayed slow unless a
second card fit in the same box. This branch puts that hand-off on a TCP link, so the later layers can run on cards
in **other PCs**:

- the main process runs layers [0, K), the head, the draft layer, sampling and the server:
  `--layer-split K --split-device 0 --remote-stage HOST:PORT`;
- a worker process on another PC runs [K, 48) without the head: `strata --serve --stage-worker PORT --stage-begin K`;
  relay workers (`--stage-end K2 --stage-next HOST:PORT`) make three or more stages;
- each process loads, caches and keeps the session of its own layers only;
- Linux (POSIX sockets) and Windows (Winsock); a Windows PC can be a worker natively or under WSL2;
- `--pipeline-windows 2` on the main process (opt-in): its layers run the next decode window, on a guess, while the
  worker and the head verify this one; workers need no new flag or protocol;
- `STRATA_REMOTE_TIMING=1` prints each stage's own time per prompt chunk and per window;
- images (`--vision`), recovery without a human, and peers that are not trusted (below);
- three standard-library Python tools: a node agent that starts workers (`tools/stage_node.py`), a splitter that
  ships a node only its layers' bytes (`tools/stage_ship.py`), and a tuner that measures configurations
  (`tools/stage_tune.py`).

Without `--remote-stage` or `--stage-worker` nothing changes (see Approach).

Docs: `docs/REMOTE_STAGE.md` (use), `docs/remote-stage/ENGINEERING.md` (design, process, every number). The raw data
(every run's JSONL, the timing lines, the tuner reports, the benchmark scripts) is on the branch `remote-stage-data`
of my fork: https://github.com/lask3802/Strata/tree/remote-stage-data/bench/results/2026-10-10-remote-stage

**The tables in this section were measured on earlier heads and engines (0.1.41 to 0.1.43.1)**: this head is the
same branch rebased onto 0.2.0-beta. What was run on this head (the default path, answers, speed, images and the
faults, on two PCs) is under Validation.

### Results (engine 0.1.41, before the pipelined decode)

PC A: RTX 3080 10 GB (PCIe 4.0 at x8), Ryzen 9 5900XT, 128 GB DDR4-3200, Linux. PC B: RTX 2080 Ti 11 GB, Ryzen 9
5900X, 64 GB DDR4-2400, Linux. PC C: RTX 3070 8 GB, Ryzen 7 5700X3D, 64 GB DDR4-3600, Windows 11. Links 1 GbE, and
10 GbE between A and B (~400 MB/s, slot-limited). `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072 --spec 4`,
greedy, one run per row. Prefill / decode tok/s; prompts of 7.5K / 30K / 57K / 91K tokens with 320-token answers.
0.1.42 turned `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP` on by default for CUDA serve; these tables were not run again.

| configuration | short decode | 8K | 32K | 100K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| RVN IQ3_S, 3080 alone | 39.9 | 791 / 38.1 | 1,118 / 37.2 | 1,120 / 38.0 |
| RVN IQ3_S, A + B (1 GbE), K=26, chunk 5888 | 53.5 | 655 / 48.1 | 1,231 / 49.7 | 1,521 / 45.6 |
| RVN IQ3_S, A + B + C (A-B 10 GbE), 24 / 16 / 8, C clocks locked | 51.3 | 658 / 47.8 | 1,110 / 46.5 | 1,640 / 44.7 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, 3080 alone (the better of two runs: prefill with a RAM budget, decode without) | 27.3 | 302 / 25.4 | 324 / 24.5 | 326 / 23.7 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, A + B (10 GbE), K=26, chunk 5888 | 38.8 | 659 / 34.4 | 1,147 / 36.9 | 1,164 / 33.6 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, A + B + C, 24 / 16 / 8, C locked | 38.4 | 549 / 35.3 | 945 / 36.6 | 1,334 / 35.2 |

Two PCs: decode +18-44% on IQ3_S, and on UD-Q4_K_XL (which one 10 GB card caches poorly) +42% and a 100K prompt in
88 s instead of 293. Long prompts need a large chunk (5888-8192). A third PC adds a hop to every window: it paid for
100K prompts and cost 1-8% of decode; the tuner's eight three-stage splits of UD-Q4_K_XL tied within the spread.

**Windows lowers a worker GPU's clocks between decode windows**, while the other stages run. The RTX 3070 under
Windows (or WSL2) waited 12-22 ms for its 8 layers per window, and 3.7-4.1 ms with `nvidia-smi -lgc 1500,1905 -lmc
7001,7001` (short decode 33.8 -> 41.8); the 2080 Ti under Linux held P2. The node agent can lock and reset the clocks
around a worker (`"gpu_clocks"`, as administrator), and the tuner's report says when a Windows node has not.

### Pipelined decode on a remote main (`--pipeline-windows 2`, engine 0.1.43 and later)

RTX 3080 main (layers 0-25), RTX 2080 Ti worker (26-47), 10 GbE, RVN IQ3_S, `--spec 4`, 40 varied prompts of 200
tokens, one binary per session, order off-on-on-off:

| build | off | on | on | off | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this branch on 0.1.43.1 (2152 and 1951 cache slots) | 65.0 | 71.5 | 70.8 | 65.4 | +9% |
| the same change on engine 0.1.43, another session | 62.8 | 70.4 | 70.7 | 62.7 | +12% |

The overlap hides part of the main process's layers behind the round trip, so with it on it pays to move layers to
the worker until the two are about even. Same PCs, fp32 rows, `--pipeline-windows 2`, this branch with #1887 and my
bf16 branch on top; 12 of the 40 prompts x 200 tokens, and a ~30K prompt read from 0 then 200 tokens; medians of 3,
one session:

| K, layers on the main process | main process's part, ms a window | round trip, ms a window | decode, tok/s | 30K prompt, tok/s | decode after it, tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26 | 22.6 | 16.6 | 70.3 | 1,351 | 53.3 |
| 24 | 19.3 | 19.1 | **73.4** | 1,218 | 58.8 |
| 22 | 17.0 | 21.6 | 73.1 | 1,158 | 59.2 |
| 20 | 15.3 | 24.1 | 71.4 | 1,130 | 55.9 |
| 26 again, at the end | 22.8 | 16.6 | 70.9 | 1,369 | 54.3 |

Prompts pull the other way: on two PCs the worker is the slowest stage per chunk (3.5-4.6 s against the main
process's 2.2-2.9 s), so K=24 is +4-5% decode and -10% on long prompts against K=26. On three PCs (an RTX 3070 last
stage over 1 GbE, clocks locked, bf16 rows) the overlap gave +15% decode at 26 / 14 / 8 (59.3 -> 68.3 tok/s), and [my
comment on the bf16 rows](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1748#issuecomment-6155624491) has the three-PC splits.

| choice | gains | costs |
|---|---|---|
| `--pipeline-windows 2` | +9-12% decode on two PCs, +15% on three | 444 MiB of the main process's expert cache (about 200 slots here); with the automatic cache the answers differ from a run without it (below) |
| fewer layers on the main process | decode, until its part matches the round trip | prompt speed while a remote stage is the slowest per chunk (K=24: -10%) |
| another PC | VRAM; long prompts once re-split (+12-16% at 30K here) | a hop and its layers on every round trip; decode ties two PCs only after re-splitting |
| a Windows card's clocks left unlocked | nothing to set up | the RTX 3070's 8 layers took 11-13 ms a window, against 5.9 ms locked |

**Answers.** The cache size is part of the result: a different slot count places other experts on the CPU, which
moves near-tie tokens, so with the automatic cache `--pipeline-windows 2` compares two cache sizes, not two loops.
Measured with one-token windows (`--spec 4 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`), `STRATA_ROUTE_TAIL_SKIP=0`, greedy, two
4-turn conversations of 16K-token prompts, 8 answers per run, the same two PCs. With the change on engine 0.1.43:

| what differs between the two runs | answers the same |
|---|---|
| `--pipeline-windows 0` vs `2`, automatic cache | 2 of 8 |
| `0` at `--expert-cache 1951` vs `0` at 2153 | 2 of 8 (the same answers differ) |

So the note "The cache size changes no output bit" in `generate.cpp` (the cache sizing comment) does not hold on this
setup.

This branch on 0.1.43.1 at `--expert-cache 1951`, each run the first replay on a freshly started server, against the
branch's first `--pipeline-windows 0` server:

| runs | servers with all 8 answers the same |
|---|---|
| `0`, the branch this one is built on | 2 of 2 |
| `0`, three more servers | 2 of 3 (the third: 4 of 8) |
| `2` | 4 of 4 |
| `2`, every third or second guess made wrong (`STRATA_PIPELINE_FORCE_MISS=3` / `2`; 256-317 of about 545 windows undone per run) | 2 of 3 (the third: 6 of 8) |

The runs that differ took another word partway into an answer, with `0` as well as with `2`. Later replays on one
server drift with either setting; the cause is not known.

### Recovery (engine 0.1.43 and 0.1.43.1)

Two PCs fail in ways one PC does not (the worker ends, either PC restarts, the link drops), and each needed a person
before. Fault injection on A + B (10 GbE, RVN IQ3_S, K=26), agent and server, none needing a hand. The first seven
rows ran on 0.1.43 (371b400f), the last three on 0.1.43.1 with `STRATA_REMOTE_CONNECT_S=60`, against the build before
them (0936f027), and again at 4bbcb16e and 5c454ed6:

| Fault | That request | The next request |
|---|---|---|
| the worker killed (`kill -9`) while idle | waited for the agent's restart, answered after 45.6 s | - |
| the worker killed in the middle of an answer | 503, `Retry-After: 30` (2.9 s) | answered after 50.2 s |
| the same, streamed | an error event of the `server_error` kind | answered after 44.8 s |
| the worker stopped and started through its agent | - | answered in 1.6 s |
| the main engine killed while idle | restarted by the server, took the worker over: answered after 20.5 s | 1.2 s |
| the main engine killed in the middle of an answer | the server's 503 for an engine that stopped | answered after 13.4 s |
| the worker stopped while a request waited, started 70 s later | answered after 109.6 s, past the 90 s check | - |
| the worker stopped; a streamed client leaves after 20 s, a second request at once | ended at the STOP, the engine kept (before: waited 60 s, then the engine ended) | 503 after 58.2 s (before: 37.9 s, for an engine that stopped) |
| the worker started again | - | answered after 12.7-15.5 s |
| the worker's port taken by a listener that never answers | 503 after 60.0 s (before: 310.5 s) | - |

### Images (`--vision`, engine 0.1.43)

On A + B (RVN IQ3_S), fixed expert sets, the tail skip off, the first token's distribution against the same model on
one card:

| prompts | KL |
|---|---|
| text, with or without the table | 1.6e-4 |
| six pictures, with the table, against without (`STRATA_STAGE_POSITIONS=0`) | geometric mean 43% lower (better on 3, the table picture 7.4e-4 against 1.7e-2; slightly worse on 3, not explained) |

With the served flags the answers were right (shapes, a table's numbers, a chart, a screenshot, text after them).

### Byte for byte without a remote stage (earlier bases)

| base | check | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.1.41 | one card, five greedy prompts (one of 9,364 tokens): this branch twice, `main` once | identical |
| 0.1.42 | fixed expert sets (the stock config does not repeat run to run), a 2 x 4-turn replay on a 16K-token prompt, `main`, this branch and #1887 twice each | the second round 8 of 8; `main`'s first run an outlier |
| 0.1.43 | the same replay: branch, `main`, `main`, branch | all four pairs 8 of 8 |
| 0.1.43.1, no `--pipeline-windows` | against the branch it is built on, two fresh servers each: the replay on the split and on one RTX 3080; five greedy prompts on the split | the same |

## Related discussion

- This PR was open before the 0.2.0-beta reset (closed with every open PR on 2026-10-19); this is the same branch
  rebased onto `main` e88ee39d. No maintainer agreement on scope yet.
- #1256 (a model split across machines) was closed as not planned, and #482 (a networked pool) was declined because it
  cannot be tested across PCs here. This is opt-in and self-contained, and it can be tested on one PC with two cards
  (Approach, "Trying it on one PC"). #1055 had the idea for decode only. If it is not wanted upstream, that is fine:
  I will keep maintaining it in my fork, and the Windows clock finding above may be useful on its own.
- CC-David-CC checked it against the in-process split: #1773 (three Tesla P4s, 9 of 9 exact) and #1813's parity gate
  (24 requests, passed on the earlier head f2673bd

pulls.title: bench: community report, 2x PH402 SKU 200 (4x GP100, sm_60), Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS at 1M, --pipeline-windows off vs on over four stages, engine 0.1.41 + patches
pulls.author: ruibeikaa
pulls.body:
Results-only submission, no engine changes. Adds bench/results/2026-10-09-community-2x-ph402-sku200/ following docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

**Headline.** `--pipeline-windows 2` (#1656 + #1674) on a four-stage layer split of four GP100 dies raises decode by **+14.6% to +28.8%** on 9 prompts of 87 to 301,147 tokens. Some examples:
- 40.5 → 51.2 tok/s on a 256-token code answer.
- 47.6 → 61.3 on a 512-token one.
- 43.2 → 53.7 after a fresh 301,108-token read.
- 41.7 → 50.3 on a follow-up at 301K.

Prompt reads are unchanged by the flag. Replies are identical bit for bit in all three arms on all 9 prompts.

Hardware:
- **GPUs:** 2× NVIDIA PH402 SKU 200, i.e. four GP100 dies (sm_60, 48 SMs, 31.91 GiB each, TCC). Each die has a 140 W cap and an application clock of 1050 MHz.
- **Links:** the two dies of a board copy peer-to-peer at 73.0–73.2 GB/s; across boards 3.3 GB/s; host to device 3.3 GB/s per die.
- **Host:** Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 256 GiB DDR5, ASUS ProArt B850-CREATOR WIFI NEO, NVMe SSD.
- **OS:** Windows 11 (build 26300), driver 581.80, CUDA 12.9.

Software: source builds for sm_60 (`-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`). The server is `serve/server.py` from v0.1.41.
- **next8:** v0.1.41 + #1674 + #1656 + the PH402 patch set. That set is #1424, #1441, #1660, #1368 and #1525, plus local sm_60 commits. The commit list is in the README.
- **next7:** the same patch set on v0.1.40.4, without pipelined windows.
- **next9:** next8 linked against ggml-cuda with a local sm_60 MMQ patch ([diff in my comment on #1639](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1639#issuecomment-6086238713)).

Model:
- [`ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF) IQ3_XXS. The dense projections and head were converted to Q8_0 with `tools/q8_dense_gguf.py` (#1424).
- Context 1,048,576 tokens (yarn ×4), int8 KV, layer split `12,24,36`, all 24,576 experts in VRAM.
- MTP `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.85 --mtp-window 8192`, greedy.

Configurations tested (every reply is hashed):
1. **Pipelined windows:** next7, next8 without the flag, and next8 with `--pipeline-windows 2`. One engine start each, the same 9 requests. These include a follow-up at 301K and a return to that conversation from the conversation cache.
2. **Prompt path:** next8 vs next9 (the MMQ patch), and `STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE` 768 / 290 / 450 on next9. Eight starts in bracketed order, 5 requests each (3 in the one start with the prefill timer).
3. **Draft floor:** `spec_min_p` 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.85 / 0.95 per request with pipelining on. 3 prompts × 2 rounds.

Other results:
- **MMQ patch:** the batched reads take 2.5–6.0% less time (bracketed next8 / next9 / next8 starts, one run each), and replies are identical.
- **`STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE` 768 → 290:**
  - The 1,158-token read goes from 4.627 / 4.632 s to 4.018 s.
  - The 34,835-token read goes from 48.967 / 49.195 s to 46.545 s.
  - 1,027 tokens appended to that conversation go from 4.339 / 4.348 s to 4.419 s (+1.7%).
  - The changed chunking changes the output bits.
- **Draft floor:** 0.85 is the fastest value on both code prompts.
- **Driver check:** `bench.py` (plan `ab`), run again on next9 at 290, reproduced that arm's 5 reply hashes.

Limitations:
- **Runs:** one run per arm for the pipelining A/B, 1–3 runs for the prompt-path arms, and 2 rounds for the floor sweep.
- **Baselines:** no stock v0.1.41 arm, and #1656 was not run without #1674.
- **Timers:** the prefill and decode timers were on in the three pipelining arms.
- **Not measured:** reply quality (replies were not graded, and every one ran to its cap), TTFT and peak memory.
- **Scope:** one model.
- **Hashes:** the sha256 of the converted Q8_0 shards and the pack/MTP preparation commands were not recorded. The README marks them.

Context:
- #1656 (@Cass67) and #1674 (@CC-David-CC): this adds four stages on CUDA sm_60 with reply hashes, at contexts up to 301K tokens. A trace breakdown is in [my comment on #1656](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1656#issuecomment-6086159617).
- #1441: `STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE`.
- #1639 (@thedrzinger, 5× P100): a PRMT dp4a emulation for the sm_60 MMQ path; [my reply there](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1639#issuecomment-6086238713) has the patch and its numbers.

pulls.title: SYCL: the PCIe probe copies from pinned host memory, as the CUDA engine's does (#1745)
pulls.author: sam-fakhreddine
pulls.body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1745

## Summary
The SYCL engine's PCIe probe now copies from pinned host memory (`sycl::malloc_host`), as the CUDA engine's probe does with `cudaMallocHost` and as the function's own comment describes. With `malloc` it timed the driver's pageable staging copy: an Arc Pro B70 on PCIe 5.0 x16 read 7.7 GB/s and got `pcie_frac` 0.21; with the fix it reads 35.6 GB/s and keeps the 0.55 default.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, `probe_pcie_h2d_gbps()`: the host buffer comes from `sycl::malloc_host` on the same in-order queue instead of `malloc`, the allocation also checks for a null pointer, and both frees are `sycl::free`. A two-line comment says why. Nothing else in the function changes (four 256 MiB bursts, the fastest counts, the `bw / 20` share).

What it leaves alone: the CUDA and HIP engines (already pinned), the share formula, `--pcie-frac` (an explicit value still skips the probe), and every kernel and switch.

## Extra Notes
How it was checked, on an Arc Pro B70 32 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16, Proxmox passthrough VM, Ubuntu 26.04, xe driver, oneAPI 2026.1.1, NEO 26.05.37020.3), IQ2_XS native pack, the documented command (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --kv int8 --prefill 4096 --max-context 32768`, `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1 STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1`), greedy, 256 new tokens:

- Build: SYCL only (the file is in `sycl/`), AOT `-DSTRATA_SYCL_AOT=bmg-g31`, 0 errors.
- Probe line before: `PCIe probe: 7.7 GB/s host->device (best of 7.5 7.5 7.0 7.7) -> pcie_frac 0.21 (default 0.55)`.
- Probe line after: `PCIe probe: 35.6 GB/s host->device (best of 27.0 35.6 33.0 31.8) -> pcie_frac 0.55 (default 0.55)`.
- Output tokens identical to main on the 20-token and 2,185-token community prompts (`bench/results/2026-10-07-community-arc-b65-v01402/benchy-{short,long}.ids`).
- Decode, main with `--pcie-frac 0.55` (what the fix now picks) against main's probed 0.18, medians of 3 interleaved pairs: 62.6 vs 61.0 tok/s (20-token prompt), 60.3 vs 60.1 (2,185-token prompt). A small difference on IQ2_XS, where 4 to 10% of routed entries come from the mirror; the share matters more for a quant with more experts in the mirror.
- A standalone SYCL copy test on the same card: pinned 34.7 to 35.3 GB/s at 256 MiB to 1 GiB, pageable 8.1 to 14.9 GB/s (table in #1745).

Not tested: other Intel cards, bare metal (only the passthrough VM), and the layer-split path's per-stage probes (`probe_pcie_h2d_gbps` is shared, so they get the same buffer).

pulls.title: CUDA SM86: opt-in IQ3 two-stage prefill build
pulls.author: InB4DevOps
pulls.body:
## Summary

Add the off-by-default **`STRATA_CUDA_SM86_IQ3_STAGE2` CMake option**, requiring an
explicit CUDA architecture 86 target. It builds a CUDA-only specialization; runtime
opt-in remains `STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 STRATA_PF_IQ3_STAGE2=1`. Only **IQ3_S/IQ4_NL and IQ3_XXS/IQ4_NL**
gate/up–down pairs use two activation stages. Every other pair and the default
retain four stages.

**Updated scope:** the shared kernel and C++ test edits from the initial draft have
been fully reverted. The specialization is selected only in the CUDA CMake branch
and only executes on runtime SM86. HIP's source/build branch and SYCL's build are
unchanged, so the original missing-ROCm gate no longer applies to this patch.
Other CUDA devices use the original implementation. SM86 includes other Ampere
cards, but only the RTX 3060 was measured. Windows/other hardware remain untested.

## What changed

### Installer integration (separate commit `0701e617`)

Eligible NVIDIA users now get an off-by-default setup question, or can use:

```sh
./setup.sh --setup --model IQ3_XXS --sm86-prefill iq3-stage2
# Windows: START-HERE.bat --setup --model IQ3_XXS --sm86-prefill iq3-stage2
```

Setup uses the detected architecture, selects the build option, bypasses plain
prebuilt engines, and writes the fused/runtime settings. It remembers the model's
choice for starts and updates, with separate engine/build caches and variant-aware
metadata. `--sm86-prefill off` returns to normal engine selection and restores the
previous fused setting. `--yes` alone leaves a new install off. The normal engine
and other models' variants are not overwritten. See `docs/INSTALL_SM86_PREFILL.md`.

**98 relevant setup tests pass**, including default-config goldens and simulated
Windows/Linux policy. Cache reuse/invalidation, disabling, config preservation,
starts and updates are covered without GPU/model downloads. Two checksum-caller
failures found by full discovery on the sibling integration also reproduce on the
untouched base (unmocked HTTP HEAD/404); the affected code is unchanged here.

### Kernel and measurement commits

- CUDA-only stage specialization with matching shared-memory sizing, copy-wait
  depth and launch attributes; conversion/routing helpers and the fallback are
  reused from the unchanged original implementation. The specialized kernel body
  must keep its arithmetic in sync with the original.
- Instantiate the two-stage family only for the eligible kernel types; select it
  only when both formats of the layer match the measured pairs.
- Fresh-process off/on numerical parity checks and scoped measurement evidence.

The blanket two-stage experiment is **not** included: it regressed IQ2_S by
4.8–5.8% at some sizes. Those kernels retain four stages. Weight prefetch distance,
tile/grid selection, residency, decode, setup defaults and HIP policy are unchanged.
This branch is independently based on `fb58e0db`, with no prefetch/head experiments.

## Measured evidence

RTX 3060 **12 GB / 100 W**, i7-12700KF AVX2, Linux, CUDA 13.4.92, native IQ3_XXS,
explicit 4096-token prefill and static residency. Six balanced pairs per realistic
prompt, 128 generated tokens:

| Prompt | Input tokens | Median paired prompt-speed gain | Faster pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Parser/test review | 12,247 | +0.199% | 5/6 |
| Runtime documentation | 20,324 | +0.304% | 5/6 |
| C++ prefill review | 30,757 | +0.239% | 5/6 |

All 18 pairs had identical output IDs and draft counts and were repeatable.
The clearer effect is in the IQ3 expert-layer workload: **+2.65–17.02%** across
six format/size combinations, all 18 process-level shape pairs faster. Untouched
IQ2 kernels stayed near baseline, rather than showing the global policy's regressions.

These are **prototype measurements of the same selective policy**. Final isolated
validation is separately recorded, not pooled into that series. The whole-engine
effect is modest; A/A controls include roughly +/-1.5% individual outliers. This
is a targeted kernel-tuning proposal, not a substantial general inference speedup.
No occupancy increase was measured, and no combined-prefetch claim is made.

## Validation

- CUDA SM86 Release: default-off reference build and this enabled build of `strata` and `prefill_fused_iq_test`.
- Architecture-86 requirement and mutually exclusive build options checked.
- Shared kernel/test bytes, HIP build branch and SYCL build file verified unchanged from upstream.
- Six formats × both tiles: isolated off/on fingerprints and prior disabled-build
  comparison against the default-off build, retaining the existing FP64/MMQ checks.
- Isolated two-pair checks on all three realistic prompts for token IDs, drafts
  and repeatability.
- `git diff --check`.
- Non-SM86 predicate checked at compile time; Windows/other GPU hardware runtime untested.

Details: `docs/benchmarks/2026-10-09-rtx3060-iq3-stage2/README.md`. Current validation
is in `cuda-only-evidence.json`/`cuda-only-parity.log`; earlier evidence remains
separately recorded, with the exact public-source prompts.

The separate one-superblock prefetch proposal (#1742) touches the same kernel but is not
a dependency. Combining or merging both policies needs additional validation.

Title: gfx906: right-size guarded QSA top-k to 17 keys near 64K

Separate integration-binary model ABBA: +1.41% TG with suffix disabled and exact IDs/counters; +1.30% on the ordinary adaptive profile with exact IDs/topology, while second-pair draft/cache counters differed and are disclosed. goldens, simulated Windows/Linux behavior, cache invalidation, opt-out, starts and

- A fresh-process numerical parity wrapper for six format pairs and both tile sizes.

## Measured evidence

RTX 3060 **12 GB / 100 W**, i7-12700KF AVX2, Linux, CUDA 13.4.92, native IQ3_XXS,
explicit 4096-token prefill and static residency. Six balanced pairs per realistic
prompt, 128 generated tokens:

| Prompt | Input tokens | Median paired prompt-speed gain | Faster pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Parser/test review | 12,247 | +0.548% | 5/6 |
| Runtime documentation | 20,324 | +0.813% | 6/6 |
