pulls.title: Trace prompt-cache costs and reuse snapshot buffers
pulls.author: InB4DevOps
pulls.body:
## Summary
- Add opt-in, log-only prompt-cache decision and phase tracing for CUDA/HIP and SYCL, including checkpoint allocation, GDN, PLE, and indexer timings and bytes.
- Add deterministic live workloads, trace analysis, and offline tooling tests.
- Reuse restored running-state host allocations for the next snapshot capture while refreshing every state byte.
- On branch switches that replace the active checkpoint chain, move that chain into the parked snapshot rather than deep-copying it. Keep the chain if admission or parking fails; preserve memory-budget accounting.
- Harden the trace runner against occupied ports, unloaded servers, paths with spaces, and backend-specific build directories.

## Performance
Measured on the local `branch_switching` workload using alternating settings on the same engine build:
- Running-state allocation reuse (first commit): total park capture 1025.0 ms -> 936.9 ms (-8.6%); eligible restored-branch parks 628.8 ms -> 540.8 ms (-14.0%).
- Checkpoint-chain move (second commit, with running-state reuse already enabled): five park captures totaled 939.0 ms -> 627.0 ms (-33.2%) across two off/on pairs. Reuse decisions and partial rereads were unchanged.
- Detailed trace of six checkpoint saves showed 174 ms spent allocating and 411 ms copying about 118 MB of GDN state per save; the chain-move optimization targets parking, not checkpoint creation.

## Verification
- `cmake --build build --target strata conversation_cache_test conversation_snapshot_test conversation_validation_test conversation_transfer_test`
- `./build/conversation_cache_test` (4,201 checks)
- `./build/conversation_snapshot_test` (3,985 checks)
- `./build/conversation_validation_test` (972 checks)
- `./build/conversation_transfer_test` (1,548 checks)
- `python3 -m unittest tools.test_analyze_prompt_cache_log tools.test_prompt_cache_workloads` (19 tests)
- `bash -n tools/prompt_cache_trace.sh` and `git diff --check`
- Live six-scenario workload (29 requests) completed with the checkpoint-chain move enabled.

SYCL source and tests are mirrored, but a SYCL toolchain was not available locally.

pulls.title: test(setup): the ready-made-engine refusal tests reach the checksum path on any PC
pulls.author: victorgabr
pulls.body:
`tools/test_setup_engine_hash.py`'s `WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller` mocked the download and the published digest, but not
the two steps that come before the checksum, so on most PCs the run never reaches the path those two tests are about:

- `get_prebuilt` returns at once when this checkout's `engine/` holds a locally built engine (`"source": "local"`) -
  which any PC that ever ran `./setup.sh --build` has;
- before downloading it `HEAD`s the release asset over the real network, and no release carries this OS's asset.
  Measured 2026-10-08: `HEAD .../releases/latest/download/strata-linux-x64.zip` and
  `.../download/v0.1.40.3/strata-linux-x64.zip` both answer **404**, while `strata-windows-x64.zip` answers **200**.

Either way the run stops before `verify_engine_archive`, prints nothing, and the two tests fail with
`AssertionError: SystemExit not raised` and `'keeping the engine that is installed' not found in ''` - on Linux always,
on Windows on a checkout with a locally built engine.

What changes: the class now points `setup.engine_dir` at the `engine/` folder its own `setUp` already makes, and mocks
the `HEAD`; the first-install case goes through that same helper instead of patching two of the four steps. No fixture
versions and no setup.py behaviour are touched.

    python tools/test_setup_engine_hash.py     -> Ran 30 tests in 0.021s, OK   (was: FAILED (failures=2))

Offline (0.02 s, no request leaves the process), and it needs no `engine/` in the checkout. The other `tools/test_setup_*.py`
suites are unchanged and green.

pulls.title: [Benchmark] community report, 2x RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB at full 250 W, IQ3_XXS (vs #1225 at 100 W), re-run on 0.1.45.3
pulls.author: caolonghao
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

The 0.2.0-beta tracker reset closed this results-only PR and asked for a re-run on the new version. Rebased on
`main` at `f57c0adc` (engine 0.1.45.3, 9 commits past `v0.2.0-beta`) and re-measured with the repository's
built-in `tools/strata_bench.py` suite (`--long`), replacing the community `benchmark.py` harness of the first
submission (no longer the guide's recommended tool). Same machine, model, pack and settings as before; the report folder is
`bench/results/2026-10-20-community-2x-rtx-2080-ti-qwen3-8-flash-next-iq3-xxs/`.

Result: 4K / 16K / 32K fresh prompts at 1,032.5 / 1,490.5 / 1,745.1 tok/s, short-chat decode 77.9 tok/s,
agent-session decode 77.5 tok/s with 69.4% conversation-cache reuse; the auto layer split kept the 0.1.40.2
placement (K=26). Against our own 0.1.40.2 cells on this pair (prompt throughput, both engines' own timings,
fresh prompts): +5.2% at 4K, +3.6% at 32K. The comparison against #1225 (100 W cap) from the first submission
stands: 4K decode 84.1 vs 52.8 was measured then and is quoted as 0.1.40.2 data in the README.

## Related discussion

none - results-only report; the reset notice on this PR asked for the re-run.

## Approach

One results folder: a README generated by `tools/strata_bench.py` and then extended by hand (hardware notes, the
version comparison, the log excerpt) + `results.json` (every request) + a hand-cut `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (the
server was started by its run script, not by the tool, because the tool's own start path hits the bug listed
under Failed). The 0.1.40.2 folder of the first submission is replaced; its prompt cells are kept as a
same-machine comparison table in the README, labelled by version. One discarded first attempt (wrong GPU label,
no cells kept) is noted in the README's limitations. No engine or server code is changed by this PR.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- source build: `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON
  -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75 -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-12.8/bin/nvcc`
  + `ninja strata` on Ubuntu 22.04.5, gcc 11.4, CUDA 12.8; `strata --version` -> 0.1.45.3.
- server: run script starts `serve/server.py --engine strata --config strata-iq3_xxs.json --port 8080`
  (packs built by 0.1.40.x setup load unchanged); READY in ~60 s with a warm page cache.
- suite: `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --config strata-iq3_xxs.json --long`
  -> all cells completed, 3 runs each, medians in the README; `reused: 0` on every fresh-prompt cell.

**Failed:**
- `python tools/strata_bench.py --config strata-iq3_xxs.json` without `--url` (the tool's own server-start path)
  crashes before starting anything: `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` (tools/strata_bench.py, the
  start-server branch of `main()`). Already reported upstream as #3188 (same traceback); the `--url` mode used
  for this report is the workaround.

**Not run:**
- correctness / needle runs (the suite is speed-only, as designed).
- a 128K prompt cell (the suite tops out at 32K with `--long`; the 0.1.40.2 run had none either).
- concurrency cells on this pair (not part of this report).

## Limits

One machine, one operator, shared NVMe with other load. Decode cells are not comparable with the 0.1.40.2
submission (the old harness used a 256-token cap on 4K/32K cells; the suite uses 100-token chats and 24-token
prompt cells), so only prompt cells are compared across versions. Power limits (250 W) are from nvidia-smi, not
an external meter.

the auto layer split moved one layer down from 0.1.40.2 (K=25 then, K=24 now; the caches hold 22,462 of
24,576 profiled pairs, ~99.8%). Against our
own 0.1.40.2 cells on this pair (prompt throughput, both engines' own timings, fresh prompts): +11.0% at 4K,
+3.3% at 32K. This stays the only two-V100 measurement; the PCIe-card-but-SXM2-string note (PCI device ID
`10DE:1DB5`, no NVLink) is kept in the README.

## Related discussion

none - results-only report; the reset notice on this PR asked for the re-run.

## Approach

One results folder: a README generated by `tools/strata_bench.py` and then extended by hand (hardware notes, the
version comparison, the log excerpt) + `results.json` (every request) + a hand-cut `engine-log-excerpt.txt` (the
server was started by its run script, not by the tool, because the tool's own start path hits the bug listed
under Failed). The 0.1.40.2 folder of the first submission is replaced; its prompt cells are kept as a
same-machine comparison table in the README, labelled by version. One discarded first attempt (wrong GPU label,
no cells kept) is noted in the README's limitations. The first submission's context ladder (to 1M) and
concurrency cells were not re-run on 0.1.45.3; their 0.1.40.2 numbers are quoted in one labelled reference
sentence each. No engine or server code is changed by this PR.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- source build: `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON
  -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70 -DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-12.8/bin/nvcc` + `ninja strata` on Ubuntu 22.04.5, gcc 11.4, CUDA 12.8
  (the NVIDIA_V100.md community build); `strata --version` -> 0.1.45.3.
- server: run script starts `serve/server.py --engine strata --config strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.json --port 8080`
  (pack built by 0.1.40.x setup loads unchanged); READY in ~90 s with a warm page cache.
- suite: `python tools/strata_bench.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --config strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.json --long`
  -> all cells completed, 3 runs each, medians in the README; `reused: 0` on every fresh-prompt cell.

**Failed:**
- `python tools/strata_bench.py --config <cfg>` without `--url` (the tool's own server-start path) crashes
  before starting anything: `NameError: name 'port' is not defined` (tools/strata_bench.py, the start-server
  branch of `main()`). Already reported upstream as #3188 (same traceback); the `--url` mode used for this
  report is the workaround.

**Not run:**
- the context ladder and concurrency cells on 0.1.45.3 (a cold 1M-context load took over 900 s from this
  machine's storage in the 0.1.40.2 run; the 0.1.40.2 numbers are quoted as such).
- correctness / needle runs (the suite is speed-only, as designed).
- the opt-in Volta decode kernels (`STRATA_SM70_TABLE=1`, #1647) - the default path was measured, as before.

## Limits

One machine, one operator, shared NVMe with other load. Decode cells are not comparable with the 0.1.40.2
submission (different harness output caps; see the 2080 Ti sibling PR for the same caveat). The ladder and
concurrency numbers in the README are 0.1.40.2 measurements, not re-runs.

pulls.title: # Chat: a context gauge, per-request timings, and conversation compaction
pulls.author: orangeswim
pulls.body: # Chat: a context gauge, per-request timings, and conversation compaction Re-opening of #350, which GitHub closed when main's history was cleaned up (not a rejection, per the heads-up there). Same change, rebuilt on the new main as three commits, one per feature. No server change. What it adds: - **A context gauge** — a small pill in the composer bar (fill bar + token count, e.g. `2.4k/200K`) showing how much of the context window the conversation uses. Amber at 70% of the window, red at 90%. Updates after each reply; passive. - **Per-request timings, and a PP t/s column** — a chevron on each reply opens one line with that request's numbers: tokens read and their speed, cache reuse, time to first token, drafts accepted (kept with the message). The Monitor's requests table gains a prompt-processing tokens/s column beside decode, computed in the UI from fields the server already returns (the reused cache share excluded; a fully cache-served request shows a dash). Also: the streaming cursor now shows from the moment a message is sent, while the prompt is still being read, not only once tokens arrive. - **Conversation compaction** — a button that asks the model itself to summarize the older turns: the newest turns stay verbatim up to a ~5k-token budget, the summary carries them as an exact client-built transcript, and from then on the API receives the summary plus the newer messages instead of everything. The page keeps every message (the summarized ones are dimmed above the divider, and only the newest summary can be put back — older ones are already contained in the one after them). Long user messages clamp with a Show-all toggle; display only. The payload rules live in `web/compaction.js`, tested by `web/test_compaction.mjs` (run through `serve/test_compaction.py` so `unittest discover` picks them up). Notes for this rebase: - The one conflict (`apiMessages`) was resolved by folding #1392's "the answer being asked for now is not history yet" rule into the new callback form. - The compaction rules were aligned with #1392's error-turn policy: `compaction.js` no longer drops error turns itself — it only decides which messages the summary replaces; the converter decides how a turn is sent (so a turn with no answer text still goes back as an empty assistant turn, as on main).

pulls.title: serve --batch: a layer split reads a prompt in STRATA_SPLIT_PIECE-token runs, decided at every boundary
pulls.author: sanastasiou
pulls.body:
## What

On a layer split under `serve --batch`, a prompt read that starts while a batch slot is decoding is cut into single chunks with a decode window between each, because the stage pipeline only overlaps within one `sp.run`. The read kept that shape to its last chunk, even when the slots finished their short turns a few seconds in. Long reads in a busy server ran at about half the speed of the same read on an idle server.

`read_part` now decides at every chunk boundary how much to read next (`prompt_read_piece` / `prompt_read_run_end` in `include/strata/program/read_piece.hpp`):

- a slot is decoding, or the engine is not a layer split: one chunk, as before;
- layer split and no slot decoding: `STRATA_SPLIT_PIECE` tokens, rounded down to whole chunks (at least one);
- `STRATA_SPLIT_PIECE` unset or 0: the whole remaining prompt in one run, as before.

The piece size bounds how long a shorter request's `BYIELD` waits behind a long read.

Scope: this applies with `--batch-groups 1` (the default). With `--batch-groups` > 1 on a split (`piped`), `read_part` still reads the whole prompt in one `sp.run`; this PR does not change that path.

**Default behaviour does not change.** With `STRATA_SPLIT_PIECE` unset, an idle split reads the whole prompt in one run, the same as today. The only thing that differs without the variable is that a read which started beside a decoding slot goes back to one run once no slot decodes, where today it stayed on single chunks.

## Measured

2× RTX 3090 layer-split pair (PCIe 3.0, no NVLink), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, `--batch 2 --prefill auto` (8K chunks), `STRATA_SPLIT_PIECE=65536`. Load: 4 parallel Claude Code compaction benchmarks, each growing to ~400K tokens, through one router onto two such pairs.

| read | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| prompt reads that began beside a decoding slot | 1,240–1,740 tok/s | 1,800–2,450 tok/s |
| e.g. a 124K read | 1,716 tok/s | 2,456 tok/s |
| e.g. a 99.5K read at long context | 1,311–1,347 tok/s | 1,793 tok/s |
| idle 249K read (unchanged path) | | 3,323 tok/s, 75 s |

Over the whole 4×400K run: time to first byte p95 123 s → 76–80 s, mean wall time per conversation 1,260 s → 1,178 s. Recall 5/5 in all four conversations.

## Tests

- `read_piece_test` (new, header-only, 15 checks): piece rules, rounding to whole chunks, run end clamped at the prompt end.
- CUDA build: `generate.cpp` compiles; ran in production on both pairs.
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: same edit, not compiled (no oneAPI here).

pulls.title: [Engine] conversation cache: never park one conversation with another's retained K/V
pulls.author: sanastasiou
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

With `--batch` and conversation parking, one conversation can be parked with **another conversation's K/V** in its snapshot. Restoring it later serves the other conversation's content.

A restore keeps the restored K/V (`ConversationCache::retain`) so the next park of the main session copies only what changed. The reuse tracked a token *count* (`unchanged_tokens`), not *whose* tokens. `copy_from_slot` (a batch slot giving its conversation back to the main session) replaces the main session's K/V but did not drop the retained image. The next park then reused the earlier conversation's K/V for the new one's prefix.

Seen in production on a 2-GPU layer split, `--batch 2`, `--conversation-cache-mib 24576`, 4 Claude Code clients:

```
conversation cache: restored 114705 tokens (live)          <- conversation P; its K/V retained
batch: slot 0 gave back 37564 tokens of this conversation   <- main session now holds Q
conversation cache: parked 37663 tokens ... reused_kv_bytes=573372672   <- Q parked with P's K/V
conversation cache: restored 37663 tokens (live)           <- Q's next turn
```

Before: Q's reply named a file path that existed only in P's context, and Q answered from P's history from then on. In five 4-conversation runs, 29 parks reused a retained image after a slot had replaced the main session.
After: a park reuses retained K/V only for the prefix the live conversation shares with the conversation it came from; otherwise it copies in full.

## Related discussion

none (focused bug fix)

## Approach

- `retain()` records the ids of the conversation the K/V belongs to.
- Parks call `take_reuse_for(live)`. It reuses only the prefix that `live` shares with those ids. With no shared prefix, or no recorded ids, nothing is reused.
- `copy_from_slot` drops the retained image before it replaces the main session's K/V.
- One stderr line is printed whenever a reuse is cut, so the guard is visible.
- The same edits are made in `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`.

Compatibility: the reuse only ever skipped a copy. Cutting it costs at most one full copy of the parked conversation's K/V; the output is otherwise identical. No flag, no default change.

## Validation

**Passed:**
- Unit tests on this branch's change applied to `main` e88ee39d (0.2.0-beta + 12 commits; the branch merges cleanly), Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3:
  `cmake -G Ninja -S . -B b -DSTRATA_BUILD_CONVERSATION_TESTS=ON -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF && cmake --build b && (cd b && ctest -R "conversation|session_save")`
  → 5/5 tests passed; `conversation_cache_test: 4778 checks passed`. The new cases: another conversation never gets the retained K/V; a diverging conversation reuses only the shared prefix; a rewrite's limit still holds on every stage; an image of unknown identity is never reused. The first case fails if the ids comparison is removed (checked by mutation on the original revision).
- CUDA build of v0.2.0-beta (3d1fb480) with this change (plus four unrelated local patches), Linux, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`, `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON`: builds. It boots and serves Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S on 2x RTX 3090 (24 GB each), layer split, `--batch 2`, conversation cache on, Debian 13, 256 GB RAM.
- On 0.1.43 with this fix: a 4 × 400K-token compaction run (4 parallel Claude Code conversations, each compacting at about 430K) on the same 2-GPU setup gave recall 5/5 in all four, and none of the transcripts mentions another conversation's working directory.

**Failed:**
none observed

**Not run:**
- SYCL build: no oneAPI environment here. The SYCL edit mirrors the CUDA `generate.cpp` edit line for line but is not compiled.
- HIP: no HIP file is touched.
- The 4-client leak reproduction has not been repeated on 0.2.0-beta; only boot and serving were run there.

## Limits

The guard only cuts reuse; it does not add any. A conversation restored, handed to a slot and given back re-copies its full K/V on its next park.

pulls.title: KV streaming under WSL: pin the K/V host copy with cudaHostRegister
pulls.author: yjamil8
pulls.body:
Under WSL2 the NVIDIA driver caps what `cudaHostAlloc(Mapped)` can pin at about 1 GiB in all. KV streaming allocates each QSA layer's K/V host copy that way (`src/core/layer.cpp`), so it cannot work under WSL, and setup turns it off there: the whole KV cache has to sit in VRAM beside the expert cache, which limits long contexts on WSL.

`cudaHostRegister` of ordinary memory is not capped the same way. Strata already relies on that: the expert arena is registered `Portable|Mapped` in `pinned.cu`, and on my WSL machine the start log shows `expert arena: cudaHostRegister PORTABLE ok` for 46.84 GiB.

This change adds `kv_host_alloc()` for the K/V host copy:

- when `/dev/dxg` exists (WSL2, the same check as `under_wddm()` in `generate.cpp`) it maps anonymous memory and registers it `Portable|Mapped` before any page is touched. This also leaves WSL's small `cudaHostAlloc` budget to the staging buffers that are still allocated that way;
- elsewhere `cudaHostAlloc` stays first;
- either way the other method is the fallback when the first is refused, and `STRATA_KV_HOST_REGISTER=1` / `=0` forces the order;
- the failure message no longer says WSL pins only 1 GiB.

The buffer lives as long as the process, like the `cudaHostAlloc` copy it replaces. By inspection, native Linux and Windows behave as before unless `cudaHostAlloc` is refused; I have not run it there.

**Tested** with this commit on one RTX 5090 (32 GB), Ryzen 9 9950X3D, WSL2 with 157 GiB, Windows driver 591.86, CUDA 13.1, IQ3_S, `--max-context 1048576 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`:

- start: `the host copy is pinned `KV streaming: 32768 of 1048576 cells per QSA layer in VRAM, the K/V in 12.38 GiB of pinned RAM`, with no environment variable set
- `tools/needle_bench.py`: 4/4 found, 128K and 1M (1,015,070 prompt tokens) at depths 10 and 90
- decode 99-124 tok/s with 0.5-1M tokens in context (4 runs, greedy); medians of 150-191 tok/s from 55-token prompts up to 128K (single runs 113-196); about 4,200 tok/s prefill for aeam_parity` still passes; it allocates its own host pools, so it checks the streaming kernels, which this change does not touch

**Not tested:** a layer split or remote experts under WSL (where t3253 applies to the expert arena, not to this copy), Docker Desktop, native Linux, Windows.

**Not in this PR:** `setup.py` still never writes `--kv-resident` on WSL (`kv_streaming_wam configs there (`upgrade_config`), so until that changes WSL users have to add `--kv-resident` by hand, and `setup.py --update` removes it again. The docs also still say WSL cannot stream. I can add this PR, gated on `MIN_ENGINE`, or send it as a follow-up, whichever you prefer.

pulls.title: docs: tool selection and recovery analysis with model-family guide
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
## Summary
A separate analysis of the completed measurements in #1491, using explicit priorities for agentic coding workflows. Q8 is labeled Reference. This adds no inference runs or engine changes and does not replace the official benchmark scores.

## Weighting
Tool selection 25%, error recovery 25%, context/state 20%, arguments 10%, planning 10%, multi-step chains 5%, code patterns 5%. Safety, structured output and all other categories have zero weight.

Score = sum(weight * earned category points / available category points), using exact fractions before rounding. These are preference weights, not a validated coding-success probability.

![Weighted ranking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/docs/agentic-code-weighting/bench/analysis/agentic-code-20261008/figures/weighted-ranking.png)

![Weights and examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/docs/agentic-code-weighting/bench/analysis/agentic-code-20261008/figures/weighting-explained.png)

## Model families
- ISTA: base-model quantization using GSQ refinement and RCO precision allocation.
- Swift 1.5: UkisAI post-training plus Swift-specific quantization; not simply another quant of identical weights.
- AP: Agention Precision, mixing standard quant formats by tensor group.
- Gyro: custom rotor-coded experts in a rotated basis, requiring compatible runtime support.
- Reference: the recorded Q8 run on the separate three-P4 runtime, not ground truth.

![Model-family guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/docs/agentic-code-weighting/bench/analysis/agentic-code-20261008/figures/model-families.png)

## Findings and limits
ISTA IQ3_XXS and Swift IQ3_XXS tie at 97.00; Gyro-S scores 96.33, Swift Q2_0 95.00, and Reference 92.54. One point in selection or recovery moves the score by 4.17, so the leaders are a shortlist rather than a statistically established order. All models saturated the small code-pattern group; repository-editing quality remains unmeasured.

Independent calculation checked all 12 scores against the original committed reports. Three figures are included as PNG/SVG and reproduce byte-for-byte locally. Source counts, hashes, weights, formulas and the rendering script are included. The branch starts from main and adds only the analysis directory.

Benchmark credit: [Tool-Eval-Bench](https://github.com/SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench) by [SeraphimSerapis](https://github.com/SeraphimSerapis). Examples are paraphrased. The report links each publisher model card and records differing runtime cohorts.

[Full analysis and publisher sources](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/docs/agentic-code-weighting/bench/analysis/agentic-code-20261008/README.md)

pulls.title: Community benchmark: RTX 3070 Ti 8 GB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 64 GB DDR4-3600 (Windows 11)
pulls.author: gbwzzy218
pulls.body:
## Title
Community benchmark: RTX 3070 Ti 8 GB, Ryzen 9 5900X, 64 GB DDR4-3600 (Windows 11). Results only; no issue.

## Summary
Measurements of Flash-Next IQ2_XS on an 8 GB card with the release engine 0.1.40.3, comparing setup's 32K default with three 128K configurations. Main result: in setup's 128K k8v4 configuration, `--kv-resident 20480` instead of 32,768 raised median prompt throughput by 38.8–41.4% in three within-session comparisons (one in reversed order); decode did not change by a comparable amount. With 32,768 the automatic planner picks a 768-token chunk, below `stream_all_min()` (1,024), so prompts go through the 8-slot `STAGE` ring; with 20,480 it picks 1,024 tokens and a 384-slot ring. Two follow-up configurations with a fixed 768-token chunk are consistent with chunk size contributing most, but do not isolate the mechanisms.

- **Hardware:** RTX 3070 Ti 8 GB (PCIe 4.0 x16, also drives the display), Ryzen 9 5900X (AVX2, no AVX-512), 64 GB DDR4-3600, NVMe, Windows 11 build 26200, driver 617.42.
- **Software:** ready-made release engine 0.1.40.3 (SHA-256 in `system.txt`), tree at `d5ea713374` (identical to `main` when measured).
- **Model:** Flash-Next IQ2_XS at setup's pinned revision, MTP on, greedy, `reasoning_effort "none"`.
- **Method:** the unmodified community `benchmark.py`; 10 server starts in two sessions; 108 measured requests (5 per length, 3 at 128,000 tokens), all with zero reused prompt tokens; `needle_bench.py` 6/6 at 32k and 128k.

## What changed
Adds `bench/results/2026-10-07-community-rtx3070ti-8gb/` only (28 files, no code changes):
- `README.md`: the report (hardware and provenance, configurations, method, results, recall, limitations).
- `results.json`, `summary.json`: every measured request with the engine's `/metrics` counters, and per-block medians and ranges.
- `engine-start.txt`, `configs/`: what the engine planned at each start, and each block's effective arguments and `env`.
- `needles.json`, `system.txt`, `orchestrator-session1.log`, `orchestrator-session2.log`, `bench_orchestrator.py`: recall results, hardware probes and hashes, execution timestamps, and the driver script (local paths replaced by placeholders).
- `quality/`: single-run supplementary checks (task prompts, scorer and its outputs; a conversation-cache check).

## Extra Notes
- Limitations: one machine and model; configurations measured as blocks rather than interleaved; a 3.2–4.2% unexplained difference between the two sessions (comparisons are made within a session); the display shares the GPU; the release binary does not log which staging path a chunk took.
- Two suggestions for the maintainers are at the end of the README: a start-log hint when `--prefill auto` picks a chunk below the streaming threshold, and setup's `KV cache: 4-bit (Hadamard-rotated)` label printed for `--kv k8v4`.
- The report was drafted with an AI assistant, and its numbers were checked against the raw data by two further AI reviews before submission.

pulls.title: bench: heterogeneous RTX 5070 Ti + 5060 Ti, experimental PP32 KV-grow and adaptive DMA
pulls.author: k93k2J-glitch
pulls.body:
## Summary

Results-only community report for a heterogeneous RTX 5070 Ti 16GB + RTX 5060 Ti 16GB pair on Windows: experimental PP32/16, native 262K int8 KV capacity, KV-grow/pipeline2, and optional pinned adaptive DMA staging.

Every changed path is under `bench/results/2026-10-08-community-5070ti-5060ti-kvg-dma/`. This PR does not apply engine changes to upstream; the prototype patches are reproduction artifacts in that folder.

## Recorded evidence

- Custom fork based on source tag v0.1.40.1, native engine string `0.1.40`: 10 interleaved paired rounds at actual 65,536 / 131,072 / 261,000 input tokens and actual 1,024 generated tokens.
- 60 steady measurements plus 60 first-request diagnostics; all selected outputs passed four functional cases, with prefix reuse disabled and native token counters checked.
- Full-ten median/ranges and independent eight-sample trimmed means are both retained, including slow samples and one disclosed validator-timeout partial-visit retry.
- Separate v0.1.40.3 prototype validation: eight functional outputs and per-device long-to-short KV/expert observations. This is not a repeated v0.1.40.3 speed comparison.
- Synthetic frozen messages, portable opt-in runner, sanitized numeric CSV/JSON, and clean-tag prototype patches are included.

## Main limits

The measured engine is a custom prototype, not stock upstream. The workload completes a Python function then generates comments to maintain the output cap; it does not establish prose speed, long-context recall, perplexity or general coding quality. At 128K, the full-ten median decode difference is about +0.93%, whereas the trimmed-mean difference is +7.49%; slow samples materially affect the latter. There is no general DMA speedup or causal paging claim.

Clocks/background load were not fully controlled, and full model/expert-profile hashes were not frozen. Public stripped-patch builds and inference reruns remain outstanding; the local full prototype previously built and ran.

## Publication preparation

Clean official-tag patch application and core-file/DONE-parser equivalence to the previously tested source were checked offline. Python syntax, synthetic fixture grammar/message hashes, default no-run behavior and an explicit outbound file allowlist were checked. No model request, GPU test or service restart was performed during publication preparation.

Machine usernames, personal email, host/network identifiers, absolute personal paths, credential values/locations, private prompt content, raw service/Codex logs, Windows launchers, auth bypass and local Git history are excluded. Git commit metadata uses the submitting account's GitHub noreply identity.

This is a **draft** for maintainer review of the report and reproduction packaging. Related work: #1223 (VMM/peer ownership), #1231 (no-loan safety), #765 (budgeting), #807 (batched-upload design). The layer-split feature discussion can be coordinated separately rather than proposing the integration branch wholesale.

Feature discussion: #1495.

pulls.title: Experimental adaptive memory relief and supervised tool resource leases
pulls.author: midhatn
pulls.body:
Local agents need room for compilers and GPU tools between model calls. This opt-in draft lets a supervisor declare that work, release inference resources, and return after a fresh capacity check. Sustained external memory pressure can trigger relief too. If resident relief is insufficient, AUTO confirms that the native and vision processes have exited before admitting the tool and later reloading.

The current integration merges [Strata v0.1.45](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/tag/v0.1.45) into public adaptive head `281220bc`, preserving the feature history and medking82's learned-profile identity correction from [fork PR #1](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/pull/1). The separate disk checkpoint bank is excluded. Results from a combined local runtime do not qualify this public branch.

The implementation reuses [#726](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/726)'s live RAM blocks, VMM expert cache and acknowledged native memory protocol. An authenticated loopback lease distinguishes admission, execution, renewal and release. A supervisor grants tool profiles, and runtime-identified workers share one broker. Uncertain execution or teardown retains the barrier instead of repeating a tool or regrowing over it.

Physical RAM, commit capacity and fresh native GPU headroom are checked separately. The ordinary additional return allowance remains 256 MiB. The optional pressure-only prefill floor reclaims more cache while retaining bounded execution workspace; defaults stay unchanged. [Protocol and limits](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/blob/codex/adaptive-background-draft/docs/TOOL_RESOURCE_LEASES.md) and [prefill behavior](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/blob/codex/adaptive-background-draft/docs/PRESSURE_PREFILL_FLOOR.md) describe these boundaries. Embedded image generation still refuses combinations that would bypass adaptive or supervised tool ownership.

The .45 compatibility work preserves adaptive preparation reservations alongside upstream prompt-cache cleanup and answer-room continuation. A native correction distinguishes generated output from the optional merged prompt window: all prompt rows must be consumed, while only the last prediction is emitted. Earlier prompt predictions, including EOS, must not shorten that window. The default nonmerged path retains the existing output-cap and EOS behavior.

Independent validation of this public composition: **1,298 Python server tests passed, 13 skipped; 54 broker tests, three setup tests, 12 browser-control tests and seven standalone native CPU fixtures passed.** Four new fake-engine cases cover ownership during answer-room wrapping, explicit reasoning budgets, opt-out and rejected context fitting. The native regression covers merged prompt rows, EOS positions, the one-token output allowance and reusable prefix state. [Results and exact boundaries](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/tree/codex/adaptive-background-draft/bench/results/2026-10-18-adaptive-0145) are recorded. No CUDA build, GPU/model/media run, HIP/SYCL build or visible Desktop acceptance was performed on this public composition. Previous CI is historical until new jobs run on the pushed head.

Earlier [compiler/prefill evidence](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/tree/codex/adaptive-background-draft/bench/results/2026-10-10-pressure-prefill), [workflow evidence](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/tree/codex/adaptive-background-draft/bench/results/2026-10-11-hermes-media) and [history-repair qualification](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/tree/codex/adaptive-background-draft/bench/results/2026-10-13-adaptive-history-repair) remain scoped to their recorded revisions. More recent local protected-compiler, fresh-owner result recovery and foreground unload/reload checks include the separate checkpoint bank and operational harness; they are not validation of this public branch. Normal compression also remains unfinished: a later summary in one attempt hit its 8,192-token allowance and was correctly rejected before adoption. The complete attempt remains failed.

This remains a draft, single-engine CUDA implementation. It is not ready for upstream review under the repository's all-touched-backend build requirement. Arbitrary detached tools, portable media installation and visible Desktop operation remain unqualified. Capacity is observed rather than reserved by the OS; finite execution memory remains, so this is not a no-OOM or uninterrupted-progress guarantee. This update makes no performance claim.

Hermes stays engine-independent: the terminal authorization seam is [Hermes #135418](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/135418), and delegation-evidence guidance is separately scoped in [#136266](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/136266). [Implementation provenance](https://github.com/midhatn/Strata/blob/codex/adaptive-background-draft/docs/ADAPTIVE_PROVENANCE.md) credits the allocator work and the narrow vision-pipe adaptation from [#1862](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1862). The separate local bank credits xrip's [#1937](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1937); it is not included here. Existing authorship and license notices are retained. Prepared with Codex.

pulls.title: [Engine] save and restore sessions without an MTP drafter
pulls.author: Momoyeyu
pulls.body:
## Problem and result

`--serve` can run without `--mtp`, but SAVE always passed `mtp.kv_state()` to the session writer. An unloaded drafter has `max_cells == 0`, so saving any nonempty conversation failed with:

```
conversation snapshot: invalid K/V extent
```

and RESTORE never got a file to read. The in-memory snapshot path already accepts an absent drafter, so the disk path now uses the same distinction: the draft K/V source, its read bounds, `sl.kv_layers` and the validate/restore calls include the drafter only when it exists. The file format and the K/V extent checks are unchanged; passing an uninitialized drafter explicitly still fails instead of bypassing validation.

Related to #1444, not closing it: the failure is reproduced with the same error, but not in the reporter's Q6_K configuration, and the launch arguments are still missing there.

## Related discussion

#1444.

## Approach

`conversation_snapshot_sources` and `conversation_session_read_limits` take `const QsaState*`; the reference overloads stay for callers that always have a drafter, so nothing else in the tree changes. SAVE/RESTORE, the memory preflight and the saved layer count follow the actual drafter presence.

## Validation

Rebased on `main` at `e88ee39d` (0.2.0-beta); the commit is now `5a14ef2a` on top of it.

**Passed:**
- `git rebase upstream/main` — the single commit replayed onto `e88ee39d` with no conflicts; `git diff --check` clean.
- Re-read every session-save/restore call site in `src/program/generate.cpp` on `e88ee39d`: SAVE sources, the read limits, validate, restore and the layer count all take the nullable `session_draft`; the only other draft-passing callers are the `batch_mtp` copies, which are guarded by `batch_mtp` and are not affected.

**Failed:**
- none observed.

**Not run:**
- The build and `conversation_transfer_test`, `conversation_validation_test`, `conversation_file_test`, `conversation_snapshot_test` were not re-run on 0.2.0-beta: the machine I have now is macOS arm64 with no CUDA toolkit and no NVIDIA GPU, so the engine does not build here. The 4055-check run in the original description was on `d5ea713`, and I am not restating it as a 0.2.0-beta result.
- The reporter's Q6_K pack, Windows, HIP and SYCL remain untested.

## Limits

The 0.2.0-beta build and test run is the one open item; I will post it in this thread as soon as a GPU is available. The SYCL copy of the session code (`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`) is not changed by this PR.

Combines the completed twelve-variant Tool-Eval-Bench report with the analysis formerly presented separately in #1497. Preserves original scenario scores, traces, model/runtime disclosures, equal-category weighting and preference-weighted scoring. No new inference or rescoring.

Current figures use the hardware-matched RTX PRO 6000 Q8 retest: short 29/30 points (97/100), standard 121/138 (88/100). The separate three-P4 receipts remain historical supporting evidence. Gyro uses its recorded patched runtime and excludes TC-45; these single trials do not establish a general model ranking.

The equal-category view assigns exactly 1/15 to every category. The preference view retains tool selection/recovery priorities and explicitly excludes zero-weight categories. Both are analysis views, not the official benchmark point percentage or coding-success probabilities.

Validation: independently recomputed all 12 weighted and 12 equal-category scores from pinned category counts. Updated against main 61b3fb5d; git diff --check passed. Data, figures, formulas and reproduction scripts are included.

pulls.title: Add a workflow that builds and pushes the Docker image on a version tag
pulls.author: nullata
pulls.body:
Issue: Resolves #1482

## Summary
Builds the CUDA Docker image in GitHub Actions on a `v*` tag and pushes it to GHCR, so users can `docker pull` instead of compiling the engine themselves (docs/INSTALL.md, "Docker (Linux)"). Closes the gap described in #1482.

## What changed
- `.github/workflows/release-docker-image.yml` (new): builds and pushes on a `v*` tag, plus `workflow_dispatch` for a manual rebuild (which does not move `:latest`). The version comes from the tag and must match `project(strata VERSION ...)` in CMakeLists.txt. amd64 only: the engine needs x86-64 AVX2, and an emulated arm64 CUDA compile could not run on an arm64 GPU host anyway. Tags: `:latest`, `:<version>`, `:<version>-cuda13` — the `-cuda13` suffix leaves room for a HIP or SYCL image later. No secrets: the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `packages: write` pushes to GHCR.
- `Dockerfile`: new `ARG PORTABLE=0`, threaded into the engine and vision cmake calls. A published image is not built on the PC it runs on, so CI sets `PORTABLE=1` to get the AVX2 floor (CMakeLists.txt's `STRATA_PORTABLE`, the same failure #411 #412 #419 fixed for the vision encoder). The default stays native, so `docker build -t strata .` is unchanged.

## Extra Notes
Measured on my fork (nullata/Strata, [run 37717607320](https://github.com/nullata/Strata/actions/runs/37717607320)): one uncached build on ubuntu-latest takes ~1h32m; the image is 5.3 GB compressed. Runner disk is not a problem (86 GB free). The image has not been run on a GPU yet — CI has none. If you'd rather keep Docker builds native-only, closing this PR (and #1482) is fine.

pulls.title: Responses persistence and disk-only cache: CUDA/HIP integration
pulls.author: CC-David-CC
pulls.body:
## Summary
Validate #1269, #1271 and #1480 together with instruction/reasoning replay corrections, experimental Responses persistence and optional generated summaries.

The point is to test the boundaries between these features: can a chat resume after another chat, a summary pass or a restart without losing its history or restoring the wrong inference state? If KV files are evicted or damaged, the server must rebuild from durable history. This provides a tested core for downstream profile-based applications.

## What changed
Preserves the original commit histories. Live testing found and fixed non-MTP snapshot failures: capture and restore now omit the absent draft ring. Adds regression coverage, a live probe and integration notes. Persistence and summary generation remain separate opt-ins.

## Simple examples
Enable server options:
```text
--experimental-responses-persistence --responses-store-path ./history
```
Add engine options to your existing configuration:
```text
--conversation-cache-disk-only --conversation-cache-spill-dir ./kv --conversation-cache-disk-mib 2048
```
Keep those directories across restarts. Generated summaries remain off by default.

Use your configured model name and API key. Each reply is capped at 128 tokens:
```python
from openai import OpenAI
c = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", api_key="your-key")
def ask(text, parent=None):
    return c.responses.create(
        model="strata", input=text, previous_response_id=parent,
        max_output_tokens=128, reasoning={"effort": "none"})

# Code chat, then an independent research chat.
code = ask("Write a Python function that squares a number.")
research = ask("Explain why a control group matters in an experiment.")

# Continue the code chat without resending its history.
reply = ask("Add a test for a negative number.", code.id)
print(reply.output_text)
print(reply.id)  # Save this ID; use it as parent after a server restart.
```
The same continuation call works after restart. KV reuse accelerates compatible prefixes; a missing cache does not erase the conversation.

## Validation and merge notes
| Check | CUDA / RTX 4090 | HIP / RX 7900 XTX |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native cache tests | 8 passed | 7 passed |
| Live integration checks | 33 passed | 33 passed |
| Cached tokens after restart | 1429 | 1429 |

Each backend ran 389 API tests with four optional skips; a dependency-enabled follow-up passed 25 tests. Live coverage includes branching, deletion, summaries on/off, cancellation, corrupt-cache fallback and eviction.

Validated engine: e6da7e11. Scope: Linux, one GPU, 8K context, int8 KV, MTP off. Maximum context, multi-GPU and live MTP remain unvalidated. This is functional validation, not a speed comparison.

Merge the combined candidate once, or use resulting main if its components land separately. Keep downstream profile selection and immutable revision binding in the application.

Detailed results: https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/work/responses-disk-cache-core/docs/RESPONSES_DISK_INTEGRATION.md

pulls.title: serve: --conversation-cache-disk-only - the conversation cache on disk, with no RAM budget (depends on #1271, #1269)
pulls.author: routhjim
pulls.body:
**Stacked on #1271 (spill directory) and #1269 (streaming restore).** The branch is #1271 (at 4af468f, which brings in v0.1.41) with #1269 (at d258f18) merged in. Only the last eight commits are new:
- dd146f4: the mode;
- b189048: tests and docs;
- ff30368: the cold-page-cache numbers in the docs;
- 2987ac4, a040357, 9eac670: persistent prefix entries (below), with tests and docs.
- 83ad1c5, 155dd84: from @ed-hch's CUDA test: a refused disk read keeps its file, and the monitor card shows the disk tier.

I will rebase once those two land, or fold this into #1271 if its author prefers.

#1271 keeps the conversations the RAM cache evicts on disk. A conversation reaches disk only through a RAM eviction (`make_room`), so the RAM budget still decides what is kept. On a machine where the expert cache takes nearly all memory (Strix Halo: 72 GiB of experts in 128 GB), the conversation cache needs that budget most and can afford it least.

`--conversation-cache-disk-only`, with `--conversation-cache-spill-dir`, keeps the conversation cache on disk only:
- When a request switches to another conversation, the outgoing one is written to the directory the way a session SAVE writes it. The running state and the deepest checkpoint are copied; the K/V streams from its pools into the file (`conversation_snapshot_sources` + the streaming `session_file_write`). No host image is made.
- When a conversation comes back, it is read the way #1269's RESTORE reads it. The read pass checks the whole file before anything on the GPU changes; a bad file is dropped, and the prompt is read as usual. Then the apply pass writes the pools 16 MiB at a time, with RESTORE's fail-stop after the first block.
- `--conversation-cache-mib` is not used. `--conversation-cache-disk-mib` is the only limit, so no conversation is refused for its size. A read or save still checks free RAM for its transient buffers (one checkpoint's running state and two 16 MiB blocks) against `--conversation-cache-min-free-mib`. When that refuses, the file is kept for a later turn.
- v0.1.41's RAM-admission eviction (#1347) is on the RAM parking path; disk-only mode never reaches it.
- The new file is written before this conversation's older copies are dropped. `drop_superseded` gains a `keep` path, because its rule alone would drop the new copy too. A failed write loses nothing.
- The agent's next turn of the live conversation writes nothing. It resumes at the newest turn checkpoint, and the outgoing tail is only the reply the client sends again.
- A clean shutdown saves the live conversation, flushed. Switch saves skip the flushes: a file torn by a crash fails the payload hash when it is read and is dropped.
- Single GPU, without `--batch` or `--peer-device`; otherwise the flag says so and is off.

**Where it helps.** A coding agent run as several sessions on one local engine: Claude Code through an Anthropic-compatible proxy, or a manager such as Happier that starts sessions from a phone. Each session is a long conversation (20-120K tokens), and they alternate. With one GPU and no RAM to spare, every switch read the whole conversation again. One real Claude Code session of 121K tokens took 181 s to read and 2.0 s to restore from disk. A new session started from a 13K-token preamble that is the same every time, and read all of it.

**Prefix entries.** When a conversation is saved, its shared opening is also saved on its own as `strata-conv-prefix-N`, once per distinct opening. The opening is the deepest `"strata_prefix"` checkpoint on the live path when the request pinned one. Otherwise it is the root by the engine's rule: the first turn boundary at least `--prompt-cache-root` tokens in. A new conversation that opens the same way resumes from it.
- Prefix entries are never removed as superseded. The disk budget evicts every ordinary conversation before one of them. A restart keeps them as prefixes, and `has_prefix` dedupes them.
- The sidecar format is unchanged; the kind is in the file name.
- In disk-only mode a request that resumes at a pinned prefix is another conversation, so the one it leaves is saved. The RAM cache's skip ("N queries cost one prefix") would drop it.

Measured with real Claude Code sessions. The client marks `"strata_prefix"` after Claude Code's leading `<system-reminder>` blocks, so the system prompt, tools and reminders form the shared part.

| first turn of a new session | prompt read | reused |
|---|---:|---:|
| without prefix entries | 15.7 s | 4,350 tokens |
| with them | **4.7 s** | **13,434 of 15,924** |
| with them, after an engine restart | **5.1 s** | **13,434** (the 420 MiB entry restored in 326 ms) |

The rest of each first turn is the user's own message and a per-session block, so it has to be read.

**Why this matters beyond the budget.** With #1271 as it is, a conversation larger than the free RAM budget is neither parked nor spilled:

```
skip parking (snapshot 1292 MiB exceeds available budget)
```

If its disk copy was restored a turn earlier, that copy was already removed as superseded, so the conversation is gone, and its next turn reads 15,954 tokens from the start (18.9 s, in the run below). The long conversations are the ones that gain the most from a disk tier. Disk-only mode never asks the RAM budget.

**Measured** on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB, Linux 7.2, ROCm 7.14.1, the iGPU alone).
- Build: per `docs/STRIX_HALO.md`.
- Model and flags: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with K-quant experts, `--mmap-experts --expert-cache auto --spec 4 --mtp mtp/rt --lookup-chain 3 --kv int8 --max-context 65536`. Spill directory on the internal NVMe.
- Workload: three agent-style conversations taking turns (A1 B1 C1 A2 ...). Each is a 9-12K-token first prompt, then turns that each add ~1.1K tokens of source text. Greedy, 64 output tokens. 3 rounds, an engine restart, then 2 more rounds.
- Reuse and prompt time come from the `/metrics` totals around each request.

| | prompt read, later turns (12) | turns resumed |
|---|---:|---:|
| no conversation cache | 11.4-22.3 s, nothing reused | 0 of 12 |
| #1271, `--conversation-cache-mib 2048 --conversation-cache-slots 1` | 2.4-3.0 s, 88-94% reused | 11 of 12 (the one above lost) |
| **this PR, `--conversation-cache-disk-only`** | **2.3-3.6 s, 88-94% reused** | **12 of 12** |

- A switch wrote 360-443 MiB in 181-196 ms. A return read it back in 291-351 ms, of which the read pass was ~150 ms.
- Cold disk: the same run again, with every spill file pushed out of the page cache before each request (`fsync`, then `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`; `fincore` showed 0 bytes resident each time). Restores took 275-361 ms (read pass 128-162 ms), and all 12 later turns resumed with the same 88-94% reuse.
- The files are smaller than #1271's parked images (1.0-1.4 GB) because only the deepest checkpoint is saved, as SAVE already does. Three conversations took 1.3 GB on disk.
- Process memory (`RssAnon`, sampled every 0.1 s) peaked 0.6 GiB above a run without the cache during a switch, and ended 0.15 GiB above it. No conversation stays in RAM.
- Greedy replies matched the run without the cache for 13 of 15 turns. The other two (the first turn after the restart, and the turn after it) are identical to #1271's replies for the same turns: a restore and a full read of the prompt round differently.

**Tests.** `conversation_spill_test`: 32 new checks, 73 pass. `test_monitor`: 2 new tests, 12 pass.
- A streamed spill writes byte for byte the file the image spill writes, matches and reads back with the same K/V.
- It refuses a host K/V image or an empty conversation.
- A failing source leaves no file and no index entry.
- `drop_superseded` spares the `keep` copy, while the rule alone would drop it.
- Prefix entries: named as prefixes, kept by `drop_superseded`, evicted last, deduped, and still prefixes after a reopen.

The engine paths were run end to end as above.

**Not tested:**
- CUDA (no NVIDIA card here) and Windows;
- `--kv-grow`: the restore calls `kvg_ensure` as the RAM restore does, but I did not run it with elastic K/V.

Measured with the help of Claude (Anthropic).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_013XBY17SSRKGmDXc2YFsrmp

pulls.title: Port Maya v1.0.14 NVIDIA GLM updates to Strata v0.1.41
pulls.author: apr3ndi5
pulls.body:
## Summary

Port compatible NVIDIA GLM updates from Project Maya `cfd2f45b506be6c02d715e3198b3ff9719de25fc` (v1.0.4) through `327cfa60d46f9d8eea33a1b38e76284646fbad86` (v1.0.14), integrated with Strata 0.1.41 main `fb58e0dbc8399662c0e47c76578c6e878b14f6cf`.

- GLM windowed MoE prefill, CPU/PCIe balancing, 3% RAM landing buffers with a 12–96 automatic range, GPU-sized chunks and next-layer read-ahead.
- Turing register WMMA and Ampere mma.sync attention, typed dense GEMV and contiguous CPU expert work pieces. Preserve the local synthetic Q4_0 path, latent sizing/alignment, slow diagnostic path and safe F32 fallback.
- Layer splits for up to 16 visible NVIDIA GPUs with input validation before planning. Add opt-in SSD text conversation slots, isolated per engine process and bounded by a disk budget/free-space reserve.
- Native GLM tool calls, streamed typed arguments, forced tool choice, and GLM tokenizer metadata at server startup. Reuse Strata 0.1.41 request hardening, API formats, dashboard and Qwen default.
- Explicit Maya-M/GSQ-RCO-3.5bit model choices alongside the existing Maya-S v2 default, immutable Hub revisions and verified SHA-256 manifests. GSQ has no MTP weights. Keep model downloads behind explicit consent.
- Opt-in GLM CPU-lane calibration through the existing installer and settings store. No measurement run with a model in this checkout.

### Conflict resolution and PR scope

Merge commits `ff9f6b8832b4d12aba40f8553204d120b7a3cc05` (PR #1420) and `0db33ad` resolve conflicts against official main without rewriting published history. Resolutions preserve the upstream CUDA toolkit discovery, baseline-ISA native-expert predicates and tokenizer piece cache together with the GLM adaptations.

This draft remains cumulative while #1420 is unmerged. The latest Maya update itself is [the incremental comparison](https://github.com/apr3ndi5/Strata/compare/0db33ad...cd297de8eaf60aea26011f50e5f4799d34d2cd42). No maintainer PR was merged or closed.

### Compatibility limits

This is a selective port, not a copy of the entire Maya fork. GLM continues to target native Linux/NVIDIA and experimental native Windows x64/NVIDIA; WSL, AMD/HIP and Intel remain rejected. Maya's new AMD extension requires its different HIP intrinsics/WMMA headers, tuning tables and GLM GEMM linkage, so it is not enabled here. The extra segment tokenizer cache, Maya launcher and benchmark command are not copied; Strata's existing piece cache, installer and diagnostics are retained.

No performance measurements from Maya are presented as measurements of this Strata integration. Full-model inference remains unverified. Installed models, configs and environments were preserved; MIT/OFL notices remain.

## Fresh validation — 2026-10-08

These results were run for this update, separately from previous PR results, on Windows with Python 3.10.5 and MSVC 19.51 / Visual Studio 2026:

- **1,116 distinct Python cases: 1,106 passed, 10 skipped**: full `serve` discovery 605 (596 passed/9 skipped), all `tools/test_setup_*.py` unittest modules 444 passed, additional pack/oracle/tokenizer/calibration modules 67 (66 passed/1 skipped). Repeated focused runs are not counted twice.
- The first full server run found an existing short-name/long-name Windows path comparison in the slots test. Canonicalizing the compared path fixed the expectation, and the final full run passed.
- **Five C++ CPU tests passed**: conversation cache, conversation memory, native split, prefill memory (19 checks) and GLM device-list parsing (12 checks).
- New Q2_K/Q3_K AVX-512 kernel and synthetic test compiled with MSVC. Arithmetic was explicitly skipped because this CPU lacks AVX-512.
- Synthetic Q4_0 fixture generated and packed on CPU: 184 tensors, 15 routed expert tensors, five disk-backed MoE layers. This is fixture/packing verification, not inference.
- CPU image encoder built; existing vendor MSBuild duplicate-source warning remains. Python/JavaScript syntax and Git whitespace checks passed.
- CMake rejected GLM with SYCL and without CUDA. Native Windows GLM configuration reached CUDA discovery and stopped at `No CUDA toolset found`.

Reproduce the Python tools group with `python -m unittest tools.test_glm_pack tools.test_glm_oracle tools.test_iq_pack tools.test_calibrate tools.test_calibrate_glm tools.test_strata_tokenizer`; server group with `python -m unittest discover -s serve -t .`. Installer modules were collected from `tools/test_setup_*.py` and loaded with `unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromNames`.

### Pending hardware checks

CUDA compilation/device linking; F32/WMMA/Turing-register/Ampere-mma attention parity; synthetic Q4_0 multichunk SSD prefill parity; real pinned-allocation cleanup; SSD slot round-trips; multiple-GPU pipelines; model calibration; full-model text/image/MTP quality and performance. The CPU kernel arithmetic also needs AVX-512 hardware. This checkout has no CUDA toolkit; VS 2026 does not meet the recommended CUDA 12.8/VS 2022 combination. The PR remains a draft.

No weights were downloaded and no production engine/server started. Mock server tests and generated local fixtures were used.

Final update commit: `cd297de8eaf60aea26011f50e5f4799d34d2cd42`.

pulls.title: Intel Arc A770 (DG2, 16 GB) support in the SYCL port
pulls.author: samsonnguyen
pulls.body:
## Title
Intel Arc A770 (DG2, 16 GB) support in the SYCL port
Issue: Resolves #692

The Alchemist cards on `xe` drivers have some weird bugs, which unfortunately need to be worked around. I've tried to ensure that these flags don't affect builds for other cards, and documented the issues i ran into.

## Summary
The SYCL port was written for the Arc Pro B70. This makes it build and run correctly on an Arc A770 (Alchemist, `xe` driver, 16 GB) with the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS model, plus a few engine fixes the A770 exposed. Everything is additive or gated to the cases that need it (a build option, an env switch, or a memory size above 4 GiB).

Measured on an A770 (xe driver, forced probe), Xeon E5 v4 host (PCIe 3.0 x16, AVX2 only), Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, oneAPI 2026.1, engine 0.1.40.3, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--stream-experts --expert-cache 5000 --vram-reserve-mib 1280 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp`, `STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=1 STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST=1`, greedy, 128 new tokens:

| | tok/s |
|---|---|
| decode, 19-token prompt | 17.5 |
| 8,191-token prompt, prefill | 491 |
| 8,191-token prompt, decode | 13.7 (2.0 tokens per round; per-round time unchanged) |

Not measured here: the B70 or any other card, the parity tests (built with `STRATA_SYCL_PARITY=OFF`), models other than IQ3_XXS (and, earlier, the Coder IQ1_M).

## What changed
- **`-DSTRATA_SYCL_NO_XMX=ON`**: compiles the `joint_matrix` kernels out. IGC for dg2 dies with a floating point exception on them.
- **Free VRAM**: `dpct::get_memory_info` asks Level Zero Sysman when the SYCL aspect is missing (xe reports nothing, so `--expert-cache auto` saw 0 bytes).
- **Pinned expert mirror** is allocated in chunks of at most 3 GiB (a single host allocation is capped near 4 GiB), and a GGUF ring slot is published only after its read has finished.
- **`-DSTRATA_SYCL_LARGE_BUFFERS=ON`** (`-ze-opt-greater-than-4GB-buffer-required`): without it, a kernel reading an expert more than 4 GiB into the cache read garbage.
- **Reversed expert cache** (`STRATA_CACHE_REVERSE`, automatic when the arena is over 4 GiB): oneMKL's bf16/f16 GEMM returns zeros when an input matrix starts 4 GiB or more into an allocation, so a prompt of about 1.5k tokens or more decoded to token 0 when the prompt path borrowed cache slots. The coldest slots now sit at the lowest addresses, the loan is the tail of the cache and capped at 3.9 GiB, and the kernels reading slots take per-slot device offsets. Reproducer: `sycl/tests/repro/mkl_gemm_4gib.cpp`; host test: `sycl/tests/expert_cache_reverse_test.cpp`.
- **A device wait that gives up is an error**: each wait kernel counts timeouts per flag; the verifier refuses the window and names the flag (`STRATA_WAIT_TIMEOUT=warn` only reports, `STRATA_SPIN_MAX` sets the bound). Before, the window went on with data the host had not written and the recurrent state kept the garbage.
- **Adaptive tier in GPU-only mode**: `resident_plan` counts routed experts on the device, so the adaptive swaps run with `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST` (hit rate 33% to 87% on the Coder IQ1_M), and a swap victim is only taken if it can be re-read from a pinned mirror.
- **Q6_K padded to 224 bytes** (`STRATA_Q6K_REPACK=1`, off by default): aligned weight loads in the decode mmvq kernel. +6% GPU-only decode on the Coder IQ1_M (9.77 to 10.37 tok/s); no measurable change on IQ3_XXS (17.5 against 17.2). `mmvq_bench --selftest` checks it against the GGUF layout.
- **Polled host memory stays plain when `STRATA_VERIFY_NO_HOST` is set**: nothing waits on a host store in that mode, and the uncached allocation cost 42 ms per decode window on the A770 (13.1 against 17.5 tok/s). Uncached allocation is unchanged in every other mode, and `STRATA_HOST_UNCACHED=0` still turns it off.
- **Docs**: `docs/INTEL_A770.md` (bring-up, what differs from the B70, measurements) and `docs/INTEL_A770_ISSUES.md` (the driver, runtime and compiler problems found, with workarounds), and a pointer in `docs/INTEL.md`.

## Extra Notes
- The A770 needs `IGC_EnableDPEmulation=1 OverrideDefaultFP64Settings=1` at build time (no fp64 in hardware; the engine uses double on purpose) and `UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1` at run time. Details are in `docs/INTEL_A770.md`.
- I built with `-DSTRATA_SYCL_SPIN_MAX=20000`; the default for a non-B-series AOT build (2,000,000 polls) is what a plain build gets.
- The commits are in dependency order and can be reviewed one by one.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pulls.title: feat: optionally offload idle session state while keeping model weights loaded
pulls.author: W1nge
pulls.body:
An idle serving process currently keeps its session VRAM and host checkpoint payloads allocated even when the model should stay loaded but no request is running. This adds opt-in session offload using the existing CUDA VMM implementation: commit a process-local snapshot, release physical session pages, then restore at the same virtual addresses on the next command.

The default remains disabled. The supported scope is one CUDA VMM GPU with fully resident KV; incompatible batch, pipeline, remote, multi-GPU and elastic-KV configurations are rejected. Writes finish before memory is released; write failure retains memory. Missing, corrupt or expired snapshots clear cached history and reread the next prompt. GPU remap failure is fatal. The server exposes cache state and released bytes in `/v1/status`. Usage and limitations are in `docs/IDLE_SESSION.md`.

Validation on Windows / RTX 2080 Ti, based on v0.1.40.3:

- Full engine build and native `idle_cache_test`: exact multi-region restore, CUDA graph replay after remapping, constants, corruption/truncation/missing/expired files and cleanup.
- 263 Python server tests passed; the cache-status test was rerun after final changes.
- Real IQ3_XXS, INT8 KV, MTP HTTP lifecycle passed twice: idle save and cache-hit restore, corrupt-file fallback, expiry fallback, cancellation followed by offload and successful generation. The 4096-context snapshot was 309,197,048 bytes, with approximately 5.3 s save and 367 ms restore in one local run. These are local operation timings, not a throughput claim.

Linux/HIP and other GPUs were not runtime-tested. Explicit conversation SAVE/RESTORE commands have not received a separate offloaded-state integration test. This is a focused port of our local idle-session implementation, adapted to upstream VmmRange and current checkpoint fields; no machine-specific tuning is enabled.

Prepared and tested with Codex at the repository owner's request.

pulls.title: bench: community report - RTX 4090, Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at 204800, engine 0.1.40.3
pulls.author: Dmitry-B
pulls.body:
Follow-up of [#1377](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1377) / [2026-10-07](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/tree/main/bench/results/2026-10-07-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-code): the same PC, the same model, the same server config and the same method, now on engine **0.1.40.3**, measured 2026-10-08.

- `bench/results/2026-10-08-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-code/` - code-explanation prompts
- `bench/results/2026-10-08-community-rtx4090-iq3xxs-200k-ru/` - Russian prose, same sweep

## Hardware, model, configuration

RTX 4090 24 GB (23028 MiB), Ryzen 9 7950X, 46464 MiB RAM, NVMe (ADATA LEGEND 960), Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-38, driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.4. Model `qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_xxs`, context 204800, INT8 KV, `--mmap-experts`, expert cache auto, MTP draft pack, `--spec 4`, `draft_vocab=cyrillic`, experimental speed projection (control vector, layers 4-44), `--vram-reserve-mib 989`, `--pool-workers 10`. Engine **compiled from source** for `sm_89` with CUDA 13.4 - the release publishes Windows archives only, so this is the only path on Linux; 0.1.40, 0.1.40.1, 0.1.40.2 and 0.1.40.3 in these reports were all built the same way on this machine.

Unchanged from the previous reports: the launch command (compared line by line in the server log), the server config files, the learned expert profile, and the engine's auto prompt chunk - `8192 tokens, a 96-slot ring` in 0.1.38 through 0.1.40.3 - so the numbers are comparable with the 0.1.38 / 0.1.39 / 0.1.40 / 0.1.40.2 reports from this PC.

Method is unchanged: full warm-up sweep discarded (its first 4K read ran at 1660.6 tok/s with a 2.416 s TTFT against 2146-2162 tok/s and 1.86-1.87 s in the measured pass - the cold expert cache, not the version), then 4K / 32K / 128K and a generation-only case, 3 runs each, random marker in every prompt (no prefix reuse), throughput from the engine's timing fields, TTFT over streaming, `tools/needle_bench.py` at 32K and 128K, depths 10/50/90.

## What each folder contains

`runs.json` (0.1.40.3) plus three reference runs, so the comparison is self-contained:

- `runs-0.1.40.2-previous.json` - the previous version, measured 2026-10-07 with this method;
- `runs-0.1.40-baseline.json` - the 0.1.40 baseline, measured 2026-10-06;
- `runs-0.1.40.1-control.json` - a full repeat of the sweep on **the identical engine binary** (0.1.40.1 changed only the Python server). This is the noise band of the method on this machine: prompt -6.6…+0.8%, decode -5.6…+8.6%.

## Results, in short

- **0.1.40.3 is not measurable on this machine.** Prompt throughput moved by -2.8…-0.6% (code) and -0.2…+3.6% (Russian) against a same-binary band of -6.6…+0.8%; decode moved by -5.0…+3.5% and -5.6…+3.2% against a band of -5.6…+8.6%; TTFT by 0.03-0.24 s. The ranges in both versions are tight (3278-3314 and 3335-3341 tok/s at 131072 tokens), so this is a negative result rather than an inconclusive one.
- **That matches what the release changes.** For a Linux/NVIDIA build the diff touches: an `n_expert == 512 && K == 10` guard on the drafter's per-token router call (#1357) - this model has `expert_count = 512` and `expert_used_count = 10` in its GGUF metadata, so the guarded native path is the one already taken; HIP/Windows-only diagnostics in `generate.cpp`; a kernel self-test in `native_multi_parity.cpp`; and the commit that made `STRATA_MMVQ_IL` opt-in is reverted in the same release, so the interleaved q8_1 projections stay on by default exactly as in 0.1.40.2. Everything else in 0.1.40.3 is Intel Arc setup, Windows AMD packaging, Docker, the web app and the tokenizer.
- **The 0.1.40 -> 0.1.40.2 prompt gain is intact.** Against the 0.1.40 baseline this build reads +2.7…+8.5% (code) and +6.4…+16.1% (Russian) with TTFT 0.02-2.5 s lower. Trend at 131072 tokens on this PC: 2962 -> 3085 -> 3119 -> 3313 -> 3292 (code) and 2984 -> 3126 -> 3136 -> 3317 -> 3336 (Russian) tok/s across 0.1.38 / 0.1.39 / 0.1.40 / 0.1.40.2 / 0.1.40.3.
- **One correction to #1377.** That report attributed the 0.1.40.2 prompt gain to the stager wait change (#1057). The 0.1.40.3 docs measure the opposite - sleeping stager waits read prompts 5-6% slower on a Ryzen 9 7940HS + RTX 4070 laptop (while whole-machine CPU use falls from 77-90% to 21-25%), and spinning is 1.2% faster on a desktop RTX 5070 - so #1057 is a CPU-load feature, not a speed feature. That attribution in the 0.1.40.2 report should be read as withdrawn; its measured numbers are unchanged. The cause of the 0.1.40.2 prompt gain is not identified by these measurements - only that it is uniform across lengths.
- Recall 6/6 at 32K and 128K, unchanged.
- The Russian variant is published as a second folder on purpose: prompt throughput is essentially script-independent (3363-3383 vs 3316-3351 tok/s at 32K), decode is not (95.4-100.9 vs 136.2-138.9 tok/s), and the gap tracks draft acceptance (47-80% vs 74-79%). Cyrillic also tokenizes ~2% denser than the code text at the same nominal length, so cross-script comparisons have to use actual token counts.

## Limitations stated in the reports

Synthetic prompts, greedy decoding, early stops on repetitive text (actual generated lengths are in the tables - and they are why the decode column is not comparable across versions when the lengths differ), the OS not isolated, and this server also serves an interactive agent session - no request from it was issued during the measured runs, and the discarded warm-up is described in each report. Opt-ins from this release (`STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE`, `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH`, `pin=N`, `STRATA_SPEC_GUMBEL`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0`, `STRATA_STAGER_SLEEP=0`) were not tested and are not part of these numbers. The measurement script is a local script, not included in the PR; available on request.

No engine changes in this PR - measurements only.

pulls.title: cuda: retain HC norm products in existing scratch
pulls.author: W1nge
pulls.body:
The split/staged HC normalization reads the residual twice and recomputes a pending write after its reduction. Store the unscaled R * norm product in the existing xn scratch during the first pass, then scale it in place. The reduction order and two multiplication roundings stay unchanged. This extracts the useful part of our local stream-norm path without adding another kernel variant or tuning flag.

Validation on RTX 2080 Ti (sm_75), Windows/MSVC, driver 560.94:
- The existing fused_gr_selftest passed all plain/split/staged comparisons, including windows of 1..8 tokens with and without a pending write, bit for bit.
- A direct norm comparison also matched xn and rs bit for bit at T=1,2,4,8, both write modes.
- A CUDA-graph microprobe (1000 launches per graph, 10 alternating rounds) measured reductions from 3.2% to 17.1% for this norm kernel. These are component timings, not end-to-end decode gains. Other GPU generations and HIP are not measured; draft pending broader validation. The existing per-device correctness check/fallback remains intact.

The existing internal selftest can be run in a small CUDA TU including src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu, calling fused_gr_selftest(ok, why), and requiring ok[1], ok[2], ok[3]. This checks the actual production kernels. No changes to public APIs, allocation sizes or hardware selection.

Based directly on d5ea713, independent of the prefill memory and prompt-reuse PRs.


Validation update (2026-10-08): a complete current-main integration build including #1451, #1454, #1455, #1457 and #1465 passed four real IQ3_XXS model baseline/integration pairs on RTX 2080 Ti: default, GR_UNFUSED, PREFILL_BF16X2 and legacy RING_BYTES modes. Each used INT8 KV, 194 input tokens, two prefill chunks and 8 output tokens; all runs exited successfully and output IDs matched within each pair. A 256K configured-context startup and short generation also passed (this did not fill a 256K prompt). These are combined regression checks, not an isolated performance result or exhaustive state equality. Other hardware/backends remain untested. The earlier draft-only status reflected the absence of any current-main model run; now requesting review with these limits explicit.
